# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## PDN Target Impedance Multi-Frequency AC Simulation & DRC Sign-off

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Step 1: Multi-Rail   │
│   S-Parameter Model    │
│       Extraction       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│        Step 2:         │
│   Multi-Frequency AC   │
│  PDN Sweep: 100 Hz to  │
│        200 MHz         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│        Step 3:         │
│  Anti-Resonance Peak   │
│     Suppression &      │
│        Damping         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Step 4: Loadboard    │
│     DRC & Current      │
│    Density Sign-off    │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

#### Step 1: Multi-Rail S-Parameter & Parasitic Model Extraction
1. Import the routed ATE loadboard layout database into the 3D planar electromagnetic (EM) field solver.
2. Define simulation ports for all primary supply rails:
   - Core Supply: $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$
   - Wordline Boost Rail: $V_{PP} = 2.5\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$
   - Bitline Precharge Reference: $V_{BLP} = V_{DD}/2 = 0.9\text{ V}$
3. Assign broadband touchstone / S-parameter models for the DUT socket pogo-pins ($L_{pin} \le 1.2\text{ nH}$, $R_{contact} \le 35\text{ m}\Omega$), via barrels, and plane-plane inter-layer capacitance.

#### Step 2: Multi-Frequency AC PDN Impedance Sweep (100 Hz to 200 MHz)
1. Configure an AC frequency sweep from $100\text{ Hz}$ to $200\text{ MHz}$ at the DUT BGA/pogo-pin interface pads.
2. Allocate decoupling stages targeting specific physical switching mechanisms:
   - **DC – 100 kHz (VRM/DPS Loop)**: Remote sense lines aligned to ATE Device Power Supply channels.
   - **100 kHz – 10 MHz (Bulk Decoupling)**: High-capacitance low-ESR polymer/tantalum capacitors ($47\ \mu\text{F}\text{ to }100\ \mu\text{F}$).
   - **10 MHz – 50 MHz (Charge Pump Resonance Damping)**: Low-inductance MLCC network placed near $V_{PP}$ breakout pins to absorb switching noise from the on-chip Dickson charge pump flying capacitor clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$ running at $20\text{ MHz to }50\text{ MHz}$).
   - **50 MHz – 200 MHz (Sense Amp Activation Spike Absorber)**: High-density 0402/0201 reverse-geometry ceramic capacitors placed under socket cavity to buffer $dI/dt$ transitions during P-sense/N-sense activation ($1\text{ to }2\text{ ns}$ delay between SAN and SAP).

```text
                        Target Impedance Profile (mOhm) 
                       ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                       │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 50 MHz - 200 MHz (DUT)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                       │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒              │
 10 MHz - 50 MHz (MLCC)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒              │
100 kHz - 10 MHz (Bulk)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                    │
                       │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                    │
     DC - 100 kHz (VRM)┤█████                          │
                       │█████                          │
                       └┬───────┬──────┬───────┬──────┬┘
                       0.0    21.2   42.5    63.8  85.0 
```

#### Step 3: Anti-Resonance Peak Suppression & Damping Optimization
1. Extract self-impedance $Z_{11}(f)$ across all power ports.
2. Inspect for anti-resonance peaks generated by planar inductance interacting with MLCC capacitance.
3. If $Z_{11}(f) > Z_{target}$ at any node, add snubbers with controlled Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR) or stagger MLCC decade values ($100\text{ nF} + 10\text{ nF} + 1\text{ nF}$) to damp the Q-factor.

#### Step 4: Loadboard DRC & DC/AC Current Density Sign-off
1. Execute multi-rail DRC checking clearance between high-voltage $V_{PP}$ copper planes and sensitive analog/reference nodes ($V_{BLP}$ reference lines).
2. Run DC electro-thermal / IR-drop simulation:
   - Verify maximum DC trace voltage drop $\le 18\text{ mV}$ ($1\%$ of $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$) under worst-case write currents.
   - Confirm trace and via current densities satisfy reliability limits for continuous HTOL burn-in operation at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Physical Unit | Evaluation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Broadband Target Impedance ($Z_{target}$)** | $\le 85.0$ | $\text{m}\Omega$ | AC $Z_{11}$ profile across $100\text{ Hz} \le f \le 200\text{ MHz}$ at DUT pogo-pin interface |
| **Max AC Ripple Voltage ($\Delta V_{ripple}$)** | $\le 54.0$ ($3\%$ of $1.8\text{ V } V_{DD}$) | $\text{mV}_{p-p}$ | Transient co-simulation with $1\text{ ns to }2\text{ ns}$ SAN/SAP sense switching loads |
| **$V_{PP}$ High-Voltage Rail Impedance** | $\le 120.0$ | $\text{m}\Omega$ | AC sweep over Dickson clock spectrum ($20\text{ MHz to }50\text{ MHz}$) |
| **DRC Max DC Current Density ($J_{max}$)** | $\le 30.0$ | $\text{mA/}\mu\text{m}^2$ | 2D/3D copper conductor current density solver at $85^\circ\text{C}$ burn-in |

---

### 3. Citations & Literature Context Verification

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Confirms stacked capacitor integration over bitline (COB), cell capacitance budget of $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$, and leakage budget ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$), dictating the refresh current profile and baseline DC load.
- **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**:
  - Verifies wordline overdrive voltage requirement of $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{overdrive} \ge 2.5\text{ V to }2.8\text{ V}$ (against nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$) and Dickson oscillator clock frequencies ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$ at $20\text{ MHz to }50\text{ MHz}$ with $C_{pump} = 20\text{ pF to }50\text{ pF}$), defining the targeted anti-resonance damping band.
- **Cross-Coupled Regenerative Sense Amplifier Timing & Charge Restoration**:
  - Establishes the $V_{BLP} = V_{DD}/2$ ($0.9\text{ V}$) equalization voltage level and the fast $1\text{ to }2\text{ ns}$ SAN-to-SAP activation transition, establishing the high-frequency switching transient ($50\text{ MHz to }200\text{ MHz}$) for loadboard MLCC bypass placement.

---
*Note: Micro-knowledge captured in [`docs/knowledge/pdn_ac_simulation_drc_signoff.md`](./docs/knowledge/pdn_ac_simulation_drc_signoff.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The power delivery network (PDN) simulation must account for the composite loop impedance spanning from the ATE pin electronics channel through the tester pogo-pin interface, loadboard PCB transmission planes, and socket contactors down to the 180nm DRAM DUT package ball grid array. The concurrent switching noise (di/dt) induced by simultaneous activation of 512 sense-amplifiers and 28 fF cell refresh operations yields transient current steps exceeding 1.8 A within 2 ns. If target AC impedance Z_target is not maintained below 85 mOhm from DC up to 250 MHz (the Nyquist limit of 200 MHz DDR operation), ground bounce and VDD sagging will exceed the +/-5% voltage budget, causing read-margin collapse on the folded bitline structure.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node with a folded bitline cell area of 0.259 um^2 and bitline-to-cell capacitance ratio of 7:1 (C_b ~ 196 fF, C_s ~ 28 fF), the differential sensing margin delta-V is only ~150 mV across bitline true and complement rails. High-frequency PDN resonance between the 1.2 nH pogo-pin inductance and the on-board decoupling ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) near 45 MHz to 90 MHz threatens to modulate the VDD/VSS reference during the sensing strobe. The frequency-domain AC simulation must enforce strict anti-resonance peak damping using staggered 0402/0201 multi-tier MLCC capacitor arrays (100nF, 10nF, 1nF NPO/X7R) placed within 3 mm of the socket footprint.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-low equivalent series inductance (ESL) reverse-geometry capacitors (such as 0306 or 0508 packages) or specialized embedded capacitance cores (e.g., 3M C-Ply) introduces 18-to-24-week lead times and single-vendor vulnerabilities. The loadboard layout must prioritize readily available automotive-grade AEC-Q200 standard 0402 X7R and 0603 multi-layer ceramic capacitors with standardized pad geometries and dual-source availability across TDK, Murata, and Kyocera.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Loadboard PCB fabrication and assembly sign-off cannot absorb iterative re-spins due to uncalibrated EM solver port settings. Automated DRC sign-off scripts and multi-frequency AC S-parameter extractions must be executed with signed rule decks prior to milestone tapeout lock, strictly preserving the 3-week timeline for physical pogo-pin loadboard fabrication before wafer sort qualification commences.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Mid-frequency anti-resonance impedance spike (> 180 mOhm at 65 MHz) exceeding the maximum dynamic noise margin of 1.8V VDD rail during simultaneous row active and refresh commands.
1. DC IR drop along narrow necked loadboard power planes starving the DUT VDD rail below 1.71V during sustained JEDEC DDR burst writes.
1. High-speed pogo-pin ground return loop inductance causing common-mode ground bounce that corrupts single-ended SSTL_2 strobe (DQS) threshold crossings.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-1-1-3-01` | **Broadband Multi-Port AC PDN S-Parameter and Z-Impedance Profile Verification** | Keysight E5080B 4-Port Vector Network Analyzer (100 kHz - 9 GHz), Picoprobe Dual Micro-coaxial 50-Ohm Probes, FormFactor Probe Station, Ansys SIwave 3D FEA Solver | 1. Perform full 2-port SOLT calibration of the VNA from 100 kHz to 1 GHz using micro-coaxial reference substrate. 2. Land micro-probes directly onto the DUT socket pogo-pin landing pads representing VDD_CORE (1.8V) and adjacent GND pins. 3. Measure two-port shunt-through S21 transmission parameters across 100 kHz to 500 MHz. 4. Convert measured S-parameters to complex loop impedance Z11(f) using standard shunt-through extraction equations. 5. Import Ansys SIwave AC multi-frequency simulation dataset and overlay simulated Z-profile with measured VNA curve. | `Measured and simulated Z_profile must remain <= 85 mOhm across 100 kHz to 250 MHz bandwidth; maximum peak anti-resonance impedance must not exceed 110 mOhm; correlation coefficient between simulation and physical VNA measurement must be R^2 >= 0.92.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-1-1-3-02` | **High-Current Transient Di/Dt Voltage Droop and Ground Bounce Verification under Simulated Row Refresh** | Tektronix MSO64B 4 GHz Digital Oscilloscope, 50-Ohm passive high-bandwidth coax probe (P6158), Programmable ATE Fast Current Sinking Load Fixture (1.8A step in 2ns) | 1. Set ATE power supply to deliver 1.80V regulated rail with current limit configured to 3.0A. 2. Trigger fast transient load pulse sinking 1.8A with rise time tr = 2.0 ns, simulating full-bank sense amplifier burst refresh. 3. Capture AC-coupled transient voltage wave on the oscilloscope at the pogo-pin socket contact pad. 4. Measure peak-to-peak voltage ripple (droop and overshoot) and settling time to within +/-2% of DC steady-state. | `Peak transient voltage droop delta-VDD must be <= 90 mV (within +/-5% of 1.8V); ground bounce on VSS must be <= 45 mV; oscillation settling time to steady state must be <= 8.5 ns.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact splash-resistant safety glasses, Class 00 ESD-safe conductive nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness), Flame-resistant static-dissipative lab coat (cotton/polyester conductive blend)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with cleaning solvents or flux residues, flush skin with copiously flowing deionized water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated apparel. For eye contact, flush eyes continuously at eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. For vapor inhalation, transport victim to fresh open air and administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized laminar exhaust hood maintaining continuous capture velocity >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) at the PCB rework/cleaning station, venting through certified VOC/HEPA filtration ducting.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent isopropyl alcohol wash solvents in designated DOT-approved UN-rated flammable polyethylene solvent waste containers; do not mix with aqueous acid or base streams; dispose of via licensed hazardous waste incinerator.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9% wt` |
| **Lead-Free Solder Rosin Flux Residue (Abietic Acid base)** | `514-10-3` | Analytical Reagent | `15.0% wt in solvent carrier` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly stripped and electro-plated ENIG (Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold, 0.05-0.10 um Au over 3-5 um Ni) pogo-pin test pad contact array, free of organic flux residue and ionic contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: S-parameter validated, cleaned and nitrogen-desiccated loadboard contact surface sealed under static-shielding moisture barrier bag (MBB) with desiccant pouch and humidity indicator card (HIC < 10% RH).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Galvanic surface oxidation and copper intermetallic migration through thin immersion gold layer causing contact resistance to spike > 250 mOhm per pogo-pin, rendering broadband S-parameter impedance sign-off invalid.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful multi-frequency AC PDN S-parameter impedance validation and DRC sign-off for the 180nm DRAM ATE DUT loadboard, demonstrating compliant loop impedance below 85 mOhm from DC up to 250 MHz, with fully verified Gerber/ODB++ layouts conforming to high-speed fabrication DRC rules.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ATE_DUT_PDN_AC_Impedance_Signoff_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `DUT_Power_Plane_S21_Measured_vs_Simulated.csv`
- [ ] `ATE_Loadboard_DRC_ERC_Zero_Violation_Log.txt`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum AC loop impedance of DUT 1.8V VDD power distribution rail across operating band (100 kHz to 250 MHz)** | `85.0` | +0.0 / -15.0 mOhm | Calibrated 2-port VNA shunt-through S21 measurement matched against Ansys SIwave simulation |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Peak transient dynamic voltage droop during 1.8A/2ns concurrent sense-amplifier activation current step** | `75.0` | +/-15.0 mV | High-bandwidth 4 GHz oscilloscope probe capture directly at socket DUT VDD pogo-pin landing pads |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Total DRC and high-speed electrical rule violations across complete 16-layer ATE DUT loadboard ODB++ layout database** | `0` | 0 (Zero defect) | Automated Altium/Cadence Allegro DRC rule engine check against fab PCB manufacturing rule decks |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Simulated and physical VNA S21-extracted PDN impedance across 100 kHz to 250 MHz strictly meets the <= 85 mOhm ceiling without anti-resonance spikes exceeding 110 mOhm, accompanied by zero DRC/ERC violations in ODB++ package, confirmed by formal engineering sign-off signatures from Systems Engineer and Domain Expert.

4. Measure peak-to-peak voltage ripple (droop and overshoot) and settling time to within +/-2% of DC steady-state.

# Standard Operating Procedure: High-Speed Controlled-Impedance Microstrip/Stripline Layout & Length Tuning

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The high-speed ATE loadboard interface must bridge the 180nm DRAM DUT package to the tester pin electronics without corrupting DDR timing margins (tIS/tIH, tDS/tDH). Microstrip routes on outer layers exhibit faster phase velocity than inner stripline layers due to effective dielectric constant disparity (eps_eff ≈ 3.1 vs eps_r ≈ 4.2 in FR4/Megtron-6). Length tuning across byte lanes (DQ/DQS) and address/command channels must strictly enforce propagation delay matching (t_pd) rather than raw physical trace length, compensating for via barrel stub capacitance and layer-transition flight-time deltas.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Controlled-impedance single-ended (50 Ω nominal, ±5%) and differential (100 Ω nominal, ±5% for CK/CK# and DQS/DQS#) routing must account for copper foil roughness (Ra/Rz) and glass weave skew effects. For high-speed DDR qualification testing on 180nm silicon, serpentine meanders introduced for length equalization must maintain a minimum serpentine loop pitch of at least 3x trace width (3W) to prevent self-coupling forward crosstalk, which introduces severe inter-symbol interference (ISI) and dynamic group delay distortion.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-low-loss core/prepreg laminates (e.g., Rogers RO4350B or Panasonic Megtron-6) directly increases PCB raw panel cost and extends prototype lead times to 4-6 weeks in Southeast Asian fabrication lines compared to standard high-Tg FR-4 (Isola 370HR). The procurement plan must secure certified panel stackup coupons with coupon TDR validation reports before releasing primary 16-layer ATE DUT board manufacturing lots.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Loadboard routing tapeout must lock drill tables and layer stackups 14 business days ahead of ATE docking validation. Any delay in post-layout 2.5D/3D full-wave electromagnetic extraction (S-parameters up to 10 GHz) will compress the qualification window for JEDEC DDR speed-binning and HTOL burn-in board socket installation, putting wafer-sort to packaged-die yield verification at risk.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. In-lane DQS-to-DQ propagation skew exceeding ±15 ps due to uncompensated microstrip-to-stripline dielectric phase-velocity mismatches, collapsing data-eye opening at ATE comparator strobe.
1. High-frequency reference-plane discontinuity across split power/ground planes inducing common-mode return current inductance and localized ground bounce (>50 mV).
1. Serpentine pitch violation (<3W spacing) generating deterministic jitter (DJ) via forward electromagnetic crosstalk, exceeding JEDEC DDR setup/hold time jitter budgets.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-1-2-01` | **Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Characteristic Impedance Verification of Microstrip and Stripline Loadboard Traces** | Keysight N1000A DCA-X Wideband Oscilloscope with N1055A 50 GHz TDR/TDT Remote Head, 2.92mm Precision Phase-Matched Coaxial Cables, GGB Industries Picoprobe Dual Ground-Signal-Ground (GSG) Probe. | 1. Launch a 35 ps incident step pulse from the TDR channel into the pogo-pin test point / SMA connector of the DQ0-DQ15 and DQS0/DQS1 trace lines. 2. Record the reflected voltage wave profile across the entire trace length from tester launch connector through breakout via to the DUT pin interface. 3. Extract the continuous instantaneous characteristic impedance profile Z0(t) across microstrip segments (top/bottom) and stripline segments (inner signal layers). 4. Evaluate maximum and minimum impedance excursions against nominal 50 Ω single-ended and 100 Ω differential design targets. | `Single-ended microstrip/stripline trace impedance Z0 must measure 50.0 Ω ± 2.5 Ω (47.5 Ω to 52.5 Ω) over the uninterrupted trace run. Differential pairs (CK/CK#, DQS/DQS#) must measure 100.0 Ω ± 5.0 Ω (95.0 Ω to 105.0 Ω). Impedance discontinuities at layer transition vias must not deviate by more than ±10% for a duration exceeding 60 ps.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-1-2-02` | **Vector Network Analyzer S-Parameter and Insertion Loss / Group Delay Flight-Time Skew Measurement** | Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67 4-Port Vector Network Analyzer (10 MHz - 67 GHz), SOLT Full 4-Port Calibration Kit, Micro-coaxial wafer RF probes (500 µm pitch GSG). | 1. Connect Port 1 and Port 2 of VNA to SMA/pogo launch pad and DUT socket pad for DQ0. 2. Perform frequency sweep from 10 MHz to 10 GHz with 10 kHz IF bandwidth; capture 4-port S-parameters (S11, S21, S22, S12). 3. Convert S21 phase to group delay tau_g(f) = -dphi/df. 4. Repeat S-parameter acquisition sequentially for all data lines in Byte 0 (DQ0-DQ7) and differential strobe DQS0/DQS0#. 5. Calculate cumulative propagation delay flight time t_pd and relative skew between DQS0 and each DQ bit. | `Differential insertion loss |S21| must be less than 1.8 dB at the Nyquist frequency of the DRAM interface (up to 1 GHz fundamental for DDR-400 / 200 MHz bus). Flight-time propagation delay skew across all DQ lines relative to DQS within Byte 0 must be strictly within ±10.0 ps. Total channel-to-channel Command/Address/Control skew relative to Clock (CK) must not exceed ±25.0 ps.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: EN 388 Level 3 cut-resistant handling gloves for bare FR4/Megtron PCB panel edge inspection, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact splash-resistant safety glasses, Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) safe dissipative lab coat with grounded wrist strap (ANSI/ESD S20.20 compliant), Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (thickness >= 4 mil) for solvent flux cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Seek ophthalmological attention if irritation persists. Skin Contact: Wash skin thoroughly with soap and water; remove contaminated apparel. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately; administer oxygen if respiration becomes labored. Ingestion: Do NOT induce vomiting; rinse mouth with water and seek emergency medical care immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized fume extraction hood with activated carbon filtration and minimum capture face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 fpm) dedicated to manual RF soldering, probe station degreasing, and solvent cleaning operations.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and contaminated IPA effluent must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-proof polyethylene hazardous chemical containers labeled 'Spent Flammable Solvents' and segregated according to local environmental hazardous waste disposal regulations. No drain discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, 2-Propanol)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.8% w/w` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (> 18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Bare ENIG (Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold, 3-5 µm Ni, 0.05-0.1 µm Au) or OSP-coated copper pads on fabricated ATE loadboard coupon, free of finger oils, particulate residue, or copper oxidation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Cleaned, micro-inspected, moisture-baked (<0.1% moisture content per J-STD-033), dry-packed PCB loadboard ready for precision pogo-block mounting and automated ATE socket installation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric exposure induces moisture absorption within hygroscopic PCB dielectric core layers (FR-4/Megtron prepregs), elevating dissipation factor tan(delta), degrading high-frequency insertion loss, and causing delamination or micro-blistering during socket reflow soldering.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed layout design, electromagnetic extraction, PCB fabrication, and metrology sign-off of the ATE DUT loadboard high-speed controlled-impedance microstrip and stripline interconnects. All single-ended 50 Ω and differential 100 Ω transmission lines, including length-matching serpentine traces, satisfy rigorous propagation delay skew tolerances for 180nm JEDEC DDR qualification testing.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ATE_DUT_LOADBOARD_IMPEDANCE_TDR_REPORT.csv`
- [ ] `ATE_DRAM_BYTE_LANE_SKEW_EXTRACTION.pdf`
- [ ] `ATE_LOADBOARD_FABRICATION_GERBER_ODB.zip`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Characteristic single-ended impedance (Z0) of microstrip and stripline traces across ATE loadboard** | `50.0` | ± 2.5 Ω (± 5.0%) | Keysight N1000A/N1055A 50 GHz TDR measurement across coupon and board test points at 25°C |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Intra-byte propagation delay flight-time skew between DQS0 strobe and DQ[7:0] lines** | `0.0` | ± 10.0 ps max | Full 4-port VNA S21 phase-derived group delay extraction up to 5 GHz on calibrated probe station |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum serpentine loop coupling forward crosstalk peak amplitude** | `0.0` | <= 15.0 mV (< 3.0% of 500 mV step) | TDT dual-channel active transmission measurement into 50 Ω terminated adjacent quiet line |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of single-ended and differential high-speed traces pass TDR impedance bounds (47.5-52.5 Ω and 95-105 Ω respectively); VNA S-parameter validation confirms intra-lane skew <= 10 ps and insertion loss <= 1.8 dB at 1 GHz; fabrication coupon microsection analysis validates copper trace geometry and layer dielectric thickness within ±7% of target stackup.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-ATE-PCB-STACKUP-IMPEDANCE-001`
**Title:** Stackup Cross-Section Synthesis & Controlled-Impedance Constraint Configuration  
**Context:** DRAM Foundation VN — 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Hierarchy:** Circuit Design / ATE Loadboard Interface Design & JEDEC Timing Vector Pattern Generation / ATE DUT Loadboard PCB Schematic & High-Speed Impedance-Matched Layout / High-Speed Controlled-Impedance Microstrip/Stripline Layout & Length Tuning  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180 nm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Scope & Engineering Objective

This standard operating procedure defines the physical cross-section synthesis, dielectric stackup engineering, and 2D field-solver constraint configuration for the Automated Test Equipment (ATE) Device-Under-Test (DUT) loadboard PCB. The board interfaces the 180nm open-source DRAM chip to high-speed ATE tester channels for JEDEC DDR speed-bin qualification and High-Temperature Operating Life (HTOL) burn-in testing.

The target DUT operates at core supply $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$, requires boosted wordline drive $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}$ to $2.8\,\text{V}$ (generated via on-chip Dickson charge pumps to eliminate the $V_{th} \sim 0.5\,\text{V}\text{--}0.7\,\text{V}$ pass-gate loss), and tests cell retention against the $25\text{--}30\,\text{fF}$ storage capacitor budget ($>64\,\text{ms}$ refresh at $85^\circ\text{C}$). Transmission lines must provide precise $50\,\Omega$ single-ended and $100\,\Omega$ differential matched impedances to avoid reflection-induced timing skew or double-clocking during ATE burst cycles.

---

### 2. Process Flow & Visual Workflow

```
Flowchart: ATE Loadboard Stackup Synthesis & Constraint Flow

 [Select Low-Loss Substrate & Layer Count]
                     │
                     ▼
 [Synthesize Symmetrical 8-Layer Core/Prepreg Stackup]
                     │
                     ▼
 [2D BEM Field Solver Extraction: Microstrip & Stripline]
                     │
                     ▼
 [Configure EDA Constraint Manager (Impedance & Spacing)]
                     │
                     ▼
 [Post-Route TDR Verification & Fab Coupon Serialization]
```

```text
             Target Impedance & Signal Integrity Budgets
            ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │░░░░░░░                                   │
Ret Loss S11┤░░░░░░░                                   │
            │      ▒▒                                  │
  Skew Match┤      ▒▒                                  │
Zdiff (100R)┤      ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
            │      ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
 Zo SE (50R)┤      ███████████████████                 │
            │      ███████████████████                 │
            └┬─────────┬──────────┬─────────┬─────────┬┘
           -18.0     11.5       41.0      70.5    100.0 
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Base Material & Symmetrical 8-Layer Stackup Definition
1. Select low-loss, high-Tg ($T_g \ge 170^\circ\text{C}$, $T_d \ge 340^\circ\text{C}$) FR-4/halogen-free core and prepreg laminate (e.g., Isola 370HR or Shengyi S1000-2M) capable of withstanding continuous HTOL thermal chamber cycling at $85^\circ\text{C}\text{--}125^\circ\text{C}$.
2. Define a symmetrical 8-layer cross-section with solid ground planes directly sandwiching all high-speed DRAM signal layers:
   - **L1 (Top Signal - Outer Microstrip):** $1.0\,\text{oz}$ finished Cu ($35\,\mu\text{m}$ thick including plating) + solder mask ($\varepsilon_r = 3.8$, thickness $18\,\mu\text{m}$).
   - **Dielectric D1-2 (Prepreg):** $1\times 2116$ prepreg glass style, nominal thickness $H_1 = 110\,\mu\text{m}$ ($4.33\,\text{mil}$), $\varepsilon_r = 4.10$, $\tan\delta = 0.016$ at $1\,\text{GHz}$.
   - **L2 (Plane 1 - Continuous GND):** $1.0\,\text{oz}$ Cu ($35\,\mu\text{m}$), dedicated solid ground reference for L1.
   - **Dielectric D2-3 (Core):** Dual-ply core laminate, thickness $H_2 = 150\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5.91\,\text{mil}$), $\varepsilon_r = 4.20$.
   - **L3 (Inner Signal 1 - Stripline):** $0.5\,\text{oz}$ Cu ($18\,\mu\text{m}$), high-speed JEDEC DDR data strobe (DQS) and byte-lane data (DQ) buses.
   - **Dielectric D3-4 (Prepreg):** Thickness $H_3 = 150\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5.91\,\text{mil}$), $\varepsilon_r = 4.15$.
   - **L4 (Plane 2 - Continuous Clean GND):** Solid ground return reference for L3.
   - **Dielectric D4-5 (Center Core):** Heavy structural core, thickness $H_4 = 400\,\mu\text{m}$ ($15.75\,\text{mil}$), $\varepsilon_r = 4.25$.
   - **L5 (Plane 3 - Power Planes):** Divided quiet split planes for $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ logic and external $V_{PP} = 2.5\text{--}2.8\,\text{V}$ monitoring rails.
   - **Dielectric D5-6 (Prepreg):** Thickness $H_5 = 150\,\mu\text{m}$, $\varepsilon_r = 4.15$.
   - **L6 (Inner Signal 2 - Stripline):** $0.5\,\text{oz}$ Cu ($18\,\mu\text{m}$), JEDEC Command/Address (C/A) and clock ($CK / \overline{CK}$) buses.
   - **Dielectric D6-7 (Core):** Thickness $H_6 = 150\,\mu\text{m}$, $\varepsilon_r = 4.20$.
   - **L7 (Plane 4 - Continuous GND):** Dedicated ground return reference for L6 and L8.
   - **Dielectric D7-8 (Prepreg):** $1\times 2116$ prepreg, thickness $H_7 = 110\,\mu\text{m}$, $\varepsilon_r = 4.10$.
   - **L8 (Bottom Signal - Outer Microstrip):** $1.0\,\text{oz}$ finished Cu ($35\,\mu\text{m}$), SMA/SMP coax breakout routes to ATE test heads.

#### Step 2: 2D Boundary Element Method (BEM) Field Solver Impedance Synthesis
1. Configure trace geometries using an IPC-2141 / 2D BEM field solver:
   - **Layer 1 & Layer 8 Microstrip ($50\,\Omega \pm 5\%$ SE):**
     - Target impedance: $Z_0 = 50.0\,\Omega$.
     - Trace width $W_1 = 185\,\mu\text{m}$ ($7.28\,\text{mil}$).
     - Dielectric height $H = 110\,\mu\text{m}$ to L2/L7 GND plane.
     - Copper etch trapezoidal factor: etch setback $5.0\,\mu\text{m}$ (top width $180\,\mu\text{m}$, base width $185\,\mu\text{m}$).
   - **Layer 3 & Layer 6 Symmetrical Stripline ($50\,\Omega \pm 5\%$ SE):**
     - Target impedance: $Z_0 = 50.0\,\Omega$.
     - Trace width $W_2 = 125\,\mu\text{m}$ ($4.92\,\text{mil}$).
     - Sandwiched height $B = 300\,\mu\text{m}$ ($H_2 + H_3$), centered between L2/L4 and L5/L7.
   - **Layer 3 & Layer 6 Differential Stripline ($100\,\Omega \pm 5\%$ Diff - Clock & DQS Pairs):**
     - Target differential impedance: $Z_{\text{diff}} = 100.0\,\Omega$.
     - Trace width $W_{\text{diff}} = 110\,\mu\text{m}$ ($4.33\,\text{mil}$).
     - Edge-to-edge differential pair separation $S_{\text{diff}} = 160\,\mu\text{m}$ ($6.30\,\text{mil}$).

#### Step 3: EDA Constraint Manager Rule Configuration
1. Instantiate Physical and Electrical Constraint Classes in the PCB EDA environment (Cadence Allegro / Altium Designer / KiCad):
   - Set `DIFF_CLK_100` and `DIFF_DQS_100` net classes with $Z_{\text{diff}} = 100\,\Omega \pm 5\%$ and strict phase-tuning tolerance $\Delta L_{\text{intra}} \le 0.127\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{mil}$) within each complementary pair.
   - Set single-ended `DQ_BUS_50` and `ADDR_BUS_50` net classes with $Z_0 = 50\,\Omega \pm 5\%$ and inter-signal length matching $\Delta L_{\text{inter}} \le 0.635\,\mu\text{m}$ ($25\,\text{mil}$) across the respective byte lane.
2. Enforce the $3W$ isolation clearance rule ($S_{\text{iso}} \ge 3 \times W = 375\,\mu\text{m}$ for stripline) between adjacent differential pairs and single-ended nets to suppress near-end crosstalk (NEXT) below $-36\,\text{dB}$.
3. Disallow routing high-speed DDR signals across plane splits or discontinuities; verify that all return paths maintain unbroken copper over adjacent GND planes.

#### Step 4: Verification, Coupon Serialization & Sign-Off
1. Export Gerber RS-274X/ODB++ files alongside IPC-2581 cross-section stackup metadata tables specifying target impedances, layer thicknesses, and resin contents.
2. Mandate impedance test coupons (IPC-2221B Type Z) embedded on test coupon rails:
   - One coupon for $50\,\Omega$ outer microstrip.
   - One coupon for $50\,\Omega$ inner stripline.
   - One coupon for $100\,\Omega$ edge-coupled differential stripline.
3. Require vendor fabrication test reports with Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) measurements at $35\,\text{ps}$ rise time ($10\text{--}90\%$) confirming compliance prior to lot acceptance.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Window | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Single-Ended Microstrip/Stripline Impedance ($Z_0$)** | `50.0` | $\pm 2.5$ ($\pm 5\%$) | $\Omega$ | TDR at $t_{\text{rise}} = 35\,\text{ps}$ on fab coupon rails |
| **Differential Stripline Impedance ($Z_{\text{diff}}$)** | `100.0` | $\pm 5.0$ ($\pm 5\%$) | $\Omega$ | Differential TDR ($100\,\Omega$ nominal probe) |
| **Intra-Pair Differential Skew Matching ($\Delta L_{\text{intra}}$)** | `0.0` | $\le 0.127$ ($5.0\,\text{mil}$) | $\text{mm}$ | Automated DRC check in PCB Layout Router |
| **High-Frequency Return Loss ($S_{11}$)** | `<-18.0` | Max $-18.0$ up to $2.0\,\text{GHz}$ | $\text{dB}$ | 2-Port Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) |

---

### 5. Verified Context References

1. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
   - 180nm channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, bitline contact sharing, high-k dielectric stack with minimum $28\,\text{fF}$ per cell capacitance budget for soft-error immunity and refresh retention.
2. **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture:**
   - Wordline pass transistor enhancement NMOS threshold voltage $V_{th} \sim 0.5\,\text{V}\text{--}0.7\,\text{V}$; requirement for boosted high-voltage wordline drive $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}\text{--}2.8\,\text{V}$ powered by on-chip 4-stage Dickson charge pumps; dedicated board power rails isolated from $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$.
3. **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
   - Standard 1T1C cell architecture, storage capacitor target of $25\text{--}30\,\text{fF}$ ensuring $>64\,\text{ms}$ data retention at $85^\circ\text{C}$ burn-in temperatures, with pitch geometry $360\text{--}400\,\text{nm}$ and gate oxide physical thickness $\sim 3.5\,\text{nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The 180nm DRAM ATE loadboard stackup cross-section must rigorously decouple the digital vector drive/receive signal paths from the core DRAM array power distribution network (PDN). A critical deficiency in standard 12-layer to 16-layer stackups is inadequate stripline reference isolation: switching noise from simultaneous bidirectional DQ toggling (up to 400 Mbps DDR/800 Mbps DDR2 rates on ATE pin electronics) easily couples into adjacent VDD/VDDQ planes if solid uninterrupted copper reference planes are not dedicated. The stackup configuration must mandate striplines sandwiched between continuous ground planes with minimum 3H ground-via stitching spacing along high-speed channels, maintaining target single-ended 50 Ohm and differential 100 Ohm trace impedance across the entire pogo-pin to socket fanout.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Controlled-impedance modeling for the loadboard cannot rely on basic 2D empirical equations (IPC-2141). High-frequency dispersion and fiber-weave skew across glass-reinforced laminates (e.g., Isola FR408HR or Megtron 6) will degrade DDR eye margins at the DUT socket interface. Dielectric constant (Dk) variation must be bounded between 3.45 and 3.65 at 1 GHz to 5 GHz. Copper surface roughness (profile Rz > 3.0 um) increases conductor insertion loss and alters effective phase velocity, skewing JEDEC setup (tDS) and hold (tDH) timing windows down to the picosecond regime. The cross-section synthesis must explicitly constrain prepreg resin content, trace trapezoidal etch-factor (typically 75-80 degrees), and soldermask dielectric loading over microstrip traces.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-low-loss core materials like Panasonic Megtron 6 or Rogers RO4350B for thick 14-layer to 18-layer ATE test boards (typically 2.4 mm to 3.2 mm board thickness to withstand pogo-pin mechanical contact force exceeding 150 N) introduces lead-time risks of 8-12 weeks in Southeast Asia / Vietnam PCB fabrication ecosystems. Standardizing the stackup on high-Tg FR-4 (such as Shengyi S1000-2M or Isola 370HR, Tg >= 180°C) with controlled copper thickness (1 oz outer, 0.5 oz inner) ensures multi-source availability and manageable board fabrication cycles under 15 business days, provided high-speed impedance coupon testing via TDR is certified by the fabricator.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Impedance synthesis and cross-section sign-off must freeze prior to the auto-routing and length-tuning phase; any post-layout dielectric thickness adjustment cascades into a full timing closure re-spin of all matched DDR bus delay lines (skew budget < 10 ps between DQ and DQS). We must enforce an automated DRC rule check linking the synthesized stackup (.stackup / IPC-2581 file) to the EDA constraint manager before committing the gerbers to panel fabrication. Fabricator impedance coupon testing must be signed off on coupon test structures before drilling and plating the production test board.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Return path discontinuity and ground bounce caused by split reference planes underneath high-speed DQ/DQS microstrip lines, leading to excessive jitter and failure of JEDEC DDR timing margin validation on ATE.
1. Impedance mismatch beyond +/-10% (exceeding 55 Ohm or dropping below 45 Ohm) caused by PCB vendor copper over-etching or resin starvation during prepreg lamination, resulting in severe transmission line reflections and degraded signal eye opening at the DUT pogo interface.
1. Fiber-weave effect inducing differential skew between true and complement clock/strobe pairs (CK/CK# and DQS/DQS#) exceeding the JEDEC tDQSQ budget (150 ps max).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-1-2-1-01` | **Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Single-Ended and Differential Characteristic Impedance Validation** | Keysight DCA-X 86100D Wide-Bandwidth Oscilloscope with 54754A Differential TDR/TDT Module, 20 GHz bandwidth, 50-Ohm matched SMA-to-probe micro-coaxial tips, precision calibration substrate (Short-Open-Load-Through). | 1. Launch a 35 ps incident step pulse from the TDR channel into the single-ended test coupon pads for Layer 1 microstrip traces (target 50 Ohm). 2. Record the reflected voltage waveform across a 100 mm trace length and extract the instantaneous characteristic impedance (Z0) profile. 3. Repeat the single-ended measurement across inner stripline layers (Layers 3, 5, 8, 10). 4. Switch to differential TDR mode with odd-mode step stimulus on the 100-Ohm differential pair coupons (representing CK/CK# and DQS/DQS# traces). 5. Capture Z_diff impedance across trace span and export raw reflection data. | `Single-ended microstrip and stripline characteristic impedance must measure 50.0 Ohm +/- 4.5 Ohm (45.5 to 54.5 Ohm, within +/-9%). Differential characteristic impedance must measure 100.0 Ohm +/- 8.0 Ohm (92.0 to 108.0 Ohm, within +/-8%) along the flat plateau region of the coupon.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-1-2-1-02` | **S-Parameter Insertion Loss and Return Loss Verification via Vector Network Analyzer (VNA)** | Rohde & Schwarz ZNA26 4-Port Vector Network Analyzer (100 kHz - 26.5 GHz), high-precision 2.92 mm phase-stable test cables, SOLT mechanical calibration kit, fixture de-embedding software (IEEE P370 compliant). | 1. Connect VNA Ports 1 and 2 to the single-ended 50-Ohm microstrip and stripline coupon SMA launch connectors. 2. Apply 2X Thru de-embedding to mathematically subtract connector launch parasitics. 3. Sweep frequency from 100 MHz to 5.0 GHz with intermediate frequency (IF) bandwidth set to 1 kHz and 1601 measurement points. 4. Measure S11 (return loss) and S21 (insertion loss) magnitude and phase response. 5. Repeat measurement in differential mode for Ports 1-4 to extract SDD11 and SDD21 for DQS differential channels. | `S11 return loss must remain below -18 dB up to 2.0 GHz (fundamental and 3rd harmonic of 400 MHz DDR bus). S21 insertion loss must be less than -1.2 dB/inch (-0.047 dB/mm) at 2.5 GHz. SDD11 differential return loss must be below -15 dB across the entire 0.1 GHz to 3.0 GHz band.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: EN 388 Level 4 cut-resistant handling gloves during raw laminate and panel shearing, Chemical splash goggles (ANSI Z87.1 approved), Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, ASTM D6319), Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) safe lab coat and conductive ground-strap heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with gently flowing water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmic medical evaluation. Skin Contact: Remove contaminated clothing and wash affected dermal area thoroughly with soap and copious running water for 15 minutes. Inhalation: Move victim to fresh air; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored. Ingestion: Do NOT induce vomiting; administer 2-3 glasses of water if conscious and contact regional poison control immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: All cross-section coupon etching, coupon mounting, and solvent cleaning operations must be conducted under a certified Class II chemical fume hood with face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 fpm) and local exhaust ventilation tied to an acid/solvent scrubber system.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent persulfate micro-etchant solutions and copper-laden rinses must not be drained into municipal sewers. Collect in dedicated labeled polyethylene hazardous waste containers; neutralize with 10% sodium hydroxide to pH 7.5-8.5 to precipitate copper hydroxide, filter precipitate for hazardous metal reclaim, and transfer liquid effluent to hazardous chemical treatment facility.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade / Cleanroom Grade | `99.8%` |
| **Copper Micro-Etchant Solution (Sodium Persulfate base)** | `7775-27-1` | Technical Reagent Grade | `15-20% aqueous solution` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `180 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Desiccated and degreased bare copper laminate / prepreg inner-layers post-AOI (Automated Optical Inspection), free of moisture and organic fingerprints.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Laminated multilayer core assembly with thermal press curing cycle complete, ENIG (Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold) plated contact fingers, vacuum-sealed with desiccant pack.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into unlaminated or partially cured prepreg causes delamination (measling/blistering) during 260°C lead-free reflow or HTOL thermal burn-in stress. Air exposure exceeding Q-time oxidizes exposed copper microstrips, shifting surface roughness Rz and causing uncontrolled attenuation and impedance deviations.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete engineering sign-off package for the 180nm DRAM ATE loadboard stackup cross-section synthesis, establishing a balanced 14-layer symmetrical high-Tg laminate construction. The stackup configuration locks controlled single-ended 50-Ohm and differential 100-Ohm trace geometries, dielectric layer thicknesses, continuous solid ground reference planes, and manufacturing constraint rules in the PCB layout database, ensuring JEDEC DDR qualification signal integrity.

| `ASSERT-02` | **Differential Impedance (Zdiff) for JEDEC Clock (CK/CK#) and Strobe (DQS/DQS#) Pairs** | `100.0 Ohm` | +/- 7.0 Ohm (+/- 7.0%) | Differential TDR measurement across 100 mm coupled stripline coupons per IPC-2141B. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Loadboard Insertion Loss Attenuation at Nyquist Frequency (2.5 GHz)** | `-0.95 dB/inch` | Maximum -1.20 dB/inch | 4-port VNA S21 measurement with 2X Thru fixture de-embedding per IEEE P370 standard. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal multi-signoff approval achieved upon: (1) 100% compliance of fabricator micro-section coupon TDR logs showing all impedance channels within specified tolerances (+/-8% single-ended, +/-7% differential); (2) Zero DRC violations in EDA constraint manager against synthesized dielectric layer elevations; (3) Multi-Layer PCB fabricator engineering signoff certifying Tg >= 180°C, decomposition temperature Td >= 340°C, and IPC-6012 Class 3 structural integrity.

testcases.title: Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Single-Ended and Differential Characteristic Impedance Validation
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight DCA-X 86100D Wide-Bandwidth Oscilloscope with 54754A Differential TDR/TDT Module, 20 GHz bandwidth, 50-Ohm matched SMA-to-probe micro-coaxial tips, precision calibration substrate (Short-Open-Load-Through).
testcases.pre_conditions: Bare fabricated ATE loadboard test panel containing integrated CITS-compliant impedance test coupons for all signal layers (Layer 1 Top Microstrip, Layer 3/5/8/10 Striplines, Layer 12 Bottom Microstrip). Ambient temperature stabilized at 23°C +/- 2°C, relative humidity 45% +/- 5%. TDR deskew and 50-Ohm reference calibration executed.
testcases.procedure:
1. Launch a 35 ps incident step pulse from the TDR channel into the single-ended test coupon pads for Layer 1 microstrip traces (target 50 Ohm).
2. Record the reflected voltage waveform across a 100 mm trace length and extract the instantaneous characteristic impedance (Z0) profile.
3. Repeat the single-ended measurement across inner stripline layers (Layers 3, 5, 8, 10).
4. Switch to differential TDR mode with odd-mode step stimulus on the 100-Ohm differential pair coupons (representing CK/CK# and DQS/DQS# traces).
5. Capture Z_diff impedance across trace span and export raw reflection data.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Single-ended microstrip and stripline characteristic impedance must measure 50.0 Ohm +/- 4.5 Ohm (45.5 to 54.5 Ohm, within +/-9%). Differential characteristic impedance must measure 100.0 Ohm +/- 8.0 Ohm (92.0 to 108.0 Ohm, within +/-8%) along the flat plateau region of the coupon.

testcases.title: S-Parameter Insertion Loss and Return Loss Verification via Vector Network Analyzer (VNA)
testcases.instrumentation: Rohde & Schwarz ZNA26 4-Port Vector Network Analyzer (100 kHz - 26.5 GHz), high-precision 2.92 mm phase-stable test cables, SOLT mechanical calibration kit, fixture de-embedding software (IEEE P370 compliant).
testcases.pre_conditions: ATE board test coupon configured with back-to-back 2X Thru de-embedding structures and transmission line channels corresponding to longest DQ route (150 mm). Instrument 4-port SOLT calibration completed up to 10 GHz.
testcases.procedure:
1. Connect VNA Ports 1 and 2 to the single-ended 50-Ohm microstrip and stripline coupon SMA launch connectors.
2. Apply 2X Thru de-embedding to mathematically subtract connector launch parasitics.
3. Sweep frequency from 100 MHz to 5.0 GHz with intermediate frequency (IF) bandwidth set to 1 kHz and 1601 measurement points.
4. Measure S11 (return loss) and S21 (insertion loss) magnitude and phase response.
5. Repeat measurement in differential mode for Ports 1-4 to extract SDD11 and SDD21 for DQS differential channels.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: S11 return loss must remain below -18 dB up to 2.0 GHz (fundamental and 3rd harmonic of 400 MHz DDR bus). S21 insertion loss must be less than -1.2 dB/inch (-0.047 dB/mm) at 2.5 GHz. SDD11 differential return loss must be below -15 dB across the entire 0.1 GHz to 3.0 GHz band.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Microstrip & Stripline Route Execution with Serpentine Skew-Matched Length Tuning

**Context & Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Final Automated Test Equipment (ATE) JEDEC DDR Speed-Bin & HTOL Burn-in Testing > ATE Loadboard Interface Design & JEDEC Timing Vector Pattern Generation > ATE DUT Loadboard PCB Schematic & High-Speed Impedance-Matched Layout > High-Speed Controlled-Impedance Microstrip/Stripline Layout & Length Tuning > Microstrip & Stripline Route Execution with Serpentine Skew-Matched Length Tuning  
**Action Type:** Make | **Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS)

---

### Process Workflow Overview

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Substrate & Layer   │
│     Stackup Setup     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Single-Ended & Diff  │
│   Impedance Routing   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Substrate Definition & Impedance Stackup Configuration:**
   - Configure a multi-layer controlled-impedance PCB loadboard stackup using low-loss dielectric substrate ($\varepsilon_r = 3.65$, $\tan\delta \le 0.004$ at $1\text{ GHz}$, dielectric thickness $H = 100\,\mu\text{m}$).
   - Set single-ended target characteristic impedance $Z_0 = 50.0\,\Omega \pm 10\%$ ($45.0\,\Omega \text{ to } 55.0\,\Omega$) by configuring trace width $W = 125\,\mu\text{m}$ for outer microstrip layers (Layer 1 / Layer 12, $1.0\text{ oz / } 35\,\mu\text{m}$ copper thickness).
   - Set internal stripline trace width $W = 100\,\mu\text{m}$ bounded symmetrically by continuous ground planes ($H_1 = H_2 = 125\,\mu\text{m}$) to achieve $Z_0 = 50.0\,\Omega \pm 10\%$.
   - For differential pairs (e.g., `CK_t / CK_c`, `DQS_t / DQS_c`), establish $Z_{\text{diff}} = 100.0\,\Omega \pm 10\%$ ($90.0\,\Omega \text{ to } 110.0\,\Omega$) with edge-to-edge separation gap $S_{\text{diff}} = 150\,\mu\text{m}$.

2. **Primary Channel Escape & Layer Assignment:**
   - Route high-speed bidirectional data groups (`DQ[15:0]`, `DM[1:0]`, `DQS/DQS#`) as striplines on internal signal layers (Layer 3 and Layer 5) to minimize radiation emissions and prevent far-end crosstalk (FEXT).
   - Route clock (`CK/CK#`) and command/address (`A[13:0]`, `BA[1:0]`, `RAS#`, `CAS#`, `WE#`, `CS#`) on dedicated internal layers shielded between ground return planes.
   - Prohibit routing across ground voids or split power planes. Provide minimum 2 stitching ground vias placed within $\le 500\,\mu\text{m}$ of any signal layer transition via.

3. **Serpentine Meander & Trombone Tuning Execution:**
   - Select the longest physical route in each byte lane group as the master timing reference ($L_{\text{ref}}$).
   - Tune all remaining lines within the same byte group (`DQ[7:0]` to `DQS0`; `DQ[15:8]` to `DQS1`) using accordion/serpentine delay matching:
     - **Meander Pitch / Spacing:** Gap between adjacent meander segments $S_{\text{meander}} \ge 3 \times W$ ($375\,\mu\text{m}$ for microstrip, $300\,\mu\text{m}$ for stripline) to prevent bridge crosstalk and self-coupling signal acceleration.
     - **Loop Amplitude:** Meander segment loop length $L_{\text{loop}} \ge 4 \times W$.
     - **Corner Geometry:** Route all corners using $45^\circ$ mitered bends or curved radial arcs ($R \ge 2 \times W$) to prevent local impedance dips.
   - Insert serpentine tuning segments as close as physically possible to the receiving DUT socket / ATE pogo pin launch to preserve eye opening along the bulk run.

4. **Return Path & Shielding Verification:**
   - Enforce minimum trace-to-trace clearance $S_{\text{iso}} \ge 3 \times W$ between unrelated net groups ($3\text{W}$ rule) and $S_{\text{iso}} \ge 5 \times W$ from asynchronous strobe/clock nets.
   - Maintain continuous copper ground floods on adjacent reference planes with zero clearance anti-pad overlap under serpentine sections.

5. **Post-Route TDR & Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) Verification:**
   - Measure loadboard channels using Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) with a $35\text{ ps}$ step pulse rise time.
   - Measure insertion loss ($S_{21}$) and return loss ($S_{11}$) up to the Nyquist frequency of the target DRAM data rate.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Serpentine length matching on high-density ATE DUT loadboards for 180nm DRAM testing introduces self-coupling and parasitic phase velocity shifts if the trombone meander pitch is tighter than 3x to 4x trace width. While compensating for macroscopic package trace length mismatch, tightly packed microstrip serpentines suffer from forward crosstalk that shortens effective electrical propagation delay, sabotaging JEDEC setup/hold timing margin verifications at the DUT pin socket.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At high-speed DDR test frequencies, stripline routing on inner layers (e.g., L3/L5 sandwiched between continuous solid ground planes) must be strictly prioritized over outer microstrip layers to suppress dispersion and eliminate far-end crosstalk (FEXT). When executing serpentine meanders, the loop height must maintain S >= 3W separation between adjacent serpentine segments to avoid dielectric loading variations, and via transitions must include stitched ground return vias within 25 mils to prevent return path inductance discontinuity.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-Tg low-loss laminates (e.g., Rogers RO4350B or Isola FR408HR) required for tight dielectric constant (Dk) tolerance (+/- 0.05) and impedance stability (+/- 5%) face 10-14 week lead times in regional SEA PCB fab ecosystems. Standard FR-4 glass-weave skew anomalies will destroy serpentine phase matching unless the CAD layout specifies a 10-degree off-axis route rotation or zigzag routing relative to the laminate weave pattern.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Serpentine routing iterations must not bottleneck the ATE loadboard fabrication tapeout milestone for the 180nm MPW wafer arrival. If length-tuning rule DRC checks stall PCB layout sign-off beyond the designated sprint window, automated script-based meander placement must be locked with frozen pin-to-pin constraints to prevent downstream delay in JEDEC speed-bin vector bring-up.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Serpentine forward cross-coupling induces signal acceleration, leading to false setup-time passes on the ATE loadboard that fail under native DRAM system timing.
1. Impedance dips at serpentine 90-degree corners and unstitched layer-transition vias generate severe reflection noise exceeding JEDEC DDR input receiver jitter tolerance.
1. Fiber weave effect (glass weave skew) in low-cost FR-4 substrates causing differential pair skew exceeding 5 ps despite physical CAD length matching.

Calculate total electrical delay for each path and evaluate intra-byte relative skew between all DQ traces and their associated DQS strobe. | `Total electrical length mismatch (intra-byte skew) between any DQ trace and its reference DQS differential pair must be <= 5.0 ps; group delay variation across the operational bandwidth (0.5 GHz to 3.0 GHz) must not exceed +/- 3.5 ps.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/chemical safety glasses with side shields, Mil-PRF-87893 ESD-safe conductive nitrile gloves (powder-free, 4 mil), Static-dissipative lab coat with grounded wrist strap (1 MOhm series resistor)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately flush skin with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated clothing. Eye contact: Rinse cautiously with water using an emergency eye-wash station for 15 minutes with eyelids held open; seek immediate ophthalmic evaluation. Inhalation: Relocate personnel to fresh air; if breathing is labored, administer medical oxygen by certified first responder.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop chemical fume extraction snorkel with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s) at the coupon cleaning and connector soldering workstation; general test lab HVAC with minimum 8 air changes per hour (ACH).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent solvent-soaked wipes and solvent wash-drainage into dedicated sealed, grounded, and clearly labeled flammable waste containers; dispose via certified hazardous waste management contractor in accordance with local environmental regulations.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched and immersion gold/silver (ENIG/ENEPIG) finished bare PCB, clean of residual solder mask flux, particulates, and oxide films; surface ionic contamination < 0.1 ug/cm2 NaCl equivalent.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Impedance-verified and TDR/VNA characterization completed; SMA/SMPM launch pads and probe landing locations solvent-cleaned and vacuum desiccant packed.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric copper/silver oxidation and moisture absorption into the polyimide/hydrocarbon dielectric matrix, causing localized dielectric loss tangent (tan delta) degradation, Dk drift, and contact resistance rise exceeding 50 mOhm at RF launch test points.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical CAD routing and high-speed electrical verification of serpentine-tuned microstrip and stripline interconnects on the ATE DUT loadboard, achieving rigorous length matching, deterministic return-path continuity, and low-jitter signal fidelity compliant with JEDEC DDR interface standards for the 180nm DRAM test campaign.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Characteristic single-ended impedance (Z0) along stripline serpentine meanders across all inner routing layers** | `50.0 Ohm` | +/- 2.5 Ohm | High-bandwidth Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) with 20 ps rise-time step stimulus |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Far-End Crosstalk (FEXT) coefficient between adjacent serpentine trombone loops within the same trace** | `-35.0 dB` | <= -30.0 dB (worst-case maximum) | Multi-line 3D EM simulation co-verified via VNA coupled S-parameter (S41) sweep up to 10 GHz |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## 2.5D/3D EM Post-Layout Signal Integrity & Differential TDR Impedance Verification

- **Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation [Foundry Tapeout & PDK] > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging [BEOL & Packaging] > Final Automated Test Equipment (ATE) JEDEC DDR Speed-Bin & HTOL Burn-in Testing [Reliability & Qualification] > ATE Loadboard Interface Design & JEDEC Timing Vector Pattern Generation [Circuit Design] > ATE DUT Loadboard PCB Schematic & High-Speed Impedance-Matched Layout [Circuit Design] > High-Speed Controlled-Impedance Microstrip/Stripline Layout & Length Tuning [Circuit Design] > 2.5D/3D EM Post-Layout Signal Integrity & Differential TDR Impedance Verification [Circuit Design]

### 1. Scope & Objective
Establish the physical protocol for post-layout 2.5D/3D full-wave electromagnetic (EM) modeling, multi-port S-parameter extraction, and differential/single-ended Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) impedance verification. This SOP guarantees that the ATE loadboard microstrip/stripline interconnects, BGA socket launch breakout regions, and interlayer via transitions maintain strict signal integrity constraints under fast edge-rate excitations, ensuring clean interface margins to the 180nm DRAM test die.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **Post-Layout Database Import & 3D Volume Boundary Setup**
   - Import the final routed ATE DUT loadboard layout database (ODB++ or IPC-2581 format) into the 2.5D/3D EM field solver.
   - Configure substrate layer dielectric properties matching the measured qualification stackup:
     - Core/prepreg relative permittivity: $\varepsilon_r = 3.66 \pm 0.05$ (at $1.0\text{ GHz}$).
     - Loss tangent: $\tan\delta \le 0.004$.
     - Copper foil surface roughness (RMS): $R_q \le 1.2\text{ }\mu\text{m}$.
   - Define full-wave 3D FEM bounding boxes around high-density transition zones:
     - ATE test socket landing footprint and pogo-pin transitions.
     - Differential clock (`CK_P` / `CK_N`) and data strobe (`DQS_P` / `DQS_N`) layer vias.
     - Byte-lane DQ/DQM microstrip-to-stripline escape routing.

2. **Meshing & Frequency-Domain S-Parameter Extraction**
   - Apply adaptive mesh refinement with convergence criterion $\Delta S \le 0.01$ across two consecutive refinement passes.
   - Set frequency sweep range from $\text{DC}$ ($0\text{ Hz}$) to $20.0\text{ GHz}$ with minimum 100 adaptive frequency sampling points.
   - Solve multi-mode wave ports placed at:
     - Port 1: ATE pin electronics (PE) coaxial launch pads (calibrated to $50.0\ \Omega$ single-ended / $100.0\ \Omega$ differential reference).
     - Port 2: DUT test socket interface contact plane.
   - Extract passive, causal, and reciprocal $N$-port Touchstone files (`.s2p`, `.s4p`). Verify passivity enforcement ($\text{eigenvalues of } [I - S^\dagger S] \ge 0$).

3. **Differential & Single-Ended TDR Impedance Profile Computation**
   - Import extracted Touchstone multiport models into the time-domain reflectometry simulator.
   - Configure virtual TDR step generator excitation:
     - Excitation step amplitude: $\Delta V = 1.80\text{ V}$ matching 180nm core/IO swing ($V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $I_{\text{on}} \ge 500\text{ }\mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$).
     - 10%–90% Step rise time: $t_r = 35.0\text{ ps}$ (reflecting high-bandwidth ATE pin electronics edge capability).
   - Compute differential TDR profile $Z_{\text{diff}}(t)$ across `CK` and `DQS` differential pairs:
     - Uniform transmission line target: $Z_{\text{diff}} = 100.0\ \Omega \pm 10\%$ ($90.0\ \Omega\text{ to }110.0\ \Omega$).
   - Compute single-ended TDR profile $Z_0(t)$ across single-ended DQ, Address, and Command lines:
     - Uniform transmission line target: $Z_0 = 50.0\ \Omega \pm 10\%$ ($45.0\ \Omega\text{ to }55.0\ \Omega$).

4. **Via Antipad & Interconnect Discontinuity Extraction**
   - Isolate lumped capacitive and inductive discontinuities along the TDR trace profile:
     - Via barrel / antipad clearance: Verify localized impedance dip does not fall below $88.0\ \Omega$ differential ($42.0\ \Omega$ single-ended).
     - Test socket pogo-pin contact parasitic: Extract equivalent lumped loading capacitance and verify $C_{\text{fixture}} < 1.0\text{ pF}$, protecting the device cell charge sensing baseline ($\ge 28\text{ fF}$ unit cell budget).
   - If excessive capacitive dipping occurs at via transitions, adjust antipad cutout radius in inner ground planes by $+50\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ to $+100\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ and re-mesh.

5. **Frequency-Domain Signal Integrity Sign-Off**
   - Evaluate differential return loss: Verify $|S_{dd11}| \le -15.0\text{ dB}$ across operating Nyquist bandwidth.
   - Evaluate differential insertion loss: Verify $|S_{dd21}| \ge -1.5\text{ dB}$ at fundamental clock frequency.
   - Extract far-end crosstalk (FEXT) between adjacent high-speed traces (e.g., adjacent DQ lines spaced $S \ge 3W$): Verify $|S_{21\text{, FEXT}}| \le -35.0\text{ dB}$.

---

### 4. Verified Physical Context Citations

- **180nm Device Operational Levels**:
  - Drain-source core voltage: $V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, driving the virtual TDR pulse generator amplitude.
  - Device threshold level: $V_{\text{thn}} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, $I_{\text{on}} \ge 500\text{ }\mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$, setting driver switching thresholds (*Source: Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification*).
- **Storage Cell Capacitance Budget**:
  - Cell minimum capacitance: $\ge 28\text{ fF}$ per cell with sub-threshold/junction leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*). Loadboard fixture parasitics are bounded ($C_{\text{fixture}} < 1.0\text{ pF}$) to prevent loading distortion during refresh and retention metrology.
- **Wordline Overdrive & Slew Boundaries**:
  - Pass transistor threshold loss requires $V_{\text{PP}} \ge 2.5\text{ V to } 2.8\text{ V}$ (*Source: High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture*). Transient signal reflections on control lines are bounded by return loss limits ($|S_{11}| \le -15\text{ dB}$) to prevent false gate triggering.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-layout 2.5D/3D EM simulation of the ATE loadboard-to-DUT interface must incorporate complete 3D full-wave modeling (Ansys HFSS / Cadence Clarity) of pogo-pin sockets, surface-mount coaxial launches, and wirebond/C4 transitions. Planar 2.5D planar solvers fail to capture vertical return-path discontinuities and mutual parasitic inductance in high-density pogo pin matrices, causing inaccurate differential TDR reflections and false eye-mask margins during 200-400 MHz JEDEC SDR/DDR-I qualification.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Differential TDR extraction for differential clock (CK/#CK) and DQS lines requires rigorous de-embedding up to the silicon DUT bond pads. Discrepancies between physical Rogers/Megtron-6 PCB prepreg weave orientations and microstrip routing cause uncompensated phase skew (intra-pair skew > 5 ps), while localized via stub resonances above 5 GHz will degrade edge rates and disturb JEDEC tAC/tDQSCK extraction.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Controlled-dielectric copper-clad laminates (e.g., Megtron-6 / Panasonic R-5775 or Rogers RO4350B) with tight thickness tolerances (+/-5%) and custom low-inductance pogo-pin contactor blocks (e.g., Cohu or Smiths Interconnect spring probes) carry lead times exceeding 14-18 weeks; failure to freeze EM stackup parameters before fabrication stalls ATE board assembly.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: All 2.5D/3D EM extraction runs and differential TDR validation gates must be finalized and signed off prior to releasing gerber data to the PCB fabrication house. Any impedance re-spin post-fabrication injects a 6-week delay and $15,000 NRE penalty, directly jeopardizing the scheduled MPW silicon arrival and ATE burn-in qualification timeline.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Differential impedance mismatch exceeding +/-10% (target 100 Ohm differential, measured <90 Ohm or >110 Ohm) causing excessive signal reflections and eye closure at the DRAM input receiver.
1. Excessive intra-pair skew (>15 ps) on differential clock (CK/CK#) and data strobe (DQS) due to fiber weave pitch effect and unoptimized serpentine routing, triggering false timing jitter failures.
1. Pogo-pin ground loop discontinuity creating common-mode noise conversion and excessive crosstalk (> -30 dB at Nyquist frequency) into adjacent DRAM command/address lines.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/chemical splash safety glasses, ESD-safe dissipative nitrile gloves (thickness >= 4 mil), Static-dissipative lab coat conforming to ANSI/ESD S20.20, Grounded ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with solvent: flush eyes immediately with tepid eyewash stream for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical evaluation. In case of inhalation: evacuate to fresh air immediately; administer oxygen if respiration becomes labored. For skin contact: wash thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated dissipative clothing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized laminar-flow extraction hood or chemical fume extractor with minimum face velocity of 100 LFPM (0.5 m/s); room air turnover >= 12 ACH (air changes per hour).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect solvent-soaked wipes and solvent run-off in airtight, grounded, explosion-proof hazardous solvent safety containers labeled 'Hazardous Flammable Solvent Waste'; dispose of via certified hazardous materials facility per EPA/RCRA regulations. Do not discharge into municipal sewer.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-assembly immersion gold/electroless nickel (ENIG) or immersion silver (IAg) pads clean, unoxidized, free of flux residue and particulate contamination (Class 10,000 cleanroom condition).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: De-fluxed, solvent-cleaned, dry nitrogen purge-cleared contact pads with zero ionic contamination (< 0.1 ug/cm2 NaCl equivalent) ready for ATE socket installation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric tarnishing and oxidation of silver/copper contact interfaces increasing pogo-pin contact resistance from < 30 mOhm to > 250 mOhm, inducing significant TDR discontinuities and false qualification failures.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed 2.5D/3D full-wave electromagnetic post-layout extraction and correlation report confirming that all differential clock, strobe, and single-ended high-speed memory command/address lines on the ATE DUT loadboard comply with JEDEC DDR-I 200/400 MHz timing and signal integrity standards, verified through physical differential TDR and 4-port VNA S-parameter measurements.

# Standard Operating Procedure: TDR Transmission Line Metrology & S-Parameter Signal Integrity Verification

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: DRC/LVS rule decks must run clean via KLayout/Magic/OpenLane with zero design rule errors. Antenna ratio rules (< 250:1) and substrate tap density checks must pass before GDSII reticle handoff to commercial foundry.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: 3D Crown capacitor ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 (ZAZ) stack must achieve equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) <= 0.8 nm and leakage current < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V. CMP dishing on M1/M2 tungsten/copper features must hold < 15 nm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Commercial foundry MPW (Multi-Project Wafer) shuttle submission has an unmovable tapeout window; GDSII/OASIS files must freeze 21 days prior. Sourced via open-source or commercial shuttle program under standard NDA.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 60-120 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: CRITICAL (A single DRC rule deck discrepancy or LVS short-circuit ruins the entire multi-thousand dollar commercial shuttle run and incurs a 4-6 month spin delay).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. DRC/LVS hierarchy discrepancy causing undetected metal-to-metal bridging or floating substrate tap.
1. ALD precursor pulse/purge saturation drift inducing pinhole dielectric breakdown in crown capacitor array.
1. Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) over-polish causing severe interconnect erosion and open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
