---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the automated workflow for translating cyclized digital test vectors into standard IEEE 1450 Standard Test Interface Language (STIL) format and executing pin-to-channel deskew, format mapping, and strobe verification on Automated Test Equipment (ATE) for the 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN MPW tapeout).

---

### 2. Physical & Architectural Verification Context
- **Manufacturing Grid & Critical Dimensions**: SkyWater SKY130 manufacturing grid placement resolution is $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\ \text{nm}$); minimum drawn poly gate length is $150\ \text{nm}$ ($0.15\ \mu\text{m}$), minimum poly spacing is $0.21\ \mu\text{m}$, contact dimension is $0.17\ \mu\text{m} \times 0.17\ \mu\text{m}$, Metal 1 minimum width is $0.14\ \mu\text{m}$, pitch is $0.34\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **Cell Electrical Targets**: 180nm DRAM access transistor channel length $L = 180\ \text{nm}$, width $W = 220\ \text{nm}$, cell storage capacitance budget $\ge 28\ \text{fF}$ per cell, sub-threshold/junction leakage target $\le 1\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Lithography & Overlay**: KrF $248\ \text{nm}$ DUV laser exposure with overlay budget between gate poly and active diffusion $\le 35\ \text{nm}$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: STIL File Header & Signal Group Definition (`IEEE 1450.1`)
1. In the `Signals` block, declare all external DUT pins matching the 180nm padframe:
   - Control: `CLK_P`, `CLK_N`, `CKE`, `CS_N`, `RAS_N`, `CAS_N`, `WE_N`.
   - Addressing: `ADDR[11:0]`, `BA[1:0]`.
   - Data & Strobe: `DQ[15:0]`, `LDQS`, `UDQS`, `LDM`, `UDM`.
2. Group bidirectional busses into `SignalGroups` with explicit drive/compare mapping:
   - `InGroup`: All direct address/command input pins.
   - `OutGroup` / `BiGroup`: Data `DQ` and `DQS` signals assigned with dynamic direction control (`DriveHigh`, `DriveLow`, `CompareHigh`, `CompareLow`, `CompareOff`).

#### Step 2: WaveformTable & Timing Edge Assignment
1. Define nominal tester cycle periods matching the target JEDEC DDR binning rate:
   - Configure cycle timing blocks: `WFT_READ`, `WFT_WRITE`, `WFT_ACTIVATE`, `WFT_REFRESH`.
2. Map edge event markers per signal group:
   - Driver Edge Events: Force Off (`Z`), Force Down (`0` at $T_0$), Force Up (`1` at $T_0$), Force Prior/Invert.
   - Output Strobe Events: Compare Low (`L`), Compare High (`H`), Window Open (`T_{\text{open}}`), Window Close (`T_{\text{close}}`), or Single Edge Strobe (`X`).
3. Ensure all timing edge placements conform to the $5\ \text{ps}$ tester vernier resolution grid.

#### Step 3: Pattern Vector Translation & Cyclization
1. Compile cyclized VCD event traces into `PatternExec` and `Pattern` blocks.
2. Embed DRAM core timing assertions:
   - Enforce row-to-column delay ($t_{\text{RCD}}$), row precharge time ($t_{\text{RP}}$), and refresh intervals constrained by the $1\ \text{fA/cell}$ leakage budget at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain charge on the $\ge 28\ \text{fF}$ storage node.
3. Validate vector compression: Check that loop counters (`Loop`), scan chains, and macro vector calls do not exceed tester vector memory depth per channel.

#### Step 4: Automated ATE Channel Deskew & TDR Calibration
1. Mount the loadboard onto the ATE test head.
2. Run automated Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) calibration across all active pins to determine electrical trace length to the DUT socket.
3. Apply channel deskew delays to calibrate driver skew and comparator skew across all pin channels.
4. Set pin electronics input thresholds ($V_{\text{IL}}$, $V_{\text{IH}}$) and active loads ($I_{\text{OH}}$, $I_{\text{OL}}$) matching the SSTL/CMOS I/O cell specification.

#### Step 5: Vector Pre-Flight Simulation & Strobe Validation
1. Execute an ATE software pre-flight loopback simulation (`dry-run` without physical DUT mounted):
   - Check for drive/compare bus collisions (undesired driving while DUT drives DQ).
   - Ensure deadband violations ($T_{\text{edge\_n}} - T_{\text{edge\_n-1}} < \text{minimum edge separation}$) are zero.
2. Insert calibration gold-die or loopback fixture; execute the pattern at reduced clock rate, sweeping compare strobes across the eye diagram to verify vector-to-hardware timing alignment.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Evaluation Method | Target Spec | Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Channel-to-Channel Pin Skew** | ATE TDR automated deskew calibration across all address, command, and DQ/DQS pins | $\le 85$ | $\text{ps}$ |
| **STIL Timing Edge Placement Resolution** | ATE vernier timing generator validation against IEEE 1450 standard | $\le 20$ | $\text{ps}$ |
| **Input Threshold Voltage Sensitivity ($V_{\text{IL}} / V_{\text{IH}}$ Margin)** | Pin electronics DC receiver calibration against SSTL reference | $\ge 150$ | $\text{mV}$ |
| **Strobe Edge Accuracy / Offset Uncertainty** | Comparator strobe timing jitter and edge placement error relative to master clock | $\le 45$ | $\text{ps}$ |

---

### 5. Context Citations
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Transistor dimensions $L = 180\ \text{nm}$, $W = 220\ \text{nm}$.
  - Storage node capacitance budget $\ge 28\ \text{fF/cell}$.
  - Maximum sub-threshold and junction leakage target $\le 1\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**:
  - Placement manufacturing grid resolution $= 0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\ \text{nm}$).
  - Minimum drawn poly gate length $= 0.15\ \mu\text{m}$ ($150\ \text{nm}$).
  - Contact hole dimension $= 0.17\ \mu\text{m} \times 0.17\ \mu\text{m}$.
  - Metal 1 pitch $= 0.34\ \mu\text{m}$, minimum width $= 0.14\ \mu\text{m}$.
  - KrF $248\ \text{nm}$ DUV lithography with maximum permissible poly-to-active overlay error $\le 35\ \text{nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Translating asynchronous event-based VCD vectors into synchronous cyclized IEEE 1450 STIL patterns risks unmodeled timing edge distortion if tester period resolution (e.g., 10 ps vernier step) and flyback dead-zones are not strictly aligned with the DRAM DLL clock jitter envelope. Automated ATE channel deskew must account for pogo-pin-to-loadboard microstrip phase matching across all DQS/DQ lanes to prevent artificial false setup/hold failures during JEDEC DDR speed-binning.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: DRAM read/write cycles require dynamic direction switching on bidirectional DQ channels with tight tDQSS and tDQSCK phase relationships. In IEEE 1450 STIL, improper drive/compare waveform shape declarations (e.g., Return-to-Zero vs Non-Return-to-Zero and active-drive-to-high-Z compare windows) can mask channel reflections or induce ground bounce during simultaneous switching outputs (SSO). Vector validation must verify cycle-by-cycle strobe masking and guardband timing against DDR-200/DDR-333/DDR-400 AC specifications.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Legacy ATE platforms (e.g., Advantest T5588 or Teradyne UltraFLEX) enforce strict vector memory depth and waveform table limits per pin channel. Uncompressed or bloated STIL patterns will exceed tester vector cache memory, triggering high multi-pass reload latencies that directly inflate index test time and cost per device during wafer sort and final test.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The tapeout timeline cannot absorb iterative manual vector translation revisions. Automated VCD-to-STIL compilation scripts, syntax linting (IEEE 1450.1 compliance), and channel-vector simulation matching against golden Verilog gate-level testbenches must achieve automated signoff within 48 hours of layout freeze.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Bidirectional DQ channel contention caused by overlapping tester drive enable and DRAM burst read output drive windows in STIL timing sets, leading to high-current pin driver clamping and signal distortion.
1. Vector cyclization phase aliasing where edge-placement quantization on 180nm ATE timing generators violates JEDEC tIS/tIH or tDS/tDH timing parameters, inducing yield fallout of functional dies.
1. Tester vector memory buffer overrun due to excessive flat vector expansion without subroutine or loop macro compression in the IEEE 1450 STIL file.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-3-2-3-01` | **Automated IEEE 1450 STIL Waveform Cyclization and Logic Vector Equivalence Verification** | Synopsys VCS / Cadence Xcelium digital simulator with IEEE 1450 STIL Vector Ingestion Engine, high-speed logic analyzer or ATE digital pin electronic simulator. | 1. Ingest the generated IEEE 1450 STIL test pattern into the cycle-accurate ATE virtual testbench harness. 2. Simulate DDR write-burst (BL=4, BL=8) and read-burst cycles across all 16 DQ pins and DQS/CK differential pairs over 100,000 continuous tester cycles. 3. Compare cycle-by-cycle drive/compare states and strobe assertions against the golden gate-level Verilog simulation dump. 4. Record any mismatch in drive data, output compare values, or float/tristate strobe timing windows. | `Vector logic mismatch count = 0 over 100,000 cycles (100% equivalence); all drive/compare timing edges lie within +/- 15 ps of target cyclized grid boundaries.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-3-2-3-02` | **ATE Pin Channel Deskew, Edge Placement Accuracy, and Eye-Opening Validation** | High-bandwidth automated test equipment (Advantest T5588 or Teradyne UltraFLEX DDR Pin Electronics) coupled with 20 GHz digital sampling oscilloscope (Keysight Infiniium or Tektronix DPO70000) via active differential probe heads on ATE loadboard DUT socket. | 1. Execute the calibrated STIL vector burst pattern driving alternating 0xAA/0x55 pseudo-random patterns at 200 MHz (400 Mbps DDR data rate). 2. Measure pin-to-pin timing skew across all 16 DQ channels, CK, and DQS at the pogo pin contact plane. 3. Measure drive edge placement accuracy (EPA) and compare strobe positioning accuracy relative to the master clock marker over 10,000 vector repetitions. 4. Determine channel jitter and effective data eye opening. | `Channel-to-channel deskew variation across all DQ/DQS pins <= 35 ps; edge placement accuracy (EPA) error <= 25 ps; total jitter TJ (at BER 10^-12) <= 120 ps; horizontal eye opening >= 65% of bit period (1.625 ns at 400 Mbps).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved anti-static safety glasses with side shields, ESD wrist strap / conductive ESD heel grounders (ANSI/ESD S20.20 compliant), Lint-free nitrile cleanroom gloves (Class 100/ISO 5 compatible, powder-free)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with IPA solvent, flush thoroughly with eyewash station water for at least 15 minutes. For skin contact, wash thoroughly with soap and water. If inhaled in high concentrations, move personnel immediately to fresh air. In electrical shock emergency from ATE high-voltage rails, de-energize emergency stop (EMO) immediately before administering CPR.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: ATE testing bay must maintain positive-pressure HEPA filtration with dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) exceeding 10 air changes per hour for solvent wipe-down areas; ambient humidity controlled at 45% +/- 5% RH to mitigate ESD hazards.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA-wetted cleanroom wipes must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-resistant solvent waste cans and disposed of via certified hazardous flammable solvent waste contractors.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (for ATE pogo-pin and loadboard contact cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C12) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly fabricated 180nm packaged dies or wafer-level probe pads clean, de-oxidized, and free of organic residues or particulate contamination post-dicing/packaging.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested and speed-binned DRAM components stored in vacuum-sealed dry packs with humidity indicator cards (HIC) and active desiccant pouches.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to atmospheric moisture leads to pad surface oxidation and contact resistance (Rc) degradation (> 1.5 ohm shift), causing false ATE continuity/parametric test failures and package delamination during subsequent burn-in thermal cycling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full synthesis, compilation, and automated hardware-in-the-loop validation of IEEE 1450 STIL test patterns for 180nm Open-Source DRAM. Delivers bit-accurate vector equivalence between EDA simulation and physical ATE channel drivers, meeting all JEDEC DDR speed-bin timing parameters and vector memory constraints.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM180_JEDEC_DDR_SPEEDBIN_REV1.stil`
- [ ] `ATE_CHANNEL_DESKEW_AND_EPA_VALIDATION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `VCD_TO_STIL_VECTOR_LOGIC_EQUIVALENCE_MATRIX.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Vector logic mismatch rate across 100k cycles between golden simulation and translated STIL pattern** | `0.00` | 0.00 | Automated cycle-by-cycle binary comparison log from digital simulator STIL pattern regression testbench. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **ATE pin channel-to-channel deskew variation across all DQS and DQ lanes at DUT contact plane** | `25.0` | +/- 10.0 ps | Multi-channel high-bandwidth digital oscilloscope edge-skew measurement calibrated via loadboard TDR. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **STIL vector memory utilization on primary ATE pattern generator hardware** | `68.5` | <= 85.0% | ATE pattern compiler memory allocation map and vector segment compilation audit log. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% vector equivalence verified with zero logic miscompares; ATE channel deskew verified under 35 ps across all DQ/DQS pins; IEEE 1450 STIL syntax fully validated with zero syntax/semantic linting errors; and signoff approved by Systems Engineering and Test Operations.

An actionable Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has been authored and documented in the repository:

👉 [sop_ate_pin_electronics_channel_deskew_tdr_fixture_calibration.md](./docs/sop_ate_pin_electronics_channel_deskew_tdr_fixture_calibration.md)

---

### Procedure Summary & Highlights

1. **Step-by-Step Calibration & De-Skew Sequence**:
   - **Thermal Stabilization**: Soak ATE test head, pin electronics (PE), and fixture at $25.0 \pm 0.5\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ (and $85.0 \pm 1.0\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ for HTOL burn-in setups) for $\ge 45\text{ min}$.
   - **TDR Impedance & Discontinuity Extraction**: Launch fast TDR step ($t_r \le 35\text{ ps}$) to evaluate characteristic impedance ($Z_0 = 50.0 \pm 2.0\text{ }\Omega$) and contact parasitics ($C_{\text{fixture}} < 1.0\text{ pF}$, protecting the $28\text{ fF}$ cell capacitance margin).
   - **Flight-Time Deskew Table**: Compute round-trip reflection transit times ($2 \times T_{\text{flight}, i}$) relative to differential clock channels (`CK_P`/`CK_N`) and program per-pin vernier hardware delays.
   - **PE Driver & Comparator Timing Alignment**: Set driver swing to $1.80\text{ V}$ ($V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ compatibility) and comparator threshold to $V_{\text{th, ref}} = 0.55\text{ V}$ ($V_{\text{thn}}$ target); execute multi-channel hardware de-skew to $\le 25\text{ ps}$ peak-to-peak.
   - **DC PMU Pre-Screen & Leakage Floor**: Verify channel PMU voltage forcing ($0\text{ to }1.8\text{ V}$) and test channel background noise floor to $\le 10\text{ pA}$ ($I_{\text{off}} \le 10\text{ pA/}\mu\text{m}$ compatibility).

2. **Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria**:
   - **Channel-to-Channel Peak-to-Peak De-Skew**: $\le 25.0\text{ ps}$
   - **Loadboard Characteristic Impedance ($Z_0$)**: $50.0 \pm 2.0\text{ }\Omega$
   - **PE Voltage Drive Accuracy ($V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$)**: $1.80 \pm 0.02\text{ V}$
   - **Fixture Socket Residual Stray Capacitance**: $< 1.0\text{ pF}$
   - **ATE Channel DC Leakage Noise Floor**: $\le 10.0\text{ pA}$

3. **Contextual Literature Citations**:
   - Sourced and strictly aligned with parameters from:
     - *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench* ($L=180\text{ nm}$, $W=220\text{ nm}$, $C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\text{ fF}$, leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
     - *Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification* ($V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{\text{thn}} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, $I_{\text{off}} \le 10\text{ pA/}\mu\text{m}$).
     - *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering* ($C_{\text{min}} = 25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$, retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: De-skewing ATE channel pin electronics up to the pogo-pin interface without accounting for dynamic fixturing trace impedance mismatch and socket parasitic inductances (L_socket ~ 1.2 nH) will corrupt high-speed DDR setup/hold window measurements at 200-400 Mbps. The automated calibration routine must run vector TDR through the actual test fixture socket using short/open/load (SOL) calibration coupons to align the pin electronic time-of-flight (T_tof) reference plane directly at the DUT pad landing interface.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For JEDEC-compliant DRAM qualification on 180nm CMOS, channel-to-channel timing skew across DQ/DQS and Command/Address pins must be constrained within +/-25 ps. Failing to compensate for temperature-induced drift in the pin electronics driver and comparator circuits across long qualification test runs will artificially degrade tAC, tDQSQ, and tDS/tDH timing margin distributions, inducing false yield fallout during wafer sort and final package test.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring specialized high-bandwidth pogo-pin arrays, precision 50-ohm calibration substrates, and gold-plated sacrificial short/open verification coupons requires strict vendor qualification with long lead-times (14-18 weeks). Dual-sourcing of custom high-frequency multi-layer RF/ATE loadboard sockets is critical to avoid single-point failure bottlenecks during the MPW package test campaign.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration protocols and automated TDR de-skew scripts must be fully locked and validated prior to the arrival of packaged silicon from the OSAT vendor. Any calibration slip directly burns expensive ATE run-time hours (costing >$250/hour) and stalls the post-tapeout critical path for the 180nm open-source DRAM bring-up schedule.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Uncompensated channel-to-channel propagation delay mismatch (>50 ps) inducing false setup/hold (tIS/tIH, tDS/tDH) timing violations during JEDEC DDR speed-binning.
1. TDR impedance discontinuity (>5 ohms delta from nominal 50 ohms) caused by socket contactor wear or via stub resonance, inducing multi-reflection ringing and eye-closure.
1. Thermal drift in comparator threshold calibration causing asymmetric edge detection and jitter amplification across pin electronics channels during HTOL burn-in test.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-3-3-01` | **Automated Channel-to-Channel Timing De-Skew and Flight-Time Alignment** | Advantest V93000 / Teradyne UltraFLEX ATE with High-Speed Digital Pin Electronics, Picosecond Sampling Oscilloscope (Keysight DCA-X 86100D, 50 GHz BW), SOL Calibration Substrate | 1. Initialize ATE automated deskew diagnostic routine across all 64 digital channels (DQ[15:0], DQS, ADDR[12:0], BA[1:0], control lines). 2. Drive 1.8V swing step pulses (tr < 120 ps) into open-circuit socket terminals and measure reflected edge arrival time (T_tof). 3. Adjust per-pin programmable vernier delay lines (1 ps resolution) until all reflection arrival times coincide at the reference plane. 4. Verify channel edge alignment using the external sampling oscilloscope connected via dedicated fixture probe pads. | `Total channel-to-channel skew across all active DRAM signal channels <= 20.0 ps peak-to-peak; per-channel timing jitter RMS <= 3.5 ps.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-1-3-3-02` | **Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Fixture Characteristic Impedance & Discontinuity Characterization** | Vector Network Analyzer / TDR Module (Keysight E5071C-TDR or Tektronix 8300 with 80E08 TDR sampling head, 35 ps incident rise time) | 1. Extract instantaneous characteristic impedance Z0(x) across PCB microstrip, via transitions, and socket contact pins. 4. Record peak impedance deviations at the fixture-to-socket transition interface. | `Trace characteristic impedance Z0 = 50.0 ohms +/- 2.5 ohms (47.5 ohms to 52.5 ohms); peak socket transition discontinuity impedance <= 54.0 ohms; reflection coefficient |rho| <= 0.05.` |

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved UV/laser-rated safety glasses with side shields, Cleanroom ESD-safe nitrile gloves (Class 100/ISO 5 compatible, minimum 5 mil thickness), Static-dissipative cleanroom lab coat / smock with conductive cuff grounding, ESD wrist strap with 1 Mohm current-limiting resistor attached to verified earth ground
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with isopropanol: Immediately flush eyes with copious clean water from emergency eyewash station for >= 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical attention. In case of inhalation: Remove individual to fresh air immediately; administer CPR if breathing ceases. In case of cryogenic N2 frostbite/burn: Immerse affected body parts in lukewarm water (38-42°C); do not rub.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Perform solvent-based pin contact cleaning inside a dedicated chemical fume hood with a certified face velocity of 80-100 FPM (0.4-0.5 m/s). Compressed N2 blow-off must be vented through point-of-use particulate/exhaust extraction to prevent asphyxiation risks in enclosed test bays.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly plated Au/Ni socket contactors and loadboard immersion gold (ENIG/ENEPIG) pads inspected under optical stereomicroscope; surface free of organic residue, copper tarnish, and particle contamination (particle count = 0 > 5 um).

# Standard Operating Procedure: HTOL Dynamic Thermal-Voltage Accelerated Burn-in Stress Execution

**Category**: Reliability Testing | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of HTOL Dynamic Thermal-Voltage Accelerated Burn-in Stress Execution: BEOL metallization, electrical die sort (EDS), wafer backgrinding/dicing, and wirebond plastic encapsulation successfully yield JEDEC-qualified DRAM packaged units.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Electrical_Die_Sort_Wafer_Yield_Map.csv`
- [ ] `Wirebond_Ball_Shear_And_Pull_CPK_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_TSOP54_Final_ATE_SpeedBin_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wirebond ball shear strength** | `>= 18.0 gf` | Minimum failure load >= 15.0 gf across 30 samples | Dage 4000 micro-tester lateral ball shear per MIL-STD-883 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) wafer array functional yield** | `>= 90.0%` | Minimum yield >= 85.0% on prime wafers | Automated wafer probe array test with March C- diagnostic patterns |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Packaged DRAM package coplanarity & lead pitch** | `<= 0.08 mm coplanarity` | JEDEC TSOP-54 mechanical envelope tolerance (+/- 0.05 mm) | Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% passing electrical continuity and JEDEC parametric DC checks; destructive wirebond shear CPK >= 1.67 with zero package voiding or delamination detected under scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).

# Standard Operating Procedure: HTOL Burn-in Board Socketing & Dynamic Stress Pattern Programming with V_PP Overdrive Cycling

**Category**: Reliability Testing | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In dynamic HTOL for 180nm DRAM, driving V_PP charge pumps to accelerated overdrive (e.g., 3.6V-3.8V against a 2.5V nominal core and 1.8V VDD) across 128 socketed units introduces severe transient IR drop across the Burn-in Board (BIB) power distribution network (PDN). Sockets with contact resistance exceeding 50 mOhm will cause localized ground bounce and suppress effective stress voltages at the internal wordline boost drivers, leading to undertesting of the thick-oxide access transistor gate dielectrics.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Dynamic stress pattern generation must execute continuous row-hammer and march stress cycling (e.g., March C- variations) while modulating V_PP overdrive. At 125°C junction temperature, V_PP overvoltage accelerates Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) of the wordline driver PMOS/NMOS isolation and wordline-to-substrate dielectric. If dynamic wordline toggling is held static during accidental firmware pauses, localized channel hot-carrier (CHC) injection or excessive gate oxide breakdown will skew Weibull early-life failure rate (ELFR) modeling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-temperature polyimide/FR5 burn-in boards equipped with Kelvin-sensing BGA sockets rated for continuous 150°C operation exhibit lead times exceeding 14 weeks. Contact pogo pins degrade through beryllium-copper spring relaxation and gold-plating intermetallic diffusion after 500 thermal hours, threatening burn-in test facility capacity and lot qualification schedules if spare contactor arrays are not maintained on-site.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: HTOL chamber utilization must hit 1,000 continuous hours (with readout checkpoints at 48h, 168h, 500h, and 1000h) under strict JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD47 qualification standards. Any intermediate socket contact fault or unexpected chamber safety trip resets the qualification countdown for the affected lot, causing multi-week slippage in commercial MPW wafer release.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. V_PP charge pump oxide TDDB rupture causing hard short-circuit to VSS and permanent wordline boost collapse across the DRAM sub-array.
1. BIB socket Beryllium-Copper (BeCu) pogo pin spring relaxation and contact intermetallic oxidation under continuous 125°C-140°C thermal exposure, resulting in false contact open failures during stress readouts.
1. BIB power plane parasitic resonance and inductive voltage overshoot during simultaneous 128-device row-activation transitions, exceeding gate breakdown limits and inducing extrinsic ESD/EOS destruction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-01` | **Dynamic V_PP Overdrive Voltage Stress and Current Regulation Verification** | Keysight N6705C DC Power Analyzer with N6781A SMU module, Tektronix MSO64B 4 GHz Oscilloscope with high-temperature active differential probes attached directly across BIB Kelvin socket decoupling terminals. | 1. critics.systems_engineer: In dynamic HTOL for 180nm DRAM, driving V_PP charge pumps to accelerated overdrive (e.g., 3.6V-3.8V against a 2.5V nominal core and 1.8V VDD) across 128 socketed units introduces severe transient IR drop across the Burn-in Board (BIB) power distribution network (PDN). Sockets with contact resistance exceeding 50 mOhm will cause localized ground bounce and suppress effective stress voltages at the internal wordline boost drivers, leading to undertesting of the thick-oxide access transistor gate dielectrics.
critics.domain_expert: Dynamic stress pattern generation must execute continuous row-hammer and march stress cycling (e.g., March C- variations) while modulating V_PP overdrive. At 125°C junction temperature, V_PP overvoltage accelerates Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) of the wordline driver PMOS/NMOS isolation and wordline-to-substrate dielectric. If dynamic wordline toggling is held static during accidental firmware pauses, localized channel hot-carrier (CHC) injection or excessive gate oxide breakdown will skew Weibull early-life failure rate (ELFR) modeling.
critics.supply_chain: Custom high-temperature polyimide/FR5 burn-in boards equipped with Kelvin-sensing BGA sockets rated for continuous 150°C operation exhibit lead times exceeding 14 weeks. Contact pogo pins degrade through beryllium-copper spring relaxation and gold-plating intermetallic diffusion after 500 thermal hours, threatening burn-in test facility capacity and lot qualification schedules if spare contactor arrays are not maintained on-site.
critics.laya_pm: HTOL chamber utilization must hit 1,000 continuous hours (with readout checkpoints at 48h, 168h, 500h, and 1000h) under strict JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD47 qualification standards. Any intermediate socket contact fault or unexpected chamber safety trip resets the qualification countdown for the affected lot, causing multi-week slippage in commercial MPW wafer release.
critical_failure_modes: V_PP charge pump oxide TDDB rupture causing hard short-circuit to VSS and permanent wordline boost collapse across the DRAM sub-array.

BIB socket Beryllium-Copper (BeCu) pogo pin spring relaxation and contact intermetallic oxidation under continuous 125°C-140°C thermal exposure, resulting in false contact open failures during stress readouts.

BIB power plane parasitic resonance and inductive voltage overshoot during simultaneous 128-device row-activation transitions, exceeding gate breakdown limits and inducing extrinsic ESD/EOS destruction.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## HTOL Burn-in Board High-Temp Socket Assembly & Trace Integrity Checkout

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-HTOL-037`  
**Revision:** Rev 1.0  
**Domain:** Packaging / Reliability & Qualification Testing  
**Technology Generation:** 180nm CMOS DRAM MPW (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Action Type:** Make / Assembly & Verification  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Substrate        │
│     Preparation &      │
│    Polyimide Baking    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    High-Temp Socket    │
│   Assembly & Torque    │
│       Fastening        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Four-Point Kelvin    │
│  Contact Resistance &  │
│   Isolation Checkout   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    TDR Impedance &     │
│    Signal Integrity    │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

This SOP governs the mechanical assembly, alignment, mounting, and trace electrical integrity validation for high-temperature operating life (HTOL) burn-in boards (BIB) carrying packaged 180nm DRAM test vehicles (ceramic DIP / QFN leadframes with 25 µm wire-bonded die attaches). HTOL stresses package contacts and PCB traces under elevated thermal and overdrive bias conditions up to 150°C.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Substrate Dehydration & Thermal Preparation
1. Clean the high-Tg polyimide / Rogers HTOL Burn-in Board (BIB) using an ESD-safe ionized nitrogen air gun.
2. Pre-bake the bare BIB at **150°C for 60 minutes** in a clean-room convection oven (matching the cure profile of silver-filled conductive die attach epoxy Ablebond 84-1LMIS) to drive out residual board moisture and prevent delamination under sustained HTOL stress.
3. Allow the board to cool inside a nitrogen-purged desiccator to **25°C** ambient before mechanical mounting.

#### Step 2: High-Temperature Socket Placement & Fastening
1. Inspect the high-temp clamshell sockets (PEEK/Torlon housing, BeCu gold-plated pogo pins/contacts rated $\ge 175^\circ\text{C}$).
2. Align the socket locator pins with the PCB alignment fiducials matching the ceramic DIP / QFN package footprint.
3. Fasten socket backing-plate mounting screws in a diagonal cross-pattern using a calibrated torque driver set to **0.25 N·m (±0.02 N·m)** to guarantee uniform coplanarity without flexing polyimide traces.

#### Step 3: Four-Point Kelvin Resistance & Trace Continuity Checkout
1. Connect an Automated Test Instrument / Source Measure Unit (SMU) via 4-wire Kelvin sensing probes from the edge finger card connector to each socket pin.
2. Measure trace loop resistance across all power distribution network lines ($V_{DD}$, $V_{SS}$, $V_{PP}$) and signal routes:
   - Ensure contact resistance ($R_{cont}$) per individual socket contact spring is $\le 50\text{ m}\Omega$.
   - Confirm total trace DC loop resistance from edge finger to socket landing is $\le 250\text{ m}\Omega$.
3. Check thermal path compliance to package frame: verify that the heat dissipation interface maintains package thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.

#### Step 4: High-Temperature Inter-Trace Isolation & Leakage Verification
1. Insert a golden ceramic mechanical test vehicle (short/open dummy package).
2. Apply an isolation checkout bias of **5.0 V DC** across adjacent bitline/wordline driver traces on the BIB inside a thermal chamber preheated to **150°C**.
3. Confirm adjacent pin isolation leakage is $\le 10\text{ nA}$ (ensuring isolation margin well above the device-level cell junction leakage budget of $< 1\text{ fA/cell at } 85^\circ\text{C}$).

#### Step 5: High-Speed Trace TDR Impedance Validation
1. Connect a Time Domain Reflectometer (TDR) with a $\le 35\text{ ps}$ rise-time incident pulse to high-speed clock ($CLK$) and control strobe traces.
2. Measure characteristic trace impedance ($Z_0$) over the entire path length:
   - Verify nominal trace impedance is **$50.0\ \Omega \pm 5.0\ \Omega$** across the board.
   - Detect and flag any localized impedance discontinuities $> 10\%$ caused by socket solder joints or via stubs.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │░                                    │
Leakage Iso @150C┤░                                    │
                 │▒▒▒▒▒▒                               │
     TDR Z0 Error┤▒▒▒▒▒▒                               │
   P/G Trace Drop┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                 │
                 │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                 │
Socket Pin R_cont┤█████████████████████████████████████│
                 │█████████████████████████████████████│
                 └┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0.0      8.8     17.5     26.2    35.0 
```

| Metric ID | Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Inspection Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-01** | Socket Pin Contact Resistance ($R_{cont}$) | **$\le 50.0$** | $\text{m}\Omega$ | 4-Wire Kelvin Milliohm Meter |
| **AC-02** | HTOL Substrate Pre-Bake Temperature & Duration | **$150 \pm 3$ for $60$** | $^\circ\text{C}$ / $\text{min}$ | Calibrated Thermal Oven / Thermocouple |
| **AC-03** | Inter-Trace Isolation Leakage ($@ 5.0\text{ V}, 150^\circ\text{C}$) | **$\le 10.0$** | $\text{nA}$ | High-Precision SMU / Picoammeter |
| **AC-04** | Signal Trace Characteristic Impedance ($Z_0$) | **$50.0 \pm 5.0$** ($45.0 \text{ to } 55.0$) | $\Omega$ | Time Domain Reflectometer (TDR) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources & Citations

1. **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:**
   - *Die Attach & Thermal Specifications:* Ablebond 84-1LMIS curing cycle at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$; thermal resistance requirement $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$; packaging standard for ceramic DIP / QFN packages; ambient handling baseline at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
   - *Capacitive and Leakage Baselines:* Unit cell geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), sub-threshold/junction leakage ceiling ($< 1\text{ fA/cell at } 85^\circ\text{C}$), and cell capacitance budget ($\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$), anchoring electrical stress requirements and board-level isolation thresholds.
3. **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
   - *Dielectric and Pitch Geometry:* $360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$ wordline/bitline pitch dimensions, $3.5\text{ nm}$ gate oxide limits, and $64\text{ ms}$ refresh retention baseline under $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-1-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-1-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of HTOL Burn-in Board High-Temp Socket Assembly & Trace Integrity Checkout: BEOL metallization, electrical die sort (EDS), wafer backgrinding/dicing, and wirebond plastic encapsulation successfully yield JEDEC-qualified DRAM packaged units.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Electrical_Die_Sort_Wafer_Yield_Map.csv`
- [ ] `Wirebond_Ball_Shear_And_Pull_CPK_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_TSOP54_Final_ATE_SpeedBin_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wirebond ball shear strength** | `>= 18.0 gf` | Minimum failure load >= 15.0 gf across 30 samples | Dage 4000 micro-tester lateral ball shear per MIL-STD-883 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) wafer array functional yield** | `>= 90.0%` | Minimum yield >= 85.0% on prime wafers | Automated wafer probe array test with March C- diagnostic patterns |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Packaged DRAM package coplanarity & lead pitch** | `<= 0.08 mm coplanarity` | JEDEC TSOP-54 mechanical envelope tolerance (+/- 0.05 mm) | Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% passing electrical continuity and JEDEC parametric DC checks; destructive wirebond shear CPK >= 1.67 with zero package voiding or delamination detected under scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).

1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Dynamic V_PP Overdrive Wordline Stress Pattern Vector Development & Chamber Loading

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Applying external V_PP overdrive beyond the nominal 2.7V regulation setpoint (e.g., accelerating to 3.3V-3.6V for HTOL) directly strains the level-shifter high-voltage PMOS/NMOS gate oxides in the wordline drivers. The vector sequencing must maintain strict interlock between the external HTOL burn-in board force-rail and the on-chip Dickson pump shutoff logic to prevent reverse current injection through the regulator's dynamic feedback divider or bandgap-referenced comparator. Furthermore, high-frequency wordline cycling across 125°C chamber runs risks excessive localized IR drops across the power mesh, potentially causing asynchronous clock skew on the two-phase flying cap driver clocks (Phi1, Phi2).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Wordline overdrive accelerated stress is vital to weed out early dielectric wear-out (TDDB) in both the NMOS access transistor thin oxide (T_ox ~ 3.2nm - 4.0nm for 1.8V core/thickened IO) and the cell trench/stacked capacitor high-k dielectric under full write-margin conditions. If dynamic cycling vectors do not evenly distribute row address activation with pseudorandom wordline toggling, localized self-heating will artificially alter the access transistor threshold voltage V_th shift, producing bimodal distribution artifacts in subsequent post-HTOL retention and refresh time testing rather than revealing true intrinsic oxide breakdown.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom HTOL Burn-in Boards (BIBs) for this 180nm MPW packaging require high-temperature polyimide PCB substrates (TG > 250°C) with low-inductance socketing capable of sustaining continuous 125°C - 150°C ambient profiles over 1000 hours. High-current high-temperature burn-in sockets and specialized discrete bypass capacitors (COG/NPO ceramic caps rated for >= 150°C, 50V) suffer from extended vendor lead times (14 to 20 weeks). Test socket wear and socket contact resistance degradation (> 150 mOhm) during thermal cycling can compromise the targeted V_PP waveform slew rate.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Chamber loading schedule and socket allocation must be gated strictly by vector validation on bench ATE prior to loading the 128-device capacity burn-in oven. Premature chamber runs with unverified vector files (WGL/STIL) risk burning scarce Gen 3 MPW prototype silicon under uncontrolled voltage transients or thermal runaway. We must tie the signoff of the dynamic overdrive vector set to an automated ATE pre-check milestone before locking the chamber door for the 168-hour interim readout.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) of the wordline driver PMOS pull-up gate oxide induced by uncalibrated V_PP voltage overshoot spikes exceeding 3.8V during fast rising transitions.
1. Back-biasing and parasitic latchup trigger in the on-chip Dickson charge pump output stage due to external V_PP overdrive back-feeding through body diodes while the internal pump clock is gated.
1. Accelerated hot-carrier injection (HCI) and drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) degradation of unselected NMOS access pass transistors along common bitlines during continuous high-V_PP row cycling.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-2-01` | **Dynamic V_PP Overdrive Wordline Vector Timing & Transient Overshoot Verification** | Advantest T5833 DRAM Memory ATE System, Keysight Infiniium MSOS804A 8GHz Real-Time Oscilloscope with high-bandwidth active differential probe (1134A), High-Temperature Burn-In Test Fixture Board. | 1. Power up DUT with V_DD = 1.80V, assert chip reset, and transition to test register mode (MRS register bit 7 set to bypass on-chip V_PP pump).\n2. Ramp external V_PP supply pin to 3.30V at a slew rate of 10 mV/us.\n3. Load the Dynamic Wordline Cycling Vector pattern (alternating row-hammer/marching-row address sequence at 25 MHz equivalent activation frequency).\n4. Trigger high-bandwidth oscilloscope on wordline driver monitor pin (WL_MON) and record 10,000 continuous switching transitions.\n5. Quantify peak instantaneous overshoot voltage, 10%-90% rise time, and steady-state high voltage plateaus across all toggled cycles. | `Peak instantaneous transient overshoot on V_PP / WL node must not exceed 3.50V (absolute maximum limit: <= 3.50V, duration above 3.30V < 2.0 ns); steady-state V_PP high voltage must stay within 3.30V +/- 60 mV; rise time (10%-90%) must be between 1.8 ns and 3.5 ns.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-2-02` | **HTOL Chamber 125C Dynamic Stress Vector In-Situ Current & Leakage Profiling** | Despatch Micro-TD 125C HTOL Burn-in Chamber with programmable N2 purge, Advantest/Innotec BIB Vector Generator and Multi-Channel DC Source Monitor Unit (SMU) with 10nA resolution. | 1. Ramp chamber ambient temperature to 125°C and hold for 30 minutes thermal soak.\n2. Apply continuous dynamic V_PP overdrive stress vector pattern (V_DD = 1.98V [1.10x nominal], V_PP = 3.30V) to all 64 DUTs simultaneously.\n3. Continuously record I_DD and I_PP supply currents per socket via SMU at 1-second sampling intervals for 120 minutes continuous run.\n4. Execute brief 5-second pause every 30 minutes to measure quiescent standby leakage current (I_PP_standby, wordlines idle/grounded) at 125°C.\n5. Post-process current drift curves across all populated sockets to detect anomalous micro-breakdown anomalies. | `Active I_PP dynamic current per device must remain within 12.0 mA to 18.5 mA across all sockets without abrupt step-up spikes (> 1.0 mA delta indicating partial gate rupture); quiescent leakage I_PP_standby at 125°C must remain < 45.0 uA per DUT.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 4 high-temperature thermal barrier gloves (EN 407 rated for >= 200°C contact), ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face safety shield with side guards, Anti-static ESD dissipative lab coat with flame-resistant aramid lining, Safety shoes with non-conductive, heat-resistant soles (ASTM F2413), Continuous wrist strap connected to 1 MOhm dissipative ground bench
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately flush affected skin under clean, lukewarm running water for a minimum of 20 minutes; do not apply ice, petroleum ointments, or chemical agents; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing and seek immediate medical evaluation. Nitrogen Asphyxiation: In case of low-oxygen alarm triggering, immediately evacuate personnel to fresh air; if unconscious, administer artificial respiration and oxygen by trained first-aid personnel; call emergency medical dispatch. Chemical/Solvent Eye Exposure: Flush eyes with sterile eye-wash saline for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; remove contact lenses.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous local mechanical exhaust rated for >= 50 ACH (air changes per hour) adjacent to the HTOL chamber venting duct; chamber pressure interlocked with facility extraction; ambient N2 gas-leak monitoring sensors set to trigger audible/visual evacuation alarms at O2 < 19.5% by volume.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA cleaning towels and solvent washes must be disposed of in dedicated grounded, self-closing metal hazardous waste cans compliant with RCRA flammables; spent electronics and solder-dross waste managed according to WEEE/RoHS electronic hazardous disposal regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 | `>= 99.999%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Electronics Cleaning Solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Lead-Free Solder Rosin Flux Residue (Cleaners)** | `65997-06-0` | Technical Grade | `< 5.0% in wash solvent` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, gold/nickel-plated package pins free of oxidation, flux residue, and organic contamination (< 5 ng/cm2 carbon contaminant density); passivated silicon package sealed.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thermally annealed package exterior with zero visible pin solder oxidation; socket contact pads verified non-pitted with contact resistance < 100 mOhm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into plastic mold compound (MSL Level 3 risk) leading to internal delamination and 'popcorn' cracking upon 125°C-150°C chamber ramp, coupled with pin oxidation increasing socket contact resistance and causing localized high-frequency voltage ringing/overstress.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete engineering development, validation, and execution package for dynamic V_PP overdrive wordline stress vectors across the 180nm DRAM Gen 3 test chips. Delivers verified binary ATE pattern files, high-frequency oscilloscope transient qualification reports, in-situ HTOL chamber current profile telemetry logs, and signoff exit criteria for the 168-hour accelerated burn-in screening phase.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `VPP_OVERDRIVE_WL_STRESS_VEC_REV3.stil`
- [ ] `HTOL_125C_VPP_CYCLING_TELEMETRY_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `VPP_TRANSIENT_OVERSHOOT_QUAL_REPORT.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Dynamic V_PP overdrive voltage plateau under active cycling at 125C chamber conditions** | `3.30 V` | +/- 0.05 V | Multi-channel calibrated SMU remote 4-wire Kelvin sensing at BIB socket boundary |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Transient wordline driver peak voltage overshoot during rising edge transitions under vector load** | `3.38 V` | <= 3.50 V max absolute | 8 GHz real-time digital oscilloscope single-shot acquisition across 10,000 clock cycles |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Quiescent V_PP leakage current (I_PP_standby) per DUT at 125C following 168-hour interim stress** | `28.5 uA` | <= 45.0 uA maximum | Automated parametric measurement unit (PMU) current sweep at 3.3V bias with wordlines unasserted |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero functional vector execution dropouts across 100% of populated sockets during a continuous 4-hour pre-HTOL chamber dry run, absolute peak transient wordline overshoot confirmed <= 3.50V across all test channels, and unanimous signoff on deliverable vector artifacts by Systems Engineering, Reliability Qualification Lead, and ATE Test Program Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Dynamic $V_{PP}$ Overdrive Wordline Stress Pattern Vector Simulation & WGL Translation

**Document ID:** `SOP-DRAM180-REL-048`  
**Process Node:** 180nm CMOS Open-Source DRAM (SKY130 / 180nm DRAM Generation)  
**Classification:** Circuit Design & Reliability Engineering (HTOL Burn-in Preparation)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Objective

This SOP defines the formal verification, transient circuit simulation, and Waveform Generation Language (WGL) test vector translation protocol for dynamic $V_{PP}$ overdrive wordline stress patterns. During High-Temperature Operating Life (HTOL) accelerated burn-in qualification, wordline drivers are subjected to elevated voltage levels ($V_{PP} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}\text{ to }2.8\,\text{V}$) across 180nm access NMOS pass transistors ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$) and stacked storage cell nodes ($C_{cell} \ge 28\,\text{fF}$) to screen gate-oxide TDDB (Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown) and junction breakdown without causing unmodeled circuit latch-up or Dickson charge pump regulator collapse.

---

## 2. Process Flow & Execution Protocol

```
                  +----------------------------------------------+
                  |  1. Setup Mixed-Signal Testbench Environment |
                  |  - Nominal V_DD = 1.8 V                      |
                  |  - Dynamic V_PP Stress Overdrive >= 2.5-2.8 V|
                  |  - NMOS Transistor (L=180nm, W=220nm)        |
                  +----------------------------------------------+
                                         |
                                         v
                  +----------------------------------------------+
                  |  2. Configure Dickson Pump & Wordline Clocks |
                  |  - Two-Phase Clocks (Phi1, Phi2: 20-50 MHz)  |
                  |  - Flying Capacitance C_pump = 20 to 50 pF   |
                  +----------------------------------------------+
                                         |
                                         v
                  +----------------------------------------------+
                  |  3. Run Transient Stress Pattern Simulation  |
                  |  - Write '1': Target Node = V_DD (1.8 V)     |
                  |  - Avoid Vt Loss (1.8V - 0.6V = 1.2V degraded|
                  |  - Verify Delta V_overdrive restoration      |
                  +----------------------------------------------+
                                         |
                                         v
                  +----------------------------------------------+
                  |  4. EVCD Dump & WGL Vector Translation       |
                  |  - Dump .evcd / .vcd waveform transitions    |
                  |  - Map ATE timing cycles & burn-in pin timing|
                  |  - Translate to ATE-compliant WGL format     |
                  +----------------------------------------------+
```

### Step 1: Netlist and Mixed-Signal Simulation Setup
1. Instantiate the extracted wordline driver slice, row decoder, and memory unit cell array with:
   - Access NMOS pass transistor gate length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$ and width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$.
   - Stacked capacitor load per cell: $C_{cell} = 28\,\text{fF}$ (utilizing ONO or high-$\kappa$ dielectric model with $\kappa > 15$).
2. Configure nominal logic supply $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$.
3. Set the transient overdrive supply rail $V_{PP}$ to the accelerated HTOL stress condition ($V_{PP} = 2.5\,\text{V}\text{ to }2.8\,\text{V}$), verifying that the wordline driver delivers $V_{PP} \ge V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{overdrive}$ (where $V_{th} \sim 0.5\,\text{V}\text{ to }0.7\,\text{V}$, nominal $0.6\,\text{V}$).

### Step 2: Oscillator & Charge Pump Dynamic Clock Setup
1. Configure the 4-stage Dickson charge pump oscillator to provide two-phase non-overlapping clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) at an operating frequency within $20\,\text{MHz}\text{ to }50\,\text{MHz}$.
2. Verify stage flying pump capacitors are parameterized to $C_{pump} = 20\,\text{pF}\text{ to }50\,\text{pF}$.
3. Enable dynamic feedback regulation against the internal bandgap reference to clamp excessive voltage spikes above $2.8\,\text{V}$.

### Step 3: Dynamic Stress Vector Sequence Execution
1. Apply the row-activation/wordline toggle stress pattern:
   - Cycle through physical wordlines sequentially to distribute thermal dissipation across row drivers.
   - Force continuous high write cycles to storage nodes to ensure access devices pass full $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ rail voltage into the $28\,\text{fF}$ storage node (preventing the un-boosted degradation threshold limit of $V_{DD} - V_{th} = 1.8\,\text{V} - 0.6\,\text{V} = 1.2\,\text{V}$).
2. Perform extended transient verification (SPICE/FastSPICE) over the HTOL temperature envelope up to $85^\circ\text{C}$ to verify that cell sub-threshold and junction leakages meet modeled bounds ($< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$).

### Step 4: EVCD Extraction and WGL Pattern Translation
1. Record digital pin states, clock edges, strobe times, and row/column address bus transitions into an Extended Value Change Dump (`.evcd`) format.
2. Filter high-impedance ($Z$) and indeterminate ($X$) states during wordline precharge transitions.
3. Run the WGL translator compiler to generate cycle-based tester patterns matching the HTOL Burn-in Board (BIB) tester channel timing:
   - Format: Waveform Generation Language (WGL).
   - Timeplate: Map clock periods corresponding to the Dickson pump clock window ($20\,\text{MHz}\text{ to }50\,\text{MHz}$, cycle periods $20\,\text{ns}\text{ to }50\,\text{ns}$).
   - Pin directions: Map bi-directional data pins and dedicated high-voltage monitor ports.
4. Execute syntax and timing rule check (TRC) validation on the compiled `.wgl` vector file before dispatching to the ATE burn-in chamber controller.

---

## 3. Measurable Acceptance Criteria (Target Metrics)

| Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Wordline Overdrive Stress Voltage ($V_{PP}$)** | $2.5 \le V_{PP} \le 2.8$ | $\text{V}$ | Transient SPICE node simulation at driver output |
| **Dickson Pump Clock Frequency ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$)** | $20 \text{ to } 50$ | $\text{MHz}$ | Oscillator waveform period measurement ($20\text{--}50\,\text{ns}$) |
| **Flying Pump Capacitance ($C_{pump}$)** | $20 \text{ to } 50$ | $\text{pF}$ | Netlist parameter & DRC/LVS physical extraction check |
| **Storage Node Restored Level (Full $V_{DD}$)** | $\ge 1.75$ (Target: $1.80$) | $\text{V}$ | Transient cell storage node probe ($> 1.2\,\text{V}$ threshold-loss limit) |

---

## 4. Verified Literature & Context Citations

* **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**:
  * Pass NMOS $V_{th} \sim 0.5\,\text{V}\text{ to }0.7\,\text{V}$ (nominal $0.6\,\text{V}$), with threshold voltage loss causing $V_{DD} - V_{th} = 1.8\,\text{V} - 0.6\,\text{V} = 1.2\,\text{V}$ written level if un-boosted.
  * Overdrive requirement: $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{overdrive} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}\text{ to }2.8\,\text{V}$.
  * Dickson pump topology: 4-stage using flying capacitors $C_{pump} = 20\,\text{pF}\text{ to }50\,\text{pF}$ driven by two-phase non-overlapping clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) at $20\,\text{MHz}\text{ to }50\,\text{MHz}$ with dynamic bandgap regulation.
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  * Unit access transistor channel geometry: length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$.
  * Cell capacitance budget: minimum $28\,\text{fF/cell}$ (stacked capacitor with dielectric $\kappa > 15$).
  * Leakage target: sub-threshold and junction leakage kept below $1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
* **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**:
  * Grid resolution: $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{nm}$).
  * Active diffusion minimum width: $0.15\,\mu\text{m}$, poly gate minimum length: $0.15\,\mu\text{m}$ ($150\,\text{nm}$ drawn).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Simulating dynamic V_PP overdrive wordline stress vectors requires modeling parasitic RC networks across the full wordline distributed line (200 fF bitline coupling, wordline resistance R_WL ~ 1.5 kOhm) simultaneously with Dickson charge pump load regulation. A major oversight is failing to couple transient V_PP voltage droop during simultaneous row activations in burn-in mode, which distorts vector timing in the WGL output and leads to edge-placement timing violations on tester pin electronics.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: During accelerated HTOL stress, the nominal V_PP level of 2.8V is intentionally overdriven up to 3.4V-3.6V to stress the thin gate oxide (tox ~ 4.2 nm) of the 180nm NMOS access transistor. In SPICE-to-WGL vector compilation, failure to account for hot carrier injection (HCI) and time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) acceleration factors will yield vector cycle counts that either under-stress the dielectric or induce premature destructive gate rupture rather than screening latent defects.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Target ATE burn-in platforms (such as Advantest T5588 or Teradyne UltraFLEX) have finite pattern vector memory depths and specific WGL dialect constraints for bidirectional I/O cycles. Translating uncompressed simulation VCD/EVCD files directly into WGL can exceed tester channel vector depth per pin, demanding complex loop/repeat compression macros that must be qualified across local OSAT burn-in board vendors.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Wordline stress vector compilation and WGL translation are directly on the critical path prior to burn-in chamber loading. Any syntax mismatch in WGL waveform timing tables or cycle-boundary race conditions discovered at the physical ATE socket requires an iterative engineering vector rebuild, which threatens the tapeout HTOL 1000-hour qualification schedule and risks wafer lot holding penalties.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. WGL vector cycle-boundary timing misalignment causing tester strobe hazard and false functional pin-strobe failures during V_PP overdrive pulse peaks.
1. Dickson charge-pump regulator clamp collapse under unthrottled concurrent all-row toggle patterns, driving V_PP below 2.2V and failing the acceleration stress criterion.
1. Excessive TDDB degradation leading to instantaneous gate-oxide pinhole shorting between WL (at V_PP=3.5V) and BL/Storage node during continuous high-stress dwell cycles.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-2-1-01` | **Dynamic V_PP Overdrive Pulse Envelope and Cycle Timing Verification in Compiled WGL** | Synopsys VCS-AMS Mixed-Signal Simulator, Waveform Generation Language (WGL) Vector Compiler, Teradyne UltraFLEX Digital Pin Timing Analyzer / Cycle Verifier | 1. Run dynamic mixed-signal simulation over 1,000,000 test clock cycles executing pseudo-random row address cycling with V_PP pump active. 2. Record dynamic V_PP rail voltage, WL driver gate overdrive waveforms, and logic states into high-resolution EVCD. 3. Translate EVCD to standard JEDEC-compliant WGL format using automated timing resolver. 4. Parse compiled WGL into ATE tester emulator; extract strobe placement, rising edge t_r, falling edge t_f, and active wordline pulse width t_RAS_stress across all 1024 wordlines. | `WGL syntax must parse with zero timing violations; simulated wordline pulse envelope must maintain V_PP >= 3.40V for >= 95% of active pulse duration; peak overshoot must not exceed 3.65V; rise/fall edge jitter in WGL timing sets must be <= 120 ps.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-2-1-02` | **WGL Vector Translation Consistency and Strobe Edge Robustness under Multi-Bank Concurrent Stress** | Mentor Graphics FastSPICE / Tessent SiliconInsight ATE Vector Audit Tool, Tektronix High-Bandwidth Digital Pattern Comparator | 1. Execute WGL test pattern through ATE pattern compiler with bidirectional channel emulation. 2. Verify bit-for-bit cycle correspondence between input SPICE logic assertions and output WGL expect states (L/H/X). 3. Perform edge shift margin test by sweeping tester compare strobe window across +/- 2.5 ns window around expected read/write refresh boundaries under V_PP overdrive conditions. | `Zero bit discrepancies across 10^7 compiled pattern cycles; timing strobe margin must remain >= 1.8 ns without ambiguous X-state transitions; maximum vector vector-block memory allocation must not exceed 64 Mvectors per ATE channel pin.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 2 ESD-safe lab coat, ANSI Z87.1 approved anti-glare safety glasses, Class 0 (1000V rated) electrical insulating gloves for high-voltage ATE power supply calibration, ESD grounding wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye exposure to IPA, flush immediately with copious clean water for at least 15 minutes at eyewash station. For inhalation of solvent vapors, move individual to fresh air immediately; administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored. In case of electric shock from high-voltage DC supplies, isolate power source before touching victim and initiate CPR/call EMS immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized exhaust fume hood with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s) active during solvent cleaning of burn-in boards and ATE socket interfaces; continuous HVAC cleanroom airflow with >= 20 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA cleaning wipes and solvent effluents into grounded, labeled hazardous waste containers for flammables; dispose of via certified hazardous waste remediation facility according to local environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (ATE board & socket contact cleaner)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade / VLSI | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Chamber purge / socket drying)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra High Purity (Grade 5.0) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Gold/Lead-free solder balled or wire-bonded packages inspect-clean, dry, and verified free of atmospheric moisture and ionic surface contaminants.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Burn-in socket contacts inspected for zero solder-drag or oxide accumulation; packages baked at 125 deg C and sealed in dry-pack carrier reels.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption causing package delamination (popcorn effect) during HTOL thermal cycling up to 125 deg C, or contact pad micro-corrosion causing spurious high-resistance V_PP rail droop during vector execution.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full synthesis, simulation, and translation of the dynamic V_PP overdrive wordline stress pattern vector suite into production-ready WGL format, validated against 180nm foundry DRC/reliability rules for accelerated HTOL testing.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `vpp_overdrive_stress_patterns_rev1_0.wgl`
- [ ] `vpp_stress_timing_simulation_report.pdf`
- [ ] `ate_channel_vector_allocation_map.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Accelerated dynamic V_PP stress voltage stability across active row assertions during multi-bank cycling** | `3.45 V` | +/- 0.08 V | FastSPICE full-chip transient simulation coupled with WGL vector voltage-level audit |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum active wordline pulse width compliance for TDDB acceleration without unrecoverable oxide breakdown** | `120 ns` | +/- 5 ns | WGL waveform timing-set edge analysis and digital pattern timing verification tool |
| `ASSERT-03` | **WGL translation vector fidelity and state correlation against golden simulation logic traces** | `100.0%` | 0.0% | Automated cycle-by-cycle binary vector equivalence check between EVCD and compiled WGL |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero syntax errors and zero cycle-timing hazards upon compiling the generated WGL through the target ATE platform toolchain, with transient V_PP dynamic rail variation strictly within 3.37V to 3.53V under all continuous simultaneous row-activation modes, formally signed off by the Circuit Design Lead and Reliability Test Engineer.
