# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## HTOL Burn-in Driver Board Vector Loading & Overdrive Voltage Calibration

### Document Metadata
- **Node / Technology**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)
- **Cell Architecture**: Access NMOS ($L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$) with Stacked MIM/ONO Storage Capacitor ($C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\,\text{fF}$)
- **Target Subsystem**: HTOL Burn-in Board (BIB), Driver Cards, and High-Voltage Wordline Dickson Charge Pump ($V_{\text{PP}}$)

---

### Calibration & Loading Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Driver Board Vector   │
│   Flash and Pattern    │
│        Loading         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  V_DD and V_PP Power   │
│      Rail Sensing      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Two-Phase Clock     │
│  Frequency Tuning (20  │
│     MHz to 50 MHz)     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     V_PP Overdrive     │
│  Voltage Calibration   │
│     (2.5V to 2.8V)     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Dynamic Stress     │
│  Pattern Verification  │
│    and Chamber Soak    │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Burn-in Driver Board Pattern Memory Vector Loading
1. Power down the HTOL driver motherboard and insert the 180nm DRAM burn-in daughterboard into the edge connector.
2. Initialize driver firmware interface and load the **Dynamic Wordline Stress Pattern Vector** into driver board pattern memory:
   - Wordline activation toggling sequence: Marching row stress pattern with alternating physical address strides to maximize gate-oxide dielectric electric field stress across adjacent rows.
   - Vector format: Synchronous clock, write enable (`/WE`), row address strobe (`/RAS`), column address strobe (`/CAS`), and bank select buses.
3. Perform vector memory checksum validation (`CRC32`) across pattern buffer addresses before asserting driver enable.

#### Step 2: Power Rail Level Pre-Calibration ($V_{\text{DD}}$ Supply)
1. Configure driver board programmable DC power supply rail $V_{\text{DD}}$ to nominal core bias:
   $$V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\,\text{V}$$
2. Verify remote Kelvin sense feedback at the furthest socket to guarantee line drop compensation within $\pm 10\,\text{mV}$ under dynamic switching load.

#### Step 3: Two-Phase Charge Pump Clock Generation Tuning ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$)
1. Enable driver board high-speed auxiliary differential clock drivers delivering the non-overlapping two-phase clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) to the on-chip 4-stage Dickson charge pump oscillator.
2. Set and trim clock frequency within the designated operating band:
   $$f_{\text{pump}} = 20\,\text{MHz} \text{ to } 50\,\text{MHz}$$
3. Calibrate non-overlapping dead time ($t_{\text{dead}} \ge 1.5\,\text{ns}$) between $\Phi_1$ and $\Phi_2$ using high-bandwidth oscilloscope probes directly at driver test headers to eliminate shoot-through current in Dickson flying capacitor stages ($C_{\text{pump}} = 20\,\text{pF} \text{ to } 50\,\text{pF}$).

#### Step 4: Wordline Overdrive Voltage ($V_{\text{PP}}$) Sensing & Calibration
1. Enable internal wordline booster feedback regulation circuit.
2. Given access NMOS threshold voltage $V_{\text{th}} = 0.5\,\text{V} \text{ to } 0.7\,\text{V}$, an unboosted wordline at $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ leads to threshold voltage loss ($V_{\text{node}} \le V_{\text{DD}} - V_{\text{th}} \approx 1.2\,\text{V}$), shedding $33\%$ stored charge on the $C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\,\text{fF}$ capacitor.
3. Measure and trim the dynamic feedback voltage divider and bandgap-referenced comparator on the driver/DUT interface until the regulated overdrive output voltage satisfies:
   $$V_{\text{PP}} = V_{\text{DD}} + V_{\text{th}} + \Delta V_{\text{overdrive}} \ge 2.5\,\text{V} \text{ to } 2.8\,\text{V}$$
4. Enforce driver clamp limits at $V_{\text{PP,clamp}} = 2.9\,\text{V}$ to prevent irreversible catastrophic gate dielectric breakdown of the $L = 180\,\text{nm}$ access transistor.

#### Step 5: High-Temperature Stress Vector Execution
1. Activate continuous pattern vector looping at elevated thermal stress environment ($85^\circ\text{C}$ to $125^\circ\text{C}$).
2. Monitor dynamic current draw ($I_{\text{DD,dyn}}$ and $I_{\text{PP,dyn}}$) across all socket channels. Ensure no thermal runaway or excessive leakage ($I_{\text{leak}} > 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ nominal baseline at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                      HTOL Stress Calibration Targets   
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 Min Cell Cap (fF)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                  │▒▒                                  │
 V_th Max Loss (V)┤▒▒                                  │
  Nominal V_DD (V)┤▓▓▓                                 │
                  │▓▓▓                                 │
V_PP Overdrive (V)┤█████                               │
                  │█████                               │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                   0        7       14      21       28 
```

| Parameter / Target Metric | Target Specification | Tolerance / Limits | Measurement Point / Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Overdrive Wordline Voltage ($V_{\text{PP}}$)** | $2.5\,\text{V} \text{ to } 2.8\,\text{V}$ | Min: $2.50\,\text{V}$, Max clamp: $2.90\,\text{V}$ | Kelvin probe at socket $V_{\text{PP}}$ test pad under active vector load |
| **Charge Pump Clock Frequency ($f_{\Phi1,\Phi2}$)** | $20\,\text{MHz} \text{ to } 50\,\text{MHz}$ | $\pm 1.0\,\text{MHz}$ | Driver board clock output pins driving $C_{\text{pump}} = 20\,\text{pF} \text{ to } 50\,\text{pF}$ |
| **Core Supply Voltage ($V_{\text{DD}}$)** | $1.80\,\text{V}$ | $\pm 0.05\,\text{V}$ ($1.75\,\text{V} - 1.85\,\text{V}$) | Regulated driver board DUT supply rail |
| **Cell Retention Leakage Threshold** | $\le 1.0\,\text{fA/cell}$ | Max limit: $1.0\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Post-calibration functional retention stress check |

---

### Literature Citations & Verification
- **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump ($V_{\text{PP}}$) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**:
  - Confirms access transistor $V_{\text{th}} = 0.5\,\text{V} \text{ to } 0.7\,\text{V}$, $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\,\text{V}$, threshold voltage write loss ($V_{\text{DD}} - V_{\text{th}} = 1.2\,\text{V}$, $33\%$ loss), required $V_{\text{PP}} \ge 2.5\,\text{V} \text{ to } 2.8\,\text{V}$, 4-stage Dickson charge pump topology ($C_{\text{pump}} = 20\,\text{pF} \text{ to } 50\,\text{pF}$), two-phase clock $\Phi_1, \Phi_2$ ($20\,\text{MHz} \text{ to } 50\,\text{MHz}$), and bandgap-referenced comparator voltage regulation.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Confirms unit cell geometry ($L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$), minimum storage capacitance $C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\,\text{fF}$, stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture, and sub-threshold leakage target $\le 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Backplane signal integrity and multi-channel trace impedance matching between the FPGA-based pattern driver board and high-density burn-in board (BIB) edge connectors must maintain signal skew under 150 ps across all 64 parallel channels; uncalibrated transmission line reflections can cause spurious clock edge triggers and indeterminate V_PP rail overdrive ringing that violates the maximum transient ratings of the 180nm DRAM peripheral oxide.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Wordline overdrive voltage (V_PP) stress accelerates Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) of the 180nm thick-oxide access transistor (t_ox = 7.0 nm, nominal V_PP = 2.8 V, overdrive stress = 3.6 V to 4.2 V at 125°C). Vector execution must guarantee precise 50% duty-cycle toggle patterns on all row decoders to prevent asymmetric Fowler-Nordheim / trap-assisted tunneling degradation and hot-carrier injection localized to unswitched pass-gate wordline segments.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-Tg polyimide burn-in sockets and gold-plated edge-finger connectors suffer from supply bottleneck lead times of 14 to 18 weeks; contact resistance drift beyond 35 mOhm per pin under prolonged 125°C chamber thermal cycles causes IR drops that invalidate calibrated V_PP overdrive targets if Kelvin four-wire remote sensing circuits are omitted.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Vector programming and automated 4-quadrant SMU overdrive calibration must complete within an allocated 45-minute window per lot insertion to prevent thermal chamber idle time and schedule slips in the 1000-hour JESD22-A108 HTOL qualification milestone for the Gen 3 DRAM run.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. V_PP overdrive regulator overshoot exceeding 4.4 V transient ceiling during vector burst transitions, inducing catastrophic dielectric punch-through across the 180nm wordline access gate oxide.
1. High contact resistance degradation in unmonitored BIB socket pins resulting in dynamic V_PP voltage droop below 3.4 V, leading to sub-acceleration stress and false-positive qualification escapes.
1. Clock-to-data pattern vector skew causing bus contention and current runaway in high-side charge-pump driver stages on the test board.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-2-2-01` | **Dynamic V_PP Overdrive Voltage Calibration and Transient Overshoot Verification** | Keysight N6705C DC Power Analyzer with N6781A SMU module, Tektronix MSO64B 4 GHz Oscilloscope with 10:1 passive low-capacitance probes (1.5 pF) | 1. Program pattern driver board with 10 MHz dynamic March C- stress vector sequence. 2. Step V_PP overdrive supply from nominal 2.80 V to accelerated stress setpoint 3.80 V in increments of 200 mV. 3. Trigger 500 MS/s waveform acquisition on V_PP rail during full-burst wordline transition. 4. Record steady-state DC voltage and peak-to-peak transient overshoot over 10,000 vector cycles. | `Steady-state V_PP must equal 3.800 V +/- 25 mV across all DUT socket sensing nodes; transient peak overshoot must not exceed 4.050 V (< 6.5% overshoot); transient settling time to within +/- 1% must be < 1.2 us.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-2-2-02` | **Pattern Vector Edge Skew and Wordline Toggle Frequency Integrity Check** | Keysight 81160A Pulse Pattern Generator, Advantest V93000 ATE digital capture subsystem / high-speed logic analyzer probe array | 1. Set HTOL chamber temperature to 125°C and soak for 30 minutes. 2. Stream wordline dynamic overdrive stress pattern vector continuously for 1x10^9 clock cycles at 20 MHz master clock. 3. Sample inter-channel skew across address bus bits A[0:12], RAS_N, and WE_N at the socket edge. 4. Measure bit toggle density and verify zero dead-cycles or parity hang states. | `Maximum channel-to-channel skew must be <= 350 ps at 125°C; eye opening width must be >= 38 ns (out of 50 ns clock period); wordline row-toggle duty cycle must measure 50.0% +/- 2.0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal safety gloves rated for 150°C continuous contact (EN 407 Level 2), ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, ANSI Z87.1 approved anti-fog safety spectacles with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with hot board/surfaces: Immediately flush with cool running water for 15 minutes and apply sterile dry dressing; do not apply salves. For IPA eye splash: Rinse cautiously with water for 15 minutes at eye-wash station; remove contact lenses if present and easy to do; seek immediate medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber room requires certified Class 100,000 / ISO 8 cleanroom HVAC with minimum 15 room air changes per hour (ACH); dedicated local exhaust canopy hood over solvent maintenance bench operating at face velocity >= 0.5 m/s.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA-impregnated cleanroom lint-free wipes must be deposited into closed, airtight, FM-approved flammable waste containers with grounded foot pedals; transfer to licensed solvent hazardous waste stream for fuel blending or incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for socket/edge-card contact cleaning** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Grade 1) | `99.9% v/v` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry-pack sealed baked DRAM packages (J-STD-033 MSL 3 post-bake < 0.1% moisture weight), gold/lead-free solder balls clean with zero flux residue or tarnish.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Pre-stressed socketed BIB with calibrated overdrive rails, seated in HTOL oven under dry nitrogen purge ready for 125°C soak.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption by plastic mold compound leads to package delamination or 'popcorning' micro-cracks during rapid chamber temperature ramp to 125°C; ambient socket pin oxidation leads to > 100 mOhm contact resistance shifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full vector loading validation and 4-quadrant V_PP overdrive voltage calibration completed across all 64 DUT positions on the HTOL burn-in driver board at both 25°C and 125°C, ensuring compliance with JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD79 standards for 180nm DRAM reliability stress.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `HTOL_VPP_Overdrive_Calibration_Matrix_LotA.csv`
- [ ] `Dynamic_Vector_Timing_Skew_Validation_Report_125C.pdf`
- [ ] `BIB_Socket_Contact_Resistance_4Wire_Log.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Calibrated steady-state V_PP stress voltage under dynamic March C- vector load at 125°C across all 64 sockets** | `3.800 V` | +/- 25 mV | Automated 4-wire Kelvin SMU telemetry acquisition via Keysight N6705C recorded over 120 seconds |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum inter-channel wordline address and control signal skew at socket terminals under 20 MHz dynamic pattern** | `220 ps` | < 350 ps maximum ceiling | High-bandwidth 4 GHz oscilloscope multi-channel deskew measurement at 125°C chamber temperature |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Kelvin four-wire pin contact resistance on V_PP and GND return pins prior to chamber thermal lock** | `18 mOhm` | <= 35 mOhm | Micro-ohmmeter 100 mA pulsed Kelvin sensing probe array audit across all loaded test sockets |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero pattern parity errors over 1x10^9 continuous cycles, 100% of socket V_PP rails calibrated within +/- 25 mV of 3.800 V target at 125°C, and formal dual signoff by Systems Test Lead and Reliability Qualification Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Environmental Burn-in Chamber Thermal Loading & Dynamic In-Situ Signal Validation

**Document ID:** `SOP-DRAM-REL-180NM-042`  
**Node Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip, 8F²/6F² Stacked Capacitor COB)  
**Process Stage:** Metrology / Reliability & Qualification (HTOL Dynamic Thermal-Voltage Stress)  
**Council Context:** DRAM Foundation VN Council  

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Chamber Pre-Purge &   │
│       MFC Sweep        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    BIB Slot Loading    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Triple-Zone PID Ramp  │
│   & Uniformity Check   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Dynamic V_PP      │
│   Overdrive Pattern    │
│       Excitation       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    In-Situ Signal &    │
│   Leakage Validation   │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Atmosphere Purge & Laminar Flow Stabilization**:
   - Initialize carrier gas sweep utilizing digital mass flow controllers (MFC) calibrated for high-purity $N_2$ (99.999% purity) at a laminar sweep rate between **1.0 and 5.0 SLPM** (standard liters per minute) to sweep out contaminants and prevent ambient back-diffusion.

2. **Chamber Mechanical Loading & Thermal Shock Prevention**:
   - Mount the populated Burn-in Boards (BIBs) / wafer carrier boat onto the automated transfer rail.
   - Insert the assembly into the chamber test zone at a controlled mechanical insertion speed of **$< 50\text{ mm/minute}$** to eliminate thermal shock and prevent crystallographic slip dislocations.
   - Position the DUTs symmetrically within the central flat zone across the central **300 mm to 350 mm** sector.

3. **Multi-Zone PID Thermal Ramp & Profile Regulation**:
   - Engage the triple-loop digital PID controller regulating heating elements across all three zones: **Load Zone**, **Center Zone**, and **Source Zone**.
   - Monitor temperature feedback using dual **Type-R / Type-S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples** per zone housed in protective quartz thermowells.
   - Stabilize thermal dwell and verify temperature uniformity across the central flat zone to within **$\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**.

4. **Dynamic Stress Pattern Generation & $V_{PP}$ Overdrive Application**:
   - Couple the automated test fixture backplane to the dynamic vector generator.
   - Assert dynamic stress vector patterns to exercise access transistor channels ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) and stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) dielectric stacks ($ONO$ or $Ta_2O_5 / Al_2O_3$, $\kappa > 15$).
   - Apply continuous dynamic $V_{PP}$ overdrive wordline switching across memory arrays to accelerate dielectric wear-out and reveal latent defect mechanisms.

5. **In-Situ Signal Validation & Parametric Retention Monitoring**:
   - Measure real-time in-situ cell parametric stability during thermal stress.
   - Validate that cell storage node retention stays compliant with the target sub-threshold and junction leakage threshold of **$< 1\text{ fA/cell at } 85^\circ\text{C}$**, ensuring the minimum storage capacitance requirement of **$\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$** is preserved across all active array sectors.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Measurement Method | Verification Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Zone Temperature Uniformity** | $\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across central $300\text{ mm}$–$350\text{ mm}$ flat zone | Dual Type-R / Type-S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples via triple-loop PID | $^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Carrier Gas Purge Flow Rate** | $1.0\text{ to } 5.0\text{ SLPM}$ | Calibrated Mass Flow Controller (MFC) | $\text{SLPM}$ |
| **Mechanical Insertion / Extraction Velocity** | $< 50\text{ mm/minute}$ | Automated servo-driven lead screw encoder | $\text{mm/min}$ |
| **DRAM Cell Junction/Sub-threshold Leakage** | $< 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (Min capacitance $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$) | In-situ parametric electrometer / retention refresh monitoring | $\text{fA/cell}$ |

---

### 3. Context & Source Citations

- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
  - Multi-zone heating (Load, Center, Source zones) with triple-loop digital PID controller and feedforward decoupling.
  - Type R / Type S Platinum-Rhodium thermocouples in quartz thermowells.
  - Temperature uniformity requirement of $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across the central $300\text{ mm}$ zone.
  - Carrier gas flow regulated at $1\text{ to } 5\text{ SLPM}$ via MFC.
  - Boat loading speed limit of $< 50\text{ mm/minute}$ to prevent thermal shock and crystallographic slip.
- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery**:
  - Three-zone division (Source, Center, Load) with dual Type-R/S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples per zone.
  - Flat zone across the middle $350\text{ mm}$ with temperature uniformity $\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
  - MFC gas delivery rate of $2.0\text{ to } 5.0\text{ SLPM}$ laminar sweep to prevent ambient back-diffusion.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - 180nm cell dimensions: channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture with ONO / high-$\kappa$ dielectric ($\kappa > 15$).
  - Storage node capacitance budget $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$.
  - Sub-threshold and junction leakage threshold $< 1\text{ fA/cell at } 85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal gradient coupling across the multi-slot HTOL burn-in chamber backplane induces localized spatial temperature non-uniformity exceeding +/-3.5°C between upper and lower card slots during dynamic V_PP overdrive toggling. The dynamic current transients (di/dt) drawn by 180nm charge-pump overdrive circuits create board-level power dissipation spikes that destabilize local airflow vectors. The chamber PID control loop must incorporate feedforward compensation tuned to multi-board active wattage dissipation rather than relying strictly on passive air-return Type-T/K thermocouples, ensuring the device junction temperature (T_j) remains clamped precisely at 125°C without runaway.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Dynamic V_PP overdrive stress (elevated to 3.6V on 180nm thick-gate oxide transistors) during 125°C chamber thermal soak triggers accelerated Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) and Hot Carrier Injection (HCI) in wordline booster circuits. In-situ signal monitoring must maintain continuous signal integrity validation of wordline rise/fall times (< 2.8 ns) and address line edge rates at the burn-in socket pogo-pin interface. Failure to calibrate high-temperature PCB transmission line trace impedance (50-ohm nominal shifting under 125°C glass transition temperature Tg) will cause signal reflections, false bit failure captures, or indeterminate gate oxide stress voltages across the array.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-temperature burn-in sockets rated for continuous 150°C operation with beryllium copper (BeCu) or phosphor bronze contacts plated with 30 u-inch hard gold suffer from long-lead times (> 14 weeks) and contact spring fatigue after repeated thermal cycling. Polyimide (PI) burn-in boards (BIB) with high Tg (> 260°C) must be qualified across multiple vendors to avoid supply-line bottlenecks. Sourcing high-purity dry nitrogen purge gas and specialized high-temperature wiring harnesses capable of withstanding continuous 125°C/1000-hour HTOL qualification cycles represents an active schedule risk.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The HTOL chamber thermal qualification and in-situ monitoring milestone must strictly align with the JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD47 qualification gate deadlines for Gen 3 180nm DRAM tapeout. Unplanned chamber downtime due to thermal trip interlocks or driver channel calibration drifts will compromise the critical 168-hour read-point commitment, inducing cascading delays to package-level qualification signoff and MPW commercial engineering release.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Spatial thermal runaway where edge-slot burn-in boards exceed 135°C junction temperature during simultaneous wordline V_PP overdrive cycling, triggering catastrophic junction thermal breakdown and gate oxide punch-through.
1. High-temperature socket contact resistance degradation (> 1.5 ohm shift) caused by solder-ball fretting corrosion and contact spring force annealing at 125°C, resulting in false functional read failures and V_PP voltage droop during in-situ cycling.
1. Transmission line dielectric loss tangent (tan delta) degradation and impedance mismatch across the burn-in board at 125°C, causing severe edge jitter, clock runt pulses, and incomplete wordline stress coverage across deep array addresses.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-2-3-01` | **Chamber Spatial-Temporal Thermal Uniformity & DUT Junction Stability Under Dynamic V_PP Overdrive Loading** | Yokogawa WT3000E Power Analyzer, Keysight 34980A Multifunction Switch/Measure Unit with 32-channel Type-T calibrated thermocouple matrix, FLIR A655sc MWIR thermal imaging camera, Agilent E3649A Programmable DC Power Supplies. | 1. Initialize Keysight 34980A data logging on all 32 thermocouple channels distributed across upper, middle, and lower BIB rack slots. 2. Enable automated pattern generator driving dynamic V_PP overdrive vectors (3.6V V_PP, 1.8V V_DD, 20 MHz active cycling) across all socketed DRAM units. 3. Monitor individual board supply current and aggregate chamber load for 180 minutes continuously. 4. Record local air temperature, board surface temperatures, and calibrated on-die diode thermal voltages across selected monitor DUTs every 10 seconds. 5. Introduce a stepped airflow perturbation (+10% blower speed) to verify PID disturbance rejection and thermal settling time. | `Chamber multi-point spatial temperature uniformity must remain within 125.0°C +/- 2.0°C across all BIB locations. In-situ DUT junction temperature (T_j) derived from calibrated thermal diode forward voltage must remain bounded between 124.0°C and 127.5°C during continuous 3.6V V_PP overdrive pattern execution with zero thermal trip events.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-2-3-02` | **In-Situ Dynamic Signal Integrity & V_PP Wordline Stress Waveform Verification at 125°C** | Tektronix MSO64B 4-channel 4 GHz Digital Storage Oscilloscope with high-temperature differential active probes (TDP1500), Advantest T5503B / Chroma 3650 Dedicated HTOL Burn-in Driver Architecture, Keysight N6705C DC Power Analyzer. | 1. Connect high-temperature differential probes to the V_PP rail and wordline select test pins on designated edge and center sockets. 2. Execute burst-mode 3.6V dynamic V_PP overdrive pattern sequences at 20 MHz continuous toggle rate. 3. Acquire 10,000 waveform cycles using Tektronix MSO64B to measure pulse rise time (10%-90%), fall time (90%-10%), overshoot amplitude, and peak-to-peak rail ripple under maximum array switching load. 4. Continuously compare in-situ detected driver logic levels against expected vector states via the burn-in system comparator channels over a 120-minute continuous run. | `V_PP voltage rail droop under active row cycling must not exceed 80 mV (target 3.60V, minimum allowable 3.52V). Dynamic wordline edge rise time must remain <= 3.2 ns with total peak overshoot clamped below 3.85V. Zero intermittent signal dropouts, clock runt pulses, or vector miscompare errors detected over 10,000 acquired cycles.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating Kevlar heat-resistant gloves (rated to 250°C continuous contact), ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and UV/thermal safety glasses, ESD-safe flame-retardant Nomex cleanroom lab coat, Static-dissipative steel-toe heat-resistant footwear, Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves worn underneath thermal outer gloves
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately flush affected skin area with copious cool, potable water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply salves or ointments; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek immediate medical attention. Nitrogen Asphyxiation: In the event of N2 leak or oxygen-depletion alarm, immediately evacuate personnel to fresh air. If victim is not breathing, administer artificial respiration and supplemental oxygen by trained personnel. # Standard Operating Procedure: In-Chamber Dynamic Signal Integrity & Wordline Boost Leakage In-Situ Monitoring

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In-chamber dynamic signal integrity monitoring across a 125°C HTOL chamber introduces severe parasitic loading from extended signal feedthrough cabling, pogo pin interfaces, and BIB (Burn-In Board) trace routing. With 180nm folded bitline sensing operating on small differential voltage margins (dV ≈ 150-200 mV governed by C_b/C_s ≈ 5:1 to 9:1, C_s=28 fF, C_b=180 fF), high-speed wordline overdrive (V_PP = 3.3V-3.8V boosted from V_DD = 1.8V) requires active RF buffering or high-bandwidth active differential probes located within 5 cm of the DUT sockets to prevent signal degradation and false trip readouts.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Wordline boost leakage (I_VPP) under elevated thermal and voltage stress (T_j = 125°C, V_PP accelerated to 3.8V) is dominated by gate dielectric stress, time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) of the 180nm thick-oxide access transistors, and drain-induced barrier lowering / junction band-to-band tunneling (BTBT). Dynamic in-situ sensing must isolate active dynamic switching charge (Q_dyn = C_WL * V_PP * f) from steady-state subthreshold and dielectric leakage (I_leak) during pattern transitions, ensuring resolution down to nanoampere levels per pin without chamber thermal EMI corruption.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-temperature Polyimide/PTFE high-Tg BIBs equipped with ceramic test sockets rated for continuous 150°C operation and 1000-hour HTOL endurance face acute procurement lead-time bottlenecks (typically 12-16 weeks). Off-the-shelf burn-in drivers and multi-channel parametric measurement units (SMUs) must utilize standardized edge connectors to prevent single-source vendor lock-in for Vietnam local OSAT qualification fixtures.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: HTOL stress execution represents the pacing critical-path milestone for commercial MPW tapeout reliability signoff. In-situ metrology execution must achieve strict parallel DUT testing without unscheduled chamber aborts or thermal runaway; socket wear-out and insertion-loss drift must be characterized prior to the 168-hour, 500-hour, and 1000-hour test gates to prevent program schedule slippage.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. V_PP charge-pump rail collapse or severe voltage sag during simultaneous multi-bank wordline activation, leading to access transistor threshold underdrive and incomplete cell capacitor refresh/write-back.
1. TDDB gate-oxide punchthrough in wordline driver level-shifters and access NMOS gate dielectrics under sustained 3.8V overdrive stress at 125°C, resulting in localized catastrophic short-circuits to substrate.
1. High-temperature signal attenuation and impedance mismatch across BIB trace routing and chamber pogo-pin bulkheads causing eye-diagram closure and clock jitter violation (>250 ps) during dynamic address decoding.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-3-01` | **In-Situ Dynamic Wordline Boost (V_PP) Accelerated Leakage Current Metrology** | High-Density Parametric Measurement Unit (Keysight N6781A SMU / Advantest V93000 HSM6800), High-Tg Polyimide In-Chamber Burn-In Board (BIB) with Kelvin 4-wire sensing lines, High-Temperature Triaxial Cabling. | 1. Program wordline overdrive regulator / external generator to apply V_PP stress voltage step-profile: 3.3V (nominal), 3.6V (stress level 1), and 3.8V (stress level 2). 2. Apply continuous alternating row-hammer and march C- stress patterns across 512 rows per bank at 100 MHz dynamic switching rate. 3. Execute periodic 10 ms quiet-hold windows with wordline driven HIGH (active unselected state) to measure pure quasi-static wordline leakage current (I_VPP_leak) via 4-wire Kelvin SMU channel. 4. Record leakage current sampling continuously at 1 kHz acquisition rate over a 168-hour baseline qualification period. | `Quasi-static in-situ leakage current I_VPP_leak at 125°C, V_PP = 3.8V must remain <= 15.0 uA per 1Mb block array. Shift in leakage current (delta-I_leak) between t=0h and t=168h must be < 20.0% with zero catastrophic dielectric breakdown (I_leak > 500 uA).` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-3-02` | **In-Chamber Wordline Transition Dynamic Signal Integrity & Eye-Margin Metrology** | Tektronix MSO64B 4 GHz Oscilloscope equipped with TDP3500 3.5 GHz Differential High-Temperature Active Probes, Low-loss semi-rigid coaxial feedthrough bulkheads. | 1. Connect differential active high-Z probe tips to dedicated calibrated microstrip test-points situated at the wordline driver output pin of edge and center DUT sockets. 2. Trigger oscilloscope on the rising edge of Wordline Enable (WL_EN) signal. 3. Acquire 100,000 continuous switching cycles to construct an accumulated persistence eye-diagram and wordline edge rise/fall transient profiles. 4. Measure wordline rise time (10% to 90% of V_PP), overshoot amplitude above V_PP, ring-back undershoot margin, and peak-to-peak jitter. | `Wordline rise time t_rise must be between 1.8 ns and 3.2 ns; voltage overshoot must not exceed 10.0% of V_PP (maximum peak <= 3.96V at 3.6V setting); ring-back undershoot must not dip below 90.0% of V_PP; total deterministic jitter (DJ) must be <= 120 ps.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating aluminized heat-resistant gloves rated for 250°C contact (EN 407), ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and UV/thermal safety glasses, Static-dissipative flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat (NFPA 70E compliant), Nitrile chemical-resistant inner gloves under ESD dissipation gloves
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn emergency: Immediately flush affected skin with cool, clean water for minimum 15 minutes; do not apply greasy ointments; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek urgent medical attention. Cryogenic/Nitrogen asphyxiation risk: Immediately move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen or artificial respiration if breathing ceases. Eye exposure to solvent: Irrigate eyes at eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous chamber exhaust ventilation maintaining a minimum air-exchange rate of 12 ACH (air changes per hour) with negative pressure enclosure; dedicated toxic/inert gas extraction manifold with continuous ambient O2 monitoring sensors interlocked to alarm at O2 < 19.5% volume.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and IPA residues must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-proof hazardous solvent containers for off-site thermal incineration. Thermal fluid leaks must be captured using non-combustible chemical absorbent pillows and treated as regulated fluorinated waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen (Gas / Liquid Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (Socket and Board Contact Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade VLSI | `99.9%` |
| **Fluorinated Heat Transfer Fluid (Chamber Thermal Loop)** | `86508-42-1` | Technical Purity Cleanroom Formulation | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, flux-free, bake-conditioned (125°C for 24h dry-bake per J-STD-033D) packaged DRAM units, post-wirebond/mold packaging with Au/Pd-Ni leadframes free from oxidation, particulate contamination, and moisture.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically stressed post-HTOL package leads, exhibiting minimal leadframe tarnishing (<= Class 2 oxidation per IPC-A-610), zero socket contact pitting or gold scrub gouging exceeding 25% of pad thickness.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption causing internal package delamination and 'popcorning' during rapid thermal chamber ramp to 125°C, accompanied by socket contact oxidation inducing high-impedance measurement artifacts and false signal integrity failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full in-chamber dynamic signal integrity and in-situ wordline boost (V_PP) leakage characterization of the 180nm DRAM test vehicle across 168-hour accelerated thermal-voltage stress at 125°C, verifying retention of dielectric integrity and signal eye margins.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `HTOL_VPP_Leakage_InSitu_TimeSeries_168H.csv`
- [ ] `Dynamic_Signal_Integrity_EyeDiagram_Analysis_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Socket_Interface_PrePost_Optical_Inspection_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum in-situ steady-state wordline boost leakage current (I_VPP_leak) under 125°C, 3.8V bias.** | `<= 15.0 uA` | +1.5 uA | Precision SMU Kelvin 4-wire quasi-static leakage logging during programmed quiet windows across 168 hours. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Dynamic wordline transition 10%-90% rise time (t_rise) under 100 MHz dynamic stress in-chamber.** | `2.40 ns` | ±0.60 ns | High-bandwidth active differential probe measurement with high-speed digital oscilloscope (100k cycle persistence histogram). |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Wordline overdrive signal total deterministic jitter (DJ) at 125°C chamber temperature.** | `<= 100 ps` | +20 ps | Oscilloscope jitter decomposition analysis on wordline driver output eye-diagram. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Completion of 168-hour uninterrupted HTOL dynamic burn-in at 125°C and V_PP = 3.8V across 100% of tested DUT sockets with zero dielectric punchthrough events, wordline leakage degradation delta-I_leak < 20.0%, and all signal integrity assertions verified within target tolerances.

3. Acquire 100,000 continuous switching cycles to construct an accumulated persistence eye-diagram and wordline edge rise/fall transient profiles.
4. Measure wordline rise time (10% to 90% of V_PP), overshoot amplitude above V_PP, ring-back undershoot margin, and peak-to-peak jitter.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Wordline rise time t_rise must be between 1.8 ns and 3.2 ns; voltage overshoot must not exceed 10.0% of V_PP (maximum peak <= 3.96V at 3.6V setting); ring-back undershoot must not dip below 90.0% of V_PP; total deterministic jitter (DJ) must be <= 120 ps.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## BIB RF Feedthrough Calibration & In-Situ Signal Integrity Instrumentation

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP defines the calibration, RF de-embedding, and in-situ dynamic signal integrity instrumentation for Burn-In Boards (BIB) inside high-temperature burn-in chambers for the **180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)**. It establishes precise protocols to eliminate chamber wall bulkhead feedthrough reflections, verify transmission lines driving wordline charge pump clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) and boosted wordline levels ($V_{PP}$), and monitor in-situ wordline boost gate dielectric/junction leakage under dynamic HTOL stress.

---

### 2. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Chamber Port VNA    │
│        SOLT Cal        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      BIB Fixture       │
│  De-embedding 2x-Thru  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   VPP Overdrive & WL   │
│    Clock Injection     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  In-Situ Wordline Eye  │
│    & TDR Monitoring    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Sub-fA Wordline     │
│     Boost Leakage      │
│       Screening        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Bulkhead Feedthrough S-Parameter Calibration (SOLT)
1. Interconnect calibrated RF coaxial cables from a 4-port Vector Network Analyzer (VNA, 100 kHz – 3 GHz bandwidth) to the external chamber bulkhead SMA/SMP feedthrough connectors.
2. Execute a full 2-port / 4-port Short-Open-Load-Through (SOLT) calibration at the chamber inner-wall bulkhead reference plane at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
3. Elevate chamber thermal profile to the target HTOL temperature ($85^\circ\text{C}$ to $125^\circ\text{C}$) and record thermal drift delta S-parameters ($\Delta S_{21}, \Delta S_{11}$) to compensate for thermal phase shift and dielectric loss across the bulkhead feedthrough assembly.

#### Step 2: In-Chamber BIB Fixture De-Embedding (2x-Thru / TRL)
1. Mount the unpopulated calibration coupon BIB featuring standard $2\times\text{-Thru}$ test fixtures into the chamber card cage.
2. Acquire the time-domain reflectometry (TDR) step response with a $35\text{ ps}$ rise-time incident step.
3. Compute the de-embedding matrix to mathematically shift the measurement reference plane directly to the target DRAM device-under-test (DUT) socket solder pad ring.
4. Verify the characteristic trace impedance matches $Z_0 = 50\ \Omega \pm 2.5\ \Omega$ across the entire length of the high-frequency clock and $V_{PP}$ distribution microstrips.

#### Step 3: Two-Phase Clock ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) Signal Integrity & Eye Diagram Instrumentation
1. Connect the external high-speed pulse generator to the de-embedded clock lines driving the Dickson charge pump clock inputs.
2. Program two-phase non-overlapping clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) at frequency $f = 20\text{ MHz}$ to $50\text{ MHz}$ with nominal amplitude $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
3. Measure the eye diagram directly at the socket terminals using high-impedance low-capacitance active differential micro-probes ($C_{in} < 0.5\text{ pF}$):
   - Measure clock edge risetime/falltime: $t_r, t_f \le 1.2\text{ ns}$.
   - Ensure phase non-overlap dead-time $t_{non-overlap} \ge 1.5\text{ ns}$ to prevent flying capacitor ($C_{pump} = 20\text{ pF}$ to $50\text{ pF}$) cross-conduction.

#### Step 4: Boosted Wordline Voltage ($V_{PP}$) Overdrive & Bias Injection
1. Inject the elevated wordline stress overdrive level: $V_{PP} = 2.5\text{ V}$ to $2.8\text{ V}$ (derived from $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{overdrive}$ where $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{thn} = 0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, and $\Delta V_{overdrive} \ge 0.2\text{ V}$).
2. Perform dynamic overdrive cycling on access transistor wordlines ($W = 220\text{ nm}, L = 180\text{ nm}$).
3. Monitor rail droop and ripple during active row access toggling: ensure ripple peak-to-peak amplitude $V_{ripple} \le 50\text{ mV}$ under peak array switching current.

#### Step 5: In-Situ Wordline Boost Leakage & Gate Dielectric Integrity Monitoring
1. Switch matrix to the precision source measure unit (SMU) connected via high-isolation triaxial lines.
2. At thermal equilibrium ($85^\circ\text{C}$), bias wordline access gates at $V_{GS} = V_{PP} = 2.5\text{ V} - 2.8\text{ V}$ while measuring quiescent leakage current on the unselected storage node and bitline terminals ($V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$).
3. Extract total cell subthreshold and junction leakage current to verify compliance against the target budget ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ for access gate and storage node dielectric ONO/$\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$). Verify the discrete sub-micron gate off-leakage baseline stays within $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA/\mu m}$ at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │
VPP Leakage Margin┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒    │
  Eye Jitter Ratio┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒    │
 TDR Impedance Tol┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                  │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
   Return Loss S11┤████████                            │
                  │████████                            │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                   0       24       48      72       96 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Physical Units | Verification Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bulkhead Feedthrough Return Loss ($S_{11}$)** | $\le -18.0$ | $\text{Max } -15.0$ | $\text{dB}$ | 4-Port VNA ($20\text{ MHz} - 50\text{ MHz}$) |
| **Trace Characteristic Impedance ($Z_0$)** | $50.0$ | $\pm 2.5\ (\pm 5\%)$ | $\Omega$ | TDR Step ($t_r = 35\text{ ps}$) |
| **Wordline Overdrive Stress Voltage ($V_{PP}$)** | $2.50\text{ to }2.80$ | $\pm 25$ | $\text{mV}$ | Digital Sampling Oscilloscope / SMU |
| **Single-Cell Boost/Retention Leakage ($I_{leak}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Low-Current Triaxial SMU at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Pass Gate Off-State Leakage Current ($I_{off}$)** | $\le 10.0$ | $\text{Max } 10.0$ | $\text{pA/\mu m}$ | Precision Parametric Analyzer at $V_{DS}=1.8\text{ V}$ |

---

### 5. Context Literature Citations

1. **Cell Layout Geometry & Leakage**:
   - Access transistor geometry: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Storage dielectric target: ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ stack with storage node capacitance $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$.
   - Retention leakage budget: Sub-threshold and junction leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   *(Source: `180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench`)*.
2. **Wordline Boost Voltage & Pump Operating Parameters**:
   - Nominal voltage rails: $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$, threshold loss compensation requiring $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{overdrive} \ge 2.5\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$.
   - Dickson charge pump flying capacitance: $C_{pump} = 20\text{ pF}\text{ to }50\text{ pF}$ driven by two-phase non-overlapping clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) at $20\text{ MHz}\text{ to }50\text{ MHz}$.
   *(Source: `High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture`)*.
3. **Static Parametric Baselines**:
   - Enhancement NMOS access transistor threshold voltage: $V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$.
   - Sub-micron device static on/off limits: $I_{on} \ge 500\ \mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$ ($V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$).
   *(Source: `Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification`)*.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Routing high-frequency DRAM clock/command strobe signals and high-voltage Wordline Boost (V_PP overdrive ~3.3V-3.8V for 180nm cell access) through multi-slot HTOL oven bulkheads presents an impedance discontinuity. The coaxial feedthrough bulkhead interfaces must maintain controlled 50-ohm characteristic impedance across 125°C to 150°C thermal excursions without dielectric thermal expansion inducing ground bounce or signal skew exceeding 45 ps between differential pairs.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Burn-In Board (BIB) FR-4/Polyimide trace dissipation factors (tan delta) degrade markedly at elevated burn-in temperatures (125°C-150°C). Vector network analyzer (VNA) de-embedding using 2X Thru or TRL calibration fixtures must be calibrated at in-situ HTOL chamber operating temperatures; otherwise, insertion loss (S21) calibration errors exceed 2.2 dB at 200 MHz-400 MHz DDR clock rates, masking true high-temperature Wordline leakage and oxide breakdown transients.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying custom hermetic high-temperature blind-mate RF coaxial bulkhead connectors rated for sustained 150°C operation involves long lead times (16-20 weeks) and single-source vendor vulnerabilities. We must standardize on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) high-temperature SMA/SMP bulkhead connectors with PTFE/PEEK dielectric inserts and procure golden SOLT/TRL cal kits early to avoid delaying the qualification burn-in schedule.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement and qualification of high-temperature RF feedthrough assemblies and custom calibration fixtures represent a high capital expenditure for Gen 3 MPW. Acceptance milestones must enforce strict vendor Gauge R&R (measurement CV < 1.0%) across all chamber slots before commissioning the dynamic HTOL stress chamber to prevent burn-in socket downtime.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Bulkhead RF feedthrough dielectric thermal fatigue causing intermittent contact resistance jumps (>1.5 ohm) during thermal cycling, leading to false DDR command framing errors.
1. V_PP wordline overdrive supply feedthrough coupling into adjacent high-speed DDR strobe lines, causing false trigger resets and unmonitored gate oxide dielectric breakdown during 150°C stress.
1. Thermal expansion mismatch between chamber wall stainless steel and BIB connector backplane causing mechanical shear and micro-cracking of soldered coaxial ground shields.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-3-1-01` | **Chamber Bulkhead RF Feedthrough In-Situ S-Parameter Insertion Loss & Return Loss Verification** | Keysight E5080B 4-Port Vector Network Analyzer (VNA), calibrated High-Temp 3.5mm SOLT Calibration Kit, Chamber Thermal Couplers, Semi-Rigid Conformable High-Temp RF Test Cables | 1. Connect VNA port 1 to external oven RF bulkhead channel CH_CLK_P and port 2 to CH_CLK_N. 2. Sweep S-parameters from 10 MHz to 1.5 GHz at 0 dBm input power. 3. Record S11 (return loss) and S21 (insertion loss) across 10 consecutive frequency sweeps over 30 minutes. 4. Elevate chamber temperature to 150°C at 2°C/min ramp rate and repeat S-parameter measurement. 5. Calculate Return Loss and Insertion Loss degradation coefficient across the band. | `Return loss (S11) must remain <= -18.0 dB and Insertion Loss (S21) magnitude must not exceed -2.5 dB up to 500 MHz across 125°C to 150°C. S21 variation over 10 consecutive sweeps must demonstrate CV < 0.8%.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-3-1-02` | **In-Situ Wordline Boost (V_PP) Feedthrough Isolation and Crosstalk Coupling Test** | Tektronix 4 GHz DPO70404C High-Performance Oscilloscope, Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer, Keithley 2410 1100V SourceMeter, 50-ohm Coaxial Probes | 1. Apply 3.6V dynamic boost pulse waveform to V_PP feedthrough input. 2. Connect oscilloscope Channel 1 to adjacent DDR clock feedthrough and Channel 2 to Command/Address bus feedthrough. 3. Measure induced peak-to-peak crosstalk noise voltage (V_xtalk) and Wordline boost line DC leakage current using B1500A. 4. Monitor baseline current over 120 minutes of continuous dynamic overdrive switching. | `Maximum peak-to-peak induced crosstalk noise on adjacent signal feedthroughs must be <= 35 mV. Wordline boost line feedthrough leakage current must not exceed 250 nA at 3.8V bias at 125°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protective Kevlar gloves rated for 200°C contact, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe flame-retardant lab coat, Class 0 insulating safety gloves for high-voltage SourceMeter handling (>50V)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn contact: Immerse affected skin immediately in cool, clean running water for minimum 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing. Chemical eye splash: Flush eyes immediately with isotonic eyewash for at least 15 minutes while retracting eyelids. Electrical shock: Cut chamber main interlock power immediately; check victim vital signs and initiate CPR/AED if unresponsive.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber exhaust must be connected to facility dedicated thermal scrubbed exhaust operating at >= 150 CFM to safely discharge outgassed plasticizers and solvent vapors during 150°C chamber heating.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and IPA residues must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-arresting stainless steel disposal bins designated for hazardous solvent waste; dispose according to EPA/local hazardous chemical waste protocols.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Electronic Cleaning Grade)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Perfluoropolyether Heat Transfer Fluid (Galden HT)** | `69991-67-9` | Technical Grade | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Gold-plated SMA/SMP connector mating surfaces and BIB edge contacts inspected clean, free of organic film residue, copper oxidation, and particulates per Mil-Std-883 Method 2009.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Sealed connector feedthrough assembly installed in chamber bulkhead with high-temperature silicone O-rings under controlled dry N2 chamber purge.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes copper-beryllium center pin galvanic oxidation and moisture adsorption in cable PTFE dielectrics, resulting in >3.0 dB insertion loss escalation and high-temperature arcing on V_PP boost line.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full hardware integration and RF calibration validation of HTOL chamber RF feedthrough bulkhead and BIB in-situ monitoring instrumentation, ensuring clean differential DDR signal fidelity and microampere-level Wordline oxide leakage resolution at 125°C-150°C burn-in conditions.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `BIB_RF_Feedthrough_S_Parameter_150C_Verification_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `InSitu_Signal_Integrity_TDR_Crosstalk_Matrix.csv`
- [ ] `VPP_Overdrive_Leakage_Calibration_Log.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Bulkhead RF Feedthrough S11 Return Loss up to 500 MHz at 150°C** | `-20.0 dB` | <= -18.0 dB | VNA S-parameter measurement after 2X-Thru de-embedding at 150°C stabilized chamber temperature |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Feedthrough Gauge R&R Repeatability across 10 repeated insertion and thermal cycles** | `0.65%` | CV < 1.0% | Statistical calculation of S21 insertion loss magnitude coefficient of variation across 9 distinct chamber slot channels |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Adjacent Channel Crosstalk Noise under 3.8V V_PP Wordline Overdrive Step Transition** | `22 mV` | <= 35 mV | High-bandwidth 4 GHz real-time digital oscilloscope capture into 50-ohm termination |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal sign-off requires all 9 chamber slots to pass VNA S-parameter specs (S11 <= -18 dB, S21 >= -2.5 dB at 500 MHz), dynamic V_PP crosstalk noise under 35 mV peak-to-peak at 150°C, and documented Gauge R&R CV < 1.0% certified by both Systems Engineer and Reliability Metrology Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Dynamic $V_{PP}$ Dickson Pump Stress & In-Situ Overdrive Degradation Logging

> **Document ID:** `SOP-REL-HTOL-VPP-001`  
> **Source Link:** [`docs/sop_dynamic_vpp_dickson_pump_stress.md`](./docs/sop_dynamic_vpp_dickson_pump_stress.md)  
> **Process Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip $\rightarrow$ MPW Tapeout $\rightarrow$ ATE JEDEC DDR Speed-Bin & HTOL Burn-in $\rightarrow$ Dynamic Stress Pattern Programming with $V_{PP}$ Overdrive Cycling $\rightarrow$ Dynamic $V_{PP}$ Dickson Pump Stress & In-Situ Overdrive Degradation Logging

---

### 1. Process Flowchart

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  HTOL Burn-in Chamber  │
│     & Socket Setup     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Dickson Pump      │
│  Clocking: Phi1/Phi2   │
│        20-50MHz        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Overdrive Cycling:   │
│  V_PP Stress at 2.5V   │
│         - 2.8V         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    In-Situ Wordline    │
│  Boost & Dynamic V_PP  │
│        Logging         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Acceptance       │
│  Screening: Retention  │
│   & Leakage Analysis   │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **HTOL Chamber Environmental Stabilization & Socket Loading**:
   - Seat packaged 180nm DRAM test devices into high-temperature Burn-in Board (BIB) sockets.
   - Stabilize the chamber ambient temperature at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to evaluate worst-case sub-threshold and junction leakages under bias.

2. **Dickson Pump Multi-Phase Clock Initialization**:
   - Drive the 4-stage Dickson charge pump using two-phase non-overlapping clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) programmed within $20\text{ MHz}$ to $50\text{ MHz}$.
   - Verify that flying capacitors ($C_{\text{pump}} = 20\text{ pF}$ to $50\text{ pF}$) across the 4 boost stages achieve synchronized dynamic charge transfer without phase collision.

3. **Dynamic Overdrive Stress Cycling**:
   - Bias nominal core supply at $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
   - Set the dynamic feedback voltage divider and bandgap-referenced comparator to regulate and stress the wordline boost node $V_{PP}$ at $2.5\text{ V}$ to $2.8\text{ V}$ ($V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{\text{overdrive}}$, covering $V_{th} \sim 0.5\text{ V}\text{--}0.7\text{ V}$).
   - Run accelerated wordline toggle patterns across memory access transistors ($L = 180\text{ nm}, W = 220\text{ nm}$) to stress the gate oxide and monitor overdrive degradation.

4. **In-Situ Metrology & Degradation Telemetry Logging**:
   - Continuously capture regulator shut-off margins, pump ramp-up latency, and wordline boost voltage drops.
   - Screen for loss of boost margin below $2.5\text{ V}$ to prevent write-loss degradation towards $V_{DD} - V_{th} = 1.8\text{ V} - 0.6\text{ V} = 1.2\text{ V}$ (which causes $33\%$ charge loss in the storage node).
   - Execute in-situ refresh scans to verify cell leakage retention compliance under sustained $85^\circ\text{C}$ operation.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                      │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░              │
     Cell Ret Cap (fF)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░              │
                      │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Flying Cap C_pump (pF)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
    Dickson Freq (MHz)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                      │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
   VPP Boost Level (V)┤███                             │
                      │███                             │
                      └┬───────┬───────┬──────┬───────┬┘
                      0.0    12.5    25.0   37.5   50.0 
```

| # | Acceptance Metric | Lower Limit | Upper Limit | Physical Unit | Test Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **Boosted Wordline Voltage ($V_{PP}$)** | $2.5$ | $2.8$ | $\text{V}$ | Active dynamic wordline toggle under $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$ |
| **2** | **Dickson Pump Clock Frequency ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$)** | $20.0$ | $50.0$ | $\text{MHz}$ | Two-phase non-overlapping clocking |
| **3** | **Per-Stage Flying Capacitance ($C_{\text{pump}}$)** | $20.0$ | $50.0$ | $\text{pF}$ | 4-stage pump capacitor array |
| **4** | **Cell Sub-Threshold & Junction Leakage** | — | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Tested in-situ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ on $180\text{ nm} \times 220\text{ nm}$ access NMOS |
| **5** | **Unit Cell Storage Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $28.0$ | — | $\text{fF}$ | Stacked MIM / ONO crown capacitor |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations
- **Source: High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**:
  - Access transistor $V_{th} \sim 0.5\text{ V}$ to $0.7\text{ V}$.
  - Nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$; non-boosted drop $V_{DD} - V_{th} = 1.2\text{ V}$ ($33\%$ charge loss).
  - Target $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{\text{overdrive}} \ge 2.5\text{ V}$ to $2.8\text{ V}$.
  - 4-stage Dickson pump with flying capacitor $C_{\text{pump}} = 20\text{ pF}$ to $50\text{ pF}$ driven by two-phase non-overlapping clocks ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) at $20\text{ MHz}$ to $50\text{ MHz}$.
  - Dynamic feedback voltage divider and bandgap-referenced comparator.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Minimum storage capacitance $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$ per cell.
  - Sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

*The complete specification has been recorded in [`docs/sop_dynamic_vpp_dickson_pump_stress.md`](./docs/sop_dynamic_vpp_dickson_pump_stress.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The Dickson charge pump driving the wordline overdrive rail (V_PP nominal 2.7 V) operates under elevated HTOL thermal-voltage conditions (T_j = 125 °C, V_DD stress = 2.2 V vs nominal 1.8 V), which drastically degrades the high-voltage pass transistors via hot-carrier injection (HCI) and positive bias temperature instability (PBTI) on the diode-configured NMOS stages. The in-situ telemetry must sample transient wordline boost activation drooping and Dickson regulator burst frequency without introducing parasitic capacitive loading (> 2 pF) that would artifactually mask real open-loop pumping degradation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In 180nm planar CMOS DRAM cell access nodes, suppressing threshold loss requires V_PP >= 2.65 V to write full '1' levels into the cell node capacitor (C_cell ~ 25 fF). During accelerated burn-in overdrive cycling, flying capacitors (C_pump = 35 pF MIM capacitors) and reservoir tank capacitors (C_filter = 500 pF) experience constant electric-field stress approaching 5 MV/cm, leading to time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) and increased leakage through the deep N-well isolation junction. The feedback resistive divider and bandgap comparator reference must be continuously cross-monitored to ensure regulation cutoff is not falsely triggered by comparator offset drift.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring specialized high-temperature burn-in board (BIB) sockets rated for continuous 150 °C operation with low-inductance Kelvin sense pins (< 1.5 nH, contact resistance < 50 mOhm) poses a 14-week lead-time risk. We must lock in vendors supplying polyimide-based HTOL BIB test boards qualified for multi-channel high-voltage dynamic logging instrumentation (such as Keysight or Advantest burn-in driver systems) to avoid staging idle ATE burn-in oven capacity.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: HTOL dynamic stress execution for 1000 hours with interim readouts at 48h, 168h, and 500h represents the critical path for JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD47 qualification. In-situ degradation logging of V_PP boost efficiency and ripple must execute autonomously inside the thermal chamber without human handling interruptions to preserve valid thermal equilibrium and prevent thermal runaway or uncontrolled annealing cycles.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. MIM Flying Capacitor TDDB leading to direct stage-to-substrate dielectric short and collapse of V_PP boost rail below 1.8 V
1. Threshold voltage shift (Delta V_th > 150 mV) on Dickson pass gates due to PBTI/HCI, causing dynamic pump impedance runaway and V_PP droop under burst refresh cycles
1. Bandgap comparator reference drift causing premature pump cutoff and excessive V_PP ripple exceeding 30 mVpp under heavy wordline activation switching load

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating Kevlar safety gloves rated for 200 °C contact, EN 166 compliant side-shield polycarbonate optical safety glasses, Arc-rated antistatic/ESD flame-resistant laboratory coat (NFPA 70E Category 1), ESD-dissipative steel-toe footwear with conductive heel grounding straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For thermal burns from HTOL oven/socket contact: Immediately irrigate affected skin under clean, cool running water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply salves or ointments; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek medical attention. For cryo/asphyxiation exposure from N2 purge leakage: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; initiate CPR if pulse absent.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: HTOL burn-in ovens must be connected to dedicated industrial exhaust ducting (face velocity >= 0.5 m/s, continuous airflow >= 150 CFM) to expel outgassed socket volatiles and thermal decomposition vapors. Install calibrated ambient O2 deficiency monitors with audible interlocks set at 19.5% O2 threshold.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used isopropyl alcohol swabs and wipe media must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-proof hazardous waste receptacles in accordance with RCRA ignitable solvent rules (EPA Waste Code D001) for off-site high-temperature solvent incineration.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry-pack vacuum-sealed moisture barrier bag (MBB) with active desiccant and cobalt-free humidity indicator card (HIC < 5% RH); leadframe/BGA package contacts free of copper/tin oxidation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically stressed packaged devices cooled to < 40 °C under dry N2 atmosphere; socket contact pads intact without pitting, tin transfer, or carbonization.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption exceeding IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 MSL-3 limits prior to 125 °C HTOL insertion leading to internal mold compound delamination, popcorning, or package cracking during thermal ramp.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed 168-hour accelerated HTOL dynamic stress and automated in-situ degradation logging of the 180nm DRAM on-chip Dickson V_PP charge pump module across 77 sample units. Measured parameters confirm that pass-gate HCI/PBTI degradation and MIM flying capacitor leakage remain strictly within JEDEC DDR retention overdrive margins without catastrophic TDDB ruptures.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero functional fails across all 77 DUTs (LTPD <= 3% at 90% confidence); steady-state V_PP >= 2.62 V at t = 168h ensuring complete cell storage capacitor write retention; formal engineering approval from Foundry Quality Council and Systems Reliability Lead.
