# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Post-Stress Wordline Gate Dielectric Leakage & $V_{th}$ Shift Metrology

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP defines the metrology protocol for evaluating post-HTOL (High-Temperature Operating Life) wordline access transistor gate dielectric degradation. It measures wordline gate oxide leakage current ($I_{g\_leak}$) and access transistor threshold voltage shift ($\Delta V_{th}$) on packaged 180nm open-source DRAM dies following accelerated dynamic thermal-voltage burn-in with $V_{PP}$ overdrive stress.

---

### 2. Device Under Test (DUT) Physical Architecture & Baseline Parameters
- **Access Transistor Geometry**: NMOS enhancement device, channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, channel width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
- **Gate Dielectric**: Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation, physical thickness $T_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$.
- **Nominal Operating Voltages**: Core $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$; boosted wordline overdrive voltage $V_{PP} = 2.5\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$.
- **Baseline Threshold Voltage ($V_{th0}$)**: $0.5\text{ V}\text{ to }0.7\text{ V}$ (nominal $\sim 0.6\text{ V}$).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Measurement Procedure

```text
[HTOL Unload & Cool-Down] ──> [ATE / SMU Docking] ──> [Gate Dielectric Leakage Test] ──> [Access Transistor Id-Vg & Vth Extr.] ──> [Data Logging & Pass/Fail]
```

#### Step 1: Post-Stress Chamber Discharge & Thermal Stabilization
1. Following completion of HTOL dynamic stress cycling (overdrive stress $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$), ramp the burn-in chamber down to ambient test temperature ($25^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$) under active dry $N_2$ purge.
2. Transfer DUTs to the precision Automated Test Equipment (ATE) parametric test fixture or Keithley 4200-SCS / Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer.
3. Establish Kelvin 4-wire connections to selected wordline test structures (Scribe Line Test Structures / addressable Wordline Test Modes) and common ground/substrate terminals.

#### Step 2: Wordline Gate Dielectric Leakage Current ($I_{g\_leak}$) Sweep
1. Ground all source/drain diffusion regions (Bitlines and Storage Node plates tied to $0\text{ V}$) and substrate ($V_{sub} = 0\text{ V}$).
2. Configure the High-Resolution Source-Monitor Unit (HRSMU) on the Wordline Gate terminal:
   - Voltage sweep range: $V_{WL} = 0\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$ (spanning up to maximum operating $V_{PP}$).
   - Step size: $50\text{ mV}$, integration time: Medium/Long (PLC $\ge 1$).
   - Current measurement compliance limit: $10\text{ }\mu\text{A}$ (to protect against catastrophic dielectric rupture).
3. Record the gate tunneling/leakage current at $V_{WL} = 2.8\text{ V}$ (peak $V_{PP}$ operating point). Ensure per-cell equivalent gate oxide leakage is evaluated across the wordline bank array.

#### Step 3: Access Transistor Transfer Characteristics ($I_D\text{--}V_G$) & $V_{th}$ Extraction
1. Apply drain-to-source bias across the access transistor: Set $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$ (linear regime) with substrate bias $V_{sub} = 0\text{ V}$.
2. Sweep gate voltage ($V_{GS} = V_{WL}$) from $0\text{ V}$ to $1.8\text{ V}$ ($V_{DD}$) with a step size of $10\text{ mV}$.
3. Extract post-stress threshold voltage $V_{th\_post}$ using the constant-current extraction method:
   $$V_{th} = V_{GS} \quad \text{at} \quad I_D = 100\text{ nA} \times \left(\frac{W}{L}\right) = 100\text{ nA} \times \left(\frac{220\text{ nm}}{180\text{ nm}}\right) \approx 122.2\text{ nA}$$
4. Alternatively, extract $V_{th}$ via maximum transconductance linear extrapolation ($G_{m\_max}$ slope intercept minus $V_{DS}/2$).
5. Compute the net threshold voltage shift:
   $$\Delta V_{th} = |V_{th\_post} - V_{th0}|$$

#### Step 4: High-Temperature (85°C) Sub-Threshold & Total Off-State Verification
1. Place the test chuck/fixture at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to verify junction and gate leakage under thermal operating ceiling.
2. Verify that off-state leakage ($V_{WL} = 0\text{ V}$, $V_{BL} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{cell} = 0\text{ V}$) meets cell retention leakage budget ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$).

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter | Test Condition | Physical Target Limit | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Max Wordline Overdrive Voltage Support ($V_{PP}$)** | Room Temp ($25^\circ\text{C}$), Gate Terminal | $\ge 2.5\text{ to }2.8$ | $\text{V}$ |
| **Wordline Transistor Threshold Voltage ($V_{th}$)** | Linear $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$, $25^\circ\text{C}$ | $0.5\text{ to }0.7$ | $\text{V}$ |
| **Threshold Voltage Degradation ($\Delta V_{th}$)** | Post-HTOL stress vs. Pre-stress ($25^\circ\text{C}$) | $\le 50$ (Max acceptable: $\le 80$) | $\text{mV}$ |
| **Per-Cell Off-State / Sub-threshold Leakage** | $85^\circ\text{C}$, $V_{WL} = 0\text{ V}$, Storage Node at $V_{DD}$ | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ |

---

### 5. Context Sources & Literature Citations
- **Source 1: High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**
  - *Citations*: Access transistor baseline $V_{th} \sim 0.5\text{ V to }0.7\text{ V}$; $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$; required wordline overdrive $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{overdrive} \ge 2.5\text{ V to }2.8\text{ V}$ to prevent write threshold voltage loss ($V_{DD} - V_{th}$).
- **Source 2: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Citations*: Access transistor unit geometry $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$; cell leakage current target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source 3: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *Citations*: Gate dielectric physical specification — thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness; wordline pitch $360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-HTOL wordline stress metrology must decouple interconnect thermal relaxation from true intrinsic oxide degradation; testing within the ATE socket at room temperature immediately following 125°C/140°C thermal pull requires tightly synchronized kelvin sensing down to 10 fA resolution to isolate array parasitic path leakage from access transistor gate dielectric breakdown.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm access transistors with tox ~3.5 nm SiO2 subjected to V_PP overdrive (typically 2.8V to 3.3V on 1.8V nominal core), positive bias temperature instability (PBTI) and hot-carrier/FN tunneling injection induce fixed oxide charge (N_ot) and interface trap generation (N_it). The threshold voltage shift (delta V_th) must not exceed 50 mV, and gate-to-channel/source-drain leakage I_gss must remain strictly below 1 fA/cell at nominal read condition to avoid draining the 28 fF cell capacitance below the minimum refresh budget.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Parametric test sockets and fine-pitch probe cards rated for low-leakage triaxial Kelvin routing and elevated thermal cycling are single-sourced with a 14-week lead time; socket contact degradation (pogo pin oxidation) during extended HTOL burn-in test cycles can introduce false contact resistance and pseudo-leakage signatures if preventive refurbishment cycles are omitted.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Ensure testing timelines allow completion of all 1,000-hour HTOL post-read points within JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD47 qualification windows without exceeding the Q-time limit between chamber unload and electrical parametric characterization, which would otherwise invalidate kinetic recovery tracking.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) of the 3.5 nm wordline gate oxide under elevated V_PP overdrive stress causing catastrophically elevated wordline-to-substrate gate leakage (>100 pA/cell).
1. Interface state generation (Delta N_it) and electron trapping causing excessive positive threshold voltage shift (Delta V_th > 65 mV), resulting in under-drive of the 180nm access transistor and incomplete bitline-to-cell charge transfer during active refresh.
1. Stress-Induced Leakage Current (SILC) at low electric fields (V_WL = 1.6V to 1.8V), accelerating cell charge degradation during standby cycles.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-3-3-01` | **Post-HTOL Wordline Access Gate Dielectric Leakage (I_gss) Test** | Advantest T5588 / Teradyne UltraFLEX ATE with Ultra-Low-Current High-Resolution Parametric Measurement Unit (DC-HR-PMU), triaxial cabling, and zero-insertion-force (ZIF) burn-in loadboard socket. | 1. Force V_BB = -0.5V, V_BL = 0V, V_SL = 0V on selected sector test structure. 2. Sweep Wordline voltage (V_WL) from 0.0V to 3.0V in 50 mV steps with 20 ms integration aperture per step using triaxial guarded Kelvin channel. 3. Record gate leakage current I_gss at nominal operating overdrive (V_WL = 2.5V) and maximum stress condition (V_WL = 3.0V). 4. Repeat across all 512 wordlines within the designated test block. | `Total cumulative wordline leakage I_gss <= 1.0 fA per individual access gate (normalized sector leakage <= 512 fA across 512-cell segment) at V_WL = 2.5V, T = 25°C. Any single hard breakdown (I_gss > 10 nA) constitutes immediate failure.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-1-3-3-02` | **Post-Stress Threshold Voltage Shift (Delta V_th) Transconductance Extraction** | Precision Parametric Device Analyzer (Keysight B1500A integrated with ATE test head) utilizing Source Monitor Units (SMUs) with 0.1 fA / 0.5 uV measurement resolution. | 1. Set access transistor drain bias V_ds = 50 mV (linear regime) and V_sub = -0.5V. 2. Sweep gate voltage V_gs from 0.0V to 1.8V in 10 mV increments; measure linear drain current I_ds. 3. Calculate transconductance g_m = dI_ds / dV_gs and extract linear threshold voltage V_th using linear extrapolation method at maximum g_m point. 4. Compute Delta V_th = V_th(post-HTOL) - V_th(pre-stress). | `Absolute threshold voltage shift |Delta V_th| <= 40 mV relative to pre-stress baseline. Maximum transconductance degradation Delta g_m / g_m0 <= 10% across all sampled access devices.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating heat-resistant silicone gloves (rated to 200°C for chamber handling), EN 166 compliant anti-fog UV/impact safety spectacles, ESD-safe dissipative cleanroom lab coat (Class 100 / ISO 5 compatible), Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, dual-layer)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For thermal burns: Immediately immerse affected area in clean, cold running water for minimum 15 minutes; do not apply salves; apply sterile burn dressing and seek medical attention. For IPA exposure: Inhalation - move to fresh air; Eye contact - flush eyes with isotonic saline or eyewash for 15 minutes; Skin contact - wash thoroughly with soap and water.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber unload zone must maintain dedicated local point-exhaust ventilation providing >= 100 FPM face velocity to disperse residual organic vapors and prevent thermal accumulation; continuous room O2 depletion monitors required near high-volume N2 purge stations.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and socket cleaning effluents must be segregated into closed, grounded, flame-proof hazardous solvent collection bins with dedicated flammability labeling in compliance with EPA/OSHA solvent disposal regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Nitrogen (compressed gas)** | `7727-37-9` | High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: DUT packages removed from 125°C HTOL chamber, free from socket pin solder transfer or carbonized organic burn-in residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Post-metrology test pins cleaned, dry, and stored in desiccated sealed dry-pack bags with humidity indicator cards (HIC < 10% RH).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time allows room-temperature hydrogen passivation and interface state trap relaxation (recovery effect), which artifically masks up to 35% of true HTOL-induced V_th shift and leads to false qualification acceptance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full electrical characterization report and parameter distribution files confirming that 180nm DRAM access transistor gate oxide meets JEDEC JESD47/JESD22-A108 lifetime requirements with no premature TDDB, SILC, or intolerable V_th drift after 1,000 hours of dynamic HTOL stress.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `HTOL_1000HR_WORDLINE_LEAKAGE_DISTRIBUTION.csv`
- [ ] `POST_STRESS_VTH_SHIFT_RELIABILITY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `WL_GATE_OXIDE_WEIBULL_TDDB_FIT.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-stress single-cell gate dielectric leakage at nominal overdrive bias** | `0.85 fA/cell` | +0.15 fA/cell | High-resolution triaxial Kelvin DC-HR-PMU measurement at V_WL = 2.5V, T = 25°C |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-HTOL access transistor threshold voltage shift magnitude** | `22.5 mV` | ±17.5 mV | Maximum-transconductance linear extrapolation from I_ds-V_gs transfer curves at V_ds = 50 mV |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-stress population Weibull TDDB projected time-to-fail (TTF) at 1.1x V_PP overdrive and 85°C** | `100000 hours` | >= 87600 hours | Maximum-likelihood Weibull parameter estimation and electric field acceleration factor (E-model) extrapolation |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of tested DUT units pass gate leakage limit (<= 1.0 fA/cell) and Delta V_th shift (<= 40 mV) with zero hard oxide dielectric breakdowns, accompanied by signed review from Lead Reliability Engineer and Foundry PDK Quality Representative.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Continuous 125°C Dynamic High-Voltage Accelerated Burn-in Chamber Stress Execution

**Category**: Reliability Testing | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Maintaining continuous 125°C chamber ambient with high-density dynamic driver boards requires active per-slot thermal monitoring. For 180nm CMOS DRAM operating at elevated core voltage (V_INT = 2.2V vs nominal 1.8V) and peripheral voltage (VDDQ = 2.0V), dynamic switching power dissipation (~350 mW/DUT) inside a multi-board burn-in chamber containing up to 1,024 DUTs generates an aggregate thermal load exceeding 350 W. Convective air velocity must be maintained at >= 2.5 m/s across BIB (Burn-In Board) slots to prevent local hot-spotting beyond Tj = 135°C, which would induce thermal runaway or unrepresentative junction degradation exceeding JESD22-A108 requirements.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Dynamic High-Voltage Stress (DHVS) at 125°C accelerates time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) of the 180nm gate dielectric (nominal tox = 4.0 nm for core, 7.0 nm for I/O) and bitline-to-substrate junction leakage via the Arrhenius and E-model field acceleration models. The vector sequence executed during dynamic burn-in must toggle wordlines, bitlines, and sense amplifiers at 50 MHz using pseudo-random marching patterns (e.g., March C-) to ensure uniform electric field polarity across cell capacitors and access transistor gate oxides without latchup induction. Power delivery networks on polyimide BIBs must maintain ripple < 35 mV under continuous dynamic toggling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: N/A
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The 1000-hour dynamic burn-in campaign (interim readouts at 48h, 168h, 500h, and 1000h) represents the pacing critical path item for JEDEC qualification of the 180nm DRAM MPW run. Chamber downtime or unexpected board-level power supply trips directly jeopardize the post-burn-in wafer sort and packaging timeline. A dual-redundant N+1 DC power delivery subsystem and automated chamber temperature/current telemetry logging every 60 seconds are mandatory to avoid invalidating cumulative stress hours.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dynamic thermal runaway induced by localized airflow starvation leading to DUT junction temperature exceeding Tj = 145°C and catastrophic package delamination or bond-wire reflow.
1. Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) or BTI (Bias Temperature Instability) causing catastrophic gate puncture in row-decoder pass gates under continuous 2.2V accelerated overdrive at 125°C.
1. Burn-in socket pin contact resistance escalation (> 1.5 Ohms) due to solder tin-lead intermetallic migration and Au-plating degradation at 125°C, inducing false dynamic functional read failures.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-01` | **Continuous 125°C Dynamic Voltage Stress (DVS) In-Situ Chamber Telemetry and Stability Verification** | Burn-In System Chamber with integrated multichannel per-slot thermal sensors (Class A Pt100 RTDs), Keysight N6705C DC Power Analyzer with precision 180nm DUT power feeds, Agilent 34970A Data Acquisition Unit, calibrated Type-T thermocouple arrays mapped to 16 reference DUT lids. | 1. Ramp chamber temperature from 25°C ambient to 125°C at a controlled slew rate of 2.0°C/minute with continuous N2 purge at 5 SLPM.\n2. Apply continuous high-voltage overdrive (VDD_core = 2.20V, VDDQ = 2.00V) under dynamic toggle pattern once chamber achieves 125.0°C isothermal flat condition.\n3. Continuously execute dynamic pattern cycling for 168 hours non-stop (Interim Readout 1).\n4. Record per-slot temperature, dynamic supply current (IDD1/IDD4), and supply voltage ripple across all active channels at 30-second sampling intervals.\n5. Monitor for any overcurrent latchup events (> 150 mA per DUT) or temperature excursion (> 128.0°C). | `Chamber ambient temperature must hold at 125.0°C ± 1.5°C across all zones for 100% of the 168-hour run. Dynamic supply current per DUT must stay within 45.0 mA ± 5.0 mA without single-event latchup or thermal excursion. 0 DUT hardware dropouts allowed during stress execution.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-02` | **Post-Stress Retention Time and Gate Dielectric Breakdown Screening on Automated Test Equipment** | Advantest T5588 or Teradyne UltraFLEX High-Speed Memory ATE with 200 MHz JEDEC DDR test capability, Keithley 2450 SourceMeter for sub-picoampere gate leakage characterization, thermal control chuck set to 85°C. | 1. critics.systems_engineer: Maintaining continuous 125°C chamber ambient with high-density dynamic driver boards requires active per-slot thermal monitoring. For 180nm CMOS DRAM operating at elevated core voltage (V_INT = 2.2V vs nominal 1.8V) and peripheral voltage (VDDQ = 2.0V), dynamic switching power dissipation (~350 mW/DUT) inside a multi-board burn-in chamber containing up to 1,024 DUTs generates an aggregate thermal load exceeding 350 W. Convective air velocity must be maintained at >= 2.5 m/s across BIB (Burn-In Board) slots to prevent local hot-spotting beyond Tj = 135°C, which would induce thermal runaway or unrepresentative junction degradation exceeding JESD22-A108 requirements.
critics.domain_expert: Dynamic High-Voltage Stress (DHVS) at 125°C accelerates time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) of the 180nm gate dielectric (nominal tox = 4.0 nm for core, 7.0 nm for I/O) and bitline-to-substrate junction leakage via the Arrhenius and E-model field acceleration models. The vector sequence executed during dynamic burn-in must toggle wordlines, bitlines, and sense amplifiers at 50 MHz using pseudo-random marching patterns (e.g., March C-) to ensure uniform electric field polarity across cell capacitors and access transistor gate oxides without latchup induction. Power delivery networks on polyimide BIBs must maintain ripple < 35 mV under continuous dynamic toggling.
critics.domain_chain: Burn-in sockets rated for continuous 150°C operation using BeCu/Au-plated spring probes face severe lead times and contact resistance (Cres) degradation after 500 hours of 125°C thermal cycling. Polyimide-glass high-Tg (Tg > 260°C) burn-in boards (BIBs) with edge fingers require hard electrolytic gold plating (minimum 50 micro-inches Au over 150 micro-inches Ni) to resist oxidation and fretting corrosion during 1000-hour HTOL campaigns. Sourcing specialized high-temperature driver pin cards and certified ceramic 0.1 uF decoupling capacitors rated for 150°C/50V poses supply chain constraints across domestic VN testing infrastructure.
critics.laya_pm: The 1000-hour dynamic burn-in campaign (interim readouts at 48h, 168h, 500h, and 1000h) represents the pacing critical path item for JEDEC qualification of the 180nm DRAM MPW run. Chamber downtime or unexpected board-level power supply trips directly jeopardize the post-burn-in wafer sort and packaging timeline. A dual-redundant N+1 DC power delivery subsystem and automated chamber temperature/current telemetry logging every 60 seconds are mandatory to avoid invalidating cumulative stress hours.
critical_failure_modes: Dynamic thermal runaway induced by localized airflow starvation leading to DUT junction temperature exceeding Tj = 145°C and catastrophic package delamination or bond-wire reflow.

Burn-in socket pin contact resistance escalation (> 1.5 Ohms) due to solder tin-lead intermetallic migration and Au-plating degradation at 125°C, inducing false dynamic functional read failures.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: HTOL Burn-in Board (BIB) Dynamic Vector Loading and In-Situ Thermal Calibration

**Category**: Reliability & Qualification | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dynamic vector loading across high-density HTOL Burn-in Boards (BIB) operating at 125°C introduces severe transmission-line reflections, ground bounce, and signal attenuation across long polyimide/FR-4 trace topologies. The driver backplane must employ active impedance matching, controlled slew rates, and localized decoupling capacitors rated for continuous 150°C endurance to avoid false clock glitches or vector corruptions during stress.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Thermal calibration of the BIB requires multi-point in-situ sensing directly on package cases and test sockets. Die self-heating during high-voltage toggle patterns (Vdd = 2.2V vs nominal 1.8V for 180nm DRAM) induces localized thermal gradients exceeding chamber ambient setpoints. Multi-zone PID feedback loops with calibrated Type-K/RTD sensors must compensate for localized airflow convective boundary layer variations to maintain junction temperatures (Tj) within JEDEC JESD22-A108 standards (125°C ± 3°C).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-temperature test sockets (e.g., polyetherimide/Torlon with BeCu or Au/Ni-plated pogo pins) rated for >1,000 hours at 150°C represent severe single-source supply chain bottlenecks with extended lead times. Thermal degradation of contact spring tension and contact oxidation will cause intermittent pin opens during extended HTOL burn-in runs if socket PM replacement cycles are not strictly budgeted.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Burn-in board fabrication, vector validation, and thermal profile characterization sit on the critical path prior to the 1,000-hour HTOL qualification signoff. Vector verification on unpopulated and populated dummy boards must run in parallel with oven thermocouple profile mapping to avoid gate review slippage for final product qualification.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway induced by excessive dynamic switching current on marginal DRAM bitcells, leading to socket contact melting or package thermal decomposition.
1. Vector clock jitter or signal attenuation causing false functional freeze (stuck-at state) where DUTs stop toggling internal charge pumps and bitlines, invalidating dynamic accelerated stress.
1. Socket spring fatigue and contact resistance escalation (>2 Ohms) causing localized IR drops and false functional failures during in-situ reads.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-1-01` | **HTOL Dynamic Vector Integrity and In-Situ Toggle Rate Verification** | High-bandwidth differential oscilloscope (1 GHz, 5 GS/s), active differential probe with high-temp micro-tips (150°C rated), automated vector capture logic analyzer. | 1. Power up BIB power supplies and initiate dynamic DRAM vector generation across all 64 DUT channels simultaneously. 2. Connect high-temp differential probe to DUT socket pin monitoring Master Clock (CLK), Row Address Strobe (/RAS), Column Address Strobe (/CAS), and dynamic bitline toggling signals at the furthest board boundary slot. 3. Measure clock eye diagram, rise/fall times (10%-90%), overshoot/undershoot, and duty cycle distortion across continuous 1-hour operation. 4. Verify DUT toggling status and power rail transient noise ripple using synchronous signal capture. | `Vector toggle frequency must maintain 50.0 MHz ± 0.5 MHz; signal rise/fall times <= 3.5 ns; clock duty cycle between 45% and 55%; peak-to-peak VDD supply rail ripple <= 85 mV; zero dropped vector cycles or logic freeze states over 60 minutes.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-1-02` | **BIB Multi-Zone In-Situ Case Thermal Uniformity and Closed-Loop Stability** | Fluke 2638A Hydra Series III Data Acquisition System with 32-channel calibrated Type-K fine-wire thermocouples (Class 1 tolerance ±1.1°C), thermal imaging camera with chamber optical port. | 1. Ramp chamber from 25°C to 125°C at controlled ramp rate of 2.0°C/min under dry nitrogen purge. 2. Allow chamber and populated BIB to dwell at 125.0°C for 120 minutes with dynamic DRAM toggling enabled. 3. Log case temperature (Tc) across all 32 channels at 10-second sampling intervals. 4. Calculate steady-state spatial temperature gradient across all DUT slots and temporal standard deviation over a 60-minute window. | `Package case temperatures across all monitored positions must stabilize within 125.0°C ± 3.0°C; slot-to-slot spatial thermal delta <= 4.0°C; temporal thermal fluctuation on any individual sensor <= ±0.8°C over 60 minutes.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 3 thermal-insulating Kevlar safety gloves (rated for 250°C continuous contact), Full-face polycarbonate heat-resistant safety shield (ANSI Z87.1 approved), High-temperature safety lab coat (flame-retardant Nomex/aramid fabric), ESD-safe safety shoes with heat-resistant vulcanized soles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately flush burned epidermal area with cool, clean, potable water for at least 15-20 minutes; do not apply ice directly; apply sterile burn dressing and seek immediate medical attention. Epoxy/Chemical Contact: Flush eyes with isotonic saline or eyewash station for 15 minutes; wash skin thoroughly with non-abrasive soap and water. Inhalation of chamber off-gas: Evacuate person to fresh air; administer oxygen if respiratory distress occurs.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber exhaust must be ducted directly to dedicated facility VOC/acid scrubbed exhaust system operating at >= 150 CFM continuous extraction to capture outgassed conformal coatings, flux, or board polyimide decomposition products during 125°C operation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Cured epoxy and spent thermal interface materials must be disposed of as hazardous solid chemical waste in accordance with EPA/RCRA regulations. Spent cleaning solvents must be collected in closed, grounded conductive flammable-waste drums.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Thermally Conductive Epoxy Part A (Bisphenol-A Diglycidyl Ether)** | `25068-38-6` | Technical Grade | `60-80% w/w` |
| **High-Temp Solder Flux Residue Cleaner (Isopropyl Alcohol)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9% v/v` |
| **Compressed Gaseous Nitrogen (Dry Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 | `99.999% vol` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Clean, bake-degassed (125°C for 24h to prevent delamination/popcorning), dry JEDEC tray-loaded packaged DRAM devices with zero pin oxidation and coplanarity <= 0.08 mm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Post-stress thermally stabilized packaged units with socket contact marks verified to have zero excessive pin gouging, zero solder reflow leakage, and lead surface wetting/resistance intact.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into plastic package mold compound leading to internal popcorn cracking, die-attach delamination, or rapid pad oxidation causing high-resistance open circuits during subsequent 125°C burn-in.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful commissioning and qualification of the 180nm DRAM HTOL Burn-in Board, verifying 100% vector generation integrity across 64 DUT channels at 50 MHz under 2.2V core bias, alongside documented multi-zone closed-loop thermal stability at 125°C ± 3°C.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `HTOL_BIB_Dynamic_Vector_Timing_Validation_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `HTOL_BIB_32Ch_Thermal_Mapping_Calibration_Data.csv`
- [ ] `DUT_Socket_Contact_Resistance_Pre_Post_HTOL.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **DUT clock and dynamic vector pin toggle frequency across all populated slots** | `50.0 MHz` | ±1.0% | Synchronous 1 GHz logic analyzer edge timestamping over 3600 consecutive seconds |
| `ASSERT-02` | **DUT package case temperature uniformity during dynamic stress at 125°C oven ambient** | `125.0°C` | ±3.0°C | Multi-channel continuous data logging via 32 calibrated Type-K thermocouples over 120 minutes |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Burn-in board power distribution network (VDD) transient peak-to-peak ripple under full vector toggle** | `65.0 mV` | <= 85.0 mV max | Active differential probe oscilloscope measurement directly at socket decoupling capacitor terminals |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal acceptance by Reliability Engineering and Quality Operations confirming: (1) 100% vector delivery fidelity without logic freeze across 64 slots for >24 consecutive dry-run hours; (2) In-situ thermal profiling showing zero DUT positions exceeding 128.0°C or falling below 122.0°C; and (3) Complete signoff on BIB electrical and mechanical safety interlocks.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## HTOL Burn-in Board (BIB) Dynamic Driver Channel Wiring & Vector Stimulus Mapping
**Document ID:** `SOP-HTOL-BIB-DRV-001`  
**Node:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS Open-Source DRAM)  
**Classification:** Reliability & Qualification / HTOL Dynamic Stress  

---

### 1. Architectural Flowchart & System Interconnect

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  ATE Vector Generator  │
│    / Pattern Source    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    BIB Driver Edge     │
│  Backplane Interface   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Active Driver      │
│    Buffers & Series    │
│   Damping Resistors    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   DUT Sockets Array:   │
│    Clock, Command,     │
│    Address, DQ/DQS     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    In-Situ Loopback    │
│  Sense & Calibration   │
│          Grid          │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Backplane Interface & Power Rail Configuration:**
   - Terminate ATE driver edge feeds into the high-temperature Polyimide/FR-4 BIB backplane interface connector.
   - Wire core nominal/stress supply rails: set $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$ to DUT socket power rings, and configure the high-voltage boost sense monitor to trace the on-chip Dickson charge pump wordline supply reaching $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\text{ V}$ to $2.8\text{ V}$ ($V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{overdrive}$, where NMOS access transistor $V_{th} \sim 0.5\text{ V}$ to $0.7\text{ V}$).

2. **Driver Channel Impedance Matching & Signal Group Wiring:**
   - Wire high-speed differential clock lines (`CLK_T` / `CLK_C`) through length-matched microstrip traces ($50\ \Omega \pm 10\%$) with series damping resistors at the driver outputs to eliminate overshoot/undershoot reflections.
   - Map Command (`/CS`, `/RAS`, `/CAS`, `/WE`) and Address (`A[0:N]`, `BA[0:M]`) channels in fly-by or balanced star topologies to all DUT sockets, ensuring uniform setup and hold time margins.
   - Connect bi-directional Data (`DQ[0:15]`, `DQS`, `DM`) channels with controlled stub lengths to preserve edge rates during high-temperature burn-in chamber stress.

3. **Dynamic Vector Stimulus Mapping & Clock Generation:**
   - Map two-phase non-overlapping clock pulses ($\Phi_1$, $\Phi_2$) at frequencies of $20\text{ MHz}$ to $50\text{ MHz}$ directly stimulating the on-chip Dickson 4-stage charge pump oscillator network (equipped with $20\text{ pF}$ to $50\text{ pF}$ flying capacitors) to maintain continuous charge transfer and dielectric stress across gate oxides.
   - Program write/read alternating checkerboard (`0xAA55`), walking one/zero, and marching patterns into the ATE vector pattern sequencer to switch bitlines and exercise the access transistors ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Ensure dynamic stimulus toggles the stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) storage nodes with minimum cell capacitance target $C_{cell} = 28\text{ fF}$ across ONO/high-$\kappa$ dielectrics.

4. **In-Situ Loopback Calibration & Diagnostic Verification:**
   - Route diagnostic loopback channels from the farthest socket column to the BIB monitor test points.
   - Verify skew, signal integrity, and voltage drops across active channels before chamber insertion.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
C_cell Target (fF)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                  │▒▒                                  │
     V_th Loss (V)┤▒▒                                  │
    V_PP Boost (V)┤▓▓▓▓▓                               │
                  │▓▓▓▓▓                               │
   V_DD Stress (V)┤███                                 │
                  │███                                 │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                   0        7       14      21       28 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Nominal Value | Acceptance Window / Tolerance | Units | Verification Point |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dickson Pump Overdrive Voltage ($V_{PP}$)** | $2.50$ to $2.80$ | $\ge 2.50$ ($V_{th} \sim 0.50$ to $0.70$) | $\text{V}$ | BIB high-voltage monitor node |
| **Driver Oscillator Clock Frequency ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$)** | $20.0$ to $50.0$ | $20.0 \text{ to } 50.0 \pm 1.0\%$ | $\text{MHz}$ | Clock driver channel termination |
| **Cell Stack Storage Capacitance ($C_{cell}$)** | $28.0$ | $\ge 28.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | In-situ impedance/CV bridge measurement |
| **Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage ($I_{leak}$ @ 85°C ref)** | $< 1.0$ | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Parametric leakage monitor pin |

---

### 4. Sources Cited

- **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture:** NMOS pass transistor dimensions, threshold voltage $V_{th} \sim 0.5\text{ V}$ to $0.7\text{ V}$, wordline overdrive target $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\text{ V}$ to $2.8\text{ V}$, 4-stage charge pump topology with $C_{pump} = 20\text{ pF}$ to $50\text{ pF}$, two-phase clocks $\Phi_1, \Phi_2$ at $20\text{ MHz}$ to $50\text{ MHz}$.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Access transistor geometry $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, stacked capacitor over bitline (COB), minimum cell capacitance budget $28\text{ fF}$, leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at 85°C.
- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation:** Thermal baseline control and thermal ramp rate considerations.

---

> [!NOTE]
> Micro-knowledge entry for this SOP has been persisted in [`docs/knowledge/htol_bib_driver_channel_wiring_sop.md`](./docs/knowledge/htol_bib_driver_channel_wiring_sop.md) per local agent documentation protocols.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Routing high-density driver channels across a multi-layer polyimide Burn-in Board (BIB) with up to 128 DUT sockets introduces severe transmission-line reflections, skin-effect losses, and crosstalk if trace impedance is not strictly held to 50 Ω ± 5% at 125°C. Uncontrolled channel skews (> 2.5 ns) between differential command/clock pairs (CLK/nCLK) will cause false command decodes and asynchronous row-hammer false triggers, corrupting stress vector determinism across DUT columns.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Dynamic HTOL for 180nm DRAM requires simultaneous activation of the on-chip 4-stage Dickson VPP charge pump (2.5V-2.8V boost for NMOS pass gate V_th overdrive) and full-rail cross-coupled sense-amp restoration. Over-stressing the array via continuous ACTIVATE-PRECHARGE cycles without enforcing minimum t_RAS (45 ns) and t_RP (15 ns) will cause thermal runaway on on-chip Dickson flying capacitors and sense amp PMOS pull-up trees, masking intrinsic gate-oxide dielectric breakdown (TDDB) under localized electromigration artifacts.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-Tg (> 250°C) polyimide laminate BIBs with gold-plated beryllium copper (BeCu) or Kelvin pogo-pin contactor sockets face 12-14 week fabrication lead times and supply constraints. Sockets degrading under continuous 125°C thermal cycling and 1.8V-2.8V multi-voltage bias will increase contact resistance from 50 mΩ to > 2 Ω, distorting driver signal integrity and prematurely invalidating long-duration 1000-hour JESD22-A108 HTOL qualifications.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Vector stimulus mapping must reconcile ATE algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG) channel limitations against the 128-DUT BIB parallel wiring grid. Failure to validate signal integrity with active TDR and eye-diagram characterization prior to chamber load risks aborting the 1000-hour HTOL run at the 168-hour readout milestone, resulting in severe schedule slippage and re-spin costs exceeding $45,000.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. In-situ ground bounce and VDD droop (> 250 mV) induced by synchronous multi-DUT row activation leading to sense amplifier latch failure and premature Dickson charge pump oscillator stall.
1. High-temperature trace degradation and dielectric breakdown on BIB polyimide layers causing short-circuit between adjacent 2.8V VPP bias tracks and 1.8V VDD logic lines.
1. Contact pin oxidation and spring fatigue in 125°C socket matrix causing intermittent clock skew, invalidating command/address hold time (t_IH) and masking bitline retention decay.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-1-1-01` | **BIB Dynamic Driver Signal Integrity, Eye Margin, and Channel Skew Verification at 125°C** | Keysight Infiniium 4-channel 4 GHz Oscilloscope, 50-ohm active differential probes, High-temperature TDR module, Fluke Calibrated Thermal Chamber | 1. Dock high-speed oscilloscope differential probes at the furthest corner socket (Socket #128) and center socket (Socket #64) across CLK, nCLK, ADDR[0:11], and CAS lines. 2. Measure rise time (10%-90%), fall time, overshoot, and undershoot under maximum driver capacitive loading. 3. Measure differential clock-to-command skew and eye height/width over 100,000 continuous pattern cycles. 4. Perform TDR measurement along the longest driver bus trace to extract characteristic impedance and reflection coefficient. | `Differential clock-to-command/address skew <= 1.20 ns; trace characteristic impedance = 50.0 Ω ± 2.5 Ω; signal eye height >= 1.25 V at 1.8V VDD rail; overshoot/undershoot <= 150 mV above VDD or below VSS; rise/fall times between 1.2 ns and 2.8 ns.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-1-1-02` | **In-Situ Dynamic VDD/VPP Power Distribution Network (PDN) Droop and Ground Bounce Stress Mapping** | Keithley 2230G-30-1 Programmable Multi-Channel DC Power Supply, Tektronix Current Probes, Keysight 8-channel Digital Storage Oscilloscope with FFT analysis | 1. Program ALPG to trigger simultaneous continuous burst read/write refresh cycles across all 128 sockets to generate maximum transient dI/dt. 2. Monitor VDD and VPP power plane ripple and localized ground rail potential at decoupled socket clusters using 50-ohm AC-coupled high-bandwidth inputs. 3. Execute 1,000,000 Dickson charge pump activation cycles and sense amplifier restoration sequences. 4. Measure peak-to-peak voltage noise, transient droop duration, and high-frequency resonance. | `Transient VDD droop <= 85 mV (<= 4.3% of nominal 1.95V stress bias); VPP rail droop <= 110 mV during Dickson pump 50 MHz oscillation bursts; ground bounce peak-to-peak amplitude <= 60 mV; no spurious DUT reset or unrecoverable pattern sync dropouts across 10^7 stress vectors.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal safety gloves rated for >= 200°C contact (EN 407 Level 3), High-temperature polyimide safety face shield and UV/thermal safety glasses (ANSI Z87.1), ESD-safe flame-resistant lab coat (NFPA 70E compliant), Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (ASTM D6319) for socket contact cleaner solvent handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn exposure: Immediately flood burned skin with cool, clean water for at least 15-20 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing and seek emergency medical evaluation. Solvent splash: Rinse affected eyes or skin with sterile eyewash/shower for 15 minutes minimum; remove contaminated clothing immediately; if inhaled, move victim to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber exhaust must be ducted directly to dedicated facility chemical scrubbed exhaust (minimum face velocity 100 FPM / 0.51 m/s) to evacuate thermal outgassing volatiles from PCB resins and soldering fluxes; solvent degreasing bench requires localized laminar extraction hood.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA and solvent-wetted wipes must be sealed in airtight, grounded, conductive flammable-waste containers labeled per RCRA regulations; thermal socket cleaning residue disposed of through licensed industrial hazardous solvent reclamation protocol.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Electronic Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 | `99.9%` |
| **Polyimide Residue Degreaser (1-Methoxy-2-propanol)** | `107-98-2` | Electronic Grade | `>= 99.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: PDK-compliant packaged/socketed 180nm DRAM chips with immersion gold (ENIG) lead finish, vacuum-sealed in moisture barrier bags (MBB) with desiccant and HIC <= 10% RH, free of flux residue and cuprous oxidation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Stress-loaded BIB with gold-plated contactor pins inspected via optical profilometry for planar seating; pins free of carbonization, pinhead oxidation, or solder transfer after pre-stress thermal cycling.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom ambient queue time leads to atmospheric moisture adsorption and surface sulfurization/oxidation on socket contact fingers and IC package leads, causing contact resistance spikes (> 500 mΩ), localized arcing, false signal degradation, and pin burn-in during 125°C chamber energization.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed engineering qualification, dynamic driver channel trace routing, signal integrity validation, and algorithmic vector stimulus mapping for the 180nm DRAM HTOL Burn-in Board, ensuring uniform accelerated electrical stress at 125°C across all 128 DUT positions in strict accordance with JESD22-A108.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `BIB_Dynamic_Channel_Routing_and_Skew_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `HTOL_Vector_Mapping_and_PDN_Droop_Matrix.csv`
- [ ] `Contactor_Socket_Thermal_TDR_Profilometry.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum channel-to-channel driver trace propagation delay skew across all 128 DUT sockets at 125°C** | `950` | +/- 150 ps | High-bandwidth Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) and 4 GHz digital storage oscilloscope differential measurement |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Worst-case transient VDD supply rail droop across active sockets during synchronous burst access** | `45.0` | +/- 15.0 mV | In-situ calibrated active oscilloscope probe measurement during 50 MHz DDR march stress pattern execution at 125°C |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Dickson charge pump VPP over-voltage driver bias level under continuous 125°C dynamic stimulus** | `2.85` | +/- 0.05 V | Automated parametric measurement unit (PMU) Kelvin sensing across designated VPP test pads on sample monitored sockets |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 100% verification that all 128 BIB sockets maintain eye height >= 1.25V, trace skew <= 1.10 ns, and PDN droop <= 60 mV under full 50 MHz dynamic vector stimulus at 125°C over a continuous 4-hour pre-HTOL burn-in bake, accompanied by unanimous approval from Systems, Foundry Integration, and Reliability Council leads.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Density Polyimide BIB Socket Array & Multi-Zone Thermal Couple Calibration Harness
**Target Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN — Gen 3)  
**Execution Context:** HTOL Continuous 125°C Dynamic Accelerated Burn-in Stress & Qualification  
**Knowledge Document:** [`docs/knowledge/htol_polyimide_bib_thermal_calibration.md`](./docs/knowledge/htol_polyimide_bib_thermal_calibration.md)

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 1: Assembly &   │

│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘

│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘

            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 3: Multi-Zone   │
│  Calibration at 125C  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Test Socket Array & Package Mechanical Verification**:
   - Inspect packaged 180nm DRAM dies connected via 25 µm wire bonding to lead frame pins on 100 µm × 100 µm aluminum pads.
   - Verify sample lot wire bond pull force complies with **$\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$** per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011, ensuring failure occurs in the wire span rather than the bond interface.
   - Inspect die attach epoxy integrity (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 minutes): acoustic microscopy must verify void area under die is **$< 5\%$**, and thermal resistance **$R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$**.
   - Seat DUTs into the high-density polyimide Burn-in Board (BIB) socket matrix, ensuring full pin co-planarity and contact resistance stability.

2. **Harness & Multi-Zone Sensor Deployment**:
   - Divide the high-density polyimide BIB socket field into three discrete thermal monitoring zones: **Load Zone**, **Center Zone**, and **Source Zone** (counteracting convective air-flow end-losses).
   - Affix calibrated reference thermocouples into the socket harness across each designated zone in direct contact with package case tops.
   - Route harness signal lines through high-temperature polyimide channels to the external automated data acquisition interface.

3. **In-Situ 125°C PID Temperature Profile & Calibration**:
   - Transfer the instrumented BIB into the HTOL burn-in chamber. Ensure mechanical insertion ramp rate does not exceed **$< 50\text{ mm/minute}$** to prevent mechanical/thermal shock.
   - Initiate inert/carrier gas purge regulation via mass flow controllers (MFC) at **1 to 5 SLPM**.
   - Enable multi-loop digital PID temperature regulation. Ramp chamber to continuous accelerated stress setpoint of **$125^\circ\text{C}$**.
   - Measure steady-state zone temperatures across Load, Center, and Source regions. Tune PID loop offset trims until isothermal uniformity across the socket array achieves **$\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**.

4. **Continuous Dynamic HTOL Vector Stress Initialization**:
   - Apply continuous accelerated dynamic high-voltage patterns to the array while operating at $125^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Continuously record multi-zone thermocouple telemetry to detect local thermal hot spots or socket contact drift.

---

---

### Verified Context Citations
1. **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
   - Multi-zone heating to counteract convective end-losses.
   - Temperature uniformity target: **$\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**.
   - Mass flow controller (MFC) gas flow regulation: **$1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$**.
   - Mechanical ramp / insertion speed limit: **$< 50\text{ mm/minute}$**.
2. **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
   - Packaging bond pad dimensions: **$100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$**.
   - Wire diameter: **$25\ \mu\text{m}$**.
   - Minimum pull force: **$\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$** per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011.
   - Die attach cure & specs: Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ min}$; thermal resistance **$R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$**; acoustic void area **$< 5\%$**.
3. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - 180nm technology generation foundation (access transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, stacked capacitor over bitline topology).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The high-density polyimide Burn-In Board (BIB) socket matrix must interface with 180nm DRAM test vehicles subjected to continuous 125°C chamber stress at elevated VDD (2.2V vs nominal 1.8V). Polyimide core dielectric materials (Tg > 260°C) prevent warpage across the 24-layer PCB, but socket contact resistance drift (Rc) under thermal cycling can induce parasitic IR drops (>50 mV) along power delivery traces, causing non-uniform supply voltages across socket columns. The multi-zone thermocouple harness must decouple thermocouple cold-junction drift and RF noise coupling from dynamic clock/command test vector lines running at 133–200 MHz.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Under JEDEC JESD22-A108 HTOL conditions, dynamic toggling accelerates gate-oxide breakdown (TDDB) and hot carrier injection in 180nm DRAM cells. Contact pins (BeCu or Pd alloy with hard gold plating >= 30 uin) inside the polyimide burn-in sockets must maintain a contact normal force >= 25 gf per pin over 1,000 thermal stress hours at 125°C to avoid intermittent open faults or false retention failures. Calibration of the multi-zone thermocouple harness requires direct contact with representative dummy silicon packages equipped with embedded RTDs/diodes to correlate socket case temperatures (Tc) to junction temperatures (Tj = 125°C +/- 3°C across all board zones).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying custom polyimide BIB sockets with tight pitch for 180nm ceramic/QFN packages poses long lead times (12 to 16 weeks) from specialized suppliers like Enplas, Wells-CTI, or Plastronics. Multi-zone Type-K/Type-T thermocouple harnesses rated for Class 1 limits of error (+/- 0.5°C or 0.4%) with high-temperature PFA/Kapton insulation must be dual-sourced. Sockets must be selected as COTS or semi-custom modular arrays to prevent tapeout schedule bottlenecks during Gen 3 post-fab reliability qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement ('Buy' action) must lock vendor specifications for the socket array, high-temperature mounting hardware, and thermocouple calibration harness at least 8 weeks prior to packaging completion. Failure to pre-validate socket life (>500 actuation cycles) and multi-channel data logger calibration before post-wafer sort package delivery will stall the 1000-hour HTOL burn-in critical path, delaying Mil-Std-883 and JEDEC qualification signoff for the 180nm DRAM Foundation VN shuttle.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Contact pin spring relaxation and intermetallic gold-copper diffusion at 125°C leading to socket pin contact resistance exceeding 100 mOhm and intermittent VDD dips during burst read/write cycles.
1. Multi-zone thermocouple debonding or thermal decoupling from DUT heat spreaders, creating false low-temperature telemetry and chamber thermal runaway exceeding the 140°C maximum junction safety cutoff.
1. Polyimide BIB substrate hygroscopic moisture absorption leading to delamination or micro-crack dendritic leakage between adjacent high-voltage trace lines during 125°C bias ramp.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

Seat daisy-chain calibration packages in all socket positions across the polyimide BIB using calibrated torque driver (0.15 Nm). 2. Soak BIB in thermal chamber at 125°C for 60 minutes. 3. Execute automated 4-wire Kelvin DC resistance measurements across every I/O, VDD, and VSS pin contact (total 256 pins per socket bank). 4. Inject 150 mA steady-state test current across power pins and measure pin-to-board IR drop. 5. Post-thermal soak resistance shift Delta-Rc <= 15 mOhm across 100% of tested contacts. Max VDD/VSS IR drop across any socket pin <= 15 mV at 150 mA continuous draw.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-1-2-02` | **Multi-Zone Thermocouple Harness Spatial Uniformity & Steady-State Thermal Correlation** | Yokogawa WT5000 / MX100 32-Channel Data Acquisition System, Class 1 PFA-insulated Type-K fine-gage thermocouples (0.075 mm), calibrated RTD reference standard. | 1. Connect thermocouple harness leads to isothermal cold-junction reference block. 2. Ramp HTOL chamber from 25°C to 125°C at 2°C/min ramp rate with airflow velocity set to 1.5 m/s. 3. Hold steady state at 125°C for 180 minutes. 4. Record temperature data from all 9 zones continuously at 1 Hz sample rate. 5. Calculate spatial delta (T_max - T_min) across all 9 zones and thermal drift over a 60-minute steady-state window. | `Spatial temperature variation across all 9 BIB zones <= 3.0°C (range 123.5°C to 126.5°C). Total thermocouple harness measurement error relative to calibrated RTD reference <= +/- 0.5°C. Temperature drift over 60-minute steady state <= +/- 0.5°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protective Kevlar gloves rated for 150°C handling, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe dissipative lab coat with grounded wrist strap, Nitrile gloves (Mil-Spec 4-mil) for chemical contact-cleaner handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burns from heated BIB surfaces: Immediately cool affected area under cold running water for minimum 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; seek medical evaluation for second-degree burns. Eye exposure to solvent or thermal compound: Flush eyes with sterile eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Move victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing becomes labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber exhaust port routed directly to facility VOC ducting operating at minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s). Chamber room air exchange rate maintained at >= 10 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent isopropanol solvent wipes and residue collected in FM-approved, fire-rated self-closing steel waste cans. Silicone thermal paste and applicator swabs segregated into hazardous solids waste streams labeled according to local EPA/DoE chemical disposal guidelines.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (Electronics Grade)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Polyimide (Kapton HN polymer backing)** | `25038-81-7` | Technical Grade Film | `>99.0%` |
| **Silicone Polydimethylsiloxane (Thermal Grease Carrier)** | `63148-62-9` | High Temperature Grade | `30-50%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Gold-plated socket contact pins clean and free of particulate/organic contamination; BIB board dried and baked at 105°C to remove residual core humidity.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated sockets populated with packages, harness mechanically strain-relieved, contacts dry and free of silicone grease contamination, ready for HTOL chamber insertion.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive ambient humidity exposure leads to polyimide hygroscopic swelling, contact pin tarnish/oxidation, and substrate blistering/delamination during high-ramp 125°C chamber activation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical procurement, incoming inspection, electrical 4-wire Kelvin mapping, and multi-zone thermal harness calibration of the high-density polyimide burn-in board socket array for 180nm DRAM Gen 3 JEDEC HTOL life testing.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `BIB_Socket_Kelvin_Resistance_Mapping_Report.csv`
- [ ] `MultiZone_Thermocouple_125C_Calibration_Cert.pdf`
- [ ] `BIB_Assembly_Thermal_Uniformity_Thermograph.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum 4-wire socket pin contact resistance across all arrayed locations under 125°C equilibrium** | `35` | <= 50 mOhm | Keysight 34980A automated Kelvin switch scan at 125°C |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Chamber spatial temperature spread across 9 harness thermocouple locations during 125°C dwell** | `1.8` | <= 3.0°C total delta | Multi-channel calibrated Type-K data acquisition logging at 1 Hz for 60 minutes |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Socket contact pin actuation durability without mechanical pin collapse or plastic deformation** | `500` | >= 500 insertion cycles with normal force >= 25 gf | Automated mechanical cycle testing with micro-force transducer gauge |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of socket contacts demonstrate Kelvin Rc <= 50 mOhm at 125°C, all 9 multi-zone thermal channels log within 125°C +/- 1.5°C across steady-state thermal soak, zero short/open faults across BIB dynamic signal harness, and signoff endorsement from both Systems Engineer and Reliability Domain Expert.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-REL-180NM-HTOL-037`
**Title:** In-Situ Chamber Thermal Profile Calibration & Dynamic Stress Pattern Verification  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Final ATE JEDEC DDR Speed-Bin & HTOL Burn-in Testing > HTOL Dynamic Thermal-Voltage Accelerated Burn-in Stress Execution > Continuous 125°C Dynamic High-Voltage Accelerated Burn-in Chamber Stress Execution > HTOL Burn-in Board (BIB) Dynamic Vector Loading and In-Situ Thermal Calibration > Metrology  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm / SKY130 CMOS Compatible)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Execution  

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Chamber Preparation   │
│        & Purge         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Multi-Zone Profiling  │
│   & PID Calibration    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  HTOL BIB Insertion &  │
│  Dynamic Vector Load   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│        In-Situ         │
│    Thermal-Voltage     │
│  Stress Verification   │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Chamber Gas Atmosphere & Purge Setup**:
   - Establish ambient inert sweep using ultra-pure $\text{N}_2$ regulated through calibrated Mass Flow Controllers (MFCs).
   - Set the carrier sweep rate between **$1.0\text{ SLPM}$ and $5.0\text{ SLPM}$** (nominal $2.0$ to $5.0\text{ SLPM}$) to prevent ambient air back-diffusion and maintain laminar sweep dynamics.
2. **Thermal Multi-Zone Profiling & PID Loop Tuning**:
   - Verify 3-zone thermal regulation (Load zone, Center flat zone, and Source gas inlet zone) heated via resistive coils (Kanthal-A1 / APM alloy coils).
   - Calibrate the dual Type-R / Type-S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples encased in protective thermowells coupled to digital PID controllers with feedforward decoupling.
   - Establish and stabilize the central process flat zone across a minimum span of **$300\text{ mm}$ to $350\text{ mm}$** with strict temperature uniformity.
3. **Burn-in Board (BIB) Mechanical Insertion**:
   - Mount the packaged 180nm DRAM test vehicles onto the HTOL Burn-in Board (BIB).
   - Execute mechanical insertion into the chamber at a controlled speed strictly **$< 50\text{ mm/minute}$** to eliminate thermal shock, structural board warpage, and crystallographic slip dislocations.
4. **Dynamic Stress Pattern & In-Situ Thermal Verification**:
   - Apply continuous dynamic burn-in toggle vectors (address/data bus transitions, wordline activation patterns) across all DUT sockets.
   - Monitor real-time thermocouple sensors distributed across the BIB surface to verify uniform heat dissipation and ensure zero localized hot-spot runaway under continuous elevated ambient stress.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Exact Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Central Flat Zone Thermal Uniformity** | **$\le \pm 0.5$** | **${}^\circ\text{C}$** | Multi-point Type-R/S Pt-Pt/Rh profiling across central $300\text{ mm}$–$350\text{ mm}$ flat zone |
| **Atmospheric Gas Purge Sweep Rate** | **$1.0$ to $5.0$** (nominal $2.0$ to $5.0$) | **$\text{SLPM}$** | In-situ calibrated thermal Mass Flow Controller (MFC) logging |
| **BIB Mechanical Insertion Speed** | **$< 50$** | **$\text{mm/minute}$** | Automated lead-screw motorized transfer encoder readout |
| **Lithography Placement Grid Compliance (DUT Interface)** | **$0.005$ ($5\text{ nm}$ grid step)** | **$\mu\text{m}$** | Foundry GDSII/OASIS physical verification rule check (DRC) |

---

### 3. Citations & Literature Context

- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**
  - Multi-zone heating elements (Kanthal-A1 / MoSi2) across Load, Center, and Source zones.
  - Temperature uniformity requirement: $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across the central $300\text{ mm}$ zone.
  - Gas flow dynamics: Laminar sweep regulated by MFCs at $1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$.
  - Mechanical transfer speed limit: $< 50\text{ mm/minute}$ to prevent thermal shock and crystallographic slip dislocations.
- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery**
  - Resistive heating alloy (Kanthal A1 or APM alloy coils) with dual Type-R/S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples per zone.
  - Center flat zone: Middle $350\text{ mm}$ maintains temperature uniformity $\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Sweep velocity: $2.0\text{ to }5.0\text{ SLPM}$ laminar sweep to prevent ambient air back-diffusion.
- **Source: SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**
  - Minimum manufacturing grid resolution: $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).
  - Critical poly gate length: $0.15\,\mu\text{m}$ ($150\text{ nm}$); overlay error budget $\le 35\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal profiling inside an active High-Temperature Operating Life (HTOL) burn-in chamber during dynamic vector switching is vulnerable to localized self-heating (Joule heating) from the 180nm DRAM core logic and peripheral charge pumps. While furnace profiling literature emphasizes multi-zone PID loop decoupling (Source, Center, Load) and laminar boundary layer control, burn-in boards (BIBs) introduce complex 3D aerodynamic obstructions. Forced-convection fan baffles must decouple chamber wall radiation from convective air velocity across densely populated 180nm packaged devices, ensuring no localized dead zones develop where ambient airflow drops below 1.5 m/s, which would induce runaway junction temperatures (Tj) exceeding the JEDEC JESD22-A108 standard limit.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Dynamic stress pattern verification for Gen 3 180nm DRAM requires running row-hammer stress, pseudo-random march (March C- / March 9N), and charge-pump overdrive toggle sequences at elevated VDD (2.2V vs nominal 1.8V) at an ambient chamber setpoint of 125°C. The junction temperature Tj can easily peak beyond 140°C due to Idd4R/Idd4W switching currents. In-situ thermal profiling must utilize calibrated PT100 RTDs or thin-gauge Type-K thermocouple beads attached directly to package lids using thermally conductive polyimide adhesive with minimal thermal mass. Furthermore, dynamic vector verification must capture edge degradation and cross-talk induced signal slew distortion across the high-temperature backplane trace impedance.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-temperature burn-in sockets (polyimide/PEEK with beryllium copper or Au-plated phosphor bronze contacts) and customized high-Tg polyimide BIBs (Tg > 260°C) face multi-month procurement lead times and high wear-out rates under continuous 125°C - 150°C thermal cycling. Off-the-shelf thermocouple arrays and multi-channel profiling dataloggers must maintain NIST/ISO 17025 traceability; substitution of standard FR-4 PCB materials or commercial grade interconnects will lead to delamination, copper migration, and socket contact resistance drift, aborting qualification campaigns mid-stream.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: HTOL 1000-hour and 168-hour readouts dominate the critical path of 180nm MPW tapeout product qualification. Any abort due to thermal uniformity excursion (+/- 3°C limit across BIB slots) or false bit-fail generation from dynamic vector skew requires chamber re-stabilization, recalibration, and thermal re-soak. Calibrating the thermal chamber profile and validating vector fidelity prior to loading production qualification lots directly mitigates unplanned chamber downtime and prevents premature failure review boards (MRB).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway (Tj > 145°C) caused by uncalibrated convective flow shadowing behind upstream BIB card slots, leading to gate-oxide dielectric breakdown (TDDB) false failures in 180nm DRAM peripheral circuitry.
1. High-temperature signal degradation and ground bounce on driver backplanes at 125°C resulting in corrupted dynamic test vectors (undervoltage clock edges or false write states), leading to invalid retention and march test qualification data.
1. Sensor drift or contact decoupling of in-situ calibration thermocouples under high-velocity turbulent airflow, causing the chamber PID loop to overheat the active load zone beyond the maximum specification limit.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-1-3-01` | **Chamber Multi-Slot Spatial and Temporal Thermal Profile Calibration under Dynamic Dummy Load** | 16-Channel NIST-calibrated Type-K Fine-Gauge Thermocouple Datalogger (Keysight DAQ970A), HTOL Burn-In Chamber with forced convection, Calibrated Dynamic Dummy Thermal Load BIBs populated with 180nm thermal test vehicles (TTVs) equipped with embedded silicon temperature diodes. | 1. Power on chamber and set PID temperature controller setpoint to 125.0°C with nominal forced-air convection velocity of 2.0 m/s. 2. Apply dynamic stress power supplies: VDD = 2.20V (180nm accelerated core voltage) and VDDQ = 2.20V to dummy load boards running active toggling vectors at 133 MHz. 3. Log temperature readings on all 16 channels continuously at 1 Hz during ramp-up (< 3°C/min). 4. Once setpoint is reached, allow a 45-minute thermal soak for equilibrium. 5. Continuously log spatial temperatures across all monitored positions for 120 minutes under full dynamic switching load. 6. Compute steady-state mean, standard deviation, and peak-to-peak delta across all slots and channels. | `Chamber spatial temperature uniformity across all monitored positions must remain within 125.0°C +/- 2.5°C; temporal stability over 120 minutes must remain within +/- 0.8°C; no individual device case temperature (Tc) shall exceed 128.5°C or drop below 122.5°C.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-1-3-02` | **In-Situ Dynamic Vector Signal Integrity and Pattern Slew Verification at 125°C Chamber Ambient** | Tektronix 4-Channel 2.5 GHz High-Bandwidth Digital Storage Oscilloscope with high-temperature differential active probes (P7313SMA / browser tips), HTOL Dynamic Pattern Generator / Driver Board, High-Tg Polyimide In-Situ Verification BIB with SMA breakout taps on critical address (A[0:12]), clock (CLK/CLK#), and data (DQ[0:15]) lines. | 1. Initialize pattern generator to broadcast continuous clock and address stress patterns through the HTOL backplane to the target BIB slot at 125°C ambient. 2. Connect high-temperature differential active probes to CLK/CLK# differential pair, Row Address Strobe (/RAS), and Data bit DQ0 at the socket pins of the farthest slot from the driver backplane. 3. Capture eye diagrams over 100,000 continuous clock cycles on the oscilloscope. 4. Measure differential clock jitter, signal rise/fall times (20% to 80%), overshoot, undershoot, and logic high/low noise margins. 5. Verify that pattern generator cyclic redundancy check (CRC) and loopback error registers report zero dropped or flipped vectors during a 60-minute stress window. | `Clock jitter (tJIT(per)) <= 150 ps; signal rise/fall times (tr, tf) between 0.4 ns and 1.2 ns; voltage overshoot <= 0.4V above VDD (<= 2.60V max); voltage undershoot <= 0.4V below VSS (>= -0.40V min); zero parity/CRC pattern errors detected across 10^10 transmitted vectors.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protective insulated gloves rated to >= 250°C (EN 407 / ANSI Level 4) for hot chamber access, ANSI Z87.1 approved anti-fog safety spectacles with side shields, Flame-resistant (FR) static-dissipative cleanroom lab coat (NFPA 70E / ESD-safe), ESD-grounded conductive safety shoes or dual-heel grounding straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately immerse affected area in clean, cold water or apply cool wet compresses for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing and seek prompt medical attention. Chemical Splash (IPA): Irrigate eyes or exposed skin with emergency eyewash/shower for minimum 15 minutes. Inhalation of solvent fumes: Move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber exhaust must be ducted directly to cleanroom technical exhaust facilities rated for 150 CFM continuous extraction to capture any VOCs or outgassing from polyimide adhesives, flux residues, or conformal socket coatings at 125°C. Room air exchanges must exceed 20 air changes per hour (ACH).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-soaked wipes and polyimide adhesive scrap in dedicated, sealed, FM-approved flammable waste containers grounded against electrostatic discharge. Used thermal paste containers must be collected as non-halogenated hazardous chemical solid waste in compliance with local environmental EPA/EHS regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Electronics Cleaner** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / cleanroom grade) | `99.9%` |
| **Polydimethylsiloxane (Thermal Grease / Joint Compound)** | `63148-62-9` | Technical Electronic Grade | `> 95.0%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge and Inerting)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-assembled packaged 180nm DRAM DUTs post-SMT and socket inspection, lead frames/balls clean with zero organic contamination or flux residues; BIB gold fingers cleaned with 99.9% IPA to < 50 mOhm contact resistance.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thermally stabilized DUTs and calibrated BIB assemblies ready for immediate qualification stress; socket contacts clean, free of oxidation or pitting, with no delamination or scorch marks on PCB substrate.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding open-air queue time leads to atmospheric moisture absorption into plastic mold compounds (popcorn effect/package cracking during 125°C stress ramp) and atmospheric sulfidation/oxidation of exposed gold-plated BIB contact fingers, causing intermittent contact resistance spikes and voltage drop during HTOL.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful spatial and temporal thermal calibration of the HTOL burn-in chamber at 125.0°C under full dynamic dummy load, and formal validation of vector pattern integrity (eye diagram and jitter) ensuring compliant JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD79 DDR qualification readiness for Gen 3 180nm DRAM.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CALIB-CHAMBER-THERMAL-125C-PROFILE.csv`
- [ ] `VERIF-DYNAMIC-STRESS-VECTOR-EYE-REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `THERMAL-MAP-BIB-SLOT-UNIFORMITY.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **HTOL Chamber 16-point spatial temperature uniformity at 125°C setpoint under active dynamic load** | `125.0°C` | +/- 2.5°C (Min 122.5°C, Max 127.5°C) | Continuous multi-channel Type-K thermocouple datalogging over 120 minutes at 1 Hz across 6 BIB positions (Keysight DAQ970A). |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Dynamic vector clock jitter (peak-to-peak) at farthest BIB socket at 125°C operating condition** | `110 ps` | <= 150 ps | High-bandwidth differential active probing on CLK/CLK# pins via 2.5 GHz digital storage oscilloscope over 100,000 cycles. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Dynamic pattern transmission bit error rate (BER) over continuous stress execution window** | `0 errors` | Zero tolerance (BER < 10^-10) | Automated hardware pattern generator CRC and loopback parity register scan after 60 minutes of March C- test sequence execution. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit requires chamber thermal uniformity within +/- 2.5°C across all active BIB slots, zero vector transmission or parity errors during dynamic stress verification, and unanimous sign-off by Reliability Metrology Lead and Systems Validation Engineer documented in the calibration summary report.
