# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Continuous 125°C Dynamic High-Voltage (1.4× $V_{DD}$) Chamber Stress Execution

---

### 1. Document Control & Process Classification
- **Domain:** Final Automated Test Equipment (ATE) JEDEC DDR Speed-Bin & HTOL Burn-in Testing
- **Node / Architecture:** 180nm CMOS Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN), Gen 3
- **Operation:** Dynamic High-Temperature Operating Life (HTOL) Accelerated Chamber Stress Execution
- **Nominal Operating Supply ($V_{DD}$):** $1.8\,\text{V}$
- **Accelerated Overdrive Supply ($1.4\times V_{DD}$):** $2.52\,\text{V}$

---

### 2. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  1. Baseline Screen:  │
│     VDD=1.8V, VPP     │
│       2.5V-2.8V       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   2. N2 Purge Flow:   │
│     1.0-5.0 SLPM      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  3. PID Thermal Ramp  │
│     to 125 deg C      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  4. Apply 1.4x VDD =  │
│  2.52V and 20-50 MHz  │
│        Clocks         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    5. In-Situ HTOL    │
│    Dynamic Current    │
│      Monitoring       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   6. Ramp Down and    │
│      Post-Stress      │
│    Retention Sort     │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Stress ATE Baseline Characterization
1. Mount the packaged 180nm DRAM DUTs (Devices Under Test) onto the high-temperature burn-in carrier board.
2. Execute baseline parametric screening at nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ and ambient temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$).
3. Measure on-chip regulated boosted wordline voltage: verify Dickson charge pump generates $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}$ to $2.8\,\text{V}$ (driven by flying capacitors $C_{\text{pump}} = 20\,\text{pF}$ to $50\,\text{pF}$).

#### Step 2: Chamber Loading and Environmental Atmosphere Stabilization
1. Load burn-in carrier boards into the isothermal chamber slot.
2. Initiate continuous inert gas sweep via mass flow controller (MFC) delivering high-purity dry $\text{N}_2$ purge gas at $1.0$ to $5.0\,\text{SLPM}$ (standard liters per minute) to prevent atmospheric moisture and oxidation.

#### Step 3: Closed-Loop PID Thermal Ramp to 125°C
1. Engage the digital multi-zone PID temperature controller utilizing Type-R or Type-S Platinum-Rhodium thermocouples.
2. Ramp chamber ambient temperature to target setpoint $T = 125.0^\circ\text{C}$ at a controlled thermal slew rate to avoid thermal mechanical shock.
3. Allow the chamber zone to soak until spatial temperature uniformity across all DUT board positions settles within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.

#### Step 4: Accelerated Dynamic Voltage Bias and Clock Injection
1. Step up the core voltage rail from nominal $1.8\,\text{V}$ to the accelerated overdrive level:
   $$V_{DD,\text{stress}} = 1.4 \times 1.8\,\text{V} = 2.52\,\text{V}$$
2. Inject continuous two-phase non-overlapping dynamic stress clock vectors ($\Phi_1, \Phi_2$) at $20\,\text{MHz}$ to $50\,\text{MHz}$ to actively cycle the Dickson charge pump oscillator, wordline decoder drivers, and internal read/write sense amplifiers under accelerated voltage conditions.

#### Step 5: Continuous Dynamic Burn-in Stress & In-Situ Health Monitoring
1. Maintain continuous soak at $125.0^\circ\text{C}$ and $V_{DD} = 2.52\,\text{V}$ for the qualification duration.
2. Perform in-situ per-channel dynamic current consumption ($I_{DD}$) logging via ATE channels to detect catastrophic oxide breakdown, gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL), or thermal runaway.

#### Step 6: Thermal Ramp-Down and Post-HTOL Functional Retention Verification
1. Isolate the $2.52\,\text{V}$ dynamic bias down to $0\,\text{V}$.
2. Controlled ramp down of chamber temperature to $25.0^\circ\text{C}$ under continuous dry $\text{N}_2$ sweep ($1.0$ to $5.0\,\text{SLPM}$).
3. Transfer DUTs to Final ATE room-temperature test socket; re-screen data retention margin and ensure the pass transistor threshold voltage drop ($V_{th} \sim 0.5\,\text{V}$ to $0.6\,\text{V}$) remains compensated with functional $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}$ storage-node write margin ($V_{DD} - V_{th} = 1.8\,\text{V} - 0.6\,\text{V} = 1.2\,\text{V}$ write recovery).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                   HTOL Chamber Stress Target Profile   
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                      │
```

### 5. Context Literature Citations

1. **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**:
   - Nominal supply $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$, NMOS pass-transistor threshold drop $V_{th} \sim 0.5\,\text{V}$ to $0.7\,\text{V}$ ($1.8\,\text{V} - 0.6\,\text{V} = 1.2\,\text{V}$ loss threshold).
   - High-voltage boosted wordline requirement $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{\text{overdrive}} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}$ to $2.8\,\text{V}$.
   - 4-stage Dickson charge pump architecture with flying capacitors $C_{\text{pump}} = 20\,\text{pF}$ to $50\,\text{pF}$ driven by two-phase clocks at $20\,\text{MHz}$ to $50\,\text{MHz}$.
2. **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
   - Digital multi-zone PID thermal controller architecture using Type-R and Type-S Platinum-Rhodium thermocouples.
   - Temperature uniformity tolerance specification across isothermal zones held at $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
3. **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery**:
   - Mass flow controller (MFC) carrier gas flow rate delivery: $1.0\text{ to }5.0\,\text{SLPM}$ / $2.0\text{ to }5.0\,\text{SLPM}$ inert dry $\text{N}_2$ purge to prevent ambient back-diffusion and oxidation.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Running dynamic HTOL at 125°C with 1.4x VDD (2.52V on nominal 1.8V core) introduces massive transient IR drop across the burn-in board (BIB) power distribution network (PDN). With dynamic toggling of open-source DRAM wordline/bitline driver banks, decoupling capacitors on the high-temp Polyimide/Rogers BIB will experience accelerated dielectric wear. Individual DUT power trace sensing via Kelvin 4-wire connections at the socket level is mandatory to ensure voltage stress stays within nominal ±1.5% across all 128 socket locations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 1.4x VDD (2.52V) on a 180nm CMOS process node with typical gate oxide thickness tox ~ 4.0 nm, gate electric field reaches ~6.3 MV/cm at 125°C. This severely accelerates Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) and Hot-Carrier Injection (HCI) in the array transfer transistors and peripheral sense amplifiers. Dynamic vector generation must continuously toggle march patterns (e.g., March C-) to prevent localized non-uniform oxide charge trapping and ensure that failure kinetics model realistic high-field defect generation in deep trench/stacked storage nodes.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: N/A
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Burn-in execution schedule covers standard 168h, 500h, and 1000h readout milestones for JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD47 compliance. Any unscheduled chamber shutdown or excursion outside the 125°C ± 2°C window voids the accumulated Arrhenius acceleration equivalent hours (activation energy Ea = 0.7 eV), forcing a reset of the 77-DUT per lot sample size. Real-time telemetry logging of individual chamber zone temperatures and supply currents must trigger automatic PagerDuty alerts.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway induced by positive feedback between temperature-dependent subthreshold leakage current (I_leak) and high-density BIB socket thermal resistance, exceeding Tj = 140°C.
1. Dielectric wearout and early breakdown (TDDB) of perimeter decoupling ceramic capacitors on the BIB, shorting the 1.4x VDD rail and masking genuine DUT intrinsic silicon failures.
1. Solder joint intermetallic compound (IMC) embrittlement (Au-Al or Cu-Sn) on the packaged DRAM BGA/QFP substrate due to continuous 1000h exposure at 125°C, causing intermittent open contacts.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

Ramp chamber from 25°C to 125°C at 2.0°C/min under static VDD = 1.8V. 2. Once thermal stabilization (125°C ± 1.0°C across 9 monitoring points) is sustained for 30 minutes, step VDD to 1.4x nominal (2.520V ± 0.025V). 3. Initiate dynamic March C- vector stimulus at 20 MHz continuous clock frequency. 4. Log individual DUT supply current and socket surface temperatures at 10 Hz sampling rate for 168 hours continuously. 5. Monitor for any overcurrent spikes (> 150% baseline dynamic current) indicating latch-up or soft gate breakdown. | `Zero DUTs exhibit hard dielectric breakdown or latch-up (Idd <= 45 mA steady-state dynamic per DUT). Total operating voltage at DUT pins maintained between 2.482V and 2.558V (2.52V ± 1.5%) throughout 168h test duration.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-2-02` | **Post-Stress Functional Retention & Readout Speed-Bin Metrology** | Advantest T5503B High-Speed Memory Test System, Temptronic ThermoStream TPO4300A thermal forcing system (-40°C to +125°C), Four-wire micro-ohmmeter contact resistance verifier. | 1. Insert DUT into ATE test head socket. 2. Verify contact resistance Rc < 50 mOhm across all pin channels. 3. Execute full parametric opens/shorts and continuity screen at VDD = 1.8V. 4. Measure data retention refresh time tREF across cell matrix at 85°C and 25°C. | `Zero functional bit failures across full 64Mb/128Mb array at 133 MHz, 1.8V ± 0.18V. 64ms refresh retention test passes with zero single-bit or column-line fails across all 77 tested units (0 Fails / 77 Units, 0% LTPD).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protective Kevlar gloves rated to 250°C (EN 407), ANSI Z87.1 certified full-face impact shield and safety spectacles, Anti-static flame-retardant Nomex cleanroom lab coat, Continuous grounding wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For thermal burns: Immediately immerse affected area in clean, cold water or apply cold compresses for a minimum of 15 minutes; do not apply salves; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek urgent medical evaluation. For cryogenic/N2 asphyxiation risk: Immediately move victim to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; apply artificial respiration if unbreathing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber exhaust must be ducted to facility general exhaust at minimum 150 CFM. Enclosed chamber room must feature dual redundant optical O2 depletion sensors (alarm setpoint at 19.5% O2) interlocked with emergency forced make-up air blowers.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes contaminated with flux or lead-free solder residue must be sealed in airtight conductive HDPE hazardous waste containers and disposed of per EPA RCRA Class 1 solvent waste guidelines. Degraded PCB test fixtures must be recycled via certified WEEE e-waste recovery.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry-pack sealed (J-STD-033 MSL-3 compliant, relative humidity indicator < 10%), lead finish free of oxidation with Au/Ni or matte Sn plating showing contact resistance < 30 mOhm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Post-HTOL baked leadframes/balls showing no thermal blistering, flux carbonization, or dendrite formation; leadframe coplanarity within ±0.05 mm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into plastic package mold compound resulting in internal delamination or package popcorning during chamber ramp-up to 125°C, or galvanic pin oxidation causing false contact opens during ATE readout.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful uninterrupted execution of 168-hour / 500-hour HTOL stress testing on 77 units of 180nm Open-Source DRAM under continuous 125°C ± 1.0°C and dynamic 1.4x VDD (2.52V) voltage excitation in full compliance with JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD47 standards, proving early life mortality rate < 50 FIT.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Post-Stress JEDEC DDR Speed-Binning, Retention, and Failure Analysis Metrology

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-HTOL high-temperature (125°C) stress testing shifts threshold voltage (Vth) and exacerbates gate oxide leakage in 180nm planar access transistors via NBTI/PBTI and hot carrier degradation. The primary systems integration challenge is decoupling ATE probe contact resistance drift (Cres degradation due to oxidized scrub marks) from true intrinsic storage-cell subthreshold leakage, ensuring test sockets do not trigger false speed-bin binning failures.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: DRAM retention degradation post-125°C HTOL directly maps to trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) and interface state generation at the Si/SiO2 dielectric boundary in the 180nm trench/stacked storage node capacitor. Metrology must isolate variable retention time (VRT) phenomena by executing multi-temperature pause refresh retention sweeps (64ms standard JEDEC vs. 128ms/256ms extended pause at 85°C and 25°C) combined with spectroscopic ellipsometry on de-processed dielectric witness coupons to quantify thin-film passivation integrity.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specialized high-frequency direct-dock ATE loadboards rated for 180nm Gen 3 DDR-200/DDR-333/DDR-400 speed-binning alongside failure-analysis delidding/plasma-etch chemicals require dual-vendor sourcing. Thermal burn-in sockets experience contact pin wear after 500+ thermal cycles; replacement pogo pins and socket contact inserts have 8-12 week procurement lead times, posing a bottleneck for qualification turn-around.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To maintain project velocity and tapeout qualification milestones, post-stress ATE speed-binning and retention metrology must achieve throughput of ≤45 seconds per packaged unit under test (UUT). Hand-off to destructive physical failure analysis (FA) de-processing must be gated strictly by electrical fault isolation (PEM/OBIRCH) to avoid premature destruction of recoverable or marginally failing silicon.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dynamic data retention failure (<64ms refresh pause survival) caused by HTOL-induced trap generation in 180nm capacitor dielectric and access transistor junction leakage.
1. JEDEC DDR timing parameter closure breakdown (tAC, tDQSCK clock-to-data-out margin violations) due to asymmetric hot-carrier degradation in I/O buffer pull-up/pull-down networks.
1. Stress-induced leakage current (SILC) causing single-bit intermittent cell flips (Variable Retention Time / VRT) post-125°C high-voltage burn-in.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-3-01` | **Post-Burn-in JEDEC Dynamic Retention & Refresh Pause Sweep** | Advantest T5588 / Teradyne UltraFLEX ATE Memory Test System with High-Density Direct-Dock Probe Interface, Temptronic ThermoStream (-40°C to +125°C) | 1. Initialize UUT registers via JEDEC MRS/EMRS command sequence (CAS Latency = 2.5, Burst Length = 4). 2. Write pseudo-random inverted checkerboard pattern (PRBS9) to all bank addresses at nominal VDD = 1.8V. 3. Suspend auto-refresh commands for stepped pause durations: 32ms, 64ms, 128ms, and 256ms at chamber chuck temperature of 85°C. 4. Read back array contents at 200MHz DDR bus frequency. 5. Log fail bit map (FBM), fail address coordinates (X, Y, Bank), and calculate total single-bit and row/column cluster defect counts. | `Zero bit fails across all addresses at 64ms pause time at 85°C (JEDEC DDR specification limit). Retention yield across 180nm array must exceed 99.85% at 64ms retention time.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-3-02` | **Post-Stress JEDEC Maximum Operating Frequency & Access Time (tAC/tDQSCK) Speed-Binning** | High-Speed Digital ATE with 50-Ohm Active Pin Electronics, Pico-second Time Measurement Unit (TMU), Digital Storage Oscilloscope (4 GHz, 20 GS/s) | 1. Set clock frequency to target speed grades: 100 MHz (DDR-200), 133 MHz (DDR-266), 166 MHz (DDR-333), and 200 MHz (DDR-400). 2. Execute March C- memory algorithmic pattern across all addresses. 3. Measure DQ output valid access time relative to CK/CK# cross point (tAC) and DQS output access time (tDQSCK). 4. Shmoo plot VDD (1.65V to 1.95V, 25mV steps) versus clock cycle time tCK (5.0ns to 10.0ns, 0.1ns steps). 5. Assign speed-bin classification based on timing pass/fail boundaries. | `Speed-Bin Bin-1 (DDR-333 minimum for Gen 3 180nm): tAC <= 0.70 ns, tDQSCK <= 0.60 ns, and zero functional pattern errors at 166 MHz (tCK = 6.0 ns) under VDD = 1.70V at 85°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant nitrile outer gloves over neoprene inner gloves, ANSI Z87.1 splash goggles with full-face polycarbonate shield, Acid-resistant heavy-duty apron, Thermal insulated gloves rated to 200°C for burn-in chamber board handling, Class 100 cleanroom anti-static lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with Piranha/acid decapsulants: Immediately flush with copious continuous emergency shower water for minimum 20 minutes; apply calcium gluconate gel (2.5%) if fluorine cross-contamination occurs; for eye contact flush at eye wash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open and seek emergency ophthalmological attention immediately; for thermal contact burns from HTOL oven racks, immerse affected area in cold water and apply sterile burn dressing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet chemical decapsulation and de-processing for Failure Analysis must be operated strictly within an FM-approved dedicated acid exhaust fume hood with face velocity of 100 ± 10 LFPM (0.5 m/s) connected to a centralized wet acid scrubber system; ATE test bay requires local heat exhaust ventilation providing >=15 air exchanges per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent acidic decapsulation mixtures (Piranha / fuming HNO3) must be allowed to cool to ambient temperature in venting chemical bins, subsequently diluted with cold DI water (10:1 ratio), neutralized using 10% sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or calcium hydroxide slurry to reach pH 6.5-8.5, and routed to the industrial heavy-metal effluent treatment plant.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sulfuric Acid** | `7664-93-9` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `96.0% w/w` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `30.0% w/w` |
| **Fuming Nitric Acid** | `7697-37-2` | TraceMetal Grade | `90.0% w/w` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade | `99.9% w/w` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly unloaded from 125°C HTOL burn-in chamber; lead/ball metallurgy un-oxidized; package dry with moisture content < 0.05% per J-STD-033.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested and speed-binned package leads intact without micro-probe scrub damage exceeding 25% pad area; FA-destined reject dies chemically decapsulated with exposed top passivation clean and residue-free.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Package solder terminal/leadframe tarnishing and atmospheric moisture absorption causing surface leakage current during nano-ampere standby current metrology, combined with native oxide re-growth on copper/aluminum bond pads skewing high-speed DDR signal integrity and Cres readings.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful electrical JEDEC DDR speed-bin categorization, dynamic refresh retention qualification, and defect physical localization on Gen 3 180nm DRAM parts following 168-hour continuous 125°C HTOL stress, yielding definitive parametric shmoo profiles, fail bit maps, and localized failure analysis verification.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM_180nm_HTOL_PostStress_SpeedBin_Shmoo_Matrix.csv`
- [ ] `DRAM_180nm_Dynamic_Retention_FBM_Analysis_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `DRAM_180nm_FA_Defect_OBIRCH_Emission_Overlay.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-HTOL JEDEC Standard Data Retention Time at 85°C** | `64.0` | +192.0 / -0.0 ms | Automated ATE algorithmic pause-refresh March pattern test across entire memory space at VDD = 1.8V |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-Stress Primary Speed-Bin Operating Frequency Yield (DDR-333)** | `166.0` | ±1.0 MHz | ATE time-measurement unit (TMU) verification of tCK=6.0ns with tAC <= 0.70ns and tDQSCK <= 0.60ns at 85°C |
| `ASSERT-03` | **ATE Probe Scrub Pad Resistance (Cres) Repeatability Gauge R&R** | `0.18` | ±0.05 Ohm (CV < 1.0%) | Four-point Kelvin contact resistance metrology logged across 50 consecutive socket insertions per test site |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All qualification test units classified into JEDEC speed bins with 100% test coverage; zero unexplained functional fails on passing bins; >=99.85% retention yield at 64ms/85°C; all failing units characterized by ATE Fail Bit Map and verified by OBIRCH/PEM fault localization with formal sign-off from Reliability and Test Engineering Leads.

critics.systems_engineer: Post-HTOL high-temperature (125°C) stress testing shifts threshold voltage (Vth) and exacerbates gate oxide leakage in 180nm planar access transistors via NBTI/PBTI and hot carrier degradation. The primary systems integration challenge is decoupling ATE probe contact resistance drift (Cres degradation due to oxidized scrub marks) from true intrinsic storage-cell subthreshold leakage, ensuring test sockets do not trigger false speed-bin binning failures.
critics.domain_expert: DRAM retention degradation post-125°C HTOL directly maps to trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) and interface state generation at the Si/SiO2 dielectric boundary in the 180nm trench/stacked storage node capacitor. Metrology must isolate variable retention time (VRT) phenomena by executing multi-temperature pause refresh retention sweeps (64ms standard JEDEC vs. 128ms/256ms extended pause at 85°C and 25°C) combined with spectroscopic ellipsometry on de-processed dielectric witness coupons to quantify thin-film passivation integrity.
critics.supply_chain: Specialized high-frequency direct-dock ATE loadboards rated for 180nm Gen 3 DDR-200/DDR-333/DDR-400 speed-binning alongside failure-analysis delidding/plasma-etch chemicals require dual-vendor sourcing. Thermal burn-in sockets experience contact pin wear after 500+ thermal cycles; replacement pogo pins and socket contact inserts have 8-12 week procurement lead times, posing a bottleneck for qualification turn-around.
critics.laya_pm: To maintain project velocity and tapeout qualification milestones, post-stress ATE speed-binning and retention metrology must achieve throughput of ≤45 seconds per packaged unit under test (UUT). Hand-off to destructive physical failure analysis (FA) de-processing must be gated strictly by electrical fault isolation (PEM/OBIRCH) to avoid premature destruction of recoverable or marginally failing silicon.
critical_failure_modes: Dynamic data retention failure (<64ms refresh pause survival) caused by HTOL-induced trap generation in 180nm capacitor dielectric and access transistor junction leakage.
JEDEC DDR timing parameter closure breakdown (tAC, tDQSCK clock-to-data-out margin violations) due to asymmetric hot-carrier degradation in I/O buffer pull-up/pull-down networks.
Stress-induced leakage current (SILC) causing single-bit intermittent cell flips (Variable Retention Time / VRT) post-125°C high-voltage burn-in.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-ATE-DDR-BIN-003`
**Title:** Post-Burn-in ATE JEDEC DDR Speed-Binning & Parametric Shmoo Characterization  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS DRAM / Commercial Foundry Implementation)  
**Process Action Type:** Buy / Test Execution & Metrology  
**Council Context:** `DRAM Foundation VN` > BEOL & Packaging > Reliability Testing > Metrology

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure defines the production metrology and characterization protocol executed on Automated Test Equipment (ATE) to evaluate packaged Gen 3 180nm DRAM units following continuous 125°C dynamic high-voltage HTOL burn-in chamber stress. The objective is to determine parametric voltage-frequency operational shmoo boundaries, establish JEDEC timing compliance, bin parts by speed grade, and isolate post-stress parametric drift.

---

### 2. ATE Hardware Setup & Pre-Test Calibration

1. **Load Board & Socket Interfacing:**
   - Mount the dedicated multi-layer DUT interface board (DIB) to the high-speed ATE test head.
   - Verify Kelvin pogo-pin contact resistance ($R_{\text{contact}} < 25\ \text{m}\Omega$) across all $V_{\text{DD}}$, $V_{\text{DDQ}}$, and DQ pin channels.
   - Load calibrated timing TDR (Time-Domain Reflectometry) skew-deskew profiles ensuring pin-to-pin driver/comparator skew is compensated within $\le 35\ \text{ps}$.

2. **DUT Thermal Conditioning:**
   - Seat the post-HTOL stressed DUTs into the automated handler with direct thermal control (ATC) active socket tooling.
   - Stabilize DUT junction temperature ($T_j$) to $25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 1.0^\circ\text{C}$ for standard nominal screen, followed by high-temperature verification at $85.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 1.0^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Test Execution Procedure

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                       ATE Post-Burn-in Test Flow                              |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. DC Open/Short & Continuity Check (Protection Diodes, -0.2V to -0.8V)       |
|                                       v                                       |
| 2. Quiescent Leakage & Standby Current Verification (IDD2P, IDD2N, IDD3N)     |
|                                       v                                       |
| 3. High-Voltage Retention Metrology & Refresh Testing (tREFI, Pause Testing)  |
|                                       v                                       |
| 4. Parametric 2D Shmoo Characterization (VDD vs. tCK / Frequency Range)       |
|                                       v                                       |
| 5. JEDEC DDR Timing Margin Screen (tAC, tDS, tDH, tRCD, tRP, tRAS)            |
|                                       v                                       |
| 6. Final Speed-Bin Classification & Wafer/Package Tracking Mapping            |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

1. **DC Parametric Continuity & Protection Check:**
   - Apply $-100\ \mu\text{A}$ clamp current to all I/O and address pins with supplies grounded; verify ESD clamp diode forward voltage is between $-0.2\ \text{V}$ and $-0.8\ \text{V}$.
   - Sweep leakage current $I_{\text{IL}} / I_{\text{IH}}$ at $V_{\text{IN}} = 0\ \text{V}$ and $V_{\text{IN}} = V_{\text{DD}}$; enforce parametric pass criteria ($\le 1.0\ \mu\text{A}$).

2. **Supply Current Profiling:**
   - Force core $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.80\ \text{V}$ and $V_{\text{DDQ}} = 1.80\ \text{V}$.
   - Measure precharge standby currents:
     - $I_{\text{DD2P}}$ (CKE low, power-down).
     - $I_{\text{DD2N}}$ (CKE high, idle).
     - $I_{\text{DD3N}}$ (Active standby).
   - Compare post-stress readings against pre-burn-in wafer sort baselines to detect excessive hot-carrier or gate-oxide leakage degradation.

3. **Parametric Shmoo Matrix Execution ($V_{\text{DD}}$ vs. $t_{\text{CK}}$):**
   - Configure algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG) to stream solid, checkerboard, and pseudo-random march (March C-) test vectors.
   - **Voltage Axis:** Sweep $V_{\text{DD}}$ in discrete steps from $1.60\ \text{V}$ to $2.00\ \text{V}$ in $25\ \text{mV}$ increments.
   - **Frequency Axis:** Sweep clock period ($t_{\text{CK}}$) from $7.50\ \text{ns}$ (133 MHz / DDR-266) down to $5.00\ \text{ns}$ (200 MHz / DDR-400) in $50\ \text{ps}$ increments.
   - Plot the 2D pass/fail boundary (Shmoo plot) across the matrix to identify the functional operating envelope and operational margin loss caused by NBTI/PBTI stress.

4. **Dynamic AC Timing & Speed-Binning Screen:**
   - Execute read/write timing margin sweeps:
     - **Clock-to-out access time ($t_{\text{AC}}$):** Compare strobe DQS to DQ window.
     - **Setup and hold timings ($t_{\text{DS}}, t_{\text{DH}}$):** Modulate edge placement around clock strobe.
     - **Core timing constraints ($t_{\text{RCD}}, t_{\text{RP}}, t_{\text{RAS}}$):** Enforce strict JEDEC clock cycle counts.
   - Classify functional units into target commercial speed bins:
     - **Bin 1 (DDR-400 / $t_{\text{CK}} = 5.0\ \text{ns}$):** Pass full pattern suite at $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\ \text{V} \pm 0.1\ \text{V}$.
     - **Bin 2 (DDR-333 / $t_{\text{CK}} = 6.0\ \text{ns}$):** Pass full pattern suite at $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\ \text{V} \pm 0.1\ \text{V}$.
     - **Bin 3 (DDR-266 / $t_{\text{CK}} = 7.5\ \text{ns}$):** Pass full pattern suite at $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\ \text{V} \pm 0.1\ \text{V}$.
     - **Reject:** Fails DDR-266 timing window, exhibits bit failures, or violates DC leakage bounds.

5. **Post-Stress Retention Screen:**
   - Write inverted checkerboard background across all banks.
   - Pause refresh commands for retention bake window ($t_{\text{pause}} = 64\ \text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Read back cell data; tag single-bit degradation and tail-cell retention drops for failure analysis (FA).

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Evaluation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **I/O Pin Leakage Current ($I_{\text{IL}} / I_{\text{IH}}$)** | $\le 1.0$ | $\mu\text{A}$ | ATE DC Parametric Measurement Unit (PMU) at $V_{\text{IN}} = 0\ \text{V} \text{ and } 1.8\ \text{V}$ |
| **Core Operating Frequency Margin (DDR-400)** | $t_{\text{CK}} \le 5.00$ | $\text{ns}$ | Full vector pass across $V_{\text{DD}} \in [1.70\ \text{V}, 1.90\ \text{V}]$ at $T_j = 85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Clock-to-Output Access Time ($t_{\text{AC}}$)** | $\le 0.70$ | $\text{ns}$ | Active comparator strobe alignment relative to differential CK edge |
| **Refresh Retention Fail Limit (Post-HTOL)** | $\le 0$ (Zero single-bit fails at $64\ \text{ms}$) | Count / Die | March C- readback verification following $64\ \text{ms}$ refresh pause |

---

### 5. Context Citations & Technical Traceability

- **Foundry Geometry & Interconnect Baseline:**  
  *Source:* `SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid`  
  - Physical manufacturing placement resolution is calibrated down to the 5 nm grid resolution ($0.005\ \mu\text{m}$).
  - Critical layer pitch and interconnect routing budgets (minimum contact hole dimension of $0.17\ \mu\text{m} \times 0.17\ \mu\text{m}$, Metal 1 minimum width of $0.14\ \mu\text{m}$, and Metal 1 pitch of $0.34\ \mu\text{m}$) dictate the parasitics ($RC$ line delays) verified during post-stress $t_{\text{AC}}$ and speed-bin timing characterization.
- **Thermal Metrology Principles:**  
  *Source:* `Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery` & `Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation`  
  - Employs calibrated multi-zone thermal control and closed-loop PID monitoring principles (analogous to the thermal stabilization requirements of $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across isothermal zones) to ensure handler socket DUT test temperature stability during hot testing.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-HTOL ATE speed-binning at 180nm must isolate thermal annealing effects from intrinsic oxide degradation (BTI/HCI). If the transfer delay between the 125°C burn-in oven and the Advantest/Teradyne test head exceeds thermal equilibration limits or allows uncontrolled room-temperature shelf recovery, threshold voltage drift anneals out, creating false-pass speed bins. Pin electronic transmission line impedance (Z0 = 50 Ohm ± 1 Ohm) and pogo-pin contact resistance repeatability (<50 mOhm shift across 5,000 insertions) must be maintained to prevent high-frequency reflection artifacts during 200 MHz/400 Mbps JEDEC DDR-400 tCK timing measurements.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: DDR1/DDR2 180nm DRAM cells exhibit post-stress storage node dielectric leakage via trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) and access transistor subthreshold swing degradation. Parametric shmoo plots (VDD vs. tCK and VDD vs. tRCD/tRP) must capture retention decay at elevated temperatures (85°C chuck) to identify true marginal fails. Standard MARCH-C patterns fail to trigger worst-case row-hammer and column disturbance without integrating customized pseudo-random disturb stress loops into the post-burn-in ATE pattern generator.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-frequency ATE load boards (DIB) populated with burn-in-compatible Kelvin socket contactors have long lead times (>16 weeks) and vendor concentration in Taiwan/US. Wear-out of pogo pins and socket contact plating (Au over Ni) under high-voltage over-stress testing (2.5V-3.3V elevated VDD) risks unplanned downtime; dedicated spare contactors and automated socket cleaning/verification cycles must be budgeted and stocked locally.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Balancing parametric shmoo resolution against test cell throughput is critical. A high-density 50x50 voltage-frequency shmoo matrix on 100% of burn-in units will overload ATE test cell utilization, ballooning overall qualification cycle time past milestones. We must enforce a gating scheme: fast 2-corner functional binning for 100% of lots, reserving comprehensive 2D shmoo profiling and retention mapping strictly for an indexed 5-unit sample per stress readout.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) / Hot Carrier Injection (HCI) induced propagation delay degradation in row address decoders, collapsing the tRCD margin and causing DDR-400 speed-bin binout.
1. Post-stress node leakage and trap-assisted tunneling in NO (Nitride-Oxide) / ONO storage capacitors causing tRET (retention time) collapse below the 64ms JEDEC refresh window at 85°C.
1. Pogo-pin socket contact resistance escalation (>200 mOhm) inducing localized ground bounce and false setup/hold (tIS/tIH) timing violations during multi-pin burst read cycles.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-3-1-01` | **Post-Burn-in Parametric VDD-tCK Shmoo & JEDEC DDR-400 Timing Binning** | Advantest T5588 / Teradyne UltraFLEX ATE, high-speed Direct Interface Board (DIB) with controlled 50-Ohm trace impedance, Kelvin pogo-pin test socket, precision Device Power Supply (DPS) with sub-mV resolution, and thermal conditioning test chuck (controlled at 85°C ± 1.0°C). | 1. Dock device into the thermal test chuck socket at 85°C. 2. Force VDD/VDDQ = 2.5V nominal; perform standard Open/Short and DC leakage pre-test. 3. Execute March C- pattern across memory array to confirm baseline functionality. 4. Initiate 2D parametric shmoo execution: sweep core VDD from 2.0V to 3.0V in 25mV increments; for each voltage step, sweep clock period (tCK) from 7.5ns (133 MHz / DDR-266) down to 4.5ns (222 MHz / DDR-400+) in 50ps increments. 5. Log PASS/FAIL status at each coordinate to establish the shmoo operational boundary. 6. Repeat test vector across address/command timing parameters: tRCD (Row to Column Delay) and tRP (Row Precharge Time) from 10ns to 25ns. | `Unit must achieve stable, continuous PASS envelope at nominal VDD = 2.5V ± 0.2V at clock period tCK <= 5.0ns (DDR-400 specification); minimum operating voltage at DDR-400 must be <= 2.30V; tRCD <= 15ns and tRP <= 15ns at 2.5V, 85°C with zero bit errors.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-3-1-02` | **Post-HTOL Cell Retention (tRET) Pause Refresh Verification** | High-speed memory ATE with programmable algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG), internal real-time hardware timers (microsecond resolution), and 85°C ± 0.5°C environmental chamber/chuck. | 1. Initialize device registers (MRS/EMRS) at VDD = 2.30V, T = 85°C. 2. Write solid '1's, solid '0's, and checkerboard data patterns to all memory banks. 3. Suspend automatic row refresh commands for an exact programmable pause time step tPAUSE = 64ms (JEDEC baseline). 4. Execute full array read-out; record bit failure map (fail bitmap). 5. Increment tPAUSE in 16ms steps up to 256ms, writing and reading array to determine retention distribution tail. 6. Log physical row/column addresses of single-bit and multi-bit retention failures. | `Zero bit errors across all 180nm DRAM cells at tPAUSE = 64ms under VDD = 2.30V at 85°C (100% yield at standard refresh window); median retention time across the array population must exceed tRET_median >= 128ms.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 2 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (antistatic ESD-safe, minimum 5 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, ESD-dissipative cleanroom coat/smock with grounded wrist strap, Closed-toe ESD protective footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye contact with IPA contact cleaner: Immediately flush affected area with copiously flowing clean eyewash/water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated PPE; seek medical evaluation if irritation persists. For asphyxiation hazard from N2 purge: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing has ceased; contact site emergency response immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: ATE socket cleaning station requires local point-of-use exhaust extraction (minimum capture face velocity 100 FPM / 0.5 m/s) to evacuate volatile IPA vapors during manual or automated pogo-pin maintenance. Room air exchange must maintain Class 10,000 (ISO 7) cleanroom standards with continuous ambient O2 deficiency monitoring.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes and contaminated cleaning swabs must be segregated into dedicated grounded, airtight, flame-resistant flammable waste bins labeled with EPA/DRAM-EHS markers; dispose via licensed hazardous solvent reclamation facility.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Electronic Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Tier 3 / VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Gaseous Nitrogen** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry, post-burn-in singulated ceramic/plastic packaged units or bare die on carrier, leadframes/balls free of flux residue, thermally equilibrated to room ambient.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically classified, socket-tested package leads/solder balls inspected for zero mechanical deformation, micro-pitting, or scrub damage, sealed in desiccated antistatic JEDEC trays.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient air causes moisture absorption into package interfaces (popcorning risk during thermal cycling) and room-temperature relaxation/annealing of fast interface traps, masking true HTOL degradation signatures and corrupting qualification speed-bin statistics.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full electrical characterization and JEDEC DDR-400 speed-bin classification of post-burn-in 180nm DRAM units, producing verified 2D parametric shmoo envelopes, retention histograms, and root-cause bin-out logs.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ATE_PostBurnIn_DDR400_SpeedBin_Summary.csv`
- [ ] `Parametric_Shmoo_VDD_vs_tCK_85C_Plots.pdf`
- [ ] `Post_HTOL_Cell_Retention_Failure_Distribution.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Minimum functional core supply voltage margin at DDR-400 (tCK = 5.0 ns, 85°C) across qualifying population** | `2.30` | +0.05 / -0.10 V | Automated ATE DPS voltage search routine during March C- execution |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-burn-in DRAM cell retention survival rate at tPAUSE = 64 ms (85°C, VDD = 2.30 V)** | `100.0` | +0.0 / -0.001 % | Full-array algorithmic pattern generator bitmap read-out on ATE |
| `ASSERT-03` | **ATE test socket Kelvin contact resistance across all signal and power pins throughout qualification run** | `35` | <= 50 mOhm absolute | 4-wire Kelvin DC continuity and short-path calibration matrix |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All post-HTOL stress units pass 100% DC parametric screening, complete 2D shmoo boundary mapping showing >= 200mV VDD margin at DDR-400 (tCK = 5.0ns) at 85°C, demonstrate zero refresh errors at 64ms tRET, and have binning logs signed off by Quality & Reliability and Test Engineering Leads.

Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation (Levinson - Principles of Lithography & Thermal Processing)
SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid (SkyWater Technology / Google Open Source Silicon)

critics.systems_engineer: Post-HTOL ATE speed-binning at 180nm must isolate thermal annealing effects from intrinsic oxide degradation (BTI/HCI). If the transfer delay between the 125°C burn-in oven and the Advantest/Teradyne test head exceeds thermal equilibration limits or allows uncontrolled room-temperature shelf recovery, threshold voltage drift anneals out, creating false-pass speed bins. Pin electronic transmission line impedance (Z0 = 50 Ohm ± 1 Ohm) and pogo-pin contact resistance repeatability (<50 mOhm shift across 5,000 insertions) must be maintained to prevent high-frequency reflection artifacts during 200 MHz/400 Mbps JEDEC DDR-400 tCK timing measurements.
critics.domain_expert: DDR1/DDR2 180nm DRAM cells exhibit post-stress storage node dielectric leakage via trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) and access transistor subthreshold swing degradation. Parametric shmoo plots (VDD vs. tCK and VDD vs. tRCD/tRP) must capture retention decay at elevated temperatures (85°C chuck) to identify true marginal fails. Standard MARCH-C patterns fail to trigger worst-case row-hammer and column disturbance without integrating customized pseudo-random disturb stress loops into the post-burn-in ATE pattern generator.
critics.supply_chain: Custom high-frequency ATE load boards (DIB) populated with burn-in-compatible Kelvin socket contactors have long lead times (>16 weeks) and vendor concentration in Taiwan/US. Wear-out of pogo pins and socket contact plating (Au over Ni) under high-voltage over-stress testing (2.5V-3.3V elevated VDD) risks unplanned downtime; dedicated spare contactors and automated socket cleaning/verification cycles must be budgeted and stocked locally.
critics.laya_pm: Balancing parametric shmoo resolution against test cell throughput is critical. A high-density 50x50 voltage-frequency shmoo matrix on 100% of burn-in units will overload ATE test cell utilization, ballooning overall qualification cycle time past milestones. We must enforce a gating scheme: fast 2-corner functional binning for 100% of lots, reserving comprehensive 2D shmoo profiling and retention mapping strictly for an indexed 5-unit sample per stress readout.
critical_failure_modes: Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) / Hot Carrier Injection (HCI) induced propagation delay degradation in row address decoders, collapsing the tRCD margin and causing DDR-400 speed-bin binout.
Post-stress node leakage and trap-assisted tunneling in NO (Nitride-Oxide) / ONO storage capacitors causing tRET (retention time) collapse below the 64ms JEDEC refresh window at 85°C.
Pogo-pin socket contact resistance escalation (>200 mOhm) inducing localized ground bounce and false setup/hold (tIS/tIH) timing violations during multi-pin burst read cycles.

testcases.title: Post-Burn-in Parametric VDD-tCK Shmoo & JEDEC DDR-400 Timing Binning
testcases.instrumentation: Advantest T5588 / Teradyne UltraFLEX ATE, high-speed Direct Interface Board (DIB) with controlled 50-Ohm trace impedance, Kelvin pogo-pin test socket, precision Device Power Supply (DPS) with sub-mV resolution, and thermal conditioning test chuck (controlled at 85°C ± 1.0°C).
testcases.pre_conditions: DUTs have completed 125°C high-voltage dynamic HTOL stress; units equilibrated to 25°C under dry N2; load board socket verified for pin contact resistance < 50 mOhm; test chuck stabilized at 85°C.
testcases.procedure: 1. Dock device into the thermal test chuck socket at 85°C. 2. Force VDD/VDDQ = 2.5V nominal; perform standard Open/Short and DC leakage pre-test. 3. Execute March C- pattern across memory array to confirm baseline functionality. 4. Initiate 2D parametric shmoo execution: sweep core VDD from 2.0V to 3.0V in 25mV increments; for each voltage step, sweep clock period (tCK) from 7.5ns (133 MHz / DDR-266) down to 4.5ns (222 MHz / DDR-400+) in 50ps increments. 5. Log PASS/FAIL status at each coordinate to establish the shmoo operational boundary. 6. Repeat test vector across address/command timing parameters: tRCD (Row to Column Delay) and tRP (Row Precharge Time) from 10ns to 25ns.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Unit must achieve stable, continuous PASS envelope at nominal VDD = 2.5V ± 0.2V at clock period tCK <= 5.0ns (DDR-400 specification); minimum operating voltage at DDR-400 must be <= 2.30V; tRCD <= 15ns and tRP <= 15ns at 2.5V, 85°C with zero bit errors.

testcases.title: Post-HTOL Cell Retention (tRET) Pause Refresh Verification
testcases.instrumentation: High-speed memory ATE with programmable algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG), internal real-time hardware timers (microsecond resolution), and 85°C ± 0.5°C environmental chamber/chuck.
testcases.pre_conditions: Device passed TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-3-1-01 functional screening; thermal chuck calibrated and stable at 85°C; power rail VDD set to minimum worst-case operating voltage VDD = 2.30V.
testcases.procedure: 1. Initialize device registers (MRS/EMRS) at VDD = 2.30V, T = 85°C. 2. Write solid '1's, solid '0's, and checkerboard data patterns to all memory banks. 3. Suspend automatic row refresh commands for an exact programmable pause time step tPAUSE = 64ms (JEDEC baseline). 4. Execute full array read-out; record bit failure map (fail bitmap). 5. Increment tPAUSE in 16ms steps up to 256ms, writing and reading array to determine retention distribution tail. 6. Log physical row/column addresses of single-bit and multi-bit retention failures.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Zero bit errors across all 180nm DRAM cells at tPAUSE = 64ms under VDD = 2.30V at 85°C (100% yield at standard refresh window); median retention time across the array population must exceed tRET_median >= 128ms.

ppe_required: Level 2 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (antistatic ESD-safe, minimum 5 mil thickness)
ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields
ESD-dissipative cleanroom coat/smock with grounded wrist strap
Closed-toe ESD protective footwear
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin or eye contact with IPA contact cleaner: Immediately flush affected area with copiously flowing clean eyewash/water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated PPE; seek medical evaluation if irritation persists. For asphyxiation hazard from N2 purge: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing has ceased; contact site emergency response immediately.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: ATE socket cleaning station requires local point-of-use exhaust extraction (minimum capture face velocity 100 FPM / 0.5 m/s) to evacuate volatile IPA vapors during manual or automated pogo-pin maintenance. Room air exchange must maintain Class 10,000 (ISO 7) cleanroom standards with continuous ambient O2 deficiency monitoring.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent IPA lint-free wipes and contaminated cleaning swabs must be segregated into dedicated grounded, airtight, flame-resistant flammable waste bins labeled with EPA/DRAM-EHS markers; dispose via licensed hazardous solvent reclamation facility.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Dry, post-burn-in singulated ceramic/plastic packaged units or bare die on carrier, leadframes/balls free of flux residue, thermally equilibrated to room ambient.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Electrically classified, socket-tested package leads/solder balls inspected for zero mechanical deformation, micro-pitting, or scrub damage, sealed in desiccated antistatic JEDEC trays.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding queue time in ambient air causes moisture absorption into package interfaces (popcorning risk during thermal cycling) and room-temperature relaxation/annealing of fast interface traps, masking true HTOL degradation signatures and corrupting qualification speed-bin statistics.

expected_result.summary: Full electrical characterization and JEDEC DDR-400 speed-bin classification of post-burn-in 180nm DRAM units, producing verified 2D parametric shmoo envelopes, retention histograms, and root-cause bin-out logs.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Minimum functional core supply voltage margin at DDR-400 (tCK = 5.0 ns, 85°C) across qualifying population
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated ATE DPS voltage search routine during March C- execution

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-burn-in DRAM cell retention survival rate at tPAUSE = 64 ms (85°C, VDD = 2.30 V)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Full-array algorithmic pattern generator bitmap read-out on ATE

quantitative_assertions.assertion: ATE test socket Kelvin contact resistance across all signal and power pins throughout qualification run
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: 4-wire Kelvin DC continuity and short-path calibration matrix

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Elevated Temperature (85°C) Data Retention Time & Pause-Refresh Profiling

**Document ID:** `SOP-ATE-RET-180NM-085C`  
**Classification:** Technical / Industrial SOP  
**Node Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm 1T1C DRAM, 8F² / 6F² architecture)  
**Process Step:** Post-Stress ATE Metrology & Pause-Refresh Retention Profiling  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Flow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Load DUT into     │
│  Thermal Chamber at   │
│          85C          │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Write Baseline     │
│    Background Bit     │
│        Pattern        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Halt Periodic     │
│    Refresh & Enter    │
│    Pause Interval     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Burst Read Out &    │
│  Compare Bit Errors   │
│        via ATE        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Increment Pause    │
│  Time: 32ms to 256ms  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Generate Retention   │
│     Tail Curve &      │
│  Identify Weak Cells  │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Thermal Stabilization:**
   - Mount the post-burn-in 180nm DRAM DUT (Device Under Test) into the automated test equipment (ATE) thermal socket/chamber.
   - Ramp and soak the chamber temperature to **85°C ± 0.5°C** (calibrated via dual thermocouple sensors) and hold for 10 minutes to reach isothermal thermal equilibrium across the package silicon die.
2. **Initial Pattern Write & Verification:**
   - Apply nominal supply voltages and configure the ATE test vector to write full-array test patterns (Solid '1's, Solid '0's, and Checkerboard `0x55`/`0xAA`) into the 1T1C storage cell array.
   - Perform an immediate burst read at standard refresh timing to verify zero initial functional bit defects.
3. **Pause-Refresh Stress Execution:**
   - Inhibit the ATE memory controller's periodic auto-refresh command stream (`tREFI` paused).
   - Hold the array in an unrefreshed, quiescent pause state at **85°C** for the target pause retention window ($t_{\text{PAUSE}}$), beginning at **32 ms** and stepping through **64 ms**, **128 ms**, and **256 ms**.
4. **Metrology Readout & Error Mapping:**
   - Resume clocking and issue immediate burst read cycles across all wordline addresses at the nominal pitch (360 nm to 400 nm).
   - Capture bit fail map (BFM) records via the ATE pin-comparator channels to detect sub-threshold and junction-leakage discharge events across cell capacitors.
5. **Cumulative Retention Distribution Profiling:**
   - Compile the fail bit count as a function of pause duration to generate the cumulative retention distribution curve (main distribution vs. variable retention time (VRT) tail distribution).
   - Flag any device failing before the JEDEC commercial retention cutoff for redundancy repair or rejection.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                         │
C_cell (Target) (fF)┤█████                             │
                    │█████                             │
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘

```

| Metric / Parameter | Lower Limit | Target | Upper Limit | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chamber Soak Temperature** | 84.5 | 85.0 | 85.5 | °C | In-chamber RTD / thermocouple monitor |

| **JEDEC Data Retention Time ($t_{\text{RET}}$)** | 64 | > 64 | — | ms | ATE burst read bit fail map (BFM) |
| **Array Bit Error Rate at $t_{\text{PAUSE}} = 64\text{ ms}$** | — | 0 | 0 | Fail Bits | ATE real-time pattern error comparator |

---

### 4. Verified Source Citations

- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - Minimum storage capacitance: **25 to 30 fF** per cell with stacked capacitor (Si3N4 or Ta2O5 high-k dielectric, EOT 3 to 4 nm).
  - Retention requirement: **Data retention time > 64 ms at 85°C**.
  - Array pitch parameters: **Bitline and wordline pitch of 360 nm to 400 nm**.
- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation / Diffusion Furnace**
  - Precision temperature regulation standards and thermocouple feedback mechanisms ensuring **±0.5°C** thermal control stability.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-HTOL 85°C data retention metrology on an automated test equipment (ATE) platform requires strict thermal chuck stabilization to ±0.5°C across the entire active device area. A critical pitfall is localized self-heating during high-frequency vector burst writes prior to entering the extended pause-refresh dwell. The test head interface and thermal stream/platen must decouple DUT dynamic thermal dissipation from the ambient 85°C soak, ensuring junction temperature (Tj) does not exceed 85.5°C during background pattern loading.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node planar DRAM cell architectures, cell storage capacitance (~25-30 fF) retention at 85°C is governed primarily by trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) and junction leakage across the storage node n+/p-well diode, accelerated by HTOL-induced interface trap state (Dit) generation. Variable Retention Time (VRT) phenomena caused by metastable deep-level traps require multi-cycle pause-time stepping from 16 ms up to 128 ms across solid-1, solid-0, and physical checkerboard topological bitmaps to accurately deconvolute static tail leakage from dynamic wordline-induced gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Qualification-grade thermal socket contactors rated for >100,000 insertions at 85°C/125°C and low-inductance pogo-pin arrays present lead times of 8 to 12 weeks. Ensuring dual-sourcing for specialized high-temperature handler change kits (Kelvin contact socket boards) and continuous supply of ultra-high purity N2 purge for condensation/oxidation prevention on exposed socket pins is mandatory to prevent unscheduled line stoppages.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To maintain schedule synchronization between Post-HTOL burn-in unloading and ATE speed-binning/retention profiling, the Q-time window must be rigorously tracked. If packaged units exceed the maximum dwell time outside environmental control, moisture re-absorption and baseline thermal relaxation will skew the statistical Weibull retention distribution, necessitating costly re-soak and validation loops.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature capacitor charge dissipation due to post-HTOL gate dielectric degradation and enhanced sub-threshold/GIDL leakage across pass transistors, yielding retention fail at tREF < 64 ms at 85°C.
1. Metastable Variable Retention Time (VRT) shifting where individual DRAM cells randomly transition between acceptable retention (>64 ms) and leaky states (<32 ms) due to atomic defect reconfiguration in the cell junction depletion zone.
1. Contact resistance instability (CRES drift) on ATE handler socket pins under prolonged 85°C thermal cycling, causing false VDD droop and erroneous bit error rate (BER) inflation during refresh pause bursts.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-3-2-01` | **Post-HTOL 85°C Pause-Refresh Retention Time Characterization & Tail Bit Profiling** | Advantest T5588 ES / Teradyne UltraFLEX-DRAM ATE with Chroma/Thermonics Precision Thermal Stream / Hot Chuck System (calibrated to ±0.2°C at 85°C), High-Density Digital Channel Cards (500 MHz), Precision Source Measurement Unit (SMU). | 1. Soak DUT at 85.0°C on thermal chuck for 180s. 2. Write Physical True/Complement Checkerboard pattern across entire memory array at 200 MHz JEDEC timing. 3. Inhibit internal/external auto-refresh cycles and enforce static pause dwell time tPAUSE starting at 16 ms, incrementing in 8 ms steps up to 128 ms. 4. Execute non-destructive single-pass burst read at tCK=5.0 ns (200 MHz) and capture fail bit address map (FBM). 5. Invert data pattern to Inverse Checkerboard, repeat pause dwell stepping and fail bit logging. 6. Repeat steps 2-5 for 50 continuous pause iterations to capture Variable Retention Time (VRT) tail-bit deviations. | `Zero single-bit retention failures across full memory array at tPAUSE = 64 ms (standard JEDEC 85°C refresh period). Retention tail bit count at tPAUSE = 96 ms must not exceed 0.005% of total array (≤ 50 PPM). No cumulative hard cell failures under 50 repeated read-pause-read cycles.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-2-3-2-02` | **85°C Dynamic Wordline Disturbs & GIDL-Induced Retention Pause Profiling** | Automated Test Equipment (ATE) with algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG), high-frequency active probe head, Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer linked to DUT test fixture via automated multiplexer. | 1. Write Solid-1 and Solid-0 patterns into alternating logical row pairs. 2. Apply continuous high-speed row-hammer / wordline toggling on victim adjacent rows (Row N-1 and Row N+1) at maximum toggle rate (tRC=55 ns) for 500,000 cycles while holding Row N inactive in unrefreshed state. 3. Maintain unrefreshed state on target Row N for a net cumulative dwell time of 64 ms. 4. Read back target Row N data and record bit error locations. 5. Monitor and record quiescent standby IDD6 and static substrate leakage current IBB during pause dwell. | `Bit Error Count on victim row N must be 0 after 500,000 adjacent-row activations within 64 ms retention pause window at 85°C. Total standby refresh/leakage current IDD6 at 85°C must remain ≤ 1.25 mA for the 180nm DRAM test vehicle.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating heat-resistant silicone gloves (rated to ≥ 150°C) for test fixture and handler interface servicing, ANSI Z87.1 certified impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative ESD-safe lab coat conforming to ANSI/ESD S20.20, ESD-grounded conductive safety shoes or dual heel grounders, Nitrile gloves (thickness ≥ 4 mil) for chemical handling during socket contact cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately immerse affected skin in cool, clean running water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek medical attention. IPA Inhalation/Eye Exposure: Move subject to fresh air immediately; flush eyes with eyewash station water for minimum 15 minutes holding eyelids open; remove contact lenses. N2 Asphyxiation: Evacuate personnel to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on ATE handler thermal conditioning enclosures providing minimum 75 linear FPM face velocity; room-level continuous HVAC with integrated ambient O2 depletion monitoring sensors (alarm threshold set at < 19.5% O2).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA and solvent-saturated lint-free cleanroom wipes must be sealed in designated, grounded, airtight flammable solvent waste containers for hazardous chemical disposal in compliance with EPA/RCRA regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI Grade) | `99.9%` |
| **Nitrogen (Compressed Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Packaged chips post-125°C HTOL chamber unloading; lead-frame/BGA contacts free of gross oxidation, thermally equilibrated to 25°C in dry ambient.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically screened and thermally profiled packaged units, socket contacts inspected for burn-in carbonization/debris, leads free of pin-transfer solder bridging.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended exposure to uncontrolled cleanroom air causes atmospheric moisture absorption into mold compound (popcorning/delamination risk during repeat thermal cycling) and parasitic copper/solder oxidation on external pins, causing false contact resistance (CRES) failures during 85°C high-speed parametric read bursts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable delivery of comprehensive 85°C post-HTOL DRAM data retention characterization for the 180nm open-source DRAM chip. Metrology confirms retention pause times up to 64 ms with zero single-bit failures across all operating voltage corners, fully quantifying VRT tail-bit distribution and verifying compliance with JEDEC DDR refresh specifications.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM_180NM_POST_HTOL_85C_RETENTION_WEIBULL_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `DRAM_180NM_85C_PAUSE_REFRESH_FAIL_BIT_MAP_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `DRAM_180NM_VRT_TAIL_BIT_CHARACTERIZATION_PLOT.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-ATE-RET-01` | **Zero Data Retention Bit Failures at JEDEC Standard 85°C Refresh Dwell Window** | `0` | 0 bit errors | Full-array physical checkerboard and solid pattern write-pause-read test on Advantest ATE at tPAUSE = 64.0 ms, VDD = 1.80V, Tj = 85.0°C ± 0.5°C. |
| `ASSERT-ATE-RET-02` | **85°C High-Temperature Self-Refresh / Standby Leakage Current (IDD6)** | `0.85` | +0.40 mA / -0.20 mA | Precision Source Measurement Unit integration over 100 ms dwell during self-refresh mode at Tj = 85.0°C, VDD = 1.80V. |
| `ASSERT-ATE-RET-03` | **Pause Retention Limit for 50% Bit Failure Cumulative Median (tRET_50%)** | `240` | ± 30 ms | Multi-step pause time sweep from 32 ms to 512 ms at 85°C followed by Weibull cumulative distribution function (CDF) parametric extraction. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of tested post-HTOL DRAM samples demonstrate flawless data retention at 85°C for tPAUSE ≥ 64 ms, tail-bit VRT shift incidence ≤ 50 PPM at 96 ms, and signoff endorsement by the Metrology Lead and Product Reliability Director.

Inhibit internal/external auto-refresh cycles and enforce static pause dwell time tPAUSE starting at 16 ms, incrementing in 8 ms steps up to 128 ms. 4. Execute non-destructive single-pass burst read at tCK=5.0 ns (200 MHz) and capture fail bit address map (FBM). 5. Invert data pattern to Inverse Checkerboard, repeat pause dwell stepping and fail bit logging. 6. Repeat steps 2-5 for 50 continuous pause iterations to capture Variable Retention Time (VRT) tail-bit deviations.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Zero single-bit retention failures across full memory array at tPAUSE = 64 ms (standard JEDEC 85°C refresh period). Retention tail bit count at tPAUSE = 96 ms must not exceed 0.005% of total array (≤ 50 PPM). No cumulative hard cell failures under 50 repeated read-pause-read cycles.

testcases.title: 85°C Dynamic Wordline Disturbs & GIDL-Induced Retention Pause Profiling
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Test Equipment (ATE) with algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG), high-frequency active probe head, Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer linked to DUT test fixture via automated multiplexer.
testcases.pre_conditions: DUT maintained at stable 85.0°C ambient; nominal VDD=1.80V, VPP elevated to worst-case active wordline overdrive of 2.70V; VBB substrate back-bias regulated at -0.60V.
testcases.procedure: 1. Write Solid-1 and Solid-0 patterns into alternating logical row pairs. 2. Apply continuous high-speed row-hammer / wordline toggling on victim adjacent rows (Row N-1 and Row N+1) at maximum toggle rate (tRC=55 ns) for 500,000 cycles while holding Row N inactive in unrefreshed state. 3. Maintain unrefreshed state on target Row N for a net cumulative dwell time of 64 ms. 4. Read back target Row N data and record bit error locations. 5. Monitor and record quiescent standby IDD6 and static substrate leakage current IBB during pause dwell.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Bit Error Count on victim row N must be 0 after 500,000 adjacent-row activations within 64 ms retention pause window at 85°C. Total standby refresh/leakage current IDD6 at 85°C must remain ≤ 1.25 mA for the 180nm DRAM test vehicle.

ppe_required: Thermal-insulating heat-resistant silicone gloves (rated to ≥ 150°C) for test fixture and handler interface servicing
ANSI Z87.1 certified impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields
Static-dissipative ESD-safe lab coat conforming to ANSI/ESD S20.20
ESD-grounded conductive safety shoes or dual heel grounders
Nitrile gloves (thickness ≥ 4 mil) for chemical handling during socket contact cleaning
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Thermal Burns: Immediately immerse affected skin in cool, clean running water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek medical attention. IPA Inhalation/Eye Exposure: Move subject to fresh air immediately; flush eyes with eyewash station water for minimum 15 minutes holding eyelids open; remove contact lenses. N2 Asphyxiation: Evacuate personnel to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on ATE handler thermal conditioning enclosures providing minimum 75 linear FPM face velocity; room-level continuous HVAC with integrated ambient O2 depletion monitoring sensors (alarm threshold set at < 19.5% O2).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent IPA and solvent-saturated lint-free cleanroom wipes must be sealed in designated, grounded, airtight flammable solvent waste containers for hazardous chemical disposal in compliance with EPA/RCRA regulations.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Packaged chips post-125°C HTOL chamber unloading; lead-frame/BGA contacts free of gross oxidation, thermally equilibrated to 25°C in dry ambient.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Electrically screened and thermally profiled packaged units, socket contacts inspected for burn-in carbonization/debris, leads free of pin-transfer solder bridging.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Extended exposure to uncontrolled cleanroom air causes atmospheric moisture absorption into mold compound (popcorning/delamination risk during repeat thermal cycling) and parasitic copper/solder oxidation on external pins, causing false contact resistance (CRES) failures during 85°C high-speed parametric read bursts.

expected_result.summary: Verifiable delivery of comprehensive 85°C post-HTOL DRAM data retention characterization for the 180nm open-source DRAM chip. Metrology confirms retention pause times up to 64 ms with zero single-bit failures across all operating voltage corners, fully quantifying VRT tail-bit distribution and verifying compliance with JEDEC DDR refresh specifications.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Zero Data Retention Bit Failures at JEDEC Standard 85°C Refresh Dwell Window
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Full-array physical checkerboard and solid pattern write-pause-read test on Advantest ATE at tPAUSE = 64.0 ms, VDD = 1.80V, Tj = 85.0°C ± 0.5°C.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: 85°C High-Temperature Self-Refresh / Standby Leakage Current (IDD6)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Precision Source Measurement Unit integration over 100 ms dwell during self-refresh mode at Tj = 85.0°C, VDD = 1.80V.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Pause Retention Limit for 50% Bit Failure Cumulative Median (tRET_50%)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-step pause time sweep from 32 ms to 512 ms at 85°C followed by Weibull cumulative distribution function (CDF) parametric extraction.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: 100% of tested post-HTOL DRAM samples demonstrate flawless data retention at 85°C for tPAUSE ≥ 64 ms, tail-bit VRT shift incidence ≤ 50 PPM at 96 ms, and signoff endorsement by the Metrology Lead and Product Reliability Director.
