# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-HTOL-031`
**Title:** MOSFET Parametric Drift Extraction & Degradation Analysis ($\Delta V_{th}$, Subthreshold Swing $S$, $I_{on}/I_{off}$)  
**Context:** DRAM Foundation VN — 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Target Nodes / Geometries:**  
- Long-channel reference transistor: $W / L = 20\,\mu\text{m} / 5\,\mu\text{m}$  
- Intermediate transistor: $W / L = 10\,\mu\text{m} / 1.0\,\mu\text{m}$  
- Target sub-micron transistor: $W / L = 2.0\,\mu\text{m} / 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$ ($180\,\text{nm}$)  
- Unit cell access transistor: $W / L = 220\,\text{nm} / 180\,\text{nm}$

---

### Process Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Pre-Stress Baseline   │
│       Metrology        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Dynamic HTOL      │
│    Thermal-Voltage     │
│         Stress         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ├─────────────────────────────╮
             ▼                             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │    │                        │
│   Post-Stress Linear   │    │      Post-Stress       │
│   Id-Vg Sweep: Vds =   │    │    Saturation Id-Vg    │
│          50mV          │    │   Sweep: Vds = 1.8V    │
│                        │    │                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘
             │                             │
             │                             ├─────────────────────────────╮
             ▼                             ▼                             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │    │                        │    │                        │
│  Extrapolate Vth via   │    │     Extract Ion at     │    │  Subthreshold Swing S  │
│  Max Transconductance  │    │   Vgs=1.8V & Ioff at   │    │       Extraction       │
│           gm           │    │         Vgs=0V         │    │                        │
│                        │    │                        │    │                        │
└──────────┬─────────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘
           │                               │                             │
           │   ╭───────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────╯
           ▼   ▼   ▼
┌────────────◇───────────┐
│                        │
│  Acceptance Screening  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Tool Setup & Environmental Stabilization:**
   - Mount DUT/wafer onto the parametric probe station chuck. Maintain chuck temperature at standard reference ($25^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$) or targeted qualification temperature post-HTOL burn-in.
   - Establish Kelvin four-terminal source-sense connections to Gate, Drain, Source, and Substrate (Bulk).

2. **Pre-Stress Baseline Measurement ($t = 0$):**
   - Record baseline transfer characteristics ($I_{D}\text{--}V_{GS}$) across all test geometries ($20\,\mu\text{m} / 5\,\mu\text{m}$, $10\,\mu\text{m} / 1.0\,\mu\text{m}$, $2.0\,\mu\text{m} / 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$).

3. **Linear Region Threshold Voltage ($V_{th}$) Extraction:**
   - Force drain-to-source bias $V_{DS} = 50\,\text{mV}$.
   - Sweep gate-to-source voltage $V_{GS}$ from $0\,\text{V}$ to $+1.8\,\text{V}$ (for NMOS) or $0\,\text{V}$ to $-1.8\,\text{V}$ (for PMOS) with a step size $\le 10\,\text{mV}$.
   - Compute the first derivative transconductance:
     $$g_m = \frac{\partial I_D}{\partial V_{GS}}\bigg|_{V_{DS}=50\,\text{mV}}$$
   - Locate maximum $g_m$ ($g_{m,\max}$). Extrapolate the tangent line from $(V_{GS,\max}, I_{D,\max})$ to the $I_D = 0$ axis to determine $V_{th}$ via:
     $$V_{th} = V_{GS}(g_{m,\max}) - \frac{I_D(g_{m,\max})}{g_{m,\max}} - \frac{V_{DS}}{2}$$
   - Calculate drift: $\Delta V_{th} = V_{th}(t_{\text{post-HTOL}}) - V_{th}(t_0)$.

4. **Saturation On/Off Current ($I_{on}/I_{off}$) Extraction:**
   - Force drain-to-source voltage $V_{DS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$.
   - Measure $I_{on}$ at maximum overdrive: $V_{GS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$. Normalize to channel width: $I_{on} / W$ in $\mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$.
   - Measure $I_{off}$ in subthreshold cut-off: $V_{GS} = 0\,\text{V}$. Normalize to channel width: $I_{off} / W$ in $\text{pA}/\mu\text{m}$.
   - Calculate ratio: $R = I_{on} / I_{off}$.

5. **Subthreshold Swing ($S$) Degradation Extraction:**
   - In the subthreshold region of the $V_{DS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ (or $50\,\text{mV}$) transfer curve, extract the inverse slope across the decade current transition:
     $$S = \left(\frac{\partial \log_{10} I_D}{\partial V_{GS}}\right)^{-1} \quad [\text{mV/decade}]$$
   - Correlate shift $\Delta S$ with interface trap density degradation ($D_{it}$) generated during HTOL stress.

6. **DRAM Array Cell Leakage Screen:**
   - For access transistors ($W/L = 220\,\text{nm}/180\,\text{nm}$), verify subthreshold and junction leakage current remains within cell refresh limits at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Test Condition | Target Specification | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **NMOS Threshold Voltage ($V_{thn}$)** | Linear region, $V_{DS} = 50\,\text{mV}$, max $g_m$ extrapolation | $0.55 \pm 0.05$ | $\text{V}$ |
| **PMOS Threshold Voltage ($V_{thp}$)** | Linear region, $V_{DS} = -50\,\text{mV}$, max $g_m$ extrapolation | $-0.60 \pm 0.05$ | $\text{V}$ |
| **Saturation Drive Current ($I_{on}$)** | $V_{DS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$, $V_{GS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ | $\ge 500$ | $\mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ |
| **Off-State Leakage Current ($I_{off}$)** | $V_{DS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$, $V_{GS} = 0.0\,\text{V}$ | $\le 10$ | $\text{pA}/\mu\text{m}$ |
| **On/Off Current Ratio ($I_{on} / I_{off}$)** | $V_{DS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ | $> 10^7$ | Dimensionless |
| **Cell Transistor Leakage** | DRAM cell access transistor ($W=220\,\text{nm}, L=180\,\text{nm}$) at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | $< 1$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ |

---

### Context Citations

1. **Discrete Transistor Geometries & Static Targets:**
   - *Source: Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification*
   - Transistor dimensions: $20\,\mu\text{m} / 5\,\mu\text{m}$, $10\,\mu\text{m} / 1.0\,\mu\text{m}$, and $2.0\,\mu\text{m} / 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$.
   - Linear region extraction at $V_{DS} = 50\,\text{mV}$ using max $g_m$ extrapolation.
   - NMOS $V_{thn} = +0.55\,\text{V} \pm 50\,\text{mV}$; PMOS $V_{thp} = -0.60\,\text{V} \pm 50\,\text{mV}$.
   - $I_{on} \ge 500\,\mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ ($V_{GS} = 1.8\,\text{V}, V_{DS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$), $I_{off} \le 10\,\text{pA}/\mu\text{m}$ ($V_{GS} = 0\,\text{V}, V_{DS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$), $I_{on} / I_{off} > 10^7$.
   - Subthreshold swing relation: $S = \ln(10) \cdot (k_B \cdot T / q) \cdot (1 + C_{dep} / C_{ox})$.

2. **DRAM Array Transistor Constraints:**
   - *Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*
   - Access transistor geometry: $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$.
   - Leakage threshold: $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-HTOL parametric drift extraction on 180nm core NMOS/PMOS structures must decouple intrinsic device hot-carrier degradation (HCD) and negative bias temperature instability (NBTI) from burn-in socket parasitic contact resistance shift and test fixture thermal hysteresis. A Kelvin 4-wire triaxial SMU routing path directly down to the micro-pad probe card is mandatory to prevent sub-millivolt Vth extraction errors induced by series lead resistance at femtoampere subthreshold leakages.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Extracted threshold voltage shifts (Delta-Vth) must be mathematically resolved via both linear maximum transconductance (max gm at Vds = 50 mV) and saturation constant-current extrapolation (Ids = 100 nA * W/L at Vds = 1.8 V) to isolate bulk oxide trapped charge (Delta-Not) from interface state generation (Delta-Nit). Subthreshold swing degradation (Delta-S) exceeding 12 mV/decade indicates unpassivated Si/SiO2 interface traps (Dit > 1e11 eV^-1 cm^-2), causing catastrophic off-state leakage increase (Ioff > 10 pA/um) that directly degrades DRAM storage cell retention time.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Parametric test throughput is throttled by high-temperature probe card needle wear and triaxial cable microphonics during post-stress automated wafer stepping. Sourcing tungsten-rhenium or palladium-alloy multi-finger probe tips with low thermal expansion ceramic rings is required to ensure consistent contact resistance across 24-hour testing cycles without continuous wafer re-probing downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Parametric drift characterization must meet the strict 96-hour post-HTOL bake and read-out window dictated by JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD85 standards. Uncontrolled room-temperature relaxation or delay in executing cryogenic/room-temperature readouts will mask defect dynamics due to room-temperature hole detrapping, invalidating the HTOL qualification milestone.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Threshold voltage shift (Delta-Vth > 50 mV) under PMOS NBTI stress, causing wordline driver skew and cell pass-gate access failure.
1. Interface trap generation causing subthreshold swing degradation (S > 85 mV/dec) and elevated off-state leakage (Ioff > 50 pA/um), severely violating DRAM refresh time budgets.
1. Parasitic contact resistance drift and pad oxidation during prolonged thermal dwell leading to artificial transconductance collapse and erroneous mobility degradation metrics.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-3-1-3-01` | **Post-HTOL Core 180nm NMOS/PMOS Linear and Saturation Vth Drift Metrology** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer equipped with high-resolution SMU (HRSMU) and multi-frequency CMU modules, coupled to a Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 semi-automated thermal probe station with triaxial shielding. | 1. Force Vds = 50 mV (linear region) on DUT; sweep Vgs from 0.0 V to 1.8 V in 10 mV steps while sampling Ids with 1 PLC integration time. 2. Calculate gm = dIds/dVgs; extract Vth_lin from the linear intercept of maximum gm slope. 3. Repeat sweep at Vds = 1.8 V (saturation region); extract Vth_sat using constant current method at Ids = (W/L) * 100 nA. 4. Compute Delta-Vth against pre-HTOL baseline reference database for both long-channel (5 um) and target sub-micron (180 nm) devices. | `NMOS Delta-Vth <= +/- 30 mV; PMOS Delta-Vth <= -45 mV; Maximum gm degradation <= 10.0% compared to pre-stress baseline across all measured dice.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-3-1-3-02` | **Subthreshold Swing (S) and Ion/Ioff Current Ratio Degradation Profiling** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer with B1517A HRSMU modules inside a dark, dry-nitrogen-purged EMI-shielded probe enclosure. | 1. Set Vds = 1.8 V and sweep Vgs from -0.2 V to 1.8 V with 5 mV step resolution. 2. Measure drain current down to sub-picoamp noise floor. 3. Extract subthreshold swing S = (d(log10(Ids))/dVgs)^(-1) in the weak inversion region over two decades of drain current (10 pA to 1 nA). 4. Record Ioff at Vgs = 0.0 V, Vds = 1.8 V. 5. Record Ion at Vgs = 1.8 V, Vds = 1.8 V. 6. Compute Ion/Ioff ratio and compare to pre-HTOL baseline metrics. | `Subthreshold swing S <= 85 mV/dec (Delta-S <= 8 mV/dec shift); Ioff <= 10 pA/um (absolute Ioff <= 20 pA for W = 2.0 um); Ion >= 450 uA/um (Ion >= 900 uA for W = 2.0 um); Ion/Ioff ratio >= 5.0e7.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-resistant insulated gloves for high-temperature chuck manipulation, Cleanroom nitrile ESD-safe gloves (Class 100), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and grounded ESD wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of thermal burn from heated chuck (125 deg C), immediately flush affected skin with cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical evaluation. For eye contact with IPA during probe cleaning, irrigate with emergency eyewash for 15 minutes. In case of localized asphyxiation symptoms from N2 enclosure purge, move personnel immediately to open, fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous local exhaust ventilation on probe station chamber operating at minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s); environmental ambient O2 monitoring with audible alarm set at < 19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-wetted lint-free cleaning wipes in designated sealed, airtight, ESD-grounded hazardous waste solvent cans. No liquid effluent discharge to municipal sewers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Gaseous Nitrogen (Dry N2)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `96 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-HTOL stressed wafers/dies cooled to room temperature, cleanroom vacuum packed or stored in sealed dry-pack pouches with relative humidity < 10%.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probe-inspected aluminum contact pads with needle scrub marks < 15% of total pad area; surfaces free from particulate contamination and carbon residue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Room-temperature recovery/annealing of oxide trapped holes and interface states (NBTI relaxation) if readout time exceeds 96 hours, resulting in false-positive reliability pass and unmonitored latent field failures in DRAM retention.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete parametric characterization and automated drift extraction report of 180nm and long-channel baseline MOSFET test structures subjected to HTOL thermal-voltage accelerated stress, quantifying Delta-Vth, subthreshold swing degradation, and Ion/Ioff retention capability.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MOSFET_Parametric_Drift_HTOL_Extracted_Data.csv`
- [ ] `MOSFET_Degradation_Analysis_Report_JESD85.pdf`
- [ ] `Probe_Pad_Scrub_Integrity_Inspection.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum linear threshold voltage shift Delta-Vth_lin on target 180nm core NMOS devices** | `<= 30 mV` | +/- 2 mV | Keysight B1500A linear max-gm extrapolation at Vds = 50 mV across 50 discrete test sites |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-stress subthreshold swing S on target 180nm NMOS devices** | `<= 85 mV/decade` | +/- 1.5 mV/dec | High-resolution subthreshold log-slope extraction over two decades of drain current (10 pA to 1 nA) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-HTOL on/off current switching ratio (Ion/Ioff) at nominal Vds = 1.8 V** | `>= 5.0e7` | +/- 0.5e7 | Quasi-static transfer curve sampling at Vgs = 1.8 V (Ion) and Vgs = 0.0 V (Ioff) |

> Parametric drift data successfully extracted across all designated wafer die sites within the 96-hour post-HTOL window with zero data dropouts, satisfying Delta-Vth <= 30 mV, Delta-S <= 8 mV/dec, and Ioff <= 10 pA/um, signed off by Reliability Metrology Lead.

critics.systems_engineer: Post-HTOL parametric drift extraction on 180nm core NMOS/PMOS structures must decouple intrinsic device hot-carrier degradation (HCD) and negative bias temperature instability (NBTI) from burn-in socket parasitic contact resistance shift and test fixture thermal hysteresis. A Kelvin 4-wire triaxial SMU routing path directly down to the micro-pad probe card is mandatory to prevent sub-millivolt Vth extraction errors induced by series lead resistance at femtoampere subthreshold leakages.
critics.domain_expert: Extracted threshold voltage shifts (Delta-Vth) must be mathematically resolved via both linear maximum transconductance (max gm at Vds = 50 mV) and saturation constant-current extrapolation (Ids = 100 nA * W/L at Vds = 1.8 V) to isolate bulk oxide trapped charge (Delta-Not) from interface state generation (Delta-Nit). Subthreshold swing degradation (Delta-S) exceeding 12 mV/decade indicates unpassivated Si/SiO2 interface traps (Dit > 1e11 eV^-1 cm^-2), causing catastrophic off-state leakage increase (Ioff > 10 pA/um) that directly degrades DRAM storage cell retention time.
critics.supply_chain: Parametric test throughput is throttled by high-temperature probe card needle wear and triaxial cable microphonics during post-stress automated wafer stepping. Sourcing tungsten-rhenium or palladium-alloy multi-finger probe tips with low thermal expansion ceramic rings is required to ensure consistent contact resistance across 24-hour testing cycles without continuous wafer re-probing downtime.
critics.laya_pm: Parametric drift characterization must meet the strict 96-hour post-HTOL bake and read-out window dictated by JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD85 standards. Uncontrolled room-temperature relaxation or delay in executing cryogenic/room-temperature readouts will mask defect dynamics due to room-temperature hole detrapping, invalidating the HTOL qualification milestone.

Interface trap generation causing subthreshold swing degradation (S > 85 mV/dec) and elevated off-state leakage (Ioff > 50 pA/um), severely violating DRAM refresh time budgets.
Parasitic contact resistance drift and pad oxidation during prolonged thermal dwell leading to artificial transconductance collapse and erroneous mobility degradation metrics.

testcases.title: Post-HTOL Core 180nm NMOS/PMOS Linear and Saturation Vth Drift Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer equipped with high-resolution SMU (HRSMU) and multi-frequency CMU modules, coupled to a Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 semi-automated thermal probe station with triaxial shielding.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafers/DUTs cooled to 25.0 deg C +/- 0.5 deg C following HTOL 125 deg C stress cycle; probe tips aligned to W/L = 2.0 um / 0.18 um and W/L = 20 um / 5.0 um discrete transistor test structures; Kelvin chuck residual leakage verified < 50 fA at 1.8 V.
testcases.procedure: 1. Force Vds = 50 mV (linear region) on DUT; sweep Vgs from 0.0 V to 1.8 V in 10 mV steps while sampling Ids with 1 PLC integration time. 2. Calculate gm = dIds/dVgs; extract Vth_lin from the linear intercept of maximum gm slope. 3. Repeat sweep at Vds = 1.8 V (saturation region); extract Vth_sat using constant current method at Ids = (W/L) * 100 nA. 4. Compute Delta-Vth against pre-HTOL baseline reference database for both long-channel (5 um) and target sub-micron (180 nm) devices.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: NMOS Delta-Vth <= +/- 30 mV; PMOS Delta-Vth <= -45 mV; Maximum gm degradation <= 10.0% compared to pre-stress baseline across all measured dice.

testcases.title: Subthreshold Swing (S) and Ion/Ioff Current Ratio Degradation Profiling
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer with B1517A HRSMU modules inside a dark, dry-nitrogen-purged EMI-shielded probe enclosure.
testcases.pre_conditions: Thermal chuck stabilized at 25.0 deg C; relative humidity < 15%; pre-HTOL I-V parametric curves loaded in analyzer workspace.
testcases.procedure: 1. Set Vds = 1.8 V and sweep Vgs from -0.2 V to 1.8 V with 5 mV step resolution. 2. Measure drain current down to sub-picoamp noise floor. 3. # Standard Operating Procedure: High-Frequency & Quasi-Static MOSCAP C-V Oxide Integrity & EOT Profiling

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-HTOL MOSCAP C-V metrology requires rigorous isolation between test-bench parasitic lead inductance and small-signal parallel conductance. Probing pad pitch must accommodate triaxial Kelvin connections directly onto 200 um - 1000 um circular test pads down to 100 fF resolution without ground-loop noise corrupting the quasi-static displacement current measurements at ramp rates under 50 mV/s.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Accurate extraction of interface trap density (Dit) across the bandgap depends upon simultaneous high-frequency (1 MHz) and quasi-static (QSCV) acquisition using the Castagné-Vapaille method. Post-HTOL thermal-voltage bias stress shifts flatband voltage (Vfb) and induces oxide bulk trapped charge (Qot); without proper quantum-mechanical correction on 3.5 nm to 7.0 nm equivalent oxide thickness (EOT), extraction of t_ox from accumulation capacitance (Cox) will suffer up to 0.4 nm systematic error.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Shadow-mask aluminum sputtered MOSCAP test wafers and precision triaxial probe cards must be sourced under ISO-9001 quality certificates with lead times under 4 weeks to avoid idling cleanroom parametric analyzers during the Post-HTOL burn-in test cycle.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The metrology turnaround time per wafer must not exceed 45 minutes across a 9-site matrix to prevent a throughput bottleneck between HTOL chamber unloads and final retention-time screening for the 180nm DRAM lot sign-off.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature gate dielectric soft-breakdown during high-frequency accumulation sweep due to cumulative HTOL electrical stress damage.
1. Leakage current obscuring quasi-static displacement current (I_disp = Cox * dV/dt), rendering low-frequency inversion capacitance and Dit extraction invalid.
1. Uncontrolled backside wafer contact resistance (series resistance Rs > 50 Ohm) causing apparent dispersion and artificial frequency dependence in high-frequency C-V accumulation curves.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-3-2-01` | **High-Frequency (1 MHz) Multi-Frequency MOSCAP C-V Accumulation & EOT Extraction** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1520A Multifrequency LCR Meter Module, Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Semi-Automatic Probe Station with triaxial shielding and gold-plated vacuum chuck. | 1. Load wafer onto gold-plated vacuum chuck and contact 500 um diameter circular Al gate dot with low-force tungsten probe. 2. Apply DC bias sweep from inversion to deep accumulation (-2.5 V to +2.5 V for P-type substrate) with 25 mV step size at 1 MHz AC oscillation level of 25 mV_rms. 3. Correct for series resistance Rs using two-frequency impedance model. 4. Extract maximum accumulation capacitance Cox and calculate EOT accounting for quantum confinement and polysilicon/metal work function. | `EOT target = 4.20 nm +/- 0.15 nm; Series resistance Rs < 25 Ohm; Flatband voltage shift Delta-Vfb post-HTOL <= 50 mV relative to pre-stress baseline.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-3-2-02` | **Quasi-Static C-V & High-Low Frequency Interface Trap Density (Dit) Profiling** | Keysight B1500A with dual B1500A-HRSMU (High Resolution SMU) capable of 0.1 fA current measurement, shielded dark box with EMI enclosure, dry nitrogen purged chamber. | 1. Position probe on 500 um MOSCAP gate dot in dark Faraday cage. 2. Execute linear voltage ramp from -2.0 V to +2.0 V at constant slew rate dV/dt = 20 mV/s while integrating quasi-static displacement current C_qs = I_gate / (dV/dt). 3. Align high-frequency 1 MHz C-V and quasi-static C-V curves along the gate voltage axis. 4. Compute interface trap density profile using Dit = (Cox / q) * [ (C_qs / (Cox - C_qs)) - (C_hf / (Cox - C_hf)) ] across midgap. | `Midgap interface trap density Dit <= 5.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2; Quasi-static leakage current baseline I_leak < 20 fA; Gate dielectric breakdown field E_bd > 10.5 MV/cm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (class 100 compatible), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, ESD-safe conductive lab coat and heel grounding straps, Thermal protective gloves for handling wafers immediately after HTOL chamber extraction
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with IPA, flush immediately with copious potable water for at least 15 minutes at cleanroom eyewash station. In case of high-voltage electrical shock from analyzer bias supply (> 40 V), disconnect system power immediately, verify breathing/pulse, and administer CPR if necessary while contacting emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober dark enclosure must be supplied with continuous ultra-pure N2 purge exhausting through dedicated cleanroom VOC scrubbed exhaust duct at >= 50 CFM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA solvent wipes and cleaning swabs must be sealed in airtight flammable solvent waste containers and disposed of per hazardous solvent waste disposal protocols. No liquid chemical drain discharge permitted.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA) Semiconductor Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade C-1 (MOS grade > 99.9%) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas (Purge/Blanket)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (Ultra-High Purity 99.999%) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-HTOL dry thermal oxide gate dots with unpassivated aluminum metal tops and gold backside ohmic metallization, free of particulate contamination (> 0.3 um zero defect).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Scrub-mark inspected aluminum gate pads (< 5 um probe scrub depth), purged and sealed in nitrogen-purged hermetic FOUP or wafer container.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption and airborne organic amine/hydrocarbon condensation on unpassivated gate oxide edges leading to spurious surface leakage, artificial Dit shoulder peaks, and invalid post-burn-in EOT shift extraction.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical verification and quantitative extraction of post-HTOL equivalent oxide thickness (EOT), flatband voltage shift (Delta-Vfb), and interface trap density (Dit) across 9 die sites per wafer, demonstrating gate dielectric reliability compliance with JEDEC JESD22-A108 and 180nm DRAM retention criteria.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MOSCAP_CV_PostHTOL_1MHz_QSCV_MasterDataset.csv`
- [ ] `MOSCAP_Oxide_Integrity_Dit_EOT_Signoff_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Wafer_Die9_ProbeContact_Microscopy_Audit.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-HTOL Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) measured in accumulation at 1 MHz** | `4.20 nm` | +/- 0.15 nm | Keysight B1520A LCR C-V extraction at 1 MHz with quantum confinement correction model |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-HTOL midgap interface state density (Dit) via Castagné-Vapaille high/low frequency method** | `4.5E10 eV^-1 cm^-2` | <= 5.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2 | Simultaneous 1 MHz high-frequency and 20 mV/s quasi-static displacement current differential C-V extraction |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-HTOL flatband voltage drift (Delta-Vfb) relative to pre-stress baseline** | `15 mV` | <= 50 mV | Second-derivative inflection method on 1 MHz C-V depletion characteristic across 9 wafer sites |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 9 wafer test sites exhibit EOT within 4.20 nm +/- 0.15 nm, midgap Dit <= 5.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2, gate leakage < 100 pA/cm^2 at Vdd = 1.8 V, zero dielectric catastrophic breakdown below 10.5 MV/cm, and complete sign-off approval by Metrology Lead and Reliability Council.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Task: MOSCAP Diagnostic Test Structure Micro-Probing & Backside Contact Preparation
**Discipline:** Metrology & Characterization / Reliability Qualification  
**Platform:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Parent Pipeline:** High-Frequency & Quasi-Static MOSCAP C-V Oxide Integrity & EOT Profiling  
**Reference Document:** [moscap_microprobing_sop.md](./docs/knowledge/moscap_microprobing_sop.md)

---

### 1. Process & Workflow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Wafer Prep &      │
│        Cleaving        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Backside Native     │
│   Oxide Strip HF 5%    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Backside Ohmic     │
│  Metallization Au/Al   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Micro-Prober Vacuum   │
│    Chuck Alignment     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        Gate Dot        │
│     Micro-Probing:     │
│    200/500/1000 um     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  HF & Quasi-Static CV  │
│    Characterization    │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Substrate Inspection & Backside Native Oxide Removal
1. Mount the P-type (100) silicon test coupon or wafer containing planar MOSCAP structures onto a Teflon carrier with frontside protective photoresist/tape.
2. Dip the substrate backside in dilute hydrofluoric acid ($5\%\text{ HF}$) for $30\text{ s}$ to strip native oxide, followed immediately by a 3-cycle cascade deionized (DI) water rinse ($>18\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$) and dry $N_2$ blow-off.

#### Step 2: Backside Ohmic Contact Metallization
1. Transfer the sample immediately into a high-vacuum thermal evaporator or sputtering chamber (base pressure $\le 5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$).
2. Deposit an ohmic contact layer on the backside:
   - Sputter or evaporate **Gold (Au)** ($150\text{ nm} \pm 10\text{ nm}$) or **Aluminum (Al)** ($200\text{ nm} \pm 15\text{ nm}$).
3. *(Optional for Al)*: Perform rapid thermal anneal in forming gas ($95\%\text{ N}_2 / 5\%\text{ H}_2$) at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $15\text{ min}$ to ensure an ideal low-resistance ohmic substrate interface.

#### Step 3: Chuck Mounting & Alignment in Shielded Micro-Probe Station
1. Position the metallized backside onto the gold-plated vacuum chuck of a low-noise, light-tight, Faraday-shielded micro-probe station.
2. Engage vacuum hold-down and verify backside contact electrical continuity ($R_{\text{series}} < 5\,\Omega$).
3. Under optical micro-zoom ($20\times - 50\times$), inspect the aluminum circular gate dots (nominal diameters: $200\,\mu\text{m}$, $500\,\mu\text{m}$, and $1000\,\mu\text{m}$) patterned through shadow masks over gate oxide ($3.5\text{ nm} - 25\text{ nm}$).

#### Step 4: Low-Force Gate Dot Micro-Probing
1. Mount a low-leakage triaxial probe arm fitted with a soft-landing tungsten (W) or beryllium-copper micro-probe tip (radius $\approx 5 - 10\,\mu\text{m}$).
2. Align the tip above the perimeter-inward region of the selected circular gate dot ($200\,\mu\text{m}$, $500\,\mu\text{m}$, or $1000\,\mu\text{m}$).
3. Lower the Z-micromanipulator until physical contact is made, applying controlled overdrive ($\le 10\,\mu\text{m}$ scrubbing) to prevent gate oxide mechanical puncturing.

#### Step 5: C-V Profiling Setup & Verification
1. Connect the top probe to the High/Signal port and chuck backside to the Low/Return port of an impedance/C-V analyzer (e.g., Keysight E4980A / B1500A).
2. Sweep gate voltage $V_G$ from accumulation ($V_G < V_{fb}$) through depletion ($V_{fb} < V_G < V_T$) to inversion ($V_G > V_T$):
   - **High-Frequency C-V**: Test frequency $1\text{ MHz}$, AC oscillation amplitude $15\text{ mV}_{\text{rms}}$.
   - **Quasi-Static C-V**: Low-frequency displacement current sweep to record inversion recovery.

---

### 3. Dimensional Profile & Acceptance Criteria Targets

| **AC-1** | **Physical Oxide Thickness Extraction Precision ($\Delta t_{ox}$)** | $\pm 0.1$ | $\text{nm}$ | Extracted from accumulation capacitance $C_{ox} = (\varepsilon_{ox} \cdot \varepsilon_0 \cdot \text{Area}) / t_{ox}$ at $V_G < V_{fb}$ |
| **AC-2** | **Gate Oxide Layer Thickness ($t_{ox}$)** | $3.5 \text{ to } 25$ | $\text{nm}$ | Thermally grown oxide on P-type (100) Si |
| **AC-3** | **Circular Gate Dot Diameter Patterning** | $200$, $500$, $1000$ ($\pm 2\%$) | $\mu\text{m}$ | Sputtered Al circular gate dots through shadow masks |
| **AC-4** | **High-Frequency Measurement AC Signal Frequency** | $1$ | $\text{MHz}$ | Signal oscillator at $15\text{ mV}_{\text{rms}}$ verifying accumulation saturation |

---

### 4. Verified Source Citations
- **Stage 2 Reality Gate: Planar MOS Capacitor C-V Profiling & Dit Extraction**: Sputtered Al circular gate dots ($200\,\mu\text{m}$, $500\,\mu\text{m}$, $1000\,\mu\text{m}$); P-type (100) Si; Au or Al ohmic backside substrate contact; thermal oxide thickness ($3.5\text{ nm}$ to $25\text{ nm}$); High-Frequency ($1\text{ MHz}$) and Quasi-Static C-V accumulation formula $C_{ox} = (\varepsilon_{ox} \cdot \varepsilon_0 \cdot \text{Area}) / t_{ox}$ yielding $t_{ox}$ precision within $\pm 0.1\text{ nm}$.
- **Stage 3 Reality Gate & 180nm DRAM Layout Topology**: Substrate baseline parameters for 180nm DRAM integration and parametric screening gates.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Backside contact impedance and parasitic series resistance (R_s) directly convolute high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V curves, inducing artificial distortion in accumulation capacitance and causing gross inaccuracies during Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) extraction. Substrate grounding must provide a true low-loss ohmic return path (< 1.5 Ohm-cm2 contact impedance) across the whole wafer chuck interface rather than relying on point-probe scratch contacts.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Direct micro-probing of aluminum gate circular dots (200 um to 1000 um diameter) over ultrathin gate oxides (3.5 nm to 25 nm) creates a severe risk of probe-tip punch-through, mechanical indentation micro-cracking, and premature dielectric breakdown. Tungsten cat-whisker probe tips must maintain landing contact force below 15 mN with radius >= 10 um, while the backside native oxide strip must strictly preserve wafer frontside passivation integrity.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specialty micro-probing needles (beryllium copper or tungsten with controlled radius) and high-purity thermal evaporation charge materials (99.999% Au or Al target pellets) face significant supply-lead volatility; contingency stock of high-purity Ga-In eutectic paste must be qualified for non-destructive rapid backside ohmic testing without requiring vacuum deposition re-work.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The post-HTOL physical sample preparation loop contains dangerous bottleneck stages between backside oxide etch/metallization and high-frequency C-V screening. If queue time between backside native oxide strip and chuck seating exceeds 30 minutes in ambient cleanroom air, native oxide regrows, corrupting C-V accumulation profiles and delaying the HTOL qualification milestone by days.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. High backside contact series resistance (R_s > 50 Ohm) creating pseudo-dispersion and roll-off in high-frequency accumulation capacitance, invalidating extraction of oxide capacitance (C_ox) and physical thickness (t_ox).
1. Mechanical puncture or micro-crack propagation through thin gate oxide (3.5 nm - 25 nm) during gate dot micro-probe touchdown, causing irreversible gate leakage (I_g > 10 nA at V_G = -1 V) and premature dielectric breakdown.
1. Frontside chemical contamination or aluminum gate corrosion caused by vapor ingress or spillover during backside buffered oxide etch (BOE) native oxide strip.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Seat wafer backside on gold-plated vacuum chuck; apply 60 kPa vacuum hold. 2. Position four tungsten probe tips along the backside periphery or adjacent substrate contact pads with 1.0 mm pitch. 3. Force DC current sweep from -10 mA to +10 mA in 0.2 mA steps across outer pins while measuring differential voltage drop across inner pins. 4. Calculate differential contact resistance dV/dI and verify linear I-V profile. | `Backside contact must exhibit strict linear ohmic behavior across -10 mA to +10 mA with total series area-normalized resistance <= 2.0 Ohm-cm2 and correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.9990.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-3-2-1-02` | **MOSCAP Micro-Probe Gate Touchdown Integrity & Pre-Stress Leakage Screening** | Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Semi-Automated Probe Station with vibration isolation table, stereomicroscope, and Keysight B1500A High-Resolution SMU (HRSMU) | 1. Optically align probe tip to center of 500 um diameter circular Al gate dot. 2. Actuate Z-axis motorized micro-stepper at 5 um/s until electrical contact detection threshold (1.0 nA at 0.1 V) is triggered. 3. Apply 5 um probe overtravel to ensure solid mechanical contact without puncturing gate oxide. 4. Force gate voltage V_G = -1.0 V for 5.0 seconds and record steady-state gate leakage current I_g. | `Gate leakage current I_g must be <= 10.0 pA at V_G = -1.0 V across all tested gate dots; optical inspection at 100x magnification must show no scrub mark exceeding 15 um length or oxide punch-through cratering.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty Neoprene/Nitrile blend chemical gloves over inner nitrile examination gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face chemical splash shield, Acid-resistant PTFE/Neoprene chemical apron and sleeves, Cleanroom acid safety goggles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium gluconate gel (2.5%) must be staged directly adjacent to the wet bench. In case of skin exposure, flush with emergency DI water for 5 minutes, immediately massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into the affected area continuously, and seek immediate specialized emergency medical evaluation. In case of eye contact, flush with isotonic sterile eye saline for minimum 15 minutes and call EMS.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated dedicated polypro wet bench with dynamic acid exhaust airflow velocity maintaining face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) with continuous magnehelic pressure drop monitoring.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Fluoride-bearing chemical effluent must be segregated into dedicated fluorochemical carboys; neutralize using saturated calcium hydroxide (slaked lime, Ca(OH)2) slurry to precipitate insoluble calcium fluoride (CaF2), settling solids prior to pH adjustment between 6.5 and 8.5.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (BOE 6:1 Component)** | `7664-39-3` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `49 wt% aqueous stock diluted in BOE` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (BOE 6:1 Component)** | `12125-01-8` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `40 wt% aqueous stock` |
| **Gallium-Indium Eutectic (Optional temporary contact)** | `12689-13-3` | 99.99% Trace Metals Basis | `75.5 wt% Ga / 24.5 wt% In` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-HTOL unpolished/lapped P-type silicon wafer backside with native chemical oxide layer (~1.5-2.0 nm) and frontside Al circular gate dots (200-1000 um diameter).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic H-terminated or metallized (300 nm Al/Au) low-resistance ohmic backside seated on gold test chuck, with dry, undamaged frontside gate dots ready for micro-probing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide regrowth (> 0.8 nm SiO2) on wafer backside introduces parasitic series capacitance and contact resistance > 100 Ohm, attenuating 1 MHz accumulation C-V response and leading to false gate oxide thinning/thickening extraction artifacts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical preparation and low-loss ohmic backside contact realization of post-HTOL wafer substrate coupled with successful non-destructive micro-probe landing on MOSCAP Al gate dots, delivering repeatable C-V test readiness without oxide damage.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MOSCAP_Backside_Ohmic_IV_Verification_Data.csv`
- [ ] `MicroProbe_Touchdown_Leakage_and_Scrub_Log.pdf`
- [ ] `PreStress_MOSCAP_Chuck_Interface_Optical_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |

| `ASSERT-01` | **Backside substrate contact specific resistance to gold vacuum chuck** | `1.0` | +/- 0.5 Ohm-cm2 | Four-point probe differential I-V current forcing (-10 mA to +10 mA) on Keysight B1500A |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Unstressed gate oxide leakage under probe mechanical touchdown at V_G = -1.0 V** | `2.5` | <= 10.0 pA | HRSMU current integration measurement for 5 seconds on 500 um diameter MOSCAP dot |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Micro-probe scrub mark length on aluminum gate dot** | `8.0` | <= 15.0 um | Post-probe optical microscope inspection at 100x magnification with calibrated reticle |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Complete backside ohmic linearity verified (R^2 >= 0.9990, series resistance <= 1.5 Ohm-cm2), all 10 site-screened MOSCAP dots demonstrate gate leakage <= 10 pA under 12 mN landing force with zero mechanical punch-through, and sample successfully transferred to 1 MHz C-V profiling within valid Q-time window.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Frequency (1 MHz) and Quasi-Static C-V Sweep Instrumentation & Profiling

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Wafer Load & Chuck   │
│         Mount          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  High-Frequency 1 MHz  │
│       C-V Sweep        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Quasi-Static C-V    │
│         Sweep          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  C_ox & EOT Parameter  │
│       Extraction       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Acceptance       │
│     Verification &     │
│       Pass/Fail        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Grounding & Wafer Mount**:
   - Mount the P-type (100) silicon test wafer onto the gold- or aluminum-metallized thermal vacuum chuck to form a low-resistance ohmic substrate backside contact.
   - Ground the backside chuck to the instrumentation common LO terminal.

2. **Probe Pin Positioning**:
   - Align tungsten/beryllium-copper micro-probes inside a light-tight, electrically shielded Faraday cage probe station.
   - Contact circular aluminum top-gate dots fabricated with standard diameters of **$200\,\mu\text{m}$**, **$500\,\mu\text{m}$**, or **$1000\,\mu\text{m}$** over gate oxide thicknesses ranging from **$3.5\,\text{nm}$ to $25\,\text{nm}$**.

3. **High-Frequency (HF) 1 MHz C-V Sweep**:
   - Connect the LCR meter / impedance analyzer with high-frequency coaxial lines (four-terminal pair / BNC Kelvin sense configuration).
   - Apply a small AC oscillation signal ($v_{ac} = 15\text{--}30\,\text{mV}_\text{rms}$) at test frequency $f = 1\,\text{MHz}$.
   - Sweep the DC gate bias $V_G$ from the strong accumulation regime ($V_G < V_{fb}$, negative bias for P-type substrate) through depletion ($V_{fb} < V_G < V_T$) into inversion ($V_G > V_T$).
   - Record high-frequency capacitance $C_{HF}(V_G)$. In accumulation ($V_G < V_{fb}$), verify saturation at maximum oxide capacitance $C_{ox}$. In high-frequency inversion, verify that $C_{HF}$ reaches and holds minimum capacitance without low-frequency recovery.

4. **Quasi-Static (QS) Low-Frequency C-V Sweep**:
   - Connect the electrometer / quasi-static C-V meter with low-leakage triaxial cabling.
   - Sweep DC gate voltage $V_G$ under slow ramp conditions ($dV/dt \le 50\,\text{mV/s}$) across the identical voltage window ($V_G < V_{fb}$ to $V_G > V_T$).
   - Record quasi-static capacitance $C_{QS}(V_G) = I / (dV/dt)$. Verify that in the inversion regime ($V_G > V_T$), $C_{QS}$ fully recovers to $C_{ox}$ due to minority carrier generation-recombination.

5. **Dielectric Thickness ($t_{ox}$ / EOT) and Parameter Extraction**:
   - Extract maximum accumulation capacitance $C_{ox}$.
   - Compute physical oxide thickness / Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT):
     $$C_{ox} = \frac{\varepsilon_{ox} \cdot \varepsilon_0 \cdot \text{Area}}{t_{ox}}$$
   - Correlate extracted oxide capacitance with access transistor parameters (target $W/L = 2.0\,\mu\text{m} / 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$, expected threshold $V_{thn} = +0.55\,\text{V} \pm 50\,\text{mV}$).

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │░░░░░                             │

                    │▒                                 │
   Target NMOS V_thn┤▒                                 │
MOSCAP Test Min Diam┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
EOT Target Precision┤█                                 │
                    │█                                 │
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0      50       100     150    200 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value | Tolerance / Condition | Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Physical Oxide Thickness Extraction Precision** ($t_{ox}$) | $\pm 0.1$ | Absolute metrology uncertainty at accumulation $C_{ox}$ | $\text{nm}$ |
| **MOSCAP Circular Gate Dot Diameter** | $200$, $500$, $1000$ | Standard shadow-mask dot sizes | $\mu\text{m}$ |
| **High-Frequency AC Test Signal** | $1.0$ | Continuous sinusoidal test frequency | $\text{MHz}$ |
| **Thermally Grown Oxide Thickness Window** | $3.5$ to $25$ | Physical gate dielectric thickness span | $\text{nm}$ |

---

### 3. Source Context Citations

- **Stage 2 Reality Gate: Planar MOS Capacitor C-V Profiling & Dit Extraction**:
  - Validates planar MOSCAP geometry: circular Al gate dots ($200\,\mu\text{m}$, $500\,\mu\text{m}$, $1000\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter) on thermally grown gate oxide ($3.5\,\text{nm}$ to $25\,\text{nm}$) on P-type (100) Si with gold/aluminum backside contact.
  - Confirms High-Frequency ($1\,\text{MHz}$) and Quasi-Static C-V behavioral profiles across accumulation ($C_{ox} = \frac{\varepsilon_{ox}\varepsilon_0 \text{Area}}{t_{ox}}$ yielding $t_{ox}$ with $\pm 0.1\,\text{nm}$ precision), depletion, and inversion recovery.
- **Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification**:
  - Provides downstream target device parameters: target sub-micron NMOS access transistor ($W/L = 2.0\,\mu\text{m} / 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$), $V_{thn} = +0.55\,\text{V} \pm 50\,\text{mV}$, and $V_{thp} = -0.60\,\text{V} \pm 50\,\text{mV}$.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Establishes $180\,\text{nm}$ DRAM unit cell integration constraints (access transistor channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$, and minimum $28\,\text{fF}$ storage capacitance budget).

---

> [!NOTE]
> Micro-knowledge entry has been captured in [sop_hf_qs_cv_sweep.md](./docs/sop_hf_qs_cv_sweep.md) in accordance with the Council Micro-Knowledge Extraction Protocol.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-HTOL high-frequency (1 MHz) and quasi-static (QSCV) sweeps on 180nm MOSCAP test structures must accurately de-embed parasitic cabling inductance, probe tip contact resistance (Rc < 0.5 Ohm), and chuck stray capacitance (< 50 fF). Neglecting open/short/load calibration on the Keithley 4200A-SCS / Keysight B1500A LCR meter introduces severe phase-shift errors, distorting Cox accumulation extraction and artificially skewing the flatband voltage (Vfb) shift calculations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Quasi-static ramp rates must be strictly constrained between 10 mV/s and 50 mV/s to maintain true thermodynamic equilibrium displacement currents (I = C * dV/dt in the 100 fA to 10 pA range) while staying comfortably above the preamplifier noise floor (50 fA). An overly fast ramp introduces non-equilibrium deep depletion, whereas an excessively slow ramp integrates excessive chuck leakage currents, causing false interface trap density (Dit) humps near midgap.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Micro-chamber triaxial probe needles (BeCu or Tungsten-Rhenium with 10 um tip radius), semi-rigid low-noise triax cables, and dry N2 purge gas regulator manifolds are single-source components from FormFactor and Keysight. Spares must be inventoried on-site at the Fab/ATE lab to prevent multi-week qualification bottlenecks in the event of probe tip contamination or cable microphonic degradation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Execution of High-Frequency and Quasi-Static C-V profiling directly gates the Post-HTOL parametric drift sign-off milestone. Probe station availability, wafer transfer logistics from the burn-in ovens to the nitrogen-purged Faraday test enclosure, and automated MATLAB/Python extraction script execution must be scheduled in a synchronized 4-hour qualification window to prevent moisture absorption and spurious oxide re-passivation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Quasi-static displacement current obscured by triaxial leakage current (> 100 fA) due to micro-scratches on probe insulation or unshielded chuck grounding.
1. High-frequency 1 MHz series resistance roll-off causing false low-accumulation capacitance reading, leading to overestimation of Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT).
1. Moisture-induced surface conduction across unpassivated scribe-line test pads yielding artificial hysteresis and pseudo-Dit states during bidirectional voltage sweeps.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Land low-leakage Kelvin probes onto the 100 um x 100 um gate oxide MOSCAP pad and adjacent substrate tap. 2. Apply 30 mV RMS AC test signal at 1.0 MHz. 3. Sweep DC gate bias from -1.8 V (accumulation for p-substrate/NMOSCAP) to +1.8 V (inversion) in 20 mV increments with 100 ms hold time per step. 4. Measure parallel capacitance Cp and conductance Gp. 5. Extract maximum accumulation capacitance Cox_acc at Vg = -1.8 V and compute EOT using standard dielectric constant eps_ox = 3.9. | `Cox_acc must equal 8.63 fF/um2 +/- 0.43 fF/um2 (equivalent to tox = 4.0 nm +/- 0.2 nm for nominal 1.8V thin-gate oxide). Series resistance corrected dissipation factor D = Gp / (omega * Cp) must remain < 0.05 across the accumulation region.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-3-2-2-02` | **Combined High-Low Frequency C-V Interface Trap Density (Dit) & Vfb Drift Profiling** | Keithley 4200A-SCS equipped with 4210-CVU (High Frequency 1 MHz) and dual 4200-PA High-Purity PreAmps (Quasi-Static Ramp Mode) coupled to a Temptronic ThermoChuck inside a grounded Faraday enclosure. | 1. Perform High-Frequency (1 MHz) C-V sweep from -1.8 V to +1.8 V and record C_HF(Vg). 2. Switch matrix to High-Purity PreAmps without lifting probes. 3. Flatband voltage drift |Delta_Vfb| must be <= 35 mV relative to pristine pre-burn-in wafer sort baseline.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe conductive lab coat with grounded wrist strap, Static-dissipative cleanroom safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Nitrogen asphyxiation: Move victim immediately to fresh air; if not breathing, initiate CPR and administer supplemental oxygen via certified personnel. IPA skin/eye exposure: Flush affected area with copious laminar flow water from cleanroom eyewash station for at least 15 minutes; seek medical attention if irritation persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober micro-chamber local exhaust ventilation (LEV) maintaining continuous negative pressure with face velocity >= 100 FPM; ambient cleanroom O2 sensor alarms calibrated to sound strobe and horn if oxygen concentration drops below 19.5% vol.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA-soaked micro-swabs and lint-free wipes must be sealed in designated airtight, antistatic flammables disposal bins and routed to licensed solvent reclamation; depleted purge cylinders returned to supplier under certified vendor take-back protocols.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-HTOL stressed wafer unmounted from burn-in boards, solvent-rinsed (spin-rinse dried), pristine dry aluminum/silicide pad surfaces free of organic burn-in residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: C-V profiled wafer with scrub-inspected probe marks (< 15% pad area consumption), purged dry under inert N2, ready for automated retention time screening.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture and atmospheric hydrocarbon chemisorption onto exposed thin gate oxides causing passivated dangling bond reversal, spurious Dit relaxation, and parasitic surface leakage distorting post-HTOL qualification data.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full High-Frequency (1 MHz) and Quasi-Static C-V characterization across 100% designated scribe-line MOSCAP test structures on post-HTOL wafer lots, quantifying oxide capacitance accumulation, EOT stability, Delta_Vfb drift, and midgap interface state density Dit in compliance with JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JEDEC JESD90 standards.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): EOT Extraction, Flatband Voltage ($V_{fb}$) Shift & Post-HTOL Oxide Degradation Analysis

**Module:** Metrology / Post-HTOL Parametric Drift Metrology  
**Node & Architecture:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Target Structures:** Planar MOSCAP Test Structures (Aluminum Gate Dots on thermally grown gate oxide on P-type (100) Si) & Peripheral Access/Charge Pump Dielectric Controls  

---

## 1. Process & Metrology Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Start: Wafer Mount &  │
│     Probe Contact      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  High-Frequency 1 MHz  │
│       C-V Sweep        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Quasi-Static      │
│   Low-Frequency C-V    │
│         Sweep          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Accumulation Cox &   │
│     EOT Extraction     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Flatband Voltage    │
│       V_fb Shift       │
│      Calculation       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Interface Trap     │
│      Density Dit       │
│       Profiling        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Pass/Fail Screening   │
│   vs HTOL Gate Oxide   │
│         Budget         │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step SOP Execution Procedure

### Step 1: Test Structure Selection & Tool Setup
1. Position the post-HTOL wafer onto the temperature-controlled probe station chuck.
2. Select circular Aluminum gate MOSCAP diagnostic structures fabricated with shadow-masked dot diameters of **$200\,\mu\text{m}$**, **$500\,\mu\text{m}$**, or **$1000\,\mu\text{m}$** atop P-type (100) silicon substrate (physical gate oxide baseline: **$3.5\,\text{nm}$ to $25\,\text{nm}$**).
3. Connect the bottom chuck contact to the Gold or Aluminum ohmic backside substrate layer, and land low-leakage Kelvin probes onto the Aluminum gate dot.

### Step 2: High-Frequency (HF, 1 MHz) Capacitance-Voltage Sweep
1. Configure the LCR meter for high-frequency mode at **$f = 1\,\text{MHz}$** with an AC signal amplitude of $15\,\text{mV}_\text{rms}$.
2. Perform a dual-direction bias sweep from strong accumulation ($V_G < V_{fb}$) through depletion ($V_{fb} < V_G < V_T$) into inversion ($V_G > V_T$).
3. Record maximum saturation capacitance in the deep accumulation regime ($C_{ox}$).

### Step 3: Quasi-Static (QS) Low-Frequency Capacitance-Voltage Sweep
1. Configure the quasi-static electrometer / pA-meter using a ramp rate of $10\,\text{mV/s}$ to $50\,\text{mV/s}$ across identical bias ranges.
2. Capture the inversion capacitance recovery curve ($C_{qs}$ recovering toward $C_{ox}$ due to thermal generation-recombination of minority electron carriers).

### Step 4: Parameter Extraction & Post-HTOL Drift Profiling
1. **Physical EOT / Oxide Thickness ($t_{ox}$) Extraction:**
   Extract $t_{ox}$ from HF accumulation capacitance saturation:
   $$C_{ox} = \frac{\varepsilon_{ox} \cdot \varepsilon_0 \cdot \text{Area}}{t_{ox}}$$
2. **Flatband Capacitance ($C_{fb}$) & $V_{fb}$ Determination:**
   Calculate Debye screening length $\lambda_D$ and flatband capacitance $C_{fb}$. Locate $V_{fb}$ on the 1 MHz C-V curve.
3. **$\Delta V_{fb}$ Shift & Trap Density ($D_{it}$) Extraction:**
   Compute the post-HTOL flatband voltage shift relative to pre-stress baseline:
   $$\Delta V_{fb} = V_{fb,\text{post-HTOL}} - V_{fb,\text{pre-stress}}$$
   Determine interface trap density ($D_{it}$) via the HF-QS combined method:
   $$D_{it} = \frac{C_{ox}}{q \cdot \text{Area}} \left( \frac{C_{qs}/C_{ox}}{1 - C_{qs}/C_{ox}} - \frac{C_{hf}/C_{ox}}{1 - C_{hf}/C_{ox}} \right)$$

---

## 3. Parametric Benchmarks & Acceptance Criteria

```text
                      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                      │██████                          │
 Stacked Cap (fF/cell)┤██████                          │
                      │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
         Access L (nm)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
      Pass Vth Min (V)┤▒                               │
                      │▒                               │
EOT Precision (+/- nm)┤░                               │
                      │░                               │
                      └┬───────┬───────┬──────┬───────┬┘
                       0      45      90     135    180 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Extraction Scope & Stress Condition | Target Acceptance Criteria | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Physical Oxide Thickness / EOT Precision** | High-Frequency ($1\,\text{MHz}$) accumulation capacitance ($C_{ox}$) on $200\,\mu\text{m}$, $500\,\mu\text{m}$, or $1000\,\mu\text{m}$ dot | **$\pm 0.1$** (within nominal $3.5$ to $25$) | $\text{nm}$ |
| **Access Transistor $V_{th}$ Margin Stability** | Post-HTOL threshold voltage verification for NMOS pass gate ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$) | **$0.5 \le V_{th} \le 0.7$** | $\text{V}$ |
| **Cell Storage Dielectric Integrity** | Minimum stacked storage capacitor capacitance budget (crown / MIM ONO / high-$k$) | **$\ge 28$** | $\text{fF/cell}$ |
| **Cell Leakage Current Budget** | Access subthreshold + junction + dielectric leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain refresh interval | **$\le 1$** | $\text{fA/cell}$ |

---

## 4. Context References Cited

- **Stage 2 Reality Gate: Planar MOS Capacitor C-V Profiling & Dit Extraction**: Test structure geometries (Aluminum gate dot diameters: $200\,\mu\text{m}$, $500\,\mu\text{m}$, $1000\,\mu\text{m}$ on P-type (100) Si with Au/Al backside contact), gate oxide thickness range ($3.5\,\text{nm}$ to $25\,\text{nm}$), accumulation extraction $C_{ox} = (\varepsilon_{ox}\varepsilon_0 \cdot \text{Area}) / t_{ox}$ providing precision of $\pm 0.1\,\text{nm}$, and 1 MHz vs Quasi-Static depletion/inversion dynamics.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: 180nm unit cell geometry ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$), stacked capacitor requirements ($\ge 28\,\text{fF/cell}$), and post-stress leakage ceiling ($\le 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
- **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**: Pass transistor baseline threshold voltage bounds ($V_{th} \sim 0.5\,\text{V}$ to $0.7\,\text{V}$) under boosted wordline conditions ($V_{PP} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}$ to $2.8\,\text{V}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In 180nm DRAM architectures, sense amplifier offset voltages and restore margins are tightly dependent on cross-coupled PMOS/NMOS threshold stability. Degradation in gate oxide EOT and flatband voltage (V_fb) shift directly induces mismatch in regenerative latch pairs (delta V_th > 15 mV), collapsing destructive read restoration dynamics and degrading retention times across wordline pass-gates and peripheral logic under HTOL thermal-voltage acceleration.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-frequency (100 kHz - 1 MHz) and quasi-static (QS) C-V profiling on dedicated scribe-line planar MOSCAP test structures must accurately decouple quantum mechanical confinement and polysilicon gate depletion effects from physical SiO2/SiON thickness. Flatband voltage shifts exceeding +/- 50 mV post-HTOL indicate excessive positive charge buildup (hole trapping) or negative fixed oxide charge generation (Delta Q_f/q > 5.0e10 cm^-2) and unacceptable midgap interface state creation (Delta D_it > 1.0e11 cm^-2 eV^-1) via silicon dangling bond depassivation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Metrology throughput is bottlenecked by quasi-static C-V ramp speeds and Kelvin-probed temperature-controlled chucks. Wafer probing must utilize standardized ceramic probe cards with low parasitic cable capacitance (< 1 pF/m) and gold-plated cantilever tips compatible with commercial wafer sort test heads (e.g., Keysight B1500A/B1505A or FormFactor probers) to prevent contact resistance artifacts and supply line delays in high-volume tapeout qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Parametric drift characterization must meet the JEDEC JESD22-A108 and JESD91 qualification schedule without triggering unplanned post-stress bake delays. Metrology execution is budgeted for <= 48 hours post-HTOL chamber unload to guarantee valid room-temperature relaxation kinetics before transient positive charge annealing skews qualification signoff records.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Room-temperature unstable charge detrapping/annealing during excessive Q-time post-HTOL, masking true operational flatband shift (Delta V_fb) and skewing JEDEC qualification pass/fail determinations.
1. Excessive midgap interface trap generation (D_it > 1.0e11 cm^-2 eV^-1) causing gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL) and threshold drift in cross-coupled sense amp restore transistors, leading to catastrophic DRAM retention failure.
1. Substrate series resistance (R_s) or cable parasitic capacitance distortion shifting accumulation capacitance (C_ox), leading to false EOT calculation errors greater than +/- 0.3 nm.

# Standard Operating Procedure: DRAM Array Pause-Refresh Retention Time Screening & Fail-Bit Mapping

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The pause-refresh retention time characterization scheme must cleanly decouple junction leakage (I_sub / band-to-band tunneling) from access transistor subthreshold leakage (V_th roll-off at elevated temperature) and ONO/high-k dielectric tunneling. At 180nm with C_s ~ 28 fF and C_b ~ 180 fF (C_b/C_s ~ 6.4:1), signal margin Delta_V is nominal VDD/2 * (Cs / (Cs + Cb)) approx 121 mV for VDD=1.8V. When testing pause retention up to 64ms-500ms at 85°C post-HTOL, thermal drift of sense amplifier offset voltages (V_os) will compound storage node decay. The tester instrumentation must control chuck temperature uniformity to <= +/-0.5°C across the array footprint to avoid misclassifying spatial thermal gradients as localized retention fail clusters.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Post-HTOL pause-refresh retention characterization must account for Variable Retention Time (VRT) phenomena induced by metastable trap generation in the depletion region of the storage-node W-plug junction contact. Standard single-pass pause-refresh screening often misses anomalous trap-assisted leakage states that flip between high-leakage and low-leakage states over time. Testing must implement multiple dynamic pause cycles across checkerboard, solid '1'/'0', and march patterns with variable pause windows (from 16ms up to 256ms at 85°C) to capture both static tail bits and dynamically switching VRT bits before committing fail-bit repair solutions to electrical fuse (eFuse) redundancy.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Automated Test Equipment (ATE) test time per die scales exponentially with prolonged pause-refresh hold intervals (e.g. cumulative hold times of 200ms+ multiplied by pattern count across 100% array bit count). For open-source 180nm MPW tapeouts with restricted packaging and test budgets, dedicated high-density ATE platforms (such as Advantest T5375/T5830 or Teradyne Magnum) require optimized multi-site parallel testing (minimum x32 or x64 DUT parallel testing) and logarithmic pause-time sampling to avoid test socket cost bottlenecks while preserving qualification yields.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test coverage and fail-bit mapping directly govern post-HTOL reliability yield signoff and laser/eFuse redundancy allocation. The fail-bit cartography must feed directly into the repair analysis algorithm (KLA-Tencor / Klarf or ATE proprietary bit-mapping format) to confirm that total single-bit, row, and column failures do not exceed redundant element capacity (typically 2-4 spare rows and columns per 512k sub-array block in 180nm design rules) within the planned tapeout timeline.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Variable Retention Time (VRT) tail-bit instability caused by silicon lattice vacancies and point defect traps near the storage-node n+/p-well junction depletion boundary switching under electric fields.
1. Post-HTOL subthreshold leakage acceleration due to negative bias temperature instability (NBTI) or hot-carrier degradation shifting the wordline access transistor threshold voltage (Vth) lower at high temperatures.
1. Dielectric leakage through degraded ONO / Ta2O5 capacitor stacks resulting from pinhole micro-breakdown during dynamic HTOL thermal-voltage overstress.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-3-3-01` | **Post-HTOL Array Pause-Refresh Retention Time Characterization & Tail-Bit Distribution at 85C** | Advantest T5830 / Teradyne UltraFLEX Memory ATE with high-precision parametric measurement unit (PMU), dual programmable pattern generator (ALPG), and Temptronic ThermoStream chuck controller (-40C to +125C, +/-0.2C stability). | 1. Write Solid '1' pattern to all memory cell locations (180nm 1T1C array, Cs=28 fF nominal) at 85C. 2. Halt automated refresh cycles and assert pause state for programmed retention interval t_pause stepped logarithmically: 16ms, 32ms, 64ms, 128ms, 256ms, and 512ms. 3. Upon pause expiration, execute high-speed burst read of entire array at JEDEC SDR/DDR-200 timing (tCK=10ns) without pre-read refresh. 4. Log bit fail coordinates (X, Y address, bank, I/O) into ATE failure buffer memory (FBM) for each pause step. 5. Invert background data to Solid '0', repeat steps 1 through 4, and record bit inversion failures. | `Array retention time t_RET at cumulative bit error rate (BER) <= 1e-6 must exceed >= 64 ms at 85.0C. Cumulative fail bits at t_pause = 64 ms must not exceed redundant row/column repair capacity (< 0.05% total array bits).` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-2-3-3-02` | **Dynamic Variable Retention Time (VRT) Screening & High-Resolution Bit-Fail Cartography** | Memory ATE with algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG), Real-Time Error Catch RAM (ECR), bit-mapping visualization software, and automated thermal chamber. | 1. Load physical Checkerboard pattern (CKBD) into memory array. 2. Apply repetitive retention stress loop: write pattern, pause 100 ms with refresh disabled, burst read array, log fail locations into Error Catch RAM. 3. Repeat the write-pause-read sequence for 1,000 continuous stress cycles at 85C to capture stochastic bit flips. 4. Classify fail bits into: Static Retention Fails (failing 100% of cycles), Dynamic VRT Fails (failing intermittently between 1% and 99% of cycles), and Soft Coupling Fails. 5. Export rasterized fail-bit map containing X-Y physical coordinates, associated bitline pair (BL/BL#), and sub-array block identifier. | `Total intermittent VRT fail bits must constitute <= 0.005% (50 ppm) of total array cells. 100% of detected static and dynamic fail bits must be routable to available on-chip spare repair elements with zero unrepairable orthogonal cluster failures.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protection gloves rated for -50C to +150C handling, ESD-safe lab coat (surface resistivity 10^6 - 10^9 ohms/sq), Safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1 certified), Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn: Immediately immerse affected area in clean, cold water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly. IPA skin exposure: Flush skin with soap and running water for 15 minutes. IPA eye contact: Irrigate eyes immediately at plumbed eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. N2 asphyxiation risk: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen or CPR if breathing has stopped.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: ATE thermal head exhaust ducting maintaining minimum face velocity of 100 LFPM (0.5 m/s); test station ambient ventilation with continuous room air changes >= 12 ACH and integrated ambient O2 depletion monitors calibrated to alarm at < 19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Wetted IPA wipes and solvent residues must be deposited in dedicated, grounded, self-closing UL-listed flammable waste containers and disposed of in compliance with local hazardous organic waste regulations; no direct sink disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, ATE thermal chuck/socket cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2, test chamber purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-HTOL unencapsulated ceramic or open-cavity package with clean gold/aluminum wire bonds; lead frame and contact pads free of thermal oxidation and organic contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically screened and mapped die/package with pristine contact pads, vacuum-sealed in ESD-safe dry pack with active desiccant and humidity indicator card (HIC < 10% RH).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric moisture absorption into exposed package die-attach interfaces and bond wire pads causing corrosion, intermetallic Kirkendall voiding, or package popcorn delamination during subsequent temperature cycling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Comprehensive post-HTOL DRAM retention time metrology and fail-bit mapping validating that the 180nm 1T1C open-source memory array satisfies JEDEC SDR/DDR 64ms pause-refresh specification at 85C, identifying static leakage defects and VRT tail bits, and outputting actionable redundancy repair solutions.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM_Gen3_PostHTOL_Retention_Weibull_Dist_85C.csv`
- [ ] `FailBit_Cartography_Physical_Coordinate_Map.pdf`
- [ ] `ATE_Redundancy_Repair_Allocation_Solution.xml`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Array pause-refresh retention time at 85C for 99.9999% of storage cells (cumulative fail probability <= 1 ppm)** | `>= 64.0` | +/- 2.0 ms measurement accuracy | Automated stepped pause-refresh scan (16ms to 512ms) on Advantest T5830 ATE at 85.0C with ALPG pattern execution. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Storage node junction plus dielectric leakage current per cell at 85C derived from retention retention slope** | `<= 1.0` | +/- 0.15 fA/cell | Calculated via I_leak = Cs * (Delta_V / t_pause) where Cs=28 fF and Delta_V threshold is determined by sense amp trip voltage. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Total post-HTOL fail bits repairable by redundant spare rows and columns across all tested dies** | `100.0` | 0.0% unrepairable dies permitted within qualification lot | ATE bit-map engine running 2D row/column repair optimization algorithm matching spare elements defined in 180nm PDK. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researchers achieve signoff when all qualification dies show >= 64ms retention at 85C with post-repair functional yield >= 98.0%, zero unallocated orthogonal bit failures, and completion of full VRT characterization across 1,000 cycles with signed approval from Domain Expert and Systems Engineer.
