# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## ATE Multi-Site Loadboard Docking & Calibration for Post-Stress DDR

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│    ATE Multi-Site    │
│       Docking        │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│     Direct-Dock      │
│      Actuation       │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│     Loopback TDR     │
│     Calibration      │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Pogo Pin & Contact  │
│     Verification     │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Post-Stress JEDEC   │
│   Shmoo Margining    │
│                      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Mechanical Loadboard Alignment & Direct Docking**:
   - Inspect the multi-site ATE loadboard interface and direct-dock latching cam mechanisms for planar seating.
   - Secure the multi-site DUT loadboard onto the ATE test head receiver ring with uniform pneumatic docking force (parallel co-planarity variance $\le 25\ \mu\text{m}$ across all test sites).
2. **Channel-to-Channel TDR & Deskew Calibration**:
   - Execute automated Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) and deskew routines using the internal calibration fixture.
   - Normalize propagation delays across all differential clock ($CK / \overline{CK}$), command/address ($CA$), and data strobe/bit ($DQS / DQ$) channels to eliminate loadboard PCB trace skew down to $\le 15\text{ ps}$.
3. **Pogo Pin & Interconnect Continuity / Contact Resistance Verification**:
   - Drive calibrated parametric measurement units (PMUs) across all pogo pins into the golden calibration loopback coupon.
   - Verify contact path resistance integrity to ensure it does not compromise the baseline interconnect budget ($R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$ derived from the 350 nm Metal-1 BEOL Al-0.5% Cu interconnect line target).
4. **Thermal Soak & Chamber Stabilization**:
   - Interface the test chamber / thermal forcing unit with the docked loadboard.
   - Ramp and soak the post-HTOL stress DUT units at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to perform temperature-accelerated DRAM leakage and margin tests.
5. **Multi-Site Baseline Shmoo Execution**:
   - Launch calibrated parallel multi-site JEDEC DDR parametric functional sweeps (Voltage: $V_{DD}$ vs. Frequency: $t_{CK}$) to detect post-stress retention degradation and cell leakage.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
            Acceptance Criteria & Physical Baselines    
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │░                                            │
  BEOL Rs┤░                                            │
         │▒▒                                           │
  Leakage┤▒▒                                           │
Retention┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
         │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
 Cell Cap┤████████████████████                         │
         │████████████████████                         │
         └┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬┘
          0         16         32         48         64 
```

| Parameter Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 28$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Stacked MIM/Crown capacitor with $\kappa > 15$ |
| **Cell Leakage Current ($I_{leak}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Sub-threshold & junction leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Data Retention Refresh Interval ($t_{REF}$)** | $> 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | Measured at $85^\circ\text{C}$ post-stress |
| **Interconnect Metal-1 Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | $\Omega/\Box$ | Planar DC sputtering Al-0.5% Cu (350 nm thickness $\pm 5\%$) |

---

### 3. Citations of Literature Context

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Cell geometry: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage capacitor target: Minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ with triple ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-$k$ stack ($\kappa > 15$).
  - Leakage requirement: Sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - 1T1C stacked capacitor architecture ($8F^2$ or $6F^2$) requiring $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$ to guarantee data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - Film thickness target for Metal-1 is $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$.
  - Sheet resistance specification post-anneal ($400^\circ\text{C}$ forming gas $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ 95/5}$): $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$.

---

> [!NOTE]
> Micro-knowledge for this procedure has been persisted to [ate_loadboard_docking_calibration.md](./docs/ate_loadboard_docking_calibration.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Docking multi-site ATE loadboards requires precise mechanical planarity and coplanarity across all test sockets (<= 25 um across a 4-site board) under 150 kgf total pogo-pin contact force. The manipulator kinematic docking mechanism must maintain sub-mil positional repeatability without inducing bending strain on the Rogers/FR4 hybrid high-speed PCB, which causes characteristic impedance detuning and pogo-pin misalignment during high-temperature thermal transitions (up to 125 deg C).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Post-stress HTOL DDR speed-binning requires dynamic TDR/TDT calibration directly at the DUT socket solder pad interface to de-embed loadboard trace insertion loss (S21 > -1.5 dB at 200 MHz/400 Mbps) and channel-to-channel timing skew (< 15 ps across DQ/DQS pairs). Failure to perform precise loopback and golden-unit AC/DC calibration causes erroneous Shmoo margin shrinkage, misclassifying legitimate silicon recovery or gate-oxide breakdown degradation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement of custom multi-site high-frequency coaxial loadboards and high-cycle Kelvin pogo-pin sockets (rated > 500,000 actuations at 125 deg C) carries an 8 to 12-week lead time. Sourcing secondary multi-site docking interface hardware compatible with legacy Teradyne/Advantest platforms is constrained by specialized fabrication vendors in East Asia, necessitating immediate buffer stock of pogo blocks and stiffener backplates.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The multi-site docking and calibration milestone gates the critical path between packaging/burn-in completion and production yield classification. A slip in loadboard planarization or calibration verification shifts final JEDEC qualification by 3 weeks, running up $1,200/hour ATE chamber idle costs. Daily calibration run-charts and socket contact resistance monitors must be enforced.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Contact resistance instability (R_contact > 50 mOhm) induced by pogo-pin tip contamination from solder migration during post-HTOL testing, causing false VDD/VSS ground bounce and DDR timing violations.
1. Mechanical PCB deflection under high-density pogo pin spring force leading to micro-cracking of internal stripline impedance traces (Z0 shifting outside 50 +/- 3 Ohm).
1. Thermal expansion mismatch between the aluminum docking ring and organic multi-layer PCB resulting in docking lock pin binding and multi-site channel deskew drift during hot-socketing.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-1-01` | **Multi-Site High-Frequency Docking Planarity and TDR Channel Impedance Calibration** | Automated Multi-Channel TDR/TDT Scope (20 GHz bandwidth), High-Precision Dial Indicator Gauge Rig (0.5 um resolution), Multi-Site Calibration Substrate (Gold-plated Short-Open-Load-Thru). | 1. Mount mechanical dial indicator array at the 4 corners and center of the 4-site docking stiffener and measure mechanical coplanarity displacement under full docking clamp engagement. 2. Connect automated TDR pulse generator (rise time <= 25 ps) sequentially to all 64 DDR DQ/DQS channel lines across all 4 sites. 3. Acquire reflected waveform profile from pogo-pin tips using SOLT standards. 4. Extract characteristic differential and single-ended trace impedance and channel propagation delay. 5. Log inter-channel skew and coplanarity variance. | `Mechanical coplanarity across all 4 socket locations <= 25.0 um; single-ended characteristic impedance Z0 = 50.0 Ohm +/- 2.5 Ohm; inter-channel propagation delay skew across DQ/DQS bus per site <= 15.0 ps.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-1-02` | **Post-Stress Kelvin Contact Resistance and DC Continuity Loopback Verification** | ATE High-Density Precision Source Measure Unit (SMU) matrix (10 nA to 100 mA, 1 uV resolution), Four-Wire Kelvin Shorting Verification Unit (CSVU). | 1. Force 10.0 mA DC current through force lines of VDD, VDDQ, VSS, and all 16 I/O pins per site. 2. Measure corresponding voltage drop across sense lines using SMU four-wire Kelvin mode. 3. Cycle socket latch mechanism 10 times to verify mechanical contact repeatability. 4. Calculate contact resistance (R_contact) for each pin. 5. Measure pin-to-pin leakage current under 1.8V reverse bias on adjacent pins. | `Kelvin contact resistance R_contact <= 35.0 mOhm for all signal pins and <= 15.0 mOhm for power pins; contact resistance delta across 10 insertions <= 5.0 mOhm; adjacent pin leakage current <= 1.0 nA at 1.8V DC.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ESD-safe conductive nitrile gloves (Class 0 ESD protection), ANSI Z87.1 approved side-shield safety glasses, ESD-safe lab coat with conductive carbon grid fibers, Static-dissipative safety shoes with heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated garments. Inhalation: Relocate individual to fresh outdoor air immediately; provide artificial respiration or supplemental oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth with water and seek immediate medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Perform solvent-based pogo-pin tip cleaning and socket degreasing inside a certified Class II Type A2 laminar flow chemical hood with minimum face velocity of 100 linear feet per minute (0.5 m/s); maintain test bay ambient air exchange >= 12 ACH with HEPA filtration.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent isopropyl alcohol and contact cleaning wipes in dedicated, grounded, flame-proof hazardous solvent waste drums clearly labeled 'Flammable Solvent Waste - Halogenated/Non-Halogenated Mixture'. Dispose of via licensed hazardous chemical disposal contractors in compliance with regional environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Grade 1) | `99.9%` |
| **Electronic Contact Cleaner / Hydrofluoroether** | `163702-07-6` | Technical / Electronic Grade | `>= 99.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly unloaded post-HTOL burn-in packages with pristine solder ball/lead finish; unoxidized gold-plated ATE loadboard socket contacts clean of flux or organic residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Clean, unmarred DUT leads/balls docked to calibrated test socket; calibrated multi-site ATE receiver interface ready for immediate automated test execution under dry nitrogen ambient purge.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure to ambient humidity exceeds moisture absorption threshold, accelerating galvanic micro-corrosion and copper/tin oxidation on package leads and pogo tips, causing contact resistance spikes (> 100 mOhm) and erroneous high-frequency signal attenuation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full multi-site docking alignment, mechanical planarity verification, and high-frequency RF/DC calibration of the 4-site ATE loadboard successfully completed, demonstrating sub-15 ps channel timing skew and stable sub-35 mOhm Kelvin contact resistance across all sites.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ATE_Loadboard_Docking_Planarity_Report_Site1_4.pdf`
- [ ] `TDR_TDT_Channel_Deskew_Calibration_Matrix.csv`
- [ ] `Kelvin_Contact_Resistance_Repeatability_Log.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Loadboard mechanical coplanarity across all active test sockets under full docking pressure** | `18.5 um` | +/- 6.5 um | Multi-point dial indicator mechanical displacement gauge measurement across 4 docking quadrants. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Worst-case DDR DQ/DQS trace-to-trace propagation delay skew per test site after de-embedding** | `10.5 ps` | +/- 4.5 ps | Automated 20 GHz TDR channel step reflection delay extraction using calibrated SOLT substrate. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum four-wire Kelvin contact resistance for all signal pogo-pin lines across 10 repeated dock cycles** | `24.0 mOhm` | +/- 8.0 mOhm | Four-wire SMU matrix continuity sweep at 10.0 mA DC across all 64 pins per socket site. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 4 socket sites achieve 100% DC Kelvin continuity with R_contact <= 35.0 mOhm, channel-to-channel timing skew <= 15.0 ps, mechanical coplanarity <= 25.0 um, and zero open/short anomalies on golden calibration reference units across 10 successive automated docking cycles.

testcases.pre_conditions: Thermal chamber preheated to 85 deg C; CSVU installed in Socket Sites 1 through 4; loadboard docked and latched with 100% pin engagement.
testcases.procedure: 1. Force 10.0 mA DC current through force lines of VDD, VDDQ, VSS, and all 16 I/O pins per site. 2. Measure corresponding voltage drop across sense lines using SMU four-wire Kelvin mode. 3. Cycle socket latch mechanism 10 times to verify mechanical contact repeatability. 4. Calculate contact resistance (R_contact) for each pin. 5. Measure pin-to-pin leakage current under 1.8V reverse bias on adjacent pins.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Kelvin contact resistance R_contact <= 35.0 mOhm for all signal pins and <= 15.0 mOhm for power pins; contact resistance delta across 10 insertions <= 5.0 mOhm; adjacent pin leakage current <= 1.0 nA at 1.8V DC.

ppe_required: ESD-safe conductive nitrile gloves (Class 0 ESD protection)
ANSI Z87.1 approved side-shield safety glasses
ESD-safe lab coat with conductive carbon grid fibers
Static-dissipative safety shoes with heel grounders
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye contact: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated garments. Inhalation: Relocate individual to fresh outdoor air immediately; provide artificial respiration or supplemental oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth with water and seek immediate medical attention.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Perform solvent-based pogo-pin tip cleaning and socket degreasing inside a certified Class II Type A2 laminar flow chemical hood with minimum face velocity of 100 linear feet per minute (0.5 m/s); maintain test bay ambient air exchange >= 12 ACH with HEPA filtration.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Collect spent isopropyl alcohol and contact cleaning wipes in dedicated, grounded, flame-proof hazardous solvent waste drums clearly labeled 'Flammable Solvent Waste - Halogenated/Non-Halogenated Mixture'. Dispose of via licensed hazardous chemical disposal contractors in compliance with regional environmental regulations.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly unloaded post-HTOL burn-in packages with pristine solder ball/lead finish; unoxidized gold-plated ATE loadboard socket contacts clean of flux or organic residue.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Clean, unmarred DUT leads/balls docked to calibrated test socket; calibrated multi-site ATE receiver interface ready for immediate automated test execution under dry nitrogen ambient purge.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exposure to ambient humidity exceeds moisture absorption threshold, accelerating galvanic micro-corrosion and copper/tin oxidation on package leads and pogo tips, causing contact resistance spikes (> 100 mOhm) and erroneous high-frequency signal attenuation.

expected_result.summary: Full multi-site docking alignment, mechanical planarity verification, and high-frequency RF/DC calibration of the 4-site ATE loadboard successfully completed, demonstrating sub-15 ps channel timing skew and stable sub-35 mOhm Kelvin contact resistance across all sites.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Loadboard mechanical coplanarity across all active test sockets under full docking pressure
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-point dial indicator mechanical displacement gauge measurement across 4 docking quadrants.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Worst-case DDR DQ/DQS trace-to-trace propagation delay skew per test site after de-embedding
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated 20 GHz TDR channel step reflection delay extraction using calibrated SOLT substrate.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum four-wire Kelvin contact resistance for all signal pogo-pin lines across 10 repeated dock cycles
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Four-wire SMU matrix continuity sweep at 10.0 mA DC across all 64 pins per socket site.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: All 4 socket sites achieve 100% DC Kelvin continuity with R_contact <= 35.0 mOhm, channel-to-channel timing skew <= 15.0 ps, mechanical coplanarity <= 25.0 um, and zero open/short anomalies on golden calibration reference units across 10 successive automated docking cycles.

# Standard Operating Procedure: JEDEC Speed-Binning Test Pattern Vector Execution (tCK, tRCD, tRP)

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Pattern vector synchronization across high-speed digital pin electronics (PE) on the Advantest V93000/Teradyne UltraFLEX must maintain round-trip flight-time (TDR) calibration within +/-15 ps across all DQ/DQS channels. When characterizing 180nm DRAM access latencies (tCK=6.0ns for DDR-333, tRCD=18ns, tRP=18ns), ground bounce and VDD power distribution network (PDN) droop on the device under test (DUT) loadboard can induce spurious jitter, artificially widening the apparent setup/hold window and leading to false speed-bin classification.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm planar node dimensions, sense amplifier sensing speed (t_sense) and bitline precharge RC constant dominate tRCD and tRP margins. Test vector patterns must execute marching (March C-) and pseudo-random data sequences (PRBS-7) combined with row-hammer/disturb patterns to stress the bitline sense amplifier differential offset. Inadequate settling time on VBLP (half-VDD bitline precharge level) during rapid PRECHARGE-to-ACTIVATE vector transitions will degrade the observed tRP by upwards of 2.4 ns.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-speed socket contacts (pogo pin arrays with >12 GHz bandwidth) and load boards for low-volume 180nm MPW packaging have an 8 to 12 week lead time and degrade after approximately 50,000 insertions. Pin contact resistance drifts above 120 mOhm skew parametric timing measurements, necessitating automated contact-check pre-tests and periodic socket cleaning with isopropyl alcohol to maintain bin yield integrity.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test time per unit directly dictates the post-stress qualification burn-in throughput and economic viability. Running comprehensive multi-corner shmoo sweeps across VDD (1.7V to 1.9V) and junction temperature (0C to 85C) can consume over 45 seconds per die. Test patterns must be optimized into segmented binary searches (bracketing search) rather than linear sweeps to compress ATE execution time below 3.5 seconds per packaged DUT.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Tester DQS strobing phase misalignment leading to false tCK min binning rejections due to uncompensated DUT PCB trace impedance mismatch.
1. Sense amplifier latch meta-stability during marginal tRCD vector execution causing localized single-bit flips that masquerade as retention leakage.
1. Thermal runaway during high-frequency burst execution under elevated VDD (1.95V) without active thermal socket feedback control.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-2-01` | **JEDEC Minimum Clock Cycle (tCK_min) Shmoo Characterization and Speed-Binning** | Advantest V93000 SmarTest ATE system equipped with Pin Scale 1600 Digital Channels, high-speed active socket card (TDR calibrated +/-10ps), Keysight Infiniium 33GHz oscilloscope for waveform cross-validation, and Temptronic ThermoStream thermal forced-air controller. | 1. Initialize DUT via standard JEDEC power-up sequence and load Extended Mode Registers (EMRS) configuring CAS Latency CL=3. 2. Set ATE pin electronics VOH/VOL threshold to 0.90V (mid-rail reference). 3. Apply continuous Burst Length 8 (BL8) read/write vectors using March C- data patterns. 4. Step clock cycle time (tCK) from 7.50 ns down to 4.50 ns in 50 ps decrements while stepping VDD from 1.60V to 2.00V in 25 mV increments. 5. Record functional pass/fail status per coordinate to construct 2D shmoo plot. 6. Determine critical transition boundary where bit error rate (BER) exceeds 1e-12. | `tCK_min <= 6.00 ns at VDD = 1.80V (+/-5%) and Tj = 85.0C across 100% address space (qualifying for DDR-333 operation) with zero hard/soft bit errors. Fail if tCK_min > 6.00 ns or if timing jitter window exceeds 180 ps.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-2-02` | **Row-to-Column Delay (tRCD) and Row Precharge Time (tRP) Margin Verification** | Advantest V93000 ATE with integrated high-density digital vector engine, programmable algorithmic pattern generator (APG), high-current DC VI sources, and high-frequency active coaxial probe interfaces. | 1. Issue PRECHARGE command to bank 0. 2. Sweep tRP delay interval from 24.0 ns down to 12.0 ns in 200 ps increments before issuing ACTIVATE command. 3. Sweep tRCD delay interval between ACTIVATE and subsequent READ/WRITE command from 24.0 ns down to 12.0 ns in 200 ps increments. 4. Execute multi-bank interleaved access pattern with checkerboard data (0xAA/0x55) followed by inverse checkerboard. 5. Monitor DQ output bus on ATE strobe for valid data capture matching expected pattern. 6. Extract minimum operational tRCD and tRP parameters. | `tRCD <= 18.00 ns and tRP <= 18.00 ns at VDD = 1.70V and Tj = 25.0C. Fail if data corruption occurs at or above 18.00 ns or if sense amp fails to restore cell storage node potential above 95% of VDD.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe dissipative nitrile gloves (Class 0 ESD protection, 4 mil thickness), Anti-static lab coat (surface resistivity 10e6 - 10e9 ohms/sq), Grounding heel/wrist straps connected to calibrated earth bench ground
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with copious clean water for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids apart; obtain medical attention. Skin Contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated garments. Inhalation of Solvent Vapors: Move person to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Thermal/Cold Burn from Thermal Stream: Warm affected tissue gently with lukewarm water (not hot); do not rub; seek immediate medical assessment.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation within Class 10,000 / ISO 7 ATE clean testing bay with dedicated point-of-use local exhaust ventilation (LEV) providing minimum face velocity of 100 ft/min (0.51 m/s) over socket cleaning and thermal stream exhaust zones.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free cleaning wipes and solvent residues must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-resistant safety waste receptacles and disposed of via licensed hazardous chemical solvent incinerator services in accordance with RCRA/local environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C12) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly unloaded post-HTOL stress burn-in packaged DRAM units, dry, mechanically undamaged, leadframes/balls free of flux residue and intermetallic discoloration.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically classified and speed-binned packages, contacts inspected and free of pogo-pin score indentation damage exceeding 15 um, packed in vacuum-sealed moisture barrier bags (MBB) with desiccant and HIC.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into plastic mold compound (MSL 3 degradation) causing micro-delamination and internal popcorning during high-temperature thermal cycling or electrical testing, accompanied by surface oxidation on leadframe contact pads causing intermittent ATE pin-contact false opens.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful automated execution of JEDEC timing vector suites (tCK, tRCD, tRP) across corner voltages and temperatures on 180nm DRAM prototypes, establishing empirical speed bins (DDR-266, DDR-333) and validating robust sense amplifier and core timing margins.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `JEDEC_SpeedBin_Shmoo_Characterization_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `ATE_Vector_Execution_Raw_Dataview_Log.csv`
- [ ] `Post_Stress_Timing_Margin_Distribution_Chart.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Minimum clock period (tCK_min) achieves target DDR-333 specifications under nominal voltage and maximum operating junction temperature.** | `6.00 ns` | +0.00 ns / -0.50 ns | Automated V93000 frequency shmoo sweep with 50 ps resolution at VDD=1.80V, Tj=85C |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Row-to-column access latency (tRCD) satisfies JEDEC DDR standard requirements under worst-case low core supply voltage.** | `18.00 ns` | +0.00 ns / -1.20 ns | Algorithmic Pattern Generator marching vector delay sweep at VDD=1.70V, Tj=25C |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Row precharge duration (tRP) allows complete bitline precharge and sense amp recovery without inducing data bit errors.** | `18.00 ns` | +0.00 ns / -1.00 ns | Fast-page cycle precharge timing step test with inverted checkerboard retention verification |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Minimum of 100 consecutively tested post-HTOL DRAM packages execute full vector suite with zero unrecoverable timing violations, achieving >= 92% yield into DDR-333 bin with bilateral signoff from the Reliability Metrology Lead and ATE Test Engineering Principal.

# Standard Operating Procedure: JEDEC Speed-Bin Digital Pattern Vector Generation and ATE Pin Timing Calibration

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Translating JEDEC DDR-200/333/400 digital timing vector specifications into automated test equipment (ATE) cyclized pattern generators requires stringent de-skewing across all driver pin electronics (PE). At 180nm commercial node operation, transmission line impedance mismatches and round-trip flight times (TDR) across the direct-dock DUT interface board (DIB) introduce channel-to-channel timing skews exceeding 120 ps if pin calibration is omitted. The test head timing generators must maintain master edge placement accuracy of less than +/- 45 ps across all CLK, DQS, DQ, and command pins under simultaneous switching noise (SSN) conditions.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating ATE pin electronics for JEDEC parameters (tCK, tRCD, tRP, tAC, and tDQSCK) requires exact edge-placement referencing against the DUT socket contact plane rather than the internal pogo tower. Using an ATE calibration substrate with planar microstrip calibration structures and high-bandwidth active picoprobe time-domain reflectometry (TDR) is non-negotiable. Pattern loops must include worst-case pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS-7) and row/column address bus transitions to capture supply bounce and rail droop during back-to-back ACTIVATE-to-READ/WRITE cycles.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: ATE tester time on high-pin-count digital systems (Advantest T5588/V93000 or Teradyne UltraFLEX) is extremely cost-intensive, exceeding $120 to $180 per hour. Dedicated RF calibration boards, calibrated pogo pins, and high-frequency coaxial load boards suffer from mechanical wear-out and contact resistance drift after ~25,000 insertions. Replacement spring-pin contacts and certified golden calibration fixtures carry lead times of 8 to 14 weeks from specialized probe/contact vendors.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Pin timing calibration and vector decompilation must be frozen and systematically verified against silicon behavioral simulations prior to allocating dedicated ATE chamber time. Inaccurate vector cyclization or uncalibrated timing sets will yield false binning rejections, skewing yield analysis and causing severe project milestone delays for the 180nm DRAM tapeout qualification phase.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. ATE channel-to-channel edge placement skew (> 100 ps) inducing false setup/hold (tIS/tIH or tDS/tDH) violations and artificial speed-bin downgrade.
1. Transmission line impedance discontinuity on the DIB socket causing signal reflections (> 10% VDD amplitude), ringing, and double-clocking on differential CLK/DQS pins.
1. Thermal drift of ATE pin-driver timing verniers over prolonged speed-binning test runs without periodic auto-deskew recalibration.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-2-1-01` | **ATE Driver/Comparator Pin Timing Deskew and TDR Edge Calibration** | Automated Test Equipment (ATE) High-Speed Digital Pin Electronics Subsystem, Calibrated Golden DIB Calibration Fixture with 50-ohm Precision Terminations, 20 GHz Equivalent-Time Sampling Oscilloscope with TDR Module | 1. Launch automated TDR calibration routine across all 64 ATE digital I/O channels (CLK, /CLK, DQS, DQ0-DQ15, ADDR, CMD). 2. Measure individual pogo-to-socket trace propagation delay and reflection coefficient (rho) at 500 ps edge rate. 3. Execute automated deskew algorithm adjusting programmable driver delay lines (vernier resolution <= 5 ps) to align all driver edges to the socket reference plane at T0 = 0.000 ns. 4. Drive alternating 1010 pattern at 200 MHz and measure channel-to-channel skew across all pins at 50% VDD threshold using the sampling scope. 5. Log edge alignment offsets and calibration polynomial coefficients into tester calibration registry. | `Channel-to-channel edge placement skew across all digital pin channels must be <= +/- 35 ps relative to master CLK; trace impedance discontinuity reflection coefficient rho must be <= 0.05 (|Z0 - 50 ohm| <= 2.5 ohm).` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-2-1-02` | **JEDEC Speed-Bin Vector Pattern Functional Margining (tCK, tRCD, tRP Shmoo)** | ATE High-Speed Pattern Generator with Algorithmic Pattern Generator (ALPG), DUT Contact Socket on Production DIB, Calibrated 180nm Open-Source DRAM Test Vehicle Sample | 1. Load compiled JEDEC DDR speed-bin digital test pattern vectors (ACTIVATE, WRITE, READ, PRECHARGE sequences with PRBS data payload). 2. Configure ALPG timing sets for target DDR-200 / DDR-333 / DDR-400 profiles (tCK = 5.0 ns to 10.0 ns, tRCD = 15.0 ns to 20.0 ns, tRP = 15.0 ns to 20.0 ns). 3. Step tCK in 100 ps increments from 12.0 ns down to 4.5 ns while sweeping VDD from 1.62 V to 1.98 V (Shmoo plot execution). 4. Execute back-to-back ACT-to-READ/WRITE bursts with programmed tRCD parameter stepped in 500 ps increments. 5. Capture pass/fail bitmaps and verify error-free output data strobe (DQS) alignment with read data (DQ) windows. | `Error-free data readback (0 bit fails across 10^7 vector cycles) at nominal VDD (1.80 V) for tCK <= 7.50 ns (DDR-266) with tRCD <= 20.0 ns and tRP <= 20.0 ns; functional Shmoo operating envelope must show >= 150 mV VDD margin at target speed bin.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved anti-glare safety glasses, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat with continuous grounding snap, Cleanroom class 100 nitrile gloves (powder-free, anti-static), Continuous ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor attached to verified earth ground
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin or eye contact with isopropanol cleaner, immediately flush with copious amounts of tempered water for at least 15 minutes. For high-voltage/high-current ATE power supply contact shock, disconnect master interlock immediately, administer CPR if pulse/respiration is absent, and call emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: ATE testing area requires minimum 10 room air changes per hour (ACH) with dedicated localized laminar airflow hood (exhaust velocity 0.45 m/s +/- 0.05 m/s) over manual solvent wipe stations. ATE chassis forced air or liquid chiller loop heat dissipation must vent externally.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and swabs contaminated with isopropanol must be disposed of in dedicated sealed, airtight, grounded flammables disposal containers labeled according to hazardous waste regulations. Wetted wipes must not enter general solid municipal waste streams.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (Electronics Grade / Pogo Contact Cleaner)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Dry, Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 Grade | `99.999%` |

critics.systems_engineer: Translating JEDEC DDR-200/333/400 digital timing vector specifications into automated test equipment (ATE) cyclized pattern generators requires stringent de-skewing across all driver pin electronics (PE). At 180nm commercial node operation, transmission line impedance mismatches and round-trip flight times (TDR) across the direct-dock DUT interface board (DIB) introduce channel-to-channel timing skews exceeding 120 ps if pin calibration is omitted. The test head timing generators must maintain master edge placement accuracy of less than +/- 45 ps across all CLK, DQS, DQ, and command pins under simultaneous switching noise (SSN) conditions.
critics.domain_expert: Calibrating ATE pin electronics for JEDEC parameters (tCK, tRCD, tRP, tAC, and tDQSCK) requires exact edge-placement referencing against the DUT socket contact plane rather than the internal pogo tower. Using an ATE calibration substrate with planar microstrip calibration structures and high-bandwidth active picoprobe time-domain reflectometry (TDR) is non-negotiable. Pattern loops must include worst-case pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS-7) and row/column address bus transitions to capture supply bounce and rail droop during back-to-back ACTIVATE-to-READ/WRITE cycles.
critics.supply_chain: ATE tester time on high-pin-count digital systems (Advantest T5588/V93000 or Teradyne UltraFLEX) is extremely cost-intensive, exceeding $120 to $180 per hour. Dedicated RF calibration boards, calibrated pogo pins, and high-frequency coaxial load boards suffer from mechanical wear-out and contact resistance drift after ~25,000 insertions. Replacement spring-pin contacts and certified golden calibration fixtures carry lead times of 8 to 14 weeks from specialized probe/contact vendors.
critics.laya_pm: Pin timing calibration and vector decompilation must be frozen and systematically verified against silicon behavioral simulations prior to allocating dedicated ATE chamber time. Inaccurate vector cyclization or uncalibrated timing sets will yield false binning rejections, skewing yield analysis and causing severe project milestone delays for the 180nm DRAM tapeout qualification phase.
critical_failure_modes: ATE channel-to-channel edge placement skew (> 100 ps) inducing false setup/hold (tIS/tIH or tDS/tDH) violations and artificial speed-bin downgrade.
Transmission line impedance discontinuity on the DIB socket causing signal reflections (> 10% VDD amplitude), ringing, and double-clocking on differential CLK/DQS pins.
Thermal drift of ATE pin-driver timing verniers over prolonged speed-binning test runs without periodic auto-deskew recalibration.

testcases.instrumentation: Automated Test Equipment (ATE) High-Speed Digital Pin Electronics Subsystem, Calibrated Golden DIB Calibration Fixture with 50-ohm Precision Terminations, 20 GHz Equivalent-Time Sampling Oscilloscope with TDR Module
testcases.pre_conditions: ATE test head thermally stabilized at 25.0 deg C +/- 0.5 deg C for >= 60 minutes; ATE diagnostic self-test passed; Golden calibration fixture docked to ATE test head pogo interface.
testcases.procedure:
1. Launch automated TDR calibration routine across all 64 ATE digital I/O channels (CLK, /CLK, DQS, DQ0-DQ15, ADDR, CMD).
2. Measure individual pogo-to-socket trace propagation delay and reflection coefficient (rho) at 500 ps edge rate.
3. Execute automated deskew algorithm adjusting programmable driver delay lines (vernier resolution <= 5 ps) to align all driver edges to the socket reference plane at T0 = 0.000 ns.
4. Drive alternating 1010 pattern at 200 MHz and measure channel-to-channel skew across all pins at 50% VDD threshold using the sampling scope.
5. Log edge alignment offsets and calibration polynomial coefficients into tester calibration registry.

```text
========================================================================================
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP)
Title: JEDEC DDR Speed-Bin Functional Pattern Synthesis & STIL/WGL Vector Compilation
Module: Metrology & Final ATE Test Engineering / 180nm Open DRAM Foundation VN
Process Node: 180nm CMOS / SKY130 Compatible MPW Tapeout (150 nm Drawn Poly Gate)
Document ID: SOP-DRAM-ATE-MET-003
========================================================================================
```

### 1. Scope & Purpose
This procedure defines the workflow for synthesizing JEDEC DDR functional speed-bin verification patterns (verifying cycle time $t_{CK}$, RAS-to-CAS delay $t_{RCD}$, and row precharge time $t_{RP}$) and compiling them into IEEE 1450 Standard Test Interface Language (STIL) and Waveform Generation Language (WGL) ATE vector formats. It ensures exact physical pin-timing calibration and edge placement compatible with the standard manufacturing grid and cell timing libraries.

---

### 2. Relevant Citations & Technical Context
* **Foundry Rules & Resolution Grid**: *SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid*
  * Physical placement grid resolution: **0.005 µm (5 nm)**.
  * Critical dimension drawn poly gate length: **0.15 µm (150 nm)**; Poly gate spacing: **0.21 µm**.
  * Metal 1 minimum width: **0.14 µm**; Metal 1 pitch: **0.34 µm**.
  * Critical layer lithography: 248 nm KrF excimer laser ($NA = 0.65, k_1 = 0.40$), yielding minimum resolvable half-pitch of **152 nm**; max overlay error: **$\le 35\text{ nm}$**.
* **Physical Implementation & Extraction Toolflow**: *OpenROAD Physical Design & Synthesis Toolflow*
  * RTL-to-GDSII stages: `Floorplanning` $\rightarrow$ `Global Placement` $\rightarrow$ `Detailed Placement` $\rightarrow$ `Clock Tree Synthesis (CTS)` $\rightarrow$ `Detailed Routing` $\rightarrow$ `Chip Finishing` (Parasitic extraction via `OpenRCX`).
* **Timing & Standard Cell Models**: *SkyWater 130nm Open PDK Overview & Architecture*
  * Liberty timing models regenerated via `make timing` across PVT corners for accurate strobe edge derivation.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+---------------------+     +----------------------+     +---------------------+
| RTL/Gate Simulation | --> | Parasitic Annotation | --> | STIL/WGL Vector Gen |
| (JEDEC DDR Vectors) |     | (SPEF via OpenRCX)   |     | & ATE Edge Mapping  |
+---------------------+     +----------------------+     +---------------------+
```

#### Step 3.1: Post-Layout Netlist & Parasitic Extraction Integration
1. Ingest post-route physical signoff netlist generated after OpenROAD `Detailed Routing` and `Chip Finishing`.
2. Extract parasitic interconnect resistance and capacitance using `OpenRCX` to generate SPEF back-annotation files.
3. Validate that clock network skew and buffers inserted during `Clock Tree Synthesis` comply with setup/hold timing limits across standard PVT corners using Liberty models (`make timing`).

#### Step 3.2: JEDEC Functional Cycle & Burst Pattern Synthesis
1. Configure functional testbench sequences in the digital simulation environment targeting JEDEC speed-bin parameters:
   * **Row Activation to Read/Write**: Sweep cycle count intervals to validate minimum $t_{RCD}$.
   * **Precharge to Activate**: Sequence Precharge (`PRE`) to Active (`ACT`) to validate minimum $t_{RP}$.
   * **Clock Period ($t_{CK}$)**: Synthesize synchronous differential clock waveforms ($CK$ / $\#CK$).
2. Run event-based Verilog gate-level simulation with full SDF/SPEF timing back-annotation to record transition events into VCD/EVCD formats.

#### Step 3.3: Waveform Formatting and STIL/WGL Vector Compilation
1. Define ATE waveform timing envelopes using the **5 nm (0.005 µm)** manufacturing grid resolution:
   * **Drive Edges ($D0, D1, D_{Z}$)**: Set input pin assertion window relative to clock period $t_{CK}$.
   * **Strobe Edges ($R0, R1, X$)**: Position compare strobes at deterministic intervals within the valid data eye ($t_{AC} / t_{DQSCK}$) accounting for parasitic delays extracted via `OpenRCX`.
2. Execute STIL/WGL translation compiler to convert EVCD/VCD event streams into IEEE 1450 standard blocks:
   * `Signals` block: Assign bidirectional DDR DQ/DQS pins, command pins (`RAS_N`, `CAS_N`, `WE_N`, `CS_N`), and address pins.
   * `Timing` block: Define test period waveforms and timing marks.
   * `PatternExec` and `Pattern` blocks: Map vectorized cycle states into ATE drive/compare tokens (`D`, `U`, `L`, `H`, `Z`, `X`).

#### Step 3.4: ATE Pin Timing Calibration & Deskew Signoff
1. Load compiled STIL/WGL test programs into the target ATE platform test executive.
2. Perform ATE pin-electronics (PE) TDR (Time Domain Reflectometry) calibration to deskew channel paths to the DUT socket/probe card.
3. Verify that pin-to-pin driver edge placement jitter meets the calibrated test specification before applying functional speed-bin bursts to the device.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Exact Physical Unit | Verification Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Grid / Edge Placement Resolution** | $= 5$ | $\text{nm}$ ($0.005\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) | Vector compiler timing quantizer against PDK grid |
| **Drawn Gate Length Feature Match** | $= 150$ | $\text{nm}$ ($0.15\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) | Physical signoff inspection / GDS layout extraction |
| **Overlay Matching Budget Tolerance** | $\le 35$ | $\text{nm}$ | ATE optical alignment & wafer prober physical log |
| **Minimum Resolvable Half-Pitch Check** | $\ge 152$ | $\text{nm}$ | Lithography rule compliance signoff ($k_1=0.40, \lambda=248\text{ nm}, NA=0.65$) |

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Pattern translation from RTL simulation dump (VCD/FSDB) into STIL (IEEE 1450) and WGL formats must strictly preserve bidirectional DQS/DQ drive-to-compare timing windows. JEDEC DDR speed-binning at 180nm requires sub-nanosecond edge placement resolution on ATE pin electronics; cycle boundary quantization errors during compilation will artificially compress valid setup/hold margins (tDS/tDH) and distort measured tCK min/max distributions.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: The STIL/WGL vector compiler must embed comprehensive parametric burst sequences (BL=4, BL=8) along with precise tRCD, tRP, and tRAS raster cycles. For 180nm planar DRAM arrays, bitline sense amplifier overdrive and write-recovery (tWR) timings are sensitive to VDD core droop during back-to-back ACTIVATE-READ/WRITE bursts. Failure to model ATE pogo-pin and loadboard trace parasitics in the WGL vector timing maps will induce false timing bin failures.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Target commercial DRAM ATE platforms (Advantest T5588/T5503 or Teradyne UltraFLEX) enforce proprietary vector formats converted from STIL. Overly dense vector sets without vector compression or loop execution will exceed vector memory depth per pin (e.g., 64M vectors), requiring expensive pattern reloads that dramatically inflate test time per device and wafer sort index cost.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Clear synchronization milestones between digital synthesis STA signoff and ATE test program release are mandatory. Vector compilation scripts, cyclized test patterns, and timing sheets must be automated in CI/CD with automated validation against Golden RTL to prevent multi-week delays during physical ATE bring-up and burn-in qualification.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. ATE Pin Skew & Jitter Injection: Vector edge placement mismatch exceeding ±120 ps across multi-bit DQ/DQS bus channels on the loadboard, causing false binning fallout for DDR-200/DDR-333 speed grades.
1. Bidirectional Bus Contention: Misaligned Hi-Z to active-drive turnaround states in compiled STIL vectors, leading to ATE pin driver fighting DUT output buffers during read bursts and causing channel driver thermal overstress.
1. Vector Memory Overflow: Uncompressed rasterization of refresh (tREFI) and marching 1/0 retention patterns exhausting local ATE vector cache, triggering split-burst vector reload pipeline stalls.

critics.laya_pm: Clear synchronization milestones between digital synthesis STA signoff and ATE test program release are mandatory. Vector compilation scripts, cyclized test patterns, and timing sheets must be automated in CI/CD with automated validation against Golden RTL to prevent multi-week delays during physical ATE bring-up and burn-in qualification.
critical_failure_modes: ATE Pin Skew & Jitter Injection: Vector edge placement mismatch exceeding ±120 ps across multi-bit DQ/DQS bus channels on the loadboard, causing false binning fallout for DDR-200/DDR-333 speed grades.

Bidirectional Bus Contention: Misaligned Hi-Z to active-drive turnaround states in compiled STIL vectors, leading to ATE pin driver fighting DUT output buffers during read bursts and causing channel driver thermal overstress.
Vector Memory Overflow: Uncompressed rasterization of refresh (tREFI) and marching 1/0 retention patterns exhausting local ATE vector cache, triggering split-burst vector reload pipeline stalls.

testcases.title: STIL Functional Vector Timing Edge Placement and Cyclization Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Test Equipment (ATE) High-Speed Digital Channel Pin Electronics (500 MHz / 1 Gbps class, e.g., Advantest T5588 or Teradyne UltraFLEX), 8 GHz Real-Time Oscilloscope with high-bandwidth active differential probes (Tektronix/Keysight), Loadboard Test Fixture with 50-ohm matched SMA breakout.
testcases.pre_conditions: DUT seated in zero-insertion-force (ZIF) socket on calibrated ATE test fixture. DUT power supplies (VDD=1.8V, VDDQ=1.8V, VREF=0.9V) stabilized with ripple < 15 mV. Compiled STIL/WGL patterns loaded into ATE pin memory. Pogo-pin deskew and TDR calibration complete with residual channel skew < 30 ps.
testcases.procedure: 1. Set ATE master clock period to tCK = 7.5 ns (DDR-266 specification) and sequentially down to tCK = 6.0 ns (DDR-333). 2. Program drive edges for Clock (CLK/CLK#), Control (CS#, RAS#, CAS#, WE#), and Address bus according to JEDEC timing sets compiled in STIL. 3. Configure ATE strobe window for DQ read data capture at tAC / tDQSCK window relative to DQS edges. 4. Execute functional pattern burst comprising Mode Register Set (MRS), PRECHARGE, ACTIVATE, WRITE, READ, and AUTO-REFRESH sequences across 10,000 cycles. 5. Measure edge placement accuracy and waveform integrity on SMA breakouts using the 8 GHz oscilloscope. 6. Log ATE compare pass/fail flags for all DQ/DQS pins across VDD nominal ±10%.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Zero functional vector compare errors across all 10,000 pattern cycles at tCK = 7.5 ns (VDD=1.8V ± 0.18V). ATE edge placement error on CLK, DQS, and DQ pins must measure <= ±50 ps relative to programmed STIL timing definitions. Strobe capture window margin must exceed >= 450 ps.

testcases.title: JEDEC Speed-Bin Boundary Shmoo Margin Metrology (tCK vs tRCD vs VDD)
testcases.instrumentation: Commercial High-Speed DRAM ATE with Parametric Measurement Units (PMUs) and Digital Pin Electronics, High-Precision Thermal Stream Forced Air System (-40°C to +125°C, Temptronic/Thermonics).
testcases.pre_conditions: Compiled WGL/STIL functional vectors mapped to ATE algorithmic pattern generator / vector sequencer. Thermal stream stabilized at +85°C junction temperature. DUT initialization sequence (tINIT = 200 us with stable clock and CKE high) verified.
testcases.procedure: 1. Program 2D Shmoo parameter sweep: X-axis = tCK varied from 10.0 ns down to 5.0 ns in 50 ps increments; Y-axis = VDD varied from 1.60 V to 2.00 V in 20 mV increments. 2. At each grid point, execute compiled read/write pattern with minimum JEDEC tRCD programmed (tRCD = 15 ns, 20 ns, and 25 ns). 3. Capture pass/fail bit map across all internal bank addresses and speed-bin pass boundaries. 4. Record transition boundary where DUT fails first bit read-back (identifying maximum operational frequency fMAX and setup/hold margin cliff).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass envelope must encompass standard DDR-266 (tCK = 7.5 ns, tRCD = 20 ns, tRP = 20 ns) across the full industrial voltage band (1.70 V <= VDD <= 1.90 V) at 85°C. Transition boundary monotonicity must show zero erratic discontinuity (> 150 ps jitter-induced bin jitter) across 3 consecutive Shmoo sweeps.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## ATE High-Precision Pin Electronics Deskew and TDR Channel Timing Calibration
**Document ID:** `SOP-ATE-CAL-180NM-001`  
**Node Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS DRAM)  
**Associated Module:** `[Metrology] > JEDEC Speed-Bin Digital Pattern Vector Generation and ATE Pin Timing Calibration`

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Signal Calibration Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   ATE Cal Generator    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    TDR Pulse Launch    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Round-Trip Echo &    │
│   Reflection at DUT    │
│      Pogo/Socket       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Extract Tau_flight &  │
│  Zero-Plane Alignment  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    PE Programmable     │
│   Delay Line Deskew    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Verification: Edge   │
│  Skew < 25 ps across   │
│      all Channels      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Calibration Procedure

#### Step 1: Calibration Fixture Docking & Thermal Stabilization
1. Mount the automated Gold/Short-Open-Load (SOL) calibration fixture onto the ATE test head pogo-pin interface.
2. Power on the Pin Electronics (PE) thermal management unit; stabilize test-head card cage ambient temperature to $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 1^\circ\text{C}$ for a minimum soak time of $20\text{ minutes}$.
3. Configure PE driver reference voltages according to baseline 180nm core and I/O rails:
   - High-level drive: $V_{OH} = 1.8\text{ V}$
   - Low-level drive: $V_{OL} = 0.0\text{ V}$
   - Linear calibration threshold: $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$ (calibrated to discrete linear transistor extraction gate points).

#### Step 2: Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Channel Flight-Time Measurement
1. Disconnect high-speed pattern generators; enable the internal ATE TDR pulse generator on each tester channel.
2. Launch a fast rise-time pulse ($t_r \le 100\text{ ps}$, $V_{step} = 500\text{ mV}$) down each coaxial transmission line through the Device Interface Board (DIB) traces to the open pogo pin tips.
3. Detect the reflected edge at the $50\%$ amplitude threshold ($250\text{ mV}$) using the high-bandwidth PE sampling comparator.
4. Calculate individual single-ended flight times:
   $$\tau_{\text{flight}, i} = \frac{t_{\text{reflected}, i} - t_{\text{incident}, i}}{2}$$
5. Record individual round-trip flight times for all address, control ($CLK, CKE, \overline{CS}, \overline{RAS}, \overline{CAS}, \overline{WE}$), and bidirectional $DQ/DQS$ channels.

#### Step 3: Programmable Delay-Line (Vernier) Deskew Alignment
1. Identify the reference baseline channel exhibiting maximum transit delay $\tau_{\text{flight, max}}$.
2. For each channel $i$, compute required hardware compensation delay:
   $$\Delta t_i = \tau_{\text{flight, max}} - \tau_{\text{flight}, i}$$
3. Program each channel's PE digital vernier / delay-locked loop (DLL) register:
   - Hardware resolution step size: $\le 5\text{ ps/LSB}$.
4. Re-measure round-trip reflection response on all channels to verify co-planar arrival at the socket contact tips.

#### Step 4: Driver-to-Comparator Loopback Calibration
1. Actuate the automated calibration matrix to engage shorting switches across adjacent channel pairs ($DQ_{2n} \leftrightarrow DQ_{2n+1}$).
2. Drive high-speed edges at $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$ with driver rise/fall times matched to device limits.
3. Align comparator strobe timing registers until receive strobe timestamps match driver edge timestamps within $\le 20\text{ ps}$.
4. Lock calibrated timing offset vectors into ATE hardware registers and generate checksum confirmation.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                        │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Vth Extraction V_DS (mV)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                        │▒▒                            │
      V_swing Driver (V)┤▒▒                            │
     TDR Resolution (ps)┤▓▓▓▓                          │
                        │▓▓▓▓                          │
    Pin Deskew Skew (ps)┤████████████████              │
                        │████████████████              │
                        └┬──────┬───────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                        0.0   12.5    25.0   37.5  50.0 
```

1. **Inter-Channel Channel-to-Channel Skew ($t_{\text{skew}}$):**
   - Target: $\le 25\text{ ps}$ peak-to-peak across all active pins (Clock, Address, Control, $DQ$, $DQS$) at the socket reference plane.
2. **TDR Measurement Vernier Resolution:**
   - Target: $\le 5\text{ ps}$ per least-significant bit (LSB) on internal PE delay line interpolators.
3. **Driver Voltage Rail Accuracy:**
   - Target: $1.8\text{ V} \pm 15\text{ mV}$ full-swing driver level ($V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$ operation) and $50\text{ mV} \pm 2\text{ mV}$ linear reference offset.
4. **Post-Calibration Jitter ($J_{\text{RMS}}$):**
   - Target: $\le 3.5\text{ ps RMS}$ on ATE clock and strobe channels.

---

### 4. Verified Literature & Context Citations
- **Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification**:
  - Linear device extraction voltage: $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$.
  - Nominal operating supply rail: $V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$ ($I_{on} \ge 500\ \mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$).
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Gate channel geometry: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**:
  - Cell footprint: $8F^2$ folded bitline ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$).
  - Capacitance limits: Storage node capacitance $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ (nominal $28\text{ fF}$); bitline parasitic $C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$ ($C_b/C_s$ between $5:1$ and $9:1$).

---
*Captured micro-knowledge documented in [ate_pin_electronics_deskew_tdr_calibration.md](./docs/ate_pin_electronics_deskew_tdr_calibration.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Calibrating ATE pin electronics deskew to the Device Under Test (DUT) pogo/socket interface rather than the internal tester chassis backplane is non-negotiable. For a 180nm DRAM running DDR clock cycles down to 5-10 ns (100-200 MHz JEDEC rates), uncalibrated pogo pin trace disparities and tester channel group delays easily induce 200-450 ps of skew across data/strobe (DQ/DQS) and command/address (CA) lanes. Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) must precisely de-embed trace impedance mismatches from the ATE pin card across the load board up to the socket boundary plane to ensure true edge placement fidelity without masking margin failures.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the physical interface, the DDR DRAM JEDEC setup (tDS/tIS) and hold (tDH/tIH) timings require sub-50 ps deskew uncertainty across all bidirectional channel pin electronics (PE). Dynamic driver/comparator deskew calibration must compensate for thermal drift of PE driver ICs during long HTOL/qualification test runs (temp coefficients typically ~1.5 ps/°C). TDR edge-rate calibration must account for open/short/load standards on a dedicated golden calibration robot/fixture rather than relying solely on software loopback or passive fixture approximations.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring commercial-grade automated deskew calibration fixture boards (Golden Cal Substrates) and specialized RF-grade pogo pin blocks (rated >6 GHz, <30 mOhm contact resistance) involves long lead times (12-16 weeks) from vendors like Cohu, Advantest, or FormFactor. Secondary sourcing for high-bandwidth calibration standard loadboards and calibrated 50-ohm coaxial probe interfaces is essential to prevent ATE cell downtime in the packaging and sort line.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The buy-and-commission milestone for the ATE deskew and TDR subsystem must be integrated before the first MPW packaged sample arrival. Automated calibration routines must run within an allocated shift-overhead budget (<15 minutes per 24 hours of continuous qualification testing). Calibration records must integrate into our open-source git-based metrology database to maintain JEDEC qualification trace integrity for open-source silicon validation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. TDR reflection false reference plane detection caused by socket pogo pin oxide buildup or tip wear, shifting the calibrated T0 plane by >120 ps.
1. Driver vs. Comparator propagation delay mismatch resulting in asymmetric bidirectional DQ timing windows during read/write turnaround verification.
1. Thermal expansion-induced channel length divergence across the test head during elevated-temperature speed-binning (e.g., 85°C/125°C), leading to false yield binning loss.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-2-1-2-01` | **Automated TDR Channel Delay and Reflection Boundary Deskew Calibration** | High-Bandwidth ATE Timing Calibration Unit (TCU) with integrated 20 GHz TDR generator, Golden Deskew Calibration Fixture (Cal-Board with 50-ohm matched reference short/open/load standards), 4-digit Picoammeter/Voltmeter. | 1. Initialize ATE calibration software module and configure TCU to pulse mode (trise ≤ 35 ps, Vstep = 400 mV into 50 ohms). 2. Sequentially route TDR pulse through all 64 ATE digital pin electronics channels to the open-circuit socket contact tips. 3. Measure round-trip flight time (2*tpd) to the positive reflection edge at 50% threshold for each channel. 4. Switch calibration board relay to short-circuit termination standard; record negative reflection boundary. 5. Calculate physical propagation delay offset per pin relative to master reference clock channel CLK0. 6. Write compensation deskew delay values into hardware digital delay line (DDL) registers. | `All calibrated channel-to-channel edge alignments at the socket interface plane must exhibit max skew |t_skew| ≤ 30.0 ps. Characteristic impedance Z0 of all loadboard pogo traces must measure 50.0 ± 2.5 ohms.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-2-1-2-02` | **Bidirectional Driver/Comparator Edge Placement and Jitter Margin Verification** | Golden Cal-Board equipped with high-speed GaAs active loopback switches, Keysight/Tektronix 33 GHz Real-Time Oscilloscope with differential active probes connected to monitor breakout points. | 1. Program ATE pattern generator to output alternating 101010 pattern at 200 MHz across all DQ, DQS, and Command/Address channels simultaneously. 2. Measure transition edge timing at the calibration fixture reference node using the external reference oscilloscope across 10,000 cycles. 3. Enable loopback mode on the Cal-Board to route driven signals directly back into ATE pin comparators. 4. Sweep comparator strobe timing in 5 ps increments to construct comparator shmoo detection curve. 5. Extract driver-to-comparator delta offset and residual random jitter (RJ_rms). | `Total residual pin-to-pin skew across all DQ/DQS pins must be ≤ 40 ps peak-to-peak. Random jitter RJ_rms must not exceed 4.5 ps. Comparator threshold accuracy must be within ±10 mV of programmed VREF.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ESD-safe cleanroom lab coat (static dissipative 10^6 - 10^9 ohms/sq), Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (powder-free, cleanroom class 100 compatible), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD grounding heel straps and dual-conductor wrist strap with continuous ground monitor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Immediately flush eyes with gently flowing isotonic saline or eyewash water for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing, wash affected area with mild soap and water. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Move victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored. Accidental ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth thoroughly with water and seek immediate medical attention with SDS.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Maintain local exhaust ventilation (LEV) or laminar flow downdraft table at calibration workstation with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 fpm) during solvent wipe and pogo pin maintenance. Tester test-cell room air exchange rate must exceed 15 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA solvent wipes and residue rinse in certified flammable solvent waste containers labeled with hazardous waste markers. Seal containers tightly to prevent VOC vapor loss; store in a dedicated Class 1A flammable cabinet for compliant disposal by certified hazardous waste contractor.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, Electronic Grade)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade (SEMI C4) | `≥ 99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 gas for socket dry-cleaning)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 (UHP) | `≥ 99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pogo pin tip array and loadboard calibration pads mechanically inspected under stereo-microscope; free of organic contamination, debris, solder paste transfer, or gold plating wear (>99.5% pristine Au surface).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated, solvent-cleaned, and dried socket contact tips seated in dry nitrogen environment with verified contact resistance < 30 mOhm across all pins.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric exposure beyond queue limit leads to particulate accumulation, surface organic adsorption, and copper/nickel sub-layer oxidation on worn pogo tips, causing contact resistance instability (>150 mOhm variation) and shifting TDR edge calibration by >50 ps.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full hardware deskew and TDR channel calibration completed across all 64 ATE digital pin electronics channels up to the DDR socket pogo contact interface. Channel deskew tables and timing offset matrices are validated and loaded into tester firmware registers, ensuring timing accuracy sufficient for sub-nanosecond JEDEC speed-binning of 180nm DRAM parts.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ATE_PE_Deskew_Calibration_Matrix_Report.csv`
- [ ] `TDR_Channel_Impedance_Reflection_Profile.pdf`
- [ ] `Pogo_Pin_Contact_Resistance_And_Skew_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum channel-to-channel pin electronics skew across all JEDEC DQ/DQS channels at the DUT socket plane** | `25.0 ps` | ±10.0 ps (Absolute Upper Bound ≤ 35.0 ps) | Automated TDR time-of-flight reflection measurement using ATE TCU referenced to Golden Cal-Board. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total integrated channel transmission line characteristic impedance (Z0) up to socket entrance** | `50.0 ohms` | ±2.0 ohms | TDR impedance discontinuity de-embedding via high-bandwidth time-domain reflectometry profile analysis. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Residual pin driver random jitter (RJ_rms) at maximum pattern generation frequency (200 MHz)** | `3.5 ps` | ≤ 4.5 ps maximum | External 33 GHz real-time oscilloscope jitter decomposition analysis across 10,000 consecutive clock edges. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researchers verify that 100% of the 64 ATE digital channels meet the ≤ 35 ps skew bound, all calibration register offsets are persisted to the ATE operational configuration file, and three consecutive verification runs demonstrate timing repeatability within ±5 ps without recalibration.
