### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Title:** TDR Calibration & Pin Electronics Timing Deskew Characterization  
**Document Link:** [sop_tdr_calibration_pin_deskew.md](./docs/sop_tdr_calibration_pin_deskew.md)  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm Commercial MPW / 1T1C DRAM Architecture)  
**Council Context:** Architecture & Integration > BEOL & Packaging > Reliability & Qualification > Metrology  

---

#### 1. Calibration Architecture & Signal Path Flow
The measurement plane extends from the ATE digital driver pin electronics, through the controlled loadboard fixture, to the socket/DUT pad contact tip:

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   ATE Channel Driver   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Direct Fixture Trace  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     DUT Loadboard      │
│      Contact Pad       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Pogo Pin / Socket    │
│        Boundary        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Reflection Edge     │
│       Metrology        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

#### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Test Fixture Mount & Instrument Initialization:**
   - Mount the precision Golden Standard Open/Short/Load (OSL) calibration substrate directly onto the ATE test head pogo-pin socket contact plane.
   - Stabilize the test cell thermal chamber at $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ (ambient metrology baseline) before correlating with $85^\circ\text{C}$ retention/stress conditions.
2. **Incident Pulse TDR Acquisition:**
   - Launch an incident fast-edge TDR step ($V_\text{step} = 500\text{ mV}$, $t_r \le 35\text{ ps}$, source impedance $Z_0 = 50.0\,\Omega$) from each ATE pin electronics channel.
   - Record the time-resolved reflection profile across all DRAM signals: `DQ[15:0]`, `DQS`, `CLK/CLK#`, `ADDR[12:0]`, `/RAS`, `/CAS`, `/WE`, `/CS`.
   - Confirm loadboard trace impedance matches $50.0\,\Omega \pm 1.5\,\Omega$ up to the pogo-pin entry boundary.
3. **Round-Trip Delay Extraction & Skew Matrix Calculation:**
   - Detect the high-impedance reflection edge discontinuity at the socket pogo-pin tip contact plane ($t_{\text{socket\_open}, i}$).
   - Compute the one-way electrical propagation delay for each pin $i$:
     $$T_{\text{flight}, i} = \frac{t_{\text{reflection}, i} - t_{\text{incident}, i}}{2}$$
   - Establish the differential `CLK/CLK#` pin pair as the master timing reference ($T_{\text{ref}}$).
   - Calculate the compensation delay delta:
     $$\Delta T_{\text{skew}, i} = T_{\text{ref}} - T_{\text{flight}, i}$$
4. **Hardware Vernier Programming & Socket-Tip Active Verification:**
   - Program the per-channel Programmable Delay Lines (PDL) hardware verniers with $-\Delta T_{\text{skew}, i}$.
   - Insert the calibrated active Short/Loopback substrate; drive coincident synchronous strobe vectors across all pins at $1.8\text{ V}$ SSTL_18 logic levels.
   - Perform equivalent-time sampling cross-correlation at the socket tips until residual channel skew converges within limits. Export calibration profile to `pin_deskew_180nm_cal.dat`.

---

#### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                       Deskew & Calibration Metrics     
                   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                   │░░░░░░                             │
  Edge Jitter (RMS)┤░░░░░░                             │
TDR Impedance Error┤▒▒▒                                │
                   │▒▒▒                                │
   Channel P2P Skew┤███████████████████████████████████│
                   │███████████████████████████████████│
                   └┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬┘
                   0.0      4.6     9.2     13.9   18.5 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Value | Hard Limit / Tolerance | Unit | Inspection Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pin-to-Pin Timing Skew** | $\le 15.0$ | $\le 20.0$ | ps (peak-to-peak) | ATE High-Speed Sampling Comparator |
| **TDR Characteristic Impedance ($Z_0$)** | $50.0$ | $\pm 1.5$ | $\Omega$ | TDR Reflection Edge Metrology Module |
| **Pin Driver Edge Jitter ($J_\text{RMS}$)** | $\le 2.5$ | $\le 3.0$ | ps (RMS) | Sampling Oscilloscope / ATE Vernier Metrology |
| **Edge Alignment Residual Error** | $\le 5.0$ | $\le 8.0$ | ps | Differential Cross-Correlation Engine |

---

#### 4. Verified Literature & Context Sources
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Transistor dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$); minimum cell storage capacitance $28\text{ fF}$; leakage budget $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: 1T1C stacked capacitor architecture ($8F^2 / 6F^2$) requiring $25 \text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$ storage capacitance for retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; bitline/wordline pitch $360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$; gate oxide thickness $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$.
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**: Physical grid resolution $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$); critical dimensions: minimum poly gate length $0.15\,\mu\text{m}$ ($150\text{ nm}$), active diffusion width $0.15\,\mu\text{m}$, Metal 1 minimum width $0.14\,\mu\text{m}$, Metal 1 pitch $0.34\,\mu\text{m}$; overlay error budget $\le 35\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated Test Equipment (ATE) pin electronics calibration for high-speed JEDEC DDR interfaces at 180nm requires establishing a calibrated Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) reference plane right at the DUT socket contact pin interface. The primary systems challenge is ensuring that pogo pin compliance, load board trace impedance variations (target 50 ohm +/- 2 ohm), and relay matrix path length differences across all 64+ data/strobe/address channels are fully characterized and compensated. Without automated TDR deskew routines, channel-to-channel propagation delay mismatch (t_skew) exceeding 25 ps will corrupt 2D VDD-frequency Shmoo boundaries, leading to false setup/hold margin failures on high-frequency DDR cycles.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Pin electronics timing deskew characterization must isolate driver edge transition jitter from transmission line reflections. Using picosecond-resolution pulse generators and ultra-fast TDR sampling heads (>20 GHz bandwidth, 10-90% risetime < 17.5 ps), the system must detect the open/short reflection artifact at the DUT pogo-pin/ball interface. At 180nm DDR speeds (e.g., DDR-200 to DDR-400), timing jitter and pin-to-pin skew eat directly into the data valid window (tDV). The calibration algorithm must generate hardware delay line correction tap coefficients to achieve residual pin-to-pin skew under +/- 15 ps across all test channels at nominal ATE operating temperatures.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement of specialized high-frequency ATE calibration fixtures, gold-plated short/open/load/through (SOLT) calibration substrates, and certified 50-ohm semi-rigid coaxial loopback assemblies involves single-source RF metrology suppliers with lead times exceeding 12 to 16 weeks. A secondary risk is pogo-pin mechanical fatigue and plating degradation (Au wear-through exposing Ni/BeCu) on the calibration dummy socket, which alters contact resistance and TDR edge profiles after repeated engagement cycles (>5,000 insertions).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibrating 64 to 128 pin electronics channels individually via manual or semi-automated TDR protocols can easily bottleneck ATE cell availability during post-HTOL burn-in test windows. The project schedule requires an automated calibration sequence executing in under 20 minutes per loadboard setup. Any drift exceeding thermal stability specs requiring intra-shift recalibration threatens throughput targets for the 180nm open-source DRAM MPW silicon qualification lot.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Contact impedance discontinuity or erratic pogo pin oxidation causing spurious TDR reflection artifacts, leading to inverted or incorrect hardware timing deskew offset coefficients.
1. Thermal drift in ATE pin electronics driver delay lines post-calibration (>0.8 ps/deg C) exceeding the tight timing deskew budget across long HTOL Shmoo margin test runs.
1. False open-circuit detection caused by mechanical micro-misalignment of the calibration golden coupon inside the DUT test socket, introducing erroneous trace flight-time offsets.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-3-1-1-01` | **ATE Pin Electronics Channel-to-Channel TDR Flight-Time Calibration** | High-Bandwidth Sampling Oscilloscope / TDR Module (>20 GHz bandwidth, <18 ps incident risetime), Automated Calibration Substrate (SOLT golden fixture with coplanar waveguide standards), Precision Torque Wrench (0.56 N-m for SMA/3.5mm connectors), Environmental Chamber Monitor (0.1 deg C resolution). | 1. Launch automated ATE TDR calibration script across all DDR channels (D0-D63, DQS0-DQS7, ADDR0-ADDR15, CLK_P/N). 2. Inject incident 200 mV step pulse (tr < 18 ps) from each pin electronics driver into the transmission path. 3. Acquire reflected waveform at the TDR sampling receiver and determine the 50% voltage transition threshold representing the reflection from the open socket interface. 4. Record electrical flight time (t_flight_i) for each channel i = 1 to N. 5. Calculate mean flight time t_mean and channel offsets delta_t_i = t_mean - t_flight_i. 6. Write calculated delay correction coefficients into ATE pin electronics vernier registers. 7. Re-run TDR reflection verification pulse across all channels to measure residual flight-time variation. | `Residual channel-to-channel timing skew across all tested pin electronics channels after calibration must be <= +/- 12.0 ps. Characteristic transmission line impedance through the loadboard trace to the socket interface must measure 50.0 +/- 2.5 ohms.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-3-1-1-02` | **Pin Driver Edge Deskew and Vernier Linearity Verification** | Multi-Channel High-Speed Real-Time Digital Storage Oscilloscope (4 channels, >= 25 GHz bandwidth, >= 80 GSa/s), Low-Capacitance Active Differential Probes (<0.2 pF loading), Golden High-Speed Loopback Coupon. | 1. Connect active differential probes to reference pin (CLK_P) and target pin electronics channels (DQS0, DQ0, DQ15). 2. Configure ATE pattern generator to fire simultaneous rising edges on all channels at 200 MHz. 3. Measure time difference (delta_t_edge) between CLK_P 50% crossing and target channel 50% crossing over 10,000 edge acquisitions. 4. Sweep vernier delay offset registers from -500 ps to +500 ps in 5 ps increments, measuring edge shift linearity (Integral Non-Linearity - INL and Differential Non-Linearity - DNL). 5. Record maximum edge placement error and calculate timing jitter (RMS and peak-to-peak). | `Simultaneous edge alignment error across all channels relative to reference clock must not exceed +/- 15.0 ps. Timing vernier DNL must be <= 1.5 ps and INL <= 4.0 ps across the +/- 500 ps adjustment range. Driver edge RMS random jitter must be <= 2.5 ps.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom ESD-Safe Lab Coat (anti-static dissipative fabric), Conductive ESD Wrist Strap and Heel Grounders (1 MOhm series resistor verified), Powder-free cleanroom nitrile gloves (thickness >= 5 mil, ANSI/ESD STM11.11 compliant), ANSI Z87.1 approved impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Move personnel immediately to fresh cleanroom air supply; seek medical attention if irritation or respiratory distress persists. Skin Contact: Remove contaminated gloves/garments; flush affected skin with copious flowing water for at least 15 minutes. Eye Contact: Immediately flush open eyes using emergency eyewash station for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids retracted; consult ophthalmologist. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth thoroughly with clean DI water and seek emergency medical assistance immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop solvent wipe and pogo-pin degreasing operations must occur under a certified chemical fume hood or localized laminar exhaust trunk with face velocity maintained between 80 to 100 LFM (0.4 to 0.5 m/s). Ambient test bay must maintain Class 10,000 (ISO Class 7) air filtration with minimum 20 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used solvent wipes and rinse liquids contaminated with electronic cleaning solvents must be collected in dedicated, grounded, self-closing stainless steel hazardous waste cans labeled 'Flammable Solvent Waste - IPA'. Do not drain into cleanroom municipal sewers; transfer to hazardous chemical disposal waste manifest for high-temperature thermal oxidation.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Electronic Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI Grade (>99.9%) | `99.9% v/v` |
| **Perfluorohexane (Fluorinert FC-72 / contact cleaner solvent)** | `355-42-0` | Electronic / Analytical Grade | `>99.0% v/v` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Gold-plated calibration coupon and pogo-pin contact array cleaned of organic residues, particulate contamination (< 0.3 um), and free of visible gold galling or oxide buildup; contact resistance < 35 mOhm per pin.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated and deskewed test socket interface sealed with dry nitrogen purge protective cover; contact pins verified mechanically undamaged and free of metallic debris or solvent residue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient factory air causes atmospheric airborne hydrocarbon condensation and surface copper/nickel tarnishing through micro-porosities in thin gold flash plating, leading to contact resistance shifts (>50 mOhm) and capacitive high-frequency signal attenuation that invalidates sub-15 ps deskew calibration.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful TDR calibration and pin electronics deskew characterization across all ATE signal channels on the 180nm DRAM test loadboard, establishing a verified sub-15 ps timing reference plane at the socket pogo pin contacts for accurate JEDEC DDR speed-binning and 2D VDD-frequency Shmoo characterization.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ATE_Pin_Deskew_Calibration_Matrix_Gen3.csv`
- [ ] `TDR_Reflection_Impedance_Profiles_Loadboard.pdf`
- [ ] `Vernier_Delay_Linearity_INL_DNL_Report.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum channel-to-channel timing skew across all calibrated ATE pin electronics channels at socket interface plane** | `10.0 ps` | +/- 5.0 ps (Absolute max <= 15.0 ps) | Multi-channel high-speed digital sampling oscilloscope simultaneous edge time-interval error (TIE) measurement across 10,000 cycles. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Characteristic transmission line impedance across all loadboard trace paths to DUT pogo pins** | `50.0 ohm` | +/- 2.0 ohm | High-bandwidth TDR step reflection rho analysis at 25 deg C with 18 ps incident risetime. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **ATE pin electronics timing vernier delay adjustment step linearity (INL)** | `2.0 ps` | <= 4.0 ps maximum deviation across +/- 500 ps range | Automated stepped delay vernier sweep against external calibrated laser-interferometer-stabilized clock reference. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 128 pin electronics channels achieve verified deskew within <= 15.0 ps peak-to-peak window, TDR impedance trace profiles show zero discontinuities outside 48.0-52.0 ohm, and the calibration matrix file ATE_Pin_Deskew_Calibration_Matrix_Gen3.csv is digitally signed and successfully integrated into the ATE Shmoo test execution engine with zero syntax or calibration checksum errors.

# SOP: Algorithmic Pattern Vector Generation for March C- & Moving Inversion

**Process Hierarchy:**  
`180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)` > `180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation` > `BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging` > `Final Automated Test Equipment (ATE) JEDEC DDR Speed-Bin & HTOL Burn-in Testing` > `Post-Stress ATE JEDEC DDR Speed-Binning & Shmoo Margin Metrology` > `2D VDD-Frequency Shmoo Plotting & Operating Margin Metrology` > `ATE Shmoo Test Pattern Vector Generation & Pin Timing Deskew Calibration` > `Algorithmic Pattern Vector Generation for March C- & Moving Inversion`

---

## 1. Process Overview & Architecture

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) specifies the algorithmic pattern vector generation (ALPG) routines for running **March C-** and **Moving Inversion (MOVI)** test suites on Automated Test Equipment (ATE). These algorithmic vectors target physical cell failures across dense 180nm folded bitline arrays, specifically screening for:
- Stuck-at faults (SAF), transition faults (TF), and address decoder faults (AF).
- Unlinked and linked coupling faults (CFin, CFid).
- Retention degradation governed by sub-threshold/junction leakage budgets ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
- Dynamic write-recovery and wordline/bitline coupling noise across stacked capacitors ($C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$).

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              ATE Vector Generator (ALPG)               │
│         X/Y Address & Vector Sequencing Unit           │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            Phase 1: March C- Algorithmic Suite         │
│ 1. ⇕ (w0)                                             │
│ 2. ⇑ (r0, w1)                                          │
│ 3. ⇑ (r1, w0)                                          │

```

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

### Step 1: Algorithmic Pattern Generator (ALPG) Address & Timing Grid Setup
1. Configure the ATE pattern generator address scrambler to map logical address pins $(A_0 - A_n)$ directly to physical row/column decoders conforming to the 180nm folded bitline cell topology ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
2. Align vector edge timing with the pin electronics deskew calibration using the standard lithographic / alignment base grid resolution ($0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ base coordinate scale).
3. Set the core operating voltage rail to nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$ ($V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$ domain).

### Step 2: March C- Algorithmic Sequence Compilation & Execution
Execute the 6-element ($10N$) March C- pattern continuously through the array:
1. **Pass 1 - Initialization:** $\Updownarrow (w0)$ — Write background data `0` to all physical cell addresses in arbitrary address order.
2. **Pass 2 - Upward Transition 1:** $\Uparrow (r0, w1)$ — In ascending address order, read data `0` (verifying background), then immediately write `1`.
3. **Pass 3 - Upward Transition 2:** $\Uparrow (r1, w0)$ — In ascending address order, read data `1`, then write `0`.
4. **Pass 4 - Downward Transition 1:** $\Downarrow (r0, w1)$ — In descending address order, read data `0`, then write `1`.
5. **Pass 5 - Downward Transition 2:** $\Downarrow (r1, w0)$ — In descending address order, read data `1`, then write `0`.
6. **Pass 6 - Final Verification:** $\Updownarrow (r0)$ — Read data `0` from all physical addresses in arbitrary address order.

### Step 3: Moving Inversion (MOVI) Stress Vector Execution
1. Initialize the array to solid `0` background at nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
2. Sequentially invert each cell to `1`, execute full-array read cycles to detect disturbance on adjacent bitline pairs (shared W-plug bitline contacts and stacked crown/MIM capacitors), and invert back to `0`.
3. Invert background across alternate physical rows/columns to create worst-case sense-amp bitline coupling noise across adjacent $28\text{ fF}$ storage nodes.
4. Shift the inversion boundary dynamically down the wordlines and bitlines across the entire address space.

### Step 4: Shmoo Margin Strobe Evaluation & Leakage Pause
1. Insert pause intervals during read strobes to verify cell retention against junction/sub-threshold leakage requirements ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
2. Sample comparator digital output channels against threshold levels ($V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$ reference for peripheral sensing and pass devices).
3. Log passing/failing functional vector coordinates into the 2D VDD-Frequency Shmoo plot engine.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Algorithmic Pattern Vector Generation (APG) for March C- and Moving Inversion (MOVI) requires tight synchronization between the ATE digital algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG) and the timing generator (TG). At 180nm core operating frequencies (133-200 MHz JEDEC SDR/DDR interface), vector compression engines running 10N March C- and 13N MOVI must not suffer cycle-boundary pipeline bubbles when transitioning across address boundaries (X-fast vs Y-fast rastering). A mismatch between the simulated WGL/STIL pattern vector cycles and the physical ATE channel pin deskew (< +/- 50 ps channel-to-channel skew) will induce false functional failures during VDD-frequency shmoo margin metrology.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: March C- ({up(w0)}; {up(r0,w1)}; {up(r1,w0)}; {down(r0,w1)}; {down(r1,w0)}; {down(r0)}) targets unlinked AFs (address decoder faults), SAFs (stuck-at faults), TFs (transition faults), and CFins (inversion coupling faults). However, in open-source 180nm DRAM architectures with planar 1T1C or stacked capacitor configurations, Moving Inversion (MOVI) must be specifically parameterized to expose pattern sensitivity faults (PSF) and wordline-to-bitline capacitive coupling. The ALPG vector timing sets must accurately honor the minimum t_RCD (15 ns), t_RP (15 ns), and t_RC (55 ns) timing corners extracted from Stage 3 discrete gate ring oscillator baselines (tau_d <= 80 ps/stage) to prevent invalid timing violations from masking cell leakage and retention faults.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: ATE tester time on commercial platforms (Advantest T5503HS2 or Teradyne UltraFLEX) scales exponentially with pattern vector depth. Emitting uncompressed, flat vector test files for a full 64Mb/128Mb DRAM array under 13N MOVI exhausts ATE vector memory depth (typically limited to 64M-128M vectors per pin slice without hardware looping). The design flow must mandate native hardware ALPG instruction compilation (microcode loops, nested address generators, and data inversion masks) rather than flat cyclized vectors to limit test execution cost below $0.035 per unit in high-volume sort and burn-in qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Pattern vector generation signoff is on the critical path linking the Foundry Tapeout PDK verification to the final ATE sort test floor. Any delay in translating pattern vectors to standard STIL/WGL formats directly impacts the packaging yield learning cycle. Clear boundary conditions must be enforced: the vector generator must output verified VCD/STIL golden vectors alongside shmoo corner matrices (VDD core 1.62V to 1.98V, VDDIO 1.8V to 3.3V, clock period 5.0 ns to 10.0 ns) with 100% automated test bench syntax linting prior to ATE bay deployment.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. ALPG Address Boundary Pipeline Bubble: Address counter pipeline stalls during March C- address direction reversal (UP to DOWN) cause missing precharge/activate commands, corrupting bank state and resulting in false-positive Address Decoder Fault (AF) binning.
1. Pin Timing Deskew Drift Induced Shmoo Distortion: ATE channel driver edge skew exceeding +/- 75 ps across DQS and DQ strobes during Moving Inversion test execution at high frequency (> 200 MHz), creating artificial timing-closure walls in the 2D VDD-Frequency Shmoo plot.
1. Capacitive Bitline Coupling Masking: Inadequate physical-to-logical address topological mapping within the March C- scrambler table causing adjacent physical bitlines to toggle in common-mode rather than differential/checkerboard inversion, concealing critical write-disturb and CFid (idempotent coupling) defects.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat (surface resistivity 10^6 to 10^9 ohms/sq), ESD-safe grounded wrist strap with integrated 1-megohm series resistor, Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, textured fingertips, 4 mil thickness), Closed-toe ESD protective footwear (static dissipative per ANSI/ESD S20.20)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with IPA: Flush immediately with copiously flowing clean tap or eyewash station water for a minimum of 15 minutes holding eyelids open; remove contact lenses if present and easy to do; seek immediate medical attention. In case of inhalation: Move subject to fresh air immediately; if breathing is irregular or stopped, administer artificial respiration and seek emergency medical assistance. In case of skin contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated clothing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: ATE test bay and probe cleaning maintenance stations must be maintained with continuous chemical exhaust hoods providing face velocity of 100 +/- 10 LFPM (0.5 m/s). Test area must operate in positive-pressure ISO Class 6 / Class 1000 cleanroom ambient with minimum 20 air volume changes per hour to prevent vapor buildup during solvent wipe maintenance.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA solvent wipes and residue must be collected in dedicated, FM-approved, self-closing steel flammable hazardous waste cans labeled per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200. Solvent waste drums must be grounded and bonded to prevent static discharge sparks. Discard via certified third-party RCRA-permitted hazardous chemical waste handler; zero drain disposal.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-ATE-SHMOO-VDD-TCK-001`
### Title: ATE Shmoo Execution & $V_{DD}$–$t_{CK}$ Operational Margin Metrology Signoff
**Context:** Gen 3 (180nm) Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | BEOL Wafer Sort & Final Packaging → Post-Stress JEDEC DDR Speed-Binning & Shmoo Margin Metrology  
**Target Environment:** Advantest / Teradyne ATE with Device Under Test (DUT) High-Speed Coaxial Interface Board

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Lifecycle

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  ATE Channel Deskew &  │
│    TDR Calibration     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    2D VDD-tCK Shmoo    │
│   Grid Matrix Setup    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Vector Execution:    │
│       March C- &       │
│     Pseudo-Random      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Sense-Amp Refresh &   │
│  Leakage Pass Margin   │
│         Audit          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Operational Envelope  │
│  Signoff & Speed-Bin   │
│        Tagging         │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pin Timing Deskew & TDR Calibration:**
   - Execute Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) and channel deskew calibration on all DRAM command, address, strobe (`DQS`), and data (`DQ`) tester channels down to pin-to-pin skew $|\Delta t_{skew}| \le 20\text{ ps}$.
   - Compensate for DUT socket board trace propagation delays using OpenRCX-extracted parasitics and pin-load capacitance matching.

2. **2D $V_{DD}$–$t_{CK}$ Parameter Grid Initialization:**
   - Configure the ATE Programmable Power Supply (DPS) voltage axis: sweep core and I/O supply voltage $V_{DD}$ from $1.50\text{ V}$ to $2.10\text{ V}$ in $25\text{ mV}$ steps (nominal $1.80\text{ V} \pm 10\%$, covering $1.62\text{ V}$ to $1.98\text{ V}$).
   - Set the clock period axis ($t_{CK}$): sweep from $5.0\text{ ns}$ ($200\text{ MHz}$) down to $12.0\text{ ns}$ ($83.3\text{ MHz}$) in $100\text{ ps}$ increments.

3. **Pattern Vector Streaming & Bitline Sense-Amplifier Read/Write:**
   - Apply algorithmic pattern generation (APG) streaming functional DRAM vectors: March C- and checkerboard pseudo-random sequences at nominal access transistor dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Assert standard read/write cycle commands across bitline contacts shared between adjacent cell pairs, driving stacked capacitor nodes (minimum $C_{cell} = 28\text{ fF}$).

4. **Retention, Temperature & Leakage Stress Verification:**
   - Execute a post-HTOL stress retention pause at thermal chamber conditions ($T_{j} = 85^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Validate that cell storage node leakage remains within the JEDEC target limits ($I_{leak} \le 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$) to ensure charge hold time across the target refresh period.

5. **2D Pass/Fail Shmoo Boundary Extraction & Signoff:**
   - Capture pass/fail bit-level bitmaps across the 2D grid matrix.
   - Evaluate boundary eye closure and timing guardbands: compute positive timing slack relative to JEDEC DDR speed targets ($t_{CK} = 7.5\text{ ns}$ for DDR-266 / $133\text{ MHz}$ core clock).
   - Sign off the operational envelope and stamp electronic bin codes into the manufacturing log.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                       ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                       │░░░░░░░                        │
   tCK Margin (@133MHz)┤░░░░░░░                        │
                       │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Corner VDD_high (1.98V)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
 Corner VDD_low (1.62V)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ │
                       │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ │
     Nominal VDD (1.8V)┤███████████████████████████████│
                       │███████████████████████████████│
                       └┬───────┬──────┬───────┬──────┬┘
                        0      25     50      75    100 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Metrology Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Storage Node Capacitance ($C_{cell}$)** | $\ge 28.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | ATE CV/charge-discharge parametric test on stacked capacitor test structures |
| **Transistor Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage ($I_{leak}$)** | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ ($@ 85^\circ\text{C}$) | Pause-time variable refresh retention test |
| **Channel Pin-to-Pin Skew ($|\Delta t_{skew}|$)** | $\le 20.0$ | $\text{ps}$ | ATE pin electronics automated TDR calibration |
| **$V_{DD}$ Operational Tolerance Window** | $1.62\text{ to }1.98$ ($1.80 \pm 10\%$) | $\text{V}$ | 2D Shmoo continuous zero-error envelope |
| **Clock Period Margin ($\Delta t_{CK}$) at DDR-266** | $\ge 1.25$ ($t_{CK} \le 6.25$) | $\text{ns}$ | Shmoo edge boundary delta from $7.50\text{ ns}$ |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - Access transistor channel dimensions: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage node structure: Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) with crown-shaped tungsten plug (W-plug).
  - Minimum capacitance budget: $28\text{ fF/cell}$ to guarantee noise immunity against alpha particles and bitline coupling.
  - Sub-threshold and junction leakage threshold: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain refresh retention intervals.
- **OpenROAD Physical Design & Synthesis Toolflow:**
  - Parasitic extraction via OpenRCX and signoff timing/delay models utilized for DUT test-fixture trace de-embedding and pin timing calibration.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The automated test equipment (ATE) test socket parasitics (typically 1.2 nH to 2.5 nH per pin inductance and 0.8 pF contact capacitance) severely distort the 180nm CMOS DRAM clock and command/address slews during high-frequency tCK stepping. If the device-under-test (DUT) load board lacks tight round-trip TDR pin deskew calibration (down to < 25 ps jitter mismatch), timing shmoo walls will misattribute socket edge dispersion to internal bitline sense amplifier or DLL marginality. Ground bounce across shared VSS return pins during concurrent burst reads also artificially contracts the VDD lower operating boundary.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In a 180nm open-source 1T-1C DRAM architecture, cell retention time and sense amplifier strobe sensitivity exhibit distinct temperature-VDD cross-couplings. Running VDD-tCK 2D shmoo sweeps across 1.62V-1.98V (nominal 1.8V ±10%) and 5.0ns-15.0ns (66MHz-200MHz) requires precise retention pause insertion and refresh cycle interspersal. If March C- or pseudo-random burst patterns do not explicitly stress tRCD and tRP under minimum tCK at the low-voltage corner (1.62V), soft bit failures arising from degraded transfer-gate gate drive will evade speed-binning signoff.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-frequency pogo-pin test sockets with tight contact pitch for 180nm packaged units face lead times exceeding 14 to 20 weeks and strict mating-cycle lifespans (approx. 250,000 insertions). Excessive contact resistance buildup (> 0.5 ohms per contact) over thousands of consecutive shmoo cycles causes false VDD droop rejects, requiring stringent automated socket cleaning and contactor replacement scheduling to prevent yield depression and test cell downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Running high-resolution 2D shmoo matrices (e.g., 50 VDD points x 50 tCK points x 5 pattern suites) inflates test execution time past 45 seconds per packaged chip, conflicting with throughput targets of < 4 seconds per unit during production binning. The engineering council must mandate sparse adaptive boundary-search algorithms (e.g., binary edge detection rather than full brute-force grid sweep) for production signoff while keeping fine-grid shmoo strictly for silicon characterization lots.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dynamic IR-drop induced false timing failure: Test pattern simultaneous switching output (SSO) on 16-bit wide DQ lines collapses core VDD below 1.55V momentarily, triggering false setup/hold wall shifts on tCK.
1. Socket contact resistance degradation: Contactor pin oxidation shifts the apparent low-voltage functional cliff higher by 80-120 mV after repeated insertions, artificially degrading speed-bin binning yields.
1. Pattern-dependent thermal drift: Prolonged continuous read/write shmoo loops without active thermal socket control induce local junction heating above 85°C, accelerating DRAM trench/stacked capacitor charge leakage and causing spurious retention-bound failures.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-3-1-3-01` | **2D VDD-tCK Shmoo Boundary Extraction and JEDEC Speed-Bin Verification** | Advantest V93000 / Teradyne UltraFLEX ATE system equipped with high-speed digital pins (PS1600 or equivalent), precision Device Power Supplies (DPS) with fast transient sense lines, and Kelvin-sensed active thermal control contact socket. | 1. Initialize DUT using standard JEDEC power-up sequence and load Mode Register (MR) settings (CAS Latency = 2.5, Burst Length = 8). 2. Configure 2D shmoo matrix: VDD axis swept from 1.50V to 2.10V in 20 mV increments; tCK axis swept from 15.00 ns (66 MHz) down to 5.00 ns (200 MHz) in 100 ps increments. 3. At each grid node, execute full March C- algorithm with alternating data backgrounds (checkerboard and solid 0/1). 4. Record pass/fail status per node into STDF (Standard Test Data Format) datalog. 5. Apply adaptive boundary-tracing algorithm to map passing envelope contour. | `Device must achieve a continuous PASS region encompassing VDD = 1.80V ± 0.18V (1.62V to 1.98V) at tCK <= 7.50 ns (133 MHz, DDR-266 specification) with zero bit errors across 100% of memory addresses; VDD margin at nominal 7.50 ns must extend down to <= 1.58V (>= 40 mV margin below VDD_min specification).` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-3-1-3-02` | **ATE Pin Timing Deskew and Jitter Tolerance Verification under Voltage Stress** | Wideband 20 GHz Digital Sampling Oscilloscope connected via matched 50-ohm pick-off probes to ATE load board calibration fixtures, high-precision Time Measurement Unit (TMU) within ATE digital channel architecture. | 1. Run ATE automated round-trip TDR skew calibration across all 32 channel pins (16 DQ, 2 DQS, 1 CLK_P, 1 CLK_N, 12 ADDR/CMD). 2. Program channel drivers to deliver a 100 MHz reference clock train. 3. Measure pin-to-pin timing skew and edge jitter (RMS and peak-to-peak) at the pogo-pin tips using the integrated TMU and external sampling scope across VDD levels of 1.62V, 1.80V, and 1.98V. 4. Verify propagation delay compensation across all data paths. | `Total pin-to-pin skew across all DQ/DQS strobe groups must be <= 35 ps peak-to-peak; clock duty-cycle distortion (DCD) must remain within 49.5% to 50.5%; channel driver intrinsic RMS jitter must measure <= 4.5 ps across the entire 1.62V to 1.98V supply range.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ESD-safe conductive lab coat with grounding snap, Calibrated continuous-monitoring ESD wrist strap, ANSI Z87.1 approved UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, Class 100 cleanroom compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, static dissipative)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with cleaning solvent, flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of tempered water for at least 15 minutes at the eyewash station. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, relocate personnel immediately to fresh air. If skin exposure occurs, wash thoroughly with soap and deionized water. For electrical shock from ATE mains/DPS, disengage emergency power off (EPO) switch before touching casualty, initiate CPR if pulse is absent, and call emergency services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: ATE testing floor maintained under positive-pressure HVAC with HEPA filtration (ISO Class 7 clean environment); dedicated laminar localized exhaust extraction hood (face velocity >= 0.5 m/s / 100 FPM) utilized during manual solvent cleaning of pogo-pin socket contactors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and socket swab applicators must be collected in closed, dedicated, red polyethylene hazardous flammables containers with flame arrestors; disposed of via licensed solvent waste incinerator protocols in compliance with RCRA regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (Electronics Contact Cleaning Grade)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / HPLC Grade >= 99.9% | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry-pack sealed plastic Quad Flat Packages (QFP) or Ball Grid Array (BGA) packages with moisture barrier bags (MBB) displaying desiccant humidity indicator card (HIC) < 10% RH; lead contacts free of copper/tin oxidation, solder-ball coplanarity within 0.08 mm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested and speed-binned packages with undamaged, clean contact pads/leads exhibiting pogo-pin contact scrub marks < 15 um depth; zero ionic residue or flux contamination; parts baked and resealed into dry-pack moisture barrier bags with fresh desiccant.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient moisture exposure queue time exceeds JEDEC MSL 3 floor life limits, causing moisture absorption into mold compound that risks internal package delamination, wire bond shearing, or popcorn cracking during subsequent qualification thermal cycles or board reflow assembly.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful automated ATE execution and metrology signoff of 2D VDD-tCK shmoo operational margins for 180nm open-source DRAM chips across JEDEC DDR-200/DDR-266 frequency domains. Signoff confirms full functional boundary contours, verifies minimum 10% supply margin and >= 15% timing margin beyond nominal targets, and establishes pin deskew alignment meeting JEDEC production test standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ATE_Shmoo_VDD_tCK_Matrix_Signoff_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_DDR_SpeedBin_STDF_Raw_Datalog.csv`
- [ ] `ATE_Socket_Pin_Deskew_TDR_Calibration_Log.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum operating clock frequency at nominal VDD (1.80V, 25°C) across all functional address spaces** | `133.33 MHz (tCK = 7.50 ns)` | +20.00 MHz / -0.00 MHz (tCK <= 7.50 ns) | Automated high-speed digital pattern vector execution on Advantest V93000 ATE datalogging STDF fail counts across full March C- vector set |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Minimum VDD operational margin boundary at rated clock cycle (tCK = 7.50 ns)** | `1.58 V` | ± 0.02 V (must not exceed 1.62 V absolute specification floor) | 2D VDD sweep boundary-search extraction using fine-step 10 mV DPS stepping and current compliance monitoring |
| `ASSERT-03` | **ATE DUT load board pin-to-pin timing skew after calibration across all DQ and DQS pins** | `20.0 ps` | ± 15.0 ps (Absolute max <= 35.0 ps) | TDR automated fixture calibration and TMU round-trip edge delay measurement |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal metrology signoff requires 100% of tested sample lot (minimum 50 packaged units) passing zero-defect criteria across the complete 1.62V-1.98V VDD and 7.50ns-15.00ns tCK operating rectangle under March C- pattern execution at 25°C, with validated STDF raw datalogs archived and co-signed by the Test Systems Engineer and Lead Metrologist.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Details
- **Title:** Multi-Corner Automated 2D $V_{DD}$-Frequency Matrix Stepping Execution
- **Tracking Path:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Final Automated Test Equipment (ATE) JEDEC DDR Speed-Bin & HTOL Burn-in Testing > Post-Stress ATE JEDEC DDR Speed-Binning & Shmoo Margin Metrology > 2D VDD-Frequency Shmoo Plotting & Operating Margin Metrology > Multi-Corner Automated 2D VDD-Frequency Matrix Stepping Execution
- **Technology Node:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS / Stacked Capacitor COB DRAM)
- **Action Type:** Make

---

## 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     ATE Test Head      │
│   Initialization and   │
│  Thermal Chuck Setup   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Device Parameter    │
│    Calibration and     │
│     Guardband Load     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    2D VDD-Frequency    │
│  Matrix Stepping Loop  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Burst Pattern      │
│  Execution and Shmoo   │
│   Boundary Detection   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Operating Margin    │
│     Evaluation and     │
│       Speed-Bin        │
│     Classification     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

### Step 1: ATE Hardware Calibration & Thermal Chuck Stabilization
1. Mount the packaged 180nm DRAM DUT (access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$) onto the high-speed ATE test fixture.
2. Initialize the automated thermal chuck to $85^\circ\text{C}$ to match worst-case qualification and retention leakage test conditions.
3. Verify test site contact resistance and fixture parasitic de-embedding against the manufacturing grid resolution ($0.005\ \mu\text{m}$) and Metal 1 pitch constraints ($0.34\ \mu\text{m}$).

### Step 2: Parametric Baseline Load & Dynamic Range Definition
1. Configure Device Power Supplies (DPS) around the nominal operating core supply $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
2. Define the two-dimensional Shmoo test matrix ranges:
   - **Voltage Axis ($V_{DD}$):** Sweep from $1.2\text{ V}$ to $2.2\text{ V}$ in discrete steps of $25\text{ mV}$ ($V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$ nominal reference).
   - **Frequency Axis ($f_{CLK}$):** Sweep across the target DDR clock domain from $50\text{ MHz}$ to $250\text{ MHz}$ in discrete steps of $5\text{ MHz}$.
3. Load calibration baseline parameters based on verified Stage 3 test structures ($W/L = 2.0\ \mu\text{m} / 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$ sub-micron transistor metrics).

### Step 3: Automated Multi-Corner Stepping & Functional Pattern Burst
1. Initiate the nested 2D matrix loop on the ATE pattern generator:
   - Outer loop: Increment core supply voltage $V_{DD}$.
   - Inner loop: Step vector clock frequency $f_{CLK}$ and program vector timing generators.
2. For each matrix coordinate $(V_{DD},\, f_{CLK})$, allow DPS settling for $500\ \mu\text{s}$.
3. Apply JEDEC DDR functional march and retention bursts across all bitcells with minimum stored node capacitance $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$.
4. Capture pin comparator responses into the ATE vector failure buffer to flag bit failure addresses and determine PASS/FAIL state.

### Step 4: Shmoo Boundary Extraction & Margin Assessment
1. Identify the operating envelope boundary line $f_{MAX}(V_{DD})$ across the 2D plane.
2. Verify that at nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$ and $85^\circ\text{C}$, the access transistor sub-threshold and junction leakage does not cause data loss during standard cycle timing.
3. Automatically log pass/fail status and compute operating voltage margin guardbands ($V_{DD,min}$ to $V_{DD,max}$) for speed-bin sorting.

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nominal Operating Supply Voltage ($V_{DD}$)** | $1.8 \pm 0.18$ | $\text{V}$ | ATE Precision DPS Metrology |
| **Array Cell Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage** | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | ATE Low-Current Parametric Measurement Unit (PMU) |
| **Cell Node Storage Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 28.0$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | ATE Impedance Metrology / High-k Stack Resonant Sense |
| **Nominal Drive Current ($I_{on}$ at $V_{GS} = V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$)** | $\ge 500.0$ | $\mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ | Test Transistor Array PMU Calibration Sweep |
| **On/Off Current Ratio ($I_{on}/I_{off}$)** | $> 1.0 \times 10^7$ | Dimensionless (Ratio) | In-line Parametric Extrapolation ($V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$ vs $0\text{ V}$) |

---

## 4. Parametric Targets & Threshold Visualization

```text
                                                        
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │█████                               │
Vthp Nom (x100 mV)┤█████                               │
                  │▓▓▓                                 │
   Cap Budget (fF)┤▓▓▓                                 │
Vthn Nom (x100 mV)┤▒▒▒▒▒                               │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒                               │
Ion Target (uA/um)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                   0       125      250     375     500 
```

---

## 5. Verified Literature Sources Cited
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Access transistor dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), minimum capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF/cell}$, ONO/high-k dielectric stack ($\kappa > 15$), and leakage budget target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification:** Device dimensions ($W/L = 2.0\ \mu\text{m} / 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$), nominal core bias $V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$, threshold voltages ($V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, $V_{thp} = -0.60\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$), $I_{on} \ge 500\ \mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ (at $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$), $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA}/\mu\text{m}$ (at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$), and $I_{on}/I_{off} > 10^7$.
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid:** Placement grid resolution ($0.005\ \mu\text{m}$), minimum poly gate length ($0.15\ \mu\text{m}$), minimum contact dimension ($0.17\ \mu\text{m} \times 0.17\ \mu\text{m}$), and Metal 1 pitch ($0.34\ \mu\text{m}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated 2D VDD-frequency stepping on ATE requires robust synchronization between programmable low-noise DC Device Power Supplies (DPS) and high-speed algorithmic pattern generators (APG). The transient settling time of the DPS rail during millivolt-scale stepping must not corrupt edge-placement timing generators or cause ground-bounce false triggers during high-density DDR pattern bursts.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In 180nm planar DRAM nodes operating at nominal VDD=1.8V (peripheral) and VDD2=1.8V/2.5V (array pump levels), the Shmoo matrix must capture the sensitive boundary between sense-amplifier evaluation failure at reduced VDD and wordline boost breakdown or subthreshold leakage at elevated VDD across DDR clock frequencies from 100 MHz to 266 MHz (DDR-200 to DDR-533 bins). Step granularity must not exceed 25mV and 5MHz to prevent missing sharp pass/fail cliff edges.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring commercial production ATE test time (e.g., Advantest T5503 or Teradyne UltraFLEX) with multi-site contactor hardware carries high hourly NRE. Test execution scripts must optimize matrix search algorithms (such as binary search or edge-tracking algorithms rather than brute-force exhaustive sweeping) to minimize test socket hold time and overall qualification test cost per packaged unit.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Multi-corner Shmoo metrology directly gates JEDEC speed-bin qualification signoff. Test socket wear on fine-pitch BGA load boards and thermal drift inside the environmental test chamber during multi-corner stepping (-40°C, 25°C, 85°C, 125°C) pose severe schedule slippage risks if uncalibrated thermal runaway invalidates qualification test lots.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway or junction temperature drift during extended stepping bursts causing artificial frequency roll-off and distorted Shmoo pass/fail boundary profiles.
1. ATE DPS voltage overshoot/undershoot transients exceeding device absolute maximum ratings (AMR) during rapid matrix step transitions, inducing irreversible dielectric breakdown in thin gate oxides.
1. High contact resistance (CRES) or socket pin degradation during repeated socketing leading to anomalous VDD droop and false pattern failures at higher operating frequencies.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-3-2-01` | **Automated 2D VDD-Frequency Shmoo Boundary Search under Nominal Room Temperature** | Automated Test Equipment (Advantest T5503HS2 or Teradyne J750/UltraFLEX equivalent) equipped with High-Speed Pin Electronics (PE), Programmable DPS (0-3.6V, 2A, <1mV resolution), Kelvin-sensed BGA-60 test socket load board, and Active Thermal Control (ATC) socket collar set to 25°C ± 1°C. | 1. Initialize ATE pattern generator with JEDEC DDR March C- test sequence (write/read checkerboard and alternating patterns across all internal banks). 2. Program VDD sweep from 1.50V to 2.10V in 25mV increments. 3. At each voltage step, initialize active thermal stabilization and allow DPS settling time of 5ms. 4. Step clock frequency (tCK) from 100 MHz to 266 MHz (equivalent to DDR-200 up to DDR-533) in 5MHz increments. 5. Run full pattern burst at each (VDD, Frequency) coordinate; log bit-failure count and categorize coordinate as PASS (0 bit errors) or FAIL (>0 bit errors). 6. Compile 25x34 coordinate matrix into structured STIL/CSV dataset. | `Device must achieve a continuous PASS region encompassing nominal operating conditions (VDD = 1.80V ± 0.10V at minimum 166 MHz / DDR-333) with zero bit errors. The measured VDD operating margin must be >= ±150mV at 133 MHz (DDR-266) with sharp, monotonic boundary transitions.` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-3-2-02` | **High-Temperature HTOL Multi-Corner Shmoo Operating Window Verification** | Production Memory ATE system integrated with Thermostream/Thermal Chamber unit with automated temperature forcing capability (-40°C to +125°C ±0.5°C), 4-wire Kelvin DPS channels with real-time current logging, calibrated high-frequency differential clock driver. | 1. Soak DUT at 85°C for 15 minutes to guarantee thermal stabilization. 2. Load JEDEC standard Read/Write stress pattern sequence including Row-Hammer stress and burst refresh margin testing (tREFI = 64ms/8192 cycles). 3. Perform 2D matrix stepping across VDD (1.60V to 2.05V in 25mV steps) and clock frequency (100 MHz to 200 MHz in 5MHz steps). 4. Record IDD4R and IDD4W dynamic currents simultaneously using synchronized ATE DPS measurement units. 5. Plot 2D pass/fail operating boundary and determine upper/lower VDD operating limits at 166 MHz. | `At 85°C, the device must maintain stable functionality at nominal VDD = 1.80V at >= 166 MHz (DDR-333 timing) without refresh fail or write-recovery violations. Operating voltage window (VDD_max - VDD_min) at 166 MHz must exceed 250mV.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ESD-safe cleanroom coat (surface resistivity < 10^9 ohms/sq), Thermal insulated safety gloves for handling hot/cold test sockets (-40°C to +125°C), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Grounded dissipative ESD wrist/heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Wash affected skin immediately with running water and soap. Thermal contact burn from hot socket/platen: Immediately flush area with cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; seek immediate medical attention. Inhalation of inert N2: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen or artificial respiration if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom HVAC airflow with localized exhaust on thermal forcing equipment (minimum 50 CFM) to vent nitrogen purge gas and prevent oxygen depletion in test bays; ambient O2 monitoring alarms calibrated to trigger below 19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA and lint-free wipes must be deposited in dedicated FM-approved flammables waste cans with self-closing foot lids; collected solvent disposed of as hazardous VOC waste via licensed chemical waste management handlers in compliance with local environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, used for test socket and load board contactor cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Tier C) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2, gaseous for chamber purge and thermal conditioning)** | `7727-37-9` | High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Packaged FBGA-60 devices singulated and dried according to JEDEC J-STD-033 MSL-3 baking standards; Au/Ni or SAC305 solder balls clean, free of organic flux residues or oxidation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested FBGA package solder balls verified free of mechanical gouging, socket pin pitting, or conductive debris; contact coplanarity preserved within JEDEC spec (< 0.08mm).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive moisture absorption leading to package popcorning during elevated thermal testing (>85°C/125°C) and surface oxidation of BGA balls inducing intermittent high contact resistance (CRES) and false ATE speed-bin failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full multi-corner 2D VDD-versus-frequency Shmoo characterization matrix successfully acquired across packaged 180nm DRAM test lots across specified voltage (1.50V-2.10V), frequency (100MHz-266MHz), and temperature (-40°C, 25°C, 85°C) corners, establishing validated JEDEC speed-bin boundaries and VDD operating margins.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM180_ATE_Shmoo_Matrix_Results_Corner_25C_85C.csv`
- [ ] `DRAM180_JEDEC_SpeedBin_Operating_Margin_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `DRAM180_2D_VDD_Freq_Shmoo_HighRes_ColorMap.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Minimum functional DDR operating frequency at nominal peripheral VDD = 1.80V and T_case = 25°C across full memory array.** | `166.0` | +100.0/-0.0 MHz | Automated ATE March C- memory pattern burst pass/fail verification. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Continuous stable VDD operating voltage margin window at DDR-266 (133 MHz clock) at T_case = 25°C.** | `350.0` | ±50.0 mV | Calculated as (VDD_pass_max - VDD_pass_min) from empirical 2D Shmoo CSV matrix data. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Device Power Supply (DPS) step-to-burst settling time during automated 2D stepping.** | `5.0` | +2.0/-0.0 ms | ATE oscilloscope/digitizer rail voltage capture during multi-step execution. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit condition requires 100% automated matrix execution across all sampled qualification units without test aborts, confirmed generation of all three deliverable artifacts, and zero unexplained non-monotonic pass/fail holes within the nominal operating envelope (VDD=1.8V ± 100mV, f >= 166 MHz) signed off by the Metrology Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Pass/Fail Boundary Extraction & JEDEC Operating Margin Statistical Yield Analysis

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated boundary extraction on 2D VDD-Frequency Shmoo matrices requires rigorous synchronization between the pattern generator clock verniers and Device Power Supply (DPS) voltage settling times. At 180nm CMOS nodes, VDD transients during rapid burst read/write patterns induce L*di/dt ground bounce on load boards if decoupling capacitor loop inductance exceeds 1.2 nH. If DPS transient droop is not decoupled from core VDD margin measurements, artificial pass/fail boundary degradation will distort statistical Cpk and incorrectly truncate JEDEC DDR-200/DDR-333 operating envelopes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Characterizing JEDEC operating margins post-HTOL stress demands isolation of transistor threshold voltage shift (NBTI/PBTI) and hot-carrier degradation from contact sheet resistance drift. Shmoo pass/fail boundary contours exhibit non-linear knee points where sense amplifier differential latching times diverge exponentially at lower VDD. The statistical extraction algorithm must fit empirical shmoo contours against a bivariate Gaussian or logistic boundary regression rather than crude linear thresholding, ensuring that the 180nm DRAM cell retention limit (tREFI = 64 ms at 85 deg C) is evaluated at the minimum operational VDD envelope.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: ATE test-time overhead per packaged unit during full 2D VDD-frequency shmoo sweeps directly dictates final test cost and packaging floor capacity. Executing exhaustive fine-pitch shmoo matrix sweeps (e.g., 50 mV x 5 MHz steps) across 100% of production units is cost-prohibitive. The metrology pipeline must employ an adaptive bisection search algorithm or diagonally biased boundary tracking to restrict tester dwell time to under 1.8 seconds per device while maintaining statistical correlation to baseline JEDEC qualification lots.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test cell scheduling on the high-speed digital ATE system requires strict coordination with socket wear-out management and pogo-pin contact resistance monitoring. Interconnect contact degradation on the test socket directly mimics VDD-min boundary collapse. The project milestone requires automated sign-off scripts that parse STDF (Standard Test Data Format) datalogs directly into yield models within 30 minutes of lot completion, preventing downstream tapeout and assembly pipeline bottlenecks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Socket contact resistance (Cres) escalation beyond 250 mOhm inducing excessive IR drop, falsely shifting the extracted VDD-min operating boundary upward by >80 mV.
1. DPS transient slew-rate under-damping triggering false latch-up or soft data corruption during dense pseudo-random bit sequence (PRBS) read bursts at elevated frequencies.
1. Algorithmic boundary fitting convergence failure on disjoint or checkerboard shmoo regions caused by single-bit retention marginalities under maximum junction temperature.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-3-3-01` | **2D VDD-Frequency Shmoo Operating Boundary Extraction & Margin Verification** | Advantest T5588 or Teradyne UltraFLEX High-Speed Memory Digital ATE, high-bandwidth active socket test fixture (<1.2 nH loop inductance), precision DPS channel with remote Kelvin sensing. | 1. Dock device in calibrated 50-ohm matched impedance test socket with remote Kelvin voltage sense at socket leads. 2. Initialize VDD sweep grid from 1.40 V to 2.00 V in 25 mV increments. 3. Initialize DDR clock frequency (tCK) sweep grid from 100 MHz to 200 MHz in 5 MHz increments. 4. Execute JEDEC compliant March C- and PRBS burst read/write patterns at each coordinate with refresh interval tREFI = 64 ms. 5. Record pass/fail status per coordinate into binary vector array. 6. Execute 2D contour boundary extraction algorithm to determine VDD_min at nominal 166 MHz (DDR-333) and F_max at nominal 1.80 V core supply. | `Extracted VDD_min at 166 MHz (DDR-333) must be <= 1.65 V (>= 150 mV margin below nominal 1.80 V JEDEC specification); maximum operating frequency F_max at VDD = 1.80 V must be >= 185 MHz (>= 11.4% frequency margin above DDR-333 rating).` |
| `TC-ATE-JEDEC-QUALIFICATION-3-3-3-02` | **JEDEC Operating Window Statistical Yield and Cpk Distribution Metrology** | Automated IC handler integrated with ATE test controller, automated STDF log parser, statistical analysis engine running R/Python yield metrology suite. | 1. Load and execute adaptive shmoo extraction pipeline across all 250 units under both 25 deg C and 85 deg C. 2. Capture extracted parameter pairs (VDD_min, F_max) per device in STDF format. 3. Calculate mean, standard deviation (sigma), and process capability indices (Cp, Cpk) for the operational margin parameter delta_VDD = (1.80 V - VDD_min). 4. Perform Anderson-Darling normality test on extracted margin boundaries. 5. Plot 6-sigma bivariate probability density contour against JEDEC DDR specification limits. | `Process capability metric Cpk for VDD operating margin (delta_VDD >= 150 mV at 166 MHz, 85 deg C) must achieve Cpk >= 1.33; cumulative statistical yield across the JEDEC DDR-333 nominal diamond window (1.80 V +/- 0.15 V, tCK = 6.0 ns) must be >= 98.5%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified ESD-dissipative safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom lab coat (Class 10,000 / ISO 7 compliant), Conductive ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, Powder-free cleanroom-grade nitrile gloves (anti-static treated), Thermal protective gloves rated to 150 deg C for handler thermal chuck servicing
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated static-dissipative clothing. Inhalation: Move individual to fresh clean air environment. Burns from thermal head: Cool thermal burn area under cold running water for 15 minutes and seek medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom laminar airflow (Class 10,000 / ISO 7) with minimum 30 air changes per hour; local exhaust ventilation ducting (>= 50 CFM) connected to thermal stream / chuck exhaust port to evacuate heated air and trace solvent vapors during socket contact defluxing.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and IPA rinse residues must be sealed in airtight conductive, flame-retardant hazardous waste bins designated for flammable organic solvents and disposed of via certified hazardous chemical waste handlers; no drain disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-plated Sn-Bi or SAC308 lead-free solder ball/pad arrays post-HTOL stress, clean of organic flux residues, ionic contamination < 0.1 ug/cm2 NaCl equivalent, with native oxide thickness < 1.8 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Passivated, electrically characterized packaged DRAM units with contact pogo-pin indentations within IPC-A-610 Class 3 tolerances (< 15 um depth), free of micro-cracks, ready for tape-and-reel or dry-pack storage.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient humidity exposure queue time induces moisture absorption into mold compound (MSL-3 degradation) and atmospheric oxidation of lead terminals, causing socket contact resistance creep (>0.5 Ohm), localized micro-arcing, and false VDD-min boundary contraction during high-frequency ATE cycling.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full algorithmic extraction and statistical yield qualification of 2D VDD-Frequency shmoo boundaries for Gen 3 180nm open-source DRAM packaged units under JEDEC DDR-333 operating conditions, establishing high-confidence process capability (Cpk >= 1.33) and validating post-burn-in reliability margins.

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
