# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: High-Vacuum Cryopump & Turbomolecular Pump Regeneration and Leak Rate Qualification
**Context Path:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > BEOL Multi-Layer Metal Interconnect Deposition (Metal 1, Metal 2, and Passivation) > M1/M2 High-Vacuum DC Magnetron Sputter Deposition & Anneal > High-Vacuum Chamber Conditioning & Base Pressure Calibration > Process Parameter Benchmarking for High-Vacuum Chamber Conditioning & Base Pressure Calibration  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm DRAM Node)  
**Process Type:** Thin Film Deposition / Vacuum Maintenance & Metrology  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP defines the technical sequence for full thermal regeneration of high-vacuum cryopumps, purging/spin qualification of turbomolecular pumping stations, and direct chamber rate-of-rise (leak/outgassing) qualification. Executing this procedure ensures that the PVD metallization chamber achieves baseline ultimate pressure conditions preventing oxygen contamination during 180nm DRAM bitline and wordline strapping interconnect sputtering.

---

### 2. Required Literature References
- **Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**
  - Vacuum chamber base pressure requirement: $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ prior to sputtering to prevent oxygen incorporation.
  - Sputtering process gas: High-purity Argon (Ar 99.999% / 5N) maintained at $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$ working pressure.
  - Target & DC Power: 99.999% (5N) Aluminum target operated at $1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$ DC magnetron power.
  - Film deposition rate benchmark: $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/min}$ (Metal-1 nominal thickness: $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Isolation & Initial Chamber Pump-Down Configuration
1. Confirm DC magnetron power supplies are locked out ($0\text{ kW}$) and high-purity Argon gas supply lines (Ar 99.999%) are isolated via pneumatic shutoff valves.
2. Close the high-vacuum isolation gate valve between the main PVD process chamber and the high-vacuum pumping package (cryopump / turbomolecular pump).
3. Verify roughing vacuum lines are pumped down below cross-over threshold via dry backing pumps.

#### Step 2: High-Vacuum Cryopump Thermal Regeneration
1. **Warm-Up Cycle:** Initiate regeneration sequence; turn off cryocooler compressor and activate internal two-stage electrical regeneration heaters. Vent the cryopump vessel with heated dry nitrogen purge gas ($N_2 \ge 99.999\%$ at $60^\circ\text{C}-70^\circ\text{C}$) to release cryo-trapped hydrogen, water vapor, and condensed argon.
2. **Purge & Vent:** Continue positive pressure dry purge until the 1st stage array reaches $> 290\text{ K}$ and 2nd stage charcoal array reaches $> 290\text{ K}$. Exhaust effluent via dedicated scrubber line.
3. **Roughing Evacuation:** Isolate nitrogen purge and open roughing valve to evacuate the pump body down to $< 50\text{ mTorr}$ using the oil-free backing pump.
4. **Cooldown Cycle:** Close roughing valve. Re-engage the helium compressor circuit to initiate cryo-refrigeration down to steady-state cryogenic temperatures: 1st stage array $\le 65\text{ K}$ and 2nd stage charcoal array $\le 15\text{ K}$.

#### Step 3: Turbomolecular Pump (TMP) Bakeout & Rotational Qualification
1. If operating on TMP high-vacuum configuration, confirm full rated rotational speed ($100\%$ nominal RPM, zero bearing drag vibration).
2. Engage chamber and foreline heating jackets to initiate mild chamber degas/bakeout ($100^\circ\text{C}-120^\circ\text{C}$) while maintaining backing line flow to eliminate desorbed atmospheric moisture.

#### Step 4: High-Vacuum Gate Valve Engagement & Deep Pump-Down
1. Open the high-vacuum main gate valve between the conditioned PVD chamber and the regenerated cryopump / qualified TMP.
2. Monitor wide-range Bayard-Alpert ion gauge telemetry during high-vacuum pump-down.
3. Pump down the PVD chamber continuously until the chamber achieves the verified qualification base pressure of $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$.

#### Step 5: Rate-of-Rise (ROR) Leak & Outgassing Rate Qualification
1. With the chamber at base pressure ($< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$), close the main high-vacuum gate valve.
2. Record initial pressure $P_0$ using calibrated capacitance manometer / high-accuracy Penning gauge at $t_0 = 0\text{ s}$.
3. Monitor pressure rise over an isolation period of $t = 300\text{ s}$ ($5\text{ minutes}$), recording final pressure $P_f$.
4. Calculate the leak/outgassing rate $Q$:
   $$Q = \frac{(P_f - P_0) \times V_{\text{chamber}}}{\Delta t}$$
5. Confirm calculated rate meets the production acceptance envelope prior to releasing tool for 5N Aluminum sputter runs.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter | Metric / Target Threshold | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **High-Vacuum Base Pressure** | $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | In-situ Bayard-Alpert Ion Gauge reading at cold pump baseline |
| **Cryopump 2nd Stage Temperature** | $\le 15$ | $\text{K}$ | Calibrated Silicon Diode Cryogenic Temperature Sensor |
| **Cryopump 1st Stage Temperature** | $\le 65$ | $\text{K}$ | Thermocouple / Diode Sensor on 1st Stage Baffle |
| **Chamber Rate-of-Rise (Leak + Outgassing)** | $< 1.0 \times 10^{-5}$ | $\text{Torr}\cdot\text{L}/\text{s}$ | 5-minute isolated Rate-of-Rise calculation |

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Cryopump regeneration sequences must be tightly interlocked with the dry backing/roughing pump and automated gate valves to prevent oil-free backstreaming or thermal runaways during warm-up purge cycles. Integrating both high-capacity cryopumps and magnetic-levitation turbomolecular pumps (TMP) requires dual-gauge Penning/Pirani sensor validation across the 760 Torr down to 10^-8 Torr range to ensure gate valves never actuate above safe crossover pressures (typically 1.0x10^-1 Torr for TMP and 1.5x10^-1 Torr for cryopump).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm BEOL DRAM M1/M2 metallization, residual partial pressures of H2O, O2, and hydrocarbon contaminants are disastrous; an unregenerated cryo-array saturated with hydrogen or water vapor limits chamber base pressure above the required 2.0x10^-6 Torr threshold. This results in direct oxygen incorporation during DC magnetron sputtering of Al-0.5% Cu interconnects, driving sheet resistance above the acceptable 0.08 Ohm/sq boundary and causing inter-die bitline RC delay variance.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring ultra-high-purity (5N5 / 99.9995%) dry gaseous nitrogen for heated purge regeneration and helium recharge circuits for closed-cycle Gifford-McMahon cryo-refrigerators has severe lead times. Standardizing on standard CF/ISO-F elastomer-free metal gasket seals (OFHC copper) and sourcing helium leak detectors locally ensures maintenance downtime does not cascade into the commercial MPW tapeout schedule.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The regeneration qualification cycle represents an unallocated 8-to-12 hour equipment maintenance window that directly compresses BEOL wafer run rate. The protocol must mandate an automated pressure-rise (rate-of-rise) leak-back test with automated CSV logging and clear pass/fail milestones so shifts can immediately resume production sputtering without waiting for manual sign-off.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal crossover failure: Opening high-vacuum gate valve when chamber pressure exceeds cryopump adsorption threshold, dumping thermal load and instantly desorbing trapped volatile gases (H2, CH4, CO).
1. Atmospheric virtual or real helium leak: Micro-fissures in CF flange copper seals or cryopump second-stage thermocouple feeds causing chamber leak rate > 1.0x10^-9 mbar*L/s, preventing ultimate base pressure below 2.0x10^-6 Torr.
1. Backing line pressure surge during TMP regeneration/purge: Rotor stall or ceramic bearing degradation due to improper backing valve sequencing against the dry scroll pump.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-2-1-01` | **Cryopump Full Thermal Regeneration and Cooldown Performance Qualification** | Calibrated Bayard-Alpert Ionization Gauge, Stage-1/Stage-2 Silicon Diode Cryo-thermometers, Mass Flow Controller for heated N2 purge, Exhaust Overpressure Relief Valve Monitor | 1. Initiate automated warm-up cycle by disabling helium compressor and activating internal 65°C N2 purge gas at 10 SLM until 1st stage reaches 300 K and 2nd stage reaches 300 K. 2. Evacuate cryopump body with roughing dry pump to < 5.0x10^-2 Torr; perform roughing rate-of-rise test for 10 minutes to verify complete outgassing. 3. Turn on closed-loop helium compressor and log cooldown temperature vs. time curve for both stages. 4. Record timestamp when Stage 1 reaches <= 65 K and Stage 2 reaches <= 15 K. 5. Measure ultimate blank-off vacuum pressure at cryopump inlet. | `Cooldown time from 300 K to Stage 1 <= 65 K and Stage 2 <= 15 K must be <= 120 minutes. Cryopump blank-off ultimate pressure after cooldown must reach <= 1.0x10^-7 Torr.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-2-1-02` | **High-Vacuum PVD Chamber Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Rate and Rate-of-Rise Qualification** | Calibrated Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Detector (sensitivity 1.0x10^-11 mbar*L/s), Calibrated Capacitance Manometer (0.1 Torr full scale), Stabilized Ionization Gauge | 1. Connect helium leak detector in sniffing/reverse-flow mode to the high-vacuum turbo/cryo backing manifold. 2. Spray certified 99.99% He gas at all chamber viewports, CF/KF flanges, magnetron cathode feedthroughs, and gas inlet lines using a calibrated needle nozzle at 2.0 sccm for 5 seconds per joint. 3. Record maximum helium peak signal in mbar*L/s. 4. Isolate the PVD chamber from all vacuum pumps by closing all gate, slit, and roughing valves. 5. Log pressure rise every 60 seconds for 30 minutes via capacitance manometer and calculate dynamic rate of rise (Torr*L/s). | `Maximum helium localized leak rate must be <= 1.0x10^-9 mbar*L/s. The chamber outgassing and leak-back rate-of-rise must be <= 5.0x10^-7 Torr*L/s over 30 minutes, confirming chamber base pressure capability < 2.0x10^-6 Torr.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cryogenic thermal-insulating gloves (EN 511 compliant), Full-face polycarbonate splash shield, Cleanroom class 100 antistatic flame-resistant lab coat, Nitrile chemical-resistant under-gloves, Steel-toe electrostatic discharge (ESD) safety footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For cryogenic burns/frostbite from cryo-array contact or liquid venting: Immediately flush affected skin with lukewarm water (40-42°C); do not rub or apply dry heat; seek immediate medical attention. For asphyxiation from N2 or He displacement: Immediately relocate victim to fresh air; administer oxygen or CPR if respiration ceases. For solvent contact: Flush eyes or skin with deionized water for at least 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Cryopump overpressure safety relief valves (set to 3-5 psig) must vent directly into an active, dedicated semiconductor house scrubber exhaust duct. Ambient oxygen deficiency monitoring sensors (ODS) set to alarm at < 19.5% O2 must be operational within 2 meters of the vacuum pumps.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Desorbed volatile hydrocarbons and process gases from cryo regeneration must flow through dedicated house scrubbers. Spent IPA cleaning wipes must be collected in closed hazardous-waste flammables bins and disposed of according to class IB solvent regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Helium (Compressor Refrigerant & Tracer Gas)** | `7440-59-7` | Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Nitrogen (Regeneration Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (99.9995%) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (Flange & O-Ring Cleaning Solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, degreased chamber internal walls and target assemblies with post-roughing vacuum level held under dry N2 atmosphere or ambient cleanroom air during maintenance seal exchange.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Bakeout-conditioned, ultra-high-vacuum decontaminated chamber interior with base pressure verified below 2.0x10^-6 Torr and cryopump Stage 2 temperature stable below 15 K.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive moisture adsorption onto unconditioned chamber walls and cryo-shields forms a condensed water film; during subsequent DC sputtering, plasma dissociation yields active oxygen that oxidizes the aluminum target face, causing severe micro-arcing and film resistivity exceeding the 0.08 Ohm/sq specification.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful full regeneration, cooldown, and leak qualification of the high-vacuum cryopump and turbomolecular pump system on the BEOL DC magnetron sputtering tool, guaranteeing base pressure pump-down below 2.0x10^-6 Torr with verified leak tightness.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CRYOPUMP_REGEN_COOLDOWN_TELEMETRY_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `HELIUM_MASS_SPEC_LEAK_CHECK_CERTIFICATE.pdf`
- [ ] `CHAMBER_RATE_OF_RISE_QUALIFICATION_REPORT.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Cryopump Second-Stage Operating Temperature** | `12.0` | +3.0 / -2.0 K | In-situ calibrated silicon diode cryo-sensor logged via PLC |
| `ASSERT-02` | **PVD Sputtering Chamber Ultimate Base Pressure** | `1.5e-6` | < 2.0e-6 Torr | Calibrated Bayard-Alpert nude ionization gauge continuous measurement |
| `ASSERT-03` | **PVD Chamber Helium Integral Leak Rate** | `5.0e-10` | <= 1.0e-9 mbar*L/s | Calibrated helium mass spectrometer leak detector reverse-flow sniffing check |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Cryopump Stage 2 temperature confirmed <= 15 K, chamber pump-down to < 2.0x10^-6 Torr reached within 120 minutes of valve opening, and 30-minute chamber rate-of-rise verified <= 5.0x10^-7 Torr*L/s with zero helium leaks detected above 1.0x10^-9 mbar*L/s.

testcases.title: Cryopump Full Thermal Regeneration and Cooldown Performance Qualification
testcases.instrumentation: Calibrated Bayard-Alpert Ionization Gauge, Stage-1/Stage-2 Silicon Diode Cryo-thermometers, Mass Flow Controller for heated N2 purge, Exhaust Overpressure Relief Valve Monitor
testcases.pre_conditions: Cryopump isolated from PVD main sputtering chamber via electro-pneumatic gate valve; roughing dry pump connected and leak-tested; heated dry N2 purge supply at 65°C verified at 15 psig.
testcases.procedure:
1. Initiate automated warm-up cycle by disabling helium compressor and activating internal 65°C N2 purge gas at 10 SLM until 1st stage reaches 300 K and 2nd stage reaches 300 K.
2. Evacuate cryopump body with roughing dry pump to < 5.0x10^-2 Torr; perform roughing rate-of-rise test for 10 minutes to verify complete outgassing.
3. Turn on closed-loop helium compressor and log cooldown temperature vs. time curve for both stages.
4. Record timestamp when Stage 1 reaches <= 65 K and Stage 2 reaches <= 15 K.
5. Measure ultimate blank-off vacuum pressure at cryopump inlet.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Cooldown time from 300 K to Stage 1 <= 65 K and Stage 2 <= 15 K must be <= 120 minutes. Cryopump blank-off ultimate pressure after cooldown must reach <= 1.0x10^-7 Torr.

testcases.title: High-Vacuum PVD Chamber Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Rate and Rate-of-Rise Qualification
testcases.instrumentation: Calibrated Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Detector (sensitivity 1.0x10^-11 mbar*L/s), Calibrated Capacitance Manometer (0.1 Torr full scale), Stabilized Ionization Gauge
testcases.pre_conditions: PVD chamber conditioning completed; cryopump and TMP fully regenerated and operational; chamber pumped down below 1.0x10^-5 Torr; external helium calibration leak standard calibrated and attached.
testcases.procedure:
1. Connect helium leak detector in sniffing/reverse-flow mode to the high-vacuum turbo/cryo backing manifold.
2. Spray certified 99.99% He gas at all chamber viewports, CF/KF flanges, magnetron cathode feedthroughs, and gas inlet lines using a calibrated needle nozzle at 2.0 sccm for 5 seconds per joint.
3. Record maximum helium peak signal in mbar*L/s.
4. Isolate the PVD chamber from all vacuum pumps by closing all gate, slit, and roughing valves.
5. Log pressure rise every 60 seconds for 30 minutes via capacitance manometer and calculate dynamic rate of rise (Torr*L/s).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Maximum helium localized leak rate must be <= 1.0x10^-9 mbar*L/s. The chamber outgassing and leak-back rate-of-rise must be <= 5.0x10^-7 Torr*L/s over 30 minutes, confirming chamber base pressure capability < 2.0x10^-6 Torr.

ppe_required: Cryogenic thermal-insulating gloves (EN 511 compliant)
Full-face polycarbonate splash shield
Cleanroom class 100 antistatic flame-resistant lab coat
Nitrile chemical-resistant under-gloves
Steel-toe electrostatic discharge (ESD) safety footwear
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For cryogenic burns/frostbite from cryo-array contact or liquid venting: Immediately flush affected skin with lukewarm water (40-42°C); do not rub or apply dry heat; seek immediate medical attention. For asphyxiation from N2 or He displacement: Immediately relocate victim to fresh air; administer oxygen or CPR if respiration ceases. For solvent contact: Flush eyes or skin with deionized water for at least 15 minutes.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Cryopump overpressure safety relief valves (set to 3-5 psig) must vent directly into an active, dedicated semiconductor house scrubber exhaust duct. Ambient oxygen deficiency monitoring sensors (ODS) set to alarm at < 19.5% O2 must be operational within 2 meters of the vacuum pumps.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Desorbed volatile hydrocarbons and process gases from cryo regeneration must flow through dedicated house scrubbers. Spent IPA cleaning wipes must be collected in closed hazardous-waste flammables bins and disposed of according to class IB solvent regulations.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Pre-cleaned, degreased chamber internal walls and target assemblies with post-roughing vacuum level held under dry N2 atmosphere or ambient cleanroom air during maintenance seal exchange.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Bakeout-conditioned, ultra-high-vacuum decontaminated chamber interior with base pressure verified below 2.0x10^-6 Torr and cryopump Stage 2 temperature stable below 15 K.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excessive moisture adsorption onto unconditioned chamber walls and cryo-shields forms a condensed water film; during subsequent DC sputtering, plasma dissociation yields active oxygen that oxidizes the aluminum target face, causing severe micro-arcing and film resistivity exceeding the 0.08 Ohm/sq specification.

expected_result.summary: Successful full regeneration, cooldown, and leak qualification of the high-vacuum cryopump and turbomolecular pump system on the BEOL DC magnetron sputtering tool, guaranteeing base pressure pump-down below 2.0x10^-6 Torr with verified leak tightness.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** Chamber Bake-Out and Base Pressure Pump-Down Conditioning ($< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$)  
**Context:** DRAM Foundation VN — 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Module:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization Interconnect Deposition (M1/M2 High-Vacuum Sputter Deposition)  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Chamber Seal & Rough  │
│          Pump          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      High-Vacuum       │
│    Cryo/Turbo Pump     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Chamber Wall      │
│        Bake-Out        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Cool-Down & Degas    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Base Pressure      │
│  Baseline < 2e-6 Torr  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Evacuation Inspection & Sealing**:
   - Inspect the planar DC magnetron PVD chamber O-rings, target dark-space shield, and 5N (99.999%) aluminum target assembly.
   - Close the loadlock isolation slit valve and rough-pump the deposition chamber using the mechanical dry backing pump to crossover pressure ($\sim 50\text{ mTorr} - 100\text{ mTorr}$).

2. **High-Vacuum Pumping Engagement**:
   - Open the high-vacuum gate valve to engage the turbomolecular pump or cryopump system.
   - Monitor the cold cathode / inverted magnetron ionization gauge during initial pump-down through the $10^{-4}\text{ Torr}$ to $10^{-5}\text{ Torr}$ transition.

3. **Chamber Bake-Out Thermal Cycle**:
   - Energize the external chamber resistive heating jackets.
   - Ramp the chamber wall temperature at $\le 5^\circ\text{C/min}$ to the bake-out setpoint ($120^\circ\text{C} - 150^\circ\text{C}$) to drive off adsorbed atmospheric moisture ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$), hydrocarbons, and ambient gases from the chamber walls and target shields.
   - Maintain isothermal bake-out dwell under continuous turbomolecular/cryogenic pumping until the outgassing rate decays and ionization current stabilizes.

4. **Cool-Down & Substrate/Target Degas**:
   - De-energize bake-out heating jackets and allow the chamber shell to cool to baseline process temperature ($\le 25^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Condition substrate heater stage and verify no thermal runaway or residual gas bursts.

5. **Final Base Pressure Baseline Verification**:
   - Confirm background chamber vacuum stabilizes below the required threshold of $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ prior to argon process gas introduction.
   - Check that the chamber is ready for 99.999% high-purity Argon gas admission at 3 to 5 mTorr working pressure.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ultimate Base Chamber Pressure** | $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | Calibrated Bayard-Alpert / Cold Cathode Ionization Vacuum Gauge |
| **Sputter Process Gas Purity** | $\ge 99.999$ | $\%$ | Online Mass Flow / Gas Inlet Purity Sensor (Ar line) |
| **Process Working Pressure Range** | $3.0\text{ to }5.0$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer Gauge under dynamic Ar flow |
| **Aluminum Target Purity Rating** | $\ge 99.999$ | $\%$ (5N) | Target Material Ingot / Lot Certificate of Conformance |

---

### 3. Context References

- **[Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects](./docs/context.yaml)**:
  - *Base Pressure Requirement*: Base pressure must pump down below $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ using turbomolecular or cryopump to prevent oxygen incorporation into the 180nm Al/Al-0.5%Cu interconnect metallization.
  - *Process Gas & Working Pressure*: Ultra-pure Argon (Ar 99.999%) maintained at 3 to 5 mTorr working pressure.
  - *Target Purity*: 99.999% (5N) Aluminum target driven by DC magnetron power supply at 1.5 to 3.0 kW.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal expansion mismatch across stainless steel chamber walls, ConFlat/ISO flanges, and viton or copper gaskets during bake-out up to 150°C risks inducing transient micro-leaks or galling vacuum feedthroughs. The system design must incorporate closed-loop proportional-integral-derivative (PID) ramp control (<=2°C/min) coupled to automated cryo/turbomolecular pump protection interlocks to prevent catastrophic mechanical failure and thermal shock.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Residual moisture and hydrocarbons desorbed insufficiently during incomplete bake-out will lead to background oxygen and hydroxyl partial pressures above 1e-8 Torr. During subsequent 180nm Al/Al-0.5%Cu DC magnetron sputtering, this residual oxygen incorporates directly into the nucleating film, elevating bulk sheet resistance above the 0.08 Ohm/sq post-anneal specification and degrading electromigration resistance.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Bake-out jackets, custom heating mantles, high-temperature copper sealing gaskets, and calibrated cold cathode/Bayard-Alpert ion gauge replacement filaments face extended lead times (6-12 weeks) from specialized ultra-high vacuum (UHV) vendors. A dual-sourcing framework and a local safety stock of consumable seals and gauge heads are mandatory to prevent prolonged line-down conditions.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scheduling a 12-to-24 hour thermal bake and cool-down cycle introduces significant BEOL metallization tool idle overhead. The qualification procedure must enforce an automated overnight bake recipe with real-time Residual Gas Analysis (RGA) tracking to ensure the tool is certified production-ready for primary wafer lots at the start of shift 1 without impacting fab cycle time.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal degradation or permanent compression set of elastomer seals leading to atmospheric helium/nitrogen breakthrough into the high-vacuum transfer chamber.
1. Outgassing saturation of cryopump regeneration arrays or turbo pump rotor drag overload due to premature high-vacuum valve opening above 1e-3 Torr crossover threshold.
1. Inadequate desorption of physisorbed water vapor (m/z=18) resulting in residual chamber pressure plateauing >2e-6 Torr, inducing premature target oxidation and film poisoning.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-2-2-01` | **Chamber Bake-Out Thermal Profile and Ultimate Base Pressure Verification** | Calibrated Bayard-Alpert Hot Cathode Ionization Gauge (NIST traceable calibration), Multi-channel Thermocouple Data Logger, Cryopump/Turbomolecular Pumping Station | 1. Initiate automated PID ramp-up of chamber bake-out heaters at 2°C/min until reaching 150°C. 2. Maintain isothermal soak at 150°C for 12 hours under continuous turbomolecular/cryo pumping. 3. Turn off bake-out jackets and ramp down naturally to ambient temperature (22°C ± 2°C). 4. Record ultimate base pressure continuously for 60 minutes after reaching 22°C. 5. Log pressure recovery curve and pump-down rate. | `Ultimate base pressure measured at 22°C must reach <= 1.8e-6 Torr within 4 hours post-cooldown, with no thermal drift exceeding ±5°C during the soak phase.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-2-2-02` | **Residual Gas Analysis (RGA) Outgassing and Leak Tightness Calibration** | 1-100 AMU Quadrupole Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA) with Faraday cup and electron multiplier detectors, Calibrated Helium Mass Spectrometer Sniffer/Spray Leak Detector | 1. Turn on RGA ion source and acquire full spectrum survey from 1 to 50 AMU. 2. Measure partial pressures for m/z = 18 (H2O), m/z = 28 (N2/CO), m/z = 32 (O2), and m/z = 44 (CO2). 3. Calculate water-to-argon and water-to-nitrogen partial pressure ratios. 4. Perform helium spray test on all perimeter flange seals while monitoring m/z = 4. 5. Execute a 10-minute rate-of-rise (RoR) pressure test by isolating the chamber valve. | `Partial pressure of H2O (m/z=18) must be < 5.0e-8 Torr; partial pressure of O2 (m/z=32) must be < 1.0e-8 Torr; Helium leak rate must be < 1.0e-9 Torr*L/s; Rate of rise must be < 5.0e-5 Torr/min.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal heat-resistant gloves (rated to 250°C), Safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1 approved), Full-face splash shield during cryogenic/heater operations, Cleanroom nitrile gloves (class 100 compatible), Anti-static ESD-safe cleanroom lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation of inert gases (N2, Ar, He) causing asphyxiation: Move victim immediately to fresh air. If breathing has stopped, administer artificial respiration and supplemental oxygen by trained medical personnel. In case of thermal burns from bake-out mantles/chambers: Flush burned area with clean, cold water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply salves or oils; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek immediate medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom HVAC airflow with certified laminar ceiling HEPA filtration; dedicated tool toxic/scrubbed vacuum roughing exhaust line venting directly to facility industrial abatement system; active ambient oxygen monitoring with audible alarms set to trigger if O2 drops below 19.5% volume.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Vacuum roughing pump oil or dry-pump condensate traps must be handled as hazardous chemical waste, collected in designated sealed containment drums, and dispatched to a licensed hazardous waste management facility in compliance with local environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen (Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Argon (Gas)** | `7440-37-1` | Research/Semiconductor Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Helium (Tracer Gas)** | `7440-59-7` | High Purity Grade 4.5 (99.995%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, degreased stainless steel/aluminum chamber shields and decontaminated PVD source assemblies installed; substrates in cassette cleaned and surface-prepared without native particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Conditioned ultra-high vacuum environment reaching base pressure < 2e-6 Torr, desorbed chamber sidewall surfaces free of condensed water monolayers, ready for continuous DC magnetron sputtering.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding allowable queue time re-exposes conditioned chamber walls or loadlock to atmospheric moisture, resulting in physisorbed water vapor re-condensation, elevated outgassing upon plasma ignition, target poisoning, and severe film oxygen contamination causing interconnect open-circuit defects.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full qualification and sign-off of the PVD sputter chamber thermal conditioning recipe, achieving an ultimate base pump-down pressure below 2.0e-6 Torr with certified leak-tightness and water partial pressure < 5.0e-8 Torr for 180nm DRAM BEOL metallization.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `chamber_bakeout_thermal_and_pumpdown_profile.csv`
- [ ] `pvd_base_pressure_rga_spectrum_report.pdf`
- [ ] `helium_leak_detection_and_rate_of_rise_log.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Ultimate chamber base pressure after bake-out and cooldown to 22°C** | `1.8e-6 Torr` | <= 2.0e-6 Torr | Calibrated hot cathode ionization gauge measurement logged continuously for 60 minutes |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Residual water vapor partial pressure (AMU 18) at base pressure state** | `3.5e-8 Torr` | <= 5.0e-8 Torr | Quadrupole residual gas analyzer mass spectrometer scan |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Chamber isolated rate of rise (RoR) leak and virtual leak check** | `2.5e-5 Torr/min` | <= 5.0e-5 Torr/min | Pressure rise logging over 10 minutes with isolated roughing/high-vacuum gate valves |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Chamber reaches base pressure <= 2.0e-6 Torr within specified pump-down curve, RGA confirms m/z=18 < 5e-8 Torr and m/z=32 < 1e-8 Torr, helium leak test passes at < 1e-9 Torr*L/s, and systems engineering approves the automated thermal bake-out recipe.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Residual Gas Analysis (RGA) Baseline Metrology & Outgassing Calibration

### Workflow Architecture
```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Base Pumpdown below  │
│       2e-6 Torr       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│     RGA Filament      │
│  Interlock and Degas  │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Baseline RGA Scan   │
│       1-100 AMU       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│     Rate of Rise      │
│    Outgassing Test    │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│       Ar Purge        │
│   Verification 3-5    │
│         mTorr         │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **High-Vacuum Base Pumpdown & Conditioning**
   - Initiate high-vacuum pumpdown cycle on the DC magnetron sputter deposition chamber utilizing the turbomolecular pump or cryopump stack.
   - Monitor cold cathode / ion gauge telemetry until chamber total pressure drops strictly below **$2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$** to ensure thorough elimination of atmospheric moisture and prevent oxygen incorporation during 180nm metallization.

2. **RGA Filament Interlock Verification & Degas**
   - Verify that the quadrupole mass spectrometer (RGA) high-vacuum protection interlock engages below $1.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ Torr}$.
   - Energize RGA ionizer filament and run an electronic degas cycle for 15 minutes at $40\text{ mA}$ emission current to desorb contaminants from the ion source cage and collector.

3. **Static Baseline Metrology (1 to 100 AMU Scan)**
   - Set RGA mass sweep range to **1–100 AMU** with a scan dwell time of $200\text{ ms/step}$ in Faraday cup / Electron Multiplier (EM) mode.
   - Acquire baseline background spectrum under static high vacuum ($< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$).
   - Measure and record key contaminant partial pressures:
     - Water vapor ($H_2O^+$: 18 AMU, $OH^+$: 17 AMU)
     - Molecular Nitrogen / Carbon Monoxide ($N_2^+ / CO^+$: 28 AMU)
     - Molecular Oxygen ($O_2^+$: 32 AMU)
     - Hydrocarbons (e.g., 43, 55, 57 AMU fragmentation peaks)

4. **Rate-of-Rise (RoR) Outgassing & Virtual Leak Rate Calibration**
   - Isolate the process chamber from the high-vacuum pumping port by closing the main gate valve.
   - Record total pressure rise ($\Delta P$) over an isolation window of $\Delta t = 180\text{ s}$ to compute chamber outgassing and virtual leak rate ($Q = V \cdot \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta t}$).
   - Concurrently monitor RGA peak trends: an escalating 28/32 AMU ratio (4:1) indicates a real physical flange/seal atmospheric leak, whereas an increasing 18 AMU peak dominant signal denotes chamber wall desorption/outgassing.

5. **Process Gas Introduction & Dynamic Baseline Qualification**
   - Open chamber gate valve to restore high-vacuum baseline ($< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$).
   - Through mass flow controllers (MFC), introduce high-purity process gas (**Argon 99.999%**) to establish dynamic working pressure between **$3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$**.
   - Sample gas purity via closed-ion-source (CIS) RGA or pressure-reduction orifice to ensure residual $O_2$ and $H_2O$ partial pressure ratios remain suppressed prior to striking the DC magnetron plasma.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
             ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
             │░░                                       │
  Hydrocarbon┤░░                                       │
             │▒▒▒▒▒                                    │
 O2 Partial P┤▒▒▒▒▒                                    │
H2O Partial P┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                │
             │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                │
Target Base P┤█████████████████████████████████████████│
             │█████████████████████████████████████████│
             └┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬┘
            0.00      0.50      1.00      1.50     2.00 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Chamber Base Pressure** | $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | Calibrated Bayard-Alpert Ion Gauge / Cold Cathode Gauge |
| **Residual Oxygen ($O_2$, 32 AMU) Partial Pressure** | $< 2.0 \times 10^{-8}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | Quadrupole RGA Peak Height (AMU 32) at Base Vacuum |
| **Residual Water Vapor ($H_2O$, 18 AMU) Partial Pressure** | $< 1.2 \times 10^{-7}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | Quadrupole RGA Peak Height (AMU 18) at Base Vacuum |
| **Ar Working Gas Process Pressure** | $3.0\text{ to }5.0$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer Gauge under 99.999% Ar flow |

---

### Context Citations

- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - *Chamber Base Vacuum*: Defines base pressure requirement below $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ via turbomolecular or cryopump to prevent oxygen incorporation into the interconnect film.
  - *Process Gas Specifications*: Dictates ultra-pure Argon (Ar 99.999%) maintained at a working pressure of $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$ for the DC magnetron sputter deposition.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integrating an in-situ quadrupole mass spectrometer (QMS/RGA) on the high-vacuum DC magnetron sputter deposition module requires precise differential pumping orifice isolation. Operating RGA sensors at typical chamber sputter pressures (2 to 5 mTorr Ar) will instantly saturate or destroy the microchannel plate/channeltron electron multiplier and filament. A dedicated differentially pumped bypass orifice with an automated gate interlock tied directly to chamber pirani/cold-cathode interlocks is non-negotiable to maintain RGA sensor pressure below 1E-5 Torr during active analysis while monitoring base pressure partial pressures down to 1E-10 Torr.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm BEOL Al-Cu / TiN barrier metallization, background partial pressures of oxidizing and reactive residuals—specifically H2O (m/z 18), O2 (m/z 32), CO (m/z 28), and hydrocarbons (m/z 41, 43, 55, 57)—must be strictly decoupled from chamber wall outgassing versus real vacuum leaks. Standard filament outgassing artifacts from hot tungsten/thoria-coated iridium cathodes can generate misleading CO and CO2 signals. Thorough RGA bakeout and degas protocols must precede baseline characterization to prevent false-positive contamination diagnoses in the metallization chamber.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Open-source 180nm MPW cleanroom lines frequently run constrained budgets on residual gas analyzers; procurement must ensure sensor heads with open-ion sources (1-100 amu or 1-200 amu Faraday/multiplier dual detectors) and replacement thoria-iridium filaments are second-sourced. Relying on proprietary closed-source differentially pumped mobile RGA carts risks downtime if turbomolecular drag pumps or ion-gauge controller calibration chips suffer supply lead times exceeding 16 weeks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scheduling baseline RGA qualification and chamber outgassing decay rate measurements must be strictly synchronized with wafer lot staging. Running outgassing calibrations during high-vacuum chamber recovery eats directly into tool availability for BEOL M1/M2 runs. Establishing an automated 15-minute diagnostic baseline check routine prevents pilot lot queuing delays and prevents wafer exposure beyond strict air/vacuum queue time boundaries.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Filament burnout and sensor baseline drift caused by inadvertent gate valve opening during chamber argon backfill or high-pressure plasma ignition.
1. Masked microscopic virtual leaks (trapped volumes in internal screw blind holes or shielding clips) presenting as persistent high outgassing decay rates, misleading vacuum integrity qualification.
1. Hydrocarbon cracking and cracking-pattern overlap at m/z 28 (N2 vs CO) and m/z 14 (N vs CH2), leading to erroneous atmospheric air leak diagnostics instead of desorbing organic/water contamination.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-2-3-01` | **High-Vacuum RGA Baseline Chamber Leak Detection & Hydrocarbon Fingerprinting** | Differentially pumped Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer (QMS, 1-200 amu range, dual Faraday cup / Electron Multiplier detector) coupled via calibrated orifice to the DC magnetron sputter deposition chamber, with calibrated Helium leak standard (leak rate 1.0E-8 mbar*L/s). | 1. Initialize RGA software in analog sweep mode across 1-100 amu at 50 ms/amu dwell time to record background baseline spectrum. 2. Measure and record partial pressure peaks for m/z 2 (H2), 14 (N/CH2), 18 (H2O), 28 (N2/CO), 32 (O2), 40 (Ar), and 44 (CO2). 3. Calculate nitrogen-to-oxygen ratio (m/z 28 to m/z 32) to distinguish atmospheric leak from water desorption. 4. Perform localized helium spray probe over chamber seals, feedthroughs, and viewports while monitoring m/z 4 (He) in selective ion monitoring (SIM) mode for 180 seconds per seal. | `Total partial pressure of H2O (m/z 18) <= 5.0E-8 Torr; partial pressure of O2 (m/z 32) <= 1.0E-9 Torr; cumulative heavy hydrocarbon sum (m/z 45 to 100) <= 5.0E-10 Torr; He leak signal delta at m/z 4 must not exceed 2.0E-10 Torr above background baseline.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-2-3-02` | **Chamber Bakeout & Outgassing Rate Decay Constant Calibration** | In-situ Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer (RGA) integrated with calibrated full-range cold cathode/Pirani combination vacuum gauge and precision chamber heater jacket controller with data logging at 1 Hz. | 1. Engage turbomolecular pumping system and monitor pressure pump-down trajectory from 1E-3 Torr to base. 2. Initiate chamber thermal bakeout jacket heating to 120°C (ramp rate 2°C/min) with RGA tracking m/z 18 (H2O), 17 (OH), 28 (CO/N2), and 44 (CO2) evolution. 3. Maintain soak temperature for 4 hours until outgassing peak plateaus and starts negative slope. 4. Ramp down chamber to 25°C and execute rate-of-rise (RoR) isolated accumulation test for 10 minutes by closing the main gate valve while RGA tracks partial gas accumulation. 5. Compute the specific outgassing rate Q (Torr*L / (s*cm2)). | `Specific outgassing rate Q after cooldown must be <= 2.5E-9 Torr*L / (s*cm2); H2O (m/z 18) signal must drop by at least two orders of magnitude within 120 minutes of cooling; base pressure of <= 3.0E-7 Torr achieved within 6 hours post-bakeout.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (class 100 compatible), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical/impact safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat / cleanroom bunny suit, Cryogenic/heat-resistant safety gloves for handling heated bakeout jackets and vacuum flanging
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin or eye contact with IPA during flange wipe-down, flush immediately with copious clean water for at least 15 minutes. For thermal burns from vacuum bakeout jackets or heated RGA sensor housing, immediately immerse affected area in cold running water; apply sterile dressing and seek cleanroom occupational medical staff. In event of localized N2 displacement resulting in dizziness or asphyxiation symptoms, evacuate personnel to fresh outdoor air and administer supplemental oxygen under trained medical supervision.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: RGA differential turbo pump exhaust and chamber roughing backing pump exhaust lines must be permanently hard-piped to the sub-fab hazardous process exhaust (HPE) or solvent scrubbed exhaust manifold with continuous negative static pressure (-0.5 to -1.2 kPa) and automated airflow pressure sensors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used cleanroom IPA wipes must be deposited into closed, grounded, flame-arrested solvent disposal cans and routed through hazardous organic chemical waste streams for certified high-temperature incineration. Trace helium and dry nitrogen effluent are vented directly to sub-fab scrubbed exhaust lines under compliant ambient air dilution.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Semiconductor Grade | `99.8%` |
| **Helium (Tracer Gas)** | `7440-59-7` | Ultra-High Purity (Grade 5.0) | `99.999%` |
| **Nitrogen (Purge / Vent Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Electronic Grade (Grade 6.0) | `99.9999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned patterned wafers with dry-etched contacts/vias, post-ash and dilute HF / solvent residue cleaned, incoming dry with native oxide < 0.8 nm, transferred under sealed FOUP / SMIF pods.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Verified ultra-high vacuum conditioned sputter deposition chamber ambient ready for pre-sputter etch and M1/M2 Ti/TiN/Al-Cu seed deposition with validated partial H2O and O2 pressures.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes moisture uptake and uncontrolled native oxide regrowth on contact/via interfaces, producing high contact resistance (Rc) and potential peeling/delamination of the subsequently deposited Ti/TiN adhesion barrier.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical qualification and baseline verification of the high-vacuum DC magnetron sputter deposition chamber via Residual Gas Analysis. Outgassing kinetics, baseline partial pressure species ratios, and vacuum hermetic seal integrity are confirmed in compliance with Gen 3 (180nm) BEOL metallization contamination specs.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RGA_Base_Pressure_Spectrum_Scan_180nm_M1M2.csv`
- [ ] `Chamber_Bakeout_Outgassing_Decay_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Helium_Sniff_Leak_Detection_Seal_Map.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Chamber baseline partial pressure for moisture (H2O, m/z 18) verified at base vacuum prior to metallization run** | `5.0E-8` | <= +1.0E-8 Torr | Differentially pumped QMS/RGA calibrated analog scan averaged across 10 consecutive sweeps |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Hydrocarbon contaminant envelope sum across m/z 45 to 100** | `5.0E-10` | <= +2.0E-10 Torr | RGA selective ion integration across mass range 45 to 100 amu using secondary electron multiplier (SEM) mode |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Helium vacuum envelope hermetic leak rate during probe check** | `1.0E-9` | <= +5.0E-10 mbar*L/s | RGA m/z 4 SIM response calibrated against secondary standard helium orifice leak calibrator |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All quantitative assertions (ASSERT-01, ASSERT-02, ASSERT-03) verified within numerical tolerance thresholds, documented RGA baseline spectra archived to the fab MES/SPC database, and both System Engineer and Metallization Module Lead digital sign-off completed.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Quality Acceptance & Metrology Protocol for High-Vacuum Chamber Conditioning & Base Pressure Calibration

**Category**: Quality Assurance | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Cryopump regeneration cycles and turbomolecular pump backing stages must be strictly decoupled from multi-wafer loadlock pumpdown transients to prevent oil/hydrocarbon backstreaming and micro-pressure shocks into the main deposition chamber during high-vacuum baseline calibration.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Attaining a validated base pressure of <= 5.0e-7 Torr (preferably < 1.0e-7 Torr) prior to DC magnetron sputter ignition is non-negotiable; residual partial pressures of H2O and O2 (m/z 18 and 32) directly oxidize Ti/Al-Cu interfaces, causing severe sheet resistance degradation and inter-metal via contact resistance blow-out.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-source dependency on ultra-high purity (UHP 99.9999%) Argon cylinders, certified copper CF gasket seals, and calibrated Bayard-Alpert ion gauge filaments risks halting the metallization pilot line if local secondary suppliers are unverified.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Chamber bakeout and RGA degassing qualification cycles consume 12-18 hours per maintenance window; protocol execution must integrate milestone gating directly with the BEOL M1/M2 lot release schedule to minimize queue-time starvation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Virtual leaks originating from trapped gas pockets behind chamber liner shielding screws, resulting in an asymptotic pumpdown plateau above 1.0e-6 Torr.
1. Residual water vapor outgassing (m/z 18 > 1.0e-8 Torr partial pressure) causing in-situ titanium target poisoning and excessive film resistivity in subsequent M1 depositions.
1. Helium hard leak across loadlock Viton O-ring seal or gate valve seal exceeding 1.0e-9 mbar*L/s under sniffer/hood testing.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-3-01` | **Chamber Base Pressure Ultimate Vacuum and Outgassing Rate Determination** | Calibrated Bayard-Alpert Hot Filament Ionization Gauge (NIST traceable), Dry Multi-stage Roots Backing Pump, Cryopump/Turbomolecular Pump High-Vacuum System, Data Acquisition Logger | 1. Isolate the sputter chamber from loadlock and roughing lines. 2. Record chamber base pressure continuously for 60 minutes using the calibrated Bayard-Alpert ion gauge. 3. Perform pressure rise test (rate-of-rise method) by isolating high-vacuum gate valve for 180 seconds and recording dP/dt. 4. Calculate total outgassing/leak rate Q = V * (dP/dt). | `Ultimate base pressure <= 5.0e-7 Torr within 4 hours post-bakeout; rate of rise dP/dt <= 2.0e-5 Torr/min (equivalent to Q < 1.0e-7 Torr*L/s for a 50L chamber).` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-3-02` | **In-Situ Residual Gas Analysis (RGA) and Helium Fine Leak Integrity Check** | Quadrupole Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA, 1-100 amu range, Faraday Cup / Secondary Electron Multiplier), Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Detector (sensitivity 1.0e-10 mbar*L/s), Calibrated UHP Helium Leak Source | 1. Power on RGA filament and acquire baseline spectrum (1-50 amu). 2. Measure partial pressure ratios of m/z 18 (H2O), m/z 28 (N2/CO), and m/z 32 (O2). 3. Direct UHP Helium probe around all ConFlat (CF) flanges, viewports, electrical feedthroughs, and bellows valves while monitoring m/z 4 signal on RGA and external helium leak detector. 4. Record peak leak excursion. | `Partial pressure of m/z 18 (H2O) < 1.0e-8 Torr; m/z 32 (O2) < 1.0e-9 Torr; total Helium leak rate across all external joints and feedthroughs < 1.0e-9 mbar*L/s with zero detectable localized leak spikes.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile gloves, UV-absorbing safety glasses / full face shield during chamber inspection, Cryogenic safety gloves and apron (for cryopump maintenance and LN2 handling), High-efficiency particulate air (P100) respirator during target and shield maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For cryogenic frostbite from cryopump lines, immediately flush affected area with lukewarm water (not hot) and seek emergency medical assistance. In case of inert gas asphyxiation (N2/He displacement in enclosed service chases), move victim immediately to fresh air, administer oxygen if breathing is labored, and initiate artificial respiration if breathing ceases. Eye contact with IPA: flush eyes with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber roughing pump exhaust must be continuously ducted into dedicated acid/solvent cleanroom scrubbed exhaust with negative differential pressure monitoring (min 150 CFM per tool bay). Dedicated room oxygen depletion sensors calibrated to alarm at < 19.5% O2 volume.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent lint-free cleanroom wipes soaked with IPA must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-resistant hazardous waste cans and routed to certified flammable solvent disposal. Sputter particulate vacuum sweepings and contaminated wipes must be treated as hazardous heavy metal waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, Cleanroom Electronic Grade)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Grade 99.99% | `> 99.8%` |

An actionable, industrial leaf Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) tailored for the DRAM Foundation VN 180nm Open-Source DRAM project is provided below.

---

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Procurement & NIST-Traceable Calibration of Bayard-Alpert Ion Gauge and RGA Sensor

**Document ID:** `SOP-BEOL-MET-001`  
**Classification:** Level 4 Technical / Industrial Leaf SOP  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS DRAM)  
**Process Step:** Thin Film Deposition / BEOL Metallization (M1/M2 DC Magnetron Sputter Vacuum Conditioning)  
**Action Type:** Buy (Procurement & Metrology Acceptance)

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP defines the procurement specifications, factory acceptance criteria, on-site incoming inspection, and NIST-traceable calibration protocol for:
1. **Bayard-Alpert (B-A) Hot Filament Ionization Gauges**
2. **Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA) Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer Sensors**

These sensors monitor ultra-high/high-vacuum base pressures and background partial pressures in the DC magnetron sputter deposition chamber for 180nm DRAM Metal-1 (350 nm Al/Al-Cu) and Metal-2 interconnects to prevent oxygen and impurity incorporation.

---

### 2. Verified Context & Parameter Baseline
* **Chamber Base Pressure Requirement:** Must reach $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ via turbomolecular or cryopump prior to Ar gas introduction.
* **Process Sputter Gas Working Pressure:** $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$ High-Purity Argon ($\text{Ar } 99.999\%$).
* **Critical Impurities Tracked:** $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($m/z = 18$), $\text{O}_2$ ($m/z = 32$), $\text{CO}_2$ ($m/z = 44$), and Hydrocarbons ($m/z = 41, 55, 57$).

---

### 3. Equipment Procurement Technical Specifications

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                EQUIPMENT SPECIFICATIONS                                 |
+------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------+
| Parameter                          | Requirement                                        |
+------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------+
| Bayard-Alpert Ion Gauge Type       | Dual Yttria-coated Iridium / Tungsten Filaments,   |
|                                    | ConFlat (CF 2.75") metal-sealed flange             |
| B-A Measurement Range              | 1.0 x 10^-10 Torr to 1.0 x 10^-3 Torr              |
| B-A Degas Mode                     | Electron Bombardment (EB) or I^2R Resistive        |
| RGA Mass Range                     | 1 to 100 amu (covers H2, He, H2O, N2/CO, O2, Ar)   |
| RGA Detector System                | Dual Faraday Cup & Secondary Electron Multiplier   |
| RGA Minimum Detectable Partial P   | <= 5.0 x 10^-11 Torr (Faraday) / 5.0 x 10^-14 Torr |
| Calibration Standard               | NIST-traceable primary/transfer calibration cert   |
+------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------+
```

---

### 4. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Phase 1: Procurement & Vendor Data Package Verification
1. **Purchase Order Execution:** Specify high-vacuum compatibility, dual filament redundancy, and mandatory NIST-traceable multi-point calibration certificates.
2. **Documentation Audit:** Verify calibration curves for $\text{N}_2$ sensitivity factor ($S_{\text{N}_2}$), linearity across $1.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ Torr}$ to $1.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ Torr}$, and mass resolution documentation at peak $m/z = 28$ and $m/z = 40$ (FWHM $\le 0.5\text{ amu}$).

#### Phase 2: Receiving Inspection & Cleanroom Unpacking
1. Inspect packaging for shock indicators and seal integrity within a Class 1000/100 (ISO 6/5) cleanroom ante-room.
2. Inspect CF 2.75" knife-edges under 10x optical magnification for scratches or burrs.
3. Verify filament continuity using a calibrated DMM: filament pin resistance must read $< 1.0\,\Omega$; filament-to-grid isolation must read $> 100\text{ M}\Omega$.

#### Phase 3: Vacuum Installation & Outgassing / Degas Routine
1. Mount the B-A gauge and RGA sensor onto dedicated line-of-sight ports on the sputter deposition chamber using new OFHC (Oxygen-Free High Conductivity) copper gaskets torqued to $15\text{ ft}\cdot\text{lbs}$ (cross-pattern).
2. Initiate roughing pump down, cross over to the turbomolecular/cryopumping system at $50\text{ mTorr}$, and evacuate until the chamber reaches $< 5.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$.
3. Execute B-A gauge filament degas:
   * Run degas cycle (EB or resistive heating) for $15\text{ minutes}$.
   * Allow $30\text{ minutes}$ for thermal equilibration.

#### Phase 4: NIST-Traceable In-Situ Cross-Calibration & Baseline Verification
1. **Zero / Background Calibration:** Record dark current and zero-offset on both B-A controller and RGA electrometer.
2. **Transfer Calibration Check:** Compare B-A reading with a calibrated NIST-traceable capacitance diaphragm/spinning rotor reference gauge at $1.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ and verify deviation is within $\pm 10\%$.
3. **RGA Cracking Pattern & Tuning:**
   * Introduce 5N high-purity Argon gas ($\text{Ar } 99.999\%$) up to leak-valve test pressures.
   * Calibrate peak positioning for $m/z = 40$ ($\text{Ar}$) and $m/z = 20$ ($\text{Ar}^{++}$).
   * Confirm base chamber background prior to Ar introduction verifies water vapor and oxygen partial pressures meet chamber conditioning requirements.

---

### 5. Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

The procurement and calibration lot are formally accepted if all metrics meet the following physical criteria:

| Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **B-A Base Pressure Verification** | $\le 2.0 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | Hot-filament B-A Gauge readout after bakeout & pump-down |
| **B-A Calibration Linearity Deviation** | $\le \pm 10.0$ | $\%$ | Compared against NIST-traceable transfer standard at $1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ |
| **RGA Mass Resolution (FWHM at $m/z = 28, 40$)** | $0.5 \pm 0.1$ | $\text{amu}$ | Quadrupole peak full-width at half-maximum under pure N2/Ar leak |
| **RGA Detection Sensitivity ($\text{O}_2\text{ at } m/z=32$)** | $\le 1.0 \times 10^{-9}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | RGA Secondary Electron Multiplier baseline before sputtering |

---

### 6. Sources & References
* **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects:** Vacuum chamber base pressure limit ($< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$), turbomolecular/cryopump requirement, high-purity Argon ($99.999\%$, $3\text{--}5\text{ mTorr}$), and Metal-1 thickness target ($350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$).
* **180nm CMOS DRAM Architecture Guidelines:** BEOL interconnect purity criteria to suppress contact resistance and maintain cell storage refresh integrity.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integration of the Bayard-Alpert (BA) nude ion gauge and quadrupole Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA, 1-100 amu) on the BEOL DC magnetron sputter chamber requires direct line-of-sight isolation via an all-metal UHV gate valve. Operating the BA gauge without interlocking to chamber roughing Pirani/capacitance manometers risks catastrophic filament burnout if chamber pressure spikes above 1e-3 Torr during sputter gas introduction. Furthermore, RF/DC plasma strike emission can introduce electromagnetic and secondary electron interference on the ion collector, mandating electrostatic shielding and optical line-of-sight baffles.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: NIST-traceable calibration must account for gas-specific relative sensitivity factors (Sx), especially calibrating the ionization cross-section for Ar (sputter process gas), N2, H2O, O2, and hydrocarbons. An uncalibrated RGA Faraday cup or secondary electron multiplier (SEM) will miscalculate the critical partial pressure ratios of water vapor (m/z 18) and oxygen (m/z 32) relative to argon (m/z 40). For 180nm BEOL M1/M2 Al-Cu metallization, residual baseline partial pressure of H2O must be verified below 5e-9 Torr prior to target pre-sputter to prevent interfacial aluminum oxide (AlOx) micro-void formation and subsequent interconnect via resistance elevation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dual-filament yttria-coated iridium (Y2O3/Ir) or thoria-coated iridium assemblies are strictly preferred over tungsten filaments due to resistance against catastrophic burnout during accidental atmospheric venting. Long lead-time risks exist for ISO/IEC 17025 accredited transfer standard calibration gauges (spinning rotor gauge or NIST-calibrated capacitance diaphragm gauges) and calibrated helium/nitrogen capillary permeation leaks; dual-sourcing agreements for replacement sensor heads and electron multipliers must be secured concurrently with the primary UHV flange order.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement and qualification milestone must be strictly phased: vendor factory acceptance test (FAT) with primary NIST-traceable calibration certificate must precede on-site cleanroom tool integration. Physical installation, bakeout cycle (150°C for 24 hours), RGA mass axis alignment, and baseline leak check must complete within a 5-day window to prevent blocking the downstream BEOL M1 sputter baseline conditioning schedule and subsequent 180nm MPW wafer tapeout deadlines.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Filament oxidization or thermal shock burnout caused by failure of the high-vacuum interlock loop during sudden argon process gas backfill.
1. Residual gas analyzer electron multiplier gain degradation or mass drift (>0.2 amu shift at m/z 28 and 40), yielding invalid background partial pressure readouts and undetected chamber micro-leaks.
1. False ultra-high vacuum readings caused by X-ray limit photo-emission currents on the Bayard-Alpert collector at pressures below 1e-9 Torr.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-3-1-01` | **NIST-Traceable Sensitivity and Linearity Calibration of Bayard-Alpert Gauge** | NIST-calibrated Transfer Standard Capacitance Diaphragm Gauge (CDG 0.1 Torr full scale), Spinning Rotor Gauge (SRG-3), High-Purity N2 Gas Inflow System, UHV Calibration Chamber. | 1. Isolate the primary ion pump and introduce research-grade N2 through an all-metal leak valve in decade steps: 1e-8, 1e-7, 1e-6, 1e-5, and 1e-4 Torr. 2. Record raw collector current (A) and simultaneous pressure reading from the reference Spinning Rotor Gauge / CDG transfer standard. 3. Calculate nitrogen sensitivity factor S_N2 = I_collector / (I_emission * P_ref). 4. Repeat measurement 5 times at each pressure decade to establish Gauge R&R and repeatability. | `The calculated sensitivity factor S_N2 must fall within 10.0 Torr^-1 to 12.5 Torr^-1 with linearity R^2 >= 0.999 across 1e-8 to 1e-4 Torr. Gauge R&R coefficient of variation (CV) must be < 1.0% across 5 consecutive runs.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-1-3-1-02` | **Quadrupole RGA Mass Axis Resolution, Sensitivity, and Baseline Leak-Tightness Verification** | 1-100 amu Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer / RGA with dual Faraday cup / Channeltron SEM detector, Calibrated Helium Sniffer/Permeation Standard Leak (nominal 1.2e-8 mbar*L/s). | 1. Perform mass scale sweep from 1 to 50 amu with resolution adjusted to 10% peak height definition between m/z 28 (N2/CO) and m/z 32 (O2). 2. Verify peak position accuracy for hydrogen (m/z 2), water (m/z 18), nitrogen (m/z 28), and argon (m/z 40). 3. Open calibrated helium leak standard to chamber port; track m/z 4 signal response time and calculate partial pressure detection sensitivity. 4. Monitor baseline partial pressures for hydrocarbon fragments (m/z 43, 55, 57). | `Mass peak alignment deviation must be <= ±0.1 amu across the 1-50 amu range with full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) between 0.9 and 1.1 amu. Background partial pressure of H2O (m/z 18) must register <= 5.0e-9 Torr, total hydrocarbon sum <= 1.0e-10 Torr, and helium leak response must match nominal calibrated leak rate within ±10%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, ASTM D6319), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses, Full cleanroom ESD gowning kit (hood, coverall, boot covers, grounding wrist strap), High-temperature thermal insulating gloves (rated to 250°C for chamber bakeout mantle handling)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin or eye contact with IPA solvent during flange gasket cleaning: flush eyes immediately with emergency eyewash for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated cleanroom garments. In case of thermal burn from heated bakeout shrouds: apply cool running water to affected area for 20 minutes, do not apply ointments, and report to cleanroom medical center. In case of localized asphyxiation alarm from N2 purge release: immediately evacuate personnel to fresh air and administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Calibration and bakeout test rig must be installed under localized exhaust ventilation (LEV) canopy hood with air face velocity >= 0.5 m/s. Vacuum turbo drag pump exhaust lines must be plumbed directly into the facility dedicated scrubbed solvent/acid BEOL exhaust system to prevent back-diffusion of volatile organic residues.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA-wetted cleanroom wipes (lint-free polyester) must be collected in closed, grounded, airtight, fire-rated safety waste bins for hazardous solvent incineration. Spent or burnt thoriated/yttriated gauge filaments must be segregated into dedicated non-ferrous electronics waste containment conforming to environmental cleanroom disposal protocols.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Electronic Grade)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Tier C / VLSI Grade (>= 99.99%) | `100%` |
| **Compressed Research Grade Nitrogen** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 6.0 (>= 99.9999%) | `100%` |
| **Calibrated Helium Gas Tracer** | `7440-59-7` | Grade 5.0 (>= 99.999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: ConFlat (CF) 2.75-inch and 4.5-inch knife-edge flange interfaces solvent-wiped with VLSI-grade IPA, mirror-polished (Ra < 0.2 um), verified free of scratches, burrs, or hydrocarbon residue under UV blacklight inspection.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully sealed UHV gauge assembly bolted with OFHC (Oxygen-Free High Conductivity) copper gaskets torqued cross-wise to 16-18 N*m, evacuated and helium leak-checked to <= 1.0e-10 mbar*L/s under continuous UHV/N2 blanket.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient atmospheric exposure (>45 min) induces atmospheric moisture and organic siloxane physisorption onto the nude ion collector surfaces and RGA quadrupole rods, requiring a mandatory 48-hour high-temperature bakeout cycle and delaying baseline sputter chamber qualification.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Procurement, installation, and NIST-traceable baseline calibration of the BEOL high-vacuum Bayard-Alpert ion gauge and 1-100 amu RGA mass spectrometer completed with full UHV compliance. Both sensors are validated on the M1/M2 sputter deposition chamber, demonstrating verified baseline ultimate pressure < 1.0e-9 Torr, zero hydrocarbon background, and NIST-traceable sensitivity slope.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `VACUUM_SYSTEM_LEAK_RATE_AND_REPEATABILITY.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-01` | **Calibrated Bayard-Alpert Gauge Nitrogen Sensitivity Factor (S_N2)** | `11.2 Torr^-1` | ±0.8 Torr^-1 | Comparison against NIST-traceable Spinning Rotor Gauge (SRG) reference across 1e-8 to 1e-4 Torr. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **RGA Mass Resolution FWHM at m/z 28 (N2) and m/z 40 (Ar)** | `1.00 amu` | ±0.10 amu | Quadrupole peak deconvolution and full-width at half-maximum scan using research-grade test gas mixture. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Chamber Ultimate Base Pressure and Helium Global Leak Rate** | `5.0e-10 Torr; 1.0e-10 mbar*L/s` | <= 1.0e-9 Torr; <= 2.0e-10 mbar*L/s | Calibrated ion gauge readout post-bakeout at 22°C and RGA helium bagging leak measurement. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
