nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## DC Magnetron Sputter Deposition of 350nm Al-0.5%Cu Metallization Layer

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Load & High-    │
│  Vacuum Pumpdown       │
│  (< 2.0e-6 Torr)       │
└───────────┬────────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Target Presputter     │
│  Conditioning (Ar)     │
└───────────┬────────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  DC Magnetron Sputter  │
│  Deposition (350 nm)   │
└───────────┬────────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Chamber Vent &        │
│  Wafer Unload          │
└───────────┬────────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Post-Metal Anneal     │
│  (Forming Gas 400°C)   │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Preparation & Loading**:
   - Inspect wafer surface following contact/via etch and clean.
   - Load wafer into the high-vacuum loadlock / process chamber onto the heated substrate stage.

2. **Chamber Evacuation & Base Vacuum Check**:
   - Pump down the process chamber using the turbomolecular or cryopump system.
   - Verify that base pressure reaches $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ before initiating gas flow to prevent oxygen incorporation into the aluminum film.

3. **Gas Flow & Process Pressure Stabilization**:
   - Introduce ultra-high-purity Argon gas ($\text{Ar } 99.999\% / 5\text{N}$).
   - Adjust throttle valve/mass flow controller to maintain working sputtering pressure within $3\text{ to } 5\text{ mTorr}$.

4. **Target Presputtering / Conditioning**:
   - Ignite DC magnetron plasma with shutter closed over the $99.999\%\text{ (5N)}$ Al-0.5%Cu target.
   - Presputter for 1–2 minutes to remove native oxide/passivation layer from the target surface.

5. **Deposition Run**:
   - Set DC magnetron power supply to an operating power between $1.5\text{ kW}$ and $3.0\text{ kW}$.
   - Maintain calibrated deposition rate within $50\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$.
   - Open substrate shutter and deposit to achieve the nominal target thickness of $350\text{ nm}$ (process run time: $3.5\text{ to } 7.0\text{ min}$ depending on calibrated rate).

6. **Chamber Vent & Wafer Unload**:
   - Ramp down DC power supply, extinguish plasma, and shut off Ar gas flow.
   - Allow wafer cooling on stage, isolate chamber, and vent loadlock with dry $\text{N}_2$ to transfer wafer to the inspection cassette.

7. **Post-Metal Sinter / Anneal**:
   - Transfer wafer to furnace/RTA chamber.
   - Anneal at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$ in forming gas ($\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ } 95/5$) to form ohmic contact and lower sheet resistance.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Measurement Unit | Inspection Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Film Thickness** | $350$ | $\pm 5\%$ ($332.5 - 367.5$) | $\text{nm}$ | Ellipsometry / Optical Profilometry / Cross-sectional SEM |
| **Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | Max $0.08$ (post-anneal) | $\Omega/\Box$ | Four-Point Probe (4PP) |
| **Chamber Base Vacuum** | $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}$ | Upper limit | $\text{Torr}$ | Ionization Vacuum Gauge |
| **Process Working Pressure** | $3.0 - 5.0$ | $3.0 \text{ to } 5.0$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - Base pressure: $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ via turbomolecular or cryopump.
  - Sputtering gas: High-purity $\text{Ar } 99.999\%$ at $3\text{ to } 5\text{ mTorr}$ working pressure.
  - Target: $99.999\%\text{ (5N)}$ Aluminum (or Al-0.5%Cu) target driven at $1.5\text{ to } 3.0\text{ kW}$.
  - Deposition rate: $50\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$.
  - Film thickness target: $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$.
  - Post-metal anneal: Forming gas ($\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ } 95/5$) at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$.
  - Sheet resistance: $R_s < 0.08\text{ }\Omega/\Box$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Deposition of a 350nm Al-0.5%Cu layer via DC magnetron sputtering must ensure stringent control over base vacuum (P_base < 2.0e-6 Torr) and target sputtering power density. Any thermal budget creep on the heated chuck above 200°C prior to dielectric cap deposition will induce excessive thermal stress, leading to tensile/compressive hysteresis, micro-void formation, and uncontrolled Cu precipitation at grain boundaries that degrade line resistance and bitline RC delay in the 180nm hierarchy.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Pure Al suffers severely from electromigration (EM) and stress-induced voiding under DRAM high-frequency write pulses. Introducing 0.5 wt% Cu provides grain boundary pinning against atomic migration, but requires strict sputter chamber thermal uniformities and controlled post-deposition cooling to prevent premature theta-phase (Al2Cu) macroscopic precipitation which acts as a preferential pitting site during subsequent metal reactive ion etching (RIE) patterning.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring 5N (99.999%) purity Al-0.5wt%Cu planar sputtering targets with homogeneous grain size (<50 um) and low oxygen/hydrogen interstitial content is vulnerable to long lead times (12-16 weeks) in domestic pilot labs. Back-up qualifications of regional target suppliers and certified ingot metallurgy traceability are required to prevent batch-to-batch resistivity and target poisoning variations.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Target erosion profiling must be tracked religiously across wafer batches to prevent non-uniform deposition (<5% across a 150mm/200mm wafer) from eating into scheduled maintenance downtime. Calibration runs must be locked to strict wafer-count intervals rather than calendar days to preserve cycle-time margins for Gen 3 BEOL metallization tapeout.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Target poisoning and chamber outgassing due to inadequate pump-down (base pressure > 2x10^-6 Torr), incorporating interstitial oxygen/nitrogen and driving sheet resistance R_s > 0.09 Ohm/sq.
1. Theta-phase (Al2Cu) coarse segregation and agglomeration at grain junctions caused by chuck temperature over-drift, inducing micro-galvanic corrosion and severe sidewall pitting during post-litho chlorine-based metal RIE.
1. Electromigration-induced open circuits along high-current bitline sensing nodes resulting from non-uniform copper distribution and sub-optimal columnar grain orientation (<111> texture degradation).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-2-2-01` | **Sheet Resistance and Film Resistivity Verification by 4-Point Probe** | Automated Four-Point Probe Resistivity Mapping System (e.g., KLA-Tencor OmniMap RS-100 or CDE ResMap) | 1. Position monitor wafer onto the 49-point polar contour mapping stage. 2. Measure sheet resistance (R_s) across 49 points with a 3mm edge exclusion using dual-configuration collinear probe heads (current I = 10mA). 3. Record mean sheet resistance, standard deviation (1-sigma), and calculate bulk resistivity using optical/stylus nominal thickness (350nm). | `Mean R_s <= 0.083 Ohm/sq (corresponding to resistivity rho <= 2.9 uOhm-cm); Across-wafer sheet resistance non-uniformity (1-sigma / mean) <= 3.0%.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-2-2-02` | **Cross-Sectional Step Coverage and Film Thickness Metrology** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM, e.g., Hitachi S-4800) and Stylus Profilometer (e.g., Bruker Dektak XT) | 1. Measure step height on etched photoresist/metal step using stylus profilometer at 5 points (center and 4 orthogonal positions at R=40mm). 2. Mount cleaved via sample in FE-SEM stub; sputter coat 1nm Pt if necessary to prevent charging. 3. Image via cross-section at 50,000x magnification; measure bottom step coverage (t_bottom / t_field) and sidewall step coverage (t_sidewall / t_field). | `Total field thickness: 350 nm ± 17.5 nm (within ±5%); Bottom step coverage in aspect ratio 1.5:1 via >= 30%; Sidewall minimum coverage >= 15%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile gloves with outer chemical/thermal cut-resistant gauntlets during target change, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering impact safety glasses/face shield for chamber viewports during plasma ignition, HEPA/P100 half-face particulate respirator during chamber shield scraping and bead-blast bead cleaning, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat and conductive cleanroom safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Asphyxiation Hazard (Argon/N2 displacement): Immediately move victim to fresh air. If breathing stops, administer artificial respiration and supplemental medical oxygen by trained personnel. Skin/Eye Contact with target flaking/particulates: Flush with copious isotonic saline or sterile water for at least 15 minutes; seek ophthalmologist review for foreign particulate trauma.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Sputter vacuum roughing pump and turbomolecular exhaust lines must be permanently ducted to continuous acid/inert scrubbed industrial exhaust with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s. Vacuum interlocks must automatically scram RF/DC magnetron power and close Ar mass flow controllers (MFC) upon exhaust pressure failure (>100 Pa differential).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent targets and peeled shield deposition flakes containing Cu/Al must be segregated as regulated heavy metal hazardous waste in sealed, anti-static poly bins for metallurgical reclamation. Do not dispose with general solid waste; prevent contact with moisture/strong oxidizers to avoid pyrophoric fine dust ignition.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Argon Gas (Compressed, Ultra-High Purity 5N)** | `7440-37-1` | Grade 5.0 (99.999% UHP) | `100%` |
| **Aluminum-Copper Alloy (Target)** | `7429-90-5 (Al) / 7440-50-8 (Cu)` | 5N Base (99.999% trace metals basis) | `99.5 wt% Al, 0.5 wt% Cu` |
| **Forming Gas (N2/H2 Anneal Mixture)** | `7727-37-9 (N2) / 1333-74-0 (H2)` | Semiconductor UHP | `95% N2 / 5% H2` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-metal dielectric (ILD/PMD) clean with native oxide/polymer residue completely stripped via dilute HF / BOE or in-situ Ar sputter pre-clean (<1.5nm native oxide).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited mirror-finish 350nm Al-0.5%Cu film with passivated surface native oxide (<2nm) under dry N2 or cleanroom ambient, free of organic staining and particulates (PWP < 0.05 particles/cm2 @ >0.2um).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time before post-metal cap/lithography creates uncontrolled native Al2O3 growth (>3.5nm) and moisture/atmospheric fluoride adsorption, resulting in poor photoresist adhesion, blistering during post-metal anneal, and severe interface via contact resistance spikes (R_c > 10 Ohm/via).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful DC magnetron sputter deposition of 350nm (±5%) Al-0.5wt%Cu film over pattern/monitor wafers, meeting DRAM interconnect sheet resistance (Rs < 0.085 Ohm/sq) and step coverage requirements without macro-particulates or phase segregation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-2-2-01_4point_sheet_resistance_contour.csv`
- [ ] `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-2-2-02_sem_cross_section_micrographs.tiff`
- [ ] `PVD_350nm_AlCu_deposition_run_summary_signoff.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Film Physical Thickness Target** | `350 nm` | ± 17.5 nm (± 5.0%) | Calibrated Contact Stylus Profilometry / X-SEM cross-section |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-Deposition As-Sputtered Sheet Resistance** | `0.080 Ohm/sq` | + 0.005 Ohm/sq / - 0.008 Ohm/sq | Automated 49-point polar Four-Point Probe mapping |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Across-Wafer Thickness Non-Uniformity (1-sigma / mean)** | `2.0 %` | <= 3.5 % maximum | 49-point map calculation over 150mm substrate with 3mm edge exclusion |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 49-point sheet resistance measurements satisfy mean Rs <= 0.085 Ohm/sq with 1-sigma <= 3.5%; optical particle counter confirms zero added defects > 0.5 um; cross-sectional SEM verifies conformality and step coverage >= 30% on control test structures.

testcases.pre_conditions: Patterned contact/via test wafer with 0.25um aspect ratio vias (180nm node rule) cleaved across contact center line; profilometer calibrated with a 360nm step height standard.

Mount cleaved via sample in FE-SEM stub; sputter coat 1nm Pt if necessary to prevent charging. 3. Image via cross-section at 50,000x magnification; measure bottom step coverage (t_bottom / t_field) and sidewall step coverage (t_sidewall / t_field).

ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering impact safety glasses/face shield for chamber viewports during plasma ignition

Static-dissipative ESD lab coat and conductive cleanroom safety shoes

If breathing stops, administer artificial respiration and supplemental medical oxygen by trained personnel. # Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## SOP-MET-180-01: Four-Point Probe Sheet Resistance & Profilometry Metrology for Al-0.5%Cu M1/M2 Thin Films

**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > BEOL Multi-Layer Metal Interconnect Deposition > DC Magnetron Sputter Deposition of 350nm Al-0.5%Cu Film > Metrology  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm)  
**Action Type:** Buy / In-line Metrology Inspection  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Wafer Load &      │
│       Pre-Check        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Stylus Profilometry   │
│      Step Height       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Four-Point Collinear  │
│         Probe          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Sheet Resistance    │
│      Calculation       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Acceptance       │
│     Verification &     │
│      Disposition       │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Preparation & Loading:**
   - Retrieve post-deposition monitor / production wafer with deposited 350 nm Al-0.5%Cu (deposited via planar DC magnetron sputtering at 1.5 to 3.0 kW, 3 to 5 mTorr Ar, base pressure $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$).
   - Ensure wafer has undergone post-metal forming gas anneal ($95\%\ \text{N}_2 / 5\%\ \text{H}_2$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for 30 minutes) prior to final sheet resistance disposition.
   - Load wafer onto the grounded vacuum chuck of the metrology tool inside the Class 100 cleanroom.

2. **Film Thickness Verification (Profilometry / Step-Height Metrology):**
   - Align the contact stylus profiler or optical profilometer across the lithographically patterned or shadow-masked calibration step.
   - Scan step height profile across the edge boundary over a 1.0 mm baseline.
   - Extract film thickness $t$ and verify conformance against the target nominal thickness ($t = 350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$, i.e., $332.5\text{ nm}$ to $367.5\text{ nm}$).

3. **Four-Point Collinear Probe Configuration:**
   - Verify probe head mechanical configuration: four collinear, equally spaced tungsten carbide tips with tip radius $r = 50\text{ to }100\ \mu\text{m}$ and inter-probe spacing $s = 1.0\text{ mm}$.
   - Gently lower the probe assembly onto the metallized wafer surface ensuring uniform tip compliance.
   - Apply a constant DC excitation current $I = 1\text{ mA to }10\text{ mA}$ through outer probes 1 and 4.
   - Measure the resultant floating voltage drop $V_{23}$ across inner probes 2 and 3.

4. **Sheet Resistance Calculation & Geometry Correction:**
   - Because film thickness $t = 350\text{ nm} \ll s/2$ ($0.5\text{ mm}$), apply the thin-film semi-infinite boundary equation:
     $$R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right) \approx 4.5324 \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right)\quad [\Omega/\square]$$
   - Apply edge correction factors $F(d/s)$ if sampling sites are closer than $40s$ ($40\text{ mm}$) to the wafer edge.
   - Sample across standard 5-point or 9-point wafer mapping sites to extract mean $R_s$ and within-wafer uniformity.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Film Thickness ($t$)** | $350\text{ nm}$ | $\pm 5\%$ ($332.5\text{ nm}$ to $367.5\text{ nm}$) | Stylus Profilometry / Ellipsometry |
| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08\ \Omega/\square$ | Upper limit: $0.08\ \Omega/\square$ | Four-Point Collinear Probe ($s=1.0\text{ mm}$, $I=1\text{ to }10\text{ mA}$) |
| **Probe Geometric Configuration** | $s = 1.0\text{ mm}$ spacing | Tip radius $r = 50\text{ to }100\ \mu\text{m}$ | Calibration Gauge / Optical Inspection |
| **Post-Metal Anneal Condition** | $400^\circ\text{C}$, $30\text{ min}$ | Forming gas $95\%\ \text{N}_2 / 5\%\ \text{H}_2$ | Anneal Furnace Controller Log |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects:** Specifies 180nm DRAM interconnect Al-0.5%Cu deposition, base pressure $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$, working pressure 3 to 5 mTorr Ar, power 1.5 to 3.0 kW, nominal thickness target $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$, and post-metal anneal ($400^\circ\text{C}$, 30 min, $95/5\ \text{N}_2/\text{H}_2$) achieving sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\square$.
- **Four-Point Collinear Probe Metrology for Semiconductor Sheet Resistance:** Specifies four collinear tungsten carbide probe tips (radius $50\text{--}100\ \mu\text{m}$, spacing $s = 1.0\text{ mm}$), constant DC current $I = 1\text{ mA to }10\text{ mA}$, thin-film sheet resistance formulation $R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot (V/I) = 4.5324 \cdot (V/I)\ [\Omega/\square]$, and edge correction factor rules $F(d/s)$ for finite wafer boundaries.
- **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity:** Confirms pad geometry ($W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$, gaps $d = 5\text{ to }80\ \mu\text{m}$) and extraction relationships ($R_T = 2R_c + (R_s/W)d$, $\rho_c = R_c W L_T$) for interconnect-to-diffusion interfaces.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Coupling sheet resistance (Rs) from a four-point probe (4PP) directly with physical thickness measurements from stylus/optical profilometry is essential to extract bulk resistivity (rho = Rs * t). For a 350 nm Al-0.5%Cu film on 180nm BEOL interconnects, non-uniformity across the wafer directly drives RC delay skew on DRAM bitlines and wordlines. Stylus tip loading force must be strictly regulated (<10 mg) to prevent mechanical puncturing or plastic deformation of the ductile aluminum alloy.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) on opaque metal films like 350 nm Al-0.5%Cu cannot measure thickness by transmission interference due to zero optical skin depth (~10-15 nm). Instead, SE measures surface pseudo-dielectric functions, Drude free-electron relaxation time, and native Al2O3 growth kinetics (delta/psi shifts). Absolute film thickness must be characterized using step-height profilometry or cross-sectional X-SEM/TEM on designated scribe-line monitor structures.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide (WC) four-point probe heads suffer tip wear, Cu/Al smearing, and contact resistance drift after ~5,000 touches. Calibrated four-point probe reference wafers (NIST-traceable bulk resistivity standards) and profilometer step-height calibration standards (VLSI Standards 180nm/350nm SiO2 steps) must be dual-sourced to avoid line halts during inline process monitoring.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Inline metrology sampling (49-point wafer mapping) takes approximately 3.5 minutes per wafer. To prevent bottlenecking the PVD cluster tool throughput in Gen 3 pilot line runs, implement a skip-lot strategy (1 pilot wafer per cassette of 25 wafers) while enforcing strict 100% inspection during initial chamber requalification and target replacement cycles.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-scratching and probe-induced gouging of the Al-0.5%Cu layer by worn or overloaded WC tips, leading to inter-metal dielectric (IMD) voids and subsequent line bridging during photolithography.
1. Native oxide (Al2O3) thickness accumulation due to queue time expiry, creating spurious high contact resistance on 4PP tips and skewed optical dispersion parameter extraction in spectroscopic ellipsometry.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-2-3-01` | **49-Point Four-Point Probe Sheet Resistance & Uniformity Verification** | Automated Dual-Configuration Four-Point Probe Mapping System with Tungsten Carbide (WC) Tips (100 micron radius, 1.0 mm spacing) | 1. Load wafer onto electrostatic chuck with notch oriented at 0 degrees. 2. Apply a 10 mA forward current between outer pins and measure voltage across inner pins using dual-configuration geometric correction. 3. Execute an automated 49-point polar map across a 200 mm wafer with 3 mm edge exclusion. 4. Calculate mean sheet resistance (Rs_mean) and 1-sigma percent standard deviation. | `Mean sheet resistance (Rs) must fall within 88.0 to 98.0 mOhm/sq (corresponding to bulk resistivity rho < 3.25 uOhm-cm at 350 nm nominal thickness). Sheet resistance uniformity (1-sigma) must be <= 2.5%.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-2-3-02` | **Step-Height Profilometry Thickness & Surface Roughness Validation** | High-Resolution Stylus Surface Profilometer (2.0 micron diamond stylus tip, 5.0 mg tracking force) | 1. Position stylus across the lithographic test step at 5 distinct sites (Center, North, South, East, West). 2. Perform a 1.0 mm scan transverse to the metal step at 50 um/s scan velocity. 3. Level baseline against substrate oxide and measure step height from plateau to base. 4. Concurrently acquire 1D root-mean-square roughness (Rq) on the planar metal plateau over a 50 um window. | `Step height thickness must be 350.0 nm +/- 15.0 nm (335 nm to 365 nm) across all 5 test sites. Plateau surface roughness Rq must be < 4.0 nm to prevent dielectric breakdown in subsequent inter-layer dielectric (ILD) deposition.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified impact-resistant cleanroom safety glasses, Full static-dissipative cleanroom bunny suit with ESD footwear, Non-shedding face mask
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Physical contact with IPA: Flush eyes or skin immediately with copious clean water or eyewash station for 15 minutes. High-pressure gas exposure: Depressurize and seek medical attention for physical impact injury. Stylus or probe puncture: Treat as sharp object puncture, disinfect with povidone-iodine and bandage.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard ISO 5 (Class 100) laminar flow cleanroom air recirculation (0.45 m/s velocity) with active exhaust for solvent stage cleaning stations.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes sealed in dedicated volatile organic chemical (VOC) disposal bins for hazardous incineration. Expired calibration wafers disposed through electronic silicon recycling channels.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) cleanroom surface wipe** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade C-1 (VLSI Purified) | `70% in DI Water` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (purge/blow-off)** | `7727-37-9` | UHP Grade 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly sputtered 350nm Al-0.5%Cu film directly exiting PVD load-lock, metallic specular finish with initial native oxide < 1.0 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized wafer with mapped sheet resistance and step height; native oxide passivated < 2.5 nm; free of probe indentation debris.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) to thicken beyond 3.5 nm, degrading ohmic tip contact on 4PP leading to false high Rs readings and inducing premature optical absorption shifts in spectroscopic ellipsometry.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical and electrical qualification of the 350 nm Al-0.5%Cu M1/M2 film stack demonstrating sheet resistance within 88-98 mOhm/sq, 49-point uniformity <= 2.5%, nominal physical thickness of 350 nm +/- 15 nm, and surface roughness Rq < 4.0 nm.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `M1_M2_350nm_AlCu_4PP_Rs_49Pt_Map.csv`
- [ ] `M1_M2_StepHeight_Stylus_Thickness_Profile.pdf`
- [ ] `M1_M2_Surface_Roughness_Ellipsometry_Spectra.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Average 49-point sheet resistance of the Al-0.5%Cu film** | `93.0 mOhm/sq` | +/- 5.0 mOhm/sq | Automated 49-point dual-configuration four-point probe mapping with 3 mm edge exclusion |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Film physical step-height thickness across 5 wafer sites** | `350.0 nm` | +/- 15.0 nm | High-resolution stylus profilometry step-height measurement across lithographic scribe-line trench |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Within-wafer sheet resistance non-uniformity (1-sigma)** | `1.8%` | <= 2.5% | Statistical standard deviation calculation over 49-point Rs polar grid |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 49 wafer sites meet 88-98 mOhm/sq Rs with 1-sigma <= 2.5%, profilometer step-height confirms 335-365 nm thickness at Center and 4-quadrant edge sites, surface roughness Rq < 4.0 nm, and zero uncorrectable probe puncture marks on active die regions.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Post-Deposition Sheet Resistance & Step Coverage Metrology

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-deposition sheet resistance (Rs) directly impacts bitline RC propagation delay and IR drop across the 180nm DRAM memory array strapping. Metrology must correlate the 4-point probe Rs wafer mapping with inline cross-sectional SEM thickness profiles; a thickness drift of ±5% on nominal 350 nm Al-0.5%Cu translates directly to sheet resistance fluctuations outside the 0.08 Ohm/sq budget. Integrating non-destructive 4PP with destructive or cleaved cross-section SEM requires explicit wafer-level sampling plans to avoid sacrificing product dice while ensuring step coverage across high aspect ratio contact and via topographies exceeds the 30% reliability threshold.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Sputtered Al-0.5%Cu metallization over high-aspect contacts exhibits severe shadowing without continuous substrate heating (150-250°C), inducing micro-voiding or cusping at the via bottom. Four-point probe (4PP) dual-configuration metrology must account for geometric correction factors near wafer edges and pad structures, as well as native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) passivation forming instantly in ambient atmosphere which distorts probe tip contact resistance. Furthermore, step coverage verification must differentiate between bottom step coverage (nominal target > 25-30%) and sidewall step coverage (nominal target > 35%) using high-resolution FE-SEM or FIB-SEM cross-sections.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dual-configuration 4-point probe heads (osmium or tungsten carbide tips with calibrated spring tension) and FE-SEM conductive stub mounts are single-source consumables with 6-to-8 week replenishment lead times. Re-tipping or wear-out of mechanical probe tips introduces contact micro-scratching or erratic punch-through into underlying inter-metal dielectrics (IMD/ILD), requiring rigid automated probe count limits (maximum 10,000 touchdowns per probe head) and local stock buffers of calibrated NIST-traceable resistivity reference standards.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology overhead threatens fab takt time if SEM cross-sections are required per production lot. To prevent queue bottlenecks at the metrology station before post-metal forming gas anneal, non-destructive 49-point 4PP resistivity wafer mapping must execute within 4 minutes per wafer, while FIB-SEM/FE-SEM step coverage inspection is restricted to 1 sacrificial test monitor wafer per 25-wafer cassette batch, keeping overall lot dispatch within the 4-hour nitrogen purge Q-time window.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Inadequate bottom step coverage (<20%) at high aspect ratio contact vias due to DC magnetron target erosion or insufficient substrate stage pre-heating, causing bitline open circuits or severe electromigration voiding during DRAM cycling.
1. Native oxide punch-through failure or probe tip micro-pitting during 4PP measurement, resulting in artificially elevated sheet resistance readings (>0.12 Ohm/sq) and false lot scrap.
1. Inter-layer dielectric micro-cracking caused by excessive 4PP probe loading force (>100 grams-force), generating micro-shorts between M1 bitline metallization and underlying polysilicon wordlines.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

Load wafer onto vacuum chuck of automated 4PP system and align notch/flat automatically. 2. Select 49-point polar contour mapping recipe across active wafer diameter. 3. Apply calibrated probe current of 10.0 mA with probe descent velocity of 1.0 mm/s and 60 gf tip loading force. 4. Execute dual-configuration (A and B) voltage sensing to eliminate edge boundary distortion effects. 5. Compute mean sheet resistance (Rs_mean) and 1-sigma uniformity percentage ((sigma / Rs_mean) * 100). 6. Export tabular and contour map data to lot metrology directory. | `Mean sheet resistance Rs_mean <= 0.080 Ohm/sq; 1-sigma wafer-level thickness/resistivity non-uniformity <= 3.5%; zero anomalous open-contact (>10 Ohm/sq) points.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-3-02` | **Cross-Sectional FE-SEM Contact Step Coverage & Profile Metrology** | Dual-Beam Focused Ion Beam and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FIB/FE-SEM) equipped with in-situ Pt gas injection system and calibrated high-resolution secondary electron detector. | 1. Mount coupon on conductive carbon stage with copper tape grounding. 2. Deposit 1.0 um protective electron/ion-beam platinum strap directly over the target contact via array. 3. Mill cross-sectional trench using 30 kV Ga+ ion beam rough cut followed by 5 kV / 50 pA polish cut. 4. Tilt stage to 52° tilt-corrected viewing angle and acquire secondary electron micrograph at 100,000x magnification. 5. Measure field thickness (T_top), bottom step thickness (T_bottom), and minimum sidewall thickness (T_sidewall). 6. Calculate bottom step coverage percentage: (T_bottom / T_top) * 100 and sidewall step coverage: (T_sidewall / T_top) * 100. | `Bottom step coverage >= 30.0% (T_bottom >= 105 nm for nominal 350 nm top field thickness); minimum sidewall step coverage >= 35.0% (T_sidewall >= 122.5 nm); zero continuous micro-voids, cusping pinch-offs, or Al-Cu delamination along contact corners.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double-gloved, EN ISO 374-1), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles, ESD-safe dissipative lab coat / full cleanroom bunny suit, Cut-resistant under-gloves (ANSI Level A3) during diamond scribe wafer cleavage for SEM sample preparation
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin cut from cleaved wafer fragments: immediately wash wound with soap and copiously flush with sterile saline/water for 15 minutes, apply pressure dressing to control bleeding, and seek medical attention for micro-particulate evaluation. In case of chemical contact (IPA) with eyes: irrigate with eyewash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors: remove victim to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: FIB/FE-SEM dry vacuum roughing pump and turbopump exhausts must be hard-ducted directly to dedicated sub-fab industrial solvent/chemical exhaust scrubbers operating at minimum negative static pressure of -1.5 in. w.g. Wafer cleavage and IPA coupon prep must occur within certified laminar flow hood with local face velocity of 0.45 ± 0.05 m/s.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All fractured GaAs/Si wafer fragments, contaminated carbon adhesive tabs, and IPA-soaked lint-free cleanroom wipes must be collected in labeled, anti-static hazardous solid waste bins for specialized incinerator disposal. No liquid solvents disposed of down cleanroom drains.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited Al-0.5%Cu thin film (nominal 350 nm) post-sputter, free from ambient condensation, moisture condensation, or halogen-containing cleanroom airborne molecular contaminants (AMC).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Metrology-inspected, un-scratched active area; non-destructive 4PP touch marks restricted to scribe line test pads; monitor wafer cross-section logged; wafer surface clean for subsequent post-metal forming gas anneal (N2/H2 95/5 at 400°C).

**Exit Objective Summary**:

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

critics.systems_engineer: Post-deposition sheet resistance (Rs) directly impacts bitline RC propagation delay and IR drop across the 180nm DRAM memory array strapping. Metrology must correlate the 4-point probe Rs wafer mapping with inline cross-sectional SEM thickness profiles; a thickness drift of ±5% on nominal 350 nm Al-0.5%Cu translates directly to sheet resistance fluctuations outside the 0.08 Ohm/sq budget. Integrating non-destructive 4PP with destructive or cleaved cross-section SEM requires explicit wafer-level sampling plans to avoid sacrificing product dice while ensuring step coverage across high aspect ratio contact and via topographies exceeds the 30% reliability threshold.
critics.domain_expert: Sputtered Al-0.5%Cu metallization over high-aspect contacts exhibits severe shadowing without continuous substrate heating (150-250°C), inducing micro-voiding or cusping at the via bottom. Four-point probe (4PP) dual-configuration metrology must account for geometric correction factors near wafer edges and pad structures, as well as native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) passivation forming instantly in ambient atmosphere which distorts probe tip contact resistance. Furthermore, step coverage verification must differentiate between bottom step coverage (nominal target > 25-30%) and sidewall step coverage (nominal target > 35%) using high-resolution FE-SEM or FIB-SEM cross-sections.
critics.supply_chain: Dual-configuration 4-point probe heads (osmium or tungsten carbide tips with calibrated spring tension) and FE-SEM conductive stub mounts are single-source consumables with 6-to-8 week replenishment lead times. Re-tipping or wear-out of mechanical probe tips introduces contact micro-scratching or erratic punch-through into underlying inter-metal dielectrics (IMD/ILD), requiring rigid automated probe count limits (maximum 10,000 touchdowns per probe head) and local stock buffers of calibrated NIST-traceable resistivity reference standards.
critics.laya_pm: Metrology overhead threatens fab takt time if SEM cross-sections are required per production lot. To prevent queue bottlenecks at the metrology station before post-metal forming gas anneal, non-destructive 49-point 4PP resistivity wafer mapping must execute within 4 minutes per wafer, while FIB-SEM/FE-SEM step coverage inspection is restricted to 1 sacrificial test monitor wafer per 25-wafer cassette batch, keeping overall lot dispatch within the 4-hour nitrogen purge Q-time window.
critical_failure_modes: Inadequate bottom step coverage (<20%) at high aspect ratio contact vias due to DC magnetron target erosion or insufficient substrate stage pre-heating, causing bitline open circuits or severe electromigration voiding during DRAM cycling.
Native oxide punch-through failure or probe tip micro-pitting during 4PP measurement, resulting in artificially elevated sheet resistance readings (>0.12 Ohm/sq) and false lot scrap.
Inter-layer dielectric micro-cracking caused by excessive 4PP probe loading force (>100 grams-force), generating micro-shorts between M1 bitline metallization and underlying polysilicon wordlines.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Four-Point Probe Sheet Resistance Mapping & Uniformity Analysis

**Context Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > BEOL Multi-Layer Metal Interconnect Deposition (Metal 1, Metal 2, and Passivation) > M1/M2 High-Vacuum DC Magnetron Sputter Deposition & Anneal > DC Magnetron Sputter Deposition of Al-0.5%Cu M1/M2 Thin Films > Post-Deposition Sheet Resistance & Step Coverage Metrology > Four-Point Probe Sheet Resistance Mapping & Uniformity Analysis  
**Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm) | **Action Type**: Make | **Document ID**: `SOP-BEOL-MET-FPP-180NM-001`

---

### 1. Metrology Process Flow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Wafer Loading and   │
│       Alignment       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Probe Head Setup    │
│    s=1.0mm WC Tips    │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    Multi-Point Map    │
│       Execution       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    Outer Probe DC     │
│  Sourcing I=1 to 10   │
│          mA           │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│      Inner Probe      │
│  Potential Metrology  │
│           V           │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Sheet Resistance    │
│   Calculation Rs =    │
│    4.5324 * V / I     │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    Geometric Edge     │
│     Correction F      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Uniformity and Spec  │
│     Verification      │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Safety & Tool Inspection**:
   - Verify Class 100/1000 cleanroom environmental controls.
   - Inspect the collinear four-point probe head assembly: ensure four tungsten carbide (WC) tips with tip radii of $50\ \mu\text{m}\text{ to }100\ \mu\text{m}$ and uniform inter-probe spacing $s = 1.0\ \text{mm}$ are clean and free of micro-debris.
2. **Wafer Placement & Alignment**:
   - Retrieve the processed wafer post-metal anneal ($95/5\ \text{N}_2/\text{H}_2$ forming gas at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for 30 minutes).
   - Load the $180\text{nm}$ DRAM wafer onto the automated vacuum chuck and execute notch/flat robotic alignment.
3. **Recipe Configuration & Metrology Mapping**:
   - Select the automated radial/contour wafer-mapping recipe across the substrate diameter (e.g., standard 49-point or 81-point polar map with designated edge-exclusion zone).
   - Set the programmable DC current source to $I = 1\ \text{mA}\text{ to }10\ \text{mA}$.
4. **Probe Landing & Contact Sequence**:
   - Lower the probe head under controlled descent velocity and contact force to contact the deposited $\text{Al-}0.5\%\text{Cu}$ film without puncturing the target thickness ($t = 350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$).
5. **Electrical Current Sourcing & Voltage Sensing**:
   - Drive constant DC current $I$ ($1\ \text{mA}\text{ to }10\ \text{mA}$) through outer pins 1 and 4.
   - Measure the floating potential drop $V$ across inner pins 2 and 3 using a high-impedance digital voltmeter.
6. **Sheet Resistance Extraction & Edge Proximity Correction**:
   - Calculate raw sheet resistance using the thin-film collinear formula ($t \ll s/2$):
     $$R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right) \approx 4.5324 \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right)\quad [\Omega/\square]$$
   - For metrology sites within edge proximity boundaries ($< 40 \times s$), multiply raw $R_s$ by the finite-boundary geometric correction factor $F(d/s)$.
7. **Wafer Uniformity & Acceptance Computation**:
   - Compute wafer mean sheet resistance ($\overline{R}_s$), standard deviation ($\sigma$), and percent non-uniformity:
     $$\%NU = \left(\frac{R_{s,\max} - R_{s,\min}}{2 \cdot \overline{R}_s}\right) \times 100\% \quad \text{or} \quad \left(\frac{1\sigma}{\overline{R}_s}\right) \times 100\%$$
   - Export full wafer sheet resistance contour maps to the Fab MES/SPC database.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text

     └┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬┘
    0.000     0.020     0.040     0.060   0.080 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Condition | Units | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | Measured post forming-gas anneal ($400^\circ\text{C}$, 30 min) | $\Omega/\square$ | Mandatory |
| **Film Thickness ($t$)** | $350$ | $\pm 5\%$ ($332.5\text{ to }367.5\ \text{nm}$) | $\text{nm}$ | Verification |
| **Sputter Deposition Rate Calibration** | $50\text{ to }100$ | Target power $1.5\text{ to }3.0\ \text{kW}$, Ar $3\text{ to }5\ \text{mTorr}$ | $\text{nm/min}$ | In-Line Control |
| **Probe Head Collinear Spacing ($s$)** | $1.0$ | Tungsten carbide tip radius $50\text{ to }100\ \mu\text{m}$ | $\text{mm}$ | Tool Baseline |

---

### 4. Context Citations

- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - Deposition of $\text{Al-}0.5\%\text{Cu}$ thin film, Metal-1 target thickness $350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$, DC magnetron power $1.5\text{ to }3.0\ \text{kW}$, deposition rate $50\text{ to }100\ \text{nm/min}$, chamber Ar working pressure $3\text{ to }5\ \text{mTorr}$, base pressure $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{Torr}$.
  - Post-metal anneal: $95/5\ \text{N}_2/\text{H}_2$ forming gas at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\ \text{minutes}$.
  - Sheet resistance specification: $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\square$.
- **Four-Point Collinear Probe Metrology for Semiconductor Sheet Resistance**:
  - Probe head parameters: collinear tungsten carbide tips, tip radius $50\text{ to }100\ \mu\text{m}$, tip spacing $s = 1.0\ \text{mm}$.
  - Electrical sourcing: DC current $I = 1\ \text{mA}\text{ to }10\ \text{mA}$ through outer pins (1 & 4), potential difference $V$ across inner pins (2 & 3).
  - Formulation: $R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot (V/I) = 4.5324 \cdot (V/I)\ [\Omega/\square]$, with geometric correction factors $F(d/s)$ applied when wafer diameter $< 40 \times s$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-sputter sheet resistance mapping directly defines interconnect delay (RC product) and IR-drop across DRAM wordline/bitline driver rails. For 180nm M1/M2 Al-0.5%Cu films (nominal thickness 450nm to 600nm), automated 49-point or 81-point contour mapping must account for geometric edge correction factors (Smits/Haldor Topsøe formulation) when probing within 10mm of the wafer edge to avoid spurious edge roll-off artifacts propagating into SPICE BEOL parasitic extraction tables.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Direct contact four-point probing using tungsten carbide (WC) tips can cause micro-scratching or severe film penetration on ductile Al-0.5%Cu layers. Probe tip radius (typically 40-100 um) and probe loading force must be strictly controlled between 20 to 50 grams per pin to minimize mechanical deformation while penetrating the native aluminum oxide (Al2O3, ~2-4nm) layer to achieve true Ohmic contact without micro-cracking the underlying ILD (TEOS/SiH4 oxide).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide probe heads undergo tip degradation, copper transfer, and tip dulling over repeated touch-downs on Al-Cu thin films, requiring scheduled refurbishment or replacement every 15,000 to 20,000 probings. Sourcing dual-source calibrated NIST-traceable reference resistivity wafers (e.g., standard VLSI Res/Thick wafers) is critical to maintaining tool-to-tool baseline calibration across multi-foundry MPW runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology queue time post-sputter and pre-passivation/dielectric deposition is critical. Any delay in 4PP mapping directly impacts lot turn rate and risks native oxidation drift or moisture-induced galvanic corrosion of exposed Cu-bearing grains, stalling fab disposition of pilot batches for the 180nm DRAM tapeout schedule.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Probe pin punch-through causing localized puncturing of the 450nm Al-0.5%Cu metallization layer into underlying inter-layer dielectric (ILD), causing erroneous substrate leakage readings and physical defect yield kill.
1. Excessive probe tip wear or native oxide barrier non-penetration yielding intermittent high-impedance contact, resulting in artificially high sheet resistance and false out-of-spec wafer rejection.
1. Probe-induced particle generation and metal flaking contaminating the automated end-effector handler, cross-contaminating downstream dielectric CVD and stepper chucks.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-3-1-01` | **49-Point Full-Wafer Sheet Resistance Mapping & Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (NU%) Determination** | Automated Dual-Configuration Four-Point Probe Resistivity Mapping System (e.g., KLA-Tencor RS-100 / CDE ResMap 178) equipped with precision Tungsten Carbide (WC) probe head (tip radius: 100 um, pin spacing: 1.0 mm, pin load: 35 g/pin) and NIST-traceable sheet resistance calibration standard. | 1. Load wafer onto electrostatic/vacuum chuck with notch aligned at 0 degrees. 2. Verify ambient chuck temperature is stabilized at 23.0 +/- 0.2 deg C for automated temperature compensation (alpha_Al = 0.0039 / deg C). 3. Full-wafer 1-sigma non-uniformity (NU%) must be <= 2.50% across 49 points (with 5mm edge exclusion).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10/100 Cleanroom Bunny Suit (Nitrile antistatic cuffs), Powder-free cleanroom-grade nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with IPA wipe solvent: flush eyes with clean eyewash station water for 15 minutes. For mechanical pinch hazard during robotic wafer transfer: emergency stop (E-stop) switch disengages all automated stage pneumatics and servos immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom laminar flow hood (Class 100 vertical laminar air flow, HEPA filtered face velocity 0.45 m/s +/- 20%). Tool internal vacuum exhaust connected to general fab scrubbed exhaust duct (min 20 CFM static draw) to exhaust solvent wipe vapors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA-saturated cleanroom wipes disposed of in sealed, antistatic flammables disposal bins lined with conductive bags. Spent probe heads containing trace copper and tungsten carbide sent to certified metals reclaim vendor; no liquid chemical waste streams generated during dry probing.

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited DC magnetron sputtered Al-0.5%Cu thin film (450-550 nm) over TiN barrier; unpassivated mirror finish with native oxide < 1.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probed wafer with verified sheet resistance map; contact marks inspected; surface free of probe flaking particles; clean and dry ready for PECVD inter-metal dielectric (IMD) deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient air queue time causes thick native Al2O3 growth (>3.5 nm) and atmospheric moisture adsorption, leading to contact resistance instability during 4PP probing and initiating galvanic pitting/corrosion at Cu-precipitate grain boundaries.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full wafer four-point probe sheet resistance map confirming uniform thickness and resistivity of sputtered Al-0.5%Cu M1/M2 interconnect layers within 180nm DRAM tapeout PDK tolerances, ensuring compliant interconnect RC delay and absence of dielectric punch-through defects.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Within-wafer sheet resistance non-uniformity (NU% 1-sigma) across 49 measurement sites with 5mm edge exclusion** | `2.00%` | <= 2.50% | Statistical standard deviation calculation over 49 sites per SEMI MF1529 standard |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Four-point probe mechanical indentation depth on Al-0.5%Cu film surface** | `25 nm` | <= 40 nm | High-resolution optical/stylus profilometry measurement of probe contact depressions |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Sheet resistance map passes Rs_mean (58.0 - 66.0 mOhm/sq) and NU% <= 2.50% criteria, short-term contact repeatability CV <= 0.25%, zero probe punch-through to ILD, and all deliverable CSV/PDF contour artifacts archived into PDK fab lot tracker with Q-time cleared for IMD PECVD deposition.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Spectroscopic Ellipsometry & X-Ray Reflectivity Thickness Profiling

**Context Module:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization > Post-Deposition Sheet Resistance & Step Coverage Metrology  
**Document ID:** `SOP-BEOL-MET-180NM-004`  
**Revision:** Rev 1.0  
**Technology Node:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS DRAM)

---

### Metrology Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Load Wafer       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Ellipsometry      │
│       Psi/Delta        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   XRR Grazing Angle    │
│        Profile         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Model Fitting &     │
│  Thickness Validation  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP specifies the non-destructive physical metrology protocol to determine film thickness, native capping oxide, and across-wafer spatial non-uniformity of as-deposited and annealed Al-0.5%Cu Metal-1 (M1) and Metal-2 (M2) layers on 180nm DRAM wafers using Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (SE) and X-Ray Reflectivity (XRR).

---

### 2. Physical Principles & Optical Modeling
1. **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Fundamental Principle:**  
   Measures the change in polarization state upon reflection from planar thin-film test pads:
   $$\rho = \frac{r_p}{r_s} = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$$
   where $r_p$ and $r_s$ are the complex Fresnel reflection coefficients, parameterized by refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$ (using Drude-Lorentz optical modeling for metal absorption and Cauchy/Sellmeier models for surface oxide).
2. **X-Ray Reflectivity (XRR) Principle:**  
   Collimated X-ray beam ($\text{Cu } K\alpha$, $\lambda = 0.15418\text{ nm}$) scans grazing incidence angles ($\theta = 0.2^\circ - 4.0^\circ$) across critical total reflection edge $\theta_c$. The period of Kiessig interference fringes directly quantifies physical layer thickness ($t \approx \lambda / (2\Delta\theta)$) independent of optical constants.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Substrate Handling & Pre-Metrology Inspection
- Transfer the post-PVD wafer (sputtered Al-0.5%Cu film target 350 nm) from the FOUP into the optical/X-ray metrology load lock under Class 100 mini-environment.
- Verify wafer notch alignment ($0^\circ$) and stage chuck vacuum ($\Delta P \ge 75\text{ kPa}$).

#### Step 2: Automated Wafer Coordinate Mapping
- Load the standardized **49-point polar wafer map** recipe (with 3mm edge exclusion on 200mm wafers) or **9-point radial map** to capture center-to-edge radial deposition gradients from the DC magnetron planar source.
- Position the optical spot inside dedicated scribeline macro test pads ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$).

#### Step 3: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Acquisition & Fitting
- Set broadband light source across spectral range $\lambda = 240\text{ nm} - 800\text{ nm}$ at angles of incidence (AOI) $\theta_0 = 65^\circ, 70^\circ, 75^\circ$.
- Acquire spectroscopic polarization response $[\Psi(\lambda), \Delta(\lambda)]$.
- Execute regression fitting against the stack model: `Si / ILD SiO2 (interlayer dielectric) / Al-0.5%Cu / Native Al2O3`.
- Ensure Mean Squared Error (MSE) goodness-of-fit $\chi^2 \le 2.0$.

#### Step 4: X-Ray Reflectivity (XRR) Validation & Density Profiling
- On golden monitor wafers or lot pilot samples, align goniometer zero position ($\theta - 2\theta$ alignment).
- Scan grazing angle from $0.2^\circ$ to $3.5^\circ$ with an angular step resolution $\Delta\theta \le 0.005^\circ$.
- Extract Kiessig fringe oscillation periodicity to cross-calibrate SE-derived bulk thickness.

#### Step 5: Lot Disposition & Pass/Fail Interlocking
- Cross-reference measured thickness with deposition calibration ($50 - 100\text{ nm/min}$) and sheet resistance specification ($R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\text{sq}$ post-anneal).
- If thickness or non-uniformity violates control limits, flag the PVD chamber for target erosion and shield maintenance.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                Metal-1 Film Thickness Spec Range (nm)  
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
   M1 Max (nm)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
M1 Target (nm)┤██████████████████████████████████████  │
              │██████████████████████████████████████  │
   M1 Min (nm)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    │
              │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
              0.0      91.9      183.8    275.6   367.5 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Metal-1 (M1) Film Thickness** | **$350.0 \pm 17.5$** ($\pm 5\%$) | **$\text{nm}$** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / XRR |
| **Wafer Non-Uniformity ($1\sigma / \text{mean}$)** | **$\le 2.5\%$** across 49 points | **$\%$** | Automated 49-point wafer mapping |
| **Measurement Precision Repeatability** | **$\le \pm 0.05$** | **$\text{nm}$** | 10-cycle dynamic load-unload repeatability |
| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance Correlation** | **$R_s < 0.08$** | **$\Omega/\text{sq}$** | 4-point collinear probe post $400^\circ\text{C}$ anneal |

---

### 5. Literature Sources Cited
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**: Baseline Metal-1 film thickness target $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$, PVD deposition rate $50 - 100\text{ nm/min}$, sheet resistance target $R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\text{sq}$ post forming gas anneal ($400^\circ\text{C}$, 30 min).
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**: Fundamental ellipsometric equation $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \exp(i\Delta)$, Cauchy/Sellmeier parameterization, sub-Angstrom precision limits ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$), and automated 9-point / 49-point polar wafer mapping.

---
*Micro-knowledge recorded at: [se_xrr_thickness_metrology.md](./docs/knowledge/se_xrr_thickness_metrology.md)*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Optical spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) cannot penetrate thick opaque metallic films (Al-0.5%Cu nominal 450-600 nm) due to skin depth limitations (<15 nm across UV-NIR), restricting direct bulk metal thickness measurement to ultra-thin barrier/seed sub-layers (Ti/TiN <40 nm) or requiring grazing-incidence X-Ray Reflectivity (XRR) combined with post-etch step-height stylus profilometry/four-point probe (4PP) correlation. System integration must enforce cross-tool calibration between 49-point SE mapping on native surface oxide/barrier layers and specular XRR fringe modeling on blanket monitor wafers to accurately decouple film density, surface roughness, and physical thickness.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Modeling metallic Al-Cu and underlying Ti/TiN stacks requires complex Drude-Lorentz oscillator formulations in SE rather than standard transparent dielectric Cauchy models. Native aluminum oxide (Al2O3, 3-5 nm) growth begins instantaneously upon atmospheric exposure, causing optical model parameter correlation between Al2O3 thickness and underlying Al roughness. For XRR, high electron density contrast between Al (rho=2.70 g/cm3) and TiN (rho=5.22 g/cm3) yields clear interference fringes, but diffuse surface scattering from sputter grain boundaries (rms roughness >4 nm) dampens critical Kiessig fringes beyond 2 theta = 3.5 deg, demanding rigorous surface micro-roughness parameterization (Debye-Waller or Nevot-Croce factors) to avoid severe thickness extraction skew.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: X-ray tube sources (Cu K-alpha anode, lambda = 1.5406 A) exhibit finite lifetimes (~3000-5000 operational hours) and require strict preventive maintenance to avoid beam drift and photon flux degradation. SE goniometer optical components, deuterium/halogen dual-source lamps, and polarizers (Glan-Thompson prisms) depend on specialized global precision optical vendors; lamp intensity roll-off directly inflates fit error (MSE > 2.5) on UV spectral channels, risking lot holds on the 180nm BEOL line if calibration monitor coupons and replacement source consumables are not buffered.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: High-resolution XRR theta-2theta specular scans across 0.2 deg to 4.0 deg require 12 to 25 minutes per wafer, presenting an unacceptable cycle-time bottleneck for production line throughput if deployed inline. Operationally, XRR must be restricted to 1x per shift or weekly calibration monitors for density/thickness baseline anchoring, while rapid 49-point automated SE and correlated 4-point probe sheet resistance (Rs) mappings serve as the primary inline high-throughput lot-release vehicle.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Native Al2O3 uncontrolled oxidation during ambient queue time creates refractive index parameter cross-correlation in SE regression, misidentifying a 2.5 nm native oxide growth as bulk Al-Cu thickness deviation.
1. Sputtered Al-Cu grain coarsening and high surface micro-roughness (>5 nm RMS) cause catastrophic diffuse X-ray scatter, completely suppressing XRR specular Kiessig oscillations and resulting in non-convergent optical model fitting.
1. Misalignment of XRR knife-edge collimator and goniometer zero-angle calibration induces systematic 2-theta offset (>0.015 deg), shifting the total external reflection critical angle (theta_c) and corrupting extracted metal mass density calculations by >8%.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-3-2-01` | **Dual-Wavelength Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Ti/TiN Liner Stack Profiling** | Automated Production Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (Rotating Compensator Ellipsometer, 193-1000 nm spectral range, automated 200mm wafer stage) | 1. Load monitor wafer onto SE vacuum chuck and initiate auto-focus and laser tip/tilt theta alignment. 2. Acquire polarized reflection spectra (Psi and Delta) across 210 nm to 850 nm at incidence angles of 65 deg, 70 deg, and 75 deg across a 49-point radial map (5 mm edge exclusion). 3. Apply parameterized Drude-Lorentz optical dispersion model for TiN top layer and Ti base layer on Si substrate. 4. Execute Levenberg-Marquardt non-linear regression minimizing Goodness of Fit Mean Squared Error (MSE). 5. Extract layer thicknesses (t_TiN, t_Ti) and 49-point wafer non-uniformity (1-sigma). | `TiN layer thickness = 25.0 nm +/- 1.5 nm; Ti liner thickness = 15.0 nm +/- 1.2 nm; Regression Mean Squared Error (MSE) <= 2.0; 49-point across-wafer thickness non-uniformity (1-sigma / mean) <= 2.5%.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-1-2-3-2-02` | **High-Resolution Grazing-Incidence XRR Density and Thickness Metrology of Al-0.5%Cu / Barrier Stack** | High-Resolution X-Ray Diffractometer / Reflectometer (Cu K-alpha radiation, lambda = 0.15406 nm, 2.2 kW sealed tube, Göbel mirror parallel-beam optics, 2-bounce Ge(220) monochromator, knife-edge incident collimator, scintillation detector) | 1. Align wafer surface to incident X-ray beam center; execute Z-height optimization and rocking curve (omega) alignment at 2-theta = 0.5 deg. 2. Perform specular theta-2theta scan from 0.20 deg to 3.50 deg in continuous scan mode with 0.005 deg step size and 1.5 s dwell time per step. 3. Extract critical angle of total external reflection (theta_c) for the Al-0.5%Cu top layer. 4. Perform Parratt recursive matrix optical fitting incorporating Nevot-Croce interface roughness to match Kiessig fringe periods and decay envelope. 5. Output bulk Al-0.5%Cu mass density, surface roughness (sigma_rms), and individual sub-layer thicknesses. | `Al-0.5%Cu total thickness = 500.0 nm +/- 15.0 nm; Extracted Al-0.5%Cu mass density = 2.70 +/- 0.05 g/cm3; Extracted surface micro-roughness sigma_rms <= 3.5 nm; Critical angle theta_c (Al-Cu) = 0.228 deg +/- 0.005 deg; Fitting figure of merit (R-factor) <= 3.0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloving required), EN 166 compliant UV-attenuating safety glasses with side shields, Personal thermoluminescent radiation dosimeter (TLD badge), Full cleanroom ESD gown, hood, conductive booties, and face mask
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with optical cleaning solvent (IPA), flush with cleanroom deionized water eyewash/shower for 15 minutes. In the event of suspected ionizing radiation exposure from X-ray tube interlock failure: immediately press Emergency Machine Off (EMO) button to cut generator high-voltage (HV) supply, isolate tool, log personal dosimeter reading, and escort personnel to medical facility for clinical radiation assessment.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Tool enclosure must maintain continuous exhaust ventilation at >= 150 CFM with static pressure differential of -0.05 in. w.g. relative to cleanroom ambient. XRR cabinet equipped with dual-channel fail-safe safety interlocks (Cat 4 / PL e) on access panels; scatter survey port maintains radiation leakage < 0.5 uSv/h at 5 cm distance from outer skin.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipe consumables must be segregated in dedicated hazardous solvent waste bins with self-closing foot-pedal lids, routed to cleanroom VOC exhaust abatement. No liquid chemical effluent generated during routine non-destructive beam/optical metrology.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

critics.systems_engineer: Optical spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) cannot penetrate thick opaque metallic films (Al-0.5%Cu nominal 450-600 nm) due to skin depth limitations (<15 nm across UV-NIR), restricting direct bulk metal thickness measurement to ultra-thin barrier/seed sub-layers (Ti/TiN <40 nm) or requiring grazing-incidence X-Ray Reflectivity (XRR) combined with post-etch step-height stylus profilometry/four-point probe (4PP) correlation. System integration must enforce cross-tool calibration between 49-point SE mapping on native surface oxide/barrier layers and specular XRR fringe modeling on blanket monitor wafers to accurately decouple film density, surface roughness, and physical thickness.
critics.domain_expert: Modeling metallic Al-Cu and underlying Ti/TiN stacks requires complex Drude-Lorentz oscillator formulations in SE rather than standard transparent dielectric Cauchy models. Native aluminum oxide (Al2O3, 3-5 nm) growth begins instantaneously upon atmospheric exposure, causing optical model parameter correlation between Al2O3 thickness and underlying Al roughness. For XRR, high electron density contrast between Al (rho=2.70 g/cm3) and TiN (rho=5.22 g/cm3) yields clear interference fringes, but diffuse surface scattering from sputter grain boundaries (rms roughness >4 nm) dampens critical Kiessig fringes beyond 2 theta = 3.5 deg, demanding rigorous surface micro-roughness parameterization (Debye-Waller or Nevot-Croce factors) to avoid severe thickness extraction skew.
critics.supply_chain: X-ray tube sources (Cu K-alpha anode, lambda = 1.5406 A) exhibit finite lifetimes (~3000-5000 operational hours) and require strict preventive maintenance to avoid beam drift and photon flux degradation. SE goniometer optical components, deuterium/halogen dual-source lamps, and polarizers (Glan-Thompson prisms) depend on specialized global precision optical vendors; lamp intensity roll-off directly inflates fit error (MSE > 2.5) on UV spectral channels, risking lot holds on the 180nm BEOL line if calibration monitor coupons and replacement source consumables are not buffered.
critics.laya_pm: High-resolution XRR theta-2theta specular scans across 0.2 deg to 4.0 deg require 12 to 25 minutes per wafer, presenting an unacceptable cycle-time bottleneck for production line throughput if deployed inline. Operationally, XRR must be restricted to 1x per shift or weekly calibration monitors for density/thickness baseline anchoring, while rapid 49-point automated SE and correlated 4-point probe sheet resistance (Rs) mappings serve as the primary inline high-throughput lot-release vehicle.
critical_failure_modes: Native Al2O3 uncontrolled oxidation during ambient queue time creates refractive index parameter cross-correlation in SE regression, misidentifying a 2.5 nm native oxide growth as bulk Al-Cu thickness deviation.

Sputtered Al-Cu grain coarsening and high surface micro-roughness (>5 nm RMS) cause catastrophic diffuse X-ray scatter, completely suppressing XRR specular Kiessig oscillations and resulting in non-convergent optical model fitting.

Misalignment of XRR knife-edge collimator and goniometer zero-angle calibration induces systematic 2-theta offset (>0.015 deg), shifting the total external reflection critical angle (theta_c) and corrupting extracted metal mass density calculations by >8%.

testcases.title: Dual-Wavelength Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Ti/TiN Liner Stack Profiling
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Production Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (Rotating Compensator Ellipsometer, 193-1000 nm spectral range, automated 200mm wafer stage)
testcases.pre_conditions: 200mm monitor wafer with DC magnetron sputtered Ti (15 nm) / TiN (25 nm) liner stack prior to main Al-0.5%Cu deposition; ambient temperature 21.5 +/- 0.5 deg C; relative humidity 40 +/- 3%; system calibration completed using certified 100 nm SiO2/Si calibration standard (MSE < 1.20).
