# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Cross-Sectional SEM Cleave & High-Aspect-Ratio Void Metrology

**Document ID:** `SOP-BEOL-MET-180-042`  
**Process Level:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization > IMD Gap-Fill Qualification > Cross-Sectional SEM Metrology  
**Node Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS DRAM)  
**Classification:** Foundational Industrial Leaf SOP  

---

### 1. Objective & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure governs the precision cross-sectional mechanical cleaving, sample preparation, and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) metrology for detecting sub-micron seams, voids, and pinch-off anomalies in Inter-Metal Dielectric 1 (IMD1 TEOS-PECVD) gap-fill between high-aspect-ratio Metal-1 (Al-0.5% Cu) interconnect lines.

---

### 2. Verified Context & Interconnect Baseline Dimensions
*Derived directly from local literature context:*
* **Metal-1 (M1) Interconnect Thickness Target:** $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$ ($332.5\text{ nm} \text{ to } 367.5\text{ nm}$) (*Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects*).
* **Interconnect Pitch (Bitline / M1 Pitch):** $360\text{ nm} \text{ to } 400\text{ nm}$ (*Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).
* **Nominal Inter-Line Spacing (Half-Pitch @ 180nm minimum):** $\approx 180\text{ nm} \text{ to } 200\text{ nm}$.
* **Aspect Ratio ($AR = H / W$):** $\approx 350\text{ nm} / 180\text{ nm} \approx 1.75:1 \text{ to } 1.94:1$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
|                      SOP WORKFLOW OVERVIEW                      |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Step 1] Wafer Scribing & Precision Cleaving (Diamond Tip)    |
|                                |                                |
|                                v                                |
|  [Step 2] Cross-Section Mount & Conductive Grounding (Carbon)   |
|                                |                                |
|                                v                                |
|  [Step 3] FE-SEM Chamber Evacuation & Beam Tuning (1-3 kV)      |
|                                |                                |
|                                v                                |
|  [Step 4] High-Aspect-Ratio IMD1 Gap-Fill & Seam Void Metrology |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Wafer Scribing and Precision Cleaving
1. Retrieve witness coupon or sacrificial wafer from the IMD1 TEOS-PECVD gap-fill queue.
2. Under an optical stereomicroscope ($50\times$), align the diamond scribe tip along the backside crystalline cleavage plane ($\langle 110 \rangle$ orientation for (100) Si substrate) perpendicular to the parallel dense Metal-1 bitline strapping arrays.
3. Apply a single controlled scribe line ($5\text{ mm}$ length) outside the active array border.
4. Execute clean cross-sectional mechanical cleaving using the 3-point bending anvil fixture to yield an unpolished, sharp, mirror-fracture edge across the $360\text{ nm} \text{ to } 400\text{ nm}$ pitch metal arrays without mechanical smear.

#### Step 2: Sample Mounting & Conductive Preparation
1. Mount the cleaved die vertically onto a $90^\circ$ cross-sectional SEM stub using ultra-pure conductive colloidal carbon adhesive paste.
2. Ensure continuous conductive path from the substrate edge to the aluminum stub to prevent charging during low-kV imaging.
3. Perform rapid dry $N_2$ blow-off ($30\text{ psi}$) to remove cleavage silicon particulate contamination.
4. *(Optional for unpassivated IMD)*: Apply ultra-thin ($1.0\text{ nm} \text{ to } 1.5\text{ nm}$) Osmium or Iridium conductive flash coat if dielectric surface charging degrades edge contrast at the TEOS/Al-Cu interface.

#### Step 3: FE-SEM Evacuation & Beam Alignment
1. Load specimen into the FE-SEM load-lock and pump down until main chamber vacuum reaches $\le 5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$.
2. Set primary beam accelerating voltage $V_{acc} = 1.0\text{ kV} \text{ to } 2.5\text{ kV}$ (low kV mode to minimize electron beam penetration and prevent shrinkage/carbon deposition on TEOS oxide).
3. Set probe current to low-current mode: $I_p = 10\text{ pA} \text{ to } 25\text{ pA}$ at a working distance ($WD$) of $3.0\text{ mm} \text{ to } 4.5\text{ mm}$.
4. Engage In-Lens Secondary Electron (In-Lens SE) detector for high surface sensitivity and edge resolution.

#### Step 4: High-Aspect-Ratio Void Metrology & Measurement
1. Locate the dense array test structure (M1 lines with pitch $360\text{ nm} \text{ to } 400\text{ nm}$, target height $350\text{ nm}$).
2. Perform fine focus, aperture centering, and stigmator correction at $150,000\times$ magnification.
3. Acquire calibrated high-resolution digital micrographs at $100,000\times$ and $200,000\times$ across at least 10 consecutive inter-metal gaps per die site (center, middle, edge).
4. Conduct digital line-profile measurements:
   - Verify Metal-1 physical height ($H_{M1}$).
   - Inspect gap sidewall profile for re-entrant deposition cusps.
   - Screen for buried keyhole/seam voids within the inter-metal space.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Metal-1 Physical Height ($H_{M1}$)** | $350 \pm 5\%$ ($332.5 - 367.5$) | $\text{nm}$ | Calibrated FE-SEM Cross-Section (100k$\times$) |
| **Interconnect Array Pitch** | $360 \text{ to } 400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Cross-Sectional Line Pitch Metrology |
| **IMD1 Seam / Keyhole Void Width** | $0$ (None detectable $\ge 5\text{ nm}$) | $\text{nm}$ | FE-SEM In-Lens SE at 200k$\times$ |
| **FE-SEM Chamber Vacuum Level** | $\le 5 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | Penning / Cold Cathode Vacuum Gauge |

---

### 5. Context Citations
* **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - Film thickness target for Metal-1: $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$.
  - Interconnect metallization material: Al-0.5% Cu / Pure Al.
* **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - Array pitch parameters: Bitline and wordline pitch is approximately $360\text{ nm} \text{ to } 400\text{ nm}$.
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Cell architecture reference: Folded bitline layouts, shared contact geometries, and stacked capacitor over bitline topologies.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Destructive cross-sectional SEM requires precision mechanical cleaving directly across dense M1 pitch arrays (0.48 µm pitch at 180nm node). Cleave path deviation exceeding ±1.5 µm off the target plane induces optical tilt artifacts and geometric distortion, which risks misclassifying sub-surface seam-void delamination as bulk micro-voids. Correlation with non-destructive optical spectroscopic ellipsometry (n and k refractive index modeling) on planar monitor pads is mandatory to establish baseline density calibration prior to cleaving.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In PECVD TEOS/O2 deposition over high-aspect-ratio (AR > 1.8:1) dense M1 aluminum interconnects, re-entrant profile cusp formation at the top metal corners causes premature pinch-off. Etch-stain delineation using buffered oxide etch (BOE 20:1) or diluted HF vapor prior to SEM inspection is required to distinguish true physical voids from refractive electron contrast boundaries in amorphous SiO2. Sputtered conductive gold/palladium or carbon coating must remain below 3 nm to avoid obscuring nanoscale keyhole seams.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-wafer diamond scriber cleavage destroys production wafers, driving scrap cost up in multi-project wafer (MPW) runs. A dedicated scribe-line drop-in test structure containing pitch comb-serpent arrays must be utilized rather than sacrificing active die. Sputter target inventory (99.999% high-purity Pt/C) and SEM LaB6/FEG filament life cycles must be scheduled to maintain 24-hour turnaround for IMD1 recipe tuning loops.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Turnaround time from PECVD IMD1 unload to SEM void signoff directly gates CMP planarization pre-conditioning. If the metrology queue exceeds 4 hours, moisture absorption in unannealed TEOS silanol (Si-OH) bonds distorts dielectric integrity. Cleave prep, sputter coating, high-magnification SEM imaging, and void aspect ratio automated measurement must be time-boxed to under 120 minutes per wafer coupon.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Keyhole pinch-off void formation along tight 240nm metal spacing due to insufficient TEOS surface mobility and premature oxide overhang bridging.
1. Mechanical cleave smearing and ductile aluminum displacement across dielectric gaps, masking or falsely creating inter-metal dielectric voids.
1. Delamination and micro-cracking at the SiN barrier / TEOS IMD1 interface triggered by cleaving stress concentration.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-2-3-01` | **Cross-Sectional FE-SEM Dense M1 Gap-Fill Void Metrology** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM, Cold-FEG source) with 1.0 nm resolution at 5 kV, Precision Diamond Scriber/Cleaver, High-Vacuum Carbon/Iridium Coater | 1. Load cleaved coupon onto 90-degree cross-section holder and align cleave edge strictly parallel to electron optical axis. 2. Navigate to M1 minimum design pitch dense comb array (240 nm linewidth / 240 nm space, 450 nm metal thickness, aspect ratio ~1.87:1). 3. Acquire calibrated digital micrographs at 50,000x and 150,000x magnification across 5 distinct gap locations. 4. Measure vertical keyhole void height, horizontal void width, and remaining dielectric overburden thickness from metal top to void boundary using calibrated line-scan profile analysis. | `Zero detectable voids with equivalent diameter >= 15 nm across all 5 inspection sites; aspect-ratio gap fill verified 100% solid oxide with no continuous seam micro-cracks.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-2-3-02` | **Delineation Wet-Etch Decoration and Seam Integrity Characterization** | Chemical Wet Delineation Bench, Precision Dispenser, Ultra-High Resolution SEM, Calibrated Ellipsometer for etch-rate tracking | 1. Submerge freshly cleaved coupon into 200:1 BOE solution for exactly 5.0 seconds to delineate latent low-density boundary seams without causing structural collapse. 2. Immediately quench in overflowing deionized water bath for 60 seconds followed by clean dry N2 blow-off. 3. Coat with 1.5 nm conductive iridium film under argon sputter discharge. 4. Image at 100,000x magnification to quantify seam etch-back depth and lateral void widening. | `Etch decoration trench depth at the dielectric merger seam must not exceed 25 nm; no preferential pit etch widening beyond 10 nm relative to bulk PECVD TEOS oxide etch rate.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: EN 374 Type A chemical resistant gloves (Neoprene over heavy-duty Nitrile), ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and splash-resistant safety goggles, Cleanroom chemical apron (acid and organic vapor resistant fluoropolymer), Safety footwear with slip-resistant chemical sole
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF/BOE exposure: Immediately flush affected skin area with copious water for 2 minutes. Continuously massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel into the burn site until medical personnel arrive. In case of eye contact, irrigate with 1% sterile calcium gluconate eye solution or saline for 15 minutes. Administer 100% oxygen if vapors are inhaled; seek emergency medical care immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: All wet-etch delineation and chemical handling must be performed in a dedicated polypropylene laminar-flow wet bench equipped with dedicated acid scrubber exhaust maintaining face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) with continuous magnehelic pressure differential monitoring.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Fluoride-bearing chemical waste streams must be segregated into dedicated labeled PVDF carboys. Neutralize acidic fluoride effluent with Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) sludge, maintaining solution pH between 7.0 and 8.5 prior to hazardous waste disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / SLSI) | `49 wt% (stock solution for dilution to 200:1)` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride** | `12125-01-8` | Semiconductor Grade (TraceMetal) | `40 wt% (buffer component for BOE)` |
| **Isopropanol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (MOS) | `99.8 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-PECVD TEOS IMD1 deposited state; unannealed dielectric surface containing active Si-OH terminal bonds, vulnerable to moisture condensation and ambient hydrocarbon contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Cleaved, carbon-coated, vacuum-desorbed coupon post-SEM qualification, validated void-free prior to batch CMP polish and furnace densification anneal.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time induces atmospheric moisture absorption into unannealed porous TEOS oxide, converting silanol groups to micro-pores, swelling the dielectric matrix, and initiating moisture-induced blistering or delamination during subsequent 400°C metallization anneal.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Quantitative validation of cross-sectional gap-fill profile and absence of sub-surface keyhole voids in PECVD TEOS IMD1 over high-aspect-ratio 180nm M1 metal pitch via high-resolution FE-SEM imaging, assuring dielectric reliability prior to ILD/IMD CMP planarization.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `IMD1_M1_Cleave_Void_Metrology_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `SEM_Micrograph_Dense_M1_Pitch_50kx_150kx.tiff`
- [ ] `IMD1_GapFill_Void_Dimensions_RawData.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum allowable equivalent keyhole void diameter in 240nm metal spacing** | `0.0 nm` | < 15.0 nm (instrument detection limit) | Calibrated 150,000x FE-SEM edge-contrast line-scan analysis across 20 consecutive metal trenches |
| `ASSERT-02` | **PECVD TEOS IMD1 dielectric overburden thickness above top of M1 aluminum lines** | `650.0 nm` | ± 30.0 nm | Cross-sectional SEM vertical cursor measurement cross-calibrated against spectroscopic ellipsometry on adjacent monitor pad |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-delineation seam etch groove depth at IMD1 convergence midline** | `0.0 nm` | <= 25.0 nm | High-resolution SEM measurement following 5-second 200:1 BOE chemical decoration |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero keyhole voids detected across 20 examined dense trench cross-sections, IMD1 overburden within 620-680 nm, post-etch seam depth <= 25 nm, and unanimous technical signoff by Thin Film Deposition Lead and Metrology Systems Engineer.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Post-Deposition IMD Thickness, Refractive Index, and Surface Planarization Metrology

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-deposition IMD metrology must decouple optical film parameters (film thickness t_IMD and refractive index n at 632.8 nm) from underlying Metal 1 topographical reflection artifacts. Measuring unpatterned scribe-line optical test pads (minimum 80x80 um) using spectroscopic ellipsometry is required to prevent destructive interference and diffraction scattering from sub-micron M1 routing lines from corrupting the Sellmeier/Cauchy dispersion fit.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm BEOL TEOS-PECVD SiO2, stoichiometric stability directly determines inter-metal parasitic capacitance and breakdown voltage (BV_ox > 8 MV/cm). Refractive index must fall strictly between 1.458 and 1.462; values above 1.465 indicate silicon-rich oxide prone to elevated leakage currents, while values below 1.452 indicate excessive Si-OH silanol moisture incorporation causing early dielectric breakdown and erratic via-contact resistance.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Automated dual-wavelength spectroscopic ellipsometry and non-contact white light interferometry stages require calibrated NIST-traceable thermal oxide calibration standards (100 nm and 1000 nm SiO2 on Si) to prevent measurement drift across multi-wafer production lots and avoid premature CMP pad conditioning or slurry consumption based on erroneous thickness readings.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: This metrology step acts as the primary quality gate controlling release to either chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) or spin-on-glass (SOG) etchback. Gate-to-gate cycle time must not exceed 25 minutes per wafer for a 49-point wafer map, ensuring the strict 120-minute Q-time window between PECVD deposition and subsequent lithography/planarization is maintained.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Optical parameter correlation failure: Fitting thickness and refractive index simultaneously over topographically varied metal lines yields non-physical Cauchy parameters (MSE > 15), leading to miscalculated CMP polish target times and fatal Metal 1 punch-through.
1. Silanol outgassing and moisture absorption: Delays exceeding the air queue-time threshold cause ambient moisture uptake by porous TEOS oxide, resulting in film swelling, reduced refractive index (< 1.450), and severe via metal bubbling/delamination during subsequent via anneals.
1. Severe topography-induced step-height underestimation: Single-point reflectometry misses severe micro-loading and keyhole voiding between tightly pitched 180nm M1 tracks, falsely reporting adequate planarization pre-conditioning.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-01` | **49-Point Spectroscopic Ellipsometry for IMD Thickness and Refractive Index Mapping** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 250 nm - 850 nm, 70-degree angle of incidence, 30 um focused micro-spot) calibrated with NIST-traceable 100 nm SiO2 standard. | 1. Load wafer onto vacuum chuck and perform automated optical pattern recognition on wafer alignment fiducials. 2. Measure spectral Psi and Delta from 300 nm to 800 nm across a standardized 49-point polar map with 3 mm edge exclusion. 3. Fit raw data using a calibrated Cauchy dispersion model: n(lambda) = A_n + B_n / lambda^2 with extinction coefficient k = 0. 4. Extract film thickness (t_IMD), refractive index (n at 632.8 nm), Goodness-of-Fit (Mean Squared Error, MSE), and compute within-wafer non-uniformity (NU% = [(Max - Min) / (2 * Mean)] * 100). | `Target thickness t_IMD = 800.0 nm +/- 25.0 nm; Refractive Index n (at 632.8 nm) = 1.460 +/- 0.005; Goodness-of-fit MSE < 3.5; 49-point thickness non-uniformity (1-sigma / mean) <= 2.5%.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-02` | **High-Resolution Optical Profilometry of Post-Deposition Surface Step-Height and Planarization Profile** | Coherence Scanning White-Light Interferometer / Optical 3D Surface Profilometer equipped with a 50x Mirau interferometric objective (lateral resolution 0.4 um, vertical resolution < 0.1 nm). | 1. Position objective over dense Metal 1 array boundary (0.28 um line / 0.28 um space transitioning to 10 um wide ground bus). 2. Acquire 150 um x 150 um 3D interferometric surface topography map using vertical scanning interferometry (VSI) mode. 3. Extract cross-sectional step height profile across the dense-to-isolated boundary. 4. Calculate maximum peak-to-valley step height (Delta_H) and local surface roughness (Ra). | `As-deposited dielectric step-height over 450 nm M1 lines Delta_H <= 380.0 nm (demonstrating compliant conformal/semi-planar step coverage); surface micro-roughness Ra <= 1.2 nm; zero detectable micro-void fissures or seam cracks.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-blocking laser safety glasses, Full cleanroom bunny suit with integrated hood, ESD booties, and particulate face mask
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Optical metrology operations present primary hazards from class 3B/4 alignment lasers, UV light sources, and solvent wipe maintenance. For ocular exposure to alignment beams: immediately turn off beam, keep eye closed and patched, seek urgent ophthalmologist evaluation. For IPA skin contact: wash area thoroughly with cleanroom DI water for 15 minutes. For IPA inhalation: move victim immediately to fresh air outside the sub-fab area.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Tool enclosure maintained at continuous laminar downflow (ISO Class 4 / FED-STD-209E Class 10 conditions, face velocity 0.45 m/s +/- 20%). Metrology stage vacuum chuck exhaust vented to sub-fab general solvent exhaust at min 15 SCFM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA cleanroom wipes sealed into airtight, antistatic hazardous waste bags and collected in dedicated closed flammable solid waste drums for off-site thermal incineration. Zero liquid chemical drainage to municipal sewer.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Cleanroom IPA for chuck maintenance)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 (VLSI/Electronic grade) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Gaseous Nitrogen (Wafer purge and chuck float)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (99.999% purity, sub-0.1 ppm H2O) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited TEOS-PECVD SiO2 layer, unpatterned or over Metal 1 topography, completely dry, cooled to 21 deg C, hydrophobic to slightly hydrophilic (water contact angle ~35-45 deg), free of vacuum particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Non-destructively inspected, optically characterized, and mapped IMD dielectric surface with validated thickness, index, and planarity, purged with ultra-pure N2, packaged in an airtight FOUP or purged cassette container.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding the queue time causes significant moisture and airborne organic siloxane uptake into the unpassivated TEOS film matrix. This alters the optical index, accelerates film densification stress, and causes severe dielectric film blistering, film pop-off, or incomplete subsequent Via 1 wet/dry etching.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full non-destructive qualification and statistical verification of the post-deposition IMD TEOS-PECVD dielectric stack, ensuring absolute thickness, stoichiometric optical index, and pre-CMP topography step height comply with 180nm BEOL design rules prior to planarization and photolithography gate release.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `imd_thickness_ri_49pt_wafermap.csv`
- [ ] `imd_dispersion_cauchy_fit_report.pdf`
- [ ] `imd_pre_cmp_surface_topography_profilometry.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean IMD TEOS dielectric film thickness across 49-point wafer map** | `800.0 nm` | +/- 25.0 nm (+/- 3.125%) | Automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (300-800 nm, 49 points, 3mm edge exclusion) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **IMD refractive index at standard helium-neon wavelength (632.8 nm)** | `1.4600` | +/- 0.0040 (range 1.4560 - 1.4640) | Cauchy dispersion model regression fit (MSE < 3.5) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Pre-planarization maximum step height over dense 450nm M1 features** | `350.0 nm` | <= 380.0 nm max allowable | Optical 3D Coherence Scanning White-Light Profilometry |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full 49-point ellipsometry map verified with 1-sigma non-uniformity <= 2.5%, Cauchy MSE < 3.5, refractive index strictly within 1.4560-1.4640, profilometry confirming step height <= 380.0 nm without seam cracks, and automated signoff certificate generated within 60 minutes of PECVD cycle completion.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Details
- **Title**: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Optical Dispersion Model Calibration for IMD TEOS Films
- **Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 3) — Foundry Tapeout & PDK / BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization / Thin Film Metrology
- **Action Type**: Buy / Metrology Calibration
- **Target Layer**: Inter-Metal Dielectric (IMD) PECVD Tetraethyl Orthosilicate ($\text{SiO}_2$ / TEOS)

---

## 1. Process Overview & Physical Principles

Spectroscopic ellipsometry measures the change in polarization state of broadband light reflected from thin-film sample interfaces. The complex reflectance ratio is governed by the fundamental ellipsometric equation:

$$\rho = \frac{r_p}{r_s} = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$$

where $r_p$ and $r_s$ are the complex Fresnel reflection coefficients for light polarized parallel ($p$) and perpendicular ($s$) to the plane of incidence, and $\Psi$ and $\Delta$ represent the amplitude ratio and phase difference, respectively. 

Transparent IMD TEOS films are parameterized across the UV-visible spectrum using the Cauchy or Sellmeier optical dispersion models:
- **Cauchy Dispersion Formulation**:
  $$n(\lambda) = A + \frac{B}{\lambda^2} + \frac{C}{\lambda^4}, \quad k(\lambda) \approx 0$$
  where $n(\lambda)$ is the refractive index, $k(\lambda)$ is the extinction coefficient ($k = 0$ in the transparent regime), and $A, B, C$ are material fit coefficients.

```
       [ Broadband Light Source ]
                   \
                    \ Polarized Incident Beam (Angle of Incidence ~ 65°-75°)
                     v
             +-----------------+
             |  IMD TEOS Film  |  d_TEOS, n(lambda), k(lambda)
             +-----------------+
             | Substrate / M1  |
             +-----------------+
                     /
                    / Reflected Elliptical Beam
                   v
          [ Analyzer & Detector ] ---> Extract (Psi, Delta) Spectrum
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Calibration & Measurement Procedure

### Step 1: System Baseline & Hardware Setup
1. Power on the spectroscopic ellipsometer light source (xenon arc lamp / deuterium-halogen combination). Allow a 30-minute warm-up stabilization period.
2. Perform straight-through air calibration and reference mirror qualification to verify detector alignment and polarizer/analyzer angle offset calibration.
3. Clean the automated wafer chuck and load the calibration baseline wafer (reference thermal oxide: $3.5\text{ nm}$ dry oxide standard). Verify sub-Angstrom measurement capability ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$ precision).

### Step 2: Optical Dispersion Model Definition
1. Open the optical modeling suite and configure the layer stack:
   - **Substrate Layer**: Single-crystal silicon ($\text{c-Si}$) or underlying metal interconnect layer.
   - **Dielectric Layer**: Cauchy or Sellmeier dispersion model for PECVD TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$.
2. Initialize model dispersion parameters:
   - Cauchy parameter $A \approx 1.45 - 1.46$ (nominal index at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$).
   - Cauchy parameter $B \approx 0.003 - 0.005\text{ }\mu\text{m}^2$.
   - Extinction coefficient $k(\lambda) = 0$ (fully transparent BEOL IMD window).
3. Set angle of incidence ($\text{AOI}$) between $65^\circ$ and $75^\circ$ (spanning the Brewster angle for $\text{SiO}_2/\text{Si}$ to maximize measurement sensitivity in $\Delta$).

### Step 3: Spectral Acquisition & Levenberg-Marquardt Regression Fit
1. Acquire experimental $\Psi(\lambda)$ and $\Delta(\lambda)$ spectra across the broadband wavelength range ($250\text{ nm} - 850\text{ nm}$).
2. Execute non-linear regression using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm minimizing the Mean Squared Error ($\text{MSE}$):
   $$\text{MSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{2N - M} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left[ \left(\frac{\Psi_{\text{meas}, i} - \Psi_{\text{model}, i}}{\sigma_{\Psi, i}}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\Delta_{\text{meas}, i} - \Delta_{\text{model}, i}}{\sigma_{\Delta, i}}\right)^2 \right]}$$
3. Float film thickness ($t_{\text{IMD}}$) and Cauchy coefficients ($A, B$) sequentially to prevent parameter correlation. Verify that the fitted extinction coefficient remains non-absorbing ($k = 0$).

### Step 4: Automated Radial Non-Uniformity Mapping
1. Configure automated wafer handling to measure across the wafer surface using an automated **9-point** or **49-point** mapping routine.
2. Ensure edge-exclusion is set to $3\text{ mm} - 5\text{ mm}$ to discard bevel bead artifacts.
3. Record thickness profile $t_{\text{IMD}}(r, \theta)$, average refractive index $n$ at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$, and calculate wafer-level non-uniformity percentage:
   $$\text{Non-Uniformity (\%)} = \frac{t_{\max} - t_{\min}}{2 \cdot t_{\text{avg}}} \times 100\%$$

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                                                        
                      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                      │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Map Uniformity (49-pt)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
   Psi/Delta Precision┤▒                               │
                      │▒                               │
               Fit MSE┤█                               │
                      │█                               │
                      └┬───────┬───────┬──────┬───────┬┘
                      0.0    24.7    49.4   74.1   98.8 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Model Fit Goodness ($\text{MSE}$)** | $\le 1.50$ (Nominal: $\le 1.20$) | Dimensionless | Levenberg-Marquardt regression residual fit across $\Psi(\lambda)$ and $\Delta(\lambda)$ |
| **Measurement Precision (Reference Oxide standard)** | $\pm 0.05$ | $\text{nm}$ | 10-run repeatability on $3.5\text{ nm}$ dry oxide reference standard (sub-Angstrom precision) |
| **Wafer Non-Uniformity Tracking** | Automated 9-point or 49-point map completed | Points per wafer | Automated stage multipoint radial mapping routine across wafer diameter |
| **Dielectric Refractive Index ($n_{632.8\text{ nm}}$)** | $1.458 \pm 0.015$ | Dimensionless | Cauchy dispersion parameter $n(\lambda)$ extracted at $632.8\text{ nm}$ |

---

## 4. Context References
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**: Principles of $\Psi$ and $\Delta$, Fresnel reflection ratio $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi)\exp(i\Delta)$, Cauchy and Sellmeier optical dispersion modeling of $n(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$, sub-Angstrom precision ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$ on $3.5\text{ nm}$ oxide), and automated 9-point / 49-point wafer mapping.
- **Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification**: Physical integration standards for 180nm process node validation.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Optical metrology parameter cross-coupling represents a severe system-level risk: in PECVD TEOS films (~600 nm to 1000 nm thick), physical thickness (t) and Cauchy refractive index coefficients (An, Bn) exhibit mathematical correlation in spectroscopic regression if the angle of incidence is fixed or spectral bandwidth is restricted. The calibrated model must mandate multi-angle acquisition (65 deg, 70 deg, 75 deg) or fix the underlying Si/thermal oxide stack dielectric function to eliminate non-uniqueness and prevent false thickness drift propagation into downstream CMP planarization loops.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: PECVD TEOS films at 180nm nodes possess residual silanol (Si-OH) bonds and sub-stoichiometric SiOx densities depending on RF power and precursor/oxidant ratio. A simple classical Cauchy model (n(lambda) = An + Bn/lambda^2 + Cn/lambda^4, k=0) is valid only in the transparent regime (400-800 nm); attempting to fit down to deep UV (193-248 nm) without adding a Tauc-Lorentz or Urbach tail oscillator will induce strong phase errors in Delta and cause unphysical index excursions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Model calibration relies on NIST-traceable calibrated thermal oxide step-height standards and deuterium/tungsten-halogen reference lamps. Lead times for NIST/BAM certified 100nm/500nm SiO2 calibration wafers currently exceed 16 weeks, and spectrometer polarization optics (analyzer/polarizer Glan-Thompson prisms) have single-source vendor vulnerability; calibration routines must accommodate secondary traceable working standards.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Over-constraining optical dispersion characterization on every monitor wafer introduces tool queue bottlenecks at the spectroscopic ellipsometer. Production recipes must decouple the extensive research-grade multi-angle dispersion calibration (performed weekly on dedicated test blankets) from the rapid single-angle 49-point thickness/refractive-index in-line monitor recipe to protect line takt time.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Mathematical cross-correlation between film thickness (t) and Cauchy parameter An resulting in compensating parameter drift and undetected CMP under-polish or over-polish
1. Model convergence to local mathematical minima due to incorrect initial film thickness estimates outside the +/- half-period optical fringe window
1. Environmental airborne molecular contamination (AMC) causing ambient moisture and hydrocarbon adsorption on TEOS, shifting surface optical phase Delta by >1.5 degrees within 45 minutes

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-1-01` | **Cauchy Optical Dispersion Model Parameter Extraction and Goodness-of-Fit Validation** | Variable-Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (VASE) equipped with rotating compensator, dual Xe/tungsten light source (240 nm - 1000 nm), automated wafer stage, and Levenberg-Marquardt regression analysis software | 1. Mount the TEOS monitor wafer on the vacuum chuck and align wafer center and tilt using the auto-collimator. 2. Collect polarization spectra (Psi, Delta) across 240 nm to 1000 nm at angles of incidence of 65°, 70°, and 75° with 5 nm spectral steps. 3. Define the layer optical model stack: Si substrate (tabulated Jellison data) / Native oxide (1.5 nm fixed) / TEOS dielectric layer / Ambient air. 4. Parameterize TEOS layer using extended Cauchy dispersion: n(lambda) = An + Bn/lambda^2 + Cn/lambda^4, k(lambda) = 0 for lambda >= 380 nm. 5. Execute unconstrained multi-parameter Levenberg-Marquardt regression simultaneously fitting thickness (t), An, and Bn. 6. critics.systems_engineer: Optical metrology parameter cross-coupling represents a severe system-level risk: in PECVD TEOS films (~600 nm to 1000 nm thick), physical thickness (t) and Cauchy refractive index coefficients (An, Bn) exhibit mathematical correlation in spectroscopic regression if the angle of incidence is fixed or spectral bandwidth is restricted. The calibrated model must mandate multi-angle acquisition (65 deg, 70 deg, 75 deg) or fix the underlying Si/thermal oxide stack dielectric function to eliminate non-uniqueness and prevent false thickness drift propagation into downstream CMP planarization loops.
critics.domain_expert: PECVD TEOS films at 180nm nodes possess residual silanol (Si-OH) bonds and sub-stoichiometric SiOx densities depending on RF power and precursor/oxidant ratio. A simple classical Cauchy model (n(lambda) = An + Bn/lambda^2 + Cn/lambda^4, k=0) is valid only in the transparent regime (400-800 nm); attempting to fit down to deep UV (193-248 nm) without adding a Tauc-Lorentz or Urbach tail oscillator will induce strong phase errors in Delta and cause unphysical index excursions.
critics.supply_chain: Model calibration relies on NIST-traceable calibrated thermal oxide step-height standards and deuterium/tungsten-halogen reference lamps. Lead times for NIST/BAM certified 100nm/500nm SiO2 calibration wafers currently exceed 16 weeks, and spectrometer polarization optics (analyzer/polarizer Glan-Thompson prisms) have single-source vendor vulnerability; calibration routines must accommodate secondary traceable working standards.
critics.laya_pm: Over-constraining optical dispersion characterization on every monitor wafer introduces tool queue bottlenecks at the spectroscopic ellipsometer. Production recipes must decouple the extensive research-grade multi-angle dispersion calibration (performed weekly on dedicated test blankets) from the rapid single-angle 49-point thickness/refractive-index in-line monitor recipe to protect line takt time.
critical_failure_modes: Mathematical cross-correlation between film thickness (t) and Cauchy parameter An resulting in compensating parameter drift and undetected CMP under-polish or over-polish
Model convergence to local mathematical minima due to incorrect initial film thickness estimates outside the +/- half-period optical fringe window
Environmental airborne molecular contamination (AMC) causing ambient moisture and hydrocarbon adsorption on TEOS, shifting surface optical phase Delta by >1.5 degrees within 45 minutes

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## 49-Point Full-Wafer IMD Thickness and Refractive Index Map Acquisition

**Module:** Metrology / Thin Film Deposition  
**Technology Node:** Gen 3 (180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip, DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Process Level:** BEOL Inter-Metal Dielectric (IMD) Post-Deposition Optical Metrology  
**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180-IMD-49PT-001`  

---

### 1. Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Recipe & Model Setup  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Wafer Alignment &    │
│        Loading         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   49-Point Metrology   │
│       Execution        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Data Fit & Quality   │
│       Validation       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Acceptance Check &   │
│       Pass/Fail        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Physical Principles & Optical Modeling

- **Physical Metrology Technique:** Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry.
- **Governing Equations:**
  $$\rho = \frac{r_p}{r_s} = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$$
  where $r_p$ and $r_s$ are the complex Fresnel reflection coefficients, and angles $\Psi$ (amplitude ratio) and $\Delta$ (phase difference) characterize the polarization change upon reflection at the film-substrate interface.
- **Optical Material Model:** Cauchy dispersion formulation parameterizing refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$ for transparent/dielectric IMD thin films:
  $$n(\lambda) = A_n + \frac{B_n}{\lambda^2} + \frac{C_n}{\lambda^4}, \quad k(\lambda) \approx 0$$

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Tool Initialization & Model Verification:**
   - Initialize automated spectroscopic ellipsometer / reflectometer optical stage.
   - Load optical dispersion model for IMD dielectric (Cauchy model parameterizing $n(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$).
   - Verify calibration standards with reference dry thermal oxide wafer with known precision (repeatability within $\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$).

2. **Wafer Transfer & Alignment:**
   - Robotically transfer the 200mm / 180nm DRAM wafer onto the vacuum chuck.
   - Perform automated pattern/notch optical pre-alignment to establish $(X, Y)$ coordinate origin $(0, 0)$ at wafer center.
   - Engage vacuum chuck and perform autofocus and tip/tilt optical signal leveling ($Z$-height adjustment).

3. **49-Point Full-Wafer Map Measurement:**
   - Select the standard **49-point polar/concentric wafer mapping recipe** with programmed edge exclusion ($3\text{ mm}$ to $5\text{ mm}$).
   - Execute step-and-scan sequence across all 49 coordinates, recording broad-spectrum polarized reflectance signals ($\tan\Psi$, $\cos\Delta$).
   - Fit experimental $\Psi(\lambda)$ and $\Delta(\lambda)$ spectra to the Cauchy optical dispersion model at each site to extract:
     - Local IMD thickness $T_i$
     - Refractive index $n_i$ at reference $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$

4. **Statistical Analysis & Wafer Map Generation:**
   - Compute mean thickness ($\bar{T}$), standard deviation ($\sigma_T$), and percent non-uniformity:
     $$\text{Non-Uniformity (\%)} = \frac{T_{\max} - T_{\min}}{2 \times \bar{T}} \times 100\%$$
   - Calculate mean refractive index ($\bar{n}$) and radial distribution profile.
   - Inspect contour map for systematic radial signatures (e.g., center-to-edge dome or bowl profiles).

5. **Lot Disposition & Unloading:**
   - Verify all 49 measurement sites against acceptance thresholds.
   - Export 49-point raw data and contour plots to the Manufacturing Execution System (MES).
   - Release vacuum chuck and return wafer to FOUP/cassette.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Lower Spec Limit (LSL) | Upper Spec Limit (USL) | Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Measurement Precision (Static Repeatability)** | $\pm 0.05$ | $-$ | $\le 0.05$ | $\text{nm}$ ($1\sigma$) |
| **Full-Wafer Thickness Non-Uniformity (49-pt)** | Radial film uniformity | $-$ | $\le 5.0$ | $\%$ ($\frac{\max - \min}{2\text{mean}}$) |
| **Dielectric Refractive Index ($n$ @ $632.8\text{ nm}$)** | $1.460$ | $1.450$ | $1.470$ | $-$ |
| **Goodness-of-Fit ($R^2$ / MSE)** | Cauchy model fit | $0.990$ | $1.000$ | $-$ |

---

### 5. Context Citations

- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology:** Provides polarization angle formulations ($\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi)\exp(i\Delta)$), Cauchy/Sellmeier dispersion modeling of $n(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$, sub-Angstrom dry gate oxide measurement precision ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$), and automated 49-point wafer mapping protocols tracking radial film non-uniformity.
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects:** Provides 180nm metallization interconnect integration context, layer thickness tolerances ($\pm 5\%$), and BEOL structural interfaces.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Contextualizes 180nm DRAM cell topology, dielectric layers, and BEOL interconnect integration rules.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated 49-point polar coordinate mapping must maintain strict optical alignment relative to the lithographic notch/flat to ensure spatial correlation with downstream chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) removal rate maps. Neglecting chuck edge exclusion zones (<3 mm) will introduce severe optical edge-scattering artifacts, distorting non-uniformity (NU%) calculations and destabilizing the feedback loop to PECVD showerhead heater zoning.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For PECVD TEOS IMD (target ~800 nm over patterned metal topography), Cauchy or Sellmeier optical dispersion modeling must account for silanol (Si-OH) incorporation, density gradients, and film stress. Measuring refractive index at 632.8 nm requires careful decoupling of extinction coefficient k(lambda) and thickness t; any unmodeled interfacial sub-oxide layer or underlying TiN anti-reflective coating reflection will cause false thickness oscillations and pseudo-birefringence artifacts.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Metrology calibration standards (NIST-traceable thermal oxide calibration wafers with verified 100 nm and 1000 nm SiO2 reference thicknesses) face long lead times and high re-certification overhead. Sourcing qualified deuterium/tungsten-halogen light sources with guaranteed spectral stability (>2000 operating hours) is critical to prevent tool down-events during multi-lot MPW qualification campaigns.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: A 49-point recipe execution must not become a cycle-time bottleneck in the BEOL metallization pilot line. Chuck loading, autofocus, pattern recognition, pattern-free test pad location acquisition, and polar-stage translation must complete in <180 seconds per wafer to maintain target wafer-per-hour (WPH >= 20) throughput while satisfying statistical process control (SPC) data transfer gates.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interference model mismatch leading to refractive index / thickness parameter correlation error (drifting calculated n beyond 1.48 with false film thinning).
1. Beam spot misalignment overlapping patterned BEOL metal line edges instead of dedicated 80x80 um scribe-line test pads, resulting in specular scatter and complete fitting divergence (MSE > 20).
1. Moisture absorption in unannealed PECVD TEOS during extended cleanroom ambient exposure distorting optical constants (n, k) and generating bogus cross-wafer non-uniformity signatures.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-2-01` | **49-Point Full-Wafer IMD TEOS Thickness and Uniformity Verification** | Automated High-Precision Spectroscopic Ellipsometer / Reflectometer with motorized r-theta stage, 75 um micro-spot optics, and NIST-traceable calibration standard | 1. Load 150/200 mm production wafer onto automated vacuum chuck with wafer notch aligned to 0.00° ± 0.05°. 2. Execute recipe 'IMD1_TEOS_49PT_POLAR' targeting 49 polar coordinate sites across 5 concentric rings. 3. Acquire raw Psi and Delta spectra over wavelength range 250 nm to 850 nm per point using 70° angle of incidence. 4. Fit spectra to Cauchy dispersion model: n(lambda) = A + B/(lambda^2) + C/(lambda^4) with extinction coefficient k = 0. 5. Record local thickness t_i, calculate mean thickness, standard deviation, and full-wafer non-uniformity NU% = ((Max - Min) / (2 * Mean)) * 100%. | `Mean thickness: 800.0 nm ± 24.0 nm (within ±3.0% of nominal target); Full-wafer 49-point non-uniformity (NU%): <= 2.5%; Goodness-of-fit Mean Squared Error (MSE): < 2.00 for all 49 measurement sites.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-2-02` | **49-Point IMD Refractive Index (n @ 632.8 nm) and Silanol Stoichiometry Screening** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer with automated spectral extraction module at He-Ne reference wavelength (632.8 nm) | 1. Using the 49-point acquisition dataset from TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-2-01, isolate the extracted optical refractive index n at wavelength lambda = 632.8 nm across all 49 coordinates. 2. Calculate average refractive index (n_mean), wafer center-to-edge Delta_n, and inspect for high-index (>1.470) silanol-rich or silicon-rich outliers indicative of RF silane/TEOS dissociation anomalies. 3. Verify optical stability across radial zones: Center (Ring 1), Mid-radius (Rings 2-3), Edge (Rings 4-5). | `Mean Refractive Index (n @ 632.8 nm): 1.458 to 1.465; Point-to-point refractive index variation across all 49 points: Delta_n <= 0.005; Zero measurement sites exhibiting n > 1.472 or n < 1.450.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double-gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, Anti-static ESD-safe cleanroom frock and hood, Laser safety protective eyewear rated for Class 3R alignment diode lasers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye exposure to IPA wipes: Flush affected eyes or skin with sterile eyewash/water for at least 15 minutes. For high-intensity broadband lamp or Class 3R laser eye exposure: Remove affected personnel immediately from direct beam, shield eyes, and seek prompt ophthalmologic evaluation. In case of inert gas (N2) leak/asphyxiation risk: Move victim to fresh air, administer CPR/supplemental oxygen if unconscious.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Metrology tool vacuum pump exhaust must be hard-ducted to cleanroom general acid/solvent exhaust (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s, negative pressure differential -50 Pa) to prevent build-up of IPA vapors or lamp ozone emission.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA-saturated cleaning wipes and optical swabs must be disposed of in dedicated flame-retardant, grounded solvent waste receptacles; purge exhaust is continuously scrubbed via facility VOC abatement system.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Cleanroom Wipes** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `70% v/v in DI Water` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Chamber purge / Chuck float)** | `7727-37-9` | Semiconductor UHP Grade (99.9999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited TEOS-PECVD dielectric film over Metal 1 topography; cool, dry, pristine particle-free surface without moisture haze.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Non-destructively characterized wafer surface free of organic micro-contamination, beam-burn marks, or mechanical chuck vacuum scratches; ready for IMD CMP planarization.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient fab atmosphere promotes atmospheric moisture (H2O) absorption into unannealed PECVD oxide films, elevating silanol (Si-OH) bonds, shifting refractive index n upward, increasing dielectric loss tangent (k), and causing blistering/delamination during subsequent metallization thermal budgets.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful non-destructive acquisition, parameter regression, and validation of full-wafer 49-point thickness and refractive index maps for 800 nm PECVD TEOS IMD, confirming strict within-wafer uniformity (NU <= 2.5%) and stoichiometric integrity (n = 1.458-1.465) prior to CMP release.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `IMD1_TEOS_49PT_METROLOGY_REPORT_LOT_RUN01.csv`
- [ ] `IMD1_CONTOUR_THICKNESS_AND_INDEX_MAP.pdf`

| `ASSERT-01` | **Full-wafer mean TEOS thickness must match nominal target window** | `800.0 nm` | ±24.0 nm (±3.0%) | Automated 49-point polar coordinate spectroscopic ellipsometry mean calculation excluding 3 mm edge boundary. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Within-wafer film thickness non-uniformity across 49 polar points** | `1.80%` | <= 2.50% (Max allowable limit) | Calculated non-uniformity metric: ((Thickness_Max - Thickness_Min) / (2 * Thickness_Mean)) * 100. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Dielectric film refractive index at standard 632.8 nm wavelength** | `1.4620` | ±0.0035 (Range 1.4585 to 1.4655) | Cauchy dispersion model regression at He-Ne reference wavelength across all 49 measurement points with MSE < 2.00. |

Neglecting chuck edge exclusion zones (<3 mm) will introduce severe optical edge-scattering artifacts, distorting non-uniformity (NU%) calculations and destabilizing the feedback loop to PECVD showerhead heater zoning.
critics.domain_expert: For PECVD TEOS IMD (target ~800 nm over patterned metal topography), Cauchy or Sellmeier optical dispersion modeling must account for silanol (Si-OH) incorporation, density gradients, and film stress. Measuring refractive index at 632.8 nm requires careful decoupling of extinction coefficient k(lambda) and thickness t; any unmodeled interfacial sub-oxide layer or underlying TiN anti-reflective coating reflection will cause false thickness oscillations and pseudo-birefringence artifacts.
critics.supply_chain: Metrology calibration standards (NIST-traceable thermal oxide calibration wafers with verified 100 nm and 1000 nm SiO2 reference thicknesses) face long lead times and high re-certification overhead. Sourcing qualified deuterium/tungsten-halogen light sources with guaranteed spectral stability (>2000 operating hours) is critical to prevent tool down-events during multi-lot MPW qualification campaigns.
critics.laya_pm: A 49-point recipe execution must not become a cycle-time bottleneck in the BEOL metallization pilot line. Chuck loading, autofocus, pattern recognition, pattern-free test pad location acquisition, and polar-stage translation must complete in <180 seconds per wafer to maintain target wafer-per-hour (WPH >= 20) throughput while satisfying statistical process control (SPC) data transfer gates.
critical_failure_modes: Interference model mismatch leading to refractive index / thickness parameter correlation error (drifting calculated n beyond 1.48 with false film thinning).
Beam spot misalignment overlapping patterned BEOL metal line edges instead of dedicated 80x80 um scribe-line test pads, resulting in specular scatter and complete fitting divergence (MSE > 20).
Moisture absorption in unannealed PECVD TEOS during extended cleanroom ambient exposure distorting optical constants (n, k) and generating bogus cross-wafer non-uniformity signatures.

testcases.title: 49-Point Full-Wafer IMD TEOS Thickness and Uniformity Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Automated High-Precision Spectroscopic Ellipsometer / Reflectometer with motorized r-theta stage, 75 um micro-spot optics, and NIST-traceable calibration standard
testcases.pre_conditions: PECVD chamber deposition completed; wafer cooled to 21.5 ± 0.5 °C; ellipsometer baseline calibrated using 100 nm SiO2 on Si reference wafer (MSE < 1.20); 3 mm edge exclusion defined.
testcases.procedure: 1. Load 150/200 mm production wafer onto automated vacuum chuck with wafer notch aligned to 0.00° ± 0.05°. 2. Execute recipe 'IMD1_TEOS_49PT_POLAR' targeting 49 polar coordinate sites across 5 concentric rings. 3. Acquire raw Psi and Delta spectra over wavelength range 250 nm to 850 nm per point using 70° angle of incidence. 4. Fit spectra to Cauchy dispersion model: n(lambda) = A + B/(lambda^2) + C/(lambda^4) with extinction coefficient k = 0. 5. Record local thickness t_i, calculate mean thickness, standard deviation, and full-wafer non-uniformity NU% = ((Max - Min) / (2 * Mean)) * 100%.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean thickness: 800.0 nm ± 24.0 nm (within ±3.0% of nominal target); Full-wafer 49-point non-uniformity (NU%): <= 2.5%; Goodness-of-fit Mean Squared Error (MSE): < 2.00 for all 49 measurement sites.

testcases.title: 49-Point IMD Refractive Index (n @ 632.8 nm) and Silanol Stoichiometry Screening
testcases.instrumentation: Spectroscopic Ellipsometer with automated spectral extraction module at He-Ne reference wavelength (632.8 nm)
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer measured within 60 minutes post-deposition; cleanroom relative humidity at 42 ± 3%; recipe loaded with Cauchy dispersion parameters unlinked from extinction coefficient.
testcases.procedure: 1. Using the 49-point acquisition dataset from TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-2-01, isolate the extracted optical refractive index n at wavelength lambda = 632.8 nm across all 49 coordinates. 2. Calculate average refractive index (n_mean), wafer center-to-edge Delta_n, and inspect for high-index (>1.470) silanol-rich or silicon-rich outliers indicative of RF silane/TEOS dissociation anomalies. 3. Verify optical stability across radial zones: Center (Ring 1), Mid-radius (Rings 2-3), Edge (Rings 4-5).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean Refractive Index (n @ 632.8 nm): 1.458 to 1.465; Point-to-point refractive index variation across all 49 points: Delta_n <= 0.005; Zero measurement sites exhibiting n > 1.472 or n < 1.450.

ppe_required: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double-gloving required)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses
Anti-static ESD-safe cleanroom frock and hood
Laser safety protective eyewear rated for Class 3R alignment diode lasers
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin or eye exposure to IPA wipes: Flush affected eyes or skin with sterile eyewash/water for at least 15 minutes. For high-intensity broadband lamp or Class 3R laser eye exposure: Remove affected personnel immediately from direct beam, shield eyes, and seek prompt ophthalmologic evaluation. In case of inert gas (N2) leak/asphyxiation risk: Move victim to fresh air, administer CPR/supplemental oxygen if unconscious.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Metrology tool vacuum pump exhaust must be hard-ducted to cleanroom general acid/solvent exhaust (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s, negative pressure differential -50 Pa) to prevent build-up of IPA vapors or lamp ozone emission.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent IPA-saturated cleaning wipes and optical swabs must be disposed of in dedicated flame-retardant, grounded solvent waste receptacles; purge exhaust is continuously scrubbed via facility VOC abatement system.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly deposited TEOS-PECVD dielectric film over Metal 1 topography; cool, dry, pristine particle-free surface without moisture haze.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Non-destructively characterized wafer surface free of organic micro-contamination, beam-burn marks, or mechanical chuck vacuum scratches; ready for IMD CMP planarization.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding queue time in ambient fab atmosphere promotes atmospheric moisture (H2O) absorption into unannealed PECVD oxide films, elevating silanol (Si-OH) bonds, shifting refractive index n upward, increasing dielectric loss tangent (k), and causing blistering/delamination during subsequent metallization thermal budgets.

expected_result.summary: Successful non-destructive acquisition, parameter regression, and validation of full-wafer 49-point thickness and refractive index maps for 800 nm PECVD TEOS IMD, confirming strict within-wafer uniformity (NU <= 2.5%) and stoichiometric integrity (n = 1.458-1.465) prior to CMP release.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Full-wafer mean TEOS thickness must match nominal target window
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated 49-point polar coordinate spectroscopic ellipsometry mean calculation excluding 3 mm edge boundary.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Within-wafer film thickness non-uniformity across 49 polar points
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calculated non-uniformity metric: ((Thickness_Max - Thickness_Min) / (2 * Thickness_Mean)) * 100.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Dielectric film refractive index at standard 632.8 nm wavelength
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Cauchy dispersion model regression at He-Ne reference wavelength across all 49 measurement points with MSE < 2.00.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: 49 of 49 coordinate sites successfully measured with optical regression fit MSE < 2.00, wafer non-uniformity confirmed <= 2.5%, mean thickness within 776.0-824.0 nm, and zero chuck scratch or particle defects added (delta defect count < 5 at >=0.18 um bin); formal digital signoff logged into MES by Metrology Module Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Resolution Surface Profilometry and Planarization Step-Height Metrology

### Scope & Process Hierarchy
- **Chip Architecture & Integration:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)
- **Foundry Tapeout & PDK:** 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation
- **Metallization & BEOL:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metal Interconnect Deposition (Metal 1, Metal 2, Passivation)
- **Metrology Level:** High-Resolution Surface Profilometry and Planarization Step-Height Metrology
- **Action Type:** Buy (Commercial Tool & Gauge Metrology Protocol)

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Wafer Loading and    │
│       Alignment        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Profilometer Optical  │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Baseline Metal-1    │
│    Step Height Scan    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Post-IMD PECVD     │
│  Topography Profiling  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Acceptance and     │
│      Step-Height       │
│     Quantification     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

#### Step 1: Tool Initialization and Reference Standard Calibration
1. Power up high-resolution stylus / optical surface profilometer metrology cluster.
2. Verify vibration isolation table active levitation and acoustic enclosure seal.
3. Perform vertical calibration check against a certified step-height calibration standard:
   - Target standard step height: $350.0\text{ nm} \pm 1.0\text{ nm}$.
   - Ensure vertical stylus resolution is calibrated within $\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$ sub-Angstrom baseline sensitivity.

#### Step 2: Automated Wafer Loading and Coordinate Alignment
1. Transfer the 180nm DRAM wafer post-Metal 1 deposition (Al-0.5% Cu or pure Al) and post-TEOS PECVD IMD pre-conditioning onto the vacuum chuck.
2. Perform pattern recognition alignment on wafer fiducials:
   - Align cell array to reference 180nm unit cell coordinates (channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, stacked capacitor over bitline / COB layout).
   - Register the dedicated test scribe-line step-height structures across an automated 9-point or 49-point wafer map.

#### Step 3: Pre-Planarization Metal-1 Step-Height Profiling
1. Position stylus / optical scan beam across isolated and dense Metal 1 interconnect lines.
2. Execute line profile scan across M1 trenches:
   - Scan length: $50\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ to $200\text{ }\mu\text{m}$.
   - Stylus tracking force: calibrated low-force contact ($\le 0.05\text{ mg}$ to prevent soft aluminum surface scratching).
3. Record raw step height: verify baseline M1 metal film target thickness of $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$ ($332.5\text{ nm}$ to $367.5\text{ nm}$).

#### Step 4: Post-IMD TEOS-PECVD Planarization Topography Metrology
1. Perform multi-point scans over the deposited Inter-Metal Dielectric (TEOS-PECVD oxide):
   - Measure residual topography step height ($\Delta h_{\text{IMD}}$) over dense stacked-capacitor array blocks and isolated periphery lines.
   - Run multi-angle optical reflectometry/ellipsometry at matched coordinates to decouple refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$ using Cauchy/Sellmeier models.
2. Evaluate radial film profile and across-wafer step-height non-uniformity across 9-point or 49-point maps.

#### Step 5: Data Export, Spec Verification, and Lot Release
1. Extract step height $h$, maximum peak-to-valley height ($R_t$), and surface roughness ($R_a$).
2. Validate measurements against acceptance limits; trigger automated disposition.
3. Unload wafer to cassette under laminar flow hood.

---

### 2. Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                    Step-Height & Interconnect Targets  
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │████████████████████████████████████│
    M1 Target (nm)┤████████████████████████████████████│
 M1 Thick Dev (nm)┤▒▒▒                                 │
                  │▒▒▒                                 │
Rs Limit (mOhm/sq)┤░░░░░░░░░                           │
                  │░░░░░░░░░                           │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0     87.5     175.0   262.5  350.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Acceptance Limit | Physical Units | Inspection Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Metal 1 Baseline Step Height** | `350` | `± 5% (± 17.5 nm)` | $\text{nm}$ | High-Resolution Stylus Profilometry |
| **Metrology Tool Precision** | `0.05` | `± 0.05` | $\text{nm}$ | Ellipsometry / Optical Profilometer Baseline |
| **Wafer Non-Uniformity Map Sampling** | `9-point / 49-point` | `100% completed` | `points/wafer` | Automated Wafer Mapping Routine |
| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | `< 0.08` | `< 0.080` ($< 80\text{ m}\Omega/\Box$) | $\Omega/\Box$ | 4-Point Probe Correlation ($N_2/H_2$ 95/5 at 400°C) |

---

### 3. Context & Source Citations
- **Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**
  - *Cited for:* Metal-1 target thickness ($350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$), deposition rate ($50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/minute}$), post-metal anneal sheet resistance constraint ($R_s < 0.08\text{ }\Omega/\Box$, forming gas $95/5\text{ }N_2/H_2$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$).
- **Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**
  - *Cited for:* Optical dispersion modeling (Cauchy and Sellmeier equations parameterizing $n(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$), sub-Angstrom precision limit ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$), and automated 9-point / 49-point wafer mapping methodology for radial non-uniformity tracking.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Cited for:* 180nm lithography feature sizes ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture, and minimum unit cell node topology.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-deposition IMD1 planarization step-height directly governs the lithographic depth-of-focus (DOF) budget for subsequent Via 1 and Metal 2 patterning in 180nm BEOL. If remaining topography over dense M1 lines exceeds 120 nm, severe optical reflection variations and resist necking will occur at the 248nm DUV / 365nm i-line exposure boundary.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Optical white-light interferometry (WLI) and contact stylus profilometry must be cross-calibrated on patterned IMD PECVD TEOS oxide. Stylus tip radii (2.0 um diamond) risk micro-scratching or plowing soft unannealed oxide films, whereas optical profilometry can suffer spurious phase shifts and apparent step-height artifacts from underlying metal line reflection and transparent SiO2 interference.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Diamond-tipped stylus cantilevers and certified silicon VLSI step-height calibration standards (e.g., 88 nm and 180 nm certified step pitch standards) require secondary supplier sourcing to mitigate lead-time spikes exceeding 16 weeks during fab line qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must support automated 9-site wafer mapping across a 200mm wafer in under 6 minutes per lot wafer to prevent queue-time bottlenecks between post-TEOS deposition/CMP and subsequent Via 1 lithography.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Phase-wrap optical artifact in coherence scanning interferometry over dual-interface IMD/metal boundaries leading to false 150nm topography errors
1. Stylus tip diamond chipping or wear introducing systematic 20nm baseline drift and undetected IMD oxide micro-gouging
1. Uncompensated wafer chuck bow causing macro-scale tilt distortion in planarization across-wafer uniformity (WIWNU) calculations

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-3-01` | **IMD1 Planarization Step-Height and Topography Profile Measurement via Stylus Profilometry** | Automated High-Resolution Contact Stylus Profilometer (KLA Tencor P-17 or equivalent) equipped with a 2.0 um diamond stylus, 0.5 mg tracking force, and certified 180.0 nm VLSI step standard | 1. Load calibration wafer and measure the 180.0 nm step standard over a 500 um scan length at 50 um/s to verify vertical calibration within ±1.0 nm. 2. Vacuum clamp the production wafer onto the precision motorized stage. 3. Perform automated coordinate alignment using optical pattern recognition on M1 test kerf structures. 4. Execute 9-site surface profile line scans (center, 4 mid-radius, 4 edge at 3mm edge exclusion) across dense M1 line-space arrays (pitch 400 nm, 1:1 duty cycle) over a 1200 um scan length with 0.1 um spatial sampling. 5. Apply 5th-order polynomial leveling algorithm to subtract wafer macro-curvature. 6. Extract average step-height (Rz) and maximum peak-to-valley topography height (Rt). | `Across all 9 sites, post-deposition planarized residual step-height over dense M1 topography must be <= 65.0 nm, with 1-sigma across-wafer step-height non-uniformity <= 6.0 nm, and zero detectable tip gouge scratches under 100x optical review.` |
| `TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-3-02` | **Full-Field Non-Contact Coherence Scanning Interferometry (CSI) Surface Roughness and Planarization Index** | Coherence Scanning White-Light Interferometer (Zygo NewView 9000 or Bruker ContourGT) with 20x Mirau objective (0.4 NA), 530nm LED filtered illumination, and calibrated piezo Z-scanner | 1. Place wafer on vacuum chuck and perform automated optical auto-focus and tilt fringe nulling (< 1 fringe across field of view). 2. Acquire 3D surface topography map over 640 um x 480 um area at 9 standard die locations across the wafer. 3. Apply model-based film stack compensation algorithm to decouple top IMD surface reflection from subsurface M1 metal boundary reflections. 4. Compute areal surface roughness parameters Sa, Sq, and the Planarization Degree (PD = 1 - [Residual Step Height / As-Deposited Step Height]). 5. Export 3D topological height matrix and high-resolution TIFF topography map. | `Areal surface roughness Sa must be <= 1.8 nm over open IMD oxide field, and Planarization Degree (PD) across isolated-to-dense transition structures must be >= 78.0% across all 9 measured dies.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 / ISO Class 5 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and laser safety impact glasses, Static-dissipative ESD cleanroom gown, hood, and conductive ESD cleanroom booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with IPA, flush skin immediately with cold DI water for 15 minutes and remove contaminated garments. In case of eye contact, flush eyes at an eyewash station for 15 minutes lifting eyelids. For pinch-point mechanical injury from motorized stage, hit emergency machine stop (E-STOP) and assess mechanical trauma.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Tool operates in ISO Class 4 laminar flow enclosure with HEPA filtration (0.1 um particle capture > 99.999%). Exhaust port connected to cleanroom general VOC solvent exhaust at face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) to vent IPA wiping vapors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free cleanroom wipes must be segregated into sealed, grounded, flame-retardant stainless steel hazardous solvent waste receptacles for certified external hazardous solvent incineration. No direct drain disposal permitted.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) cleanroom wiping solvent** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Tier C / Ultra-Pure VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2) for surface blow-off** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 6.0 (99.9999% purity, dewpoint < -85°C) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited and planarized IMD1 TEOS oxide; moisture-free, unpatterned surface with hydrophobic-to-neutral native finish and zero particulate defect additions (> 0.2 um count < 10 per wafer).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized, non-scratched, step-height certified IMD1 dielectric surface; moisture-free and stored in clean purge FOUP/cassette ready for Via 1 lithography coating.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive queue time in ambient air causes surface silanol (Si-OH) group hydration and moisture absorption into porous PECVD TEOS oxide, resulting in dielectric film swelling, apparent step-height drift, resist adhesion loss, and severe outgassing/via-poisoning during subsequent via etch.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Quantitative baseline verification of IMD1 post-deposition planarization step-height across 200mm wafers, ensuring residual topography conforms to the 180nm DUV lithographic depth-of-focus window prior to Via 1 patterning.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `IMD1_PLANARIZATION_9PT_STEP_HEIGHT_REPORT.csv`
- [ ] `IMD1_SURFACE_TOPOGRAPHY_3D_CSI_MAPS.tiff`
- [ ] `IMD1_METROLOGY_QUALIFICATION_CERTIFICATE.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum residual IMD1 step-height across dense M1 line arrays** | `55.0 nm` | +10.0 nm / -15.0 nm | Contact stylus profilometry 9-point wafer mapping according to TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-3-01 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Across-wafer residual step-height non-uniformity (1-sigma)** | `4.5 nm` | <= 6.0 nm max | Statistical standard deviation calculation across 9 wafer sites from profilometer dataset |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Areal surface micro-roughness (Sa) over planarized oxide field** | `1.20 nm` | <= 1.80 nm max | White-light coherence scanning interferometry 20x Mirau field according to TC-BEOL-METAL-STACK-2-1-3-3-02 |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer lot step-height average <= 65.0 nm across all 9 inspection sites with 1-sigma non-uniformity <= 6.0 nm, zero mechanical gouge marks verified by post-metrology optical scan, and formal digital sign-off from both BEOL Metrology Engineer and Integration Lead within the Fab MES.
