When running a dynamic checkerboard pattern (alternating physical '1's and '0's), adjacent victim bitlines experience worst-case differential noise injection during sense amplifier activation. If the sense amp strobe timing (t_RSD) is under-margined, capacitive coupling kicks the floating bitline below the sensing threshold (V_sig < 150 mV), leading to false sensing and catastrophic array-wide bit failure.
critics.domain_expert: Physical-to-logical address scrambling must be precisely mapped before executing checkerboard tests. In folded bitline arrays, true physical adjacent cells do not always correspond to contiguous logical memory space. Furthermore, bitline-to-wordline fringe coupling during rapid precharge cycles can induce subthreshold leakage through unselected 1T1C access NMOS transistors (V_th ~ 0.45V). The test suite must decouple sense-amplifier latch imbalance from true dielectric leakage of the storage node (C_s = 28 fF) across varying supply voltages (V_DD = 1.8V +/- 10%).
critics.supply_chain: Executing comprehensive checkerboard coupling patterns at wafer sort introduces non-negligible automated test equipment (ATE) index time. Automated probe card cantilever or vertical MEMS pin wear scales with extended multi-vector dwell times, risking probe tip oxidation and elevated contact resistance (> 1.5 Ohm). Contact resistance degrades V_DD array power integrity during high-current simultaneous sense-amplifier strobing, requiring strict budgeting of touchdown counts and alignment maintenance.
critics.laya_pm: Test floor throughput and wafer sort cycle time are tightly constrained. While 100% vector-coverage checkerboard stress is vital for parametric screening, running extensive algorithmic pattern permutations without early failure abort logic will blow out the ATE test time allocation beyond the 45-second per-die budget. Test sequencing must prioritize rapid screen-out of catastrophic coupling failures before proceeding to fine-grain retention/voltage-shmoo sweeps.
critical_failure_modes: Adjacent Bitline Cross-Talk Induced Inversion: Worst-case C_bl-bl differential coupling swings adjacent victim BL/BL_bar pairs during sensing, corrupting low-margin logic '0' or '1' levels.

Sense Amplifier Power Droop & Strobe Jitter: Simultaneous switching noise (SSN) on array virtual V_DD/V_SS rails during array-wide checkerboard sensing collapses V_sig below the minimum 100 mV sense window.

Bitline-to-Substrate Junction Degradation: Elevated test temperatures (85C) combined with high-frequency bitline precharge-discharge stress induce localized hot-carrier injection or junction leakage at access transistor source/drain diffusions.

testcases.title: Static Physical Checkerboard Bitline Coupling Noise Margin & Sense Margin Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Advantest T5833 Wafer ATE with 50-Ohm matched high-density probe card, Keysight B1500A Parametric Analyzer for sub-pA leakage verification, Temptronic thermal chuck (set to 85C +/- 0.5C).
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer aligned on ATE chuck; probe contact resistance confirmed <= 0.8 Ohm per pin; array V_DD set to 1.80 V; internal V_PP set to 3.30 V; V_BLP calibrated to V_DD/2 (0.90 V +/- 10 mV); open/short parametric pre-screen passed.
testcases.procedure: 1. Write topological physical checkerboard pattern (Pattern A: alternating physical 1s and 0s: BL_even='1', BL_odd='0') into the 1Mb target subarray at 85C. 2. Hold array for t_pause = 100 ms with bitlines precharged to V_BLP. 3. Read back subarray at nominal clock frequency (50 MHz) and record bit error map (fail count N_err1). 4. Invert pattern to inverse checkerboard (Pattern B: BL_even='0', BL_odd='1') and write into subarray. 5. Hold array for t_pause = 100 ms. 6. Read back subarray and record bit error map (fail count N_err2). 7. Re-execute steps with V_DD shmoo from 1.62 V to 1.98 V in 20 mV increments.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total bit failure count (N_err1 + N_err2) must be strictly 0 bits across all nominal cells at 1.80 V. Across V_DD shmoo (1.62 V to 1.98 V), sensed signal margin Delta-V_BL must remain >= 120 mV with zero adjacent coupling bit-flips.

testcases.title: Dynamic Disturbed Checkerboard Cross-Talk & Adjacent Wordline Toggle Stress Test
testcases.instrumentation: Teradyne UltraFLEX-plus SoC/Memory Test System with specialized DRAM algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG), low-noise multi-channel oscilloscope for bitline transient observation, thermal chuck set to 25C and 85C.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer loaded; ambient temperature stabilized; array V_DD = 1.80 V; bitlines balanced; memory address descrambling table loaded and physically verified against GDSII array orientation.
testcases.procedure: 1. Write background physical checkerboard pattern across entire array macro. 2. Define Victim Row (WL_n) containing alternate '1'/'0' cells. 3. Apply active wordline disturb stress by toggling Aggressor Rows (WL_n-1, WL_n+1) at 10 MHz for N = 100,000 cycles while holding BLs at static read state to maximize C_bl-wl and C_bl-bl coupling stress. 4. Assert sense amplifier strobe on Victim Row WL_n at marginal strobe delay (t_RSD adjusted from nominal 3.5 ns down to 2.2 ns in 100 ps steps). 5. Read out data and log dynamic cross-talk fail addresses as a function of t_RSD.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Zero functional bit failures on Victim Row WL_n under 100,000 disturb toggles at nominal t_RSD (3.5 ns). Bitline cross-talk induced sensing delay degradation must not exceed Delta-t_RSD <= 400 ps at V_DD = 1.62 V (worst-case corner).

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Thermal Chuck Conditioning & Wafer Loading**:
   - Heat automated prober thermal chuck to $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ and stabilize within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ using multi-zone RTD control.
   - Load wafer with vacuum $\ge 70\text{ kPa}$; set probe card overdrive to $35\,\mu\text{m} - 50\,\mu\text{m}$ to maintain contact resistance $R_{\text{cont}} < 1\,\Omega/\text{pad}$.
2. **Array Initialization & Pattern Write**:
   - Bias rails: $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{\text{BLP}} = 0.9\text{ V}$, $V_{\text{PP}} = 3.0\text{ V} - 3.3\text{ V}$, and $V_{\text{BB}} = -0.5\text{ V} - -0.8\text{ V}$.
   - Write full-chip test vectors: Solid '1's, Solid '0's, and Checkerboard ($0101..1010...$) to stress worst-case lateral electric fields across $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$ pitch wordlines and bitlines.
3. **Wordline Inactive Pause Interval**:
   - Inhibit all ATE and on-chip Auto-Refresh (`CBR`) and Self-Refresh clocks.
   - Hold wordlines inactive ($0\text{ V}$ to $-0.3\text{ V}$) for a calibrated pause interval $t_{\text{pause}} = 64.0\text{ ms}$ at $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ (with characterization steps up to $1024\text{ ms}$).
4. **Fast Synchronous Readout & Sense Amp Latching**:
   - Execute synchronous burst read at $100\text{ MHz} - 133\text{ MHz}$ immediately upon pause expiration.
   - Bitlines equalize to $V_{\text{BLP}} = 0.9\text{ V}$; strobe sense amplifiers to latch differential signal $\Delta V_{\text{BL}} = \frac{C_s}{C_s + C_b}(V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{BLP}})$.
5. **Fail-Bit Mapping, Descrambling & Tail Profiling**:
   - Capture bit-level flip errors in ATE error memory.
   - Run logical-to-physical address descrambler to reconstruct physical failure coordinates on the folded-bitline $8F^2$ array, binning random tail leakage vs. wordline/bitline structural defects.

### Literature Context Citations
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB), $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, ONO/$\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$/$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dielectric ($\kappa > 15$), $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$, and junction/sub-threshold leakage ceiling $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: 1T1C $8F^2/6F^2$ cell layout, $C_s \in [25, 30]\text{ fF}$ ensuring retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, EOT $3 - 4\text{ nm}$, wordline/bitline pitch $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$, gate oxide $3.5\text{ nm}$.
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**: $8F^2$ folded bitline footprint ($0.259\,\mu\text{m}^2$), $C_b = 150\text{ to } 250\text{ fF}$, and strict $C_b / C_s \in [5:1, 9:1]$ limit.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal chuck stabilization at 85°C to 125°C induces thermal expansion differentials between the alumina/tungsten probe card needle block, pogo interface, and silicon wafer, generating lateral scrub drift exceeding ±3.5 µm over extended 500 ms pause cycles; closed-loop thermal compensation and periodic re-alignment tracking are mandatory to prevent pad punch-through or contact resistance spikes (>1.5 Ohm).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Elevated-temperature retention sort exposes trap-assisted leakage (TAT) across 180nm planar transfer gate junctions, band-to-band tunneling (BTBT), and subthreshold channel leakage. Tail-bit distributions (variable retention time / VRT phenomena) cannot be screened using a single static pause interval; multi-pause stepped bitmaps (10 ms, 64 ms, 256 ms, and 1024 ms at 85°C) are necessary to resolve intrinsic Gaussian retention limits versus random telegraph noise (RTN) defect clusters.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-temperature cantilever/vertical probe cards rated for 125°C continuous soak with low thermal drift have lead times exceeding 14-18 weeks; lack of high-purity IPA and specialized probe-tip abrasive cleaning pads will cause rapid probe tip oxidation and false bit-failure escalations during long-duration sort runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal soaking of 200mm wafers adds 12 minutes of thermal ramp/settle overhead per wafer plus 8 minutes per stepped retention pause bitmap test, capping tester throughput at less than 1.8 wafers per hour on standard ATE platforms; requires batch pause testing or multi-DUT parallel probing to keep MPW sort budgets within schedule.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal expansion-induced probe needle scrub walk-off resulting in bond pad passivation edge chipping and open-circuit contact faults during pause cycle soaking.
1. Variable Retention Time (VRT) tail-bit instability where metastable silicon-substrate interface trap switching causes intermittent pass/fail screening errors across test passes.
1. Local thermal chuck gradients (>1.5°C across 200mm chuck) creating false radial retention fail signatures correlated with chuck heating element geometry rather than silicon leakage.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protective Kevlar gloves (rated to 200°C) for chuck and probe handling, ESD-safe cleanroom nitrile gloves (Class 100 compliant, double-gloved), Cleanroom safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1 certified), Flame-resistant cleanroom smock and conductive ESD heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn exposure: Immediately flood affected skin with cold, running deionized water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply salves or ointments; seek cleanroom emergency medical assistance immediately. Eye contact with IPA solvent splash: Flush eyes at eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Nitrogen asphyxiation: Relocate victim to fresh outdoor air immediately, administer oxygen if breathing is labored, initiate CPR if pulse absent.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous prober enclosure mini-environment exhaust operating at >=45 CFM to remove thermal dissipation and trace IPA solvent vapors during probe tip cleaning; ambient oxygen sensor interlock installed in test cell monitoring >=19.5% O2 levels for N2 chuck purge systems.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA wipes and probe abrasive cleaning pads collected in dedicated, grounded, airtight flammable solvent disposal cans; no aqueous drains permitted for chemical disposal; hazardous waste manifest routing to certified thermal incinerator facility.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, passivation-opened Al-0.5%Cu top bond pads free of organic residue, native oxide layer thickness <=3.5 nm, stored under vacuum sealed wafer cassette.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested wafer with micro-probe scrub marks <=25% of pad area, probe scrub depth <=0.6 µm (no barrier layer puncture), pad surface free of thermal oxidation discoloration or foreign particulate.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption and atmospheric native oxidation of exposed Al-Cu pads under cleanroom humidity (>45% RH) causing probe contact resistance jumps (>5 Ohm), resulting in false marginal retention fails and probe card pin fouling.

2. Inhibit auto-refresh commands and hold array in quiescent retention state for calibrated pause intervals: 10 ms, 32 ms, 64 ms, 128 ms, 256 ms, and 512 ms.

4. Invert pattern to solid '0' and repeat pause cycle steps 1 through 3.
5. Compute cumulative failure bit count as a function of pause time to construct wafer retention cumulative distribution function (CDF) Weibull plots.

testcases.title: Pause-Refresh Topological Failure Bitmap Metrology (March C- Under Thermal Stress)
testcases.instrumentation: Memory ATE with Real-Time Failure Analysis (RTFA) Bitmap Software Engine, high-speed multichannel digital comparator, Agilent 4156C Precision Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer (quiescent leak check).
testcases.pre_conditions: Thermal chuck set to 105.0°C ±0.3°C; probe alignment verified via optical auto-alignment microscope showing probe marks centered on Al-Cu top pads within 15 µm margin; VDD set to low-voltage margin condition (1.62V).

1. Execute modified March C- pattern: Up-address (W0); Up-address (R0, W1); Up-address (R1, W0); Down-address (R0, W1); Down-address (R1, W0); Down-address (R0).
2. Insert a programmable 100 ms pause state prior to the final Down-address (R0) read pass while maintaining wordlines deselected and bitlines precharged to VBLP (0.90V).
3. Map every failing X-Y physical topological coordinate and classify signatures: isolated single-bit fails, adjacent bitline pair fails, full wordline open/short leaks, and transfer gate junction leakage blocks.
4. Correlate coordinate fail clusters with ellipsometric gate-oxide and capacitor dielectric thickness maps.

ESD-safe cleanroom nitrile gloves (Class 100 compliant, double-gloved)

# Standard Operating Procedure: High-Density Wafer Fail-Bitmapping & Defect Clustering Metrology Analysis

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Fail-bitmap address unscrambling from logical column/row to physical topological X/Y coordinates must be validated against the exact 180nm open-source DRAM cell layout topology (folded bitline architecture, twisted bitline pairs, and interleaved sense amplifier banks). Any latency mismatch or probe card skew exceeding 150 ps at the ATE digital pin electronics will corrupt high-density burst write/read cycles, injecting false bitmap signatures and misidentifying systemic array defects as random cell retention failures.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Defect clustering metrology must clearly decouple lithographic line-end shortening/bridging (single-bit or double-bit column pairs) from BEOL metal bridging (M1 bitline or M2 wordline strap leakage) and deep capacitor dielectric pinholes. Spatial point process algorithms (such as hierarchical DBSCAN or nearest-neighbor cluster indices) must run on raw fail-bit coordinates with spatial resolution down to the individual 180nm 6F2/8F2 unit cell, verifying whether clusters correlate with radial CMP dishing signatures or periphery sense amplifier threshold voltage (Vth) offsets.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom multi-site high-pin-count vertical probe cards (cantilever or Cobra-style fine-pitch probe heads rated for 180nm bond pads) suffer long lead times (16-20 weeks) and contact resistance (Cres) degradation after 50,000 touchdowns. Sourcing replacement probe needles and securing continuous availability of ultra-flat ceramic probe interfaces is critical to prevent testing downtime during multi-project wafer (MPW) qualification runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: High-density full-wafer bitmap vector collection across all 200mm wafer dies generates gigabytes of raw raster data per wafer, risking serious test cell throughput bottlenecks if bitmap streaming isn't compressed in real-time on the tester workstation. The engineering team must balance full-array topological bitmap logging against aggressive ATE run-time targets (<180 seconds per die) to prevent sort lot queue-time breaches.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Physical-to-logical address scramble inversion in test vector software resulting in incorrect spatial clustering assignment and false identification of row/column repair redundancy allocation targets.
1. Probe needle scrub wear, Cres escalation (>1.5 Ohms), and aluminum bond pad pitting/oxidation leading to pseudo-open bitline/wordline signatures during high-speed vector functional probing.
1. Excessive wafer chuck thermal drift during extended sort cycles causing probe misregistration and mechanical shorting across neighboring I/O pads.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-PACKAGING-ROOT-2-2-3-01` | **High-Density DRAM Array Topological Bitmap Vector Verification & Address Unscramble Accuracy** | Automated DRAM Memory Test System (Advantest T5588ES or Teradyne UltraFLEX), 200mm Semi-Automatic Wafer Prober with thermal chuck (Cascade Microtech / FormFactor Summit 12000), Vertical Probe Card with tungsten-rhenium needles | 1. Execute parametric continuity and contact resistance verification on all VDD, VSS, address, and data pins. 2. Apply nominal power rails (VDD = 1.8V, VPP = 3.3V, VBB = -0.8V) and run March C- vector pattern at 100 MHz clock rate across full 180nm cell array array matrices. 3. Stream raw cycle-by-cycle pass/fail pin response data directly to tester real-time bitmap processor buffer. 4. Apply mathematical coordinate unscrambling transform to translate multiplexed logical address sequences (RA0-RA11, CA0-CA9) to physical array matrix X/Y topological bit coordinates. 5. Compare unscrambled fail coordinates against intentionally programmed hardware laser-fuse dummy blown address locations. | `Address unscrambling accuracy must achieve exactly 100.0% match against known hardware address calibration signatures; zero false bitline-pair inversions; bit error location repeatability CV < 0.5% across 5 consecutive wafer re-probe touchdowns.` |
| `TC-BEOL-PACKAGING-ROOT-2-2-3-02` | **Spatial Defect Clustering Algorithm & Redundancy Allocation Yield Metrology** | Metrology Offline Analysis Workstation running Klarity Defect / YieldExplorer EDA Metrology Software, SEMVision Defect Review G3/G4 Inline SEM | 1. Import raw bitmap failure point coordinates (X, Y) for all dies across the 200mm wafer. 2. Run spatial clustering algorithm (DBSCAN with min_pts = 4, epsilon = 2.5 µm) to segment defects into single-bit fails, bitline pairs, wordline opens/shorts, sense-amp block failures, and macro-area particulate clusters. 3. Calculate cluster defect density (D0) using Murphy/Seeds yield model and evaluate redundancy repairability index based on available spare row/column count (16 redundant rows, 16 redundant columns per 1Mb block). 4. Export high-density cluster coordinates to Inline Review SEM coordinate translation file. 5. Execute automated SEM navigation and imaging on top 20 representative defect cluster centroids across edge and center dies. | `Cluster classification algorithm must achieve > 98.0% defect signature categorization accuracy confirmed by review SEM; automated redundancy allocation solver must successfully generate valid repair fuse-blowing maps for all repairable dies with calculated repair efficiency >= 95.0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (double gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and conductive ESD cleanroom booties, ESD wrist strap connected to certified grounding terminal during probe maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Remove contaminated gloves immediately, wash exposed skin thoroughly with soap and copious clean water for 15 minutes. Eye contact: Flush eyes at cleanroom emergency eyewash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if dizziness or respiratory irritation persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober load port and offline probe tip chemical wash stations must be connected to dedicated solvent exhaust with face velocity maintained between 0.45 to 0.60 m/s (90-120 fpm); test floor ambient HVAC Class 1000/ISO 6 laminar flow.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA swabs, cleaning sheets, and solvent residue must be collected in dedicated airtight, grounded solvent waste containers (labeled hazardous organic solvent waste) and transferred to chemical storage for certified industrial incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (electronic grade for probe card tip cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (for rinse pads)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly singulated/sorted wafer surface post-BEOL passivation etch and pad anneal; aluminum bond pads clean, native oxide < 2.5 nm, free of organic residues, moisture, or particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probed wafer with controlled probe scrub marks (scrub mark area <= 20% of bond pad metallization area, scrub depth < 0.35 µm); probe-tested surface free of carbonized needle debris or metallic micro-shavings.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits causes native Al2O3 growth on open bond pads (> 6.0 nm), driving up probe contact resistance (Cres > 3.0 Ohms), false electrical fail signatures during sort, and catastrophic non-stick pad failures during subsequent wire bonding or wafer bumping.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete full-wafer functional fail-bitmap generation, spatial defect clustering analysis, and laser redundancy allocation mapping for the 180nm open-source DRAM 200mm wafer lot, demonstrating 100% address unscramble integrity, quantitative spatial defect classification, and automated laser repair fuse file generation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM_180nm_Wafer_Topological_Fail_Bitmap_Lot01.tiff`
- [ ] `Defect_Spatial_Clustering_and_D0_Yield_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Wafer_Sort_Redundancy_Allocation_Fuse_Map.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Probe card contact resistance (Cres) per pin across full-wafer sort testing touchdowns** | `0.65` | ±0.25 Ohm (must remain < 1.0 Ohm) | Automated Kelvin 4-wire parametric continuity measurement prior to array vector test |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Physical-to-logical fail-bit address unscramble spatial coordinate registration fidelity** | `100.0` | 0.0% (zero tolerance for inverted bitline/wordline coordinates) | Deterministic test vector correlation against dedicated physical test structures and blown fuse addresses |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Spatial defect cluster classification accuracy across bitline, wordline, and macro clusters** | `98.5` | ±1.5% | Automated metrology defect clustering review validated by SEM review of 50 sampled cluster centroids |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full 200mm wafer fail-bitmap dataset generated without memory buffer overflow; topological unscrambler verified with zero coordinate inversion errors; repair allocation algorithm generates viable laser fuse maps for all repairable dies yielding >= 95% post-repair array recovery; signoff approval recorded by Metrology Lead, Test Systems Engineer, and Foundry Product Engineering.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Tester Bitmapping Algorithm & Address Scramble Translation Setup

**Context Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (`DRAM Foundation VN`) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Wafer Electrical Sort, Parametric Test & Die Singulation > Full-Wafer Functional DRAM Cell Array Sort & Bitmap Probing > High-Density Wafer Fail-Bitmapping & Defect Clustering Metrology Analysis > Automated Tester Bitmapping Algorithm & Address Scramble Translation Setup  
**Generation**: Gen 3 (180 nm) | **Action Type**: Make

---

### 1. Process & Topology Flowchart

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  ATE Logical Address   │
│          X/Y           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Bitline/Wordline    │
│  Scramble Translation  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Physical Silicon    │
│    X_phys / Y_phys     │
│        Mapping         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Tester Real-Time    │
│  Fail Memory Capture   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Defect Cluster &    │
│   Physical Topology    │
│        Analyzer        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Logical-to-Physical Address Scramble Matrix Configuration**:
   - Extract the decoder address topological transformations from GDSII layout routing files for the folded bitline ($8F^2$, cell area $= 0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$, $F = 180\text{ nm}$, access transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}, W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Load the bitline transposition table into the Automated Test Equipment (ATE) algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG) to un-scramble complementary bitline pairs ($BL / \overline{BL}$) and staggered wordline layout tracks into contiguous physical coordinates $(X_{\text{phys}}, Y_{\text{phys}})$.

2. **Array Block Segmentation & Bitline Architecture Mapping**:
   - Define sub-array boundary partitions based on the bitline block architecture consisting of 256 or 512 cells per bitline with shared bitline contacts.
   - Configure the ATE real-time bit fail memory (BFM) depth and stride matching the physical bitline parasitic capacitance span ($C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$) against the stacked capacitor storage node ($C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$, nominal $28\text{ fF}$).

3. **Parametric Calibration & Bias Condition Setup**:
   - Verify array peripheral drivers against discrete MOSFET parametric baselines: linear threshold voltage $V_{\text{thn}} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$ (measured at $V_{\text{DS}} = 50\text{ mV}$), $V_{\text{thp}} = -0.60\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, and $I_{\text{off}} \le 10\text{ pA}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\text{ V}, V_{\text{GS}} = 0\text{ V}$.
   - Ensure the cell refresh retention timer aligns with the storage node sub-threshold/junction leakage threshold ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

4. **Algorithmic Test Execution & Real-Time Bitmapping**:
   - Execute Marching, Checkerboard, and Row/Column disturb pattern vectors through the ALPG at nominal $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
   - Capture pass/fail bit arrays into the BFM buffer, mapping each failing bit through the address scramble translation engine directly to silicon physical coordinates.
   - Correlate fail signatures into physical defect clusters: single-cell fails ($C_s$ defect or leakage), paired-bit fails (shared contact short), single-wordline fails (WL open/bridging), and single-bitline fails (BL open/short).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
 Baseline Physical Verification Metrics (180nm DRAM Sort)
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │░░░░░░░░░░░░                     │
I_off Leakage (pA/um)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░                     │
                     │▒▒                               │
       NMOS V_thn (V)┤▒▒                               │
 Capacitance C_s (fF)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                     │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
      C_b / C_s Ratio┤█████████                        │
                     │█████████                        │
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                      0       7      14      21      28 
```

1. **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)**: $\ge 25\text{ fF}$ per cell (Nominal Target: $28\text{ fF}$; allowable range: $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$).
2. **Bitline-to-Storage Node Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)**: Maintained between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (Must not exceed $10:1$, where $C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$ for 256/512 cells/BL).
3. **Discrete Access/Peripheral Transistor Threshold Voltage ($V_{\text{th}}$)**:
   - NMOS: $V_{\text{thn}} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$ (at $V_{\text{DS}} = 50\text{ mV}$).
   - PMOS: $V_{\text{thp}} = -0.60\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$ (at $V_{\text{DS}} = 50\text{ mV}$).
4. **Leakage & Drive Current Metrics**:
   - Access node sub-threshold/junction leakage: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Transistor $I_{\text{off}} \le 10\text{ pA}/\mu\text{m}$ (at $V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\text{ V}, V_{\text{GS}} = 0\text{ V}$), with $I_{\text{on}} \ge 500\ \mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ ($I_{\text{on}}/I_{\text{off}} > 10^7$).

---

### 4. Sources Cited

- **Source: 1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**: 
  - $8F^2$ folded bitline footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$), 256 or 512 cells per bitline block, $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF} - 30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$), $C_b = 150\text{ fF} - 250\text{ fF}$, and capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s \in [5:1, 9:1]$ ($< 10:1$).
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: 
  - Access transistor channel dimensions $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, shared bitline contact, stacked capacitor topology with ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5/\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dielectric, $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$, and leakage current $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification**: 
  - Physical reference devices: $V_{\text{thn}} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, $V_{\text{thp}} = -0.60\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, $I_{\text{on}} \ge 500\ \mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $I_{\text{off}} \le 10\text{ pA}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{\text{GS}} = 0\text{ V}$, and $I_{\text{on}}/I_{\text{off}} > 10^7$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-PACKAGING-ROOT-2-2-3-1-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-BEOL-PACKAGING-ROOT-2-2-3-1-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Automated Tester Bitmapping Algorithm & Address Scramble Translation Setup: BEOL metallization, electrical die sort (EDS), wafer backgrinding/dicing, and wirebond plastic encapsulation successfully yield JEDEC-qualified DRAM packaged units.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Electrical_Die_Sort_Wafer_Yield_Map.csv`
- [ ] `Wirebond_Ball_Shear_And_Pull_CPK_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_TSOP54_Final_ATE_SpeedBin_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-01` | **Wirebond ball shear strength** | `>= 18.0 gf` | Minimum failure load >= 15.0 gf across 30 samples | Dage 4000 micro-tester lateral ball shear per MIL-STD-883 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) wafer array functional yield** | `>= 90.0%` | Minimum yield >= 85.0% on prime wafers | Automated wafer probe array test with March C- diagnostic patterns |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Packaged DRAM package coplanarity & lead pitch** | `<= 0.08 mm coplanarity` | JEDEC TSOP-54 mechanical envelope tolerance (+/- 0.05 mm) | Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% passing electrical continuity and JEDEC parametric DC checks; destructive wirebond shear CPK >= 1.67 with zero package voiding or delamination detected under scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Full-Wafer High-Density Electrical Fail-Bit Array Probing Execution

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180-EBI-001`  
**Node / Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip, 1T1C Stacked Capacitor Over Bitline)  
**Classification:** Metrology & Electrical Wafer Sort (EWS) Leaf SOP  
**Knowledge Record:** [full_wafer_electrical_fail_bit_probing.md](./docs/knowledge/full_wafer_electrical_fail_bit_probing.md)

---

### 1. Process Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Step 1: Automated   │
│   Chuck Loading and   │
│       Alignment       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 2: Probe Card   │
│      Contact and      │
│     Overdrive Set     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 3: Baseline DC  │
│    Parametric and     │
│      Continuity       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 4: Functional   │
│  Array Marching Test  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Step 5: Retention   │
│   Time and Leakage    │
│      Stress Sort      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Step 6: Defect     │
│      Cluster and      │
│  Fail-Bitmap Export   │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Automated Wafer Chuck Loading & Thermal Stabilization**
   - Load the 180nm production/MPW wafer onto the prober vacuum chuck.
   - For ambient baseline runs, regulate temperature at $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$. For elevated leakage sort screening, ramp chuck thermal setpoint to $85^\circ\text{C} \pm 1.0^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Perform optical pattern recognition alignment on primary wafer notch/flat and global fiducial alignment marks.

2. **Probe Card Touchdown & Contact Calibration**
   - Align multi-die high-density probe card tips to the peripheral bond pads and array test pads matching the $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$ pitch interconnect layout.
   - Execute controlled z-axis touchdown with calibrated overdrive (typically $35\text{ µm}$ to $50\text{ µm}$) ensuring low contact resistance across all power, ground, and I/O channels without punch-through damage to BEOL metallization.

3. **Baseline DC Parametric & Continuity Verification**
   - Execute open/short continuity checks across all bitline/wordline test structures and power rails ($V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{SS} = 0\text{ V}$).
   - Probe on-wafer parametric drop-in test transistors ($W/L = 2.0\text{ µm} / 0.18\text{ µm}$):
     - Extract linear threshold voltage $V_{thn}$ at $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$ via maximum transconductance ($g_m$) extrapolation.
     - Measure on-state current $I_{on}$ at $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
     - Measure off-state leakage current $I_{off}$ at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$, $V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$.

4. **Full-Array Functional Marching Pattern Probing**
   - Apply algorithmic test patterns (March C-, Checkerboard, Row-Hammer stress) across all $8F^2 / 6F^2$ DRAM cell blocks via high-speed digital ATE channels.
   - Sequence write and read cycles at operational rail $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$ to capture stuck-at faults, transition faults, and adjacent bitline coupling bridges.

5. **Elevated Retention Time & Sub-Threshold Leakage Stress Screening**
   - Set chuck temperature to $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Write solid pattern data (`All-1` and `All-0`) into array storage cells ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ access transistors).
   - Inhibit refresh commands for a pause duration of $t_{pause} = 64\text{ ms}$.
   - Read back array contents to identify retention fails driven by cell junction leakage or capacitor dielectric loss.

6. **Defect Clustering & Fail-Bitmap Reconstruction**
   - Stream vector fail data to the yield analysis workstation.
   - Classify fail bits into topological defect classes: Single Bit Fail, Paired Bit Fail (adjacent cells sharing bitline contacts), Wordline Open/Short, and Bitline Leakage Cross-point.
   - Overlay X-Y coordinate bitmaps with BEOL metallization inspection layers to flag systematic lithography or particle anomalies.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │████                                  │
  Vthn (x100 mV)┤████                                  │
                │▓▓▓▓▓                                 │
Ion/Ioff (log10)┤▓▓▓▓▓                                 │
  Ret. Time (ms)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
                │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Capacitance (fF)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                     │
                │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                     │
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0       16        32       48       64 
```

1. **Storage Cell Capacitance ($C_{cell}$):**  
   $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$ (Nominal operational budget: $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF/cell}$).
2. **Data Retention Time ($t_{ret}$):**  
   $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ chuck temperature.
3. **Cell Leakage Current ($I_{leak}$):**  
   $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ sub-threshold and junction leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
4. **Access Transistor Current Ratio ($I_{on}/I_{off}$) & Threshold Voltage ($V_{thn}$):**  
   - $I_{on}/I_{off} > 10^7$ (with $I_{on} \ge 500\text{ µA/µm}$ at $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA/µm}$ at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$, $V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$).  
   - $V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$ (for $W/L = 2.0\text{ µm} / 0.18\text{ µm}$).

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source 1: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Unit cell geometry: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, $8F^2 / 6F^2$ folded bitline layout with stacked capacitor over bitline (COB).
  - Storage capacitor target: Minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ budget; dielectric stack $\kappa > 15$.
  - Leakage requirement: Sub-threshold and junction leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source 2: Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification**
  - Target sub-micron transistor geometry: $W / L = 2.0\text{ µm} / 0.18\text{ µm}$ ($180\text{ nm}$).
  - NMOS linear threshold voltage: $V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$ at $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$.
  - Current targets at $V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$: $I_{on} \ge 500\text{ µA/µm}$, $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA/µm}$, $I_{on}/I_{off} > 10^7$.
- **Source 3: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - Minimum storage capacitance: $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF/cell}$.
  - Retention limit: $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Array pitch geometry: Bitline and wordline pitch around $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: High-density functional fail-bit array probing requires seamless integration between the automated prober (e.g., TEL Precio or FormFactor Cascade), high-speed memory ATE channels, and the wafer map coordinate translation pipeline. The primary architectural risk is mechanical tip scrub misalignment degrading pad pitch tolerances (180nm pad window pitch: ~60 um) and signal integrity degradation over long cable harness runs, which can introduce parasitic capacitance (>30 pF) that distorts high-frequency read/write cycle timings.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical fail-bit mapping of 180nm 1T1C DRAM arrays must accurately separate bitline leakage, wordline-to-substrate breakdown, and cell capacitor dielectric defects from sense amplifier imbalance. At Gen 3 (180nm node, 1.8V core), probing must run March C- or checkerboard patterns at nominal and corner retention windows (t_REF = 64 ms at 85°C) to isolate retention-critical weak bits from hard physical shorts without inducing thermal drift across the 200mm wafer chuck.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring dedicated vertical or MEMS probe cards with high-density multi-die touchdown capabilities carries lead times of 12 to 18 weeks and substantial NRE. Outright turnkey service buy contracts from external OSAT/foundry test houses must include strict probe card needle wear guarantees (minimum 500k touchdowns before rebuild) and probe mark depth compliance (<25% of aluminum top pad thickness) to preserve bondability.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test cell throughput directly drives cost per good die. Full-wafer functional array testing cannot exceed allocated test budgets (target: <90 seconds per 200mm wafer across multi-site parallel testing). Milestone signoff requires synchronized data delivery of STDF and XML bitmap files into the defect clustering engine without uncoordinated engineering pauses.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Over-scrubbing induced aluminum pad cratering or interlayer dielectric (ILD) cracking beneath probe pads leading to packaging bond lift-off
1. Thermal expansion mismatch between wafer chuck and high-pin-count probe card causing progressive pin mis-registration during 85°C retention sort
1. False fail-bit artifact generation caused by power distribution network (PDN) supply rail droop (V_DD bounce > 100 mV) during simultaneous column sensing

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-PACKAGING-ROOT-2-2-3-2-01` | **Full-Wafer Contact Resistance & Pad Scrub Depth Metrology** | Automated 200mm Wafer Prober with Optical Scrub Inspection & Integrated Parametric Source Measure Unit (SMU) | 1. Align wafer optical fiducials and initialize probe card reference height (Z=0). 2. Step to 9 standard wafer sites (center, four mid-radius, four edge dies). 3. Apply standard overdrive of 40 um against Al-Cu test pads. 4. Force 10 mA DC through Kelvin force/sense pin pairs to measure contact resistance (R_cont) across 50 consecutive touchdowns. 5. Retract chuck and capture confocal optical surface profilometry of pad scrub marks to quantify scrub length and depth. | `Contact resistance R_cont <= 1.2 Ohms across all 9 sites with Gauge R&R CV < 1.0%; maximum probe scrub indentation depth <= 20% of top-metal Al-Cu thickness (nominal 800 nm, max penetration <= 160 nm).` |
| `TC-BEOL-PACKAGING-ROOT-2-2-3-2-02` | **Full-Array Functional March C- Bitmap Probing & Retention Sort** | Automated Memory Test System (ATE) interfaced via 50-Ohm matched high-density probe interface to 200mm wafer prober with thermal chuck (85°C) | 1. Power up device rails with monitored inrush current. 2. Execute March C- functional algorithmic test pattern: {up(w0); up(r0,w1); up(r1,w0); down(r0,w1); down(r1,w0); up(r0)} at 100 MHz clock rate. 3. Write solid background data '1's across the entire array, suspend refresh clocks for t_pause = 64 ms (retention pause test at 85°C), then read back data. 4. Stream fail coordinates, cycle counts, and DUT addresses directly into STDF v4 and raw fail-bitmap raster formats. | `Gross functional yield >= 70.0% of array blocks passing March C- without catastrophic column/row decoder failures; single-bit retention failure rate <= 0.05% of total cell population across wafer; zero unmapped fail bits during STDF raster parsing.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) compliant lab coat and grounded heel straps, Thermal protective gloves for 85°C chuck handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and copious water for at least 15 minutes. Eye exposure: Flush eyes immediately at certified eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Chuck thermal contact/burns: Submerge affected area in clean, cold running water; apply sterile dry dressing and seek cleanroom occupational health personnel immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober thermal chuck requires continuous dedicated enclosure exhaust (minimum 100 CFM flow rate) to prevent volatile VOC build-up from probe tip cleaning media; wafer test cell must maintain Class 100 laminar downward airflow (0.45 m/s ± 20%).

critics.systems_engineer: High-density functional fail-bit array probing requires seamless integration between the automated prober (e.g., TEL Precio or FormFactor Cascade), high-speed memory ATE channels, and the wafer map coordinate translation pipeline. The primary architectural risk is mechanical tip scrub misalignment degrading pad pitch tolerances (180nm pad window pitch: ~60 um) and signal integrity degradation over long cable harness runs, which can introduce parasitic capacitance (>30 pF) that distorts high-frequency read/write cycle timings.
critics.domain_expert: Physical fail-bit mapping of 180nm 1T1C DRAM arrays must accurately separate bitline leakage, wordline-to-substrate breakdown, and cell capacitor dielectric defects from sense amplifier imbalance. At Gen 3 (180nm node, 1.8V core), probing must run March C- or checkerboard patterns at nominal and corner retention windows (t_REF = 64 ms at 85°C) to isolate retention-critical weak bits from hard physical shorts without inducing thermal drift across the 200mm wafer chuck.
critics.supply_chain: Procuring dedicated vertical or MEMS probe cards with high-density multi-die touchdown capabilities carries lead times of 12 to 18 weeks and substantial NRE. Outright turnkey service buy contracts from external OSAT/foundry test houses must include strict probe card needle wear guarantees (minimum 500k touchdowns before rebuild) and probe mark depth compliance (<25% of aluminum top pad thickness) to preserve bondability.
critics.laya_pm: Test cell throughput directly drives cost per good die. Full-wafer functional array testing cannot exceed allocated test budgets (target: <90 seconds per 200mm wafer across multi-site parallel testing). Milestone signoff requires synchronized data delivery of STDF and XML bitmap files into the defect clustering engine without uncoordinated engineering pauses.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Spatial Defect Clustering Classification & Yield Signature Spatial Analysis
**Project**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Process Layer / Step**: Gen 3 Metrology — Full-Wafer Functional DRAM Cell Array Sort & Bitmap Probing  
**Document Tracking**: [`docs/knowledge/spatial_defect_clustering_sop.md`](./docs/knowledge/spatial_defect_clustering_sop.md)

---

### Process Flow & Spatial Signature Overview

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Fail-Bitmap Sort    │
│     Data Ingestion     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Spatial Coordinate   │
│      De-Aliasing       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Density Clustering   │
│    DBSCAN and Hough    │
│       Transform        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Yield Signature     │
│   Classification and   │
│      Attribution       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Excursion Gating and  │
│       Metrology        │
│      Feedforward       │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

```text
Defect Cluster Signature Yield Impact (%)
                          ┌────────────────────────────┐
                          │░░░░░░░                     │
   Random Single Bit Fails┤░░░░░░░                     │
                          │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒               │
    Die Cluster / Repeater┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒               │
   Scratch / Linear Streak┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓              │
                          │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓              │
Ring / Edge Exclusion Zone┤████████████████████████████│
                          │████████████████████████████│
                          └┬──────┬──────┬─────┬──────┬┘
                          0.0   10.6   21.2  31.9  42.5 
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

#### Step 1: Automated Full-Wafer Fail-Bitmap Ingestion & Coordinate De-Aliasing
1. Ingest raw Automated Test Equipment (ATE) wafer functional sort bitmaps recorded across all dies during march/checkerboard/retention tests at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. Perform physical address descrambling: Map logical bitline (BL) and wordline (WL) fail coordinates to exact physical silicon coordinates $(X, Y)$ using the 180nm cell topology:
   - Access transistor geometry: Gate length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Array grid pitch: Wordline pitch = $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$, Bitline pitch = $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Cell unit layout: $8\text{F}^2$ folded bitline ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$) or $6\text{F}^2$ open bitline ($0.194\ \mu\text{m}^2$).

#### Step 2: Spatial Density Filtering & Neighborhood Clustering (DBSCAN)
1. Apply DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) on physical $(X, Y)$ defect locations per die and across whole-wafer coordinates:
   - Define neighborhood radius $\varepsilon = 1.6\ \mu\text{m}$ (corresponding to 4 wordline/bitline array pitches).
   - Set minimum points threshold $\text{MinPts} = 5$ fails within radius $\varepsilon$.
2. Separate isolated single-bit fails (random Poisson distribution) from clustered fail zones (systematic manufacturing defect signatures).

#### Step 3: Yield Signature Morphology Extraction & Geometry Classification
1. **Linear / Streak Classification**: Run Hough Transform / Radon Transform on defect clusters. Classify clusters with aspect ratio $\ge 10:1$ oriented along non-Manhattan angles as **Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) Scratches** or **Handling Streaks**.
2. **Radial / Concentric Ring Signatures**: Calculate radial density distribution $D(r)$ from wafer center ($r=0$) to edge ($r = R_{\text{wafer}}$). Signatures concentrated in the outer $3\text{ mm}$ edge exclusion zone indicate **Bevel/Edge Bead Removal (EBR) or Rapid Thermal Anneal (RTA) temperature gradients**.
3. **Repeater / Lithographic Reticle Fingerprints**: Cross-correlate spatial defect clusters across stepped exposure reticle fields $(X_{\text{reticle}}, Y_{\text{reticle}})$. A spatial cross-correlation coefficient $R_{\text{reticle}} \ge 0.85$ triggers an automatic **Photomask Pellicle / Reticle Defect** alert.
4. **Sub-Array Column / Row Fail Signatures**: Defect tracks aligned strictly along single WL or BL pitches across $\ge 256$ cells denote wordline driver faults, bitline shorts, or tungsten plug (W-plug) contact open vias.

#### Step 4: Physical Root-Cause Correlation & Capacitance Partitioning
1. Flag localized micro-clusters exhibiting retention failure ($t_{\text{retention}} < 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$) for storage capacitor dielectric integrity:
   - Identify localized dielectric thinning where Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) deviates from nominal $3\text{ to } 4\text{ nm}$ in the $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-$k$ or ONO stack ($\kappa > 15$).
   - Identify bitlines with parasitic capacitance anomalies causing $C_b / C_s > 10:1$ (exceeding nominal operational ratio of $5:1$ to $9:1$, where nominal $C_s = 28\text{ fF}$ and $C_b = 150\text{ to } 250\text{ fF}$).
   - Isolate junctions exceeding the sub-threshold and junction leakage threshold of $I_{\text{leak}} > 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

#### Step 5: Lot Disposition & Metrology Feedback Gating
1. If systematic defect cluster area exceeds $1.5\%$ of array area on $> 3$ consecutive dies, automatically gate the wafer lot.
2. Feed physical $(X, Y)$ centroids directly to Defect Review SEM (inline high-resolution scanning electron microscopy) and Focused Ion Beam (FIB-TEM) cross-section stations for physical confirmation.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Metric ID | Parameter Description | Nominal / Target Spec | Critical Control Limit | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-01** | Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$) Retention Yield Floor | $28.0\text{ fF}$ ($\ge 25.0\text{ to } 30.0\text{ fF}$) | $< 25.0$ (Triggers Cluster Fail) | $\text{fF/cell}$ |
| **AC-02** | Cell Junction & Dielectric Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$) | $\le 1.0$ | $> 1.0$ (Causes $t_{\text{ret}} < 64\text{ ms}$) | $\text{fA/cell}$ |
| **AC-03** | Parasitic Bitline-to-Cell Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$) | $5.0 : 1\text{ to } 9.0 : 1$ | $> 10.0 : 1$ (Severe Read Margin Loss) | Dimensionless ratio |
| **AC-04** | Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) of Capacitor Dielectric Stack | $3.0\text{ to } 4.0$ | $< 2.8\text{ or } > 4.5$ | $\text{nm}$ |

---

### 3. Citations of Literature Context Sources

1. **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - Access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Shared bitline contact via tungsten plug (W-plug) to crown/MIM capacitor.
   - ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-$k$ stack ($\kappa > 15$).
   - Storage capacitance minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$; cell leakage limit $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
   - 1T1C stacked capacitor (Crown/Cylinder) with $C_s = 25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF/cell}$ ensuring data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) of $3\text{ to } 4\text{ nm}$.
   - Array bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Gate dielectric physical thickness $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ dry $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}-900^\circ\text{C}$.
3. **Source: 1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**:
   - $8\text{F}^2$ folded bitline cell area ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$) vs $6\text{F}^2$ open bitline ($0.194\ \mu\text{m}^2$).
   - Storage capacitance target $C_s \ge 25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$ (nominal $28\text{ fF}$).
   - Bitline capacitance $C_b = 150\text{ to } 250\text{ fF}$ per 256/512 cell segment.
   - Operating capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$ maintained between $5:1$ and $9:1$, with degradation threshold $> 10:1$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Fail-bitmap coordinate mapping must rigorously preserve orientation across wafer flat/notch alignments and probe tester coordinate systems. If ATE address-scramble tables do not match physical DRAM bitcell topological layouts (specifically true bitline/wordline twisting and sub-array sense amplifier interleaving), spatial clustering algorithms like DBSCAN will misclassify orthogonal address decoder line failures as diffuse random bit errors, corrupting fab yield-learning feedback.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Spatial signature decomposition requires differentiating between lithographic radial field anomalies (e.g. scanner lens aberration, defocus across wafer topography where DOF >= 0.5 um), spin-coating radial thickness non-uniformities from dielectric deposition (monitored via spectroscopic ellipsometry delta/psi parameters), and mechanical probe damage signatures (ring or crescent patterns along wafer edge zones from clamp/chuck misalignment).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Exporting spatial yield bitmaps and clustering classification models requires strict compliance with open-source MPW governance and foundry non-disclosure restrictions. Aggregated defect density and spatial cluster coordinates must be decoupled from sensitive foundry baseline macro telemetry before external dissemination across the DRAM Foundation VN ecosystem.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Automated cluster classification execution must not become a cycle-time bottleneck for production lot release; bitmap extraction and spatial classification inference must complete within 45 seconds per 200mm wafer on the sorting cluster, preventing tester idle queue accumulation during high-density multi-site functional probing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Address-to-physical bit coordinate descrambler mismatch leading to systematic wordline/bitline array faults being misclassified as random Poissonic spatial clusters
1. Overfitting of clustering hyper-parameters (epsilon and MinPts in DBSCAN) causing dense ring/scratch patterns to fragment into false isolated defect clusters
1. Thermal probe card expansion during full-wafer sort shifting touchdown coordinates, inducing false edge-die clustered contact-open signatures

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BEOL-PACKAGING-ROOT-2-2-3-3-01` | **Machine Verification of Spatial Defect Clustering and Signature Classification Accuracy** | Automated DRAM Wafer Prober (Accretech UF3000EX / TEL Pronto300), Advantest T5588 DRAM Test System, Spatial Pattern Recognition Metrology Server (Python/SciPy DBSCAN + Hough Transform pipeline) | 1. Ingest raw physical fail-bitmaps from 25 wafers across 3 MPW sort lots into the classification engine. 2. Execute spatial density-based clustering (DBSCAN with eps=3.5 dies, min_samples=8) to isolate cluster cores. 3. Apply Hough Transform and radial projection to identify scratches, ring/radial concentric patterns, and cluster patches. 4. Compare classified spatial signatures against golden synthetic and review-verified defect signature databases. | `Spatial clustering classification purity >= 96.5% against golden defect library; scratch detection sensitivity >= 99.0% with zero false negatives on wafer edge exclusion zones; total inference runtime <= 35.0 s per 200mm wafer.` |
| `TC-BEOL-PACKAGING-ROOT-2-2-3-3-02` | **Correlation of Spatial Fail-Bit Clusters with Optical Dielectric Thickness Non-Uniformity** | KLA-Tencor SpectraCD / Woollam M-2000 Spectroscopic Ellipsometer, Wafer-Sort Yield Analytics Platform | 1. Load 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry dielectric thickness maps for BEOL IMD layers (model Cauchy n=1.46 at 632.8 nm). 2. Align polar coordinates with wafer sort bitmap spatial cluster density zones. 3. Calculate spatial Pearson correlation coefficient r between local dielectric thickness gradient (d_ox/dr) and fail-bit cluster frequency across concentric radial zones (r = 0 to 95 mm). | `Radial cluster correlation coefficient |r| >= 0.85 when film non-uniformity exceeds +/- 3.5%; spatial centroid distance between maximum dielectric film deviation and highest density cluster centroid <= 2.5 mm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/ISO 5 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static), ESD-Safe Lab Coat and Cleanroom Booties, ANSI Z87.1 Approved UV/Impact Safety Glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with IPA, flush with copious deionized water for at least 15 minutes. For eye splash, rinse immediately at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For inhalation of vapor, move victim to fresh air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on manual clean stations maintaining minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); prober test floor maintained under positive laminar airflow (ISO 5/Class 100).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA solvent wipes and cleaning liquids collected in dedicated, grounded, flammable waste containers for off-site licensed hazardous solvent incineration; no sewer disposal.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`

- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric moisture absorption and airborne molecular contamination (AMC) causing bond pad copper/aluminum oxidation and galvanic corrosion at probe scrub marks, leading to high-resistance contact open failures and bond lift during subsequent packaging.

If ATE address-scramble tables do not match physical DRAM bitcell topological layouts (specifically true bitline/wordline twisting and sub-array sense amplifier interleaving), spatial clustering algorithms like DBSCAN will misclassify orthogonal address decoder line failures as diffuse random bit errors, corrupting fab yield-learning feedback.
critics.domain_expert: Spatial signature decomposition requires differentiating between lithographic radial field anomalies (e.g. scanner lens aberration, defocus across wafer topography where DOF >= 0.5 um), spin-coating radial thickness non-uniformities from dielectric deposition (monitored via spectroscopic ellipsometry delta/psi parameters), and mechanical probe damage signatures (ring or crescent patterns along wafer edge zones from clamp/chuck misalignment).
critics.supply_chain: Exporting spatial yield bitmaps and clustering classification models requires strict compliance with open-source MPW governance and foundry non-disclosure restrictions. Aggregated defect density and spatial cluster coordinates must be decoupled from sensitive foundry baseline macro telemetry before external dissemination across the DRAM Foundation VN ecosystem.
critics.laya_pm: Automated cluster classification execution must not become a cycle-time bottleneck for production lot release; bitmap extraction and spatial classification inference must complete within 45 seconds per 200mm wafer on the sorting cluster, preventing tester idle queue accumulation during high-density multi-site functional probing.
critical_failure_modes: Address-to-physical bit coordinate descrambler mismatch leading to systematic wordline/bitline array faults being misclassified as random Poissonic spatial clusters
Overfitting of clustering hyper-parameters (epsilon and MinPts in DBSCAN) causing dense ring/scratch patterns to fragment into false isolated defect clusters
Thermal probe card expansion during full-wafer sort shifting touchdown coordinates, inducing false edge-die clustered contact-open signatures

testcases.title: Machine Verification of Spatial Defect Clustering and Signature Classification Accuracy
testcases.instrumentation: Automated DRAM Wafer Prober (Accretech UF3000EX / TEL Pronto300), Advantest T5588 DRAM Test System, Spatial Pattern Recognition Metrology Server (Python/SciPy DBSCAN + Hough Transform pipeline)
testcases.pre_conditions: 200mm DRAM sort wafers probed through full retention and march functional patterns; raw address fail logs converted to physical XY coordinates using verified PDK topological descrambling matrix; prober alignment verified to notch with < 1.0 um theta error.
testcases.procedure: 1. Ingest raw physical fail-bitmaps from 25 wafers across 3 MPW sort lots into the classification engine. 2. Execute spatial density-based clustering (DBSCAN with eps=3.5 dies, min_samples=8) to isolate cluster cores. 3. Apply Hough Transform and radial projection to identify scratches, ring/radial concentric patterns, and cluster patches. 4. Compare classified spatial signatures against golden synthetic and review-verified defect signature databases.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Spatial clustering classification purity >= 96.5% against golden defect library; scratch detection sensitivity >= 99.0% with zero false negatives on wafer edge exclusion zones; total inference runtime <= 35.0 s per 200mm wafer.

testcases.title: Correlation of Spatial Fail-Bit Clusters with Optical Dielectric Thickness Non-Uniformity
testcases.instrumentation: KLA-Tencor SpectraCD / Woollam M-2000 Spectroscopic Ellipsometer, Wafer-Sort Yield Analytics Platform
testcases.pre_conditions: Inter-metal dielectric (IMD) oxide and passivation film 49-point ellipsometry maps (psi, delta, thickness) pre-measured and archived in MES; sorted wafer functional fail density mapped onto identical polar coordinate mesh.
testcases.procedure: 1. Load 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry dielectric thickness maps for BEOL IMD layers (model Cauchy n=1.46 at 632.8 nm). 2. Align polar coordinates with wafer sort bitmap spatial cluster density zones. 3. Calculate spatial Pearson correlation coefficient r between local dielectric thickness gradient (d_ox/dr) and fail-bit cluster frequency across concentric radial zones (r = 0 to 95 mm).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Radial cluster correlation coefficient |r| >= 0.85 when film non-uniformity exceeds +/- 3.5%; spatial centroid distance between maximum dielectric film deviation and highest density cluster centroid <= 2.5 mm.

ppe_required: Class 100/ISO 5 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static)
ESD-Safe Lab Coat and Cleanroom Booties
ANSI Z87.1 Approved UV/Impact Safety Glasses

cas_chemicals.name: Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for prober chuck/optics maintenance

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin contact with IPA, flush with copious deionized water for at least 15 minutes. For eye splash, rinse immediately at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For inhalation of vapor, move victim to fresh air immediately.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on manual clean stations maintaining minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); prober test floor maintained under positive laminar airflow (ISO 5/Class 100).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent IPA solvent wipes and cleaning liquids collected in dedicated, grounded, flammable waste containers for off-site licensed hazardous solvent incineration; no sewer disposal.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Completed BEOL passivation and top-metal Al-Cu/Cu pad anneal; wafer surface clean, dry, and free of organic residues, probe scrub marks uncorroded.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Post-probe passivated surface with verified cantilever/vertical probe scrubs (< 15 um scrub length), stored in sealed N2 purge container prior to laser dicing.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Atmospheric moisture absorption and airborne molecular contamination (AMC) causing bond pad copper/aluminum oxidation and galvanic corrosion at probe scrub marks, leading to high-resistance contact open failures and bond lift during subsequent packaging.
