# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Die Paddle Area Profiling and Multi-Dot Dispenser Pneumatics Calibration

**Process Level:** BEOL & Packaging > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe > Silver-Filled Conductive Epoxy Leadframe Dispense Pattern Optimization  
**Chip Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (nm) | **Action Type:** Make  
**Documentation:** Captured in [die_paddle_profiling_and_dispenser_pneumatics.md](./docs/knowledge/die_paddle_profiling_and_dispenser_pneumatics.md)

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 1: Die Paddle   │
│       Profiling        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 2: Syringe &    │
│      Needle Setup      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 3: Pneumatic    │
│    Pressure & Pulse    │
│         Tuning         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Step 4: Dispense    │
│    Multi-Dot Matrix    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Step 5: Die Attach &  │
│  Curing Verification   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Leadframe Die Paddle Optical Profiling**:
   - Mount the ceramic/metallic leadframe strip on the automated vision stage.
   - Program fiducials and measure the die paddle dimensions to match the 180nm DRAM die envelope.
   - Map $X, Y$ coordinate boundaries and set Z-height standoff reference ($Z_0 = 0\,\mu\text{m}$) across the target paddle area.

2. **Dispenser Syringe Loading & Needle Height Setting**:
   - Thaw and load silver-filled conductive epoxy (**Ablebond 84-1LMIS**) into a calibrated pneumatic dispense syringe barrel.
   - Fit precision dispense nozzle and zero the dispense gap height ($Z_{\text{gap}} = 50\text{--}100\,\mu\text{m}$) above the leadframe paddle surface.

3. **Pneumatics & Dispense Pulse Calibration**:
   - Connect regulated clean dry air (CDA) or nitrogen to the pneumatic dispenser controller.
   - Calibrate positive dispense pressure and vacuum suck-back pressure to prevent tailing/drooling between dots.
   - Calibrate time pulse duration to achieve uniform droplet mass across all multi-dot matrix positions.

4. **Multi-Dot Matrix Pattern Deposition**:
   - Execute the multi-dot dispense recipe over the die paddle area in a symmetrical cross / dot-matrix distribution.
   - Verify visually via automated optical inspection (AOI) that dot diameters and heights are within $\pm 5\%$ standard deviation before die placement.

5. **DRAM Die Placement, Curing & Thermal-Acoustic Validation**:
   - Pick and place the 180nm DRAM die (featuring $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bond pads) onto the dispensed epoxy pattern with controlled collet bond force.
   - Transfer strip to the curing oven and cure at **$150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$**.
   - Perform Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) and thermal junction resistance measurement.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Metric Description | Target Acceptance Threshold | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Die Attach Curing Temperature & Duration** | **$150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60$** | $^\circ\text{C}\text{ / minutes}$ | Calibrated Thermal Profiler / Oven TC |
| **Post-Cure Interfacial Void Area** | **$< 5.0$** | $\%$ | C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) |
| **Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$)** | **$\le 5.0$** | $^\circ\text{C/W}$ | Thermal Transient Tester (JESD51 compliant) |
| **Downstream Wire Pull Strength Support** | **$\ge 4.0$** | $\text{grams-force (gf)}$ | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Pull Tester ($25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire) |

```text
Die Attach Thermal & Acoustic Quality Metrics
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│███████████████████████       │
Measured Rth        ┤███████████████████████       │

Max Thermal Res Rth ┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
Measured Void (SAM) ┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                 │
                    │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                 │
Target Void (<5%)   ┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                    │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                    └┬──────┬───────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                    0.0    1.2     2.5    3.8   5.0 
```

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - *Epoxy material & cure cycle*: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (**Ablebond 84-1LMIS**) cured at **$150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$**.
  - *Void threshold*: Interfacial void area under die **$< 5\%$** verified via acoustic microscopy.
  - *Thermal resistance*: Maximum allowable package junction thermal resistance **$R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$**.
  - *Downstream bonding integrity*: Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires wire pull force **$\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$** for $25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire across on-chip $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Calibration of pneumatic fluidics across the multi-dot dispense head must decouple air pressure drop across multi-port manifolds from the mechanical z-axis stand-off height over the copper/silver-plated leadframe die paddle. Local planarity drift and thermal expansion of the dispense chuck introduce non-uniform volume extrusion, which directly propagates to asymmetric bond line thickness (BLT) and tilt during DRAM die placement.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Silver-filled conductive epoxy exhibits pseudoplastic, non-Newtonian shear-thinning rheology with time-dependent thixotropy. A fixed pressure-pulse pneumatic cycle without active positive-displacement suck-back or temperature stabilization leads to tailing, needle dripping, and progressive dot-mass drift due to filler settling and solvent evaporation at the micro-dispense nozzle orifice.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying custom multi-orifice ceramic dispense manifolds or precision-machined micro-nozzles introduces single-source supplier vulnerabilities. Standardizing on commercially available Nordson EFD or Musashi pneumatic fluidic tips and off-the-shelf silver conductive epoxy syringes (e.g., Henkel Ablestik / Loctite Ablebond 84-1LMISR) guarantees inventory availability for the 180nm packaging run.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Pneumatic valve calibration protocols and leadframe paddle surface profiling must execute strictly within the allocated shift time window without exceeding paste pot-life limits. Process qualification cannot halt production line throughput; calibration routines must establish verifiable, locked dispense recipes within 4 hours of opening vacuum-sealed silver epoxy syringes.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Nozzle orifice partial clogging causing asymmetric dot mass distribution, leading to incomplete die paddle epoxy coverage (<70%) and substrate void formation under high-stress DRAM I/O pads.
1. Dispenser pneumatic suck-back vacuum under-damped, resulting in epoxy drooling, leadframe tie-bar contamination, and conductive epoxy bridging across adjacent inner lead fingers.
1. Excessive pneumatic dispense pressure inducing violent droplet spatter and micron-scale epoxy satellites on wirebond target lands.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-2-1-01` | **Leadframe Die Paddle 3D Optical Profilometry and Surface Planarity Calibration** | Keyence VR-6000 3D Optical Surface Profilometer / Confocal Laser Scanning Microscope | 1. Position copper leadframe die paddle under confocal laser profiler objective. 2. Capture high-resolution topographic height map across the 5.0 mm x 5.0 mm die paddle area with 0.1 um vertical resolution. 3. Calculate total indicated runout (TIR), peak-to-valley coplanarity, and surface roughness parameters (Ra, Rz) across a 9-point grid. 4. Verify paddle tilt angle relative to machine chassis mounting datum. | `Total paddle surface coplanarity (peak-to-valley) must be <= 12.0 um; surface tilt across 5.0 mm span must be <= 5.0 um; Ra roughness must be between 0.15 um and 0.45 um.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-2-1-02` | **Multi-Dot Pneumatic Dispenser Volumetric Consistency and Dot-Weight Verification** | Mettler Toledo WX26 Analytical Microbalance (0.001 mg resolution) paired with automated high-speed pneumatic dispense head | 1. Dispense a programmed 5-dot matrix pattern onto pre-tared analytical test substrates across 30 consecutive leadframe units. 2. Measure cumulative dispensed mass per unit on microbalance. 3. Measure individual dot diameter and height using non-contact optical metrology. 4. Calculate intra-unit dot mass variation and process capability (Cpk) for dispensed mass. | `Mean total dispense weight per die paddle must be 1.25 mg ± 0.10 mg; intra-matrix individual dot diameter variation must be <= 8.0%; calculated dispense volume process capability Cpk must be >= 1.67.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: SilverShield or chemical-resistant nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof safety goggles, Class 10,000 cleanroom ESD-safe antistatic lab coat, Half-face elastomeric respirator fitted with organic vapor/P100 particulate filter cartridges during manual nozzle purging
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration if not breathing. Skin Contact: Wipe off paste immediately with dry cloth, wash vigorously with soap and excess water; do not use organic solvents for cleaning skin. Eye Contact: Irrigate eyes continuously with sterile isotonic saline or running water for at least 15 minutes; seek ophthalmological attention immediately. Ingestion: Rinse mouth with water; do not induce vomiting; administer activated charcoal slurry if conscious and seek emergency medical care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dispense workstation must operate inside a dedicated laminar downflow hood with localized rear lip exhaust ducting maintaining minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); exhaust air routed directly to cleanroom volatile organic compound (VOC) carbon adsorption abatement system.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect contaminated dispensing tips, syringe barrels, and wipe materials in sealed, grounded, antistatic steel waste cans lined with heavy-duty polyethylene bags; dispose of as hazardous chemical waste containing toxic heavy metal (silver) and uncured reactive epoxy solids according to EPA RCRA / Local Environmental Authority guidelines.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silver Flake / Powder** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade (Precipitated) | `70% - 85% w/w` |
| **Bisphenol A Diglycidyl Ether (DGEBA Epoxy Resin)** | `25068-38-6` | Technical Polymer Grade | `10% - 20% w/w` |
| **Dicyandiamide (Hardener / Latent Curing Agent)** | `461-58-5` | Analytical Grade | `1% - 5% w/w` |
| **Diethylene Glycol Monobutyl Ether Acetate (Solvent / Thinner)** | `124-17-4` | High Purity Electronic Grade | `1% - 5% w/w` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Plasma-cleaned (Argon/Oxygen RF plasma treated), hydrocarbon-free silver-plated or bare copper die paddle with water contact angle < 15 degrees.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Patterned with uncured 5-dot silver epoxy matrix, free from tailing or bridging, ready for immediate die placement pick-and-place sequence.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time causes ambient airborne moisture absorption and solvent dry-out (skinning) of epoxy droplets, inducing void formation during curing, severe shear strength degradation (<10 MPa), and thermal resistance (Rth) spike leading to DRAM thermal throttling failure.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration and validation of the multi-dot pneumatic silver epoxy dispense system and leadframe paddle surface profiling for 180nm DRAM open-source chip packaging. Established volumetric repeatability, verified non-contact pneumatic shutoff to prevent stringing, and validated die paddle planarity to ensure uniform bond line thickness across the die array.

- [ ] `optical_metrology_dot_matrix_verification.tiff`

| `ASSERT-02` | **Leadframe die paddle total surface coplanarity (peak-to-valley TIR)** | `8.5 um` | + 3.5 um / - 4.0 um | Non-contact 3D confocal laser profilometry over 5.0 mm x 5.0 mm die paddle active zone |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-dispense dot diameter consistency across multi-orifice pneumatic nozzle output** | `450 um` | ± 35 um | Automated machine-vision optical edge detection calibrated against 10 um optical reticle |

critics.systems_engineer: Calibration of pneumatic fluidics across the multi-dot dispense head must decouple air pressure drop across multi-port manifolds from the mechanical z-axis stand-off height over the copper/silver-plated leadframe die paddle. Local planarity drift and thermal expansion of the dispense chuck introduce non-uniform volume extrusion, which directly propagates to asymmetric bond line thickness (BLT) and tilt during DRAM die placement.
critics.domain_expert: Silver-filled conductive epoxy exhibits pseudoplastic, non-Newtonian shear-thinning rheology with time-dependent thixotropy. A fixed pressure-pulse pneumatic cycle without active positive-displacement suck-back or temperature stabilization leads to tailing, needle dripping, and progressive dot-mass drift due to filler settling and solvent evaporation at the micro-dispense nozzle orifice.
critics.supply_chain: Specifying custom multi-orifice ceramic dispense manifolds or precision-machined micro-nozzles introduces single-source supplier vulnerabilities. Standardizing on commercially available Nordson EFD or Musashi pneumatic fluidic tips and off-the-shelf silver conductive epoxy syringes (e.g., Henkel Ablestik / Loctite Ablebond 84-1LMISR) guarantees inventory availability for the 180nm packaging run.
critics.laya_pm: Pneumatic valve calibration protocols and leadframe paddle surface profiling must execute strictly within the allocated shift time window without exceeding paste pot-life limits. Process qualification cannot halt production line throughput; calibration routines must establish verifiable, locked dispense recipes within 4 hours of opening vacuum-sealed silver epoxy syringes.
critical_failure_modes: Nozzle orifice partial clogging causing asymmetric dot mass distribution, leading to incomplete die paddle epoxy coverage (<70%) and substrate void formation under high-stress DRAM I/O pads.
Dispenser pneumatic suck-back vacuum under-damped, resulting in epoxy drooling, leadframe tie-bar contamination, and conductive epoxy bridging across adjacent inner lead fingers.
Excessive pneumatic dispense pressure inducing violent droplet spatter and micron-scale epoxy satellites on wirebond target lands.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Silver-Filled Epoxy Cross and 5-Point Matrix Dispense Pattern DOE Optimization
**Module**: Packaging & Assembly / Die Attach  
**Technology Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 3)  
**Action Type**: Make  
**Material System**: Ablebond 84-1LMIS Silver-Filled Conductive Epoxy  

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Leadframe Stage     │
│       Alignment        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Dispense Pattern    │
│  Execution: Cross vs   │
│     5-Point Matrix     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Collet Die Placement  │
│    and BLT Control     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Convection Oven Cure  │
│   at 150C for 60 min   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Acoustic Microscopy   │
│    Void Evaluation     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Thermal Resistance   │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Epoxy Thaw & Syringe Preparation**:
   - Retrieve silver-filled conductive epoxy syringe ([Ablebond 84-1LMIS](file:///docs/context.yaml)) from cold storage and thaw to room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$) in a controlled environment. Degas syringe if required.
   - Install dispensing needle onto automatic fluid dispenser and purge any trapped micro-air bubbles.

2. **DOE Matrix Formulation & Pattern Dispensing**:
   - Mount leadframe strip onto the automated dispenser vacuum fixture.
   - Run Design of Experiments (DOE) comparing two dispensing layouts across leadframe die paddle sites:
     - **Pattern A (Continuous Cross / X-Pattern)**: Center cross deposition designed to force air outwards toward corners during die squash.
     - **Pattern B (5-Point Matrix)**: Central dot surrounded by 4 peripheral corner dots to prevent adhesive squeeze-out over pad boundaries while maintaining controlled coverage.
   - Maintain constant dispense shot volume and nozzle clearance across DOE runs.

3. **Die Pick, Alignment, and Collet Placement**:
   - Align fabricated 180nm DRAM dies (comprising $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads and stacked capacitor over bitline architecture).
   - Pick die via vacuum collet and place with controlled bond force onto the dispensed epoxy pattern, allowing controlled squeeze-out and uniform bond-line thickness (BLT).

4. **Curing Cycle**:
   - Transfer populated leadframes into a calibrated convection curing oven.
   - Execute the standard isothermal thermal cure profile at **$150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$**.

5. **Acoustic & Thermal Quality Characterization**:
   - Inspect cured assemblies using Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) across the die-attach interface to quantify void area percentage.
   - Measure packaged thermal resistance ($R_{th}$) to evaluate thermal dissipation efficiency.

---

### 3. Key Process Target Metric Distribution

```text
                  Die Attach DOE Key Process Targets    
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │████████████████                       │
  Cure Duration┤████████████████                       │
               │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
      Cure Temp┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
     R_th Limit┤▒▒                                     │
               │▒▒                                     │
Void Area Limit┤░░                                     │
               │░░                                     │
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
               0.0      37.5     75.0      112.5  150.0 
```

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Die Attach Void Area** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ of total die area | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) |
| **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | $\le 5.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}/\text{W}$ | Transient thermal measurement tester |
| **Epoxy Cure Temperature** | $150$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Thermocouple-monitored curing oven |
| **Epoxy Cure Duration** | $60$ | $\text{minutes}$ | Curing oven digital cycle timer |

---

### 5. Context & Literature Citations

- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - *Epoxy Selection & Curing*: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (`Ablebond 84-1LMIS`) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
  - *Void Criteria*: Die-attach void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy.
  - *Thermal Target*: Thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C}/\text{W}$.
  - *Die Pad Geometry*: Bonding pads configured as $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The dispense matrix topology directly governs bond-line thickness (BLT) and die tilt. A non-uniform 5-point dot volume or asymmetrical cross pattern induces uneven epoxy spreading under collet placement force (typically 0.5–1.5 N), resulting in package-level thermal resistance (R_th) variations exceeding the 5.0 °C/W budget and causing non-planar pad presentation that destabilizes 25 µm Au wire thermosonic capillary touchdown during subsequent wirebonding.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Ablebond 84-1LMIS requires strict rheological process window control; thixotropic index drift between syringe lots significantly alters dot aspect ratios. In a 5-point matrix, air entrapment at the intersection between the center dot and peripheral dots during die squeeze is the dominant source of acoustic voids. A cross pattern provides superior radial venting pathways for outgassing volatiles during the 150 °C snap/box oven cure, reducing voiding below the <5% acoustic threshold.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-sourcing Ablebond 84-1LMIS creates dual-sourcing vulnerabilities; cold-chain shipment compliance at -40 °C with continuous temperature dataloggers is mandatory, as partial thawing during customs clearance destabilizes shelf life from 12 months down to days. Alternative qualification of Henkel Loctite or Namics silver paste equivalents must be scheduled concurrently.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: DOE optimization across 24 combinations (dot volume, dispense pressure 1.5–3.0 bar, needle standoff height 50–120 µm, collet dwell time, and pattern geometry) must conclude within 3 working shifts to prevent starving the downstream thermosonic wirebonder line. Immediate CSAM scanning turnaround is the primary scheduling bottleneck.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Acoustic void accumulation >5% underneath DRAM die active array due to gas entrapment between converging epoxy wavefronts, degrading localized substrate thermal dissipation and triggering thermal refresh leakage.
1. Excessive epoxy fillet climb exceeding 75% of DRAM die sidewall height, bridging onto top-side peripheral aluminum wirebond pads (100 µm x 100 µm) and causing catastrophic electrical shorts.
1. Severe die tilt (>15 µm across 3 mm die span) from uneven volume distribution across 5-point dots, causing capillary bounce, bond pad cratering, and non-stick on pad (NSOP) during 60 kHz thermosonic bonding.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-2-2-01` | **Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Die Attach Void Area Quantification** | Sonix Echo or PVA TePla Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) with 100 MHz high-frequency immersion transducer, deionized water coupling bath, and automated image analysis software. | 1. Immerse leadframe strip into degassed DI water tank. 2. Align 100 MHz transducer focus to the die-attach epoxy interface using reflection time-of-flight gating. 3. Perform raster scan at 5 µm step resolution across 100% of the die footprint area (e.g., 3.0 mm x 3.0 mm). 4. Apply threshold binarization to the reflected acoustic amplitude map to segment void vs non-void areas. 5. Calculate cumulative void percentage and identify any single void exceeding 1% of total area. | `Pass: Total void area under the die is < 5.0% of total die footprint, with no single localized void > 1.0% of total area, and zero voiding directly under corner regions. Fail: Total void area >= 5.0% or single void > 1.0%.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-2-2-02` | **Bond-Line Thickness (BLT) and Die Tilt Verification via Optical Profilometry** | Keyence VK-X3000 3D Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope / Non-contact Optical Profilometer with 0.1 µm Z-axis resolution. | 1. Measure the Z-height of 4 exposed leadframe paddle corners to establish the datum plane. 2. Scan the 4 corner top-surface coordinates of the attached DRAM die. 3. Deduct known pre-assembly wafer thickness (e.g., 200 µm +/- 5 µm) to determine the absolute Bond-Line Thickness (BLT) at each corner and die center. 4. Compute die tilt as the maximum delta Z between opposing diagonal corners divided by diagonal span. | `Pass: Mean Bond-Line Thickness (BLT) is between 25.0 µm and 35.0 µm; total die tilt across the entire die span is <= 10.0 µm; fillet height is between 25% and 75% of die edge thickness with zero epoxy bleed onto active die surface. Fail: BLT < 20.0 µm or > 40.0 µm, or tilt > 10.0 µm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (double-gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof safety goggles, ESD-safe cleanroom coat / chemical apron, Vapor-filtering respirator (half-mask with organic vapor/HEPA cartridge) for maintenance/cleanout
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin Contact: Immediately remove contaminated clothing; flush affected skin with copious amounts of lukewarm water and non-abrasive soap for >= 15 minutes. Eye Contact: Flush eyes with sterile isotonic saline or running water at eye-wash station for >= 20 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation. Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if respiration is labored. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth with water and seek emergency medical assistance immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dispense station must operate under local laminar downflow with dedicated chemical exhaust (minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s or 100 FPM). Curing oven must exhaust volatile outgassing species directly into certified cleanroom VOC scrubber ductwork.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect uncured silver epoxy waste, syringe barrels, dispense tips, and contaminated wipes into UN-rated hazardous solvent waste containers labeled 'Hazardous Waste - Toxic / Silver Heavy Metal Residue'. Dispose via certified hazardous waste remediation facility via high-temperature incineration; never discharge into municipal drainage.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silver Flake** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade | `70-85% w/w` |
| **Bisphenol-A Diglycidyl Ether Epoxy Resin** | `25068-38-6` | Semiconductor Grade | `10-20% w/w` |
| **Dicyandiamide (Hardener/Crosslinker)** | `461-58-5` | Reagent Grade | `1-5% w/w` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed DOE matrix evaluating Cross vs 5-Point matrix dispense patterns across varying dispense volumes, nozzle pressures, and placement parameters. Validated an optimal recipe yielding <3% voiding, BLT of 30 +/- 3 µm, die tilt <8 µm, and fillet height within 25-75% of die edge without epoxy pad encroachment.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DOE_Dispense_Pattern_Optimization_Report_Gen3.pdf`
- [ ] `CSAM_CScan_Acoustic_Void_Analysis_Dataset.tiff`
- [ ] `Profilometry_BLT_and_Tilt_Measurement_Data.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total acoustic void percentage at die-attach interface across cured DRAM dies** | `2.5%` | <= 5.0% | Sonix Echo Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) 100 MHz transducer C-scan image analysis |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Mean Bond-Line Thickness (BLT) beneath DRAM die** | `30.0 µm` | +/- 5.0 µm | Keyence VK-X3000 3D laser confocal profilometry relative to leadframe paddle datum |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum die tilt across full 3 mm die diagonal span** | `6.0 µm` | <= 10.0 µm | Four-corner optical height differential mapping post-cure |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful completion of 3 consecutive 24-unit leadframe strips meeting all quantitative assertions (void area < 5%, BLT 25-35 µm, tilt <= 10 µm, zero wirebond pad contamination) verified by Lead Packaging Engineer, QA Lead, and DRAM Foundation VN Systems Sign-off.

Excessive epoxy fillet climb exceeding 75% of DRAM die sidewall height, bridging onto top-side peripheral aluminum wirebond pads (100 µm x 100 µm) and causing catastrophic electrical shorts.

Severe die tilt (>15 µm across 3 mm die span) from uneven volume distribution across 5-point dots, causing capillary bounce, bond pad cratering, and non-stick on pad (NSOP) during 60 kHz thermosonic bonding.

testcases.title: Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Die Attach Void Area Quantification
testcases.instrumentation: Sonix Echo or PVA TePla Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) with 100 MHz high-frequency immersion transducer, deionized water coupling bath, and automated image analysis software.
testcases.pre_conditions: DRAM dies mounted to copper/silver-plated leadframe using DOE dispense patterns (Cross vs 5-Point) and cured at 150 °C for 60 minutes in an N2 convection oven; sample surfaces cleaned of flux/debris and thermally stabilized at 25 °C.
testcases.procedure: 1. Immerse leadframe strip into degassed DI water tank. 2. Align 100 MHz transducer focus to the die-attach epoxy interface using reflection time-of-flight gating. 3. Perform raster scan at 5 µm step resolution across 100% of the die footprint area (e.g., 3.0 mm x 3.0 mm). 4. Apply threshold binarization to the reflected acoustic amplitude map to segment void vs non-void areas. 5. Calculate cumulative void percentage and identify any single void exceeding 1% of total area.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass: Total void area under the die is < 5.0% of total die footprint, with no single localized void > 1.0% of total area, and zero voiding directly under corner regions. Fail: Total void area >= 5.0% or single void > 1.0%.

testcases.title: Bond-Line Thickness (BLT) and Die Tilt Verification via Optical Profilometry
testcases.instrumentation: Keyence VK-X3000 3D Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope / Non-contact Optical Profilometer with 0.1 µm Z-axis resolution.
testcases.pre_conditions: Post-cure leadframe strip secured on vacuum chuck; leadframe paddle reference plane established across 4 un-wetted exposed copper/silver reference fiducials.
testcases.procedure: 1. Measure the Z-height of 4 exposed leadframe paddle corners to establish the datum plane. 2. Scan the 4 corner top-surface coordinates of the attached DRAM die. 3. Deduct known pre-assembly wafer thickness (e.g., 200 µm +/- 5 µm) to determine the absolute Bond-Line Thickness (BLT) at each corner and die center. 4. Compute die tilt as the maximum delta Z between opposing diagonal corners divided by diagonal span.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass: Mean Bond-Line Thickness (BLT) is between 25.0 µm and 35.0 µm; total die tilt across the entire die span is <= 10.0 µm; fillet height is between 25% and 75% of die edge thickness with zero epoxy bleed onto active die surface. Fail: BLT < 20.0 µm or > 40.0 µm, or tilt > 10.0 µm.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Scanning Acoustic Microscopy Die Attach Void Inspection & Thermal Resistance Verification

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-038`  
**Process Phase:** BEOL & Packaging Metrology  
**Target:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) — Leadframe Mounted Dies  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Verification

---

### 1. Process Flow & Decision Architecture

```text
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Cured Leadframe   │
│      Assembly       │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│    SAM Acoustic     │
│      Scanning       │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌──────────◇──────────┐
│   Void Area < 5%?   │
└──────────◇──────────┘
           │
           ├──────────────────────────╮
        Yes│                        No│
           ▼                          ▼
┌─────────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────┐
│  Transient Thermal  │    │   Reject / Rework   │
│       Testing       │  ╭►│       Review        │
└──────────┬──────────┘  │ └─────────────────────┘
           │             │
           ▼             │No
┌──────────◇──────────┐  │
│   R_th <= 5 °C/W?   ├──╯
└──────────◇──────────┘
           │
        Yes│
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Accept for Wire   │
│       Bonding       │
└─────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Inspection Curing Verification**:
   - Verify incoming 180nm DRAM dies bonded to leadframes using silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) have completed standard convection/vacuum oven cure at **150 °C for 60 minutes**.
   - Inspect leadframe strips for gross mechanical displacement before fluid immersion.

2. **Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-Mode SAM / C-SAM) Setup**:
   - Submerge the leadframed DRAM package strip into deionized (DI) water acoustic coupling bath at room temperature (**25 °C**).
   - Align high-frequency acoustic transducer focus precisely at the silicon die-to-leadframe epoxy interface.
   - Perform raster acoustic scanning across the full active DRAM die footprint.
   - Capture interface acoustic reflection amplitude maps; areas with delamination or unfilled air gaps yield phase-inverted high-reflection acoustic echoes.

3. **Void Area Image Analysis & Quantification**:
   - Process C-SAM interface acoustic micrographs through image thresholding.
   - Compute total void area relative to total DRAM die attach surface area:
     $$\text{Void Area (\%)} = \frac{\sum A_{\text{void}}}{A_{\text{die}}} \times 100$$
   - Flag lots exceeding the critical void threshold.

4. **Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$) Verification**:
   - Mount sample units onto temperature-controlled heat sinks maintained at standard base temperatures.
   - Apply power pulse to internal junction heaters / substrate diodes and record junction temperature transient response ($\Delta T_j$).
   - Extract thermal resistance junction-to-case/leadframe:
     $$R_{\text{th}} = \frac{\Delta T_j}{P_{\text{dissipated}}}$$
   - Confirm thermal heat conduction performance across the silver-filled conductive epoxy layer.

5. **Lot Disposition**:
   - Units passing both C-SAM void area and $R_{\text{th}}$ metrics advance directly to 25 µm thermosonic gold ball or ultrasonic aluminum wedge wire bonding.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                     │
Cure Time (60 min)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                     │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
 Cure Temp (150 C)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
    R_th (<=5 C/W)┤▓▓                                  │
                  │▓▓                                  │
   Void Area (<5%)┤██                                  │
                  │██                                  │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0     37.5     75.0    112.5  150.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Inspection Tool / Method | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Pass/Fail Limit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Die Attach Total Void Area** | C-SAM Acoustic Microscopy | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ | $> 5.0\%$ (Reject) |
| **Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$)** | Transient Thermal Tester / Dual-Interface | $\le 5.0$ | $^{\circ}\text{C}/\text{W}$ | $> 5.0\ ^{\circ}\text{C}/\text{W}$ (Reject) |
| **Epoxy Pre-Inspection Curing Profile** | Convection Oven Data Logger | $150 \pm 5$ / $60 \pm 2$ | $^{\circ}\text{C}$ / $\text{min}$ | $< 145\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ or $< 58\ \text{min}$ (Hold) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - *Die Attach Material & Cure Condition*: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ for $60\ \text{minutes}$.
  - *Thermal Resistance Target*: Thermal resistance $R_{\text{th}} \le 5\ ^{\circ}\text{C}/\text{W}$.
  - *Acoustic Inspection Target*: Total void area under the DRAM die $< 5\%$ determined via scanning acoustic microscopy.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM acoustic impedance matching requires deionized water coupling, which introduces immediate galvanic and surface corrosion risks to exposed 100 um x 100 um aluminum bond pads prior to wirebonding. Furthermore, junction-to-case transient thermal measurement (JEDEC JESD51-14) requires accurate calibration of the DRAM substrate temperature-sensing diode or internal heater circuit; any parasitic resistance variation in the leadframe clamp interface directly skews the extraction of junction-to-case thermal resistance (R_th_jc).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Scanning acoustic microscopy in C-mode (C-SAM) operating at 100 MHz to 230 MHz transducer frequency must gate specifically on the silicon-to-conductive-epoxy interface and epoxy-to-leadframe paddle interface. Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C typically exhibits entrapment voids at the die corners or center cross-junction if dispense squeeze-out is non-uniform. Phase-inversion of the acoustic reflection echo is mandatory to distinguish true mechanical delamination voids (acoustic impedance Z_air ~ 0.0004 MRayl yielding negative reflection coefficient) from high-density Ag-filler agglomerations.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic microscopy transducers with high-frequency acoustic lenses (e.g. 100–230 MHz LiNbO3 or PVDF elements) and specialized transient thermal testers (e.g. Mentor Graphics MicReD T3Ster) have long procurement lead times and high calibration maintenance overhead in domestic packaging facilities. In addition, immersion immersion drying consumables (electronic grade IPA, high-purity N2 blowguns) must be tightly controlled to avoid line starvation during continuous MPW pilot packaging runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The post-cure C-SAM inspection gate introduces a major bottleneck in cycle time (roughly 3–5 minutes per leadframe strip immersion, raster scan, and post-immersion bake-out). Metrology sampling must balance 100% inline inspection for initial NPI/pilot runs with an AQL statistical sampling plan (e.g. 5 units per strip) once the cross/dot-matrix dispense recipe stabilizes, preventing queue-time violations before thermosonic gold ball or ultrasonic Al wedge wirebonding.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Moisture entrapment and pad corrosion: Residual DI water trapped in package crevices post-acoustic scan causes galvanic corrosion on 100 um Al pads and blister-induced delamination during wirebond preheat at 150°C.
1. Acoustic phase-inversion misinterpretation: Failure to monitor echo polarity causes high-density silver particle clustering or meniscus fillets to be falsely classified as interfacial voids, skewing yield metrics.
1. Thermal bottleneck due to localized void clustering: Even if total void percentage remains below 5%, clustering directly beneath high-power peripheral charge pump/wordline booster circuitry causes localized hot spots exceeding junction limits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-2-3-01` | **C-SAM High-Frequency Acoustic Die Attach Void and Delamination Analysis** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (PVA TePla / Sonix or equivalent) equipped with a 100-230 MHz focused high-frequency transducer, degassed deionized water coupling immersion tank, and automated image void-fraction quantification software. | 1. Immerse the cured leadframe strip into the temperature-stabilized (22°C-25°C) degassed DI water acoustic tank. 2. Align the 100 MHz/230 MHz transducer focal plane to the die-to-die-attach epoxy interface using A-scan oscilloscope time-of-flight gating. 3. Configure the C-scan raster step pitch to <= 5 um and enable phase-inversion echo polarity tracking. 4. Execute full area C-mode raster scan across the entire DRAM die footprint (including active area and die perimeter fillets). 5. Process the acquired acoustic contrast map via threshold segmentation to calculate the percentage of total interfacial void area relative to the total active die area. 6. Remove leadframe strip immediately, perform high-pressure N2 blow-off, and bake at 110°C for 15 minutes to eliminate all residual moisture. | `Total interfacial void area under the silicon die must be < 5.0% of total die footprint; single contiguous void area must not exceed 0.5% of total die area; no void clustering permitted beneath internal charge pump circuitry; zero interfacial delamination detected by acoustic phase inversion.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-2-3-02` | **Transient Thermal Resistance (R_th_jc) Verification via Thermal Transient Testing** | Transient Thermal Tester (MicReD T3Ster or equivalent electrical transient test system), temperature-controlled liquid-cooled cold plate test fixture, calibrated Kelvin sensing probes, and thermal interface material (phase change or high-conductivity thermal grease). | 1. Mount the packaged/leadframe assembly onto the cold plate using calibrated torque (0.4 Nm) with thin-layer thermal interface material to ensure minimal contact resistance. 2. Calibrate the forward voltage temperature coefficient (dV/dT) of the DRAM substrate isolation p-n diode over 25°C to 75°C with a 1 mA calibration current. 3. Apply a continuous heating power step pulse (P_heat = 500 mW to 1.0 W) through on-chip test resistor/circuitry until steady-state junction temperature is reached. 4. Switch rapidly (< 1 us) from heating current to 1 mA measurement current and record the transient cooling curve with microsecond time resolution over 100 seconds. 5. Perform mathematical deconvolution of the cooling curve into structure functions (cumulative and differential thermal capacitance vs. thermal resistance) according to JEDEC JESD51-14. 6. Identify the inflection point on the differential structure function corresponding to the junction-to-case boundary and extract R_th_jc. | `Measured junction-to-case thermal resistance R_th_jc must be <= 5.0 °C/W across all tested samples. Repeatability across 3 consecutive transient thermal pulses must be within ± 0.2 °C/W.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (chemical resistant, double-gloved during cleaning), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Class 10,000 / ISO 7 cleanroom ESD smock and grounded conductive heel straps, Vapor respirator (half-face mask with organic vapor cartridge) for IPA solvent handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with IPA: Immediately flush with clean water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated cleanroom apparel. For eye contact: Rinse cautiously with sterile eyewash for 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation. For inhalation of solvent vapors: Move personnel to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing becomes labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Maintain acoustic microscopy workstation and drying station under cleanroom bench laminar downflow hood with dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) operating at a minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) to safely vent evaporating IPA drying solvents.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA solvent must be collected in closed, grounded, flammable-waste stainless steel carboys labeled 'Hazardous Flammable Solvent Waste' and transferred to an EPA/DOT certified chemical recycling contractor. Acoustic tank DI water must be tested for dissolved silver/organic residues prior to neutral discharge into the cleanroom industrial wastewater neutralization system (pH 6.5–8.5).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI Grade 3/4) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Deionized Water (DI Water)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I Cleanroom Grade (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-cured silver-filled epoxy die attach at 150°C/60min; cooled to ambient; leadframe and DRAM 100 um Al bonding pads dry and free of particulate contamination or epoxy bleed-out.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: 100% dry, vacuum-baked post-immersion surface with zero residual moisture; clean 100 um x 100 um Al bonding pads with contact angle < 20 deg ready for ultrasonic ball/wedge wirebonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding allowable air queue time causes ambient airborne moisture and organic contamination absorption on 100 um Al bond pads, precipitating high bond liftoff rates during ultrasonic wirebonding and micro-corrosion degradation under leadframe humidity bias testing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete metrological verification of die attach structural integrity and thermal dissipation performance for 180nm DRAM dies mounted with Ablebond 84-1LMIS. Verification confirms void area < 5% via high-frequency C-SAM acoustic inspection and junction-to-case thermal resistance R_th_jc <= 5°C/W via transient thermal structure function analysis, leaving the die and pads dry and pristine for wirebonding.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_VOID_INSPECTION_MAP_GEN3_DRAM.tiff`
- [ ] `THERMAL_TRANSIENT_STRUCTURE_FUNCTION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `DIE_ATTACH_METROLOGY_SUMMARY_DATA.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total interfacial void percentage under 180nm DRAM die** | `< 5.0 %` | +0.0 %, -5.0 % | High-frequency (100-230 MHz) C-mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy image segmentation analysis |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Junction-to-case thermal resistance (R_th_jc)** | `<= 5.0 °C/W` | +0.0 °C/W, -1.5 °C/W | Transient thermal electrical measurement (JEDEC JESD51-14) using deconvolution structure functions |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum single contiguous void fraction** | `<= 0.5 %` | +0.0 %, -0.5 % | Automated C-SAM morphological cluster and area quantification |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal metrology engineering signoff requires 100% compliance on all tested units across the strip: total void area < 5.0%, no single void > 0.5%, verified R_th_jc <= 5.0 °C/W, zero observable moisture residue or pad staining verified via post-bake optical inspection, and complete archival of raw acoustic TIFFs and transient thermal PDFs in the tapeout repository.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) Die-Attach Void & Bondline Metrology

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) at the die-attach interface is the sole non-destructive gate before wirebonding. Acoustic impedance mismatch (Z = rho * v) between cured silver-filled epoxy (~5-8 MRayl), copper leadframe (~40 MRayl), and backside silicon (~19.7 MRayl) creates high-reflection coefficients; however, resolving bondline thickness (BLT) variations of 25-35 um requires high-frequency transducers (>=100-230 MHz) where ultrasonic attenuation in water and the die substrate severely limits penetration depth and signal-to-noise ratio. The gate delay and trigger calibration must be phase-locked to isolate the epoxy-to-paddle interface from top-surface reflections.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Silver epoxy dispense patterns (e.g., cross, multi-dot, or star) frequently entrap micro-voids during die placement when wetting velocity exceeds epoxy displacement rate. According to MIL-STD-883 Method 2030, total die-attach voiding must not exceed 10-15% of the total chip area, with single void limits <5% and zero contiguous void bridging across corners to prevent local thermal hot-spot generation in 180nm DRAM sensing circuitry and localized thermal runaway. Acoustic polarity inversion (negative phase shift) must be rigorously analyzed to differentiate delamination/voiding (epoxy-air interface) from silver filler agglomeration.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: CSAM immersion tank transducers with specialized acoustic focal lengths (e.g., Sonix, PVA TePla, or Sonoscan 150 MHz UHF transducers) have 12-18 week procurement lead times and high fragility. Furthermore, sourcing semiconductor-grade deionized water (DIW) with resistivity >= 18.0 MOhm*cm and degassing membrane contractors (<1 ppm dissolved oxygen/nitrogen) is required for the immersion coupling bath to prevent micro-bubble nucleation on leadframe surfaces, which yields false-positive void flags.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: CSAM mapping represents an inline throughput bottleneck. At 0.5 um scan step resolution over an 8x12 unit DRAM leadframe strip, image acquisition exceeds 4.5 minutes per strip. Project schedule risk demands batch statistical sampling (AQL 0.65 Level II) during steady-state production rather than 100% strip inspection, while maintaining 100% C-SAM inspection across pilot lots (N=500 units) to freeze the dispense volume and bondhead touchdown parameters.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-bubble entrapment in coupling DI water bath causing false-positive acoustic voiding detection and unjustified lot quarantine.
1. Die-tilt resulting in uneven bondline thickness (BLT) where acoustic focus drifts outside the focal gate depth across the die plane, leading to corrupted void area quantification.
1. Delamination propagation at leadframe-epoxy interface during reflow/curing thermal expansion (CTE mismatch: Cu ~16.5 ppm/K vs Si ~2.6 ppm/K) masked by low-frequency transducer ringing.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-3-01` | **CSAM Die-Attach Total Interface Void Area and Single-Void Screening Metrology** | Sonoscan / PVA TePla C-SAM with 150 MHz focused transducer (Focal length = 0.50 inch, F-number = 2), degassed DI water tank (<0.5 ppm dissolved O2), automated X-Y-Z raster scanner. | 1. Immerse leadframe strip into degassed DI water bath ensuring no surface bubbles adhere to die backside. 2. Align transducer normal to die center; optimize pulser-receiver gain and damping to obtain 80% full-screen height (FSH) A-scan echo from die-paddle interface. 3. Set C-mode time-of-flight gate across the inverted phase peak. 4. Execute raster scan at 10 um resolution across all leadframe strip units. 5. Process acoustic C-scan contrast map using automated threshold segmentation to compute total void percentage and largest contiguous void area per die. | `Total void area <= 10.0% of die area; single void area <= 3.0% of die area; zero voiding within 100 um of die perimeter; zero phase-inversion bridge across die corners.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-3-02` | **Acoustic Time-of-Flight Bondline Thickness (BLT) and Die-Tilt Measurement** | High-Frequency CSAM (230 MHz UHF acoustic transducer) with 10 GHz digital oscilloscope time-of-flight (ToF) acquisition module, automated stage leveler. | 1. Position transducer over 4 die corners and center point. 2. Capture acoustic A-scan waveforms at each coordinate. 3. Measure delta-T (time differential between reflection echo from top of epoxy bondline and bottom reflection from leadframe surface). 4. Calculate BLT = (v_epoxy * delta-T) / 2. 5. Compute die tilt as maximum delta in BLT between opposite corners (Delta_BLT = BLT_max - BLT_min). | `Nominal bondline thickness (BLT) between 25.0 um and 35.0 um; die tilt (BLT_max - BLT_min) <= 5.0 um across entire 180nm DRAM die.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, minimum 6 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash goggles, Antistatic ESD-safe cleanroom coat and safety footwear, N95/cleanroom face mask for particulate and water aerosol protection
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with IPA or bacteriostat: flush with copious running DI water for >=15 min. Eye contact: irrigate eyes at eyewash station for 15 min while holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation. Inhalation: remove personnel to fresh air. CSAM immersion tank presents electrical immersion shock risk: verify daily GFCI trip integrity; in electrical accident, hit emergency EMO before operator retrieval.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank and sample prep area must operate under local laminar exhaust hood with minimum face velocity of 0.45 m/s (90 FPM) to extract IPA drying vapors and prevent aerosolized bioaerosol/moisture accumulation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Acoustic tank drainage routed to chemical industrial wastewater line; IPA cleaning wipes disposed of in sealed, designated solvent-contaminated solid waste canisters; leadframes dried via clean dry air (CDA) or N2 knife in enclosed station.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Ultra-Pure Grade (ASTM Type E-1) | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C4) | `99.9%` |
| **Sodium Azide (Bacteriostatic agent in DI water loop, optional)** | `26628-22-8` | Reagent Grade | `<0.05%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Oven-cured silver epoxy on leadframe, fully cross-linked (Tg >= 130°C), dry, free of organic outgassing residues, and cooled to ambient (22°C).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully dried leadframe strip (baked at 100°C for 15 min post-water immersion), bond pads free of moisture residues, oxidation, or water-spotting stains.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture ingress along copper-epoxy interface from immersion immersion tank exceeding drying window causes micro-corrosion of bond pads and interfacial delamination (popcorn effect) during subsequent wirebond thermosonic heating (200-240°C).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full non-destructive C-SAM acoustic verification of 180nm DRAM die-attach integrity, generating spatial void distribution maps, individual defect metrics, and bondline thickness profiles meeting packaging quality standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_DieAttach_Void_Analysis_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `CSAM_DieAttach_Defect_Map_RawData.csv`
- [ ] `Acoustic_A_C_Scan_Composite_Images.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total die-attach interface voiding fraction across active die footprint** | `<= 8.0%` | +1.5% | Automated acoustic impedance threshold segmentation on 150 MHz C-mode scan |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum area of single worst-case individual contiguous void** | `<= 2.5%` | +0.5% | Blob analysis and watershed morphological contouring algorithm on C-SAM C-scan image |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Average cured silver epoxy bondline thickness (BLT)** | `30.0 um` | ±5.0 um | 5-point acoustic time-of-flight (ToF) pulse-echo delay calculation with calibrated sound velocity |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of units inspected within the pilot lot exhibit zero corner void bridges, total void area <= 10.0%, maximum single void area <= 3.0%, BLT within 25.0 to 35.0 um, and full post-inspection moisture desiccation confirmed before release to thermosonic wirebonding.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Acoustic Transducer Selection & C-SAM Calibration Standard Setup for 180nm DRAM Die-Attach Metrology

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure establishes the physical setup, acoustic transducer selection, time-domain gate positioning, and calibration standards for C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM). It is designed to evaluate post-cure conductive silver epoxy die attach (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 minutes) beneath 180nm DRAM dies mounted to leadframes or ceramic packages, ensuring void metrology compliance prior to ultrasonic or thermosonic wirebonding.

---

### 2. Workflow & Metrology Architecture

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Transducer Selection & Tank Preparation                                        |
| - High-purity Deionized (DI) Water coupling fluid                              |
| - 50 MHz to 100 MHz focused acoustic transducer (Focal length: 12.7 mm / 0.5")  |
+---------------------------------------+----------------------------------------+
                                        |
                                        v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| A-Scan RF Waveform Time-Flight & Gate Calibration                              |
| - Measure ToF across Silicon Die -> Die-Attach (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) Interface   |
| - Set Hardware Receiver Gate precisely to Silicon/Epoxy Interface             |
| - Invert phase gate to identify acoustic impedance drop (Delamination/Void)   |
+---------------------------------------+----------------------------------------+
                                        |
                                        v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Calibration Standard Verification & Scanning Execution                         |
| - Scan flat-bottom hole (FBH) calibration coupon                               |
| - Execute raster scan over DRAM die area with step resolution <= 10 um         |
| - Quantify void area percentage & confirm R_th conformance                     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Transducer Selection & Acoustic Coupling Setup
1. **Transducer Selection**:
   - For penetrating typical silicon bulk thickness (approx. 200–400 $\mu\text{m}$) down to the die-attach plane while resolving micro-voids, select a high-frequency, short focal length transducer:
     - Center Frequency ($f_c$): **50 MHz to 100 MHz** (narrow band/broadband pulse).
     - Focal Length: **12.7 mm (0.5 inch)** with sapphire delay line.
2. **Coupling Medium**:
   - Submerge sample holder in degassed, deionized (DI) water ($>18\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$) maintained at **22°C to 25°C** to eliminate microbubble artifacts.

#### Step 2: A-Scan RF Echo Alignment & Focal Plane Positioning
1. Place a reference 180nm DRAM leadframe assembly into the immersion fixture.
2. Align the transducer normal to the top silicon surface using electronic pulse-echo tilt leveling (maximize peak amplitude of the front-surface echo).
3. Adjust the Z-axis focus stage until the acoustic focal zone is located at the die-to-substrate interface:
   - Identify Front Surface Reflection: Reflection from DI Water to Silicon passivation.
   - Calculate Time-of-Flight (ToF) through bulk silicon ($v_{\text{Si}} \approx 8430\text{ m/s}$, longitudinal):
     $$\Delta t = \frac{2 \cdot d_{\text{die}}}{v_{\text{Si}}}$$
   - Align focus to the second major echo corresponding to the **Silicon / Silver-Filled Epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS)** boundary.

#### Step 3: Hardware Gating & Phase Polarity Calibration
1. Position the hardware data collection gate (Gate 1) directly over the die-attach interface echo:
   - **Gate Width**: Set to encompass the full RF pulse envelope (**20 ns to 50 ns**).
   - **Trigger / Threshold**: Set receiver gain and attenuation such that the bonded reference reflection amplitude is calibrated to **80% full screen height (FSH)**.
2. Set up phase polarity detection:
   - **Bonded Interface (Silicon to High-Impedance Epoxy)**: Positive initial phase excursion.
   - **Delamination / Void Interface (Silicon to Air/Vacuum)**: Negative phase excursion (180° phase inversion due to lower acoustic impedance $Z_{\text{air}} \ll Z_{\text{Si}}$) with higher reflected amplitude.

#### Step 4: Calibration Standard Run & Raster Scan Metrology
1. Run a known calibration standard (calibrated flat-bottom hole defect coupon or pre-characterized reference package).
2. Set raster scan parameters across the DRAM chip active area:
   - X-Y scanning step pitch: $\le 10\ \mu\text{m} \times 10\ \mu\text{m}$.
   - Pulser repetition rate synchronized to motor stage velocity (ensuring zero skipped scan lines).
3. Acquire the C-SAM acoustic image and run automated threshold binarization to calculate total void area relative to total die surface area.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Units | Tolerance / Pass Condition | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die-Attach Void Area** | $< 5.0$ | `%` of total die area | Maximum allowable limit per Mil-Std-883 / DRAM Spec | C-SAM automated threshold image integration |
| **Die-Attach Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | $\le 5.0$ | $^{\circ}\text{C/W}$ | Upper limit post-cure ($150^{\circ}\text{C}$, 60 min) | Transient thermal tester / junction metrology |
| **Wire Pull Strength (Post-C-SAM Verification)** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{grams-force (gf)}$ | Failure must occur in wire span, not bond interface | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 (for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire) |
| **Transducer Center Frequency** | $50 \text{ to } 100$ | $\text{MHz}$ | Nominal operational band for leadframe die attach | RF spectrum analyzer / transducer factory calibration |

---

### 5. Context Sources & Literature References
- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - *Ablebond 84-1LMIS* silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at **$150^{\circ}\text{C}$ for 60 minutes**.
  - Void area under die **$< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy**.
  - Thermal resistance requirement **$R_{th} \le 5^{\circ}\text{C/W}$**.
  - Subsequent mechanical quality standard: **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011** requiring wire pull test force **$\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$** for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - 180nm DRAM unit cell integration context and geometry constraints.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Transducer acoustic focal length (F-number) and frequency selection must balance penetration depth through the copper leadframe/epoxy matrix against axial spatial resolution. For a 180nm DRAM die (typically 250-350 um silicon thickness on a 150 um Cu leadframe), selecting a 100-230 MHz transducer without optimizing water-path de-bubbling and ultrasonic gating will cause the die-attach interface reflection to merge with front-surface ringing.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating C-SAM for Ag-epoxy die attach requires a dedicated acoustic impedance standard replicating the Cu-leadframe (Z ~ 44.3 MRayl), Ag-epoxy (Z ~ 6-8 MRayl), and Si die (Z ~ 19.7 MRayl) acoustic stacks. Failure to machine calibrated flat-bottom holes (FBH) down to 25 um diameter in the calibration coupon will prevent accurate void area quantification per MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 / J-STD-035.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-high-frequency acoustic transducers (100 MHz to 230 MHz spherically focused immersion transducers) have 16-24 week lead times and single-source dependencies (e.g., Sonoscan/Nordson or PVA TePla). Procurement must bundle dual-frequency transducers (50 MHz for macro package inspection and 150 MHz for bondline delamination) with NIST-traceable aluminum/copper acoustic resolution target blocks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-SAM setup must integrate with the line's MES and be completed prior to pilot leadframe dispensing validation. Calibration cycle time must not exceed 15 minutes per batch changeover, and transducer alignment verification must be fully automated to maintain the target assembly takt time of 45 seconds per strip.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Transducer center frequency mismatch resulting in pulse overlap between leadframe-epoxy and epoxy-silicon interfaces, blinding void detection below 50 um.
1. Acoustic couplant (deionized water) micro-bubble adhesion on the transducer lens or leadframe paddle, causing false positive void indications.
1. Inaccurate time-of-flight gating causing acoustic reflection inversion from copper leadframe flags to be falsely binned as delamination.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-3-1-01` | **Acoustic Transducer Center Frequency & Axial Resolution Verification** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (Nordson Sonoscan Gen7 or equivalent) equipped with 150 MHz UHF transducer (0.25 inch focal length), 1 GHz digital oscilloscope / pulser-receiver module, NIST-traceable acoustic calibration block. | 1. Align 150 MHz transducer normal to the polished front surface of the calibration block. 2. Capture RF A-scan waveform of the front-surface echo using 50 Ohm input impedance at 1 GS/s. 3. # Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Frequency C-Scan Reflection Acoustic Imaging of Die-Paddle Interface

**Context Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > BEOL & Packaging > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe > Silver Epoxy Dispensing and DRAM Die Attach Curing > Silver-Filled Conductive Epoxy Leadframe Dispense Pattern Optimization > Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) Die-Attach Void & Bondline Metrology > **High-Frequency C-Scan Reflection Acoustic Imaging of Die-Paddle Interface**  
**Generation**: Gen 3 (nm) | **Action Type**: Make | **Owner**: Domain Expert AI (Multi-Agent Council)

---

### Process Flowchart

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Sample Immersion in  │
│   Degassed DI Water   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Transducer Acoustic  │
│   Alignment & Focus   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│        RF Echo        │
│  Time-of-Flight Gate  │
│        Setting        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Raster C-Scan Data   │
│      Acquisition      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     A-Scan Phase      │
│    Inversion & FFT    │
│       Metrology       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Automated Void Area  │
│     & R_th Defect     │
│    Classification     │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Acoustic Tank & Couplant Preparation**:
   - Fill the scanning acoustic microscope (C-SAM) immersion basin with deionized (DI) water couplant maintained at $22 \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Degas DI water using an inline vacuum membrane degassing system until dissolved oxygen levels drop below $1.0\text{ ppm}$ to eliminate micro-bubble ultrasonic scattering.
   - Clean the cured DRAM package leadframe (mounted with silver-filled conductive epoxy such as Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$) with dry ionized nitrogen ($N_2$) at $30\text{ psi}$ prior to fixture clamping.

2. **Transducer Setup & Focal Alignment**:
   - Mount a high-frequency spherical focus acoustic transducer operating at nominal center frequency $f_0 = 100\text{ to }230\text{ MHz}$ (focal length $F = 12.7\text{ mm}$, acoustic lens aperture $D = 6.35\text{ mm}$).
   - Submerge transducer and align optical normal axis perpendicular to the DRAM die top surface using a motorized 5-axis stage ($X, Y, Z, \theta_x, \theta_y$) with tilt error $< 0.05^\circ$.
   - Drive transducer pulser/receiver with an impulse excitation voltage of $-150\text{ V}$ to $-250\text{ V}$ and pulse width matched to half-period resonance ($2.5\text{ to }5.0\text{ ns}$).

3. **Time-of-Flight (ToF) Gating & Interface Isolation**:
   - Capture the full radiofrequency (RF) A-scan waveform: identify Top Surface Reflection (water/Si die interface) and Back Surface Reflection (Si die / conductive epoxy die-paddle interface).
   - Set an electronic hardware acquisition gate width $\Delta t_{\text{gate}} = 20\text{ to }35\text{ ns}$ precisely positioned across the silicon-to-epoxy bondline interface reflection echo.
   - Set peak detection mode to capture both peak amplitude (positive/negative absolute peak) and RF phase inversion polarity.

4. **High-Resolution X-Y Raster C-Scan Imaging**:
   - Set linear raster scan step pitch: $\Delta X = 5.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$, $\Delta Y = 5.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ across the active die boundary area.
   - Scan speed: $100\text{ to }250\text{ mm/s}$ with synchronized hardware encoder position triggering.
   - Acquire 12-bit peak amplitude matrix and phase polarity map across the entire die area.

5. **Phase Inversion & Quantitative Void Defect Extraction**:
   - **Phase Reflection Sign Rule**: Acoustic impedance of silicon $Z_{\text{Si}} \approx 19.7\text{ MRayl}$, conductive silver epoxy $Z_{\text{epoxy}} \approx 5.5\text{ MRayl}$, and trapped air/void $Z_{\text{air}} \approx 0.0004\text{ MRayl}$.
   - Classify bondline status:
     - Well-bonded epoxy: Normal reflected echo with amplitude attenuation and non-inverted polarity.
     - Delamination / Void: High-amplitude reflected echo with $180^\circ$ phase inversion (negative phase polarity).
   - Execute binary threshold segmentation on the gated C-scan image; calculate total void area fraction, single largest contiguous void area, and perimeter corner void ratios.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

