```text
                       │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 Thermal Res R_th (C/W)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                       │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                        │
   Corner Void Area (%)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                        │
Single Largest Void (%)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                  │
                       │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                  │
Total Die Void Area (%)┤███████████████████████████████│
                       │███████████████████████████████│
                       └┬───────┬──────┬───────┬──────┬┘
                       0.0     1.2    2.5     3.8   5.0 
```

1. **Total Die-Attach Void Area Fraction**:
   - **Target**: $< 5.0\%$ of the total die area footprint via acoustic reflection C-scan.
2. **Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$)**:
   - **Target**: $\le 5.0^\circ\text{C/W}$ junction-to-case across cured silver-filled epoxy bondline.
3. **Single Contiguous Defect Void Area**:
   - **Target**: $\le 2.0\%$ maximum single void area of the total die attach interface.
4. **Die Corner & Edge Delamination Fraction**:
   - **Target**: $\le 1.0\%$ void area within $150\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ of any die perimeter corner.

---

### Literature Citations & Verification Sources
- **Source**: *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*
  - Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cure condition: $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
  - Thermal resistance requirement: $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
  - Die-attach void metrology requirement: Void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy.
  - On-chip bonding pad geometry: $100\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 100\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
- **Source**: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench* & *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*
  - Access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), 1T1C stacked capacitor charge retention budget ($> 25\text{--}30\text{ fF/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$) defining die thermal heat dissipation thresholds.

---

*Extracted micro-knowledge recorded in [csam_die_attach_metrology.md](./docs/knowledge/csam_die_attach_metrology.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM acoustic impedance matching requires deionized water coupling. System-level integration must ensure that acoustic immersion does not induce ionic contamination or corrosion on exposed copper leadframe pads and unpassivated DRAM edge seal structures prior to wirebonding. Acoustic reflection at the silicon-to-epoxy and epoxy-to-copper paddle interfaces must resolve acoustic impedance mismatches (Z_Si ~ 19.7 MRayl, Z_epoxy ~ 3-5 MRayl, Z_Cu ~ 44.3 MRayl) with a high-frequency transducer (>=100 MHz) without RF signal clipping or excessive focal spot attenuation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 100-230 MHz acoustic frequencies, acoustic attenuation in the 180nm DRAM silicon substrate (bulk thickness ~250-300 um) limits penetration if the focal length is improperly gated. Gating must be precisely synchronized to the back-surface silicon/conductive silver epoxy interface. Total voiding area within the die attach bondline must strictly remain below 5% total area and under 0.5% in any single concentrated zone under the DRAM cell array core to prevent localized thermal hot spots and differential mechanical shear stress during wirebond ultrasonic excitation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic transducer consumables (particularly high-frequency 100-230 MHz transducers with sapphire delay lines and acoustic lenses) have single-source lead times exceeding 16 weeks. Furthermore, high-purity immersion fluid (degassed ultra-pure DI water) and cleanroom-compatible nitrogen dry-off fixtures must be secured locally in Vietnam to maintain production cadence without line-down risks during Gen 3 qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die-attach acoustic metrology is on the critical path between thermal curing and thermosonic ball bonding. The total C-scan raster time per leadframe strip (16-32 units) must not exceed 8 minutes to meet throughput targets; prolonged wet immersion directly threatens the queue time window for subsequent ball bonding.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Acoustic gate drift leading to false-positive bondline void detection or failure to resolve micro-delamination at the die perimeter.
1. Moisture ingress into micro-cracks or uncured epoxy fillets during water immersion, inducing post-cure package popcorning during subsequent reflow/assembly.
1. Leadframe paddle oxidation or ionic contamination during immersion bath exposure, degrading wirebond intermetallic bond strength.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-3-2-01` | **C-Scan Die-Attach Void Area Ratio Metrology** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (PVA TePla / Sonix C-SAM) equipped with 100 MHz / 150 MHz UHF transducer (Focal length 0.5 inch, sapphire delay line) and degassed DI water tank. | 1. Fixture cured leadframe in acoustic inspection stage immersed in degassed DI water. 2. Align transducer focal plane to the die-to-paddle interface using A-scan time-of-flight reflection peak between silicon bulk and Ag-filled epoxy. 3. Set electronic gate width to 15 ns encompassing the interface echo. 4. Execute C-scan XY raster scan at 5 um step size over the entire 3 mm x 3 mm DRAM die area. 5. Process acoustic amplitude matrix via image thresholding to segment void regions (180° phase inversion / high-amplitude reflection). 6. Remove leadframe, immediately perform N2 blow-dry (30 psi, 60 s), and bake at 80°C for 5 minutes. | `Total cumulative void area across the entire die-attach interface must be <= 5.0% of total die area; single contiguous void area must not exceed 0.5% of total area (<= 0.045 mm^2); zero voiding directly beneath the edge seal ring.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-3-2-02` | **Acoustic Bondline Thickness (BLT) Uniformity & Tilt Verification** | High-Frequency C-SAM with precision RF A-scan time-of-flight (TOF) digitizer (>= 1 GHz sampling rate). | 1. Position transducer at 4 corner fiducials and central coordinate of the mounted DRAM die. 2. Measure delta-t (time-of-flight) between reflection echo 1 (die back-surface/epoxy interface) and echo 2 (epoxy/leadframe paddle interface) across all 5 coordinates. 3. Calculate localized Bondline Thickness BLT = (v_epoxy * delta-t) / 2. 4. Compute mean BLT, standard deviation, and die tilt gradient across opposite corners. | `Mean Bondline Thickness must fall within 25.0 um ± 5.0 um; maximum die tilt (BLT_max - BLT_min across diagonally opposing corners) must be <= 6.0 um.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety splash goggles, Cleanroom ESD-safe lab coat / smock
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with contaminated acoustic bath water or solvent: Flush thoroughly with running tap water for 15 minutes. For eye contact: Rinse cautiously with water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open, seek immediate medical evaluation. In case of electrical acoustic pulser shock: Disconnect power, evaluate consciousness, apply CPR if indicated.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom laminar airflow bench (ISO Class 5) with local dedicated exhaust ducting for IPA solvent wipe-down stations (>50 FPM face velocity).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Acoustic bath deionized water effluent must be drained through industrial wastewater neutralization lines (pH balanced 6.5-8.5). Solvent-soaked cleanroom wipes must be segregated into sealed hazardous waste bins for hazardous VOC disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Immersion Couplant)** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-Pure Grade (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (Drying / Cleaning Solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `>= 99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Thermally cured silver-filled epoxy die-attach fillet fully cross-linked (Tg >= 110°C, zero surface tackiness), leadframe dry and free of unreacted amine bloom.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Completely dried (<0.01% moisture residue), zero watermarks/drying stains on leadframe bond fingers, paddle oxidation-free ready for thermosonic gold/copper wirebonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time promotes moisture condensation and atmospheric copper leadframe oxidation (formation of Cu2O/CuO passivating layers), drastically lowering wirebond shear strength and risking catastrophic non-stick-on-pad (NSOP) wirebond failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full non-destructive acoustic inspection of the die-attach interface for Gen 3 180nm DRAM packages, ensuring die-paddle adhesion integrity, compliant bondline thickness, and absence of critical voiding prior to wirebonding.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `Die_Attach_Void_Analysis_Metrics.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total die-attach interface voiding ratio** | `<= 3.0%` | +2.0% absolute maximum threshold | Automated C-SAM grayscale pixel thresholding and void segmentation algorithm on calibrated 150 MHz C-scan image |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Mean die-attach bondline thickness (BLT)** | `25.0 um` | ± 5.0 um | RF A-scan acoustic time-of-flight measurement calibrated at 2400 m/s sound velocity across 5 spatial points |

critics.systems_engineer: C-SAM acoustic impedance matching requires deionized water coupling. System-level integration must ensure that acoustic immersion does not induce ionic contamination or corrosion on exposed copper leadframe pads and unpassivated DRAM edge seal structures prior to wirebonding. Acoustic reflection at the silicon-to-epoxy and epoxy-to-copper paddle interfaces must resolve acoustic impedance mismatches (Z_Si ~ 19.7 MRayl, Z_epoxy ~ 3-5 MRayl, Z_Cu ~ 44.3 MRayl) with a high-frequency transducer (>=100 MHz) without RF signal clipping or excessive focal spot attenuation.
critics.domain_expert: At 100-230 MHz acoustic frequencies, acoustic attenuation in the 180nm DRAM silicon substrate (bulk thickness ~250-300 um) limits penetration if the focal length is improperly gated. Gating must be precisely synchronized to the back-surface silicon/conductive silver epoxy interface. Total voiding area within the die attach bondline must strictly remain below 5% total area and under 0.5% in any single concentrated zone under the DRAM cell array core to prevent localized thermal hot spots and differential mechanical shear stress during wirebond ultrasonic excitation.
critics.supply_chain: Acoustic transducer consumables (particularly high-frequency 100-230 MHz transducers with sapphire delay lines and acoustic lenses) have single-source lead times exceeding 16 weeks. Furthermore, high-purity immersion fluid (degassed ultra-pure DI water) and cleanroom-compatible nitrogen dry-off fixtures must be secured locally in Vietnam to maintain production cadence without line-down risks during Gen 3 qualification.
critics.laya_pm: Die-attach acoustic metrology is on the critical path between thermal curing and thermosonic ball bonding. The total C-scan raster time per leadframe strip (16-32 units) must not exceed 8 minutes to meet throughput targets; prolonged wet immersion directly threatens the queue time window for subsequent ball bonding.
critical_failure_modes: Acoustic gate drift leading to false-positive bondline void detection or failure to resolve micro-delamination at the die perimeter.
Moisture ingress into micro-cracks or uncured epoxy fillets during water immersion, inducing post-cure package popcorning during subsequent reflow/assembly.
Leadframe paddle oxidation or ionic contamination during immersion bath exposure, degrading wirebond intermetallic bond strength.

testcases.title: C-Scan Die-Attach Void Area Ratio Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Scanning Acoustic Microscope (PVA TePla / Sonix C-SAM) equipped with 100 MHz / 150 MHz UHF transducer (Focal length 0.5 inch, sapphire delay line) and degassed DI water tank.
testcases.pre_conditions: 180nm DRAM dies attached to copper leadframe post-epoxy thermal cure (175°C, 60 min); sample cooled to 22°C ambient; acoustic coupling tank filled with de-aerated DI water (dissolved O2 < 1.0 ppm).
testcases.procedure: 1. Fixture cured leadframe in acoustic inspection stage immersed in degassed DI water. 2. Align transducer focal plane to the die-to-paddle interface using A-scan time-of-flight reflection peak between silicon bulk and Ag-filled epoxy. 3. Set electronic gate width to 15 ns encompassing the interface echo. 4. Execute C-scan XY raster scan at 5 um step size over the entire 3 mm x 3 mm DRAM die area. 5. Process acoustic amplitude matrix via image thresholding to segment void regions (180° phase inversion / high-amplitude reflection). 6. Remove leadframe, immediately perform N2 blow-dry (30 psi, 60 s), and bake at 80°C for 5 minutes.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total cumulative void area across the entire die-attach interface must be <= 5.0% of total die area; single contiguous void area must not exceed 0.5% of total area (<= 0.045 mm^2); zero voiding directly beneath the edge seal ring.

testcases.title: Acoustic Bondline Thickness (BLT) Uniformity & Tilt Verification
testcases.instrumentation: High-Frequency C-SAM with precision RF A-scan time-of-flight (TOF) digitizer (>= 1 GHz sampling rate).
testcases.pre_conditions: C-SAM transducer calibrated against standard silicon-epoxy-copper step-wedge reference block with acoustic velocity in cured silver epoxy set to 2400 m/s.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position transducer at 4 corner fiducials and central coordinate of the mounted DRAM die. 2. Measure delta-t (time-of-flight) between reflection echo 1 (die back-surface/epoxy interface) and echo 2 (epoxy/leadframe paddle interface) across all 5 coordinates. 3. Calculate localized Bondline Thickness BLT = (v_epoxy * delta-t) / 2. 4. Compute mean BLT, standard deviation, and die tilt gradient across opposite corners.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean Bondline Thickness must fall within 25.0 um ± 5.0 um; maximum die tilt (BLT_max - BLT_min across diagonally opposing corners) must be <= 6.0 um.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Acoustic Image Void Area Fraction Analysis & Bondline Thickness Metrology

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Inspection Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Transducer Launch &   │
│       Immersion        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Acoustic Echo Gating  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      C-Scan Peak       │
│   Amplitude Mapping    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Void Segmentation &   │
│     Area Fraction      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Time-of-Flight BLT   │
│       Metrology        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Acoustic Tank & Sample Preparation**:
   - Secure the leadframe strip containing 180nm DRAM dies attached with cured silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ min}$) into the scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM) immersion fixture.
   - De-gas and fill the acoustic tank with deionized (DI) water couplant at $25^\circ\text{C}$. Ensure no micro-bubbles adhere to the DRAM die or leadframe surfaces.
2. **Transducer Calibration & Focal Gating**:
   - Align a high-frequency acoustic transducer (e.g., 100–230 MHz focused transducer) perpendicular to the backside of the leadframe or top surface of the silicon DRAM die.
   - Adjust the focal height until the acoustic RF A-scan pulse reaches peak reflection at the silicon-to-epoxy bondline interface.
   - Set the hardware receiver data acquisition gate tightly across the die-attach interface echo (between the top silicon/epoxy reflection and the epoxy/leadframe paddle reflection).
3. **C-Scan Acoustic Image Acquisition**:
   - Execute an $X$-$Y$ raster scan over the full DRAM die footprint at an acoustic pixel pitch $\le 5\ \mu\text{m}$.
   - Record peak amplitude and phase inversion: a high-reflectivity acoustic echo with $180^\circ$ phase inversion identifies a delamination/air void (acoustic impedance mismatch between silicon and air).
4. **Void Area Fraction Extraction & Computation**:
   - Apply a dual-threshold binarization mask over the gated C-scan image corresponding to the die attach footprint:
     $$\text{Void Area Fraction (\%)} = \left(\frac{\sum A_{\text{void}}}{\sum A_{\text{die}}}\right) \times 100\%$$
   - Identify both total void percentage across the entire die boundary and the single largest localized contiguous void cluster.
5. **Bondline Thickness (BLT) Metrology**:
   - Extract the acoustic Time-of-Flight ($\Delta t$) between the die-epoxy interface reflection echo and the epoxy-leadframe paddle interface reflection echo.
   - Compute the local bondline thickness ($BLT = \frac{v_{\text{epoxy}} \cdot \Delta t}{2}$), verifying thickness uniformity across 5 points (center and four corners).

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                  Acoustic Metrology & Thermal Thresholds
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │████████████████████████████████████│
        R_th Limit┤████████████████████████████████████│
Max Allowable Void┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Void Area Fraction┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                      │
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                      │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0      1.2      2.5     3.8     5.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Evaluation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die Attach Void Area** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ | C-SAM C-scan gated acoustic reflection analysis |
| **Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$)** | $\le 5.0$ | $^\circ\text{C/W}$ | Thermal transient tester verification |
| **Die Attach Cure Profile Integrity** | $150 \pm 5$ for $60 \pm 2$ | $^\circ\text{C}$, $\text{minutes}$ | In-line thermal oven profiler |
| **Bonding Pad Pitch / Size Clearance** | $100 \times 100$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical / acoustic surface verification |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources

- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - *Epoxy & Cure*: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
  - *Thermal & Void Limits*: Thermal resistance $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$; total void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy.
  - *Pad Dimension*: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum square bonding pads.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM transducer acoustic impedance mismatch between deionized coupling water (Z ≈ 1.5 MRayls), copper leadframe (Z ≈ 44 MRayls), and silver epoxy composite (Z ≈ 8-12 MRayls) generates severe acoustic ringing; gating windows for echo separation must resolve time-of-flight differentials < 15 ns to isolate the die-epoxy bondline interface without signal aliasing.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-frequency ultrasound (> 100 MHz) provides lateral resolution down to ~15 µm for void perimeter extraction, but material attenuation in the silicon bulk (thickness 280 µm) risks acoustic shadow zones; dual-gate C-SAM algorithm must strictly delineate contiguous interfacial delamination from sub-surface micro-voiding to prevent false-positive rejection of compliant die attach layers.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic immersion immersion tanks require semiconductor-grade deionized water and anti-fungal de-aeration loops to prevent dissolved micro-bubbles from masquerading as epoxy voids; reliance on single-source high-frequency transducers (Sonoscan/PVA TePla 110 MHz-230 MHz range) exposes packaging validation throughput to 16-week transducer refurbishment lead times.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die attach void screening throughput is a bottleneck for MPW leadframe lots; manual A-scan/C-scan thresholding induces gate-drift operator error. Automated gray-level binarization via Otsu/adaptive thresholding and rapid bondline thickness (BLT) cross-verification must achieve < 45 seconds per DRAM unit inspection time to meet Gen 3 tapeout milestones.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial delamination masking caused by trapped air bubbles in deionized acoustic coupling medium producing acoustic total reflection indistinguishable from die-attach epoxy voids.
1. Acoustic ringing and echo overlap between leadframe-paddle bottom reflection and silver epoxy bondline causing > 35% error in calculated Bondline Thickness (BLT).
1. Corrosion or copper oxidation of unpassivated leadframe tie-bars during post-scan DI water immersion and inadequate dry-out cycling.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-3-3-01` | **C-SAM Acoustic Void Area Fraction Segmentation and Thresholding** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) equipped with 100 MHz / 12.7 mm focal length focused transducer, 500 MHz A/D digitizer, motorized XYZ raster stage (0.5 µm step resolution), and degassed DI water immersion bath. | 1. Immerse leadframe assembly into degassed DI water acoustic coupling bath. 2. Align transducer focal plane to the Si DRAM backside-to-epoxy attach interface using real-time A-scan peak tracking. 3. Adjust time gating window (width = 20 ns) centered on the interface reflected echo. 4. Execute C-mode raster scan over the 4.5 mm x 3.2 mm die area with a pixel pitch of 10 µm. 5. Process RF acoustic amplitude matrix using Otsu adaptive thresholding to identify phase-inverted, high-amplitude void reflections. 6. Integrate void pixel area and divide by total die attach surface area. | `Total void area fraction must be <= 5.0% of total die footprint; single contiguous void area must not exceed 0.5% of total die area; zero edge-voiding or corner-voiding extending > 150 µm along die periphery.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-1-3-3-02` | **Time-of-Flight Acoustic Bondline Thickness (BLT) Metrology** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope in high-resolution A-scan/B-scan mode (150 MHz UHF transducer, 1.0 GHz digital acquisition sampling rate), cross-calibrated against dual-beam Focused Ion Beam / Scanning Electron Microscope (FIB-SEM). | 1. Position transducer above five calibrated test coordinates (center, four corners 250 µm inward from die edges). 2. Acquire digitized RF echo waveforms (A-scan) averaging 64 pulses per site. 3. Detect time delta (delta_t) between the Si-to-epoxy interface negative reflection peak and the epoxy-to-Cu leadframe positive reflection peak. 4. Compute Bondline Thickness: BLT = 0.5 * v_epoxy * delta_t. 5. Cross-verify BLT uniformity and coplanarity across all 5 measurement sites. | `Mean Bondline Thickness (BLT) must be 25.0 µm ± 5.0 µm; total BLT variation (max - min across 5 points) must be <= 6.0 µm; calculated die tilt must not exceed 0.15°.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10,000 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, 6 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles, Static-dissipative cleanroom coat, Closed-toe ESD-protective footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye exposure to IPA: Flush eyes with sterile eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Skin contact with solvents: Remove contaminated clothing and wash area thoroughly with soap and water. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Move victim to fresh cleanroom air supply. Water splash: Standard dry-down; deionized water presents no chemical toxicity hazard.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank operated in Class 10,000 cleanroom air flow; IPA solvent cleaning and sample drying stations require localized point exhaust mini-hood with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA rinsate captured in labeled secondary containment carboys for hazardous chemical waste disposal. Deionized immersion water filtered and routed to facility acid/industrial waste neutralization (AWN) after biocide inspection.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Acoustic Coupling Medium)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (ASTM Type E-1, 18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Post-Scan Rinse)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Electronic Grade (>= 99.8%) | `99.8%` |
| **Cured Silver-Filled Epoxy (Solid Residue)** | `7440-22-4` | Polymer matrix composite | `70-85% Ag by weight` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Oven-cured silver conductive epoxy die-attach on bare/silver-plated copper leadframe, dry, unpassivated copper tie-bars free of flux residues or organic bleed-out.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Ultrasonically dried, IPA-rinsed, moisture-free (< 0.1% RH equivalent) leadframe assembly ready for wirebonding, zero Cu oxidation staining.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture adsorption at cured epoxy/leadframe boundary causing popcorn delamination during subsequent wirebond heating stages (220°C stage temperature), and atmospheric galvanic oxidation of leadframe bonding fingers.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified C-SAM acoustic void fraction < 5.0% and validated bondline thickness within 25 ± 5 µm across all leadframe-mounted 180nm DRAM dies, complete with dry-out protocol signoff preventing wirebond thermosonic degradation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_VOID_FRACTION_MAP_GEN3_DRAM.tiff`
- [ ] `BLT_5POINT_ACOUSTIC_METROLOGY_REPORT.csv`
- [ ] `PACKAGE_DIE_ATTACH_QUALITY_CONFORMANCE_SIGNOFF.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total die-attach acoustic interfacial void area fraction across the 180nm DRAM die footprint** | `3.2%` | <= 5.0% absolute maximum | 100 MHz C-SAM automated interface echo amplitude binarization and pixel area summation |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Mean acoustic bondline thickness (BLT) of silver-filled conductive epoxy layer** | `24.8 µm` | ± 5.0 µm (Range: 20.0 µm - 30.0 µm) | Time-of-flight dual-peak reflection differential extraction at 150 MHz RF A-scan across 5 points |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-acoustic metrology residual moisture content after dry-out bake (125°C for 20 min in N2)** | `0.02 wt%` | <= 0.05 wt% | Thermogravimetric moisture balance test on sample witness leadframe strip coupon |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Acoustic void analysis demonstrates total void area <= 5.0% with no peripheral corner voiding > 150 µm; 5-point BLT is within 20.0 to 30.0 µm with coplanarity tilt < 0.15°; post-scan dry-out confirmed with zero copper finger oxidation, certified by Lead Packaging Process Engineer.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Automated DRAM Die Pick-and-Place and 150°C Thermal Curing Recipe Execution

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Automated DRAM Die Pick-and-Place and 150°C Thermal Curing Recipe Execution: BEOL metallization, electrical die sort (EDS), wafer backgrinding/dicing, and wirebond plastic encapsulation successfully yield JEDEC-qualified DRAM packaged units.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Electrical_Die_Sort_Wafer_Yield_Map.csv`
- [ ] `Wirebond_Ball_Shear_And_Pull_CPK_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_TSOP54_Final_ATE_SpeedBin_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wirebond ball shear strength** | `>= 18.0 gf` | Minimum failure load >= 15.0 gf across 30 samples | Dage 4000 micro-tester lateral ball shear per MIL-STD-883 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) wafer array functional yield** | `>= 90.0%` | Minimum yield >= 85.0% on prime wafers | Automated wafer probe array test with March C- diagnostic patterns |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Packaged DRAM package coplanarity & lead pitch** | `<= 0.08 mm coplanarity` | JEDEC TSOP-54 mechanical envelope tolerance (+/- 0.05 mm) | Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% passing electrical continuity and JEDEC parametric DC checks; destructive wirebond shear CPK >= 1.67 with zero package voiding or delamination detected under scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Die Ejector Pin and Rubber/Vespel Collet Tooling Selection & Calibration

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Inspect Ejector     │
│  Needles & Collet Tip  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Multi-Point Height   │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Collet Planarity &   │
│    Theta Alignment     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Vacuum Level & Pick   │
│      Confirmation      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Placement on Silver   │
│  Epoxy & Post-Attach   │
│         Check          │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Scope & Tooling Selection Rationale
- **Application**: 180nm DRAM Gen 3 die pick-and-place packaging, handling fragile crown-shaped stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) topologies and surface aluminum interconnects (Metal-1 thickness 350 nm ± 5%, sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$).
- **Ejector Pin Tooling**:
  - Multi-pin tungsten carbide needle array (4-corner + 1-center pin configuration).
  - Needle tip radius: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ to $40\ \mu\text{m}$ spherical radius to evenly distribute delamination peeling stress across wafer mount tape without puncturing the silicon backside.
- **Collet Tooling**:
  - High-precision static-dissipative Vespel SP-1 or ESD-safe rubber perimeter-contact collet.
  - Collet lip engages the die perimeter edge excluded from active memory arrays, clearing the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ peripheral aluminum wire-bond pads to prevent metallization gouging and dielectric micro-cracking.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Calibration & Execution Procedure

1. **Tooling Inspection & Collet Setup**:
   - Inspect collet lip surface under optical microscope at $50\times$ magnification for wear, epoxy residue, or micro-chipping.
   - Mount the selected Vespel/rubber collet onto the pick-and-place z-axis bond head tool holder. Torque set screw to $0.15\ \text{N}\cdot\text{m}$.
2. **Ejector Needle Multi-Pin Height Zeroing**:
   - Zero the motorized ejector cap assembly against the wafer film frame underside datum plate.
   - Position a precision contact dial indicator (or laser triangulation sensor) over the ejector pin tips.
   - Calibrate needle height coplanarity across all pins to within $\pm 2.0\ \mu\text{m}$. Set maximum ejector stroke push-up height to $350\ \mu\text{m}$ above the wafer table vacuum chuck plane.
3. **Collet Planarity & Optical Alignment ($\theta, X, Y$)**:
   - Perform two-point PR (Pattern Recognition) calibration on wafer diced street fiducials and leadframe target attach sites.
   - Align collet face planarity to the stage chuck using pressure-sensitive Fuji Prescale film or an auto-collimator target (tilt error $< 0.1^\circ$).
4. **Vacuum Line Calibration & Pick Confirmation**:
   - Set vacuum supply to the collet pick nozzle at $\le -75\ \text{kPa}$ (gauge pressure).
   - Synchronize ejector pin upward stroke ($v_{\text{stroke}} = 10\ \text{mm/s}$) with collet vacuum contact dwell time ($20\ \text{ms}$ delay) to achieve smooth wafer tape release.
5. **Epoxy Placement & Bond Force Calibration**:
   - Transfer die to the silver-filled conductive epoxy site (Ablebond 84-1LMIS dispensed on lead frame pad).
   - Apply calibrated placement bond force of $40\ \text{gf}$ to $50\ \text{gf}$ (well above standard $4.0\ \text{gf}$ wire pull threshold to ensure wetting without squeeze-out bridging).
   - Release vacuum, purge pick head with $10\ \text{ms}$ positive $N_2$ blow-off pulse, and index leadframe toward thermal curing oven.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
Eject Height┤██████████████████████████████████████████│
            │██████████████████████████████████████████│
            └┬─────────┬──────────┬─────────┬─────────┬┘
            0.0      87.5       175.0     262.5   350.0
```

1. **Ejector Pin Tip Coplanarity & Stroke Height**:
   - Needle tip height variation across array: $\le \pm 2.0\ \mu\text{m}$.
   - Peak ejector push-up stroke: $350\ \mu\text{m} \pm 10\ \mu\text{m}$.
2. **Collet Pick Vacuum & Dwell Integrity**:
   - Vacuum pick suction level: $\le -75\ \text{kPa}$ gauge pressure; vacuum rise time to $-70\ \text{kPa} \le 15\ \text{ms}$.
3. **Die Placement Bond Force & Planarity**:
   - Applied placement bond force: $45\ \text{gf} \pm 5\ \text{gf}$ with die tilt $\le 0.1^\circ$ relative to leadframe flag.
4. **Die Attach Epoxy Void Area & Thermal Performance**:
   - Acoustic microscopy (C-SAM) interface void area: $< 5\%$ under die footprint.
   - Post-cure ($150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\ \text{minutes}$) thermal resistance: $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.

### 4. Verified Literature Citations
- **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging]**: Specifies 180nm DRAM bonding pad geometry ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares), silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS), $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\ \text{minutes}$ curing schedule, void area $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy, $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$, and wire pull baseline threshold ($\ge 4.0\ \text{gf}$).
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Specifies crown-shaped stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) mechanical sensitivity, requiring strict perimeter-only collet clearance and controlled ejector pin lift height.
- **[Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects]**: Specifies top Metal-1 film thickness ($350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$) and sheet resistance ($R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$) critical to pad contact integrity during pick tooling engagement.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Tooling interfaces between the sub-micron pick-and-place gantry, the vacuum ejector pin mechanism, and the Vespel/conductive rubber collet must maintain rigorous coplanarity (< 5 µm across the die perimeter) to prevent uneven pressure distribution during the pick cycle. Non-parallel pick dynamics induce micro-bending stress across the 180nm thinned DRAM substrate, triggering localized micro-fractures in active capacitor/transistor arrays and mechanical drift during transfer to the dispensed Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver epoxy.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Material selection for the pick collet demands high-temperature static-dissipative Vespel (polyimide SP-1/CR-6100) or compliant fluorosilicone/NBR rubber with surface resistivity between 10^6 and 10^9 ohms/sq to eliminate ESD charge accumulation without organic outgassing or silicone contamination on bonding pads. Ejector pin radius (typically 0.35 mm to 0.50 mm spherical tip) and synchronous multi-pin stage stroke height must be tuned to stay below the critical fracture toughness of thinned silicon (K_IC ≈ 0.9 MPa·m^(1/2)), mitigating punch-through backside micro-chipping.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom machined Vespel pick tips and high-precision tungsten carbide ejector pins carry extended lead times of 6 to 10 weeks from specialized tooling vendors (e.g., Micro-Mechanics, CoorsTek, or Kulicke & Soffa). Sourcing must establish dual-sourcing agreements for standard collet geometries (2.5 mm x 2.5 mm to 5.0 mm x 5.0 mm die envelopes) and maintain safety stock of consumable tip inserts to safeguard continuous packaging lots against tool chipping and wear cycles.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Tool qualification must strictly integrate with the overall packaging line scheduling, specifically avoiding bottle-necks prior to silver epoxy open-time expiration. Calibration routines for ejector pin stroke velocity and vacuum release timing must be completed within a 2-hour shift window, supported by automated load-cell verification protocols to prevent unplanned downtime during Gen 3 MPW packaging.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die backside punch-through micro-cracking caused by excessive ejector pin stroke displacement (> 350 µm) or excessive pin acceleration punching through dicing tape.
1. Collet tip silicone/polymer transfer onto DRAM aluminum bond pads (100 µm x 100 µm), causing severe non-stick-on-pad (NSOP) failure during ultrasonic wire bonding.
1. Inadequate vacuum seal or collet wear causing die tilt (> 2°), resulting in catastrophic silver epoxy bleed-out or die skew during placement on leadframe paddles.

| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-1-1-02` | **Vespel Collet Planarity, Vacuum Retention, and Die Tilt Verification** | Dual optical split-field inspection microscope / autocollimator (0.01° angular resolution), digital vacuum sensor (-100 kPa full scale), high-accuracy coordinate measuring machine (CMM). | 1. Measure collet face coplanarity relative to bond stage reference plane using optical autocollimator. 2. Command pick sequence of a 4.0 mm x 4.0 mm polished test die from waffle pack. 3. Place die onto optical flat and measure resultant die tilt across X and Y axes using split-field microscope. 5. Perform surface energy / contact angle measurement on die surface to ensure absence of collet organic residues. | `Collet face parallel alignment to bonding plane <= 3.0 µm total indicator reading; vacuum hold pressure >= -75 kPa with vacuum leakage rate <= 0.5 kPa/s; post-placement die tilt <= 0.5° (<= 8.7 mrad) relative to substrate surface.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/1000 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, static dissipative), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Anti-static ESD lab coat / cleanroom smock with ground snaps, Conductive ESD heel straps or ESD cleanroom shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA inhalation, remove victim to fresh air; for eye contact with solvent cleaner, flush immediately with copious clean water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical evaluation; in case of mechanical puncture or pinch from ejector pin mechanism, flush wound with sterile saline and apply sterile dressing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Maintain local exhaust extraction on the collet cleaning bench (minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s or 100 fpm) during solvent wipe operations; cleanroom ambient airflow minimum 45-60 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-soaked wipes and contaminated collet cleaning swabs in sealed, grounded flammable waste containers; obsolete or broken tungsten carbide ejector pins and Vespel tips must be segregated into heavy metal / solid packaging scrap containers according to cleanroom hazardous waste procedures.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Cleanroom Grade** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Electronic Grade (>= 99.9%) | `100%` |
| **Polyimide Resin (Vespel SP-1)** | `25038-81-7` | Solid Polymer Tooling Grade | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Diced 180nm DRAM wafers on expanded UV tape, backgrind finished to 150 µm thickness with backside roughness Ra < 0.05 µm, bond pads pristine and free of oxidation or organic particulates.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Intact, non-cracked DRAM dies secured in vacuum collet and transferred onto dispensed Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver conductive epoxy without surface residue, pad contamination, or mechanical tilt.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time in ambient cleanroom air causes pad passivation / atmospheric oxidation and organic absorption, degrading wire bond intermetallic shear strength, while causing moisture absorption and silver epoxy skinning/curing prior to die touchdown.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full engineering validation and sign-off for die ejector pin and static-dissipative Vespel collet assembly tooling on the Gen 3 180nm DRAM packaging line, guaranteeing zero micro-cracking, calibrated ejection force, and sub-micron pick-and-place coplanarity.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Die placement parallelism / tilt relative to leadframe paddle reference plane** | `0.25 degrees` | <= 0.50 degrees | Dual-objective split-field optical autofocus profilometry across die diagonals |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Collet contact surface ESD electrostatic discharge decay time** | `< 0.50 s` | <= 1.00 s (from 1000 V to 100 V) | Charged plate monitor (CPM) measurement per ANSI/ESD STM11.11 standards |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100 consecutive pick-and-place cycles executed on 180nm thinned test dies with 0% die fracture rate, zero ejector pin punch marks under 100x optical microscopy, die attach placement tilt <= 0.5°, and all quantitative assertions verified and logged into the manufacturing execution system.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Die Pick-and-Place Machine Vision Pattern Alignment & Bond Force Recipe Optimization

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                      │
│  Vision Pattern Match (Bond Pads)    │
│                                      │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                      │
│   Collet Pick & Theta Alignment      │
│                                      │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                      │
│   Epoxy Touchdown & Controlled Force │
│                                      │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                      │
│  Post-Placement Fillet Verification  │
│                                      │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Optical Fiducial & Pattern Recognition (PR) Training**:
   - Calibrate the machine vision camera optics targeting the perimeter metallization features.
   - Register the corner aluminum bonding pads ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ squares) as primary alignment fiducials.
   - Program the pattern matching algorithm to achieve an alignment positioning threshold within $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ across $X, Y,$ and rotational $\theta$ axes.

2. **Die Collet Pick & Stage Indexing**:
   - Position the vacuum pick-up collet centered over the sawn DRAM die.
   - Engage vacuum suction and index the leadframe paddle with pre-dispensed silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) directly beneath the placement head.

3. **Placement & Controlled Touchdown Recipe**:
   - Lower the collet to the pre-dispensed epoxy target at a controlled approach velocity to prevent dynamic splashing.
   - Apply a calibrated bond force recipe to compress the silver epoxy into a uniform bond-line thickness (BLT) without inducing microcracks on the die face.
   - Disengage collet vacuum and execute a clean Z-axis retract.

4. **Fillet & Pre-Cure Visual Inspection**:
   - Inspect all four die edges under vision optics to confirm continuous epoxy squeeze-out (fillet height between 25% and 75% of die sidewall thickness).
   - Transfer parts to the thermal curing oven for 60 minutes at $150^\circ\text{C}$ to cross-link the silver epoxy.

---

### 2. Acceptance Criteria Targets

### 3. Source Context Citations

- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - Pad size: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum square geometry.
  - Die attach epoxy: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 minutes.
  - Thermal resistance: $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C}/\text{W}$.
  - Void area threshold: $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy.
  - Wire pull strength threshold: $\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$ per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011.
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:
  - Alignment tolerance progression down to $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Machine vision template matching on the DRAM active area must account for variations in top passivation reflectance (SiN/SiO2 thin-film interference) across tapeout wafer lots. Optical fiducials (crosshairs and bounding corners) must use distinct metal layers (M3/M4) to prevent normalized cross-correlation false locks caused by dense periodic DRAM cell capacitor arrays. Closed-loop Z-axis bond head motion requires dynamic piezoelectric force feedback integration to decouple collet decel inertia from static contact force.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Placement of the 180nm DRAM die onto uncured isotropic conductive silver epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablestik 84-1LMISR) requires strict bond force ramping (0.5 N to 1.5 N) and dwell timing (<200 ms). Excessive bond force leads to catastrophic epoxy squeeze-out and meniscus climb exceeding 75% die edge height, bridging edge perimeter bond pads or shorting the substrate paddle, while insufficient force causes interfacial voiding >10% and unacceptable thermal impedance degradation for high-refresh DRAM operation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Rubber/polyurethane pick-and-place collets degrade rapidly upon exposure to solvent vapors from silver paste thinners, resulting in tip warpage and particulate shedding onto wirebond pads. We must qualify ESD-safe dissipative Vespel or ceramic tungsten carbide pick tools with dual vacuum ports compatible with ASM Pacific Technology (ASMPT) or Datacon multi-chip die bonders, maintaining a second-source supplier for lead times exceeding 16 weeks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die attach recipe optimization directly paces the downstream ultrasonic thermosonic ball wirebonder schedule. Any uncalibrated placement tilt or X-Y theta offset (>0.5°) introduces automated pattern recognition failure during wirebonding, causing non-stick-on-pad (NSOP) alarms and halting Gen 3 qualification runs. Optimization runs must complete within a 48-hour batch window using dedicated test leadframes.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die cracking or edge micro-chipping caused by instantaneous kinetic impact spike exceeding 3.0 N during pick-and-place collet touch-down prior to piezo force-loop stabilization.
1. Epoxy bleed-out/squeeze-out onto leadframe tie bars and active DRAM perimeter seal rings due to over-compression, causing high-voltage leakage or epoxy fillet crowning on wirebond pads.
1. Die tilt exceeding 15 um corner-to-corner caused by asymmetric silver epoxy dispensing dots, preventing uniform wirebond ball squash and capillary engagement.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-1-2-01` | **Machine Vision Alignment Accuracy and Post-Placement Positional Verification** | Automated Die Bonder Pattern Recognition System (PRS) paired with Olympus STM7 Dual-Axis Measuring Microscope (0.1 um encoder resolution) and Keyence VK-X3000 3D Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope. | 1. Teach fiducial recognition coordinates on leadframe die paddle center and DRAM die corner alignment targets. 2. Execute automated pick-and-place recipe at 100% standard speed across a 20-die strip. 3. Transfer strip to optical coordinate measuring microscope without mechanical shock. 4. Measure delta X, delta Y offsets relative to paddle datum centerlines. 5. Measure rotational theta misalignment across diagonal corner fiducials. | `Pass if absolute positional deviation |delta X| <= 10.0 um, |delta Y| <= 10.0 um, and rotational theta misalignment |delta theta| <= 0.25 degrees across all 20 consecutive placements; zero pattern match false identification.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-1-2-02` | **Bond Force Recipe Squeeze-Out and Bondline Thickness (BLT) Profilometry** | Piezoelectric Load Cell dynamic profiler (Kistler 9217A), Keyence VK-X3000 3D Laser Profilometer, Dage 4000Plus Die Shear Tester, and Sonix Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM, 100 MHz transducer). | 1. Execute die attach on 15 test units across variable force setpoints (0.5 N, 1.0 N, 1.5 N, 2.0 N). 2. Measure wet fillet height and perimeter meniscus expansion under 3D laser profiler immediately after placement. 3. Cure units according to standard schedule (150°C for 60 min under N2). 4. Measure final Bondline Thickness (BLT) across 4 die corners and center. 5. Inspect for epoxy interfacial voiding using C-SAM. 6. ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10,000 cleanroom compatible chemical-resistant nitrile gloves (double-gloved, 6 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and chemical splash goggles, Anti-static ESD lab coat with continuous conductive carbon striping, Closed-toe cleanroom ESD boots with grounding heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with emergency eyewash for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing, wash skin thoroughly with soap and copious running water; do not clean skin with organic solvents. Inhalation: Move victim to fresh air; supply oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth with water and seek emergency medical assistance immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation must be conducted within a dedicated laminar flow enclosure equipped with localized point-exhaust snorkel (face velocity >= 0.5 m/s or 100 FPM) directly over the heated die attach stage to vent epoxy outgassing solvents (GBL and curing amines).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of uncured silver epoxy contaminated wipes, syringe tips, and dispensing needles into sealed hazardous waste receptacles labeled for toxic heavy metal/epoxy resin waste. Pre-cure bulk paste residues at 150°C in an exhaust-vented oven to solidify and chemically crosslink prior to solid hazardous waste handling.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Oxygen/Argon plasma-cleaned copper/silver-plated leadframe paddle with water contact angle < 15 degrees, free of organic contamination and oxide layers; singulated DRAM wafer dice on UV tape with zero backside particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: DRAM dies mechanically seated in uncured silver epoxy with verified fillet formation; wirebond pads completely free of epoxy splatter or airborne condensable outgas residues.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding open stage Q-time causes surface solvent evaporation and skinning of the dispensed epoxy dot, leading to interfacial void formation, poor wetting, die tilt, and total loss of joint shear strength post-cure.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified die pick-and-place alignment and bond force recipe delivering consistent, sub-10-micron X/Y placement repeatability, calibrated bondline thickness, zero die cracking, and zero epoxy encroachment onto active DRAM wirebond pads on Gen 3 leadframes.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Post-Placement Die Tilt, Placement Accuracy Metrology & Epoxy Fillet Height Inspection
**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-034`  
**Node / Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Packaging & Assembly > Metrology  
**Equipment Class:** Automated Optical Metrology & Non-Contact Laser Profilometry System (e.g., Dual-Magnification Telecentric Vision + Confocal Laser Sensor)  
**Action Type:** Buy / Inspection Run  

---

### 1. Process Flow & Inspection Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Leadframe        │
│     Pre-Inspection     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Die Placement      │
│   Optical Metrology    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Laser Profilometry /  │
│     Die Tilt Scan      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Epoxy Fillet Height   │
│       & Coverage       │
│       Inspection       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Acceptance       │
│       Validation       │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Alignment & Leadframe Fiducial Registration**
   - Transfer the leadframe strip bearing placed DRAM dies (prior to or post 150°C silver-filled conductive epoxy curing) onto the vacuum chuck of the metrology tool.
   - Activate stage vacuum ($\ge 75\text{ kPa}$) to eliminate carrier warpage.
   - Utilize downward telecentric optics ($1\times\text{--}2\times$ magnification) to register the leadframe reference fiducials and compute the coordinate transformation matrix $(X_0, Y_0, \theta_0)$.

2. **Die Placement Accuracy & Theta Offset Measurement**
   - Switch optical head to high-resolution magnification ($5\times\text{--}10\times$ telecentric lens, coaxial ring-light illumination).
   - Locate the four physical corners of the placed 180nm DRAM die and the peripheral aluminum bond pad array ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ pads).
   - Compute die centroid coordinates $(X_d, Y_d)$ relative to the leadframe die paddle target center:
     $$\Delta X = X_d - X_{\text{ref}}, \quad \Delta Y = Y_d - Y_{\text{ref}}$$
   - Calculate die rotational skew:
     $$\Delta \theta = \theta_d - \theta_{\text{ref}}$$

3. **Multi-Point Surface Profilometry for Die Tilt Determination**
   - Engage non-contact laser confocal triangulation sensor (spot diameter $\le 10\,\mu\text{m}$, vertical resolution $\le 50\text{ nm}$).
   - Sample $Z$-heights at four symmetric top-surface coordinate locations proximate to the die corners ($Z_1, Z_2, Z_3, Z_4$), keeping measurement clear of the active $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads to avoid specular reflectance artifacts.
   - Calculate total planar tilt:
     $$\text{Tilt}_{\text{Total}} = \max(Z_1, Z_2, Z_3, Z_4) - \min(Z_1, Z_2, Z_3, Z_4)$$
   - Calculate angular tilt across die span ($L$):
     $$\theta_{\text{tilt}} = \arctan\left(\frac{|Z_{\text{corner\_A}} - Z_{\text{corner\_B}}|}{L}\right)$$

4. **Silver Epoxy Fillet Height & Wetting Angle Metrology**
   - Position side-view or dark-field oblique illumination ($\sim 45^\circ\text{--}60^\circ$ angle) around the die perimeter to contrast the silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS).
   - Scan all 4 edges of the die to measure:
     - **Fillet Height ($H_f$):** Measured vertically from leadframe paddle surface to the top apex of the wetting meniscus on the die edge sidewall.
     - **Epoxy Squeeze-out / Run-out ($W_{\text{so}}$):** Lateral extension from die sidewall outward onto the paddle.
     - **Clearance to Bonding Pads:** Confirm that epoxy bleed and fillets maintain zero encroachment onto the active die surface and maintain clearance from the peripheral $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ Al bonding pads.

5. **Data Logging & Lot Disposition**
   - Export coordinate offsets ($\Delta X, \Delta Y, \Delta \theta$), die tilt metrics, and 4-sided fillet heights to factory SPC (Statistical Process Control).
   - Flag any units failing automated boundaries for immediate engineering disposition prior to ultrasonic/thermosonic wire bonding.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Inspection Parameter | Target Specification | Tolerance Limit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Die Placement Accuracy ($\Delta X, \Delta Y$)** | $0.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | $|\Delta X|, |\Delta Y| \le \pm 15.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Optical Vision (Edge Detection) |
| **Die Rotational Misalignment ($\Delta \theta$)** | $0.00^\circ$ | $|\Delta \theta| \le \pm 0.50^\circ$ | 2-Point / 4-Corner Optical Fit |
| **Die Total Planar Tilt ($\Delta Z_{\text{max-min}}$)** | $\le 5.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | $\Delta Z \le 12.0\,\mu\text{m}$ across die span | Non-contact Confocal Laser Profilometry |
| **Epoxy Fillet Height ($H_f$) & Coverage** | $50\%\text{--}75\%$ die thickness | $25\%\text{ to }100\%$ die thickness; $0\%$ pad encroachment | Dark-field Optical Edge/Meniscus Profiling |
| **Pad Encroachment Clearance** | $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ Al pad active area | Zero conductive epoxy bleed on pads (Clearance $\ge 50\,\mu\text{m}$) | High-mag Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**
  - *Bonding Pad Geometry:* On-chip bonding pads are verified at $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares, dictating stringent placement accuracy and keep-out zones to guarantee reliable thermosonic gold ball bonding ($25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire, $150^\circ\text{C}$) or ultrasonic aluminum wedge bonding ($25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire, $25^\circ\text{C}$).
  - *Die Attach Medium & Thermal Cure:* Uses silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$, targeting thermal resistance $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$ and void area under die $< 5\%$.
- **Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**
  - *Metallization Integrity:* Top-level pad/interconnect metallization consists of pure aluminum or aluminum-copper alloy (Al-0.5% Cu) with sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\text{sq}$, requiring clean, epoxy-free pad surfaces prior to ultrasonic bonding.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Cell Integration & Physical Sensitivity:* 180nm DRAM topology features delicate stacked capacitor structures over bitline (COB) and access gates ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$); non-contact optical/laser metrology is essential to eliminate mechanical shock or point loading risks to the active memory array during post-placement inspection.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-placement die tilt and XY rotational skew directly degrade subsequent ultrasonic thermosonic ball wirebonding quality. A die tilt greater than 15 um across the 5 mm DRAM die edge introduces uneven capillary impact force, non-uniform wire scrub, and asymmetrical ball shear strength, potentially inducing silicon cratering beneath bond pads or premature neck fractures during 180nm wire looping.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Epoxy fillet height inspection must resolve both minimum wetting height (>= 50% die thickness to prevent die edge delamination under thermal cycling) and maximum allowable fillet climb (< 100% die thickness, with zero epoxy overflow onto the active DRAM perimeter circuitry or bond pads). Non-contact chromatic confocal sensor profilometry or 3D structured light metrology is essential to inspect uncured or semi-cured Ag epoxy without mechanical disturbance.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Automated dual-optical/confocal inspection systems (e.g., Koh Young, CyberOptics SQ3000, or Keyence VR series) face long lead times and calibration overhead for custom QFP/leadframe strips; failure to establish robust automated visual thresholding in-house will force reliance on manual optical microscope inspection, bottlenecking packaging line throughput and risking lot-to-lot repeatability.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The metrology station must operate within strict in-line takt time (< 45 seconds per leadframe strip) to avoid violating the un-cured silver epoxy open-time window before transfer to the 150°C box oven, preventing skinning, moisture uptake, and void nucleation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die tilt exceeding 15 um across die diagonal inducing non-coplanar ultrasonic capillary touchdown, leading to unbonded leadframe pads or pad cratering.
1. Excessive silver epoxy squeeze-out climbing onto die top surface causing electrical shorting across peripheral BEOL bond pads or guard rings.
1. Epoxy fillet starvation (< 25% die edge height coverage) leading to interfacial shear failure during post-mold thermal stress testing (JEDEC JESD22-A104).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-1-3-01` | **Automated Non-Contact 4-Corner Die Tilt and Placement Accuracy Inspection** | 3D High-Speed Optical Profilometer / Chromatic Confocal Displacement Sensor (0.01 um vertical resolution, 0.5 um lateral accuracy) | 1. Position leadframe strip under sensor using automated X-Y stage aligned to leadframe fiducials. 2. Measure absolute Z-height at four corner coordinates (150 um inward from each die corner) and the die center. 3. Calculate planar tilt angle (pitch and roll) and total corner-to-corner Z-height variance across die diagonal. 4. Capture high-resolution top-down telecentric camera image to compute X, Y offset and theta rotational misplacement relative to leadframe paddle center. | `Total corner-to-corner die tilt delta Z <= 12.0 um across 5 mm die dimension; lateral placement error delta X, delta Y <= +/- 15.0 um; theta rotation <= +/- 0.50 degrees.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-1-3-02` | **360-Degree Continuous Epoxy Fillet Height and Squeeze-Out Metrology** | Multi-Angle 3D Structured Light AOI System with high-magnification telecentric lens and blue LED structured pattern illumination | 1. Acquire 3D point cloud around the complete perimeter of the 4 die edges. 2. Extract cross-sectional profiles every 200 um along each edge. 3. Quantify fillet height relative to top active die surface and leadframe substrate plane. 4. Scan die chamfers and active pad perimeter (keep-out zone of 100 um) for silver epoxy climb or micro-droplet contamination. | `Fillet height is between 50% and 80% of total die thickness (125 um to 200 um) along >= 95% of die perimeter; epoxy climb on active die top surface is 0.0 um (zero epoxy beyond die bevel edge); fillet meniscus angle >= 30 deg and <= 75 deg.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, minimum 6 mil thickness, double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Class 10,000 / ISO 7 cleanroom ESD smock, head cover, and ESD grounded conductive footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately wash affected area with mild soap and copious cold water for at least 15 minutes; do not use organic solvents to remove resin. Eye contact: Flush open eyes at eyewash station for 15 minutes and seek medical evaluation. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local cleanroom bench exhaust canopy providing minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); continuous downflow laminar air filter unit (ISO Class 5 localized canopy).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect solvent-soaked cleanroom wipers and uncured epoxy contaminated disposables into marked hazardous solid waste drums lined with antistatic polyethylene; dispose of via certified hazardous chemical incineration; do not drain silver residues into cleanroom drainage.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silver (metallic micro-flakes in epoxy carrier)** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade | `70-85 wt%` |
| **Bisphenol-F epoxy resin (uncured paste component)** | `9003-36-5` | Semiconductor Grade | `10-20 wt%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (optics cleaning solvent)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Grade | `>= 99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints
