# Standard Operating Procedure: 150°C Convection Oven Nitrogen-Purged Thermal Curing Recipe Execution (Ablebond 84-1LMIS)

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal ramp rate mismatch between the Kanthal/Nichrome heating elements and the low-thermal-mass copper leadframe boats can induce non-uniform volatile solvent evaporation prior to crosslinking, causing localized voiding in Ablebond 84-1LMIS. Nitrogen purge flow dynamics must guarantee oxygen partial pressure below 50 ppm across all chamber zones without inducing convective turbulence that displaces floating DRAM die prior to gelation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Ablebond 84-1LMIS is a silver-filled, electrically conductive epoxy requiring precise 150°C isothermal dwell for 60 minutes to achieve complete bismaleimide/epoxy matrix crosslinking and low ionic outgassing. Deviations in thermal profile or incomplete ramp-up will elevate volatile condensable material (VCM), which condenses onto adjacent 180nm wirebond bond pads (Al-Cu metallization) and suppresses subsequent ultrasonic thermosonic gold ball bond intermetallic formation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Henkel Ablebond 84-1LMIS necessitates strict cold-chain governance (-40°C storage with cumulative unthawed shelf life limits). Syringe thaw protocols (30 minutes ambient equilibration prior to dispensing) and working syringe pot life (16 hours at 25°C) must be tightly traced to prevent dispensing pre-gelled paste that degrades fillet geometry and bond line thickness (BLT) consistency on the packaging line.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Curing cycle lot throughput must balance nitrogen consumption costs with cleanroom floor queue times. In-line convection oven batch queues must synchronize directly with die pick-and-place uptime and wirebonding schedule to prevent leadframe tarnishing and ensure predictable OEE across packaging work cells.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial void accumulation (>15% total area or single void >5% under DRAM active area) due to rapid solvent flashing at uncontrolled initial ramp rates (>5°C/min), causing thermal resistance escalation and localized hot spots.
1. Silver resin bleed-out onto leadframe paddle and perimeter bonding pads, leading to high-frequency leakage currents or total ultrasonic ball bond lift-off during post-cure assembly.
1. Thermal-stress-induced microcracking and mechanical die warping exceeding 25 µm across the 180nm silicon substrate due to excessive post-cure cooling ramp rates (>3°C/min).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-2-01` | **Acoustic Micro-Imaging (CSAM) Post-Cure Die Attach Voiding Analysis** | Sonix or PVA TePla C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) with 100 MHz high-frequency transducer and deionized water acoustic coupling tank | 1. Fixture cured leadframe strip into CSAM immersion fixture using vacuum hold-down. 2. Focus 100 MHz transducer on the die-to-leadframe epoxy interface using gate-width spanning the 15-30 µm bond line thickness. 3. Perform raster scan at 0.5 µm/step resolution across 100% of the active DRAM die footprint. 4. Calculate total void area percentage and single largest void percentage using automated threshold image segmentation. | `Total interfacial voiding area must be <= 5.0% of total die attach area; single isolated void area must be <= 1.0%; zero edge voiding connecting to die perimeter.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-2-02` | **Mil-Std-883 Method 2019 Die Shear Strength Verification** | Dage 4000Plus Multi-Function Bondtester with calibrated 50 kgf load cell and tungsten carbide shear tool tip (width matched to die dimension) | 1. Clamp leadframe strip rigidly onto heated/vacuum specimen chuck. 2. Align tungsten carbide shear tool perpendicular to die edge with standoff height set strictly to 10 µm (or 1/3 of die thickness) from substrate surface. 3. Apply continuous lateral load at 100 µm/second until mechanical separation occurs. 4. Record peak force at rupture and inspect fracture surface mode under 50x optical microscope. | `Minimum die shear strength must exceed 2.5 kg/mm² (exceeding MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 baseline); failure mode must exhibit cohesive epoxy shear (>80% epoxy residue on leadframe paddle) with zero adhesive separation or silicon die fracturing.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 rated chemical splash goggles, Cleanroom-grade nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, dual-layer), Static-dissipative cleanroom gowning/coat, Heat-resistant Nomex thermal handling gloves for loading/unloading hot boats
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately strip contaminated apparel and flush skin thoroughly with copious water and mild soap for >= 15 minutes. Eye contact: Rinse eyes under emergency eyewash for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist assessment. Inhalation of off-gassed curing fumes: Move individual immediately to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Thermal burns: Immerse affected skin in cool water; do not apply ice directly.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber exhaust must connect directly to dedicated scrubbed VOC effluent line maintaining continuous negative pressure (-0.05 to -0.15 in. w.g.) and minimum extraction velocity of 100 FPM at oven collar. Nitrogen displacement monitoring: Ambient cleanroom O2 sensor interlocked with automated alarm set at 19.5% minimum threshold.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Liquid or paste epoxy residues: Collect in labeled hazardous waste bins; allow solid polymerization in controlled bake-out enclosure before hazardous waste disposal as solid non-leachable epoxy. Expired or wiped residues must be packaged for specialized off-site high-temperature thermal incineration per regional environmental statutes.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silver (Metallic filler)** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade (Pre-dispersed flake) | `70-85% w/w` |
| **Bisphenol A epoxy resin** | `25068-38-6` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `10-20% w/w` |
| **Dicyandiamide (Crosslinking agent)** | `461-58-5` | Reagent Grade | `1-5% w/w` |
| **Nitrogen (Inert purging gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100% v/v` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly dispensed Ablebond 84-1LMIS with intact 180nm DRAM die placed; bond line thickness 20-30 µm; leadframe free of organic carbon contamination (water contact angle < 20° after plasma clean).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully polymerized crosslinked thermoset matrix; leadframe copper/silver plating free of silver-resin bleed or oxidation; wirebonding pads exhibiting zero condensable organic haze.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient air queue time causes spontaneous solvent evaporation and surface skinning, resulting in interfacial voiding during cure, loss of wetting, and total failure of die shear adhesion.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful execution of the 150°C N2-purged thermal curing profile for Ablebond 84-1LMIS die attach on the 180nm DRAM chip packaging line, achieving complete polymer crosslinking, void-free acoustic verification, and mechanically robust shear adhesion complying with Mil-Std-883 standards without pad contamination.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ABLEBOND_84_1LMIS_THERMAL_PROFILE_RUN_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `DRAM_180NM_DIE_ATTACH_CSAM_VOID_INSPECTION.tiff`
- [ ] `DIE_SHEAR_STRENGTH_LOT_TEST_REPORT.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Oven internal thermal dwell temperature during active curing cycle** | `150.0°C` | ± 2.0°C | Multi-channel K-type thermocouple datalogger profiling across load boat positions |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Chamber residual oxygen concentration during isothermal cure** | `20 ppm` | < 50 ppm max | In-line zirconia oxygen trace analyzer sampling exhaust stream |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Total acoustic interface void area beneath DRAM active die** | `2.0%` | <= 5.0% max | 100 MHz C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy automated image segmentation |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Completion of 60-minute isothermal dwell at 150°C with verified O2 level < 50 ppm, zero visual silver bleed under 50x magnification, 100% passing CSAM voiding across sampled leadframe strips, and die shear strength exceeding 2.5 kg/mm² across 5 sacrificial dies per cassette lot.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-PKG-DRAM180-OVEN-001
**Title:** Convection Oven Chamber Preparation and Inert $\text{N}_2$ Purge Line Flow Profiling  
**Target Process:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) — Epoxy Die Attach Thermal Curing (Ablebond 84-1LMIS)  
**Classification:** Semiconductor Packaging & Assembly / Cleanroom Facility Line  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the exact protocol for preparing, cleaning, baseline-calibrating, and inert gas flow profiling of the batch convection oven chamber prior to executing the 150°C thermal curing cycle for Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled conductive die attach epoxy.

---

### 2. Required Equipment & Materials
- **Convection Curing Oven:** Hermetically sealed, high-precision convection oven chamber equipped with multi-point digital PID temperature control.
- **Inert Gas Supply:** High-purity Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2 \ge 99.999\%$).
- **Flow Metering:** Calibrated Mass Flow Controller (MFC) plumbed to the chamber sweep manifold.
- **Exhaust & Monitoring:** Residual oxygen sensor / analyzer and laminar exhaust back-pressure regulator.
- **Substrates:** DRAM dies mounted on leadframes via Ablebond 84-1LMIS conductive silver epoxy.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| STEP 1: Chamber Inspection & Pre-Clean (IPA wipe down, inspect door seal gasket) |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                         |
                                         v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| STEP 2: Gas Line Sealing & Inert N2 Flow Sweep Calibration (1.0 to 5.0 SLPM via MFC)|
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                         |
                                         v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| STEP 3: Positive-Pressure Purge Verification (Prevent ambient air back-diffusion) |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                         |
                                         v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| STEP 4: Thermal Stabilization & Recipe Execution (Hold at 150°C for 60 minutes)   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Chamber Pre-Clean and Seal Inspection
1. Inspect the internal stainless-steel/quartz cavity for residual outgassing condensates or particulate contamination.
2. Wipe down the chamber walls and tray rails using cleanroom-grade wipes wetted with electronic-grade IPA.
3. Inspect the door sealing gasket for cracks, deformation, or foreign debris to guarantee chamber hermetic integrity.

#### Step 2: $\text{N}_2$ Gas Delivery Line Priming and MFC Calibration
1. Open the high-purity $\text{N}_2$ supply valve ($\ge 99.999\%$ purity).
2. Set the calibrated Mass Flow Controller (MFC) to establish a continuous laminar gas sweep velocity between **1.0 and 5.0 SLPM** (Standard Liters Per Minute).
3. Ensure no gas line leaks exist across inlet fittings using an inert gas pressure decay check.

#### Step 3: Chamber Atmospheric Inerting & Purge Sweep Profiling
1. Close and clamp the oven chamber door.
2. Initiate the primary purge sequence at **5.0 SLPM** for a minimum of 15 minutes to displace ambient air, moisture, and mobile oxygen.
3. Regulate chamber exhaust back-pressure to maintain positive chamber pressure, preventing ambient air back-diffusion into the heating zone.
4. Reduce and lock the steady-state laminar flow sweep to **2.0 to 5.0 SLPM** to maintain an inert blanket across the substrate boats throughout the curing sequence.

#### Step 4: Temperature Flatness & Thermal Profiling Setpoint
1. Program the digital PID loop to ramp to the cure target temperature of **150°C**.
2. Verify that thermocouple sensors maintain tight spatial uniformity ($\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$) across the processing zone.
3. Once thermal equilibrium and inert atmospheric stability are validated, load the leadframe magazines and maintain isothermal soak at **150°C for 60 minutes** for Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver epoxy polymerization.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Inspection / Validation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Inert $\text{N}_2$ Gas Purge Flow Rate** | **1.0 to 5.0** (Steady-state sweep: **2.0 to 5.0**) | SLPM | Inline calibrated Mass Flow Controller (MFC) telemetry |
| **Curing Process Temperature** | **150** (Uniformity within $\pm 0.5$) | °C | Digital PID controller via calibrated thermocouples |
| **Epoxy Cure Soak Duration** | **60** | minutes | Automated oven recipe digital cycle timer |
| **Die Attach Void Area** | **$< 5$** | % | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) |
| **Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | **$\le 5$** | °C/W | Post-cure thermal junction transient characterization |

---

### 5. Context Citations & Traceability
- **[Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation]**:
  - Laminar carrier gas flow regulated by Mass Flow Controllers (MFC) at **1 to 5 SLPM**; PID loop temperature uniformity maintenance down to **$\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**.
- **[Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery]**:
  - High-purity gas sweep rates of **2.0 to 5.0 SLPM** preventing ambient air back-diffusion into process zones; temperature flat zone regulation within **$\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**.
- **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging]**:
  - Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled conductive die attach epoxy thermal curing standard at **150°C for 60 minutes**; post-cure acceptance criteria of **$R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$** and **die attach void area $< 5\%$** evaluated via acoustic microscopy.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Inert convection curing of silver-filled die-attach adhesives (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) requires decoupling convective heat transfer from laminar gas sweeping. If N2 purge flow dynamics exceed critical Reynolds numbers (>2000) or generate local recirculation eddies within the oven plenum, temperature uniformity across the multi-tier leadframe carrier fails to achieve the required ±2.5°C envelope. Furthermore, chamber overpressure must maintain a strict 15 to 30 Pa positive differential relative to the cleanroom ambient to block back-diffusion of oxygen and moisture through exhaust damper seals and silicone door gaskets without blowing out volatile outgassing products into the room.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Ablebond 84-1LMIS contains reactive bismaleimide/epoxy chemistry and silver flake micro-suspensions that are highly prone to surface oxidation, skinning, and voiding if residual oxygen levels exceed 50 ppm during the ramp to 150°C. Pure thermal convective distribution depends on stable pre-heated nitrogen sweep lines. Insufficient pre-heating of incoming N2 purge gas induces localized thermal quenching on the perimeter leadframe strips, producing non-uniform polymerization kinetics, incomplete crosslinking, reduced glass transition temperature (Tg < 120°C), and degraded electrical conductivity along the DRAM ground substrate paddle.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-high purity (UHP) liquid nitrogen Dewars or pipeline bulk boil-off with Grade 5.0 (99.999% purity, <2 ppm O2, <3 ppm H2O) is mandatory. Standard industrial N2 lines exhibit unmonitored oxygen spikes during bulk cylinder changeovers. High-precision Mass Flow Controllers (MFC, calibrated for 10-50 SLPM N2) and electro-polished 316L stainless steel tubing with face-seal VCR fittings must be maintained with localized second-source suppliers in Vietnam to avoid prolonged line-down maintenance risks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Chamber purge validation and thermal profiling represent a non-bypassable pre-requisite gate before executing pilot batch curing on active 180nm MPW DRAM wafer strips. The recipe qualification milestone requires stable N2 flow stabilization under 12 minutes to sustain throughput targets of 8 leadframe boats per 8-hour shift without accumulating work-in-progress (WIP) beyond the die-attach resin open-time boundary.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Plenum dead-zone oxygen entrapment causing localized O2 concentration >100 ppm, resulting in copper leadframe oxidation and silver flake tarnishing.
1. Turbulent jet impingement from un-diffused N2 purge nozzles directly onto uncured epoxy fillets, inducing die shift, tilt (>10 µm), and surface resin voiding.
1. Exhaust back-pressure oscillation causing ambient air ingestion through the oven flue during convective blower cycling.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-2-1-01` | **Chamber Inert Atmosphere Oxygen Depletion and Purge Transient Verification** | Rapid-response Zirconia/Electrochemical Trace Oxygen Analyzer (Ametek/Systech Illinois EC900, range 0.1 ppm to 1000 ppm, ±1% accuracy) connected via heated 1/8-inch 316L stainless steel sample probe; calibrated 0-100 SLPM Digital Mass Flow Controller (Horiba STEC or Brooks Instrument GF120). | 1. Seal empty oven chamber and record initial ambient O2 concentration (approx. 209,000 ppm). 2. Initiate N2 purge sequence at 45.0 SLPM through pre-heating distribution manifold with exhaust damper opened to 25% nominal. 3. Sample oxygen concentration continuously at 1.0 Hz from 5 distributed internal coordinates (Center, Front-Left, Front-Right, Rear-Left, Rear-Right). 4. Record elapsed time required to achieve <20 ppm O2 across all 5 sampling points. 5. Step down N2 flow rate to 20.0 SLPM sustain level and log steady-state O2 concentration for 60 minutes. | `Chamber oxygen concentration must drop below 20.0 ppm across all 5 monitoring zones within <= 15.0 minutes of purge initiation at 45 SLPM, and sustain steady-state O2 <= 15.0 ppm under 20 SLPM sweep flow with no individual point exceeding 25.0 ppm.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-2-1-02` | **Multi-Zone Dynamic Thermal Uniformity and Flow Profiling under 150°C N2 Purge** | 9-channel calibrated Type-K fine-gauge (0.2 mm) thermocouple profiler datalogger (ECD M.O.L.E. or Datapaq Q18 calibrated to ±0.3°C); calibrated hot-wire micro-anemometer (TSI VelociCalc, 0.05 to 5.0 m/s range) for chamber convective flow velocity mapping. | 1. Mechanically mount 9 calibrated thermocouples across a 3x3 planar matrix on the leadframe fixture (corners, side-centers, geometric centroid). 2. Position hot-wire micro-anemometer at rack inlet slits to measure laminar cross-flow sweep velocity. 3. Execute 150°C thermal ramp recipe at 5.0°C/min under steady 20 SLPM N2 flow until PID reaches 150°C setpoint. 4. Log temperature data continuously at 1-second intervals across 45 minutes of isothermal soak at 150°C. 5. Calculate maximum temperature Delta-T across all 9 probe positions during steady-state soak. | `Peak steady-state temperature across all 9 thermocouple locations must remain within 150.0°C ± 2.5°C (maximum Delta-T between any two points <= 4.0°C). Convective N2 sweep velocity across the leadframe plane must maintain laminar flow between 0.25 m/s and 0.65 m/s without localized stagnation zones (<0.10 m/s).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level B cryogenic/inert gas handling safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1), Thermal-resistant Kevlar/Nomex oven gloves rated to 250°C for carrier load/unload, Nitrile cleanroom gloves (Class 100 compatible, anti-static), Personal portable ambient oxygen depletion monitor (optical/electrochemical, low-alarm set at 19.5% O2)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation of purge effluent or N2-rich atmosphere: Immediately remove victim to fresh air. If breathing has stopped, administer artificial respiration and provide supplemental medical oxygen by trained personnel. Skin/Eye contact with hot chamber elements: Flush burn area with cool, clean water for minimum 15 minutes; do not apply salves or ointments without medical authorization. Seek immediate medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous dedicated chemical solvent scrubbed exhaust line connected to oven vent port with active pressure extraction maintaining -50 Pa to -80 Pa duct static pressure. Minimum face extraction velocity >= 0.5 m/s at oven flue connector to eliminate cured bismaleimide/epoxy condensates. Room ventilation must guarantee >= 12 room air changes per hour (ACH) equipped with dual wall-mounted O2 ambient depletion sensors interlocked to purge emergency shutoff valves.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Condensed oven exhaust resin residues trapped in in-line demisters/baffles must be collected during PM using isopropanol swabs and disposed of as regulated solid hazardous polymer waste. Purge gas effluent is scrubbed and vented externally above building roof envelope in compliance with local clean air standards.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen (Inert Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 Ultra-High Purity (UHP) | `>= 99.999% vol` |
| **Silver Flake (Ablebond 84-1LMIS Filler Outgassing Precursor)** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Suspension | `70-85% wt in resin matrix` |
| **Bismaleimide / Epoxy Monomer Condensate** | `13676-54-5` | Formulated Semiconductor Grade | `< 5% wt (volatile effluent fraction)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly dispensed Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver epoxy dot array on bare copper/silver-spot leadframe with die placed at specified bond line thickness (25-35 µm); leadframe free of organic contaminants and un-oxidized (contact angle < 30°).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully polymerized cross-linked silver epoxy matrix (die shear strength >= 15.0 kgf, electrical volume resistivity <= 5.0e-4 ohm-cm), zero leadframe surface copper oxidation (surface oxide layer < 3.0 nm by XPS/AES), ready for thermosonic gold/copper wirebonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding 30 minutes air exposure triggers premature solvent evaporation, resin skinning, and atmospheric moisture absorption, causing severe die attach voiding (>15% area) and interface delamination during solder reflow; leadframe tarnish inhibits ultrasonic wirebond stitch intermetallic formation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Validation and profiling of the packaging convection oven chamber and inert nitrogen gas distribution lines. Establishes validated laminar N2 purge flow profiles that ensure chamber oxygen levels <= 15 ppm and thermal uniformity of 150°C ± 2.5°C across the operational payload zone, guaranteeing zero copper leadframe tarnishing and complete, void-free cure of Ablebond 84-1LMIS epoxy on 180nm DRAM dies.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `OVEN_N2_PURGE_TRANSIENT_O2_PROFILE_REPORT.csv`
- [ ] `THERMAL_UNIFORMITY_9POINT_150C_MAPPING.pdf`
- [ ] `LEADFRAME_SURFACE_OXIDATION_XPS_INSPECTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Chamber steady-state residual oxygen concentration under 20 SLPM N2 sustain purge** | `12.0` | <= 15.0 ppm O2 | Multi-point Zirconia/Electrochemical Trace O2 Analyzer inline sampling across 60-minute duration |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Steady-state spatial temperature uniformity across multi-point leadframe boat zone at 150°C setpoint** | `150.0` | ± 2.5 °C (Delta-T <= 4.0 °C) | 9-channel calibrated Type-K datalogger temperature profiling during 45-minute isothermal soak |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Transient purge pulldown duration from atmospheric closure to sub-20 ppm O2 threshold** | `10.5` | <= 15.0 minutes at 45 SLPM N2 flow | Continuous datalogger acquisition of purge gas start to O2 analyzer 20 ppm trip threshold |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit signoff requires 3 consecutive qualification runs demonstrating chamber residual O2 <= 15 ppm within 15 minutes of purge initiation, steady-state thermal uniformity within 150.0°C ± 2.5°C across all 9 fixture points, zero detectable Cu2O/CuO discoloration on leadframe coupons verified by optical inspection (100x) and XPS depth profiling, and formal EHS approval of the dual-interlocked room O2 depletion safety system.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** 150°C Isothermal Profile Programming and Multi-Zone Thermal Curing Execution  
**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-CUR-150C-01`  
**Process Domain:** Packaging & Assembly — Die Attach Thermal Curing  
**Target Material:** Silver-filled Conductive Die Attach Epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS)  
**Applicability:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)  

---

### Process Architecture Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Die-Attached Boats   │
│         Loaded         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   N2 Purge at 2.0 to   │
│        5.0 SLPM        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Slow Boat Ingestion   │
│     speed under 50     │
│         mm/min         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     PID Multi-Zone     │
│  Regulation flat zone  │
│      +/-0.5 deg C      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Isothermal Soak at   │
│  150 deg C for 60 min  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Slow Boat Extraction  │
│    under 50 mm/min     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Acoustic Microscopy   │
│    and Thermal Rth     │
│       Metrology        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Inert Atmosphere Sweep & Purge Setup**:
   - Verify gas delivery manifold and mass flow controllers (MFC) for ultra-pure carrier nitrogen ($N_2$).
   - Establish a laminar sweep velocity of **2.0 to 5.0 SLPM** (standard liters per minute) through the horizontal quartz process tube (outer diameter 150 mm to 200 mm, purity 99.999% $\text{SiO}_2$) to purge oxygen and prevent ambient air back-diffusion.

2. **Digital Multi-Zone PID Recipe Programming**:
   - Initialize the triple-loop digital PID controller with feedforward decoupling linked to dual Type-R / Type-S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples encased in quartz thermowells.
   - Program the 3 resistive heating zones (Load Zone, Center Zone, and Source Zone) using Kanthal-A1 or APM alloy coils to balance convective end-losses.
   - Tune zone offsets to establish a uniform isothermal flat zone spanning **300 mm to 350 mm** in the center boat region with thermal stability within **$\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$** at the **150°C** setpoint.

3. **Substrate Boat Loading & Thermal Shock Prevention**:
   - Load the leadframes carrying die-attached DRAM chips (Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled epoxy) onto the process boat.
   - Set the automated push/pull mechanical boat loader to an ingestion speed **$< 50\text{ mm/minute}$** into the flat zone to eliminate thermal shock and prevent crystallographic slip dislocations.

4. **Isothermal Cross-Linking Soak Execution**:
   - Upon center flat-zone temperature stabilization at **$150^\circ\text{C}$**, initiate the isothermal curing dwell timer for **60 minutes**.
   - Maintain continuous laminar $N_2$ sweep at **2.0 to 5.0 SLPM** throughout the 60-minute cycle to remove solvent outgassing volatiles without turbulent disturbance.

5. **Slow Extraction & Unloading**:
   - At the completion of the 60-minute soak, actuate the pull mechanism at a controlled rate of **$< 50\text{ mm/minute}$** from the center zone to the load zone.
   - Allow substrates to cool to room ambient under laminar $N_2$ shroud before transferring to downstream inspection and wire bonding.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                           ┌───────────────────────────┐
                           │●●●                        │
      Thermal Res (deg C/W)┤●●●                        │
                           │■■■                        │
          Max Void Area (%)┤■■■                        │
                           │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
            Cure Time (min)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
       Purge N2 Flow (SLPM)┤▒▒▒                        │
                           │▒▒▒                        │
    Max Ramp/Speed (mm/min)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓    │
                           │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓    │
Temp Uniformity (+/- deg C)┤█                          │
                           │█                          │
                           └┬──────┬─────┬──────┬─────┬┘
                            0     15    30     45    60 
```

1. **Center Flat Zone Thermal Uniformity**: **$\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$** across the central 300–350 mm boat region at $150^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **Isothermal Soak Duration**: **$60.0 \pm 0.5\text{ minutes}$** at $150^\circ\text{C}$ under **2.0 to 5.0 SLPM** $N_2$ laminar flow.
3. **Die Attach Interfacial Void Area**: **$< 5\%$** total void area underneath the DRAM die footprint verified via scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).
4. **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)**: **$\le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$** junction-to-case post-cure.
5. **Boat Mechanical Insertion/Extraction Velocity**: **$< 50\text{ mm/min}$** continuous drive speed.

---

### Literature Citations & Traceability

- *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*: Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled conductive epoxy curing condition ($150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 minutes), thermal resistance ($R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$), and void area acoustic microscopy threshold ($< 5\%$).
- *Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery*: Three-zone thermal regulation (Load, Center, Source), dual Type-R/S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples with digital PID control, flat zone uniformity ($\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across 350 mm), and laminar gas delivery (MFC regulated at 2.0 to 5.0 SLPM $N_2$).
- *Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation*: Triple-loop digital PID controller, center flat-zone tolerance ($\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across 300 mm), and boat motion mechanical speed limit ($< 50\text{ mm/min}$) to suppress crystallographic slip dislocations and thermal shock.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Applying multi-zone quartz diffusion furnace profiling paradigms to Ablebond 84-1LMIS die-attach curing introduces significant thermal coupling hazards: convective forced-N2 oven heating exhibits drastically lower thermal mass and higher convective heat transfer coefficients than radiant quartz tubes, meaning boundary zone ramping rates can induce thermal shock or asymmetric epoxy skinning if leadframe carrier boats are not thermally mapped using calibrated traveling instrumented thermocouples.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled epoxy cross-linking demands strict isothermal hold at 150°C for 60 minutes with an N2 environment maintaining residual O2 under 15 ppm; failure to control the ramp profile (must not exceed 5°C/min) induces explosive solvent flashing of reactive diluents (e.g., mono-/di-functional acrylates/epoxies), causing micro-voiding beneath the 180nm DRAM die, reducing thermal conductivity below 2.5 W/m-K, and leading to acoustic microscopy interfacial delamination.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ablebond 84-1LMIS requires cold-chain integrity at -40°C with finite 24-hour syringe thaw-and-pot-life limits; batch inconsistencies or carrier gas purity drops in the N2 purge line (below 99.999% Grade 5.0) directly accelerate copper leadframe oxidation, necessitating strict incoming nitrogen dew point certifications (-70°C) and qualified dual-source silver flake epoxy formulations to avoid wafer-lot packaging stoppages.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Multi-zone profile qualification and thermal stabilization directly throttle line packaging throughput; if stabilization times between recipe loading exceeds 15 minutes or carrier loading boats require manual profiling runs per batch, the BEOL-to-packaging cycle time SLA of 120 minutes will breach, compromising MPW wafer lot turn-around times.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Solvent entrained micro-voiding (>15% total bondline area or single void >5% area) caused by excessive temperature ramp rate (>5°C/min) inducing premature resin skinning and volatile entrapment.
1. Copper leadframe paddle oxidation due to N2 purge failure (>50 ppm O2) during the 150°C soak, preventing robust interfacial adhesion and inducing post-mold acoustic delamination.
1. Die tilt and warpage exceeding 15 µm driven by asymmetric thermal gradients across the multi-zone carrier boat, leading to subsequent wirebond ball shear and heel fracture failures.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-2-2-01` | **Multi-Zone Isothermal Profile Uniformity and O2 PPM Verification** | Datapaq Q18 6-Channel Thermal Profiler with Type-K calibrated thermocouple instrumented leadframe test boat and Servomex DF560E Trace Oxygen Analyzer | 1. Attach 6 calibrated thermocouples across leadframe positions (front, center, rear, left, right, top surface). 2. Insert instrumented carrier boat into the multi-zone convection furnace. 3. Execute 150°C isothermal recipe: ramp from ambient (25°C) to 150°C at 3.5°C/min, hold at 150°C for 60 minutes, cool down to <50°C at 2.5°C/min under 15 SLPM continuous N2 purge. 4. Continuously log 1 Hz thermal and O2 telemetry. 5. Extract peak temperature, dwell time, and zone temperature delta. | `Peak isothermal dwell temperature must be 150.0°C ± 2.5°C across all 6 channels; soak duration >= 60.0 minutes; thermal gradient between zones <= 1.5°C; chamber O2 concentration <= 15.0 ppm throughout entire soak cycle.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-2-2-02` | **Post-Cure Die Shear Strength and Acoustic Interfacial Void Inspection** | Dage 4000Plus Bondtester with 100 kg load cartridge and Sonix Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) operating at 100 MHz transducer frequency | 1. Subject 10 randomly sampled cured leadframe units to C-SAM pulse-echo ultrasonic inspection focusing at the die-attach epoxy interface. 2. Measure cumulative void area percentage and largest continuous single void size using image threshold analysis. 3. Mount leadframes onto Dage 4000Plus fixture with shear tool positioned at 25 µm standoff height above leadframe paddle. 4. Apply continuous lateral displacement rate of 500 µm/s until die detachment occurs. 5. Record peak shear force and inspect failure fracture mode (cohesive vs adhesive). | `Die shear strength must exceed 2.5 kg/mm² (minimum force >= 36.0 kg for 14.4 mm² die area) per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019; total epoxy void area <= 10.0% of die area; no single contiguous void > 3.0%; failure mode must exhibit >= 85% cohesive epoxy fracture.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal heat-resistant gloves (rated to 250°C) for carrier handling, Chemical-resistant nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, dual-layered), ANSI Z87.1 certified impact and splash safety goggles, Class 100 cleanroom lint-free antistatic coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; if breathing is difficult, administer oxygen by certified personnel. Skin Contact: Wash immediately with soap and copious water for at least 15 minutes; do not use organic solvents. Eye Contact: Flush eyes with sterile eye wash solution or running water for at least 20 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist care. Ingestion: Never induce vomiting in an unconscious person; rinse mouth thoroughly with water and seek emergency medical assistance.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Oven effluent must connect to dedicated solvent exhaust with continuous static negative pressure (0.25 to 0.50 in. w.g.) and face velocity >= 100 FPM at oven port, venting volatile organic diluents and degassed amines to a thermal oxidizer/scrubber. Room must feature ambient O2 depletion monitors with audible/visual interlocks set at 19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Uncured epoxy residues and contaminated dispensing tips must be collected in labeled, vapor-tight hazardous waste containers for high-temperature RCRA hazardous waste incineration. Cured solid epoxy is non-reactive and disposed of as solid industrial packaging waste. Nitrogen purge exhaust is non-toxic and safely vented through external cleanroom rooftop stack.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silver Flake** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade (EG) | `70-85% wt` |
| **Bisphenol-F Epichlorohydrin Epoxy Resin** | `28064-14-4` | Semiconductor Grade | `10-20% wt` |
| **Dicyandiamide (Cross-linking Agent)** | `461-58-5` | Analytical Reagent | `1-5% wt` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge/Blanketing)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100% vol` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly dispensed Ablebond 84-1LMIS on Ag/Cu leadframe with placed DRAM die; epoxy fillet height between 50% and 75% die thickness with 100% circumferential wetting; zero particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully cross-linked silver epoxy matrix (glass transition temperature Tg >= 120°C); leadframe paddle and wirebond fingers free of silver bleed-out, oxidation, and resin film hazing; ready for 240°C thermosonic wirebonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure causes atmospheric moisture absorption and room-temperature solvent evaporation, leading to premature skinning, catastrophic epoxy matrix voiding during 150°C curing, and bondline delamination during subsequent wirebonding.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful programming and execution of a 150°C multi-zone isothermal thermal curing recipe under ultra-high-purity nitrogen purge for Ablebond 84-1LMIS epoxy die-attach, achieving full cross-linking, minimal voiding, and high shear strength on 180nm DRAM dies mounted to copper/silver leadframes without surface oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RECIPE_150C_ISOTHERMAL_DATAPAQ_PROFILE.csv`
- [ ] `CSAM_EPOXY_INTERFACE_VOID_INSPECTION.tiff`
- [ ] `DIE_ATTACH_SHEAR_AND_CROSS_LINK_REPORT.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Isothermal plateau temperature accuracy across all thermal zones** | `150.0°C` | ±2.5°C | Multi-channel calibrated Datapaq profile logging during 60-minute soak period |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Chamber residual oxygen concentration during isothermal cure** | `10.0 ppm` | < 15.0 ppm | In-situ trace electrochemical O2 sensor continuous telemetry extraction |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Cured die attach interface acoustic void percentage** | `4.0%` | <= 10.0% total area, <= 3.0% single void | 100 MHz C-SAM automated ultrasonic attenuation image analysis |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% compliance across all 3 quantitative assertions across a full 20-unit qualification run, zero leadframe discoloration/oxidation, and signoff approval by Lead Packaging Engineer and EHS Compliance Officer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Post-Cure Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) Die-Attach Void Inspection and Shear Metrology

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-180NM-001`  
**Node Level:** Leaf Node | **Generation:** Gen 3 (nm) | **Action Type:** Make  
**Hierarchy Context:** `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip` $\rightarrow$ `Foundry Tapeout & PDK` $\rightarrow$ `BEOL & Packaging` $\rightarrow$ `Packaging & Assembly` $\rightarrow$ `Packaging` $\rightarrow$ `Metrology`  
**Knowledge Record:** [docs/knowledge/csam_die_attach_metrology.md](./docs/knowledge/csam_die_attach_metrology.md)

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Post-Cure Leadframe   │
│        Loading         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acoustic Immersion &  │
│    Focus Gate Setup    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    CSAM Die-Attach     │
│   Interface Scanning   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Void Area        │
│  Segmentation & Total  │
│  Percent Calculation   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Mechanical Die Shear  │
│    Strength Testing    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Thermal R_th &     │
│   Adhesion Clearance   │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Inspection Sample Prep & Water Immersion
1. Take the cured leadframe strips or ceramic DIP carriers (processed through nitrogen-purged convection oven at $150\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$ using Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver conductive epoxy).
2. Allow cooling to room temperature ($25\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$).
3. Mount the sample into the C-SAM immersion fixture using deionized (DI) water ($> 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$) as the acoustic coupling fluid. Degas coupling water to eliminate micro-bubbles on the silicon backside.

#### Step 2: C-SAM Transducer Setup and Gating
1. Select a high-frequency acoustic transducer ($100\text{ MHz}$ to $230\text{ MHz}$ focal length) to resolve die-attach interface features beneath the $180\text{nm}$ DRAM silicon substrate.
2. Focus the acoustic beam normal to the silicon die surface and configure time-of-flight gating:
   - **Gate Start**: Top interface of Ablebond 84-1LMIS epoxy layer.
   - **Gate Width**: Set window specifically across the die-to-leadframe epoxy bondline thickness.
3. Perform a pulse-echo reflection sweep. Map reflection amplitude: positive acoustic impedance transitions indicate bonded regions, while phase-inversion/high-amplitude echoes denote air/void delamination.

#### Step 3: High-Resolution Raster C-Scan & Void Quantification
1. Execute an X-Y raster C-scan over the entire die footprint (encompassing on-chip bonding pad array and active memory cell matrix).
2. Apply automated threshold segmentation on acoustic reflection amplitude data:
   $$\text{Void Area (\%)} = \left(\frac{A_{\text{void}}}{A_{\text{die}}}\right) \times 100$$
3. Flag any localized single void or cumulative void coverage exceeding $5\%$.

#### Step 4: Destructive Die Shear & Mechanical Verification
1. Transfer sacrificial coupon samples from the inspection lot to the bond shear tester (per MIL-STD-883 standards).
2. Align the shear tool chisel parallel to the die edge at a standoff height of $\sim 25\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ (above the epoxy fillet line).
3. Apply lateral shear displacement at a constant ramp rate until mechanical separation.
4. Optical verification: Verify cohesive failure within the silver epoxy matrix rather than catastrophic adhesive peeling at the silicon or leadframe interface. Correlate with downstream wire bonding readiness ($25\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ wire pull baseline requirement $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$).

#### Step 5: Post-Test De-watering & Bake-out
1. Rinse inspected non-destructive units with clean DI water followed by an isopropyl alcohol (IPA) displacement rinse.
2. Bake in dry $N_2$ convection oven at $100\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ for $15\text{ minutes}$ to remove all residual moisture before forwarding to the $25\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ gold ball or aluminum wedge wire bonder.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                         Die-Attach Metrology Thresholds
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                        │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓      │
Pull Force Baseline (gf)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓      │
Thermal Resistance (C/W)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
                        │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
     Void Area Limit (%)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                        │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                        └┬──────┬───────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                        0.0    1.2     2.5    3.8   5.0 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die-Attach Void Area** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ of total die area | C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) |
| **Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | $\le 5.0$ | $^\circ\text{C/W}$ | Transient Thermal Impedance Tester |
| **Epoxy Cure Condition Compliance** | $150 \pm 2$ for $60$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ / $\text{min}$ | Calibrated Convection Oven Thermal Profiler |
| **Downstream Wire Pull Strength Baseline** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull Gauge ($25\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ wire) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

* **Source 1:** *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*
  > *"Die Attach: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g. Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at 150°C for 60 minutes. Thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5\text{ }^\circ\text{C/W}$; void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy."*  
  > *"Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$ for $25\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ wire. Failure must occur in wire span, not at bond interface."*  
  > *"Final packaging of fabricated DRAM dies connects on-chip bonding pads ($100\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 100\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares) to external lead frame pins."*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-cure acoustic microscopy requires deionized water immersion or a focused water-column couplant, creating an immediate galvanic and moisture-corrosion risk for freshly cured copper or silver-plated leadframes and exposed 180nm Al-0.5%Cu bond pads. The metrology sequence must strictly enforce dry-out bake protocols prior to wirebonding to prevent popcorning or pad oxidation. Furthermore, automated alignment gating must correlate high-frequency acoustic impedance shifts with thermal resistance (Rth_jc) dissipation bottlenecks across the memory array.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C, high-frequency scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM) must employ a 100 MHz to 230 MHz transducer with appropriate focal length to resolve micro-voids down to <25 µm at the die-attach interface without suffering excessive acoustic attenuation through 250 µm thick bulk silicon. Die shear testing per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 must monitor cohesive failure within the silver-epoxy matrix versus adhesive failure at the backside metallization (Ti/Ni/Ag or bare Si), ensuring minimum shear strength exceeds 2.5 kg/mm² (>= 25 MPa).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Sonix or PVA TePla scanning acoustic microscopes and Dage/Nordson shear test cartridges (100 kgf load cell) have specialized calibration standards (ASTM F1089 calibration blocks and sapphire shear test standards) that require quarterly calibration tracking. Any test bottleneck or leadframe coupon contamination from non-demineralized immersion water risks holding lot release of Gen 3 180nm DRAM wafers prior to critical thermosonic gold/copper wirebonding.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-SAM and die-attach shear testing act as an irreversible stop-gate: if destructive shear or non-destructive acoustic voiding reveals >10% cumulative void area or >0.5% single-void area under critical high-voltage DRAM charge-pump circuitry, the entire carrier strip must be quarantined. Metrology cycle time per leadframe strip must be held below 18 minutes to preserve downstream Q-time toward wirebonding.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Total cumulative die-attach interfacial voiding exceeding 10% or contiguous corner voiding exceeding 5%, causing localized hot-spots and premature DRAM cell retention degradation.
1. Adhesive delamination at the silicon-to-epoxy boundary during 260°C reflow simulation due to unevaporated solvent entrapment from out-of-spec 150°C curing kinetics.
1. Immersion couplant water residue or incomplete post-CSAM drying inducing dendritic corrosion or bond-pad fluorine/chlorine pitting corrosion prior to wirebonding.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-2-3-01` | **Non-Destructive C-SAM Die-Attach Interfacial Void Analysis** | Sonix Echo High-Frequency Acoustic Microscope equipped with 175 MHz / 0.5-inch focal length transducer, automated RF gated C-scan acquisition software, and Ultra-pure DI Water couplant system (resistivity > 18.0 MOhm-cm) | 1. Fixture cured DRAM leadframe carrier strip securely onto the acoustic immersion stage. 2. Align 175 MHz transducer perpendicular to die top surface and adjust focal plane precisely to the silicon-to-die-attach adhesive interface (Z-gate width: 30 ns centered on the reflected negative-polarity echo). 3. Perform raster scan over 100% of die attach area (die size: 3.2 mm x 4.5 mm) at a step resolution of 5 µm. 4. Run automated image thresholding to segment acoustic reflection amplitude: high-amplitude white reflections indicate air/die-attach void interface. 5. Calculate cumulative void area percentage, single largest void percentage, and peripheral corner voiding. 6. Remove leadframe strip immediately, rinse in ultra-pure IPA, and bake at 110°C in N2 for 15 minutes. | `Total cumulative void area <= 10.0% of nominal die footprint; single largest void <= 0.5% of total area; zero contiguous void bridging from die center to perimeter; zero detectable corner voiding extending > 150 µm inward.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-2-3-02` | **Destructive Die Shear Strength and Failure Mode Characterization** | Nordson DAGE 4000Plus Bondtester configured with DS100KG die shear load cartridge, calibrated tungsten carbide shear tool tip (width 4.0 mm), optical stereomicroscope with digital image capture (50x - 200x) | 1. Clamp leadframe carrier firmly in custom mechanical vacuum holding fixture ensuring zero deflection. 2. Position shear tool parallel to die edge at a standoff height of 25 µm (<= 10% of 250 µm die thickness) and 50 µm clearance from adjacent leadframe pins. 3. Apply shear load normal to die edge at a controlled rate of 0.2 mm/s until mechanical detachment occurs. 4. Record peak shear force in kgf and calculate shear strength in MPa: Strength = Force (kgf) * 9.80665 / Die Area (mm²). 5. - **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash and impact safety glasses, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock with conductive ESD wrist strap, Mechanical puncture-resistant safety gloves for handling shear tool fixtures
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA splash to eyes: Flush with emergency eyewash for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek ophthalmologist review if irritation persists. For skin contact with rinse solvents or post-shear leadframe edges: Wash skin thoroughly with mild soap and DI water; treat minor lacerations with antiseptic and clean dressing. Inhalation of solvent fumes: Move personnel immediately to fresh laminar airflow area.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Post-acoustic drying and IPA decontamination station must operate inside a localized chemical exhaust bench providing minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). Acoustic microscope immersion chamber maintained under localized laminar airflow enclosure (ISO Class 5 / Class 100).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA rinse solutions must be segregated into dedicated flammable solvent hazardous waste carboys with flame-arrestor funnels. Acoustic couplant DI water must pass through a fine particulate silver trap before drainage into the central industrial neutralization plant.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **Cured Silver Epoxy Dust (Post-Shear Debris)** | `7440-22-4` | Technical Particulate | `< 0.05% suspended` |

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly cured Ablebond 84-1LMIS epoxy fillet at 150°C with nitrogen purge; zero flux residue, dry leadframe finish, and pristine 180nm Al-Cu bond pads.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful acoustic microscopy non-destructive qualification verifying <10% total interfacial voiding and destructive mechanical validation demonstrating >=25 MPa shear strength with >=85% cohesive failure for 150°C cured DRAM die-attach lots.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_DieAttach_Interfacial_Void_Map_Report.tiff`
- [ ] `Die_Shear_Force_Displacement_Metrology_Data.csv`

| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-CSAM moisture desiccation residual level prior to wirebonding hand-off** | `0.005 wt%` | <= 0.020 wt% | Thermogravimetric moisture balance verification following 110°C 15-minute N2 dehydration bake |

# Standard Operating Procedure: Post-Cure Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Die Attach Voiding and Shear Strength Metrology

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: DRC/LVS rule decks must run clean via KLayout/Magic/OpenLane with zero design rule errors. Antenna ratio rules (< 250:1) and substrate tap density checks must pass before GDSII reticle handoff to commercial foundry.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: 3D Crown capacitor ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 (ZAZ) stack must achieve equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) <= 0.8 nm and leakage current < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V. CMP dishing on M1/M2 tungsten/copper features must hold < 15 nm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Commercial foundry MPW (Multi-Project Wafer) shuttle submission has an unmovable tapeout window; GDSII/OASIS files must freeze 21 days prior. Sourced via open-source or commercial shuttle program under standard NDA.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 60-120 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: CRITICAL (A single DRC rule deck discrepancy or LVS short-circuit ruins the entire multi-thousand dollar commercial shuttle run and incurs a 4-6 month spin delay).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. DRC/LVS hierarchy discrepancy causing undetected metal-to-metal bridging or floating substrate tap.
1. ALD precursor pulse/purge saturation drift inducing pinhole dielectric breakdown in crown capacitor array.
1. Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) over-polish causing severe interconnect erosion and open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-3-01` | **Automated DRC/LVS Golden Rule Deck Physical Sign-Off** | KLayout / Magic / Pegasus Industrial Physical Verification Batch Engine | 1. Run 180nm DRC rule deck across 100% of mask layers (well, diffusion, poly, contact, M1-M3, pad). 2. Execute Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) netlist extraction against golden SPICE schematic. 3. Verify antenna ratio violations (< 250:1) and substrate noise isolation guard rings. | `DRC clean: 0 violations (Pass); LVS netlist match: 100% topological equivalence with 0 discrepancy (Pass).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-3-02` | **3D Crown Capacitor High-k Dielectric TEM & C-V Metrology** | Field-Emission TEM (FEI/Thermo Fisher) & High-Frequency C-V Parameter Analyzer (Keysight B1500A) | 1. Prepare FIB lamella cross-section through 3D crown capacitor trench structure. 2. Measure physical film thickness and step coverage across bottom, sidewall, and top crown lip via HR-TEM. 3. Perform high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V sweep to extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and dielectric breakdown voltage. | `ALD step coverage >= 95% (Pass); EOT <= 0.8 nm (Pass); Dielectric leakage < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom bunny suit with conductive ESD booties, Pyrophoric precursor handling apron and dual-layer fluoropolymer gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and UV-blocking safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Pyrophoric precursor emergency: TMA spontaneously ignites upon contact with air or moisture! Do NOT use water on metal alkyl fires. Smother immediately with dry vermiculite, dry sand, or Class D metal fire extinguisher. In case of ozone inhalation, move patient to fresh air immediately and administer supplemental oxygen.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Ultra-high vacuum ALD exhaust manifold connected to dedicated point-of-use thermal decomposition burn-box and wet chemical scrubber. Continuous gas leak detection monitors for TMA/TEMAZ and ozone.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent ALD bubbler purging into mineral oil bubblers with inert argon ballast. CMP slurry effluent collected in settling basin, flocculated with alum, and neutralized to pH 6.5-8.0.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trimethylaluminum (TMA)** | `75-24-1` | Electronic Grade (99.999% trace metals) | `Pyrophoric liquid ALD precursor` |
| **Tetrakis(ethylmethylamino)zirconium (TEMAZ)** | `175923-04-3` | High-purity ALD grade | `Liquid precursor for ZrO2 dielectric` |
| **Ozone (O3)** | `10028-15-6` | Generated in-situ from UHP O2 | `15-20 wt% in O2 carrier gas (Strong Oxidizer)` |
| **Silica / Ceria CMP Slurry** | `1344-28-1` | Semiconductor Colloidal CMP grade | `15-30 wt% colloidal abrasive slurry` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched 3D crown capacitor trench structure post-DHF strip, completely free of native oxide.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Uniform ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 high-k dielectric stack with TiN top electrode encapsulation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Air exposure exceeding 20 minutes allows uncontrolled spontaneous SiO2 interfacial layer regrowth (> 0.4 nm), which severely increases Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and drastically degrades bitcell storage capacitance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Post-Cure Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Die Attach Voiding and Shear Strength Metrology: PDK setup, physical verification rule decks, and full-chip GDSII layouts pass 100% DRC/LVS sign-off and satisfy foundry commercial tapeout design rules.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Golden_180nm_PDK_DRC_LVS_Signoff_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Commercial_MPW_Tapeout_GDSII_OASIS_Archive.tar.gz`
- [ ] `ALD_3D_Crown_TEM_StepCoverage_Analysis.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Foundry Design Rule Check (DRC) Violations** | `0 violations` | Zero tolerance across full chip and seal ring | Automated batch DRC run using KLayout / Pegasus Golden Rule Deck |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) Netlist Equivalence** | `100% match` | Zero net/port mismatches, zero floating pins | Hierarchical LVS extraction against golden SPICE schematic |
| `ASSERT-03` | **3D Crown Capacitor ALD Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | `<= 0.80 nm` | +/- 0.05 nm across wafer | High-frequency 1 MHz C-V accumulation capacitance metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% clean DRC/LVS verification logs signed off by lead tapeout architect; checksum of streamed GDSII package validated against foundry MPW shuttle intake submission portal.

### 1. Process Overview & Visual Flow

This procedure details the calibration of high-frequency ultrasonic transducers (e.g., 50–230 MHz range) and precision interface time-gating in Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) to inspect post-cure silver epoxy die attach layers (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 minutes) beneath 180nm DRAM chips.

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Transducer Setup and  │
│  Deionized Water Tank  │
│          Prep          │
│                        │

             │
             ▼

│                        │
│    A-Scan Gating at    │

             │

│                        │

             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐

│   Metrology and Void   │
│  Area Quantification   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Immersion Tank & Couplant Preparation:**
   - Fill the C-SAM immersion tank with degassed, deionized (DI) water maintained at room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$). Degassing prevents micro-bubble formation on acoustic lens surfaces.
   - Secure the leadframe/package carrier onto the motorized scanning stage fixture.

2. **Transducer Mounting & Alignment:**
   - Mount a high-frequency focused acoustic immersion transducer into the Z-axis scanning fixture.
   - Position the transducer normal ($90^\circ \pm 0.5^\circ$) to the DRAM silicon die surface to eliminate refraction artifacts and wavefront tilt.

3. **A-Scan Reflection Signal Acquisition & Focal Calibration:**
   - Lower the transducer along the Z-axis toward the top surface of the DRAM die while pulsing the acoustic emitter.
   - Monitor the RF A-scan oscilloscope trace for the initial top-surface echo (water-to-silicon interface).
   - Adjust the Z-focus so that the focal waist of the acoustic beam is positioned through the silicon bulk directly onto the silicon-to-conductive-epoxy die-attach plane.

4. **Time-of-Flight Interface Gating:**
   - On the A-scan waveform, identify the secondary reflection peak corresponding to the back of the die (die-attach interface).
   - Set an electronic data collection gate tightly bounding the die-attach interface reflection echo:
     - Set Gate Start immediately following the substrate bulk attenuation decay.
     - Set Gate Width to encompass the full positive/negative pulse width of the interface echo.
   - Configure phase-polarity tracking to detect phase inversion ($180^\circ$ phase shift) indicative of acoustic impedance drop at delaminations or air voids ($Z_{\text{air}} \ll Z_{\text{silicon}}$).

5. **XY Raster C-Scan Image Acquisition:**
   - Define the scanning bounding box covering the entire die footprint (with a $0.5\,\text{mm}$ outer margin around all die edges).
   - Initiate high-speed XY raster scanning with scanning pitch matched to the lateral spot resolution.
   - Record the peak amplitude and echo phase polarity at each $(x, y)$ coordinate to generate the 2D acoustic reflection C-scan map.

6. **Post-Processing & Automated Defect Quantification:**
   - Apply intensity thresholding to segment solid bonded silver epoxy interfaces vs. high-reflectivity inverted-phase void regions.
   - Execute the image metrology algorithm to calculate total void area percentage relative to the nominal die surface area.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Inspection Metric | Target Specification | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die-Attach Void Area** | **$< 5\%$** total area under die | C-SAM Interface Gated C-Scan segmentation |
| **Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$)** | **$\le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$** | Post-assembly thermal transient metrology |
| **Die-Attach Epoxy Curing Integrity** | **$150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ min}$** thermal profile verified | Thermal cure profile logger |
| **Adjacent Bond Pad Clearance** | $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad free of epoxy bleed | High-magnification optical inspection |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Sources

- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**
  - *Cured Die Attach Specification:* Conductive silver-filled epoxy (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
  - *Acoustic Metrology & Thermal Limit:* Measured void area under the die must be $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy; thermal resistance target is $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
  - *Bonding Pad Dimension:* DRAM on-chip bonding pads are $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: DRC/LVS rule decks must run clean via KLayout/Magic/OpenLane with zero design rule errors. Antenna ratio rules (< 250:1) and substrate tap density checks must pass before GDSII reticle handoff to commercial foundry.

- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Commercial foundry MPW (Multi-Project Wafer) shuttle submission has an unmovable tapeout window; GDSII/OASIS files must freeze 21 days prior. Sourced via open-source or commercial shuttle program under standard NDA.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 60-120 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: CRITICAL (A single DRC rule deck discrepancy or LVS short-circuit ruins the entire multi-thousand dollar commercial shuttle run and incurs a 4-6 month spin delay).

1. DRC/LVS hierarchy discrepancy causing undetected metal-to-metal bridging or floating substrate tap.
1. ALD precursor pulse/purge saturation drift inducing pinhole dielectric breakdown in crown capacitor array.
1. Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) over-polish causing severe interconnect erosion and open circuits.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Title: Die-Attach Acoustic Echo Analysis & Under-Die Void Area Ratio Quantification (<5%)

---

### 1. Document Control & Objective
- **SOP ID**: `SOP-PKG-CSAM-001`
- **Revision**: 1.0
- **Process Step**: Post-Cure Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Die Attach Voiding Metrology
- **Objective**: Execute pulse-echo acoustic microscopy on 180nm open-source DRAM packages (cured silver epoxy die attach on leadframe) to quantify interfacial voiding, verify acoustic impedance boundary reflections, and enforce an under-die void area ratio of $<5\%$.

---

### 2. Process Flow & Execution Steps

```
[150°C Cured DRAM Package]
           │
           ▼
[Immersion / Coupling Setup: Deionized Water Bath]
           │
           ▼
[Transducer Focus & A-Scan Echo Alignment (Die/Epoxy Interface)]
           │
           ▼
[C-Scan Raster Area Scan Execution]
           │
           ▼
[Phase Inversion Analysis & Binary Threshold Segmentation]
           │
           ▼
[Acceptance Criteria Verification (<5% Void Area, R_th <= 5°C/W)]
```

#### Step 1: Pre-Inspection Sample Preparation & Immersion
1. Verify that the DRAM die has completed silver-filled conductive epoxy attach (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) and cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
2. Submerge the leadframe package assembly into the C-SAM tank filled with degassed, high-purity deionized water ($25^\circ\text{C}$) acting as the acoustic coupling fluid.
3. Align the DRAM die planar surface parallel to the scanning XY stage.

#### Step 2: Transducer Selection & A-Scan Gating
1. Select a high-frequency acoustic transducer (typically 50 MHz to 100 MHz focused acoustic lens) to resolve the interfacial boundary between the silicon die substrate ($Z_{\text{Si}} \approx 19.7\text{ MRayl}$) and the silver epoxy layer ($Z_{\text{epoxy}} \approx 3\text{--}5\text{ MRayl}$).
2. Perform A-scan time-of-flight (ToF) calibration: locate the reflection echo sequence:
   - Front surface (water-to-silicon surface echo).
   - Die-to-attach interface (silicon-to-silver epoxy interface echo).
   - Leadframe interface (silver epoxy-to-copper/alloy leadframe echo).
3. Set an electronic gate window strictly over the **die-to-silver epoxy interface echo**.

#### Step 3: Phase Inversion & Echo Polarity Analysis
1. Calibrate the phase of the gated echo pulse:
   - **Bonded / Good interface**: Silicon to epoxy represents high-to-low acoustic impedance ($Z_1 > Z_2$), resulting in a negative acoustic reflection coefficient with phase inversion ($180^\circ$ phase shift).
   - **Void / Delamination (Air gap)**: Silicon to air gap/vacuum represents an extreme impedance mismatch ($Z_1 \gg Z_{\text{air}}$), yielding total positive reflection with high echo amplitude and $0^\circ$ relative phase shift.
2. Invert the polarity color map to flag positive-phase, high-amplitude reflections as void defects.

#### Step 4: High-Resolution C-Scan Raster Acquisition
1. Execute an XY raster scan across the entire DRAM die boundary (covering the full die footprint).
2. Set scan step resolution $\le 5\,\mu\text{m}$ to accurately delineate micro-void boundaries.
3. Store the 8-bit peak amplitude matrix and phase correlation map.

#### Step 5: Under-Die Void Area Ratio Quantification
1. Define the die attachment Area of Interest (AOI) bounding box: $A_{\text{die}} = \text{Die Length} \times \text{Die Width}$.
2. Apply binary intensity segmentation on the gated interface map using the calibrated threshold for acoustic delamination/air gaps.
3. Compute total void area $A_{\text{void}} = \sum A_{\text{void\_pixels}}$.
4. Calculate the Under-Die Void Ratio:
   $$\text{Void Area Ratio (\%)} = \frac{A_{\text{void}}}{A_{\text{die}}} \times 100\%$$

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value | Engineering Tolerance | Units | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Under-Die Total Void Area Ratio** | $< 5.0$ | Max allowable limit | $\%$ | C-SAM acoustic interface C-scan image segmentation |
| **Curing Process Recipe** | $150$ | $\pm 2.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Thermocouple-monitored curing oven (Hold: $60\text{ min}$) |
| **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$)** | $\le 5.0$ | Max allowable limit | $^\circ\text{C}/\text{W}$ | Transient thermal metrology (T3Ster / JEDEC JESD51) |
| **Bond Pad Footprint Clearance** | $100 \times 100$ | Reference nominal | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical/acoustic inspection of active pad area |

---
