# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Destructive Die Shear Strength Testing & Bond Line Fracture Mode Verification

### 1. Process Workflow Overview

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Die Placement & Cure  │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Tool Alignment &    │
│  Shear Tool Clearance  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Lateral Load      │
│      Application       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Peak Shear Force    │
│     Logging & Mode     │
│   Optical Metrology    │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Test Inspection & Fixture Clamping**:
   - Verify sample lot cured with silver-filled conductive epoxy (**Ablebond 84-1LMIS**) at **150°C for 60 minutes**.
   - Secure the leadframe / package carrier into the mechanical clamping stage of the automated die shear tester. Ensure rigid bottom clamping without stage deflection.

2. **Shear Tool Selection and Alignment**:
   - Mount a hardened tungsten carbide shear chisel tool with contact width matching or slightly exceeding die edge dimension.
   - Adjust the shear tool height clearance to **25 µm to 50 µm** above the leadframe substrate surface (ensuring contact is within the lower third of the DRAM silicon die thickness and strictly above the epoxy fillet to avoid plowing into the substrate).
   - Align tool edge parallel to the die edge within **±1°**.

3. **Destructive Shear Load Application**:
   - Set test parameters:
     - **Travel Speed**: Constant displacement rate of **50 µm/s to 100 µm/s**.
     - **Load Cell Range**: 0 to 50 kgf (calibrated load cell).
   - Initiate motorized lateral displacement toward the die edge until complete mechanical separation occurs.
   - Record the continuous force-displacement profile and capture the peak ultimate shear force ($F_{\text{shear}}$).

4. **Bond Line Fracture Mode Optical Inspection**:
   - Place sheared leadframe pad and die backside under an optical inspection microscope (50×–200× magnification).
   - Classify failure modes:
     - **Cohesive Epoxy Fracture**: Separation inside the conductive epoxy matrix (acceptable, indicating strong interfacial adhesion).
     - **Adhesive Interface Failure**: Complete delamination at the die backside metallization or leadframe silver plating interface (rejectable if below baseline threshold).
     - **Silicon Fracture / Die Cracking**: Silicon bulk fracture.
   - Verify residual epoxy coverage area on the leadframe attach pad.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                           Quality Metric Thresholds    
                       ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                       │░░░                            │
     Thermal Resist Max┤░░░                            │
          Void Area Max┤▒▒▒                            │
                       │▒▒▒                            │
Shear Strength Pass Min┤███████████████████████████████│
                       │███████████████████████████████│
                       └┬───────┬──────┬───────┬──────┬┘
                        0      25     50      75    100 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Die Attach Pre-Cure Thermal Cure Profile** | **$150$** (for **$60$** duration) | **°C** (time in **minutes**) | In-line thermal oven thermocouple profile |
| **Die Attach Acoustic Voiding Area** | **$< 5$** | **% of total die area** | C-SAM (Scanning Acoustic Microscopy) |
| **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$)** | **$\le 5.0$** | **°C/W** | Transient dual-interface thermal tester |
| **Post-Shear Epoxy Cohesive Coverage** | **$\ge 50$** | **% area** | Optical inspection metrology (Mil-Std-883) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source**: *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*
  - *"Die Attach: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g. Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at 150°C for 60 minutes. Thermal resistance $R_{\text{th}} \le 5\text{°C/W}$; void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy."*
  - Bonding pad geometry: *"100 um x 100 um aluminum squares"*.

---
Captured and persisted micro-knowledge to [sop_die_shear_testing.md](./docs/sop_die_shear_testing.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Destructive die shear testing isolates the mechanical shear plane of the cured Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver epoxy layer on the copper/silver-plated leadframe flag, but lacks correlation to in-situ thermo-mechanical stress profiles if thermal cycling preconditioning (-40°C to +125°C JEDEC JESD22-A104) is omitted. The test rig must rigidly clamp the leadframe fixture with zero compliance along the lateral shearing axis to avoid parasitic vertical bending moments that falsely depress measured shear strength values.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Under MIL-STD-883 Method 2019.9, die shear testing must enforce a controlled shear tool standoff of 15-25 µm above the leadframe surface and a continuous stroke rate between 0.1 mm/s and 0.5 mm/s. Critical verification centers on distinguishing cohesive epoxy failure (>80% epoxy remaining across die attach area) from adhesive de-bonding at the backside metallization (Ti/Ni/Ag) or leadframe paddle, where adhesive separation signals unacceptable intermetallic contamination or surface oxidation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-source vulnerability on semiconductor-grade conductive silver epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) and custom tungsten carbide die shear tool wedges requires establishing secondary vendor qualifications (e.g., Henkel Loctite Ablestik 2000 series). Sub-ambient cold-chain storage at -40°C must be logged continuously with thaw time tracking to prevent localized resin separation that degrades lot-level shear force metrics.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Destructive metrology consumes sacrificial sample dies from MPW Gen 3 packaging runs; sampling frequency must be budgeted strictly at 5 coupon dies per leadframe strip lot (AQL 0.65 Level II). Test execution timelines must not bottleneck the subsequent wirebonding packaging line, mandating real-time database ingest of force-displacement curves and automated failure-mode imaging signoffs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial adhesive delamination between silicon die backside metallization (Ti/Ni/Ag) and cured epoxy matrix caused by native oxide growth or organic residue prior to die attach.
1. Brittle cohesive fracture of bulk epoxy at sub-threshold shear forces due to incomplete cross-linking, resin aging, or silver flake agglomeration.
1. Die cracking/shattering under shear tool contact point resulting from excessive contact tool height or localized point loading.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-3-3-01` | **MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 Destructive Die Shear Strength Testing** | Dage 4000Plus Multi-Function Bondtester equipped with 50 kgf lateral shear load cell (DS50KG) and calibrated tungsten carbide shear wedge tool (3.0 mm width). | 1. Secure leadframe coupon onto vacuum fixture beneath microscope alignment optics. 2. Calibrate shear tool zero-height reference against leadframe paddle surface. 3. Index shear tool to standoff height of 20 µm above paddle and 25 µm lateral distance from die edge. 4. Engage lateral shear displacement at uniform rate of 0.2 mm/s until mechanical detachment occurs. 5. Record peak shear force (kgf) and displacement curve. | `Die shear force must exceed 2.5x MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 minimum threshold (minimum >= 5.0 kgf for 2.0 mm x 2.0 mm DRAM die, target >= 12.5 kgf). Force drop-off must be sudden without premature micro-slippage below 5.0 kgf.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-2-3-3-02` | **Post-Shear Fracture Mode & Bond Line Interface Optical Metrology** | Calibrated High-Resolution Optical Inspection Microscope (Keyence VHX-7000) with motorized stage and image analysis package for area percentage measurement. | 1. Position sheared leadframe flag and corresponding die backside beneath 100x/500x polarized telecentric lenses. 2. Capture high-depth-of-field composite images of the fracture site. 3. Map fracture zones using segmentation software: cohesive epoxy failure (epoxy-to-epoxy), adhesive leadframe failure (clean copper/silver flag), adhesive die failure (exposed silicon/backside metallization), or die fracture (silicon tear). 4. Calculate areal percentages across the 2.0 mm x 2.0 mm die footprint. | `Cohesive fracture of the conductive silver epoxy matrix must account for >= 80% of total bond interface area. Interfacial adhesive delamination from leadframe or die backside must be <= 20%. Die silicon fracturing/shattering must be 0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact splash-resistant safety glasses, Cleanroom-compatible disposable nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, double-gloved), ESD-safe anti-static cleanroom lab coat / smock, Class 100 particle-filtering face mask
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and copious water; remove contaminated garments. Inhalation of particulate/solvent vapors: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Ingestion: Rinse mouth thoroughly with water; do not induce vomiting and seek emergency medical evaluation immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operate metrology station in ISO Class 6 cleanroom under dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) canopy or elephant trunk with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) to extract IPA vapors and aerosolized micro-debris during destructive fracture.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect sheared leadframe scrap, fractured silicon remnants, and solvent-wetted wipes into designated hazardous heavy-metal / solid resin waste containers. Segregate silver-bearing conductive adhesive residues for precious metal recovery per EPA/RCRA regulations. Do not discharge solvents into municipal cleanroom drain lines.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silver Flake (Conductive Filler in Cured Epoxy Residue)** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade (99.9% metal basis) | `70-85% w/w in uncured precursor` |
| **Bisphenol-F Epoxy Resin (Cured Matrix Decomposition Dust)** | `9003-36-5` | Technical/Electronic Grade | `10-20% w/w in uncured precursor` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Cleaning Solvent for Fixtures)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `99.9% v/v` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Leadframe strips post-150°C 60-min convection cure and room temperature cooling; C-SAM verified with <5% acoustic voiding; clean, dry, free of flux or organic contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Destructively sheared sample flags flagged as scrapped; surviving qualification package lots purged with clean dry nitrogen (CDA dew point <= -40°C) with leadframe bond pads pristine for ultrasonic wirebonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom ambient air exposure before destructive shear and subsequent wirebond processing causes atmospheric oxidation of leadframe silver/copper plating and aluminum pad corrosion, leading to unrepresentative shear testing values and liftoff during thermosonic ball bonding.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical, mechanical, and fractographic verification of die attach bond integrity for 180nm DRAM Gen 3 package prototypes, ensuring cured silver epoxy withstands extreme lateral shear stresses with predominantly cohesive failure modes per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DIE_SHEAR_METROLOGY_REPORT_GEN3.pdf`
- [ ] `SHEAR_FORCE_DISPLACEMENT_RAWDATA.csv`
- [ ] `FRACTURE_MODE_HIGHRES_SURFACE_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Ultimate destructive die shear strength** | `14.5 kgf` | >= 10.0 kgf (Absolute minimum threshold: 5.0 kgf) | Dage 4000Plus automated peak force transducer logging per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Epoxy cohesive fracture mode area ratio** | `90.0%` | +10.0% / -10.0% (Minimum allowable: >= 80.0%) | Digital image segmentation analysis of post-shear fracture surface via Keyence VHX-7000 optical metrology |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum allowable silicon die shatter incidence** | `0.0%` | +0.0% (Zero tolerance) | Brightfield visual optical inspection of fractured die remnants and leadframe paddle |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of tested sample dies (minimum 5 units per cured lot) exhibit shear strength exceeding 10.0 kgf with cohesive epoxy fracture coverage >= 80% and zero die fracture; complete signoff documented in DIE_SHEAR_METROLOGY_REPORT_GEN3.pdf signed by Packaging Lead and QA Director.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Void Analysis and Die Shear Strength Metrology

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: DRC/LVS rule decks must run clean via KLayout/Magic/OpenLane with zero design rule errors. Antenna ratio rules (< 250:1) and substrate tap density checks must pass before GDSII reticle handoff to commercial foundry.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: 3D Crown capacitor ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 (ZAZ) stack must achieve equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) <= 0.8 nm and leakage current < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V. CMP dishing on M1/M2 tungsten/copper features must hold < 15 nm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Commercial foundry MPW (Multi-Project Wafer) shuttle submission has an unmovable tapeout window; GDSII/OASIS files must freeze 21 days prior. Sourced via open-source or commercial shuttle program under standard NDA.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 60-120 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: CRITICAL (A single DRC rule deck discrepancy or LVS short-circuit ruins the entire multi-thousand dollar commercial shuttle run and incurs a 4-6 month spin delay).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. DRC/LVS hierarchy discrepancy causing undetected metal-to-metal bridging or floating substrate tap.
1. ALD precursor pulse/purge saturation drift inducing pinhole dielectric breakdown in crown capacitor array.
1. Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) over-polish causing severe interconnect erosion and open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-01` | **Automated DRC/LVS Golden Rule Deck Physical Sign-Off** | KLayout / Magic / Pegasus Industrial Physical Verification Batch Engine | 1. Run 180nm DRC rule deck across 100% of mask layers (well, diffusion, poly, contact, M1-M3, pad). 2. Execute Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) netlist extraction against golden SPICE schematic. 3. Verify antenna ratio violations (< 250:1) and substrate noise isolation guard rings. | `DRC clean: 0 violations (Pass); LVS netlist match: 100% topological equivalence with 0 discrepancy (Pass).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-02` | **3D Crown Capacitor High-k Dielectric TEM & C-V Metrology** | Field-Emission TEM (FEI/Thermo Fisher) & High-Frequency C-V Parameter Analyzer (Keysight B1500A) | 1. Prepare FIB lamella cross-section through 3D crown capacitor trench structure. 2. Measure physical film thickness and step coverage across bottom, sidewall, and top crown lip via HR-TEM. 3. Perform high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V sweep to extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and dielectric breakdown voltage. | `ALD step coverage >= 95% (Pass); EOT <= 0.8 nm (Pass); Dielectric leakage < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom bunny suit with conductive ESD booties, Pyrophoric precursor handling apron and dual-layer fluoropolymer gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and UV-blocking safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Pyrophoric precursor emergency: TMA spontaneously ignites upon contact with air or moisture! Do NOT use water on metal alkyl fires. Smother immediately with dry vermiculite, dry sand, or Class D metal fire extinguisher. In case of ozone inhalation, move patient to fresh air immediately and administer supplemental oxygen.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Ultra-high vacuum ALD exhaust manifold connected to dedicated point-of-use thermal decomposition burn-box and wet chemical scrubber. Continuous gas leak detection monitors for TMA/TEMAZ and ozone.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent ALD bubbler purging into mineral oil bubblers with inert argon ballast. CMP slurry effluent collected in settling basin, flocculated with alum, and neutralized to pH 6.5-8.0.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trimethylaluminum (TMA)** | `75-24-1` | Electronic Grade (99.999% trace metals) | `Pyrophoric liquid ALD precursor` |
| **Tetrakis(ethylmethylamino)zirconium (TEMAZ)** | `175923-04-3` | High-purity ALD grade | `Liquid precursor for ZrO2 dielectric` |
| **Ozone (O3)** | `10028-15-6` | Generated in-situ from UHP O2 | `15-20 wt% in O2 carrier gas (Strong Oxidizer)` |
| **Silica / Ceria CMP Slurry** | `1344-28-1` | Semiconductor Colloidal CMP grade | `15-30 wt% colloidal abrasive slurry` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched 3D crown capacitor trench structure post-DHF strip, completely free of native oxide.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Uniform ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 high-k dielectric stack with TiN top electrode encapsulation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Air exposure exceeding 20 minutes allows uncontrolled spontaneous SiO2 interfacial layer regrowth (> 0.4 nm), which severely increases Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and drastically degrades bitcell storage capacitance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Void Analysis and Die Shear Strength Metrology: PDK setup, physical verification rule decks, and full-chip GDSII layouts pass 100% DRC/LVS sign-off and satisfy foundry commercial tapeout design rules.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Golden_180nm_PDK_DRC_LVS_Signoff_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Commercial_MPW_Tapeout_GDSII_OASIS_Archive.tar.gz`
- [ ] `ALD_3D_Crown_TEM_StepCoverage_Analysis.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Foundry Design Rule Check (DRC) Violations** | `0 violations` | Zero tolerance across full chip and seal ring | Automated batch DRC run using KLayout / Pegasus Golden Rule Deck |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) Netlist Equivalence** | `100% match` | Zero net/port mismatches, zero floating pins | Hierarchical LVS extraction against golden SPICE schematic |
| `ASSERT-03` | **3D Crown Capacitor ALD Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | `<= 0.80 nm` | +/- 0.05 nm across wafer | High-frequency 1 MHz C-V accumulation capacitance metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% clean DRC/LVS verification logs signed off by lead tapeout architect; checksum of streamed GDSII package validated against foundry MPW shuttle intake submission portal.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-PKG-CSAM-001`
**Title:** C-SAM Transducer Calibration & Immersion Tank Setup for Epoxy Interface  
**Process Step:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe > Silver Epoxy Dispensing and DRAM Die Attach Curing > Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Void Analysis and Die Shear Strength Metrology  
**Technology Generation:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 3)  
**Classification:** Restricted / Cleanroom Protocol (Class 10,000 / ISO 7 Metrology Bay)

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the exact protocol for preparing the Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) immersion tank, calibrating the high-frequency acoustic transducer, and gating the A-scan waveform specifically at the silicon die-to-conductive silver epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) attach interface. This guarantees precise, non-destructive measurement of void percentage underneath fabricated 180nm DRAM dies mounted onto leadframes.

---

### 2. Required Equipment & Materials
- **Metrology Platform:** Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM / Sonix / PVA TePla or equivalent).
- **Acoustic Transducer:** 15–50 MHz focused immersion acoustic transducer (focal length $f = 12.7\text{ mm}$ / 0.5 in).
- **Immersion Medium:** Deionized (DI) water ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ resistivity at $25^\circ\text{C}$), vacuum-degassed (dissolved oxygen $< 2.0\text{ ppm}$).
- **Wetting Agent:** Non-ionic surfactant (0.05% v/v solution, semiconductor-grade).
- **Calibration Standard:** Reference copper leadframe with bare silicon calibration die containing EDM acoustic void reference wells.
- **Test Samples:** Cured DRAM assemblies (conductive silver epoxy cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 min).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 1: Tank Preparation (Degassed DI Water & Surfactant)   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 2: Transducer Installation & Fixture Leveling (<0.02°) |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 3: A-Scan Acoustic Waveform Gating & Pulse Alignment   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 4: C-Scan Void Scanning (<5% Area Threshold)           |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Immersion Tank Fluid Preparation & Degassing
1. Drain, rinse, and refill the immersion tank with clean $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized (DI) water maintained at room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$).
2. Engage the integrated inline vacuum degasser for 30 minutes to reduce dissolved air in the water below $2.0\text{ ppm}$. Micro-bubbles act as acoustic attenuators and cause false void reflections.
3. Dispense semiconductor-grade non-ionic surfactant into the DI water bath to maintain a $0.05\%\text{ v/v}$ concentration to minimize liquid surface tension at the sample interface.

#### Step 2: Transducer Mounting and Mechanical Leveling
1. Mount the high-frequency focused immersion transducer onto the automated Z-axis scanning stage fixture.
2. Place the DRAM leadframe fixture into the sample holder within the tank. Submerge the leadframe slowly at a $30^\circ$ angle to prevent air pocket entrapment under the package cavity.
3. Align the transducer perpendicular to the silicon die top surface. Execute a three-point optical/laser tilt leveling sweep to ensure sample parallelism within $< 0.02^\circ$.

#### Step 3: Transducer Focal Plane & A-Scan Gate Calibration
1. Position the transducer over the center of the silicon die ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ pad array region).
2. Set the ultrasonic pulser/receiver damping and attenuation to optimize reflection signal-to-noise ratio ($> 26\text{ dB}$).
3. Lower the Z-stage until the primary echo from the top surface of the silicon die is observed on the RF A-scan oscilloscope trace.
4. Adjust the focal distance $Z$ until the secondary echo corresponding to the **Silicon Die-to-Silver Epoxy Interface** (backside of the die) reaches peak reflection amplitude.
5. Set the electronic data-acquisition **Gate**:
   - **Gate Start:** Position immediately before the silicon-to-epoxy echo ($t_0 - 15\text{ ns}$).
   - **Gate Width:** Cover the entire epoxy bondline thickness echo window ($40\text{ to }60\text{ ns}$).
   - **Gate Polarity:** Set to monitor phase inversion (a negative-to-positive phase reversal indicates a silicon-to-air void boundary due to acoustic impedance drop $Z_{\text{Si}} \gg Z_{\text{air}}$).

#### Step 4: Spatial C-Scan Scanning & Pixel Void Analysis
1. Define the rectangular C-scan XY scan area encompassing the full die footprint with a boundary margin of $+0.5\text{ mm}$.
2. Set the scanner scan speed to $150\text{ mm/s}$ and step resolution to $5\,\mu\text{m/pixel}$.
3. Execute the C-scan. Collect reflection peak amplitude and phase data.
4. Process the image using binary thresholding to segment and compute total void area relative to total die attach footprint area.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Tolerance / Limit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die Attach Void Area** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ of die footprint | Max $5.0\%$ (single void $< 1.0\%$) | Automated C-Scan Image Binary Threshold Segmentation |
| **Water Immersion Tank Temperature** | $25.0$ | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | $\pm 1.0\,{^\circ}\text{C}$ | Calibrated Immersion RTD Sensor |
| **A-Scan Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)** | $\ge 26$ | $\text{dB}$ | Minimum limit | RF Oscilloscope Peak Amplitude vs Noise Floor |
| **Transducer Stage Orthogonality/Tilt** | $\le 0.02$ | Degrees ($^\circ$) | Maximum planar deviation | 3-Point Acoustic Surface Reflection Sweep |

---

### 5. Context Citations & References
- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:** Defines standard packaging requirements for 180nm DRAM dies (leadframe bonding pads of $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$), silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) curing at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 minutes, thermal resistance $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$, and the strict acceptance limit of **void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy**.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Transducer acoustic focal length (typically 100 MHz to 230 MHz for die attach inspection) must match the Z-axis displacement limits and scanner step resolution of the linear stage. Coupling immersion degas levels must be closed-loop monitored: dissolved microbubbles in deionized water will generate severe impedance mismatch artifacts, mimicking pseudo-voids at the silicon-to-silver epoxy interface. Furthermore, RF pulse-receiver damping and gain linearity across the dynamic range (up to 60 dB) require daily calibration against an acoustic resolution standard block (e.g., tungsten or fused silica reference) to prevent false void reject triggers across automated sorting lanes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm DRAM packaging node, inspecting 20-35 µm bondline thickness (BLT) of conductive silver epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablestik 84-1LMIS or equivalent) under a 250-350 µm thick silicon die requires precise gating on the second interface (Si-epoxy boundary, reflection coefficient R ~ -0.45). If transducer frequency is below 75 MHz, axial resolution is insufficient to decouple die surface reflection from the epoxy bondline. Conversely, frequencies above 175 MHz suffer severe acoustic attenuation in high-density silver-loaded matrices. Transducer focal spot diameter must be calibrated to ≤ 40 µm at -6 dB spot size to resolve voids smaller than 50 µm diameter.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-frequency acoustic transducers (100–150 MHz UHF quartz/PVDF or lithium niobate piezoelectric elements) with sapphire buffer rods and acoustic lenses face lead times of 16-24 weeks from tier-1 suppliers (e.g., Nordson SONOSCAN or PVA TePla). Procurement must maintain at least one dual-element spare kit in temperature-regulated nitrogen storage. Ultrasonic immersion bath de-aerators, non-ionic surfactant anti-bubble agents, and precision calibration test coupons with photo-lithographically etched subterranean air cavities must be dual-sourced to prevent line stoppage.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement and operational setup of the C-SAM immersion scanner represent a major capital expenditure ($220k-$380k) with strict cleanroom footprint requirements. If deionized water immersion requires post-inspection centrifugal bakeout, it introduces a packaging queue bottleneck prior to wirebonding. Signoff milestones must demonstrate Gauge R&R < 10% on simulated void area fractions before releasing line operations for DRAM qualification lots.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dissolved microbubble nucleation on die surface or transducer acoustic lens during scanning, producing acoustic shadow voids (false positive void rejects).
1. Transducer tilt misalignment exceeding 0.05° relative to the package leadframe plane, causing phase cancellation and signal loss across the outer array of the die attach area.
1. Inadequate post-acoustic inspection wafer/strip drying leading to residual moisture trapped within micro-capillaries of uncured or semi-cured epoxy, resulting in explosive popcorn cracking during reflow or wirebond thermal cycles.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-1-01` | **Acoustic Transducer Beam Profile and Center Frequency Verification** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) system with 100 MHz UHF focused transducer (Focal length = 12.7 mm), calibrated RF pulser/receiver with 1 GHz digital oscilloscope digitizer, polished optical-grade quartz/fused silica calibration standard. | 1. Position transducer above polished quartz calibration standard. 2. Adjust Z-stage height to maximize peak-to-peak amplitude of front-surface reflection echo (focal point). 3. Capture RF A-scan waveform and compute Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to extract center frequency (-6 dB power bandwidth). 4. Perform orthogonal 2D raster scan over standard edge with 1 µm step size to derive line spread function (LSF) and calculate full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) acoustic spot size. 5. Repeat across 5 consecutive acquisition cycles. | `Measured center frequency must be within 100.0 ± 5.0 MHz; measured acoustic beam focal spot diameter (FWHM at -6 dB) must be ≤ 42.0 µm; signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of reference echo must be ≥ 36.0 dB across all 5 runs.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-1-02` | **Immersion Tank Acoustic Coupling and Known-Void Area Fraction Calibration** | C-SAM immersion tank platform equipped with inline degasser and recirculating sub-micron filter, standard calibration copper leadframe strip with etched subterranean target voids (sizes: 25 µm, 50 µm, 100 µm, 200 µm diameter). | 1. Mount standard calibration leadframe coupon into the rigid vacuum nest fixture within the immersion tank. 2. Scan standard coupon in C-scan mode at 10 µm pixel resolution with scan velocity of 150 mm/s. 3. Apply automated image segmentation threshold (Otsu method) to extract void area pixels. 4. Calculate measured area against certified laser confocal profilometry benchmarks for each nominal void size. 5. Perform 10 consecutive replicate scans across the strip without manual repositioning to determine repeatability. | `Detection rate of 50 µm and larger calibrated voids must be 100.0%; area measurement accuracy must be within ± 5.0% of certified reference dimensions; measurement coefficient of variation (CV) across 10 replicate scans must be CV < 1.0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (12-inch, powder-free, double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-resistant chemical goggles, Full cleanroom ESD smock with conductive grounding footwear, Face shield during chemical tank reservoir filling and fluid drain maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Flush exposed skin with copious DI water for 15 minutes. Eye contact: Rinse open eyes immediately at eye-wash station for 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air laminar plenum. Ingestion: Rinse mouth thoroughly; do not induce vomiting unless instructed by medical personnel. Consult SDS and internal safety hotline immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank maintenance area requires dedicated local exhaust capture (slot velocity ≥ 0.5 m/s) to capture volatile isopropanol vapors during transducer head wipe-down. Cleanroom HVAC must sustain positive laminar downflow (ISO Class 5 / Class 100) with 60 to 90 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent immersion water containing trace non-ionic wetting agents and potential metallic particulates must be plumbed to the packaging facility Industrial Wastewater Treatment System (IWTS) neutralization sump (pH balanced to 6.5 - 8.5) and never dumped directly to municipal drain. Solvent-saturated wipes must be segregated into sealed hazardous flammables disposal bins.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Immersion Medium)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1 Microelectronics Grade | `100.0%` |
| **Non-ionic Surfactant (Fluorosurfactant wetting agent)** | `65545-80-4` | Semiconductor Cleanroom Grade | `0.05% in DI Water` |
| **Isopropanol (Transducer & Nest Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade (0.1 µm filtered) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-die-attach cured leadframe strips; silver epoxy fully cross-linked (solidified); leadframe fingers and die top active surface dry, free of silver bleed-out and airborne particulate contamination (PCO < Class 1000).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: 100% moisture-free; centrifugal spin-dried and baked in vacuum oven (110 °C, 10 Torr, 20 min); zero trace DI water residue in package crevices or bond pads; ready for ultrasonic wirebonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding allowable queue time post-curing or post-immersion allows ambient moisture reabsorption into the epoxy matrix and oxidation of copper/silver-plated leadframe bond pads, inducing ultrasonic wirebond non-stick (NSOP/NSOL) and high-temperature solder reflow delamination/popcorn cracking.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration and operational signoff of the C-SAM acoustic microscope immersion tank, RF pulser/receiver, and 100 MHz transducer assembly. The system achieves repeatable sub-50 µm void resolution at the 180nm DRAM silver epoxy die attach interface with verified acoustic beam focus, stable degassed DI water coupling, and automated A/C-scan gating.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_Transducer_100MHz_Acoustic_Beam_Profile_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Calibration_Standard_Void_Gauge_RR_Dataset.csv`
- [ ] `Immersion_Tank_Water_Quality_Degas_Log.csv`
- [ ] `Die_Attach_Epoxy_Interface_CSAM_Master_Reference_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Transducer acoustic center frequency via FFT power spectrum analysis** | `100.0 MHz` | ± 5.0 MHz | 5-point FFT spectral acquisition of front-surface echo off polished optical quartz standard in 1 GHz digitizer. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **C-SAM void area metrology measurement repeatability (CV) across multi-strip repeat testing** | `0.65%` | < 1.00% max | Gauge R&R 10-cycle automated C-scan void area integration across standard calibrated etched test pattern. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration in immersion tank acoustic coupling DI water** | `0.50 ppm` | ≤ 1.00 ppm | In-situ luminescent optical dissolved oxygen sensor telemetry recorded prior to and immediately after scanning run. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Transducer center frequency and focal beam profile pass criteria on the quartz optical reference; automated 10-run repeatability on 50 µm reference void test coupon exhibits CV < 1.0%; dissolved oxygen in the coupling fluid remains below 1.0 ppm throughout 4-hour operation; and leadframe strips post-immersion bake yield contact angle ≤ 15° with zero moisture trace prior to release to ultrasonic wirebond staging.

180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects (Vossen & Kern - Thin Film Processes)

critics.systems_engineer: Transducer acoustic focal length (typically 100 MHz to 230 MHz for die attach inspection) must match the Z-axis displacement limits and scanner step resolution of the linear stage. Coupling immersion degas levels must be closed-loop monitored: dissolved microbubbles in deionized water will generate severe impedance mismatch artifacts, mimicking pseudo-voids at the silicon-to-silver epoxy interface. Furthermore, RF pulse-receiver damping and gain linearity across the dynamic range (up to 60 dB) require daily calibration against an acoustic resolution standard block (e.g., tungsten or fused silica reference) to prevent false void reject triggers across automated sorting lanes.
critics.domain_expert: At the 180nm DRAM packaging node, inspecting 20-35 µm bondline thickness (BLT) of conductive silver epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablestik 84-1LMIS or equivalent) under a 250-350 µm thick silicon die requires precise gating on the second interface (Si-epoxy boundary, reflection coefficient R ~ -0.45). If transducer frequency is below 75 MHz, axial resolution is insufficient to decouple die surface reflection from the epoxy bondline. Conversely, frequencies above 175 MHz suffer severe acoustic attenuation in high-density silver-loaded matrices. Transducer focal spot diameter must be calibrated to ≤ 40 µm at -6 dB spot size to resolve voids smaller than 50 µm diameter.
critics.supply_chain: High-frequency acoustic transducers (100–150 MHz UHF quartz/PVDF or lithium niobate piezoelectric elements) with sapphire buffer rods and acoustic lenses face lead times of 16-24 weeks from tier-1 suppliers (e.g., Nordson SONOSCAN or PVA TePla). Procurement must maintain at least one dual-element spare kit in temperature-regulated nitrogen storage. Ultrasonic immersion bath de-aerators, non-ionic surfactant anti-bubble agents, and precision calibration test coupons with photo-lithographically etched subterranean air cavities must be dual-sourced to prevent line stoppage.
critics.laya_pm: Procurement and operational setup of the C-SAM immersion scanner represent a major capital expenditure ($220k-$380k) with strict cleanroom footprint requirements. If deionized water immersion requires post-inspection centrifugal bakeout, it introduces a packaging queue bottleneck prior to wirebonding. Signoff milestones must demonstrate Gauge R&R < 10% on simulated void area fractions before releasing line operations for DRAM qualification lots.
critical_failure_modes: Dissolved microbubble nucleation on die surface or transducer acoustic lens during scanning, producing acoustic shadow voids (false positive void rejects).
Transducer tilt misalignment exceeding 0.05° relative to the package leadframe plane, causing phase cancellation and signal loss across the outer array of the die attach area.

Inadequate post-acoustic inspection wafer/strip drying leading to residual moisture trapped within micro-capillaries of uncured or semi-cured epoxy, resulting in explosive popcorn cracking during reflow or wirebond thermal cycles.

testcases.title: Acoustic Transducer Beam Profile and Center Frequency Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) system with 100 MHz UHF focused transducer (Focal length = 12.7 mm), calibrated RF pulser/receiver with 1 GHz digital oscilloscope digitizer, polished optical-grade quartz/fused silica calibration standard.
testcases.pre_conditions: Immersion tank filled with 18.2 MOhm-cm deionized water degassed to dissolved oxygen (DO) < 1.0 ppm and temperature stabilized at 22.0 ± 0.5 °C; transducer aligned perpendicular to reference target via motorized goniometer within ± 0.02°.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position transducer above polished quartz calibration standard. 2. Adjust Z-stage height to maximize peak-to-peak amplitude of front-surface reflection echo (focal point). 3. Capture RF A-scan waveform and compute Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to extract center frequency (-6 dB power bandwidth). 4. Perform orthogonal 2D raster scan over standard edge with 1 µm step size to derive line spread function (LSF) and calculate full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) acoustic spot size. 5. Repeat across 5 consecutive acquisition cycles.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Measured center frequency must be within 100.0 ± 5.0 MHz; measured acoustic beam focal spot diameter (FWHM at -6 dB) must be ≤ 42.0 µm; signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of reference echo must be ≥ 36.0 dB across all 5 runs.

testcases.title: Immersion Tank Acoustic Coupling and Known-Void Area Fraction Calibration
testcases.instrumentation: C-SAM immersion tank platform equipped with inline degasser and recirculating sub-micron filter, standard calibration copper leadframe strip with etched subterranean target voids (sizes: 25 µm, 50 µm, 100 µm, 200 µm diameter).
testcases.pre_conditions: Transducer calibrated per TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-1-01; tank degassing cycle run for minimum 30 minutes; water surface free of meniscus contamination; gate set strictly across epoxy interface depth window (15 ns delay, 20 ns width).
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount standard calibration leadframe coupon into the rigid vacuum nest fixture within the immersion tank. 2. Scan standard coupon in C-scan mode at 10 µm pixel resolution with scan velocity of 150 mm/s. 3. Apply automated image segmentation threshold (Otsu method) to extract void area pixels. 4. Calculate measured area against certified laser confocal profilometry benchmarks for each nominal void size. 5. Perform 10 consecutive replicate scans across the strip without manual repositioning to determine repeatability.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Detection rate of 50 µm and larger calibrated voids must be 100.0%; area measurement accuracy must be within ± 5.0% of certified reference dimensions; measurement coefficient of variation (CV) across 10 replicate scans must be CV < 1.0%.

ppe_required: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (12-inch, powder-free, double-gloved)
ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-resistant chemical goggles
Full cleanroom ESD smock with conductive grounding footwear
Face shield during chemical tank reservoir filling and fluid drain maintenance

# Standard Operating Procedure: Die-Attach Acoustic Scanning & Sub-5% Interfacial Void Area Quantification

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM transducer acoustic impedance matching between the DRAM Si die (Z ~ 19.7 MRayl) and cured conductive silver epoxy matrix (Z ~ 5-8 MRayl) requires strict RF gate positioning. At a 180nm BEOL thickness with multi-level metalization, high-frequency transducers (>= 100 MHz - 230 MHz) must be selected with precision to avoid ring-down artifacts obscuring interfacial reflections at the epoxy bondline without excessive attenuation in DI water couplant.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Thermal dissipation from the 180nm open-source DRAM array during fast burst read/write cycles directly relies on zero localized voiding beneath high-power row-decoder and charge pump circuitry. A global sub-5% void fraction threshold is insufficient if single voids exceed 0.5 mm in major diameter or if perimeter fillet wetting is incomplete, which triggers localized thermal hot-spots and shear crack propagation under JEDEC standard temp-cycling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic microscopy couplant deionized water requires continuous de-aeration and temperature stabilization (+/- 0.5 deg C) to prevent micro-bubble nucleation on leadframe packages. Sourcing high-purity immersion transducers (Sonix/Nordson Sonoscan standard) and ISO 14644-1 compatible drying fixtures represents a single-point operational vulnerability for regional assembly houses in Southeast Asia.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-SAM scanning throughput is the primary offline metrology bottleneck for Gen 3 packaging. At raster step sizes necessary to resolve 10-micron microvoids (< 15 um pixel pitch), per-die scanning times exceed 90 seconds. We must mandate statistical batch sampling (AQL 0.65 Level II) rather than 100% inspection once epoxy dispensing volume and thermal cure recipes stabilize.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial micro-delamination and acoustic phase inversion (180-degree phase shift) at die-attach corners caused by incomplete silver epoxy outgassing during stage-curing.
1. Moisture entrapment and post-scan galvanic corrosion of copper/silver-plated leadframe bond pads during water couplant immersion without rapid post-inspection bake.
1. Transducer focal-plane drift causing erroneous acoustic attenuation readings and threshold segmentation false-positives for interfacial voiding.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-01` | **High-Frequency C-SAM Interfacial Die-Attach Void Area Quantification** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (Nordson Sonoscan Gen7 or equivalent) equipped with a 100 MHz (focal length 12.7 mm) UHF acoustic transducer, de-aerated ultra-pure DI water bath (18.2 MOhm-cm, dissolved O2 < 15 ppb), and automated image segmentation software. | 1. Immerse leadframe strip in de-aerated DI water tank maintained at 22.0 +/- 0.5 deg C. 2. Calibrate Z-axis focus to maximize interfacial reflection amplitude at the die backside / epoxy interface. 3. Acquire C-scan acoustic image at 10 um/pixel raster resolution across the full 4.2 mm x 4.2 mm die footprint. 4. Apply grayscale histogram thresholding to isolate interfacial void regions exhibiting inverted acoustic phase reflections. 5. Calculate cumulative void area percentage relative to total die surface area and measure maximum individual void diameter. | `Total interfacial void area <= 4.8% of total die active area; no individual single void area > 0.05 mm^2; zero voiding within 100 um of die perimeter.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-02` | **Post-Acoustic Scan Die Shear Destructive Strength Correlation** | Dage 4000Plus Multi-Function Die Shear Tester with 100 kg shear load cell and tungsten carbide shear tool tip. | 1. Mount leadframe rigidly in the precision mechanical clamping vise. 2. Position shear tool tip perpendicular to the die edge at a standoff height of 25 um above leadframe surface (<= 25% of die thickness). 3. Apply uniform shear force at a constant rate of 100 um/s until mechanical detachment occurs. 4. Record peak shear force at failure. 5. Inspect fracture surface under optical microscope to classify failure mode (epoxy cohesive failure vs. die-adhesion interfacial failure). | `Minimum peak die shear force >= 2.5 kg/mm^2 (>= 44.1 kgf total failure load across 17.64 mm^2 die); epoxy residue remaining on leadframe pad must exhibit > 80% cohesive failure area coverage.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (chemical-resistant, 8 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 Impact and Splash Certified Safety Glasses, Cleanroom ESD Lab Coat with conductive grounding wrist strap, Chemical splash apron for couplant bath chemical additives handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with couplant/surfactant or uncured epoxy residues, wash immediately with copious water and mild soap for 15 minutes. For eye contact with IPA rinse or couplant additives, flush with eyewash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmic evaluation. For accidental ingestion, do not induce vomiting; drink water and seek medical emergency services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Acoustic microscopy workstation requires localized air exhaust canopy operating at a face velocity of >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) to extract volatile solvent vapors from IPA pre-wetting and post-scan wafer drying stations. Room ambient ventilation must maintain >= 30 cleanroom air volume changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used acoustic immersion couplant water contaminated with surfactant and trace metal particulates must be routed to industrial heavy metal/fluoride wastewater neutralization tanks (pH adjusted to 6.5 - 8.5) before municipal discharge. Spent IPA drying rinse solvent must be segregated into dedicated labeled DOT-approved flammable liquid waste drums.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Acoustic Couplant)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I Analytical Grade (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA couplant wetting agent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Silver Flake Conductive Filler Residue (Epoxy)** | `7440-22-4` | Technical Micro-Flake Grade | `75-85% in uncured paste` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Thermally cured die-attach epoxy fillet with zero liquid bleedout; leadframe and silicon backside dry, clean, and unoxidized.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Complete vacuum-dried surface (H2O desorption bake verified); zero liquid couplant residues on bond pads; packaged units purged and sealed under dry N2 desiccant.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure prior to post-scan dehydration bake induces capillary condensation of couplant water under package micro-crevices, triggering copper leadframe dendrite growth and severe wirebond pad corrosion during subsequent thermosonic gold/copper wirebonding.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full non-destructive C-SAM acoustic verification of Gen 3 180nm DRAM die-attach integrity showing sub-5% global interfacial void fraction, absence of critical edge-delamination, and full validation of die adhesion strength matching MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_VOID_QUANT_MAP_GEN3_REV1.tiff`
- [ ] `DIE_ATTACH_ACOUSTIC_METROLOGY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `DIE_SHEAR_FAILURE_DATASET.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total interfacial die-attach void area fraction across the DRAM die footprint** | `4.2%` | +/- 0.6% | Sonoscan Sonolytics Automated Binary Histogram Area Segmentation |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Critical perimeter corner delamination length along die boundary** | `0.0 um` | + 25.0 um | High-frequency 100 MHz acoustic edge gate peak reflection trace |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-curing die shear mechanical failure strength** | `3.1 kgf/mm^2` | +/- 0.4 kgf/mm^2 | Dage 4000Plus destructive mechanical shear testing per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal acceptance requires 100% of tested die samples in the qualification batch to demonstrate total acoustic interfacial void area < 5.0%, zero single void diameter > 250 um, zero corner acoustic phase-inversion delamination, post-scan bake residual moisture < 50 ppm, and post-drying die shear strength exceeding 2.5 kgf/mm^2 with dominant epoxy cohesive failure.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: High-Frequency C-SAM Transducer Calibration & Acoustic Coupling Setup
**Module:** BEOL Packaging & Assembly — Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Metrology  
**Target Device:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (nm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Flow & Setup Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Deionized Water Tank  │
│      & Degassing       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Transducer Mounting   │
│    & RF Cable Check    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acoustic Immersion &  │
│      Focus Height      │
│       Adjustment       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  A-Scan RF Echo Gate   │
│     Calibration at     │
│  Leadframe Interface   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│         C-SAM          │
│  High-Resolution Area  │
│      Scan & Void       │
│     Quantification     │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Acoustic Coupling Medium Preparation**:
   - Fill the C-SAM immersion tank with high-purity deionized (DI) water maintained at room ambient ($25^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Run the ultrasonic degassing cycle in the immersion fluid reservoir for 15 minutes to eliminate micro-bubbles that cause ultrasonic scatter and false void signatures.

2. **Transducer Fixturing & Electrical Inspection**:
   - Mount the high-frequency acoustic transducer onto the motorized $Z$-axis scanning head.
   - Secure RF coaxial connections to the pulser/receiver unit; confirm pulse impedance matching ($50\ \Omega$) and pulse excitation voltage to prevent signal distortion.

3. **Substrate Mounting & Focal Alignment**:
   - Position the packaged DRAM sample (die attached via silver-filled conductive epoxy, e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$ onto the leadframe) into the immersion fixture.
   - Submerge the transducer lens into the DI water coupling bath. Lower the $Z$-stage toward the sample while monitoring real-time A-scan RF reflections to locate the front surface echo.
   - Adjust focal height $Z$ until the acoustic focal zone intersects the die-attach epoxy interface beneath the silicon substrate.

4. **A-Scan Echo Gating & Phase Calibration**:
   - On the A-scan waveform, identify the primary reflection from the silicon-to-die-attach epoxy boundary and the secondary reflection from the epoxy-to-leadframe boundary.
   - Set the electronic data acquisition gate strictly across the die-attach interface echo window.
   - Calibrate the RF phase inverter: acoustic reflections from solid-solid interfaces (die-epoxy-leadframe) exhibit standard phase polarity, whereas delaminations/voids (solid-air or solid-water interfaces) exhibit phase inversion with a high-amplitude reflection peak.

5. **C-SAM Raster Scanning & Void Metrology**:
   - Initialize raster scanning over the die active footprint ($X$-$Y$ stage motion).
   - Capture peak amplitude and phase data across the die-attach plane.
   - Perform automated pixel-threshold area integration to compute total interfacial void area as a percentage of overall die footprint area.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                   Die-Attach & Metrology Target Specs  
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │░░                                   │
  Max R_th (°C/W)┤░░                                   │
                 │▒▒                                   │
Max Void Area (%)┤▒▒                                   │
  Cure Time (min)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                      │
                 │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                      │
   Cure Temp (°C)┤█████████████████████████████████████│
                 │█████████████████████████████████████│
                 └┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0.0     37.5     75.0     112.5  150.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Inspection / Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Interfacial Void Area Under Die** | **$< 5\%$** total area | C-SAM Interface Gated C-Scan Image Quantification |
| **Die-Attach Epoxy Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | **$\le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$** | Thermal Impedance Test (Post-Attach Curing) |
| **Epoxy Cure Condition (Ablebond 84-1LMIS)** | **$150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$** | Calibrated Thermal Oven Profile Log |
| **Subsequent Interconnect Wire Pull Force** | **$\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$** (for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire) | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Mechanical Pull Tester |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Sources Cited
- **Source:** *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*
  - Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cure profile: $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
  - Thermal resistance constraint: $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
  - Acoustic microscopy criterion: void area under die $< 5\%$.
  - Downstream bonding wire pull strength: $\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Transducer acoustic focal length calibration and linear stage positioning directly impact depth-gate resolution; structural vibration coupling through extruded aluminum frames must be mitigated with sorbothane isolation to maintain Abbe errors below 1.5 um across the 100 mm scan axis during high-frequency ultrasonic pulsing.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 100 MHz to 230 MHz inspection frequencies for 180nm DRAM die attach interfaces, deionized water acoustic couplant surface tension and microbubble formation can attenuate acoustic reflectance by >12 dB. The wetting setup must utilize degassed ultra-pure DI water and an integrated acoustic impedance standard to prevent mischaracterizing interfacial delamination.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring calibrated high-frequency focused transducers (100-230 MHz, PVDF or LiNbO3 piezoelectric elements) faces specialized vendor lead times (12-16 weeks); standardizing on a dual-frequency interchangeable fixture with domestic sourcing for degassed couplant reservoirs prevents equipment qualification bottlenecks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Acoustic microscopy calibration must integrate with the post-cure packaging workflow without violating the post-cure queue time before wirebonding. The automated acoustic calibration and scanning setup must execute in under 12 minutes per leadframe strip to sustain MPW assembly cycle targets.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Microbubble cavitation or entrapment in the acoustic couplant medium causing spurious acoustic impedance mismatches and false-positive interfacial void identification.
1. Acoustic focal plane drift due to mechanical stage Abbe error or thermal expansion of the transducer holder during prolonged raster scanning.
1. Moisture ingress into unsealed DRAM die-attach silver epoxy caused by prolonged exposure to DI water couplant without proper post-inspection drying.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-1-01` | **Acoustic Transducer Center Frequency & Pulse-Echo Signal-to-Noise Ratio Calibration** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope equipped with 100 MHz / 230 MHz focused acoustic transducer, 1 GHz digital oscilloscope / pulser-receiver, polished fused silica acoustic calibration standard. | 1. Mount polished fused silica reference standard perpendicularly to the acoustic axis. 2. Position the transducer to the calculated focal distance (Z-height = 12.7 mm). 3. Trigger RF pulser-receiver at 100 MHz excitation and capture reflected front-wall echo on the oscilloscope. 4. Perform 1024-point Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) on the reflected waveform to compute center frequency, bandwidth (-6 dB), and peak-to-peak SNR. 5. Repeat measurement across 9 distinct grid points to calculate Gauge R&R coefficient of variation. | `Transducer center frequency within 100 MHz +/- 5.0 MHz, -6 dB relative bandwidth >= 50%, front-wall peak-to-peak SNR >= 36 dB, and measurement coefficient of variation CV < 1.0% across 9 repetitions.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-1-02` | **Acoustic Couplant Immersion Wetting and Sub-Surface Resolution Validation** | High-Frequency C-SAM station with micro-stepping X-Y raster stage, degasser recirculator unit, and calibrated tungsten carbide wire resolution phantom (25 um diameter wires embedded at 150 um depth). | 1. Immerse the resolution target under the laminar couplant meniscus. 2. Configure time-of-flight depth gate corresponding to 150 um depth in silicon (velocity = 8430 m/s). 3. Execute raster scan at 1.0 um step resolution over a 5 mm x 5 mm region. 4. Extract acoustic intensity line profile across the embedded wire image. 5. Measure full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) lateral acoustic spot size and background noise variance. | `Lateral acoustic resolution FWHM <= 35.0 um at 100 MHz gate, zero microbubble acoustic shadow artifacts (> 3 dB drop) detected across target surface, and stage scan straightness deviation < 2.0 um per 50 mm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (chemical resistant), ANSI Z87.1 Approved Safety Glasses with Side Shields, Cleanroom ESD-safe Lab Coat, Fluid-resistant chemical apron during tank drainage
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA eye contact, flush immediately with eyewash for at least 15 minutes. For skin contact, wash thoroughly with soap and cleanroom water. Inhalation of solvent vapors requires moving individual to fresh air and medical evaluation if dizziness persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Maintain dedicated local chemical exhaust over the solvent rinse/drying zone with continuous face velocity >= 100 FPM (0.5 m/s). Acoustic water tank area maintained under laminar HEPA cleanroom downflow.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent deionized couplant water routed to cleanroom industrial wastewater neutralization stream. Contaminated IPA solvent collected into dedicated grounded hazardous solvent waste drums for certified recycling.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Degassed)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (UPW Type 1) | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA couplant drying)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `>= 99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-die-attach cured silver epoxy leadframes, fully baked at 150 deg C for 60 min, dry, room temperature, free from moisture condensation and unreacted volatile outgassing.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Ultrasonically inspected, completely purged of liquid couplant via CDA/N2 knife dry followed by 80 deg C dehydration bake for 10 minutes; moisture-free pad and leadframe surfaces ready for wirebonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into cured silver epoxy and copper leadframe oxidation causing severe wirebond non-stick on lead (NSOL) failures and acoustic impedance degradation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> High-frequency C-SAM transducer acoustic path and stage scanning system calibrated and qualified with verified center frequency, pulse-echo signal fidelity, degassed DI couplant stability, and sub-35 um acoustic resolution on reference phantoms.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_Transducer_Calibration_Certificate_100MHz.pdf`
- [ ] `Acoustic_Resolution_Phantom_Scan_Raw_Data.csv`
- [ ] `Transducer_Signal_Fidelity_FFT_Analysis.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |

| `ASSERT-01` | **Acoustic center frequency of calibrated high-frequency immersion transducer** | `100.0 MHz` | +/- 5.0 MHz | 1024-point FFT spectral analysis of front-wall echo from fused silica reference standard |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Measurement coefficient of variation (CV) for peak-to-peak acoustic echo amplitude across 9-point grid** | `0.65%` | < 1.0% | Multi-point Gauge R&R repeatability scan across reference substrate in degassed UPW tank |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Lateral acoustic beam spot size (FWHM) at focal zone** | `32.0 um` | <= 35.0 um | Spatial line-spread function derivation across embedded 25 um tungsten wire phantom |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All quantitative assertions satisfied with documented calibration certificate, couplant dissolved oxygen confirmed < 1.0 ppm, and baseline acoustic noise floor verified <= -36 dB prior to production leadframe release.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-PKG-MET-038`
### Title: Interface Gated Ultrasonic C-Scan Acquisition Across Die-Attach Substrates

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Lifecycle

The following ultrasonic C-SAM inspection workflow isolates and quantifies interfacial die-attach delamination/voids between the 180nm DRAM silicon backside and the cured silver epoxy leadframe pad:

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Load Cured Die     │
│       Leadframe        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Acoustic Immersion &  │
│      De-bubbling       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Focus Transducer on   │
│     Silicon/Epoxy      │
│       Interface        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Set Time-of-Flight   │
│        TOF Gate        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Raster C-Scan & Echo  │
│   Amplitude Mapping    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Void Pixel       │
│  Thresholding & Area   │
│     Quantification     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Post-Cure Sample Ingestion**:
   - Verify prior thermal curing of conductive silver-filled epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) completed at **150°C for 60 minutes**.
   - Mount the leadframe strip onto the Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) vacuum stage immersed in deionized (DI) water couplant at room temperature (**25°C**). Degas the liquid bath to eliminate microbubbles.
2. **Acoustic Transducer Selection & Alignment**:
   - Install a high-frequency focused ultrasonic transducer (center frequency $\ge 100\text{--}230\text{ MHz}$) to achieve sub-$20\ \mu\text{m}$ lateral acoustic resolution across the die dimensions.
   - Align the acoustic beam perpendicular ($Z$-normal) to the top surface of the DRAM die.
3. **A-Scan Signal Optimization & Interface Gating**:
   - Acquire the primary RF A-Scan waveform reflecting through the silicon substrate.
   - Identify the front silicon-water reflection peak, followed by the secondary reflection originating from the silicon/silver-epoxy die-attach interface.
   - Position an electronic Time-of-Flight (TOF) tracking gate strictly across the die-to-epoxy interface echo pulse (capturing phase inversion and peak amplitude variation corresponding to acoustic impedance mismatch between bulk silicon and epoxy/voids).
4. **Raster C-Scan Acquisition**:
   - Execute an $X\text{-}Y$ mechanical stage raster scan over the full DRAM die active footprint, including periphery bonding zones surrounding the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.
   - Digitize peak reflection amplitude and polarity per pixel onto an 8-bit or 16-bit acoustic reflectance matrix.
5. **Thresholding & Interfacial Void Area Quantification**:
   - Segment the acoustic image using calibrated echo-amplitude thresholds (air-gap void reflection produces high-amplitude phase-reversed acoustic echo compared to bonded silver epoxy).
   - Integrate total void pixels versus total die area:
     $$\text{Interfacial Void Area (\%)} = \frac{A_{\text{void}}}{A_{\text{die}}} \times 100\%$$
   - Flag any unit exceeding specifications for review or rejection prior to thermosonic gold ball or ultrasonic aluminum wedge wire bonding.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                  Die-Attach C-Scan & Thermal Metrics Target
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                     │
     Cure Duration┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                     │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
         Cure Temp┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Thermal Res (R_th)┤██                                  │
                  │██                                  │
         Void Area┤▓▓                                  │
                  │▓▓                                  │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0     37.5     75.0    112.5  150.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Interfacial Void Area Under Die** | **$< 5.0$** | **$\%$** (Percent of total die attach area) | C-SAM Interface-Gated C-Scan |
| **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{\text{th}}$)** | **$\le 5.0$** | **$^\circ\text{C/W}$** | Transient Thermal Impedance Tester |
| **Epoxy Cure Temperature** | **$150$** | **$^\circ\text{C}$** | In-line Cure Oven Thermocouple Profile |
| **Epoxy Cure Duration** | **$60$** | **$\text{minutes}$** | Integrated Cure Timer Controller |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Sources Cited

- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**
  - Conductive die attach specification: Silver-filled epoxy (*Ablebond 84-1LMIS*) cured at **$150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$**.
  - Acoustic quality criterion: Interfacial void area under die **$< 5\%$** verified via scanning acoustic microscopy.
  - Thermal conduction criterion: Thermal resistance **$R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$**.
  - Upstream/Downstream packaging compatibility: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum square bonding pads connected via $25\ \mu\text{m}$ thermosonic Au ball bonding or room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$) Al-1% Si wedge bonding meeting Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 minimum wire pull strength $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM transducer acoustic impedance matching between the deionized water coupling bath (Z ≈ 1.5 MRayl), the silicon bulk (Z ≈ 19.7 MRayl), and the silver epoxy bond line (Z ≈ 6-8 MRayl) requires strict RF waveform digitization and electronic gate synchronization. Inadequate gate tracking or temporal jitter across non-coplanar leadframe paddles will result in false echo peak acquisition, confounding bulk silicon reflections with interfacial delamination echoes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm packaging scale, inspecting a 20-35 µm thick cured conductive epoxy (Ag flakes suspended in bisphenol-A resin) necessitates a high-frequency transducer (typically 100 MHz to 230 MHz, focal length 0.25 to 0.5 inches). Operating at lower frequencies (<50 MHz) loses axial resolution for detecting micro-voids <50 µm diameter, while exceeding 230 MHz causes excessive acoustic attenuation through thick copper/alloy-42 leadframes and backside silicon rough grinding (~300-400 µm thickness).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-high-frequency focused acoustic transducers (e.g., Sonix, Sonoscan 100-230 MHz piezo-composite elements) have single-source vendor vulnerability with lead times exceeding 24 weeks. Furthermore, the specialized low-cavitation degassed DI water recirculating filters and corrosion-resistant sample fixtures represent consumable bottlenecks during high-throughput packaging pilot runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-Scan acquisition cycle time per QFP/SOP leadframe strip (typically 4x10 matrix) directly gates the downstream wirebonding step. The recipe raster speed must balance pixel resolution (step size <= 5 µm) against the 30-minute post-cure queue time window before moisture absorption forces re-baking under nitrogen storage.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Water bath micro-bubble entrapment on the silicon backside or leadframe cavity inducing pseudo-delamination artifacts and false reject classifications (>5% void count).
1. Time-domain gate drift caused by temperature-dependent acoustic velocity variations in the coupling fluid (0.15% per °C), shifting the echo detection window off the die-attach interface into the bulk substrate.
1. Post-acoustic scanning residual moisture ingress causing popcorning, corrosion, or silver dendrite growth during subsequent wirebonding and transfer molding thermo-compression cycles.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-2-01` | **Interface Gated C-Scan Echo Polarity and Void Area Fraction Qualification** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) equipped with a 150 MHz focused transducer (0.5-inch focal length), 1 GHz digitizer, and automated XY raster scanning stage. | 1. Secure leadframe fixture and planarize sample tilt within ±2.5 µm across the strip using 3-point automated Z-sensor alignment. 2. Position the focal point at the die-attach interface using the A-scan echo trace. 3. Execute raster scan at 10 µm XY pitch covering 100% of the active die footprint (die size: 4.2 mm x 3.8 mm). 4. Capture peak amplitude and phase inversion C-scan maps. 5. Run automated thresholding binarization (JEDEC J-STD-020E / J-STD-035) to quantify single-void maximum area and cumulative interface void percentage. | `Total interfacial void area must be < 5.0% of total die attach surface area; single isolated void area must not exceed 0.5% (or >200 µm equivalent circle diameter); zero perimeter edge void bridging exceeding 10% of die boundary.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-2-02` | **Post-C-Scan Bake-Out and Surface Dehydration Verification** | Vacuum bake-out convection oven, Precision Analytical Balance (0.01 mg resolution), and Contact Angle Goniometer. | 1. Measure initial post-blow-dry sample weight. 2. Transfer strip to vacuum bake-out oven set to 125 °C and < 10 Torr vacuum under N2 purge. 3. Bake for 60 minutes to extract absorbed moisture from exposed epoxy fillet. 4. Measure post-bake mass on analytical balance. 5. Measure DI water contact angle on bond pads across 5 sample dies. | `Mass loss after bake must match pre-immersion baseline within ±0.02 mg (100% moisture desorbed); bond pad surface water contact angle must remain <= 35° confirming absence of surfactant/organic residue contamination.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom gown, Chemical splash apron during water-tank drain and biocide maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with bath fluid: Flush eyes immediately with copious sterile eyewash for at least 15 minutes. Skin contact: Wash thoroughly with neutral soap and water; remove wet ESD clothing. Inhalation of organic solvent trace or IPA: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if respiration is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Acoustic scanner workstation must operate inside an ISO Class 6 laminar flow enclosure with localized exhaust canopy (face velocity >= 100 fpm) for IPA blow-off and tank maintenance.

testcases.instrumentation: Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) equipped with a 150 MHz focused transducer (0.5-inch focal length), 1 GHz digitizer, and automated XY raster scanning stage.
testcases.pre_conditions: Leadframe strip with cured 180nm DRAM dies immersed in 23.0 ± 0.5 °C degassed DI water (dissolved oxygen < 2.0 ppm); acoustic gate calibrated to a 25 ns window centered at the Si-to-epoxy interface with positive/negative RF peak phase tracking enabled.
