1. Secure leadframe fixture and planarize sample tilt within ±2.5 µm across the strip using 3-point automated Z-sensor alignment.

testcases.pre_conditions: Leadframe strips immediately removed from C-SAM DI water tank, blow-dried with 0.2 µm filtered clean dry air (CDA) at 30 psi.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Inspection Sample Verification**:
   - Verify that the 180nm DRAM dies mounted with silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS) have completed curing at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
   - Ensure the bonded substrate/leadframe is free of particulate debris. Submerge the test vehicle into the acoustic immersion tank filled with deaerated deionized (DI) water (acoustic couplant).

2. **Acoustic Transducer Setup & Focal Alignment**:
   - Mount a high-frequency focused acoustic transducer (nominal center frequency: $50\text{ to }100\text{ MHz}$).
   - Adjust the Z-axis focus to position the acoustic beam waist precisely at the interfacial boundary between the backside of the silicon DRAM die and the silver-filled conductive epoxy attach layer.

3. **A-Scan Time-of-Flight (ToF) Gating**:
   - Inspect the real-time RF waveform (A-Scan). Identify the primary reflection peaks: front die surface echo, silicon-epoxy interface echo, and leadframe back-interface echo.
   - Set an electronic data collection gate tightly over the silicon-to-die-attach epoxy reflection echo to isolate interface signals from package surface reflections.

4. **C-Scan High-Resolution Raster Acquisition**:
   - Program the XY scanning stage to execute a raster C-scan over the full perimeter of the die attach area.
   - Record peak reflection amplitudes and phase inversion data for each spatial pixel across the die footprint.

5. **Acoustic Reflection Amplitude & Phase Thresholding**:
   - At a sound silicon-to-epoxy boundary, acoustic impedance mismatch produces an echo of moderate amplitude and positive phase.
   - At an air void or delamination, the drastic impedance mismatch ($Z_{\text{silicon}} \gg Z_{\text{air}}$) generates total acoustic reflection accompanied by a $180^\circ$ phase inversion (negative reflection coefficient).
   - Set the amplitude discrimination threshold to segregate high-amplitude phase-inverted void echoes from bonded epoxy regions.

6. **Binarization & Total Interfacial Void Area Quantification**:
   - Convert the gated C-scan image into a binary matrix ($1 = \text{void/delamination}$, $0 = \text{bonded epoxy interface}$).
   - Integrate the total void pixels ($N_{\text{void}}$) relative to total die interfacial pixels ($N_{\text{total}}$):
     $$\text{Void Area } (\%) = \left(\frac{\sum A_{\text{void}}}{A_{\text{die}}}\right) \times 100\% = \left(\frac{N_{\text{void}}}{N_{\text{total}}}\right) \times 100\%$$
   - Check if $\text{Void Area } < 5\%$. Release passed lots to wirebonding ($25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire thermosonic gold ball or ultrasonic aluminum wedge bonding); quarantine failing units for acoustic cross-sectioning and failure analysis.

---

| **Silver Epoxy Pre-Attach Cure Profile** | $150$ for $60$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ / $\text{minutes}$ | In-Line Convection Oven Thermal Profiler |

### 4. Verified Context Citations
- **Source**: `Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging`
  - *Context extract*: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g. Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$. Thermal resistance $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C}/\text{W}$; void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy. On-chip bonding pads are $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares; $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire requires pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$ per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM transducer acoustic impedance matching requires precise acoustic focal zone positioning at the DRAM backside-to-leadframe epoxy interface (Z_silicon ≈ 19.7 MRayl, Z_epoxy ≈ 3.5 MRayl, Z_copper ≈ 44.3 MRayl). Phase inversion of the acoustic reflected radio-frequency (RF) A-scan echo must be tracked dynamically to distinguish void/delamination (silicon-to-air acoustic impedance boundary causing a 180-degree phase flip, reflection coefficient R ≈ -1.0) from benign epoxy-thickness variations. Digital threshold gating without dynamic RF waveform tracking introduces systematic over- or under-counting of void boundaries.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Silver epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablebond 84-1LMIS or equivalent) outgassing during thermal curing at 150-175°C typically nucleates sub-50 µm micro-voids that coalesce under high-stress die corners. High-frequency acoustic transducers (100 MHz to 230 MHz UHF) are mandatory to achieve lateral resolution below 15 µm; operating at standard 15-30 MHz will suffer from Raleigh scattering and beam broadening, failing to resolve isolated void areas and masking true sub-5% cumulative void percentages across the 180nm DRAM active core area.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic transducer heads (specifically 100-230 MHz spherically focused piezoelectric/PVDF or lithium niobate lenses) carry lead times exceeding 16 weeks with high risk of quartz/piezo element damage if subjected to unbuffered DI-water immersion without degasification. Deionized water coupling tanks require constant filtration and UV-sterilization to avoid bio-film and micro-bubble accumulation on the DRAM leadframe strip, which causes false-positive void detection and premature transducer face degradation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must balance scan pitch against raster speed. Full-die C-scan at 5 µm pixel resolution on an entire 16-unit leadframe strip currently takes >45 minutes per strip, creating a severe operational bottleneck prior to wirebonding. An automated two-stage screening protocol (coarse 25 µm A/C-scan gate followed by 5 µm fine C-scan on borderline strips exceeding 3.5% apparent voiding) is required to sustain pilot-line schedule milestones.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-bubble cavitation in immersion deionized water couplant adhering to package backside, falsely flagged as interfacial die-attach delamination (Type I error).
1. Epoxy fillet acoustic shadow masking peripheral die edge delamination due to acoustic refraction at angled silver-epoxy menisci.
1. Post-scan moisture entrapment inside micro-fissures or unsealed die margins inducing popcorn cracking or dendritic silver migration during subsequent wirebond pre-heat (200°C).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-3-01` | **C-SAM C-Scan Interfacial Acoustic Reflection Phase-Gated Void Area Quantification** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (Sonix ECHO or Nordson SONOSCAN Gen7) equipped with a 100 MHz spherically focused immersion transducer (focal length = 12.7 mm, spot size = 18 µm), automated RF A-scan phase-inversion gating module, and calibrated image analysis software (ImageJ/FIJI or C-SAM Analysis Suite). | 1. Secure leadframe strip in automated sample fixture immersed in degassed DI water couplant. 2. Position the 100 MHz transducer focal plane precisely at the silicon-to-die-attach epoxy interface using time-of-flight RF A-scan delay. 3. Configure electronic gate width to 15 ns centered around the die-attach interface reflection echo. 4. Set phase detection logic: negative echo polarity (phase inversion) flagged as delamination/void, positive echo flagged as intact epoxy bond. 5. Perform raster C-scan across 100% of the die active area (nominal 2.5 mm x 2.5 mm) at a step pitch of 5.0 µm. 6. Segment void pixels via dual-threshold histogram binarization and compute cumulative void area percentage: Total Void % = (Sum of Void Pixels / Total Die Area Pixels) * 100. | `Total interfacial void area must be < 5.00% of total die footprint area; single contiguous void area must not exceed 0.50 mm²; zero corner delamination exceeding 1.0% contiguous area.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-3-02` | **Acoustic Reflection Amplitude Calibration and Transducer Linearity Verification** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope with digital RF oscilloscope capture (minimum 1.0 GSa/s sampling rate), calibrated air-gap delamination calibration block (silicon-vacuum standard), and calibrated 50 MHz-230 MHz pulser-receiver. | 1. Position transducer over the reference standard containing known simulated 100 µm, 50 µm, and 25 µm interfacial voids. 2. Capture peak-to-peak amplitude (V_pp) of the interface echo at an intact reference region (silicon-epoxy) and a total air-gap void region. 3. Calculate acoustic reflection amplitude ratio R_measured = (V_void - V_bond) / (V_void + V_bond). 4. Verify system linearity by stepping gain from 0 dB to 40 dB in 6 dB increments while verifying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) >= 26 dB. 5. Measure spatial measurement repeatability across 5 consecutive scans over the 50 µm reference void target. | `Spatial resolution must resolve isolated 25 µm void structures; repeated void area measurement variance (1-sigma) must be <= 0.20% across 5 consecutive runs; interface echo SNR >= 26 dB.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (Class 100/ISO 5 compatible, minimum 6 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof chemical safety goggles, Antistatic ESD-safe cleanroom coat and footwear, Face mask (cleanroom particle certified)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with couplant additive or isopropanol: flush skin thoroughly with copious water for 15 minutes. For eye splash: rinse eyes immediately at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For isopropanol inhalation: move individual to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if irritation, dizziness, or respiratory distress develops.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank maintenance, IPA cleaning, and leadframe post-drying must be performed under dedicated localized exhaust ventilation (LEV) or laminar flow clean hood providing minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent couplant containing micro-biocide must be collected in dedicated labeled aqueous waste carboys and neutralized to pH 6.5-8.5 prior to hazardous waste disposal. Spent isopropanol solvent must be segregated into flammable solvent waste containers; do not discharge to general cleanroom drain.

| **Biocide / Algaecide (Couplant Tank Maintenance)** | `26172-55-4` | Technical Grade | `<0.05%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-cure silver epoxy die attach assembly; fully polymerized epoxy fillet with zero unreacted monomer residue; clean Cu/Ag leadframe surface free of condensation or organic films.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Acoustically scanned, fully IPA-rinsed and vacuum-baked dried die assembly; absolute moisture content < 0.1 wt% on leadframe/die; leadframe pads free of oxidation ready for wirebonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time or failing to perform immediate bake-out (120°C for 30 minutes in N2) following acoustic immersion testing drives atmospheric water absorption into epoxy micro-voids, causing catastrophic steam-induced popcorn cracking and wirebond lift during subsequent 220°C ultrasonic ball bonding.

**Exit Objective Summary**:

Phase inversion of the acoustic reflected radio-frequency (RF) A-scan echo must be tracked dynamically to distinguish void/delamination (silicon-to-air acoustic impedance boundary causing a 180-degree phase flip, reflection coefficient R ≈ -1.0) from benign epoxy-thickness variations. Digital threshold gating without dynamic RF waveform tracking introduces systematic over- or under-counting of void boundaries.
critics.domain_expert: Silver epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablebond 84-1LMIS or equivalent) outgassing during thermal curing at 150-175°C typically nucleates sub-50 µm micro-voids that coalesce under high-stress die corners. High-frequency acoustic transducers (100 MHz to 230 MHz UHF) are mandatory to achieve lateral resolution below 15 µm; operating at standard 15-30 MHz will suffer from Raleigh scattering and beam broadening, failing to resolve isolated void areas and masking true sub-5% cumulative void percentages across the 180nm DRAM active core area.
critics.supply_chain: Acoustic transducer heads (specifically 100-230 MHz spherically focused piezoelectric/PVDF or lithium niobate lenses) carry lead times exceeding 16 weeks with high risk of quartz/piezo element damage if subjected to unbuffered DI-water immersion without degasification. Deionized water coupling tanks require constant filtration and UV-sterilization to avoid bio-film and micro-bubble accumulation on the DRAM leadframe strip, which causes false-positive void detection and premature transducer face degradation.
critics.laya_pm: Metrology throughput must balance scan pitch against raster speed. Full-die C-scan at 5 µm pixel resolution on an entire 16-unit leadframe strip currently takes >45 minutes per strip, creating a severe operational bottleneck prior to wirebonding. An automated two-stage screening protocol (coarse 25 µm A/C-scan gate followed by 5 µm fine C-scan on borderline strips exceeding 3.5% apparent voiding) is required to sustain pilot-line schedule milestones.
critical_failure_modes: Micro-bubble cavitation in immersion deionized water couplant adhering to package backside, falsely flagged as interfacial die-attach delamination (Type I error).
Epoxy fillet acoustic shadow masking peripheral die edge delamination due to acoustic refraction at angled silver-epoxy menisci.
Post-scan moisture entrapment inside micro-fissures or unsealed die margins inducing popcorn cracking or dendritic silver migration during subsequent wirebond pre-heat (200°C).

testcases.title: C-SAM C-Scan Interfacial Acoustic Reflection Phase-Gated Void Area Quantification
testcases.instrumentation: Scanning Acoustic Microscope (Sonix ECHO or Nordson SONOSCAN Gen7) equipped with a 100 MHz spherically focused immersion transducer (focal length = 12.7 mm, spot size = 18 µm), automated RF A-scan phase-inversion gating module, and calibrated image analysis software (ImageJ/FIJI or C-SAM Analysis Suite).
testcases.pre_conditions: Cured 180nm DRAM dies on Cu leadframe strips; couplant tank filled with degassed, deionized water (dissolved oxygen < 1.0 ppm, resistivity >= 18.0 MOhm*cm at 22°C); transducer alignment calibrated against standard quartz resolution target (MIL-STD-883 Method 2030).
testcases.procedure: 1. Secure leadframe strip in automated sample fixture immersed in degassed DI water couplant. 2. Position the 100 MHz transducer focal plane precisely at the silicon-to-die-attach epoxy interface using time-of-flight RF A-scan delay. 3. Configure electronic gate width to 15 ns centered around the die-attach interface reflection echo. 4. Set phase detection logic: negative echo polarity (phase inversion) flagged as delamination/void, positive echo flagged as intact epoxy bond. 5. Perform raster C-scan across 100% of the die active area (nominal 2.5 mm x 2.5 mm) at a step pitch of 5.0 µm. 6. Segment void pixels via dual-threshold histogram binarization and compute cumulative void area percentage: Total Void % = (Sum of Void Pixels / Total Die Area Pixels) * 100.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total interfacial void area must be < 5.00% of total die footprint area; single contiguous void area must not exceed 0.50 mm²; zero corner delamination exceeding 1.0% contiguous area.

testcases.title: Acoustic Reflection Amplitude Calibration and Transducer Linearity Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Scanning Acoustic Microscope with digital RF oscilloscope capture (minimum 1.0 GSa/s sampling rate), calibrated air-gap delamination calibration block (silicon-vacuum standard), and calibrated 50 MHz-230 MHz pulser-receiver.
testcases.pre_conditions: Ambient cleanroom temperature controlled at 21.0 ± 1.0°C; couplant water degassed for minimum 60 minutes via inline vacuum deaerator; pulser energy stabilized for 30 minutes.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position transducer over the reference standard containing known simulated 100 µm, 50 µm, and 25 µm interfacial voids. 2. Capture peak-to-peak amplitude (V_pp) of the interface echo at an intact reference region (silicon-epoxy) and a total air-gap void region. 3. Calculate acoustic reflection amplitude ratio R_measured = (V_void - V_bond) / (V_void + V_bond). 4. Verify system linearity by stepping gain from 0 dB to 40 dB in 6 dB increments while verifying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) >= 26 dB. 5. Measure spatial measurement repeatability across 5 consecutive scans over the 50 µm reference void target.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Spatial resolution must resolve isolated 25 µm void structures; repeated void area measurement variance (1-sigma) must be <= 0.20% across 5 consecutive runs; interface echo SNR >= 26 dB.

ppe_required: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (Class 100/ISO 5 compatible, minimum 6 mil thickness)
ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof chemical safety goggles
Antistatic ESD-safe cleanroom coat and footwear
Face mask (cleanroom particle certified)
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin contact with couplant additive or isopropanol: flush skin thoroughly with copious water for 15 minutes. For eye splash: rinse eyes immediately at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For isopropanol inhalation: move individual to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if irritation, dizziness, or respiratory distress develops.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Immersion tank maintenance, IPA cleaning, and leadframe post-drying must be performed under dedicated localized exhaust ventilation (LEV) or laminar flow clean hood providing minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent couplant containing micro-biocide must be collected in dedicated labeled aqueous waste carboys and neutralized to pH 6.5-8.5 prior to hazardous waste disposal. Spent isopropanol solvent must be segregated into flammable solvent waste containers; do not discharge to general cleanroom drain.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Post-cure silver epoxy die attach assembly; fully polymerized epoxy fillet with zero unreacted monomer residue; clean Cu/Ag leadframe surface free of condensation or organic films.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Acoustically scanned, fully IPA-rinsed and vacuum-baked dried die assembly; absolute moisture content < 0.1 wt% on leadframe/die; leadframe pads free of oxidation ready for wirebonding.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding queue time or failing to perform immediate bake-out (120°C for 30 minutes in N2) following acoustic immersion testing drives atmospheric water absorption into epoxy micro-voids, causing catastrophic steam-induced popcorn cracking and wirebond lift during subsequent 220°C ultrasonic ball bonding.

expected_result.summary: Full non-destructive acoustic scanning metrology qualification confirming total interfacial void area below 5.0% across 100% of tested 180nm DRAM dies, complete elimination of air cavitation artifacts via phase-inversion gating, and post-metrology moisture extraction protocol verification.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Total interfacial die-attach void area across active DRAM die footprint
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated pixel threshold count of 100 MHz phase-inverted C-SAM image segmented per TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-2-3-01

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum single contiguous void area at die corner or edge zone
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Morphological blob analysis of calibrated C-SAM acoustic reflection image

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-metrology residual moisture content after vacuum dehydration bake
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Karl Fischer coulometric moisture titration on sacrificed leadframe epoxy coupons

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Zero lots exhibiting > 5.00% total voiding across a 32-unit sample; zero single voids > 0.35 mm²; 100% verification of moisture removal (< 0.05 wt%) with sign-off signatures from Systems Integration Engineer and Quality/Packaging Metrology Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Destructive Die Shear Testing per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 & Fracture Analysis

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Destructive die shear testing per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 is the final mechanical integrity check for the 180nm DRAM die-to-leadframe interface. From a packaging architecture perspective, testing must be correlated with pre-shear Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) acoustic impedance scans to verify whether low shear force readings stem from bulk epoxy curing deficits or localized adhesive delamination caused by micro-void clusters (<5% total die area specification).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For a standard 180nm open-source DRAM die mounted with conductive silver epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min), MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 defines a minimum breaking force curve based on die attach area. Testing requires a motorized die shear tester equipped with a precision tungsten carbide shear tool positioned at a standoff height of 25 to 50 µm (or < 1/3 die thickness) parallel to the die edge. Post-shear fracture mode analysis must classify separation into adhesive failure, cohesive failure within the silver epoxy matrix, or substrate/silicon fracture, with acceptable samples demonstrating predominantly cohesive bulk epoxy failure (>80% die attach material coverage).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Destructive die shear consumes prototype silicon and leadframe units from multi-project wafer (MPW) runs; test coupons and dedicated mechanical test dies (dummy silicon) should be allocated during wafer dicing to preserve functional DRAM units. Calibration standards, calibrated load cells (5 kgf / 50 kgf ranges), and certified tungsten carbide shear tips must be secured to maintain traceability under ISO/IEC 17025 testing protocols.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die shear execution gates the release of downstream wire bonding parameter freeze and final encapsulation in packaging lot validation. To avoid process hold-ups, fracture analysis and automated optical failure categorization must conclude within 4 hours post-shear to immediately feed corrective cure profile adjustments back into the convection oven dispensing line.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial adhesive separation between leadframe silver plating and conductive epoxy due to organic contamination or oxidation prior to die placement.
1. Die edge chipping and premature silicon brittle fracture caused by excessive shear tool contact height (>1/3 die thickness) or angular misalignment during lateral ram displacement.
1. Under-cured epoxy cohesive rupture exhibiting ductile tearing and shear strength below MIL-STD-883 threshold due to thermal ramp-rate lag or oven zone temperature non-uniformity.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-3-01` | **MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 Die Shear Strength Metrology** | Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Bondtester equipped with 50 kgf calibrated shear load cell and 2.0 mm wide flat-edge tungsten carbide shear tool | 1. Position the shear tool tip 35 um (+/- 5 um) above the leadframe surface to ensure contact within the lower 1/3 of the DRAM die thickness. 2. Advance the shear tool toward the die edge at a controlled test speed of 100 um/s until contact is sensed. 3. Apply lateral shear displacement at 100 um/s continuously until complete die detachment or load peak drop exceeding 50% occurs. 4. Record peak rupture force in kilogram-force (kgf) and plot the full force-versus-displacement profile. | `Peak shear force must exceed MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 minimum threshold based on die area (for 4 mm^2 die, minimum shear force >= 2.5 kgf; target >= 5.0 kgf for robust epoxy attachment). Any premature mechanical detachment below standard limit constitutes a test failure.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-3-02` | **Post-Shear Fracture Surface Mode and Area Coverage Metrology** | High-resolution optical inspection microscope with digital calibrated image analyzer (Keyence VHX-7000) and Scanning Electron Microscope / Energy Dispersive X-Ray Spectrometer (SEM-EDS) | 1. Place the leadframe die attach pad and inverted die backside under optical microscope at 50x-200x magnification. 2. Capture high-resolution digital micrographs across the full contact footprint. 3. Apply digital thresholding image analysis to quantify relative area percentages of: (a) cohesive epoxy failure, (b) leadframe/epoxy adhesive peeling, and (c) silicon fracture. 4. Perform SEM-EDS micro-spot elemental analysis on exposed non-epoxy regions to identify residual silver flakes or bare metal/organic contamination. | `Post-shear epoxy residue remaining on the leadframe die attach pad must show >= 80% cohesive epoxy failure across the nominal die footprint. Complete interfacial peeling exposing bare leadframe silver plating over > 20% area constitutes rejection.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved chemical splash safety glasses with side shields, Nitrile gloves (minimum 4 mil thickness), Anti-static ESD lab coat, Closed-toe safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with solvent residue or uncured epoxy debris, wash immediately with soap and plenty of water for at least 15 minutes. In case of eye contact with fractured silicon micro-shards or solvent splash, rinse cautiously with eyewash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open and seek medical evaluation. If IPA vapors inhaled, remove casualty to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation of shear tester and solvent-based coupon cleaning must be performed under local chemical exhaust hood or dedicated laminar flow clean-bench with exhaust face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA solvent wipes and fractured silicon/epoxy fragments must be collected in labeled, vapor-tight, hazardous solvent waste containers. Discarded silicon shards must be contained in puncture-proof sharps containers and disposed of per local semiconductor hazardous solid waste regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Silver Flake Filler (in cured matrix residue)** | `7440-22-4` | Technical Grade | `> 70% in epoxy matrix` |
| **Diglycidyl Ether of Bisphenol-A (Epoxy Resin base)** | `25068-38-6` | Reagent Grade | `< 25% (cured thermoset)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Leadframe packages post-oven cure (150°C, 60 min) with C-SAM inspection completed; package dry, ambient cooled, and free of moisture or finger oils.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Sheared leadframe pad and fracture silicon surfaces documented, purged with dry N2, and stored in desiccated vacuum carrier for SEM-EDS validation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive queue time in open air causes ambient moisture absorption and atmospheric sulfurization/tarnish of exposed silver leadframe plating and epoxy fracture interfaces, invalidating SEM-EDS surface elemental contamination analysis.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical, mechanical, and fractographic validation of the DRAM die attach interface in accordance with MIL-STD-883 Method 2019, confirming peak shear strength >= 5.0 kgf (for 4 mm^2 die) with cohesive epoxy failure mode >= 80% coverage.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_die_shear_force_displacement_curves.csv`
- [ ] `mil_std_883_die_shear_metrology_report.pdf`
- [ ] `post_shear_fracture_optical_micrographs.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Peak die shear breaking force meets or exceeds MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 specification for 4.0 mm^2 DRAM die footprint** | `5.0 kgf` | +/- 0.5 kgf (absolute minimum >= 2.5 kgf) | Calibrated load cell data recording on automated bond tester during 100 um/s shear ram displacement |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-destructive shear cohesive fracture coverage area of silver epoxy on leadframe die attach pad** | `85%` | >= 80% minimum | High-magnification optical digital threshold image analysis across the complete 4 mm^2 pad surface |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Shear tool contact clearance height above leadframe paddle surface during test execution** | `35 um` | +/- 5 um | Pre-test contact touchdown zeroing and precision optical z-axis micro-stepper gauge |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of tested sample coupons (sample size n >= 5 per packaging lot) exhibit shear strength >= 2.5 kgf with zero instances of catastrophic interfacial leadframe delamination (<20% bare metal exposure), corroborated by formal engineering sign-off on the generated metrology report.

### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Shear Tool Alignment and Fixture Setup per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019

**Module Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe > Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Void Analysis and Die Shear Strength Metrology > Destructive Die Shear Testing per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019

---

#### 1. Setup & Execution Flow

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Fixture Clamping &  │
│       Leveling       │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│     Tool Angle &     │
│  Parallelism Check   │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   Stand-off Height   │
│       Setting        │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│      Shear Rate      │
│    Calibration &     │
│       Zeroing        │
│                      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

#### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate & Package Fixturing**:
   - Mount the leadframe / ceramic DIP package containing the 180nm DRAM die (attached with silver-filled conductive epoxy Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ min}$) into the micro-mechanical shear tester universal vice fixture.
   - Tighten torque clamps to secure the carrier against lateral slippage. Verify zero mechanical deflection under pre-load.
2. **Tool Selection & Parallelism Alignment**:
   - Select a hardened tungsten carbide shear tool whose contact width exceeds the full die edge length by $10\%\text{ to }20\%$, ensuring no edge overhang or point stress concentrations.
   - Adjust the rotational goniometer stage so that the shear tool face is strictly parallel to the DRAM die edge ($\le 1.0^\circ$ angular deviation, $< 5\,\mu\text{m}$ clearance gap variation across the interface).
3. **Stand-Off (Clearance) Height Calibration**:
   - Drive the shear tool vertically downward until it lightly contacts the substrate floor directly adjacent to the bond line (auto-touch contact sense at $< 5\text{ gf}$).
   - Retract the tool vertically to establish the calibrated stand-off height $H_{\text{stand-off}} = 12.5\,\mu\text{m}$ (maintained between $10\,\mu\text{m}$ and $25\,\mu\text{m}$ above the substrate surface to clear the epoxy meniscus while engaging the lower third of the die sidewall without scraping the substrate).
4. **Shear Axis Travel & Rate Zeroing**:
   - Align the tool face perpendicular ($90^\circ \pm 1^\circ$) to the shear travel axis to eliminate peel, tilt, or rotational moments.
   - Set the crosshead shear stroke rate to a controlled quasi-static velocity of $0.10\text{ to }0.50\,\text{mm/s}$ until destructive shear separation occurs.

---

#### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

| Metric Parameter | Target Value / Specification | Units | Verification Tool / Protocol |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shear Tool Stand-off Height** | $12.5 \pm 2.5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical Z-encoder / contact touch-down sensor |
| **Tool-to-Die Edge Parallelism** | $\le 1.0$ (gap deviation $< 5$) | degrees ($\mu\text{m}$) | High-magnification microscope / camera split-prism |
| **Substrate Fixture Deflection** | $0.00 \pm 0.02$ | $\text{mm}$ | Linear displacement dial gauge during pre-load |
| **Die Attach Pre-Test Acoustic Voiding** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) |
| **Die Attach Thermal Resistance** | $R_{\text{th}} \le 5.0$ | $^\circ\text{C/W}$ | Transient thermal junction tester |

```text
                    │██                                │
       Void Area Max┤██                                │
                    │▓▓                                │

```

---

#### 4. Context Source Citations
- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - Die attach adhesive: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (*Ablebond 84-1LMIS*) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
  - Thermal resistance requirement: $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
  - Acoustic inspection requirement: Void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).
  - Mechanical baseline test protocol: MIL-STD-883 compliance framework.

*The micro-knowledge for this procedure has been persisted in [`docs/knowledge/sop_die_shear_alignment_mil_std_883.md`](./docs/knowledge/sop_die_shear_alignment_mil_std_883.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The kinematic rigidity and coplanarity of the shear tester fixture chuck relative to the load cell axis must maintain mechanical runout under 2.5 µm across the entire 12 mm travel stroke. Tool tip clearance above the substrate metallization plane must be strictly locked to 10% of total die thickness (or max 25 µm per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019) to eliminate parasitic bending moments or shear tool contact skiving into the copper leadframe.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Method 2019 mandates pure horizontal shear without rotational yaw; tool misalignment greater than 1.0 degree causes localized stress concentrations at die edge corners, artificially precipitating low-force brittle edge-chipping rather than genuine bulk conductive epoxy adhesive/cohesive failure. Fixture clamping must hold leadframe paddle flat without inducing mechanical pre-stress or micro-cracking in the 180nm CMOS active circuitry.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide and diamond-faced shear tool inserts require dual-source supplier qualification (e.g., Dage/Nordson and Royce) with verified NIST-traceable calibration gauge blocks. Custom vacuum clamping nests for 180nm DRAM open-frame leadframes have a 6-week CNC lead time; stock multi-cavity modular clamp jaws must be inventoried to prevent assembly line stoppage during qualification runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die shear fixture alignment sign-off is on the critical gating path for Packaging & Metrology Lot Clearance; automated optical alignment recipes and calibrated torque screw protocols must be finalized within Sprint 3 to enable destructive sampling of the 25-unit pilot lot without budget overrun on sacrificial functional die.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Shear tool ground clearance set too low (< 5 µm), resulting in tungsten carbide tool directly impacting and skiving into the leadframe silver plating, yielding false-high shear force readings.
1. Shear tool face yaw angular deviation (> 1.5 degrees off die edge parallel), concentrating initial impact force onto a single die corner and triggering silicon fracture at sub-specification thresholds (< 2.5 kgf).
1. Insufficient vacuum or mechanical hold-down clamping rigidity allowing leadframe flexure/slippage during load application, generating invalid multi-peak force-displacement curves.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Powder-free chemical-resistant nitrile gloves (min 6 mil thickness), ESD-safe cleanroom coat, Polycarbonate flying-debris scatter shield mounted around shear fixture
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with solvent or flying silicon particulate: Flush eyes immediately with copious clean water at eyewash station for 15 minutes. In case of skin cuts from silicon die fragments: Wash wound with antiseptic soap and water, apply sterile dressing, and seek medical attention. If solvent vapors inhaled: Move person to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation within localized exhaust canopy or dedicated laminar flow clean bench with min face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) to vent solvent fumes during cleaning.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of cracked silicon shards and fractured leadframes in dedicated sharps container; collect solvent wipe waste in sealed, grounded, fire-rated flammables disposal bins per RCRA guidelines.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-cured Ag epoxy die attach leadframes, free of unreacted epoxy outgassing residues, surface moisture, or foreign particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Destructively sheared leadframe paddle exposed for optical/SEM fracture surface metrology, stored in inert N2 desiccator to prevent copper/silver oxidation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into epoxy filleting causing plasticization, lower measured shear strength, and oxidation of exposed copper/silver leadframe metallization skewing failure mode analysis.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: Destructive Die Shear Loading and Critical Fracture Force Metrology
**Module:** BEOL Packaging, Assembly & Reliability Testing  
**Technology Node:** 180nm CMOS DRAM (Open-Source DRAM Chip Architecture)  
**Standard Reference:** MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 (Die Shear Strength)  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Sequence

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Sample Fixturing and  │
│        Clamping        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Tool Touchdown and   │
│        Standoff        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Lateral Force      │
│  Loading at Constant   │
│        Velocity        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Critical Fracture    │
│   Force Acquisition    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Interface and      │
│  Residue Failure Mode  │
│        Analysis        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Execution Procedure

1. **Pre-Test Preparation & Verification:**
   - Confirm die attach curing parameters: Conductive silver-filled epoxy (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured on leadframe at **150°C for 60 minutes**.
   - Verify acoustic integrity: Perform pre-shear Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) to confirm die-attach void area is **< 5%** across the whole die footprint.
   - Inspect package and substrate for zero contamination and flat planar seating.

2. **Substrate Fixturing & Clamping:**
   - Mount the ceramic DIP/QFN or leadframe carrier into the rigid mechanical shear anvil clamp.
   - Clamp the leadframe securely to eliminate any parasitic compliant deflection or horizontal slipping during force application.

3. **Shear Tool Alignment & Standoff Configuration:**
   - Select a hardened tungsten carbide or diamond-tipped shear wedge whose contact width exceeds the edge length of the DRAM die.
   - Lower the shear blade to the leadframe zero-datum (touchdown surface).
   - Set the vertical tool clearance standoff height between **13 µm and 25 µm** (or ≤ 1/3 of the total die thickness) from the leadframe surface to prevent contacting the adhesive meniscus or scraping the leadframe substrate.
   - Align the tool face parallel to the DRAM die edge at a lateral approach angle perpendicular to the die wall ($90^\circ \pm 1^\circ$).

4. **Constant-Speed Lateral Force Loading:**
   - Initiate motorized lateral travel at a controlled test displacement rate of **0.1 mm/s to 0.5 mm/s** per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019.
   - Continuously record the dynamic force displacement profile using a calibrated load cell.

5. **Critical Fracture Force & Event Trigger:**
   - Advance the shear tool until catastrophic bond separation occurs (detected as a sudden drop of $\ge 50\%$ in load cell readout).
   - Capture and record the peak load as the **Critical Fracture Force ($F_{\text{crit}}$)**.

6. **Post-Fracture Failure Mode & Interface Metrology:**
   - Remove the sheared specimen and inspect the fractured die-pad interface under an optical inspection microscope (at $\ge 50\times$ magnification).
   - Classify the fracture mechanism into standard failure categories:
     - *Cohesive failure*: Fracture through the bulk silver epoxy (acceptable if $F_{\text{crit}}$ exceeds threshold).
     - *Adhesive failure*: Interfacial debonding between epoxy-leadframe or epoxy-silicon backside.
     - *Die cracking / fracture*: Silicon fragmentation.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                       Die Attach Qualification Limits  
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │██████████████                    │
     Cure Time (min)┤██████████████                    │
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
       Cure Temp (C)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
Thermal Resist (C/W)┤▒▒                                │
                    │▒▒                                │
  CSAM Void Area (%)┤░░                                │
                    │░░                                │
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                    0.0    37.5     75.0    112.5 150.0 
```

| Parameter Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Die Attach Pre-Test Void Area** | **$< 5.0$** | **$\%$** | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) |
| **Silver Epoxy Cure Thermal Profile** | **$150 \pm 5$ for $60$** | **$^\circ\text{C}$ / $\text{min}$** | Calibrated Convection / Box Oven Profiler |
| **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | **$\le 5.0$** | **$^\circ\text{C/W}$** | Junction-to-Case Thermal Metrology |
| **Wire Bond Pull Strength Compliance** | **$\ge 4.0$** | **$\text{grams-force (gf)}$** | MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull Metrology |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations
* **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:**
  - *Epoxy curing condition:* Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at **150°C for 60 minutes**.
  - *Package acoustic and thermal metrics:* Thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$; acoustic microscopy void area under die $< 5\%$.
  - *Interconnect pull strength:* MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$ for $25\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ wire.
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - 180nm DRAM cell layout context, folded bitline topologies, and metallization interface integration.
* **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - Physical layer stack thermal budgets, substrate integrity, and back-end packaging constraints.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Destructive die shear testing per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 introduces significant localized mechanical stress gradients across the 180nm DRAM die edge. Tool tip contact height must be strictly controlled at 25 um to 50 um (or <= 1/3 of die thickness) above the substrate surface to avoid inducing artificial bending moments or edge-chipping artifacts that distort true interfacial shear force measurement. Fixturing rigidity and load cell alignment are paramount to ensure purely uniaxially applied lateral displacement without off-axis parasitic torques.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For conductive silver-filled epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablestik 84-1LMISR) cured on a copper or silver-plated leadframe, failure mode classification is as critical as peak rupture force. Researchers must distinguish between bulk cohesive epoxy rupture (>80% epoxy remaining on leadframe flag), clean adhesive interfacial failure at the die backside / leadframe interface (indicative of organic contamination or incomplete cross-linking), and catastrophic silicon cleavage/die cracking. The 180nm DRAM die area (approx. 6.25 mm^2) mandates a minimum rupture threshold exceeding 2.5x the baseline MIL-STD-883 limit of 2.5 kg force.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide shear tool tips and calibrated piezoelectric load cells (range 0-50 kgf, class 0.5 accuracy) face lead times of 8-12 weeks from precision metrology vendors like Dage or Nordson Sonobond. Leadframe material consistency, specifically Ag-plating thickness (3.0-5.0 um) and micro-roughness variations across production lots, directly impact shear adhesion repeatability, requiring lot-matched control coupons to avoid false rejections during lot qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Destructive die shear consumes 5-10 fully assembled DRAM packages per cured batch, directly conflicting with tight MPW silicon budget constraints. Metrology scheduling must tightly align with C-SAM acoustic void scanning runs to correlate non-destructive acoustic void percentages with destructive shear failure thresholds, preventing unscheduled test bottlenecks and optimizing sample utilization prior to molding encapsulation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Adhesive delamination at the silicon backside to Ag-epoxy interface occurring below 1.5 kgf/mm^2 due to native oxide contamination or insufficient cure cross-linking.
1. Shear tool slippage or silicon wedge fracture induced by improper tool clearance (>50 um clearance or tool contact angle misaligned by >0.5 degrees), invalidating interfacial shear data.
1. Silver flake segregation or localized resin bleed-out along leadframe paddle perimeter causing non-uniform stress distribution and catastrophic premature cohesive separation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-3-2-01` | **Automated Lateral Die Shear Loading and Critical Rupture Force Measurement** | Nordson DAGE 4000Plus Multi-Function Bondtester with 100 kgf lateral shear load cell, 5.0 mm wide Tungsten Carbide shear tool tip, integrated touch-down contact sensor and calibrated optical microscope | 1. Secure leadframe package into motorized X-Y test stage with vacuum hold-down and mechanical edge clamps. 2. Align tungsten carbide shear tool parallel to the DRAM die edge (die width 2.5 mm, thickness 250 um) using optical alignment cameras with zero angular yaw (<0.2 deg). 3. Perform automated surface touchdown on leadframe flag adjacent to die edge and automatically retract tool to test height of 35 um. 4. Initiate lateral travel toward die edge at a constant crosshead displacement speed of 100 um/s until fracture. 5. Record continuous force-displacement curve at 10 kHz sampling frequency up to fracture event (sudden force drop >= 50% of peak load). 6. Export maximum peak force (kgf) and failure displacement distance (um). | `Minimum peak fracture force must exceed 12.5 kgf across a 2.5 mm x 2.5 mm die (equivalent to >= 2.0 kgf/mm^2 shear strength), and force curve must demonstrate elastic-plastic ramp without premature slippage plateau.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-3-2-02` | **Post-Shear Interfacial Fracture Morphology and Failure Mode Area Fraction Quantification** | High-resolution Optical Metrology Microscope (Olympus BX53M) equipped with calibrated 20MP digital CMOS camera and image analysis software (ImageJ/FIJI calibrated grid) | 1. Position sheared leadframe flag under 10x/20x brightfield illumination. 2. Capture calibrated multi-tile focus-stacked optical micrographs of the entire 2.5 mm x 2.5 mm die attach paddle footprint. 3. Perform color-segmentation thresholding to distinguish remaining Ag-epoxy residue, exposed bare leadframe metal, and fractured silicon fragments. 4. Calculate total surface area fraction of cohesive epoxy failure (epoxy left on paddle vs total die footprint area). 5. Inspect sheared die backside under optical microscope to quantify silicon cratering/cracking area. 6. Classify primary failure mode according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 guidelines. | `Cohesive failure within the Ag-epoxy matrix must account for >= 80% of total die footprint area; adhesive interface delamination (bare paddle or bare die backside) must not exceed 20%; silicon substrate cratering/die fracture area must be 0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved polycarbonate safety glasses with side shields, Powder-free cleanroom-grade nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness), ESD-safe dissipative lab coat / cleanroom smock, Cut-resistant under-gloves during shear blade handling or replacement
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush eyes immediately with copious gentle stream of water at eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical attention if irritation persists. Skin contact: Wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and warm water; remove contaminated garments. Mechanical puncture/cut from fractured silicon shards: Disinfect wound with sterile saline solution, apply sterile pressure dressing to control bleeding, and seek immediate medical evaluation for embedded micro-particulate removal.

critics.systems_engineer: Destructive die shear testing per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 introduces significant localized mechanical stress gradients across the 180nm DRAM die edge. Tool tip contact height must be strictly controlled at 25 um to 50 um (or <= 1/3 of die thickness) above the substrate surface to avoid inducing artificial bending moments or edge-chipping artifacts that distort true interfacial shear force measurement. Fixturing rigidity and load cell alignment are paramount to ensure purely uniaxially applied lateral displacement without off-axis parasitic torques.
critics.domain_expert: For conductive silver-filled epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablestik 84-1LMISR) cured on a copper or silver-plated leadframe, failure mode classification is as critical as peak rupture force. Researchers must distinguish between bulk cohesive epoxy rupture (>80% epoxy remaining on leadframe flag), clean adhesive interfacial failure at the die backside / leadframe interface (indicative of organic contamination or incomplete cross-linking), and catastrophic silicon cleavage/die cracking. The 180nm DRAM die area (approx. 6.25 mm^2) mandates a minimum rupture threshold exceeding 2.5x the baseline MIL-STD-883 limit of 2.5 kg force.
critics.supply_chain: Tungsten carbide shear tool tips and calibrated piezoelectric load cells (range 0-50 kgf, class 0.5 accuracy) face lead times of 8-12 weeks from precision metrology vendors like Dage or Nordson Sonobond. Leadframe material consistency, specifically Ag-plating thickness (3.0-5.0 um) and micro-roughness variations across production lots, directly impact shear adhesion repeatability, requiring lot-matched control coupons to avoid false rejections during lot qualification.
critics.laya_pm: Destructive die shear consumes 5-10 fully assembled DRAM packages per cured batch, directly conflicting with tight MPW silicon budget constraints. Metrology scheduling must tightly align with C-SAM acoustic void scanning runs to correlate non-destructive acoustic void percentages with destructive shear failure thresholds, preventing unscheduled test bottlenecks and optimizing sample utilization prior to molding encapsulation.
critical_failure_modes: Adhesive delamination at the silicon backside to Ag-epoxy interface occurring below 1.5 kgf/mm^2 due to native oxide contamination or insufficient cure cross-linking.
Shear tool slippage or silicon wedge fracture induced by improper tool clearance (>50 um clearance or tool contact angle misaligned by >0.5 degrees), invalidating interfacial shear data.
Silver flake segregation or localized resin bleed-out along leadframe paddle perimeter causing non-uniform stress distribution and catastrophic premature cohesive separation.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Post-Shear Optical and SEM Fracture Interface Mode Analysis

**Hierarchy:** DRAM Foundation VN > 180nm CMOS MPW Tapeout > BEOL & Packaging > Metrology  
**Target:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip Die Attach Interface Post MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 Die Shear Testing  
**Applicable Materials:** Conductive silver-filled die attach epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C, 60 min), 100 µm × 100 µm bonding pad metallurgy, silicon substrate, leadframe paddle.

---

### Metrology & Workflow Architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│   Destructive Die    │
│      Shear Test      │
│  (MIL-STD-883 M2019) │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│  Post-Shear Optical  │
│  Microscopy (10x-50x)│
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│  Fracture Interface  │
│  Mode Classification │
│  (Cohesive vs Adhes) │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│ High-Resolution SEM  │
│  & Micro-Void Metr.  │
│  (10 kV - 15 kV EDX) │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│  Acceptance Criteria │
│  Verification & Log  │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Analytical Procedure

#### Step 1: Specimen Preparation & Post-Shear Mounting
1. Retrieve sheared leadframe paddle and detached 180nm DRAM die immediately following MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 destructive shear testing.
2. Secure the leadframe substrate and inverted die onto conductive carbon tape mounted on aluminum SEM stubs.
3. Clean surfaces using filtered, dry nitrogen ($N_2$) blow (< 15 psi) to remove loose particulate debris without altering the fracture topography.

#### Step 2: Low-to-Medium Magnification Optical Inspection
1. Place specimen under a calibrated metallurgical stereomicroscope with coaxial and ring LED illumination.
2. Image the full die attach paddle interface under $10\times$ to $50\times$ optical magnification.
3. Map and quantify the fracture area coverage using digital planimetry:
   - **Mode 1 (Cohesive Epoxy Failure):** Bulk fracture occurring completely within the cured silver-filled epoxy matrix.
   - **Mode 2 (Adhesive Failure - Die Interface):** Clean separation at the backside silicon/metallization to epoxy boundary.
   - **Mode 3 (Adhesive Failure - Leadframe Interface):** Delamination between epoxy and leadframe metal paddle.
   - **Mode 4 (Die Fracturing / Silicon Cleavage):** Bulk silicon fracture prior to bond shear.

#### Step 3: High-Resolution Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM)
1. Load stub into the FE-SEM chamber and pump down to high vacuum ($< 1 \times 10^{-4}\text{ Pa}$).
2. Configure electron beam parameters:
   - Accelerating Voltage: $10.0\text{ kV} - 15.0\text{ kV}$.
   - Working Distance (WD): $8.0\text{ mm} - 10.0\text{ mm}$.
   - Detector: Secondary Electron (SE) mode for 3D fracture morphology; Backscattered Electron (BSE) mode (compositional contrast) to distinguish silver (Ag) flakes from organic resin matrices.
3. Perform high-magnification imaging ($500\times$ to $5,000\times$) along fracture initiation sites, shear tool impingement edges, and internal cured epoxy cavities.

#### Step 4: SEM Void Analysis & Cured Epoxy Morphology Metrology
1. Inspect exposed internal micro-voids in the sheared Ablebond 84-1LMIS epoxy layer.
2. Measure void perimeter, cumulative exposed void area fraction, and inspect Ag-flake distribution and resin cross-linking density at the failure plane.
3. Verify that the total void area fraction across the sheared die attach footprint aligns with the C-SAM acoustic microscopy non-destructive baseline ($< 5\%$).

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cohesive Epoxy Fracture Coverage** | $\ge 85\%$ | Min $80\%$ of die attach footprint | Optical Planimetry / BSE-SEM Digital Image Segmentation |
| **Post-Shear Exposed Void Area** | $< 5\%$ | Max $5.0\%$ cumulative footprint area | Digital image analysis per C-SAM baseline / SEM planimetry |
| **Epoxy Thermal Resistance State ($R_{th}$)** | $\le 5.0\ \mathrm{^\circ C/W}$ | Max $5.0\ \mathrm{^\circ C/W}$ correlation | Thermal resistance verification for Ablebond 84-1LMIS |
| **Silicon Cleavage / Die Cracking Area** | $0\%$ | Must occur in epoxy matrix, not silicon | Optical & SE-SEM Inspection |

---

### 3. Context Citations

* **Epoxy Die Attach Material & Cure Schedule:** Silver-filled conductive epoxy (*Ablebond 84-1LMIS*) cured at $150\ \mathrm{^\circ C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$ (*Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*).
* **Package Thermal Resistance Limit:** $R_{th} \le 5\ \mathrm{^\circ C/W}$ (*Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*).
* **Maximum Allowable Void Area:** Void area under die $< 5\%$ verified by acoustic microscopy and fracture analysis (*Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*).
* **On-Chip Interface Boundary:** Bonding pad metallurgy dimensioned at $100\ \mathrm{\mu m} \times 100\ \mathrm{\mu m}$ aluminum squares (*Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-shear fracture analysis must establish a closed feedback loop connecting mechanical shear strength degradation to upstream thermal curing kinetics and downstream wirebond integrity. Optical surface topography mapping and cross-sectional SEM must quantitatively correlate cohesive versus adhesive failure percentages with acoustic C-SAM void distributions to ensure thermomechanical stress redistribution during DRAM refresh cycling does not trigger silicon substrate microcracking.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Failure mode partitioning requires sub-micron discrimination between adhesive failure at the Ag-filled epoxy/die backside metallization (Ti/Ni/Ag) interface, cohesive fracture within the crosslinked polymeric matrix, and silicon bulk cratering. Optical polarized microscopy must measure fillet meniscus wet-out boundaries, while FE-SEM and EDX point-line mapping must inspect for silver flake agglomeration, resin bleed-out (RBO), and interfacial interdiffusion layer delamination without inducing electron-beam carbon contamination.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dual-sourcing qualified silver-filled conductive epoxies (such as Henkel Ablestik or Henkel Loctite equivalents) requires strict adherence to MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 criteria across differing silver flake geometries and resin viscosities. Failure interface metrology turn-around-time (TAT) directly gates lot release for the MPW ceramic dual-in-line packaging run, meaning rapid optical screening must filter false rejects before committing to high-vacuum SEM/EDX inspection.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Fracture mode inspection throughput must be constrained within a 45-minute analytical window per sample lot to maintain 180nm DRAM packaging milestone velocity. All image sets, EDX spectrum profiles, and failure classification matrices must be automatically ingested into the open-source PDK data repository to preserve traceability prior to downstream wirebond destructive pull testing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial adhesive delamination along the silicon backside metallization (Ti/Ni/Ag) caused by incomplete organic outgassing or sub-optimal surface activation prior to epoxy cure.
1. Silicon die cratering and subsurface bulk microfracture due to localized stress concentration from excessive shear tool ram contact velocity or silver filler agglomeration.
1. Cohesive shear failure within the epoxy bulk showing uncured resin pockets and high void density (>10% localized) resulting from inadequate thermal ramp rates during oven curing.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-3-3-01` | **Quantitative Optical Failure Mode Area Ratio & Fillet Meniscus Mapping** | Calibrated High-Resolution Motorized Optical Metallurgical Microscope (Olympus BX53M or Keyence VHX-7000) with motorized XYZ stage, polarized filter, ring illuminator, and image analysis software (ImageJ/Fiji calibrated grid). | 1. Position sheared leadframe substrate and detached die on stage under 100x and 500x magnification under co-axial and polarized illumination. 2. Capture multi-focus composite Z-stack images across the 2.4 mm x 2.4 mm die attach pad (DAP) footprint. 3. Define regions of interest: Area_A (Adhesive failure at die metallization), Area_B (Cohesive failure within epoxy), and Area_C (Silicon fracture/cratering). 4. Perform color threshold segmentation and compute surface area percentages for each failure zone relative to total nominal die footprint. 5. Record perimeter epoxy fillet height and wet-out coverage around all four leadframe margins. | `Cohesive failure within epoxy matrix must be >= 85.0% of total die attach area; adhesive delamination at die backside or substrate must be <= 15.0%; silicon substrate cratering/die fracture area must be 0.0% (zero silicon pull-out exceeding 50 um lateral diameter).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-1-3-3-3-02` | **FE-SEM High-Magnification Fracture Microstructure and EDX Elemental Interface Analysis** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM, Thermo Scientific Apreo or Zeiss Gemini) equipped with Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS/EDX silicon drift detector, Oxford Aztec). | 1. Load specimen into FE-SEM load lock and align electron beam to the sheared fracture boundary. 2. Perform Secondary Electron (SE) imaging at 2,000x, 10,000x, and 25,000x at 5 representative locations (center and four quadrants) to characterize Ag filler dispersion, void morphology, and polymeric micro-voiding. 3. Switch to Backscattered Electron (BSE) mode to enhance atomic number contrast between Ag flakes (Z=47), Cu/Ag leadframe (Z=29/47), and Si substrate (Z=14). 4. Execute EDX 50-point line scan (step size 0.2 um) and element map across fracture interface capturing Si-Kalpha (1.74 keV), Ag-Lalpha (2.98 keV), Cu-Kalpha (8.04 keV), and C-Kalpha (0.28 keV). 5. Quantify organic resin contamination and check for native oxide/halide segregation. | `EDX elemental profile must confirm uniform Ag flake distribution with no local depletion zones > 5.0 um; interfacial oxygen atomic concentration at sheared metallic boundary must be <= 3.0 at.%; no chlorine or halogen contamination above detection limit (< 0.1 at.%); zero presence of brittle silicon intermetallic/micro-cleavage planes.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, double-gloved during chemical wipe), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Conductive ESD-safe laboratory coat, Respirator half-face mask with organic vapor/P100 particulate cartridge during solvent chamber cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin Contact: Remove contaminated clothing and wash skin thoroughly with non-abrasive soap and water. Inhalation: Relocate individual to fresh cleanroom air; seek immediate medical attention if dizziness or respiratory distress occurs. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth with water and seek emergency toxicological evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Specimen preparation and chemical cleaning must be conducted inside a certified Class II laminar flow exhaust fume hood with face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). SEM turbo-molecular and roughing vacuum pump exhausts must be ducted directly to the dedicated facility toxic/solvent exhaust scrubber line.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect solvent-saturated cleanroom wipes and swabs in airtight, grounded, FM-approved flammable waste cans. Spent cleaning solvents (IPA/Acetone) must be segregated into clearly labeled hazardous organic solvent drums for licensed chemical incineration. Solid silver-containing residues must be collected in dedicated hazardous solid containers for heavy-metal reclamation.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly sheared leadframe paddle and detached die backside surfaces, clean and free of physical touch, particulate contamination, or chemical condensation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Completed multi-spectral optical micrographs and vacuum-stabilized, carbon-coated or colloidal-Ag grounded SEM specimen mounted on metal stub ready for archival storage or FIB cross-sectioning.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to ambient cleanroom humidity (>45% RH) induces rapid surface oxidation and moisture chemisorption onto exposed copper/silver interfaces, creating false artifactual adhesive delamination signatures during SEM/EDX elemental quantification.

> Completed definitive fracture mode categorization and microstructural failure analysis protocol for 180nm DRAM open-source chip die attach assemblies following MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 destructive shear testing. Failure interface metrology turn-around-time (TAT) directly gates lot release for the MPW ceramic dual-in-line packaging run, meaning rapid optical screening must filter false rejects before committing to high-vacuum SEM/EDX inspection.
critics.laya_pm: Fracture mode inspection throughput must be constrained within a 45-minute analytical window per sample lot to maintain 180nm DRAM packaging milestone velocity. All image sets, EDX spectrum profiles, and failure classification matrices must be automatically ingested into the open-source PDK data repository to preserve traceability prior to downstream wirebond destructive pull testing.
critical_failure_modes: Interfacial adhesive delamination along the silicon backside metallization (Ti/Ni/Ag) caused by incomplete organic outgassing or sub-optimal surface activation prior to epoxy cure.
Silicon die cratering and subsurface bulk microfracture due to localized stress concentration from excessive shear tool ram contact velocity or silver filler agglomeration.
Cohesive shear failure within the epoxy bulk showing uncured resin pockets and high void density (>10% localized) resulting from inadequate thermal ramp rates during oven curing.

testcases.title: Quantitative Optical Failure Mode Area Ratio & Fillet Meniscus Mapping
testcases.instrumentation: Calibrated High-Resolution Motorized Optical Metallurgical Microscope (Olympus BX53M or Keyence VHX-7000) with motorized XYZ stage, polarized filter, ring illuminator, and image analysis software (ImageJ/Fiji calibrated grid).
testcases.pre_conditions: Destructive die shear testing executed per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019.5 on 180nm DRAM test vehicle (die dimension 2.4 mm x 2.4 mm, leadframe Ag-plated Cu paddle); sheared interface exposed and cleared of loose debris with 0.2-bar dry N2 blow.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position sheared leadframe substrate and detached die on stage under 100x and 500x magnification under co-axial and polarized illumination. 2. Capture multi-focus composite Z-stack images across the 2.4 mm x 2.4 mm die attach pad (DAP) footprint. 3. Define regions of interest: Area_A (Adhesive failure at die metallization), Area_B (Cohesive failure within epoxy), and Area_C (Silicon fracture/cratering). 4. Perform color threshold segmentation and compute surface area percentages for each failure zone relative to total nominal die footprint. 5. Record perimeter epoxy fillet height and wet-out coverage around all four leadframe margins.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Cohesive failure within epoxy matrix must be >= 85.0% of total die attach area; adhesive delamination at die backside or substrate must be <= 15.0%; silicon substrate cratering/die fracture area must be 0.0% (zero silicon pull-out exceeding 50 um lateral diameter).

testcases.title: FE-SEM High-Magnification Fracture Microstructure and EDX Elemental Interface Analysis
testcases.instrumentation: Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM, Thermo Scientific Apreo or Zeiss Gemini) equipped with Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS/EDX silicon drift detector, Oxford Aztec).
testcases.pre_conditions: Sheared leadframe specimen mounted on conductive carbon tape onto 32 mm aluminum SEM stub; chamber vacuum pumped to <= 5.0e-4 Pa; accelerating voltage calibrated to 15.0 kV with beam current of 1.6 nA and working distance of 10.0 mm.
testcases.procedure: 1. Load specimen into FE-SEM load lock and align electron beam to the sheared fracture boundary. 2. Perform Secondary Electron (SE) imaging at 2,000x, 10,000x, and 25,000x at 5 representative locations (center and four quadrants) to characterize Ag filler dispersion, void morphology, and polymeric micro-voiding. 3. Switch to Backscattered Electron (BSE) mode to enhance atomic number contrast between Ag flakes (Z=47), Cu/Ag leadframe (Z=29/47), and Si substrate (Z=14). 4. Execute EDX 50-point line scan (step size 0.2 um) and element map across fracture interface capturing Si-Kalpha (1.74 keV), Ag-Lalpha (2.98 keV), Cu-Kalpha (8.04 keV), and C-Kalpha (0.28 keV). 5. Quantify organic resin contamination and check for native oxide/halide segregation.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: EDX elemental profile must confirm uniform Ag flake distribution with no local depletion zones > 5.0 um; interfacial oxygen atomic concentration at sheared metallic boundary must be <= 3.0 at.%; no chlorine or halogen contamination above detection limit (< 0.1 at.%); zero presence of brittle silicon intermetallic/micro-cleavage planes.

ppe_required: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, double-gloved during chemical wipe)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields
Conductive ESD-safe laboratory coat
Respirator half-face mask with organic vapor/P100 particulate cartridge during solvent chamber cleaning
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin Contact: Remove contaminated clothing and wash skin thoroughly with non-abrasive soap and water. Inhalation: Relocate individual to fresh cleanroom air; seek immediate medical attention if dizziness or respiratory distress occurs. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth with water and seek emergency toxicological evaluation.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Specimen preparation and chemical cleaning must be conducted inside a certified Class II laminar flow exhaust fume hood with face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). SEM turbo-molecular and roughing vacuum pump exhausts must be ducted directly to the dedicated facility toxic/solvent exhaust scrubber line.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Collect solvent-saturated cleanroom wipes and swabs in airtight, grounded, FM-approved flammable waste cans. Spent cleaning solvents (IPA/Acetone) must be segregated into clearly labeled hazardous organic solvent drums for licensed chemical incineration. Solid silver-containing residues must be collected in dedicated hazardous solid containers for heavy-metal reclamation.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly sheared leadframe paddle and detached die backside surfaces, clean and free of physical touch, particulate contamination, or chemical condensation.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Completed multi-spectral optical micrographs and vacuum-stabilized, carbon-coated or colloidal-Ag grounded SEM specimen mounted on metal stub ready for archival storage or FIB cross-sectioning.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excessive exposure to ambient cleanroom humidity (>45% RH) induces rapid surface oxidation and moisture chemisorption onto exposed copper/silver interfaces, creating false artifactual adhesive delamination signatures during SEM/EDX elemental quantification.

expected_result.summary: Completed definitive fracture mode categorization and microstructural failure analysis protocol for 180nm DRAM open-source chip die attach assemblies following MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 destructive shear testing. Metrology establishes quantitative proof of cohesive epoxy failure dominance, absence of silicon cratering, and absence of chemical or elemental segregation across the joint interface.

quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calibrated optical digital threshold segmentation per ASTM D5573 and MIL-STD-883 Method 2019

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Silicon bulk cratering or substrate pull-out area relative to total nominal die area
quantitative_assertions.tolerance: 0.0% (Zero tolerance for Si pull-out > 50 um diameter)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated high-magnification optical Z-stacking combined with FE-SEM Backscattered Electron topography

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum silver filler agglomeration cluster diameter in cross-sectional SEM
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-resolution FE-SEM image analysis using calibrated particle sizing at 10,000x magnification
