# Standard Operating Procedure: Thermosonic Ball-Wedge Bonding Recipe DOE Optimization on 100um Al Pads

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermosonic wirebonding on 100um x 100um Al pads with 25um Au wire imposes severe thermo-mechanical stress on underlying dielectric layers (such as inter-metal dielectrics and pre-metal dielectric stacks in 180nm CMOS). Excessive ultrasonic power (>100 mW) or bonding force risks pad cratering and inter-layer dielectric cracking beneath the pad, which directly induces bitline-to-substrate or wordline leakage in DRAM arrays. The DOE must constrain ultrasonic power, bonding force, stage temperature (150°C), and ultrasonic burst time (20-30 ms) to balance metallurgical intermetallic compound (IMC) formation against sub-pad dielectric yield degradation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 150°C stage temperature, the intermetallic reaction between the 25um 4N gold ball and 100um sputtered aluminum pad yields Au-Al intermetallics (predominantly Au8Al3 and Au4Al). If bonding energy or stage temperature is insufficiently controlled or if Al native oxide (>5 nm) is not adequately scrubbed by the ultrasonic vibration (60 kHz), unreacted interfaces form, leading to Kirkendall voiding during post-mold cure or high-temperature storage (HTSL). EFO firing must yield a symmetrical Free Air Ball (FAB) diameter of 1.8x to 2.2x wire diameter (45-55 um) without neck necking or surface oxidation to ensure squashed ball diameters stay strictly within 70-80 um, leaving >=10 um passivation clearance on 100 um pads.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: 25 um 4N (99.99%) Au wire is subject to market volatility and spool-to-spool elongation/break-load tolerances (typically 2-6% elongation, >=9 gf break load). Sourcing ceramic capillaries with matched tip diameter (typically 90-100 um outer diameter, 34-38 um hole diameter) from Kulicke & Soffa or Small Precision Tools (SPT) requires strict tracking of capillary tip lifespan (<200k touchdowns) to avoid tip wear and inconsistent ultrasonic energy coupling. Nitrogen shielding gas (99.999% purity) during EFO sparking must maintain constant flow to prevent FAB eccentricity.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: DOE execution across split lots must be tightly synchronized with die attach curing (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min). Silver-filled conductive epoxy outgassing of volatile silicones or amine catalysts can cross-contaminate adjacent 100um Al bond pads if post-cure plasma cleaning (Ar/O2 or Ar/H2) is delayed. Production schedules must enforce a strict <=120 min Q-time window between plasma surface activation and wirebonding to safeguard against pad re-oxidation and airborne organic adsorption.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Pad cratering / Si microcracking under 100um Al pad due to excessive ultrasonic burst power (>100 mW) or excessive static bond force (>45 gf), leading to structural collapse of IMD and DRAM peripheral line shorting.
1. Ball lift-off / poor intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage (<70% Au-Al intermetallic phase formation) caused by insufficient ultrasonic scrubbing or contaminated Al pad native oxide, yielding early wire pull failure (<4.0 gf) at the interface.
1. Heel cracking or wire span necking immediately above the bonded ball caused by excessive EFO sparking spark-gap discharge or improper capillary chamfer angle, resulting in break-load degradation and open circuit under thermal cycling.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-2-01` | **Destructive Wire Pull Strength and Interface Failure Mode Characterization** | Dage 4000Plus Bondtester equipped with 0-100 gf pull hook and calibrated precision load cell (+/-0.1 gf accuracy), high-magnification optical microscope (50x-1000x). | 1. Fixture the leadframe/package strip firmly onto the Dage 4000Plus motorized stage under vacuum hold-down. 2. Center the pull hook at mid-span of the 25um Au wire loop between the ball on the 100um Al pad and the wedge on the leadframe finger. 3. Lower hook until bottom clearance is 1/3 of loop height above die surface. 4. Initiate pull test at a controlled vertical displacement speed of 100 um/s until fracture. 5. Record peak pull force in grams-force (gf) and classify failure site (Code 1: Ball lift, Code 2: Neck break, Code 3: Mid-span break, Code 4: Heel break, Code 5: Wedge lift, Code 6: Pad crater). Repeat for 30 wires per DOE split leg. | `Peak pull force >= 4.0 gf across 100% of tested wires (Mil-Std-883 Method 2011.9). Zero instances of Code 1 (ball lift) or Code 6 (pad cratering); >=95% failures must occur in the wire span or neck (Code 2 or Code 3) with mean pull strength >= 6.5 gf and standard deviation sigma <= 0.8 gf.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-2-02` | **Ball Shear Strength and IMC Area Coverage Verification** | Nordson DAGE 4000 / Royce 650 Bondtester with 100um shear tool blade, precision optical stylus profilometer, and post-shear chemical etching inspection microscope. | 1. Clamp leadframe carrier onto the shear tester stage under rigid vacuum clamp. 2. Position the flat shear tool parallel to the squashed gold ball base, maintaining a standoff height of 3 um above the 100um Al pad surface to avoid pad gouging. 3. Advance shear ram at a test rate of 50 um/s against the gold ball until detachment occurs. 4. Record peak shear force in grams-force (gf) and calculate normalized shear strength (gf/mil^2). 5. Inspect sheared ball pad crater under optical microscope and measure remaining intermetallic compound (Au-Al) footprint percentage on the Al pad. Repeat for 30 bonded balls per DOE recipe. | `Individual ball shear force >= 15.0 gf (or >= 5.5 gf/mil^2 of bonded contact area per Mil-Std-883 Method 2017). Sheared pad interface must exhibit >= 75% gold-aluminum intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage remaining on pad with 0% silicon pull-out or sub-pad dielectric fracture.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-resistant silicone/Nomex safety gloves for handling 150°C heated vacuum chuck stages, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/spark safety glasses for protection against Electronic Flame-Off (EFO) micro-arcing and wire snapping, Class 100 cleanroom ESD-safe nitrile gloves (free of silicones and sulfur), ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor attached to ground bus, Full static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and conductive shoe covers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn contact from 150°C stage: immediately irrigate affected skin under cold, clean running water for minimum 15 minutes; do not apply greasy ointments; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing and seek cleanroom medical triage. EFO electrical or spark flash injury: flush eyes with clean eyewash station for 15 minutes if flash glare irritation occurs. High-pressure N2 line release: isolate valve immediately and move personnel to well-ventilated area to prevent asphyxiation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) operating at >= 100 FPM face velocity positioned directly over the heated stage and capillary EFO spark head to extract trace thermal desorption vapors and IPA wipe fumes; general cleanroom air exchange rate >= 60 ACH with laminar HEPA downflow.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent capillary tips and cut Au wire remnants (>99.99% Au) collected in dedicated sealed ESD-safe scrap containers for precious metal reclamation and recycling. IPA wipes sealed in dedicated flammable hazardous waste bins for chemical solvent disposal per RCRA regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gold wire (Au 99.99%)** | `7440-57-5` | 4N Semiconductor Grade (99.99%) | `99.99% wt` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (EFO Shielding & Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 (99.999%) | `>= 99.999% vol` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA, Stage & Capillary Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / VLSI Grade | `99.9% vol` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Die attach epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) fully cured at 150°C for 60 min, acoustic voiding <5%, followed by in-line Ar/O2 plasma treatment (5 min, 100W RF) ensuring Al bond pad native oxide <= 2.0 nm and carbonaceous organic contamination < 5 at% by XPS.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Complete thermosonically bonded wire loops (25um Au wire) anchored on 100um Al pads with squashed ball diameter 75 um (+/-5 um), free of loop sagging, mechanically stable under inert cover, awaiting transfer to transfer molding / epoxy encapsulation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient cleanroom air leads to atmospheric moisture adsorption and re-oxidation of the 100um aluminum pad surfaces (Al2O3 passivation layer growth >5 nm) as well as airborne silicone/organic condensation, resulting in incomplete ultrasonic scrub, low ball shear strength (<15 gf), and interfacial ball lift failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full DOE optimization (Central Composite Design across Ultrasonic Power [50-100 mW], Bond Force [25-45 gf], Bond Time [20-30 ms], and Stage Temperature [140-160°C]) established for 25um Au wire thermosonic bonding onto 100um x 100um Al pads of 180nm DRAM dies. Yields robust metallurgical intermetallic bonding meeting Mil-Std-883 requirements with zero cratering, wire pull force >= 4.0 gf, and ball shear force >= 15.0 gf.

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal acceptance requires 100% compliance across all 100 test samples: wire pull strength >= 4.0 gf with zero interface ball lifts (Code 1) or pad craters (Code 6), ball shear strength >= 15.0 gf with IMC coverage >= 75%, squashed ball diameter centered at 75 um (+/-5 um) centered within the 100um Al pad, and formal sign-off approval by Packaging Lead, Foundry Integration Lead, and Quality Assurance.

critics.systems_engineer: Thermosonic wirebonding on 100um x 100um Al pads with 25um Au wire imposes severe thermo-mechanical stress on underlying dielectric layers (such as inter-metal dielectrics and pre-metal dielectric stacks in 180nm CMOS). Excessive ultrasonic power (>100 mW) or bonding force risks pad cratering and inter-layer dielectric cracking beneath the pad, which directly induces bitline-to-substrate or wordline leakage in DRAM arrays. The DOE must constrain ultrasonic power, bonding force, stage temperature (150°C), and ultrasonic burst time (20-30 ms) to balance metallurgical intermetallic compound (IMC) formation against sub-pad dielectric yield degradation.
critics.domain_expert: At 150°C stage temperature, the intermetallic reaction between the 25um 4N gold ball and 100um sputtered aluminum pad yields Au-Al intermetallics (predominantly Au8Al3 and Au4Al). If bonding energy or stage temperature is insufficiently controlled or if Al native oxide (>5 nm) is not adequately scrubbed by the ultrasonic vibration (60 kHz), unreacted interfaces form, leading to Kirkendall voiding during post-mold cure or high-temperature storage (HTSL). EFO firing must yield a symmetrical Free Air Ball (FAB) diameter of 1.8x to 2.2x wire diameter (45-55 um) without neck necking or surface oxidation to ensure squashed ball diameters stay strictly within 70-80 um, leaving >=10 um passivation clearance on 100 um pads.
critics.supply_chain: 25 um 4N (99.99%) Au wire is subject to market volatility and spool-to-spool elongation/break-load tolerances (typically 2-6% elongation, >=9 gf break load). Sourcing ceramic capillaries with matched tip diameter (typically 90-100 um outer diameter, 34-38 um hole diameter) from Kulicke & Soffa or Small Precision Tools (SPT) requires strict tracking of capillary tip lifespan (<200k touchdowns) to avoid tip wear and inconsistent ultrasonic energy coupling. Nitrogen shielding gas (99.999% purity) during EFO sparking must maintain constant flow to prevent FAB eccentricity.
critics.laya_pm: DOE execution across split lots must be tightly synchronized with die attach curing (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min). Silver-filled conductive epoxy outgassing of volatile silicones or amine catalysts can cross-contaminate adjacent 100um Al bond pads if post-cure plasma cleaning (Ar/O2 or Ar/H2) is delayed. Production schedules must enforce a strict <=120 min Q-time window between plasma surface activation and wirebonding to safeguard against pad re-oxidation and airborne organic adsorption.
critical_failure_modes: Pad cratering / Si microcracking under 100um Al pad due to excessive ultrasonic burst power (>100 mW) or excessive static bond force (>45 gf), leading to structural collapse of IMD and DRAM peripheral line shorting.

Ball lift-off / poor intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage (<70% Au-Al intermetallic phase formation) caused by insufficient ultrasonic scrubbing or contaminated Al pad native oxide, yielding early wire pull failure (<4.0 gf) at the interface.

Heel cracking or wire span necking immediately above the bonded ball caused by excessive EFO sparking spark-gap discharge or improper capillary chamfer angle, resulting in break-load degradation and open circuit under thermal cycling.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## EFO Free-Air Ball Formation & Ultrasonic Transducer Calibration for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ Au Wire

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-EFO-US-001`  
**Process Level:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Packaging & Assembly  
**Target Substrate:** 180nm DRAM Die on Leadframe / Package Workholder ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Al bonding pads)  
**Wire Type:** $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter 99.99% Au Wire  

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Load 25um 99.99% Au   │
│   Wire in Capillary    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Trigger EFO Spark    │
│       Discharge        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Inspect Free-Air    │
│     Ball Formation     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Calibrate Ultrasonic  │
│   Transducer 60 kHz    │
│       50-100 mW        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Stabilize Substrate   │
│  Workholder at 150 C   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Thermosonic Ball    │
│  Bond on 100um Al Pad  │
│      for 20-30 ms      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Perform Mil-Std-883   │
│    Method 2011 Wire    │
│       Pull Test        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Wire Feed & Capillary Setup:**
   - Thread $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter 99.99% gold (Au) wire through the ceramic wire-bonding capillary and wire clamps.
   - Adjust wire tail extension past the capillary chamfer to the standard free-air ball (FAB) gap distance relative to the electronic flame-off (EFO) electrode.

2. **Electronic Flame-Off (EFO) Discharge & FAB Formation:**
   - Activate the high-voltage EFO spark generator to strike an electric arc across the gold wire tail under ambient nitrogen/air shielding.
   - Form the spherical Free-Air Ball (FAB) at the tip of the $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire. Verify optically that the ball is concentric, non-oxidized, and fully seated against the capillary chamfer.

3. **Ultrasonic Transducer Resonance & Power Calibration:**
   - Tune and lock the wirebonder piezoelectric ultrasonic transducer drive frequency to the resonance point of **$60\ \text{kHz}$**.
   - Calibrate the ultrasonic power output to deliver **$50\text{--}100\ \text{mW}$** via the calibrated transducer power driver.
   - Set the ultrasonic pulse duration (bond time) window to **$20\text{--}30\ \text{ms}$**.

4. **Thermal Stage Stabilization:**
   - Mount the leadframe/package containing the 180nm DRAM die onto the bonder workholder stage.
   - Heat and stabilize the workholder stage temperature at **$150^\circ\text{C}$**.

5. **Thermosonic Ball Placement & Bonding:**
   - Position the capillary carrying the gold FAB directly over the DRAM die's **$100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Aluminum pad**.
   - Descend the capillary to apply mechanical bond force while triggering the synchronized **$60\ \text{kHz}$**, **$50\text{--}100\ \text{mW}$** ultrasonic pulse for **$20\text{--}30\ \text{ms}$** at **$150^\circ\text{C}$** to achieve thermosonic gold-aluminum solid-state intermetallic bonding.

6. **Post-Bond Destructive Pull Verification:**
   - Perform sample destructive wire pull tests adhering strictly to **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011**.
   - Ensure the pull hook is placed at mid-span and verify that break failures occur strictly within the gold wire span rather than as interfacial pad peel or cratering.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transducer Resonant Frequency** | $60$ | $\text{kHz}$ | Transducer frequency sweep & auto-tune impedance analyzer |
| **Ultrasonic Bond Power** | $50\text{--}100$ | $\text{mW}$ | Transducer power controller / Laser vibrometer calibration |
| **Ultrasonic Pulse Duration** | $20\text{--}30$ | $\text{ms}$ | Wirebonder trajectory timing oscilloscope log |
| **Stage Workholder Temperature** | $150$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Surface thermocouple / Pyrometer at leadframe clamp |
| **Wire Pull Strength (Mil-Std-883)** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Calibrated wire pull tester (Mil-Std-883 Method 2011) |
| **Bond Failure Mode** | Wire span break (no bond lift) | Categorical / Pass-Fail | Optical microscope inspection post-pull |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Sources

- **Source: *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging***
  - *Thermomechanical & Ultrasonic Parameters:* $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter 99.99% gold wire bonded at $150^\circ\text{C}$ with an ultrasonic transducer pulse of $60\ \text{kHz}$, $50\text{--}100\ \text{mW}$, and duration $20\text{--}30\ \text{ms}$.
  - *Pad Geometry:* On-chip bonding pads measuring $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
  - *Mechanical Quality Standard:* Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 wire pull test force $\ge 4.0\ \text{gf}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire, with failure restricted to the wire span.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermosonic Au wirebonding on 180nm DRAM requires closed-loop synchronization between EFO firing and piezo-driven vertical Z-axis motion. For 25um 4N Au wire on 100um x 100um top-metal Al pads, the Free-Air Ball (FAB) diameter must be tightly maintained at 1.5x to 2.0x wire diameter (37.5um to 50.0um). Uncalibrated 60 kHz transducer impedance drifts shift resonance under 150°C stage heating, resulting in uncoupled acoustic energy, inadequate scrub, or pad cratering into underlying dielectric inter-metal layers (IMD). Closed-loop resonance tuning and load-cell impact calibration must precede EFO discharge.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Capillary chamfer geometry and spark gap distance govern EFO discharge stability. Using high-purity (99.99%) Au wire, EFO current (typically 20-40 mA) and firing time (0.5-2.0 ms) determine FAB sphericity. Asymmetry, golf-ball dimpling, or micro-voiding at the neck/heat-affected zone (HAZ) directly degrade neck pull strength below the Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 minimum of 4.0 gf. Ultrasonic transducer calibration must achieve a stable resonance admittance peak at 60 kHz (+/-0.5 kHz) across 50-100 mW ultrasonic power settings to ensure complete intermetallic compound (Au8Al3 / Au4Al) formation without excessive Al splash beyond the 100um pad boundaries.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: 25um 4N (99.99%) gold bonding wire with controlled elongation (2-6%) and breaking load (>8 gf) carries tight lot-to-lot hardness variations. Capillaries (fine-pitch ceramic/zirconia-toughened alumina with 38um hole diameter, 50um chamfer diameter, and 90° inner chamfer angle) have limited mechanical lifetimes of ~200,000 bonds before tip wear causes asymmetrical FAB seating and transducer acoustic decoupling. Ceramic DIP/QFN leadframes and Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured substrates must be secured from vetted packaging supply chains to avoid oxidized leadframe finishes.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermosonic recipe DOE optimization controls the packaging critical path prior to final wafer sort verification and functional DRAM testing. The team must qualify FAB morphology and transducer power sweeps within 3 shifts to keep packaging turn-around time within budget. Immediate acoustic microscopy and wire pull/shear sampling are gating requirements before assembling multi-die prototype batches.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Pad Cratering: Excessive ultrasonic transducer amplitude (>100 mW) or uncalibrated impact force causing micro-cracking and fracture through the 100um Al bond pad into underlying ILD/IMD oxide.
1. Neck Fracture (HAZ Failure): Overly high EFO discharge energy extending the heat-affected zone up the Au wire, causing premature wire span breakage below 4.0 gf under post-attach thermal fatigue.
1. Asymmetric FAB / Off-Center Ball Bond: Inconsistent spark gap distance or oxidized wire tail resulting in skewed free-air ball, causing edge overhang or shorting to adjacent passivation lines.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-2-1-01` | **EFO Free-Air Ball (FAB) Sphericity and Dimensional Metrology** | High-speed optical wirebonder inspection camera, Field-Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM), Non-contact optical coordinate measuring system (microscope 1000x) | 1. Program wirebonder EFO current to 30 mA and sweep discharge pulse duration from 0.8 ms to 1.6 ms in 0.2 ms increments (n=30 FABs per condition). 2. Fire EFO in free air without touchdown. 3. Retract wire and capture automated optical images of each FAB at 0° and 90° orthogonal views. 4. Transfer representative coupons to FE-SEM to verify surface morphology, absence of HAZ dimpling, and absence of tail spike. 5. Measure orthogonal diameters D_major and D_minor. | `FAB mean diameter must be between 42.0 um and 48.0 um (1.7x to 1.9x wire diameter). Aspect ratio (D_max / D_min) <= 1.05 across 100% of tested balls. Zero micro-cavities or surface craters visible at 5000x FE-SEM inspection.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-2-1-02` | **60 kHz Ultrasonic Transducer Resonant Admittance & Vibration Velocity Calibration** | Laser Doppler Vibrometer (LDV) targeting capillary tip, RF Impedance/Gain-Phase Analyzer, Dynamic piezoelectric load cell sensor integrated into test heater stage | 1. Connect impedance analyzer to transducer terminals and perform frequency sweep from 58.0 kHz to 62.0 kHz at 150°C stage idle. 2. Measure electrical resonance frequency (f_r), anti-resonance frequency (f_a), and dynamic impedance at resonance. 3. Point LDV laser beam perpendicular to capillary tip (50um above chamfer). 4. Drive transducer at 60 kHz with calibrated power settings (50 mW, 75 mW, 100 mW) for 25 ms burst duration. 5. Measure peak-to-peak tip displacement amplitude and record load cell contact scrub force signature. | `Resonance frequency f_r must lock at 60.0 kHz +/- 0.4 kHz with resonant impedance |Z_min| < 35 Ohms. Capillary tip peak vibration amplitude must scale linearly between 1.2 um +/- 0.1 um (at 50 mW) and 2.4 um +/- 0.15 um (at 100 mW). Phase jitter across 25 ms burst must remain < 3.0 degrees.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-resistant Kevlar handling gloves for 150°C heated workholder, Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, static-dissipative), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/spark safety glasses for EFO discharge observation, Conductive ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately flush affected skin under clean, cold running water for a minimum of 15 minutes. critics.systems_engineer: Thermosonic Au wirebonding on 180nm DRAM requires closed-loop synchronization between EFO firing and piezo-driven vertical Z-axis motion. For 25um 4N Au wire on 100um x 100um top-metal Al pads, the Free-Air Ball (FAB) diameter must be tightly maintained at 1.5x to 2.0x wire diameter (37.5um to 50.0um). Uncalibrated 60 kHz transducer impedance drifts shift resonance under 150°C stage heating, resulting in uncoupled acoustic energy, inadequate scrub, or pad cratering into underlying dielectric inter-metal layers (IMD). Closed-loop resonance tuning and load-cell impact calibration must precede EFO discharge.
critics.domain_expert: Capillary chamfer geometry and spark gap distance govern EFO discharge stability. Using high-purity (99.99%) Au wire, EFO current (typically 20-40 mA) and firing time (0.5-2.0 ms) determine FAB sphericity. Asymmetry, golf-ball dimpling, or micro-voiding at the neck/heat-affected zone (HAZ) directly degrade neck pull strength below the Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 minimum of 4.0 gf. Ultrasonic transducer calibration must achieve a stable resonance admittance peak at 60 kHz (+/-0.5 kHz) across 50-100 mW ultrasonic power settings to ensure complete intermetallic compound (Au8Al3 / Au4Al) formation without excessive Al splash beyond the 100um pad boundaries.
critics.supply_chain: 25um 4N (99.99%) gold bonding wire with controlled elongation (2-6%) and breaking load (>8 gf) carries tight lot-to-lot hardness variations. Ceramic DIP/QFN leadframes and Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured substrates must be secured from vetted packaging supply chains to avoid oxidized leadframe finishes.
critics.laya_pm: Thermosonic recipe DOE optimization controls the packaging critical path prior to final wafer sort verification and functional DRAM testing. critical_failure_modes: Pad Cratering: Excessive ultrasonic transducer amplitude (>100 mW) or uncalibrated impact force causing micro-cracking and fracture through the 100um Al bond pad into underlying ILD/IMD oxide.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Full-Factorial DOE Execution for Thermosonic Ball-Wedge Bonding on $100\,\mu\text{m}$ Al Pads

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Mount 25um 99.99% Au  │
│          Wire          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Set Stage Temp to    │
│        150 °C          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Full-Factorial DOE   │
│   Execution (Power x   │
│      Time Matrix)      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Thermosonic Ball    │
│    Bond on 100um x     │
│      100um Al Pad      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Mil-Std-883 Pull Test │
│     (>= 4.0 gf)        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Wire and Tooling Setup**:
   - Thread $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter, $99.99\%$ (4N) gold ($\text{Au}$) wire through the ceramic capillary on the automated thermosonic ball bonder.
   - Align the DRAM die containing $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ square aluminum ($\text{Al}$) bond pads attached to the leadframe.

2. **Stage Thermal Preheating**:
   - Set and stabilize the heated workholder stage temperature to **$150\,^\circ\text{C}$**.
   - Verify temperature stabilization on the leadframe surface before commencing bonding operations.

3. **EFO Free-Air Ball (FAB) Formation**:
   - Trigger the Electronic Flame-Off (EFO) discharge wand across the gold wire tail to form a spherical Free-Air Ball (FAB) at the capillary tip.

4. **DOE Factorial Matrix Execution**:
   - Execute a full-factorial Design of Experiments ($2^2$ or multilevel factorial) crossing **Transducer Ultrasonic Power** and **Bond Time** at the fixed **$60\,\text{kHz}$** transducer resonance frequency:
     - **Factor A (Ultrasonic Power)**: Low level = $50\,\text{mW}$, High level = $100\,\text{mW}$ (intermediate levels evaluated within $50\text{--}100\,\mu\text{W}/\text{mW}$ range).
     - **Factor B (Bond Time)**: Low level = $20\,\text{ms}$, High level = $30\,\text{ms}$.
   - Apply the capillary downward to press the gold ball onto the $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad while firing the ultrasonic pulse at the designated treatment cell.

5. **Looping & Wedge Stitch Termination**:
   - Form the wire loop span toward the leadframe pin and perform the wedge/stitch bond to complete the interconnect.

6. **Post-Bond Mechanical & Destructive Pull Testing**:
   - Calibrate the micro-hook wire pull tester according to **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011**.
   - Position the pull hook at mid-span of each bonded $25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire loop and execute destructive pull testing to measure peak failure force and document failure mode.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
 Wire Pull Strength Target vs DOE Runs (grams-force)
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │██████████████████████████████████████████████████│ DOE High Pwr (100mW): 6.8 gf
 │████████──────────────────────────────────────────│
 │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒               │ DOE Low Pwr (50mW): 5.2 gf
 │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒──────────────────────────────────────────│
 │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                        │ Min Specification: 4.0 gf
 └┬────────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬┘
 0.0                      3.5                     7.0
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value / Tolerance | Measurement Instrument / Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Wire Pull Strength** | $\ge 4.0\,\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Dage / Nordson Pull Tester via **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011** |
| **Pull Test Failure Mode** | $100\%$ failure in wire span (no bond pad lift or interface peel) | Optical / SEM inspection post-pull |
| **Ultrasonic Transducer Frequency & Power** | $60\,\text{kHz}$; $50\text{--}100\,\text{mW}$ | Transducer controller / Calibrated power sensor |
| **Bond Time Duration** | $20\text{--}30\,\text{ms}$ | Bonder digital timer / Oscilloscope transducer signal |
| **Stage Temperature** | $150\,^\circ\text{C} \pm 5\,^\circ\text{C}$ | Surface thermocouple / IR pyrometer |

---

### 3. Context & Source Citations
- **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging](file:///d:/coding/dram/docs/context.yaml)**:
  - Wire material: $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire.
  - Substrate stage temperature: $150\,^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Ultrasonic transducer specifications: $60\,\text{kHz}$, $50\text{--}100\,\text{mW}$ power pulse, $20\text{--}30\,\text{ms}$ duration.
  - Bond pad dimensions: $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
  - Quality and reliability standard: Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 pull strength limit $\ge 4.0\,\text{gf}$ with mid-span failure.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Execution of a full-factorial DOE (bonding temperature 130-170°C, ultrasonic transducer power 50-100 mW, time 15-35 ms, bonding force 15-35 gf) directly impacts package reliability and interconnect parasitics. Excessive ultrasonic energy or force during the ball bond on 100x100 um Al pads induces silicon cratering and dielectric micro-fractures under the pad oxide, while insufficient scrub energy fails to disperse native aluminum oxide (Al2O3), leading to poor intermetallic compound (Au-Al IMC) coverage and elevated pad-to-lead resistance across the 180nm DRAM data bus.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Au-Al thermosonic wirebonding requires optimized initial ball squash diameter (nominally 1.8x to 2.2x wire diameter, i.e., 45-55 um for 25 um Au wire) centered on the 100 um Al pad (leaving >20 um edge clearance to prevent passivation chipping). Maintaining stage temperature at 150°C during ultrasonic vibration ensures proper formation of Au4Al and Au8Al3 phases without driving rapid Kirkendall voiding (formation of brittle AuAl2 purple plague) during downstream thermal curing or reliability stress.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: 25 um 4N (99.99%) Au bonding wire, ceramic capillaries (e.g., fine-pitch matte-finish alumina), and leadframe stock are subject to precious metal spot prices and single-vendor lead times. Ensuring capillary tip life limits (<100k bonds before ultrasonic attenuation and tip buildup) and managing gold scrap/tailing disposal are critical to maintaining package unit cost within open-source MPW budget allocations.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The full-factorial matrix (4 factors at 3 levels = 81 distinct bonding parameter runs, 5 sample wires per run = 405 bonds) must be scheduled sequentially within machine reservation blocks. Failure to control stage pre-heat dwell and wire tail feed will cause drift in replicate metrics, jeopardizing tapeout packaging milestones and stalling post-assembly functional DRAM test campaigns.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Intermetallic interface micro-cracking and pad cratering into the underlying field/inter-metal dielectric due to excessive ultrasonic power (>100 mW) or excessive initial impact bonding force (>40 gf).
1. Non-stick on pad (NSOP) or ball lift caused by heavy native Al2O3 growth (>5 nm) following queue time breach between wafer saw/plasma clean and thermosonic wirebonding.
1. Capillary heel-crack fracture at the leadframe wedge bond caused by excessive ultrasonic energy, sharp capillary chamfer radius, or improper wire loop profile geometry.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-2-2-01` | **Destructive Wire Bond Pull Strength and Failure Mode Verification** | Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Bondtester equipped with 0-100 gf calibrated pull hook load cell, stereo inspection microscope (100x magnification). | 1. Position test leadframe package securely in mechanical clamping fixture under calibrated pull hook. 2. Calibrate bondtester hook height to position exactly at wire loop apex (mid-span, 1/3 to 1/2 distance from ball to wedge). 3. Apply vertical pull rate of 100 um/s until physical rupture occurs. 4. Record peak rupture force in grams-force (gf) and classify failure site (Code 1: Ball lift, Code 2: Wire break at neck/heat-affected zone, Code 3: Mid-span wire break, Code 4: Heel break, Code 5: Wedge lift). 5. Repeat across n=5 test wires per DOE condition. | `Peak pull strength must be >= 6.0 gf across all replicate bonds (exceeding Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 minimum threshold of 4.0 gf). 100% of failures must occur in the wire span or neck (Codes 2, 3, or 4); zero instances of ball lift (Code 1) or pad cratering permitted.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-2-2-02` | **Ball Bond Shear Strength and Intermetallic (IMC) Area Ratio Inspection** | Dage 4000Plus Bondtester with 25 um tungsten carbide shear tool, high-resolution optical metallurgical microscope with calibrated digital reticle. | 1. Align shear tool perpendicular to ball bond diameter at standard standoff height (3 um). 2. Drive shear tool forward at 50 um/s across the pad to displace the gold ball. 3. Record peak shear force in grams-force (gf). 4. Inspect residual pad footprint under 500x optical/metallurgical microscope to visually quantify Au-Al intermetallic coverage area relative to original ball footprint area. 5. Perform chemical etch (concentrated HNO3 dip) on selected witness dies to verify absence of micro-cracks/cratering in the underlying silicon dioxide substrate. | `Minimum ball shear force must exceed 15.0 gf (or >= 5.5 gf per mil^2 of ball shear area). Au-Al intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage area must be >= 70% of the ball contact footprint. Substrate cratering inspection must show zero cracks or silicon divots.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (accelerator-free, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 approved UV and impact safety glasses, Thermal-resistant Kevlar/Nomex under-gloves for heated stage handling (>150°C), Cleanroom ESD coat, conductive ESD heel straps, and hair/beard covers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn from 150°C heated work stage: Immediately flush affected skin under clean cold running water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek cleanroom medical triage. IPA splash to eyes: Flush eyes with emergency eyewash for 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Physical puncture from wire/tweezers: Disinfect with sterile antiseptic and report to cleanroom safety officer.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Localized dedicated point-of-use extraction plenum over thermosonic bonder stage to capture trace outgassing volatiles from die attach epoxy remnants during 150°C heating. Certified cleanroom laminar flow hood maintaining ISO Class 5 air quality with exhaust face velocity of 0.45 m/s.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect cut gold wire tails, expired spool ends, and used capillaries into a locked, labeled precious metal reclamation container. Spent IPA cleaning wipes must be collected in grounded, airtight hazardous waste flammables bins and disposed of via certified chemical disposal protocols.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA, cleanroom wipe)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9 wt%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge/Blanket Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP, Grade 5.0) | `>= 99.999 vol%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-die-attach cured DRAM dies on leadframe; 100x100 um Al-0.5%Cu pads free of epoxy bleed-out, particulates, or fluorocarbon residues; native Al2O3 thickness < 2.5 nm confirmed via witness ellipsometry/XPS.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully wire-bonded DRAM leadframe units; Au ball-wedge interconnects completed; packaged units stored in vacuum-sealed moisture barrier bags (MBB) with active desiccant and humidity indicator card.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient air causes native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) to thicken beyond 4.0 nm and absorb ambient organic/airborne molecular contaminants (AMCs), severely attenuating ultrasonic scrub efficiency and inducing catastrophic Non-Stick On Pad (NSOP) or latent bond lift under thermal cycling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed full-factorial DOE matrix execution (81 conditions, 405 total bond sites) defining the optimized operating window for thermosonic Au ball-wedge wirebonding on 180nm DRAM 100 um Al pads, demonstrating compliant mechanical pull/shear strengths with zero cratering and >70% IMC intermetallic formation.

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean destructive wire pull strength across optimal DOE parameter set** | `>= 7.5 gf` | ± 0.8 gf (std dev <= 0.6 gf, Cpk >= 1.67 relative to 4.0 gf lower spec limit) | Calibrated pull hook bondtester per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 on n=30 validation wires. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Mean ball shear strength on 100 um Al bonding pads** | `>= 22.0 gf` | ± 2.5 gf (minimum single read >= 16.0 gf) | Dage 4000Plus shear tester at 3 um tool standoff per JEDEC JESD22-B116. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

critics.systems_engineer: Execution of a full-factorial DOE (bonding temperature 130-170°C, ultrasonic transducer power 50-100 mW, time 15-35 ms, bonding force 15-35 gf) directly impacts package reliability and interconnect parasitics. Excessive ultrasonic energy or force during the ball bond on 100x100 um Al pads induces silicon cratering and dielectric micro-fractures under the pad oxide, while insufficient scrub energy fails to disperse native aluminum oxide (Al2O3), leading to poor intermetallic compound (Au-Al IMC) coverage and elevated pad-to-lead resistance across the 180nm DRAM data bus.
critics.domain_expert: Au-Al thermosonic wirebonding requires optimized initial ball squash diameter (nominally 1.8x to 2.2x wire diameter, i.e., 45-55 um for 25 um Au wire) centered on the 100 um Al pad (leaving >20 um edge clearance to prevent passivation chipping). Maintaining stage temperature at 150°C during ultrasonic vibration ensures proper formation of Au4Al and Au8Al3 phases without driving rapid Kirkendall voiding (formation of brittle AuAl2 purple plague) during downstream thermal curing or reliability stress.
critics.supply_chain: 25 um 4N (99.99%) Au bonding wire, ceramic capillaries (e.g., fine-pitch matte-finish alumina), and leadframe stock are subject to precious metal spot prices and single-vendor lead times. Ensuring capillary tip life limits (<100k bonds before ultrasonic attenuation and tip buildup) and managing gold scrap/tailing disposal are critical to maintaining package unit cost within open-source MPW budget allocations.
critics.laya_pm: The full-factorial matrix (4 factors at 3 levels = 81 distinct bonding parameter runs, 5 sample wires per run = 405 bonds) must be scheduled sequentially within machine reservation blocks. Failure to control stage pre-heat dwell and wire tail feed will cause drift in replicate metrics, jeopardizing tapeout packaging milestones and stalling post-assembly functional DRAM test campaigns.
critical_failure_modes: Intermetallic interface micro-cracking and pad cratering into the underlying field/inter-metal dielectric due to excessive ultrasonic power (>100 mW) or excessive initial impact bonding force (>40 gf).
Non-stick on pad (NSOP) or ball lift caused by heavy native Al2O3 growth (>5 nm) following queue time breach between wafer saw/plasma clean and thermosonic wirebonding.
Capillary heel-crack fracture at the leadframe wedge bond caused by excessive ultrasonic energy, sharp capillary chamfer radius, or improper wire loop profile geometry.

testcases.title: Destructive Wire Bond Pull Strength and Failure Mode Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Bondtester equipped with 0-100 gf calibrated pull hook load cell, stereo inspection microscope (100x magnification).
testcases.pre_conditions: DRAM dies mounted with Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min on leadframes; 25 um 4N Au wire thermosonic bonds completed across full-factorial matrix; ambient cleanroom temperature 22±2°C, RH 45±5%.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position test leadframe package securely in mechanical clamping fixture under calibrated pull hook. 2. Calibrate bondtester hook height to position exactly at wire loop apex (mid-span, 1/3 to 1/2 distance from ball to wedge). 3. Apply vertical pull rate of 100 um/s until physical rupture occurs. 4. Record peak rupture force in grams-force (gf) and classify failure site (Code 1: Ball lift, Code 2: Wire break at neck/heat-affected zone, Code 3: Mid-span wire break, Code 4: Heel break, Code 5: Wedge lift). 5. Repeat across n=5 test wires per DOE condition.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Peak pull strength must be >= 6.0 gf across all replicate bonds (exceeding Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 minimum threshold of 4.0 gf). 100% of failures must occur in the wire span or neck (Codes 2, 3, or 4); zero instances of ball lift (Code 1) or pad cratering permitted.

testcases.title: Ball Bond Shear Strength and Intermetallic (IMC) Area Ratio Inspection
testcases.instrumentation: Dage 4000Plus Bondtester with 25 um tungsten carbide shear tool, high-resolution optical metallurgical microscope with calibrated digital reticle.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafers/leadframes post-thermosonic bonding; stage cooled to room temperature; shear tool tip calibrated for 3-5 um standoff height above the 100 um Al bond pad surface.
testcases.procedure: 1. Align shear tool perpendicular to ball bond diameter at standard standoff height (3 um). 2. Drive shear tool forward at 50 um/s across the pad to displace the gold ball. 3. Record peak shear force in grams-force (gf). 4. Inspect residual pad footprint under 500x optical/metallurgical microscope to visually quantify Au-Al intermetallic coverage area relative to original ball footprint area. 5. Perform chemical etch (concentrated HNO3 dip) on selected witness dies to verify absence of micro-cracks/cratering in the underlying silicon dioxide substrate.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Minimum ball shear force must exceed 15.0 gf (or >= 5.5 gf per mil^2 of ball shear area). Au-Al intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage area must be >= 70% of the ball contact footprint. Substrate cratering inspection must show zero cracks or silicon divots.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Title:** Mil-Std-883 Wire Pull & Ball Shear Strength Metrology with Failure Mode Analysis  
**Technology Node:** 180nm CMOS DRAM Generation 3  
**Classification:** Metrology & Assembly Quality Assurance (Packaging)  

---

### Process Workflow
```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Mount Assembly to    │
│        Fixture         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Perform Mil-Std-883   │
│    Method 2011 Wire    │
│          Pull          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────◇───────────┐
│   Measure Pull Force   │
└────────────◇───────────┘
             │
             ├─────────────────────────────────────╮ F < 4.0 gf
  F >= 4.0 gf│                                     │
             ▼                                     ▼
┌────────────────────────┐            ┌────────────────────────┐
│  Ball Shear Metrology  │            │   Reject Lot & Root    │
│    on 100um Al Pad     │            │   Cause Failure Mode   │
└────────────┬───────────┘            └────────────────────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Optical SEM       │
│     Inspection of      │
│  Interfacial Failure   │
│          Mode          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Lot Release & SPC    │
│        Archive         │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate & Package Fixturing**
   - Secure the assembled DRAM ceramic package (after 150°C 60-minute die attach cure) onto the calibrated bond tester mechanical vacuum stage.
   - Align the optics perpendicular to the $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads (Metal-1 sputtered at $350\,\text{nm} \pm 5\%$ thickness).

2. **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull Metrology**
   - Position a calibrated pull hook directly beneath the midpoint of the $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter 99.99% gold (Au) wire span (formed via thermosonic bonding at $150^\circ\text{C}$, $60\,\text{kHz}$, $50\text{--}100\,\text{mW}$, $20\text{--}30\,\text{ms}$).
   - Execute a vertical pull test at a controlled rate of $1.0\,\text{mm/s}$ normal to the die surface until rupture.
   - Record the peak force in grams-force ($\text{gf}$) on the digital load cell.

3. **Ball Shear Strength Testing**
   - Position the shearing tool chisel at a standoff height of $3\text{--}5\,\mu\text{m}$ above the $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ Al bond pad metallization.
   - Drive the tool horizontally against the thermosonic Au ball bond interface at a steady displacement rate.
   - Record peak shear force and monitor for cratering into the underlying dielectric/die substrate.

4. **Failure Mode Categorization & Inspection**
   - Inspect the fracture site under high-magnification optical/SEM inspection:
     - **Acceptable Failure Mode:** Wire span neck break or mid-span wire break.
     - **Rejectable Failure Modes:** Ball lift-off (bond interface separation), wedge peel-off, or silicon cratering under the $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ pad.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                            ┌──────────────────────────┐
                            │░░░░░░░░                  │
         Pad Dim (Width/Len)┤░░░░░░░░                  │
                            │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
           M1 Film Thickness┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
        EFO Au Wire Diameter┤▓▓▓                       │
                            │▓▓▓                       │
Min Pull Force (Mil-Std-883)┤█                         │
                            │█                         │
                            └┬─────┬──────┬─────┬──────┘
                            0.0  87.5   175.0 262.5     
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Destructive Wire Pull Strength** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Calibrated Hook Load Cell / Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 |
| **Wire Pull Failure Site** | Wire span rupture (0% interface lift) | Categorical mode | High-Magnification Optical / SEM Inspection |
| **Bonding Pad Geometry** | $100 \times 100$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical Metrology Stage |
| **Metal-1 Underlayer Thickness** | $350 \pm 5\%$ | $\text{nm}$ | Stylus Profilometry / Ellipsometry |

---

### Verified Context Citations
- **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull & Wire Diameter:** Sourced directly from *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging* ("Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0$ grams-force for $25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire. Failure must occur in wire span, not at bond interface").
- **Thermosonic Au Bonding Parameters & Pad Size:** Sourced from *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging* ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares; $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter 99.99% Au wire; $150^\circ\text{C}$ stage; $60\,\text{kHz}$, $50\text{--}100\,\text{mW}$, $20\text{--}30\,\text{ms}$).
- **Interconnect Metallization Foundation:** Sourced from *Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects* (Metal-1 thickness target $350\,\text{nm} \pm 5\%$, sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\text{sq}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Wire pull and ball shear metrology on 100um Al pads must trace back to thermomechanical stress models during DRAM ceramic DIP packaging and thermal cycling. Hook positioning at exactly mid-span or one-third loop height alters resolved normal and shear stress vectors, meaning Gauge R&R across 9-site leadframes requires rigid micro-positioning repeatable within +/-2 um to avoid false failures.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Method 2011.7 requires destructive pull testing force >= 4.0 gf for 25 um Au wire, but pad metallization cratering under the Au-Al intermetallic (Au4Al, Au5Al2) interface indicates excessive ultrasonic energy (over 100 mW) or capillary force. Ball shear height must be calibrated to 3-5 um above the pad surface; shearing above 5 um shears pure gold neck without stressing the intermetallic bond.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dataram and local assembly partners in VN require certified calibrated load cells (0-100 gf pull hook and 0-250 gf shear chisel) with traceable calibration artifacts. Lead time on replacement tungsten carbide bond tester shear tools and hook tips exceeds 8 weeks, necessitating strict wear-monitoring protocols.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To prevent wafer sort and assembly bottlenecks for Gen 3 tapeout, destructive pull and shear sampling must be integrated into automated lot-traveler gatekeeping; any yield excursion or pad lift failure mode must halt leadframe indexing prior to epoxy encapsulation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Pad peeling/silicon cratering underneath the 100um Al pad due to excessive ultrasonic power during thermosonic bonding
1. Interfacial bond lift (Mode 2) exhibiting <4.0 gf pull strength from inadequate Au-Al intermetallic coverage or native Al2O3 oxidation
1. Heel fracture at wedge bond or neck break adjacent to ball bond caused by mechanical over-crimping and capillary wear

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-2-3-01` | **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Destructive Wire Pull Strength and Failure Mode Classification** | Dage 4000Plus Bondtester equipped with 100gf miniature pull hook cartridge and high-magnification optical inspection microscope | 1. Secure leadframe fixture under the pull tester stage with vacuum clamp. 2. Center the 25 um hook under wire span at 1/3 distance between ball and wedge bond. 3. Lower hook until clear of adjacent loop and actuate vertical pull at 200 um/s until fracture. 4. Record peak force in grams-force (gf). 5. Inspect fracture locus via microscope at 100x and log failure mode (Mode 1: Wire break at neck; Mode 2: Ball lift; Mode 3: Mid-span break; Mode 4: Heel break; Mode 5: Pad lift/crater). | `Destructive pull force >= 4.0 gf for all tested wires (n=30 per lot). Failure mode must be Wire Span Break (Mode 3) or Neck Break (Mode 1); zero occurrences of Bond Lift (Mode 2) or Pad Cratering (Mode 5).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-2-3-02` | **JESD22-B116 Ball Shear Strength and Intermetallic Compound (IMC) Area Metrology** | Nordson DAGE 4000Plus Multi-Function Bondtester with 250gf shear tool chisel, stylus contact sensor, and metallurgical optical microscope with image analysis | 1. Position tungsten carbide shear chisel 15 um behind the Au ball bond along leadframe orientation axis. 2. Verify shear clearance height of 4.0 um +/- 0.5 um from pad plane. 3. Drive chisel horizontally against the ball at 100 um/s until ball detachment. 4. Record peak shear force in grams-force (gf). 5. Calculate shear strength normalized to ball bonded area (gf/mil^2). 6. Inspect sheared footprint under metallurgical microscope at 200x to quantify intermetallic coverage percentage. | `Mean ball shear force >= 15.0 gf (or >= 5.5 gf/mil^2 based on 65 um squashed ball diameter); minimum individual shear force >= 12.0 gf; remaining intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage on pad footprint >= 70% with zero silicon cratering.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, chemical resistant), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe dissipative lab coat, Class 10,000 cleanroom face mask
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with solvent, wash immediately with soap and copious water for 15 minutes. For eye contact, flush with isotonic eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention. If mechanical wire puncture occurs, sanitize wound, apply antiseptic dressing, and monitor for foreign body irritation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operate within ISO Class 6 / Class 1000 laminar flow bench with local mechanical exhaust ventilation providing face velocity >= 0.5 m/s during solvent cleaning of metrology fixtures.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect IPA solvent wipes and broken gold/aluminum wire fragments in dedicated ESD-safe hazardous waste containers. Segregate precious metal scrap (Au wire remnants) for reclamation; solvent waste disposed according to industrial solvent neutralization protocols.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Epoxy (Cured Ablebond 84-1LMIS residue clean)** | `7440-22-4` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `70-80% Ag in Bisphenol-A epoxy matrix` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-thermosonic wirebonding, cured die-attach leadframes, pristine unoxidized Au loops with no particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Post-pull and post-shear tested leadframes with documented destructive fracture sites, purged with dry filtered N2 prior to failure analysis or disposal.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits causes atmospheric moisture adsorption, sulfur corrosion of leadframe silver plating, and galvanic micro-corrosion at Au-Al interfaces, distorting baseline shear/pull readings and invalidating statistical process control.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full qualification and metrological validation of thermosonic Au ball and wedge bond mechanical integrity on 180nm DRAM 100um Al pads according to Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 and JESD22-B116 standards, delivering statistically validated Cpk >= 1.67 for wire pull and ball shear forces.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `mil_std_883_wire_pull_shear_distribution_report.csv`
- [ ] `failure_mode_analysis_intermetallic_coverage_atlas.pdf`
- [ ] `sem_optical_ball_shear_fracture_micrographs.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Thermosonic gold ball shear force on 100 um Al bond pad** | `>= 18.0 gf` | +/- 1.5 gf | JESD22-B116 shear chisel test at 4.0 um shear height across n=30 ball bonds |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Gauge R&R measurement coefficient of variation (CV) for bondtester load cells** | `< 1.0%` | Max 1.0% | 10-run repeatability Gage R&R evaluation against certified calibration micro-weights |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of tested wires exceed Mil-Std-883 minimum threshold (>= 4.0 gf pull, >= 15.0 gf shear), zero observed occurrences of bond lift (Mode 2) or Si cratering (Mode 5), Gage R&R CV < 1.0%, and formal signoff by Lead Packaging Engineer and Metrology Quality Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Mil-Std-883 Wire Pull Test & Ball Shear Metrology Validation

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Wire pull and ball shear metrology must close the verification loop for thermosonic packaging integrity across thermal cycling (-40°C to 125°C). However, using manual hook placement risks non-standard hook angle vectors (non-perpendicular pulling), which distorts measured gram-force calculations by up to 18% via trigonometric resolution error. Metrology systems must enforce auto-centering hook algorithms and optical fiducial alignment on 100 um x 100 um DRAM pads to guarantee statistical process control (Cpk >= 1.67).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Under MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 (Bond Strength) and Method 2019 / ASTM F1269 (Ball Shear), a simple gram-force reading is insufficient without precise failure mode categorization. For 25 um 99.99% Au wire thermosonic bonding on Al-0.5%Cu DRAM metallization, neck breaks or mid-span wire breaks indicate robust intermetallic compound (IMC) formation (Au4Al / Au5Al2). Conversely, bond pad lift-off or heel shearing below 4.0 gf denotes improper ultrasonic power transfer, pre-existing microcracking in the underlying ILD/IMD stack (low-k or SiO2 cracking), or incomplete native oxide breakdown.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Qualification of 99.99% (4N) gold bonding wire requires second-source validation (e.g., Heraeus vs. Tanaka Kikinzoku) due to subtle differences in dopant levels (e.g., 5-10 ppm Be or Ca) altering elongation, heat-affected zone (HAZ) recrystallization, and loop sagging under vibration. Dicing tape, leadframes (copper alloy C7025 vs. Alloy 42), and ceramic DIP-28 carriers must maintain certified lots to avoid leadframe silver plating oxidation that degrades wedge adhesion.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Destructive physical analysis (DPA) metrology cycles must not deplete prototype 180nm MPW wafer lots. Sample sizes must strictly balance statistical confidence against unit cost: exactly 30 wires per leadframe package sampled across 5 separate packages per recipe batch. Data pipeline must ingest automated hook/shear test load vs. displacement curves into the DRAM Foundation VN QA repository within 2 hours of test completion.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die metallization/ILD cratering underneath ball bond caused by excessive bonding force (>35 gf) or excessive ultrasonic power (>100 mW), fracturing the underlying SiO2 dielectric stack.
1. Intermetallic Kirkendall voiding and thermal aging embrittlement (Au-Al purple plague formation) resulting in premature ball lift-off during high-temperature storage or shear testing.
1. Heel cracking at the wedge/leadframe transition caused by severe capillary over-clamping or excessive deformation ratio (>1.5x wire diameter), leading to low-force wire failure below 3.0 gf.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-01` | **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Destructive Wire Pull Strength and Failure Mode Classification** | Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Bondtester equipped with calibrated 100 gf pull cartridge, automated hook positioning optical microscope, and 25 um tungsten carbide pull hook. | 1. Fixture the leadframe assembly rigidly onto the motorized vacuum chuck of the bond tester. 2. Calibrate pull hook zero-load offset at 100 um above package surface. 3. Position the hook at mid-span of the 25 um Au wire loop (between ball on DRAM pad and crescent wedge on leadframe pin) at a 90° ± 5° normal angle relative to die surface. 4. Engage Z-axis pull motor at a controlled test speed of 1000 um/s until wire failure occurs. 5. Record peak fracture load (grams-force) and capture high-resolution optical image of failure site to classify failure mode (Code 1: Wire break in mid-span/HAZ; Code 2: Ball lift; Code 3: Wedge lift; Code 4: Pad/die cratering). Repeat across N=30 randomized wires per device. | `Minimum pull strength for each individual 25 um Au wire must be >= 4.0 gf. Mean pull strength across N=30 wires must be >= 6.5 gf with standard deviation sigma <= 0.8 gf. 100% of failure modes must be mid-span wire break or neck break (Code 1); 0 occurrences of ball lift (Code 2), wedge lift (Code 3), or pad cratering (Code 4).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-02` | **ASTM F1269 / JEDEC JESD22-B116 Destructive Ball Bond Shear Strength and IMC Area Assessment** | Dage 4000Plus Bondtester with 250 gf shear cartridge, precision ground flat-tip shear tool (width 75 um), and high-resolution optical / SEM imaging station. | 1. Clamp die-attach package flat on vacuum stage. 2. Align shear tool perpendicular to the ball bond axis with shear tool edge positioned 3 um to 5 um above the aluminum pad surface (below 10% of deformed ball height to prevent ball rolling/levering). 3. Drive shear ram horizontally at 100 um/s against the gold ball until complete interfacial displacement occurs. 4. Record peak shear force (grams-force) and calculate shear strength normalized to bonded area (gf/mil^2 or g/um^2). 5. Inspect sheared footprint under 200x optical microscope / SEM to measure residual Au-Al intermetallic coverage percentage on the pad. | `Minimum ball shear force must be >= 15.0 gf for 25 um wire (deformed ball diameter 60-70 um). Normalized shear strength must exceed 5.5 gf/mil^2 (0.0085 gf/um^2). Residual intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage on the aluminum bonding pad must exceed 75% of the total bonded ball footprint area, with 0% silicon/dielectric cratering detected.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 approved UV and impact safety glasses, ESD cleanroom smock and grounded wrist strap, Safety shoes with static dissipative soles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean isotonic eyewash for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical evaluation. Skin contact with IPA: Wash affected skin with soap and water; remove contaminated garments. Inhalation of IPA fumes: Evacuate worker to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Mechanical puncture from micro-hooks/wire: Clean puncture wound with antiseptic, bandage immediately, and report to cleanroom occupational health officer.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Bond testing station and solvent wiping bench must operate under laminar flow HEPA hoods (0.45 m/s face velocity) with local slot exhaust extraction for organic solvent vapors (IPA) exhausting directly to cleanroom VOC scrubbers.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Wipes contaminated with IPA must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-resistant hazardous waste bins for chemical solvent disposal. Expended gold wire scraps, sheared gold ball residues, and defective leadframes must be collected in dedicated ESD-safe precious metal reclamation containers for precious metal recycling.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gold Wire (99.99% Au)** | `7440-57-5` | 4N High Purity Semiconductor Grade | `99.99%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for stage/tool cleaning** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.8%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 purge gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: DRAM dies post-die attach cure (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min) with pristine, unoxidized 100 um x 100 um Al-0.5%Cu bond pads free of epoxy bleed-out, particulates, or organic condensate.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Mechanically validated, clean-tested wirebonded leadframe units ready for transfer to post-wirebond encapsulation (transfer molding) with zero particulate re-contamination.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive queue time in cleanroom air (>120 min) exposes bare Al bond pads and Cu leadframes to atmospheric moisture and airborne organic volatiles, forming a passivating native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) layer and silver/copper tarnish that severely inhibits Au-Al atomic interdiffusion, yielding brittle intermetallics, high electrical contact resistance, and catastrophic ball lift failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical, mechanical, and statistical validation of thermosonic Au ball and wedge bonds on 180nm DRAM prototype leadframes meeting MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 and ASTM F1269 standards, proving robust wire pull strength, high ball shear resistance, absence of pad cratering, and high-yielding Cpk metrics.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MIL_STD_883_WirePull_BallShear_Statistical_Report.csv`
- [ ] `DRAM_Pad_Intermetallic_Coverage_FailureMode_Atlas.pdf`
- [ ] `HighRes_ShearFootprint_SEM_Micrographs.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Individual wire pull force for 25 um 4N Au wire on DRAM bond pad and leadframe** | `>= 6.5 gf (mean), >= 4.0 gf (individual min)` | +3.0 gf / -0.0 gf above minimum | Calibrated Dage 4000Plus Bondtester 100 gf pull cartridge pulling at 1000 um/s per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Ball shear force on 100 um x 100 um Al pad for 25 um diameter wire (ball diameter 65 um)** | `>= 20.0 gf` | +10.0 gf / -5.0 gf (absolute minimum 15.0 gf) | Dage 4000Plus 250 gf shear cartridge, tool height 4 um, shear rate 100 um/s per ASTM F1269 |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Interfacial Au-Al intermetallic compound (IMC) residual area post-ball shear** | `>= 85.0%` | >= 75.0% absolute lower limit | SEM backscatter electron imaging and automated threshold image analysis of sheared pad footprint |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero package samples exhibit bond pad lift-off, ILD cratering, or pull forces < 4.0 gf across 150 sampled wires (5 packages x 30 wires); calculated process capability index Cpk >= 1.67 for wire pull and ball shear strength; formal signoff by Packaging Lead and DRAM Metrology QA Director.
