# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Hook & Shear Tool Calibration with ASTM/MIL Destructive Test Fixture Setup
**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-032`  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Packaging & Assembly > Metrology  
**Target Action Type:** Buy / Setup / Calibration  
**Classification:** Destructive Metrology Calibration Protocol  

---

### 1. Equipment, Fixturing & Materials Required
- **Bond Pull & Ball Shear Tester:** Multipurpose precision bond tester (e.g., Dage / Nordson / Royce equivalent) fitted with a 0–100 gf load cartridge.
- **Wire Pull Hook:** Miniature micro-hook sized for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire loops (hook radius $15\text{--}25\ \mu\text{m}$).
- **Shear Tool:** Precision tungsten carbide shear chisel matching $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pad pitch and $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire ball diameters.
- **Calibration Standards:** Certified dead-weight calibration kit with class E2 precision weights ($1.00\text{ gf}$, $4.00\text{ gf}$, $10.00\text{ gf}$, $50.00\text{ gf}$).
- **Reference Substrate Fixture:** Universal vacuum/mechanical clamping vice for Ceramic DIP/QFN leadframes with $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.

---

### 2. Process & Calibration Workflow Diagram

```
[Certified Dead-Weight Verification]
                 │
                 ▼
[Hook & Shear Chisel Fixture Zeroing]
                 │
                 ▼
[Z-Touchdown & Landing Height Offset Calibration]
                 │
                 ▼
[Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Destructive Pull / Shear Execution]
                 │
                 ▼
[Acceptance Criteria Verification & Failure Code Logging]
```

```text
       Wire Pull & Hook Calibration Limits (grams-force / um)
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                             │
Hook Tol┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                             │
Pull Typ┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
        │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Pull Min┤████████████████████████                    │
        │████████████████████████                    │
        └┬──────────┬──────────┬─────────┬──────────┬┘
        0.0        1.9        3.8       5.6       7.5 
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Calibration & Setup Procedure

#### Step 1: Tool Load Cell Calibration & Transducer Verification
1. Power on the bond tester and allow load cell thermal stabilization for $\ge 30\text{ minutes}$.
2. Mount the calibrated dead-weight calibration arm onto the strain-gauge load transducer.
3. Perform a 3-point dead-weight calibration at $1.00\text{ gf}$, $4.00\text{ gf}$, and $10.00\text{ gf}$.
4. Ensure load cell linearity error is within $\le \pm 0.1\%\text{ full-scale}$ ($0.1\text{ gf}$).

#### Step 2: Micro-Hook Installation & Alignment (Wire Pull Mode)
1. Install the micro-hook for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire testing (Au or Al-1% Si wire).
2. Align hook perpendicular to the bond span using an optical microscope ($50\times\text{--}100\times$ magnification).
3. Set pull speed to $100\ \mu\text{m/s}\text{ to }200\ \mu\text{m/s}$ in pure vertical ($90^\circ \pm 5^\circ$) orientation relative to the leadframe plane.
4. Position hook tip midway along the wire span between the on-chip $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pad and the leadframe pin.

#### Step 3: Shear Tool Fixturing & Landing Height Calibration (Ball Shear Mode)
1. Mount the tungsten carbide shear tool; ensure the tool face is parallel to the die edge within $\le 1^\circ$.
2. Perform contact touchdown on the bare die passivated surface next to the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ bond pad to define $Z=0$.
3. Back off the shear tool to a fixed shear height of $3.0\ \mu\text{m}\text{ to }5.0\ \mu\text{m}$ above the pad metallization to avoid dragging across the $350\text{ nm}$ aluminum layer.
4. Set shear travel velocity to $50\ \mu\text{m/s}$ across a minimum stroke length of $100\ \mu\text{m}$.

#### Step 4: Test Fixture Clamping & Verification Run
1. Secure the packaged leadframe into the vacuum chuck; apply vacuum pressure $\ge 600\text{ mmHg}$ to prevent device movement.
2. Execute destructive pull tests on sample bonds according to **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011**.
3. Verify failure modes: valid tests must result in failure across the wire span rather than premature bond interface peeling.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Measurement Target Metric | Physical Unit | Verification Standard / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Wire Pull Strength** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{grams-force (gf)}$ | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 ($25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire) |
| **Load Cell Linearity Error** | $\le \pm 0.1$ | $\text{grams-force (gf)}$ | Dead-weight standard ($1\text{--}10\text{ gf}$) |
| **Shear Tool Clearance Height** | $3.0\text{ to }5.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical displacement / Z-micrometer |
| **Failure Location Mode** | $100\%$ Mid-span wire neck/breakage | $\%$ occurrence | Post-test optical review (No pad lift/interface peel) |

---

### 5. Context Sources & Citations
- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:** Defines $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter Au / Al-1% Si wire, $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads, Ceramic DIP/QFN packages, and **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011** minimum pull test threshold ($\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$ with wire span failure mode).
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects:** Specifies the Metal-1 target thickness ($350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$) and pad surface metallurgy context ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Al pads).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Load cell calibration across sub-gram to 100gf ranges requires stiff fixturing and dynamic vibration isolation (<1.5 Hz cutoff) to eliminate environmental noise during micro-pull and shear force acquisition. Parallax error and optical alignment drift between the high-magnification stereomicroscope and the motorized Z/X-axis travel stages must be systematically compensated via closed-loop encoder feedback to prevent shear tool tip-to-pad collision or false failure trigger on wire loops.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 (wire pull) and JEDEC JESD22-B116 / ASTM F1269 (ball shear), tool geometry and clearance height (typically 3-5 um above the metallization pad) are paramount. A dull or contaminated tungsten carbide shear chisel alters shear plane stress distribution, leading to artificial pad lift-off or silicon cratering under 180nm CMOS Al-0.5%Cu bonding pads rather than true intermetallic compound (Au-Al IMC) ductile ball shear.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement of NIST-traceable micro-gram calibration weights (Class E2/F1 standards) and certified tungsten carbide shear tool chisels and pull hooks faces a 6-to-8 week import lead time. Second-sourcing options for high-precision strain-gauge cartridges (Dage/Nordson or Royce compatible) must be qualified locally to mitigate packaging assembly line downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Tool calibration and fixture qualification must be completed within a 3-day window prior to packaging pilot runs to avoid blocking BEOL wafer sort packaging schedules. The calibration procedure and documentation must be audit-ready for ISO 17025 / MIL-STD compliance without expanding capital tooling budget allocation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Shear tool clearance height drift resulting in chisel rubbing against the passivation layer, causing catastrophic pad tear-out and silicon cratering.
1. Load cell nonlinearity or zero-drift exceeding 0.5% full scale, masking weak Au ball neck metallization fatigue and invalidating MIL-STD-883 batch qualification.
1. Misalignment of pull hook radius with 25um Au wire diameter causing localized stress concentration and premature wire neck-break.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-1-01` | **NIST-Traceable Static Load Cell Calibration and Linearity Verification (0 to 100 gf)** | Nordson DAGE 4000Plus / Royce 650 Bondtester with 100gf miniature load cell cartridge, Class E2 certified non-magnetic stainless steel calibration weights (1gf, 5gf, 10gf, 20gf, 50gf, 100gf), optical micrometer stage. | 1. Zero and tare the load cell cartridge via the software interface. 2. Sequentially apply NIST-certified weights in ascending order (1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 gf) to the hook/chisel fixture. 3. Record raw transducer voltage and converted gram-force values after 5 seconds dwell per point. 4. Remove weights in descending order to quantify hysteresis. 5. Compute full-scale linearity, repeatability error, and hysteresis percentage across 5 complete cycles. | `Measurement accuracy within +/-0.25% of full scale (<= 0.25 gf maximum deviation); load cell linearity R-squared >= 0.9999; hysteresis error <= 0.20 gf across the entire 0-100 gf measurement range.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-1-02` | **ASTM F1269 / JEDEC JESD22-B116 Ball Shear Tool Clearance Height and Touchdown Reproducibility** | Automated Bondtester contact touchdown sensor system, 38um tungsten carbide shear chisel tool, laser displacement interferometer (Keyence LK-G5000), optical inspection stereomicroscope (100x). | 1. Execute automated surface touchdown calibration to locate pad metallization datum (Z=0). 2. Program nominal shear tool offset height to 4.0 um. 3. Drive the shear tool to 30 pre-selected test pad coordinates across the substrate. 4. Measure actual tool tip clearance from pad surface using laser displacement interferometer. 5. Inspect test pads under optical microscope post-touchdown to verify absence of mechanical indentation. | `Absolute tool standoff clearance within 4.0 um +/- 0.5 um across all 30 points; zero observable physical denting or scratch damage on Al-0.5%Cu bonding metallization prior to shear actuation.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/1000 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, antistatic), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, Cleanroom lint-free smock and conductive ESD heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Flush immediately with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes. Eye contact: Rinse thoroughly at cleanroom eyewash station for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek medical evaluation. Inhalation: Relocate to fresh air immediately. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; contact emergency toxicological services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local chemical bench fume extraction hood with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) during solvent swab cleaning of tungsten carbide tooling; general cleanroom laminar airflow recirculation maintaining positive pressure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA/Acetone wipes and cotton swabs must be segregated in dedicated fire-rated, airtight, self-closing hazardous solvent waste receptacles. Spent solvent rinses disposed of via designated flammable solvent waste carboys according to local hazardous material regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Electronic Grade (>=99.9%) | `99.9%` |
| **Acetone** | `67-64-1` | Semiconductor Grade | `99.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly thermosonic-bonded 180nm DRAM leadframe/substrate units with clean, unoxidized 25um Au wires and Al-0.5%Cu bonding pads free of organic residue, flux, or particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Sheared and pulled bond sites with documented fracture topography and intact uncratered silicon substrate, wiped clean with IPA to remove shear debris, sealed in dry antistatic carrier.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended atmospheric exposure causes atmospheric moisture and sulfur/halogen adsorption on exposed Al-Cu pad interfaces, leading to galvanic corrosion, inaccurate shear force readings, and false failure categorization of intermetallic bonding.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration and setup sign-off of the wire pull and ball shear metrology station adhering to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 and ASTM F1269 standards, achieving sub-gram load cell accuracy and reproducible sub-micron tool clearance for 180nm DRAM packaging quality assurance.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CAL_CERT_NIST_LOADCELL_100GF_20261015.pdf`
- [ ] `SHEAR_TOOL_STANDOFF_VERIFICATION_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `IMC_FRACTURE_TOPOGRAPHY_MICROGRAPH_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Static load cell measurement error across 1gf to 100gf range** | `<= 0.25 gf` | +/- 0.05 gf | Multi-point calibration using Class E2 certified weights on Nordson DAGE 4000Plus tester. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Shear tool clearance height accuracy over Al-Cu bond pad datum** | `4.00 um` | +/- 0.50 um | Non-contact laser displacement triangulation interferometry across 30 distinct pad locations. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Shear force repeatability (Cp/Cpk) on baseline qualified 25um Au ball bonds** | `Cpk >= 1.67` | +/- 0.10 | Statistical process control analysis on 100 consecutive destructive ball shear tests per JESD22-B116. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful completion of 5-point calibration cycle with zero deviation exceeding +/-0.25% FS, verified clearance height compliance at 4.0 um +/- 0.5 um across 30 sites without passivation scratching, formal attachment of calibration certificates signed by Quality Assurance and Metrology Lead, and signoff approval in the MES equipment tracking module.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-2011-001`  
**Title:** MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull Testing & Failure Mode Classification  
**Target Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Process Step:** Assembly & Packaging — Metrology & Quality Assurance  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP defines the destructive/non-destructive bond pull testing protocol and failure mode classification for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ ($1.0\ \text{mil}$) diameter thermosonic gold ($\text{Au}\ 99.99\%$) and ultrasonic aluminum ($\text{Al-}1\%\ \text{Si}$) wirebonds connecting $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum die pads to leadframe pins on 180nm DRAM packages, in strict compliance with MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.

---

### 2. Equipment & Tooling Setup
- **Pull Tester:** Calibrated micro-wire pull tester (e.g., Dage / Nordson series) equipped with a miniature tungsten carbide hook.
- **Hook Geometry:** Hook diameter matched to wire pitch, positioned at the center of the wire loop span (or at $H_1/H_2$ mid-span at a $90^\circ \pm 5^\circ$ pull angle perpendicular to the die surface).
- **Fixturing:** Universal vacuum chuck and mechanical leadframe clamp holding package rigid to prevent stage compliance or vibration.
- **Optics:** Stereo inspection microscope ($30\times$ to $100\times$ magnification) with coaxial ring lighting.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Sample Clamping & Alignment                              |
|    - Clamp package onto vacuum chuck at 25 °C               |
|    - Align 25 µm wire loop directly under the pull hook      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Hook Engagement & Positioning                            |
|    - Position hook at mid-span of the loop                  |
|    - Verify 90° ± 5° normal pull trajectory                 |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Controlled Pull Execution                                |
|    - Pull rate: 0.1 mm/s to 0.5 mm/s                        |
|    - Record peak destructive pull force (grams-force)       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. Optical Inspection & Failure Classification              |
|    - Classify failure site (Wire Break vs. Lift/Shear)      |
|    - Verify Pad Metal Integrity (Al 350 nm pad stack)       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

1. **Substrate Mounting & Zero Calibration:**
   - Mount the packaged DRAM die securely onto the micro-tester stage at room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Perform load cell zero-tare and auto-calibration against certified reference weights.
2. **Hook Insertion & Positioning:**
   - Under stereo optical guidance, maneuver the pull hook beneath the $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire loop.
   - Position the hook precisely at mid-span (highest loop apex) to ensure balanced load distribution between the 1st bond (ball on $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Al pad) and 2nd bond (wedge/crescent on leadframe).
   - Ensure the pull force vector is perpendicular ($90^\circ \pm 5^\circ$) to the die surface.
3. **Tensile Pull Application:**
   - Apply continuous z-axis tensile displacement at a controlled pull rate between $0.1\ \text{mm/s}$ and $0.5\ \text{mm/s}$.
   - Terminate pull automatically upon catastrophic separation; record the peak breaking force in grams-force ($\text{gf}$).
4. **Microscopic Failure Mode Classification:**
   - Examine the break location under $\ge 50\times$ optical magnification:
     - **Mode 1 (Acceptable):** Wire span break / mid-span necking (intrinsic wire tensile failure).
     - **Mode 2 (Acceptable):** Break at heel / neck directly above ball/wedge (acceptable only if peak force exceeds limit).
     - **Mode 3 (Rejectable):** Ball lift / interfacial bond detachment from the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Al pad metallization ($350\ \text{nm}$ Al layer).
     - **Mode 4 (Rejectable):** Crescent / wedge lift from the leadframe post.
     - **Mode 5 (Rejectable / Critical):** Die pad cratering (silicon or dielectric tear-out beneath pad).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Evaluation Method | Target Specification | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Wire Pull Force ($25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire)** | Micro-tester load cell | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{grams-force}\ (\text{gf})$ |
| **Failure Mode Yield** | Optical stereo inspection ($50\times$) | $100\%$ Wire Span Break (Zero interfacial bond lifts) | $\%$ |
| **Bond Pad Visual Cratering / Delamination** | Post-pull optical check on $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pad | $0$ (No dielectric/silicon pull-out) | Count |
| **Al Pad Metallization Thickness Integrity** | Cross-section / PVD reference baseline | $350 \pm 5\%$ | $\text{nm}$ |

---

### 5. Literature Sources & Citations
- **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging](./docs)**:
  - Wire specification: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%\ \text{Au}$ and $\text{Al-}1\%\ \text{Si}$ wire.
  - Die bond pad dimension: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
  - Pull strength threshold: MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 minimum force requirement $\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire.
  - Failure criterion: Failure must occur in the wire span, not at the bond interface.
- **[Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects](./docs)**:
  - Metal-1 bond pad metallization thickness: $350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$ Al deposited by magnetron sputtering.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Wire pull testing according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 on 25 um Au thermosonic wire bonds must account for geometric hook positioning along the 100 um x 100 um Al pad to leadframe pin loop. If the pull hook is not placed at mid-span or corrected via resolution-of-forces trigonometry, apparent breaking force will drift, causing false rejection or masking interfacial heel microcracking.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Failure mode classification must strictly separate mid-span neck/wire fracture (acceptable failure mode) from pad-metallization peel or cratering of underlying dielectric under the 100 um x 100 um Al pad. In 180nm CMOS BEOL, excessive ultrasonic power (60 kHz, >100 mW) risks micro-cracking ILD oxide (SiO2/low-k) beneath the bond pad, which is unmasked during pull testing as pad lift-off.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: 25 um 99.99% high-purity gold wire spool quality must adhere to ASTM F72 with certified tensile elongation (2-6%) and break load limits (>7.0 gf). Lot-to-lot variance in dopants (e.g. Be or Ca grain stabilizers) shifts recrystallization temperature at the heat-affected zone (HAZ), directly causing premature neck-break failures.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Statistical process control requires continuous verification of Cpk >= 1.67 for wire pull strength across all 180nm DRAM package qualification lots, ensuring destructive sample pulling (Method 2011 Condition D) does not exhaust prototype MPW package inventory while maintaining MIL-PRF-38535 Class Q/V compliance.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial Ball Lift / Pad Cratering: Ball separates cleanly from the 100 um Al pad or fractures underlying BEOL dielectric due to inadequate intermetallic compound (Au-Al IMC) growth or excessive acoustic stress.
1. Heel/Neck Break at HAZ: Wire snaps at the heat-affected zone immediately above the gold ball prior to reaching the minimum 4.0 gf pull threshold, driven by grain boundary embrittlement or improper EFO ball formation.
1. Leadframe Crescent/Wedge Lift: Inadequate stitch bond adherence to Ag-plated leadframe pin under low stage temperature (<150°C) or contaminated leadframe plating causing zero-force detachment.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-2-01` | **Destructive Wire Pull Strength Metrology via MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Condition D** | Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Bondtester equipped with 0-100 gf calibrated load cell (hook tip radius 25 um, resolution 0.01 gf) and stereomicroscope (50x-100x) | 1. Position test hook under wire span at center position (or 1/3 to 1/2 span length as defined by geometry). 2. Align hook perpendicular to wire loop plane to eliminate angular side-loading. 3. Initiate motorized Z-axis pull test at a controlled pull speed of 1000 um/s until wire rupture occurs. 4. Record peak breaking load in grams-force (gf) and optical coordinate. 5. Repeat across sample size of N = 40 wires per package lot. | `Peak pull strength must be >= 4.0 gf for every individual 25 um Au wire tested (mean >= 7.5 gf with Cpk >= 1.67 across lot). Any pull value < 4.0 gf constitutes an immediate lot failure.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-2-02` | **Wire Bond Failure Mode Optical Metrology and SEM/EDX Intermetallic Analysis** | High-resolution optical inspection microscope (up to 1000x) and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM) with EDX elemental mapping | 1. Inspect all 40 rupture sites under optical microscopy at 100x magnification. 2. Categorize failure modes according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 classifications: Mode 1 (Die bond lift), Mode 2 (Wire break at neck/HAZ), Mode 3 (Wire break in span), Mode 4 (Lead bond/wedge lift), Mode 5 (Pad cratering / dielectric lift). 3. Transfer representative samples to FE-SEM/EDX at 15 kV acceleration voltage to inspect pad surface for remnant Au-Al intermetallic phase coverage (Au4Al, Au5Al2). | `>= 95% of failures must be Mode 3 (mid-span break) or Mode 2 (neck break above 4.0 gf). 0% occurrence permitted for Mode 1 (pad lift) and Mode 5 (pad cratering). Interfacial IMC coverage on pad footprint must exceed 80% area.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10,000 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (ESD safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Cleanroom lab coat / ESD smock, Point-of-use micro-tweezers and wire fragment containment sharps container
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For chemical splash of IPA/Acetone, flush affected eyes or skin at nearest eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, relocate personnel to fresh air immediately. For fine gold wire puncture wounds, cleanse immediately with antiseptic and remove foreign wire fragments under medical supervision.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized exhaust sniffer hood or certified laminar flow wet bench with face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s) during solvent wipe and cleaning steps.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solvent wipes and rinse flushes must be disposed of in dedicated hazardous organic solvent carboys. Gold wire clippings collected in dedicated precious metal recovery containers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Electronic Grade / VLSI | `99.9%` |
| **Acetone** | `67-64-1` | Semiconductor Grade | `99.5%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 | `>= 99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-bonded DRAM leadframe assemblies directly emerging from thermosonic wire bonder, free of particulate contamination, organic flux, and moisture.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Pull-tested and failure-classified packages cleared of detached micro-wire fragments, inspected and logged for mold encapsulation / ceramic hermetic seal.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding atmospheric Q-time induces ambient moisture adsorption and accelerated atmospheric oxidation/corrosion of exposed 100 um Al pad periphery and Ag-plated leadframes, confounding failure mode classification and degrading bond shear integrity prior to encapsulation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full mechanical validation and failure mode classification of 25 um Au thermosonic wire bonds on 180nm DRAM chip leadframes per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011, establishing robust process margins with pull strengths >= 4.0 gf and zero dielectric cratering.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MIL_STD_883_Method2011_Wire_Pull_Raw_Data.csv`
- [ ] `Wire_Bond_Failure_Mode_Distribution_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `SEM_EDX_IMC_Pad_Cratering_Micrograph.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Minimum Individual Destructive Wire Pull Strength** | `>= 4.0 gf` | +/- 0.05 gf gauge measurement error | Calibrated automated wire pull tester (Dage 4000Plus / Nordson) per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Condition D |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Process Capability Index (Cpk) of Wire Pull Strength** | `>= 1.67` | +/- 0.02 | Statistical process analysis of pull force distribution over N=40 wire sample size |

critics.systems_engineer: Wire pull testing according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 on 25 um Au thermosonic wire bonds must account for geometric hook positioning along the 100 um x 100 um Al pad to leadframe pin loop. If the pull hook is not placed at mid-span or corrected via resolution-of-forces trigonometry, apparent breaking force will drift, causing false rejection or masking interfacial heel microcracking.
critics.domain_expert: Failure mode classification must strictly separate mid-span neck/wire fracture (acceptable failure mode) from pad-metallization peel or cratering of underlying dielectric under the 100 um x 100 um Al pad. In 180nm CMOS BEOL, excessive ultrasonic power (60 kHz, >100 mW) risks micro-cracking ILD oxide (SiO2/low-k) beneath the bond pad, which is unmasked during pull testing as pad lift-off.
critics.supply_chain: 25 um 99.99% high-purity gold wire spool quality must adhere to ASTM F72 with certified tensile elongation (2-6%) and break load limits (>7.0 gf). Lot-to-lot variance in dopants (e.g. Be or Ca grain stabilizers) shifts recrystallization temperature at the heat-affected zone (HAZ), directly causing premature neck-break failures.
critics.laya_pm: Statistical process control requires continuous verification of Cpk >= 1.67 for wire pull strength across all 180nm DRAM package qualification lots, ensuring destructive sample pulling (Method 2011 Condition D) does not exhaust prototype MPW package inventory while maintaining MIL-PRF-38535 Class Q/V compliance.
critical_failure_modes: Interfacial Ball Lift / Pad Cratering: Ball separates cleanly from the 100 um Al pad or fractures underlying BEOL dielectric due to inadequate intermetallic compound (Au-Al IMC) growth or excessive acoustic stress.

Heel/Neck Break at HAZ: Wire snaps at the heat-affected zone immediately above the gold ball prior to reaching the minimum 4.0 gf pull threshold, driven by grain boundary embrittlement or improper EFO ball formation.
Leadframe Crescent/Wedge Lift: Inadequate stitch bond adherence to Ag-plated leadframe pin under low stage temperature (<150°C) or contaminated leadframe plating causing zero-force detachment.

testcases.title: Destructive Wire Pull Strength Metrology via MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Condition D
testcases.instrumentation: Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Bondtester equipped with 0-100 gf calibrated load cell (hook tip radius 25 um, resolution 0.01 gf) and stereomicroscope (50x-100x)
testcases.pre_conditions: DRAM packaging assembly completed: 180nm DRAM dies attached via Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min; 25 um 99.99% Au wires bonded from 100 um x 100 um Al pads to DIP/QFN leadframe pins. Leadframe clamped rigidly into test fixture at 25°C ambient.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position test hook under wire span at center position (or 1/3 to 1/2 span length as defined by geometry). 2. Align hook perpendicular to wire loop plane to eliminate angular side-loading. 3. Initiate motorized Z-axis pull test at a controlled pull speed of 1000 um/s until wire rupture occurs. 4. Record peak breaking load in grams-force (gf) and optical coordinate. 5. Repeat across sample size of N = 40 wires per package lot.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Peak pull strength must be >= 4.0 gf for every individual 25 um Au wire tested (mean >= 7.5 gf with Cpk >= 1.67 across lot). Any pull value < 4.0 gf constitutes an immediate lot failure.

testcases.title: Wire Bond Failure Mode Optical Metrology and SEM/EDX Intermetallic Analysis
testcases.instrumentation: High-resolution optical inspection microscope (up to 1000x) and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM) with EDX elemental mapping
testcases.pre_conditions: Destructive pull test TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-2-01 executed with rupture sites preserved without mechanical contact or swab damage.
testcases.procedure: 1. Inspect all 40 rupture sites under optical microscopy at 100x magnification. 2. Categorize failure modes according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 classifications: Mode 1 (Die bond lift), Mode 2 (Wire break at neck/HAZ), Mode 3 (Wire break in span), Mode 4 (Lead bond/wedge lift), Mode 5 (Pad cratering / dielectric lift). 3. Transfer representative samples to FE-SEM/EDX at 15 kV acceleration voltage to inspect pad surface for remnant Au-Al intermetallic phase coverage (Au4Al, Au5Al2).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: >= 95% of failures must be Mode 3 (mid-span break) or Mode 2 (neck break above 4.0 gf). 0% occurrence permitted for Mode 1 (pad lift) and Mode 5 (pad cratering). Interfacial IMC coverage on pad footprint must exceed 80% area.

In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, relocate personnel to fresh air immediately. ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Solvent wipes and rinse flushes must be disposed of in dedicated hazardous organic solvent carboys. Gold wire clippings collected in dedicated precious metal recovery containers.

q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Pull-tested and failure-classified packages cleared of detached micro-wire fragments, inspected and logged for mold encapsulation / ceramic hermetic seal.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): JESD22-B116 Ball Shear Strength Metrology & Intermetallic Coverage Inspection

## Document Metadata
- **SOP ID**: `SOP-PKG-MET-B116-01`
- **Revision**: 1.0
- **Chip Target**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)
- **Standard**: JEDEC JESD22-B116 / Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Reference
- **Action Type**: Buy / Execution SOP

---

## 1. Process Flowchart

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Sample Clamping and   │
│       Fixturing        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Shear Tool Alignment  │
│      and Standoff      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Ball Shear Metrology  │
│    per JESD22-B116     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Au Ball Selective    │
│     Chemical Etch      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Optical or SEM IMC   │
│  Coverage Inspection   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acceptance Criteria   │
│      Verification      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

### Step 1: Workpiece Clamping & Vacuum Fixturing
1. Mount the DRAM assembly (die attached to ceramic DIP/QFN leadframe with silver-filled epoxy cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 min) onto the precision vacuum shear fixture stage.
2. Engage stage vacuum ($P_{\text{vac}} \ge 70\text{ kPa}$) and tighten mechanical edge clamps to ensure zero sample deflection or stage wobble during shearing.

### Step 2: Shear Tool Setup & Standoff Calibration
1. Install a calibrated tungsten carbide / hardened steel shear chisel tool matching wire bond dimensions (chisel width: $100\ \mu\text{m}$ to $125\ \mu\text{m}$, aligned with the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad aperture).
2. Perform touch-down zero-point calibration on the bare die passivation / pad surface adjacent to the thermosonic ball bond.
3. Set the shear tool clearance height (standoff) strictly per JESD22-B116 guidelines:
   - Tool standoff height: $3.0\ \mu\text{m}$ to $5.0\ \mu\text{m}$ above the pad surface (less than 10% of the deformed ball height, ensuring no tool contact with the $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$ aluminum metallization layer).
4. Set shear tool lateral approach speed to $50\ \mu\text{m/s}$ to $100\ \mu\text{m/s}$.

### Step 3: Ball Shear Strength Metrology (JESD22-B116)
1. Position the shear tool flat edge perpendicular to the thermosonic $25\ \mu\text{m}$ Au ball.
2. Execute the shear stroke until interfacial fracture or ball shear separation occurs.
3. Record peak shear force in grams-force ($\text{gf}$) via the high-resolution load cell.
4. Record failure mode:
   - **Mode 1**: Shear through gold ball (acceptable ductile gold shear).
   - **Mode 2**: Intermetallic compound (IMC) interface fracture.
   - **Mode 3**: Pad metallization peeling / cratering (defect / reject).

### Step 4: Selective Wet Chemical Etch for IMC Inspection
1. For companion bond samples designated for intermetallic coverage assessment, selectively remove unreacted gold using a chemical potassium iodide / iodine ($\text{KI} / \text{I}_2$) solution or aqua regia variant that selectively dissolves bulk Au without attacking the $\text{Au-Al}$ intermetallic layers ($\text{Au}_4\text{Al}$, $\text{Au}_5\text{Al}_2$) or the underlying $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Al pad.
2. Rinse thoroughly with deionized (DI) water ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$) and blow dry with filtered nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$).

### Step 5: Intermetallic Coverage Area Metrology
1. Inspect the footprint under high-resolution optical metrology microscope ($\ge 1000\times$) or FE-SEM.
2. Image and measure the total bonded footprint area and the intermetallic coverage zone using calibrated digital planimetry.
3. Compute the IMC coverage percentage:
   $$\text{IMC Coverage (\%)} = \left(\frac{\text{Area}_{\text{IMC}}}{\text{Area}_{\text{bonded footprint}}}\right) \times 100\%$$

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
Target Parameters & Acceptance Thresholds
                      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                      │███████████████████████         │
      IMC Coverage Min┤███████████████████████         │
                      │░░░░░░                          │
       Min Shear Force┤░░░░░░                          │
    Au Wire Dia (25um)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                       │
                      │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                       │
    Bond Height Z-step┤▓▓▓                             │
                      │▓▓▓                             │
Al Pad (100um x 100um)┤████████████████████████████████│
                      │████████████████████████████████│
                      └┬───────┬───────┬──────┬───────┬┘
                       0      25      50     75     100 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Unit | Target / Specification Threshold | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Ball Shear Strength** | grams-force ($\text{gf}$) | $\ge 15.0\ \text{gf}$ (with zero cratering; significantly exceeding the Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 wire pull lower limit of $4.0\ \text{gf}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire) | JESD22-B116 Precision Load Cell |
| **Intermetallic Coverage (IMC)** | $\%$ | $\ge 70.0\%$ of total bonded ball footprint area | Optical / FE-SEM Planimetry post-etch |
| **Shear Tool Standoff Height** | $\mu\text{m}$ | $3.0\ \mu\text{m}$ to $5.0\ \mu\text{m}$ above Al pad metallization | Touch-down Optical / Contact Z-encoder |
| **Substrate/Pad Structural Integrity** | $\%$ | $0.0\%$ pad peeling, dielectric micro-cracking, or Si cratering | Post-shear SEM / Optical Darkfield Inspection |

---

## 4. Context References & Verification
- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - Thermosonic gold ball bonding using $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire onto $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads at $150^\circ\text{C}$ transducer pulse ($60\text{ kHz}, 50\text{--}100\text{ mW}, 20\text{--}30\text{ ms}$).
  - Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 wire pull strength specification ($\ge 4.0\ \text{gf}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire).
  - Die attach using silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 minutes.
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - Aluminum metallization target thickness of $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$ and sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$, setting the physical boundaries for tool standoff calibration to avoid pad gouging.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: DRC/LVS rule decks must run clean via KLayout/Magic/OpenLane with zero design rule errors. Antenna ratio rules (< 250:1) and substrate tap density checks must pass before GDSII reticle handoff to commercial foundry.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: 3D Crown capacitor ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 (ZAZ) stack must achieve equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) <= 0.8 nm and leakage current < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V. CMP dishing on M1/M2 tungsten/copper features must hold < 15 nm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Commercial foundry MPW (Multi-Project Wafer) shuttle submission has an unmovable tapeout window; GDSII/OASIS files must freeze 21 days prior. Sourced via open-source or commercial shuttle program under standard NDA.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 60-120 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: CRITICAL (A single DRC rule deck discrepancy or LVS short-circuit ruins the entire multi-thousand dollar commercial shuttle run and incurs a 4-6 month spin delay).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. DRC/LVS hierarchy discrepancy causing undetected metal-to-metal bridging or floating substrate tap.
1. ALD precursor pulse/purge saturation drift inducing pinhole dielectric breakdown in crown capacitor array.
1. Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) over-polish causing severe interconnect erosion and open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-3-01` | **Automated DRC/LVS Golden Rule Deck Physical Sign-Off** | KLayout / Magic / Pegasus Industrial Physical Verification Batch Engine | 1. Run 180nm DRC rule deck across 100% of mask layers (well, diffusion, poly, contact, M1-M3, pad). 2. Execute Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) netlist extraction against golden SPICE schematic. 3. Verify antenna ratio violations (< 250:1) and substrate noise isolation guard rings. | `DRC clean: 0 violations (Pass); LVS netlist match: 100% topological equivalence with 0 discrepancy (Pass).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-2-3-3-02` | **3D Crown Capacitor High-k Dielectric TEM & C-V Metrology** | Field-Emission TEM (FEI/Thermo Fisher) & High-Frequency C-V Parameter Analyzer (Keysight B1500A) | 1. Prepare FIB lamella cross-section through 3D crown capacitor trench structure. 2. Measure physical film thickness and step coverage across bottom, sidewall, and top crown lip via HR-TEM. 3. Perform high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V sweep to extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and dielectric breakdown voltage. | `ALD step coverage >= 95% (Pass); EOT <= 0.8 nm (Pass); Dielectric leakage < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom bunny suit with conductive ESD booties, Pyrophoric precursor handling apron and dual-layer fluoropolymer gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and UV-blocking safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Pyrophoric precursor emergency: TMA spontaneously ignites upon contact with air or moisture! Do NOT use water on metal alkyl fires. Smother immediately with dry vermiculite, dry sand, or Class D metal fire extinguisher. In case of ozone inhalation, move patient to fresh air immediately and administer supplemental oxygen.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Ultra-high vacuum ALD exhaust manifold connected to dedicated point-of-use thermal decomposition burn-box and wet chemical scrubber. Continuous gas leak detection monitors for TMA/TEMAZ and ozone.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent ALD bubbler purging into mineral oil bubblers with inert argon ballast. CMP slurry effluent collected in settling basin, flocculated with alum, and neutralized to pH 6.5-8.0.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trimethylaluminum (TMA)** | `75-24-1` | Electronic Grade (99.999% trace metals) | `Pyrophoric liquid ALD precursor` |
| **Tetrakis(ethylmethylamino)zirconium (TEMAZ)** | `175923-04-3` | High-purity ALD grade | `Liquid precursor for ZrO2 dielectric` |
| **Ozone (O3)** | `10028-15-6` | Generated in-situ from UHP O2 | `15-20 wt% in O2 carrier gas (Strong Oxidizer)` |
| **Silica / Ceria CMP Slurry** | `1344-28-1` | Semiconductor Colloidal CMP grade | `15-30 wt% colloidal abrasive slurry` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched 3D crown capacitor trench structure post-DHF strip, completely free of native oxide.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Uniform ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 high-k dielectric stack with TiN top electrode encapsulation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Air exposure exceeding 20 minutes allows uncontrolled spontaneous SiO2 interfacial layer regrowth (> 0.4 nm), which severely increases Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and drastically degrades bitcell storage capacitance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of JESD22-B116 Ball Shear Strength Metrology & Intermetallic Coverage Inspection: PDK setup, physical verification rule decks, and full-chip GDSII layouts pass 100% DRC/LVS sign-off and satisfy foundry commercial tapeout design rules.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `Commercial_MPW_Tapeout_GDSII_OASIS_Archive.tar.gz`

| `ASSERT-02` | **Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) Netlist Equivalence** | `100% match` | Zero net/port mismatches, zero floating pins | Hierarchical LVS extraction against golden SPICE schematic |
| `ASSERT-03` | **3D Crown Capacitor ALD Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | `<= 0.80 nm` | +/- 0.05 nm across wafer | High-frequency 1 MHz C-V accumulation capacitance metrology |

# Standard Operating Procedure: MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull & Ball Shear Metrology Validation

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: DRC/LVS rule decks must run clean via KLayout/Magic/OpenLane with zero design rule errors. Antenna ratio rules (< 250:1) and substrate tap density checks must pass before GDSII reticle handoff to commercial foundry.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: 3D Crown capacitor ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 (ZAZ) stack must achieve equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) <= 0.8 nm and leakage current < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V. CMP dishing on M1/M2 tungsten/copper features must hold < 15 nm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Commercial foundry MPW (Multi-Project Wafer) shuttle submission has an unmovable tapeout window; GDSII/OASIS files must freeze 21 days prior. Sourced via open-source or commercial shuttle program under standard NDA.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 60-120 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: CRITICAL (A single DRC rule deck discrepancy or LVS short-circuit ruins the entire multi-thousand dollar commercial shuttle run and incurs a 4-6 month spin delay).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. DRC/LVS hierarchy discrepancy causing undetected metal-to-metal bridging or floating substrate tap.
1. ALD precursor pulse/purge saturation drift inducing pinhole dielectric breakdown in crown capacitor array.
1. Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) over-polish causing severe interconnect erosion and open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-01` | **Automated DRC/LVS Golden Rule Deck Physical Sign-Off** | KLayout / Magic / Pegasus Industrial Physical Verification Batch Engine | 1. Run 180nm DRC rule deck across 100% of mask layers (well, diffusion, poly, contact, M1-M3, pad). 2. Execute Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) netlist extraction against golden SPICE schematic. 3. Verify antenna ratio violations (< 250:1) and substrate noise isolation guard rings. | `DRC clean: 0 violations (Pass); LVS netlist match: 100% topological equivalence with 0 discrepancy (Pass).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-02` | **3D Crown Capacitor High-k Dielectric TEM & C-V Metrology** | Field-Emission TEM (FEI/Thermo Fisher) & High-Frequency C-V Parameter Analyzer (Keysight B1500A) | 1. Prepare FIB lamella cross-section through 3D crown capacitor trench structure. 2. Measure physical film thickness and step coverage across bottom, sidewall, and top crown lip via HR-TEM. 3. Perform high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V sweep to extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and dielectric breakdown voltage. | `ALD step coverage >= 95% (Pass); EOT <= 0.8 nm (Pass); Dielectric leakage < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom bunny suit with conductive ESD booties, Pyrophoric precursor handling apron and dual-layer fluoropolymer gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and UV-blocking safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Pyrophoric precursor emergency: TMA spontaneously ignites upon contact with air or moisture! Do NOT use water on metal alkyl fires. Smother immediately with dry vermiculite, dry sand, or Class D metal fire extinguisher. In case of ozone inhalation, move patient to fresh air immediately and administer supplemental oxygen.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Ultra-high vacuum ALD exhaust manifold connected to dedicated point-of-use thermal decomposition burn-box and wet chemical scrubber. Continuous gas leak detection monitors for TMA/TEMAZ and ozone.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent ALD bubbler purging into mineral oil bubblers with inert argon ballast. CMP slurry effluent collected in settling basin, flocculated with alum, and neutralized to pH 6.5-8.0.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trimethylaluminum (TMA)** | `75-24-1` | Electronic Grade (99.999% trace metals) | `Pyrophoric liquid ALD precursor` |
| **Tetrakis(ethylmethylamino)zirconium (TEMAZ)** | `175923-04-3` | High-purity ALD grade | `Liquid precursor for ZrO2 dielectric` |
| **Ozone (O3)** | `10028-15-6` | Generated in-situ from UHP O2 | `15-20 wt% in O2 carrier gas (Strong Oxidizer)` |
| **Silica / Ceria CMP Slurry** | `1344-28-1` | Semiconductor Colloidal CMP grade | `15-30 wt% colloidal abrasive slurry` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched 3D crown capacitor trench structure post-DHF strip, completely free of native oxide.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Uniform ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 high-k dielectric stack with TiN top electrode encapsulation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Air exposure exceeding 20 minutes allows uncontrolled spontaneous SiO2 interfacial layer regrowth (> 0.4 nm), which severely increases Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and drastically degrades bitcell storage capacitance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull & Ball Shear Metrology Validation: PDK setup, physical verification rule decks, and full-chip GDSII layouts pass 100% DRC/LVS sign-off and satisfy foundry commercial tapeout design rules.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Golden_180nm_PDK_DRC_LVS_Signoff_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Commercial_MPW_Tapeout_GDSII_OASIS_Archive.tar.gz`
- [ ] `ALD_3D_Crown_TEM_StepCoverage_Analysis.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Foundry Design Rule Check (DRC) Violations** | `0 violations` | Zero tolerance across full chip and seal ring | Automated batch DRC run using KLayout / Pegasus Golden Rule Deck |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) Netlist Equivalence** | `100% match` | Zero net/port mismatches, zero floating pins | Hierarchical LVS extraction against golden SPICE schematic |
| `ASSERT-03` | **3D Crown Capacitor ALD Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | `<= 0.80 nm` | +/- 0.05 nm across wafer | High-frequency 1 MHz C-V accumulation capacitance metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% clean DRC/LVS verification logs signed off by lead tapeout architect; checksum of streamed GDSII package validated against foundry MPW shuttle intake submission portal.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Micro-Hook Pull Testing Setup and Fixture Calibration
**Module:** BEOL Packaging & Assembly > MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Metrology Validation  
**Target:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) — 25 µm Au Wire Bonds on 100 µm × 100 µm Al Pads  

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Tool Calibration &   │
│      5.0 gf Tare       │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Die Vacuum Clamping   │
│   & Fixture Leveling   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Micro-Hook Alignment  │
│  under 25 um Au Wire   │
│          Span          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Destructive Wire    │
│     Pull at 90 deg     │
│     Normal Vector      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Pass/Fail Screening:  │
│    Force >= 4.0 gf     │
│    Mid-Span Break      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

#### Step 1: Load Cell & Sensor Tare Calibration
- Mount a certified miniature tension load cell (rated full-scale: $10.0\text{ gf}$).
- Apply a precision calibration reference mass ($5.000\text{ gf} \pm 0.010\text{ gf}$) to the micro-hook fixture along the vertical Z-axis.
- Tare electronic offset to $0.000\text{ gf}$; confirm measurement linearity error $\le \pm 0.05\text{ gf}$.

#### Step 2: Fixture Clamping & Substrate Planarity Alignment
- Position the leadframe carrier containing the bonded 180nm DRAM chip onto the vacuum clamping chuck.
- Engage vacuum chuck draw ($\ge 60\text{ kPa}$) to eliminate package mechanical vibration and spring compliance.
- Use dual-axis leveling dial/optical depth sensor to verify substrate coplanarity across the die boundary to within $< 10\ \mu\text{m}$ height deviation.

#### Step 3: Automated Micro-Hook Positioning
- Calibrate the optical vision system focusing on the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pad and corresponding leadframe post.
- Actuate the micro-hook ($30\ \mu\text{m}$ inner hook radius) underneath the $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire span.
- Center the micro-hook at loop apex or mid-span ($50\% \pm 5\%$ distance between ball neck and stitch bond) at a pull angle of $90^\circ \pm 5^\circ$ normal to the leadframe plane.

#### Step 4: Destructive Wire Pull Execution & Data Acquisition
- Initiate automated vertical Z-axis pull at a constant displacement speed of $1.0\text{ mm/s}$.
- Sample force profile dynamically until wire rupture occurs.
- Automatically log the peak pull force ($F_{\text{pull}}$ in grams-force) and microscopic post-break image.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Load Cell Full Scale┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
  Measured Wire Pull┤███████████████████████           │
                    │███████████████████████           │
   MIL-STD Threshold┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                    │
                    │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                    │
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                    0.0     2.5      5.0     7.5   10.0 
```

| Metric ID | Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Verification Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-01** | Minimum Wire Pull Breaking Force | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 |
| **AC-02** | Wire Failure Break Mode | $100\%$ Wire Span / Mid-Loop Break ($0\%$ Ball Lift / Pad Peel) | Categorical / Failure Mode Class | Visual/Optical AOI |
| **AC-03** | Aluminum Bond Pad Integrity | Zero pad lift, cratering, or dielectric tear-out on the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Al pad | Defect Count | Post-test Optical Inspection |
| **AC-04** | Fixture Pull Angle Alignment | $90.0 \pm 5.0$ | Degrees ($^\circ$) | Vision Motion System |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Local Knowledge Persistence

- **Primary Metrology & Packaging Reference**:  
  *Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*  
  - Wire specification: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire on $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.
  - Pull force threshold: MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 requirement: pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire, requiring failure to occur in the wire span rather than at the bond interface.
- **Interconnect Metallization Reference**:  
  *Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects*  
  - Validates bond pad top metal layer criteria ($350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$ aluminum alloy with $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$).

> [!NOTE]
> Micro-knowledge for this procedure has been persisted in [`docs/knowledge/sop_micro_hook_pull_testing.md`](./docs/knowledge/sop_micro_hook_pull_testing.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated micro-hook pull testing for 180nm DRAM thermosonic 25um Au wirebonds requires strict kinematic coupling and 3-axis motion stage decoupling to eliminate lateral shear vectors during hook engagement. A non-calibrated Z-axis compliance or hook pitch misalignment exceeding 5 degrees off normal induces artificial bending moments, distorting true rupture forces and yielding false failure mode classifications.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 Condition D, hook placement must maintain a strict loop apex centering (d/2 +/- 10% span) to ensure uniform tension distribution between the ball neck and wedge bond. The pull rate must be maintained at a steady 1.0 mm/s; instantaneous hook jerk from closed-loop PID overshoot can precipitate premature heel tears below the 3.0 gf statistical threshold for 1.0 mil gold wire.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring precision-etched tungsten carbide or high-stiffness phosphor-bronze micro-hooks with calibrated tip radii (r = 15-25 um) demands dual-sourcing to counter long lead times and high attrition from hook bending. Calibration weights (0.5 gf to 100 gf class E2/F1) must possess traceable NVLAP/NIST certifications to validate optical load cell resolution down to 0.01 gf.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Acquisition and integration of an automated bond pull tester must adhere to a strict 6-week installation qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) gate. Delays in standardizing the multi-leadframe clamp fixture will halt downstream BEOL reliability screening and delay qualification lot release for open-source DRAM packaging.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Hook slipping along the wire loop toward the first bond (neck) or second bond (stitch), producing acute peel stress and artificially skewed low pull forces.
1. Mechanical fixture resonance or load-cell drift exceeding 0.05 gf during high-speed multi-pin indexing, leading to false rejects.
1. Hook tip deformation or burr accumulation causing micro-notching and premature wire severed failure during hook positioning.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-1-01` | **Automated Micro-Hook Load Cell Static Linearity and Gage Repeatability Calibration** | Automated Micro-Bond Tester (Nordson Dage 4000Plus or XYZTEC Condor Sigma) equipped with 100 gf load cartridge, NIST-traceable Class E2 precision calibration mass set (1.000 gf, 5.000 gf, 10.000 gf), Anti-vibration air-bearing table. | 1. Mount the 100 gf load cartridge and zero the digital signal processor. 2. Suspend calibrated NIST masses (1.000 gf, 5.000 gf, 10.000 gf) sequentially along the vertical axis via fixture-guided monofilament. 3. Record raw transducer voltage and converted gram-force across 10 discrete loading/unloading cycles per mass. 4. Compute linearity error, hysteresis, and Gage R&R percentage. | `Static linearity error <= +/- 0.1% of full scale (+/- 0.10 gf). Gage R&R <= 5.0% across 30 repeated load trials. Load cell drift <= 0.02 gf over 30 minutes continuous hold.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-1-02` | **MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Automated Hook Positioning and Dynamic Pull Validation** | Automated Wire Pull Metrology Station with machine vision pattern recognition, 20 um radius tungsten micro-hook, calibrated DRAM 180nm leadframe clamp fixture. | 1. Program pattern recognition to automatically locate bond pads and leadframe fingers across all 32 pins. 2. Auto-target hook descent to loop apex (0.50 +/- 0.05 span distance) with hook landing clearance of 15 um above substrate. 3. Execute vertical pull at a constant rate of 1.0 mm/s until wire rupture occurs. 4. Record peak force (gf) and auto-classify failure code (Code 1: Neck break, Code 2: Mid-span rupture, Code 3: Stitch break, Code 4: Ball lift). | `Mean pull force >= 6.0 gf with zero bonds failing below 3.0 gf across 32 pins. Hook landing spatial accuracy <= +/- 3.0 um in X/Y axes relative to programmed apex. 100% of failures must register as Code 1 or Code 2 (zero interfacial ball lifts allowed).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 1000 compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, 4 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat, ESD wrist strap connected to 1 MOhm workstation ground
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with IPA, rinse thoroughly with clean running water for 15 minutes. In case of eye contact, flush eyes at emergency eye-wash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. If inhaled vapors cause dizziness, remove victim to fresh air. Mechanical pinch hazards from automated stages: shut down emergency stop (E-stop) immediately before attending to injured personnel.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted in standard semiconductor cleanroom bay with recirculating laminar air flow (HEPA filtered, min 90 FPM face velocity). IPA wipe-down of stage fixtures requires local chemical exhaust or laminar downdraft table.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be deposited into closed, airtight, grounded, flame-resistant flammable waste bins. Severed micro-wire remnants (gold) collected in dedicated sealed ESD sharps containers for precious metal scrap recycling.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA) for fixture degreasing** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / MOS) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-wirebonding thermosonic Au ball and wedge bonds on Al-0.5%Cu DRAM pads and Ag-plated leadframe fingers, free of organic contamination, flux residues, and mechanical pad cratering.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Destructively or non-destructively pull-tested wirebonded leadframe with documented rupture topography, categorized fracture interfaces, and zero metallic debris on active DRAM die circuitry.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits causes atmospheric moisture and sulfur adsorption on exposed Ag-plated leadframe fingers and Al-Cu bond pad margins, leading to micro-galvanic corrosion and skewing interfacial bond shear/pull adhesion measurements.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full hardware installation, stage calibration, and analytical verification of the automated micro-hook wire pull tester meeting MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 requirements for 180nm open-source DRAM 25um gold wirebonds.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `micro_hook_stage_calibration_report.pdf`
- [ ] `dram_180nm_wirepull_raw_dataset.csv`
- [ ] `fracture_interface_optical_micrographs.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Load cell vertical calibration accuracy across full 0-100 gf range** | `0.05 gf` | +/- 0.02 gf | Multi-point calibration using certified NIST Class E2 micro-weights at 1.0 gf, 5.0 gf, and 10.0 gf |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Stage micro-hook automated apex centering alignment accuracy** | `0.0 um` | +/- 2.5 um | Automated machine vision optical pattern recognition verified against high-resolution calibrated reticle |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Thermosonic 25um Au wire minimum destructive pull strength threshold** | `7.5 gf` | >= 3.0 gf minimum absolute cutoff | Destructive micro-hook pull test at 1.0 mm/s pull rate per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful completion of 100 consecutive automated micro-hook pull cycles on standard qualification test coupons with Gage R&R <= 5%, zero load-cell overshoots, and formal engineering approval of the signed calibration certificate.

The pull rate must be maintained at a steady 1.0 mm/s; instantaneous hook jerk from closed-loop PID overshoot can precipitate premature heel tears below the 3.0 gf statistical threshold for 1.0 mil gold wire.
critics.supply_chain: Procuring precision-etched tungsten carbide or high-stiffness phosphor-bronze micro-hooks with calibrated tip radii (r = 15-25 um) demands dual-sourcing to counter long lead times and high attrition from hook bending. Calibration weights (0.5 gf to 100 gf class E2/F1) must possess traceable NVLAP/NIST certifications to validate optical load cell resolution down to 0.01 gf.
critics.laya_pm: Acquisition and integration of an automated bond pull tester must adhere to a strict 6-week installation qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) gate. Delays in standardizing the multi-leadframe clamp fixture will halt downstream BEOL reliability screening and delay qualification lot release for open-source DRAM packaging.
critical_failure_modes: Hook slipping along the wire loop toward the first bond (neck) or second bond (stitch), producing acute peel stress and artificially skewed low pull forces.
Mechanical fixture resonance or load-cell drift exceeding 0.05 gf during high-speed multi-pin indexing, leading to false rejects.
Hook tip deformation or burr accumulation causing micro-notching and premature wire severed failure during hook positioning.

testcases.title: Automated Micro-Hook Load Cell Static Linearity and Gage Repeatability Calibration
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Micro-Bond Tester (Nordson Dage 4000Plus or XYZTEC Condor Sigma) equipped with 100 gf load cartridge, NIST-traceable Class E2 precision calibration mass set (1.000 gf, 5.000 gf, 10.000 gf), Anti-vibration air-bearing table.
testcases.pre_conditions: Tester powered on and thermally stabilized for >= 60 minutes in Class 1000 cleanroom at 22 +/- 1 deg C and 45 +/- 5% RH. Anti-vibration table leveled to within 0.1 degrees.
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount the 100 gf load cartridge and zero the digital signal processor. 2. Suspend calibrated NIST masses (1.000 gf, 5.000 gf, 10.000 gf) sequentially along the vertical axis via fixture-guided monofilament. 3. Record raw transducer voltage and converted gram-force across 10 discrete loading/unloading cycles per mass. 4. Compute linearity error, hysteresis, and Gage R&R percentage.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Static linearity error <= +/- 0.1% of full scale (+/- 0.10 gf). Gage R&R <= 5.0% across 30 repeated load trials. Load cell drift <= 0.02 gf over 30 minutes continuous hold.

testcases.title: MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Automated Hook Positioning and Dynamic Pull Validation
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Wire Pull Metrology Station with machine vision pattern recognition, 20 um radius tungsten micro-hook, calibrated DRAM 180nm leadframe clamp fixture.
testcases.pre_conditions: Packaged 180nm DRAM leadframe with 32 thermosonic 25um Au wirebonds secured in rigid vacuum clamp fixture; vision fiducial alignment verified with loop height profile mapped.
testcases.procedure: 1. Program pattern recognition to automatically locate bond pads and leadframe fingers across all 32 pins. 2. Auto-target hook descent to loop apex (0.50 +/- 0.05 span distance) with hook landing clearance of 15 um above substrate. 3. Execute vertical pull at a constant rate of 1.0 mm/s until wire rupture occurs. 4. Record peak force (gf) and auto-classify failure code (Code 1: Neck break, Code 2: Mid-span rupture, Code 3: Stitch break, Code 4: Ball lift).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean pull force >= 6.0 gf with zero bonds failing below 3.0 gf across 32 pins. Hook landing spatial accuracy <= +/- 3.0 um in X/Y axes relative to programmed apex. 100% of failures must register as Code 1 or Code 2 (zero interfacial ball lifts allowed).

ppe_required: Cleanroom Class 1000 compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, 4 mil)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields
Static-dissipative ESD lab coat
ESD wrist strap connected to 1 MOhm workstation ground
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: In case of skin contact with IPA, rinse thoroughly with clean running water for 15 minutes. In case of eye contact, flush eyes at emergency eye-wash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. If inhaled vapors cause dizziness, remove victim to fresh air. Mechanical pinch hazards from automated stages: shut down emergency stop (E-stop) immediately before attending to injured personnel.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Operation conducted in standard semiconductor cleanroom bay with recirculating laminar air flow (HEPA filtered, min 90 FPM face velocity). IPA wipe-down of stage fixtures requires local chemical exhaust or laminar downdraft table.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be deposited into closed, airtight, grounded, flame-resistant flammable waste bins. Severed micro-wire remnants (gold) collected in dedicated sealed ESD sharps containers for precious metal scrap recycling.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Post-wirebonding thermosonic Au ball and wedge bonds on Al-0.5%Cu DRAM pads and Ag-plated leadframe fingers, free of organic contamination, flux residues, and mechanical pad cratering.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Destructively or non-destructively pull-tested wirebonded leadframe with documented rupture topography, categorized fracture interfaces, and zero metallic debris on active DRAM die circuitry.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding air exposure limits causes atmospheric moisture and sulfur adsorption on exposed Ag-plated leadframe fingers and Al-Cu bond pad margins, leading to micro-galvanic corrosion and skewing interfacial bond shear/pull adhesion measurements.

expected_result.summary: Full hardware installation, stage calibration, and analytical verification of the automated micro-hook wire pull tester meeting MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 requirements for 180nm open-source DRAM 25um gold wirebonds.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Load cell vertical calibration accuracy across full 0-100 gf range
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-point calibration using certified NIST Class E2 micro-weights at 1.0 gf, 5.0 gf, and 10.0 gf

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Stage micro-hook automated apex centering alignment accuracy
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated machine vision optical pattern recognition verified against high-resolution calibrated reticle

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Thermosonic 25um Au wire minimum destructive pull strength threshold
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Destructive micro-hook pull test at 1.0 mm/s pull rate per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Successful completion of 100 consecutive automated micro-hook pull cycles on standard qualification test coupons with Gage R&R <= 5%, zero load-cell overshoots, and formal engineering approval of the signed calibration certificate.
