# Standard Operating Procedure: Thermosonic Au Wire Pull Strength Testing to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Limit

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Wire pull testing to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 directly probes the mechanical reliability of the 25 µm 4N Au wire interconnection between the 180nm DRAM on-chip Al pads (100 µm x 100 µm) and leadframe fingers. The test hook placement must maintain a consistent 1:1 or mid-span geometry to avoid artificial asymmetric load vectors that skew pull force readings away from true normal tension. Furthermore, destructive pull testing must be coupled with acoustic microscopy (C-SAM) and electrical continuity mapping to decouple package epoxy attach delamination or die cratering from thermosonic metallurgical failure.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 25 µm (1.0 mil) Au wire bonded to 100 µm x 100 µm Al-Cu BEOL bond pads at 150°C stage temperature, MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 Condition D dictates a post-assembly minimum destructive pull strength of >= 4.0 grams-force (gf) (pre-seal) or >= 3.0 gf after environmental stress. The critical metallurgical concern is intermetallic compound (IMC) formation—specifically AuAl2 ('purple plague') and Au9Al4—which accelerates Kirkendall voiding at elevated temperatures, leading to neck/heel fractures or catastrophic pad lift/cratering under the ultrasonic transducer pulse (60 kHz, 50-100 mW). Failure must exclusively reside in the wire mid-span (Code 1/2) or neck (Code 3); pad peel (Code 4) or cratering (Code 5) indicates defective ultrasonic recipe parameters or BEOL ILD dielectric cracking.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-purity 99.99% (4N) 25 µm Au bonding wire and certified 90-degree calibrated pull test hooks (calibrated against NIST-traceable micro-gram deadweights) are vulnerable to lead times and vendor lot variations in elongation (2-6%) and tensile strength (breaking load 8-12 gf). Substitute bonding wires (such as Cu or Pd-coated Cu) cannot be arbitrarily qualified without recalibrating capillary wear cycles, ultrasonic transducer coupling parameters, and flame-off electronic gas envelopes. Second-source qualification for leadframe plating (Ag spot or Ni/Pd/Au) must maintain strict surface purity limits to avoid bond lift.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Destructive pull testing destroys active 180nm DRAM sample dies; thus, sample sizing per lot must balance wafer MPW quota constraints against statistical process control (SPC) sample rules (minimum 30 wires sampled across corners, center, and peripheral edge leadframe pins per run to ensure Cpk >= 1.33 above the 4.0 gf limit). Sign-off milestones require high-resolution optical fracture code logging and automatic data logging into the packaging MES database before passing batches to final hermetic packaging and wafer sort qualification.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die cratering and ILD shear crack beneath 100 µm Al pads due to excessive ultrasonic transducer power (>100 mW) or excessive capillary impact force during ball deformation.
1. Pad interfacial lift / bond peeling (MIL-STD-883 failure code 4) caused by pad surface oxidation, organic contamination, or insufficient thermosonic intermetallic bonding at 150°C stage temperature.
1. Heel/neck embrittlement at the neck of the ball bond caused by excessive heat-affected zone (HAZ) recrystallization during electronic flame-off (EFO) spark discharge, yielding premature wire snap below 4.0 gf.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-01` | **Destructive Wire Pull Strength and Break Force Distribution Test (MIL-STD-883 Method 2011)** | Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Bondtester equipped with calibrated 100 gf pull load cartridge, 30°/90° tungsten carbide micro-hook (50 µm throat depth), and motorized high-precision XYZ micro-positioning stage with optical microscope. | 1. Secure the leadframe strip onto the vacuum hold-down fixture of the bond tester. 2. Align the optical reticle and position the pull hook directly beneath the midpoint of the 25 µm Au wire loop (mid-span, perpendicular to the wire axis). 3. Raise the hook at a constant test speed of 1000 µm/s until destructive break occurs. 4. Record peak force in grams-force (gf) and categorize fracture location per MIL-STD-883 failure codes (Code 1: wire break at mid-span, Code 2: wire break at neck/heel, Code 3: ball lift, Code 4: pad cratering/metallization lift). 5. Repeat across n=30 consecutive bonding wires spanning inner and outer DRAM leadframe pins. | `Every individual wire pull strength must measure >= 4.00 gf (zero non-conformance per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 limit for 25 µm Au wire). Mean pull force >= 6.50 gf with process capability Cpk >= 1.33. 100% of failures must be Code 1 (wire span break) or Code 2 (heel/neck break); any occurrence of ball lift (Code 3) or die cratering (Code 4) constitutes immediate lot rejection.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-02` | **Post-Pull Bond Pad Interfacial Integrity and Cratering Optical/SEM Metrology** | High-resolution Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM) equipped with Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS) and 1000x Nomarski differential interference contrast (DIC) metallurgical optical microscope. | 1. Inspect all fractured bonding sites under 1000x Nomarski optical microscope for exposed underlying dielectric or silicon tears. 2. Transfer samples to FE-SEM chamber and pump down to < 1e-4 Pa. 3. Image bond pad residue at 10 kV acceleration voltage with secondary electron (SE) detector at 2500x magnification. 4. Perform EDS spot scan on the remnant bonded area to measure elemental Al and Au composition across the intermetallic footprint. 5. Measure remaining Au ball remnant shear thickness and verify zero fracture penetration into the BEOL SiO2/SiN dielectric under-pad stack. | `Zero evidence of dielectric cracking, Si micro-fracture, or substrate cratering beneath the 100 µm x 100 µm Al pad. Residual gold coverage on pad interface after span fracture must remain intact (>70% pad area covered by intact metallurgical squash nugget). Remnant IMC interdiffusion zone shows stoichiometric Au-Al bonding without Kirkendall micro-voiding (> 0.2 µm void cluster).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100/1000 nitrile gloves (powder-free, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with UV/optical glare side-shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and grounded ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm resistor, Cut-resistant under-gloves for handling sharp ceramic/leadframe dicing edges
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with solvents: Remove contaminated clothing and wash skin immediately with copious clean water and soap for 15 minutes. Eye exposure: Flush eyes immediately with isotonic eye wash solution or running water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmic medical evaluation. Inhalation: Relocate technician to fresh air immediately. Mechanical puncture from sharp tungsten carbide micro-hook or broken Au wire: Sanitize puncture site with antiseptic, apply sterile dressing, and report to occupational health clinic.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted in ISO Class 6 / Fed Std 209E Class 1000 cleanroom laminar flow hood (face velocity 0.45 m/s ± 20%). Solvent cleaning must be conducted inside a designated flammables chemical fume hood with point-of-use local exhaust ventilation (LEV) operating at minimum 100 FPM face velocity.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent wipes and swabs saturated with IPA/acetone must be sealed in airtight, grounded, FM-approved hazardous chemical disposal cans. Spent Au wire remnants and sacrificial leadframe pieces must be sorted into dedicated ESD-safe precious metal reclamation bins for gold recovery.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for fixture cleaning** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / MOS) | `99.9%` |
| **Acetone for residue solvent strip** | `67-64-1` | Electronic Grade | `99.5%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2) propellant** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (Grade 5.0) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Die attach epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) fully cured at 150°C for 60 min; bond pads clean, unpassivated 100 µm x 100 µm Al metallization free of epoxy bleedout, moisture, or particulate contamination; wire bonding completed on 150°C stage.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Destructively evaluated sample dies logged and segregated; surviving validated leadframe strips blown clean with ionized N2, zero debris, sealed in dry antistatic carrier boxes.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient factory air causes atmospheric moisture absorption, organic hydrocarbon condensation, and native Al2O3 growth on Al bond pads, promoting Kirkendall void formation, moisture-induced galvanic corrosion, and interfacial bond peeling failure below 4.0 gf limit.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical, mechanical, and statistical qualification of thermosonic 25 µm 99.99% Au wire bonds to 180nm DRAM Al pads conforming to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 Condition D. Verification confirms pull strength values exceed the mandatory >= 4.0 gf threshold across all tested pins with mid-span/neck fracture modes and zero pad cratering or bond lift.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MIL_STD_883_2011_Wire_Pull_Raw_Data_Log.csv`
- [ ] `Thermosonic_Wirebond_Metrology_Summary_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `SEM_EDS_Bond_Interface_Fracture_Micrographs.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Destructive pull strength for 25 µm Au wire on 180nm DRAM bonding pad must exceed the minimum MIL-STD-883 threshold** | `>= 4.00 gf` | +5.00 gf / -0.00 gf (Lower Specification Limit = 4.00 gf) | Automated micro-hook pull test on calibrated Dage 4000Plus bondtester at 1000 µm/s pull speed across n=30 wires |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Statistical process capability (Cpk) of the wire pull force distribution** | `>= 1.33` | ± 0.05 Cpk calculation tolerance | Statistical normal distribution fitting of 30-point pull force test data against the 4.00 gf lower specification limit in JMP/Minitab |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Incidence rate of non-conforming bond failure modes (ball lift, pad peel, or silicon cratering per MIL-STD-883 codes 3 and 4)** | `0.0%` | 0.0% (Zero tolerance defect criterion) | High-magnification optical and FE-SEM post-pull fractography inspection of 100% of tested bond sites |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Packaging Metrology Lead and DRAM Reliability Director sign-off achieved when all 30 sample wires exhibit pull force >= 4.00 gf (with Cpk >= 1.33), 100% fracture occurrences reside in wire span or neck, zero die cratering/pad lift is observed via SEM, and the comprehensive metrology report is archived in the DRAM Foundation VN packaging qualification portal.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Bond Pull Tester Calibration and Micro-Hook Alignment Setup
**Classification:** SOP-PKG-MET-003 | **Node:** 180nm DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) | **Standard:** MIL-STD-883 Method 2011

Persisted in knowledge base: [sop_bond_pull_tester_calibration.md](./docs/knowledge/sop_bond_pull_tester_calibration.md)

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────┐
│                    │
│    Calibration     │
│    Verification    │
│                    │
└──────────┬─────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌────────────────────┐
│                    │
│    Hook Radius     │
│     Inspection     │
│                    │
└──────────┬─────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌────────────────────┐
│                    │
│  Stage & Fixture   │
│     Alignment      │
│                    │
└──────────┬─────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌────────────────────┐
│                    │
│     Micro-Hook     │
│     Engagement     │
│                    │
└──────────┬─────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌────────────────────┐
│                    │
│  Pull Metrology &  │
│     Validation     │
│                    │
└────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Load Cell Tare and Static Calibration:**
   - Power on the bond pull tester station and allow the electronic transducer to thermally stabilize.
   - Tare the load cell to `0.0 gf`.
   - Perform static weight verification using certified calibration dead weights covering the operational range, validating measurement response against the minimum test threshold ($\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$).

2. **Micro-Hook Tooling Inspection:**
   - Inspect the tungsten/carbide micro-hook under optical magnification ($50\times - 100\times$).
   - Confirm the hook curvature radius accommodates $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire without burrs, bending deformation, or mechanical notch defects that could cause premature wire cut.

3. **Package & Workholder Fixturing:**
   - Mount the leadframe package (bearing the 180nm DRAM die bonded via silver-filled epoxy cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$) onto the vacuum clamp stage.
   - Adjust planar leveling screws so the leadframe and die surface are perpendicular to the vertical $Z$-axis pull vector ($90^\circ \pm 5^\circ$).

4. **Micro-Hook Alignment to Wire Span:**
   - Using the micromanipulator controls, align the micro-hook below the thermosonic gold wire loop connecting the on-chip $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad to the leadframe pin.
   - Target the apex/mid-span of the wire loop per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011, ensuring zero mechanical contact with adjacent bonding loops or aluminum pad metallization edges.

5. **Pull Metrology Execution & Failure Mode Classification:**
   - Execute the vertical pull sequence at a constant displacement speed.
   - Acquire peak force in grams-force ($\text{gf}$).
   - Inspect the break site: failure must occur in the wire span; interface ball lift or pad metallization peeling constitutes non-conformance.

---

### Quantitative Metric Comparison

```text
                   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                   │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Bond Pad Width (um)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
   Au Wire Dia (um)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                         │
                   │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                         │
Min Pull Force (gf)┤██                                 │
                   │██                                 │
                   └┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬┘
                    0       25      50       75     100 
```

---

### Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Operational / Acceptance Limit | Metrology Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Wire Pull Strength** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Calibrated Load Cell (MIL-STD-883 Method 2011) |
| **Bond Wire Diameter** | $25$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical Caliper / Sourced Spec (99.99% Au) |
| **Bond Pad Dimensions** | $100 \times 100$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | High-magnification Optical Metrology (Al square) |
| **Bond Failure Mode** | Break in wire span ($0\%$ bond pad interface lift) | Qualitative Category | Post-test Optical Inspection ($50\times - 100\times$) |

---

### Verified Context Citations
- **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging]**: 
  - Die pad geometry: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
  - Wire specification: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire.
  - Mechanical Quality Standards: MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 wire pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire; failure required within wire span rather than bond interface.
  - Die attach context: Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ min}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The wire pull tester (e.g., Dage 4000Plus or Nordson Dage equivalent) load cell must be verified across 0.5 gf to 50.0 gf range with deadweight calibration standards traceable to NIST. Micro-hook hook-up geometry and stage kinematics must ensure zero off-axis lateral shear during Z-axis vertical pull, otherwise artificial vector force components will skew MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 compliance data.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 25 µm (1.0 mil) thermosonic Au wire on 180nm DRAM bond pads, hook positioning relative to loop apex is critical: placing the micro-hook off-center induces asymmetric stress between the ball neck and wedge bond. Micro-hook tip diameter must be matched to wire loop clearance (hook tip radius ≤ 25 µm) to avoid nicking or premature mechanical notching of the annealed gold wire prior to tensile load ramp.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide and hardened steel micro-hooks (1 mil and 1.2 mil wire hook geometry) and certified Class M1/E2 micro-gram calibration weight sets face lead times of 6 to 10 weeks from specialized metrology suppliers; dual-sourcing calibrated pull tool cartridges and spare micro-hooks is required to prevent downtime during MPW package qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration and alignment procedures must be locked into standard operating protocols before executing destructive pull tests on packaged Gen 3 DRAM prototypes. Over-tightening micro-hook lock collars or operator manual jog errors risk bending the hook, invalidating the calibration certificate and halting the assembly verification timeline.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-hook tip misalignment causing frictional wire shaving or pre-stress nicking, leading to false-low bond pull force readings.
1. Load cell calibration drift or non-linear tare offset error exceeding ±0.1 gf across the 0-10 gf low-force regime.
1. Off-axis angular pull vector (>5° deviation from vertical normal) inducing combined shear-tensile stress that invalidates MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 break mode categorization.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-1-01` | **Static Deadweight Calibration and Linearity Verification of Bond Pull Load Cell** | Nordson Dage / XYZTEC Bond Tester equipped with calibrated 100 gf load cartridge, NIST-traceable precision weight set (1.0 gf, 5.0 gf, 10.0 gf, 20.0 gf, 50.0 gf Class E2), anti-vibration optical table. | 1. Secure the calibration jig beneath the load cell cartridge hook fixture. 2. Suspend certified deadweights sequentially: 1.0 gf, 5.0 gf, 10.0 gf, 20.0 gf, and 50.0 gf. 3. Record raw transducer voltage and converted gram-force for 5 consecutive loading/unloading cycles per weight. 4. Compute linearity regression coefficient (R^2) and hysteresis deviation across the full range. | `Full-scale linearity R^2 ≥ 0.9999; absolute measurement error ≤ ±0.05 gf for loads ≤ 10.0 gf; absolute measurement error ≤ ±0.20 gf for loads > 10.0 gf; zero return hysteresis ≤ 0.05 gf.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-1-02` | **Optical Alignment and Verticality Verification of Micro-Hook Kinematics** | Dual-axis stereo microscope with calibrated reticle and digital motorized stage (0.1 µm resolution), dual-camera orthogonal optical vision system (top-down and side-profile). | 1. Position micro-hook above the alignment target crosshair under 50x optical magnification. 2. Drive the Z-axis vertical stroke through 2.0 mm total travel at standard test speed (200 µm/s). 3. Measure lateral deflection (X and Y drift) of the micro-hook tip using the optical measurement software. 4. Verify hook opening perpendicularity relative to leadframe wire loop axis. | `Total lateral displacement (X-Y deviation) across 2.0 mm vertical Z-stroke ≤ 2.0 µm; hook angular tilt deviation from vertical normal ≤ 0.5 degrees.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 approved safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and conductive heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with IPA, rinse thoroughly with copious amounts of water. In case of eye contact, flush eyes immediately at eye-wash station for at least 15 minutes. In case of micro-puncture injury from sharp micro-hook, clean wound with antiseptic and report to cleanroom medical officer.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom laminar flow bench ventilation (ISO Class 6/7) or benchtop chemical local exhaust for IPA cleaning wipes.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of IPA-wetted cleanroom wipes in designated closed flammable solvent waste bins; spent or bent micro-hooks disposed of in dedicated sharps container.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA) for hook/fixture cleaning** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-bonded DRAM leadframe packages with intact 25 µm thermosonic Au wire loops, clean of organic flux or particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated pull tester station with micro-hook aligned, ready for destructive/non-destructive bond wire pull execution.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive environmental exposure of bonded packages prior to testing risks atmospheric sulfur/chloride contamination, leadframe tarnishing, and mechanical handling damage altering baseline wire pull values.

**Exit Objective Summary**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Thermosonic 25 µm Au Wire Destructive Pull Testing to MIL-STD-883 Limit

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Die & Package     │
│        Staging        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Hook Positioning &   │
│       Alignment       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Destructive Pull    │
│       Execution       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Force Measurement &  │
│     Failure Mode      │
│       Metrology       │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Package Fixturing & Environmental Stabilization**:
   - Secure the assembled 180nm DRAM package (die attached with silver-filled epoxy cured at 150°C for 60 min) onto the precision mechanical vacuum workholder of the calibrated micro-wire pull tester.
   - Maintain ambient testing temperature at $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$ with relative humidity $\le 50\%$.

2. **Hook Selection & Optical Alignment**:
   - Install a calibrated pull hook sized for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire (inner hook radius $1.5\times$ to $2.0\times$ wire diameter, $\approx 35\text{--}50\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Under microscope vision ($50\times\text{--}100\times$ magnification), align the hook perpendicularly under the $25\ \mu\text{m}$ 99.99% Au wire loop connecting the on-chip $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad to the leadframe pin.
   - Position the hook at mid-span (highest loop apex, equidistant between the ball bond and crescent/stitch bond) to ensure uniform pull force vector distribution without introducing shear torques.

3. **Destructive Pull Execution**:
   - Set the automated Z-axis pull travel rate to $0.1\text{--}0.5\ \text{mm/s}$ (quasi-static pull rate per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011).
   - Initiate Z-travel pull until destructive wire rupture occurs.
   - Record the peak load at break via the calibrated load cell transducer.

4. **Failure Mode Metrology & Pad Inspection**:
   - Inspect the rupture site under high-magnification optical inspection / SEM.
   - Classify the failure mode (e.g., span break, neck break above ball, ball lift, or pad lift).
   - Log the pull force (grams-force) and failure location directly into the packaging metrology quality tracking system.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                     Au Wire Pull Strength (grams-force)
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │█████████████████████████████████│
Nominal Pull Strength┤█████████████████████████████████│
   Min Required Force┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░               │
                     │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░               │
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0.0     1.9     3.8     5.6    7.5 
```

| Target Metric | Parameter Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Destructive Pull Force** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Calibrated Micro-load Cell Transducer |
| **Bond Failure Mode** | Break in wire span / neck (zero interfacial lift) | Categorical / Count ($0\%$ at interface) | Optical Metrology / SEM ($50\times\text{--}200\times$) |
| **Bonding Pad Geometry** | $100 \times 100$ | $\mu\text{m} \times \mu\text{m}$ | Optical Calibrated Reticle |
| **Wire Diameter Verification** | $25 \pm 1$ | $\mu\text{m}$ (99.99% Au) | Calibrated Micrometry / SEM Metrology |

---

### 3. Context Citations
- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - *Wire Pull Strength*: MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire. Failure must occur in wire span, not at bond interface.
  - *Wire Composition & Geometry*: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter 99.99% gold wire bonded onto $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum square bonding pads.

---
*Micro-knowledge entry has been persisted to [thermosonic_au_wire_pull_testing.md](./docs/knowledge/thermosonic_au_wire_pull_testing.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Destructive pull testing under MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 is an essential statistical gatekeeper for the open-source 180nm DRAM packaging pipeline. However, manual hook positioning introduces significant operator-dependent geometric variation. Pull force is geometrically related to true bond wire tension via F_wire = F_pull / (2 * sin(theta)); pulling off-center shifts stress disproportionately to either the die ball bond or the leadframe stitch. The test platform must utilize motorized micro-positioning stages and enforce standardized pull-hook placement at exactly mid-span (or 1/3 span if specified) with automated optical pattern recognition to guarantee repeatable stress vectoring.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 25 um diameter 99.99% (4N) Au wire bonded to 100 um x 100 um Al-Cu pads at 150°C, the minimum baseline failure limit specified by MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 is 3.0 to 4.0 gf (grams-force) depending on test condition, but a robust production thermosonic process must yield mean pull forces > 8.0 gf with Cpk >= 1.67. Crucially, failure mode classification is as critical as numerical force: ductile mid-span wire neck breaks or heat-affected zone (HAZ) breaks above the ball neck are acceptable, whereas pad metallization lift-off, dielectric cratering (under-pad ILD cracking in 180nm BEOL stack), or ball unseating signal severe ultrasonic over-power, inadequate intermetallic compound (Au-Al IMC) formation, or excessive Kirkendall voiding.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Destructive pull testing requires continuous replenishment of tungsten/carbide micro-pull hooks (e.g., 2.0-3.0 mil hook radius for 25 um wire) and calibrated Dage/Nordson or Royce load cells (0-100 gf range). Supply bottlenecks arise when custom hooks wear out or bend due to mishandling. In addition, sacrificial packaging runs consuming genuine functional 180nm DRAM silicon must be planned carefully; leadframes and Ablebond 84-1LMIS conductive epoxy lots must have strict cold-chain tracking (-40°C storage) to prevent baseline shift in bond integrity.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Destructive pull testing consumes bonded units and requires immediate feedback to the wirebonder operator. A rigid sample size policy (e.g., 5 wires per package across 4 packages per lot minimum, covering corner and center pins) must be scheduled to avoid blocking downstream ceramic DIP hermetic sealing and wafer-sort/package-test release. Bottlenecks will occur if test results require manual spreadsheet entry; automated datalogging directly from the pull tester to the MES/LIMS database is mandatory.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial Bond Lift / Pad Cratering: Ball lift with underlying SiO2/low-k dielectric fracture caused by excessive ultrasonic energy (>100 mW) or excessive capillary bonding force damaging the 180nm BEOL ILD stack.
1. Premature Neck/HAZ Snap below 4.0 gf: Excessive recrystallization and grain growth in the Heat-Affected Zone directly above the Au ball due to improper Electronic Flame-Off (EFO) spark duration or contaminated N2 shielding.
1. Hook Slippage and Geometric Off-Center Distortion: Manual or misaligned hook placement pulling adjacent to the stitch/wedge, causing artificial shear-peel forces and invalidating MIL-STD-883 failure mode criteria.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-2-01` | **Destructive Mid-Span Wire Pull Force & Failure Mode Characterization** | Nordson DAGE 4000Plus / Royce 620 Bond Tester with calibrated 0-100 gf load cell, 3.0 mil radius tungsten pull hook, high-resolution stereo microscope with 100x magnification and calibrated reticle. | 1. Secure the wire-bonded leadframe into the vacuum clamping workholder. 2. Calibrate and tare load cell to 0.000 gf. 3. Under microscope guidance, position the 3.0 mil tungsten hook at exact mid-span (50% ± 5% of wire length) beneath the 25 um Au wire loop. 4. Initiate vertical pull at a constant rate of 1.0 mm/s normal to the die surface until wire rupture occurs. 5. Record peak force in grams-force (gf). 6. Inspect break site at 100x magnification and classify failure mode per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Table 2011-I (e.g., Mode 1: wire break at neck/HAZ, Mode 2: mid-span break, Mode 3: ball lift, Mode 4: stitch lift). | `Pass: Peak pull force >= 4.0 gf for every individual wire, lot average >= 8.0 gf with standard deviation sigma <= 0.8 gf; Failure mode must be 100% mid-span wire break or neck/HAZ break. Fail: Any individual pull force < 4.0 gf, or any occurrence of ball lift, stitch lift, or pad cratering.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-2-02` | **Post-Stress Thermal Cycling Wire Pull Integrity Validation** | Environmental Thermal Shock / Thermal Cycling Chamber (-55°C to +125°C per MIL-STD-883 Method 1010 Condition B), Nordson DAGE 4000Plus Bond Tester, Optical Inspection Scope. | 1. Remove test packages from thermal chamber and stabilize at 25°C for 2 hours. 2. Visually inspect under 50x magnification for sag, micro-cracks, or wire-to-wire shorting. 3. Mount sample into pull tester fixture. 4. Execute vertical pull test on 20 consecutive wires per package at mid-span with 1.0 mm/s pull speed. 5. Record peak rupture force and failure mode classification. | `Pass: Post-thermal cycling pull force >= 3.5 gf absolute minimum per wire, mean degradation < 15% relative to pre-stress baseline, zero pad cratering or intermetallic Au-Al delamination. Fail: Any wire pull force < 3.5 gf, or evidence of Kirkendall void-induced bond lifting.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses, Class 100 cleanroom compatible powder-free nitrile gloves (anti-static/ESD safe), ESD wrist strap with 1 Mohm safety resistor, Cleanroom lint-free lab coat / smock
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin/Eye Contact with IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious clean water at eyewash station for >= 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; wash skin with mild soap and water. Physical Hook Puncture/Snag: Disinfect wound with sterile antiseptic, bandage, and evaluate for foreign metallic micro-fragment. Inhalation of inert N2 purge gas: Move victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if hypoxic.

Local chemical exhaust snorkel required if IPA solvent wipe-down is conducted for hook/workholder decontamination.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Severed Au wire fragments and broken bond leads must be collected in a grounded anti-static scrap container for precious metal reclamation. critics.systems_engineer: Destructive pull testing under MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 is an essential statistical gatekeeper for the open-source 180nm DRAM packaging pipeline. However, manual hook positioning introduces significant operator-dependent geometric variation. Pull force is geometrically related to true bond wire tension via F_wire = F_pull / (2 * sin(theta)); pulling off-center shifts stress disproportionately to either the die ball bond or the leadframe stitch. The test platform must utilize motorized micro-positioning stages and enforce standardized pull-hook placement at exactly mid-span (or 1/3 span if specified) with automated optical pattern recognition to guarantee repeatable stress vectoring.
critics.domain_expert: For 25 um diameter 99.99% (4N) Au wire bonded to 100 um x 100 um Al-Cu pads at 150°C, the minimum baseline failure limit specified by MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 is 3.0 to 4.0 gf (grams-force) depending on test condition, but a robust production thermosonic process must yield mean pull forces > 8.0 gf with Cpk >= 1.67. Crucially, failure mode classification is as critical as numerical force: ductile mid-span wire neck breaks or heat-affected zone (HAZ) breaks above the ball neck are acceptable, whereas pad metallization lift-off, dielectric cratering (under-pad ILD cracking in 180nm BEOL stack), or ball unseating signal severe ultrasonic over-power, inadequate intermetallic compound (Au-Al IMC) formation, or excessive Kirkendall voiding.
critics.supply_chain: Destructive pull testing requires continuous replenishment of tungsten/carbide micro-pull hooks (e.g., 2.0-3.0 mil hook radius for 25 um wire) and calibrated Dage/Nordson or Royce load cells (0-100 gf range). Supply bottlenecks arise when custom hooks wear out or bend due to mishandling. In addition, sacrificial packaging runs consuming genuine functional 180nm DRAM silicon must be planned carefully; leadframes and Ablebond 84-1LMIS conductive epoxy lots must have strict cold-chain tracking (-40°C storage) to prevent baseline shift in bond integrity.
critics.laya_pm: Destructive pull testing consumes bonded units and requires immediate feedback to the wirebonder operator. A rigid sample size policy (e.g., 5 wires per package across 4 packages per lot minimum, covering corner and center pins) must be scheduled to avoid blocking downstream ceramic DIP hermetic sealing and wafer-sort/package-test release. Bottlenecks will occur if test results require manual spreadsheet entry; automated datalogging directly from the pull tester to the MES/LIMS database is mandatory.
critical_failure_modes: Interfacial Bond Lift / Pad Cratering: Ball lift with underlying SiO2/low-k dielectric fracture caused by excessive ultrasonic energy (>100 mW) or excessive capillary bonding force damaging the 180nm BEOL ILD stack.

Premature Neck/HAZ Snap below 4.0 gf: Excessive recrystallization and grain growth in the Heat-Affected Zone directly above the Au ball due to improper Electronic Flame-Off (EFO) spark duration or contaminated N2 shielding.

Hook Slippage and Geometric Off-Center Distortion: Manual or misaligned hook placement pulling adjacent to the stitch/wedge, causing artificial shear-peel forces and invalidating MIL-STD-883 failure mode criteria.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-PKG-MET-003`
**Title:** Failure Mode Analysis and Statistical Grams-Force Compliance Verification  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe > Thermosonic Gold Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe Pins > MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull & Ball Shear Metrology Validation > Thermosonic Au Wire Pull Strength Testing to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Limit > Failure Mode Analysis and Statistical Grams-Force Compliance Verification  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure specifies the operational steps and statistical criteria for conducting non-destructive and destructive wire-pull metrology, classifying failure modes, and statistically verifying grams-force pull strength compliance on thermosonic 25 µm Au wire bonds formed between 180nm DRAM on-chip bonding pads (100 µm × 100 µm Al) and leadframe pins in accordance with **MIL-STD-883 Method 2011**.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                            MIL-STD-883 METHOD 2011                               |
|                         WIRE PULL STRENGTH METROLOGY                              |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Step 1: Fixturing & Hook Placement]                                             |
|   - Clamp 180nm DRAM package / leadframe securely onto metrology stage.           |
|   - Position calibrated pull hook at mid-span / apex of 25 µm Au wire loop.       |
|                                                                                   |
|  [Step 2: Force Application]                                                      |
|   - Apply vertical pull force at calibrated test rate until failure occurs.       |
|   - Record peak force in grams-force (gf) via digital transducer.                 |
|                                                                                   |
|  [Step 3: Failure Mode Categorization (High-Power Optical/SEM Inspection)]        |
|   - Mode 1: Wire Mid-Span Break / Wire Neck Break (ACCEPTABLE).                   |
|   - Mode 2: Ball Bond Lift / Interfacial Separation at Al Pad (REJECT).           |
|   - Mode 3: Stitch/Wedge Lift at Leadframe Pin (REJECT).                          |
|   - Mode 4: Die Pad Crater / Silicon Pitting Under Pad (REJECT).                  |
|                                                                                   |
|  [Step 4: Statistical Process Control (SPC) & Grams-Force Compliance]             |
|   - Verify all measured pull values exceed the threshold: Force >= 4.0 gf.        |
|   - Confirm 0% bond-interface separation failures across sample lot.              |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Specimen Preparation & Fixturing
1. Mount the packaged 180nm DRAM die (attached via silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at 150°C for 60 min) securely onto the pull tester vacuum chuck or mechanical clamp fixture.
2. Align the calibrated micro-hook under high-magnification optical positioning (30×–100×) under the apex/center of the 25 µm Au wire span connecting the 100 µm × 100 µm Al bond pad to the leadframe pin. Hook angle must be perpendicular ($90^\circ \pm 5^\circ$) to the die surface.

#### Step 2: Automated Grams-Force Pull Metrology
1. Initiate the pull test sequence at a controlled pull rate per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.
2. Continuously log the load profile; record the peak breaking force in grams-force ($\text{gf}$) with high-precision load-cell telemetry.

#### Step 3: Microscopic Failure Mode Analysis
1. Inspect each pulled bond location under high-magnification stereomicroscopy or SEM:
   - **Acceptable Failure Mode:** Wire span break or wire neck break above the ball.
   - **Unacceptable / Critical Defect Modes:** Ball bond interfacial lift-off from the 100 µm × 100 µm Al pad, metallization peeling, cratering beneath the pad, or heel/stitch liftoff at the leadframe pin.

#### Step 4: Statistical Compliance & Lot Disposition
1. Aggregate pull test data across the sample size.
2. Verify that all individual pull forces meet or exceed the absolute specification limit of $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$.
3. Verify that zero ($0$) interfacial bond separations occurred. If any sample exhibits bond interface failure or pull force $< 4.0\text{ gf}$, quarantine the assembly lot for ultrasonic transducer pulse calibration (60 kHz, 50–100 mW, 20–30 ms at 150°C stage).

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Tolerance / Limit | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Wire Pull Strength** | $\ge 4.0$ | Minimum lower specification limit | $\text{grams-force (gf)}$ | MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Pull Tester |
| **Interfacial Failure Rate** | $0$ | Exactly $0$ (must fail in wire span, not at bond interface) | $\%$ | High-Power Optical / SEM Inspection |
| **Wire Diameter Verification** | $25$ | $\pm 0.5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical Micrometry / Calibrated SEM |
| **Bond Pad Footprint Target** | $100 \times 100$ | Nominal on-chip pad dimension | $\mu\text{m} \times \mu\text{m}$ | Metrology Microscope / Layout Verification |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources
- **`Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging`**:
  - Validates 25 µm diameter 99.99% Au wire thermosonic ball bonding onto 100 µm × 100 µm aluminum pads (EFO free-air ball, stage at 150°C, 60 kHz transducer, 50–100 mW, 20–30 ms).
  - Specifies MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 requirement: pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$ for 25 µm wire.
  - Dictates failure criteria: failure must occur in the wire span, not at the bond interface.
- **`180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench`**:
  - Contextualizes 180nm technology generation integration with access transistor and unit cell architecture.
- **`Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects`**:
  - Validates underlying Al metallization parameters for bitlines/strapping and bonding pad layers.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated wire pull metrology to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 requires strict alignment between the micro-hook positioning vector and the loop apex geometry. For our 1.0 mil (25.4 um) 4N Au wire looped over 180nm DRAM bond pads, any hook displacement exceeding 5% of loop span induces parasitic peel moments rather than pure normal-tension pull vectors, which artificially skews the Weibull distribution tail. Metrology instrumentation must incorporate automated vision-guided z-axis touchdown and closed-loop hook placement to guarantee Gauge R&R measurement coefficient of variation CV < 1.0% across the full 48-pin leadframe matrix.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Failure mode partitioning must explicitly differentiate between Mode 1 (first bond ball neck break / HAZ recrystallization failure), Mode 2 (mid-span tensile break), Mode 3 (heel break at leadframe wedge/stitch), Mode 4 (ball lift / intermetallic delamination), and Mode 5 (die cratering / Si rupture under the TiN/Al-0.5%Cu pad). Under MIL-STD-883 Condition D criteria for 1.0 mil wire, the absolute minimum destructive threshold is 3.0 gf, but for Gen 3 open-source DRAM reliability, we mandate a statistical floor of Cpk >= 1.67 against a process lower limit of 6.0 gf with zero tolerance for Mode 4 or Mode 5 interfacial shear or cratering occurrences.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dataram/foundry assembly houses in Vietnam or SEA regional OSAT partners must standardize on calibrated Dage 4000Plus or Nordson XYZEC push/pull bond testers with certified 0-100 gf load cartridges. Sourcing calibrated micro-hooks with tip radius r = 12.5 um (+/-1.5 um) and traceable ERS/NIST load cell calibration weights is critical to prevent inter-site measurement offsets. Supply disruptions of certified 4N Au (99.99%) wire spools with consistent elongation (3-7%) directly corrupt breaking force baselines.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Statistical grams-force compliance and failure mode extraction represent the final gating milestone before transfer to transfer molding. Destructive pull testing of 5 leadframe strips per lot (minimum 120 wires sampled per lot, covering corners, center, and high-frequency clock/DQS DRAM pads) must complete within a strict 60-minute window post-wirebond to ensure lot release without stalling the downstream epoxy molding compound (EMC) encapsulation queue.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial Ball Lift (Failure Mode 4) resulting from inadequate Au-Al intermetallic compound (IMC, Au8Al3/Au4Al) formation or organic contaminant residue on the 180nm top Al bond pad.
1. Silicon Sub-Pad Cratering (Failure Mode 5) caused by excessive ultrasonic energy / bonding impact fracturing underlying dielectric layers (SiO2/inter-metal dielectrics) during first bond placement.
1. Brittle Heat-Affected Zone (HAZ) Neck Rupture (Failure Mode 1) driven by grain coarsening during free-air ball (FAB) formation, leading to catastrophic low-force (< 3.0 gf) tensile failure.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-3-01` | **Automated Destructive Wire Pull Strength and Grams-Force Statistical Verification** | Nordson DAGE 4000Plus Multi-Function Bondtester with 100gf miniature pull cartridge (calibrated to ASTM F459 / MIL-STD-883 Method 2011), 25 um hook radius, automated optical alignment vision system, and vibration-isolated granite platform. | 1. Clamp the leadframe securely into the mechanical fixture on the DAGE 4000Plus stage.\n2. Teach vision fiducials on die corners and leadframe tips to establish local coordinate frames.\n3. Position the micro-hook under the wire loop at exactly 50% (+/-2%) of the horizontal span between first bond (die pad) and second bond (lead post).\n4. Lower the hook until optical z-clearance is 15 um above the substrate plane.\n5. Execute vertical pull at a constant rate of 5.0 mm/s until mechanical rupture occurs.\n6. Record peak pull force in grams-force (gf) at 10 kHz acquisition rate across 120 consecutive wire pulls per lot.\n7. Automatically calculate sample mean, standard deviation, and process capability metrics (Cp, Cpk). | `PASS: Mean breaking strength >= 8.5 gf, minimum recorded pull force >= 5.5 gf (exceeding MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 limit of 3.0 gf), standard deviation sigma <= 0.65 gf, and process capability Cpk >= 1.67. FAIL if any single wire breaks below 4.0 gf or Cpk < 1.67.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-3-02` | **Optical and SEM Failure Mode Classification and Interfacial Integrity Verification** | High-magnification motorized optical inspection microscope (Keyence VHX-7000 at 500x-2000x) and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM with Bruker Quantax EDS at 15 kV acceleration voltage). | 1. Inspect all 120 rupture sites under optical microscope at 1000x magnification.\n2. Categorize each failure locus into standardized bins: Mode 1 (HAZ/Neck), Mode 2 (Mid-span), Mode 3 (Heel/Wedge), Mode 4 (Ball Lift/Interfacial), Mode 5 (Sub-pad Cratering).\n3. Mount any suspect non-ductile rupture sites into FE-SEM for secondary electron imaging at 5000x magnification.\n4. Perform EDS spot analysis and elemental mapping on die pad surface if Mode 4 is observed to measure residual Au-Al intermetallic coverage (AuAl2, Au4Al).\n5. Examine underlying pad oxide/metal stack under SEM for cracking, pitting, or silicon micro-cleavage (Mode 5). | `PASS: Zero occurrences (0.00%) of Mode 4 (Ball Lift) and Mode 5 (Die Cratering) across all 120 tested sites; >= 95% of failures must reside in Mode 1 (HAZ neck break) or Mode 2 (mid-span ductile rupture with classic cup-and-cone necking morphology). FAIL if any Mode 4 or Mode 5 defect is detected.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, 6 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe conductive lab coat with grounded wrist strap, Cleanroom face mask (lint-free non-woven polypropylene)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash affected area with mild soap and copious water. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately. Mechanical micro-needle puncture from hook/wire: Clean wound with antiseptic solution, apply sterile dressing, and verify tetanus vaccination status.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized exhaust snorkel (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s) active during solvent pad wipe cleaning. Metrology area operates under positive-pressure cleanroom airflow (ISO Class 6 / Fed Std 209E Class 1000) with HEPA filtration.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect solvent-soaked wipes and rinse residues in designated fire-safe, grounded flammables disposal bins. Expended gold bonding wire clippings and destructive pull remnants must be segregated into dedicated precious-metal scrap recovery containers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / SEMI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Acetone** | `67-64-1` | Electronic Grade | `99.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Completed thermosonic gold ball wirebonded leadframe strip directly out of wirebonder stage, pristine unoxidized Al pads and Au loops free from flux, organic haze, or particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Pull-tested metrology strip cataloged and segregated; non-destructively passed production strips forwarded to transfer molding with uncompromised wire loops and bond integrity.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive queue time exposure in ambient air induces atmospheric sulfur and moisture adsorption on silver/copper leadframes and promotes galvanic micro-corrosion at Au-Al interfaces, causing premature bond heel embrittlement and false Mode 4 interfacial delaminations during testing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full metrology signoff confirming compliant statistical distribution of wire pull grams-force (Cpk >= 1.67, mean >= 8.5 gf) according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Condition D for 1.0 mil Au wire on 180nm DRAM bond pads, verified with zero instances of ball lifting or pad cratering.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MIL_STD_883_Wire_Pull_Grams_Force_Statistical_Distribution.csv`
- [ ] `Failure_Mode_Classification_and_SEM_Micrograph_Atlas.pdf`
- [ ] `Metrology_Gauge_RR_and_Cpk_Compliance_Certificate.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean destructive wire pull breaking force across sampled 180nm DRAM pins** | `8.50 gf` | +/- 1.50 gf (absolute minimum >= 5.50 gf) | High-speed calibrated load-cell strain sensor on DAGE 4000Plus bondtester operating at 5.0 mm/s pull velocity. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Process capability index (Cpk) against MIL-STD-883 lower specification limit (LSL = 3.0 gf)** | `1.85` | >= 1.67 minimum threshold | Statistical calculation: Cpk = (Mean - LSL) / (3 * Sigma) over N=120 randomized pull trials. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Occurrence rate of Failure Mode 4 (Interfacial Ball Lift) and Mode 5 (Die Sub-Pad Cratering)** | `0.00%` | 0 occurrences allowed out of 120 wire pulls | High-magnification optical microscopy at 1000x and FE-SEM EDS confirmation of ruptured bonding sites. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher signoff requires N=120 consecutive wire pull measurements yielding Cpk >= 1.67 with normal distribution fit (Anderson-Darling p > 0.05), mean breaking force >= 8.50 gf, absolute minimum reading >= 5.50 gf, zero Mode 4/5 failures confirmed via optical/SEM audit, and formal countersignature by Lead Reliability Metrologist and Assembly Packaging Lead.

180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects (Vossen & Kern - Thin Film Processes)

critics.systems_engineer: Automated wire pull metrology to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.9 requires strict alignment between the micro-hook positioning vector and the loop apex geometry. For our 1.0 mil (25.4 um) 4N Au wire looped over 180nm DRAM bond pads, any hook displacement exceeding 5% of loop span induces parasitic peel moments rather than pure normal-tension pull vectors, which artificially skews the Weibull distribution tail. Metrology instrumentation must incorporate automated vision-guided z-axis touchdown and closed-loop hook placement to guarantee Gauge R&R measurement coefficient of variation CV < 1.0% across the full 48-pin leadframe matrix.
critics.domain_expert: Failure mode partitioning must explicitly differentiate between Mode 1 (first bond ball neck break / HAZ recrystallization failure), Mode 2 (mid-span tensile break), Mode 3 (heel break at leadframe wedge/stitch), Mode 4 (ball lift / intermetallic delamination), and Mode 5 (die cratering / Si rupture under the TiN/Al-0.5%Cu pad). Under MIL-STD-883 Condition D criteria for 1.0 mil wire, the absolute minimum destructive threshold is 3.0 gf, but for Gen 3 open-source DRAM reliability, we mandate a statistical floor of Cpk >= 1.67 against a process lower limit of 6.0 gf with zero tolerance for Mode 4 or Mode 5 interfacial shear or cratering occurrences.
critics.supply_chain: Dataram/foundry assembly houses in Vietnam or SEA regional OSAT partners must standardize on calibrated Dage 4000Plus or Nordson XYZEC push/pull bond testers with certified 0-100 gf load cartridges. Sourcing calibrated micro-hooks with tip radius r = 12.5 um (+/-1.5 um) and traceable ERS/NIST load cell calibration weights is critical to prevent inter-site measurement offsets. Supply disruptions of certified 4N Au (99.99%) wire spools with consistent elongation (3-7%) directly corrupt breaking force baselines.
critics.laya_pm: Statistical grams-force compliance and failure mode extraction represent the final gating milestone before transfer to transfer molding. Destructive pull testing of 5 leadframe strips per lot (minimum 120 wires sampled per lot, covering corners, center, and high-frequency clock/DQS DRAM pads) must complete within a strict 60-minute window post-wirebond to ensure lot release without stalling the downstream epoxy molding compound (EMC) encapsulation queue.
critical_failure_modes: Interfacial Ball Lift (Failure Mode 4) resulting from inadequate Au-Al intermetallic compound (IMC, Au8Al3/Au4Al) formation or organic contaminant residue on the 180nm top Al bond pad.
Silicon Sub-Pad Cratering (Failure Mode 5) caused by excessive ultrasonic energy / bonding impact fracturing underlying dielectric layers (SiO2/inter-metal dielectrics) during first bond placement.
Brittle Heat-Affected Zone (HAZ) Neck Rupture (Failure Mode 1) driven by grain coarsening during free-air ball (FAB) formation, leading to catastrophic low-force (< 3.0 gf) tensile failure.

testcases.title: Automated Destructive Wire Pull Strength and Grams-Force Statistical Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Nordson DAGE 4000Plus Multi-Function Bondtester with 100gf miniature pull cartridge (calibrated to ASTM F459 / MIL-STD-883 Method 2011), 25 um hook radius, automated optical alignment vision system, and vibration-isolated granite platform.
testcases.pre_conditions: 48-pin ceramic/leadframe test strips containing wirebonded Gen 3 DRAM dies inspected; wire gauge confirmed as 25.4 um (1.0 mil) 4N Au; room ambient maintained at 22 +/- 2 deg C and 45 +/- 5% RH; load cell calibrated against certified 5.00 gf and 10.00 gf deadweights.
testcases.procedure:
1. Clamp the leadframe securely into the mechanical fixture on the DAGE 4000Plus stage.
2. Teach vision fiducials on die corners and leadframe tips to establish local coordinate frames.
3. Position the micro-hook under the wire loop at exactly 50% (+/-2%) of the horizontal span between first bond (die pad) and second bond (lead post).
4. Lower the hook until optical z-clearance is 15 um above the substrate plane.
5. Execute vertical pull at a constant rate of 5.0 mm/s until mechanical rupture occurs.
6. Record peak pull force in grams-force (gf) at 10 kHz acquisition rate across 120 consecutive wire pulls per lot.
7. Automatically calculate sample mean, standard deviation, and process capability metrics (Cp, Cpk).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: PASS: Mean breaking strength >= 8.5 gf, minimum recorded pull force >= 5.5 gf (exceeding MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 limit of 3.0 gf), standard deviation sigma <= 0.65 gf, and process capability Cpk >= 1.67. FAIL if any single wire breaks below 4.0 gf or Cpk < 1.67.

testcases.title: Optical and SEM Failure Mode Classification and Interfacial Integrity Verification
testcases.instrumentation: High-magnification motorized optical inspection microscope (Keyence VHX-7000 at 500x-2000x) and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM with Bruker Quantax EDS at 15 kV acceleration voltage).
testcases.pre_conditions: Completion of destructive pull test TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-2-3-01 on 120 sampled wires; substrate surface de-dusted with filtered dry N2 blow; SEM vacuum chamber pumped below 5e-4 Pa.
testcases.procedure:
1. Inspect all 120 rupture sites under optical microscope at 1000x magnification.
2. Categorize each failure locus into standardized bins: Mode 1 (HAZ/Neck), Mode 2 (Mid-span), Mode 3 (Heel/Wedge), Mode 4 (Ball Lift/Interfacial), Mode 5 (Sub-pad Cratering).
3. Mount any suspect non-ductile rupture sites into FE-SEM for secondary electron imaging at 5000x magnification.
4. Perform EDS spot analysis and elemental mapping on die pad surface if Mode 4 is observed to measure residual Au-Al intermetallic coverage (AuAl2, Au4Al).
5. Examine underlying pad oxide/metal stack under SEM for cracking, pitting, or silicon micro-cleavage (Mode 5).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: PASS: Zero occurrences (0.00%) of Mode 4 (Ball Lift) and Mode 5 (Die Cratering) across all 120 tested sites; >= 95% of failures must reside in Mode 1 (HAZ neck break) or Mode 2 (mid-span ductile rupture with classic cup-and-cone necking morphology). FAIL if any Mode 4 or Mode 5 defect is detected.

ppe_required: Class 100 cleanroom compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, 6 mil)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields
ESD-safe conductive lab coat with grounded wrist strap
Cleanroom face mask (lint-free non-woven polypropylene)
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye contact: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash affected area with mild soap and copious water. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately. Mechanical micro-needle puncture from hook/wire: Clean wound with antiseptic solution, apply sterile dressing, and verify tetanus vaccination status.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Benchtop localized exhaust snorkel (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s) active during solvent pad wipe cleaning. Metrology area operates under positive-pressure cleanroom airflow (ISO Class 6 / Fed Std 209E Class 1000) with HEPA filtration.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Collect solvent-soaked wipes and rinse residues in designated fire-safe, grounded flammables disposal bins. Expended gold bonding wire clippings and destructive pull remnants must be segregated into dedicated precious-metal scrap recovery containers.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Completed thermosonic gold ball wirebonded leadframe strip directly out of wirebonder stage, pristine unoxidized Al pads and Au loops free from flux, organic haze, or particulate contamination.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Pull-tested metrology strip cataloged and segregated; non-destructively passed production strips forwarded to transfer molding with uncompromised wire loops and bond integrity.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excessive queue time exposure in ambient air induces atmospheric sulfur and moisture adsorption on silver/copper leadframes and promotes galvanic micro-corrosion at Au-Al interfaces, causing premature bond heel embrittlement and false Mode 4 interfacial delaminations during testing.

expected_result.summary: Full metrology signoff confirming compliant statistical distribution of wire pull grams-force (Cpk >= 1.67, mean >= 8.5 gf) according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Condition D for 1.0 mil Au wire on 180nm DRAM bond pads, verified with zero instances of ball lifting or pad cratering.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Mean destructive wire pull breaking force across sampled 180nm DRAM pins
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-speed calibrated load-cell strain sensor on DAGE 4000Plus bondtester operating at 5.0 mm/s pull velocity.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Process capability index (Cpk) against MIL-STD-883 lower specification limit (LSL = 3.0 gf)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Statistical calculation: Cpk = (Mean - LSL) / (3 * Sigma) over N=120 randomized pull trials.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Occurrence rate of Failure Mode 4 (Interfacial Ball Lift) and Mode 5 (Die Sub-Pad Cratering)
quantitative_assertions.tolerance: 0 occurrences allowed out of 120 wire pulls
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-magnification optical microscopy at 1000x and FE-SEM EDS confirmation of ruptured bonding sites.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Researcher signoff requires N=120 consecutive wire pull measurements yielding Cpk >= 1.67 with normal distribution fit (Anderson-Darling p > 0.05), mean breaking force >= 8.50 gf, absolute minimum reading >= 5.50 gf, zero Mode 4/5 failures confirmed via optical/SEM audit, and formal countersignature by Lead Reliability Metrologist and Assembly Packaging Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Ball Shear Force Metrology & Fracture Mode SEM Failure Analysis

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Ball shear metrology must directly correlate shear strength to bond pad metallization stack integrity (Ti/Al-Cu/TiN/AICu) in 180nm CMOS BEOL. Without automated shear tool standoff height calibration (1.5-3.0 um above pad surface), tool contact drag will generate artificial shear force inflation, masking sub-surface intermetallic dielectric cracking and pad peeling failure modes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Per JEDEC JESD22-B116 and MIL-STD-883 Method 2011, thermosonic Au ball bonds on 0.8 mil (20.3 um) to 1.0 mil (25.4 um) wire diameter must yield minimum shear strength > 0.0055 g/um^2 bond area. Fracture mode SEM failure analysis must verify ductile Au shearing (Mode 1: >75% residual Au on pad) rather than brittle intermetallic Au-Al Kirkendall voiding or pad cratering into the underlying TEOS inter-metal dielectric (IMD).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide shear tool tips (Dage/Nordson compatible) and ultra-high-resolution FE-SEM consumable apertures face 6-8 week procurement lead times in Vietnam domestic supply chains; backup multi-cartridge shear load cells (0-250 gf) and gold reference calibration standards must be dual-sourced and maintained in controlled dry packs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must maintain <90 seconds per 30-bond sampling coupon per leadframe strip to support real-time wirebonder SPC loop feedback; failing shear SPC limits halts assembly line lot movement, requiring immediate automated containment and automated FIB-SEM root-cause escalation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Si/Dielectric cratering under bond pad metallization due to excessive ultrasonic power during thermosonic bonding
1. Interfacial brittle fracture along AuAl2/Au4Al intermetallic compound (IMC) boundary with <25% remnant Au
1. Shear tool dragging across passivation edge or polyimide layer causing false-high force readouts and misleading fracture grading

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-3-01` | **Thermosonic Au Ball Shear Force & Standoff Calibration SPC Test** | Nordson DAGE 4000Plus Bondtester with calibrated 250 gf micro-shear cartridge, automated Z-height touchdown laser/sensor, and optical alignment microscope (100x magnification) | 1. Clamp leadframe strip onto vacuum fixture and perform optical crosshair alignment on peripheral DRAM I/O bond pads. 2. Auto-touchdown shear stylus to adjacent bare die silicon reference and retract exactly 2.5 um. 3. Advance shear tool at 50 um/s shear speed perpendicularly against thermosonic Au ball (ball diameter 45-55 um) until rupture occurs. 4. Record peak shear force (gram-force) and force-displacement curve across 30 consecutive peripheral pads per sample strip. 5. Calculate mean shear strength, standard deviation, and Cpk index. | `Minimum peak shear force >= 15.0 gf (for 1.0 mil Au wire, ball diameter ~50 um) with normalized shear strength >= 0.0060 gf/um^2; Cpk >= 1.67 across 30 pads; no zero-force brittle lifts or tool drag events permitted.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-3-02` | **Post-Shear Fracture Interface SEM & EDS Material Mode Characterization** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM, Thermo Fisher Apreo/FEI) equipped with Oxford Instruments Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS) detector | 1. Load sample stub into SEM chamber and navigate to sheared bond pad coordinates mapped from TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-3-01. 2. Capture secondary electron (SE) micrographs at 2,000x and 10,000x magnification for each sheared pad site. 3. Quantify projected remnant Au area percentage relative to original ball bond footprint using calibrated image threshold analysis. 4. Perform EDS spot analysis and elemental mapping on exposed pad fracture floor for Au (M-alpha), Al (K-alpha), Si (K-alpha), and O (K-alpha) to detect dielectric exposure. | `Fracture mode classified as Mode 1 (ductile shear through bulk Au with >= 75% residual Au coverage) on >= 95% of tested pads; exactly 0% instances of Mode 4 (pad cratering exposing raw Si/SiO2 with Si atomic concentration > 5.0% on EDS).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10,000 cleanroom compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, 6 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Anti-static dissipative cleanroom coat (ESD safe), Non-magnetic stainless steel wafer tweezers and ESD wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush with emergency eyewash for minimum 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash immediately with soap and excess water; remove contaminated clothing. Inhalation: Relocate individual to cleanroom fresh-air plenums; administer medical oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop VOC local exhaust ventilation hood operating at face velocity 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) for IPA solvent sample degreasing; FE-SEM roughing rotary pump exhaust routed to dedicated facility scrubber vacuum line.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA and solvent-wetted lint-free wipers collected in marked, self-closing FM-approved flammable waste containers; segregated from strong oxidizers and collected by licensed semiconductor hazardous waste disposal contractor.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (MOS/VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Ethanol (Anhydrous)** | `64-17-5` | Spectroscopic Grade | `99.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly thermosonic-bonded gold balls on 180nm CMOS Al-0.5%Cu pads, post-die attach curing, free of organic outgassing residues or halogenic flux contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Sheared bond pad surfaces post-mechanical destructive testing, desiccated under dry N2 environment, free of atmospheric moisture, hydrocarbon adsorption, or native oxide growth prior to high-vacuum SEM.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric exposure beyond Q-time promotes ambient sulfur/halogen adsorption and oxidation of exposed Al-Cu underlayers on sheared interfaces, distorting EDS elemental quantification and obscuring baseline Kirkendall intermetallic corrosion.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical, mechanical, and fractographic characterization of 180nm DRAM thermosonic Au ball bonds validating compliance with MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 and JEDEC JESD22-B116 standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM_180nm_Ball_Shear_Force_SPC_Distribution.csv`
- [ ] `Fracture_Mode_SE_Micrographs_HighRes.tiff`
- [ ] `Metrology_Shear_EDS_Failure_Analysis_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean thermosonic Au ball shear strength across 30 tested peripheral pads** | `>= 18.5 gf` | ± 1.5 gf | Calibrated Nordson DAGE 4000Plus micro-shear force load cell logging per JEDEC JESD22-B116 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Percentage of sheared pads exhibiting ductile Mode 1 bulk gold fracture** | `100%` | -5% acceptable lower threshold (minimum 95%) | Automated SEM backscatter/secondary electron digital planimetry on 2000x micrographs |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Bond pad cratering or IMD dielectric tear-out occurrence count** | `0 occurrences` | 0 (zero-defect tolerance across lot) | FE-SEM secondary electron topography inspection and EDS silicon elemental signature verification at 15 kV |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 30 of 30 tested Au ball bonds exhibit shear strength > 15.0 gf (Cpk >= 1.67), zero instances of pad cratering (Mode 4), SEM/EDS validation confirming > 75% residual Au coverage on all sites, and signoff endorsement from Packaging Lead and Metrology QA.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Dage BondTester Tool Fixturing & Shear Tool Standoff Calibration

- **Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS DRAM MPW)
- **Module:** Metrology & Package Reliability (BEOL & Packaging)
- **Compliance Standard:** MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull & Ball Shear Metrology Validation

---

### 1. Workflow Process Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│                                │
│       Specimen Fixturing       │
│  (Leadframe Vacuum & Clamping) │
│                                │
└───────────────┬────────────────┘
                │
                ▼
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│                                │
│    Optical Planarity Check     │
│   (Focal Plane Die Leveling)   │
│                                │
└───────────────┬────────────────┘
                │
                ▼
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│                                │
│     Touch-Down Z-Zeroing       │
│  (Substrate Reference Contact) │
│                                │
└───────────────┬────────────────┘
                │
                ▼
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│                                │
│    Standoff Height Offset      │
│  (Z-axis Step for 25 µm Wire)  │
│                                │
└───────────────┬────────────────┘
                │
                ▼
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│                                │
│     Shear Metrology Ready      │
│   (Pad Clearance & Shear Run)  │
│                                │
└────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Fixturing & Specimen Clamping**:
   - Secure the DRAM leadframe (holding the 180nm DRAM die bonded with silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ min}$) onto the Dage universal work holder.
   - Engage vacuum chuck hold-down and tighten mechanical clamp levers diagonally across the package perimeter to eliminate specimen compliance and deflection under shear loading.

2. **Optical Alignment & Die Tilt / Planarity Calibration**:
   - Align the stereo microscope / alignment optics over the corners of the DRAM die surface.
   - Verify planarity across the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads by checking focal consistency. Adjust the fixture leveling goniometer until the focal plane variation across the active die surface is $\le 2\ \mu\text{m}$.

3. **Shear Tool Selection & Visual Inspection**:
   - Select a calibrated tungsten carbide ball shear tool designed for fine-pitch interconnects (tool tip width $\ge 1.5\times$ ball diameter, suited for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire thermosonic gold balls).
   - Inspect the shear chisel edge under $50\times$ magnification to confirm zero gold debris buildup, chipping, or edge rounding.

4. **Touch-Down Sensing (Z-Datum Zeroing)**:
   - Jog the shear tool in $X/Y$ to an unbonded reference metallization pad or adjacent flat leadframe/substrate clearance zone.
   - Initiate automated electrical/piezo touch-down sensing at a controlled descent speed ($\le 100\ \mu\text{m/s}$) until contact is detected at a contact force threshold ($\le 0.5\ \text{gf}$). Register this height as $Z_0$ (Datum Zero).

5. **Standoff Height Setting & Travel Validation**:
   - Program the programmable vertical standoff offset height $Z_{\text{standoff}}$ to guarantee that the shear tool passes directly above the pad metallization ($350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$ aluminum thickness) without scrubbing into the silicon substrate or pad metallization, shearing within the lower third of the ball.
   - Retract tool to home position, align laterally in front of the target $25\ \mu\text{m}$ gold ball bond on the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pad, and verify non-contact approach.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                     Calibration Acceptance Envelope    
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
```

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - *Thermosonic Gold Ball Bonding*: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ Au wire; capillary bonding at $150^\circ\text{C}$ with ultrasonic transducer pulse ($60\text{ kHz}$, $50\text{--}100\text{ mW}$, $20\text{--}30\text{ ms}$) on $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.
  - *MIL-STD-883 Method 2011*: Wire pull strength requires $\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire with failure occurring in the wire span.
  - *Die Attach Assembly*: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$, thermal resistance $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$, acoustic void area $< 5\%$.
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - *Pad Metallization Thickness*: Metal-1 film thickness target calibrated at $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$ Al / Al-0.5% Cu (sputter rate $50\text{--}100\text{ nm/min}$, sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$).
