### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The Dage BondTester fixturing must isolate mechanical compliance, thermal drift, and substrate vibration to sub-micron accuracy. In a 180nm DRAM wirebonded package, improper vacuum chuck rigidity or clamping planarization directly perturbs the vertical touch-down sensing mechanism, injecting spurious contact force spikes that induce premature calibration cut-offs and drift in the capacitive Z-stage displacement loop.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Per JEDEC JESD22-B116 and MIL-STD-883 Method 2011, shear tool standoff calibration is exceptionally critical for 180nm DRAM thermosonic Au ball bonds. Standoff height must maintain precisely 3.0 µm to 5.0 µm above the metallized bond pad (10% to 20% of the compressed ball height). Exceeding this introduces tensile bending moments rather than pure shear, whereas tool dragging gouges the Si/SiO2 passivated inter-metal dielectric (IMD) stack, masking bond interfacial failure with catastrophic cratering.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom Dage tungsten carbide (WC) shear chisels (width ~50-70 µm matching the 180nm DRAM pad pitch) and kinematic leadframe vacuum clamping inserts present an 8-to-12 week procurement lead time. Sourcing interchangeable calibrated touch-down sensor heads and traceable tungsten calibration steps requires dual-vendor qualification (Nordson Dage and XYZTEC) to mitigate single-supplier shutdown risks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Tool fixturing and standoff calibration represent an immediate critical path gate prior to executing statistical ball shear testing on MPW Gen 3 packaging. Fixture unreliability or drift invalidates all subsequent wire bond process qualification batches, causing cumulative project delays in packaging sign-off. Operator-independent calibration recipes must be frozen and version-controlled.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Shear chisel touchdown overshoot inducing pad gouging, IMD micro-fracture, or tool-tip chipping during zero-reference datum initialization.
1. Mechanical compliance or planar tilt in the vacuum chuck fixture causing variable effective standoff height across the DRAM die perimeter (exceeding ±1.0 µm variance).
1. Dynamic load cell hysteresis and drift exceeding 0.25% full-scale due to uncalibrated transducer strain gauges or unstable ambient vibration.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/1000 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, >= 6 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and conductive grounding wrist/heel straps, Particulate face mask (Class II / N95 cleanroom compatible)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of water from dedicated eyewash station for >= 15 minutes; seek ophthalmologist review if irritation persists. Skin Contact: Wash exposed skin with soap and DI water; remove contaminated clothing. Inhalation: Relocate individual to fresh cleanroom ambient air; provide supplemental oxygen if respiratory distress occurs.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted within laminar flow hood or tool canopy maintaining clean laminar air flow at 0.45 m/s ± 20%. Solvent wipe down must be performed under local solvent exhaust bench with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes, swabs, and solvent waste must be accumulated in labeled, grounded, self-closing FM-approved hazardous solvent cans. Disposed via certified hazardous chemical waste handlers; no drain disposal allowed.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-bonded DRAM die wirebonded with thermosonic 25 µm Au wire on Al-0.5%Cu pads; pristine, unoxidized pad metallurgy free of moisture, organic residues, or particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated fixture and tool holder clamped and certified; die pads untouched or sheared according to sample plan, stored immediately under dry nitrogen purge.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes moisture adsorption and atmospheric galvanic corrosion of open Al-Cu bond pad metallization, altering interfacial friction and corrupting shear force baseline measurements.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Ball Shear Testing on $100\,\mu\text{m}$ Al Pads per JEDEC JESD22-B116

---

### 1. Workflow & Metrology Lifecycle Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Stage DRAM Die & Fixture Vacuum Clamp"] --> B["Calibrate Z-Reference Touchdown on 100 µm Al Pad"]
    B --> C["Set Shear Tool Standoff Height (3 to 5 µm above Al Pad)"]
    C --> D["Execute Automated Shear at Constant Velocity (50 µm/s)"]
    D --> E["Log Peak Shear Force & Load-Displacement Profile"]
    E --> F["Post-Shear Optical / SEM Inspection & Fracture Mode Classification"]
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate & Package Fixturing**:
   - Secure the ceramic DIP / leadframe containing the cured DRAM die (die attach: Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\,\text{min}$) onto the precision vacuum fixture chuck of the automated bond tester (e.g., Dage / Nordson automated shear platform).
   - Verify vacuum hold-down pressure is $\ge 70\,\text{kPa}$ to ensure zero mechanical compliance or lateral deflection during shear travel.

2. **Optical Alignment & Pad Targeting**:
   - Align the optics to target the thermosonic gold ball bonds on the $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad metallization (deposited via PVD planar DC magnetron sputtering at $350\,\text{nm} \pm 5\%$ thickness, $R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\square$).
   - Identify the bonded ball geometry formed from the $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire (typical bonded ball diameter $D \approx 50\text{--}65\,\mu\text{m}$, height $H \approx 12\text{--}18\,\mu\text{m}$).

3. **Touchdown Calibration & Shear Standoff Height Setting (per JEDEC JESD22-B116)**:
   - Perform automated surface sensing (touchdown) directly adjacent to the bond pad on the silicon/dielectric passivated surface or top metal plane to establish the $Z = 0$ datum.
   - Retract the tungsten carbide shear tool to a fixed standoff clearance height of **$3.0\,\mu\text{m}$ to $5.0\,\mu\text{m}$** above the pad metallization surface (ensuring clearance $\le 10\%$ of ball height to avoid tool ride-over or pad gouging).

4. **Shear Test Execution**:
   - Position the shear chisel tip behind the ball at a programmed back-off distance of $15\,\mu\text{m}$ to $25\,\mu\text{m}$.
   - Actuate the shear tool along the axis towards the bond at a programmed test speed of **$50\,\mu\text{m}/\text{s}$** (JESD22-B116 compliant speed range: $10\text{--}100\,\mu\text{m}/\text{s}$) through a total travel distance of $100\,\mu\text{m}$.
   - Simultaneously acquire the peak shear force ($F_{\text{shear}}$) using a calibrated load cell.

5. **Fracture Surface & Residual Aluminum Inspection**:
   - Perform post-shear optical microscopy (or high-resolution SEM) to evaluate failure modes across all sampled bonds.
   - Categorize fracture mode per JESD22-B116: Type 1 (Ductile shear in Au ball), Type 2 (Shear through Au-Al intermetallic compound / IMC layer), Type 3 (Adhesive pad lift / de-wetting), or Type 4 (Silicon cratering / pad tear-out).

---

### 3. Quantitative Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                         │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│

                         │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒    │
      Ball Diameter Range┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒    │
Min Shear Force (25um Au)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                      │
                         │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                      │
      Shear Tool Standoff┤███                          │
                         │███                          │
                         └┬──────┬──────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                         0.0   18.8   37.5   56.2  75.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target & Limit | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Ball Shear Force ($F_{\text{shear}}$)** | $\ge 15.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Calibrated Bond Tester Load Cell |
| **Shear Tool Standoff Height** | $3.0\text{--}5.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Touchdown $Z$-Stage Encoder |
| **Shear Tool Velocity** | $50.0 \pm 5.0$ | $\mu\text{m}/\text{s}$ | Precision Motion Controller Feedback |
| **Residual Interfacial Shear Area / Ductility** | $\ge 75.0\%$ residual Au/IMC on pad (Type 1 ductile shear; zero cratering) | $\%$ area | Post-Test Optical / SEM Analysis |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Standard Citations

- **JEDEC JESD22-B116**: *Wire Bond Shear Test Procedure*, defining tool standoff heights, shear displacement speed, and failure mode classifications (Types 1–4).
- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum square bonding pads.
  - $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire thermosonic ball bonding; electronic flame-off (EFO); capillary bonding at $150^\circ\text{C}$ with $60\,\text{kHz}$, $50\text{--}100\,\text{mW}$, $20\text{--}30\,\text{ms}$ pulse.
  - Die attach Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\,\text{min}$.
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - Pad metallization film thickness: $350\,\text{nm} \pm 5\%$, sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\square$.
- **MIL-STD-883 Method 2011**: Mechanical bond pull validation context ($\ge 4.0\,\text{gf}$ for $25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Ball shear testing per JESD22-B116 must avoid inducing mechanical micro-cracks in underlying interlayer dielectric (ILD: TEOS/FSG) and active circuitry beneath the 100um Al pads (0.8-1.2 um thickness). The shear tool z-height clearance (shear standoff) must be strictly calibrated to 3-5 um above the metallization layer to prevent tool dragging into adjacent passivation or pad edges.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 25um (1.0 mil) 4N Au wire on 100um Al-0.5%Cu metallization pads, bonded ball diameter typically ranges from 50 to 70 um with 12 to 18 um ball height. Shear strength must exceed 0.0055 gf/um^2 (or minimum 15 gf total shear load for 60um ball diameter). Intermetallic compound (IMC) formation (Au-Al phases such as Au4Al, Au5Al2) must be evaluated post-shear; ductile shear through Au or cohesive shear with >75% residual Au/IMC coverage on pad is required to prevent Kirkendall voiding failures.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide or diamond-tipped shear chisels (width 80-100 um) must maintain traceable calibration cycles under ISO/IEC 17025. Standard lead times for replacement micro-force load cells (range 0-100 gf, resolution 0.01 gf) are currently 6-8 weeks from Dage/Nordson or XYZTEC, necessitating on-site buffer spares of verified shear tips and calibration weights.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test coupon metrology cycle time must stay under 45 seconds per bond pad across a 30-bond sampling matrix per leadframe strip to avoid creating a line-down bottleneck prior to epoxy mold compound (EMC) encapsulation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Pad lift / cratering failure mode exhibiting catastrophic Si/SiO2 dielectric fracture beneath the 100um Al metallization due to excessive thermosonic bonding power.
1. Tool-to-pad collision/dragging causing false high shear readings and physical gouging of the Al metallization.
1. Interfacial separation along unbonded Au-Al interface (<25% intermetallic coverage) indicating insufficient bonding temperature/ultrasonic energy.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): FE-SEM/EDX Post-Shear Fracture Surface Analysis & Intermetallic Assessment

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation [Foundry Tapeout & PDK] > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging [BEOL & Packaging] > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe [Packaging & Assembly] > Thermosonic Gold Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe Pins [Packaging] > MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull & Ball Shear Metrology Validation [Metrology] > Ball Shear Force Metrology & Fracture Mode SEM Failure Analysis [Metrology] > FE-SEM/EDX Post-Shear Fracture Surface Analysis & Intermetallic Assessment [Metrology]
**Target Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm) | **Action Type**: Buy

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: DRC/LVS: 0 Violations, ALD EOT <= 0.8 nm, CMP Dishing < 15 nm.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Automated Batch DRC/LVS & Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / AFM.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-shear fracture analysis on 180nm DRAM bond pads must directly correlate mechanical shear force values (grams-force) with the spatial distribution of Au-Al intermetallic compounds (IMCs) across the bond pad area. If residual Au coverage is evaluated in isolation without cross-referencing cratering risks in the underlying ILD (inter-layer dielectric) stack—specifically TEOS/Si3N4 capping layers above the DRAM wordline/bitline driver periphery—sub-surface micro-cracks will escape detection during ball shear force metrology, precipitating latent thermal cycle failures.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Under MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 and JEDEC JESD22-B116 standards, the fracture mode must be categorized cleanly: ductile Au tear (Mode 1), Au-Al IMC interface separation (Mode 2), pad lift/peeling (Mode 3), or silicon/ILD cratering (Mode 4). EDX spot and area quantification must specifically differentiate between stoichiometric phases (AuAl2 'purple plague', Au2Al 'white plague', Au4Al, and Au5Al2). A high-resolution FE-SEM operating at 10-15 kV with a low beam current (~100 pA to 1 nA) is required to avoid electron beam-induced carbon deposition and charge buildup on the surrounding passivation oxide.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: FE-SEM/EDX equipment utilization in OSAT and backend qualification labs represents a major throughput bottleneck. EDX drift and silicon drift detector (SDD) calibration against certified Au and Al pure standards must be maintained on a strict weekly cycle. High-purity conductive carbon tabs and gold/palladium sputter targets for secondary charge mitigation must be kept in steady inventory to prevent lot holds during packaging metrology qualification for commercial 180nm MPW packaging.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To meet Gen 3 DRAM packaging milestone commitments, post-shear failure analysis turnaround time must not exceed 2 hours per sampled leadframe strip. Metrology protocol workflows must mandate automated stage-coordinate mapping from the bond tester shear coordinates directly into the FE-SEM stage navigation file, eliminating manual optical hunting for sheared bond sites across the multi-pin leadframe.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Si/ILD Dielectric Cratering (Mode 4 fracture) below the 1.0 um Al-0.5%Cu metallization pad caused by excessive ultrasonic power during thermosonic bonding.
1. Accelerated Kirkendall voiding and brittle interfacial fracture at the Au-rich IMC boundary (Au4Al/Au5Al2) due to improper thermal profile during epoxy die attach cure or wirebond preheat.
1. Surface re-oxidation or hydrocarbon contamination of the sheared fracture plane prior to vacuum pump-down, resulting in spurious EDX oxygen and carbon artifacts that mask thin IMC boundaries.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-3-3-01` | **FE-SEM Quantitative Fracture Surface Mode & Residual Au Area Ratio Assessment** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM) equipped with Everhart-Thornley SE detector and in-lens secondary electron detector, calibrated against NIST SRM 484 pitch standard. | 1. Load sample stub into FE-SEM load lock and pump down to high vacuum (<5e-4 Pa). 2. Navigate stage to sheared bond pad coordinates identified during destructive shear metrology. 3. Acquire high-contrast secondary electron images at 500x overview and 3000x localized magnifications centered on the fracture foot. 4. Apply grayscale thresholding algorithm (Otsu method) over the pad contact zone to segment sheared gold remnant from exposed aluminum metallization. 5. Compute the percentage area of residual Au relative to the total bonded area and record fracture mode per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Fracture Mode must be 100% Type 1 (ductile Au shear through the bulk ball) or Type 2 (fracture through continuous IMC) with Residual Au Area Ratio >= 75.0% of the original bonded ball footprint. Zero instances (0%) of Mode 3 (pad metallization peeling) or Mode 4 (ILD/silicon cratering).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-2-3-3-3-02` | **EDX Elemental Stoichiometry & Au-Al Intermetallic Phase Boundary Verification** | FE-SEM integrated Silicon Drift Detector (SDD) Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectrometer (EDX) with >= 30 mm^2 active area, energy resolution <= 129 eV at Mn-Kalpha. | 1. Perform a 5-point EDX spot analysis across the central exposed fracture plane and interfacial rim of the sheared ball bond. 2. Acquire live spectra for 60 seconds live-time per point with beam current normalized to 1.0 nA. 3. Execute atomic ZAF/phi-rho-z standardless matrix correction to extract atomic percentages (at%) of Au, Al, Cu, Si, and O. 4. Generate a 256x256 pixel elemental EDX hyperspectral net-intensity map covering the complete 80 um x 80 um bond pad area for Au-Malpha, Al-Kalpha, and Si-Kalpha lines. 5. Calculate the atomic ratio of Au:Al across the interfacial reaction layer to identify intermetallic phases. | `Intermetallic coverage in the bonded peripheral region must exhibit Au:Al atomic stoichiometry corresponding to stable high-integrity phases (Au8Al3 or Au4Al) with total Au+Al content >= 90.0 at%; underlying Si-Kalpha signal must remain <= 1.0 at% across the pad area (confirming zero ILD punch-through or micro-crater delamination).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Static-dissipative cleanroom nitrile gloves (thickness >= 5 mil), ANSI Z87.1 approved UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Class 100 / ISO 5 lint-free antistatic cleanroom smock and conductive ESD heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with cleaning solvents, flush immediately with copious amounts of deionized water for 15 minutes. For eye splash, rinse at eye wash station for >= 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. For solvent vapor inhalation, remove casualty to fresh air immediately. If asphyxiation symptoms occur due to N2 purge displacement, administer artificial respiration or oxygen via trained personnel.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: FE-SEM roughing vacuum pump exhaust lines must be plumbed directly into the facility dedicated scrubbed solvent exhaust duct (minimum face velocity 100 LFPM). Sample preparation cleaning stations must operate under a laminar flow exhaust hood with negative static pressure >= 0.05 inches water gauge.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent wipes and contaminated cotton swabs must be segregated into closed, grounded, flame-resistant flammable waste receptacles. Liquid solvent effluent must be collected in dedicated labeled polyethylene carboys for hazardous chemical waste reclamation; zero drain disposal permitted.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `>= 99.9%` |
| **Ethanol (Anhydrous)** | `64-17-5` | Semiconductor Grade | `>= 99.5%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (Grade 5.0) | `>= 99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly sheared gold ball bond pads on 180nm DRAM leadframe assembly, post-Dage shear testing, free of mechanical debris, burrs, or particulate dust.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: High-vacuum inspected, carbon-stabilized fracture surface, mapped and metallurgically categorized with zero electron beam hydrocarbon contamination scars.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient cleanroom exposure creates native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) regrowth (>2 nm) and airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) condensation on the freshly ruptured intermetallic interface, artificially skewing EDX quantitative stoichiometry and masking delicate nanoscale ductile rupture micro-voids.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Comprehensive failure analysis and intermetallic validation of thermosonic gold ball bonds on 180nm DRAM pad metallization following destructive shear metrology. Delivers quantitative fracture mode classification (MIL-STD-883 Method 2011), residual gold area coverage ratios, and high-resolution EDX stoichiometric mapping of Au-Al intermetallic phases ensuring zero ILD cratering.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `FESEM_Fracture_Morphology_Mode_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `EDX_AuAl_Stoichiometry_Spectral_Dataset.csv`
- [ ] `Post_Shear_Fracture_Surface_Map_HighRes.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Residual gold area ratio within the primary ball bond perimeter after mechanical shear** | `80.0%` | >= 75.0% minimum | Automated binary threshold area segmentation on 3000x FE-SEM SE images |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Silicon substrate and ILD layer signal intensity on the sheared fracture contact area** | `0.0 at%` | <= 1.0 at% maximum | Standardless ZAF-corrected quantitative EDX area scan (15 kV, 60s live time) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Au-Al stoichiometric intermetallic compound phase formation ratio across the bonded interface** | `4.00` | Au:Al atomic ratio between 3.50 and 4.20 (Au4Al predominant phase) | 5-point calibrated EDX point spectrometry with SDD detector |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal acceptance requires 100% verification across all sampled leadframe die bond pads exhibiting Mode 1/2 ductile fracture with >= 75% residual Au coverage, zero detected Si/ILD cratering (Si concentration <= 1.0 at%), confirmed Au4Al/Au8Al3 intermetallic stoichiometry, and formal sign-off by Packaging Metrology Lead and Quality Reliability Engineering.

5. Compute the percentage area of residual Au relative to the total bonded area and record fracture mode per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Fracture Mode must be 100% Type 1 (ductile Au shear through the bulk ball) or Type 2 (fracture through continuous IMC) with Residual Au Area Ratio >= 75.0% of the original bonded ball footprint. Zero instances (0%) of Mode 3 (pad metallization peeling) or Mode 4 (ILD/silicon cratering).

testcases.title: EDX Elemental Stoichiometry & Au-Al Intermetallic Phase Boundary Verification
testcases.instrumentation: FE-SEM integrated Silicon Drift Detector (SDD) Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectrometer (EDX) with >= 30 mm^2 active area, energy resolution <= 129 eV at Mn-Kalpha.
testcases.pre_conditions: FE-SEM beam aligned at 15.0 kV accelerating voltage to ensure adequate excitation of Au-Lalpha (9.71 keV) and Al-Kalpha (1.48 keV) lines; dead time maintained between 20% and 30%; energy calibration verified with pure copper standard.
testcases.procedure:
1. Perform a 5-point EDX spot analysis across the central exposed fracture plane and interfacial rim of the sheared ball bond.
2. Acquire live spectra for 60 seconds live-time per point with beam current normalized to 1.0 nA.
3. Execute atomic ZAF/phi-rho-z standardless matrix correction to extract atomic percentages (at%) of Au, Al, Cu, Si, and O.
4. Generate a 256x256 pixel elemental EDX hyperspectral net-intensity map covering the complete 80 um x 80 um bond pad area for Au-Malpha, Al-Kalpha, and Si-Kalpha lines.
5. Calculate the atomic ratio of Au:Al across the interfacial reaction layer to identify intermetallic phases.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Intermetallic coverage in the bonded peripheral region must exhibit Au:Al atomic stoichiometry corresponding to stable high-integrity phases (Au8Al3 or Au4Al) with total Au+Al content >= 90.0 at%; underlying Si-Kalpha signal must remain <= 1.0 at% across the pad area (confirming zero ILD punch-through or micro-crater delamination).

ppe_required: Static-dissipative cleanroom nitrile gloves (thickness >= 5 mil)
ANSI Z87.1 approved UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields
Class 100 / ISO 5 lint-free antistatic cleanroom smock and conductive ESD heel straps
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin contact with cleaning solvents, flush immediately with copious amounts of deionized water for 15 minutes. For eye splash, rinse at eye wash station for >= 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. For solvent vapor inhalation, remove casualty to fresh air immediately. If asphyxiation symptoms occur due to N2 purge displacement, administer artificial respiration or oxygen via trained personnel.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: FE-SEM roughing vacuum pump exhaust lines must be plumbed directly into the facility dedicated scrubbed solvent exhaust duct (minimum face velocity 100 LFPM). Sample preparation cleaning stations must operate under a laminar flow exhaust hood with negative static pressure >= 0.05 inches water gauge.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent solvent wipes and contaminated cotton swabs must be segregated into closed, grounded, flame-resistant flammable waste receptacles. Liquid solvent effluent must be collected in dedicated labeled polyethylene carboys for hazardous chemical waste reclamation; zero drain disposal permitted.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly sheared gold ball bond pads on 180nm DRAM leadframe assembly, post-Dage shear testing, free of mechanical debris, burrs, or particulate dust.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: High-vacuum inspected, carbon-stabilized fracture surface, mapped and metallurgically categorized with zero electron beam hydrocarbon contamination scars.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding ambient cleanroom exposure creates native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) regrowth (>2 nm) and airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) condensation on the freshly ruptured intermetallic interface, artificially skewing EDX quantitative stoichiometry and masking delicate nanoscale ductile rupture micro-voids.

expected_result.summary: Comprehensive failure analysis and intermetallic validation of thermosonic gold ball bonds on 180nm DRAM pad metallization following destructive shear metrology. Delivers quantitative fracture mode classification (MIL-STD-883 Method 2011), residual gold area coverage ratios, and high-resolution EDX stoichiometric mapping of Au-Al intermetallic phases ensuring zero ILD cratering.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Residual gold area ratio within the primary ball bond perimeter after mechanical shear
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated binary threshold area segmentation on 3000x FE-SEM SE images

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Silicon substrate and ILD layer signal intensity on the sheared fracture contact area
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Standardless ZAF-corrected quantitative EDX area scan (15 kV, 60s live time)

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Au-Al stoichiometric intermetallic compound phase formation ratio across the bonded interface
quantitative_assertions.tolerance: Au:Al atomic ratio between 3.50 and 4.20 (Au4Al predominant phase)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: 5-point calibrated EDX point spectrometry with SDD detector

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Formal acceptance requires 100% verification across all sampled leadframe die bond pads exhibiting Mode 1/2 ductile fracture with >= 75% residual Au coverage, zero detected Si/ILD cratering (Si concentration <= 1.0 at%), confirmed Au4Al/Au8Al3 intermetallic stoichiometry, and formal sign-off by Packaging Metrology Lead and Quality Reliability Engineering.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Acoustic Microscopy Void Metrology and Destructive Wire Pull Testing

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: DRC/LVS rule decks must run clean via KLayout/Magic/OpenLane with zero design rule errors. Antenna ratio rules (< 250:1) and substrate tap density checks must pass before GDSII reticle handoff to commercial foundry.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: 3D Crown capacitor ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 (ZAZ) stack must achieve equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) <= 0.8 nm and leakage current < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V. CMP dishing on M1/M2 tungsten/copper features must hold < 15 nm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Commercial foundry MPW (Multi-Project Wafer) shuttle submission has an unmovable tapeout window; GDSII/OASIS files must freeze 21 days prior. Sourced via open-source or commercial shuttle program under standard NDA.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 60-120 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: CRITICAL (A single DRC rule deck discrepancy or LVS short-circuit ruins the entire multi-thousand dollar commercial shuttle run and incurs a 4-6 month spin delay).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. DRC/LVS hierarchy discrepancy causing undetected metal-to-metal bridging or floating substrate tap.
1. ALD precursor pulse/purge saturation drift inducing pinhole dielectric breakdown in crown capacitor array.
1. Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) over-polish causing severe interconnect erosion and open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-01` | **Automated DRC/LVS Golden Rule Deck Physical Sign-Off** | KLayout / Magic / Pegasus Industrial Physical Verification Batch Engine | 1. Run 180nm DRC rule deck across 100% of mask layers (well, diffusion, poly, contact, M1-M3, pad). 2. Execute Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) netlist extraction against golden SPICE schematic. 3. Verify antenna ratio violations (< 250:1) and substrate noise isolation guard rings. | `DRC clean: 0 violations (Pass); LVS netlist match: 100% topological equivalence with 0 discrepancy (Pass).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-02` | **3D Crown Capacitor High-k Dielectric TEM & C-V Metrology** | Field-Emission TEM (FEI/Thermo Fisher) & High-Frequency C-V Parameter Analyzer (Keysight B1500A) | 1. Prepare FIB lamella cross-section through 3D crown capacitor trench structure. 2. Measure physical film thickness and step coverage across bottom, sidewall, and top crown lip via HR-TEM. 3. Perform high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V sweep to extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and dielectric breakdown voltage. | `ALD step coverage >= 95% (Pass); EOT <= 0.8 nm (Pass); Dielectric leakage < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom bunny suit with conductive ESD booties, Pyrophoric precursor handling apron and dual-layer fluoropolymer gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and UV-blocking safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Pyrophoric precursor emergency: TMA spontaneously ignites upon contact with air or moisture! Do NOT use water on metal alkyl fires. Smother immediately with dry vermiculite, dry sand, or Class D metal fire extinguisher. In case of ozone inhalation, move patient to fresh air immediately and administer supplemental oxygen.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Ultra-high vacuum ALD exhaust manifold connected to dedicated point-of-use thermal decomposition burn-box and wet chemical scrubber. Continuous gas leak detection monitors for TMA/TEMAZ and ozone.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent ALD bubbler purging into mineral oil bubblers with inert argon ballast. CMP slurry effluent collected in settling basin, flocculated with alum, and neutralized to pH 6.5-8.0.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trimethylaluminum (TMA)** | `75-24-1` | Electronic Grade (99.999% trace metals) | `Pyrophoric liquid ALD precursor` |
| **Tetrakis(ethylmethylamino)zirconium (TEMAZ)** | `175923-04-3` | High-purity ALD grade | `Liquid precursor for ZrO2 dielectric` |
| **Ozone (O3)** | `10028-15-6` | Generated in-situ from UHP O2 | `15-20 wt% in O2 carrier gas (Strong Oxidizer)` |
| **Silica / Ceria CMP Slurry** | `1344-28-1` | Semiconductor Colloidal CMP grade | `15-30 wt% colloidal abrasive slurry` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched 3D crown capacitor trench structure post-DHF strip, completely free of native oxide.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Uniform ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 high-k dielectric stack with TiN top electrode encapsulation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Air exposure exceeding 20 minutes allows uncontrolled spontaneous SiO2 interfacial layer regrowth (> 0.4 nm), which severely increases Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and drastically degrades bitcell storage capacitance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Acoustic Microscopy Void Metrology and Destructive Wire Pull Testing: PDK setup, physical verification rule decks, and full-chip GDSII layouts pass 100% DRC/LVS sign-off and satisfy foundry commercial tapeout design rules.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Golden_180nm_PDK_DRC_LVS_Signoff_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Commercial_MPW_Tapeout_GDSII_OASIS_Archive.tar.gz`
- [ ] `ALD_3D_Crown_TEM_StepCoverage_Analysis.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Foundry Design Rule Check (DRC) Violations** | `0 violations` | Zero tolerance across full chip and seal ring | Automated batch DRC run using KLayout / Pegasus Golden Rule Deck |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) Netlist Equivalence** | `100% match` | Zero net/port mismatches, zero floating pins | Hierarchical LVS extraction against golden SPICE schematic |
| `ASSERT-03` | **3D Crown Capacitor ALD Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | `<= 0.80 nm` | +/- 0.05 nm across wafer | High-frequency 1 MHz C-V accumulation capacitance metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% clean DRC/LVS verification logs signed off by lead tapeout architect; checksum of streamed GDSII package validated against foundry MPW shuttle intake submission portal.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (SAM) Die Attach Void Inspection

### 1. Overview & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure governs non-destructive acoustic micro-imaging metrology to inspect silver-filled conductive epoxy die-attach interfaces under 180nm open-source DRAM dies bonded to leadframe substrates prior to post-packaging release.

---

### 2. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Die Attach Assembly   │
│         & Cure         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   SAM Coupling Tank    │
│       Immersion        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Acoustic Focus &    │
│      Gating Setup      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  C-Scan Raster Image   │
│      Acquisition       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acoustic Echo & Void  │
│     Quantification     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Disposition:      │
│  Pass/Fail Evaluation  │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Inspection Verification & Curing Check**:
   - Confirm die attach was performed with silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS).
   - Verify post-mount cure cycle was completed at **150°C for 60 minutes**.
2. **Sample Loading & Acoustic Coupling**:
   - Place leadframe-mounted DRAM units into the SAM fixture immersion tank using deionized (DI) water as the acoustic coupling fluid.
   - De-gas water bath to eliminate dissolved air bubbles that cause acoustic artifacts.
3. **Transducer Alignment & Focus**:
   - Mount high-frequency acoustic transducer.
   - Adjust Z-axis height to focus the acoustic beam through the back of the leadframe or top silicon surface directly onto the die-to-paddle attach interface.
4. **Time-of-Flight (A-Scan) Gating**:
   - Locate the primary interface echo on the A-scan waveform.
   - Place electronic gating specifically on the reflected signal corresponding to the silver-filled conductive epoxy bond layer.
5. **C-Scan Raster Image Acquisition**:
   - Execute an X-Y raster scan over the full die footprint (corresponding to the bonded 180nm DRAM die area).
   - Record phase and peak amplitude reflections across the die-attach plane. High-amplitude positive phase reversals indicate air/delamination voids.
6. **Automated Void Area Calculation**:
   - Apply threshold segmentation to the C-scan image.
   - Compute total contiguous and cumulative void areas relative to the full die active attach surface area.
7. **Post-Scan Cleaning & De-watering**:
   - Remove parts from immersion tank, rinse with DI water, and dry via filtered N₂ air-knife followed by vacuum bakeout at 100°C for 15 minutes.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                Die Attach & Quality Acceptance Metrics 
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                       │
  Cure Duration┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                       │
               │▒▒                                     │
Wire Pull Force┤▒▒                                     │
Epoxy Cure Temp┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
               │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
  Max Void Area┤██                                     │
               │██                                     │
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
               0.0      37.5     75.0      112.5  150.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Measurement Unit | Inspection Tool / Verification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Die Attach Total Void Area** | **< 5.0%** of total die area | `%` | SAM C-Scan Acoustic Metrology |
| **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | **$\le$ 5.0** | `°C/W` | Thermal Characterization / SAM Verification |
| **Die Attach Pre-Cure Schedule** | **150** (Hold for **60**) | `°C` / `minutes` | In-line Cure Oven Data Logger |
| **Post-Mount Wire Pull Strength** | **$\ge$ 4.0** (Mil-Std-883 Method 2011) | `grams-force (gf)` | Destructive Wire Pull Tester (25 µm wire) |

---

### 5. Context Citations
- **Source**: *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*
  - Die attach material: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS).
  - Curing profile: 150°C for 60 minutes.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: Mil-Std-883 Destructive Wire Pull Strength Testing
**Classification:** Packaging & Assembly Metrology | **Technology Generation:** 180nm CMOS DRAM (Gen 3) | **Action Type:** Buy (Test & Metrology Service / Equipment)

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Lifecycle Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Sample Clamping &    │
│    Stage Alignment     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Micro-Hook       │
│     Positioning at     │
│        Mid-Span        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Z-Axis Vertical Pull  │
│       Execution        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Force Recording &    │
│   Rupture Metrology    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Optical Failure Mode  │
│     Classification     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate & Package Fixturing**:
   - Secure the DRAM die packaged on the ceramic DIP / leadframe onto the precision vacuum or mechanical clamping chuck of the micro-pull tester (e.g., Dage / Royce pull tester).
   - Ensure stage planarity with zero tilt relative to the bonding plane of the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.
2. **Micro-Hook Tooling Selection & Inspection**:
   - Select a calibrated tungsten-carbide micro-hook sized for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire (hook radius $r \approx 30\text{--}40\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Perform optical inspection under microscope to verify the hook is clean, burr-free, and free of metallic debris.
3. **Hook Alignment & Mid-Span Engagement**:
   - Align the hook under high-magnification optical positioning directly beneath the wire loop at mid-span (nominally midway between the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ on-chip pad and the external leadframe post).
   - Ensure the pull angle is strictly perpendicular ($90^\circ \pm 5^\circ$) to the substrate/die surface.
4. **Z-Axis Controlled Destructive Pull**:
   - Zero and calibrate the load cell dynamically.
   - Initiate the automated vertical pull in Z-direction at a continuous rate until physical wire rupture occurs.
   - Continuously log the real-time tensile force curve up to failure.
5. **Rupture Metrology & Failure Mode Classification**:
   - Record the peak destructive pull force (in grams-force, $\text{gf}$).
   - Inspect the fracture site under optical microscope at $\ge 100\times$ magnification:
     - **Acceptable Failure Mode**: Wire break occurring cleanly within the wire span (mid-span ductile necking/rupture).
     - **Rejectable Failure Mode**: Bond interface lifting/peeling from the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pad metallization, cratering through pad dielectric/silicon, or separation at the leadframe stitch/wedge interface.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                                                        
                             ┌─────────────────────────┐
                             │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒          │
Pad Metal Thickness (x0.1 um)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒          │
     Pull Force Margin Target┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                             │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
        Min Pull Force (25um)┤█████████████████        │
                             │█████████████████        │
                             └┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬┘
                             0.0   1.5   3.0   4.5  6.0 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Status / Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Destructive Pull Force** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Pass threshold per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire |
| **Failure Location Distribution** | $100\%$ within wire span | $\%$ of tested wires | Zero interface peeling/lift permitted |
| **Pad Metallization Integrity** | Interconnect film thickness $350 \pm 5\%$ ($R_s < 0.08$) | $\text{nm}$ ($\Omega/\square$) | No pad peel or underlying layer cratering on $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pads |
| **Bond Lift Rate** | $0$ | $\%$ defects | Total rejection if bond separation occurs at pad interface |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging]**:
  - *Standard & Pull Force Target:* "Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire."
  - *Failure Mode Rule:* "Failure must occur in wire span, not at bond interface."
  - *Bonding Wire & Geometry:* $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire or $\text{Al-}1\%\ \text{Si}$ wire connecting to $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.
- **[Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects]**:
  - *Pad Metallization Baseline:* Metal-1 thickness target of $350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$ and sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\square$ establishing substrate bonding pad layer robustness.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Destructive wire pull testing per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 on 25 µm wire must correlate hook placement geometry with mechanical stress distributions across the DRAM bond pad stack. Hook positioning at midpoint versus near the capillary ball introduces up to a 20% normal-force bias. For 180nm BEOL integration, testing must explicitly evaluate pad cratering risk where ultrasonic energy and thermal stress degrade underlying inter-metal dielectric (IMD) SiO2/SiN layers beneath the 100 µm x 100 µm Al bond pad.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Test Condition D specifies a strict minimum breaking force of 4.0 gf for 25 µm (1.0 mil) diameter gold or Al-1%Si wire. Crucially, pass criteria require recording failure modes: bond-lift failures (Mode 1 at ball/wedge or Mode 5 at leadframe stitch) indicate poor intermetallic compound (IMC) formation such as Au-Al Kirkendall voiding or non-optimized ultrasonic transducer power (60 kHz, 50-100 mW). Valid mechanical integrity demands failure predominantly via mid-span wire neck break (Mode 2/3/4) rather than pad delamination.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Destructive metrology requires dedicated automated pull test instrumentation (e.g., Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Bondtester) equipped with calibrated micro-hooks (25-38 µm hook radius) and BS500/BS100 load cartridges. Lead times for NIST-traceable calibration weights, replacement tungsten carbide pull hooks, and certified calibration fixtures represent critical procurement bottlenecks for local OSAT and pilot-line operations in Vietnam.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Executing destructive pull testing requires a balanced lot sampling plan (e.g., 5 wires per package across 10 sample packages per assembly batch) without excessive sacrifice of functional 180nm DRAM tapeout prototype dies. Metrology cycles must execute within strict Q-time windows post-wirebonding to avoid ambient oxidation or intermetallic degradation confounding the baseline packaging qualification timeline.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Ball bond lift / interfacial shear separation with pull force < 4.0 gf caused by insufficient ultrasonic energy coupling or severe aluminum oxide contamination on the 100 µm x 100 µm pad.
1. Die pad cratering / underlying SiO2/SiN dielectric fracture beneath Al pad caused by excessive capillary bonding impact force or excessive ultrasonic power during EFO ball placement.
1. Premature heel break at the leadframe stitch bond caused by micro-cracking during wire deformation and capillary clamping.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-2-01` | **Automated MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Destructive Wire Pull Force and Failure Code Metrology** | Nordson DAGE 4000Plus Bondtester with calibrated 100 gf (BS100) load cartridge, 30 µm radius tungsten wire pull hook, optical positioning microscope (50x-200x) with CCD digital reticle. | 1. Position test package on precision X-Y motorized stage beneath optical microscope reticle. 2. Align 30 µm pull hook directly underneath the 25 µm Au wire loop at 0.5 span length (mid-span between on-chip ball pad and leadframe stitch). 3. Lower hook until clear of loop base, then actuate automated vertical Z-axis pull stroke at a constant speed of 100 µm/s until mechanical fracture occurs. 4. Record peak force (gf) and record optical failure mode (Mode 1: Ball lift, Mode 2: Neck break, Mode 3: Mid-span break, Mode 4: Heel break, Mode 5: Stitch lift, Mode 6: Pad cratering). 5. Repeat across 30 consecutive wire bonds across 3 sample dies. | `Peak pull force must be >= 4.0 gf across 100% of tested wires (30/30). Zero instances of bond pad lift (Mode 1) or pad cratering (Mode 6); wire rupture must occur exclusively in wire neck or mid-span (Modes 2, 3, or 4).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-2-02` | **Post-Pull Bond Pad IMD Cratering and Residual Footprint Inspection Metrology** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM) with Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS) and Optical Nomarski Differential Interference Contrast Microscope. | 1. Inspect exposed bond pad sites under high-resolution optical microscope (1000x) and FE-SEM at 10 kV beam energy. 2. Verify pad surface morphology for bare silicon, torn dielectric, or cratered Si substrate under the fractured 100 µm x 100 µm aluminum pad metallization. 3. Perform EDS line scan across fractured pad perimeter to confirm gold-aluminum intermetallic coverage (AuAl2/Au4Al) and verify absence of exposed Inter-Metal Dielectric (SiO2/SiN) cratering. | `Residual bonded gold coverage >= 80% of original ball foot area with zero visible underlying oxide cracking, silicon micro-fracture, or metal peeling (0% cratering rate on all evaluated pads).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, Class 100/ISO 5 cleanroom-compatible ESD-safe nitrile gloves (powder-free), ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, Lint-free cleanroom smock and conductive ESD heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for minimum 15 minutes. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Relocate to fresh air immediately. Mechanical micro-hook puncture: Wash wound with antiseptic solution and apply sterile dressing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom laminar airflow bench (ISO Class 5) with minimum 90 FPM air velocity; local exhaust ventilation for solvent wipe cleaning of test stages.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-soaked wipes in dedicated sealed flammable waste containers; store sheared micro-wire scrap (Au/Al) in labeled hazardous metallurgical reclamation containers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Dry Compressed Nitrogen (Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly thermosonic-bonded 25 µm Au/Al wire loops over 100 µm x 100 µm Al pads on cured Ablebond 84-1LMIS die attach leadframes; clean, dry, void-free.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Destructively tested fractured wire loops with exposed bond foot remnants and leadframe post-pull surfaces, preserved in dry desiccated environment.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding allowable queue time in ambient air causes surface oxidation of aluminum bond pads and moisture-driven galvanic corrosion of Au-Al intermetallic couples, leading to artificial degradation of interfacial bond strength.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical and statistical validation of destructive wire pull strength per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 Test Condition D for 25 µm thermosonic ball-bonded DRAM packaging prototypes, verifying pull force margins and zero-cratering integrity.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `mil_std_883_wire_pull_statistical_distribution.csv`
- [ ] `wire_bond_pull_failure_analysis_report.pdf`
- [ ] `sem_eds_bond_pad_cratering_micrographs.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Minimum individual wire pull strength across all tested 25 µm gold wire bonds** | `>= 4.0 gf` | +/- 0.05 gf gauge measurement error | Calibrated 100 gf load cell measurement during MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 pull cycle |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Mean statistical process wire pull force (Cpk >= 1.67)** | `8.5 gf` | +/- 1.5 gf | Normal distribution statistical analysis of 30-point pull force test dataset |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Rate of bond lift (Mode 1) or pad cratering (Mode 6) failures** | `0.0%` | 0.0% | Optical Nomarski inspection and FE-SEM post-pull fracture surface review |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful execution of destructive pull tests on 30 sample bonds across 3 packaging units showing 100% compliance with pull force >= 4.0 gf, standard Cpk >= 1.67, zero pad cratering or bond lift failure modes, and formal engineering approval of the signed metrology report.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Packaging Interconnect Failure Mode & Bond Interface Analysis

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Wirebond interconnect reliability at the 180nm DRAM node demands strict mechanical decoupling from die-attach thermomechanical stress; non-uniform epoxy curing induces substrate warpage that elevates shear stress on corner bond pads (100 um x 100 um), threatening pad lift and cratering during high-speed ultrasonic energy transfer.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Thermosonic Au-Al intermetallic compound (IMC) growth (predominantly Au4Al and Au5Al2) must be strictly governed; excessive thermal exposure during 150°C curing or poor acoustic impedance matching induces Kirkendall voiding at the pad metallurgical boundary, causing heel cracking or interfacial bond lifting under sub-4.0 gf pull stress.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-source vulnerability on Mil-Spec 99.99% Au wire (25 um) and Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled epoxy necessitates qualified secondary sourcing of Al-1% Si wedge wire and equivalent low-outgassing conductive die attach adhesives to mitigate lead-time spikes exceeding 16 weeks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Destructive pull and acoustic void metrology gates must achieve high-throughput statistical confidence (Cpk >= 1.67) without bottle-necking assembly cycle times; schedule contingency must accommodate immediate root-cause teardown upon any first-pass pull failure below Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 thresholds.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Intermetallic Kirkendall voiding and pad cratering causing catastrophic wire bond lift under shear and thermal cycle stress
1. Die-attach conductive epoxy delamination with acoustic void fraction >= 5%, inducing localized thermal runaway and substrate cracking
1. Heel fracture in wire span adjacent to capillary neck due to excessive ultrasonic transducer energy delivery during bonding

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-01` | **Destructive Wire Bond Pull Strength & Interfacial Failure Mode Metrology** | Dage 4000Plus Bondtester with calibrated 0-100 gf wire pull hook, 25 um hook radius, and optical stereomicroscope (100x magnification) | Position pull hook beneath midpoint of 25 um wire loop; execute vertical pull at a controlled rate of 1.0 mm/s until mechanical separation occurs; record peak force in grams-force (gf); inspect fracture site under 100x optical magnification to categorize failure mode (wire break, heel crack, ball lift, or pad cratering). | `Peak pull force >= 4.0 gf per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011; 100% of failures must occur within the wire loop span; zero occurrences (0%) of ball lift, bond pad peeling, or silicon cratering.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-02` | **C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Die Attach Void Area Quantification** | Sonix Echo C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) with 100 MHz high-frequency focused acoustic transducer in deionized water bath | Submerge packaged unit in DI water coupling bath; align 100 MHz transducer focal plane precisely at the silicon die-to-die-attach epoxy interface; execute raster scan with 5 um step resolution across the complete die active area; capture acoustic reflection amplitude data; apply image threshold segmentation to calculate total interface void percentage. | `Total accumulated void area must be < 5.0% of nominal die footprint area; single localized void area must not exceed 0.5 mm^2; zero continuous void channels extending from die center to edge perimeter.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (double-gloving protocol), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and conductive shoe covers, Vapor-tight full face shield for resin dispensing and chemical cleanout operations
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately strip contaminated garments and wash skin with copious water and mild soap for >= 15 minutes; Eye contact: Flush open eyes under emergency eye wash station for >= 15 minutes and seek ophthalmological evaluation; Inhalation: Move victim immediately to fresh air; Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting, rinse mouth thoroughly with water, and seek immediate emergency medical care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operate epoxy dispensing and thermal curing exhaust under dedicated Class 100 chemical fume hood with minimum 100 LFM face velocity; curing ovens must vent directly to dedicated acid/solvent scrubbed exhaust.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Uncured epoxy paste and contaminated applicator tips must be collected in closed, vapor-rated hazardous chemical waste containers; collect liquid wash solvents in dedicated solvent carboys for disposal via licensed certified hazardous waste management services.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silver Flake (Conductive Filler)** | `7440-22-4` | Technical Grade (Filler) | `70-80% wt` |
| **Bisphenol-A Diglycidyl Ether Epoxy Resin** | `25068-38-6` | Electronic Grade | `15-25% wt` |
| **Dicyandiamide (Epoxy Curing Agent)** | `461-58-5` | Reagent Grade | `1-5% wt` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly cured die attach post-bake; 100 um x 100 um Al pad surfaces clean, free of organic outgassing residues, moisture, and native oxide thickness <= 3.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully bonded 25 um Au ball/wedge bonds with hermetic intermetallic interface, clean pad perimeter, and zero epoxy bleed contamination.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture condensation and native alumina passivation thickening on bonding pads degrade ultrasonic energy coupling, resulting in non-stick on pad (NSOP), poor Au-Al weld intermixing, and interfacial bond liftoff.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Robust packaging interconnect validation for Gen 3 180nm open-source DRAM chip dies, verifying compliant thermosonic Au ball bonding to 100 um x 100 um pads and conductive die attach integrity meeting Mil-Std-883 standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PKG_INTERCONNECT_WIREPULL_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `DIE_ATTACH_CSAM_VOID_ANALYSIS.tiff`
- [ ] `INTERFACIAL_FAILURE_MODE_REPORT.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean destructive wire pull strength across all measured sample loops meets or exceeds Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 minimum threshold** | `>= 6.5 gf` | +/- 0.5 gf | Dage 4000Plus automated bond pull metrology over 30 test bonds |
| `ASSERT-02` | **C-SAM cumulative void area under attached DRAM die interface remains below maximum allowable reliability envelope** | `< 3.0%` | +/- 0.5% | 100 MHz acoustic reflection image histogram thresholding on Sonix Echo C-SAM |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Die attach thermal resistance R_th path to leadframe package flag meets thermal dissipation baseline** | `<= 4.5 C/W` | +/- 0.3 C/W | Transient thermal impedance analyzer test bench |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 30 consecutive wire pull measurements yielding zero failures below 4.0 gf with zero interfacial ball lifts or cratering, accompanied by C-SAM verification confirming < 5.0% total voiding across the entire die footprint.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Bond Shear and Wire Pull Destructive Failure Classification

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Destructive bond testing on 180nm DRAM pads directly evaluates the intermetallic compound (IMC) kinetics between 25 um 4N Au wire and the top aluminum metallization (Al-0.5%Cu, 1.0 um thick). Over-ultrasonic energy or misaligned tool contact during ball bonding induces micro-cracking in the underlying inter-metal dielectric (TEOS/SiN stack) or silicon substrate beneath the 100 um x 100 um pad, leading to pad cratering during pull/shear testing. The metrology pipeline must systematically differentiate wire neck fracture, mid-span tensile break, and IMC shear from destructive pad lift-off or dielectric fracture.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 (wire pull) and JEDEC JESD22-B116 / ASTM F1269 (ball bond shear), for 25 um Au wire bonded to Al pad metallization, acceptable minimum shear force must exceed 15.0 grams-force with ductile Au residual sheared area >= 75%, and wire pull strength must exceed 4.0 grams-force with primary failure occurring in the wire span or neck (heat-affected zone). Any bond shear exhibiting interfacial peel without residual gold or any wire pull showing pad cratering indicates unacceptable metallization interdiffusion, excessive Kirkendall voiding, or insufficient ultrasonic energy transfer.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dual-sourcing of 25 um 99.99% (4N) gold wire (e.g., Heraeus or Tanaka) requires tight spool-to-spool yield strength (8-12% elongation, 16-22 cN breaking load) to ensure test reproducibility. Hook and shear tool consumable wear (tungsten carbide shear tool tips and hardened tool steel pull hooks) requires replacement after every 2,500 tests or whenever edge tip chipping exceeds 2 um under optical inspection to avoid artifact shear readings and pad gouging.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Destructive testing consumes 5 units per lot (30 bonds per unit, 150 pull tests and 150 shear tests total) as a statistical gate before lot disposition to final ceramic DIP/QFN packaging. Testing must execute within a strict 60-minute window post-wirebonding to catch real-time ultrasonic generator drift, with immediate MES lot hold triggered if any single bond shear displays cratering or pull strength drops below the 4.0 gf statistical process control threshold.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Silicon pad cratering beneath the 100 um x 100 um DRAM bonding pad caused by excessive ultrasonic power (transducer overdrive) propagating micro-fractures through the underlying dielectric stack.
1. Interfacial delamination (non-stick on pad / lift-off) due to native aluminum oxide accumulation, photoresist residue, or post-plasma de-scum queue time expiration.
1. Heavily weakened Heat-Affected Zone (HAZ) wire neck snapping below 3.0 gf resulting from excessive Electronic Flame-Off (EFO) spark duration or current spike during free-air ball formation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-1-01` | **Thermosonic Au Ball Bond Shear Strength and Remnant Intermetallic Metrology** | Dage 4000Plus / Nordson Dage Multi-Function Bondtester equipped with DS100G shear cartridge (0.1 gf resolution) and tungsten carbide shear tool (50 um width, 5 um tool-to-pad standoff height). | 1. Calibrate DS100G load cell zero point and optical touchdown sensor. 2. Align shear tool perpendicular to ball center, setting shear standoff height to 5.0 um above pad surface. 3. Advance shear tool horizontally across the ball bond at 100 um/s test speed until ball detachment. 4. Record peak shear force in grams-force (gf). 5. Inspect sheared footprint under optical microscope at 200x magnification to categorize failure mode: Type 1 (Ball Shear / Ductile Au tearing), Type 2 (Intermetallic Shear), Type 3 (Pad Lift), Type 4 (Pad Cratering). Repeat across 30 consecutive ball bonds. | `Peak shear force must be >= 15.0 grams-force for all tested bonds with Mean >= 22.0 gf and Cpk >= 1.33. Minimum 75% of pad bond area must retain Au-Al intermetallic / sheared gold remnant. 100% of bonds must classify as Type 1 or Type 2; zero occurrences of Type 3 (Pad Lift) or Type 4 (Pad Cratering) permitted.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-1-02` | **Destructive Wire Pull Test and Break Mode Classification per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011** | Nordson Dage 4000Plus Bondtester equipped with WP100G hook cartridge (precision calibrated to +/-0.05 gf) and 1.5 mil diameter hardened steel wire pull hook. | 1. Position pull hook beneath wire apex at mid-span position (50% distance between first ball bond and second wedge/leadframe bond). 2. Initiate vertical Z-axis pull test at a uniform pull speed of 500 um/s until wire failure occurs. 3. Record peak tensile force at fracture. 4. Record failure location mode: Mode A (Wire break in span), Mode B (HAZ neck break above ball), Mode C (Ball lift-off from Al pad), Mode D (Leadframe stitch/wedge lift), Mode E (Dielectric / pad cratering). 5. Test 30 wire interconnects per package across 5 sample units (n = 150). | `Tensile pull breaking force must be >= 4.0 grams-force for every individual wire with Lot Mean >= 6.5 gf and Standard Deviation <= 0.8 gf. 100% of failures must occur in Mode A (wire span) or Mode B (HAZ neck). Zero occurrences of Mode C, D, or E permitted across all 150 sampled wires.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static, powder-free, chemical resistant), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields for mechanical flying wire protection, Static dissipative ESD lab coat and grounded conductive heel straps, High-purity lint-free finger cots during precision hook/tool alignment
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye exposure to cleaning solvent (IPA), flush immediately with continuous copious isotonic eyewash or potable water for >= 15 minutes. For mechanical puncture from broken 25 um Au wire or tungsten carbide shear tool tip, wash wound with sterile antiseptic solution, apply direct sterile dressing, and seek medical attention for micro-splinter extraction.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom ISO Class 6 laminar airflow workbench with local exhaust ducting operating at minimum 100 LFM face velocity for IPA cleaning wipe solvent vapor dispersion.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All fractured 4N gold wires, leadframes, and clipped bond remnants must be collected in an anti-static precious metal reclamation container. IPA-soaked lint-free wipes must be placed in sealed, designated hazardous flammable waste disposal bins.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Semiconductor Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 Ultra-Pure | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Completed thermosonic ball bonding on 100 um x 100 um Al-0.5%Cu pads with 25 um Au wire and silver-filled epoxy die attach cured at 150°C for 60 min; bond pads clean of flux and corrosion residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Destructively tested bond pads with sheared Au ball remnants, fractured wire stubs, and clean fracture surfaces ready for high-resolution SEM/EDX metallurgical cross-section analysis.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended cleanroom air exposure causes atmospheric sulfur and chlorine moisture condensation, inducing electrochemical galvanic corrosion of exposed Al-Cu pad margins and artificially altering shear strength and interface fracture modes.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed statistical shear force and destructive wire pull failure classification on 180nm DRAM test vehicles per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 and JEDEC JESD22-B116, confirming robust Au-Al intermetallic formation and zero pad cratering.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `wirebond_destructive_test_data.csv`
- [ ] `failure_mode_optical_inspection_map.pdf`
- [ ] `bond_shear_fracture_interface_microscopy.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Thermosonic ball bond shear force for 25 um Au wire on 100 um Al pad** | `>= 15.0 gf minimum (Mean >= 22.0 gf)` | +/- 0.5 gf | Dage 4000Plus DS100G shear cartridge calibrated per ASTM F1269 at 100 um/s |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Destructive vertical wire pull breaking force at mid-span** | `>= 4.0 gf minimum (Mean >= 6.5 gf)` | +/- 0.1 gf | Nordson Dage WP100G hook cartridge per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 at 500 um/s |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Non-acceptable failure mode incidence (cratering or interfacial lift-off)** | `0.00%` | 0 occurrences out of 150 tested bonds | Optical stereomicroscopy at 200x with automated image classification of sheared bond pad footprint |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero occurrences of pad cratering (Mode E / Type 4) or pad lift-off across 150 pull and 150 shear tests; all ball shear forces exceed 15.0 gf and wire pull forces exceed 4.0 gf with Cpk >= 1.33, validated by Lead Packaging Metrology Engineer and QA Signoff in MES.

testcases.instrumentation: Nordson Dage 4000Plus Bondtester equipped with WP100G hook cartridge (precision calibrated to +/-0.05 gf) and 1.5 mil diameter hardened steel wire pull hook.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wire-bonded 180nm DRAM test vehicle on leadframe mounted on rigid fixture. Loop height normalized between 150 um and 200 um. Clean nitrogen purge completed; test area illuminated with fiber-optic ring light.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position pull hook beneath wire apex at mid-span position (50% distance between first ball bond and second wedge/leadframe bond). 2. Initiate vertical Z-axis pull test at a uniform pull speed of 500 um/s until wire failure occurs. 3. Record peak tensile force at fracture. 4. Record failure location mode: Mode A (Wire break in span), Mode B (HAZ neck break above ball), Mode C (Ball lift-off from Al pad), Mode D (Leadframe stitch/wedge lift), Mode E (Dielectric / pad cratering). 5. Test 30 wire interconnects per package across 5 sample units (n = 150).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Tensile pull breaking force must be >= 4.0 grams-force for every individual wire with Lot Mean >= 6.5 gf and Standard Deviation <= 0.8 gf. 100% of failures must occur in Mode A (wire span) or Mode B (HAZ neck). Zero occurrences of Mode C, D, or E permitted across all 150 sampled wires.

ppe_required: Class 1000 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static, powder-free, chemical resistant)
ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields for mechanical flying wire protection
Static dissipative ESD lab coat and grounded conductive heel straps
High-purity lint-free finger cots during precision hook/tool alignment
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin or eye exposure to cleaning solvent (IPA), flush immediately with continuous copious isotonic eyewash or potable water for >= 15 minutes. For mechanical puncture from broken 25 um Au wire or tungsten carbide shear tool tip, wash wound with sterile antiseptic solution, apply direct sterile dressing, and seek medical attention for micro-splinter extraction.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Standard cleanroom ISO Class 6 laminar airflow workbench with local exhaust ducting operating at minimum 100 LFM face velocity for IPA cleaning wipe solvent vapor dispersion.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: All fractured 4N gold wires, leadframes, and clipped bond remnants must be collected in an anti-static precious metal reclamation container. IPA-soaked lint-free wipes must be placed in sealed, designated hazardous flammable waste disposal bins.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Completed thermosonic ball bonding on 100 um x 100 um Al-0.5%Cu pads with 25 um Au wire and silver-filled epoxy die attach cured at 150°C for 60 min; bond pads clean of flux and corrosion residues.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Destructively tested bond pads with sheared Au ball remnants, fractured wire stubs, and clean fracture surfaces ready for high-resolution SEM/EDX metallurgical cross-section analysis.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Extended cleanroom air exposure causes atmospheric sulfur and chlorine moisture condensation, inducing electrochemical galvanic corrosion of exposed Al-Cu pad margins and artificially altering shear strength and interface fracture modes.

expected_result.summary: Completed statistical shear force and destructive wire pull failure classification on 180nm DRAM test vehicles per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 and JEDEC JESD22-B116, confirming robust Au-Al intermetallic formation and zero pad cratering.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Thermosonic ball bond shear force for 25 um Au wire on 100 um Al pad
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Dage 4000Plus DS100G shear cartridge calibrated per ASTM F1269 at 100 um/s

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Destructive vertical wire pull breaking force at mid-span
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Nordson Dage WP100G hook cartridge per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 at 500 um/s

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Non-acceptable failure mode incidence (cratering or interfacial lift-off)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Optical stereomicroscopy at 200x with automated image classification of sheared bond pad footprint

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Zero occurrences of pad cratering (Mode E / Type 4) or pad lift-off across 150 pull and 150 shear tests; all ball shear forces exceed 15.0 gf and wire pull forces exceed 4.0 gf with Cpk >= 1.33, validated by Lead Packaging Metrology Engineer and QA Signoff in MES.
