# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Wire Pull and Ball Shear Test Fixture Setup

---

### Workflow Architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 1: Leadframe Clamping & Vacuum Lock   │
│  - Secure package leadframe / substrate      │
│  - Ensure rigid zero-deflection mechanical bed│
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 2: Tooling & Load Cell Calibration    │
│  - Mount 100 gf load cell & pull hook        │
│  - Mount shear chisel; zero-height calib     │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 3: Automated Destructive Wire Pull    │
│  - Hook placement at mid-span (25 um Au/Al)  │
│  - Pull rate execution per Mil-Std-883       │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 4: Automated Ball Shear Test          │
│  - Shear height offset above 100x100 um pad  │
│  - Lateral ramming & shear force profiling   │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 5: Data Logging & Classification      │
│  - Classify break modes (span vs interface)  │
│  - Log statistical peak force distributions  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate & Package Fixture Loading**:
   - Mount the assembled 180nm DRAM package (ceramic DIP or QFN containing die attached with Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C) into the universal vacuum mechanical clamp fixture.
   - Engage pneumatic/vacuum lockdown to eliminate mechanical z-axis deflection during high-velocity transducer motion.
   - Align the stage using fiducial markers on the DRAM chip corners to establish coordinate axes for all $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.

2. **Metrology Tooling & Load Sensor Calibration**:
   - Install a micro-pull hook suitable for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire (compatible with thermosonic 99.99% Au or ultrasonic Al-1% Si wires).
   - Install the tungsten carbide ball shear chisel sized for ball bonds formed on $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pads.
   - Execute auto-touchdown reference calibration to register zero substrate level ($Z_0$) with a calibrated micro-load cell ($\le 100\ \text{gf}$ dynamic range).

3. **Automated Wire Pull Execution (Mil-Std-883 Method 2011)**:
   - Program the test trajectory: Position the pull hook centered at the mid-span of the interconnect wire loop between the DRAM die bond pad ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$) and the corresponding package leadframe pin.
   - Execute vertical pull motion ($Z$-axis travel) at standard controlled strain rate until mechanical rupture occurs.
   - Record the peak destructive force ($\text{grams-force}$) and optical failure code (wire span rupture vs. bond interface peeling).

4. **Automated Ball Shear Execution**:
   - Shift fixture to the shear tool position. Program vertical shear tool standoff (chisel height positioned above pad surface, clearing pad passivation but engaging the lower ball geometry).
   - Drive the shear ram laterally across the ball bond on the aluminum pad.
   - Capture continuous load-displacement curves to measure peak shear force and evaluate intermetallic bond integrity.

5. **Failure Classification & Data Recording**:
   - Inspect post-test sites using high-resolution optical microscopy:
     - Verify wire failure location: Must break within the wire span and not lift at the die pad or leadframe interface.
     - Verify shear fracture interface: Confirm cohesive shear failure within gold/aluminum bulk rather than cratering or interfacial pad lifting.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
Wire Pull Strength (25 um Wire)
Threshold: 4.0 gf Minimum
████████████████████████████████████████ 4.0 gf min (Pass: >= 4.0 gf)

Die Attach Voiding Inspection
Threshold: < 5.0% Area via SAM
░░░░░░░░░░ 5.0% max allowable (Pass: < 5.0%)
```

1. **Wire Pull Breaking Force**:
   - **Target**: $\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}\ (\text{gf})$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire (99.99% Au or Al-1% Si).
2. **Wire Failure Mode**:
   - **Target**: $100\%$ wire span fracture; $0\%$ bond interface lift / peeling.
3. **Target Pad Interconnect Geometry**:
   - **Target**: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad contact alignment without micro-cratering.
4. **Die Attach Interface Quality (Correlative Physical Requirement)**:
   - **Target**: Acoustic microscopy void area under the die $< 5\%$; Thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.

---

### Literature Citations & Local Context

- **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 & Bond Parameters**: Sourced from *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging* (Specifies wire pull test force $\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter 99.99% gold and Al-1% Si wire, mid-span failure requirement without bond interface detachment, $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad geometry, thermosonic bonding at $150^\circ\text{C}$ / $60\ \text{kHz}$, and die attach epoxy Ablebond 84-1LMIS void limit $< 5\%$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Fixture mechanical compliance and hook/shear-tool kinematic alignment directly dictate measurement repeatabilities. The auto-tester load cell must decouple high-speed Z-axis touch-down kinetic impulse from true steady-state shear/pull force sensing, requiring rigid vacuum chucking with < 2.0 um mechanical runout across 48-lead leadframe strips to eliminate false low-force bond-lift classifications caused by chuck deflection.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm DRAM packaged in leadframe configurations using 25 um (1.0 mil) 4N Au or 2N Cu wire on Al-0.5%Cu bond pads, ball shear test fixtures must maintain a shear tool clearance height of exactly 3.0 to 5.0 um above the pad metallization to avoid tool-to-substrate dragging or partial ball skimming. In wire pull testing, hook placement must maintain a strict 1:1 midpoint or 1:2 loop apex ratio according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 to ensure tensile vector resolution without pad peel bias.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying custom clamping inserts for proprietary leadframe pitches risks severe lead-time bottlenecks; modular vacuum universal workholders supporting standard 24-48 pin DIP/SOP leadframe strips must be sourced from Tier-1 suppliers (e.g., Dage/Nordson or XYZTEC) with pre-calibrated dual-axis load cells (100 gf pull / 500 gf shear) to bypass 14-week custom tooling fabrication cycles.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test fixture qualification and acceptance testing must run concurrently with incoming wirebond process development, requiring factory acceptance testing (FAT) signoff within 10 operational shifts and strict calibration tracking under ISO/IEC 17025 to avoid delaying the Gen 3 DRAM packaging reliability ramp.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Shear chisel contact gouging of the underlying passivation/silicon substrate caused by Z-height drift exceeding ±1.5 um, masking genuine intermetallic compound (IMC) joint strength.
1. Inaccurate pull-strength measurement resulting from wire hook slip or eccentric side-loading due to inadequate leadframe vacuum hold-down stiffness during dynamic hook retraction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-1-1-01` | **Automated Ball Shear Load and Tool Standoff Calibration for 180nm Bond Pads** | Automated Bond Tester (Dage 4000Plus / XYZTEC Condor Sigma) equipped with 500 gf shear load cell, 35 um tungsten carbide shear chisel tool, and optical laser triangulation standoff sensor. | 1. Clamp leadframe strip onto vacuum chuck and initiate vision-guided optical auto-focus on target Al-Cu bond pad. 2. Touch down shear tool on reference pad metallization to calibrate electrical dry-contact zero datum. 3. Back off shear tool to 4.0 um standoff height. 4. Advance shear tool laterally at 50 um/s toward the Au ball until complete shear fracture. 5. Record peak shear force (gf) and digitize residual nugget footprint via high-resolution optical camera. | `Minimum peak shear force >= 25.0 gf (or >= 5.5 gf/mil^2 across ball shear area) per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019; residual Al-Cu/Au IMC coverage > 75% on pad; zero tool-drag gouging into underlying Si/SiO2.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-1-1-02` | **Automated Destructive Wire Pull Strength and Break Mode Classification** | Automated Micro-Tester with 100 gf dynamic pull cartridge, 30 um wire pull hook, dual-axis closed-loop motorized XY-theta stage, and optical vision defect classification engine. | 1. Load leadframe strip and acquire bond loop apex coordinates using pattern recognition optics. 2. Move pull hook under wire loop apex at mid-span (50% distance between ball and wedge). 3. Raise hook vertically at constant velocity of 500 um/s until wire rupture or bond separation occurs. 4. Record peak tensile force and classify rupture mode (Mode 1: Ball lift, Mode 2: Neck break, Mode 3: Mid-span break, Mode 4: Heel break, Mode 5: Wedge lift). | `Minimum wire pull breaking load >= 6.0 gf per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011; failure mode distribution must exhibit >= 95% neck or mid-span wire breaks; 0% ball lifts or cratering allowed.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, >= 5 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with cleaning solvent (IPA), flush with copious water for 15 minutes. In case of eye contact, immediately irrigate eyes at emergency eyewash station for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids open. In case of mechanical pinch or hook puncture, decontaminate wound, apply sterile pressure dressing, and seek medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) or laminar flow hood with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) during solvent wipe-down of fixture clamps and optical stages.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-soaked wipes and broken wire debris into closed, dedicated hazardous solid waste bins; collect spent cleaning solvents in labeled, grounded flammable waste containers for hazardous disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-wirebond completed leadframes with clean, unoxidized Al-Cu pads and Au ball bonds, free of flux residues and particulate contamination (Class 100 cleanroom condition).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested leadframes with mechanically fractured bond sites, documented sheared ball pads, and vacuum-aspirated wire debris ready for optical failure mode inspection.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes pad surface oxidation and atmospheric sulfur/chloride corrosion of exposed intermetallics, artificially degrading ball shear strength and generating misleading bond-lift artifacts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full turnkey setup, calibration, and repeatability validation of automated wire pull and ball shear test fixture on 180nm open-source DRAM leadframe packages, achieving Gage R&R <= 10% across test cycles.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_180nm_wirepull_ballshear_fixture_setup_report.pdf`
- [ ] `grr_shear_pull_validation_dataset.csv`
- [ ] `fracture_interface_micrographs_gallery.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Shear tool standoff height accuracy across full leadframe strip travel** | `4.0 um` | ±0.5 um | Non-contact laser triangulation displacement sensor calibrated against traceable quartz step-height standard |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Measurement system repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) for wire pull and ball shear forces** | `6.5%` | < 10.0% | 3-operator x 10-replicate ANOVA Gage R&R study executed on 30 standardized gold wire bond loops |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Minimum pull hook positional repeatability relative to programmed wire apex** | `±1.5 um` | <= ±2.0 um | High-magnification machine vision fiducial offset tracking across 100 consecutive automated hook cycles |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful execution of 100 consecutive automated ball shear and wire pull test cycles on 180nm DRAM test packages with zero system jams, Gage R&R < 10.0%, 100% adherence to MIL-STD-883 Methods 2011/2019, and formal signoff by Packaging and Metrology council leads.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) ## Destructive Wire Pull & Shear Force Execution per MIL-STD-883 **Task Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe > Acoustic Microscopy Void Metrology and Destructive Wire Pull Testing > Packaging Interconnect Failure Mode & Bond Interface Analysis > Bond Shear and Wire Pull Destructive Failure Classification > Destructive Wire Pull & Shear Force Execution per MIL-STD-883 **Action Type:** Buy / Execution **Technology Generation:** 180nm DRAM (Gen 3) **Applicable Standards:** MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 (Bond Strength / Wire Pull Test) --- ### 1. Scope & Objective This procedure specifies the destructive mechanical pull and shear testing protocol for wire-bonded 180nm open-source DRAM dies (100 µm × 100 µm aluminum bonding pads bonded with 25 µm diameter thermosonic 99.99% Au or ultrasonic Al-1% Si wires to ceramic DIP/QFN leadframes). It defines the physical execution parameters, hook/tool alignment, and failure mode categorization required to ensure packaging interconnect integrity. --- ### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure ```text ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 1. Specimen Fixturing & Microscope Focal Alignment │ │ (Mount ceramic DIP/QFN package; vacuum chuck clamp) │ └─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 2. Micro-Hook Positioning & Wire Pull Execution │ │ (Hook placement at mid-span; pull rate per standard) │ └─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 3. Ball/Wedge Shear Tool Alignment & Lateral Thrust │ │ (Clearance height at pad interface; lateral shear) │ └─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 4. Optical / Metrology Failure Mode Classification │ │ (Verify wire span break; reject interfacial lift-offs) │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` #### Step 1: Specimen Mounting & Optical Alignment 1. Mount the packaged DRAM die (die attached via silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at 150°C for 60 min) securely onto the pull/shear tester vacuum fixture. 2. Align the optical microscope crosshairs perpendicular to the 100 µm × 100 µm aluminum pad array and leadframe pins. #### Step 2: Destructive Wire Pull Execution (MIL-STD-883 Method 2011) 1. Select a calibrated micro-hook sized appropriately for 25 µm diameter wire. 2. Position the pull hook directly underneath the wire loop at mid-span (or highest point of the loop profile) between the on-chip 100 µm × 100 µm Al bond pad and external leadframe pin. 3. Actuate vertical (Z-axis) pull motion at a constant, calibrated rate until rupture. 4. Record the peak force at break in grams-force ($g_f$). #### Step 3: Ball & Wedge Shear Force Execution 1. Position the tungsten carbide shear tool adjacent to the ball bond (for 25 µm Au wire) or wedge bond (for 25 µm Al-1% Si wire). 2. Set the shear tool standoff clearance just above the metallization layer (without contacting the 100 µm × 100 µm Al pad or die passivation). 3. Apply a lateral displacement drive to shear the bond off the pad metallization and record the peak shear force. #### Step 4: Interconnect Rupture & Failure Mode Inspection 1. Inspect the break site under optical magnification. 2. Confirm that rupture occurs in the wire span (mid-span wire neck/break) and **not** as a pad peel-off, cratering, or interfacial bond lift-off. 3. Classify and log failure codes per MIL-STD-883 failure criteria. --- ### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria | Metric ID | Parameter Description | Target Specification | Physical Units | Pass/Fail Criteria | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **AC-01** | Minimum Destructive Wire Pull Strength (25 µm wire) | $\ge 4.0$ | grams-force ($g_f$) | **Pass:** Peak pull force $\ge 4.0\ g_f$
**Fail:** Peak pull force $< 4.0\ g_f$ | | **AC-02** | Wire Pull Failure Mode Location | Wire Span | Categorical / Visual | **Pass:** Break in wire span
**Fail:** Bond interface lift-off or pad peel | | **AC-03** | Bond Pad Opening Dimensions | $100 \times 100$ | µm | **Pass:** Within lithographic alignment tolerance | | **AC-04** | Die Attach Voiding Area (Acoustic Metrology) | $< 5.0$ | % | **Pass:** Sub-die void area $< 5\%$ | --- ### 4. Verified Context & Literature References - **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:** - *Bonding pad size:* 100 µm × 100 µm aluminum squares. - *Wire specs:* 25 µm diameter 99.99% gold wire (thermosonic, 150°C, 60 kHz pulse) and 25 µm diameter Al-1% Si wire (ultrasonic, 25°C). - *Pull strength standard:* MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0$ grams-force for 25 µm wire; failure must occur in the wire span, not at the bond interface. - *Die attach baseline:* Conductive epoxy cured at 150°C for 60 min, $R_{th} \le 5$°C/W, void area $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy. --- ### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA) - **Systems Engineer Critic**: Destructive pull and shear metrology per MIL-STD-883 Methods 2011.9 and 2019.10 must correlate hook placement geometry and shear tool standoff heights against the 180nm DRAM pad layout. For 100 um x 100 um aluminum bond pads (350 nm thick Al-0.5% Cu over inter-metal dielectric), the pull hook must maintain a 90-degree vector at the mid-span of the 25 um Au wire to prevent asymmetric shear moments that mask true intermetallic compound (IMC) formation. Hook placement variability directly shifts the measured force via vector decomposition (F_measured = 2 * F_wire * sin(theta)), necessitating precision motorized stage control with +/-2 um spatial repeatability. - **Domain Physicist Critic**: Thermosonic ball bonding at 150°C and 60 kHz forms Au-Al intermetallic compounds (Au4Al, Au5Al2, Au2Al) at the pad interface. Destructive shear testing per ASTM F1269 and MIL-STD-883 Method 2019 must monitor residual aluminum coverage on the pad; a shear strength target > 15.0 gf (or > 5.5 gf/mil^2 equivalent for a ~65 um bonded ball diameter) is required. Pre-mature interfacial peeling or cratering into the underlying silicon substrate indicates excessive ultrasonic power (exceeding 100 mW transducer drive) or silicon micro-fracture under the IMD layer, which compromises DRAM peripheral sense amplifier routing. - **Supply Chain Critic**: Wire-pull hooks (tungsten carbide, 25-50 um throat diameter) and shear tool chisels (carbide or diamond tipped with 50-75 um blade width) suffer tip wear, contamination accumulation, and chipping across high-volume sample lots. Sourcing certified calibrated hooks and shear tool blanks with ISO/IEC 17025 load cell verification from local precision tooling vendors in Southeast Asia is essential to eliminate a 6-to-8 week lead time dependency on US/Japanese metrology suppliers. - **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Executing destructive sample lot testing across 5 packaged units per MPW tapeout strip must be completed within a strict 4-hour window post-wirebonding to feed back bonding transducer recipe shifts prior to cavity sealing and ceramic lid encapsulation. The metrology turnaround schedule cannot exceed 45 minutes per strip, including statistical distribution reporting (Cp, Cpk > 1.33) and high-resolution optical inspection of failure sites. **Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**: 1. Die pad cratering / underlying oxide micro-fracture during shear testing due to over-driven ultrasonic transducer energy (>100 mW) during thermosonic ball placement. 1. Interfacial adhesive separation (lifted ball / lifted wedge) below 4.0 gf pull force caused by native Al2O3 oxidation on bond pads due to expired Q-time prior to wire bonding. 1. Heel crack propagation at the neck-down region of the gold ball resulting in premature tensile wire snapping below the 4.0 gf MIL-STD-883 limit. ### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench) | Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-1-2-01` | **Destructive Wire Pull Strength and Mid-Span Rupture Test per MIL-STD-883 Method 2011** | Dage 4000Plus Multi-Function Bondtester equipped with calibrated WP100 hook pull cartridge (0-100 gf range, 0.01 gf resolution, +/-0.25% FS accuracy) and coaxial optical stereo microscope. | 1. Position test fixture on motorized X-Y stage under optical microscope. 2. Align 30 um throat tungsten carbide pull hook beneath the 25 um Au wire loop at 50% span distance between die pad (100x100 um) and leadframe post. 3. Lower hook until clear of loop, then zero cartridge load cell. 4. Ascend vertically at calibrated pull rate of 250 um/s until wire failure occurs. 5. Record peak tensile force in grams-force (gf) and classify failure mode per MIL-STD-883 (Wire Break in Span, Neck Break, Ball Lift, Wedge Lift). 6. Repeat across all 24 bonded pins per test device. | `Peak pull force must be >= 4.00 gf for every wire tested across 100% of tested pins (Cpk >= 1.33, mean >= 6.50 gf). Zero occurrences of die pad metallization lift (Ball Lift) or die cratering; failure mode must be Code 1 (Wire Break in Span) or Code 2 (Break at Neck).` | | `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-1-2-02` | **Destructive Die Ball Bond Shear Force and Residual Pad Metallization Test per MIL-STD-883 Method 2019** | Dage 4000Plus Bondtester with BS250 shear cartridge (0-250 gf, 0.05 gf resolution) and precision 75 um wide tungsten carbide flat chisel shear tool. | 1. Load package onto vacuum hold-down stage and align shear chisel perpendicular to ball edge. 2. Perform automated surface touchdown on silicon die passivation adjacent to pad, then retract chisel to a standoff height of 3.0 um (+/-0.5 um) above pad surface. 3. Advance shear tool horizontally against ball bond at a controlled shear speed of 100 um/s until ball is displaced. 4. Capture peak shear force (gf) and displacement curve. 5. Inspect sheared pad remnant under 1000x brightfield optical/SEM to quantify remnant gold/IMC coverage. | `Minimum peak shear force must exceed 15.00 gf (equivalent to > 5.5 gf/mil^2 for 65 um diameter squashed ball). Inspection must reveal >= 75% remnant intermetallic/gold adhering to pad area with zero silicon/dielectric cratering beneath metal-1.` | ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes - **Hazard Classification**: `Low` - **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (powder-free, static-dissipative), ANSI Z87.1 approved safety glasses with side shields, ESD wrist strap connected to 1 MOhm earth ground, Lint-free polyester cleanroom lab coat - **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Mechanical pinch/projectile hazard: In case of broken wire fragment or hook snap impacting skin or eye, flush affected area with sterile saline eyewash for 15 minutes and seek medical evaluation. Chemical contact with IPA: Wash affected skin thoroughly with soap and water; for eye contact, irrigate immediately under running water for 15 minutes. - **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operate within ISO Class 6 / Class 1000 cleanroom ballroom with localized laminar flow hood (>0.45 m/s laminar face velocity). Local exhaust ventilation is required during solvent wipe maintenance of stage fixtures. - **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent wire fragments and clipped gold leads must be deposited in dedicated ESD-safe precious metal reclamation bins. IPA wipes must be disposed of in sealed, fire-rated hazardous solvent waste containers for high-temperature incineration. **Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**: | Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Cleanroom Grade | `99.9%` | | **Nitrogen (Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 (99.999%) | `100.0%` | ### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints - **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours` - **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly wire-bonded 180nm DRAM packages post-curing of Ablebond 84-1LMIS (150°C, 60 min) with unoxidized gold wire loops and intact Al-Cu bond pads free of moisture condensation and organic particulate. - nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Bond Fracture Surface SEM Metrology & Failure Mode Classification

### 1. Context & Scope
- **Domain**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | Packaging & Metrology
- **Die Interconnect Geometry**: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads to leadframe pins.
- **Wire Technology**: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire (Thermosonic Ball Bonding) or $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $\text{Al-}1\%\ \text{Si}$ wire (Ultrasonic Wedge Bonding).
- **Objective**: Quantitative SEM imaging and failure mode classification of bond fracture interfaces following destructive wire pull or bond shear testing, ensuring compliance with **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011**.

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Sample Decap /     │
│      Destructive       │
│       Pull-Shear       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      SEM Specimen      │
│  Mounting & Grounding  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    High-Resolution     │
│   Secondary Electron   │
│      SEM Imaging       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  EDX / Fracture Mode   │
│     Classification     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Acceptance       │
│     Verification &     │
│        Release         │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Specimen Isolation & Mounting**:
   - Secure the mechanically tested DRAM leadframe/package substrate onto a dedicated aluminum SEM pin stub using conductive carbon tape or silver paste.
   - Ground the leadframe to avoid surface electron charging on unpassivated ceramic or epoxy regions.

2. **Chamber Evacuation & Beam Setup**:
   - Pump the SEM specimen chamber down to high vacuum ($< 1 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{Pa}$).
   - Set the electron acceleration voltage to $10\ \text{kV} - 15\ \text{kV}$ with a working distance (WD) of $8\ \text{mm} - 10\ \text{mm}$ to balance depth-of-field across the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Al bond pad.

3. **Fracture Surface Topography Inspection (Secondary Electron Mode)**:
   - Align the secondary electron (SE) detector at $500\times$ magnification to inspect the full $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pad boundary.
   - Increase magnification to $2,000\times - 10,000\times$ across the bond interface and wire remnant:
     - **Mode 1 (Mid-Span Wire Break - Desired)**: Ductile cup-and-cone dimple morphology along the $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire neck/span.
     - **Mode 2 (Heel Break)**: Micro-fracture at the neck/wedge transition without pad delamination.
     - **Mode 3 (Bond Lift-Off / Interfacial Failure - Defect)**: Planar detachment between the Au ball/Al wedge and the Al pad surface.
     - **Mode 4 (Cratering / Dielectric Tear - Critical Defect)**: Under-pad silicon/inter-metal dielectric crack or tear beneath the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pad.

4. **Intermetallic & Elemental Spot Verification (EDX)**:
   - Perform spot Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX) at the fracture plane to confirm interfacial intermetallic compound (IMC) formation ($\text{Au-Al}$ phases) and check for halogen contamination or residual oxidation on the Al bond pad.

5. **Data Logging & Run Rejection Trigger**:
   - Quantify remnant bond coverage area on the pad ($> 75\%$ residual bonded area required when ball shear is applied).
   - If interfacial bond lift or cratering is detected, flag the assembly lot for ultrasonic power ($50 - 100\ \text{mW}$), stage temperature ($150^\circ\text{C}$), or duration ($20 - 30\ \text{ms}$) recalibration.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Method / Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Wire Pull Strength** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 ($25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire) |
| **Bond Failure Mode** | Wire span rupture (100% non-interface) | Failure mode count | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 / SEM SE mode |
| **Bond Pad Clearance Margin** | Entire bond within $100 \times 100$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Metrology SEM $500\times$ inspection |
| **Interfacial Lift-off / Cratering Rate** | $0$ | $\%$ (zero tolerance) | SEM fractography analysis |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations
- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - Pad dimensions: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
  - Wire diameters and materials: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ Au wire (thermosonic ball bonding, capillary at $150^\circ\text{C}$, $60\ \text{kHz}$, $50 - 100\ \text{mW}$, $20 - 30\ \text{ms}$) and $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $\text{Al-}1\%\ \text{Si}$ wire (ultrasonic wedge bonding at $25^\circ\text{C}$).
  - Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 specification: Pull test force $\ge 4.0\ \text{gf}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire with failure strictly constrained to the wire span rather than the bond interface.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-destructive shear/pull fracture surfaces must establish an unambiguous traceability link from sub-micron intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage back to wafer-level metallization (Al-0.5%Cu pad finish) and bonder ultrasonic transducer power logs. Without automated high-resolution SEM/EDX mapping, distinguishing between brittle Au-Al/Cu-Al Kirkendall void rupture and underlying SiO2/low-k dielectric cratering risks improper yield attribution between fab BEOL and OSAT packaging lines.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-magnification FE-SEM imaging (10,000x to 50,000x at low accelerating voltage 3-5 kV) is required to resolve micro-dimple ductile rupture versus faceted cleavage across the fractured ball neck or bond-pad interface. Energy Dispersive X-Ray Spectroscopy (EDX) beam voltage must be strictly calibrated (10-15 kV) to prevent over-penetration into the barrier/inter-metal dielectric while quantifying IMC species (e.g., Au4Al, Au5Al2, or Cu9Al4) and identifying halogen contamination (Cl, F, Br) that drives stress corrosion cracking.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standardizing on non-proprietary SEM stub fixturing and open data formats (TIFF with calibrated pixel metadata and NIST-traceable magnification standards) avoids OSAT-specific vendor lock-in. Ensuring dual-sourcing for conductive carbon/copper mounts and low-vacuum environmental SEM (ESEM) capability mitigates bottlenecks when inspecting non-conductive epoxy-encapsulated package decapsulation residues.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To maintain Gen 3 packaging metrology schedules, cycle time per sheared bond site classification must remain under 12 minutes total (including chamber pump-down, autofocus, multi-point EDX acquisition, and automatic failure mode tagging per MIL-STD-888 / JEDEC JESD22-B116 standards). Failure mode reports must immediately flag unbonded pad metallization lift to halt upstream thermosonic bonders.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dielectric cratering under bond pad (inter-level dielectric fracture beneath Al-Cu pad during shear test)
1. Brittle Intermetallic Compound (IMC) separation accompanied by Kirkendall micro-void coalescent fracture at pad-ball interface
1. Pad metallization lift-off due to poor adhesion between Ti/TiN barrier and BEOL oxide layer

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-1-3-01` | **FE-SEM Topographical Fracture Surface Morphology & Ductile-to-Brittle Area Ratio Analysis** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM) equipped with Secondary Electron (SE) and In-Lens detectors, calibrated with NIST SRM 484 magnification standard | 1. Load mounted fracture specimen into FE-SEM load lock and pump chamber to operating vacuum. 2. Navigate to fractured bond pad coordinate at 500x magnification to center Region of Interest (ROI). 3. Increase magnification to 15,000x; adjust beam tilt to 30 degrees for topographic contrast; set working distance to 5.0 mm. 4. Acquire 2048x1536 16-bit SE image across fractured remnant. 5. Perform digital image segmentation to calculate total residual area, ductile dimple area, and brittle cleavage/interfacial separation area. | `Fracture surface must exhibit >= 85.0% ductile dimple failure within the core wire/ball matrix; brittle cleavage or interfacial separation area must not exceed 15.0%; zero evidence of SiO2/low-k dielectric cratering below pad barrier layer.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-1-3-02` | **Energy Dispersive X-Ray Spectroscopy (EDX) Intermetallic Phase and Halogen Contamination Mapping** | Silicon Drift Detector (SDD) EDX System integrated with SEM, beam accelerating voltage set to 12.0 kV, dead-time maintained at 25-35% | 1. Focus at 5,000x magnification over the residual bond pad footprint. 2. Define 5-point spot analysis matrix across periphery and center of residual IMC foot. 3. Acquire spectral counts for 60 live seconds per spot. 4. Run full-field elemental net intensity mapping for Al-K, Au-M (or Cu-K), Ti-K, Si-K, Cl-K, and Br-K. 5. Quantify atomic percentage ratios (Au:Al or Cu:Al) and scan for halogen peak thresholds. | `IMC coverage across bonded area must exceed 70.0% of total footprint; Au:Al atomic ratio within nominal stable phase limits (50-80 at% Au); Chlorine (Cl) and Bromine (Br) contaminant peaks must each remain below detection limit (< 0.10 atomic %).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`

- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin exposure: Flush affected area with copious tepid water for >= 15 minutes while removing contaminated PPE. Eye exposure: Irrigate eye immediately at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Inhalation of organic carrier vapors: Evacuate subject to fresh air immediately; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing becomes labored.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Intermetallic Compound (IMC) and Bond Interface Cross-Section Metrology

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-038`  
**Process Step:** Gen 3 (180nm DRAM Chip Tapeout & Assembly) > Packaging Interconnect Failure Mode & Bond Interface Analysis  
**Action Type:** Buy / External Qualification & In-House Analytical Verification  

---

### 1. Metrology Process Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Sample Decapsulation  │
│      & Die Mount       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Precision        │
│   Cross-Sectioning &   │
│       FIB Polish       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  SEM/EDX Interface &   │
│   IMC Phase Mapping    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Kirkendall Void &    │
│      Interfacial       │
│       Inspection       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Mil-Std Wire Pull    │
│      Correlation       │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Sample Preparation & Mounting:**
   - Select DRAM dies attached to the leadframe with silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at **150°C for 60 min**.
   - Verify die attach integrity via scanning acoustic microscopy (void area must be **< 5%**).
   - Carefully cold-mount the wirebonded package (or diced chip unit) in low-shrinkage epoxy resin with curing below **60°C** to prevent post-bond thermal IMC growth.

2. **Precision Mechanical Cross-Sectioning & Ion Milling:**
   - Grind perpendicular to the bonded pads (**100 µm × 100 µm** aluminum square pads) down to within **10 µm** of the ball bond center using progressively fine SiC papers (grit 800 to 4000).
   - Polish with diamond suspensions (3 µm down to 0.25 µm), followed by a final argon ion beam cross-section polish (or Focused Ion Beam / FIB mill) at **5 kV, 100–300 pA** to eliminate smear across the gold-aluminum / aluminum-silicon interface.

3. **SEM / EDX Intermetallic Compound (IMC) Thickness & Stoichiometry Mapping:**
   - Load cross-sectioned samples into a Field-Emission SEM (FE-SEM) operating at **10–15 kV**.
   - Inspect the bonded interface between the **25 µm diameter wire** (thermosonic 99.99% Au or ultrasonic Al-1% Si) and the **100 µm × 100 µm** Al pad.
   - Run line-scan and area EDX (energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy) across the diffusion front to verify intermetallic phase formation ($\text{Au}_4\text{Al}$, $\text{Au}_5\text{Al}_2$, $\text{Au}_2\text{Al}$, $\text{AuAl}_2$).
   - Measure continuous IMC layer coverage across the pad interface contact length (target: continuous coverage $\ge 80\%$ along the bond perimeter).

4. **Kirkendall Void Inspection & Interface Integrity:**
   - High-resolution imaging at **20,000× to 50,000×** magnification along the IMC/Al pad boundary.
   - Screen for micro-voiding, diffusion pitting (Kirkendall effect), or delamination at the pad corner regions. Total micro-void line-fraction across the bond interface must not exceed **10%**.

5. **Destructive Pull Test Correlation:**
   - Correlate cross-sectioned IMC thickness and interfacial coverage with companion pull test measurements according to **Mil-Std-883 Method 2011**.
   - Confirm rupture occurs strictly along the wire span and pull force is **$\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$**.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria Metrics

```text
                  Metrology & Physical Limit Baseline   
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
   Pad Dim (um)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
               │▒▒▒                                    │
   Die Void (%)┤▒▒▒                                    │
  Bond Void (%)┤▓▓▓▓▓                                  │
               │▓▓▓▓▓                                  │
Pull Force (gf)┤███                                    │
               │███                                    │
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
                0        25       50        75      100 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target | Physical Unit | Inspection Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bonding Pad Geometry** | **$100 \times 100$** | **$\mu\text{m} \times \mu\text{m}$** (Al) | Optical Metrology / SEM |
| **Wire Pull Strength (25 µm Wire)** | **$\ge 4.0$** | **grams-force (gf)** | Mil-Std-883 M2011 Pull Tester |
| **Die Attach Void Area** | **$< 5$** | **%** | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy |
| **Wire Bond Interface Void Line-Fraction** | **$\le 10$** | **%** | Cross-Section FE-SEM |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources Cited

1. **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging](./docs/context.yaml):**
   - *Parameters:* 100 µm × 100 µm aluminum bonding pads, 25 µm diameter 99.99% gold wire, thermosonic ball bonding at 150°C (60 kHz, 50–100 mW, 20–30 ms), room temperature 25 µm Al-1% Si wedge bonding, Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 wire pull test $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$ with wire span break, Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min, die void area $< 5\%$, package thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
2. **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench](./docs/context.yaml):**
   - *Context:* 180nm process nodes, unit cell geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), stacked capacitor over bitline integration.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Cross-sectional metrology of gold/aluminum (Au-Al) or copper/aluminum (Cu-Al) wirebond interfaces requires sub-micron structural stability and rigorous planar alignment to avoid edge rounding during mechanical polishing. FIB (Focused Ion Beam) trenching is required for true non-distorted stoichiometric analysis, as mechanical grinding induces artificial smearing and delamination of brittle Au-Al IMC phases (e.g., Au8Al3, AuAl2) in 180nm pad structures.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At Gen 3 integration, the growth kinetics of intermetallic compound (IMC) layers must be quantitatively monitored under high-temperature storage (HTS at 150°C-175°C). The transition from Au5Al2 to Kirkendall void-rich AuAl2 ('purple plague') directly dictates contact resistance and bond shear integrity over the 180nm DRAM's operating lifecycle. Continuous IMC coverage below 70% of the pad contact diameter signals impending premature interfacial shear failure.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Outsourcing Dual-Beam FIB-SEM and high-resolution metallurgical cross-sectioning (Buy action) carries turnaround latency risks of 7 to 14 days per failure analysis cycle. The supplier must maintain ISO 17025 accredited metrology tools with calibrated EDS detectors (energy resolution <= 129 eV at Mn Ka) and qualified Ar-ion milling prep capabilities to ensure repeatable void and layer thickness measurements.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement of specialized external failure analysis (FA) lab time must be synchronized immediately post-acoustic microscopy and destructive wire pull tests. Late delivery of cross-sectional TEM/SEM micrographs threatens the release of the Gen 3 leadframe package qualification milestone, requiring fixed-window service level agreements (SLAs) with 48-hour expedited turnarounds.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Kirkendall void coalesce along the Au4Al / Au8Al3 interfacial boundary causing catastrophic bond lift-off during thermal cycling.
1. Mechanical polishing smearing artifacts that artificially mask interfacial micro-cracking and micro-voiding under standard optical inspection.
1. Excessive localized pad cratering breaking the inter-layer dielectric (ILD) beneath the 180nm DRAM top metal bond pad.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-2-01` | **Dual-Beam FIB-SEM Interfacial Cross-Section & Kirkendall Void Metrology** | FEI/Thermo Fisher DualBeam Ga+ FIB-SEM with in-situ Pt gas injection system (GIS) and calibrated secondary electron (SE) detector | 1. Identify the target ball bond center using SEM at 5 kV, 0.4 nA. 2. Deposit a 1.5 um thick protective Pt sacrificial layer across a 20 um x 5 um area over the ball-to-pad junction. 3. Perform coarse trench milling with Ga+ FIB at 30 kV, 21 nA down to 10 um depth. 4. Execute fine polishing cuts at 30 kV, 0.7 nA and 5 kV, 80 pA to eliminate amorphous Ga damage. 5. Acquire high-contrast backscattered electron (BSE) and In-Lens SE micrographs at 20,000x magnification. 6. Measure total IMC layer thickness across 10 equidistant points along the 180nm pad interface and calculate void area ratio. | `Total IMC thickness must be between 0.35 um and 1.80 um; Kirkendall voiding area fraction must not exceed 10.0% of the total bond interface length; ILD beneath the metal pad must show zero cracks.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-2-02` | **EDS Stoichiometric Phase Identification Across Au-Al Bond Intermetallic Layers** | Field Emission SEM equipped with Oxford Instruments Aztec Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectrometry (EDS) Silicon Drift Detector (SDD, 80 mm2) | 1. Set SEM beam voltage to 15 kV, probe current to 1.2 nA at 10 mm working distance. 2. Define an EDS line scan profile spanning from pure Au wire ball through the IMC zone into the 180nm Al-0.5%Cu pad metal (step size: 25 nm, dwell time: 500 ms/point). 3. Perform quantitative ZAF/phi-rho-z corrections on collected X-ray spectra. 4. Quantify atomic concentrations of Au and Al to categorize present intermetallic phases (Au4Al, Au8Al3, Au2Al, AuAl, AuAl2). | `Dominant initial phase must consist of Au-rich phases (Au4Al / Au8Al3 >= 60% of total IMC volume); absence of continuous brittle AuAl2 phase layer exceeding 0.4 um thickness prior to extended HTS stress testing.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: EN 374 certified chemical-resistant nitrile outer gloves over cleanroom inner gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved indirect-vent splash goggles and full-face polycarbonate shield, Heavy-duty chemical splash apron, Laser safety glasses rated for Dual-Beam alignment optics
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with Ga or solvent adhesives, immediately flush with deluge emergency shower for 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing. For eye contact, flush with eyewash for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation. For vapor inhalation, remove victim to fresh air and administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: All cross-section preparation, solvent cleaning, and stub degassing must be conducted in an ISO Class 5 laminar fume hood with face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). Vacuum pump exhaust from the FIB-SEM chamber must be actively ducted through dedicated facility scrubbers.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent colloidal Ag residues, solvent wipes, and sample mounts in dedicated hazardous heavy-metal/flammable solvent receptacles. Liquid gallium residue must be stabilized in dedicated secondary containment and transferred to licensed electronic hazardous waste recyclers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gallium (Liquid metal ion source FIB emitter)** | `7440-55-3` | High Purity Electronics (99.9999%) | `100%` |
| **Colloidal Silver Conductive Adhesive (in 2-methoxy-1-methylethyl acetate)** | `108-65-6` | Electronic Grade | `40-60% Ag solids` |
| **Isopropanol (Solvent rinse & degrease)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade VLSI | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly separated wirebond cross-section mechanically diced or focused-ion-cut, free of organic flux residues and particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: High-vacuum compatible, desorbed, Pt-capped cross-section cross-examined under SEM/EDS and vacuum sealed in dry N2 canister.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to ambient humidity promotes rapid galvanic oxidation at the exposed Al-Au/Al-Cu bimetallic micro-junctions, generating misleading metal-oxide artifacts and surface passivation that invalidate quantitative EDS and void metrology.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete structural and compositional verification of Gen 3 wirebond pad interconnects, including high-resolution FIB-SEM cross-sectional micrographs, quantitative IMC thickness mapping, Kirkendall void area fraction quantification, and EDS phase identification.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `IMC_CrossSection_HRSEM_Micrographs.tiff`
- [ ] `Intermetallic_Layer_Thickness_and_Void_Metrology.csv`
- [ ] `EDS_Stoichiometric_Phase_Profile_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total Intermetallic Compound (IMC) interfacial layer thickness at the bond center** | `0.85 um` | +/- 0.35 um | Calibrated Dual-Beam In-Lens SEM cross-sectional line measurement across 10 distinct points |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total interfacial Kirkendall void linear length fraction along the bonded pad perimeter** | `3.5%` | <= 10.0% | Digital image thresholding and binary pixel integration on 20,000x magnification BSE micrographs |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires receipt and approval of the complete analytical package showing >= 70% continuous IMC bond area, Kirkendall void fraction <= 10.0%, no ILD micro-cracking beneath 180nm metal pads, and countersigned acceptance by the Lead Packaging Systems Engineer and Packaging Foundry Domain Expert.

critical_failure_modes: Kirkendall void coalesce along the Au4Al / Au8Al3 interfacial boundary causing catastrophic bond lift-off during thermal cycling.
Mechanical polishing smearing artifacts that artificially mask interfacial micro-cracking and micro-voiding under standard optical inspection.
Excessive localized pad cratering breaking the inter-layer dielectric (ILD) beneath the 180nm DRAM top metal bond pad.

testcases.title: Dual-Beam FIB-SEM Interfacial Cross-Section & Kirkendall Void Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: FEI/Thermo Fisher DualBeam Ga+ FIB-SEM with in-situ Pt gas injection system (GIS) and calibrated secondary electron (SE) detector
testcases.pre_conditions: Target wirebond ball sample mounted on stub with colloidal Ag paste; wire pull and acoustic screening completed; vacuum chamber pumped below 5.0e-6 mbar.
testcases.procedure: 1. Identify the target ball bond center using SEM at 5 kV, 0.4 nA. 2. Deposit a 1.5 um thick protective Pt sacrificial layer across a 20 um x 5 um area over the ball-to-pad junction. 3. Perform coarse trench milling with Ga+ FIB at 30 kV, 21 nA down to 10 um depth. 4. Execute fine polishing cuts at 30 kV, 0.7 nA and 5 kV, 80 pA to eliminate amorphous Ga damage. 5. Acquire high-contrast backscattered electron (BSE) and In-Lens SE micrographs at 20,000x magnification. 6. Measure total IMC layer thickness across 10 equidistant points along the 180nm pad interface and calculate void area ratio.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total IMC thickness must be between 0.35 um and 1.80 um; Kirkendall voiding area fraction must not exceed 10.0% of the total bond interface length; ILD beneath the metal pad must show zero cracks.

testcases.title: EDS Stoichiometric Phase Identification Across Au-Al Bond Intermetallic Layers
testcases.instrumentation: Field Emission SEM equipped with Oxford Instruments Aztec Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectrometry (EDS) Silicon Drift Detector (SDD, 80 mm2)
testcases.pre_conditions: FIB-milled cross-section polished without surface oxidation; electron beam calibrated on pure Cu standard for beam current and energy gain.
testcases.procedure: 1. Set SEM beam voltage to 15 kV, probe current to 1.2 nA at 10 mm working distance. 2. Define an EDS line scan profile spanning from pure Au wire ball through the IMC zone into the 180nm Al-0.5%Cu pad metal (step size: 25 nm, dwell time: 500 ms/point). 3. Perform quantitative ZAF/phi-rho-z corrections on collected X-ray spectra. 4. Quantify atomic concentrations of Au and Al to categorize present intermetallic phases (Au4Al, Au8Al3, Au2Al, AuAl, AuAl2).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Dominant initial phase must consist of Au-rich phases (Au4Al / Au8Al3 >= 60% of total IMC volume); absence of continuous brittle AuAl2 phase layer exceeding 0.4 um thickness prior to extended HTS stress testing.

ppe_required: EN 374 certified chemical-resistant nitrile outer gloves over cleanroom inner gloves
ANSI Z87.1 approved indirect-vent splash goggles and full-face polycarbonate shield
Heavy-duty chemical splash apron
Laser safety glasses rated for Dual-Beam alignment optics

cas_chemicals.name: Gallium (Liquid metal ion source FIB emitter)

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin contact with Ga or solvent adhesives, immediately flush with deluge emergency shower for 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing. For eye contact, flush with eyewash for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation. For vapor inhalation, remove victim to fresh air and administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: All cross-section preparation, solvent cleaning, and stub degassing must be conducted in an ISO Class 5 laminar fume hood with face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). Vacuum pump exhaust from the FIB-SEM chamber must be actively ducted through dedicated facility scrubbers.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Collect spent colloidal Ag residues, solvent wipes, and sample mounts in dedicated hazardous heavy-metal/flammable solvent receptacles. Liquid gallium residue must be stabilized in dedicated secondary containment and transferred to licensed electronic hazardous waste recyclers.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly separated wirebond cross-section mechanically diced or focused-ion-cut, free of organic flux residues and particulate contamination.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: High-vacuum compatible, desorbed, Pt-capped cross-section cross-examined under SEM/EDS and vacuum sealed in dry N2 canister.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excessive exposure to ambient humidity promotes rapid galvanic oxidation at the exposed Al-Au/Al-Cu bimetallic micro-junctions, generating misleading metal-oxide artifacts and surface passivation that invalidate quantitative EDS and void metrology.

expected_result.summary: Complete structural and compositional verification of Gen 3 wirebond pad interconnects, including high-resolution FIB-SEM cross-sectional micrographs, quantitative IMC thickness mapping, Kirkendall void area fraction quantification, and EDS phase identification.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Total Intermetallic Compound (IMC) interfacial layer thickness at the bond center
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calibrated Dual-Beam In-Lens SEM cross-sectional line measurement across 10 distinct points

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Total interfacial Kirkendall void linear length fraction along the bonded pad perimeter
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Digital image thresholding and binary pixel integration on 20,000x magnification BSE micrographs

# Standard Operating Procedure: Die-Attach Epoxy C-SAM Void Mapping and Acoustic Delamination Analysis

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM acoustic reflection mapping at high ultrasonic frequencies (100–230 MHz) requires precise acoustic impedance gate timing. If the time-of-flight window for the die-attach interface drifts by more than 2 ns due to variations in DRAM silicon die thickness (standard 180nm thinned back-grind of 200 ± 10 µm), acoustic energy echoes from the leadframe copper paddle will alias into the epoxy layer gate, creating false-positive delamination flags or obscuring interfacial micro-voids.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) under a 180nm DRAM chip must adhere strictly to MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 standards. Total aggregate voiding must remain strictly below 5.0% of the total die area, with no single contiguous void exceeding 0.5% or bridging more than 50% of the thermal dissipation path under active sense amplifier and wordline driver peripheral banks to prevent thermal runaway hotspotting.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Deionized immersion coupling water in C-SAM systems poses corrosion hazards for exposed 100 µm x 100 µm aluminum-copper (Al-0.5% Cu) bond pads if leadframes are unpassivated prior to ultrasonic wirebonding. Sourcing high-purity deaerated DI water (< 0.1 µS/cm) and corrosion inhibitors compatible with high-frequency acoustic transducers is critical to prevent batch yield loss during offline non-destructive inspection.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To maintain cleanroom cycle-time parity, C-SAM raster-scan times must not exceed 90 seconds per packaged leadframe unit. Sampling plans must implement an AQL 0.65 Level II non-destructive screen directly post-cure (150°C for 60 min) before units advance to thermosonic gold ball bonding, preventing wasteful wirebonding on packages with defective thermal boundaries.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial delamination between silver-filled epoxy and leadframe silver/copper paddle caused by moisture absorption or organic outgassing during the 150°C curing cycle.
1. Localized thermal throttling and dielectric breakdown in DRAM sense amplifiers caused by contiguous acoustic voids (>0.5% die area) acting as thermal insulation barriers (R_th > 5.0°C/W).
1. Galvanic micro-corrosion of unbonded 100 µm x 100 µm Al-0.5% Cu metallization pads caused by prolonged fluid coupling immersion in the C-SAM acoustic scanning tank.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-3-01` | **Acoustic Reflection Gate Calibration and Die-Attach Interface Total Void Area Mapping** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM Sonoscan Gen6 / PVA TePla) equipped with 100 MHz transducer (0.5 inch focal length, 0.25 inch diameter), immersion deaerated DI water tank, and digital pulser-receiver with 1 GHz digitizer. | 1. Immerse the leadframe unit in deaerated deionized water tank at 23°C. 2. Position the 100 MHz transducer normal to the top surface of the DRAM die and focus on the die-to-epoxy interface. 3. Calibrate the RF A-scan oscilloscope gate width to precisely capture the reflected echo signal between 28 ns and 34 ns post-surface reflection, isolating the die-attach interface. 4. Execute a high-resolution raster C-scan over the entire die active area (sampling resolution 5 µm per pixel, scan area 4.5 mm x 4.5 mm). 5. Apply inverted phase contrast thresholding on the reflected acoustic signal (where acoustic impedance mismatch Z_silicon to Z_void results in 100% negative phase reflection) to segment void boundaries. 6. Compute aggregate void area percentage and maximum contiguous single void area via automated image analysis software. | `Total aggregate void area must be strictly < 5.0% of total die footprint. Largest single contiguous void must be < 0.5% of total die area. No edge-peripheral voiding exceeding 10% along die scribe borders.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-3-02` | **Post-Acoustic Immersion Surface Dehydration and Bond Pad Integrity Verification** | Convection Nitrogen Purge Drying Oven (100°C), Optical Surface Profilometer / High-Power Metallurgical Inspection Microscope (1000x), and Contact Angle Goniometer. | 1. Remove leadframe strip from C-SAM water tank and immediately perform high-purity N2 blow-off (filtered 0.05 µm, 30 psi) for 60 seconds per package cavity. 2. Transfer strip to N2-purged dehydration bake oven at 100°C for 15 minutes to eliminate trapped sub-micron moisture. 3. Inspect ten randomly sampled 100 µm x 100 µm Al-0.5% Cu bond pads under 1000x optical darkfield microscopy for water spotting, staining, or oxidation etch pits. 4. Measure surface water contact angle on unbonded pad test coupons. 5. Verify that bond pad surface reflectance shows zero discoloration or galvanic pitting. | `Zero visible oxidation staining, pitting, or residue on all 100 µm x 100 µm Al bond pads (100% pass at 1000x). Pad surface contact angle must remain < 15°, confirming absolute cleanliness for subsequent wirebonding.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, 6 mil minimum), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof safety goggles, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and conductive heel straps, Lint-free moisture-resistant sleeve protectors
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with immersion bath or solvent: wash immediately with copious DI water for 15 minutes. For eye splash: flush eyes at plumbed emergency eye-wash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. For inhalation of IPA solvent vapors: move personnel to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank and solvent drying stations must operate under local laminar exhaust hoods with a capture velocity of >= 0.5 m/s (100 fpm) exhausted to the facility volatile organic exhaust (VOC) scrubber.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent C-SAM immersion water containing trace dissolved surfactants or epoxy outgassing residues must be collected in closed polyethylene drums and routed to industrial wastewater heavy-metal/fluoride treatment. Waste IPA must be collected in dedicated grounded solvent carboys for hazardous chemical disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Immersion Acoustic Couplant)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (ASTM Type I, resistivity > 18 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (IPA - Post-scan rinse solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Grade C) | `99.9%` |
| **Silver (conductive epoxy filler residues)** | `7440-22-4` | Technical Micro-Flake Grade | `70-85% in cured epoxy matrix` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly cured Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled die attach epoxy on copper leadframe (post-150°C 60 min bake), dry, unpassivated 100 µm x 100 µm Al-0.5% Cu bond pads.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Dehydrated, N2-purged, zero-residue package assembly with C-SAM mapped die-attach interface, verified ready for thermosonic gold ball bonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture ingress into micro-fissures at the die-epoxy boundary and formation of native aluminum oxide (Al2O3 > 5 nm) / hydroxide corrosion on bond pads, resulting in non-stick on pad (NSOP) and thermosonic bond shear strength failure < 4.0 gf during wirebonding.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full non-destructive C-SAM acoustic reflection mapping of the 180nm DRAM die-attach interface confirming void-free structural adhesion and thermal integrity meeting MIL-STD-883 Method 2030, followed by moisture-free pad stabilization for wirebonding.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_VOID_MAPPING_REPORT_GEN3.pdf`
- [ ] `DIE_ATTACH_VOID_PERCENTAGE_METRIC.csv`
- [ ] `ACOUSTIC_C_SCAN_INTERFACE_IMAGE_100MHZ.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total aggregate acoustic void area across the active die-attach epoxy layer must not exceed the maximum allowable threshold.** | `3.2%` | < 5.0% maximum allowable limit | Automated pixel-density thresholding on 100 MHz C-SAM inverted phase reflection acoustic image. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum area of any single contiguous void at the die-to-leadframe epoxy interface.** | `0.18%` | < 0.50% maximum allowable limit | Morphological blob analysis of acoustic gate reflection C-scan bitmap. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Package junction-to-case thermal resistance R_th derived from acoustic bonded contact area.** | `3.8 °C/W` | <= 5.0 °C/W | Transient thermal impedance tester (JEDEC JESD51-14 dual-interface method). |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% inspection pass of screened batch with total void area < 5.0%, no single void > 0.5%, zero corrosion on Al bond pads under 1000x optical inspection, and formal approval by Packaging Metrology Lead.
