# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Frequency Acoustic Transducer Selection and Immersion Couplant Calibration

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Select Transducer:   │
│    50MHz-100MHz UHF    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Immersion Tank:     │
│   Degassed DI Water    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   A-Scan Alignment:    │
│   Silicon-Die Attach   │
│        Boundary        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Time-of-Flight Gate   │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  C-SAM Scanning: Void  │
│  Metrology Under Die   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Scope & Purpose
This SOP defines the setup, transducer selection, immersion liquid calibration, and A-Scan/C-Scan time-of-flight (ToF) gating protocols for C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) metrology. It validates die-attach epoxy integrity (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min) on 180nm DRAM dies packaged on leadframes prior to or following destructive wire pull testing.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Acoustic Transducer Selection
1. Select an ultra-high-frequency (UHF) focused piezoelectric immersion transducer in the **50 MHz to 100 MHz** range (focal length $F = 8\text{ mm}$ to $12\text{ mm}$, acoustic lens diameter $\approx 6\text{ mm}$).
2. Verify transducer acoustic impedance matching layer to optimize pulse resolution across the silicon ($Z_{\text{Si}} \approx 19.7\text{ MRayl}$) and silver-filled epoxy interface ($Z_{\text{epoxy}} \approx 3.5\text{–}6.0\text{ MRayl}$).

#### Step 2: Immersion Couplant Preparation & Degassing
1. Fill the C-SAM immersion scanner tank with high-purity deionized (DI) water (resistivity $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at 25°C).
2. Degas the immersion fluid via inline vacuum membrane degassing to achieve dissolved oxygen $\text{DO} < 1.5\text{ ppm}$ to eliminate micro-bubble nucleation at the die and transducer lens surface.
3. Stabilize bath temperature at **$22.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 1.0^\circ\text{C}$** to maintain constant acoustic velocity in water ($v_{\text{water}} \approx 1488\text{ m/s}$).

#### Step 3: Z-Axis Focus & A-Scan RF Signal Alignment
1. Mount the packaged 180nm DRAM die fixture in the immersion bath.
2. Position the transducer over the die center and adjust the Z-stage until the front-surface echo (water-to-silicon top boundary) matches the nominal focal distance.
3. Lower the focus into the silicon bulk towards the backside die-attach interface (longitudinal acoustic velocity in silicon $v_{\text{Si}} \approx 8430\text{ m/s}$).

#### Step 4: Time-of-Flight (ToF) Gate Calibration
1. Isolate the RF A-scan reflection waveform originating from the silicon-to-conductive-epoxy boundary (Ablebond 84-1LMIS interface).
2. Set the electronic data acquisition tracking gate strictly around the die-attach reflection peak:
   - Gate width: **15 ns to 30 ns**.
   - Set signal phase inversion detection: positive phase indicates bonded silicon-epoxy; negative phase inversion (180° phase flip) denotes acoustic delamination/air void ($Z_{\text{air}} \approx 0.0004\text{ MRayl}$).

#### Step 5: Raster Scanning & Void Fraction Metrology
1. Execute XY raster scanning across the active die area with an optical encoder step resolution $\le 5\,\mu\text{m}$.
2. Generate the acoustic reflection C-SAM amplitude and phase map.
3. Apply binary thresholding on phase inversion pixels to quantify total contiguous and cumulative void area percentages beneath the die footprint.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                                                        
                          ┌────────────────────────────┐
                          │████████████                │
           Cure Time (min)┤████████████                │
                          │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
             Cure Temp (C)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
Max Thermal Res R_th (C/W)┤▒▒                          │
                          │▒▒                          │
       Void Area Limit (%)┤░░                          │
                          │░░                          │
                          └┬──────┬──────┬─────┬───────┘
                          0.0   37.5   75.0  112.5      
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Inspection Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die-Attach Void Area** | **$< 5.0\%$** | Maximum allowable cumulative void under die | C-SAM acoustic reflection mapping |
| **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | **$\le 5.0^\circ\text{C/W}$** | Maximum upper bound post-attach | Thermal transient measurement |
| **Die-Attach Epoxy Cure Temperature** | **$150^\circ\text{C}$** | $\pm 5^\circ\text{C}$ | Thermocouple oven profile |
| **Die-Attach Epoxy Cure Time** | **$60\text{ min}$** | Nominal soak time | Automated convection cure timer |

---

### 4. Verified Source Citations
- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**
  - *Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at 150°C for 60 minutes.*
  - *Thermal resistance specification: $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.*
  - *Acoustic microscopy defect criteria: Total void area under die $< 5\%$.*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Transducer frequency selection for Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) represents a hard trade-off between axial/lateral spatial resolution and ultrasonic attenuation through mold compound and silicon. For 180nm DRAM packaged in leadframe configurations, interrogating the die-attach epoxy interface through a 350-500 um Si substrate requires selecting high-frequency UHF transducers (typically 100 MHz to 230 MHz) with appropriate focal lengths (e.g., 0.25 to 0.50 inch in water). High-frequency acoustic signals suffer excessive attenuation (alpha ~ f^2) if the immersion couplant exhibits micro-bubbles, temperature drift, or impedance mismatch, degrading the signal-to-noise ratio below 18 dB and corrupting time-of-flight gating for void quantification.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Acoustic impedance matching between the piezoelectric element (e.g., ZnO or LiNbO3 on sapphire buffer rod), the immersion medium, and the silicon die back-surface is critical. Degassed deionized water (Z ~ 1.5 MRayl) at controlled temperature (22.0 +/- 0.5 C) must be maintained to prevent acoustic velocity drift (c_water ~ 1488 m/s, dc/dT ~ +2.5 m/s/C). Dissolved gases precipitate under high-frequency acoustic cavitation at the focal point, producing pseudo-void artifacts or false phase inversions. Calibration requires a certified flat quartz/Si standard with machined micro-voids to verify beam spot size (-6 dB lateral resolution < 15 um at 150 MHz) and RF A-scan phase polarity confirmation (180-degree phase flip for epoxy delamination).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-crystal UHF acoustic transducers (100 MHz to 230 MHz) with sapphire buffer rods and acoustic quarter-wave matching layers have extended lead times (16-24 weeks) from specialized suppliers (e.g., Sonix, PVA TePla, Nordson Sonoscan). The procurement strategy must include dual-frequency matched pairs (e.g., 100 MHz for mold-compound penetration and 175-230 MHz for backside Si die-attach inspection) and backup stock of degassed ultra-pure couplant delivery cartridges, transducer mounting fixtures, and RF coaxial cables (SMA/BNC double-shielded RG-178/RG-316) to avoid test bay line-stops.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement and calibration of the high-frequency acoustic transducer must be executed within Q2 before commercial packaging line qualification. Immersion couplant degasser and temperature stabilization modules must be checked out within 10 operational days. Delays in couplant calibration or false delamination calls directly jeopardize MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 compliance and postpone the 180nm DRAM tapeout assembly reliability signoff.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dissolved micro-bubble precipitation in non-degassed DI water couplant causing acoustic shadowing, false-positive die-attach delamination calls, and acoustic beam refraction.
1. Acoustic velocity thermal drift (> 1.5 C shift) distorting electronic gating windows, leading to reflection signal overlap between the Si die back-surface and the die-attach epoxy interface.
1. Piezoelectric crystal ringing or sapphire buffer rod face chipping causing RF waveform distortion, lowering signal-to-noise ratio (SNR < 12 dB) and obscuring micro-voids under 20 um diameter.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-3-1-01` | **UHF Acoustic Transducer Frequency Spectrum and Beam Spot Resolution Verification** | C-SAM Instrument (Sonoscan/PVA TePla) equipped with 150 MHz transducer (0.25 inch focal length, sapphire delay line), 500 MHz digital oscilloscope/RF receiver, calibrated Si resolution target with photolithographically etched micro-voids (5 to 50 um). | 1. Position transducer above polished silicon reference block and optimize Z-height for peak focal reflection amplitude. 2. Record RF A-scan pulse-echo waveform and compute Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to determine center frequency and -6 dB bandwidth. 3. Scan across calibrated micro-edge target in 1 um steps to generate line spread function (LSF). 4. Calculate full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of LSF to establish lateral spatial resolution at focus. 5. Measure peak-to-peak signal and baseline noise over 10 consecutive acquisitions to compute SNR. | `Center frequency must measure 150 MHz +/- 10 MHz; -6 dB bandwidth >= 50%; lateral spatial resolution (FWHM) <= 15.0 um; RF pulse-echo signal-to-noise ratio SNR >= 24 dB.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-3-1-02` | **Immersion Couplant Degassing and Acoustic Velocity Stability Calibration** | In-line vacuum membrane degasser, dissolved oxygen (DO) meter (Mettler Toledo / Hach), dual-thermistor temperature logging probe (+/- 0.05 C accuracy), pulse-echo acoustic velocity calibration cell with quartz standard. | 1. Measure dissolved oxygen concentration of the immersion water at the transducer head nozzle. 2. Direct 150 MHz acoustic pulse into calibrated 5.000 mm quartz gauge block at 10-minute intervals over a 4-hour continuous duration. 3. Record time-of-flight (ToF) between front-surface and back-surface reflections. 4. Calculate acoustic velocity in water and quartz across all timepoints. 5. Inspect A-scan baseline for acoustic scattering noise spikes caused by micro-bubble formation. | `Dissolved oxygen concentration <= 1.0 mg/L (ppm); couplant bath temperature stability 22.0 +/- 0.3 C over 4 hours; acoustic velocity variation delta_c <= 1.5 m/s (drift < 0.1%); zero micro-bubble acoustic burst artifacts (> 2x baseline RMS) detected.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved splash-proof chemical safety goggles, Chemical-resistant nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, dual-gloved), ESD-safe anti-static cleanroom lab coat (Class 1000/ISO 6 compatible), Closed-toe ESD protective footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with IPA or surfactant: Immediately flush eyes with sterile isotonic eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek medical evaluation if irritation persists. Skin contact: Wash affected area with mild soap and deionized water. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Move individual to fresh air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation within Class 1000 (ISO 6) cleanroom with dedicated local laminar flow hood; solvent wiping stations must have active extraction snorkel exhaust maintaining face velocity >= 100 FPM (0.5 m/s).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA cleanroom wipes collected in grounded, sealed, fire-rated flammables bins. DI water effluent routed through cleanroom industrial wastewater neutralization system (pH balancing 6.5 to 8.5) prior to municipal discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (degassed couplant)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (ASTM D5127 Type E-1 / 18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (transducer face / stage cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / MOS) | `99.9%` |
| **Fluorochemical Surfactant (optional acoustic surface tension reducer)** | `29457-72-5` | Analytical Reagent | `< 0.05% aqueous solution` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-die-attach cured leadframes with exposed silicon die backside free of organic contamination, flux residues, and particulate debris (MIL-STD-883 Class A visual compliance).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: De-wetted, blown-dry with ionized N2 gun (zero residual water droplets or watermarks), moisture-baked at 60 C for 15 min, and sealed in dry N2 purged purge box.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture ingress into unsealed die-attach epoxy package causing hygroscopic swelling, popcorn cracking during downstream wirebonding pre-heat, and galvanic leadframe corrosion.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed qualification and calibration of the high-frequency UHF acoustic transducer (150 MHz) and degassed DI water immersion couplant delivery system. Metrology establishes quantitative spatial resolution, signal-to-noise ratio, and acoustic velocity stability to perform non-destructive die-attach void inspection per MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 for 180nm DRAM leadframe packages.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TRANS-150MHZ-CAL-SPEC.pdf`
- [ ] `COUPLANT-DEGASS-METRICS.csv`
- [ ] `VOID-RESOLUTION-VERIFICATION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Acoustic transducer center frequency and -6 dB fractional bandwidth** | `150.0 MHz` | +/- 5.0 MHz (Bandwidth >= 50%) | FFT spectral analysis of pulse-echo RF waveform on polished reference quartz block |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Dissolved oxygen concentration in active immersion couplant reservoir** | `0.80 ppm` | <= 1.00 ppm | Electrochemical dissolved oxygen probe measurement at nozzle outlet |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Lateral acoustic resolution (FWHM spot size) on calibrated micro-void target** | `12.5 um` | <= 15.0 um | Edge-spread line scan profiling across laser-etched silicon micro-pattern |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 100% adherence to all three quantitative assertions: FFT center frequency within 150 +/- 5 MHz, in-line couplant dissolved oxygen <= 1.0 ppm over 4-hour endurance test, and lateral spatial resolution <= 15 um with SNR >= 24 dB. Delivery and signoff of signed calibration report (TRANS-150MHZ-CAL-SPEC.pdf) and clean post-inspection bake verification by Metrology and Reliability Leads.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-PKG-MET-038
**Title:** C-Mode Time-of-Flight Interface Gating and Die-Paddle Acoustic Reflection Raster Scanning  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe > Acoustic Microscopy Void Metrology and Destructive Wire Pull Testing > Die-Attach Epoxy C-SAM Void Mapping and Acoustic Delamination Analysis  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm DRAM MPW)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Execution  

---

### 1. Equipment & Coupling Setup
1. **Specimen Submersion & Coupling:** Place the cured leadframe assembly (mounted with 180nm DRAM die on silver-filled conductive epoxy, e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min) into the Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) immersion tank using deionized (DI) water as the acoustic coupling medium.
2. **Transducer Selection & Alignment:** Mount a high-frequency focused acoustic transducer (nominal 50–100 MHz for silicon-die/epoxy interfaces). Align the acoustic axis normal ($90^\circ \pm 0.5^\circ$) to the active front surface of the DRAM die.
3. **Focal Point Positioning:** Adjust the Z-height stage to focus the acoustic beam through the 180nm DRAM silicon substrate toward the rear die-to-epoxy attach interface and leadframe die paddle.

---

### 2. Time-of-Flight (ToF) A-Scan Interface Gating
1. **Signal Acquisition (A-Scan):** Capture the radio frequency (RF) time-domain echo waveform displaying distinct reflection peaks:
   - Front silicon surface reflection ($t_0$).
   - Die-to-attach interface reflection ($t_1$).
   - Epoxy-to-paddle back interface reflection ($t_2$).
2. **Electronic Gate Configuration:**
   - Set the Time-of-Flight (ToF) electronic gate window precisely around the die-to-epoxy attach boundary ($t_1$).
   - Calibrate the phase inversion detector: an acoustic wave transitioning from high acoustic impedance ($Z_{\text{Si}}$) into low acoustic impedance air/delamination void produces a positive-to-negative phase reversal with maximum peak-to-peak amplitude.
   - Set signal detection threshold to capture echo reflection amplitudes associated with acoustic impedance mismatch at delamination boundaries.

---

### 3. C-Mode Acoustic Reflection Raster Scanning
1. **Raster Scan Grid Setup:** Define the scan area covering the full die footprint (including active pad perimeter of $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads) plus a $0.5\ \text{mm}$ leadframe paddle border margin.
2. **X-Y Stage Translation:** Execute high-speed raster scanning along the X-axis with stepped Y-axis increment ($\Delta X, \Delta Y \le 5\ \mu\text{m}$ per pixel).
3. **Data Logging & Void Mapping:** Record peak amplitude values per pixel across the gated ToF window. Generate a 2D grayscale/false-color C-SAM interface map displaying void distributions, trapped air pockets, and interfacial delamination.
4. **Post-Scan Drying:** Remove sample from the DI water immersion tank and dry under clean dry air (CDA) or $\text{N}_2$ gun blow-off ($25^\circ\text{C}$) to avoid moisture corrosion on aluminum pad metallization.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                  C-SAM Packaging Acceptance Thresholds 
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │░░                                   │
        Wire Pull┤░░                                   │
                 │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                      │
    Cure Duration┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                      │
Die Attach Cure T┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                 │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
        Void Area┤██                                   │
                 │██                                   │
                 └┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0.0     37.5     75.0     112.5  150.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Engineering Unit | Inspection / Validation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die Attach Void Area** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ of total die area | C-SAM automated pixel area integration |
| **Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | $\le 5.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}/\text{W}$ | Steady-state thermal transient tester |
| **Die Attach Pre-Scan Cure Temperature** | $150 \pm 5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Thermocouple-monitored inline curing oven |
| **Post-Cure Wire Pull Strength Baseline** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{grams-force}\ (\text{gf})$ | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 destructive wire pull |

---

### 5. Verified Literature Citations
* **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:**
  * *Die attach epoxy:* Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\ \text{minutes}$.
  * *Thermal & acoustic spec:* Thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C}/\text{W}$; void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy.
  * *Interconnect geometry & strength:* $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad dimensions; destructive wire pull strength $\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011.
* **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects:**
  * *Bonding pad metallization:* Metal-1 thickness $350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$, sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM scanning raster step size must be deterministically matched to transducer focal spot size (-6 dB beamwidth) to eliminate undersampling artifacts and acoustic speckle, while maintaining stage scan velocity below acoustic immersion tank meniscus cavitation thresholds. Integration with automated A-scan time-of-flight (ToF) peak detection requires rigorous trigger thresholding on the front-surface echo to dynamically compensate for leadframe warpage (up to 150 um across package) without slipping the electronic time gate into the silicon bulk or paddle back-reflection.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm DRAM Gen 3 packaging, Silver-filled conductive epoxy attach lines are typically 25-35 um thick with acoustic impedance ~5-8 MRayls, sandwiched between Si die (19.7 MRayls) and Cu leadframe (44.3 MRayls). A high-frequency transducer (100 MHz to 230 MHz UHF) with acoustic focal length f=12.7 mm is required to resolve interfacial epoxy delamination from internal cohesive epoxy voids. Phase inversion (+/- 180 deg phase shift) of the reflected RF A-scan wave at the Si-to-epoxy and epoxy-to-paddle interfaces must be tracked: an epoxy-to-air/void interface produces a 100% negative reflection coefficient (R = -1.0), whereas intact epoxy-to-copper produces a positive reflection coefficient.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic couplant purity is critical; deionized immersion fluid requires continuous closed-loop filtration and degasification systems (<1.0 ppm dissolved O2/N2) to prevent micro-bubble nucleation on leadframe paddle edges during high-speed raster scanning. Ultrasonic transducers with sapphire delay lines and piezoelectric LiNbO3 or PVDF elements have 16-24 week lead times and are prone to mechanical shock degradation if stage limit switches or automated crash detection fails during rapid Z-axis auto-focus.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-Mode acoustic raster scanning represents a throughput bottleneck in assembly metrology; full-strip mapping of 64-lead QFP/QFN leadframes at 5 um raster resolution can exceed 18 minutes per leadframe. Must establish a validated sampling plan (ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 Level II S-4) or multi-transducer array architecture to enforce a takt time under 45 seconds per packaged DRAM device without compromising void area detection limits (<0.5% die-paddle delamination threshold).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Transducer focal gate drift due to thermal expansion/gradient in immersion DI water tank, causing gating window to shift out of the 30 um epoxy bondline into the Si substrate bulk or copper leadframe.
1. Entrapment of micro-air bubbles at the leadframe downset or beneath leadframe tie-bars during immersion, mimicking false positive die-paddle delamination and void signatures.
1. Leadframe paddle warpage exceeding the confocal Rayleigh range (depth of focus) of the high-frequency transducer, leading to acoustic signal defocusing and missed delamination voids along die corners.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-3-2-01` | **Acoustic ToF Interface Gate Calibration and Die-Paddle Epoxy Void Fraction Metrology** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (Sonix / PVA TePla SAM) equipped with 100 MHz UHF focused transducer (f=12.7 mm, focal spot diameter <= 28 um), 1.0 GHz digital RF A-scan oscilloscope digitizer, automated XYZ stage with 0.5 um linear encoder resolution, and closed-loop degassed deionized water immersion tank. | 1. Immerse leadframe strip fixture into degassed DI water tank and execute automated ultrasonic degas cycle for 30 seconds. 2. Align transducer normal to the die top surface; perform Z-axis focus sweep to capture the primary front-surface reflection peak (water-silicon interface). 3. Calculate acoustic flight time through silicon thickness (t = 2 * d_Si / v_Si, where v_Si = 8430 m/s for longitudinal waves, d_Si = 250 um -> delta_t ~ 59.3 ns). 4. Position the electronic data acquisition gate starting at 58.0 ns with a gate width of 14.0 ns to precisely isolate the die-attach epoxy and die-paddle interface. 5. Perform bidirectional C-mode raster scan across 5.0 mm x 5.0 mm die footprint at 5.0 um step size in X and Y directions. 6. Extract peak-to-peak RF amplitude and phase-inverted reflection map; apply threshold segmentation in image processing engine to delineate void/delamination areas from bonded matrix. | `Total cumulative void area at the die-attach to die-paddle interface must not exceed 5.0% of total die footprint area (MIL-STD-883 Method 2030.2 / IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020E); any single contiguous corner void must not exceed 1.0% of die area (<= 0.25 mm^2); signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) on intact bonded region must be >= 18 dB.` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-3-2-02` | **Dynamic Leadframe Warpage Tracking and Dynamic ToF Interface Gating Verification** | Ultra-high resolution C-SAM system with real-time hardware surface-following trigger generator, 140 MHz transducer (f=8.0 mm), 500 MS/s multi-channel digitizer, and non-contact laser confocal triangulation sensor for Z-displacement cross-referencing. | 1. Map initial leadframe topographical tilt and warpage using laser confocal displacement sensor at 0.1 mm grid spacing. 2. Synchronize C-SAM dynamic surface-tracking gate: configure hardware trigger off the Si front surface echo with fixed internal delay delta_tau = 59.0 ns +/- 0.5 ns relative to local front reflection. 3. Execute high-speed raster scan (scan velocity = 150 mm/s, raster index step = 8 um) across 4 consecutive QFP unit sites on the strip. 4. Verify that the time-of-flight gating window maintains its relative position centered on the epoxy-paddle reflection across all Z-elevations (+/- 60 um warpage profile). 5. Record RF A-scan waveforms at 5 designated control points (die center, 4 die corners) and measure gate clipping or signal drift. | `Interface gating time drift must remain <= 1.2 ns relative to local front-surface trigger across the entire 120 um warpage profile; 100% of recorded corner A-scan waveforms must maintain > 95% peak amplitude capture without window truncation; false delamination detection rate on defect-free reference die must be 0.0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles, Cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, dual-layer), ESD-safe cleanroom frock / smock with grounded wrist-strap interface, Slip-resistant water-resistant cleanroom safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For isopropanol eye/skin exposure: immediately flush eyes or affected skin with copious flowing water at dedicated eyewash station for >= 15 minutes. For aerosol inhalation: move personnel to fresh cleanroom air; seek immediate medical evaluation if respiratory irritation or dizziness persists. For DI water electrical contact: immediately de-energize high-voltage RF pulser-receiver stage via E-stop.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank and cleaning station must operate under local laminar exhaust canopy with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) to safely vent IPA vapors and surfactant aerosol droplets; cleanroom air exchange >= 45 air changes/hour (ISO Class 6 / Fed Std 209E Class 1000).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Immersion bath DI water effluent containing trace fluorosurfactant and dissolved copper ions must be routed to designated industrial wastewater treatment / heavy metal neutralization system; spent IPA must be collected in closed, grounded flammable solvent waste drums for certified hazmat recovery.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Acoustic Couplant)** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-Pure Type I (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

| **Cationic Fluorosurfactant (Wetting Agent / Surface Tension Reducer)** | `29457-72-5` | Analytical Reagent Grade | `< 0.05%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-die attach snap cure (175 deg C, 60 min in N2); leadframe and die surface pristine, dry, and free of epoxy bleed-out or condensable organic contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Acoustic-scanned units must be blown dry using high-purity ionized N2 gun (gun pressure 30 psi, ionizer offset < +/- 15V) followed by bake-out at 125 deg C for 30 minutes; leadframe copper leads free of water spots, oxidation tarnish, or halide residues.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time before post-scan bake causes moisture absorption into hygroscopic die-attach epoxy and bare copper leadframe oxidation, leading to interfacial popcorning and complete delamination during subsequent reflow/molding (MSL 3 / MSL 1 degradation).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full non-destructive C-mode acoustic reflection raster scanning of the die-attach epoxy layer and copper paddle interface on packaged 180nm DRAM units, providing quantitative void mapping, interface delamination percentages, and time-of-flight gated acoustic impedance profiles.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `Acoustic_Reflection_ToF_Gating_Metrics.csv`
- [ ] `Die_Paddle_Delamination_Inspection_Report_Rev1.pdf`

| `ASSERT-02` | **Single largest contiguous interfacial delamination void area** | `<= 0.15 mm^2` | +/- 0.02 mm^2 | Morphological blob analysis and bounding polygon extraction algorithm on inverted RF phase reflection raster data. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Acoustic ToF interface gate alignment accuracy across die area** | `59.3 ns` | +/- 1.5 ns | Digital RF A-scan oscilloscope trace interrogation at 5-point die inspection coordinates. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of sampled DRAM devices exhibit <= 5.0% cumulative die-paddle voiding with zero edge/corner voids >= 0.25 mm^2, ToF gating verified without transducer signal clipping across package warpage bounds, post-scan bake completed with moisture content < 0.05 wt%, and acoustic inspection dataset formally approved by Packaging Metrology Lead.

critics.domain_expert: At 180nm DRAM Gen 3 packaging, Silver-filled conductive epoxy attach lines are typically 25-35 um thick with acoustic impedance ~5-8 MRayls, sandwiched between Si die (19.7 MRayls) and Cu leadframe (44.3 MRayls). A high-frequency transducer (100 MHz to 230 MHz UHF) with acoustic focal length f=12.7 mm is required to resolve interfacial epoxy delamination from internal cohesive epoxy voids. critics.supply_chain: Acoustic couplant purity is critical; deionized immersion fluid requires continuous closed-loop filtration and degasification systems (<1.0 ppm dissolved O2/N2) to prevent micro-bubble nucleation on leadframe paddle edges during high-speed raster scanning. Leadframe paddle warpage exceeding the confocal Rayleigh range (depth of focus) of the high-frequency transducer, leading to acoustic signal defocusing and missed delamination voids along die corners.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-PKG-CSAM-003`
**Title:** Phase-Inversion Delamination Metrology and Die-Attach Epoxy Void Area Fraction Analysis  
**Hierarchy Path:** `BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Epoxy Die Attach & Ultrasonic Ball Wirebonding to Leadframe > Acoustic Microscopy Void Metrology and Destructive Wire Pull Testing > Packaging Interconnect Failure Mode & Bond Interface Analysis > Die-Attach Epoxy C-SAM Void Mapping and Acoustic Delamination Analysis`  
**Technology Generation:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Characterization  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the acoustic inspection, phase-inversion analysis, and automated area-fraction quantification protocol for silver-filled conductive die-attach epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min) bonding 180nm DRAM dies onto leadframe/substrate packages. The goal is to detect interface delamination, map acoustic impedance mismatches, and verify thermal resistance compliance ($R_{th} \le 5\text{ }^\circ\text{C/W}$).

---

### 2. Physical Process & Metrology Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Prepare Sample: 180nm DRAM Die on Leadframe (Cured 150°C, 60 min)"] --> B["Submerge in Deionized Water Coupling Bath (25°C)"]
    B --> C["Align High-Frequency Acoustic Transducer (50 - 100 MHz)"]
    C --> D["Set Time-of-Flight Gate: Die-to-Epoxy Interface"]
    D --> E["C-SAM Raster Scan & RF A-Scan Waveform Capture"]
    E --> F["Phase-Inversion Signal Discrimination (Positive vs Negative Peak)"]
    F --> G["Threshold Binarization & Void Area Fraction Calculation"]
    G --> H{"Acceptance Gate: Void Area < 5% & R_th <= 5°C/W"}
    H -- Pass --> I["Release to Wire Bonding (25 um Au / Al Wire)"]
    H -- Fail --> J["Reject / Quarantine for Die Shear Failure Analysis"]
```

#### Detailed Step-by-Step Procedure:
1. **Sample Preparation & Immersion**:
   - Inspect the mounted DRAM die cured with silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$).
   - Submerge the leadframe package assembly into a temperature-stabilized ($25\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$) deaerated deionized (DI) water acoustic coupling bath.
2. **Transducer Setup & Gating**:
   - Install a high-frequency focused acoustic transducer ($50\text{ MHz}$ to $100\text{ MHz}$, focal length $0.5\text{ inches}$).
   - Focus the acoustic beam onto the die-attach interface (bottom of the silicon die to the top surface of the epoxy layer).
   - Set the C-mode acoustic scanning (C-SAM) electronic gate strictly spanning the reflected RF pulse at the Si/Epoxy boundary.
3. **Phase-Inversion Delamination Discrimination**:
   - Calibrate the RF waveform polarity:
     - **Intact Bond ($Z_{\text{silicon}} \rightarrow Z_{\text{epoxy}}$)**: Acoustic impedance transition from higher ($Z_{\text{Si}} \approx 19.7\text{ MRayls}$) to lower ($Z_{\text{epoxy}} \approx 3\text{--}5\text{ MRayls}$) yields an in-phase reflection with standard polarity.
     - **Delamination / Air Void ($Z_{\text{silicon}} \rightarrow Z_{\text{air}}$)**: Reflection at the Si/air interface ($Z_{\text{air}} \approx 0.0004\text{ MRayls}$) produces a total acoustic reflection with a $180^\circ$ phase inversion (opposite polarity sign and high amplitude).
   - Configure the acoustic signal processor to flag phase-inverted echoes as delamination/void sites.
4. **Automated Area Fraction Quantification**:
   - Acquire a full two-dimensional planar C-scan image across the complete die area footprint.
   - Apply intensity and phase-based binary segmentation.
   - Compute the void area fraction:
     $$\text{Void Area Fraction (\%)} = \frac{A_{\text{void}}}{A_{\text{die}}} \times 100$$
   - Flag any clustering beneath active circuitry regions.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                        │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                   │
Actual Measured Baseline┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                   │
   Max Allowed Void Area┤██████████████████████████████│
                        │██████████████████████████████│
                        └┬──────┬───────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                        0.0    1.2     2.5    3.8   5.0 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Value / Limit | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die-Attach Void Area Fraction** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ | C-SAM acoustic imaging & automated area integration |
| **Die-Attach Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | $\le 5.0$ | $^\circ\text{C/W}$ | Transient dual interface thermal testing / T3Ster |
| **Die-Attach Epoxy Cure Baseline** | $150 \pm 5$ for $60$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ / $\text{min}$ | Calibrated convection curing oven logger |
| **Post-Mount Wire Pull Strength Integrity** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 wire pull ($25\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ wire) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Citations
- **Source:** *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*
  - *"Die Attach: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g. Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at 150°C for 60 minutes. Thermal resistance R_th <= 5°C/W; void area under die < 5% via acoustic microscopy."*
  - *"Mechanical Quality Standards: - Wire Pull Strength: Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force >= 4.0 grams-force for 25 um wire. Failure must occur in wire span, not at bond interface."*
  - *"Thermosonic Gold Ball Bonding: 25 um diameter 99.99% gold wire... pad at 150°C with ultrasonic transducer pulse (60 kHz, 50-100 mW, 20-30 ms)."*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM acoustic phase-inversion mapping must resolve interface reflections between the silicon backside, silver-filled die-attach epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablebond 84-1LMISR), and copper leadframe pad. Using a 100-230 MHz high-frequency transducer requires precise acoustic impedance (Z) matching: Z_Si ≈ 19.7 MRayl, Z_epoxy ≈ 3.5-5.0 MRayl, and Z_air ≈ 0.0004 MRayl. A true delamination or void inverts acoustic phase polarity (180° phase flip from negative to positive reflection amplitude relative to the excitation pulse), but surface roughness, tilt, or incomplete acoustic gate synchronization will induce false phase reversals, corrupting the automated void area fraction algorithm.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Die-attach voiding directly governs thermal dissipation and mechanical stress concentration in 180nm DRAM dies. MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 and IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 demand that total die-attach void area fraction not exceed 10-15%, with no single continuous void exceeding 5% or bridging across >50% of the die perimeter. A high void fraction elevates localized junction temperature (R_th_jc spikes > 15 K/W), triggering localized DRAM cell retention degradation and thermal runaway during refresh cycles.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic coupling relies on ultra-pure degassed deionized water (resistivity > 18.0 MOhm*cm, dissolved O2 < 15 ppb) to prevent micro-bubble cavitation on the leadframe surface that mimic void signatures. Coupling fluid immersion requires immediate post-scan bake-out; failure to procure semiconductor-grade dry-nitrogen desorbers and specialized C-SAM transducers (Sonix, PVA TePla, or Nordson Sonoscan) creates lead-time bottlenecks and corrosion exposure on exposed leadframe silver/copper metallization.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die-attach inspection is an inline quality gate gating downstream gold/copper wirebonding. Metrology throughput must not exceed 90 seconds per leadframe strip. If C-SAM immersion requires cumbersome manual fixturing or prolonged drying cycles, the entire backend packaging queue will breach the strict Q-time envelope between epoxy cure and wirebonding.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-bubble cavitation in DI coupling fluid yielding false-positive phase-inversion void artifacts exceeding the 10% threshold
1. Epoxy outgassing and moisture entrapment during reflow causing popcorn delamination across the Si-epoxy interface
1. Acoustic gate misalignment capturing leadframe-epoxy bottom interface instead of die-epoxy interface, masking critical interfacial delamination

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-3-3-01` | **C-SAM Acoustic Phase-Inversion Interface Delamination Metrology** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM, Nordson Sonoscan Gen7 or equivalent) equipped with a 100 MHz / 230 MHz broadband transducer (0.25 inch focal length, spot size ~25 um) and degassed DI water tank (< 10 ppb dissolved gas) | 1. Submerge leadframe strip in degassed DI water coupling bath at 22.0 ± 1.0°C. 2. Position 100 MHz transducer over die surface; verify peak RF reflection echo and adjust focal plane to maximum reflection at the die-epoxy boundary. 3. Configure gate width to 15 ns encompassing the interface echo. 4. Enable A-scan phase detection mode: monitor polarity where positive-going RF peak indicates intact epoxy interface (Z_epoxy < Z_Si, negative reflection inverted by receiver) and 180° inverted phase indicates void/delamination (Z_air << Z_Si). 5. Execute 2D C-scan raster across 100% of die area (5 mm x 5 mm) at 10 um step pitch. 6. Record raw RF amplitude and phase-inversion maps. | `Total phase-inversion delamination area must be <= 10.0% of total active die attach area; maximum single contiguous delamination area must be <= 3.0%; zero delamination detected under the DRAM sense amplifier perimeter (outer 150 um margin).` |
| `TC-DIE-ATTACH-WIREBOND-3-3-3-3-02` | **Digital Image Thresholding Void Area Fraction Calculation & Thermal Cross-Verification** | Digital Image Analysis Workstation running ImageJ / MATLAB automated segmentation algorithms, calibrated optical micrometer stage, and dual-junction transient thermal tester (T3Ster). | 1. Import raw C-scan acoustic intensity matrix into image processing pipeline. 2. Apply Otsu automated binary thresholding combined with phase-mask logic to segment void clusters from bonded epoxy matrix. 3. Execute morphological opening (3x3 kernel) to eliminate single-pixel acoustic shot noise. 4. Compute cumulative void area fraction: Area_void_fraction = (Sum of void pixels / Total die attach pixels) * 100%. 5. Measure major axis dimension of largest continuous void. 6. Mount sample to thermal fixture and measure junction-to-case thermal resistance (R_th_jc) via 100 mA transient thermal pulse. | `Computed Die-Attach Void Area Fraction <= 12.0% across the full die footprint; largest single void dimension < 300 um; junction-to-case thermal resistance R_th_jc <= 12.5 K/W (nominal baseline without voids: 9.8 K/W).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, 6 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles, ESD-safe anti-static cleanroom smock and ground heel straps, Face shield during chemical bath transfers and IPA ultrasonic cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with copious clean water or sterile saline for at least 15 minutes while lifting eyelids. Skin Contact: Wash with soap and clean running water; remove contaminated clothing. Inhalation: If IPA vapor headache or dizziness occurs, immediately remove victim to fresh air. Ingestion: Do NOT induce vomiting; seek medical attention immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank operated in cleanroom with >= 30 air changes per hour (ACH). Post-scan solvent drying and IPA rinse must be conducted inside a certified laminar flow wet bench or chemical fume hood with face velocity of 0.5 ± 0.1 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used degassed DI water may be discharged into the industrial wastewater neutralization system after monitoring pH (6.5-8.5). Spent IPA solvent waste must be collected in closed, grounded conductive stainless-steel hazardous solvent waste drums for certified hazardous disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Acoustic Couplant)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (UPW Type 1) | `100.0%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA, Post-Scan De-watering)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Bisphenol-A Diglycidyl Ether Epoxy Resin (Cured Residue Trace)** | `25068-38-6` | Technical Grade | `< 0.1% trace` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-die-attach thermal cure complete (e.g., 175°C for 60 min in N2); package surface dry, free from flux or adhesive bleed-out; die top metallization pristine.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: 100% moisture-free; baked at 110°C for 20 minutes in dry nitrogen (< 5% RH); leadframe copper and bond pads free of oxidation, staining, or coupling water residue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Water droplet entrapment or prolonged ambient air exposure induces copper leadframe oxidation and aluminum/copper bond pad passivation corrosion, causing wirebond lift failures during ultrasonic bonding and subsequent package popcorn delamination during reflow.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Robust, non-destructive acoustic metrology protocol verifying die-attach epoxy integrity, interfacial delamination, and void area fraction for Gen 3 180nm DRAM dies mounted on copper leadframes, achieving verifiable compliance with MIL-STD-883 Method 2030.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_DieAttach_Acoustic_Phase_Map_Report.tiff`
- [ ] `Void_Area_Fraction_Spatial_Distribution.csv`
- [ ] `Die_Attach_Metrology_PassFail_Certificate.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total Die-Attach Epoxy Acoustic Delamination / Void Area Fraction** | `8.5%` | <= 10.0% max limit | Automated Otsu threshold segmentation on 230 MHz C-SAM inverted-phase C-scan image matrix |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum Single Continuous Interfacial Void Dimension** | `180 um` | <= 250 um max limit | Acoustic spatial calibration caliper measurement on high-contrast RF reflection map |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-Metrology Leadframe Moisture Desorption / Dewatering Bake** | `110°C for 20 min in N2` | Moisture residual < 0.05 wt% by Karl Fischer / gravimetric balance | Thermogravimetric desorption analysis and surface contact angle measurement (> 70° on clean Cu) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal sign-off requires: 100% C-SAM scan coverage on all test dies with acoustic gate alignment verified against RF A-scan reference, confirmed void area fraction <= 10.0% with zero perimeter-bridging voids, post-inspection de-watering bake completed within 30 minutes in dry N2, and zero observable surface oxidation on wirebond pads.
citations: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging (Harman, G. - Wire Bonding in Microelectronics: Materials, Processes, Reliability)
180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering (IEEE / Legacy Foundry Technical Reports)

critics.systems_engineer: C-SAM acoustic phase-inversion mapping must resolve interface reflections between the silicon backside, silver-filled die-attach epoxy (e.g., Henkel Ablebond 84-1LMISR), and copper leadframe pad. Using a 100-230 MHz high-frequency transducer requires precise acoustic impedance (Z) matching: Z_Si ≈ 19.7 MRayl, Z_epoxy ≈ 3.5-5.0 MRayl, and Z_air ≈ 0.0004 MRayl. A true delamination or void inverts acoustic phase polarity (180° phase flip from negative to positive reflection amplitude relative to the excitation pulse), but surface roughness, tilt, or incomplete acoustic gate synchronization will induce false phase reversals, corrupting the automated void area fraction algorithm.
critics.domain_expert: Die-attach voiding directly governs thermal dissipation and mechanical stress concentration in 180nm DRAM dies. MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 and IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 demand that total die-attach void area fraction not exceed 10-15%, with no single continuous void exceeding 5% or bridging across >50% of the die perimeter. A high void fraction elevates localized junction temperature (R_th_jc spikes > 15 K/W), triggering localized DRAM cell retention degradation and thermal runaway during refresh cycles.
critics.supply_chain: Acoustic coupling relies on ultra-pure degassed deionized water (resistivity > 18.0 MOhm*cm, dissolved O2 < 15 ppb) to prevent micro-bubble cavitation on the leadframe surface that mimic void signatures. Coupling fluid immersion requires immediate post-scan bake-out; failure to procure semiconductor-grade dry-nitrogen desorbers and specialized C-SAM transducers (Sonix, PVA TePla, or Nordson Sonoscan) creates lead-time bottlenecks and corrosion exposure on exposed leadframe silver/copper metallization.
critics.laya_pm: Die-attach inspection is an inline quality gate gating downstream gold/copper wirebonding. Metrology throughput must not exceed 90 seconds per leadframe strip. If C-SAM immersion requires cumbersome manual fixturing or prolonged drying cycles, the entire backend packaging queue will breach the strict Q-time envelope between epoxy cure and wirebonding.
critical_failure_modes: Micro-bubble cavitation in DI coupling fluid yielding false-positive phase-inversion void artifacts exceeding the 10% threshold
Epoxy outgassing and moisture entrapment during reflow causing popcorn delamination across the Si-epoxy interface
Acoustic gate misalignment capturing leadframe-epoxy bottom interface instead of die-epoxy interface, masking critical interfacial delamination

testcases.title: C-SAM Acoustic Phase-Inversion Interface Delamination Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM, Nordson Sonoscan Gen7 or equivalent) equipped with a 100 MHz / 230 MHz broadband transducer (0.25 inch focal length, spot size ~25 um) and degassed DI water tank (< 10 ppb dissolved gas)
testcases.pre_conditions: DRAM silicon die attached to copper leadframe with thermally cured silver-filled epoxy; leadframe degreased and free of particulate debris; transducer calibrated against a polished acoustic quartz reference block; acoustic gate time-window synchronized to the Si-epoxy interface echo (depth ~250-300 um).
testcases.procedure: 1. Submerge leadframe strip in degassed DI water coupling bath at 22.0 ± 1.0°C. 2. Position 100 MHz transducer over die surface; verify peak RF reflection echo and adjust focal plane to maximum reflection at the die-epoxy boundary. 3. Configure gate width to 15 ns encompassing the interface echo. 4. Enable A-scan phase detection mode: monitor polarity where positive-going RF peak indicates intact epoxy interface (Z_epoxy < Z_Si, negative reflection inverted by receiver) and 180° inverted phase indicates void/delamination (Z_air << Z_Si). 5. Execute 2D C-scan raster across 100% of die area (5 mm x 5 mm) at 10 um step pitch. 6. Record raw RF amplitude and phase-inversion maps.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total phase-inversion delamination area must be <= 10.0% of total active die attach area; maximum single contiguous delamination area must be <= 3.0%; zero delamination detected under the DRAM sense amplifier perimeter (outer 150 um margin).

testcases.title: Digital Image Thresholding Void Area Fraction Calculation & Thermal Cross-Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Digital Image Analysis Workstation running ImageJ / MATLAB automated segmentation algorithms, calibrated optical micrometer stage, and dual-junction transient thermal tester (T3Ster).
testcases.pre_conditions: C-SAM C-scan grayscale acoustic contrast map exported at >= 1000 x 1000 pixels with calibrated spatial resolution (<= 5 um/pixel); background noise normalized against leadframe baseline.
testcases.procedure: 1. Import raw C-scan acoustic intensity matrix into image processing pipeline. 2. Apply Otsu automated binary thresholding combined with phase-mask logic to segment void clusters from bonded epoxy matrix. 3. Execute morphological opening (3x3 kernel) to eliminate single-pixel acoustic shot noise. 4. Compute cumulative void area fraction: Area_void_fraction = (Sum of void pixels / Total die attach pixels) * 100%. 5. Measure major axis dimension of largest continuous void. 6. Mount sample to thermal fixture and measure junction-to-case thermal resistance (R_th_jc) via 100 mA transient thermal pulse.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Computed Die-Attach Void Area Fraction <= 12.0% across the full die footprint; largest single void dimension < 300 um; junction-to-case thermal resistance R_th_jc <= 12.5 K/W (nominal baseline without voids: 9.8 K/W).

ppe_required: Class 1000 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, 6 mil)
ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles
ESD-safe anti-static cleanroom smock and ground heel straps
Face shield during chemical bath transfers and IPA ultrasonic cleaning

# Standard Operating Procedure: Transfer Molding Epoxy Plastic Encapsulation

High-pressure transfer molding of epoxy resin over wirebonded leadframe strips, post-mold cure at 175°C for 4 hours, laser marking, and tie-bar trim-and-form.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Transfer Molding Epoxy Plastic Encapsulation (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package): BEOL metallization, electrical die sort (EDS), wafer backgrinding/dicing, and wirebond plastic encapsulation successfully yield JEDEC-qualified DRAM packaged units.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Electrical_Die_Sort_Wafer_Yield_Map.csv`
- [ ] `Wirebond_Ball_Shear_And_Pull_CPK_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_TSOP54_Final_ATE_SpeedBin_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wirebond ball shear strength** | `>= 18.0 gf` | Minimum failure load >= 15.0 gf across 30 samples | Dage 4000 micro-tester lateral ball shear per MIL-STD-883 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) wafer array functional yield** | `>= 90.0%` | Minimum yield >= 85.0% on prime wafers | Automated wafer probe array test with March C- diagnostic patterns |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Packaged DRAM package coplanarity & lead pitch** | `<= 0.08 mm coplanarity` | JEDEC TSOP-54 mechanical envelope tolerance (+/- 0.05 mm) | Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% passing electrical continuity and JEDEC parametric DC checks; destructive wirebond shear CPK >= 1.67 with zero package voiding or delamination detected under scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Pellet Sourcing & Pre-Heating Optimization
**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-EMC-180NM-003`  
**Target Architecture:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package)  
**Process Stage:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Transfer Molding Plastic Encapsulation  
**Knowledge Record:** [docs/knowledge/emc_pellet_preheating_sop.md](./docs/knowledge/emc_pellet_preheating_sop.md)

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  EMC Pellet Receiving  │
│     & Cold Storage     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Thawing &        │
│   High-Frequency RF    │
│      Pre-Heating       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Transfer Molding    │
│       Injection        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Quality & Viscosity   │
│  / Void Verification   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pellet Receiving, Sourcing & Cold-Chain Storage:**
   - Source ultra-low stress, silica-filled (80–88 wt% spherical SiO₂ filler) Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) formulated with epoxy novolac/biphenyl resin compatible with 180nm DRAM metallization.
   - Inspect vacuum-sealed moisture barrier bags upon arrival. Store pellets immediately in cold storage at **5°C ± 3°C** with relative humidity **RH < 30%** to prevent moisture uptake and advance of B-stage polymerization.

2. **Controlled Thawing Protocol:**
   - Transfer sealed moisture-barrier pellet containers from cold storage to cleanroom ambient (**25°C ± 2°C**).
   - Maintain sealed condition in a dry cabinet/desiccator for a minimum of **4 to 8 hours** until pellet core reaches room temperature (25°C). Unsealing cold pellets directly in ambient air is prohibited to avoid atmospheric moisture condensation.

3. **High-Frequency (RF) Dielectric Pre-Heating:**
   - Transfer cylindrical EMC pellets into the high-frequency RF dielectric pre-heater (27.12 MHz).
   - Set RF pre-heating target temperature to **85°C to 95°C** with an exposure cycle time of **20 to 35 seconds**.
   - Verify plasticization: The pellet must soften uniformly from core to skin without localized scorched crusts or advanced gelation.

4. **Transfer to Pot & Injection Molding Window:**
   - Transfer pre-heated pellets to the transfer molding press pot within a maximum transfer latency window of **< 15 seconds** to prevent thermal loss or premature curing.
   - Transfer mold at **175°C ± 5°C** with a clamp pressure of **10 to 15 MPa** and plunger transfer velocity calibrated to avoid wire sweep on the **25 µm thermosonic gold ball bonds**.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                    EMC & Packaging Parameter Tolerances
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
       Bond Temp (C)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                    │▒▒                                │
Wire Pull Force (gf)┤▒▒                                │
 Die Attach Void (%)┤██                                │
                    │██                                │
   Pre-heat Temp (C)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓              │
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓              │
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                    0.0    37.5     75.0    112.5 150.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Condition | Measurement Tool / Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **RF Pre-Heating Pellet Temperature** | **85°C to 95°C** | ± 3°C across pellet core & surface | Calibrated optical IR thermometer / contact probe |
| **Package Encapsulation Void Area** | **< 5%** | Max void under die / mold interface < 5% | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) |
| **Wire Bond Integrity (Post-Mold)** | **≥ 4.0 gf** | 25 µm Au wire, span break mode | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull Test |
| **Pre-Mold Wire Bond Stage Temp** | **150°C** | ± 5°C, pulse 60 kHz (50–100 mW, 20–30 ms) | Calibrated heater block thermocouple |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:**
  - *Thermosonic Gold Ball Bonding*: 25 µm diameter 99.99% gold wire bonded at **150°C** stage temperature with ultrasonic pulse (60 kHz, 50–100 mW, 20–30 ms) to connect 100 µm × 100 µm pads.
  - *Wire Pull Strength*: Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force **≥ 4.0 gf** for 25 µm wire, failing in span.
  - *Die Attach & Interface Hermeticity*: Silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at **150°C for 60 min**, requiring thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5\text{°C/W}$ and **void area < 5%** verified via acoustic microscopy.
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects:**
  - Pad and metal layer interface integrity: Al-0.5% Cu / 5N pure aluminum interconnects under standard thermal budget.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-1-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-1-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Pellet Sourcing & Pre-Heating Optimization: BEOL metallization, electrical die sort (EDS), wafer backgrinding/dicing, and wirebond plastic encapsulation successfully yield JEDEC-qualified DRAM packaged units.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Electrical_Die_Sort_Wafer_Yield_Map.csv`
- [ ] `Wirebond_Ball_Shear_And_Pull_CPK_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_TSOP54_Final_ATE_SpeedBin_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wirebond ball shear strength** | `>= 18.0 gf` | Minimum failure load >= 15.0 gf across 30 samples | Dage 4000 micro-tester lateral ball shear per MIL-STD-883 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) wafer array functional yield** | `>= 90.0%` | Minimum yield >= 85.0% on prime wafers | Automated wafer probe array test with March C- diagnostic patterns |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Packaged DRAM package coplanarity & lead pitch** | `<= 0.08 mm coplanarity` | JEDEC TSOP-54 mechanical envelope tolerance (+/- 0.05 mm) | Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% passing electrical continuity and JEDEC parametric DC checks; destructive wirebond shear CPK >= 1.67 with zero package voiding or delamination detected under scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Pre-Heat & Transfer Press Parameter Setup

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-EMC-003`  
**Classification:** Packaging & Assembly (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA DRAM Packaging)  
**Target Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Die Attach & Wire   │
│     Bond Verified     │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│      EMC Pellet       │
│     Dielectric RF     │
│       Pre-Heat        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Chase & Mold Tool   │
│       Clamping        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│     Hydraulic Ram     │
│  Transfer Injection   │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  In-Mold Pack & Cure  │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   De-Mold & In-Line   │
│      Inspection       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Upstream Verification & Carrier Loading**
   - Confirm die attach integrity on the lead frame: cured conductive silver epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ min}$) must demonstrate acoustic void area under die $< 5\%$ and thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
   - Ensure $25\,\mu\text{m}$ interconnect wires ($99.99\%\text{ Au}$ thermosonic bonded at $150^\circ\text{C}$ to $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bond pads) meet pull strength $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$ prior to mold encapsulation.

2. **EMC Pellet Dielectric RF Pre-Heating**
   - Retrieve thermoset epoxy molding compound (novolak/silica-filled compound pellet) from dry-pack storage.
   - Load pellet into the high-frequency Dielectric RF Pre-Heater.
   - Pre-heat pellet to a core plastication temperature of $90^\circ\text{C} \text{ to } 95^\circ\text{C}$ for $15 \text{ to } 25\text{ seconds}$ to lower compound viscosity, desorb residual volatiles, and prevent wire sweep during injection.

3. **Mold Tooling & Platen Thermal Stabilization**
   - Pre-heat upper and lower mold platens (chase) to $175^\circ\text{C} \pm 5^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Inspect vacuum vents and cavity surfaces for residual resin flash; apply automated dry-air vacuum purge.

4. **Transfer Press Clamping & Injection Sequence**
   - Load pre-heated lead frame strip containing DRAM dies into lower chase locating pins.
   - Insert pre-heated EMC pellet into the center transfer pot.
   - Apply hydraulic clamping force: $120 \text{ to } 180\text{ kN}$ across mold chase to eliminate mold parting-line flashing.
   - Actuate transfer plunger ram:
     - **Transfer Injection Velocity:** $1.5 \text{ to } 3.0\text{ mm/s}$ (controlled laminar flow through runners and sub-gates to avoid wire sweep).
     - **Transfer Pressure:** $6.0 \text{ to } 10.0\text{ MPa}$ ($60 \text{ to } 100\text{ bar}$).
     - **Transfer Time:** $10 \text{ to } 16\text{ seconds}$.

5. **In-Mold Curing & De-molding**
   - Maintain packing holding pressure at $5.0 \text{ to } 7.0\text{ MPa}$ at $175^\circ\text{C}$ for $90 \text{ to } 120\text{ seconds}$ to achieve sufficient polymer cross-linking (green strength).
   - De-clamp press, actuate ejector pins, and transfer molded strip to off-loader magazine for post-mold cure (PMC) batch bake ($175^\circ\text{C}$ for $4\text{ hours}$).

---

- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**
  - *Bond Pad Dimension:* $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
  - *Thermosonic Ball Bonding Parameters:* $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%\text{ Au}$ wire, capillary stage temperature $150^\circ\text{C}$, transducer pulse $60\text{ kHz}$, $50\text{--}100\text{ mW}$, $20\text{--}30\text{ ms}$.
  - *Die Attach Parameters:* Conductive silver-filled epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS), cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{ minutes}$.
  - *Quality Metrics:* Wire pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$ (Mil-Std-883 Method 2011, failure in wire span); thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$; acoustic void area under die $< 5\%$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)
