Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-1-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: High-Pressure Transfer Molding & Post-Mold Cure (PMC) Chamber Run

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal expansion mismatch between the 180nm silicon DRAM die (CTE ~2.6 ppm/°C), copper leadframe/BT substrate (CTE ~16-17 ppm/°C), and Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC, CTE1 ~8-12 ppm/°C) generates severe residual thermo-mechanical stress during the 175°C transfer molding and subsequent 175°C Post-Mold Cure (PMC) cycle, risking package warpage exceeding 75 µm and corner ball co-planarity failures on 54-ball FBGA.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-pressure transfer molding poses acute risk of gold or copper wire sweep during the melt injection phase if viscous drag force exceeds wire stiffness (drag force proportional to compound viscosity and transfer speed); transfer ram velocity must be dynamically profiled to maintain laminar flow past 25µm wire bonds while mold vacuum de-gassing (<5 mbar) is essential to eliminate micro-voids in TSOP-54 lead pockets.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Low-stress, halogen-free multi-functional epoxy molding compounds (e.g., biphenyl or ortho-cresol novolac loaded with 85-90 wt% spherical fused silica) require strict sub-zero (-40°C to -20°C) cold-chain storage and tight shelf-life control; delayed lead times or batch-to-batch spiral flow length variation directly impair mold cavity filling stability.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: PMC batch cycle times (typically 4 to 8 hours at 175°C) represent the primary packaging WIP bottleneck; mold tool chase changes between TSOP-54 and 54-ball FBGA must be scheduled strictly with dedicated dummy-run conditioning to avoid compound cross-contamination and mold-sticking yield fallout.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Wire bond sweep causing electrical shorting between adjacent DRAM I/O bonding wires (DQ0-DQ15) under excessive molten resin transfer pressure.
1. Internal acoustic micro-voids and interfacial delamination at the EMC-to-die or EMC-to-die-attach paddle interface leading to moisture-induced popcorn cracking during solder reflow.
1. Incomplete cross-linking / under-cure from PMC thermal gradient resulting in low Glass Transition Temperature (Tg < 160°C) and long-term package warpage/reliability drift.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-01` | **Automated X-Ray Inspection (AXI) for Wire Sweep and Void Detection** | High-resolution micro-focus 2D/3D X-Ray Inspection System with sub-micron focal spot size (<0.5 µm) | 1. Load molded TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA strip onto the automated AXI stage. 2. Calibrate optical/X-ray magnification to 100x focused on DRAM wire bonding perimeter (inner lead bond and pad bond areas). 3. Image all 54 active bond wires per die across 10 sample units per strip. 4. Measure maximum lateral deflection of each wire relative to the nominal centerline connecting ball bond to leadfinger. 5. Compute wire sweep percentage = (Max Deflection / Total Wire Length) * 100. 6. Execute multi-threshold image segmentation across die-attach paddle and active surface to compute volumetric void percentage. | `Wire sweep <= 3.0% of total wire span for all 54 bond wires; zero bridged wires; total package internal void area <= 1.0% of package cross-sectional area with no single void > 0.1 mm².` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-02` | **Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) Interfacial Delamination & Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) Verification** | High-Frequency C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscope (110 MHz transducer) and Differential Scanning Calorimeter (DSC) | 1. Submerge package samples into deionized water acoustic immersion tank at 25°C. 2. Align 110 MHz acoustic transducer gate at EMC-to-silicon die active surface interface and EMC-to-die-attach pad interface. 3. Raster-scan package footprint at 5 µm step resolution and record acoustic reflection amplitude phase-inversion maps. 4. Excise 15 mg of cured EMC flash coupon from the same runner strip and load into DSC pan. 5. Ramp temperature from 30°C to 250°C at 10°C/min under nitrogen atmosphere to measure inflection midpoint Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) and residual cure exotherm (delta-H). | `Delamination at active die surface = 0.0%; delamination at die paddle backside < 5.0% perimeter non-critical zone; EMC Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) >= 165°C; residual curing heat delta-H < 2.0 J/g (confirming >98% cross-linking conversion).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating Kevlar safety gloves (rated >=250°C) for hot mold chase handling, Nitrile chemical-resistant inner gloves under cleanroom gloves, Half-face air-purifying respirator equipped with organic vapor and P100 particulate filter cartridges, ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash goggles and safety face shield, Flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat / ESD static-dissipative smock
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burns from hot mold chase (175°C): Immediately flush affected area with cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; seek immediate medical attention. Inhalation of off-gas vapors/phenolic fumes: Evacuate person to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; seek emergency medical care. Eye contact with mold flash/dust: Irrigate eyes with isotonic emergency eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local dedicated exhaust ventilation hoods with capture velocity >= 0.75 m/s installed directly over transfer mold platen gates and PMC oven exhaust ports to extract volatile organic compounds (phenols, cresols, release waxes); exhaust line routed through activated carbon bed adsorption scrubbers.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solid cured runners, cull biscuits, and cured mold flash pellets are chemically inert and disposed of via regulated industrial non-hazardous solid waste streams; uncured chemical residues and contaminated mold-cleaning wax sheets must be segregated in sealed drums for certified high-temperature hazardous thermal incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Fused Silica (Silicon Dioxide powder filler)** | `60676-86-0` | Electronic / Microfine Grade (<50µm) | `75-90 wt%` |
| **Epoxy Cresol Novolac Resin (Poly[(o-cresyl glycidyl ether)-co-formaldehyde])** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `5-15 wt%` |
| **Phenol Novolac Hardener / Resin Curing Agent** | `9003-35-4` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `3-8 wt%` |
| **Carbon Black (Pigment)** | `1333-86-4` | Industrial Pigment Grade | `0.1-0.5 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Wire-bonded DRAM strips post-plasma clean with organic carbon contamination < 5 at% by XPS, contact angle <= 15°, completely free of ionic halides and moisture condensation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Solidified, void-free matte black epoxy package casing with cross-linking conversion >= 85% pre-PMC, transitioning to fully cross-linked, thermally stable thermoset body (>98% conversion) post-PMC.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric exposure prior to molding causes moisture uptake on BT substrates and oxidation of copper leadframes, resulting in interfacial steam micro-explosions ('popcorning') and complete acoustic delamination during PMC or solder ball attach.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful high-pressure transfer molding encapsulation and post-mold curing of 180nm DRAM TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA strips meeting zero-void, sub-3% wire sweep, full chemical cross-linking (>98%), and JEDEC Level 3 moisture sensitivity compatibility.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TRANSFER_MOLD_PMC_PARAMETRIC_RUN_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `AXI_WIRE_SWEEP_VOID_INSPECTION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `CSAM_INTERFACIAL_ACOUSTIC_DELAMINATION_MAPS.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum wire bond sweep percentage across all active 180nm DRAM bonding channels** | `1.8%` | <= 3.0% | High-Resolution Automated X-Ray Inspection (AXI) lateral deviation measurement against nominal wire vector |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total internal acoustic delamination area at the active die surface interface** | `0.0%` | 0.0% (Zero Tolerance) | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) 110 MHz gated pulse-echo phase inversion mapping |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Cured Epoxy Molding Compound Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) post-PMC** | `172.0°C` | +/- 5.0°C (Absolute minimum >= 165.0°C) | Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) inflection point analysis at 10°C/min ramp rate under N2 |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% inspection pass on wire sweep (<=3.0%) across all sampled leadframes, zero detectable active-area delamination via CSAM, package total warpage <= 60 µm across 54-ball FBGA strips, and sign-off verification from Lead Packaging Engineer and QA Manager.

testcases.instrumentation: High-resolution micro-focus 2D/3D X-Ray Inspection System with sub-micron focal spot size (<0.5 µm)
testcases.pre_conditions: Stripped leadframes/strips unloaded from transfer molding press prior to or immediately following PMC, cooled to 25°C ambient.
testcases.procedure:
1. Load molded TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA strip onto the automated AXI stage.
2. Calibrate optical/X-ray magnification to 100x focused on DRAM wire bonding perimeter (inner lead bond and pad bond areas).
3. Image all 54 active bond wires per die across 10 sample units per strip.
4. Measure maximum lateral deflection of each wire relative to the nominal centerline connecting ball bond to leadfinger.
5. Compute wire sweep percentage = (Max Deflection / Total Wire Length) * 100.
6. Execute multi-threshold image segmentation across die-attach paddle and active surface to compute volumetric void percentage.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Wire sweep <= 3.0% of total wire span for all 54 bond wires; zero bridged wires; total package internal void area <= 1.0% of package cross-sectional area with no single void > 0.1 mm².

testcases.title: Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) Interfacial Delamination & Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) Verification
testcases.instrumentation: High-Frequency C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscope (110 MHz transducer) and Differential Scanning Calorimeter (DSC)
testcases.pre_conditions: Post-Mold Cure (PMC) complete at 175°C for 4 hours; strip de-paneling or coupon excision completed; samples cleaned in DI water ultrasonic bath and dried.
testcases.procedure:
1. Submerge package samples into deionized water acoustic immersion tank at 25°C.
2. Align 110 MHz acoustic transducer gate at EMC-to-silicon die active surface interface and EMC-to-die-attach pad interface.
3. Raster-scan package footprint at 5 µm step resolution and record acoustic reflection amplitude phase-inversion maps.
4. Excise 15 mg of cured EMC flash coupon from the same runner strip and load into DSC pan.
5. Ramp temperature from 30°C to 250°C at 10°C/min under nitrogen atmosphere to measure inflection midpoint Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) and residual cure exotherm (delta-H).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Delamination at active die surface = 0.0%; delamination at die paddle backside < 5.0% perimeter non-critical zone; EMC Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) >= 165°C; residual curing heat delta-H < 2.0 J/g (confirming >98% cross-linking conversion).

ppe_required: Thermal-insulating Kevlar safety gloves (rated >=250°C) for hot mold chase handling
Nitrile chemical-resistant inner gloves under cleanroom gloves
Half-face air-purifying respirator equipped with organic vapor and P100 particulate filter cartridges
ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash goggles and safety face shield
Flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat / ESD static-dissipative smock

cas_chemicals.name: Epoxy Cresol Novolac Resin (Poly[(o-cresyl glycidyl ether)-co-formaldehyde])
Phenol Novolac Hardener / Resin Curing Agent

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Thermal burns from hot mold chase (175°C): Immediately flush affected area with cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; seek immediate medical attention. Inhalation of off-gas vapors/phenolic fumes: Evacuate person to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; seek emergency medical care. Eye contact with mold flash/dust: Irrigate eyes with isotonic emergency eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Local dedicated exhaust ventilation hoods with capture velocity >= 0.75 m/s installed directly over transfer mold platen gates and PMC oven exhaust ports to extract volatile organic compounds (phenols, cresols, release waxes); exhaust line routed through activated carbon bed adsorption scrubbers.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Solid cured runners, cull biscuits, and cured mold flash pellets are chemically inert and disposed of via regulated industrial non-hazardous solid waste streams; uncured chemical residues and contaminated mold-cleaning wax sheets must be segregated in sealed drums for certified high-temperature hazardous thermal incineration.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Wire-bonded DRAM strips post-plasma clean with organic carbon contamination < 5 at% by XPS, contact angle <= 15°, completely free of ionic halides and moisture condensation.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Solidified, void-free matte black epoxy package casing with cross-linking conversion >= 85% pre-PMC, transitioning to fully cross-linked, thermally stable thermoset body (>98% conversion) post-PMC.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excessive atmospheric exposure prior to molding causes moisture uptake on BT substrates and oxidation of copper leadframes, resulting in interfacial steam micro-explosions ('popcorning') and complete acoustic delamination during PMC or solder ball attach.

expected_result.summary: Successful high-pressure transfer molding encapsulation and post-mold curing of 180nm DRAM TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA strips meeting zero-void, sub-3% wire sweep, full chemical cross-linking (>98%), and JEDEC Level 3 moisture sensitivity compatibility.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum wire bond sweep percentage across all active 180nm DRAM bonding channels
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-Resolution Automated X-Ray Inspection (AXI) lateral deviation measurement against nominal wire vector

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Total internal acoustic delamination area at the active die surface interface
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) 110 MHz gated pulse-echo phase inversion mapping

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Cured Epoxy Molding Compound Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) post-PMC
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) inflection point analysis at 10°C/min ramp rate under N2

expected_result.signoff_criteria: 100% inspection pass on wire sweep (<=3.0%) across all sampled leadframes, zero detectable active-area delamination via CSAM, package total warpage <= 60 µm across 54-ball FBGA strips, and sign-off verification from Lead Packaging Engineer and QA Manager.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Pellet Conditioning & Mold Chase Preheating
**Module / Target:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package)  
**Process Step:** BEOL Packaging & Assembly — Transfer Molding Execution  
**Action Type:** Buy (Qualified Off-the-Shelf Commercial EMC Pellets)

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Cold Storage      │
│     Retrieval: 5°C     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Pellet Acclimation &  │
│   Desiccant Thawing    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Dielectric       │
│   Preheating: 80°C -   │
│          95°C          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     PID Mold Chase     │
│  Preheating: 175°C ±   │
│          3°C           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Transfer Tooling    │
│    Insertion & Mold    │
│         Clamp          │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Cold-Storage Retrieval & Thermal Acclimation:**
   - Retrieve sealed EMC pellet pouches from cold storage (refrigerated at $5^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Allow the pellets to equilibrate within their sealed, moisture-barrier vacuum packaging at room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$) for $\ge 4.0\text{ hours}$ to prevent atmospheric moisture condensation on the pellet surfaces.
   - Verify unsealed pellet surface relative moisture remains $\le 0.10\text{ wt}\%$ prior to staging.

2. **Dielectric Preheating (RF Preheater Station):**
   - Transfer acclimated pellets into the high-frequency dielectric preheater chamber.
   - Apply RF dielectric energy (27.12 MHz) to ramp core pellet temperature to $80^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }95^\circ\text{C}$ uniformly within $15\text{ to }30\text{ seconds}$. 
   - Ensure the transfer time from preheater discharge to the transfer mold pot is strictly $\le 15\text{ seconds}$ to eliminate premature epoxy B-stage cross-linking/gelation.

3. **Multi-Zone Mold Chase PID Thermal Equilibrium:**
   - Energize top and bottom mold chase heating platens using multi-zone digital PID thermal control loops (analogous to multi-zone thermal dynamics with thermocouple feedback).
   - Set platen target temperature to $175^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Soak mold chase under clamping pressure for a stabilization period of $\ge 30\text{ minutes}$ until temperature uniformity across all mold cavities settles within $\pm 2.0^\circ\text{C}$.

4. **Mold Chase Surface Preparation & Insertion:**
   - Inspect top and bottom mold chase cavities with clean filtered $\text{N}_2$ blow (purge rate $2\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$) to clear particulate debris.
   - Load pre-heated conditioned EMC pellets into the pre-warmed transfer pot immediately followed by lead-frame strip insertion (handling TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA substrates with thermosonic gold ball or ultrasonic aluminum wedge-bonded DRAM dies).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
Normalized Process Parameter Window
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                        │░░░░░                         │
    Pellet Transfer Time┤░░░░░                         │
                        │▒                             │
  Equilibration Moisture┤▒                             │
Pellet Core Preheat Temp┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                        │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
   Chase Temp Uniformity┤█                             │
                        │█                             │
                        └┬──────┬───────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                        0.0   22.5    45.0   67.5  90.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Window | Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mold Chase Surface Temperature** | $175.0$ | $\pm 3.0$ | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | Surface contact pyrometer / embedded Type K/R thermocouples |
| **Mold Platen Zone Temperature Uniformity** | $\le 2.0$ | Max allowable delta across chase | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | 9-point surface thermocouple array survey |
| **Pellet Core Preheating Temperature** | $88.0$ | $80.0\text{ to }95.0$ | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | Calibrated non-contact infrared thermal pyrometer |
| **Pellet Exposure / Transfer Time** | $\le 12.0$ | $\le 15.0$ max | $\text{seconds}$ | Automated transfer cycle inline hardware timer |
| **Pellet Moisture Content** | $\le 0.08$ | $\le 0.10$ max | $\text{wt}\%$ | Karl Fischer titration / moisture balance analyzer |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **`Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging`**:
  - Validates BEOL die package structure, connecting $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads via $25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire bonds to TSOP/FBGA leads, requiring mold chase temperatures and low-stress encapsulation to preserve bond integrity ($F_{\text{pull}} \ge 4.0\,\text{gf}$) and die attach stability ($R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$).
- **`Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation`**:
  - Establishes multi-zone closed-loop PID control architectures with thermocouple sensors and laminar purge dynamics ($1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$) essential for preventing thermal gradients and maintaining isothermal uniformity ($\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ boundary control translated to mold chase zone regulation).

---
*Captured micro-knowledge documented in [emc_pellet_conditioning_sop.md](./docs/knowledge/emc_pellet_conditioning_sop.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-1-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-1-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Pellet Conditioning & Mold Chase Preheating: BEOL metallization, electrical die sort (EDS), wafer backgrinding/dicing, and wirebond plastic encapsulation successfully yield JEDEC-qualified DRAM packaged units.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Electrical_Die_Sort_Wafer_Yield_Map.csv`
- [ ] `Wirebond_Ball_Shear_And_Pull_CPK_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_TSOP54_Final_ATE_SpeedBin_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wirebond ball shear strength** | `>= 18.0 gf` | Minimum failure load >= 15.0 gf across 30 samples | Dage 4000 micro-tester lateral ball shear per MIL-STD-883 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) wafer array functional yield** | `>= 90.0%` | Minimum yield >= 85.0% on prime wafers | Automated wafer probe array test with March C- diagnostic patterns |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Packaged DRAM package coplanarity & lead pitch** | `<= 0.08 mm coplanarity` | JEDEC TSOP-54 mechanical envelope tolerance (+/- 0.05 mm) | Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% passing electrical continuity and JEDEC parametric DC checks; destructive wirebond shear CPK >= 1.67 with zero package voiding or delamination detected under scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).

# Standard Operating Procedure: High-Pressure Transfer Molding Injection & In-Mold Polymerization

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Transfer molding parameter integration requires strict synchronization between hydraulic ram velocity profile, mold chase heating uniformity (+/-2 deg C across all 54 package cavities), and vacuum assist evacuation (<10 mbar before transfer). Inadequate vacuum pull timing leads to adiabatic micro-dieseling of compressed ambient air at the end-of-fill corners, inducing localized carbonization, bonding wire degradation, and internal package voids on the TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA leadframe.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) melt viscosity exhibits a tight chemo-rheological window: the spiral flow length must reach maximum fluidity (minimum dynamic viscosity between 10 and 25 Pa*s at 175 deg C) prior to the onset of the cross-linking gel point (gel time typically 22 to 30 seconds). Premature gelation before cavity pack-out induces severe wire sweep (>3% wire deflection on 180nm gold/copper ball bonds) and incomplete lead encapsulation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Multi-die lot transfer reliability depends on tight inventory cold-chain storage for preformed EMC pellets. Pellets must be stored at -20 deg C to -40 deg C with zero condensation risk during controlled 24-hour thaw staging at 22 deg C. Pellet shelf life degrades rapidly under room temperature ambient exposure, shifting the cure kinetic profile and exhausting critical mold-release additives (such as carnauba wax or synthetic ester blends).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Molding tool uptime and cavity release cycling directly dictate line throughput. In-mold polymerization requires an optimized 90-120 second cure cycle; excessive in-mold dwell bottlenecks the entire backend line, while premature mold opening causes structural green-body warpage and resin tear-out on external leads. Post-Mold Cure (PMC) batching schedules must seamlessly integrate with down-stream degate and deflash tools.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Wire sweep exceeding 3.5% causing adjacent lead/pad shorting due to unbalanced runner flow fronts or excessive transfer ram velocity.
1. Internal acoustic micro-voiding and interfacial package delamination at the die-attach/silicon passivation interface exceeding IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 MSL-3 thresholds.
1. Incomplete cavity filling (short shots) resulting from pellet pre-cure, resin freezing in narrow package gates, or inadequate transfer pressure hold.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-2-01` | **Wire Sweep and In-Cavity Wire Deflection Verification via Real-Time X-Ray Inspection** | High-resolution microfocus 2D/3D X-Ray Inspection System (Phoenix/Nordson Dage Quadra 5, 0.1 um detail detectability) with automated wire-sweep angle measurement software. | 1. Position molded leadframe strip on the motorized inspection stage. 2. Calibrate geometric magnification and beam energy (80 kV, 40 uA). 3. Identify and scan 100% of wire loops across 10 sample package units across runner extremities (corners and center cavities). 4. Measure maximum perpendicular lateral displacement (d) from nominal straight-line projection (L) for every critical long-span bond wire. 5. Compute percentage wire sweep: (d / L) * 100. | `Maximum wire sweep must be <= 3.0% across all measured wire spans (average wire sweep <= 1.8%). Zero instances of wire touching, bridging, or broken wire necks at heat-affected zone (HAZ).` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-2-02` | **Acoustic Micro-Imaging of Internal Voids and Die-Face Interfacial Delamination** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM / Sonix Echo CSAM) equipped with high-frequency 110-230 MHz transducer in deionized water coupling immersion tank. | 1. Mount molded package strip in C-SAM immersion fixture with die active surface facing transducer. 2. Gate acoustic return echoes at: Interface 1 (Mold Compound to Die Surface / Passivation), Interface 2 (Die Paddle / Substrate Interface). 3. ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal heat-resistant safety gloves rated to 250 deg C for mold chase handling, Viton/Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves for mold-release agent and cleaner handling, Half-face elastomeric respirator fitted with organic vapor / HEPA particulate cartridges (OV/P100), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Flame-retardant anti-static cleanroom ESD lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation of molding off-gas fumes: Immediately move victim to fresh air. Provide oxygen if breathing is difficult; obtain medical attention. Skin contact with molten resin: Douse immediately with cold running water for at least 15 minutes; do not attempt to peel solidified resin off skin; seek burn treatment. Eye contact: Flush eyes with sterile eyewash solution for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Accidental ingestion: Rinse mouth thoroughly; do not induce vomiting unless instructed by medical staff.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) hooded directly over the mold chase and transfer pot platen with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM), routed to an industrial activated-carbon bed scrubber to capture phenol, cresol, and organic amine volatile off-gases during press opening.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solid cured runners, culls, and purge biscuits must be collected in dedicated labeled non-hazardous composite polymer waste bins for certified high-temperature incineration. Uncured pellet residues, expired resin, and solvent contaminated wipes must be classified and incinerated as hazardous organic waste per local environmental regulations.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Plasma-cleaned (Argon/O2 vacuum RF plasma treated) leadframe and die surface with surface free energy > 65 mN/m, zero organic hydrocarbon contamination (contact angle < 10 degrees).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Cross-linked green polymer body (>85% in-mold cure degree) at 175 deg C, dimensionally stable, free of surface blister, flashing thickness < 15 um on lead fingers.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding open-air queue time leads to atmospheric moisture adsorption and surface re-oxidation/contamination of gold/copper wire loops and bond pads, causing severe mold-to-passivation interfacial delamination and 'popcorn' package cracking during subsequent reflow.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Execution of high-pressure transfer molding injection and in-mold polymerization for 180nm DRAM TSOP-54/54-FBGA packages, achieving void-free cavity filling, wire sweep below 3.0%, and a cross-linking degree exceeding 85% prior to post-mold cure dispatch.

critics.systems_engineer: Transfer molding parameter integration requires strict synchronization between hydraulic ram velocity profile, mold chase heating uniformity (+/-2 deg C across all 54 package cavities), and vacuum assist evacuation (<10 mbar before transfer). # Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Pellet Conditioning & Plunger Pre-Heat Calibration

- **Document File:** [sop_emc_pellet_conditioning_plunger_preheat.md](./docs/sop_emc_pellet_conditioning_plunger_preheat.md)
- **Hierarchy:** 180nm CMOS MPW Tapeout > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Transfer Molding Epoxy Plastic Encapsulation (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA) > EMC Pellet Conditioning & Plunger Pre-Heat Calibration
- **Action Type:** Buy (Procured solid EMC pellets & automated transfer molding toolsets)

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Cold Storage      │
│       Retrieval        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Desiccator Thaw &    │
│     Stabilization      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     RF Pre-Heater      │
│  Calibration & Pellet  │
│          Load          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Plunger & Pot      │
│   Thermal Profiling    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Transfer Injection   │
│       Clearance        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Cold Storage Retrieval & Nitrogen Desiccator Stabilization:**
   - Retrieve sealed moisture-barrier bags of semiconductor-grade B-stage Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) pellets from cold storage (**-5°C to 5°C**).
   - Place intact foil bags into a dry $N_2$-purged desiccator cabinet maintained at ambient cleanroom conditions (**25°C**, laminar $N_2$ purge 2.0 to 5.0 SLPM).
   - Allow passive thermal equilibration for a minimum dwell time of **4.0 hours** until pellets reach ambient temperature (**25°C**). Do not break foil seal until stabilization completes to avoid surface condensation.

2. **Dielectric Radio-Frequency (RF) Pre-Heater Setup & Tuning:**
   - Initialize the 27.12 MHz RF dielectric pre-heating chamber (500 W to 1.5 kW output).
   - Position pellets uniformly on the non-stick PTFE carrier between high-frequency electrode plates.
   - Execute an RF pre-heating cycle for **15 to 30 seconds** to uniformly heat the pellet core to **90°C – 100°C** (nominal target: **95.0°C**).
   - Verify core and surface temperature using non-contact infrared pyrometry to ensure homogeneous softening without premature thermoset gelation.

3. **Plunger & Mold Pot Multi-Zone PID Thermal Calibration:**
   - Energize the transfer press heating cartridges for the upper chase, lower chase, and plunger/pot assembly.
   - Engage digital triple-loop PID controllers with feedforward compensation, driving the mold pot and transfer plunger tip to an isothermal setpoint of **175.0°C**.
   - Profile the plunger tip and pot cylinder bore using dual Type-R / Type-S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples across a 30-minute soak window to guarantee temperature uniformity within **±0.5°C**.

4. **Automated Transfer Loading & Injection Clearance:**
   - Using cleanroom vacuum handling wands, transfer pre-heated pellets (core temperature **95.0°C ± 5.0°C**) into the pre-heated mold pot (**175.0°C**).
   - Ensure the transfer dwell time is strictly $\le \mathbf{5.0\text{ s}}$ to prevent uneven resin skin polymerization.
   - Verify plunger-to-pot radial clearance (**15 µm to 25 µm**) to eliminate resin flash leakage and prevent mechanical binding.

---

### 2. Thermal Process Target Profile

```text
                EMC Thermal Conditioning Profile (°C)   
             ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
             │█████████████████████████████████████████│
 Mold Chase T┤█████████████████████████████████████████│
             │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
Plunger PID T┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
Pellet Core T┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                  │
             │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                  │
Ambient Equil┤░░░░░░░                                  │
             │░░░░░░░                                  │
             └┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬┘
             0.0      43.8      87.5      131.2   175.0 
```

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Inspection / Measurement Method | Target Value | Physical Unit | Tolerance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pellet Core Temperature** | In-line non-contact IR pyrometer / thermal probe | `95.0` | `°C` | `± 5.0 °C` |
| **Plunger & Pot Isothermal Uniformity** | Type S/R Pt-Pt/Rh dual thermocouple grid with PID logging | `175.0` | `°C` | `± 0.5 °C` |
| **Pellet-to-Pot Transfer Dwell Time** | Automated robotic transfer arm / PLC cycle timer | `≤ 5.0` | `s` | `Max limit` |
| **Encapsulation Void Area** | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) across package & die interface | `< 5.0` | `%` | `Area %` |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:**
  - Ambient room temperature baseline (**25°C**) for wire-bonding handling and pre-conditioning staging.
  - Wire pull and mechanical interconnect integrity standards on 25 µm wire spans connecting 100 µm × 100 µm pads, dictating void limits (**void area < 5%** via acoustic microscopy) and gentle rheological flow during molding to avoid wire sweep.
- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation:**
  - Multi-zone PID temperature regulation framework utilizing dual Type-R / Type-S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples.
  - High-precision isothermal zone stability standards enforcing thermal uniformity within **±0.5°C**.
  - Mechanical velocity ramping constraints preventing thermal shock dislocations.
- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery:**
  - Inert $N_2$ laminar sweep velocity dynamics (2.0 to 5.0 SLPM) utilized in moisture-controlled desiccator chambers for oxygen and ambient condensation suppression.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: EMC pellet conditioning and transfer plunger pre-heating must be synchronized with the mold chase thermal equilibrium (175°C ± 2°C). Under-preheating the pellet or plunger induces thermal shock and a steep viscosity gradient across the transfer pot, resulting in localized shear heating, runner freezing, or wire sweep on the 25 µm Au bonding wires connecting the 180nm DRAM bond pads to the TSOP-54 leadframe/FBGA substrate. Conversely, excessive pre-heat dwelling triggers premature B-stage epoxy crosslinking prior to runner entry, severely constricting the gelation process window.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Epoxy molding compounds (ortho-cresol novolac or biphenyl resin filled with 80-88 wt% fused spherical silica) require controlled high-frequency dielectric preheating to elevate core pellet temperature to 85°C-95°C within 10-15 seconds. This drops the compound viscosity to its minimum processing plateau (<20 Pa·s) without advancing the conversion degree beyond 3%. Plunger tip temperature must be calibrated to match the pot liner surface within ±1.5°C to avoid crusting/flash ring formation on the plunger circumference.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Novolac and multi-functional epoxy pellets (e.g., Sumitomo EME-G700 series or Henkel Hysol) demand continuous cold-chain logistics at -20°C or 5°C with strictly monitored dew-point thaw cycles. Uncontrolled moisture absorption during warm-up degrades hydrolytic stability, inducing popcorn cracking during subsequent lead-free solder reflow (260°C peak JEDEC J-STD-020D). Dual-sourcing qualification must account for filler distribution variance affecting dielectric heating rates.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Plunger pre-heat calibration and pellet staging represent a critical throughput gating step in the TSOP-54/54-ball FBGA packaging line. Any pellet dwell-time overshoot in the dielectric heater (>45 seconds) requires automated rejection and purge protocols to avoid tooling contamination, scrap mold downtime, and subsequent leadframe misfeeds, directly impacting package cycle time targets of <90 seconds per shot.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature B-stage resin gelation in the transfer pot causing incomplete cavity fill (short shots) and excessive wire sweep (>5% wire deflection) under hydraulic surge pressure.
1. Moisture condensation on cold-conditioned pellets inducing micro-void generation, steam expansion delamination at the die-attach/silicon interface, and die cracking during post-mold cure.
1. Plunger-to-pot thermal mismatch causing polymer flash bypass, scoring the hardened carbide pot sleeve, and generating uneven packing pressure across peripheral TSOP-54 cavities.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-2-1-01` | **RF Dielectric Pre-Heater Core Pellet Temperature Uniformity & Conversion Verification** | Multi-channel calibrated fast-response K-type thermocouple probe datalogger, differential scanning calorimeter (DSC Q2000), and non-contact IR thermal imager (FLIR A655sc). | 1. Insert calibrated thermocouple into the radial geometric center of three test EMC pellets. 2. Place pellets into the high-frequency dielectric pre-heater electrode nest (approx. 27-70 MHz). 3. Energize pre-heater with recipe target 90°C for 12.0 seconds. 4. Record core, surface, and base temperatures upon cycle termination. 5. Immediately extract 5 mg core sample into hermetic DSC pan and ramp at 10°C/min to 250°C to measure residual reaction enthalpy (delta H_res) against unheated baseline enthalpy (delta H_0) to compute degree of conversion alpha = 1 - (delta H_res / delta H_0). | `Core pellet temperature must reach 90.0°C ± 3.0°C across all test pellets with surface-to-core gradient <= 4.0°C. Chemical conversion degree alpha must remain <= 3.0% (residual enthalpy retention >= 97.0%).` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-2-1-02` | **Transfer Plunger Dynamic Pre-Heat Thermal Equilibrium & Pot Clearance Calibration** | Surface contact pyrometer (calibrated against NIST standard), laser micrometric dial bore gauge (0.1 µm resolution), dynamic load cell sensor pack. | 1. Measure plunger head face and radial perimeter temperature at 8 equidistant points using surface pyrometer. 2. Measure transfer pot liner inner diameter and plunger outer diameter at 175°C to calculate effective dynamic diametral clearance. 3. Execute 5 dry transfer cycles with automated plunger travel profile (1.5 mm/s transfer speed, 12 MPa clamping force). 4. Record dynamic friction load profile and temperature stability of plunger face across strokes. | `Plunger face temperature must equal 175.0°C ± 1.5°C with circumferential delta <= 1.0°C. Dynamic diametral clearance between plunger and pot liner must be within 25.0 µm to 35.0 µm, with no galling, binding, or mechanical load fluctuation > 0.5 kN.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protective Kevlar gloves rated for 250°C contact (EN 407), Half-face air-purifying elastomeric respirator with multi-gas/organic vapor/P100 particulate cartridge (3M 60926), Chemical splash and impact-resistant face shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1+, Lint-free ESD cleanroom smock and conductive safety footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation of thermal outgassing fumes: Evacuate person to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; seek emergency medical attention. Skin contact with molten or hot resin: Do not peel adhered resin forcibly; flush with copious cold water for >= 15 minutes to quench heat; dress with sterile non-adherent burn dressing. Eye contact: Flush immediately with isotonic eye wash for 15 minutes; consult ophthalmologist.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) hoods directly enclosing the pre-heater and mold pot opening with minimum face capture velocity of 0.75 m/s (150 FPM), routed through an activated charcoal scrubbing bed and HEPA filtration unit prior to exterior discharge.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solid uncured purge slugs and rejected pre-heated pellets must be segregated in dedicated steel fire-rated collection drums, allowed to fully crosslink/quench in an exhaust-cooled zone, and disposed of as regulated hazardous polymer solid waste via certified high-temperature incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Fused Silica (Respirable crystalline/amorphous blend)** | `60676-86-0` | Electronic Encapsulation Grade | `80.0-88.0 wt%` |
| **o-Cresol Novolac Epoxy Resin** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `5.0-12.0 wt%` |
| **Phenol-Formaldehyde Novolac Hardener** | `9003-35-4` | Electronic Grade | `3.0-8.0 wt%` |
| **Carbon Black (Pigment)** | `1333-86-4` | Technical Ultra-Pure | `0.1-0.5 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-conditioned cold-thawed solid cylindrical EMC pellet, free of surface condensation, frost, moisture film, or mechanical particulate flaking.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Homogeneously pre-heated plasticized pellet at 90°C core temperature ready for instant transfer pot loading without crusting or liquid drip.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient air queue time results in moisture uptake (>0.08 wt%), triggering internal steam blistering during transfer molding and package delamination; exceeding pre-heater dwell time causes premature B-stage gelation, blocking mold runners and shearing bond wires.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Engineering completion of EMC pellet RF dielectric pre-heating and transfer plunger thermal calibration for the Gen 3 180nm DRAM TSOP-54 encapsulation line, guaranteeing repeatable pellet core plasticization at 90°C (conversion <= 3%) and stable plunger-pot thermal alignment at 175°C with verified dynamic clearance.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `EMC_Pellet_Dielectric_PreHeat_Thermal_DSC_Log.csv`
- [ ] `Plunger_PreHeat_Thermal_Equilibrium_Calibration_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Dynamic_Pot_Plunger_Clearance_Metrology_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Pre-heated EMC pellet core temperature uniformity at transfer loading** | `90.0°C` | ±3.0°C | Fast-response embedded thermocouple penetration datalogger |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Chemical conversion degree (alpha) of EMC matrix post pre-heat cycle** | `2.0%` | ≤3.0% maximum allowable | Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) residual exotherm integration |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Plunger face temperature alignment with upper/lower mold chase setpoint** | `175.0°C` | ±1.5°C | NIST-traceable surface contact pyrometer multipoint survey |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful validation of 10 consecutive pre-heat cycles achieving core temperatures within 90.0°C ± 3.0°C and DSC-verified conversion <= 3.0%, paired with verified plunger-pot thermal equilibrium at 175.0°C ± 1.5°C exhibiting zero binding and zero compound bypass across 5 dry qualification strokes, formally signed off by Packaging Process Engineering and Quality Assurance Leads.

Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation (Levinson - Principles of Lithography & Thermal Processing)
Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery (Thermco / Bruce Technologies Semiconductor Furnace Manual)

critics.systems_engineer: EMC pellet conditioning and transfer plunger pre-heating must be synchronized with the mold chase thermal equilibrium (175°C ± 2°C). Under-preheating the pellet or plunger induces thermal shock and a steep viscosity gradient across the transfer pot, resulting in localized shear heating, runner freezing, or wire sweep on the 25 µm Au bonding wires connecting the 180nm DRAM bond pads to the TSOP-54 leadframe/FBGA substrate. Conversely, excessive pre-heat dwelling triggers premature B-stage epoxy crosslinking prior to runner entry, severely constricting the gelation process window.
critics.domain_expert: Epoxy molding compounds (ortho-cresol novolac or biphenyl resin filled with 80-88 wt% fused spherical silica) require controlled high-frequency dielectric preheating to elevate core pellet temperature to 85°C-95°C within 10-15 seconds. This drops the compound viscosity to its minimum processing plateau (<20 Pa·s) without advancing the conversion degree beyond 3%. Plunger tip temperature must be calibrated to match the pot liner surface within ±1.5°C to avoid crusting/flash ring formation on the plunger circumference.
critics.supply_chain: Novolac and multi-functional epoxy pellets (e.g., Sumitomo EME-G700 series or Henkel Hysol) demand continuous cold-chain logistics at -20°C or 5°C with strictly monitored dew-point thaw cycles. Uncontrolled moisture absorption during warm-up degrades hydrolytic stability, inducing popcorn cracking during subsequent lead-free solder reflow (260°C peak JEDEC J-STD-020D). Dual-sourcing qualification must account for filler distribution variance affecting dielectric heating rates.
critics.laya_pm: Plunger pre-heat calibration and pellet staging represent a critical throughput gating step in the TSOP-54/54-ball FBGA packaging line. Any pellet dwell-time overshoot in the dielectric heater (>45 seconds) requires automated rejection and purge protocols to avoid tooling contamination, scrap mold downtime, and subsequent leadframe misfeeds, directly impacting package cycle time targets of <90 seconds per shot.
critical_failure_modes: Premature B-stage resin gelation in the transfer pot causing incomplete cavity fill (short shots) and excessive wire sweep (>5% wire deflection) under hydraulic surge pressure.
Moisture condensation on cold-conditioned pellets inducing micro-void generation, steam expansion delamination at the die-attach/silicon interface, and die cracking during post-mold cure.
Plunger-to-pot thermal mismatch causing polymer flash bypass, scoring the hardened carbide pot sleeve, and generating uneven packing pressure across peripheral TSOP-54 cavities.

testcases.title: RF Dielectric Pre-Heater Core Pellet Temperature Uniformity & Conversion Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Multi-channel calibrated fast-response K-type thermocouple probe datalogger, differential scanning calorimeter (DSC Q2000), and non-contact IR thermal imager (FLIR A655sc).
testcases.pre_conditions: EMC pellets (Sumitomo EME series or equivalent biphenyl/novolac, 18mm diameter) stabilized at 22°C ± 1°C, relative humidity < 30% after completing mandatory 4-hour sealed nitrogen thaw protocol.
testcases.procedure: 1. Insert calibrated thermocouple into the radial geometric center of three test EMC pellets. 2. Place pellets into the high-frequency dielectric pre-heater electrode nest (approx. 27-70 MHz). 3. Energize pre-heater with recipe target 90°C for 12.0 seconds. 4. Record core, surface, and base temperatures upon cycle termination. 5. Immediately extract 5 mg core sample into hermetic DSC pan and ramp at 10°C/min to 250°C to measure residual reaction enthalpy (delta H_res) against unheated baseline enthalpy (delta H_0) to compute degree of conversion alpha = 1 - (delta H_res / delta H_0).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Core pellet temperature must reach 90.0°C ± 3.0°C across all test pellets with surface-to-core gradient <= 4.0°C. Chemical conversion degree alpha must remain <= 3.0% (residual enthalpy retention >= 97.0%).

testcases.title: Transfer Plunger Dynamic Pre-Heat Thermal Equilibrium & Pot Clearance Calibration
testcases.instrumentation: Surface contact pyrometer (calibrated against NIST standard), laser micrometric dial bore gauge (0.1 µm resolution), dynamic load cell sensor pack.
testcases.pre_conditions: Hydraulic/electric transfer mold press powered on; mold chases clamped at 175.0°C nominal setpoint for >= 45 minutes; plunger heaters energized.
testcases.procedure: 1. Measure plunger head face and radial perimeter temperature at 8 equidistant points using surface pyrometer. 2. Measure transfer pot liner inner diameter and plunger outer diameter at 175°C to calculate effective dynamic diametral clearance. 3. Execute 5 dry transfer cycles with automated plunger travel profile (1.5 mm/s transfer speed, 12 MPa clamping force). 4. Record dynamic friction load profile and temperature stability of plunger face across strokes.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Plunger face temperature must equal 175.0°C ± 1.5°C with circumferential delta <= 1.0°C. Dynamic diametral clearance between plunger and pot liner must be within 25.0 µm to 35.0 µm, with no galling, binding, or mechanical load fluctuation > 0.5 kN.

ppe_required: Thermal protective Kevlar gloves rated for 250°C contact (EN 407)
Half-face air-purifying elastomeric respirator with multi-gas/organic vapor/P100 particulate cartridge (3M 60926)
Chemical splash and impact-resistant face shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1+
Lint-free ESD cleanroom smock and conductive safety footwear
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Inhalation of thermal outgassing fumes: Evacuate person to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; seek emergency medical attention. Skin contact with molten or hot resin: Do not peel adhered resin forcibly; flush with copious cold water for >= 15 minutes to quench heat; dress with sterile non-adherent burn dressing. Eye contact: Flush immediately with isotonic eye wash for 15 minutes; consult ophthalmologist.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) hoods directly enclosing the pre-heater and mold pot opening with minimum face capture velocity of 0.75 m/s (150 FPM), routed through an activated charcoal scrubbing bed and HEPA filtration unit prior to exterior discharge.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Solid uncured purge slugs and rejected pre-heated pellets must be segregated in dedicated steel fire-rated collection drums, allowed to fully crosslink/quench in an exhaust-cooled zone, and disposed of as regulated hazardous polymer solid waste via certified high-temperature incineration.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Pre-conditioned cold-thawed solid cylindrical EMC pellet, free of surface condensation, frost, moisture film, or mechanical particulate flaking.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Homogeneously pre-heated plasticized pellet at 90°C core temperature ready for instant transfer pot loading without crusting or liquid drip.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding ambient air queue time results in moisture uptake (>0.08 wt%), triggering internal steam blistering during transfer molding and package delamination; exceeding pre-heater dwell time causes premature B-stage gelation, blocking mold runners and shearing bond wires.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: High-Pressure Transfer Ram Injection & In-Mold Thermal Polymerization Cycle Run
- **Context:** DRAM Foundation VN — 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 3)
- **Hierarchy:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Transfer Molding Epoxy Plastic Encapsulation (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package) > High-Pressure Transfer Molding & Post-Mold Cure (PMC) Execution
- **Action Type:** Make
- **Reference Doc:** [`docs/sop_transfer_ram_injection_mold_cure.md`](./docs/sop_transfer_ram_injection_mold_cure.md)

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Pre-Heat Leadframe &  │
│       Mold Chase       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Pellet Dispense &    │
│      Ram Transfer      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Controlled Velocity   │
│    Injection Phase     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     High-Pressure      │
│       Packing &        │
│     Densification      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        In-Mold         │
│  Polymerization Hold   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Chase Opening &     │
│      Ejection Pin      │
│       De-molding       │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Run Inspection & Substrate Pre-Heating**:
   - Verify incoming wire-bonded leadframe strip/substrate: ensure die attach with silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at 150°C for 60 min exhibits baseline thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5\text{ }^\circ\text{C/W}$ and pad bonding (25 $\mu$m wire on 100 $\mu$m $\times$ 100 $\mu$m Al pads) integrity.
   - Load strip into the transfer mold chase pre-heated to $175^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Ensure the chase vacuum seal activates ($P_{chase} \le 5\text{ Torr}$) to evacuate ambient air from runners and cavity wells before injection.

2. **Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Loading & Ram Transfer**:
   - Dispense pre-formed solid Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) tablet/pellet into the transfer pot.
   - Initiate high-pressure hydraulic/servo transfer ram down-stroke to compress and liquefy the EMC pellet under conductive heat transfer from the pot walls ($170^\circ\text{C}\text{--}180^\circ\text{C}$).

3. **Controlled Velocity Flow & Cavity Filling**:
   - Advance the transfer ram at a calibrated initial velocity ($1.0\text{--}3.5\text{ mm/s}$) to drive molten low-viscosity epoxy resin through the primary runner, sub-runners, and narrow package gates.
   - Maintain laminar melt front velocity across the TSOP-54 leadframe / FBGA wire loops (25 $\mu$m Au ball or Al wedge bonds) to prevent wire sweep, bond neck fatiguing, or ball shear deformation.

4. **High-Pressure Packing & Densification**:
   - Switch from velocity control to pressure packing upon $95\%\text{--}98\%$ cavity volume fill.
   - Apply pack pressure of $6.0\text{--}10.0\text{ MPa}$ ($60\text{--}100\text{ bar}$) via transfer ram to compress micro-voids and pack filler particulates into micro-gaps surrounding die edges and leadframe tie-bars.

5. **In-Mold Thermal Polymerization (Cross-Linking Hold)**:
   - Maintain clamping force ($150\text{--}300\text{ kN}$ dependent on mold platen size) and hold in-mold temperature at $175^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$ for a dwell time of $90\text{ to }120\text{ s}$.
   - Achieve cross-linking conversion ($> 80\%$) until resin reaches rigid green strength beyond the mold release threshold.

6. **Chase De-Clamping, Ejection, and Inspection**:
   - Disengage hydraulic clamp and separate upper and lower mold chases.
   - Actuate vertical mechanical ejector pins uniformly against leadframe rails and runners at controlled speed ($< 25\text{ mm/min}$) to eject the encapsulated strip without substrate warpage or cracking.
   - Route encapsulated strips to Post-Mold Cure (PMC) batch oven ($175^\circ\text{C}$ for 4 hours) for complete polymer network vitrification.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
Critical Thermal & Mechanical Packaging Targets
```
