---

### 4. Verified Context Citations
- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**: Multi-zone Kanthal heating coils (Load, Center, Source); triple-loop digital PID controller; Type-R/S thermocouples; temperature uniformity $\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ over central 300 mm; boat velocity $< 50\text{ mm/min}$.
- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery**: 350 mm flat zone maintaining $\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$; mass flow controller (MFC) gas sweep at 2.0 to 5.0 SLPM laminar flow.
- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**: 150°C cure for 60 minutes; package thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$; acoustic microscopy void area $< 5\%$; 25°C baseline ambient.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: PMC batch convection ovens exhibit non-uniform convective mass-transfer vectors across densely stacked magazine racks, causing localized thermal lag where center-boat packages lag outer-rail packages by up to 12°C during ramp. Relying on single-setpoint furnace thermocouple inputs without 9-point calibrated trailing thermocouples directly affixed to dummy leadframes will skew the closed-loop PID control, driving cross-linking gradients and uncompensated warpage across the TSOP-54 strip.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) vitrification kinetics require a tightly controlled ramp rate (1.5°C/min to 3.0°C/min) to prevent exothermic runaway during the secondary cross-linking reaction between 150°C and 175°C. Exceeding a 3.5°C/min ramp accelerates conversion before entrapped low-molecular volatiles (e.g., residual solvent, silane coupling agents) can diffuse out, driving micro-void coalescences at the silicon die-to-die attach paddle (DAP) interface and degrading Tg below the required 165°C threshold.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying custom molybdenum disilicide or proprietary high-alloy heating coils for packaging-grade batch ovens introduces a 16-to-20 week single-source procurement lead time from European vendors; standard Nichrome or Kanthal APM elements with multi-zone digital PID controllers and off-the-shelf mineral-insulated Type-K thermocouples must be prioritized to ensure local fab second-sourcing in Vietnam.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Tuning multi-zone profiles across multiple magazines consumes up to 8 production dummy leadframe strips and 16 hours of oven cycle availability per recipe iteration. The qualification protocol must lock multi-zone PID gains (P, I, D, and anti-windup deadband) within 3 qualification runs to prevent schedule slippage of the 180nm commercial MPW assembly gate.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal gradient-induced package warpage exceeding 75 µm across the TSOP-54 leadframe length due to asynchronous cure rates across magazine slots.
1. Interfacial delamination between EMC and copper leadframe/silicon die caused by incomplete cross-linking (conversion < 98%) or trapped outgassed volatiles during accelerated ramp-up.
1. Glass transition temperature (Tg) depression and high residual stress leading to internal wire bond neck fracture (25 µm Au wire) under thermal cycling.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-3-1-2-01` | **Multi-Zone Convection Batch Oven 9-Point Thermal Uniformity & Ramp Profile Verification** | Datapaq Q18 12-channel calibrated thermal data logger with high-temperature glass-fiber insulated Type-K thermocouples (calibrated to ±0.2°C traceable to NIST), calibrated dummy TSOP-54 copper test strips. | 1. Load dummy magazine rack into central heating zone of PMC batch oven. 2. Initialize recipe: Controlled ramp from 25°C to 175°C at programmed 2.0°C/min. 3. Maintain isothermal soak at 175°C for 240 minutes under 50 SLPM N2 purge. 4. Controlled cool-down ramp from 175°C to 50°C at 1.5°C/min. 5. Log all 9 channels at 1 Hz sampling rate across entire 360-minute duration. | `Ramp rate across all 9 zones must remain strictly within 1.8°C/min to 2.2°C/min; isothermal soak plateau (175°C) must maintain spatial uniformity <= ±2.0°C across all channels; no channel may overshoot 178.0°C during ramp-to-soak transition.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-3-1-2-02` | **EMC Degree of Cure (Conversion) & Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) Verification** | Differential Scanning Calorimeter (TA Instruments DSC2500) with sealed aluminum pans, calibrated to Indium reference standards; Dynamic Mechanical Analyzer (DMA Q800) in dual cantilever mode. | 1. Mill 10 mg (±0.5 mg) of cured EMC sample from center-zone and corner-zone package bodies, avoiding silicon and leadframe metal. 2. Hermetically seal sample in aluminum DSC pan. 3. Ramp DSC cell from 25°C to 300°C at 10°C/min under 50 mL/min N2 sweep to quantify residual exothermic heat of reaction (Delta H_residual). 4. Compare against un-cured raw pellet total heat of reaction (Delta H_total). 5. Measure Tg via DMA loss modulus peak at 1 Hz frequency from 30°C to 220°C at 3°C/min. | `Degree of cure (Conversion = [1 - Delta H_residual / Delta H_total] * 100%) must be >= 98.5%; Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) by DMA must be >= 165.0°C; delta Tg between corner and center magazine samples must be <= 3.0°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal heat-resistant aramid/Kevlar gauntlet gloves rated for 250°C contact, ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical/thermal splash face shield and safety glasses, Cleanroom-compatible flame-retardant lab coat (Nomex/cotton blend), N95 or half-mask air-purifying respirator equipped with organic vapor/particulate cartridges (3M 60926)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn: Immediately flush skin with cold, clean water for at least 15 minutes; apply sterile burn dressing; do not apply salves; transport to emergency medical facility. Inhalation of oven outgassing fumes: Evacuate exposed personnel to fresh air; administer oxygen if respiration is depressed; seek immediate medical evaluation. Nitrogen asphyxiation: Remove victim to open air; administer artificial respiration or CPR if not breathing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated high-temperature acid/solvent local exhaust ventilation (LEV) connected to oven plenum maintaining face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) and negative pressure >= 50 Pa relative to packaging bay; continuous optical N2 oxygen depletion monitors with audible/visual alarms set to trigger at < 19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Oven condensate traps must be cleaned bi-weekly using isopropanol wipes; solid cured resin waste collected in labeled hazardous material containers and routed to high-temperature thermal incineration; purge exhaust directed to fab central acid/VOC wet scrubber.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (99.999% pure) | `100.0%` |
| **Phenol-Formaldehyde Novolac Resin (EMC Outgassing Volatiles)** | `9003-35-4` | Technical/Decomposition Trace | `< 0.5% v/v in exhaust` |
| **Carbon Black (Filler additive outgassing aerosol)** | `1333-86-4` | Industrial Grade | `< 0.1 mg/m3` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly demolded TSOP-54 leadframe strips post-transfer molding at 175°C, free of visible mold flash, particulate contamination, or mechanical blistering.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully polymerized, vitreous thermoset EMC body with uniform matte black appearance, verified degree of cure >= 98.5%, warpage <= 50 µm across strip, ready for de-junk, trim, and form.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes atmospheric moisture absorption (> 0.15 wt%) by the uncured epoxy resin matrix, which vaporizes explosively during subsequent 175°C PMC ramp, generating severe popcorn microcracking and internal package delamination.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Multi-zone thermal ramp profile and isothermal soak recipe fully tuned and qualified for TSOP-54 DRAM encapsulation in convection batch ovens. Establishes uniform 2.0°C/min ramp, tight ±1.5°C soak control at 175°C for 240 minutes under N2 sweep, achieving >98.5% polymer conversion and package warpage < 50 µm.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PMC_THERMAL_PROFILING_9POINT_RUN03.csv`
- [ ] `EMC_DSC_CONVERSION_TG_METROLOGY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `TSOP54_POST_PMC_WARPAGE_CSAM_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Isothermal soak temperature uniformity across all 9 spatial monitoring locations in the loaded batch magazine** | `175.0°C` | ±1.5°C | Multi-channel calibrated Datapaq thermal logger recording at 1 Hz for 240 minutes |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Epoxy Molding Compound post-cure chemical cross-linking conversion rate** | `99.0%` | >= 98.5% | Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) residual exotherm quantification per ASTM E2160 |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Total end-to-end package strip coplanarity warpage post-PMC cycle** | `35.0 µm` | <= 50.0 µm | Shadow Moiré non-contact optical profilometry across full TSOP-54 leadframe strip at 25°C |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Completion of three consecutive dummy-load and live-package PMC oven cycles demonstrating 9-point thermal uniformity within ±1.5°C at 175°C, zero thermal runaway overshoots exceeding 178°C, DSC conversion >= 98.5% on center and edge packages, zero acoustic microscopy (CSAM) delamination at leadframe/die interfaces, and formal joint signoff by Packaging Integration Lead and Quality Assurance Manager.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Batch Temperature Uniformity Mapping & Thermal Shock Ramp-Down Qualification

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation [Foundry Tapeout & PDK] > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging [BEOL & Packaging] > Transfer Molding Epoxy Plastic Encapsulation (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package) [Packaging & Assembly] > High-Pressure Transfer Molding & Post-Mold Cure (PMC) Execution [Packaging] > High-Pressure Transfer Molding & Post-Mold Cure (PMC) Chamber Run [Packaging] > Post-Mold Cure (PMC) Batch Oven Run & Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) Void Metrology [Packaging] > PMC Convection Batch Oven Thermal Profile Setup & Ramp Qualification [Packaging] > Batch Temperature Uniformity Mapping & Thermal Shock Ramp-Down Qualification [Packaging]
**Target Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Oxide Thickness Tox: 3.5 nm (Gate) / 350 nm (Field).
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Spectroscopic Ellipsometer / C-V Profiler.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-mold cure (PMC) convection batch ovens require 9-to-16-point spatial thermocouple profiling across all magazine rack tiers to resolve boundary-layer convective velocity dead spots; applying high-temperature quartz tube furnace PID loop constants will cause severe overshoot or undershoot in low-thermal-mass nitrogen/air convection ovens operating at 175°C.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Epoxy molding compound (EMC) kinetics during PMC require precise isothermal soaking at 175°C to achieve full cross-linking density (>98% conversion) while avoiding thermal shock during ramp-down. A ramp-down rate exceeding 2.0°C/min introduces steep thermal gradients across the TSOP-54 copper leadframe and silicon die interface, resulting in residual thermo-mechanical stress, package warpage, and leadframe-to-epoxy delamination.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Class 10,000 / ISO 7 cleanroom-compatible convection batch ovens with calibrated multi-channel DataPaq loggers and semiconductor-grade high-purity N2 purge systems face long calibration turnaround times; failure to secure spare pre-calibrated Type-K thermocouple wire reels and calibrated data loggers risks packaging batch line stoppage.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: PMC thermal mapping and ramp-down qualification must align tightly with upstream transfer molding runs; any delay in oven qualification blocks leadframe strip release, which increases queue-time aging of molded strips and risks uncrosslinked matrix degradation before final electrical wafer sort/package test.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal shock ramp-down cracking and internal package delamination at the die-attach / leadframe / EMC interface caused by uncontrolled cooling gradients exceeding 2.0°C/min.
1. Spatial cure non-uniformity across batch racks leading to localized under-cured EMC zones (<95% glass transition temperature Tg attainment) and package warpage in TSOP-54 strips.
1. Outgassing volatile condensate redeposition onto exposed lead fingers caused by inadequate positive-pressure N2 convective exhaust sweep.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-3-1-3-01` | **Batch Chamber 9-Point Spatial Temperature Uniformity Mapping at 175°C Isothermal Dwell** | Calibrated 16-channel DataPaq thermal tracker with Type-K calibrated thermocouples (NIST traceable, ±0.5°C accuracy), high-temperature fixture jigs placed at top, middle, and bottom tiers of batch magazine rack, anemometer for convective airflow profiling. | 1. Load instrumented magazine fixture into the batch convection oven. 2. Initiate PMC thermal profile: Ramp up from 25°C to 175°C at 3.0°C/min. 3. Maintain isothermal soak at 175°C for 240 minutes. 4. Continuously log temperature data across all 9 channels at 1.0 Hz sampling rate. 5. Compute steady-state temperature delta (T_max - T_min) across all 9 points during the final 120 minutes of isothermal dwell. | `Temperature uniformity across all 9 spatial measurement points must satisfy 175.0°C ± 3.0°C (delta <= 5.0°C between extreme channels) throughout the 240-minute dwell period.` |

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Epoxy Molding Compound Multi-Hour Isothermal PMC Cure Execution
**Module:** BEOL Packaging & Assembly  
**Node/Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip — DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Package Types:** TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Workflow

Post-Mold Cure (PMC) completes cross-linking of the epoxy matrix, drives off residual volatile organic compounds, relieves molding-induced thermal stresses, and ensures package integrity to preserve wire bonds and die-attach thermal interfaces.

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Load Leadframes into  │
│     Batch Carrier      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Nitrogen Purge &    │
│  Thermal Ramp to 175C  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Isothermal PMC Soak:  │
│   175C, 4 to 6 Hours   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Controlled Ramp Down  │
│         to 50C         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  C-SAM Acoustic Void   │
│     & Delamination     │
│       Metrology        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Cure Inspection & Batch Staging:**
   - Transfer molded TSOP-54 leadframe strips or 54-ball FBGA substrate strips into slotted stainless-steel PMC cassette racks.
   - Maintain a minimum strip clearance of $12\text{ mm}$ between tiers to ensure uniform convection air/nitrogen circulation.
   - Verify all carrier lots within 2 hours post-transfer molding to prevent ambient moisture absorption prior to polymer network finalization.

2. **Chamber Loading & Environment Purge:**
   - Load cassette racks into the industrial batch convection PMC oven.
   - Close chamber door, initiate $N_2$ positive-pressure purge until residual oxygen levels drop below $100\text{ ppm}$ to prevent copper leadframe/wire oxidation.

3. **Thermal Ramp-Up:**
   - Ramp chamber temperature from ambient ($25^\circ\text{C}$) to $175^\circ\text{C} \pm 3^\circ\text{C}$ at a controlled rate of $2.0^\circ\text{C/min}$ to $3.0^\circ\text{C/min}$ to avoid thermal shock to internal 25 µm gold or aluminum wire bonds.

4. **Multi-Hour Isothermal PMC Soak:**
   - Hold isothermal soak at **$175^\circ\text{C} \pm 3^\circ\text{C}$** for **$4.0\text{ hours}$ to $6.0\text{ hours}$** continuous dwell time.
   - Ensure temperature uniformity across all oven monitoring zones is within $\pm 2.5^\circ\text{C}$.

5. **Controlled Cooldown & Unload:**
   - Cool down at a maximum ramp rate of $\le 1.5^\circ\text{C/min}$ until chamber reaches $\le 50^\circ\text{C}$ before opening chamber door.
   - Transfer cured lots into dry desiccator cabinets ($< 10\%\text{ RH}$) for acoustic microscopy metrology.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                  PMC Thermal & Physical Metric Thresholds
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░                           │
Pull Strength (gf)┤░░░░░░░░░                           │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                         │
 Void Area Max (%)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                         │
  PMC Soak (Hours)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                           │
                  │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                           │
   PMC Temp (C/10)┤████████████████████████████████████│
                  │████████████████████████████████████│
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0      4.4      8.8    13.1    17.5 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value | Verification Standard & Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Acoustic Void Area Under Die** | **$< 5.0\%$** of total die surface area | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM, Mil-Std-883) |
| **Die-Attach Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | **$\le 5.0^\circ\text{C/W}$** | Thermal Transient Tester (T3Ster / Ablebond spec) |
| **Post-Cure Wire Pull Strength** | **$\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force (gf)}$** (span failure mode) | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 Wire Pull Gauge (25 µm wire) |
| **Package Delamination** | **$0\%$ delamination** at die-to-molding & leadframe interfaces | C-SAM (High-frequency transducer $100\text{–}230\text{ MHz}$) |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

* **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:**
  - *Die Attach & Interface Metrology:* Silver-filled conductive epoxy cured with target thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$; acoustic microscopy void area threshold under die $< 5\%$.
  - *Wire Interconnect Integrity:* Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 minimum pull strength force $\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force (gf)}$ for $25\text{ µm}$ wire diameter with mandatory failure in wire span rather than bond interface.
* **Positive Photoresist Spin Dynamics, Soft Bake & Development Protocol:**
  - Standard thermal dehydration and convection profiles ($150^\circ\text{C}$ desorption kinetics) governing solvent evacuation and thermal dwell mechanics.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-mold cure (PMC) must provide thermal profile uniformity across all magazine slots within +/- 2.5°C to avoid CTE differential mismatch and localized warpage between the 180nm DRAM silicon die (CTE ~2.6 ppm/°C), copper leadframe/substrate (CTE ~16.5 ppm/°C), and epoxy molding compound (CTE ~10-12 ppm/°C below Tg). Inadequate isothermal soak results in spatial gradients of cross-linking density, shifting internal residual stresses that manifest as retention degradation or dielectric cracking across TSOP-54 packages.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Epoxy molding compound (EMC) conversion kinetics require a multi-hour isothermal dwell at 175°C (+/- 5°C) to push thermoset epoxy-phenol novolac cross-linking conversion from the in-mold green state (~80-85%) to greater than 98%. Heating ramp rates must strictly remain below 3°C/min to prevent sudden outgassing of volatile cross-linking byproducts and moisture, which induces internal micro-void formation and delamination at the die-attach fillet and active DRAM metallization interface.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: PMC batch convection ovens represent a critical assembly bottleneck; chamber loading must be balanced against nitrogen consumption (purity >= 99.999% to prevent leadframe tarnish/oxidation) and furnace uptime. Standardizing magazines to standard 54-ball FBGA/TSOP-54 carriers minimizes lead time and avoids tooling changeover delays across multi-lot runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: PMC cycle duration directly dictates work-in-progress (WIP) cycle time between transfer molding and CSAM void metrology. Strict queue-time enforcement into the PMC chamber within 120 minutes of transfer molding ejection is mandatory to ensure consistent green-state curing kinetics and avoid premature room-temperature moisture uptake.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete EMC cross-linking resulting in glass transition temperature (Tg) depression below 140°C, causing package swelling and popcorning during JEDEC reflow.
1. Non-uniform thermal gradients inducing asymmetric shrinkage stress, package warpage exceeding 50 um, and severe delamination at the EMC-to-die interface.
1. Excessive thermal ramp rates generating blister voids and popcorning from trapped volatiles and moisture.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-3-2-01` | **Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) EMC Degree of Cure Verification** | TA Instruments Q2000 / Discovery DSC with hermetic aluminum sample pans and analytical microbalance (0.01 mg precision) | 1. Weigh 10.0 mg cured EMC sample and seal in hermetic aluminum pan. 2. Equilibrate cell at 30°C. 3. Ramp temperature at 10.0°C/min under 50 mL/min N2 purge up to 300°C. 4. Record residual exothermic reaction peak area (Delta H_residual). 5. Compare against reference baseline un-cured EMC enthalpy (Delta H_total = 112.5 J/g). 6. Calculate Degree of Cure: alpha = (1 - Delta H_residual / Delta H_total) * 100%. | `Pass if residual exothermic enthalpy Delta H_residual <= 2.25 J/g, corresponding to Degree of Cure alpha >= 98.0%, and glass transition temperature Tg >= 150.0°C.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-3-2-02` | **Shadow Moiré Dynamic Package Warpage Metrology** | Akrometrix TherMoiré AXP Thermal Warpage Metrology System with calibrated 300 lines/inch optical grating | 1. Mount molded package strip onto TherMoiré sample stage. 2. Position shadow moiré optical fringe head and adjust optical contrast. 3. Acquire 3D surface topography map at 25°C room ambient across entire package body. 4. Execute simulated JEDEC J-STD-020 reflow profile (ramp to 260°C peak, cool down to 25°C). 5. Continuously measure out-of-plane displacement (coplanarity / warpage vector) across active die zone and package corners. | `Pass if maximum package warpage at 25°C <= 35.0 um and peak dynamic warpage throughout the 260°C thermal cycle <= 50.0 um without package cracking.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal heat-resistant gloves (rated >= 250°C), Safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1), Lab coat / anti-static chemical-resistant ESD smock, N95 particulate / organic vapor half-face respirator (during oven loading/unloading)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn: Immediately immerse affected area in cool, clean running water for at least 15 minutes; cover with sterile dry dressing; do not apply salves; seek medical attention. Inhalation of oven outgassing vapors: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored; seek immediate medical assessment.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Batch curing convection oven must be connected to dedicated solvent/VOC chemical scrubbed local exhaust with negative pressure extraction rate >= 150 CFM, preventing off-gas migration into cleanroom air.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Fully cured epoxy polymer dummy strips are non-hazardous solid polymer waste; dispose of through approved industrial solid waste stream. Contaminated un-cured or partially cured resin scrap must be segregated into sealed hazardous chemical waste drums for licensed high-temperature incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Biphenyl/o-Cresol Novolac Epoxy Resin** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Molding Grade | `10-20 wt%` |
| **Phenolic Hardener (Phenol-Formaldehyde Novolac)** | `9003-35-4` | Electronic Grade | `5-15 wt%` |
| **Fused Silica Filler (Silicon Dioxide)** | `60676-86-0` | High-Purity Spherical Microfine (>99.9%) | `75-88 wt%` |
| **High-Purity Nitrogen Gas (N2)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 (>= 99.999%) | `100 vol%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly ejected green-state transfer-molded leadframe strips, degated, deflashed, dry, with degree of cure >= 80% and surface temperature cooled below 40°C.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully polymerized, vitreous thermoset EMC surface (cure conversion >= 98%), moisture-desorbed, cooled to <= 30°C in cleanroom air, zero oxidation on exposed leadframe copper/leads.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time prior to PMC causes green-state EMC to absorb atmospheric ambient moisture (relative humidity > 30%), inducing micro-voiding, explosive interfacial delamination, and popcorning blistering during subsequent PMC heating.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Execution of multi-hour isothermal Post-Mold Cure (PMC) cycle (175°C for 4 hours with controlled ramp/cool <= 2°C/min under N2 inert blanket) for TSOP-54 packaged 180nm DRAM devices, achieving >98% cross-linking conversion, package warpage <35 um, and zero interfacial delamination.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PMC_Isothermal_Run_Thermal_Log_Lot180DRAM.csv`
- [ ] `DSC_EMC_Cure_Degree_Analysis_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `TherMoire_Package_Warpage_Profile_Lot180DRAM.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Degree of cure (cross-linking conversion) of molded EMC body** | `98.5%` | +/- 1.0% (>= 98.0% minimum) | Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) residual enthalpy measurement according to ASTM E2160 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Glass transition temperature (Tg) of post-cured EMC** | `155.0°C` | +/- 5.0°C (>= 150.0°C minimum) | Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) / TMA glass transition inflection method |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Room-temperature package out-of-plane warpage post-PMC** | `22.0 um` | +/- 10.0 um (<= 35.0 um maximum) | Shadow Moiré optical interferometry topography across 54 package units per strip |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Signoff accepted when DSC demonstrates cross-linking conversion >= 98.0% with Tg >= 150.0°C across 3 sample locations (front, center, back of furnace magazine), oven thermal logger confirms 175°C dwell maintained for 240 +/- 5 minutes with all sensor channels within +/- 2.5°C, and shadow moiré warpage remains <= 35.0 um with 0% detected delamination by subsequent CSAM inspection.

Inadequate isothermal soak results in spatial gradients of cross-linking density, shifting internal residual stresses that manifest as retention degradation or dielectric cracking across TSOP-54 packages.
critics.domain_expert: Epoxy molding compound (EMC) conversion kinetics require a multi-hour isothermal dwell at 175°C (+/- 5°C) to push thermoset epoxy-phenol novolac cross-linking conversion from the in-mold green state (~80-85%) to greater than 98%. Heating ramp rates must strictly remain below 3°C/min to prevent sudden outgassing of volatile cross-linking byproducts and moisture, which induces internal micro-void formation and delamination at the die-attach fillet and active DRAM metallization interface.
critics.supply_chain: PMC batch convection ovens represent a critical assembly bottleneck; chamber loading must be balanced against nitrogen consumption (purity >= 99.999% to prevent leadframe tarnish/oxidation) and furnace uptime. Standardizing magazines to standard 54-ball FBGA/TSOP-54 carriers minimizes lead time and avoids tooling changeover delays across multi-lot runs.
critics.laya_pm: PMC cycle duration directly dictates work-in-progress (WIP) cycle time between transfer molding and CSAM void metrology. Strict queue-time enforcement into the PMC chamber within 120 minutes of transfer molding ejection is mandatory to ensure consistent green-state curing kinetics and avoid premature room-temperature moisture uptake.
critical_failure_modes: Incomplete EMC cross-linking resulting in glass transition temperature (Tg) depression below 140°C, causing package swelling and popcorning during JEDEC reflow.
Non-uniform thermal gradients inducing asymmetric shrinkage stress, package warpage exceeding 50 um, and severe delamination at the EMC-to-die interface.
Excessive thermal ramp rates generating blister voids and popcorning from trapped volatiles and moisture.

testcases.title: Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) EMC Degree of Cure Verification
testcases.instrumentation: TA Instruments Q2000 / Discovery DSC with hermetic aluminum sample pans and analytical microbalance (0.01 mg precision)
testcases.pre_conditions: Select post-cure molded TSOP-54 dummy sample; extract 10 +/- 2 mg of cured EMC scrap material from package perimeter; purge cell with high-purity N2 at 50 mL/min.
testcases.procedure: 1. Weigh 10.0 mg cured EMC sample and seal in hermetic aluminum pan. 2. Equilibrate cell at 30°C. 3. Ramp temperature at 10.0°C/min under 50 mL/min N2 purge up to 300°C. 4. Record residual exothermic reaction peak area (Delta H_residual). 5. Compare against reference baseline un-cured EMC enthalpy (Delta H_total = 112.5 J/g). 6. Calculate Degree of Cure: alpha = (1 - Delta H_residual / Delta H_total) * 100%.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass if residual exothermic enthalpy Delta H_residual <= 2.25 J/g, corresponding to Degree of Cure alpha >= 98.0%, and glass transition temperature Tg >= 150.0°C.

testcases.title: Shadow Moiré Dynamic Package Warpage Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Akrometrix TherMoiré AXP Thermal Warpage Metrology System with calibrated 300 lines/inch optical grating
testcases.pre_conditions: TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA strips after completed PMC cool-down to 25°C; surface clean and dust-free; fixture calibrated with zero-deflection quartz reference flat.
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount molded package strip onto TherMoiré sample stage. 2. Position shadow moiré optical fringe head and adjust optical contrast. 3. Acquire 3D surface topography map at 25°C room ambient across entire package body. 4. Execute simulated JEDEC J-STD-020 reflow profile (ramp to 260°C peak, cool down to 25°C). 5. Continuously measure out-of-plane displacement (coplanarity / warpage vector) across active die zone and package corners.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass if maximum package warpage at 25°C <= 35.0 um and peak dynamic warpage throughout the 260°C thermal cycle <= 50.0 um without package cracking.

ppe_required: Thermal heat-resistant gloves (rated >= 250°C)
Safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1)
Lab coat / anti-static chemical-resistant ESD smock
N95 particulate / organic vapor half-face respirator (during oven loading/unloading)
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Thermal burn: Immediately immerse affected area in cool, clean running water for at least 15 minutes; cover with sterile dry dressing; do not apply salves; seek medical attention. Inhalation of oven outgassing vapors: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored; seek immediate medical assessment.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Batch curing convection oven must be connected to dedicated solvent/VOC chemical scrubbed local exhaust with negative pressure extraction rate >= 150 CFM, preventing off-gas migration into cleanroom air.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Fully cured epoxy polymer dummy strips are non-hazardous solid polymer waste; dispose of through approved industrial solid waste stream. Contaminated un-cured or partially cured resin scrap must be segregated into sealed hazardous chemical waste drums for licensed high-temperature incineration.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly ejected green-state transfer-molded leadframe strips, degated, deflashed, dry, with degree of cure >= 80% and surface temperature cooled below 40°C.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Fully polymerized, vitreous thermoset EMC surface (cure conversion >= 98%), moisture-desorbed, cooled to <= 30°C in cleanroom air, zero oxidation on exposed leadframe copper/leads.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding queue time prior to PMC causes green-state EMC to absorb atmospheric ambient moisture (relative humidity > 30%), inducing micro-voiding, explosive interfacial delamination, and popcorning blistering during subsequent PMC heating.

expected_result.summary: Execution of multi-hour isothermal Post-Mold Cure (PMC) cycle (175°C for 4 hours with controlled ramp/cool <= 2°C/min under N2 inert blanket) for TSOP-54 packaged 180nm DRAM devices, achieving >98% cross-linking conversion, package warpage <35 um, and zero interfacial delamination.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Degree of cure (cross-linking conversion) of molded EMC body
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) residual enthalpy measurement according to ASTM E2160

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Glass transition temperature (Tg) of post-cured EMC
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) / TMA glass transition inflection method

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Room-temperature package out-of-plane warpage post-PMC
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Shadow Moiré optical interferometry topography across 54 package units per strip

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Signoff accepted when DSC demonstrates cross-linking conversion >= 98.0% with Tg >= 150.0°C across 3 sample locations (front, center, back of furnace magazine), oven thermal logger confirms 175°C dwell maintained for 240 +/- 5 minutes with all sensor channels within +/- 2.5°C, and shadow moiré warpage remains <= 35.0 um with 0% detected delamination by subsequent CSAM inspection.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Frequency C-SAM Acoustic Microscopy Void & Delamination Inspection

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-CSAM-001`  
**Process Level:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS DRAM) — Metrology & Package Reliability  
**Target Package:** TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Applicable Layer:** Mold Compound & Die-Attach Interface (Ablebond 84-1LMIS)

---

### 1. Process Flowchart

│                       │
│  Immerse Package in   │

│                       │

┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Select 100MHz to    │
│   230MHz Transducer   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Calibrate A-Scan    │
│  Interface Echo and   │
│       Set Gate        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    XY Raster Scan     │
│    Across Die and     │
│   Paddle Interface    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Evaluate Reflection  │
│  Amplitude and Phase  │
│       Inversion       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────◇───────────┐
│                       │
│  Void Area under Die  │
│      below 5pct       │
│                       │
└───────────◇───────────┘
            │
            ├─────────────────────────────╮Fail
        Pass│                             │
            ▼                             ▼
┌───────────────────────┐     ┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │     │                       │
│    Dry Package and    │     │    Quarantine and     │
│    Release to Next    │     │  Trigger MRB Review   │
│         Stage         │     │                       │
└───────────────────────┘     └───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Couplant Bath Preparation**:
   - Fill the C-SAM immersion tank with high-purity deionized (DI) water. Degas the water bath to prevent micro-air bubbles from adhering to package surfaces and inducing false acoustic reflections.
2. **Fixture & Transducer Setup**:
   - Secure the post-mold cured (PMC) TSOP-54 or 54-ball FBGA units into the level multi-unit scanning tray.
   - Install a high-frequency acoustic transducer (100 MHz – 230 MHz, focal length 0.25"–0.5") to provide depth resolution for 180nm DRAM packaging interfaces.
3. **Acoustic Focus & A-Scan Gating**:
   - Position the transducer over a known reference standard or package center.
   - Adjust the Z-axis focus until the reflection peak from the silicon die backside and the conductive epoxy die-attach interface (Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at 150°C for 60 min) is maximized on the A-scan waveform.
   - Set the data acquisition time gate precisely spanning the die-attach interface between the silicon die bottom and the lead frame paddle / substrate.
4. **C-Scan Raster Scanning**:
   - Execute an automated XY raster scan over 100% of the active die footprint at a scan step size $\le 10\ \mu\text{m}$.
   - Monitor RF signal phase inversion and reflection amplitude. A high-amplitude signal accompanied by a $180^\circ$ phase flip indicates an acoustic impedance transition from solid to air/vacuum (delamination or voiding).
5. **Image Processing & Void Area Calculation**:
   - Generate acoustic pseudo-color intensity maps for both die-to-epoxy and epoxy-to-paddle interfaces.
   - Run automated pixel thresholding to sum the cumulative void area across the die footprint.
6. **Post-Inspection De-hydration & Release**:
   - Remove passed packages from the DI tank, blow dry with filtered clean dry air (CDA) or $\text{N}_2$, and transfer to a dry oven bake (100°C–125°C) to eliminate moisture before wafer sort and final electrical test.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

M1 Sheet Resist┤██                                     │

               │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│

               0.0       1.2      2.5       3.8     5.0 
```

1. **Die-Attach Void Area**:
   - **Target Metric**: Total cumulative void area under the die **$< 5\%$** of total die interface area via acoustic microscopy integration.
2. **Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)**:
   - **Target Metric**: Package thermal junction-to-case resistance **$R_{th} \le 5\ ^\circ\text{C/W}$** under silver-filled conductive epoxy attachment.
3. **Wire Bond Integrity (Pre-C-SAM Verification)**:
   - **Target Metric**: Wire pull strength **$\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$** for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011, with rupture restricted to wire span.
4. **Interconnect Sheet Resistance (BEOL Baseline)**:
   - **Target Metric**: Metal-1 sheet resistance **$R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$** with film thickness target of $350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$.

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - Die attach specification: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at 150°C for 60 minutes.
  - Thermal criteria: $R_{th} \le 5\ ^\circ\text{C/W}$.
  - Acoustic microscopy criterion: Void area under die $< 5\%$.
  - Wire pull strength: Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire.
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - Metal-1 interconnect thickness $350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$ with measured sheet resistance target $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$.

---
*Micro-knowledge persisted to [`sop_csam_acoustic_microscopy.md`](./docs/sop_csam_acoustic_microscopy.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM transducer frequency selection (typically 100 MHz to 230 MHz for thin plastic TSOP-54 and FBGA packages) must balance acoustic attenuation through silica-filled epoxy molding compound (EMC) against spatial resolution at the die-attach and leadframe/interposer interfaces. Focusing gate depth must be synchronized with time-of-flight (TOF) algorithms to distinguish top package surface reflections from active silicon die-surface delamination without ringing artifacts shadowing underlying micro-voids.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Acoustic impedance mismatch between EMC (Z ~ 3 to 6 MRayls) and silicon (Z ~ 19.7 MRayls) yields positive phase reflection, whereas air voids or delamination interfaces yield 100% negative phase reversal (phase shift of 180 degrees) with near-total reflection amplitude. Calibration using acoustic phase inversion gating is strictly required to differentiate between resin-rich fillet boundaries and true interfacial delamination per IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020E criteria.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-frequency transducers (e.g., Sonix, Nordson SONOSCAN 150-230 MHz piezoelectric UHF transducers) have extended procurement lead times (16 to 24 weeks) and fragile focal lenses susceptible to physical shock or cavitation damage. A secondary vendor or local OSAT metrology subcontracting route in SE Asia (e.g., Vietnam/Taiwan) must be qualified for high-volume lot screening to avoid production halt during PMC release.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-SAM metrology represents an inline non-destructive quality gate prior to environmental stress testing (MSL-3 baking and temperature cycling). Inspection throughput is bounded by immersion raster scan speed (typically 1.5 to 3 minutes per strip); sample plan gating (AQL 0.4 Level II vs. 100% screening) must be strictly defined to prevent a metrology bottleneck right out of the PMC batch oven.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial delamination between EMC and active die face exceeding 10% total surface area or crossing bond pad pitch, inducing shear failure of gold/copper wire bonds during thermal cycling.
1. Paddle/die-attach voiding exceeding 15% cumulative area or 5% single-void area under the silicon die, causing localized thermal hot spots and package popcorning during reflow soldering.
1. Water ingress via immersion tank during scanning through defective package seal lines or micro-cracks, causing latent package swelling and false acoustic impedance readings.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-3-3-01` | **Die Surface and Wire Bond Interface Delamination C-SAM Verification** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) equipped with 150 MHz UHF focused immersion transducer (focal length 12.7 mm), deionized water immersion bath, RF pulse pulser/receiver, and automated phase-analysis defect mapping software. | 1. Fixture TSOP-54 leadframe strip into the planarizing immersion stage. 2. Align acoustic focus to the EMC-to-die top active surface interface utilizing pulse echo time-of-flight gating (gate width: 15 ns centered on silicon front-surface echo). 3. Calibrate RF signal phase so that intact mold-to-silicon boundary produces a positive polarity echo. 4. Execute raster scan at 0.5 um step resolution across 100% of sample units. 5. Process reflected amplitude and phase inversion to calculate interfacial delamination percentage per die area. | `Pass: Zero interfacial delamination across active die circuitry and wire bond regions (0.0% area); peripheral non-critical die margin delamination < 5.0% total area; phase inversion reflection amplitude < -6.0 dB relative to reference air boundary.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-2-3-3-02` | **Die Attach Epoxy Voiding and Leadframe Paddle Acoustic Inspection** | Dual-frequency C-SAM operating at 100 MHz transducer with long focal length for backside/leadframe acoustic penetration, RF digitizer (minimum 1 GHz sampling rate), and automated image segmentation thresholding tool. | 1. Position inverted package strip in DI water carrier. 2. Set focus gate depth to die-attach epoxy layer between silicon substrate backside and copper leadframe paddle. 3. Acquire transmission (Through-Scan / T-Scan) and reflective C-Scan acoustic data. 4. Execute image binarization at 50% acoustic attenuation threshold. 5. Quantify individual void dimensions and aggregate void percentage across die-attach area. | `Pass: Cumulative die-attach void area <= 10.0% of total die footprint; single contiguous void area <= 3.0%; corner voiding length <= 0.20 mm from die edge; zero continuous void path extending across leadframe pad width.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom chemical-resistant nitrile gloves (EN 374-1), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety splash glasses with side shields, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and anti-static ESD conductive footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For DI water: Non-hazardous; in case of floor spill, wipe dry immediately to eliminate slip/fall hazards. For IPA: Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air. Eye contact: Rinse immediately with copious physiological saline or eye wash station water for >= 15 minutes. Skin: Wash thoroughly with soap and water.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom recirculating HEPA laminar flow bench (ISO Class 6 / Fed Std 209E Class 1000). Dedicated low-velocity solvent point-of-use exhaust hood (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s) at IPA post-wash package drying station.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used DI water tank effluent drains directly to standard semiconductor industrial wastewater neutralizer system. Spent IPA solvent is collected in designated grounded stainless-steel flammable waste carboys for hazardous chemical waste reclamation.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Acoustic Coupling Medium)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type II Ultra-Pure Cleanroom Water | `100.0%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) (Post-Scan Package Drying Agent)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Semiconductor Grade | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Cured EMC plastic encapsulation post 175°C Post-Mold Cure (PMC) batch oven run, completely cooled to ambient, clean and free of mold flash, mold release residue, or mechanical surface scratches.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: 100% acoustically inspected TSOP-54 packages, rinsed of coupling DI water, dried via dry-N2 air knife and vacuum oven desiccation (0.0% residual surface/subsurface moisture), loaded in anti-static JEDEC trays.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time before drying or post-inspection baking induces moisture absorption into hygroscopic epoxy molding compound (> 0.05 wt% H2O uptake), causing false acoustic attenuation readings or triggering steam popcorn package delamination during subsequent board assembly reflow.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete, non-destructive volumetric acoustic microscopy evaluation of 180nm DRAM TSOP-54 molded leadframe strips, quantifying internal EMC-to-die delamination, leadframe adhesion, and die-attach void percentages in strict compliance with IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020E.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_METROLOGY_INSPECTION_REPORT_LOT_RUN.pdf`
- [ ] `CSAM_ACOUSTIC_DEFECT_MAPS_AND_VOID_STATISTICS.csv`
- [ ] `CSAM_RAW_ACOUSTIC_TIME_OF_FLIGHT_RF_SCANS.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **EMC-to-active silicon die interface delamination percentage across entire wafer-sort-qualified lot sample** | `0.0%` | +0.5% (confined strictly to inactive non-circuit silicon periphery) | High-Frequency C-SAM 150 MHz RF phase-inversion acoustic gate analysis |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Backside silicon die-attach epoxy voiding percentage relative to total die paddle area** | `<= 8.0%` | +2.0% (absolute upper limit <= 10.0% cumulative void area) | Automated gray-scale thresholding binarization of 100 MHz backside acoustic reflection C-Scan |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Acoustic void analysis across sample lot demonstrates 0.0% active die area delamination and <= 10.0% cumulative die-attach voiding with zero wire-bond shadow delaminations; 100% inspected packages verified desiccated and documented in CSAM_METROLOGY_INSPECTION_REPORT_LOT_RUN.pdf; formal QA release approval logged in MES.

# Standard Operating Procedure: SAM Acoustic Void Metrology & Package Delamination Inspection

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM (Scanning Acoustic Microscopy) pulse-echo analysis at 100 MHz to 230 MHz UHF acoustic transducer frequencies must decouple acoustic reflection phase reversals (die-to-EMC or substrate-to-EMC negative acoustic impedance boundary mismatches, indicating total delamination) from bulk viscoelastic acoustic attenuation through silica-filled epoxy molding compounds. Gate delays and time-of-flight (TOF) depth-windowing must be calibrated to within +/-2.5 ns to resolve the active DRAM die surface and prevent acoustic shadow artifacts from leadframe tie-bars and wire bond stitch loops.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Epoxy molding compound (EMC) post-mold cure (PMC) completeness dictates ultrasonic velocity (v = sqrt(C11/rho), typically 2800-3100 m/s); under-cured resin creates artificial acoustic velocity dispersion and phase distortion. For TSOP-54 and 54-ball FBGA packages, JEDEC J-STD-020E and J-STD-035 criteria dictate that any single delamination along the active DRAM die face exceeding 10% interfacial area, or interfacial delamination along wire bonds bridging adjacent bond pads, constitutes an automatic structural reliability rejection.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Deionized water coupling fluid in acoustic immersion tanks must be monitored for ionic contamination (<0.1 uS/cm conductivity) to prevent galvanic corrosion of exposed Cu/Ni-Pd-Au leads during extended dwell times. Transducer piezoelectric element wear and immersion tank automated scanning axes (linear motor XY resolution <= 0.5 um) require calibrated quartz reference blocks and backup transducer stock to avoid halting inline packaging lot verification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: SAM inspection cycle times represent an inline bottleneck: full lot A-scan/C-scan scanning at 1 um pixel pitch requires 180 seconds per unit, which violates the throughput budget. Implementation of a strict sample-gate protocol (ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 Level II Normal Inspection, AQL 0.40) coupled with automated ROI thresholding is required to maintain the 4-hour post-PMC dry-pack Q-time window before moisture absorption occurs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Active die-surface interfacial delamination (EMC-to-passivation acoustic phase inversion, reflection coefficient R approaches -1.0) leading to shear-stress-induced aluminum/copper interconnect peeling during thermal cycling.
1. Internal bulk mold voids (>50 um diameter) or corner leadframe stitch-delamination causing moisture entrapment, vapor pressure expansion, and catastrophic 'popcorn' package cracking during 260 deg C lead-free reflow.
1. Coupling fluid ingress through microscopic microcracks during immersion inspection, generating false acoustic transmission readings and unremovable moisture contamination inside unsealed packages.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-01` | **C-Mode High-Frequency Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) Die-Attach & Die-Surface Delamination Verification** | Sonix or Sonoscan Gen6 C-SAM with 100 MHz to 230 MHz wideband focused piezoelectric transducer (F-number = 2.0), automated deionized water immersion scanning tank with 0.5 um linear encoder resolution, digital oscilloscope digitizer (>= 1 GSa/s), and acoustic phase-inversion gating software. | 1. Fixture 20 sample packages in the automated tray and immerse in the degassed DI water tank. 2. Align transducer focal point to the die-to-EMC interface by adjusting Z-axis to peak echo return amplitude. 3. Configure digital time-of-flight (TOF) gate window across the primary die surface echo (+/- 15 ns width centered on the die interface peak). 4. Execute raster scan over package surface at 2.0 um step pitch in X and Y axes. 5. Capture RF waveform, peak amplitude, and phase sign (positive peak = bonded interface, negative inverted peak = delamination/air gap). 6. Apply image processing thresholding to compute contiguous delamination area percentage over active die surface. | `Pass: Zero (0%) active die-surface interfacial delamination across wire-bond pad regions; total contiguous die-face delamination < 5.0% of total die surface area (excluding non-active wafer edge exclusion zone); zero phase inversion (R > 0) along bond wire stitch perimeters.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-02` | **High-Resolution Through-Transmission Acoustic (T-Scan) and Bulk Void Volumetric Inspection** | Dual-transducer Through-Transmission Acoustic Microscopy (TTAM) system (50 MHz transmit transducer, 50 MHz receive hydrophone/transducer pair), calibrated acoustic attenuator, 16-bit A/D RF data acquisition system. | 1. Position dual transducers axially aligned along the vertical Z-axis through the package center. 2. Perform calibration scan through an unfilled, void-free reference epoxy block to establish baseline 0 dB signal attenuation. 3. Execute raster through-scan across the entire package body at 5.0 um step size. 4. Map transmitted amplitude attenuation matrix across the package volume. 5. Detect localized acoustic transmission drops (void shadowing where transmission drops > 20 dB due to air-void acoustic scattering). 6. Extract size, equivalent spherical diameter, and spatial coordinates of each detected void. | `Pass: Zero voids with equivalent diameter > 75 um in the bulk mold compound; zero void > 25 um situated within 50 um of any wire bond or active die edge; total bulk void volumetric fraction < 0.05% of total package encapsulant volume.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof chemical safety goggles, Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (double-gloving recommended during solvent cleaning), ESD-safe cleanroom lab coat / antistatic smock, Closed-toe slip-resistant cleanroom safety footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye exposure to IPA/surfactant bath: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; seek ophthalmological attention if irritation persists. Skin exposure: Remove contaminated gloves and rinse thoroughly with clean deionized water and mild soap. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Move victim to fresh cleanroom air supply; administer oxygen if respiration becomes labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank and sample spin-dry/IPA rinse stations must be operated under local exhaust canopy or laminar downdraft hood with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); volatile solvent vapors vented directly to the dedicated cleanroom VOC scrubbed exhaust header.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent acoustic immersion tank water containing trace surfactant and particulate matter must be routed to industrial wastewater neutralization facilities; spent IPA and solvent wipes collected in dedicated, grounded, flame-arrested stainless steel hazardous waste drums for off-site licensed hazardous thermal disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Acoustic Coupling Medium)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I Cleanroom Grade | `100.0%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA / 2-Propanol, Post-Scan Drying Solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Tier 1) | `99.9%` |
| **Non-Ionic Wetting Agent / Surfactant (Triton X-100 / Octoxynol-9)** | `9002-93-1` | Analytical Reagent Grade | `0.05%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Completed Post-Mold Cure (PMC: 175 deg C, 4 hours), fully cooled to ambient temperature (25 +/- 2 deg C) in cleanroom Class 1000 environment; surface free of mold flash, oil, or particulate contaminants.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Centrifugally spin-dried and baked at 125 deg C for 30 minutes; zero residual DI water moisture, surface moisture content < 0.05 wt% verified by moisture balance; leadframes clean, unoxidized, and ready for lead finish/trim-and-form.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time prior to moisture bake-out causes ambient moisture absorption into micro-voids and epoxy-copper interfaces, inducing J-STD-020 MSL3 failure and catastrophic package delamination/popcorning during subsequent solder reflow testing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> 100% verifiable inline metrology qualification verifying zero structural delamination along the active 180nm DRAM die surface, die attach paddle, and internal leadframe leads, with comprehensive C-SAM phase-analysis mapping and bulk void quantification conforming to JEDEC J-STD-035 and MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `SAM_Acoustic_Inspection_Report_Lot_DRAM180_PMC.pdf`
- [ ] `Delamination_Phase_and_Void_Distribution_Matrix.csv`
- [ ] `Full_Die_Surface_CScan_Acoustic_Images_100MHz.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Active DRAM die-to-EMC top-face contiguous delamination area** | `0.0` | +0.0% | Automated C-SAM RF phase-inversion pixel thresholding within active die boundary |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum bulk mold compound void equivalent spherical diameter** | `0.0` | +50.0 um | Through-transmission acoustic attenuation peak-valley image segmentation |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-inspection package residual moisture content prior to trim-and-form** | `0.02` | +/-0.01 wt% | Thermogravimetric / moisture analyzer balance sample verification post-125 deg C bake |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero lot rejections on active die face delamination across all sampled units; all detected bulk voids under 50 um; all units pass 125 deg C post-scan bake with moisture content verified below 0.03 wt%; metrology package deliverables signed off by Lead Metrology Researcher and Packaging QA Manager.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: Acoustic Transducer Calibration & Immersion Fluid Setup
**Process Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Transfer Molding Epoxy Plastic Encapsulation (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package) > High-Pressure Transfer Molding & Post-Mold Cure (PMC) Execution > SAM Acoustic Void Metrology & Package Delamination Inspection > **Acoustic Transducer Calibration & Immersion Fluid Setup**  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (nm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Deionized Water     │
│    Degassing & Temp    │
│     Stabilization      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Transducer Mounting   │
│      & Alignment       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Acoustic Focal Plane  │
│       & RF Echo        │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    C-SAM Metrology     │
│        Baseline        │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Immersion Fluid Preparation & Degassing:**
   - Fill the Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (SAM) immersion reservoir with ultra-pure deionized (DI) water (resistivity $\ge 18\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
   - Run the in-line degassing cycle / ultrasonic bubbler degassing system to remove dissolved microbubbles.
   - Maintain the fluid temperature stabilized at room ambient of **$25^\circ\text{C}$** to establish constant acoustic velocity ($c \approx 1498\text{ m/s}$) and minimize thermal impedance drift.

2. **Transducer Mounting & Mechanical Co-Planarity Alignment:**
   - Mount the high-frequency acoustic transducer (e.g., 50–100 MHz focused piezoelectric immersion lens) onto the scanning Z-axis stage fixture.
   - Lower the transducer lens into the degassed immersion water over the optical flat / silicon calibration coupon.
   - Adjust the motorized tilt/swivel goniometer stages until normal incidence acoustic reflection is attained, maximizing the amplitude of the first front-surface return echo.

3. **RF Echo Waveform Calibration & Gating:**
   - Trigger the pulser/receiver unit and align the front-surface echo response on the oscilloscope/A-scan RF trace.
   - Position the dynamic software electronic time gate to isolate the internal package interface reflections (specifically targeting the epoxy mold-to-die and silver-filled epoxy die-attach boundary).
   - Adjust focal depth ($Z$-position) so the acoustic beam waist is located at the die-attach plane, confirming symmetrical RF waveform peak-to-peak amplitude.

4. **Metrology Baseline & Baseline Resolution Check:**
   - Perform a reference scan over an Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured die-attach calibration standard coupon.
   - Verify that spatial scanning resolution and signal-to-noise ratio allow unambiguous detection and segmentation of void areas below the specified threshold.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                           ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                           │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓      │
Wire Pull Strength Min (gf)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓      │
  Die Thermal Res Max (C/W)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
                           │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
  Die Attach Void Limit (%)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                           │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                           └┬───────┬──────┬───────┬──────┬┘
                           0.0     1.2    2.5     3.8   5.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value / Limit | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Die-Attach Acoustic Void Area** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM acoustic interface area integration) |
| **Immersion Fluid & Ambient Temp** | $25$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | In-situ calibrated digital immersion bath thermometer |
| **Post-Cure Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | $\le 5.0$ | $^\circ\text{C/W}$ | Steady-state junction thermal impedance testing |
| **Wire Bond Pull Strength Standard** | $\ge 4.0$ | $\text{gf}$ | Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 destructive pull test |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Sources

- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**
  - *Die Attach & Metrology Quality Standards:* Silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 minutes; Thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$; **void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy**.
  - *Temperature Constraints:* Ultrasonic aluminum wedge bonding operates at room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$); Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ grams-force}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire. Bonding pad dimensions: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Transducer acoustic focal length calibration must dynamically account for deionized water temperature drift and acoustic velocity variation (approx. 2.5 m/s per degree Celsius). If water bath thermal stabilization is uncoupled from the Z-axis piezo feedback loop, focal plane displacement during TSOP-54/FBGA leadframe depth profiling causes inaccurate echo reflection amplitudes, skewing C-SAM delamination quantification at the die attach and mold compound interfaces.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Operating high-frequency acoustic transducers (100 MHz to 230 MHz for thin DRAM encapsulation inspection) requires degassed, ultra-pure immersion fluids. Entrained micro-bubbles act as high acoustic impedance mismatch voids (Z_air approx. 0.0004 MRayl vs. Z_water approx. 1.5 MRayl), inducing acoustic shadow artifacts, beam scattering, and false delamination flags at leadframe tie bars and mold-compound-to-silicon interfaces.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-source vulnerability on piezoelectric composite/lithium niobate transducers (e.g., Sonix, Sonoscan/Nordson) and specialized non-corrosive acoustic coupling fluids or high-grade surfactants introduces 12 to 16 week lead times. Sourcing backup broadband transducers and qualifying local inline degassers with standardized 0.1 um filtration assemblies is vital for continuous OSAT metrology operations.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration protocols and bubble-purging procedures must align strictly with JEDEC J-STD-020 and J-STD-035 acoustic inspection schedules without bottlenecking post-mold cure inspection.
