nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: C-SAM Pulse-Echo Scanning for Die Attach & Molding Voids

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM (Scanning Acoustic Microscopy) pulse-echo analysis at Gen 3 for TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA encapsulation must maintain high acoustic impedance contrast fidelity between the mold compound (Z ~ 3.5-5.5 MRayls) and silicon die (Z ~ 19.7 MRayls) or copper/alloy-42 leadframe (Z ~ 40 MRayls). A critical system bottleneck is transducer frequency selection: while a 15 MHz to 50 MHz transducer provides sufficient depth penetration through thick mold caps (>1.0 mm), resolving sub-100 µm micro-delaminations at the die attach fillet and die face passivation requires a high-frequency (100 MHz to 230 MHz) focused immersion transducer. Scanning automation must integrate synchronized X-Y piezoelectric linear rastering with sub-micron step resolution and precise time-of-flight (TOF) electronic gating to isolate front-mold-to-silicon, die-attach adhesive, and back-package interfaces without waveform clipping.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Per J-STD-020E and J-STD-035 acoustic inspection guidelines, voiding and delamination criteria are strictly differentiated between die-top active circuitry, die attach boundary, and lead fingers. For 180nm DRAM fabricated dies, any interfacial delamination covering >10% of the active die surface area or any continuous delamination track bridging adjacent lead fingers/bond pads causes catastrophic thermal dissipation degradation and wire bond stitch shear failure during reflow. The acoustic pulse-echo phase inversion signature (180-degree phase shift where reflection coefficient R = (Z2 - Z1)/(Z2 + Z1) transitions from positive to negative at air/delamination gaps) must be digitally discriminated from high-frequency acoustic attenuation in highly filled (>85 wt% fused silica) epoxy molding compounds (EMC).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic microscopy scanning requires ultra-pure, degassed deionized (DI) immersion water to prevent microscopic microbubbles (acting as artificial acoustic voids) on package surfaces. High-precision transducers (Sonix, PVA TePla, or Nordson Sonoscan 100-230 MHz focused UHF transducers) carry long lead times of 16-24 weeks and high replacement costs if dropped or mechanically crashed into the immersion tank jig. Sourcing specialized anti-corrosion, non-ionic surface tension wetting agents (e.g., fluoro-surfactants or low-foaming ethoxylates) compatible with cleanroom packaging lines requires verified domestic supply chains within Vietnam to avoid import delays.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-SAM metrology acts as the decisive QA gate between Post-Mold Cure (PMC) and final test/reliability qualification (MSL-3 bake & moisture soak, autoclave/HAST). Inspection cycle time per TSOP-54 strip or FBGA JEDEC tray must not exceed 6 minutes for 100% sample lot screening, or strict statistical process control (SPC) 5-unit sample per mold chase cycle must be enforced. If C-SAM fails to close out within the designated post-cure Q-time, packages run the risk of uncontrolled ambient atmospheric moisture ingress prior to moisture barrier bag (MBB) sealing, distorting baseline SAM acoustic echo signatures.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-bubble entrapment on mold package surface generating false-positive air void indications during acoustic pulse-echo rastering.
1. Improper time-of-flight (TOF) gate alignment leading to acoustic signal overlap between the mold-compound-to-die interface and the die-attach adhesive layer, masking critical die-shear delamination.
1. Transducer focus misalignment causing signal diffusion and missed planar delamination micro-cracks (<1 µm gap) at active die corner passivation boundaries.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-2-01` | **C-SAM Pulse-Echo Die Attach Void and Fillet Coverage Verification** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) equipped with 100 MHz / 0.5-inch focal length UHF immersion transducer, motorized XYZ scan stage with 0.5 µm optical encoder resolution, and 1 GHz high-speed RF digitizer with real-time A/B/C-scan and phase inversion detection. | 1. Fixture post-PMC DRAM package strip into the immersion scanning nest. 2. Position the 100 MHz transducer normal to the package top surface and optimize acoustic pulse focus onto the die attach interface. 3. Configure RF echo receiver gain to 42 dB and set electronic time-of-flight (TOF) Gate 1 to isolate the die-to-substrate adhesive boundary (window width: 45 ns). 4. Execute bidirectional raster C-scan across 100% of package area at 100 mm/s scan speed and 10 µm step resolution. 5. Process acoustic amplitude and RF waveform phase data to identify negative phase peaks indicative of air/void interfaces. 6. Compute total void area percentage and single largest continuous void area using automated image thresholding per MIL-STD-883 Method 2030. | `Total die attach voiding must be <= 10.0% of total die attach area; no single continuous void exceeding 5.0% of die attach area; zero voiding or delamination spanning across the package edge boundary to die edge fillet.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-2-02` | **Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Interfacial Delamination & Bulk Void Inspection** | C-Mode High-Frequency Scanning Acoustic Microscope with dual-gated RF acquisition, 50 MHz wideband transducer for bulk penetration and 100 MHz transducer for top surface/die passivation interface, DI water immersion tank with degasser and ultrasonic bubble eliminator. | 1. Mount molded DRAM package onto automated vacuum hold-down fixture submerged in degassed immersion water. 2. Align focal plane of 100 MHz transducer at the EMC-to-die active face passivation interface. 3. Establish Gate A at the front mold-silicon interface and Gate B within the bulk EMC thickness (0.1 mm to 0.8 mm depth). 4. Perform high-resolution acoustic C-scan with 5 µm pixel grid across active die surface and leadframe paddle. 5. Record phase polarity map (positive reflection = intact bonding; negative 180° inverted phase = delamination/air gap). 6. Extract acoustic intensity histogram and flag any contiguous low-impedance acoustic anomalies exceeding 50 µm equivalent diameter. | `0% interfacial delamination across active DRAM circuit region, bond pads, and wire bond stitch areas; bulk EMC internal voids must not exceed 75 µm in diameter; zero contiguous delamination along leadframe paddle exceeding 15% total contact area per J-STD-020E.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10,000 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, minimum 5 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side splash shields, ESD-safe anti-static cleanroom lab coat, Closed-toe chemical/water-resistant cleanroom safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with surfactant solution or IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean running water or saline solution for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; wash affected skin with mild soap and water. If IPA vapors cause dizziness: Move victim immediately to fresh air; provide artificial respiration if breathing ceases and seek urgent medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank area requires ambient laminar cleanroom HEPA airflow (ISO Class 6/7) with 30-45 air changes per hour; post-scan IPA drying hotplate/blowoff station must be equipped with dedicated point-of-use local exhaust ventilation (LEV) maintaining minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent immersion water containing trace non-ionic surfactant must be collected in cleanroom greywater effluent drains routed to dedicated industrial wastewater neutralization; IPA rinse residues must be stored in grounded, flame-proof hazardous solvent waste drums for approved thermal oxidation/incineration per local environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Immersion Acoustic Couplant)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (ASTM D5127 Type E-1) | `100.0%` |
| **Non-ionic Wetting Agent / Surfactant (Octylphenol Ethoxylate)** | `9002-93-1` | Analytical Reagent (AR) Grade | `0.05% to 0.1% aqueous solution` |
| **Isopropanol (Drying and Cleaning Agent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C4) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Molded packages freshly discharged from Post-Mold Cure (PMC) convection oven (175°C, 4 hours), fully cooled to room temperature (22°C), visually free from mold resin bleed, flash, or particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Packages fully rinsed with clean DI water, nitrogen blow-dried, baked dry at 125°C for 30 minutes to eliminate all residual acoustic immersion moisture, verified zero moisture condensation, and stored in desiccated bake trays.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time before SAM inspection or delayed post-scan drying causes unmonitored ambient moisture absorption into the hydrophilic epoxy matrix; upon subsequent solder reflow or thermal shock testing, entrapped moisture induces popcorn cracking, artificial interfacial delamination, and copper leadframe oxidation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete non-destructive acoustic pulse-echo verification of die-attach void percentage, EMC bulk density, and interfacial bonding integrity for TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA 180nm DRAM packages, ensuring zero active circuit delamination and full compliance with J-STD-020E and MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_DieAttach_VoidAnalysis_LotReport.csv`
- [ ] `CSAM_PhaseInversion_CScan_AcousticMap.tiff`
- [ ] `CSAM_Package_Integrity_QA_Signoff_Summary.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total die attach voiding percentage across the die paddle surface area** | `<= 8.0%` | +2.0% absolute maximum (upper specification limit <= 10.0%) | Automated C-SAM C-scan image analysis with acoustic threshold segmentation per MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Interfacial delamination area at the active DRAM die surface and wire bond stitch perimeter** | `0.0%` | +0.0% (zero tolerance, strictly non-detected) | High-frequency (100 MHz) RF phase inversion peak detection across electronic Gate A |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum diameter of individual bulk epoxy molding compound micro-voids** | `<= 35.0 µm` | +15.0 µm (maximum allowable single void <= 50.0 µm) | B-scan acoustic depth profile cross-sectional sizing calibrated against 1 GHz digitizer timebase |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All sampled packages from the mold/PMC lot demonstrate total die attach voiding under 10.0%, zero active circuit interface phase inversion delamination, zero popcorn micro-cracks, and 100% completion of post-acoustic inspection dry bake (125°C, 30 min) documented with digital engineering QA signoff in CSAM_Package_Integrity_QA_Signoff_Summary.pdf.

testcases.title: Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) Interfacial Delamination & Bulk Void Inspection
testcases.instrumentation: C-Mode High-Frequency Scanning Acoustic Microscope with dual-gated RF acquisition, 50 MHz wideband transducer for bulk penetration and 100 MHz transducer for top surface/die passivation interface, DI water immersion tank with degasser and ultrasonic bubble eliminator.
testcases.pre_conditions: Packages dried and inspected under optical stereo microscope at 40x to verify absence of gross external surface flash or contamination; C-SAM acoustic gain and attenuator calibrated to 80% full screen height (FSH) from unblemished die active surface echo; water immersion tank temperature stabilized at 23.0°C ± 0.5°C.
testcases.procedure:
1. Mount molded DRAM package onto automated vacuum hold-down fixture submerged in degassed immersion water.
2. Align focal plane of 100 MHz transducer at the EMC-to-die active face passivation interface.
3. Establish Gate A at the front mold-silicon interface and Gate B within the bulk EMC thickness (0.1 mm to 0.8 mm depth).
4. Perform high-resolution acoustic C-scan with 5 µm pixel grid across active die surface and leadframe paddle.
5. Record phase polarity map (positive reflection = intact bonding; negative 180° inverted phase = delamination/air gap).
6. Extract acoustic intensity histogram and flag any contiguous low-impedance acoustic anomalies exceeding 50 µm equivalent diameter.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: 0% interfacial delamination across active DRAM circuit region, bond pads, and wire bond stitch areas; bulk EMC internal voids must not exceed 75 µm in diameter; zero contiguous delamination along leadframe paddle exceeding 15% total contact area per J-STD-020E.

ppe_required: Class 10,000 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, minimum 5 mil thickness)
ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side splash shields
ESD-safe anti-static cleanroom lab coat
Closed-toe chemical/water-resistant cleanroom safety shoes
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin/eye contact with surfactant solution or IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean running water or saline solution for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; wash affected skin with mild soap and water. If IPA vapors cause dizziness: Move victim immediately to fresh air; provide artificial respiration if breathing ceases and seek urgent medical evaluation.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Immersion tank area requires ambient laminar cleanroom HEPA airflow (ISO Class 6/7) with 30-45 air changes per hour; post-scan IPA drying hotplate/blowoff station must be equipped with dedicated point-of-use local exhaust ventilation (LEV) maintaining minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent immersion water containing trace non-ionic surfactant must be collected in cleanroom greywater effluent drains routed to dedicated industrial wastewater neutralization; IPA rinse residues must be stored in grounded, flame-proof hazardous solvent waste drums for approved thermal oxidation/incineration per local environmental regulations.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Molded packages freshly discharged from Post-Mold Cure (PMC) convection oven (175°C, 4 hours), fully cooled to room temperature (22°C), visually free from mold resin bleed, flash, or particulate contamination.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Packages fully rinsed with clean DI water, nitrogen blow-dried, baked dry at 125°C for 30 minutes to eliminate all residual acoustic immersion moisture, verified zero moisture condensation, and stored in desiccated bake trays.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding air exposure queue time before SAM inspection or delayed post-scan drying causes unmonitored ambient moisture absorption into the hydrophilic epoxy matrix; upon subsequent solder reflow or thermal shock testing, entrapped moisture induces popcorn cracking, artificial interfacial delamination, and copper leadframe oxidation.

expected_result.summary: Complete non-destructive acoustic pulse-echo verification of die-attach void percentage, EMC bulk density, and interfacial bonding integrity for TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA 180nm DRAM packages, ensuring zero active circuit delamination and full compliance with J-STD-020E and MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 standards.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum diameter of individual bulk epoxy molding compound micro-voids

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Deionized Water Immersion Couplant & Acoustic Transducer Calibration

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-SAM-001`  
**Revision:** `1.0`  
**Process Branch:** 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation $\rightarrow$ BEOL Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging $\rightarrow$ TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package $\rightarrow$ C-SAM Pulse-Echo Scanning for Die Attach & Molding Voids  
**Subject:** High-Frequency Acoustic Immersion Couplant Preparation and Transducer Calibration for 180nm DRAM Post-Mold SAM Inspection

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP defines the setup, conditioning, and quantitative calibration of the deionized (DI) water immersion acoustic couplant bath and high-frequency piezoelectric transducer (pulse-echo mode). The objective is to achieve an optimal signal-to-noise ratio ($> 30\text{ dB}$) and linear ultrasonic propagation required to detect delamination, resin voids, and die attach voiding under the 180nm DRAM die ($< 5\%$ void area specification as mandated by die attach reliability criteria).

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   DI Water Prep &    │
│        Degas         │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Water Bath Loading  │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Transducer Mount &  │
│      Alignment       │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│    A-Scan RF Peak    │
│        Tuning        │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│     Calibration      │
│     Verification     │
│                      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Couplant Bath Fluid Preparation & Degassing
1. Draw ultra-pure deionized (DI) water from the semiconductor supply loop. Verify resistivity $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ to prevent ionic residue or corrosion on package leadframe finishes and substrate balls.
2. Transfer DI water into the vacuum membrane degassing unit. Run active ultrasonic vacuum degassing at $-85\text{ kPa}$ gauge pressure for 30 minutes to reduce dissolved oxygen (DO) content to $< 2.0\text{ ppm}$.
3. Fill the scanning immersion tank slowly along the tank sidewalls at a flow rate $\le 1.0\text{ L/min}$ to suppress micro-bubble entrainment.
4. Maintain tank couplant temperature at $22.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 1.0^\circ\text{C}$ using an inline chiller/heater loop to lock acoustic velocity in water at $1488\text{ m/s}$.

#### Step 2: Transducer Fixturing & Gimbal Alignment
1. Mount the selected focused ultrasonic transducer (nominal center frequency: $100\text{ MHz}$ or $150\text{ MHz}$, focal length $F = 12.7\text{ mm}$ / $0.5\text{ in}$) onto the Z-axis scanning carriage.
2. Inspect acoustic lens surface under an optical magnifier; ensure the sapphire/fused silica concave acoustic lens is free of micro-bubbles, particulate contamination, and mechanical scratches.
3. Place a polished silicon reference standard (mirror-polished bare $180\text{ nm}$-grade test substrate) flat on the immersion sample stage.
4. Align transducer normal vector perpendicular to the silicon standard utilizing the two-axis mechanical gimbal ($\theta_X, \theta_Y$):
   - Adjust tip/tilt micrometer screws while monitoring the real-time A-scan RF reflected waveform until peak-to-peak reflection amplitude ($V_{pp}$) from the front surface is strictly maximized and symmetrical.

#### Step 3: A-Scan RF Pulse-Echo Tuning & Focal Plane Calibration
1. Set the pulser-receiver excitation voltage to $-150\text{ V}$ spike or square pulser mode with a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of $10\text{ kHz}$ to prevent ghost reverberation echoes.
2. Set pulse damping to $50\ \Omega$ impedance-matched load.
3. Translate the Z-axis motorized stage vertically toward the reference surface. Track the front surface echo amplitude envelope to identify the acoustic focal waist:
   - Identify the point of maximum amplitude corresponding to the true focal length ($Z_0 \approx 12.7\text{ mm}$).
4. Zero the scanning system Z-axis coordinate at this focal reference plane.
5. Calibrate the receiver gain ($0\text{ to }60\text{ dB}$) such that the primary interface echo reaches $80\% \pm 2\%$ Full Screen Height (FSH) without clipping or preamplifier saturation.

#### Step 4: Spatial Resolution & Amplitude Linearity Verification
1. Position the transducer over a certified acoustic calibration standard block containing calibrated flat-bottom holes (FBH, diameter $\le 50\ \mu\text{m}$).
2. Execute a precision raster C-scan over the standard ($X\text{-}Y$ step size: $5\ \mu\text{m}$).
3. Measure the -6 dB beamwidth across the test feature to ensure spatial resolution $\le 35\ \mu\text{m}$ at focal depth.
4. Lock calibrated parameters in the SAM recipe database for the TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA DRAM package inspection run.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                    Acoustic Metrology Setup Parameters 
                   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                   │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
   RF Amp Match (%)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                   │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                            │
Resistivity (MO-cm)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                            │
   DO Content (ppm)┤▓▓                                 │
                   │▓▓                                 │
     Water Temp (C)┤█████████                          │
                   │█████████                          │
                   └┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬┘
                   0.0     24.6    49.2     73.9   98.5 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Couplant DI Water Resistivity** | $18.2$ | $\ge 18.0$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ ($@ 25^\circ\text{C}$) | Inline resistivity probe |
| **Dissolved Oxygen (DO) Content** | $1.8$ | $< 2.0$ | $\text{ppm}$ | Optical DO meter probe |
| **Couplant Bath Temperature** | $22.0$ | $\pm 1.0$ | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | Calibrated RTD thermistor |
| **Interface Reflection Echo Amplitude** | $80.0$ | $80.0 \pm 2.0$ | $\%$ FSH | Oscilloscope / A-scan digitizer |
| **Die Attach Void Area Detection Limit** | $< 5.0$ | $\le 5.0$ | $\%$ of die attach area | C-SAM pulse-echo gating integration |

---

### 4. Verified Literature & Context Citations
* **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging]**: 
  - Standardizes die attach reliability criteria: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS) requiring thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$ and acoustic microscopy inspection verifying **void area under die $< 5\%$**.
  - Provides mechanical assembly boundaries for DRAM dies and bonding interfaces.
* **[Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects]**:
  - Sets 180nm metallization parameters for bitline and interconnect stacks ($350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$ metal thickness) ensuring acoustic impedance boundary definition across backend metallization layers.
* **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
  - Establishes the 180nm technology node cell layout topology and silicon substrate specifications.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Couplant water degassing and temperature stability are critical for acoustic impedance matching; thermal drift directly shifts the acoustic velocity in water (approx. 2.5 m/s per °C), causing gate timing misregistration and focal plane defocus across the 180nm TSOP-54/FBGA packages.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-frequency ultrasound (>50-100 MHz) attenuation in DI water increases quadratically with frequency; micro-bubble formation on the acoustic lens or package mold compound creates severe acoustic shadow artifacts resembling mold voids or delamination. In-line ultrasonic degassing (<2 ppm dissolved O2) and wetting surfactant control are strictly mandatory.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Focused acoustic transducers with high center frequencies (50-230 MHz, PVDF or LiNbO3 piezoelectric elements) have lead times exceeding 12-16 weeks and fragile sapphire or silica delay lines prone to chipping during automated tray handling; dual-sourcing and matched spare transducers must be maintained in stock.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibrating transducers and deionized couplant tanks must adhere to a strict bi-weekly baseline routine to prevent false-positive rejection of assembled DRAM batches, ensuring inspection throughput meets tapeout qualification milestones without bottlenecking PMC-to-Reliability queues.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-bubble nucleation on transducer acoustic lens causing acoustic impedance mismatch, beam scattering, and false delamination callouts.
1. Acoustic transducer delay-line wear or piezo element depoling resulting in >3 dB center frequency drift and loss of axial resolution at the die-attach interface.
1. Dissolved ionic contamination in the immersion couplant bath causing dendritic corrosion or moisture-induced pad degradation on exposed package leads/solder balls.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-2-1-01` | **Transducer Center Frequency & -6dB Bandwidth Calibration on Quartz Reference** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) pulser-receiver, 500 MHz 8-bit Digitizer, Polished Optical-Grade Fused Quartz Calibration Block, 75 MHz Focused Acoustic Transducer | 1. Position the 75 MHz transducer normal to the fused quartz reference flat at the nominal focal distance (0.50 inches). 2. Acquire the time-domain pulse-echo signal from the top surface of the quartz block. 3. Perform Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) on the front-wall reflection echo to extract the frequency spectrum. 4. Record peak center frequency (fc) and calculate the -6 dB fractional bandwidth. | `Center frequency fc must be 75.0 MHz ± 3.75 MHz (within ±5%); -6 dB bandwidth must exceed 55% of nominal center frequency.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-2-1-02` | **Deionized Water Couplant Dissolved Oxygen & Resistivity Qualification** | In-line dissolved oxygen (DO) optical sensor, Traceable benchtop resistivity meter with 0.01 cell constant probe, Pt100 temperature sensor | 1. Sample 250 mL of immersion bath water directly from the transducer scanning nozzle. 2. Measure dissolved oxygen content via luminescent optical probe. 3. Measure couplant electrical resistivity and fluid temperature concurrently. 4. Verify surface tension using standard Wilhelmy plate or contact angle monitor. | `Dissolved oxygen concentration <= 1.5 ppm; electrical resistivity >= 15.0 MOhm*cm at 25.0°C; bath temperature 22.0°C ± 1.0°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves, ANSI Z87.1 certified splash goggles, ESD-safe cleanroom coat, Closed-toe ESD cleanroom footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush eyes with sterile eyewash for 15 minutes in case of surfactant splash. Skin contact: Wash with soap and clean water. Inhalation: Move to fresh air if aerosolized mist causes irritation. Ingestion: Non-toxic at trace dilutions; drink water and seek medical attention if symptoms develop.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom HEPA laminar airflow unit; local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on degassing vacuum pump exhaust to exhaust oil mist or ozone outside the cleanroom envelope.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous effluent routed directly to the facility industrial acid/waste neutralization (AWN) system; no halogenated or toxic organic solvents permitted in couplant reservoir.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-Pure Electronic Grade (Type 1) | `100%` |
| **Non-ionic Surfactant (Triton X-100 / Octoxynol-9, trace wetting agent)** | `9002-93-1` | Reagent Grade | `< 0.05%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-Mold Cured (PMC) TSOP-54 / FBGA package surface clean, dry, residue-free, and degreased.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Blow-dried with high-purity filtered N2 knife; moisture purged via vacuum bake-out; zero water droplet residues.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Package lead oxidation, copper leadframe tarnishing, moisture absorption into epoxy molding compound causing steam explosion (popcorning) during subsequent solder reflow testing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration of high-frequency acoustic scanning transducer and qualification of degassed DI water couplant system, ensuring artifact-free C-SAM imaging capable of resolving delamination and voids >= 50 um at the die-attach interface of 180nm DRAM packages.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `transducer_acoustic_spectrum_calibration_report.pdf`
- [ ] `couplant_bath_water_quality_log.csv`
- [ ] `c_sam_quartz_reference_resolution_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Transducer center frequency stability under pulse-echo mode** | `75.0 MHz` | ±5.0% (71.25 MHz to 78.75 MHz) | FFT spectral analysis of pulse-echo from optical-grade fused quartz standard block |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Couplant dissolved oxygen level to prevent micro-bubble acoustic scatter** | `1.0 ppm` | <= 2.0 ppm maximum | In-line optical luminescence dissolved oxygen sensor reading |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Couplant electrical resistivity at scanning temperature** | `18.0 MOhm*cm` | >= 15.0 MOhm*cm | Calibrated temperature-compensated resistivity probe |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Transducer achieves nominal center frequency within ±5%, couplant dissolved oxygen verifies <= 2.0 ppm with resistivity >= 15.0 MOhm*cm, and zero bubble artifacts are detected across a 50 mm x 50 mm scan area on the quartz reference standard signed off by the packaging metrology lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Frequency C-SAM Pulse-Echo Scanning Recipe Execution for Leadframe & Die Attach Interface

**Classification:** Metrology SOP | 180nm Open-Source DRAM Package Reliability  
**Package Types:** TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA  
**Target Interface:** Silicon Die (100 µm × 100 µm pads) to Silver-Filled Epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) to Leadframe Paddle  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Scan Sequence

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Sample Loading and   │
│    Degas Immersion     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Transducer Focus and  │
│   Acoustic Coupling    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  A-Scan Gating at Die  │
│    Attach Interface    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    C-SAM Pulse-Echo    │
│    Raster Scanning     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Phase Inversion and   │
│       Void Area        │
│     Quantification     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Acoustic Bath Preparation & Sample Immersion:**
   - Fill the C-SAM immersion tank with deaerated, deionized (DI) water maintained at room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$). Ensure degas cycles prevent micro-bubble accumulation on package surfaces.
   - Secure the TSOP-54 leadframe strip or 54-ball FBGA carrier onto the motorized $X\text{--}Y\text{--}Z$ scanning stage.

2. **Transducer Setup & Focal Alignment:**
   - Install a high-frequency focused acoustic transducer ($100\text{--}230\text{ MHz}$, calibrated for silicon package penetration).
   - Adjust the $Z$-axis acoustic focus through the package backside or silicon die bulk directly onto the die attach plane.

3. **RF Waveform & A-Scan Gating Calibration:**
   - Acquire the pulse-echo A-scan RF signal. Identify the primary echo interfaces:
     - Peak 1: Water/silicon (or mold compound) top interface.
     - Peak 2: Silicon die-to-die attach epoxy interface.
     - Peak 3: Die attach-to-leadframe paddle interface.
   - Configure a narrow time-domain hardware gate spanning Peak 2 and Peak 3 (tracking the silver-filled conductive epoxy layer).
   - Set signal polarity tracking to detect phase inversion ($180^\circ$ phase flip, indicating an acoustic impedance drop caused by air voids/delamination).

4. **Pulse-Echo C-Scan Raster Acquisition:**
   - Execute an $X\text{--}Y$ raster scan over the full active die footprint ($X\text{-pitch} \le 5\ \mu\text{m}$, $Y\text{-pitch} \le 5\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Record peak amplitude and phase inversion maps across the entire die attach boundary.

5. **Void & Delamination Quantification:**
   - Apply binary image thresholding to delineate delaminated and voided regions (areas with phase inversion and high reflected amplitude).
   - Integrate total void pixel count relative to the calibrated total die area.

---

  - *Thermal & acoustic tolerances:* Thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$; total void area under die $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy.
  - *Bonding interface context:* Aluminum bonding pads ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$) wire-bonded to external leadframe pins.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Pulse-echo C-SAM acoustic inspection at high frequencies (100-230 MHz) requires precise time-of-flight gating synchronization between the acoustic transducer, pulser-receiver, and 3-axis scanning gantry. For the TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA package, acoustic impedance mismatches between the epoxy molding compound (Z ≈ 5.5 to 6.5 MRayl), silver-filled epoxy die attach (Z ≈ 8.0 MRayl), silicon die substrate (Z ≈ 19.7 MRayl), and copper/alloy-42 leadframe (Z ≈ 30 to 45 MRayl) generate complex boundary reflections. Inadequate RF gate positioning will misidentify die-attach voids as molding compound delamination or leadframe flag unbonds, directly contaminating downstream yield binning.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-frequency ultrasound inspection (specifically 100 MHz to 175 MHz focused transducers with focal lengths of 0.5 to 0.75 inches) is mandatory to resolve sub-50 µm micro-voids in the Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled epoxy matrix without experiencing catastrophic attenuation through 0.7 mm of silica-filled epoxy molding compound. The A-scan RF waveform phase inversion (+ to - polarity flip) at the die-attach/silicon or die-attach/leadframe flag interface serves as the unambiguous signature of an acoustic mismatch against air (Z_air ≈ 0.0004 MRayl, reflection coefficient R ≈ -1.0). Total cumulative void area must not exceed 5.0% of the die footprint, with no single contiguous void spanning > 1.0% or bridging active DRAM bitline periphery.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acoustic transducer heads operating above 100 MHz incorporate fragile piezoelectric single-crystal zinc oxide (ZnO) or lithium niobate (LiNbO3) elements that degrade or depole rapidly under thermal shock or improper deionized water immersion. Sourcing calibrated Sonix/PVA TePla/Nordson acoustic transducers has a 16-to-20 week lead time. Maintaining dual-source qualified transducers and standardized acoustic reference calibration wafers with micro-machined back-side air pockets is essential to avoid packaging line metrology halts.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-SAM inspection is a known packaging cycle-time bottleneck, requiring up to 90-120 seconds per leadframe strip at 20 µm raster step pitch. The metrology recipe must establish a 2-stage screening rule: high-speed C-scan screening at 50 µm resolution across the full strip, with automated micro-focus 15 µm rescan only triggered when localized acoustic phase inversion threshold exceeds 3% area. This guarantees takt-time alignment with the high-pressure transfer molding and post-mold cure (PMC) cycle.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial phase-inversion misinterpretation: Failure to calibrate RF phase gating causes acoustic shadow attenuation from dense silica filler particles in the mold compound to be falsely flagged as die-attach delamination.
1. Immersion deionized water ingress and package swelling: Prolonged immersion during high-resolution multi-strip acoustic scanning causes moisture absorption into uncured or micro-cracked mold compound, inducing post-PMC popcorning during subsequent reflow.
1. Acoustic transducer mechanical clipping: Transducer collision with misaligned leadframe clamps or package ejector pins during high-speed raster scanning, causing permanent fracturing of the 100+ MHz acoustic lens.

Validate polarity alignment on gold-plated reference leadframe flag. | `Acoustic focal spot diameter <= 35 µm at 100 MHz; RF gate position drift <= ±1.5 ns over 10 consecutive leadframe index steps; reference signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) >= 28 dB.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level-2 Cleanroom Nitrile gloves (puncture-resistant, double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash goggles, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and anti-static ESD grounding heel straps, Acoustic splash shield enclosure barrier
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye contact with biocide-treated immersion fluid or isopropanol: flush immediately with copious clean water for >= 15 minutes at nearest certified eyewash station. In case of inhalation of solvent vapours, remove subject to fresh cleanroom air supply. For electrical shock from high-voltage pulser (>300V internal), disconnect main breaker immediately and initiate CPR if unresponsive.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom laminar airflow (Class 1000 / ISO 6) maintained at 0.45 m/s ± 0.05 m/s. Dedicated chemical fume canopy exhaust over solvent lens-cleaning bench operating at >= 50 CFM face velocity.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Acoustic tank drainage effluent containing biocide must be diverted to specialized hazardous wastewater neutralization sump (pH adjustment 6.5-8.5 prior to municipal drain release). Spent isopropanol wipes disposed of in sealed, grounded, fire-rated solvent disposal cans.

| **Biocide Additive (immersion tank bacterial inhibitor, Kathon-based)** | `55965-84-9` | Technical Grade | `0.05%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-PMC (Post-Mold Cure at 175°C for 4 hours) dry, fully polymerized TSOP-54 leadframe strips cooled to room temperature (25°C ± 2°C) without surface condensation or particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Completely dried via high-purity dry N2 air-knife blow-off (zero residual moisture droplets), baked at 125°C for 15 minutes if wet immersion exceeded 5 minutes, stored in desiccant dry-pack cabinet (RH < 5%).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time post-PMC allows moisture adsorption into mold compound interfaces, causing capillary water retention during C-SAM wet immersion and subsequent interfacial delamination (popcorn failure) during subsequent solder reflow validation.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## **A-Scan Signal Gate Analysis & Die Attach Void Area Quantification (<5% JEDEC/MIL-STD-883 Compliance)**

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-SAM-003`  
**Process Step:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Packaging & Assembly > Metrology > SAM Acoustic Void Metrology > A-Scan Signal Gate Analysis & Die Attach Void Area Quantification  
**Package Scope:** TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package (Silver-filled Conductive Epoxy Die Attach)

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Package Immersion &  │
│       Coupling        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     A-Scan Signal     │
│     Optimization      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Echo Gate Alignment  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     C-Scan Raster     │
│       Scanning        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│       Threshold       │
│     Segmentation      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│       Void Area       │
│    Quantification     │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Sample Preparation & Acoustic Immersion Coupling**:
   - Place the post-PMC encapsulated DRAM TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA packages onto the Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) fixture tray.
   - Immerse the package in deionized (DI) water bath at ambient cleanroom conditions ($25^\circ\text{C}$) to serve as an acoustic impedance matching coupling medium. Ensure zero micro-bubbles adhere to the package surface.

2. **High-Frequency Transducer Setup & Focal Alignment**:
   - Select an ultra-high frequency acoustic transducer (typically 50 MHz to 230 MHz focused broadband PVDF/PZT transducer depending on package mold thickness).
   - Position the acoustic focal point along the Z-axis precisely at the interface between the bottom of the 180nm DRAM silicon die and the silver-filled conductive epoxy layer (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 minutes).

3. **RF A-Scan Signal Optimization & Gate Positioning**:
   - Acquire the primary RF A-Scan waveform (amplitude vs. time-of-flight).
   - Identify the primary reflection peaks:
     - Top mold surface reflection.
     - Mold compound-to-silicon die top surface interface.
     - Silicon die bulk transmission echo.
     - **Die-to-Attach Interface Echo**: Isolate the return signal from the die back interface. A phase inversion (180° phase flip) and high reflection amplitude indicate acoustic mismatch caused by an air void or delamination.
   - Position the electronic time gate (Gate A) strictly across the die-attach interface echo window:
     - Set Gate Start immediately after the silicon substrate back-surface boundary echo.
     - Set Gate Width to encompass the entire die attach epoxy thickness prior to the lead frame / substrate paddle reflection.

4. **Pulse-Echo C-Scan Raster Acquisition**:
   - Set raster scan resolution across the full $X\text{-}Y$ die boundary (including corners and active circuitry region).
   - Record the peak amplitude and phase inversion within Gate A across every pixel coordinate.

5. **Image Processing, Thresholding & Void Quantification**:
   - Digitize the C-Scan acoustic reflection image.
   - Apply binary segmentation threshold based on acoustic impedance contrast: normal bonded silver epoxy reflects partial energy, whereas total internal reflection ($R \approx 1.0$ with negative phase polarity) indicates voiding/delamination.
   - Calculate total die attach void area:
     $$\text{Void Area (\%)} = \left( \frac{\sum A_{\text{void}}}{A_{\text{die}}} \right) \times 100$$
   - Evaluate single isolated void size, corner delamination clusters, and cumulative void area against MIL-STD-883 / JEDEC standards.

---

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Die Attach Void Area** | **$< 5.0\%$** | $\%$ of die footprint area | C-SAM Gate A Peak Amplitude / Phase Integration |
| **Die Attach Package Thermal Resistance ($R_{th}$)** | **$\le 5.0$** | $^\circ\text{C/W}$ | Thermal transient tester / MIL-STD-883 |
| **Single Isolated Void Area** | **$< 1.0\%$** | $\%$ of die footprint area | Automated SAM Defect Classifier |
| **Die Attach Material & Cure Schedule** | **Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 min** | $^\circ\text{C}$, $\text{minutes}$ | In-line thermal cure log verification |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **Source:** *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*
  - *"Die Attach: Silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g. Ablebond 84-1LMIS) cured at 150°C for 60 minutes."*
  - *"Thermal resistance R_th <= 5°C/W; void area under die < 5% via acoustic microscopy."*
  - *"Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force >= 4.0 grams-force for 25 um wire. Failure must occur in wire span, not at bond interface."*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: C-SAM transducer focal length and gate timing delay synchronization must maintain a time-of-flight resolution tighter than 1.5 ns to isolate the die-to-die-attach interface from the leadframe/substrate copper boundary in TSOP-54 packages (nominal 180nm DRAM die thickness ~150-200 um). Jitter in acoustic pulse gating risks convolving top-surface mold delamination with true die attach voiding, skewing automated area quantification.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Per MIL-STD-883 Method 2030 and J-STD-020, total die attach void area must not exceed 5.0% of the active silicon boundary, with no single contiguous void spanning >0.5% or bridging across high-heat dissipation zones (sub-array sense-amplifier periphery). Acoustic impedance phase inversion (180-degree phase shift with negative peak amplitude) must be explicitly programmed as the thresholding condition for acoustic acoustic-reflection void gating.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Deionized water coupling fluid immersion cycles for molded TSOP-54/54-ball FBGA must avoid package ionic contamination; coupling bath resistivity must remain >15 MOhm-cm. Sourcing automated high-frequency acoustic scanning microscopes (100 MHz to 230 MHz transducers) requires calibrated silicon/epoxy acoustic velocity reference standards to ensure yield repeatability across OSAT test benches.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Acoustic gate inspection must fit within a 45-second per package scan budget to sustain line throughput without violating moisture barrier bag (MBB) sealing Q-times post-PMC bake. High-density tray scanning (JEDEC matrix) requires automated multi-site rastering and instantaneous threshold segmentation to prevent post-PMC inspection bottlenecks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Transducer gate misalignment capturing the leadframe flag paddle reflection rather than the die attach interface, producing false zero-void artifacts.
1. Acoustic phase inversion masking due to inadequate acoustic impedance differentiation between partially oxidized epoxy mold compound and cured die attach film, undercounting contiguous edge delamination.
1. Prolonged DI water bath soak causing package micro-ingress prior to bake/seal, inducing 'popcorn' cracking failure during subsequent board-level reflow (JEDEC Level 3).

Position transducer normally above TSOP-54 top mold surface. 2. Acquire A-Scan RF echo train identifying mold-to-silicon surface echo (Echo 1) and silicon-to-die-attach interface echo (Echo 2). 3. Position the A-Scan evaluation gate precisely over Echo 2 with a gate width of 12.0 ns. 4. Record baseline phase polarity and peak-to-peak amplitude across a known void-free silicon reference zone. 5. Verify 180-degree phase inversion and minimum 6.0 dB amplitude rise on an intentional acoustic air gap reference. | `Acoustic gate time-of-flight lock jitter < 1.0 ns across 54-ball/TSOP-54 package area; phase inversion detection threshold SNR >= 12 dB relative to package bulk noise floor.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-2-3-02` | **C-SAM Full-Die Attach Void Area Quantification and Single Void Bridging Verification** | Automated C-SAM raster imaging system (5 um encoder step resolution) coupled with pixel-threshold segmentation and JEDEC void-counting image processing software. | 1. Measure maximum contiguous void area and measure clearance from die edge to void periphery. | `Total die attach void area < 5.0% of total active silicon footprint; maximum contiguous void area < 0.5% of total die area; zero void bridging across corner stress-relief zones or scribe lines.` |

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant nitrile gloves (15 mil), ANSI Z87.1 approved impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe cleanroom coat, Splash-resistant chemical apron
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with biocide-treated DI water or IPA, flush immediately at eye wash station for 15 minutes. For skin contact, wash thoroughly with neutral soap and water. If IPA vapors cause dizziness, evacuate to fresh air. Provide supportive medical care; no specific antidote required.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Immersion tank maintenance bench requires localized point exhaust (minimum face velocity 100 FPM) during IPA transducer wipe-down and tank biocide purging. Acoustic room maintained at Class 10,000 / ISO 7 cleanroom positive pressure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent coupling DI water containing biocide traces neutralized to pH 6.5-8.5 with dilute sodium bisulfite prior to drain discharge. IPA wipe waste disposed of in designated sealed hazardous flammable solvent bins.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry post-mold cured TSOP-54/FBGA packages at ambient room temperature, free of external mold bleed, mechanical cracks, or package warpage (>35 um).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thoroughly N2 blow-dried package body (zero surface moisture), DI water dried at 60 deg C for 30 min, ready for JEDEC moisture-barrier dry-bagging.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Acoustic Reflection Phase Inversion & JEDEC Delamination Analysis

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Acoustic reflection phase inversion relies on measuring the reflection coefficient R = (Z2 - Z1) / (Z2 + Z1) between epoxy molding compound (EMC, acoustic impedance Z1 ~ 6-8 MRayl) and die/leadframe substrates (Si Z2 ~ 19.7 MRayl, Cu Z2 ~ 44.5 MRayl, air/gap Z2 ~ 0.0004 MRayl). An intact EMC-to-die interface produces a positive acoustic impedance mismatch (Z2 > Z1) yielding an in-phase reflection (R > 0). When delamination occurs, the interface becomes an EMC-air or EMC-vacuum boundary (Z2 << Z1), yielding an inverted negative reflection (180° phase inversion, R ~ -1). The metrology acquisition chain must maintain ultra-high bandwidth RF digitizer fidelity (>1 GHz sampling rate, >=8-bit vertical resolution) using a 100 MHz-230 MHz high-frequency focused transducer to ensure the negative-going echo peak can be distinguished from ring-down interference without clipping or baseline drift.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Under JEDEC/IPC J-STD-020E criteria, delamination must be evaluated across the active die surface, die paddle, and lead fingers post-Moisture Sensitivity Level (MSL-3) preconditioning and 3x reflow (260°C peak). Any delamination on the active die face exceeding 0% area is an automatic failure due to shear stress on top passivation (SiN/SiO2) and wire bond ball neck fracturing. For leadframe tie-bars and die paddle back, delamination >10% cumulative area or propagating across trace boundaries breaches isolation. High-frequency Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-mode SAM) gating must precisely track the top-of-die echo gate (gate width 15-30 ns) with automated surface-tracking algorithm to suppress false phase inversion signatures caused by package tilt, mold cap warpage, or acoustic beam refraction through silica filler particles.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Decoupled lead times for custom acoustic delay-line transducers (110-230 MHz focused UHF transducers with sapphire buffer rods and acoustic lens radius r = 4-8 mm) exceed 16-24 weeks from specialized vendors (e.g., Sonix, PVA TePla, Sonoscan). Consumable deionized water coupling bath requires continuous closed-loop degassing (vacuum membrane degasser) and active filtration (0.2 um) to prevent micro-bubble nucleation on package surfaces, which mimics 180° delamination phase inversion and triggers false-positive rejection rates above 12% in production test lots.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Acoustic microscopy metrology represents an operational bottleneck for post-PMC and post-reliability stress characterization. C-SAM raster scanning of a full 54-lead TSOP / 54-ball FBGA tray (48 units per JEDEC matrix tray at 50 um step size) takes 42 minutes per tray, directly threatening the 4-hour Q-time window between MSL moisture soak and reflow simulation. Automated A-scan waveform recording with concurrent B-scan and C-scan multi-gate reconstruction must be deployed to capture both die surface and paddle interface in a single scan pass.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-bubble cavitation/adhesion on TSOP-54 package exterior surface producing acoustic shadow zones and 180-degree phase shift false positives indistinguishable from internal EMC-die delamination.
1. Gate tracking failure due to package warpage (>35 um corner-to-center deflection) causing the temporal data-acquisition window to clip the die-top interface echo, misclassifying phase polarity as null or inverted.
1. Acoustic attenuation and excessive beam scattering caused by high-density silica filler clustering (>75 wt% filler loading) in transfer mold compound, attenuating high-frequency return echoes below the 12 dB SNR threshold.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-3-01` | **A-Scan Phase Polarity & C-SAM Active Die Delamination Area Mapping** | Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) equipped with 175 MHz / 0.5 inch focal length acoustic transducer, 1.25 GS/s digitizer, and degassed DI water immersion scanning tank. | 1. Immerse sample tray into DI water bath maintained at 23°C with dissolved oxygen level <1.5 ppm and zero visible micro-bubbles. 2. Position the 175 MHz transducer over the center of the active DRAM die and optimize the Z-axis focus to maximize the peak-to-peak amplitude of the EMC-to-silicon interface echo. 3. Configure A-scan temporal acquisition gate to isolate the interface reflection (gate start: 5 ns prior to die echo onset; gate width: 25 ns). 4. Calibrate phase polarity reference using a bare silicon calibration wafer (positive lead phase: positive polarity peak preceding negative valley). 5. Execute a full raster C-scan over the complete package envelope at 15 um pixel resolution with phase inversion detection enabled. 6. Compute total surface area showing inverted phase (negative initial peak) over the active die circuit area and calculate delamination percentage. | `Active die surface delamination area must be exactly 0.00% (zero tolerance, no phase inversion echoes detected over active die passivation). Die paddle back and leadframe delamination must not exceed 5.0% cumulative area and must not bridge across adjacent package lead traces.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-2-3-3-02` | **Acoustic Reflection Coefficient & Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) Calibration** | UHF Focused Acoustic Transducer (230 MHz, F-number 1.5), 2 GHz broadband RF pulser-receiver, digital oscilloscope (10 GS/s, 1 GHz analog bandwidth), automated X-Y stage (1 um repeatability). | 1. Position transducer over a calibrated polished optical-grade single-crystal Silicon reference block (Z = 19.7 MRayl) and capture reference reflected waveform V_ref. 2. Translate transducer to the center of test TSOP-54 package and focus on the EMC-to-die passivation interface. 3. Measure peak positive amplitude (V_pos) and peak negative amplitude (V_neg) of the primary interface reflection in RF raw signal mode without envelope smoothing. 4. Calculate the acoustic reflection phase metric phi = arctan(V_neg / V_pos) and the signal-to-noise ratio SNR = 20 * log10(V_peak / V_noise_floor). 5. Verify that RF pulse waveform exhibits a dominant positive half-cycle peak prior to the first negative zero-crossing for an intact bonded interface. | `Reflected interface echo SNR must be >= 18.0 dB across 100% of tested die-top coordinate points. Acoustic phase polarity metric must confirm non-inverted positive reflection (V_pos / |V_neg| >= 1.85) at the bonded silicon die interface.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Splash-resistant chemical safety goggles (ANSI Z87.1 approved), Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (thickness >= 4 mil), Anti-static ESD lab coat / cleanroom smock (Class 10,000 compatible), Closed-toe slip-resistant ESD safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin or eye contact with immersion tank biocide or cleaning solvent, flush thoroughly with copious running water for at least 15 minutes. For IPA inhalation, move affected personnel immediately to fresh air. If irritation or dizziness persists, seek medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Maintain ambient cleanroom ventilation at 15-25 air changes per hour. Local point-of-use exhaust snorkel (face velocity >= 100 FPM) required during solvent wipe maintenance and tank disinfection procedures.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Immersion tank effluent containing dilute biocide must be collected in closed PE containers and neutralized with sodium bisulfite before routing to facility industrial chemical waste treatment. Spent IPA wipes disposed in designated airtight hazardous solvent waste bins.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (degassed acoustic coupling medium)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (transducer and stage degreasing solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / Cleanroom) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Biocide Additive (Microbicide 5-chloro-2-methyl-4-isothiazolin-3-one solution for tank anti-algae preservation)** | `26172-55-4` | Technical Grade | `< 0.05%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-Mold Cure (PMC) complete at 175°C, packages dry and degassed, mold flash fully deflashed, leadframes chemically de-oxidized with zero external mold release residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Acoustic water immersion dried via 0.2 um filtered heated N2 air-knife (45°C), moisture content verified at <0.02 wt% via analytical balance, zero water spotting or ionic residue on leads.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure Q-time allows uncontrolled ambient moisture absorption into the epoxy mold compound matrix; upon subsequent thermal testing or reflow, vaporized water creates severe popcorning, false delamination expansion, and accelerated intermetallic compound (IMC) corrosion on bond pads.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Non-destructive acoustic micro-imaging and phase-inversion verification of 180nm DRAM TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA encapsulation assemblies demonstrating 100% void-free die adhesion and full conformance to JEDEC/IPC J-STD-020E criteria post-MSL3 reflow preconditioning.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CSAM_Die_Top_Phase_Inversion_Map_LotA.tiff`
- [ ] `JEDEC_JSTD020E_Delamination_Quantitative_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Acoustic_Ascan_Polarity_Raw_Waveforms.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Delamination area across the active DRAM silicon die top surface** | `0.00` | +0.00% | High-frequency (175 MHz) C-SAM raster imaging with automated phase polarity gating over 100% of the active die boundary. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Acoustic return echo signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the EMC-die interface** | `21.5` | >= 18.0 dB | Broadband RF A-scan amplitude analysis comparing peak-to-peak die reflection against pre-trigger baseline noise. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Cumulative leadframe paddle delamination area relative to total paddle area** | `1.8` | <= 5.0% | Multi-gate C-scan threshold segmentation calculating inverted phase pixel area relative to CAD leadframe footprint. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All sampled packages from the DRAM packaging lot must exhibit zero phase inversion (0.00% delamination) across active die passivation surfaces and cumulative paddle delamination <= 5.0% post-MSL3 preconditioning, certified with signed JEDEC J-STD-020E inspection reports and raw C-SAM scan archives uploaded to the QA metrology repository.

Consumable deionized water coupling bath requires continuous closed-loop degassing (vacuum membrane degasser) and active filtration (0.2 um) to prevent micro-bubble nucleation on package surfaces, which mimics 180° delamination phase inversion and triggers false-positive rejection rates above 12% in production test lots.
critics.laya_pm: Acoustic microscopy metrology represents an operational bottleneck for post-PMC and post-reliability stress characterization. C-SAM raster scanning of a full 54-lead TSOP / 54-ball FBGA tray (48 units per JEDEC matrix tray at 50 um step size) takes 42 minutes per tray, directly threatening the 4-hour Q-time window between MSL moisture soak and reflow simulation. Automated A-scan waveform recording with concurrent B-scan and C-scan multi-gate reconstruction must be deployed to capture both die surface and paddle interface in a single scan pass.
critical_failure_modes: Micro-bubble cavitation/adhesion on TSOP-54 package exterior surface producing acoustic shadow zones and 180-degree phase shift false positives indistinguishable from internal EMC-die delamination.

Gate tracking failure due to package warpage (>35 um corner-to-center deflection) causing the temporal data-acquisition window to clip the die-top interface echo, misclassifying phase polarity as null or inverted.

Acoustic attenuation and excessive beam scattering caused by high-density silica filler clustering (>75 wt% filler loading) in transfer mold compound, attenuating high-frequency return echoes below the 12 dB SNR threshold.

testcases.title: A-Scan Phase Polarity & C-SAM Active Die Delamination Area Mapping
testcases.instrumentation: Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) equipped with 175 MHz / 0.5 inch focal length acoustic transducer, 1.25 GS/s digitizer, and degassed DI water immersion scanning tank.
testcases.pre_conditions: Packaged DRAM chips (TSOP-54 or 54-ball FBGA) completed post-mold cure (PMC: 175°C for 4 hours), subjected to JEDEC J-STD-020E MSL-3 soak (30°C / 60% RH for 192 hours) and 3x 260°C Pb-free reflow profile. Samples equilibrated to 22°C ± 2°C.
testcases.procedure:
1. Immerse sample tray into DI water bath maintained at 23°C with dissolved oxygen level <1.5 ppm and zero visible micro-bubbles.
2. Position the 175 MHz transducer over the center of the active DRAM die and optimize the Z-axis focus to maximize the peak-to-peak amplitude of the EMC-to-silicon interface echo.
3. Configure A-scan temporal acquisition gate to isolate the interface reflection (gate start: 5 ns prior to die echo onset; gate width: 25 ns).
4. Calibrate phase polarity reference using a bare silicon calibration wafer (positive lead phase: positive polarity peak preceding negative valley).
5. Execute a full raster C-scan over the complete package envelope at 15 um pixel resolution with phase inversion detection enabled.
6. Compute total surface area showing inverted phase (negative initial peak) over the active die circuit area and calculate delamination percentage.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Active die surface delamination area must be exactly 0.00% (zero tolerance, no phase inversion echoes detected over active die passivation). Die paddle back and leadframe delamination must not exceed 5.0% cumulative area and must not bridge across adjacent package lead traces.

testcases.title: Acoustic Reflection Coefficient & Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) Calibration
testcases.instrumentation: UHF Focused Acoustic Transducer (230 MHz, F-number 1.5), 2 GHz broadband RF pulser-receiver, digital oscilloscope (10 GS/s, 1 GHz analog bandwidth), automated X-Y stage (1 um repeatability).
testcases.pre_conditions: Acoustic immersion tank filled with ASTM Type I deionized water. Transducer delay line verified clean with zero acoustic pitting or sapphire facet degradation.
testcases.procedure:
1. Position transducer over a calibrated polished optical-grade single-crystal Silicon reference block (Z = 19.7 MRayl) and capture reference reflected waveform V_ref.
2. Translate transducer to the center of test TSOP-54 package and focus on the EMC-to-die passivation interface.
3. Measure peak positive amplitude (V_pos) and peak negative amplitude (V_neg) of the primary interface reflection in RF raw signal mode without envelope smoothing.
4. Calculate the acoustic reflection phase metric phi = arctan(V_neg / V_pos) and the signal-to-noise ratio SNR = 20 * log10(V_peak / V_noise_floor).
5. Verify that RF pulse waveform exhibits a dominant positive half-cycle peak prior to the first negative zero-crossing for an intact bonded interface.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Reflected interface echo SNR must be >= 18.0 dB across 100% of tested die-top coordinate points. Acoustic phase polarity metric must confirm non-inverted positive reflection (V_pos / |V_neg| >= 1.85) at the bonded silicon die interface.

ppe_required: Splash-resistant chemical safety goggles (ANSI Z87.1 approved)
Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (thickness >= 4 mil)
Anti-static ESD lab coat / cleanroom smock (Class 10,000 compatible)
Closed-toe slip-resistant ESD safety shoes

cas_chemicals.name: Isopropyl Alcohol (transducer and stage degreasing solvent)
Biocide Additive (Microbicide 5-chloro-2-methyl-4-isothiazolin-3-one solution for tank anti-algae preservation)

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: In case of skin or eye contact with immersion tank biocide or cleaning solvent, flush thoroughly with copious running water for at least 15 minutes. For IPA inhalation, move affected personnel immediately to fresh air. If irritation or dizziness persists, seek medical attention.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Maintain ambient cleanroom ventilation at 15-25 air changes per hour. Local point-of-use exhaust snorkel (face velocity >= 100 FPM) required during solvent wipe maintenance and tank disinfection procedures.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Immersion tank effluent containing dilute biocide must be collected in closed PE containers and neutralized with sodium bisulfite before routing to facility industrial chemical waste treatment. Spent IPA wipes disposed in designated airtight hazardous solvent waste bins.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Post-Mold Cure (PMC) complete at 175°C, packages dry and degassed, mold flash fully deflashed, leadframes chemically de-oxidized with zero external mold release residue.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Acoustic water immersion dried via 0.2 um filtered heated N2 air-knife (45°C), moisture content verified at <0.02 wt% via analytical balance, zero water spotting or ionic residue on leads.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding air exposure Q-time allows uncontrolled ambient moisture absorption into the epoxy mold compound matrix; upon subsequent thermal testing or reflow, vaporized water creates severe popcorning, false delamination expansion, and accelerated intermetallic compound (IMC) corrosion on bond pads.

expected_result.summary: Non-destructive acoustic micro-imaging and phase-inversion verification of 180nm DRAM TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA encapsulation assemblies demonstrating 100% void-free die adhesion and full conformance to JEDEC/IPC J-STD-020E criteria post-MSL3 reflow preconditioning.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Delamination area across the active DRAM silicon die top surface
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-frequency (175 MHz) C-SAM raster imaging with automated phase polarity gating over 100% of the active die boundary.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Acoustic return echo signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the EMC-die interface
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Broadband RF A-scan amplitude analysis comparing peak-to-peak die reflection against pre-trigger baseline noise.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Cumulative leadframe paddle delamination area relative to total paddle area
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-gate C-scan threshold segmentation calculating inverted phase pixel area relative to CAD leadframe footprint.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: All sampled packages from the DRAM packaging lot must exhibit zero phase inversion (0.00% delamination) across active die passivation surfaces and cumulative paddle delamination <= 5.0% post-MSL3 preconditioning, certified with signed JEDEC J-STD-020E inspection reports and raw C-SAM scan archives uploaded to the QA metrology repository.
