Mount the JIMA RT RC-02B resolution chart at the calibrated focal stage reference plane (Z = 15 mm). 2. Set tube voltage to 80 kV and current to 50 uA. 3. Acquire 16-frame averaged projection images across 100x, 500x, and 1000x geometric magnifications. 4. Measure line-pair resolution down to 0.4 um line/space structures. 5. Translate the calibrated grid target across the full field-of-view in 10 mm increments along X and Y axes to extract magnification scaling factors. | `Resolve 0.5 um line/space patterns with contrast modulation > 20%; magnification scale factor linearity error <= 0.25% across full FOV.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-2-1-02` | **Manipulator Stage Orthogonality and Planar Repeatability Verification** | Multi-axis motorized precision specimen stage (X-Y-Z-Theta), dual-axis laser displacement interferometer / capacitive displacement gauge, polished silicon reference calibration artifact with patterned Au fiduciary marks. | 1. Secure the silicon reference artifact on the motorized specimen stage vacuum chuck. 2. Align artifact reference fiducials to the X-ray optical center axis. 3. Execute 20 continuous bidirectional translation cycles across 150 mm travel in X and Y axes. 4. Record stage position coordinates at 9 discrete matrix locations using X-ray feature recognition. 5. Measure wedge error / Z-axis height deviation during full X-Y rastering. | `Bidirectional stage repeatability <= 1.0 um across X/Y axes; angular orthogonality error between X and Y axes <= 0.02 deg; Z-axis coplanarity deviation <= 5.0 um over 100 mm travel.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Personal radiation dosimeter (TLD badge or electronic personal dosimeter), Lead-lined shielding apron (0.5 mm Pb equivalent, during maintenance access), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, static-dissipative)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: External radiation: Immediately de-energize the X-ray tube via Emergency Off (EMO); evacuate personnel from enclosure; document dosimeter exposure reading and notify Radiation Safety Officer (RSO). Chemical exposure (IPA): For eye contact, flush eyes immediately with emergency eyewash for 15 minutes; for skin contact, wash thoroughly with soap and water; move victim to fresh air if vapors cause dizziness.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom air exchange (ISO Class 6 / Class 1000 minimum) with dedicated local heat exhaust duct (minimum 150 CFM) connected to the high-voltage generator and X-ray tube chiller exhaust.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be deposited into closed, grounded, flame-resistant flammable solvent waste receptacles; damaged lead shielding panels must be tagged and returned to an authorized hazardous heavy-metal recycling facility.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (for stage and calibration target cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / Cleanroom 99.9%) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Lead (solid radiation shielding panels and collimator components)** | `7439-92-1` | Commercial Shielding Grade | `>= 99.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-transfer-mold cured TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA strip arrays with degassed epoxy mold compound (EMC) surfaces free of particulate contamination and mold flash.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Radiographically inspected package strips with validated baseline wire loop profiles and calibrated stage coordinates, ready for automated laser deflash and post-mold cure (PMC).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption by uncured or partially cured EMC causing acoustic impedance shifts in subsequent CSAM metrology and popcorn delamination risks during solder reflow.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration of the 2D X-ray metrology system and alignment of the motorized specimen stage, achieving sub-micron spatial resolution and geometric distortion correction for quantitative wire sweep and bond loop height metrology on 180nm DRAM packages.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `STAGE_KINEMATIC_ORTHOGONALITY_MATRIX.csv`

| `ASSERT-02` | **Geometric magnification measurement linearity across active field of view** | `100.0%` | +/- 0.25% | Automated feature-pitch edge detection on NIST-traceable calibrated optical grid reticle |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Specimen stage planar orthogonality skew angle** | `90.000 deg` | +/- 0.020 deg | Laser displacement interferometer dual-axis squareness measurement over 150mm stroke |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Orthogonal Radiographic Imaging & Wire Trajectory Ray-Tracing Scan
**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-XRAY-088`  
**Node Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm DRAM Chip Tapeout)  
**Package Level:** TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Encapsulated Packaging  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Execution  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objective
This SOP establishes the industrial execution standard for orthogonal high-resolution X-ray radiographic inspection and 3D ray-tracing reconstruction of bonded die interconnects in molded DRAM packages. The procedure accurately measures wire sweep, loop height, and trajectory deformation following transfer molding epoxy plastic encapsulation to prevent electrical shorts or wire sweep failure between adjacent $25\ \mu\text{m}$ gold or aluminum bonding wires connecting $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pads to lead-frame/substrate fingers.

---

### 2. Equipment & Tool Setup
* **Equipment:** Dual-axis Micro-focus X-Ray Metrology System with 5-axis motorized tilt/rotation stage ($X, Y, Z, \theta, \phi$) and flat-panel digital detector (DDA).
* **Target Sample:** TSOP-54 or 54-ball FBGA package post-epoxy transfer molding.
* **Focal Spot Size:** $\le 2.0\ \mu\text{m}$ nanofocus/microfocus source.
* **Tube Voltage:** $80\ \text{kV} - 110\ \text{kV}$.
* **Tube Current:** $60\ \mu\text{A} - 120\ \mu\text{A}$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```text
       [Top-Down X-Ray (Z-Axis Projection)]
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │   Pad (100 um x 100 um)                      │
  │     [■]═══════════════════════╗ (Lead Finger)│
  │        \ Wire Sweep ΔX        ║              │
  │         \--> (Max Deviation)  ║              │
  │                                              │
  │   Bond Wire: 25 um diameter (Au / Al-1%Si)   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                         │
                         ▼
        [Orthogonal Tilt Profile (X/Y Angle)]
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │         ,-''''-.  Loop Height Z_peak         │
  │       .'        `.                           │
  │   [■]             `═══════════════[Finger]   │
  │   Die Surface                                │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### Step 3.1: Sample Alignment & Planar Normalization
1. Secure the molded TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA package onto the carbon-fiber low-attenuation vacuum chuck.
2. Align the package reference edge along the X/Y Cartesian motion axis using fiducial markers.
3. Set the detector normal vector perpendicular to the package planar surface ($\theta = 0^\circ$, normal top-down $Z$-axis view).

#### Step 3.2: 2D Orthogonal Radiographic Imaging
1. Energize the X-ray tube to $90\ \text{kV}$ and $85\ \mu\text{A}$.
2. Acquire the top-down radiographic image across all 54 wire bonding channels (connecting $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads to external package leads).
3. Tilt the stage by $+45^\circ$ (and orthogonal $-45^\circ$) along the package long axis to capture side-angle wire loop profiles and avoid wire overlap in perspective views.
4. Apply a 16-frame recursive median integration filter to minimize quantum shot noise and establish clean boundary contrast on the $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wires.

#### Step 3.3: 3D Ray-Tracing Trajectory Reconstruction & Edge Extraction
1. Import the orthogonal image pairs ($\theta = 0^\circ$ and $\theta = \pm 45^\circ$) into the ray-tracing reconstruction engine.
2. Extract the centerline trajectory vector $\vec{P}(s) = [x(s), y(s), z(s)]$ along the full span of each $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire from the initial ball/wedge bond footprint at the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pad to the lead-frame stitch.
3. Compute the theoretical straight-line interconnect chord $\vec{L}_{0}$ between ball and wedge bond locations.

#### Step 3.4: Wire Sweep & Quantitative Loop Profile Calculation
1. Measure maximum lateral deflection $\Delta X_{\text{max}}$ perpendicular to $\vec{L}_{0}$. Calculate the percentage wire sweep:
   $$\text{Wire Sweep (\%)} = \left(\frac{\Delta X_{\text{max}}}{L_{\text{chord}}}\right) \times 100$$
2. Extract the minimum clearance distance $D_{\text{min}}$ between adjacent wire trajectories:
   $$D_{\text{min}} = \min_{s, s'} \|\vec{P}_i(s) - \vec{P}_{i+1}(s')\|$$
3. Quantify loop height profile $Z(s)$ above the active silicon surface to ensure encapsulation clearance and verify loop integrity.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Inspection Metric | Physical Target / Threshold | Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bond Wire Diameter Verification** | $25.0 \pm 1.5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Calibrated X-ray edge absorption profile |
| **Maximum Wire Sweep Deflection** | $\le 3.0$ (Critical limit $\le 5.0$) | $\%$ | Top-down orthogonal lateral deflection relative to span |
| **Adjacent Wire Clear Distance ($D_{\text{min}}$)** | $\ge 50$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Ray-tracing 3D minimum distance extraction |
| **Bond Pad Alignment Boundary** | Within $100 \times 100$ pad perimeter ($\ge 15\ \mu\text{m}$ edge margin) | $\mu\text{m}$ | Orthogonal radiograph of pad contact area |

---

### 5. Context Sources & Citations
* **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:**
  * Connects on-chip bonding pads ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares) to external lead frame pins.
  * Wire specifications: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire (thermosonic ball bonding) or $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter Al-1%Si wire (ultrasonic wedge bonding).
  * Packaging standard compliance: Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 wire pull standards ($\ge 4.0\ \text{grams-force}$).
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology & Legacy Architecture Context:**
  * Defines packaging integration constraints for 180nm commercial tapeout, folded bitline layouts ($8F^2 / 6F^2$), and transfer molding reliability envelopes.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dual-axis orthogonal X-ray inspection (0° top-down Z-axis and 90° cross-sectional tilt) must synchronize geometric magnification across differing package focal planes in TSOP-54 and 54-ball FBGA. In 180nm DRAM wire bonding (25.4 um 4N Au or Cu wire), sub-micron parallax errors during orthogonal projection introduce systematic wire length distortion. Ray-tracing back-projection algorithms must mathematically compensate for package tilt, leadframe shadow interference, and cone-beam geometric distortion to resolve wire sweep down to +/- 0.5% of total wire span without phantom ghosting.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Epoxy molding compound (EMC) high-pressure transfer molding induces hydrodynamic drag on bond wire loops. Orthogonal 2D radiographic projections often confound vertical wire sag/loop height collapse with lateral wire sweep (X-Y plane displacement). The ray-tracing metrology pipeline must extract the complete 3D wire trajectory polynomial (B-spline or catenary curve) from orthogonal stereo projections, distinguishing between neck-down thermal damage near the ball neck and laminar drag-induced curvature across the 1.2 mm to 2.5 mm DRAM wire spans.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Micro-focus open-tube nanofocus X-ray systems (< 0.5 um focal spot size, 160 kV) face high tungsten target degradation and vacuum pump maintenance downtime. Sourcing detector flat-panel arrays with CsI scintillators capable of high dynamic range (16-bit) and > 30 fps without pixel burn-in or ghosting requires dual-vendor qualification (e.g., Hamamatsu, Varex Imaging). Long lead-time spare parts for the high-voltage generator and turbomolecular pump present operational bottlenecks during high-volume MPW packaging runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Orthogonal radiographic ray-tracing cannot become a 100% inline gating bottleneck during Gen 3 DRAM packaging. Full 3D trajectory reconstruction per unit exceeds standard UPH (units per hour) targets if scan times exceed 12 seconds per package. The team must implement an automated AXI (Automated X-Ray Inspection) screening routine with 5-point keyframe trajectory extraction for production lots, reserving full-volume 360-degree ray-tracing tomosynthesis exclusively for NPI qualification and out-of-spec wire sweep excursion lots.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Adjacent bond wire electrical short-circuit caused by transfer molding compound hydrodynamic wash exceeding 3% lateral wire sweep tolerance.
1. Ball neck fatigue fracture and heel crack propagation obscured during single-axis projection due to leadframe tie-bar radiographic attenuation.
1. Loop sagging causing wire-to-die edge or wire-to-paddle electrical short due to excessive loop height collapse under mold injection velocity.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-2-2-01` | **Quantitative Orthogonal Lateral Wire Sweep Extraction** | High-resolution microfocus X-ray inspection system (160 kV, 0.5 um focal spot size) equipped with 16-bit CMOS flat panel detector and calibrated 3D geometric metrology stage. | 1. Position encapsulated DRAM package at normal 0° incidence (Z-axis top-down view). 2. Acquire high-contrast radiograph at 90 kV, 80 uA with 16-frame recursive averaging. 3. Execute automated edge-detection to map bond pad center (x1, y1) and lead finger tip center (x2, y2). 4. Calculate baseline chord length L0 between bond pad and lead finger. 5. Trace actual wire path trajectory along peak attenuation gradient to locate maximum perpendicular lateral deviation (d_max). 6. Compute percentage wire sweep: Sweep (%) = (d_max / L0) * 100. | `Maximum lateral wire sweep must be <= 3.0% of total wire span L0 across all 54 bond wires. Wire clearance between adjacent traces must remain >= 35.0 um.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-2-2-02` | **Dual-Axis Ray-Tracing Loop Height and Clearance Profile Reconstruction** | Microfocus X-ray metrology workstation with 6-axis motorized goniometer stage and automated 3D wire trajectory ray-tracing analysis software. | 1. Acquire 0° top-down radiograph to establish planar wire coordinates. 2. Tilt goniometer stage to 45° and 90° orthogonal projection angles. 3. Acquire transmission radiographs maintaining constant focal-to-object distance (FOD). 4. Ingest multi-angle projection data into ray-tracing back-projection engine. 5. Reconstruct 3D spatial coordinate vectors (X, Y, Z) along the full wire trajectory from ball neck to stitch bond. 6. Measure maximum loop height relative to active die surface (Z_loop) and minimum vertical clearance to silicon die edge (Z_clearance). | `Loop height Z_loop must be 180.0 um +/- 25.0 um above active die surface. Minimum vertical wire clearance to silicon die edge corner must be >= 50.0 um with zero evidence of loop sag or die-touchdown.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Personal radiation dosimeter badge (thermoluminescent dosimeter TLD or electronic dosimeter), Lead-lined protective apron (0.5 mm Pb equivalence minimum) during chamber maintenance, Lead-impregnated safety glasses, Nitrile cleanroom gloves (Class 100 compatible), Electrostatic dissipative (ESD) lab coat and grounded heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For ionizing radiation exposure: Immediately de-energize the high-voltage source via E-stop, evacuate interlocked perimeter, and report to Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) for dosimeter reading evaluation and biological dosimetry blood panel assessment. For solvent (IPA) eye/skin contact: Flush affected area with clean isotonic saline or eye-wash station water for 15 minutes; remove contaminated clothing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous mechanical cabinet exhaust interlocked to high-voltage generator; vacuum turbopump exhaust routed to dedicated facility toxic/solvent exhaust duct maintaining negative cabinet pressure (> 50 Pa differential). Lead-shielded enclosure must maintain leakage radiation rate < 0.5 uSv/hr at 5 cm from any external surface.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be sealed in airtight conductive flammables waste bins and processed as hazardous organic waste. Degraded lead shielding or discarded open-tube tungsten targets must be disposed of via licensed hazardous heavy metal reclamation protocols under strict manifest tracking.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Lead (shielding enclosure panels)** | `7439-92-1` | Technical Grade Sheet | `> 99.0%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (detector & optical stage cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Tungsten (X-ray target tube anode)** | `7440-33-7` | Ultra-High Purity | `99.99%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

critics.systems_engineer: Dual-axis orthogonal X-ray inspection (0° top-down Z-axis and 90° cross-sectional tilt) must synchronize geometric magnification across differing package focal planes in TSOP-54 and 54-ball FBGA. In 180nm DRAM wire bonding (25.4 um 4N Au or Cu wire), sub-micron parallax errors during orthogonal projection introduce systematic wire length distortion. Ray-tracing back-projection algorithms must mathematically compensate for package tilt, leadframe shadow interference, and cone-beam geometric distortion to resolve wire sweep down to +/- 0.5% of total wire span without phantom ghosting.
critics.domain_expert: Epoxy molding compound (EMC) high-pressure transfer molding induces hydrodynamic drag on bond wire loops. Orthogonal 2D radiographic projections often confound vertical wire sag/loop height collapse with lateral wire sweep (X-Y plane displacement). The ray-tracing metrology pipeline must extract the complete 3D wire trajectory polynomial (B-spline or catenary curve) from orthogonal stereo projections, distinguishing between neck-down thermal damage near the ball neck and laminar drag-induced curvature across the 1.2 mm to 2.5 mm DRAM wire spans.
critics.supply_chain: Micro-focus open-tube nanofocus X-ray systems (< 0.5 um focal spot size, 160 kV) face high tungsten target degradation and vacuum pump maintenance downtime. Sourcing detector flat-panel arrays with CsI scintillators capable of high dynamic range (16-bit) and > 30 fps without pixel burn-in or ghosting requires dual-vendor qualification (e.g., Hamamatsu, Varex Imaging). Long lead-time spare parts for the high-voltage generator and turbomolecular pump present operational bottlenecks during high-volume MPW packaging runs.
critics.laya_pm: Orthogonal radiographic ray-tracing cannot become a 100% inline gating bottleneck during Gen 3 DRAM packaging. Full 3D trajectory reconstruction per unit exceeds standard UPH (units per hour) targets if scan times exceed 12 seconds per package. The team must implement an automated AXI (Automated X-Ray Inspection) screening routine with 5-point keyframe trajectory extraction for production lots, reserving full-volume 360-degree ray-tracing tomosynthesis exclusively for NPI qualification and out-of-spec wire sweep excursion lots.
critical_failure_modes: Adjacent bond wire electrical short-circuit caused by transfer molding compound hydrodynamic wash exceeding 3% lateral wire sweep tolerance.
Ball neck fatigue fracture and heel crack propagation obscured during single-axis projection due to leadframe tie-bar radiographic attenuation.
Loop sagging causing wire-to-die edge or wire-to-paddle electrical short due to excessive loop height collapse under mold injection velocity.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-PKG-MET-038`
## Title: Geometric Wire Sweep Calculation & MIL-STD-883 Yield Acceptance Metrology
**Branch Hierarchy:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Transfer Molding Epoxy Plastic Encapsulation (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package) > Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) & Wire Sweep Metrology > X-Ray Radiography Wire Sweep & Loop Profile Quantitative Metrology > Radiographic Orthogonal Projection & Geometric Wire Sweep Measurement > Geometric Wire Sweep Calculation & Mil-Std-883 Yield Acceptance Metrology  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm DRAM)  
**Process Action:** Make / Metrology Execution  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the quantitative radiography metrology, orthogonal coordinate extraction, mathematical wire sweep percentage calculation, and MIL-STD-883 yield disposition for encapsulated 180nm DRAM dice packaged in TSOP-54 or 54-ball FBGA plastic packages post-transfer molding.

---

### 2. Physical Process Parameters & Analytical Model

```
       Die Bond Pad (100 µm x 100 µm)
                [ X_pad, Y_pad ]
                      •
                       \
                        \   d_max (Max Lateral Deflection)
                         \-------• Wire Apex
                          \     /
                           \   /
                            \ /
                             •
                      [ X_lead, Y_lead ]
                     Lead Frame Post / Ball
```

- **Wire System:** $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ Au wire (thermosonic ball bond) or $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $\text{Al-}1\%\ \text{Si}$ wire (ultrasonic wedge bond).
- **Die Pad Geometry:** $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad target.
- **Wire Sweep Formulation:**
  $$\text{Wire Sweep } (\%) = \left( \frac{d_{\max}}{L} \right) \times 100$$
  where:
  - $d_{\max}$ is the maximum perpendicular lateral deviation from the straight chord line connecting the die pad bond center to the lead frame finger.
  - $L$ is the straight chord length between the die bond pad center and lead post.
  - Per **MIL-STD-883 Method 2017 / 2011**, maximum allowable wire sweep is $\le 10\%$ of total wire chord length, with no wire-to-wire clearance violating minimum dielectric isolation ($< 2 \times$ wire diameter clearance or touching).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                            WIRE SWEEP METROLOGY PIPELINE                          |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Step 1: Setup]        Load TSOP-54 / FBGA into 2D High-Resolution X-Ray System  |
|                                     |                                             |
|  [Step 2: Projection]   Orthogonal Normal View (0 deg Tilt, Pad-to-Lead Plane)    |
|                                     |                                             |
|  [Step 3: Coordinates]  Extract Coordinates: Pad (X1, Y1), Lead (X2, Y2), Apex   |
|                                     |                                             |
|  [Step 4: Computation]  Compute Chord Length L and Maximum Deflection d_max       |
|                                     |                                             |
|  [Step 5: Pull Test]    Destructive Wire Pull Test Verification (MIL-STD-883 M2011) |
|                                     |                                             |
|  [Step 6: Disposition]  Disposition Lot against MIL-STD-883 Yield Acceptance Specs|
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Specimen Loading & Radiographic Alignment
1. Mount the post-mold cured TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA package strip onto the high-resolution micro-focus digital X-ray inspection stage.
2. Establish orthogonal normal incidence ($\theta = 0^\circ$ stage tilt) perpendicular to the die attach plane to eliminate foreshortening distortion.
3. Calibrate magnification using a NIST-traceable grid reticle to ensure spatial resolution $\le 1.0\ \mu\text{m/pixel}$.

#### Step 2: Feature Identification & Reference Vector Mapping
1. Locate the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum bond pad center coordinates $(X_{\text{pad}}, Y_{\text{pad}})$.
2. Locate the corresponding external lead frame pin / stitch bond contact point $(X_{\text{lead}}, Y_{\text{lead}})$.
3. Construct the nominal reference wire chord vector:
   $$L = \sqrt{(X_{\text{lead}} - X_{\text{pad}})^2 + (Y_{\text{lead}} - Y_{\text{pad}})^2}$$

#### Step 3: Maximum Perpendicular Deflection Extraction
1. Trace the curved centerline of the $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire contour under the digital projection.
2. Calculate the perpendicular distance $d_i$ from each traced point $(X_i, Y_i)$ along the wire profile to the reference chord line:
   $$d_i = \frac{|(Y_{\text{lead}} - Y_{\text{pad}})X_i - (X_{\text{lead}} - X_{\text{pad}})Y_i + X_{\text{lead}}Y_{\text{pad}} - Y_{\text{lead}}X_{\text{pad}}|}{L}$$
3. Identify the maximum lateral displacement $d_{\max} = \max(d_i)$.

#### Step 4: Sweep Ratio Calculation & Proximity Checking
1. Compute the percentage wire sweep:
   $$\text{Sweep } (\%) = \left(\frac{d_{\max}}{L}\right) \times 100$$
2. Measure the inter-wire clearance between adjacent bond wires across the TSOP-54 lead pitch. Flag any pair where edge-to-edge distance drops below $25\ \mu\text{m}$ ($1.0\times$ wire diameter) or where contact bridging occurs.

#### Step 5: Mechanical Pull Integrity Audit (Sample Basis)
1. On designated control units prior to encapsulation or on decapsulated QA validation samples, perform wire pull testing per **MIL-STD-883 Method 2011**.
2. Position the micro-hook at mid-span of the $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire loop. Pull vertically at $90^\circ$ relative to the substrate plane until rupture occurs. Record peak breaking force. Ensure failure occurs in the wire span and not at the bond interface.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Inspection / Metrology Parameter | Target / Limit Specification | Engineering Unit | Verification Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Maximum Allowable Wire Sweep** | $\le 10.0$ | $\%$ of chord length | MIL-STD-883 Method 2017 / X-Ray Inspection |
| **Bond Wire Pull Strength** | $\ge 4.0$ | grams-force ($\text{gf}$) | MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 ($25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire diameter) |
| **Minimum Adjacent Wire Clearance** | $\ge 25.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Radiographic Orthogonal Projection |
| **Acoustic Void Area under Die Attach** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ | C-Mode Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (CSAM) |

---

### 5. Context Citations
- **Wire Bond Geometry, Pull Force & Die Attach Specs:** *Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging* ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ Al pads; $25\ \mu\text{m}$ Au and $\text{Al-}1\%\ \text{Si}$ wire diameter; MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 minimum pull strength $\ge 4.0\ \text{gf}$ in wire span; die attach void area $< 5\%$).
- **Die Interconnect & Pad Top Layer:** *Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects* ($350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$ Al metallization layer).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Radiographic projection of TSOP-54 and 54-ball FBGA leadframe geometries introduces geometric parallax and focal plane distortion if the micro-focus X-ray source spot size exceeds 2 um or if detector non-orthogonality exceeds 0.05 degrees. Geometric wire sweep calculations must dynamically decouple perspective scaling from true lateral displacement across 25 um Au/Cu wire spans reaching lengths up to 4.2 mm, ensuring that apparent loop deflection does not trigger false rejects or mask adjacent wire-to-wire electrical bridging under high-velocity transfer molding epoxy flow.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Under MIL-STD-883 Method 2011/2019/2024 and JEDEC JESD22-B101, wire sweep percentage must strictly not exceed 10% (sweep = (d_max / L_span) * 100) for standard 180nm DRAM interconnects, with critical inner-row clearances remaining >= 2.5 wire diameters (>= 62.5 um for 25 um wire). Epoxy mold compound viscosity transients during the transfer filling stage induce significant hydrodynamic drag forces (drag force F_d proportional to compound viscosity eta, filler particle Reynolds number, and mold gate velocity v). Automated edge-detection metrology algorithms must isolate wire trajectories from dense fused-silica filler background noise (mean particle size d50 = 8 to 15 um) without morphological dilation artifacts.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-sourcing high-resolution micro-focus closed-tube X-ray inspection systems (e.g., 160 kV with flat-panel digital detector arrays) creates a single-point metrology bottleneck. Maintenance overhead on filament/target erosion and detector scintillator degradation (CsI(Tl)) directly limits packaging test line throughput to fewer than 120 units per hour per metrology cell unless dual-head automated defect recognition (ADR) algorithms with off-axis rotational fixturing are qualified across secondary OSAT vendors in Vietnam.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Automated wire sweep metrology signoff serves as the gating milestone between transfer molding post-mold cure (PMC) and singulation/final test. Inability to establish rapid, in-line automated 100% sample inspection on lot pilots risks undetected yield slippage exceeding 14% on dense corner-pin address lines (A0-A12, RAS#, CAS#), driving non-recoverable packaging scrap and delaying MPW sample tapeout qualification timelines by at least 6 weeks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Viscous drag induced wire-to-wire contact (bridging) and micro-shorting between adjacent DQ pin bond wires due to local EMC flow velocity gradients exceeding 12 mm/s across the package mold cavity.
1. Ball neck fatigue fracture and heel micro-cracking caused by plastic deformation during wire deflection exceeding 12% lateral sweep, leading to intermittent open circuits during post-mold cure temperature cycling (-40°C to 150°C).
1. Epoxy filler entrapment and localized wire sag altering wire loop profile height below the minimum 75 um clearance to the silicon die active edge, resulting in die-edge short circuits under biased temperature-humidity stress.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-2-3-01` | **Quantitative Orthogonal Radiographic Wire Sweep Calculation and Lateral Deflection Metrology** | Micro-focus X-Ray Inspection System (160 kV, 2 um focal spot size, 30 fps flat-panel detector array, motorized 5-axis stage with 0.1 um encoder resolution) equipped with Automated Defect Recognition (ADR) image analysis software. | 1. Mount molded leadframe strip on the motorized orthogonal vacuum chuck and align the DRAM die fiducials along the X-Y axes to within 0.05° theta. 2. Acquire top-down (0° normal) orthogonal X-ray transmission radiographs of all 54 wire interconnects at 90 kV accelerating voltage and 80 uA tube current with 16-frame spatial averaging. 3. Apply edge-detection filters to locate the first bond (die ball pad center) and second bond (leadframe stitch center) to establish baseline reference vector L_span. 4. Execute sub-pixel contour tracking along the entire wire length to calculate maximum orthogonal deviation d_max normal to the reference vector. 5. Compute percentage wire sweep using the formula: Wire Sweep (%) = (d_max / L_span) * 100. 6. Repeat across all corner-pin high-aspect-ratio wire loops (wires 1, 27, 28, 54). | `Maximum wire sweep for every individual wire must be <= 8.0% (MIL-STD-883 allowable limit <= 10.0%); adjacent wire-to-wire spatial clearance must be >= 62.5 um (>= 2.5 wire diameters for 25 um wire); zero adjacent wire bridging across all 54 pins.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-2-3-02` | **Dual-Axis Loop Profile Height and Die-Edge Clearance Quantitative Radiography** | Oblique/Tilting Micro-focus X-Ray Radiography System (tilting stage capable of 30° to 60° calibrated off-axis projection, 3.0 um spatial resolution) calibrated against NIST-traceable height gauge. | 1. Tilt sample fixture to calibrated 45.0° ± 0.1° relative to the incident X-ray beam to decouple vertical loop profile from horizontal plane. 2. Image the corner die-pad transitions where bond wires cross the die paddle and active silicon periphery. 3. Measure vertical loop height (h_loop) from die surface to peak wire trajectory and calculate vertical die-edge clearance (z_edge) at the silicon die boundary using perspective trigonometric correction: z_true = z_projected / sin(45°). 4. Record loop neck angle and inspect for heel thinning or neck pinching (> 15% wire diameter reduction). | `Die-edge vertical clearance (z_edge) must be >= 75.0 um; maximum loop profile height (h_loop) must remain within 180 um ± 25 um; minimum wire neck residual diameter must be >= 21.25 um (>= 85% of nominal 25 um wire diameter); zero wire sagging or substrate contact.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Personal thermoluminescent radiation dosimeter badge (TLD), Lead-lined apron (0.5 mm Pb equivalent for open-chamber maintenance), ANSI Z87.1 certified radiation/impact-resistant safety glasses, Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (12 mil thickness), Cleanroom anti-static ESD-dissipative lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: External X-ray beam exposure: Immediately press emergency red stop button; clear personnel from inspection bay; notify radiation safety officer (RSO); seek medical evaluation for ionizing dose assessment if interlock fail occurs. Skin or eye contact with cleaning solvent (IPA): Flush exposed eyes or skin with flowing clean water for at least 15 minutes; seek ophthalmological attention if eye irritation persists. Inhalation of solvent fumes: Move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous interlocked enclosure exhaust with negative pressure maintenance; chamber radiation leakage monitored via external Geiger-Müller counter ensuring dose rate remains < 0.5 uSv/h (0.05 mrem/h) at 5 cm from outer cabinet surface; dedicated solvent vapor point exhaust at 100 FPM face velocity for stage maintenance.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solvent wipes contaminated with IPA must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-proof hazardous waste receptacles for dedicated high-temperature solvent incineration; damaged lead shielding panels or depleted X-ray tube assemblies must be decommissioned via certified RCRA licensed heavy-metal recycling and hazardous waste handling facilities.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Lead (contained in radiation shielding enclosure cabinets)** | `7439-92-1` | Technical Sheet / Solid Alloy Shielding | `> 99.0% w/w` |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, optical lens and stage alignment chuck cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI Tier 3 / VLSI Grade) | `99.9% v/v` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Transfer-molded TSOP-54 / FBGA strips post-mold cured or freshly ejected from transfer press; mold flash cleaned from leadframe rails; dry, degassed epoxy surface free of oily release agents.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Radiographically verified strips with logged sub-pixel wire sweep and clearance coordinates, packaged in anti-static ESD carrier magazines under cleanroom Class 1000 conditions ready for laser marking and mechanical trim-and-form singulation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding allowable queue time in uncontrolled ambient humidity (> 45% RH) prior to post-mold cure or singulation leads to moisture absorption into the uncured epoxy resin matrix, causing hydrolytic package swelling, stress-induced wire bond neck shearing, and catastrophic internal delamination (popcorning) during subsequent solder reflow testing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full quantitative geometric wire sweep and loop profile metrology validation across all 54 interconnect channels of transfer-molded 180nm DRAM test vehicles. Sub-pixel micro-focus X-ray imaging definitively establishes lateral wire sweep, die-edge vertical clearance, and wire-to-wire spacing in strict compliance with MIL-STD-883 Method 2024 and JEDEC JESD22-B101, ensuring complete mechanical robustness against hydrodynamic mold flow deformation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram180_tsop54_wire_sweep_quantitative_distribution.csv`
- [ ] `mil_std_883_wire_sweep_metrology_conformance_report.pdf`
- [ ] `orthogonal_high_res_xray_sweep_composite_radiographs.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-WS-01` | **Maximum geometric lateral wire sweep across all 54 wire channels per packaged DRAM unit** | `4.5%` | <= 8.0% absolute maximum (MIL-STD-883 limit <= 10.0%) | Automated sub-pixel orthogonal digital X-ray radiographic edge tracking and vector displacement calculation |
| `ASSERT-WS-02` | **Minimum inter-wire spatial clearance between adjacent high-density bond wire channels** | `78.0 um` | >= 62.5 um (>= 2.5 nominal wire diameters) | Centroid-to-centroid edge-detection distance analysis on orthogonal 16-frame averaged radiographs |
| `ASSERT-WS-03` | **Minimum vertical clearance between bond wire loop under-curve and active silicon die edge** | `85.0 um` | >= 75.0 um absolute floor | Calibrated 45-degree oblique-angle radiographic projection with trigonometric depth deconvolution |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero package units exhibiting wire sweep > 8.0%, zero wire bridging or die-edge clearance violations (< 75 um) across a continuous 5-strip lot sample (minimum 120 packaged DRAM devices evaluated), accompanied by full Gage R&R analysis demonstrating measurement variance < 10% on wire sweep calculation algorithms.

Epoxy mold compound viscosity transients during the transfer filling stage induce significant hydrodynamic drag forces (drag force F_d proportional to compound viscosity eta, filler particle Reynolds number, and mold gate velocity v). Automated edge-detection metrology algorithms must isolate wire trajectories from dense fused-silica filler background noise (mean particle size d50 = 8 to 15 um) without morphological dilation artifacts.
critics.supply_chain: Single-sourcing high-resolution micro-focus closed-tube X-ray inspection systems (e.g., 160 kV with flat-panel digital detector arrays) creates a single-point metrology bottleneck. Maintenance overhead on filament/target erosion and detector scintillator degradation (CsI(Tl)) directly limits packaging test line throughput to fewer than 120 units per hour per metrology cell unless dual-head automated defect recognition (ADR) algorithms with off-axis rotational fixturing are qualified across secondary OSAT vendors in Vietnam.
critics.laya_pm: Automated wire sweep metrology signoff serves as the gating milestone between transfer molding post-mold cure (PMC) and singulation/final test. Inability to establish rapid, in-line automated 100% sample inspection on lot pilots risks undetected yield slippage exceeding 14% on dense corner-pin address lines (A0-A12, RAS#, CAS#), driving non-recoverable packaging scrap and delaying MPW sample tapeout qualification timelines by at least 6 weeks.
critical_failure_modes: Viscous drag induced wire-to-wire contact (bridging) and micro-shorting between adjacent DQ pin bond wires due to local EMC flow velocity gradients exceeding 12 mm/s across the package mold cavity.

Ball neck fatigue fracture and heel micro-cracking caused by plastic deformation during wire deflection exceeding 12% lateral sweep, leading to intermittent open circuits during post-mold cure temperature cycling (-40°C to 150°C).

Epoxy filler entrapment and localized wire sag altering wire loop profile height below the minimum 75 um clearance to the silicon die active edge, resulting in die-edge short circuits under biased temperature-humidity stress.

testcases.title: Quantitative Orthogonal Radiographic Wire Sweep Calculation and Lateral Deflection Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Micro-focus X-Ray Inspection System (160 kV, 2 um focal spot size, 30 fps flat-panel detector array, motorized 5-axis stage with 0.1 um encoder resolution) equipped with Automated Defect Recognition (ADR) image analysis software.
testcases.pre_conditions: Post-transfer-molded TSOP-54 or 54-ball FBGA DRAM sample strip cooled to 25°C ± 2°C following mold ejection and prior to post-mold cure (PMC); surface free of flash and leadframe warp < 50 um across strip length; system calibrated with certified optical/X-ray grid target (100 um pitch).
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount molded leadframe strip on the motorized orthogonal vacuum chuck and align the DRAM die fiducials along the X-Y axes to within 0.05° theta. 2. Acquire top-down (0° normal) orthogonal X-ray transmission radiographs of all 54 wire interconnects at 90 kV accelerating voltage and 80 uA tube current with 16-frame spatial averaging. 3. Apply edge-detection filters to locate the first bond (die ball pad center) and second bond (leadframe stitch center) to establish baseline reference vector L_span. 4. Execute sub-pixel contour tracking along the entire wire length to calculate maximum orthogonal deviation d_max normal to the reference vector. 5. Compute percentage wire sweep using the formula: Wire Sweep (%) = (d_max / L_span) * 100. 6. Repeat across all corner-pin high-aspect-ratio wire loops (wires 1, 27, 28, 54).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Maximum wire sweep for every individual wire must be <= 8.0% (MIL-STD-883 allowable limit <= 10.0%); adjacent wire-to-wire spatial clearance must be >= 62.5 um (>= 2.5 wire diameters for 25 um wire); zero adjacent wire bridging across all 54 pins.

testcases.title: Dual-Axis Loop Profile Height and Die-Edge Clearance Quantitative Radiography
testcases.instrumentation: Oblique/Tilting Micro-focus X-Ray Radiography System (tilting stage capable of 30° to 60° calibrated off-axis projection, 3.0 um spatial resolution) calibrated against NIST-traceable height gauge.
testcases.pre_conditions: Units successfully passed TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-2-3-01 orthogonal lateral sweep metrology; ambient cleanroom Class 1000 environment; X-ray tube warmed up and beam intensity stability verified < 0.5% drift over 1 hour.
testcases.procedure: 1. Tilt sample fixture to calibrated 45.0° ± 0.1° relative to the incident X-ray beam to decouple vertical loop profile from horizontal plane. 2. Image the corner die-pad transitions where bond wires cross the die paddle and active silicon periphery. 3. Measure vertical loop height (h_loop) from die surface to peak wire trajectory and calculate vertical die-edge clearance (z_edge) at the silicon die boundary using perspective trigonometric correction: z_true = z_projected / sin(45°). 4. Record loop neck angle and inspect for heel thinning or neck pinching (> 15% wire diameter reduction).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Die-edge vertical clearance (z_edge) must be >= 75.0 um; maximum loop profile height (h_loop) must remain within 180 um ± 25 um; minimum wire neck residual diameter must be >= 21.25 um (>= 85% of nominal 25 um wire diameter); zero wire sagging or substrate contact.

ppe_required: Personal thermoluminescent radiation dosimeter badge (TLD)
Lead-lined apron (0.5 mm Pb equivalent for open-chamber maintenance)
ANSI Z87.1 certified radiation/impact-resistant safety glasses
Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (12 mil thickness)
Cleanroom anti-static ESD-dissipative lab coat

cas_chemicals.name: Lead (contained in radiation shielding enclosure cabinets)
Isopropanol (IPA, optical lens and stage alignment chuck cleaning)

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: External X-ray beam exposure: Immediately press emergency red stop button; clear personnel from inspection bay; notify radiation safety officer (RSO); seek medical evaluation for ionizing dose assessment if interlock fail occurs. Skin or eye contact with cleaning solvent (IPA): Flush exposed eyes or skin with flowing clean water for at least 15 minutes; seek ophthalmological attention if eye irritation persists. Inhalation of solvent fumes: Move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous interlocked enclosure exhaust with negative pressure maintenance; chamber radiation leakage monitored via external Geiger-Müller counter ensuring dose rate remains < 0.5 uSv/h (0.05 mrem/h) at 5 cm from outer cabinet surface; dedicated solvent vapor point exhaust at 100 FPM face velocity for stage maintenance.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Solvent wipes contaminated with IPA must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-proof hazardous waste receptacles for dedicated high-temperature solvent incineration; damaged lead shielding panels or depleted X-ray tube assemblies must be decommissioned via certified RCRA licensed heavy-metal recycling and hazardous waste handling facilities.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Transfer-molded TSOP-54 / FBGA strips post-mold cured or freshly ejected from transfer press; mold flash cleaned from leadframe rails; dry, degassed epoxy surface free of oily release agents.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Radiographically verified strips with logged sub-pixel wire sweep and clearance coordinates, packaged in anti-static ESD carrier magazines under cleanroom Class 1000 conditions ready for laser marking and mechanical trim-and-form singulation.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding allowable queue time in uncontrolled ambient humidity (> 45% RH) prior to post-mold cure or singulation leads to moisture absorption into the uncured epoxy resin matrix, causing hydrolytic package swelling, stress-induced wire bond neck shearing, and catastrophic internal delamination (popcorning) during subsequent solder reflow testing.

expected_result.summary: Full quantitative geometric wire sweep and loop profile metrology validation across all 54 interconnect channels of transfer-molded 180nm DRAM test vehicles. Sub-pixel micro-focus X-ray imaging definitively establishes lateral wire sweep, die-edge vertical clearance, and wire-to-wire spacing in strict compliance with MIL-STD-883 Method 2024 and JEDEC JESD22-B101, ensuring complete mechanical robustness against hydrodynamic mold flow deformation.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum geometric lateral wire sweep across all 54 wire channels per packaged DRAM unit
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated sub-pixel orthogonal digital X-ray radiographic edge tracking and vector displacement calculation

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Minimum inter-wire spatial clearance between adjacent high-density bond wire channels
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Centroid-to-centroid edge-detection distance analysis on orthogonal 16-frame averaged radiographs

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Minimum vertical clearance between bond wire loop under-curve and active silicon die edge
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calibrated 45-degree oblique-angle radiographic projection with trigonometric depth deconvolution

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Zero package units exhibiting wire sweep > 8.0%, zero wire bridging or die-edge clearance violations (< 75 um) across a continuous 5-strip lot sample (minimum 120 packaged DRAM devices evaluated), accompanied by full Gage R&R analysis demonstrating measurement variance < 10% on wire sweep calculation algorithms.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Loop Height Profilometry & MIL-STD-883 Clearance Compliance Verification

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Wire loop height profilometry and clearance verification under MIL-STD-883 Method 2011/2014 must bridge the physical interface between wire bonding and post-mold structural integrity. In TSOP-54 and 54-ball FBGA DRAM architectures, the spatial envelope is constrained to package thicknesses under 1.0 mm (FBGA) or 1.2 mm (TSOP). High loop height elevates the risk of mold cap exposure, wire sweeping, and mold sweep-induced shorting during transfer molding cavity injection, while insufficient clearance to die-edge or paddle leads to electrical breakdown under 3.3V/1.8V DRAM operating rails.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Loop profiling requires dual-axis verification: Z-axis maximum loop trajectory height (target: 150 to 220 µm above active die surface for 25 µm Au/Cu wire) and minimum clearance between the lowest wire contour and unpassivated die edge (must exceed MIL-STD-883 minimum requirement of 25.4 µm or 1.0 mil, specified to >= 38 µm margin). Optical laser confocal displacement sensors or micro-focus 2D/3D X-ray systems must maintain a sub-micron Z-resolution (<= 0.5 µm) to avoid parallax distortion across dense 54-lead fanouts.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Qualification of non-destructive X-ray laminography and non-contact confocal profilometers hinges on automated recipe calibration across multiple OSAT subcontractors. Capital expenditure constraints necessitate dual-sourcing compatibility between Nordson Dage Quadra/Yxlon high-resolution X-ray systems and Keyence VK-X optical profilometers, preventing single-vendor proprietary measurement lock-in across the packaging supply line.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must align with the takt time of inline packaging sort: inline sampling requires 100% inspection on pilot runs and a 5-unit/strip AQL on mature high-volume production. Gauge R&R must maintain %GRR < 10% and ndc >= 5 across operators and shifts prior to releasing lot clearance for transfer molding epoxy resin injection.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die-edge shorting caused by wire sag violating the MIL-STD-883 25.4 µm clearance limit, causing intermittent grounding to the 180nm silicon substrate.
1. Wire sweep-induced adjacent wire shorting during transfer molding high-viscosity epoxy front advancement due to excessively high loop profiles (> 250 µm).
1. Heel crack propagation and neck-down fatigue induced by excessive capillary looping tension during low-loop trajectory formation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-3-01` | **Dual-Axis Non-Contact Optical Confocal Loop Height Profilometry** | Keyence VK-X3000 3D Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope with 405nm violet laser and 50x telecentric objective lens (0.5 nm Z-display resolution). | 1. Fixture strip in vacuum chuck and register global fiducials. 2. Calibrate Z-reference plane (Z0) on primary active die bond pad surface. 3. Execute continuous laser confocal scan along wire trajectory from ball neck to leadframe stitch. 4. Extract peak loop apex height (Z_max) and die-edge intersection distance (Z_edge - Die_edge). 5. Record profilometric profile across all 54 interconnect channels. | `Apex loop height must measure between 175.0 µm and 215.0 µm (mean +/- 3 sigma <= 225.0 µm); minimum vertical die-edge clearance must be >= 45.0 µm (absolute lower spec limit >= 38.1 µm vs MIL-STD-883 25.4 µm baseline).` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-3-02` | **Sub-Micron Micro-Focus 2D/3D X-Ray Inspection for Die-Paddle and Adjacent Wire Clearance** | Nordson Dage Quadra 7 Micro-Focus X-ray Metrology System (0.1 µm feature recognition, 160 kV open tube, flat panel detector). | 1. Position sample at 45-degree oblique tilt angle to eliminate planar leadframe shadowing. 2. Capture high-resolution digital radiograph at 50x geometric magnification across corner wire groups (most vulnerable to sweep). 3. Measure line-to-line 3D clearance between adjacent bond wires. 4. Measure line-to-die-edge clearance under MIL-STD-883 Method 2014 criteria. 5. Perform automated image processing to compute Gauge R&R metrics. | `Adjacent wire-to-wire spacing must be >= 50.8 µm (2.0 wire diameters); wire-to-paddle/die-edge clearance must be >= 38.1 µm; measurement repeatability standard deviation sigma <= 0.8 µm across 30 repeated cycles.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, minimum 5 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/laser safety glasses (optical density OD >= 5+ at 405 nm), Electrostatic dissipative (ESD) lab coat and grounded heel straps, Personal radiation dosimeter badge (thermoluminescent dosimeter TLD) for open-beam X-ray enclosure operators
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious clean water for >= 15 minutes; seek ophthalmologist review if irritation persists. Skin exposure: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and DI water. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Relocate subject to fresh air immediately. Laser exposure: Immediate medical evaluation by ophthalmology if retinal laser exposure is suspected.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local chemical exhaust hood maintaining capture velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) for IPA wipe-down stations. X-ray cabinet internal negative pressure venting to facility exhaust; enclosure radiation leakage monitored to <= 0.5 µSv/hr (0.05 mR/hr) at 5 cm distance.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be deposited into closed, airtight ESD-safe flammables disposal bins with flame-arresting foot-pedal lids. Collected organic solvent waste routed to hazardous waste incinerator stream; lead-shielded components recycled under authorized e-waste/toxic metals reclamation.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / cleanroom grade) | `99.9%` |
| **Lead (contained in radiation shielding enclosure glass/panels)** | `7439-92-1` | Technical Grade (structural shielding) | `>= 95.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed thermosonic ball/wedge wire bonds on 180nm DRAM pads; clean unpassivated die edge with zero particulate contamination and bond pads free of intermetallic voiding.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Verified loop profilometry parameters documented; unoxidized wire loops (free of Cu-oxide if copper/Pd-coated Cu wire is used); certified clearance ready for epoxy mold compound (EMC) transfer injection.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time triggers atmospheric oxidation of wire bond surfaces and leadframe copper, degrading interfacial adhesion with epoxy mold compound (EMC), leading to interfacial delamination, popcorn cracking during reflow, and copper-wire embrittlement.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full metrological qualification and MIL-STD-883 clearance compliance verification for TSOP-54/FBGA-54 wire loops, delivering sub-micron spatial profiles, automated clearance verification, and statistical pass/fail release for downstream transfer molding.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TSOP54_Loop_Height_3D_Profilometry_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Wire_Clearance_Raw_Pointcloud_Metrology_Data.csv`
- [ ] `MicroFocus_XRay_Clearance_Inspection_Maps.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum wire loop apex height across all 54 DRAM interconnect channels** | `195.0 µm` | +/- 20.0 µm | Automated 3D laser confocal scan using Keyence VK-X3000 with 50x objective |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Minimum wire-to-die-edge vertical clearance under MIL-STD-883 Method 2014** | `48.0 µm` | +15.0 / -9.9 µm (absolute floor 38.1 µm) | 45-degree oblique micro-focus X-ray inspection on Nordson Dage Quadra 7 |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Measurement system repeatability and reproducibility (%GRR)** | `6.5%` | <= 10.0% (ndc >= 5) | 10-part, 3-operator, 3-trial Gauge R&R ANOVA execution per AIAG MSA standard |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero clearance violations below 38.1 µm across 100% of measured DRAM wire bonds, %GRR <= 10.0% validated on both confocal laser and micro-focus X-ray systems, and automated QA clearance approval logged into MES prior to epoxy mold cavity loading.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Dual-Axis Optical & X-Ray Micro-CT Loop Profilometer Calibration

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-007`  
**Process Level:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Metrology > MIL-STD-883 Loop Profilometry  
**Target Device:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) — TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA Package  
**Referenced Specification:** [docs/knowledge/sop_profilometer_calibration.md](./docs/knowledge/sop_profilometer_calibration.md)

---

## 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Step 1: Calibration   │
│    Target Mounting     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 2: Dual-Axis    │
│  Optical Profilometer  │
│       Alignment        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        Step 3:         │
│    High-Resolution     │
│     X-Ray Micro-CT     │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Step 4: Cross-Modal   │
│  Registration & Loop   │
│       Profiling        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Step 5: MIL-STD-883   │
│     Wire Clearance     │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

### Step 1: Calibration Target & Reference Standard Mounting
1. Load a certified NIST-traceable multi-feature reference artifact containing calibrated step-height targets and $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum fiducial pads onto the dual-axis stage.
2. Initialize stage vacuum chuck and verify ambient cleanroom environment at room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$).

### Step 2: Dual-Axis Optical Profilometer Alignment & Scale Calibration
1. Engage the closed-loop piezo actuators with **$0.1\ \mu\text{m}$ sensitivity** to calibrate the optical Z-height travel and eliminate mechanical backlash.
2. Use crosshair fiducial alignment marks on the reference standard to calibrate lateral axes across the optical field of view.
3. Verify dual-axis optical focal depth and vertical linearity over a range encompassing wire heights for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire assemblies.

### Step 3: High-Resolution X-Ray Micro-CT Geometric Calibration
1. Align the microfocus X-ray source and flat-panel detector axis using the calibration phantom with standard tungsten/gold wire benchmarks ($25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter Au wire).
2. Measure magnification factor, center-of-rotation (COR), and beam projection linearity.
3. Ensure voxel resolution meets sub-micron accuracy thresholds for quantitative reconstruction of wire loop trajectories and die-attach interface voiding (monitoring void criteria of $< 5\%$).

### Step 4: Cross-Modal Dual-Axis Optical & X-Ray Registration
1. Co-register the coordinate frames of the optical surface profilometer and X-ray Micro-CT volume using the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad corner fiducials as absolute spatial tie points.
2. Calculate spatial transformation matrix (translation, rotation, scale factor) ensuring co-axial offset residual between optical profile and X-ray 3D trajectory is minimized.

### Step 5: Wire Loop Profilometry & MIL-STD-883 Clearance Verification
1. Position the packaged DRAM sample (TSOP-54 / 54-ball FBGA containing $25\ \mu\text{m}$ 99.99% gold ball-bonded or Al-1% Si wedge-bonded wires).
2. Scan 3D wire profile from the $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ die pad across the loop apex to the substrate/lead frame post.
3. Validate minimum vertical clearance above active DRAM circuitry ($180\text{ nm}$ access transistor / stacked capacitor topography) and adjacent wire-to-wire spacing according to MIL-STD-883 clearance rules prior to destructive pull testing (spec $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$).

---

## 3. Physical Parameters & Acceptance Criteria

```text
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │░                                     │
 Piezo Sens (um)┤░                                     │
                │▒▒                                    │
 Pull Force (gf)┤▒▒                                    │
Au Wire Dia (um)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                            │
                │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                            │
   Bond Pad (um)┤██████████████████████████████████████│
                │██████████████████████████████████████│
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0       25        50       75      100 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value & Tolerance | Unit | Verification Tool / Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Piezo Stage Positioning Sensitivity** | $0.1$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Closed-loop piezo actuator displacement |
| **Bond Pad Dimensional Metrology** | $100 \times 100$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Calibrated dual-axis optical optical profilometry |
| **Wire Diameter Verification** | $25.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Dual-axis optical & X-Ray Micro-CT cross-section |
| **Die-Attach Void Metrology Threshold** | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ area | X-Ray Micro-CT / Acoustic microscopy ($R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$) |
| **Post-Metrology Mechanical Pull Force** | $\ge 4.0$ (wire span failure) | $\text{gf}$ | MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 pull test |

---

## 4. Context Citations

1. **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**  
   - Die bonding pads: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
   - Wire specifications: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter $99.99\%$ gold wire and $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter Al-1% Si wire.
   - Quality standard: MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 requires pull test force $\ge 4.0\text{ gf}$ for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire.
   - Thermal & void threshold: Void area under die $< 5\%$; thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
2. **Source: Optical Mask Aligner Mechanics: Gap Control and UV Exposure Dose**  
   - Actuator precision: Closed-loop piezo actuators with $0.1\ \mu\text{m}$ sensitivity.
   - Fiducial alignment: High-precision fiducial mark alignment methodology.
3. **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**  
   - Access transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}$, stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture.

> **Micro-Knowledge Note:** Captured in documentation repository at [docs/knowledge/sop_profilometer_calibration.md](./docs/knowledge/sop_profilometer_calibration.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dual-axis cross-calibration between confocal optical profilometry (surface/pre-encapsulation) and high-resolution cone-beam X-ray Micro-CT (sub-surface/post-encapsulation) requires rigid coordinate frame co-registration. Coordinate mapping errors between the optical stage (Z-piezo travel with 0.1 nm resolution) and the micro-CT high-precision air-bearing rotary table will introduce geometric projection distortion and volumetric voxel skew (scaling drift > 0.05%), directly compromising wire loop height measurement integrity according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2014.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating wire loop profile metrology across TSOP-54 and 54-ball FBGA DRAM packages must resolve bond wire trajectories (18-25 um 4N Au / Cu wires) against dense epoxy molding compound (EMC). X-ray tube focal spot blooming (< 1.0 um spot size required at 90-130 kV) and beam hardening artifacts through silica filler particles (60-85 wt% SiO2) induce edge blurring on loop crests; calibration must utilize a NIST-traceable multi-wire tungsten/gold phantom target to establish edge point-spread-function (PSF) deconvolution limits.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement of a dual-axis sub-micron calibration target (NIST-traceable 3D grid and multi-pitch wire micro-phantom) faces strict export controls and long lead times (>16 weeks). Off-the-shelf tungsten carbide or ruby sphere calibration artifacts must be paired with OEM-certified micro-CT geometric calibration suites to prevent multi-month commissioning stalls for DRAM packaging yield ramp.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The buy-action Capex allocation must encompass vendor installation qualification (IQ), operational qualification (OQ), and performance qualification (PQ) documentation alongside ISO/IEC 17025 accredited calibration artifacts. Skipping certified phantom artifacts to cut upfront costs will stall tapeout packaging sign-off under Gen 3 timeline milestones.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal-induced volumetric drift of micro-CT manipulator stage (>1.2 um/hr), introducing magnification and loop height calculation skew.
1. X-ray source spot defocusing causing penumbra broadening on wire edges, resulting in false MIL-STD-883 Method 2014 loop-to-cap clearance violations.
1. Dual-axis optical-to-CT affine transformation matrix rotation error (>0.02 deg), yielding non-convergent loop sweep spatial vectors.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

Position NIST-traceable phantom at geometric magnification corresponding to 1.50 um/voxel. 2. Acquire 1440 radiographic projections over 360-degree rotation with frame averaging N=8. 3. Reconstruct 3D volumetric data using filtered back-projection with beam hardening correction. 4. Extract center-to-center sphere distances and sphere diameters across X, Y, and Z axes using automated 3D edge-fitting algorithms. 5. Compute dimensional scaling deviation and orthogonal axis orthogonality angle. | `Pass if absolute linear dimension measurement error across all axes is <= 0.35 um and geometric orthogonality deviation is <= 0.015 degrees across the 10 mm x 10 mm measurement volume.` |
| `TC-PLASTIC-ENCAPSULATION-3-3-3-1-02` | **Optical Confocal to X-Ray Micro-CT Cross-System Loop Profilometry Gauge R&R** | White Light Interferometer / Confocal Optical Profilometer (0.55 NA, 20x objective), High-Resolution Micro-CT Inspection System, and Standard Calibrated 25 um Au Bond Wire TSOP-54 Test Vehicle (unencapsulated reference standard). | 1. Correlate optical vs. X-ray datasets and calculate Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility (Gage R&R) percentage. | `Pass if total Gage R&R <= 10.0% of tolerance band (tolerance = +/- 15 um) and absolute delta between mean optical loop height and mean micro-CT loop height is <= 0.75 um for all wires.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Personal thermoluminescent dosimeter (TLD) badge or real-time electronic radiation dosimeter, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/radiation safety glasses with side shields, Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, minimum 6 mil), ESD-safe cleanroom coat and anti-static ESD-grounded footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For ionizing radiation exposure alarm (>0.5 uSv/h outside cabinet): Immediately hit system E-Stop, de-energize high-voltage generator, evacuate enclosure, and notify Radiation Safety Officer (RSO). For isopropanol skin/eye contact: Flush affected areas with cleanroom eye wash/shower station for 15 minutes. For inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated enclosure interlock cabinet with forced air ventilation (minimum 10 ACH) to evacuate ozone generated by high-voltage X-ray tube and local solvent exhaust for wafer/target cleaning stations.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be segregated into sealed, grounded flammables bins. Lead containment surfaces must be surveyed annually; damaged lead materials are disposed of as toxic RCRA D008 hazardous metal waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Lead (Shielding Lining & Collimators)** | `7439-92-1` | Technical Grade Sheet | `>99.0%` |
| **Isopropanol (Optical & Stage Cleaning Solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `>=99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-wire bond or post-transfer molded DRAM package strips clean, dry, and free of ionic salt or organic residue; calibration phantom targets degreased with zero oxide/particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated metrology workspace logged; inspected package units certified with zero ESD charging and zero radiation-induced latchup damage ready for molding compound cure verification.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excess ambient exposure induces moisture absorption in unsealed EMC or atmospheric corrosion on Cu/Au bond wires, altering refractive/scattering characteristics and inducing post-mold delamination during subsequent temperature cycling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Dual-Axis Optical and X-Ray Micro-CT loop profilometer fully commissioned, aligned, and calibrated against NIST-traceable micro-geometry phantoms, guaranteeing non-destructive wire sweep, loop height, and clearance metrology for TSOP-54 and FBGA packages conforming to MIL-STD-883 Method 2014.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CAL-MICROCT-NIST-VERIFICATION-REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `DUAL-AXIS-PROFILOMETER-ALIGNMENT-MATRIX.csv`
- [ ] `TSOP54-WIRE-LOOP-METROLOGY-GAGE-RR.pdf`

| `ASSERT-02` | **Cross-system optical vs. X-ray wire loop apex height correlation** | `0.00 um offset` | +/- 0.75 um | Dual-axis spatial co-registration analysis across 10 golden reference test vehicle bonds |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum external radiation cabinet leakage at 10 cm from chassis surface** | `0.10 uSv/h` | <= 0.50 uSv/h maximum limit | Survey meter ionizing radiation scan across all seam joints, doors, and viewing windows under 160 kV full tube load |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
