nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: High-Speed Diamond Blade Street Dicing Recipe Execution

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: High-speed diamond blade dicing introduces severe acoustic vibration and micro-mechanical shock into thinned 180nm DRAM wafers (typically 150-200 um post-backgrind). Spindle runout must be constrained below 1.0 um at 30,000 to 40,000 RPM, and feed rate acceleration curves must be strictly profile-controlled to prevent kerf wander and structural micro-cracking across deep-trench capacitor arrays and sensitive seal rings located within 15 um of dicing street boundaries.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: The street design in 180nm DRAM contains residual metal test structures (PCM/TEG pads) that cause rapid diamond blade loading, blade glazing, and thermal kerf chipping. Utilizing an electroformed diamond blade with 3-5 um grit in a nickel matrix paired with a constant surfactant-doped DI water coolant flow (>1.8 L/min at 0.25 MPa) is mandatory to clear silicon swarf, prevent back-side chipping exceedances (>25 um), and eliminate ESD surface charges across DRAM bitline/wordline periphery pads.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standard ultra-thin diamond dicing blades (e.g., Disco NBC/ZH series) and UV-curable dicing tape (polyolefin substrate, 85-110 um base film with 10-15 um acrylic UV adhesive) face extended lead times and temperature-controlled freight requirements. Sourcing certified resin-bonded or electroformed blades compatible with low-kerf width (20-30 um) requires pre-qualified second-source suppliers (e.g., ADT, K&S) to mitigate tapeout assembly bottlenecks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Dicing recipe qualification represents a zero-yield-loss gate between back-end foundry wafers and pick-and-place wire bonding. Process must maintain throughput >= 1.5 wafers/hour while enforcing a hard 30-minute queue time post-cut to spin-rinse-dry and UV cure, preventing tape delamination, slurry dry-in, and galvanic corrosion on exposed aluminum/copper bond pads.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Subsurface micro-chipping and micro-cracking propagating past the die seal ring into active peripheral wordline decoders and trench DRAM storage cells.
1. Blade deflection/kerf wander exceeding 5 um causing catastrophic severance of outermost probe/wire bond pads and PCM monitor structures.
1. Silicon slurry/swarf redeposition and drying on DRAM bond pads causing intermetallic bond failure (non-stick on pad) during subsequent ultrasonic gold/copper wire bonding.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-2-01` | **Dicing Kerf Width, Street Alignment Accuracy, and Front-Side Chipping Verification** | Automated High-Resolution Optical Inspection Microscope (AOI) with motorized X-Y stage (0.1 um linear optical encoder resolution) and Nomarski DIC contrast optics. | 1. Perform automated pattern recognition alignment on wafer street fiducials (Channel X and Channel Y). 2. Execute high-speed cut across 10 sample dicing streets at 35,000 RPM, feed rate 15 mm/s, cut depth into sub-tape 25 um. 3. Spin-rinse-dry (SRD) wafer at 1,500 RPM for 180 s. 4. Measure cut kerf width at 30 discrete points along X and Y axes. 5. Measure front-side top chipping dimension (perpendicular distance from cut edge to maximum chip apex) across 100 randomly sampled DRAM die corners and edges. | `Kerf width must be 28.0 um ± 3.0 um; street center cut offset <= 2.5 um; maximum front-side chipping length <= 10.0 um; zero chipping encroaching past the outer moisture barrier seal ring.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-2-02` | **Backside Chipping and Die Fracture Strength Characterization Post-Singulation** | Infrared (IR) Backside Transmission Microscope and 3-Point / 4-Point Die Bend Mechanical Stress Tester with load cell (accuracy ± 0.05 N). | 1. Inspect backside edges of 50 singulated DRAM dies under IR/backside illumination microscopy to quantify chipping depth and lateral spalling. 2. Mount 20 singulated dies (dimensions 2.5 mm x 3.0 mm, nominal thickness 150 um) into the 3-point bend fixture with mirror-polished backgrind surface in tension. 3. Apply continuous load at crosshead displacement rate of 0.5 mm/min until catastrophic fracture occurs. 4. Record peak fracture force (N) and calculate Weibull fracture strength (MPa). | `Backside edge chipping dimension <= 25.0 um maximum apex-to-edge; Weibull characteristic fracture strength sigma_0 >= 450 MPa with no individual die failing below 350 MPa.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof safety goggles and full face shield, Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (double gloving), Anti-static fluid-resistant cleanroom smock and ESD protective safety shoes, Hearing protection (earplugs/muffs rated NRR >= 25 dB for high-frequency spindle noise)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately irrigate eyes with clean water at emergency eyewash for minimum 15 minutes, holding eyelids open. Skin Contact: Wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated cleanroom garments. Inhalation (aerosolized mist): Relocate subject to fresh air immediately. Mechanical Trauma: In case of rotating blade contact, immediately press E-Stop, apply direct pressure with sterile cleanroom gauze to stem laceration bleeding, and summon emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: High-velocity mist collector and local HEPA exhaust ventilation with laminar face velocity maintained at 0.45 - 0.55 m/s directly over the cutting chamber; continuous negative pressure interlocked with spindle run state to capture silicon aerosol mist and aerosolized surfactant vapors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All wastewater effluent containing silicon particulate swarf and surfactant must route to an isolated slurry collection sump; pass effluent through a multi-stage polypropylene depth cartridge filter (5.0 um pre-filter, 0.5 um absolute final filter) and sedimentation centrifuge before discharging neutral water (pH 6.5 - 8.5) to municipal semiconductor industrial drain.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Coolant Carrier)** | `7732-18-5` | Semi Grade 1 (Resistivity > 18.0 MOhm-cm) | `> 99.8% w/w` |
| **Polyoxyethylene Alkyl Ether (Dicing Surfactant / Anti-Corrosion Additive)** | `68439-50-9` | Semiconductor Ultra-Pure Electronic Grade | `0.1% - 0.5% w/w in DI water` |
| **Silicon Dust / Particulate Swarf (Generated by-product)** | `7440-21-3` | Electronic Ingot Scrap | `< 0.1% w/v slurry suspension` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Mount-complete, defect-free 180nm DRAM wafer on UV tape with vacuum-sealed backside; front-side passivated with zero particulate contamination (PCO <= 10 particles @ > 0.2 um) and free of moisture.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully singulated die array on dicing ring, spin-rinsed with ultra-pure DI water and nitrogen blow-dried; bond pads strictly free of silicon slurry redeposition (< 1 particle > 0.3 um per pad); UV tape cured.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Silicon slurry dry-in and galvanic oxidation on exposed aluminum-copper wire bond pads causing non-stick-on-pad (NSOP) failure; UV dicing tape acrylic adhesive cross-linking or irreversible tack increase preventing automated die pick-and-place without silicon backside spalling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Execution of high-speed diamond blade dicing recipe on 180nm DRAM wafers with kerf precision <= 2.5 um offset, front-side chipping <= 10 um, backside chipping <= 25 um, zero seal ring breach, and bond pad contamination-free surfaces ready for die attach.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dicing_kerf_inspection_report.pdf`
- [ ] `die_fracture_strength_weibull_data.csv`
- [ ] `high_mag_kerf_sealring_optical_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Dicing kerf center alignment relative to street midline** | `0.0 um` | ± 2.5 um | Automated post-dicing optical pattern recognition measurement across 50 street intersections. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum allowable front-side chipping dimension into dicing street margin** | `0.0 um` | <= 10.0 um | Brightfield/darkfield optical microscopy inspection at 500x magnification. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Silicon swarf particulate redeposition on wire bond pads** | `0 particles` | <= 1 particle (> 0.3 um) per 100 pads | Automated optical defect inspection (AOI) with darkfield scatterometry. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All kerf alignment and chipping assertions met with 100% compliance across 3 consecutive qualification wafers, Weibull characteristic fracture strength sigma_0 >= 450 MPa, zero bond pad corrosion/slurry residue confirmed by automated optical inspection, and UV tape release peel force verified <= 0.1 N/25mm.

Sourcing certified resin-bonded or electroformed blades compatible with low-kerf width (20-30 um) requires pre-qualified second-source suppliers (e.g., ADT, K&S) to mitigate tapeout assembly bottlenecks.
critics.laya_pm: Dicing recipe qualification represents a zero-yield-loss gate between back-end foundry wafers and pick-and-place wire bonding. Process must maintain throughput >= 1.5 wafers/hour while enforcing a hard 30-minute queue time post-cut to spin-rinse-dry and UV cure, preventing tape delamination, slurry dry-in, and galvanic corrosion on exposed aluminum/copper bond pads.
critical_failure_modes: Subsurface micro-chipping and micro-cracking propagating past the die seal ring into active peripheral wordline decoders and trench DRAM storage cells.
Blade deflection/kerf wander exceeding 5 um causing catastrophic severance of outermost probe/wire bond pads and PCM monitor structures.
Silicon slurry/swarf redeposition and drying on DRAM bond pads causing intermetallic bond failure (non-stick on pad) during subsequent ultrasonic gold/copper wire bonding.

testcases.title: Dicing Kerf Width, Street Alignment Accuracy, and Front-Side Chipping Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Automated High-Resolution Optical Inspection Microscope (AOI) with motorized X-Y stage (0.1 um linear optical encoder resolution) and Nomarski DIC contrast optics.
testcases.pre_conditions: Thinned 180nm DRAM wafer mounted on rigid stainless steel dicing ring using UV-dicing tape; spindle dynamic runout verified < 1.0 um at 35,000 RPM; DI water nozzle aligned at 45 degrees to blade interface.
testcases.procedure:
1. Perform automated pattern recognition alignment on wafer street fiducials (Channel X and Channel Y).
2. Execute high-speed cut across 10 sample dicing streets at 35,000 RPM, feed rate 15 mm/s, cut depth into sub-tape 25 um.
3. Spin-rinse-dry (SRD) wafer at 1,500 RPM for 180 s.
4. Measure cut kerf width at 30 discrete points along X and Y axes.
5. Measure front-side top chipping dimension (perpendicular distance from cut edge to maximum chip apex) across 100 randomly sampled DRAM die corners and edges.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Kerf width must be 28.0 um ± 3.0 um; street center cut offset <= 2.5 um; maximum front-side chipping length <= 10.0 um; zero chipping encroaching past the outer moisture barrier seal ring.

testcases.title: Backside Chipping and Die Fracture Strength Characterization Post-Singulation
testcases.instrumentation: Infrared (IR) Backside Transmission Microscope and 3-Point / 4-Point Die Bend Mechanical Stress Tester with load cell (accuracy ± 0.05 N).
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafers diced according to qualified recipe, cleaned, and UV cured (365nm exposure at 250 mJ/cm2) to reduce tape adhesive peel strength below 0.1 N/25mm; 20 dies sampled across center, mid-radius, and edge exclusion zones.
testcases.procedure:
1. Inspect backside edges of 50 singulated DRAM dies under IR/backside illumination microscopy to quantify chipping depth and lateral spalling.
2. Mount 20 singulated dies (dimensions 2.5 mm x 3.0 mm, nominal thickness 150 um) into the 3-point bend fixture with mirror-polished backgrind surface in tension.
3. Apply continuous load at crosshead displacement rate of 0.5 mm/min until catastrophic fracture occurs.
4. Record peak fracture force (N) and calculate Weibull fracture strength (MPa).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Backside edge chipping dimension <= 25.0 um maximum apex-to-edge; Weibull characteristic fracture strength sigma_0 >= 450 MPa with no individual die failing below 350 MPa.

ppe_required: ANSI Z87.1 certified splash-proof safety goggles and full face shield
Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (double gloving)
Anti-static fluid-resistant cleanroom smock and ESD protective safety shoes
Hearing protection (earplugs/muffs rated NRR >= 25 dB for high-frequency spindle noise)

Skin Contact: Wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated cleanroom garments. Inhalation (aerosolized mist): Relocate subject to fresh air immediately. Mechanical Trauma: In case of rotating blade contact, immediately press E-Stop, apply direct pressure with sterile cleanroom gauze to stem laceration bleeding, and summon emergency medical services.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Dicing Blade Alignment & Optical Street Registration Calibration

- **Process Node / Module**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip | BEOL Packaging & Assembly
- **Process Step**: `Packaging > High-Speed Diamond Blade Street Dicing Recipe Execution > Dicing Blade Alignment & Optical Street Registration Calibration`
- **Documentation Link**: [docs/dicing_blade_alignment_sop.md](./docs/dicing_blade_alignment_sop.md)

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌─────────────────────┐
│ Load Mounted Frame  │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│   WEC Parallelism   │
│      Leveling       │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│ Microscope Fiducial │
│    Registration     │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│  Sub-Micron Piezo   │
│     Calibration     │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│      Kerf Cut       │
│    Verification     │
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Calibration Procedure

1. **Substrate Mounting & Mechanical Leveling (Wedge Error Compensation - WEC)**:
   - Secure the 100mm tape-mounted wafer frame onto the dicing chuck.
   - Activate spherical air bearings to mechanically level the chuck plate against the optical reference datum, establishing stage parallelism **$< 1\ \mu\text{m}$ across the 100mm wafer**.
   - Lock pneumatic clamps using regulated nitrogen pressure at **$0.1\ \text{to}\ 0.5\ \text{bar}$** (soft hold) or **$1.0\ \text{bar}$** for rigid seating.

2. **Optical System & Objective Selection**:
   - Initialize the split-field dual-objective optical microscope paired with high-resolution CMOS cameras.
   - Engage the **$10\times\ \text{Plan Achromat (NA 0.25)}$** or switch between **$5\times$**, **$10\times$**, and **$20\times$** objectives to locate dicing street crosshair fiducial marks on the opposing wafer perimeter edges.

3. **Street Crosshair Registration & Angle ($\theta$) Correction**:
   - Identify primary scribe street crosshair marks located at opposing die corners.
   - Adjust theta rotation until the dicing street center line is parallel to the linear travel axis of the saw. Operator overlay alignment precision must be verified to **$\le 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$** (with coarse mechanical tolerance within **$\pm 2\ \text{to}\ 5\ \mu\text{m}$**).

4. **Closed-Loop Blade Height & Kerf Offset Calibration**:
   - Set the optical reference gap and blade clearance using closed-loop piezo actuators with **$0.1\ \mu\text{m}$ sensitivity** (or precision differential micrometers).
   - Perform a reference test touch / hair cut into sacrificial edge dicing streets.
   - Verify that diamond saw kerf placement centers within the street width to within **$\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$** (Gen 2 standard alignment tolerance).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                   Calibration Target Tolerances (um)   
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │░░                                   │
     Actuator Res┤░░                                   │
                 │▒▒▒▒▒                                │
Overlay Precision┤▒▒▒▒▒                                │
  WEC Parallelism┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                             │
                 │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                             │
  Kerf Offset Tol┤█████████████████████████████████████│
                 │█████████████████████████████████████│
                 └┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0.0      1.2      2.5      3.8     5.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **WEC Chuck Parallelism** | **$< 1.0$** | $\mu\text{m}$ across 100mm | Spherical air bearing dial gauge indicator |
| **Fiducial Overlay Precision** | **$\le 0.5$** | $\mu\text{m}$ | Split-field dual CMOS camera crosshair match |
| **Stage Actuator Resolution** | **$0.1$** | $\mu\text{m}$ | Closed-loop piezo actuator encoder readback |
| **Kerf Centerline Offset** | **$\le \pm 5.0$** | $\mu\text{m}$ | Post-cut optical metrology (Gen 2 tolerance) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Karl Suss MA6 Mask Aligner Standard Operating Procedure & Gap Control**:
  - Mechanical Wedge Error Compensation (WEC) achieving parallelism $< 1\ \mu\text{m}$ across 100mm wafers via spherical air bearings.
  - Split-field microscope with $5\times$, $10\times$, and $20\times$ objectives paired with dual CMOS cameras.
  - Overlay alignment precision $\le 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ in vacuum contact mode and $\pm 2\ \text{to}\ 5\ \mu\text{m}$ in proximity mode.
  - Pneumatic clamping pressure levels: $0.1\ \text{to}\ 0.5\ \text{bar}$ (soft) and $1.0\ \text{bar}$ (hard).
- **Optical Mask Aligner Mechanics: Gap Control and UV Exposure Dose**:
  - Gap and alignment setting controlled via differential micrometers or closed-loop piezo actuators with $0.1\ \mu\text{m}$ sensitivity.
  - Crosshair alignment marks for fiducial registration.
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:
  - Optical microscope objective configuration ($10\times\ \text{Plan Achromat}$, NA 0.25) resolving micron-scale features.
  - Alignment precision tolerance progression: $\pm 100\ \mu\text{m}$ (Gen 1) calibrated down to $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ (Gen 2).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Optical street registration on thin 180nm DRAM wafers (thinned to ~150-200 um) requires closed-loop cross-axis telecentric vision feedback to correct for thermal drift of the high-speed air-bearing dicing spindle (30,000-60,000 RPM) and tape expansion during wafer mounting. A static blade-to-camera offset lookup table will result in kerf drift exceeding +/-3 um across a 200mm substrate, violating the street boundary and encroaching on the DRAM seal ring and test pad arrays.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm CMOS BEOL, dicing streets measure approximately 60-80 um in width with embedded crack-stop rings and metal drop-in test structures. Using a 25-30 um resinoid or nickel-electroformed diamond blade leaves only a 15-25 um clearance window to the active DRAM active die boundary. Non-contact optical alignment must account for kerf widening due to diamond grit pull-out, requiring automated hair-line kerf checks on dummy silicon test cuts prior to product wafer commitment.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dual-camera vision lighting pods (coaxial vs. oblique darkfield LED rings) and high-precision diamond hubbed blades (grit size 2-4 um) face intermittent regional supply lead times of 8-12 weeks. Sourcing standardized diamond dicing blades and calibrated optical reticle targets from secondary ISO 9001 certified packaging consumables suppliers is necessary to avoid single-source production halts on the DRAM pilot line.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration cycles must not bottleneck the automated saw cell throughput. Optical street teaching and blade hair-line positioning must complete within a 4-minute calibration budget per frame mount. Failure to maintain fast optical alignment routines will extend wafer-on-tape dwell time, risking premature UV dicing tape delamination and adhesive plasticizer migration into diced DRAM street sidewalls.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Kerf offset misalignment causing the diamond blade to breach the die seal ring and cut into sensitive DRAM edge guard rings or peripheral wordline/bitline decoders.
1. Spindle thermal growth and optical camera parallax causing angular theta misalignment (kerf tilt > 0.05 degrees), resulting in progressive chipping and mechanical micro-fractures extending into active memory arrays.
1. Inadequate optical illumination mode selection over BEOL dielectric stacks causing pattern recognition failure on street fiducials, triggering automated kerf offset fallback errors.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-2-1-01` | **Dual-Axis Non-Contact Optical Blade Kerf Offset and Centerline Calibration** | Automated Dual-Spindle Dicing Saw Optical Alignment Vision System (5x/20x dual-magnification coaxial telecentric microscope, 0.1 um linear optical encoders), Hairline Optical Calibration Target Wafer | 1. Load calibration mirror silicon substrate onto porous ceramic chuck and apply 80 kPa vacuum. 2. Execute a single 50 um depth test cut along the X-axis at 20 mm/s with 1.8 L/min DI cooling water. 3. Automatically traverse the telecentric optical camera to three designated coordinates along the cut kerf (X = 20mm, 100mm, 180mm). 4. Measure cut kerf width and true kerf centerline relative to the optical hairline vision crosshairs using sub-pixel edge detection. 5. Compute translational delta (dY) and angular offset (dTheta) and write corrections directly into the motion controller registers. | `Kerf centerline optical registration offset |dY| <= 1.5 um across all 3 measurement locations; angular deviation |dTheta| <= 0.015 degrees; kerf width variation <= 1.2 um from nominal blade specification.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-2-1-02` | **DRAM Die Scribe Street Optical Fiducial Pattern Recognition & Kerf Clearance Verification** | High-Resolution Dual-Field Optical Microscope with darkfield/brightfield coaxial LED illumination, automated image pattern recognition (PR) engine, calibrated glass grid reticle | 1. Position mounted frame on saw chuck and initiate automated two-point global fiducial alignment on peripheral DRAM alignment keys. 2. Verify optical pattern recognition score and autofocus repeatability across 4 cardinal wafer quadrants. 3. Perform dry optical overlay simulation across five X-streets and five Y-streets, projecting the calibrated kerf profile (nominal 30 um blade + 4 um side-chipping margin). 4. Measure remaining clearance distance between predicted kerf outer edge and DRAM active seal ring. | `Fiducial pattern recognition match correlation score >= 98.0%; optical street registration positional repeatability <= 1.0 um (3-sigma); minimum predicted clearance from cut margin to DRAM seal ring >= 12.0 um.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: EN 166 compliant UV/impact-resistant safety spectacles with side shields, Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness), Anti-static ESD lab coat / cleanroom bunny suit, Closed-toe ESD protective footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with high-velocity dicing spray or silicon particulate: flush eyes immediately with eyewash station DI stream for 15 minutes; seek ophthalmological attention. Skin contact with IPA or surfactant: wash exposed area with running water and mild soap. Inhalation of aerosolized mist: evacuate operator to fresh air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Enclosed saw cabinet maintained under negative pressure relative to cleanroom with dedicated local exhaust ventilation extracting mist and micro-silicon debris at >= 15 m3/min face velocity; HEPA-filtered cleanroom return.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dicing slurry containing suspended crystalline silicon fines and diamond grit must be routed to the packaging facility specialized silicon wastewater settlement and filtration system (1 um cartridge filter cascade followed by pH neutralization between 6.5 and 8.5) prior to final industrial discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (DIW cooling fluid)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade ASTM D5127 Type E-1 | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA for optical calibration optics cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Non-ionic Dicing Surfactant (polyoxyethylene alkyl ether)** | `9002-92-0` | Electronic Grade | `0.1 - 0.5% in DIW` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `180 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Background and polished wafer mounted on dicing tape/frame; frontside BEOL passivation dry, free of residual grinding slurry, organic films, and tape mounting air bubbles.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated dicing street coordinates locked in system recipe; wafer street surfaces pre-wetted with surfactant DIW layer, ready for immediate first-pass high-speed dicing cut.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to ambient cleanroom humidity and air leads to moisture uptake and micro-corrosion of exposed aluminum/copper test pads inside the dicing street, as well as gradual relaxation and adhesion degradation of the dicing tape causing die fly-off during saw penetration.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full optical alignment and blade street registration calibration completed for 180nm DRAM wafers on dicing frames, validating sub-1.5 um blade centerline accuracy, zero seal-ring encroachment, and repeatable optical pattern recognition on street fiducials.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `blade_optical_alignment_calibration_report.pdf`
- [ ] `kerf_centerline_offset_telecentric_data.csv`
- [ ] `street_registration_overlay_fiducial.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Optical blade-to-camera kerf centerline registration offset (|dY|)** | `0.0 um` | <= 1.5 um | Automated sub-pixel image edge analysis of silicon test cuts captured via 20x telecentric vision system |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Angular theta alignment deviation across 200mm diameter street length** | `0.000 deg` | <= 0.015 deg | Linear regression calculation on two-point fiducial registration coordinates across maximum wafer chord |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Minimum physical clearance between outer kerf chipping boundary and DRAM active die seal ring** | `15.0 um` | >= 12.0 um | Calibrated optical measurement at 20x magnification across 10 random sample dies post-kerf verification cut |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All quantitative assertions (ASSERT-01 through ASSERT-03) verified and passing 3 consecutive dummy silicon test cuts, optical street registration repeatability demonstrated at <= 1.0 um across 200mm wafer field, and alignment calibration data logged and signed off in MES.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Speed Dual-Spindle Dicing Recipe Execution & DI Water Cooling

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Mount on Frame  │
│     & Chuck Vacuum     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Z1 Rough Cut 60-70%   │
│         Depth          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Z2 Clean Kerf      │
│  Separation into Tape  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  DI Water Jet Cooling  │
│     & Swarf Flush      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Post-Saw DI Rinse &   │
│      N2 Spin Dry       │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objective
Establish an automated high-speed dual-spindle step-cut dicing procedure for 180nm/130nm open-source DRAM/CMOS MPW silicon wafers (such as fabricated on the commercial SkyWater SKY130 grid), utilizing sequential blade grooving and continuous deionized (DI) water cooling to prevent thermal damage, die fly-off, silicon swarf redeposition, and micro-chipping along scribe streets.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Dicing Alignment & Vacuum Stage Clamping:**
   - Transfer dicing-frame mounted wafer onto the porous ceramic vacuum chuck.
   - Verify chuck vacuum pressure reaches $\le -85\text{ kPa}$.
   - Pattern match alignment marks using dual-magnification CCD optics. Align dicing street coordinates to the foundry placement grid resolution ($0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ / $5\text{ nm}$).
   - Verify street alignment angle theta ($\theta$) deviation is $\le 0.001^\circ$ across both X and Y axes.

2. **Spindle Parameter Setup (Dual-Spindle Step-Cut):**
   - **Spindle 1 (Z1 - Rough Bevel/Half-Cut):** Equip a wider diamond blade ($35\text{--}40\ \mu\text{m}$ hubbed blade). Set rotation speed to $30{,}000\text{--}40{,}000\text{ RPM}$. Configure cutting depth to 60%–70% of total wafer substrate thickness to groove the BEOL dielectric stack and top silicon without chipping the backside.
   - **Spindle 2 (Z2 - Final Through-Cut):** Equip a ultra-thin resin/metal-bonded diamond blade ($20\text{--}25\ \mu\text{m}$). Set rotation speed to $40{,}000\text{--}50{,}000\text{ RPM}$. Set height to cut completely through remaining silicon and enter mounting dicing tape by $20\text{--}30\ \mu\text{m}$.
   - Set table feed speed along street axes to $20\text{--}40\text{ mm/s}$.

3. **DI Water Jet Cooling & Flushing Setup:**
   - Direct dual blade-flange cooling nozzles symmetrically at the diamond blade cutting contact zones.
   - Set blade cooling DI water flow rate to $1.2\text{--}1.8\text{ L/min}$ per spindle.
   - Direct secondary shower curtain nozzles onto the wafer kerf surface at $\ge 1.5\text{ L/min}$ to suppress airborne silicon swarf redeposition.
   - Verify DI water resistivity is maintained at $> 12\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ (with carbon dioxide $\text{CO}_2$ bubbler injector active to mitigate ESD charging on exposed BEOL metallization).

4. **Automated Step-Cut Execution:**
   - Initiate Z1 + Z2 step cutting along all primary parallel streets ($X$-axis).
   - Rotate table by $90.000^\circ$ and repeat step cutting along orthogonal streets ($Y$-axis).
   - In-line monitoring monitors blade wear, spindle motor current loads, and DI water pressure.

5. **Post-Dicing High-Pressure Cleaning & Dry:**
   - Transfer diced frame to the integrated spinner station.
   - Execute atomized DI water high-pressure jet cleaning at $2.0\text{--}3.0\text{ MPa}$ nozzle pressure at $500\text{ RPM}$ for 30 seconds to dislodge sub-micron swarf.
   - Ramp to $2{,}500\text{ RPM}$ under high-purity dry $\text{N}_2$ purge ($> 99.999\%$, $0.2\ \mu\text{m}$ filtered) for 45 seconds until surface moisture is completely evacuated.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Inspection / Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Frontside Topside Chipping ($W_{\text{chip}}$)** | $\le 10\ \mu\text{m}$ (maximum allowable edge breakout) | Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) / High-mag optical microscopy |
| **Backside Kerf Chipping ($W_{\text{back}}$)** | $\le 20\ \mu\text{m}$ (maximum breakout depth) | Infrared (IR) microscopy / Optical backside inspection |
| **Kerf Placement Offset Error** | $\le \pm 2.5\ \mu\text{m}$ (relative to scribe line center) | In-line laser kerf width measurement tool / AOI metrology |
| **Wafer Surface Particle Cleanliness** | $\le 5$ particles ($> 0.2\ \mu\text{m}$) per individual DRAM die | Automated laser surface particle scanner / Darkfield defect inspection |

---

### 4. Context & Literature Citations

- **Foundry Layout & Street Alignment Grid:** Aligned according to the *SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid*, specifying a physical placement grid resolution of $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$) and BEOL routing geometries (Metal 1 width: $0.14\ \mu\text{m}$, pitch: $0.34\ \mu\text{m}$).
- **DI Water & Surface Conditioning Controls:** Dehydration desorption requirements and spin drying aerodynamics align with surface preparation dynamics established in *Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming* (water desorption and centrifugal drag mechanics).
- **Process Technology Node Integration:** Process parameters adapted for commercial 130nm-to-180nm open-source MPW architectures documented in *SkyWater 130nm Open PDK Overview & Architecture*.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dual-spindle blade dicing (Z1 rough cut / Z2 finish cut) introduces dynamic hydrodynamic drag and high-frequency vibrational coupling into the thinned 180nm DRAM wafer substrate (150-200 um thickness). The dual-nozzle DI water cooling jet delivery system must maintain laminar boundary-layer flushing with balanced forward/sub-nozzle flow rates (1.5-2.2 L/min per spindle) to avoid Bernoulli flutter, blade deflection, and ESD damage while scrubbing silicon swarf from narrow 80 um dicing streets.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For open-source 180nm DRAM with BEOL Al-Cu metallization and SiN/SiO2 passivation, step dicing is mandatory: Z1 resinoid/metal-bond blade cuts through the passivation and active layers to 50-60% wafer depth, while Z2 resinoid blade severs the remaining silicon bulk into the dicing tape by 20-30 um. Insufficient DI water specific resistivity (target 1.0-3.0 Mohm-cm via CO2 bubbler injection) will cause severe static charge accumulation (>100V) inducing dielectric breakdown across sensitive DRAM gate oxides and peripheral decode transistors.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Hubless electroformed diamond blades (grit size 2-4 um for Z1, 1-2 um for Z2) and ultra-pure carbon dioxide bubbler re-injection canisters are subject to extended lead times and consignment stock fluctuations. Synthetic resin dicing tapes with UV-curable acrylic adhesives must be sourced under qualified lot-controlled tack-force stability (pre-UV peel strength >= 5.0 N/25mm) to avoid supply interruptions and die fly-off.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Dual-spindle dicing throughput dictates overall packaging BEOL takt time. Balancing spindle RPM (30,000 to 45,000 RPM) and chuck feed speed (30-50 mm/s) is necessary to keep UPH targets >= 15 wafers/hour while maintaining street alignment drift under 1.5 um across 200mm diameter wafers, strictly adhering to scheduled preventative maintenance blade truing cycles.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Subsurface silicon microcracking and backside chipping (>25 um) extending into DRAM seal rings due to blade loading and insufficient coolant lubrication.
1. Electrostatic discharge (ESD) dielectric punch-through on peripheral input/output pads caused by non-carbonated ungrounded high-resistivity DI water.
1. Die fly-off during high-speed feed motion resulting from surfactant-induced tape debonding or excessive hydrodynamic coolant pressure lift.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-2-2-01` | **Dual-Spindle Kerf Width, Street Centering, and Chipping Metric Verification** | Automated High-Resolution Optical Metrology System / Confocal Laser Scanning Microscope (Keyence VK-X3000) | 1. Execute Z1 half-cut dicing (spindle 1 at 35,000 RPM, feed speed 40 mm/s, depth 60% of wafer thickness) along street channels. 2. Execute Z2 through-cut dicing (spindle 2 at 40,000 RPM, feed speed 40 mm/s, depth 100% wafer thickness + 25 um into tape). 3. Transfer frame to metrology chuck and measure kerf width, street offset, top-side chipping, and backside chipping at 25 designated die locations (center, mid-radius, wafer edge). | `Kerf width = 35 um +/- 3 um; Street alignment offset <= 2.0 um; Maximum top-side chipping width <= 10.0 um; Maximum backside chipping size <= 15.0 um; Zero cracking into the DRAM active seal ring.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-2-2-02` | **DI Water Coolant Hydrodynamic Flow, Resistivity, and ESD Surface Potential Verification** | Inline Toroidal Resistivity Meter, Dual-Channel Coolant Flowmeter, Non-Contact Electrostatic Fieldmeter (Trek 520) | 1. Measure inline resistivity of the DI water supply during active spindle rotation at 40,000 RPM. 2. Record instantaneous coolant flow rates at Z1 primary, Z1 sub-nozzle, Z2 primary, and Z2 sub-nozzle. 3. Position non-contact electrostatic fieldmeter probe 5.0 mm above diced wafer surface immediately upon spindle retraction and record peak residual voltage. | `DI water resistivity maintained between 1.0 and 3.0 Mohm-cm; DI water total flow rate = 3.6 L/min +/- 0.3 L/min (>= 1.6 L/min per spindle); Wafer surface electrostatic peak potential <= +/- 50 V.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (Class 100 compatible), ANSI Z87.1 Impact and Splash Safety Goggles, Hearing Protection (NRR >= 25 dB for high-frequency spindle noise), Anti-Static Cleanroom Frock and ESD Conductive Safety Shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For eye contact with water/silicon swarf: Immediately flush eyes with clean isotonic saline or eye wash solution for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For high-speed mechanical pinch or cut: Press emergency spindle stop immediately, apply sterile compression bandage to control bleeding, and seek medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing chamber laminar exhaust velocity maintained at 0.5-0.8 m/s with integrated mist collector to exhaust aerosolized coolant and silicon micro-particulates; room fresh air turnover >= 30 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dicing effluent containing silicon swarf must be routed to cleanroom sedimentation tanks and multi-stage microfiltration units (pore size 0.5 um) before neutralizing pH (6.5-8.5) and discharging to municipal wastewater.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (DI Water)** | `7732-18-5` | SEMI Grade E-1 (Ultrapure) | `100%` |
| **Carbon Dioxide (CO2 for resistivity bubbling)** | `124-38-9` | Electronic Grade 4.5 (>= 99.995%) | `Saturated solution (1.0-3.0 Mohm-cm)` |
| **Silicon (Suspended particulate swarf)** | `7440-21-3` | Semiconductor Grade | `Suspended solids < 500 ppm in wastewater` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Thinned 180nm DRAM wafer securely laminated onto UV dicing tape on stainless steel ring frame, surface free of slurry and particle residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully singulated DRAM die matrix on unexpanded dicing tape, cleaned via high-pressure DI water spray, spun dry, zero residual silicon slurry or moisture spots.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Drying of residual silicon swarf slurry onto Al-Cu bond pads causing irreversible adhesion/corrosion, and humidity-induced degradation of dicing tape adhesive causing die misalignment or premature detachment.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Execution of dual-spindle step-dicing recipe yielding 100% singulated 180nm DRAM dies with nominal kerf width, zero seal ring intrusions, top/backside chipping within specifications, and residual surface electrostatic charges suppressed via CO2-treated DI water cooling.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dicing_kerf_metrology_report_gen3.csv`
- [ ] `chipping_optical_inspection_map.tiff`
- [ ] `dicing_recipe_and_esd_verification_log.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Average kerf width across all diced dicing streets** | `35.0 um` | +/- 2.5 um | Automated Optical Metrology at 200x magnification |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum allowable backside chipping size along die edges** | `12.0 um` | +3.0 um max threshold | Confocal Laser Scanning Microscope (VK-X3000) backside edge scan |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-cut wafer surface static charge potential** | `0.0 V` | +/- 50.0 V | Non-contact electrostatic fieldmeter measurement |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of dies on the 200mm wafer are fully singulated without die fly-off, kerf centering error is <= 2.0 um, zero active seal-ring breach across 100% sampled inspection sites, and metrology signoff log approved by Packaging Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: Post-Dicing Kerf Width Metrology & Chipping Defect Inspection
**Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip MPW Tapeout)  
**Process Step Path**: `[Architecture & Integration] > [Foundry Tapeout & PDK] > [BEOL & Packaging] > [Packaging & Assembly] > [Packaging] > [Packaging] > [Metrology]`  
**Action Type**: Buy (Commercial Assembly & Metrology Facility Execution)

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Mount Diced Frame    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Optical Inspection &  │
│       Metrology        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ├─────────────────────────────╮
             ▼                             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │    │                        │
│       Kerf Width       │    │      Die Chipping      │
│      Measurement       │    │       Assessment       │
│                        │    │                        │
└───────────┬────────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘
            │                              │
            │ ╭────────────────────────────╯
            ▼ ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Acceptance Gate     │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Dicing Frame Loading & Alignment**:
   - Secure the expanded dicing tape frame onto the optical inspection motorized stage under vacuum hold-down.
   - Align the wafer coordinate axes using primary street fiducials with macroscopic alignment tolerance $\le \pm 5\,\mu\text{m}$.
2. **Optical Metrology Calibration**:
   - Engage calibrated projection/objective optics (Plan Achromat objective, $\text{NA} \ge 0.25$) configured with sub-micron pixel mapping aligned to the PDK manufacturing grid resolution ($0.005\,\mu\text{m} / 5\,\text{nm}$).
3. **Kerf Width & Street Placement Scan**:
   - Measure cut channel street width along horizontal ($X$) and vertical ($Y$) scribe lines across 9 standard inspection sites (Center, North, South, East, West, and 4 intermediate quadrants).
   - Verify dicing cut centerline displacement relative to the designed scribe street center.
4. **Top-Surface & Edge Chipping Inspection**:
   - Perform brightfield optical scanning along all die perimeters. Measure the maximum lateral intrusion of silicon chipping from the kerf sidewall toward the die seal ring.
5. **Backside Chipping Inspection**:
   - Utilize infrared (IR) transmission microscopy or flip-stage optical inspection through the UV dicing tape to quantify backside micro-chipping depth and width along blade exit edges.
6. **Defect Disposition & Gate Review**:
   - Flag any die exhibiting chipping penetrating within the outer boundary of the die seal ring or exceeding dimensional thresholds for automatic rejection and electronic wafer mapping (EWM).

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                   Post-Dicing Inspection Limits (um)   
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │░░░░                                  │
Street Placement┤░░░░                                  │
                │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                       │
   Back Chipping┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                       │
    Top Chipping┤▓▓▓▓▓▓                                │
                │▓▓▓▓▓▓                                │
      Kerf Width┤██████████████████████████████████████│
                │██████████████████████████████████████│
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                0.0      9.5      19.0     28.5    38.0 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value / Limit | Inspection Technique | Tool Resolution / Grid |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Kerf Width ($W_{\text{kerf}}$)** | $38.0\,\mu\text{m} \pm 4.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Optical Metrology | Calibrated to $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ grid |
| **Top-Side Die Chipping ($L_{\text{chip, top}}$)** | $\le 5.0\,\mu\text{m}$ (Must not breach seal ring) | Brightfield Optical ($10\times\text{--}50\times$, $\text{NA} \ge 0.25$) | $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ manufacturing grid |
| **Backside Die Chipping ($L_{\text{chip, back}}$)** | $\le 15.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | IR Transmission / Optical Back-side Metrology | Optical sub-micron scale |
| **Street Placement Accuracy** | Center offset $\le \pm 3.5\,\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Edge Detection | Alignment tolerance within $\pm 5\,\mu\text{m}$ |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Citations

1. **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**:
   - *Physical Placement Grid Resolution*: $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{nm}$) physical manufacturing grid defining discrete measurement boundaries and metrology calibration steps.
   - *Overlay & Alignment Constraints*: Maximum permissible gate overlay budget ($\le 35\,\text{nm}$) and strict alignment tolerances dictate sub-micron inspection repeatability for BEOL boundary preservation.
2. **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:
   - *Optics & Alignment*: $10\times$ Plan Achromat objective ($\text{NA} = 0.25$) providing sub-micron feature resolution with alignment precision scaling from baseline Gen 1 ($\pm 100\,\mu\text{m}$) down to Gen 2/3 tolerances of $\pm 5\,\mu\text{m}$.

---
*Micro-knowledge recorded in [docs/sop_post_dicing_metrology.md](./docs/sop_post_dicing_metrology.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-dicing kerf and chipping metrology represents the physical boundary integrity check for the 180nm DRAM die. System-level integration failure occurs if backside micro-cracks or sidewall chipping propagate into the seal ring during subsequent die attach and thermal cycling, compromising DRAM storage node charge retention and peripheral gate oxide reliability. Optical automated defect inspection (ADI) must register kerf center offset relative to the dicing street fiducials within sub-micron repeatability, ensuring dicing blade drift does not breach the 15 um guard ring margin.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In 180nm BEOL DRAM processing, dicing through multi-layer metallization (up to 4-5 Al/Cu metal layers with TEOS/FSG dielectric stacks) creates high mechanical shear stress. Topside chipping along kerf edges must strictly not exceed 10 um in width or encroach within 10 um of the active seal ring. - **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Researchers must achieve 100% automated optical inspection of kerf street corners and critical array boundaries on all thinned DRAM qualification lots without manual operator bias. 1. Blade wander or vibration induced kerf deviation (>5 um offset from street centerline), causing metallization smearing and inter-die substrate shorts.
1. Backside silicon micro-cracking hidden beneath UV dicing tape that propagates into catastrophic die fracture during pick-and-place.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: Post-Dicing Die Kerf Width & Chipping Metrology Inspection

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-dicing kerf and chipping metrology must interface directly with the factory MES and automated wafer sort prober map to dynamically mask die with severe perimeter defectivity. At 180nm BEOL nodes, excessive kerf wander or cumulative edge chipping exceeding 25 um breaches the seal ring boundary, inducing passivation delamination, moisture-induced aluminum metallization corrosion, and premature refresh degradation in peripheral DRAM sense amplifiers. Optical metrology inspection recipes must maintain sub-micron repeatability across street intersections while compensating for dicing tape stretch, UV-release tape warpage, and optical contrast variations between saw street oxide steps and silicon substrate.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-speed diamond blade saw dicing induces thermo-mechanical microcracking governed by grit size (e.g., 2-4 um diamond grit in nickel matrix), blade spindle feed rate, and deionized DI water coolant delivery. For this 180nm DRAM process, kerf width must be constrained within nominal blade kerf + 10 um, and backside/topside chipping depth must remain under 15 um to prevent propagation into active peripheral guard rings and seal rings. Critical attention must be given to micro-cracks propagating along the (110) cleavage planes of the crystalline silicon wafer; automated brightfield/darkfield confocal defect inspection at 50x magnification is mandatory to resolve sub-surface micro-cleaves hidden beneath polyimide/Si3N4 overcoats.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standardizing post-dicing inspection protocols ensures compatibility with outsourced assembly and test (OSAT) partners. Using standardized UV dicing tapes (such as Nitto Denko or Furukawa Electric UV-curable PO/PET tapes) and standard SEMI wafer ring frames (8-inch SUS304) minimizes tooling changeover costs. However, metrology cycle times per wafer must be bounded under 6 minutes for 100% kerf street screening; otherwise, inspection becomes a major throughput bottleneck, jeopardizing wafer sort queue time constraints and driving up packaging NRE costs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Inspection milestones must yield unambiguous digital defect maps (SEMI E142/Klarf compliant) before advancing diced frames to UV tape cure and automated pick-and-place die attach. Metrology throughput must achieve >= 10 wafers per hour with zero false-negative seal ring breaches. Researchers must deliver audited kerf profiles and chippage distribution data to validate blade wear curves, preventing unmonitored blade catastrophic loading and safeguarding tapeout MPW deliverables.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Seal ring micro-fracture breach: Topside chipping propagating deeper than 25 um into the die periphery, severing the continuous metal/via moisture barrier and causing catastrophic DRAM retention and refresh failure in humid environments.
1. Dicing tape cut-through and frame relaxation: Excess saw depth of cut penetrating >50% into the dicing tape, causing tape relaxation, kerf closure during inspection, die-to-die collision, and false kerf width optical readings.
1. Silicon dust redeposition bridging: Inadequate DI water cooling flush during dicing leading to dried silicon slurry encrustation along kerf sidewalls, obstructing automated optical image segmentation and masking true micro-chipping.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-3-01` | **Automated Topside Kerf Width and Step-Wander Metrology Inspection** | Automated Die/Wafer Metrology Optical Inspection System (Confocal Brightfield/Darkfield, 0.1 um/pixel optical resolution, motorized X-Y vacuum ring stage, calibrated with NIST-traceable stage micrometer). | 1. Load dicing frame onto the metrology vacuum chuck and align fiducials to establish global wafer coordinate grid.\n2. Execute automated 100% street scan along X and Y dicing channels at 20x magnification.\n3. Measure kerf width (distance between opposing cut edges) at 5 locations per dicing line across 49 sampling sites (center, mid-radius, edge).\n4. Compute kerf centerline wander relative to the designed PDK seal ring street centerlines.\n5. Export raw coordinate measurements and defect overlays to Klarf inspection report. | `Kerf width must be 35.0 um ± 5.0 um across all 49 measured sites. Maximum kerf centerline wander must not exceed ± 4.0 um from design street nominal. Zero instances of kerf intrusion into the outer 5.0 um seal ring exclusion zone.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-3-02` | **Automated Die Edge Chipping Size and Clearance Metrology** | High-Resolution Automated Optical Defect Inspection System with Darkfield UV Illumination (365 nm) and edge-detection morphological software. | 1. Set optical defect inspection threshold for edge irregularities with darkfield illumination to highlight scattering at chip edges.\n2. Inspect 100% of die perimeters across active array and peripheral logic regions.\n3. Record maximum lateral chipping dimension (depth into the die edge) and longitudinal chipping length for every detected edge chip.\n4. Measure residual distance (clearance margin) from the innermost apex of each chip to the outermost metal layer of the DRAM seal ring.\n5. Generate Pareto distribution of chipping size and location map. | `Maximum top-surface chipping depth must be <= 15.0 um along any die edge. Chipping length along dicing street must be <= 30.0 um. Minimum clearance between deepest chip apex and seal ring must be >= 10.0 um. Zero occurrences of seal ring penetration across all functional die.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, Full cleanroom ESD smock with conductive grounding boots, Lint-free chemical-resistant apron for manual solvent cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA eye contact: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean running water or saline solution for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing and wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and DI water. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Immediately move victim to fresh air; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored; seek medical evaluation. For cuts from dicing silicon fragments: Cleanse wound immediately with sterile saline, do not rub, and refer to medical personnel for micro-splinter extraction.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated cleanroom laminar flow hood (ISO Class 5) with certified Class I Division 2 local solvent exhaust providing minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); continuous volatile organic compound (VOC) monitoring and automatic interlocks on solvent dispensing areas.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA solvent rags and wipe waste must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-proof red bio/solvent disposal cans; liquid IPA effluents must be segregated into dedicated organic solvent waste carboys for commercial incineration. No solvent discharge into acid/base neutralization or municipal sewer systems.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Tier 3) | `99.9% wt` |
| **Deionized Water (DI Water)** | `7732-18-5` | SEMI Standard Grade E-1 (18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C) | `100% vol` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (N2)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra High Purity (UHP) 99.999% | `100% vol` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer frame, DI water spin-dried, top-surface polyimide passivation and dicing channels clean of visible slurry, mounted under uniform tension on UV-curable tape.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: 100% metrology-inspected, defect-mapped, pristine dry die surface; tape tension verified; ready for UV tape curing and die attach.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time in ambient cleanroom air causes moisture-induced galvanic corrosion along exposed saw-channel aluminum test pads, environmental particle deposition inside dicing street fissures, and degradation/aging of UV tape acrylic adhesive making subsequent peel-force release during die pickup erratic or catastrophic.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of 100% automated optical kerf width, kerf wander, and die edge chipping metrology across the 180nm DRAM diced wafer frame, delivering verified digital defect maps, statistically quantified kerf process capability, and certified seal ring clearance compliance for all known good die (KGD).

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram180_post_dicing_metrology_inspection_report.pdf`
- [ ] `kerf_width_chipping_wafer_map.klarf`
- [ ] `kerf_wander_chippage_statistical_summary.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean dicing kerf width across all street intersections** | `35.0 um` | ± 3.5 um | Automated confocal optical metrology image edge analysis across 49 sampled wafer coordinates |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum allowable lateral chipping depth from die edge** | `0.0 um` | + 15.0 um max | Automated high-magnification darkfield edge segmentation inspection on 100% of diced perimeter |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Minimum physical clearance between deepest edge chip and active seal ring** | `15.0 um` | - 5.0 um max (absolute minimum >= 10.0 um) | Automated image distance transform from chip contour apex to calibrated seal ring GDSII CAD overlay |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of dice on the wafer frame inspected with zero unmapped kerf zones; maximum chipping depth <= 15.0 um with minimum seal ring clearance >= 10.0 um across all candidate good die; Klarf defect map and SEMI E142 wafer map files successfully uploaded to manufacturing MES database; signed approval from both Packaging Metrology Lead and Assembly QA Engineer.

3. Record maximum lateral chipping dimension (depth into the die edge) and longitudinal chipping length for every detected edge chip.
4. Measure residual distance (clearance margin) from the innermost apex of each chip to the outermost metal layer of the DRAM seal ring.
5. Generate Pareto distribution of chipping size and location map.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Maximum top-surface chipping depth must be <= 15.0 um along any die edge. Chipping length along dicing street must be <= 30.0 um. Minimum clearance between deepest chip apex and seal ring must be >= 10.0 um. Zero occurrences of seal ring penetration across all functional die.

Inhalation of solvent vapors: Immediately move victim to fresh air; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored; seek medical evaluation. For cuts from dicing silicon fragments: Cleanse wound immediately with sterile saline, do not rub, and refer to medical personnel for micro-splinter extraction.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) Recipe Setup & Kerf Reference Alignment

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-AOI-003`  
**Classification:** Semiconductor Packaging & BEOL Metrology  
**Node/Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) / Post-Dicing Die Kerf Metrology  

---

### 1. Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Wafer Mounting &    │
│  Dicing Frame Loading  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Wedge Error       │
│      Compensation      │
│  Parallelism Leveling  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Microscope Objective  │
│  Selection: 5x to 20x  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Optical Pattern     │
│     Recognition &      │
│     Reference Kerf     │
│       Alignment        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Multi-Point       │
│  Automated Mapping &   │
│    Recipe Execution    │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate & Dicing Frame Loading**
   - Transfer the diced wafer mounted on the tape frame onto the metrology vacuum stage.
   - Clamp the stage and engage vacuum hold-down pressure.

2. **Wedge Error Compensation (WEC) & Chuck Parallelism Calibration**
   - Execute mechanical leveling of the chuck using the spherical air bearing assembly.
   - Adjust chuck planar tilt until total parallelism across the 100mm substrate is strictly `< 1 µm` to eliminate focal planarity drift across the wafer field.

3. **Optical Metrology Head & Microscope Magnification Setup**
   - Configure the split-field dual-objective optical microscope paired with high-resolution CMOS cameras.
   - Initialize global die search under the **5x** objective to acquire gross dicing street orientation.
   - Index up through the **10x** objective and lock optical inspection resolution under the **20x** objective for sub-micron edge definition.
   - Confirm optical focus satisfies process depth of focus:
     $$\text{DOF} = k_2 \cdot \frac{\lambda}{\text{NA}^2} \ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$$
     ensuring complete vertical focus margin across diced surface topography.

4. **Kerf Reference Alignment & Pattern Registration**
   - Locate the reference street fiducials and diced street edges.
   - Set the automated image pattern recognition (PR) overlay alignment threshold to $\le 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ (matching vacuum contact optical alignment precision limit) to prevent false kerf skewing.
   - For proximity non-contact baseline scans, set the optical z-gap buffer within $10\ \mu\text{m}\text{ to }30\ \mu\text{m}$ to safeguard blade-separated die sidewalls against objective contact.

5. **Multi-Point Automated Inspection Recipe Execution**
   - Configure automated wafer mapping sampling routines selecting either standard **9-point** or extended **49-point** test grids to evaluate radial kerf width consistency, chipping severity, and street edge non-uniformity.
   - Save and lock the AOI execution recipe.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                      │░░                              │
  Gate Oxide Metrology┤░░                              │
                      │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
 Photoresist Metrology┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Vacuum Contact Overlay┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                       │
                      │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                       │
    WEC Chuck Leveling┤█████████████████               │
                      │█████████████████               │
                      └┬───────┬───────┬──────┬───────┬┘
                     0.00    0.50    1.00   1.50   2.00 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chuck Leveling Parallelism (WEC)** | $< 1.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Spherical air bearing mechanical leveling across 100mm wafer diameter |
| **Optical Alignment Overlay Precision** | $\le 0.5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | 20x split-field CMOS camera pattern recognition |
| **Optical Depth of Focus (DOF)** | $\ge 0.5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | $k_2 \cdot (\lambda / \text{NA}^2)$ optical window validation |
| **Wafer Metrology Map Sampling Density** | $9 \text{ or } 49$ | Inspection Points | Automated radial non-uniformity wafer map tracking |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources

- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**: Lithography process window and depth of focus specification: $\text{DOF} = k_2 \cdot (\lambda / \text{NA}^2) \ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **Karl Suss MA6 Mask Aligner Standard Operating Procedure & Gap Control**: Wedge Error Compensation (parallelism $< 1\ \mu\text{m}$ across 100mm substrates via spherical air bearings); Split-field binocular optical microscope with 5x, 10x, and 20x objectives and CMOS sensors; Alignment precision $\le 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$; Calibrated air gap ranges of $10\ \mu\text{m}\text{ to }30\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**: Thin-film optical modeling and automated radial 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping protocols.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The AOI recipe must establish closed-loop integration with the dicing saw wafer-map translation coordinates. Kerf reference alignment algorithms typically assume rigid-body translation, but tape relaxation and UV-dicing tape expansion induce non-linear localized pin-cushion distortion across the 200mm wafer frame. The vision algorithm must employ multi-point local kerf pattern-matching rather than a simple 2-point global die-pitch dead-reckoning model, otherwise false-positive chipping flags will explode toward the wafer periphery.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm DRAM nodes, kerf streets contain process control monitoring (PCM) drop-in structures and seal rings. The optical inspection recipe must segment the diamond saw cut channel from the residual crack-stop metallization. Using co-axial brightfield illumination alone causes high specular glare off top-level Al-Cu metal pads, blinding edge detection; the recipe must combine oblique darkfield LED illumination (wavelength 455-525 nm) with polarizing filters to resolve micro-chipping exceeding 5 um within the 60 um wide dicing kerf.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying a commercial AOI platform with proprietary recipe formats risks single-vendor lock-in for packaging lines in Southeast Asia. We must mandate SECS/GEM (SEMI E5/E30) compliance and SEMI G85 (Wafer Map Data Format) export to ensure recipes and defect coordinate files (.xml / .klrf) are directly ingestible by alternative second-source inspection tooling (e.g., Camtek, Onto Innovation, or local OSAT inspection tools).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Recipe engineering time must be bounded to less than 4 hours per wafer batch to meet tapeout schedule milestones for MPW Gen 3. The golden die teaching and thresholding boundary setup must not bottleneck downstream die sort and pick-and-place operations; baseline alignment repeatability must be established prior to dicing lot arrival.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Kerf centerline drift due to optical contrast loss over silicon-tape interface, causing false acceptance of backside chipping propagating into the active seal ring.
1. Pattern-recognition failure from tape stretching or tape discoloration post-UV cure, leading to global alignment abort and manual inspection escalation.
1. Misclassification of dicing slurry residue / dried DI water stains as top-surface silicon micro-cleavage or delamination.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-3-1-01` | **Automated Fiducial & Kerf Reference Pattern Recognition Repeatability** | Automated Die/Wafer Optical Inspection System (AOI) with 5x and 20x objectives, closed-loop piezo autofocus, and calibrated optical reticle grid (NIST-traceable) | 1. Load frame onto AOI motorized vacuum chuck. 2. Execute recipe auto-alignment routine using 4 corner-die optical kerf intersection fiducials. 3. Unload and reload wafer frame, repeating alignment procedure 30 consecutive cycles. 4. Record detected fiducial coordinates (X, Y, Theta) and calculate 3-sigma repeatability. 5. Inspect kerf recognition lock on primary and orthogonal secondary streets. | `Pattern recognition success rate = 100% across 30 cycles; fiducial registration positional repeatability 3-sigma <= 0.5 um; theta alignment error <= 0.005 degrees.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-3-1-02` | **Kerf Width & Edge Chipping Measurement Accuracy Verification** | High-magnification AOI optical channel (50x metallurgical objective, 0.8 NA) cross-verified against calibrated Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscope (CD-SEM) | 1. Run automated AOI recipe measuring 50 designated street locations across center, mid-radius, and edge exclusion zones. 2. Measure blade cut width and maximum lateral chipping intrusion into the street margin. 3. Transfer wafer to CD-SEM and measure the identical 50 physical sites. 4. Correlate AOI optical measurements against CD-SEM ground truth. | `AOI kerf width measurement offset vs CD-SEM <= ±0.5 um; micro-chipping detection sensitivity >= 2.0 um lateral intrusion with zero false non-detections (escape rate = 0%).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat and conductive ESD cleanroom booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Move exposed individual to clean fresh air; seek medical attention if irritation persists. Skin contact: Flush skin thoroughly with DI water for at least 15 minutes. Eye contact: Rinse immediately with eyewash solution for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Accidental ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; contact local poison control center and emergency response immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Tool enclosure equipped with integrated HEPA/ULPA laminar airflow hood (Class 1 cleanliness); stage wiping area connected to local solvent VOC exhaust operating at >= 100 FPM face velocity.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and IPA residue must be segregated into closed, dedicated hazardous waste bins for flammable organics; aqueous rinse water drained to chemical industrial waste neutralization system (pH maintained between 6.0 and 9.0).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / SEMI Grade 1) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (>18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Diced wafer on frame, fully dried of DI water cooling spray, zero residual silicon dust slurry, mounted on intact dicing tape.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Inspected wafer on frame with defect map logged, zero organic contamination, ready for automated pick-and-place sorting.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive ambient air exposure causes native oxidation and moisture adsorption on exposed copper/aluminum PCM pads along the kerf edge, accompanied by progressive adhesive migration from the dicing tape onto silicon sidewalls, degrading die attach integrity.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed, validated, and frozen AOI inspection recipe package capable of high-throughput automated kerf width calculation, edge chipping detection, and fiducial alignment for 180nm open-source DRAM 200mm wafers mounted on dicing frames.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `AOI_180nm_DRAM_Kerf_Recipe_Rev1.0.xml`
- [ ] `AOI_Kerf_Chipping_Metrology_Validation_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `WaferMap_Defect_Classification_Data.klrf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Optical kerf fiducial pattern recognition success rate under varying illumination** | `100.0%` | +0.0% / -0.0% | Automated execution log of 100 consecutive step-and-repeat alignment cycles across 5 test wafers |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Edge chipping detection limit along diced die boundaries** | `2.5 um` | ±0.5 um | Comparison of defect pixel clustering against calibrated NIST line-width standard target |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Full 200mm wafer AOI inspection scan throughput (including kerf and active die area)** | `180.0 s` | +30.0 s | System timer timestamp from cassette load to SEMI G85 wafer-map file generation |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Recipe demonstrates 100% automated fiducial capture across 3 qualification wafers, achieves measurement correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.98 against CD-SEM kerf measurements, produces zero false defect flags exceeding 5 um on reference golden dies, and successfully exports valid SEMI G85/SECS-GEM wafer maps without operator intervention.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Kerf Street Width & Blade Wear Profile Metrology Measurement

- **Module**: Packaging & Assembly / Post-Dicing Metrology Inspection
- **Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) / Gen 3
- **Action Type**: Buy (Automated Optical Inspection System / Station)
- **Document**: [sop_kerf_street_blade_wear_metrology.md](./docs/sop_kerf_street_blade_wear_metrology.md)

---

### Process Flow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Wafer Mounted on    │
│      Film Frame       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Automated Optical   │
│  Metrology Alignment  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Kerf Street Width &  │
│  Blade Profile Scan   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Chipping & Kerf    │
│  Deviation Analysis   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│      Acceptance       │
│  Verification & Tool  │
│       Feedback        │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Wafer Frame Stage Loading & Grid Registration**:
   - Secure the wafer dicing tape frame onto the automated optical metrology vacuum chuck.
   - Configure coordinate stage stepping to align strictly to the physical manufacturing grid resolution of **0.005 µm (5 nm)**.
   - Register dicing street alignment fiducials across wafer coordinate axes to achieve alignment repeatability within **±5 µm**.

2. **Optical Calibration**:
   - Select Plan Achromat optical objective ($0.25\text{ NA}$) under calibrated top-down brightfield illumination.
   - Perform automated telecentric pixel-to-micron dimensional calibration against a certified standard target to ensure measurement repeatability within sub-micron precision.

3. **Automated Wafer Mapping & Street Sampling**:
   - Initiate automated wafer mapping sampling using a **9-point or 49-point** wafer distribution pattern covering wafer center, mid-radius, and peripheral die locations.
   - Acquire orthogonal high-contrast optical image strips along both X and Y dicing kerf streets.

4. **Kerf Profile & Blade Wear Analysis**:
   - Apply sub-pixel edge detection algorithms to measure kerf width ($W_{\text{kerf}}$) continuously along the street cut channel.
   - Calculate blade wear degradation: $\Delta W = W_{\text{measured}} - W_{\text{nominal\_blade}}$.
   - Quantify centerline cut wander relative to drawn dicing street coordinates.
   - Detect topside micro-chipping depth and measure lateral intrusion into the die seal ring margins.

5. **Closed-Loop Feedback & Disposition**:
   - Export kerf and chipping metrics to the MES/dicing log.
   - If kerf drift or lateral blade wear exceeds **±5 µm**, flag the dicing saw for immediate blade dressing or replacement.

---

### Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                                                        
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
```
