| **Topside Edge Chipping Extent** | Maximum lateral chipping intrusion | $\le 5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ |

---

### Context Literature Citations
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**: Physical placement manufacturing grid resolution of **0.005 µm (5 nm)**.
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**: Standard automated **9-point or 49-point wafer mapping** methodology for across-wafer spatial tracking.
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**: High-resolution optical microscopy alignment baseline of **±5 µm** using Plan Achromat objective optics (**0.25 NA**).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Kerf street width metrology in 180nm DRAM must bridge physical diamond blade kerf loss (typically 30-40 um nominal blade thickness expanding to 45-60 um effective kerf) with the wafer-level coordinate mapping of the dicing street pitch (nominal 80 um scribe width). The primary architectural risk is measurement drift caused by tape stretch distortion on the dicing frame during stage indexing, which can cause false positives in kerf width excursions and distort blade taper wear calculations across a 200mm wafer diameter.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Blade wear manifests as radial diamond grain loss, binder matrix erosion, and kerf edge asymmetric chipping. Relying solely on 2D top-down optical reflectometry/brightfield microscopy misses the kerf cross-sectional profile (V-shape taper or rounded kerf floor). We must mandate synchronized high-magnification automated optical inspection (AOI) calibrated with confocal 3D laser profiler depth tracking or SEM cross-sectioning to correlate blade edge bevel angle wear against silicon sidewall chipping limits (must remain <15 um chipping into seal ring).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Resinoid, electroformed nickel, and metal bond diamond dicing blades (grit size 2-4 um, concentration 30-45) suffer lead-time fragility and lot-to-lot diamond concentration variances. Metrology calibration coupons and blade wear monitoring routines must be standardized so operators do not prematurely scrap costly blades or, conversely, run blades past their 30% diamond abrasive strip limit, which risks catastrophic wafer blade breakage and destruction of active 180nm DRAM dice.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must align with the post-dicing line cycle time; a 100% kerf scan on 200mm wafers will bottleneck packaging throughput. The measurement plan must define a statistically validated multi-point inspection scheme (e.g., 9-die cross-wafer Kerf Street Profile with automated coordinate logging) and establish rigid inline stop-work thresholds if blade wear rate exceeds 0.25 um kerf widening per wafer pass.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Subsurface micro-crack propagation and silicon sidewall micro-chipping breaching the DRAM moisture seal ring due to excessive blade vibration and dull diamond grits.
1. Blade deflection and dynamic taper wear causing skewed non-vertical kerf streets (>3 degree sidewall tilt), leading to die cracking during pick-and-place ejector pin impact.
1. Silicon slurry redeposition and surfactant residue bridging kerf trenches, leading to false optical autofocus locks and inaccurate blade wear profile readings.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-3-2-01` | **Automated 9-Point Optical Kerf Street Width and Chipping Dimension Inspection** | Automated High-Resolution Optical Metrology System / AOI with sub-micron motorized XY stage, 20x/50x Plan Apochromat objectives (NA >= 0.8), calibrated brightfield/darkfield illumination, and image analysis edge-detection software. | 1. Load wafer hoop onto vacuum chuck and perform automated 3-point fiducial global alignment.\n2. Drive stage to 9 standardized test locations across the wafer (Center, North, South, East, West at 0.5R and 0.85R).\n3. Acquire autofocus image stack at each site under combined brightfield and darkfield mode across X and Y street cuts.\n4. Execute sub-pixel edge detection algorithm to measure kerf trench width between active die cut borders.\n5. Quantify maximum silicon chipping intrusion from the nominal kerf cut edge toward the seal ring barrier.\n6. Log individual street widths, maximum chipping length, and mean cut center offset into metrology run-card. | `Kerf Street Width must be within 52.0 um +/- 4.0 um across all 9 sample sites; maximum top-side chipping intrusion must not exceed 10.0 um; distance from cut edge to active seal ring must remain >= 15.0 um.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-3-2-02` | **Confocal 3D Laser Profilometry of Dicing Blade Wear Profile and Trench Taper** | Non-contact 3D Laser Confocal Scanning Profilometer (405nm violet laser diode, lateral resolution 0.12 um, axial resolution 0.01 um) with multi-axis goniometer stage. | 1. Position confocal laser probe over the center intersection of orthogonal dicing streets.\n2. Perform vertical Z-scan profile across the full trench depth (target depth: wafer thickness + 25 um tape overcut).\n3. Extract 2D transverse cross-sectional profile curve of the trench sidewalls and floor.\n4. Calculate trench sidewall taper angle (theta_left, theta_right) relative to wafer normal.\n5. Measure trench bottom kerf width vs top kerf width to derive effective blade profile shoulder rounding and binder erosion wear.\n6. Calculate cumulative blade wear index: Delta_W = Top_Kerf - Bottom_Kerf. | `Sidewall taper angle must be <= 2.5 degrees from vertical (90.0 +/- 2.5 deg); profile width difference Delta_W (Top vs Bottom kerf) must be <= 3.5 um; blade kerf widening rate must be <= 0.20 um per wafer pass.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/1000 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (micro-textured, 6 mil), ANSI Z87.1 approved UV and laser safety goggles (optical density OD >= 5 at 405nm), Static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and ESD conductive shoe covers, Cleanroom face mask (3-ply polypropylene)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with IPA or surfactant solution: Flush immediately with clean eyewash or tempered water for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. If skin irritation develops, wash thoroughly with mild soap and water. For inhalation of IPA vapors: Move individual to fresh air immediately; administer CPR or supplemental oxygen if breathing becomes labored. In case of glass/silicon sliver puncture: Flush wound with sterile saline, do not rub, and seek occupational medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local cleanroom bench exhaust maintaining face velocity of 0.45 m/s (90 fpm) +/- 20%; Class 100 laminar downflow enclosure for metrology inspection area to prevent airborne dust redeposition; VOC exhaust ducting for solvent wipe stations.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent lens-cleaning IPA wipes in sealed, FM-approved fire-retardant self-closing solvent waste bins; route post-dicing DI water rinse effluent containing silicon swarf through a central micro-filtration settling tank (<= 0.5 um sediment filtration) before pH balance adjustment (pH 6.5-8.5) and industrial sewer discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Dicing Coolant / Rinse)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I Cleanroom Grade (Resistivity > 18.0 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (IPA - Metrology Lens & Stage Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Non-ionic Dicing Surfactant (Slurry Dispersant Additive)** | `9016-45-9` | Electronic Grade Formulation | `0.05% - 0.2% aqueous dilution` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-saw rinsed and spin-dried silicon wafer mounted on frame; kerf trenches free of bulk standing water droplets and cutting swarf; frontside passivation clean and un-chipped.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Metrology-verified diced wafer on frame; kerf streets dried and mapped; certified free of residue/swarf; vacuum-sealed or nitrogen-purged ready for UV tape cure and die pick-and-place.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes atmospheric hydrocarbon and moisture condensation in open kerf channels, inducing silicon oxidation, corrosion of exposed seal-ring metallization (Al/Cu layers), and irreversible adhesion/bonding of dried colloidal silicon swarf onto active DRAM bond pads.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Metrology qualification demonstrating compliant kerf cut width, minimal silicon chipping, and controlled diamond blade wear profile across 200mm DRAM wafers, ensuring die mechanical integrity and seal ring isolation prior to die attach.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `KERF_STREET_WIDTH_9PT_MAP.csv`
- [ ] `BLADE_WEAR_3D_PROFILE_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `CHIPPING_INSPECTION_HIGHRES_DEFECT_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean Kerf Street Cut Width** | `52.0 um` | +/- 3.0 um | Automated 9-point optical brightfield edge detection metrology |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum Edge Chipping Intrusion** | `6.0 um` | <= 10.0 um max limit | Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) calibrated image analysis |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Blade Sidewall Kerf Taper Angle** | `90.0 deg` | +/- 2.0 deg | Non-contact 3D laser confocal depth profiling across cut trench |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 100% compliance across all 9 metrology sites showing mean kerf width within 52.0 +/- 3.0 um, zero chipping violations encroaching within 15.0 um of the DRAM moisture seal ring, Delta_W blade taper delta <= 3.5 um, and verification that deliverable data artifacts (CSV, PDF, TIFF) are cryptographically hashed and uploaded to the DRAM Foundation VN packaging MES.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Die-Edge Top/Backside Chipping & Crack Propagation Defect Analysis

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-180-042`  
**Node Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm Open-Source DRAM / MPW Tapeout)  
**Parent Process:** Post-Dicing Die Kerf Width & Chipping Metrology Inspection  

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Sample Selection &   │
│      Preparation       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Top-Side Kerf &     │
│    Chipping Optical    │
│       Metrology        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Backside & Sidewall   │
│         Defect         │
│    Characterization    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Subsurface       │
│  Micro-Crack Acoustic  │
│   / Cross-Sectional    │
│        Analysis        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Defect Disposition &  │
│   Scribing Parameter   │
│        Feedback        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

#### Step 1: Diced Frame Load & Alignment on Automated Optical Metrology Stage
1. Mount the UV dicing tape ring carrying the diced 180nm DRAM wafer dies onto the vacuum chuck of an automated brightfield/darkfield optical defect inspection system.
2. Align fiducial alignment marks on the scribe street aligned to the orthogonal silicon crystal axes $\langle 110 \rangle$.
3. Set the measurement coordinate system on the wafer's physical manufacturing grid ($0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ grid resolution).

#### Step 2: Top-Side Kerf Centerline & Chipping Metrology
1. Inspect the dicing kerf street under $50\times - 100\times$ objective optics (or automated vision system calibrated to $\le 0.05\,\mu\text{m}$ resolution).
2. Measure the physical kerf width across 5 sampling points along orthogonal scribe streets ($X$ and $Y$).
3. Identify top-edge silicon chipping (mechanical fractures through passivation and top metallization).
4. Measure maximum top chipping lateral penetration depth ($\Delta W_{\text{top}}$) from the cut edge inward toward the active die circuitry and outer seal ring.
5. Verify that chipping does not breach the protective seal ring border or approach active bitline/wordline pitches ($360\,\text{nm} - 400\,\text{nm}$).

#### Step 3: Backside Micro-Chipping & Sidewall Delamination Inspection
1. Using high-angle darkfield illumination or infrared (IR) backside inspection (or flipping sample dies onto an inspection carrier), scan the die bottom edges.
2. Quantify maximum backside breakout/chipping width ($\Delta W_{\text{back}}$).
3. Inspect for diamond blade wear signatures (asymmetrical kerf profile, diagonal step fractures along silicon cleavage planes).

#### Step 4: Micro-Crack Propagation & Subsurface Damage (SSD) Verification
1. Inspect high-stress corners and maximum-chipping sites under confocal scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM) or cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with focused ion beam (FIB) milling.
2. Verify that micro-crack tip propagation into the bulk silicon substrate terminates prior to the active diffusion/well zones (minimum active diffusion spacing $\ge 0.15\,\mu\text{m}$).
3. Confirm absence of delamination or shear-induced fracture along the stacked capacitor dielectric stack (ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ / $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, effective $\kappa > 15$, $\text{EOT} = 3 - 4\,\text{nm}$) and tungsten plug (W-plug) interfaces.

#### Step 5: Engineering Disposition & Saw Feedback
1. Record defect classification: Pass, Quarantine, or Scrap based on acceptance criteria.
2. If chipping exceeds threshold, flag dicing feed rate or blade diamond grit degradation to prevent yield fallout from refresh degradation ($I_{\text{leak}} > 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                    Max Allowed Metrology Limits (um)   
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │████████                              │
     Kerf Offset┤████████                              │
                │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░       │
Seal Ring Margin┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░       │
   Back Chipping┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
                │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
    Top Chipping┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓               │
                │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓               │
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                0.0      6.2      12.5     18.8    25.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Hard Limit / Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Max Top-Side Chipping Depth ($\Delta W_{\text{top}}$)** | $\le 8.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | $\le 15.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Optical Metrology ($50\times / 100\times$) |
| **Max Backside Chipping Depth ($\Delta W_{\text{back}}$)** | $\le 12.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | $\le 25.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | Darkfield / Backside IR Optical Inspection |
| **Crack-to-Seal-Ring Exclusion Margin** | $\ge 30.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | $\ge 20.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | Brightfield Micro-Coordinate Stage ($\pm 0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ grid) |
| **Kerf Centerline Offset (Dicing Wander)** | $\le 2.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | $\le 5.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | Fiducial-Referenced Kerf Profile Analysis |

---

### 4. Verified Context Literature Citations

1. **[SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid]**:
   - Physical placement grid resolution: $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{nm}$).
   - Active diffusion critical dimension: Minimum active diffusion width $= 0.15\,\mu\text{m}$.
   - Interconnect geometry: Metal 1 minimum width $= 0.14\,\mu\text{m}$; minimum metal 1 pitch $= 0.34\,\mu\text{m}$.
2. **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
   - Unit cell architecture: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$.
   - High-$\kappa$ stacked capacitor dielectric stack: ONO triple dielectric or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ ($\kappa > 15$) erected via tungsten plug (W-plug).
   - Cell electrical constraint: Leakage current target $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain refresh integrity.
3. **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**:
   - Layout & pitch constraints: Bitline and wordline pitch $= 360\,\text{nm} - 400\,\text{nm}$.
   - Gate oxide: Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ with $\sim 3.5\,\text{nm}$ physical thickness.
   - Storage capacitance requirement: $25\,\text{fF} - 30\,\text{fF}$ per cell ensuring retention $> 64\,\text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topside and backside dicing chipping in 180nm DRAM architectures directly threatens the seal ring integrity and periphery guard rings, where stress concentration can induce sub-surface micro-cracks penetrating the active diffusion regions (0.15 um design rule) and outer capacitor array boundaries. The dicing lane metrology must resolve chipping dimension relative to the 15 um seal-ring-to-scribe-line clearance margin, guaranteeing that lateral crack arrestor trenches are unbreached across all 4 die corners.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Backside chipping during mechanical high-speed diamond blade dicing originates from tensile micro-cleavage along Si (111) and (110) planes when the blade exits the thinned wafer (typically 150-200 um post-backgrinding). High-resolution confocal laser scanning microscopy and brightfield/darkfield automated optical inspection (AOI) must differentiate between benign ductile spalling within the dicing street and brittle conchoidal cracks extending beyond 25 um laterally into the die edge, as thermal cycling during wire bonding will propagate backside micro-fissures into catastrophic die fracture.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dicing saw blade loading matrices (resinoid vs. nickel-electroformed diamond grit 2-4 um) and UV dicing tapes (e.g. polyolefin with acrylic adhesive) suffer from strict lead-time and lot-to-lot diamond concentration variability. If blade wear is not monitored via cumulative dicing distance and edge chipping metrology, premature blade blunting forces excessive spindle current, exponentially increasing chipping rates and wafer-level scrap across shared-reticle multi-project wafer (MPW) runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die-edge defect analysis must achieve high-throughput inline sampling (100% outer perimeter scanning on 5 sample die per quadrant) without exceeding a 45-minute inspection window per diced frame to avoid bottlenecking downstream die attach and automated pick-and-place packaging workflows.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Sub-surface Si micro-crack propagation crossing the outer passivation seal ring into peripheral high-voltage sense amplifier circuits, causing catastrophic post-assembly leakage current.
1. Backside conchoidal chipping exceeding 35 um depth, leading to mechanical fracture during thermo-compression die pick-up or gold ball wire bonding.
1. Interfacial delamination of BEOL interlayer dielectric (SiO2/SiN stacks) induced by blade vibrational shear stress along the kerf border.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-3-3-01` | **Automated Topside Kerf Edge Chipping & Seal Ring Clearance Inspection** | Automated Die-Sort Optical Metrology System (Dual-illumination Confocal Laser Scanning Microscope, 0.14 um lateral optical resolution) | 1. Load diced frame onto motorized vacuum chuck and register global wafer fiducials. 2. Execute 100x high-magnification brightfield line-scan along all orthogonal dicing streets across 20 designated sample die (5 die per wafer quadrant). 3. Measure maximum top-side edge chipping width (W_chip) perpendicular to the nominal kerf cut line. 4. Measure remaining unchipped distance between the deepest chip apex and the outermost seal ring metal boundary (D_clearance). 5. Compute mean chipping width and 3-sigma maximum across all measured die edges. | `Topside maximum chipping width W_chip <= 15.0 um; minimum residual clearance D_clearance to seal ring >= 10.0 um; zero instances of micro-cracks crossing the seal ring perimeter.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-2-3-3-02` | **Post-Dicing Backside Chipping Depth & Crack Propagation Optical Metrology** | High-Resolution Laser Confocal Depth-Profiling Microscope / Acoustic Micro-Imaging (AMI, 230 MHz transducer) | 1. Invert frame or utilize dual-telecentric bottom-side optics to image backside die boundaries through transparent tape backing. 2. Identify and record the 10 largest backside edge spallations across the wafer periphery and center die. 3. Perform 3D optical profilometry z-stack scans to determine chipping penetration depth into the Si substrate bulk. 4. Perform acoustic micro-imaging along high-stress chipped edges to verify absence of internal cleavage micro-cracks extending beyond optical spall boundaries. | `Backside maximum lateral chip extension <= 25.0 um; maximum chip penetration depth <= 20.0 um; internal acoustic reflection confirms zero sub-surface crack propagation beyond the optical chip boundary.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom ISO 5 nitrile gloves (double gloving), UV-blocking ANSI Z87.1 approved safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and conductive ESD footwear, Particulate respirator (N95 or better) during saw cleaning / dry waste handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with silicon particulate coolant: Immediately flush eyes at cleanroom eyewash station with isotonic saline or copious DI water for 15 minutes while lifting eyelids. Skin contact with IPA: Wash affected skin with mild soap and water; remove contaminated garments. Inhalation of solvent fumes: Move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing and metrology tool localized exhaust ventilation maintaining capture face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); continuous facility HEPA laminar air flow (Class 100/ISO 5) with negative static pressure at dicing saw enclosure to prevent aerosolized Si particulate escape.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dicing saw effluent containing abrasive silicon fines must route to dedicated industrial slurry sedimentation and filtration tanks (0.2 um cartridge filtration) prior to pH neutralization (6.5-8.5) and discharge into the industrial wastewater treatment system.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (DIW Dicing Coolant)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade Ultra-Pure Water (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Post-Dice Solvent Cleaner)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic/VLSI Grade (SEMI-C12) | `99.9%` |
| **Silicon Suspended Micro-Particulate Slurry (Kerf Residue)** | `7440-21-3` | Process-generated Sludge | `<1.5% wt/vol in DI water` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Completed backgrinding with post-grind stress-relief etching, mounted on dicing ring tape, saw-diced with residual DI water centrifugally spun off, surface free of slurry caking.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Inspected, verified defect-free die edge margins, UV-tape cured for adhesive peel reduction, stored in clean N2-purged FOUP/cassette awaiting automated die pick-and-place.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excess air exposure promotes native oxide (SiO2) re-growth and atmospheric moisture chemisorption along micro-fractured die edges, accelerating stress-corrosion crack extension under residual dicing tensile stress and increasing bond-pad corrosion.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Comprehensive quantitative validation and metrology signoff confirming that high-speed diamond blade saw dicing on thinned 180nm DRAM wafers produces topside and backside edge chipping and kerf-induced micro-cracks strictly within the non-critical scribe margins, ensuring zero encroachment onto the perimeter seal ring or active capacitor/periphery regions.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dicing_kerf_chipping_distribution_report.csv`
- [ ] `edge_crack_confocal_inspection_summary.pdf`
- [ ] `high_res_chipping_defect_stitched_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum topside edge chipping width along active die perimeter** | `12.0 um` | +3.0 um / -5.0 um | Automated confocal laser optical line-scan microscopy at 100x magnification |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Minimum residual distance between topside chip boundary and outer seal ring** | `13.0 um` | +5.0 um / -3.0 um | Calibrated dual-axis digital coordinate metrology referenced to wafer layout CAD GDSII overlay |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum backside edge spallation depth into thinned bulk silicon** | `15.0 um` | +5.0 um / -5.0 um | Non-contact 3D optical confocal profilometry z-depth stack analysis |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of inspected sample die across all four quadrants and center must exhibit topside chipping <= 15.0 um, backside chipping <= 25.0 um lateral / <= 20.0 um depth, zero seal ring breaches, and acoustic imaging confirming zero sub-surface cleavage crack propagation.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: Post-Dicing Die Metrology, Kerf Quality Inspection & Die Pick-and-Place Sort

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-dicing die-level metrology and automated pick-and-place sorting form the critical bridge between mechanical wafer singulation and microelectronic packaging. The automated vision inspection system (AOI) must execute real-time die-to-database registration and kerf edge-reconstruction at sub-micron resolution while synchronizing high-speed motorized stages with ultra-low vibration pick heads. A key system integration risk is coordinate distortion caused by non-uniform dicing tape stretch during wafer ring expansion, which induces die rotation and pitch walk-off across the 200mm film frame. The sorting module must dynamically correct die coordinates via dual-camera fiducial vision alignment to ensure die ejector pin placement does not induce localized backside micro-cracks or punch-through on 150 um thinned 180nm DRAM dies.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Kerf quality evaluation on 180nm open-source DRAM architecture mandates rigorous quantitative tracking of top-side active dielectric/metal chipping, silicon micro-cleaving, and backside edge flaking. Chipping must strictly terminate at least 15 um outside the seal-ring passivation perimeter; any breach of the moisture barrier will cause unpassivated Al-Cu interconnect corrosion and retention loss in cell storage capacitors. Furthermore, dicing tape UV cure release doses (typically 120-180 mJ/cm^2 at 365 nm) must be tightly controlled prior to pick-and-place: insufficient UV cure leaves high adhesive peel resistance (>0.4 N/25mm), leading to die cracking or corner shear failure under mechanical ejector needle push-up, whereas excessive UV cure can cause pre-mature die fly-off during tape indexing.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standardizing high-precision tungsten carbide multi-needle ejector caps, anti-static high-temperature rubber/polyetheretherketone (PEEK) vacuum pick-up collets, and standard 2-inch/4-inch conductive Gel-Pak or waffle pack trays requires strict qualified multi-sourcing. Sourcing UV-dicing tape (e.g., polyolefin base with acrylic UV-curable adhesive) with guaranteed low ionic impurity (Cl- < 5 ppm, Na+ < 2 ppm) is critical to prevent post-singulation bond pad contamination. Disruptions in cleanroom tray consumables or UV lamp bulb degradation (causing incomplete polymer cross-linking) present immediate assembly bottleneck risks that can halt backend MPW delivery.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die pick-and-place sorting represents the final backend yield gate where gross electrical sort maps (wafer probe inkless wafer map XML/SEMI E142 format) correlate with optical kerf integrity. Line throughput must sustain >= 3,600 units per hour (UPH) with zero misclassification between known-good-die (KGD) and edge-damaged perimeter dies. Project milestone exit depends on establishing automated yield binning and generating traceable inspection defect maps compatible with downstream wire-bonding and ceramic DIP/QFP assembly line loaders.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Sub-surface backside chipping or micro-cracks induced by mechanical ejector needle stroke exceeding critical stress limits during die pick-up, causing delayed mechanical fracturing during package molding or thermal cycling.
1. Chipping penetration exceeding the outer edge of the DRAM seal-ring moisture barrier, exposing edge dummy patterns and causing ambient moisture ingress and leakage degradation in perimeter memory cells.
1. Adhesive residue transfer from poorly cured UV tape onto backside silicon or frontside wire bond pads, causing die-attach voiding and subsequent ultrasonic wire-bond non-stick on pad (NSOP) defects.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-01` | **Post-Dicing Optical Kerf Chipping and Seal-Ring Clearance Metrology** | Automated High-Resolution Optical Inspection (AOI) System equipped with 50x/100x telecentric lenses, dual darkfield/brightfield LED illumination, and sub-micron image-stitching metrology software. | 1. Clamp wafer frame onto the automated motorized granite stage with vacuum chuck engagement. 2. Calibrate global Cartesian coordinates using wafer center and perimeter alignment fiducials. 3. Perform automated 100% surface scan of all singulated die perimeters along dicing lanes (kerf). 4. Measure maximum top-side kerf chipping width (perpendicular to cut line) and measure minimum remaining distance from outermost chip edge to outer boundary of DRAM seal-ring. 5. Record maximum top-side and corner chipping dimensions for 100% of candidate KGD dies. | `Pass: Maximum kerf chipping width <= 15.0 um; minimum distance from chip edge to seal-ring >= 15.0 um across all 4 edges; zero structural micro-cracks propagating into the seal-ring. Any die with chipping > 15.0 um or breach of seal-ring must be flagged as rejected in the bin map.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-02` | **Die Pick-and-Place Collet Placement Accuracy, Die Tilt, and Ejector Force Verification** | Automated Die Sorter / Pick-and-Place Handler with motorized multi-needle ejector stage, closed-loop vacuum sensing pick tool, and calibrated dual-axis optical optical coordinate measuring system (CMM). | 1. Align pick tool head to candidate die centroid using top-side high-speed CCD camera. 2. Synchronize ejector pin ascent (stroke = 250 um, velocity = 5 mm/s) with collet vacuum grip (vacuum level >= -80 kPa). 3. Transfer and place 100 consecutive singulated dies into designated JEDEC tray pockets. 4. Using secondary vision CMM, measure die placement offset (delta X, delta Y), rotational die theta misalignment, and post-pick backside silicon surface for needle punch indentations under 50x Nomarski differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy. | `Pass: Placement position error delta X and delta Y <= ±10.0 um; theta orientation error <= ±0.5 degrees; zero backside ejector pin micro-cracking or punch indentation depth exceeding 1.0 um; 100% pick-and-place success rate without dropped or misoriented dies.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/1000 Cleanroom Bunny Suit with Hood, Conductive ESD Cleanroom Booties with Heel Grounding Straps, Chemical and Mechanical Resistant Nitrile Gloves (ASTM D6319, powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-blocking and Anti-impact Safety Glasses, ESD Grounding Wrist Strap (1 MOhm inline resistor)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean running water or saline solution at an eyewash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing, wash affected area with mild soap and water. Inhalation of organic vapors: Evacuate worker to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored. Accidental mechanical pinch/needle puncture: Disinfect wound with betadine/antiseptic, apply sterile dressing, report to occupational health clinic.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on manual wipe stations and dicing/sorter enclosure maintaining face air velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); laminar downflow clean air (ISO Class 5 / Class 100) inside the automated pick-and-place enclosure with constant positive pressure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and solvent swabs must be deposited into dedicated airtight, grounded, fire-rated hazardous solvent waste cans; exhausted IPA vapors routed to central VOC solvent scrubbers; contaminated broken silicon fragments collected in dedicated sharp containers for hazardous solid disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Tier 3) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-pure Semiconductor Grade (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Singulated thinned wafer mounted on UV dicing tape film frame; frontside Al-Cu/passivation dried without standing water droplets, backside grind surface free of residual slurry.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Sorted, verified KGD dies seated in dry nitrogen-purged ESD waffle packs or vacuum-sealed Gel-Pak containers; dies free of kerf silicon debris, chipping, and tape adhesive residue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended atmospheric air exposure causes native copper/aluminum oxide growth and airborne molecular hydrocarbon contamination on exposed bond pads, leading to wire-bond lift-off or high contact resistance; moisture exposure initiates galvanic corrosion along diced edges where seal-ring margins are compromised.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> 100% automated optical inspection of diced 180nm DRAM dies on expanded tape frames, verifying kerf chipping within strict 15 um limits with seal-ring integrity intact, followed by precision automated pick-and-place sort yielding sorted KGD dies in vacuum-sealed ESD carriers.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram180_die_sort_bin_map.xml`
- [ ] `kerf_chipping_metrology_report.pdf`
- [ ] `pick_and_place_placement_accuracy.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum allowable top-side and corner kerf chipping width on singulated DRAM dies** | `10.0 um` | +5.0 um max (absolute upper ceiling 15.0 um) | Automated telecentric optical inspection system with 100x magnification image-stitching measurement tool. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Automated pick-and-place die placement positional accuracy in waffle pack carrier pockets** | `0.0 um` | ±10.0 um (X/Y axis offset), ±0.5 deg (theta rotation) | Calibrated dual-axis optical Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) vision system. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-pick backside ejector needle indentation depth and micro-crack incidence** | `0.0 um` | <= 1.0 um max indentation depth, 0 micro-cracks | 50x Nomarski Differential Interference Contrast (DIC) optical microscopy and white-light interferometry. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of candidate KGD dies across the 200mm wafer exhibit kerf chipping strictly <= 15.0 um with >= 15.0 um clearance to the outer seal ring; zero dropped, chipped, or cracked dies during automated pick-and-place sorting; final electronic SEMI E142 XML wafer sort map matches physical waffle pack coordinates with 100% traceability; package-ready dies vacuum sealed under dry N2.

testcases.title: Post-Dicing Optical Kerf Chipping and Seal-Ring Clearance Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Automated High-Resolution Optical Inspection (AOI) System equipped with 50x/100x telecentric lenses, dual darkfield/brightfield LED illumination, and sub-micron image-stitching metrology software.
testcases.pre_conditions: Thinned and diced 200mm DRAM wafer mounted on expanded stainless steel film frame; wafer de-ionized water post-saw wash and spin-dry complete; wafer map XML loaded.
testcases.procedure: 1. Clamp wafer frame onto the automated motorized granite stage with vacuum chuck engagement. 2. Calibrate global Cartesian coordinates using wafer center and perimeter alignment fiducials. 3. Perform automated 100% surface scan of all singulated die perimeters along dicing lanes (kerf). 4. Measure maximum top-side kerf chipping width (perpendicular to cut line) and measure minimum remaining distance from outermost chip edge to outer boundary of DRAM seal-ring. 5. Record maximum top-side and corner chipping dimensions for 100% of candidate KGD dies.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass: Maximum kerf chipping width <= 15.0 um; minimum distance from chip edge to seal-ring >= 15.0 um across all 4 edges; zero structural micro-cracks propagating into the seal-ring. Any die with chipping > 15.0 um or breach of seal-ring must be flagged as rejected in the bin map.

testcases.title: Die Pick-and-Place Collet Placement Accuracy, Die Tilt, and Ejector Force Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Die Sorter / Pick-and-Place Handler with motorized multi-needle ejector stage, closed-loop vacuum sensing pick tool, and calibrated dual-axis optical optical coordinate measuring system (CMM).
testcases.pre_conditions: UV tape irradiated at calibrated dosage (150 mJ/cm^2, 365 nm); vacuum collet tip inspected and free of debris; JEDEC waffle tray or Gel-Pak seated in output tray nest.
testcases.procedure: 1. Align pick tool head to candidate die centroid using top-side high-speed CCD camera. 2. Synchronize ejector pin ascent (stroke = 250 um, velocity = 5 mm/s) with collet vacuum grip (vacuum level >= -80 kPa). 3. Transfer and place 100 consecutive singulated dies into designated JEDEC tray pockets. 4. Using secondary vision CMM, measure die placement offset (delta X, delta Y), rotational die theta misalignment, and post-pick backside silicon surface for needle punch indentations under 50x Nomarski differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass: Placement position error delta X and delta Y <= ±10.0 um; theta orientation error <= ±0.5 degrees; zero backside ejector pin micro-cracking or punch indentation depth exceeding 1.0 um; 100% pick-and-place success rate without dropped or misoriented dies.

ppe_required: Class 100/1000 Cleanroom Bunny Suit with Hood
Conductive ESD Cleanroom Booties with Heel Grounding Straps
Chemical and Mechanical Resistant Nitrile Gloves (ASTM D6319, powder-free)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-blocking and Anti-impact Safety Glasses
ESD Grounding Wrist Strap (1 MOhm inline resistor)
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye contact with IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean running water or saline solution at an eyewash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing, wash affected area with mild soap and water. Inhalation of organic vapors: Evacuate worker to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored. Accidental mechanical pinch/needle puncture: Disinfect wound with betadine/antiseptic, apply sterile dressing, report to occupational health clinic.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on manual wipe stations and dicing/sorter enclosure maintaining face air velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); laminar downflow clean air (ISO Class 5 / Class 100) inside the automated pick-and-place enclosure with constant positive pressure.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Used IPA wipes and solvent swabs must be deposited into dedicated airtight, grounded, fire-rated hazardous solvent waste cans; exhausted IPA vapors routed to central VOC solvent scrubbers; contaminated broken silicon fragments collected in dedicated sharp containers for hazardous solid disposal.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Singulated thinned wafer mounted on UV dicing tape film frame; frontside Al-Cu/passivation dried without standing water droplets, backside grind surface free of residual slurry.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Sorted, verified KGD dies seated in dry nitrogen-purged ESD waffle packs or vacuum-sealed Gel-Pak containers; dies free of kerf silicon debris, chipping, and tape adhesive residue.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Extended atmospheric air exposure causes native copper/aluminum oxide growth and airborne molecular hydrocarbon contamination on exposed bond pads, leading to wire-bond lift-off or high contact resistance; moisture exposure initiates galvanic corrosion along diced edges where seal-ring margins are compromised.

expected_result.summary: 100% automated optical inspection of diced 180nm DRAM dies on expanded tape frames, verifying kerf chipping within strict 15 um limits with seal-ring integrity intact, followed by precision automated pick-and-place sort yielding sorted KGD dies in vacuum-sealed ESD carriers.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum allowable top-side and corner kerf chipping width on singulated DRAM dies
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated telecentric optical inspection system with 100x magnification image-stitching measurement tool.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Automated pick-and-place die placement positional accuracy in waffle pack carrier pockets
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calibrated dual-axis optical Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) vision system.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-pick backside ejector needle indentation depth and micro-crack incidence
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: 50x Nomarski Differential Interference Contrast (DIC) optical microscopy and white-light interferometry.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: 100% of candidate KGD dies across the 200mm wafer exhibit kerf chipping strictly <= 15.0 um with >= 15.0 um clearance to the outer seal ring; zero dropped, chipped, or cracked dies during automated pick-and-place sorting; final electronic SEMI E142 XML wafer sort map matches physical waffle pack coordinates with 100% traceability; package-ready dies vacuum sealed under dry N2.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) of Kerf Width, Chipping & Crack Defect Metrology

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-dicing Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) must integrate deterministic multi-wavelength telecentric illumination (brightfield and darkfield segmented LEDs) to decouple dicing tape surface scattering from true silicon micro-cracks. With 180nm DRAM wafers thinned down to 150-200 um on UV dicing tape, kerf measurement algorithms must compensate for kerf tape stretch, die tilt, and residual cooling water droplet artifacts during inline image stitching at 50 mm/s scan velocities.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Frontside and backside chipping metrology must adhere strictly to MIL-STD-883 Method 2010.14 internal visual requirements. On a nominal 80 um dicing street, lateral chipping encroaching into the outer seal ring must be flagged instantaneously; any micro-crack or chip propagating closer than 15 um to active DRAM peripheral circuitry or guard rings induces immediate unrepairable junction leakage or moisture ingress during plastic encapsulation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Optical inspection throughput cannot form an unmanageable assembly bottleneck. High-resolution 0.5 um/pixel TDI (Time Delay Integration) line-scan camera sensors and high-magnification plan-apochromatic objectives face prolonged lead times (26-32 weeks). Standardizing on calibrated multi-die dual-objective AOI inspection heads ensures multi-vendor source redundancy across Asian OSAT ecosystems.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Every diced wafer frame must execute 100% kerf visual defect classification and yield logging within <= 3.5 minutes to maintain pace with high-speed automated diamond saw dicing lines. Defect coordinates must be output directly into standard SEMI G85-0701 Wafer Map files to feed downstream high-speed die pick-and-place sorting without manual operator intervention.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Sub-surface sidewall micro-cracking propagating along Si <110> cleavage planes under mechanical saw vibration, escaping top-down 2D brightfield AOI detection and causing catastrophic die fracturing during wire bonding.
1. Chipping encroaching past the outer seal ring (>25 um width) into edge-adjacent dummy DRAM memory structures, initiating long-term ionic corrosion and thermal cycling dielectric breakdown.
1. False defect clustering triggered by dried DI water slurry residue and silicon swarf deposits adhering to the kerf channel, skewing automated binning and artificially degrading wafer sort yield.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-1-01` | **Automated Kerf Width Uniformity & Street Centering Metrology** | Automated High-Resolution Line-Scan AOI Metrology Tool equipped with 12k TDI CMOS Sensor, 0.35 um/pixel optical resolution, motorized 300mm vacuum chuck, and dual Coaxial/Darkfield LED Ring Illuminators. | 1. Load film frame onto motorized AOI vacuum chuck and align wafer using notch and outer DRAM scribe alignment targets. 2. Execute full-frame continuous serpentine TDI line-scan along horizontal (X) and vertical (Y) dicing streets at 45 mm/s. 3. Segment blade cut channel boundaries using adaptive edge-detection filtering across 500 equidistant sampling points per dicing street. 4. Calculate absolute kerf width, kerf centerline deviation relative to nominal street center, and kerf edge raggedness index. | `Kerf cut width must measure 42.0 um ± 3.5 um across 100% of measured streets; centerline offset from street axis must be <= 5.0 um; edge roughness (3-sigma standard deviation) must remain <= 2.2 um.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-1-02` | **Frontside Edge Chipping & Micro-Crack Encroachment Defect Classification** | High-Magnification Optical Metrology Inspection System with 10X/20X Plan Apo objectives, multi-angle oblique darkfield illumination, and integrated SEMI G85 wafer map export engine. | 1. Position high-magnification optical head to inspect all individual die perimeters and die corners across the wafer. 2. Capture multi-focus Z-stack images at 15 mm/s across each die perimeter under 460nm darkfield illumination to highlight scattering at chip fractures. 3. Extract maximum penetration depth (D_chip) of every edge chip measured perpendicularly from the diced silicon edge toward the die center. 4. Measure minimum clearance distance between the apex of the chip/crack tip and the outermost seal ring metal-dielectric boundary. 5. Log defect coordinates, bin classifications, and generate updated wafer sort map. | `Maximum chipping depth into silicon street must be <= 20.0 um; distance from chip tip to outer active seal ring must be >= 18.0 um across 100% of inspected die; zero die permitted with micro-cracks penetrating the seal ring boundary.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and laser safety eyewear for high-intensity inspection illuminators, Cleanroom antistatic ESD smock, conductive hood, and grounded ESD wrist/heel straps, Cleanroom face mask (3-ply polypropylene particle filtration)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with IPA lens cleaning agent, flush skin with copious amounts of DI water for at least 15 minutes. In case of vapor inhalation causing dizziness, move individual immediately to fresh air; provide oxygen if breathing is labored. For eye contamination, flush eyes at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open and seek prompt ophthalmologic evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: AOI inspection enclosure must maintain local laminar ISO Class 5 HEPA downflow (0.45 m/s ± 20%) with dedicated tool exhaust port venting VOC solvent cleaning vapors at minimum 50 CFM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA solvent wipes and cleaning residues must be segregated into designated airtight, grounded hazardous solvent waste receptacles. Spent rinse fluid must drain directly into the fab acid-solvent neutralization and reclamation facility; no uncontrolled drain disposal permitted.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DI Water)** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-Pure Water (ASTM Type E-1, 18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Singulated wafer on expanded UV dicing frame; street kerfs washed free of silicon dicing slurry, surface spin-dried, with native oxide and passivated nitride/polyimide topcoat intact.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Inspected, defect-mapped, and verified clean wafer frame ready for UV curing release and automated die pick-and-place into carrier tape or gel pack.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding allowable queue time in ambient cleanroom air causes airborne molecular contamination (AMC) organic deposition and moisture absorption into micro-fractures, precipitating latent sub-critical crack propagation and reducing UV tape debonding efficiency.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> 100% automated optical inspection and automated defect classification (ADC) completed for diced 180nm DRAM wafer. Kerf width, street centering, edge chipping dimensions, and seal-ring clearance are validated against semiconductor packaging design rules, with defective die classified and mapped into a standardized SEMI G85 format ready for high-speed pick-and-place sort.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WAFER_DICING_AOI_METROLOGY_REPORT_LOT01.csv`
- [ ] `SEMI_G85_SORT_WAFER_MAP_LOT01.xml`
- [ ] `HIGH_RES_KERF_CHIPPING_DEFECT_ATLAS_LOT01.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean dicing kerf width across all horizontal and vertical dicing streets** | `42.0 um` | ±3.0 um | Automated TDI optical line-scan image analysis across 500 edge-segmented measurement sites per street |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum allowable lateral chipping encroachment from diced silicon edge** | `15.0 um` | +5.0 um / -15.0 um | Calibrated 20X high-magnification darkfield optical edge metrology relative to design database GDSII boundary |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Minimum clearance distance between micro-crack/chip apex and DRAM seal ring boundary** | `20.0 um` | >= 18.0 um minimum threshold | Multi-focus Z-stack brightfield/darkfield feature extraction software |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Inspection of 100% of die sites across the entire diced wafer frame completed; zero critical unmapped defect escapes; SEMI G85 wafer map validated with 100% die coordinate checksum match; lead metrology engineer and packaging QA manager co-signoff recorded in MES.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## AOI High-Resolution Telecentric Optics Calibration & Dicing Film Frame Fixturing Setup

**Module:** BEOL Packaging, Assembly & Metrology — 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Process Step:** Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) Hardware Calibration & Frame Fixturing  
**Knowledge Record:** [aoi_telecentric_optics_calibration.md](./docs/knowledge/aoi_telecentric_optics_calibration.md)

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Film Frame Alignment  │
│     & Vacuum Lock      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Z-Stage Telecentric   │
│   Focus Calibration    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Spatial Distortion &  │
│     Pixel Scaling      │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Multi-Angle       │
│      Darkfield /       │
│      Brightfield       │
│  Illumination Balance  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Sub-Pixel Kerf Edge   │
│   Detection Baseline   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Dicing Film Frame Fixturing & Vacuum Clamping:**
   - Load the diced wafer mounted on dicing tape within the standardized metal film frame onto the AOI inspection chuck.
   - Engage multi-zone vacuum retention to secure the tape flat against the chuck, suppressing vertical tape wrinkles and z-bowing.
   - Ensure the alignment pins mate positively with the film frame orientation notches to constrain angular theta tilt ($\theta < 0.05^\circ$).

2. **Z-Stage Telecentric Optical Alignment & Depth of Focus Baseline:**
   - Initialize the bilateral telecentric objective lens assembly over the optical calibration target standard.
   - Adjust the motorized Z-stage autofocusing system across the wafer plane to ensure the operational focal window stays centered within the process depth of focus limit ($DOF \ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$, verified from $DOF = k_2 \cdot \lambda / NA^2$).
   - Verify constant image magnification across vertical focus travel of $\pm 0.25\ \mu\text{m}$ to prevent dimensional measurement skew from dicing tape deflection.

3. **Spatial Pixel Scaling & Distortion Calibration:**
   - Align the optics to an ultra-precise optical calibration grid standard with physical reference marks matching the foundry manufacturing grid resolution ($0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ / $5\text{ nm}$).
   - Execute a multi-point spatial calibration across the full field-of-view (FOV); calibrate effective optical resolution down to the optical resolving threshold ($R = 152\text{ nm}$, based on Rayleigh criteria $R = k_1 \cdot \lambda / NA$).
   - Compute and apply sub-pixel optical distortion correction mapping matrices to ensure lateral geometric fidelity across the sensor array.

4. **Illumination Balancing & Contrast Standardization:**
   - Calibrate coaxial brightfield and multi-angle low-incidence darkfield LED ring illuminators against a calibrated diffuse reflectance reference target.
   - Balance illumination intensity to establish high-contrast edge discrimination between the silicon substrate, dicing kerf channel, metal seal rings, and poly/dielectric passivation boundaries.

5. **Sub-Pixel Kerf Edge & Defect Metrology Zeroing:**
   - Traverse the stage across kerf test lines along both orthogonal dicing axes ($X$ and $Y$).
   - Calibrate the edge-detection algorithm baseline using a calibrated test kerf to ensure repeat measurements of kerf width, silicon breakout chipping, and micro-cracks conform to PDK overlay budget limits ($\le 35\text{ nm}$).

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                  AOI Metrology Target Limits (nm)      
             ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
             │░░░░                                     │
Overlay Error┤░░░░                                     │
             │▒                                        │
   Stage Grid┤▒                                        │
   DOF Margin┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
             │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
 Resolution R┤█████████████                            │
             │█████████████                            │
             └┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬┘
              0        125       250       375      500 
```

1. **Optical Half-Pitch Resolution ($R$):**
   - **Target Metric:** Minimum resolvable optical half-pitch $\le 152\text{ nm}$ ($0.152\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - **Measurement:** Contrast transfer verification across calibrated line-pair target with $\lambda = 248\text{ nm}$, $NA = 0.65$, $k_1 = 0.40$.

2. **Optical Depth of Focus ($DOF$):**
   - **Target Metric:** Process optical focus depth margin $\ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ ($500\text{ nm}$).
   - **Measurement:** Z-stack telecentric MTF evaluation maintaining constant magnification across $\ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ vertical range ($DOF = k_2 \cdot \lambda / NA^2 \ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$).

3. **Stage Coordinate Grid Resolution:**
   - **Target Metric:** Stage positioning and measurement grid stepping resolution $= 0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).
   - **Measurement:** Laser interferometer stage encoder verification calibrated against the foundry physical placement grid.

4. **Metrology Overlay & Kerf Alignment Error:**
   - **Target Metric:** Maximum permissible overlay error $\le 35\text{ nm}$.
   - **Measurement:** Statistical die-to-kerf reference edge displacement across automated step-and-repeat scans.

---

### Source Citations
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**:
  - *Manufacturing Grid:* $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).
  - *Rayleigh Resolution Criteria:* $R = k_1 \cdot (\lambda / NA) = 152\text{ nm}$ with $\lambda = 248\text{ nm}$, $NA = 0.65$, $k_1 = 0.40$.
  - *Depth of Focus:* $DOF = k_2 \cdot (\lambda / NA^2) \ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$.
  - *Overlay Error Budget:* Maximum permissible overlay error $\le 35\text{ nm}$.
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
  - Optical modeling and automated wafer mapping for thin film reflectivity, refractive dispersion, and surface planarization uniformity.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |

Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

**Exit Objective Summary**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Kerf Profile & Multi-Threshold Edge-Detection Defect Metrology Algorithm Recipe Optimization

- **Document Reference**: [sop_kerf_profile_defect_metrology.md](./docs/sop_kerf_profile_defect_metrology.md)
- **Hierarchy Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Packaging & Assembly > Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) > Kerf Profile & Multi-Threshold Edge-Detection Defect Metrology Algorithm Recipe Optimization
- **Technology Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm / SkyWater SKY130 compatible)
- **Action Type**: Make

---

### Process Flow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Wafer Load &      │
│   Fiducial Alignment   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Multi-Wavelength    │
│   Brightfield / DUV    │
│          Scan          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Kernel Convolution &  │
│     Gradient Edge      │
│       Extraction       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        Adaptive        │
│  Multi-Threshold Kerf  │
│      Segmentation      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Sub-Pixel Metric &   │
│        Chipping        │
│     Quantification     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Automated Binning &   │
│    PnP Feedforward     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Substrate Vacuum Clamping & Global Fiducial Pattern Alignment**:
   - Secure the tape-mounted, thinned wafer (post-diamond saw dicing) on the motorized theta-X-Y chuck under vacuum suction $\ge 75\text{ kPa}$.
   - Perform coordinate system registration using peripheral alignment fiducials matching the physical placement grid resolution of **$0.005\text{ µm}$ ($5\text{ nm}$)**.
   - Adjust theta tilt such that angular misalignment along the dicing channel street axis is $\le \pm 0.002^\circ$.

2. **Optical Train & Illumination Balancing**:
   - Initialize high-resolution DUV / i-line dual-band optics ($\lambda_1 = 248\text{ nm}$ KrF excimer source, $\lambda_2 = 365\text{ nm}$ i-line) with numerical aperture $\text{NA} = 0.65$ capable of resolving sub-micron defects down to $R = k_1 \cdot (\lambda / \text{NA}) = 0.40 \cdot (248 / 0.65) = 152\text{ nm}$.
   - Calibrate autofocus Z-axis tracking within the optical Depth of Focus window ($\text{DOF} = k_2 \cdot (\lambda / \text{NA}^2) \ge 0.5\text{ µm}$) to accommodate post-dicing trench topography.
   - Normalize reflection intensity baselines across silicon substrate and oxide/nitride passivation interfaces using Fresnel reflection coefficient principles $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$.

3. **Multi-Threshold Convolution & Dynamic Kerf Edge Detection**:
   - Execute a $5 \times 5$ Gaussian smoothing filter ($\sigma = 1.0$) followed by dual-kernel Sobel directional edge gradient filtering ($G = \sqrt{G_x^2 + G_y^2}$).
   - Segment image into 3 optical domains via dynamic multi-thresholding:
     - **$T_1$ (Street Center / Tape Trench)**: Low-reflectance threshold calibrated to dicing trench floor ($I < 0.25 I_{\text{max}}$).
     - **$T_2$ (Chipping & Delamination Fringe)**: Intermediate reflectance threshold detecting micro-fractures into the die-seal margin ($0.25 I_{\text{max}} \le I \le 0.65 I_{\text{max}}$).
     - **$T_3$ (Active Die & Seal Ring Passivation)**: High-reflectance threshold defining undamaged die edge boundary ($I > 0.65 I_{\text{max}}$).
   - Apply sub-pixel zero-crossing interpolation on the edge gradient profile down to the $0.005\text{ µm}$ ($5\text{ nm}$) manufacturing grid resolution.

4. **Kerf Profile Metrology & Die Chipping Quantification**:
   - Measure bilateral kerf width $W_k$ at $10\text{ µm}$ pitch intervals along horizontal and vertical dicing scribe lanes.
   - Calculate maximum chipping encroachment $\Delta X_{\text{chip}}$ perpendicular to the nominal cut line toward the active die seal ring.
   - Verify that micro-fractures maintain clearance from active circuitry: minimum active diffusion width boundary ($0.15\text{ µm}$) and Metal 1 pitch boundary ($0.34\text{ µm}$).

5. **Defect Binning & SECS/GEM Pick-and-Place Mapping**:
   - Flag dies as non-conforming if:
     - Chipping protrusion exceeds $\Delta X_{\text{chip}} > 10.0\text{ µm}$.
     - Kerf width deviation $|\Delta W_k| > 5.0\text{ µm}$ from nominal blade cut profile ($35.0\text{ µm}$).
     - Crack propagation breaches the die seal ring toward the active core ($< 0.15\text{ µm}$ safety margin).
   - Export classified defect map via SECS/GEM protocol to the downstream Pick-and-Place sorter.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

