```text
                          │░                           │
Inspection Grid Resolution┤░                           │
                          │▒▒                          │
    Edge Roughness 3-Sigma┤▒▒                          │
       Chipping Max Extent┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                   │
                          │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                   │
         Dicing Kerf Width┤████████████████████████████│
                          │████████████████████████████│
                          └┬──────┬──────┬─────┬──────┬┘
                          0.0    8.8   17.5  26.2  35.0 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Method | Literature Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Physical Inspection Grid Resolution** | $\le 0.005$ | $\mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$) | Sub-pixel stage coordinate registration | SkyWater SKY130 PDK Grid |
| **Minimum Resolvable Defect Feature Size** | $\le 152$ | $\text{nm}$ ($0.152\ \mu\text{m}$) | Rayleigh optical resolution test ($k_1=0.40, \lambda=248\text{ nm}, \text{NA}=0.65$) | SkyWater SKY130 Lithography / Rayleigh |
| **Depth of Focus Window (Topography)** | $\ge 0.5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical Z-scan across diced kerf trench | SkyWater SKY130 Rayleigh Criteria |
| **Chipping Encroachment Limit** | $\le 10.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Multi-threshold AOI edge segmentation | Packaging & Assembly Scribe Margin |
| **Nominal Dicing Kerf Width Window** | $35.0 \pm 5.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Continuous line scan profiling | Saw Dicing Process Recipe |

---

### Verified Context Citations
1. **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**:
   - Physical placement grid resolution: $0.005\text{ µm}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).
   - Rayleigh Criteria resolution limit: $R = k_1 \cdot (\lambda / \text{NA}) = 0.40 \cdot (248\text{ nm} / 0.65) = 152\text{ nm}$.
   - Depth of focus limit: $\text{DOF} = k_2 \cdot (\lambda / \text{NA}^2) \ge 0.5\text{ µm}$.
   - Circuit design references: Minimum active diffusion width ($0.15\text{ µm}$), minimum poly gate length ($0.15\text{ µm}$ / $150\text{ nm}$), minimum metal 1 pitch ($0.34\text{ µm}$), poly-to-active overlay error budget ($\le 35\text{ nm}$).
2. **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
   - Complex reflection ratio: $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$ for thin film and interface reflectance calibration across silicon and passivation boundaries.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) multi-threshold edge-detection algorithms must dynamically compensate for saw kerf sidewall tilt and surface reflectivity shifts caused by diamond blade binder degradation and silicon grain variation. A rigid single-threshold segmentation fails under optical dispersion from silicon slurry residue, leading to kerf width overestimation (>2.5 µm error) and false positive micro-crack calls. Dynamic illumination normalization (combining coaxial brightfield and low-angle darkfield LED arrays) must be integrated directly into the image processing pipeline to decouple surface roughness noise from genuine structural chippings.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm CMOS/DRAM interface, dicing-induced micro-cracks penetrating the seal ring or crack arrest structures represent fatal reliability hazards due to moisture ingress and interlayer dielectric (ILD) delamination. The multi-threshold edge-detection recipe must employ Canny-Sobel hybrid gradient filtering coupled with morphological closing to resolve sub-pixel edge transitions at 0.05 µm/pixel resolution. In particular, chipping intrusion into the active die region exceeding 15 µm from the dicing street center must trigger automated binning rejection, separating cosmetic topside silicon spalling from catastrophic crystalline cleavage.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Optical defect classification recipes must not become a bottleneck for downstream die sort pick-and-place throughput. Overly conservative edge-detection kernels that trigger high false-reject rates (>0.8%) will prematurely deplete available 180nm MPW silicon dies and inflate packaging yields costs. Calibration reference targets (NIST-traceable chrome-on-quartz optical reticles) and high-NA optical lenses must be dual-sourced to avoid AOI tool recipe drift and single-vendor lock-in during multi-site assembly ramp.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Algorithm recipe tuning and defect classification library signoff must fit within the strict 72-hour window post-wafer dicing before dicing tape adhesive relaxation and plastic tape shrinkage distort die-to-die street spacing. Tool inspection recipe files, defect review runtimes (target <180 ms/die), and golden reference templates must be version-controlled and verified against manual confocal/SEM validation before advancing the lot to high-speed die bonder pick-and-place.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Sub-threshold crack underdetection: Micro-cracks propagating beneath the polyimide passivation or inter-metal dielectric (IMD) layers escape darkfield edge-detection due to shadow masking from topside metal seal rings.
1. Silicon slurry ghost chipping: Dried colloidal silica or deionized water drying stains along the kerf margin cause localized intensity gradients that trigger false chipping defect calls, causing erroneous yield loss.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-1-2-01` | **Kerf Width Measurement Accuracy & Repeatability Verification** | High-Resolution Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) System equipped with 0.8 NA 50x Telecentric Lens, Dual-Channel Darkfield/Brightfield LED Illuminator, and NIST-Traceable Calibration Target (Model KR-850) | 1. Load NIST-traceable calibration reticle, execute automated autofocus and brightness auto-calibration across 9 field points. 2. Load diced 180nm DRAM qualification wafer onto the motorized vacuum chuck. 3. Execute the Multi-Threshold Edge-Detection Kerf Metrology Recipe across 50 randomly sampled dicing street intersections (X and Y orientations). 4. Record automated kerf width measurements across 3 consecutive inspection runs without unchucking the wafer. 5. Benchmark automated measurement values against manual calibrated cross-sectional optical microscope ground truth. | `Kerf width measurement mean absolute error (MAE) <= 0.50 µm compared to NIST-traceable optical standard; static measurement gauge repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) <= 8.0%; 3-sigma measurement variation across 3 repeated cycles <= 0.35 µm.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-1-2-02` | **Chipping and Micro-Crack Multi-Threshold Detection Sensitivity & False Alarm Audit** | Automated Optical Defect Metrology Station with High-Speed TDI Line-Scan Camera (16k resolution), High-Angle Coaxial Brightfield / Low-Angle Darkfield Lighting, and Offline Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) for defect review | 1. Scan entire 8-inch diced DRAM wafer using the Multi-Threshold Edge-Detection recipe at 0.1 µm spatial pixel resolution. 2. Extract coordinates for all flagged kerf anomalies: Topside Chipping (>10 µm size), Sidewall Micro-Cracks, and Kerf Deviation (>5 µm lateral offset). 3. Re-scan the wafer using 100% manual review mode on a high-resolution SEM/Confocal microscope for all identified defect sites plus 100 randomly sampled 'clean' sites. 4. Calculate Defect Capture Rate (Sensitivity) for actual chippings >= 15 µm and False Alarm Rate across defect-free street boundaries. | `Defect Capture Rate (Sensitivity) >= 99.5% for all chipping intrusions >= 15.0 µm; sub-surface crack detection probability >= 95.0% for cracks > 20.0 µm length; False Reject / False Alarm Rate <= 0.50% across verified defect-free kerf segments.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/ISO 5 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, static dissipative), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and conductive ESD booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with optical lens cleaning solution (IPA), flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes. For skin contact, wash thoroughly with soap and water; replace contaminated PPE. If vapors cause dizziness, evacuate operator to a fresh air cleanroom plenum.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom laminar airflow (Class 100 / ISO 5) with dedicated point-of-use HEPA filtration and mini-environment enclosure exhausted at minimum 50 CFM face velocity to prevent VOC buildup during manual optical calibration wiping.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA-wetted optical lens lint-free wipes must be deposited into dedicated, grounded, fire-rated flammables disposal containers with self-closing lids, collected for licensed solvent incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Electronic Grade (>=99.9%) | `70% in Deionized Water` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `180 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-saw rinsed, blow-dried diced wafer mounted on UV/dicing tape frame, free of standing DI water droplets and silicon slurry residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: 100% optically mapped, defect-classified diced wafer ready for automated die pick-and-place sort, with defect coordinate map synced to manufacturing execution system (MES).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time causes dicing frame tape stress relaxation, adhesive migration onto die edges, and atmospheric oxidation/corrosion of exposed Al-Cu/Cu bond pads, rendering automated optical recognition and pick-and-place vision tracking inaccurate.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable signoff of the optimized Multi-Threshold Edge-Detection Defect Metrology Algorithm Recipe for 180nm DRAM wafer dicing. The algorithm delivers sub-pixel edge detection resolving kerf profile boundaries and distinguishing silicon spalling from structural seal ring cracks with a false alarm rate under 0.5%.

- [ ] `KERF_PROFILE_VALIDATION_REPORT.pdf`

critics.systems_engineer: Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) multi-threshold edge-detection algorithms must dynamically compensate for saw kerf sidewall tilt and surface reflectivity shifts caused by diamond blade binder degradation and silicon grain variation. A rigid single-threshold segmentation fails under optical dispersion from silicon slurry residue, leading to kerf width overestimation (>2.5 µm error) and false positive micro-crack calls. Dynamic illumination normalization (combining coaxial brightfield and low-angle darkfield LED arrays) must be integrated directly into the image processing pipeline to decouple surface roughness noise from genuine structural chippings.
critics.domain_expert: At the 180nm CMOS/DRAM interface, dicing-induced micro-cracks penetrating the seal ring or crack arrest structures represent fatal reliability hazards due to moisture ingress and interlayer dielectric (ILD) delamination. The multi-threshold edge-detection recipe must employ Canny-Sobel hybrid gradient filtering coupled with morphological closing to resolve sub-pixel edge transitions at 0.05 µm/pixel resolution. In particular, chipping intrusion into the active die region exceeding 15 µm from the dicing street center must trigger automated binning rejection, separating cosmetic topside silicon spalling from catastrophic crystalline cleavage.
critics.supply_chain: Optical defect classification recipes must not become a bottleneck for downstream die sort pick-and-place throughput. Overly conservative edge-detection kernels that trigger high false-reject rates (>0.8%) will prematurely deplete available 180nm MPW silicon dies and inflate packaging yields costs. Calibration reference targets (NIST-traceable chrome-on-quartz optical reticles) and high-NA optical lenses must be dual-sourced to avoid AOI tool recipe drift and single-vendor lock-in during multi-site assembly ramp.
critics.laya_pm: Algorithm recipe tuning and defect classification library signoff must fit within the strict 72-hour window post-wafer dicing before dicing tape adhesive relaxation and plastic tape shrinkage distort die-to-die street spacing. Tool inspection recipe files, defect review runtimes (target <180 ms/die), and golden reference templates must be version-controlled and verified against manual confocal/SEM validation before advancing the lot to high-speed die bonder pick-and-place.
critical_failure_modes: Sub-threshold crack underdetection: Micro-cracks propagating beneath the polyimide passivation or inter-metal dielectric (IMD) layers escape darkfield edge-detection due to shadow masking from topside metal seal rings.

Silicon slurry ghost chipping: Dried colloidal silica or deionized water drying stains along the kerf margin cause localized intensity gradients that trigger false chipping defect calls, causing erroneous yield loss.

testcases.title: Kerf Width Measurement Accuracy & Repeatability Verification
testcases.instrumentation: High-Resolution Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) System equipped with 0.8 NA 50x Telecentric Lens, Dual-Channel Darkfield/Brightfield LED Illuminator, and NIST-Traceable Calibration Target (Model KR-850)
testcases.pre_conditions: AOI tool optical magnification calibrated to 0.050 µm/pixel; calibration reticle verified with residual scale error <0.02 µm; 180nm DRAM diced test wafer mounted on 8-inch UV dicing tape under tension.
testcases.procedure:
1. Load NIST-traceable calibration reticle, execute automated autofocus and brightness auto-calibration across 9 field points.
2. Load diced 180nm DRAM qualification wafer onto the motorized vacuum chuck.
3. Execute the Multi-Threshold Edge-Detection Kerf Metrology Recipe across 50 randomly sampled dicing street intersections (X and Y orientations).
4. Record automated kerf width measurements across 3 consecutive inspection runs without unchucking the wafer.
5. Benchmark automated measurement values against manual calibrated cross-sectional optical microscope ground truth.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Kerf width measurement mean absolute error (MAE) <= 0.50 µm compared to NIST-traceable optical standard; static measurement gauge repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) <= 8.0%; 3-sigma measurement variation across 3 repeated cycles <= 0.35 µm.

testcases.title: Chipping and Micro-Crack Multi-Threshold Detection Sensitivity & False Alarm Audit
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Optical Defect Metrology Station with High-Speed TDI Line-Scan Camera (16k resolution), High-Angle Coaxial Brightfield / Low-Angle Darkfield Lighting, and Offline Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) for defect review
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer diced under standard production diamond saw parameters (spindle speed 30,000 RPM, feed rate 30 mm/s); deionized water rinse and air knife dry completed; defect classification threshold recipe v1.3 loaded.
testcases.procedure:
1. Scan entire 8-inch diced DRAM wafer using the Multi-Threshold Edge-Detection recipe at 0.1 µm spatial pixel resolution.
2. Extract coordinates for all flagged kerf anomalies: Topside Chipping (>10 µm size), Sidewall Micro-Cracks, and Kerf Deviation (>5 µm lateral offset).
3. Re-scan the wafer using 100% manual review mode on a high-resolution SEM/Confocal microscope for all identified defect sites plus 100 randomly sampled 'clean' sites.
4. Calculate Defect Capture Rate (Sensitivity) for actual chippings >= 15 µm and False Alarm Rate across defect-free street boundaries.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Defect Capture Rate (Sensitivity) >= 99.5% for all chipping intrusions >= 15.0 µm; sub-surface crack detection probability >= 95.0% for cracks > 20.0 µm length; False Reject / False Alarm Rate <= 0.50% across verified defect-free kerf segments.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Full-Wafer Dicing Street Scan, Die Chipping Quantification & Electronic Wafer Map Binning

### 1. Process Overview & Workflow
This leaf SOP governs automated optical inspection (AOI) across post-saw dicing streets on expanded dicing tape frames for the **180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)**. It quantifies mechanical kerf width deviation, topside silicon chipping encroachment relative to the die seal ring and active circuitry, and outputs an updated electronic wafer map (SEMI G85 / SECS-GEM XML) directly to pick-and-place die sorters.

```text
┌─────────────────────────┐
│                         │
│    Wafer Film Frame     │
│    Mount & Alignment    │
│                         │
└────────────┬────────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐
│                         │
│  Brightfield/Darkfield  │
│   Dicing Street Scan    │
│                         │
└────────────┬────────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐
│                         │
│    Kerf Deviation &     │
│        Chipping         │
│     Quantification      │
│                         │
└────────────┬────────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐
│                         │
│    SECS/GEM XML/SEMI    │
│   G85 Bin Assignment    │
│                         │
└────────────┬────────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐
│                         │
│   Pick-and-Place Feed   │
│         Forward         │
│                         │
└─────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Film Frame Loading & Vacuum Chuck Clamping**:
   - Transfer the dicing cassette film frame holding the thinned wafer onto the automated AOI chuck stage. Apply a uniform vacuum level of $\ge -75\text{ kPa}$ across the porous ceramic stage to eliminate film wrinkles and topography flutter.
2. **Global Fiducial Registration & Grid Coordinate Origin**:
   - Align wafer notch/edge orientation using an automated pattern-recognition camera.
   - Detect 4 global corner fiducials and register against the CAD kerf street coordinate database, matching the foundry design grid resolution of $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).
3. **High-Speed Telecentric Scan & Dual Illumination**:
   - Execute a serpentine continuous raster scan along all horizontal ($X$) and vertical ($Y$) dicing streets using a continuous line-scan / TDI (Time Delay Integration) sensor with $0.5\ \mu\text{m/pixel}$ optical resolution.
   - Synchronize coaxial brightfield illumination (for metallization and seal ring boundaries) with high-angle darkfield oblique LED ring illumination (to resolve silicon micro-fractures, edge spalling, and sub-surface chipping steps).
4. **Kerf Profile & Chipping Metric Quantification**:
   - Extract kerf edges using edge-detection algorithms referenced to the nominal $35.0\ \mu\text{m}$ dicing blade path.
   - Measure the lateral excursion of silicon chipping along both die sides relative to the outer edge of the die seal ring (guard ring protection boundary).
   - Detect and flag any directional cracking extending through dielectric passivation or toward active bitline/wordline array boundaries.
5. **Defect Bin Classification & Wafer Map Update**:
   - Ingest baseline wafer probe test maps (CP1/CP2 electrical sort).
   - Classify dies exceeding chipping or kerf encroachment limits as **Bin 7 (Mechanical Chipping / Visual Defect)**.
   - Formulate and serialize the updated wafer map compliant with **SEMI G85** (XML / SECS-GEM format), archiving raw coordinates and defect images to the shop-floor MES server for downstream pick-and-place sort gating.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                                                        
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                        │                              │
      SEMI G85 Bin Error┤                              │
                        │                              │
  Side Crack Propagation┤                              │
Kerf Street Center Drift┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                     │
                        │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                     │
     Max Chipping Extent┤██████████████████████████████│
                        │██████████████████████████████│
                        └┬──────┬───────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                         0      3       6      9     12 
```

| Acceptance Metric | Target Specification | Measurement Unit | Inspection Tool / Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Maximum Topside Chipping Extent** | $\le 12.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | High-resolution AOI edge-to-peak defect measurement (clearance $> 15.0\ \mu\text{m}$ to active seal ring) |
| **Kerf Centerline Tracking Drift** | $\le 3.5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Full-wafer dicing street trajectory regression against CAD grid coordinates |
| **Crack Propagation to Active Circuitry** | $0$ (Zero Tolerance) | Defect Count | Darkfield oblique optical scan & micro-cleavage edge inspection |
| **SEMI G85 Wafer Map Serialization Error** | $0$ (100% matched die index) | Mismatch Count | Automated schema validation check (SECS-GEM / SEMI G85 XML vs physical die pitch) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**:
  - Manufacturing placement grid resolution is strictly maintained at $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$) for precise wafer map coordinate registration and die boundary definition. Minimum metal and contact dimensions establish guard boundary constraints against dicing-induced micro-fractures.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Preserves cell capacitance ($\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$) and leakage requirements ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$) by enforcing complete mechanical isolation and crack containment outward of the folded bitline memory array perimeter and seal ring.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - Dicing street clearance prevents delamination or stress-induced cracking into the $3.5\text{ nm}$ gate oxide and stacked capacitor dielectric layers ($3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$ EOT), eliminating retention degradation beyond the required $64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---
*Captured micro-knowledge has been persisted to [docs/knowledge/aoi_dicing_street_scan_and_binning.md](./docs/knowledge/aoi_dicing_street_scan_and_binning.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated dicing street optical scanning at 180nm BEOL must seamlessly link high-resolution line-scan/area-scan CMOS imaging data with SEMI G85-compliant electronic wafer maps (SECS/GEM-compatible XML/KLARF) without incurring data pipeline bottlenecks or spatial coordinate drift across 200mm/300mm wafer stages.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Topside die chipping along the diamond saw kerf must not breach the seal ring boundary (<15 µm penetration from kerf cut edge into active die periphery), and backside microcracks exceeding 25 µm depth must trigger automated binning rejection to prevent package stress-induced die delamination during DRAM thermal cycling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Inspection throughput must match or exceed the upstream high-speed diamond saw dicing and UV tape expansion indexers; any defect-scoring bottleneck or proprietary wafer-map encoding will throttle downstream pick-and-place sorters (e.g., Besi/Datacon) and increase Work-In-Progress (WIP) holding costs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Clear visual defect classification models must be calibrated against golden ground-truth dies to eliminate false kills (>0.15% scrap rate of functional DRAM dies) and avoid wafer-level yield discrepancies between automated optical inspection (AOI) scoring and electrical wafer sort (CP) results.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Kerf edge chipping propagation across the moisture seal ring causing long-term DRAM bit retention failure and sense-amp leakage.
1. Electronic wafer map spatial inversion or coordinate misalignment between the AOI inspection tool and downstream automated die pick-and-place equipment leading to package assembly of chipped/defective die.
1. UV dicing tape relaxation or micro-shift during extended optical inspection scan causing optical defocus and false-positive kerf breach classifications.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-1-3-01` | **Automated Kerf Width and Topside Chipping Quantification Test** | Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) Wafer Inspection System equipped with high-resolution TDI/CMOS telecentric line-scan camera, sub-micron motorized XY linear air-bearing stage, and automated image processing algorithm. | 1. Load wafer ring onto automated vacuum chuck and acquire global fiducial alignment marks. 2. Execute automated 100% full-wafer serpentine scan of all dicing streets (horizontal and vertical kerfs) at 0.5 um/pixel optical resolution. 3. Run automated image edge-detection algorithm to extract kerf centerline, cut width, and maximum topside chipping length/depth relative to seal ring margin across all dies. 4. Aggregate defect coordinates and generate defect overlay map. | `Maximum topside chipping depth into the street margin must be <= 12.0 µm (with absolute exclusion zone > 8.0 µm away from the seal ring outer edge); kerf width variation across the entire wafer must remain within 45.0 µm +/- 4.0 µm.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-1-3-02` | **SEMI G85 Electronic Wafer Map Binning and Coordinate Verification** | SECS/GEM Host Controller Interface, Automated Die Sorter / Pick-and-Place Simulator with wafer map parsing software, calibrated optical verification reticle. | 1. Run binning translation algorithm classifying dies into Bin 1 (Good Die - Zero Critical Chipping), Bin 7 (Kerf Chipping Reject), Bin 8 (Crack/Corner Defect Reject), and Bin 9 (Saw Cut Inactive Margin Breach). 2. Export SEMI G85 electronic wafer map file. 3. Ingest generated map file into pick-and-place simulator and perform coordinate cross-registration against physical wafer fiducial coordinates at 20 randomly sampled die locations across center, mid-radius, and edge. 4. Verify 1:1 binning match between AOI defect coordinates and sorter target bin selection. | `Wafer map coordinate translation error must be 0.0 µm (100% exact die row/column matching); binning translation consistency must be 100.0% with zero misclassified or shifted die positions across all inspectable sites.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000 Cleanroom Bunny Suit, ESD-safe Nitrile Gloves, ANSI Z87.1 Approved Safety Glasses, Cleanroom Static-Dissipative Booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye exposure to isopropyl alcohol wiping solvent: flush immediately with copious clean water or eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, move individual to fresh cleanroom air supply.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom laminar airflow (Class 100/ISO Class 5 mini-environment inside inspection enclosure); dedicated tool local exhaust for solvent wipe vapors at 50 CFM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-contaminated cleanroom wipes in designated grounded, flame-retardant hazardous chemical waste receptacles; zero bulk liquid chemical discharge generated during dry optical inspection.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Cleanroom Wipes)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C12) | `70% in DI Water` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge/Dry)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.5 | `99.9995%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `180 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Diced 180nm DRAM wafer on UV release tape, DI water rinsed, spin-dried, free of macroscopic saw silicon slurry residue, mounted on tensioned metal wafer frame.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: 100% optically inspected and classified wafer, defect log and SEMI G85 electronic wafer map generated, packaged in anti-static cassette sealed under N2 purge ready for UV tape curing and die attach.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended atmospheric exposure causes airborne organic contamination and moisture condensation in kerf micro-fissures, inducing corrosion of exposed peripheral aluminum bond pad metallization and adhesion degradation of the UV dicing tape.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> 100% automated optical dicing street and kerf scan completed across all reticle fields of the 180nm DRAM wafer, establishing quantitative chipping depth distributions, classifying all edge/kerf anomalies, and generating a verified SEMI G85 electronic wafer map for automated pick-and-place die sorting.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WAFER_DICING_INSPECTION_METROLOGY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `DIE_CHIPPING_AND_KERF_STATS.csv`
- [ ] `ELECTRONIC_WAFER_MAP_SEMI_G85.xml`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum allowable kerf edge chipping penetration into street safety margin** | `10.0 µm` | +/- 2.0 µm | Calibrated optical line-scan sub-pixel edge detection metrology |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total electronic wafer map die coordinate translation fidelity and binning accuracy** | `100.0%` | 0.0% | Automated cross-check between AOI defect image coordinates and SECS/GEM host map bin register |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Inspection metrology report approved by Packaging Quality Engineering showing 100% dicing street coverage, zero unmapped dies, electronic wafer map validation checksum matching SECS/GEM host upload, and all dies categorized with deterministic binning assignments.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Wafer Map Coordinate Translation & Die Binning Recipe Setup

**Category**: Packaging | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Coordinate system parity failure between CP (Circuit Probe) ATE test origin (typically notch/flat-down, upper-left or center-die reference) and automated high-speed die-sorter vision chuck (often inverted Y-axis, notch-relative polar/Cartesian transformation) risks off-by-one die indexing. If the wafer map rotation matrix (0°, 90°, 180°, or 270°) and mirror axis (flip-X/flip-Y due to backside tape mounting on dicing frame) are not mathematically synchronized across SEMI E142 and SECS/GEM formats, known bad dies (KBD) will be picked into qualified package cavities.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Post-dicing kerf expansion and tape stretching induce non-linear cumulative mechanical pitch distortion (nominal pitch 180nm DRAM die step size +/- kerf width). A static Cartesian step-and-repeat coordinate map will fail pattern-matching optical recognition near wafer edge regions. The translation recipe must enforce dynamic optical fiducial alignment using local die-corner coordinates and global wafer alignment marks (WEC-referenced from photolithography) rather than blind encoder interpolation across expanded UV dicing tape.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Incompatible wafer map serialization between foundry fab sortie (KLARF/XML/SINF formats) and domestic packaging OSAT pick-and-place sorters (Disco/Besi/Datacon XML/SECS-II) creates manual operator transcoding risks. Tapeout data pipeline must establish a validated, automated script schema mapping bin code categories (Bin 1: Prime DRAM, Bin 2: Refresh Marginal, Bin >7: Hard Functional/Open-Short Fails) directly to standard JEDEC trays without manual spreadsheet handoffs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Lack of closed-loop electronic bin-map verification directly bottlenecks lot release for packaging assembly. A 100% dry-run validation protocol must be signed off on blank dummy frame setups before actual production thin-die picking to eliminate assembly scrap caused by misconfigured binning recipes.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Inverted X/Y or mirrored axes during wafer map format conversion causing functional sorting inversion (picking rejected Bin 8/9 dies into hermetic/ceramic test packages while discarding Bin 1 DRAM dies).
1. Accumulated kerf pitch drift on expanded dicing tape exceeding vision field-of-view (+/- 50 um drift), causing die pick collet to strike silicon edges and induce mechanical micro-chipping or cracking.
1. Loss of wafer orientation tracking due to obscured notch/flat reference on dicing ring tape, leading to 90-degree rotated coordinate mismatch.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-2-01` | **SEMI E142 / SINF Wafer Map Coordinate and Orientation Transformation Verification** | Automated Die Sorter Vision Subsystem (Besi/Datacon or Disco), Off-line Automated Wafer Map Translation Parser, High-Resolution Industrial Inspection Camera | 1. Ingest foundry CP ATE SINF file into wafer map translation parser and execute coordinate translation script targeting sorter-native XML recipe. 2. Mount dicing ring on sorter chuck; perform two-point global fiducial alignment on alignment keys. 3. Execute dry optical verification traversing 100% of die coordinates without picking, recording physical coordinate offsets (dX, dY, theta) and optical pattern match against translated bin assignment. | `Coordinate translation parity must be 100.0% matching CP sortie map (0 misallocated die bins across entire wafer); physical optical die center alignment error <= +/- 12.0 um across all 100% die locations on tape.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-2-02` | **Post-Dicing Tape Expansion Non-Linear Pitch Correction and Collet Pick Accuracy** | High-Speed Die Bonder / Sorter with Local Vision Tracking and Vacuum Collet Touchdown Sensor (Gram-force resolution +/- 0.5 gf) | 1. Program automated pick-and-place sequence for 100 Bin 1 dies sampled equally across center, middle ring, and extreme edge radius. 2. Record optical pattern alignment delta prior to collet descent. 3. Pick die, measure ejector pin offset and collect placement in 2-inch waffle pack pocket; inspect die edge chipping using 20x optical inspection. | `Dynamic local vision lock success rate = 100.0%; pick collet landing offset <= +/- 8.0 um from die center; zero mechanical chipping or kerf micro-cracks exceeding 5.0 um depth.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 Approved Safety Glasses with Side Shields, Conductive ESD Heel Straps and Grounded Lab Smock
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For IPA skin contact: Wash thoroughly with deionized water for at least 15 minutes. For eye splash: Flush immediately at emergency eye-wash station for 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical attention. For nitrogen purge asphyxiation risk: Evacuate operator to fresh air immediately; administer CPR/oxygen if breathing ceases.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated cleanroom local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on solvent cleaning wipes station maintaining face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); laminar airflow bench Class 100 (ISO 5) over pick-and-place chuck.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used solvent IPA-impregnated wipes must be sealed in airtight, grounded, FM-approved flammable waste containers and disposed of via hazardous solvent incineration streams. Zero drain disposal permitted.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Cleanroom Grade** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Ultra-Pure Nitrogen Gas (Chuck / Vision Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Singulated 180nm DRAM wafer on UV-dicing tape with DI water post-saw rinse and spin-dry complete; kerfs clear of residual silicon slurry.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Binned Known-Good-Die (KGD) seated in conductive waffle pack or Gel-Pak under continuous ESD-safe dry N2 environment, free of silicon particulates.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient air queue time causes native oxide growth and airborne organic molecular contamination on bare top-metal aluminum/copper bond pads, causing non-stick wire bonding or elevated contact resistance during backend assembly.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full algorithmic translation, validation, and execution of automated wafer map and die binning recipes transitioning from foundry CP ATE test output to OSAT pick-and-place die sorting for 180nm DRAM dies, guaranteeing zero coordinate inversion and verified pick accuracy.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `180nm_DRAM_Gen3_WaferMap_Translation_Recipe.xml`
- [ ] `Wafer_Sort_Coordinate_Parity_Verification_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Die_Binning_Yield_and_Pick_Discrepancy_Log.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Coordinate and Bin Category Concordance between CP ATE SINF and Sorter XML Recipe** | `100.0` | +/-0.0% | Automated bitwise cross-comparison script comparing input SINF die bin matrices against translated sorter recipe map |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Die Sorter Vision Pattern-Recognition Positioning Error** | `0.0` | <= 10.0 um (3-sigma) | In-situ high-resolution optical vision measurement of die fiducial marks relative to pick collet vacuum axis across entire wafer diameter |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Ejector Pin and Collet Pick Success Rate on Validated Bin 1 Dies** | `99.95` | +/-0.05% | Automated optical inspection (AOI) tally of picked pockets and vacuum sensor confirmation during continuous automated run |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 100% zero-mismatch bitwise map parity verification report signed by Systems and Test Integration Engineers, coupled with a successful 1-wafer dummy pick run demonstrating zero die cracking and <= 10 um alignment drift.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## SEMI-E142 Wafer Map Parser & Dicing Frame Coordinate Transform Implementation

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Lifecycle

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     SEMI-E142 XML      │
│       Ingestion        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Wafer Map Parse &    │
│       Bin Matrix       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Fiducial Align &    │
│     Theta Rotation     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Dicing Frame      │
│  Coordinate Transform  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Pick-and-Place     │
│     Machine Recipe     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **SEMI-E142 Schema Parsing & Bin Matrix Extraction**
   - Ingest wafer map XML compliant with SEMI-E142 (`<MapData>`, `<Substrate>`, `<BinCode>`).
   - Extract reference origin $(0, 0)$, die pitch $(P_x, P_y)$, and orientation notch/flat direction.
   - Filter dies by bin quality: isolate Pass dies intended for packaging from rejected/edge dies. Verify pad geometry definitions correspond to $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum square bonding pads.

2. **Dicing Tape Expansion & Fiducial Optical Alignment**
   - Mount sawn wafer on film frame / dicing ring across UV release or expanding tape.
   - Using machine vision on a linear stage guided by precision ground rails (MGN12H) with closed-loop optical/magnetic encoders ($1\ \mu\text{m}$ resolution), detect at least two reference fiducials or corner bonding pads ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Compute physical orientation angle $\theta$ and translation offset $(\Delta X_0, \Delta Y_0)$ relative to the frame center.

3. **Affine Coordinate Transformation to Dicing Frame Space**
   - Translate wafer grid indices $(Col, Row)$ to wafer physical coordinates $(X_w, Y_w)$:
     $$X_w = Col \times P_x, \quad Y_w = Row \times P_y$$
   - Apply rigid affine coordinate transformation (accounting for rotation $\theta$, linear stage straightness $< 5\ \mu\text{m} / 100\text{mm}$, and tape stretch factor $S_x, S_y$):
     $$\begin{bmatrix} X_f \\ Y_f \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} S_x \cos\theta & -S_y \sin\theta \\ S_x \sin\theta & S_y \cos\theta \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} X_w \\ Y_w \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} \Delta X_0 \\ \Delta Y_0 \end{bmatrix}$$

4. **Pick-and-Place Machine Recipe Generation & Export**
   - Translate frame coordinates $(X_f, Y_f)$ into pick-and-place motion vectors for NEMA 17 drive mechanisms with 1/16 microstepping and C7 rolled ball screws / anti-backlash lead screws.
   - Generate die-ejector pin target sequences and dispense recipes targeting die attach with silver-filled conductive epoxy (e.g., Ablebond 84-1LMIS cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 minutes) to ensure void area under die $< 5\%$ and $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
   - Ensure target placement coordinates align the die pads within tolerance for $25\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter wire bonding (Au ball bonding at $150^\circ\text{C}$ or room-temperature $25^\circ\text{C}$ Al wedge bonding).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                             ┌───────────────────────────┐
                             │▓▓                         │
      Die Attach Max Void (%)┤▓▓                         │
                             │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
            Bond Pad Dim (um)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
      Encoder Resolution (um)┤▒                          │
                             │▒                          │
Stage Straightness (um/100mm)┤██                         │
                             │██                         │
                             └┬──────┬─────┬──────┬─────┬┘
                              0     25    50     75   100 
```

| Metric ID | Parameter Description | Target Specification | Exact Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-01** | Stage Motion Straightness Deviation | $< 5.0$ | $\mu\text{m} / 100\text{mm}$ | Linear displacement interferometer / dial indicator |
| **AC-02** | Coordinate Feedback Resolution | $\le 1.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical linear encoder / magnetic scale reading |
| **AC-03** | Target Pad Pitch/Dimension Alignment | $100 \times 100$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Optical Metrology (AOI) on bond pads |
| **AC-04** | Post-Attach Die Acoustic Void Area | $< 5.0$ | $\%$ | Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) |

---

### 4. Context Source Citations

- **Source: Precision Linear Stage Design & Vibration Damping**
  - Linear stage straightness $< 5\ \mu\text{m}/100\text{mm}$ using MGN12H rails on 4040 aluminum frames.
  - Closed-loop positioning resolution of $1\ \mu\text{m}$ via optical encoders / linear magnetic scales.
  - Drive mechanism: NEMA 17 stepper motors with 1/16 microstepping paired with C7 rolled ball screws or anti-backlash lead screws.
- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**
  - On-chip bonding pad dimensions: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares.
  - Die attach specification: Silver-filled conductive epoxy cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for 60 min with post-attach void area $< 5\%$ and thermal resistance $R_{th} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$.
  - Downstream wire bonding interface tolerances: $25\ \mu\text{m}$ wire diameter (thermosonic Au ball bonding at $150^\circ\text{C}$ / ultrasonic Al-1% Si wedge bonding at $25^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Parsing SEMI-E142 XML schema maps and mapping them to kinematic physical dicing frame coordinates requires rigorous affine transformation handling. In wafer saw mounting and film-frame expansion, tape stretch introduces non-linear radial distortion (up to 150 um at wafer perimeter) and rotational runout (theta misorientation up to +/- 1.5 degrees). If the coordinate translation engine assumes an ideal rigid Euclidean grid without multi-point fiducial registration and local pitch compensation, pick-and-place nozzles will misalign with good dies, causing vacuum pick misses or edge chipping during ejector pin stroke.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: SEMI-E142 structures bin codes and die coordinates relative to the wafer notch/flat, whereas dicing tape stretch frames utilize physical frame alignment notches (DISCO or Kulicke & Soffa standard). Dicing kerf loss (typically 25-40 um with standard diamond blades) coupled with wafer thinning stress relaxation creates kerf wander and physical die shifts. The software parser must dynamically resolve bin quality flags (Pass, Fail, Gross Die, Probe Scratch Reject) and translate the discrete die pitch grid into true frame coordinates using at least 4 global optical fiducials plus local cell alignment.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Downstream OSAT and test facilities utilize heterogeneous equipment interfaces (e.g., DISCO DFD6361 saws, Datacon or Besi die attach systems) that often run legacy variants of SEMI-E142 or SECS/GEM formats. Relying on an unvalidated custom open-source translation parser without equipment vendor round-trip validation creates risk of rejecting valid Known Good Die (KGD) or picking unbinned edge rejects, resulting in low assembly yield and warranty scrap.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Implementation schedule must lock the SEMI-E142 XML schema parser and transformation pipeline to the 180nm DRAM MPW delivery schedule. Any delay in establishing deterministic coordinate mapping between foundry wafer sort test vectors and post-dicing frame maps blocks the die attach recipe setup and jeopardizes the packaging turnaround window.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Coordinate frame inversion or axis swap (e.g., inverted Y-axis or 90-degree notch offset mismatch between SEMI-E142 orientation and pick-and-place coordinate system) leading to picking defective/untested bin dies instead of Known Good Die.
1. Non-linear tape expansion error exceeding half-kerf width (>15 um), causing collet/nozzle mechanical collision with adjacent dies or ejector pin puncturing active silicon circuitry.
1. SEMI-E142 XML encoding schema parse failure on multi-site bin records, causing software crash during automated inline high-speed die sort.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-2-1-01` | **SEMI-E142 XML Schema Parsing & Bin Code Matrix Integrity Validation** | Automated SEMI-E142 XML Test Validator Suite, Python 3.10 lxml/schema engine, Foundry Golden Wafer Sort Data Log (200mm wafer, 180nm DRAM array layout). | 1. Ingest the golden wafer sort SEMI-E142 XML file into the parser pipeline. 2. Validate XML against SEMI E142-0211 schema XSD. 3. Extract bin matrix, origin position, wafer orientation notch angle (0, 90, 180, 270 deg), and total die counts. 4. Cross-reference parsed die count and bin classification against raw ATE test log summary. 5. Verify reference die coordinate registration (Col 0, Row 0) relative to physical wafer center. | `Schema validation status = 100% PASS with 0 schema violations. Parsed die count must equal exact ATE log die count (100.0% matching). Bin classification error rate = 0 ppm across all dies.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-2-1-02` | **Affine Dicing Frame Coordinate Translation & Optical Fiducial Alignment Accuracy** | Automated Vision Metrology Station / Optical Die Sorter (sub-micron optical encoder resolution <= 0.5 um, calibrated high-magnification telecentric CCD). | 1. Clamp the diced film frame onto the metrology vacuum stage. 2. Locate primary frame fiducial notch and 4 optical die fiducials at wafer periphery (North, South, East, West). 3. Compute affine transformation matrix (translation dx/dy, scale factor sx/sy accounting for tape stretch, and rotation theta). 4. Command stage to navigate to 50 predetermined Known Good Die coordinates spread across center, mid-radius, and edge zones. 5. Measure absolute position deviation between nozzle target center and physical die street center using machine vision. | `Maximum absolute positional offset |delta_x| and |delta_y| <= 10.0 um across all 50 measured dies. Rotational misorientation theta <= 0.05 degrees. Zero die index collision or misidentification.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000 Cleanroom Antistatic Nitrile Gloves, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-absorbing and impact safety glasses, Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) safe lab coat and grounded conductive heel straps, Cut-resistant under-gloves for handling stainless steel wafer dicing frames
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean water at an emergency eye wash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek ophthalmic attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing and wash skin thoroughly with soap and water. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Remove individual to fresh clean air; administer CPR if breathing ceases. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; seek immediate medical emergency treatment.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted within laminar flow hood (Class 100 / ISO 5) with exhaust air velocity maintained at 0.45 m/s (+/- 0.05 m/s); local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on manual stage cleaning stations with solvent vapor capture velocity >= 0.5 m/s ducting to VOC scrubbers.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA and cleaning solvent wipes must be segregated into clearly labeled, grounded, fire-rated stainless steel flammable waste drums; do not drain to municipal sewers. Contaminated dicing tape remnants and lint-free wipes disposed of as hazardous chemical solid waste via licensed industrial incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Tier 1) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-Pure Type I (18.2 MOhm-cm at 25C) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Diced 180nm DRAM wafer on UV-curable dicing tape mounted on film frame; active die surface dry, de-taped from backgrinding tape, DI water rinsed and spin-dried post-sawing, free of silicon slurry contamination.

critics.systems_engineer: Parsing SEMI-E142 XML schema maps and mapping them to kinematic physical dicing frame coordinates requires rigorous affine transformation handling. In wafer saw mounting and film-frame expansion, tape stretch introduces non-linear radial distortion (up to 150 um at wafer perimeter) and rotational runout (theta misorientation up to +/- 1.5 degrees). If the coordinate translation engine assumes an ideal rigid Euclidean grid without multi-point fiducial registration and local pitch compensation, pick-and-place nozzles will misalign with good dies, causing vacuum pick misses or edge chipping during ejector pin stroke.
critics.domain_expert: SEMI-E142 structures bin codes and die coordinates relative to the wafer notch/flat, whereas dicing tape stretch frames utilize physical frame alignment notches (DISCO or Kulicke & Soffa standard). Dicing kerf loss (typically 25-40 um with standard diamond blades) coupled with wafer thinning stress relaxation creates kerf wander and physical die shifts. The software parser must dynamically resolve bin quality flags (Pass, Fail, Gross Die, Probe Scratch Reject) and translate the discrete die pitch grid into true frame coordinates using at least 4 global optical fiducials plus local cell alignment.
critics.supply_chain: Downstream OSAT and test facilities utilize heterogeneous equipment interfaces (e.g., DISCO DFD6361 saws, Datacon or Besi die attach systems) that often run legacy variants of SEMI-E142 or SECS/GEM formats. Relying on an unvalidated custom open-source translation parser without equipment vendor round-trip validation creates risk of rejecting valid Known Good Die (KGD) or picking unbinned edge rejects, resulting in low assembly yield and warranty scrap.
critics.laya_pm: Implementation schedule must lock the SEMI-E142 XML schema parser and transformation pipeline to the 180nm DRAM MPW delivery schedule. Any delay in establishing deterministic coordinate mapping between foundry wafer sort test vectors and post-dicing frame maps blocks the die attach recipe setup and jeopardizes the packaging turnaround window.
critical_failure_modes: Coordinate frame inversion or axis swap (e.g., inverted Y-axis or 90-degree notch offset mismatch between SEMI-E142 orientation and pick-and-place coordinate system) leading to picking defective/untested bin dies instead of Known Good Die.
Non-linear tape expansion error exceeding half-kerf width (>15 um), causing collet/nozzle mechanical collision with adjacent dies or ejector pin puncturing active silicon circuitry.
SEMI-E142 XML encoding schema parse failure on multi-site bin records, causing software crash during automated inline high-speed die sort.

1. Ingest the golden wafer sort SEMI-E142 XML file into the parser pipeline.
2. Validate XML against SEMI E142-0211 schema XSD.

testcases.instrumentation: Automated Vision Metrology Station / Optical Die Sorter (sub-micron optical encoder resolution <= 0.5 um, calibrated high-magnification telecentric CCD).
testcases.pre_conditions: 200mm thinned DRAM wafer mounted on dicing tape and 8-inch stainless steel film frame post-saw dicing; SEMI-E142 parsed coordinate recipe loaded into die sorter controller.

1. Clamp the diced film frame onto the metrology vacuum stage.
2. Locate primary frame fiducial notch and 4 optical die fiducials at wafer periphery (North, South, East, West).

testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Maximum absolute positional offset |delta_x| and |delta_y| <= 10.0 um across all 50 measured dies. Rotational misorientation theta <= 0.05 degrees. Zero die index collision or misidentification.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Die Sorter Vision Alignment & Bin Classification Recipe Setup

**Task ID / Classification:** Gen 3 (nm) | Action Type: Make  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Wafer Backgrinding Thinning & High-Speed Diamond Saw Dicing > Post-Dicing Die Metrology, Kerf Quality Inspection & Die Pick-and-Place Sort > Wafer Map Coordinate Translation & Die Binning Recipe Setup > Automated Die Sorter Vision Alignment & Bin Classification Recipe Setup

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌─────────────────────┐
│Wafer Table Clamping │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│     Dual-Camera     │
│     Split-Field     │
│      Alignment      │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│Fiducial Recognition │
│& Theta Compensation │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Wafer Map Coord   │
│     Translation     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│  High-Speed Collet  │
│ Pick & Bin Sorting  │
└─────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Stage & Frame Clamping (Leveling & Parallelism Calibration)**
   - Mount the sawn wafer on its dicing tape frame onto the automated sorter vacuum chuck.
   - Activate the vacuum chuck and verify mechanical leveling utilizing the spherical air-bearing Wedge Error Compensation (WEC) mechanism to enforce stage planarity across the substrate (< 1 µm across 100 mm span) [Karl Suss MA6 SOP].
   - Confirm substrate flatness and optical focal clearance against the calculated depth of focus window ($DOF = k_2 \cdot (\lambda / NA^2) \ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$) across die surface topography [SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK].

2. **Optical Calibration & Split-Field Dual-Camera Pattern Registration**
   - Initialize the split-field vision subsystem utilizing dual CMOS cameras paired with 10x Plan Achromat objectives (NA 0.25) [Karl Suss MA6 SOP, Sam Zeloof Z1 Journal].
   - Calibrate optical magnification using 5x, 10x, and 20x objectives to establish sub-pixel scaling factors on fiducial kerf targets [Karl Suss MA6 SOP].
   - Focus the camera system to maintain sharp image acquisition of alignment fiducials etched into the street/kerf grid.

3. **Global Alignment, Theta ($\theta$) Skew Compensation & Fiducial Teaching**
   - Teach the vision model the primary reference fiducials located at opposite wafer perimeter coordinates.
   - Execute dual-point optical registration to compute rotational skew ($\Delta\theta$) and translational offsets ($\Delta X, \Delta Y$).
   - Apply micro-stepper motor compensation to correct theta alignment to within Gen 2 precision bounds ($\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$), ensuring precision overlay targets ($\le 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ to $\pm 2\ \mu\text{m}$) are met prior to coordinate translation [Karl Suss MA6 SOP, Sam Zeloof Z1 Journal].

4. **Wafer Map Coordinate Translation & Defect Classification Setup**
   - Ingest the electronic wafer map (`.xml` / `.map`) output from the Wafer Sort Electrical Test.
   - Correlate the wafer probe test coordinate origin $(0, 0)$ with the optical vision coordinate frame using the taught kerf alignment points.
   - Configure optical bin classification thresholds for edge chipping, crack detection, and probe mark distortion. Map classified bin codes into target destination trays (e.g., Bin 1: Pass Grade A, Bin 2: Secondary Speed, Bin 8: Functional Fail, Bin 9: Mechanical Reject).

5. **Collet Pick-and-Place Recipe Execution & Verification**
   - Synchronize the high-speed pneumatic pick-and-place collet with the translated vision coordinate table.
   - Run a 10-die verification cycle at slow speed: verify ejector needle stroke, vacuum retention, and accurate placement into assigned gel-pack / waffle tray pockets without mechanical kerf collisions.
   - Lock recipe parameters in the sorter host system and transition to production run mode.

---

### Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                       Baseline Physical Recipe Metrics 
                      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                      │████████████████████████████████│
 Shipley 1813 Softbake┤████████████████████████████████│
                      │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓               │
      MF-319 Dev Rinse┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓               │
Vacuum Contact Overlay┤▒                               │
                      │▒                               │
    WEC Chuck Leveling┤░                               │
                      │░                               │
                      └┬───────┬───────┬──────┬───────┬┘
                      0.0    28.8    57.5   86.2  115.0 
```

| Metric Parameter | Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria | Relevant Physical Unit | Source Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage Parallelism / Leveling (WEC)** | $\le 1\ \mu\text{m}$ across 100 mm chuck | $\mu\text{m}$ | *Karl Suss MA6 SOP* |
| **Vision Alignment & Overlay Precision** | $\le 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ (vacuum contact mode limit) / $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ (Gen 2 alignment threshold) | $\mu\text{m}$ | *Karl Suss MA6 SOP*, *Sam Zeloof Z1 Journal* |
| **Optical Depth of Focus (DOF) Margin** | $\ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ ($DOF = k_2 \cdot (\lambda / NA^2)$) | $\mu\text{m}$ | *SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK* |
| **Microscope Objective Lens Standard** | 10x Plan Achromat ($NA = 0.25$) with split-field CMOS camera | Dimensionless ($NA$) / Magnification | *Karl Suss MA6 SOP*, *Sam Zeloof Z1 Journal* |

---

### Cited Source Contexts
- **Karl Suss MA6 Mask Aligner Standard Operating Procedure & Gap Control**: Stage Wedge Error Compensation (WEC) $< 1\ \mu\text{m}$ across 100 mm wafers, split-field optical microscope with 5x, 10x, and 20x objectives with CMOS cameras, overlay alignment precision $\le 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ to $\pm 2$–$5\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**: 10x Plan Achromat objective ($NA = 0.25$), Gen 2 alignment threshold $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$, thermal and chemical recipe baselines (115°C soft bake, 45–60 s MF-319 rinse).
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**: Depth of Focus process window relationship $DOF = k_2 \cdot (\lambda / NA^2) \ge 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Vision alignment recipe integration with SECS/GEM (E142 substrate mapping) requires deterministic sub-pixel pattern matching across varying dicing street contrast and kerf sidewall chipping. The primary systemic risk is an uncalibrated optical parallax between the dual-camera split-field microscope and the pick-and-place collet theta axis, inducing systematic X/Y offset accumulation (>5 um) across a 200mm diced wafer frame on UV dicing tape.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm DRAM dies with top-metal Al-0.5%Cu bond pads and polyimide passivation, illumination angle and optical wavelength (coaxial white LED vs. darkfield ring illumination) drastically alter pad corner edge-detection confidence. If dicing saw slurry residues or kerf micro-cracking propagate into the outer guard ring, template matching algorithms risk false rejection or, worse, classifying cracked dies as Bin 1 pass dies due to inadequate contrast thresholding.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying turnkey automated die sorters (e.g., ASM Pacific, Besi, or Kulicke & Soffa) under a Buy workflow faces an 18 to 26 week lead time for specialized rubber/PEEK vacuum pick tips and customized wafer frame expander rings. Secondary supply risks involve sourcing cleanroom-grade UV de-taping lamps and calibrated glass grid reticles with NIST-traceable grid pitch certification for vision coordinate calibration.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The capital expenditure for automated vision alignment recipe verification must not bottleneck the pilot packaging schedule. Recipe training sets must be locked using at least 5 representative dummy wafers exhibiting varying kerf quality before production lot transfer, ensuring UPH (units per hour) exceeds 4,500 with a false binning misclassification rate strictly under 0.05%.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Theta rotational misalignment (>0.3 deg) during vision capture resulting in edge chipping or micro-crack propagation upon vacuum collet touch-down.
1. SECS/GEM wafer map coordinate inversion (mirroring/rotational 90-degree offset) causing Bin 1 good dies and ink-dot/probe-failed reject dies to be swapped during tape-and-reel sorting.
1. Excessive UV tape stretch distortion (>50 um non-linear displacement across outer wafer radius) causing optical search window timeout and die drop failures.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-2-2-01` | **Machine Vision Alignment Accuracy and Repeatability Calibration** | Automated Die Sorter with dual-magnification split-field CMOS camera system (5x wide-field, 20x high-res), calibrated chrome-on-quartz NIST-traceable grid distortion reticle (1.000 mm pitch +/- 0.05 um), and laser displacement sensor. | 1. Mount calibrated quartz standard reticle onto wafer frame stage and engage vacuum hold-down (min 70 kPa). 2. Execute automated 9-point fiducial registration across the reticle. 3. Measure reticle center and four quadrant corner coordinates across 30 consecutive load/unload pick-cycle iterations without physical picking. 4. Calculate 3-sigma positional repeatability for X, Y, and Theta axes. | `Optical vision alignment positioning repeatability must be <= 1.5 um (3-sigma) for X/Y translation and <= 0.05 degrees (3-sigma) for Theta rotation across all 30 consecutive cycles.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-2-2-02` | **Wafer Map Coordinate Binning Fidelity and Misclassification Stress Test** | Automated Die Sorter SECS/GEM interface emulator, high-resolution automated optical inspection (AOI) review station, and diced 180nm DRAM test vehicle wafer (diced on expanded UV tape) with pre-verified electronic wafer map containing known fail patterns (checkerboard test die distribution). | 1. Load pre-characterized checkerboard wafer frame into loader cassette. 2. Align wafer reference die (die coordinate [0,0]) and synchronize map orientation. 3. Execute sorting recipe at nominal speed (4,500 UPH) for 500 consecutive dies. 4. Collect sorted dies and inspect waffle packs and reject bin using AOI to verify die physical ID matching map bin classification. | `Zero bin misclassification errors (100% bin fidelity, 0/500 misbinned dies); die pick-and-place placement accuracy within carrier pocket <= 15 um X/Y offset.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (powder-free, static dissipative), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-blocking safety glasses, ESD wrist strap connected to common ground point, Full cleanroom bunny suit with conductive soles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Remove contaminated clothing, flush skin with copious running water for 15 minutes. Eye contact: Rinse cautiously with eyewash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Inhalation: Move personnel to cleanroom air intake or fresh air. In case of mechanical pinch injury from high-speed pick arm, hit E-Stop, apply sterile gauze compression, and seek medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on manual stage cleaning stations with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s. Sorter optical enclosure maintained under positive laminar flow HEPA filtration (ISO Class 4/5) with dedicated vacuum pump exhaust piped out of cleanroom.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be deposited in dedicated grounded, airtight flammable solvent disposal cans. Liquid solvent residues segregated into designated solvent hazardous waste drums for licensed industrial incineration. No organic solvents permitted in drain.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI-C12) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I Cleanroom Grade (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Diced 180nm DRAM wafer on expanded UV dicing tape mounted on metal wafer ring, thoroughly spin-rinsed and dried, free from DI water droplets, saw silicon dust slurry, or tape adhesive bleed.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Singulated DRAM dies placed into anti-static waffle pack/Gel-Pak or embossed carrier tape, top Al-Cu bond pads unmarred by vacuum collet, packaged under vacuum-sealed moisture barrier bag (MBB) with desiccant and HIC card.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom air Q-time causes galvanic micro-corrosion and native oxide hydration on exposed Al-Cu wirebond pads, while prolonged UV tape holding induces adhesive transfer and permanent die-sticking resulting in cracked dies or pick failure.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful commissioning and signoff of the automated die sorter vision alignment and bin classification recipe for 180nm Open-Source DRAM dies, demonstrating micron-scale optical alignment repeatability, deterministic SECS/GEM map coordinate translation, and damage-free pick-and-place handling.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RECIPE_DRAM180_ALIGN_BIN_REV1.xml`
- [ ] `VISION_ALIGNMENT_REPEATABILITY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `WAFER_MAP_BIN_VERIFICATION_MATRIX.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Vision alignment stage repositioning precision (3-sigma across 9 wafer points)** | `1.2` | <= 1.5 um | High-magnification quartz reticle multi-point optical coordinate measurement |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Wafer map bin translation error rate during automated sorting** | `0.0` | 0.0% (Zero misbinned dies across 500 consecutive picks) | Post-sort AOI verification of sorted waffle pack dies against SECS/GEM electronic wafer map |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Die pickup yield without mechanical damage or collet pad scuffing** | `99.9` | >= 99.8% | Automated post-pick top and backside optical inspection at 50x magnification |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full formal signoff requires zero optical alignment faults over three consecutive 200mm test frames, zero binning discrepancies confirmed via SECS/GEM E142 audit, verified UPH >= 4,500, and unanimous signoff from Packaging Lead, Systems Engineer, and Foundry Quality Director.
