# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: Post-Sort Bin Map Reconciliation & Pick-and-Place Physical Yield Verification

**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-MET-180-044`  
**Process Level:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip / MPW Tapeout / BEOL & Packaging / Post-Dicing Metrology & Sort  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm / SKY130 Hybrid Compatible Node)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Wafer Sort ATE Test   │
│          Logs          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Coordinate Transform  │
│    & Bin Alignment     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Post-Sort Bin Map    │
│       Ingestion        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   PnP Physical Pick    │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Reconciliation &    │
│    Tray Inspection     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Automated Yield     │
│    Ledger Sign-off     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **ATE Electrical Bin Map Ingestion & Coordinate Transformation:**
   - Ingest wafer sort electrical test data (STDF/SECS-GEM map) with functional classification: Bin 1 (Pass / Known-Good-Die: refresh retention $\ge 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, leakage $\le 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$, capacitance $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$), Bin 2–7 (Marginal / Parametric Failures), and Bin 8+ (Gross Shorts / Open Failures).
   - Align the electrical $(X, Y)$ coordinate origin to the physical dicing tape wafer frame reference notch/flat. Transform probe coordinates to the physical pick-and-place (PnP) dicing grid using the physical placement grid resolution step of $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).

2. **Dicing Street & Kerf Metrology Calibration:**
   - Position automated optical inspection (AOI) pattern recognition over diced street fiducials.
   - Verify dicing kerf street centering against design boundary limits: active diffusion-to-kerf edge isolation must maintain the PDK overlay error safety margin $\le 35\text{ nm}$ ($0.035\ \mu\text{m}$), and die edge clearance must guarantee no micro-cracking propagating into active diffusion or outer Metal 1 seal rings (minimum M1 width $0.14\ \mu\text{m}$, minimum M1 pitch $0.34\ \mu\text{m}$).

3. **Automated Pick-and-Place (PnP) Sorting Execution:**
   - Load wafer ring frame onto the expander stage; apply controlled multi-axis radial expansion ($1.5\text{ mm}$ to $2.0\text{ mm}$) to widen inter-die kerf separation.
   - Set rubber/polyimide collet vacuum pick head to a differential suction pressure of $-75\ \text{kPa} \pm 5\ \text{kPa}$ with an ejector pin upward stroke velocity $\le 10\ \text{mm/s}$ and max height displacement $\le 350\ \mu\text{m}$ to prevent stacked capacitor crown or MIM structural micro-fracture.
   - Pick only validated Bin 1 (KGD) dies and transfer into JEDEC standard waffle packs or Gel-Pak matrix pockets. Reject or divert Bin 2+ dies into designated reject output carriers based on the mapped die coordinates.

4. **Waffle Pack Post-Sort Optical & Positional Verification:**
   - Perform post-placement camera scanning across populated pocket matrix coordinates $(R_i, C_j)$.
   - Measure die placement orientation error ($\theta \le \pm 1.0^\circ$) and in-pocket lateral displacement ($\Delta X, \Delta Y \le \pm 15\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Run optical pattern matching across the die surface to ensure zero physical chipping, zero delamination of stacked capacitor dielectric layers, and zero particle contamination $> 0.17\ \mu\text{m}$ (critical contact dimension resolution limit).

5. **Physical Yield Reconciliation & Discrepancy Gate:**
   - Execute an automated cross-check between ATE Bin 1 electrical counts ($N_{\text{ATE\_PASS}}$), PnP physically picked die counts ($N_{\text{PICKED}}$), and waffle pack pocket verification counts ($N_{\text{POCKET}}$).
   - Reconcile the wafer tape remnant frame: verify that remaining unpicked dies on the dicing ring frame exactly correspond to reject bins ($N_{\text{REJECT}} = N_{\text{TOTAL}} - N_{\text{ATE\_PASS}}$).
   - Lock wafer yield ledger: trigger an automated line halt if any die misplacement, double-pick, dropped die, or bin assignment mismatch is detected.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Window | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Physical Placement Grid Alignment** | $0.005$ | $\pm 0.000$ | $\mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$) |
| **Max Permissible Edge / Overlay Error** | $\le 35.0$ | $\pm 5.0$ | $\text{nm}$ |
| **Single-Cell Leakage Limit (Bin 1 Gate)** | $\le 1.0$ | $\pm 0.1$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Cell Capacitance Budget (Bin 1 Gate)** | $\ge 28.0$ | $+10.0 / -0.0$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ |
| **Bin Map Reconciliation Accuracy** | $100.0$ | $\pm 0.0$ (Zero discrepancy) | $\%$ |

---

### 4. Verification Integrity Chart

```text
Post-Sort Physical Yield Verification Integrity (%)
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Kerf Clearance Margin┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                     │                                 │
   Collet Vacuum Loss┤                                 │
    Placement Overlay┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                     │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
        Bin Map Match┤█████████████████████████████████│
                     │█████████████████████████████████│
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                      0      25      50      75     100 
```

---

### 5. Context Literature Citations

1. **Source: SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**
   - *Physical placement grid resolution:* $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).
   - *Lithography & overlay budget:* Poly gate length $0.15\ \mu\text{m}$ ($150\text{ nm}$), contact dimension $0.17\ \mu\text{m} \times 0.17\ \mu\text{m}$, Metal 1 minimum width $0.14\ \mu\text{m}$, Metal 1 pitch $0.34\ \mu\text{m}$, and maximum permissible overlay error budget $\le 35\text{ nm}$.
2. **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
   - *Unit cell layout:* Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, stacked capacitor over bitline (COB).
   - *Electrical parametric limits:* Capacitance budget $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$, leakage current target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ for retention integrity.
3. **Source: SkyWater 130nm Open PDK Overview & Architecture**
   - *PDK rules and tooling:* Implementation within the standard open-source EDA flow framework and manufacturing guidelines for 130nm/180nm commercial MPW tapeouts.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-sort bin map reconciliation requires deterministic handshaking between the automated wafer prober electronic wafer map (SEMI E142 XML format) and the pick-and-place handler vision coordinates. Any subtle coordinate frame misalignment, reference notch/flat rotation error, or pitch scaling delta caused by wafer expansion during dicing tape expansion will trigger catastrophic mis-binning where known-good die (KGD) are discarded and electrically failing die are packaged.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical yield verification must reconcile electrical prober yield (Bin 1 gross pass count) against physical pick-and-place yield accounting for edge-die exclusion, mechanical micro-chipping during diamond sawing, and vacuum collet pick failures. A high delta (>0.5%) between prober electrical yield and physical reel/tray pack count indicates mechanical damage, incomplete kerf release, or defective ejector needle puncture through the dicing tape.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Traceability across multi-project wafer (MPW) runs is critical; mis-binned customer dies packed into wrong tape-and-reel carriers result in immediate RMA and complete lot quarantine. Pick-and-place reconciliation logs must provide 100% auditable serialized tracking per wafer ID down to X-Y die coordinates to avoid mixed-lot exposure in downstream packaging houses.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Bin map translation and physical reconciliation represent the absolute gateway to packaging assembly. Any cycle time delays caused by manual map verification or false optical inspection rejects directly idle the wire bonding lines, inflating assembly WIP holding costs and violating production lot turnover schedules.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Wafer coordinate transformation inversion or origin offset (e.g., prober origin at lower-left vs. pick handler origin at upper-left) causing 100% inversion of Good Die vs. Reject Die pick actions.
1. Dicing frame tape expansion non-uniformity causing optical pattern recognition (PR) search failure, leading to unpicked good dies being recorded as missing/defective.
1. Ejector pin over-travel causing mechanical backside micro-cracking or silicon punch-through on thinned 180nm DRAM dies during vacuum collet extraction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-2-3-01` | **SEMI E142 Electronic Map to Physical Pick Position Alignment and Bin Verification** | Automated Die Sorter & Pick-and-Place Handler with High-Resolution Machine Vision (Cognex In-Sight / Keyence optical PR system, resolution 1.5 um/pixel) and SEMI E142 Map Interpreter | 1. Load film frame onto automated handler stage and vacuum clamp. 2. Perform 2-point optical global alignment on wafer notch and perimeter fiducial die. 3. Query host E142 wafer map for Bin 1 (Pass) die coordinates (X, Y). 4. Step handler camera to 5 designated Bin 1 coordinates and 5 known Reject/Fail coordinates across 4 quadrants and center. 5. Inspect die surface, cross-check visual inkless electronic bin assignment with physical die presence, and verify ejector needle centering under die center-of-mass within ±15 um. 6. Execute dry-run mapping sequence across full wafer array without mechanical pick to log coordinate match score. | `Coordinate transformation correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.99999; 0% coordinate offset errors across all verified sites; vision pattern recognition placement error <= ±5.0 um from die center.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-2-3-02` | **Post-Sort Physical Reconciliation and Pick-and-Place Gross Yield Audit** | Automated Waffle Pack / Gel-Pak Inspection System with Integrated Top-Down Optical Metrology, Precision Force Gauge on Pick Head (0.1 - 5.0 N range), and Barcode/DataMatrix Reader | 1. Extract post-pick XML production log recording total attempted picks, successful placements, vision optical rejects, and vacuum drop errors. 2. Scan output waffle pack trays using automated optical macro-inspection to count total physically placed intact dies. 3. Scan remnant dicing film frame to count remaining unpicked dies (both known rejects and unpicked good dies). 4. Compute physical yield: Y_phys = (Total Good Dies Placed) / (Total Electrical Bin 1 Dies on Prober Map) * 100%. 5. Perform automated 100% visual inspection of placed dies in tray pockets for die orientation (Pin 1 indicator), surface scratch, and edge chipping > 25 um. | `Physical to electrical yield reconciliation delta |Y_elec - Y_phys| <= 0.10%; Total pick drop/misplacement rate = 0 ppm (0 defects allowed); Edge chipping > 25 um on placed dies = 0 units.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 1000 compatible nitrile gloves (electrostatic discharge safe, 4-6 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Static dissipative cleanroom gown and conductive ESD heel grounders / ESD shoes, Face mask (particulate filtering cleanroom facemask)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA eye contact: Flush immediately with clean emergency eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. In case of skin exposure: Remove contaminated clothing and wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and DI water. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors: Move individual immediately to fresh air; seek prompt medical evaluation if dizziness or nausea persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on machine pick-and-place enclosure operating with continuous negative pressure; cleanroom laminar flow canopy maintaining airflow velocity between 0.35 and 0.45 m/s (70-90 fpm); solvent wipe stations equipped with dedicated VOC exhaust ducting.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free cleaning wipes and contaminated swab waste must be disposed of in dedicated, grounded, airtight flammable solvent disposal bins. Ejector needle breakage shards and cracked silicon fragments collected in rigid, puncture-resistant biohazard/sharps containers for hazardous solid waste handling.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Grade 1) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 Ultra-Pure Water (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Diced 180nm DRAM wafer on UV-cured expanded dicing tape, clean and dry with topside metallization (Al-0.5%Cu/TiN bond pads) and SiN passivation free of dicing slurry residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Singulated KGD (Bin 1) dies placed in ESD-safe JEDEC waffle pack/tape-and-reel under dry N2 seal; bond pads pristine with native oxide thickness <= 1.5 nm and zero organic contamination.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure to ambient air beyond 120 minutes promotes atmospheric moisture adsorption and galvanic oxidation of exposed aluminum bond pads, while prolonged mechanical tension on expanded dicing tape induces adhesive creep, causing die tilt, rotation, and loss of vision alignment coordinates.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful end-to-end execution of post-sort bin map reconciliation and pick-and-place physical yield verification for 180nm DRAM Gen 3 dies, demonstrating zero coordinate misalignment, complete traceability between SEMI E142 prober map and physical carrier locations, and 100% visual integrity of picked KGD dies.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `reconciled_bin_map_report_lot_wp323.csv`
- [ ] `pnp_physical_yield_audit_summary.pdf`
- [ ] `waffle_pack_tray_vision_inspection_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Reconciliation Delta between Electrical Prober Bin 1 Die Count and Physical Picked Die Count** | `0.0%` | <= 0.05% | Automated database cross-check between tester datalog STDF/E142 gross pass count and pick-and-place machine end-of-lot event log |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Die Placement Orientation and Center Offset in Carrier Pocket** | `0.0 um offset, 0.0 deg rotation` | <= ±20.0 um translational offset, <= ±1.5 deg rotational skew | High-magnification automated optical metrology (AOI) post-pack tray scanner |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-Pick Bond Pad Micro-crack and Chipping Defect Density** | `0 defects` | 0 units per wafer lot (0 ppm) | Brightfield automated optical defect inspection at 20x magnification across 100% of placed dies |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 100% numerical match between SEMI E142 electrical wafer map Bin 1 die coordinates and physical tray carrier coordinates with zero missing/misplaced dies, zero wafer map orientation discrepancies, all quantitative assertions meeting stated tolerances, and packaging QA engineering signoff on the generated audit CSV and PDF reports.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: High-Precision Die Ejector Needle & Pick-and-Place Sorter Collet Tooling
**Document ID:** `SOP-PKG-180-EJP-001`  
**Process Branch:** 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation → BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging → Wafer Backgrinding Thinning & High-Speed Diamond Saw Dicing → Post-Dicing Die Metrology, Kerf Quality Inspection & Die Pick-and-Place Sort  
**Technology Generation:** 180nm Gen 3 (nm) Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Mechanical Tooling Architecture

Die ejection and pick-and-place sorting transfer diced 180nm DRAM dies from UV/blue dicing tape onto leadframe package cavities without mechanical chipping, micro-cracking, or contact abrasion across sensitive frontside active circuitry.

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Dicing Tape Stage    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Ejector Pin       │
│       Elevation        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Collet Vacuum Pickup  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Die Attach Placement  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

```text

              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░      │

              │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒        │

              │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓           │

```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

#### Step 1: Ejector Needle Selection and Stage Pre-Alignment
1. Install a multi-needle ejector pin chuck configured with tungsten-carbide needles having a spherical tip radius of $R = 25\,\mu\text{m}$ to $35\,\mu\text{m}$.
2. Align needle array geometry symmetrically beneath the die boundaries, setting needle spacing to distribute lifting force evenly while avoiding localized point-stress beneath the central capacitor crown field.
3. Calibrate ejector pin zero-reference plane against the vacuum chuck surface to within $\pm 1.5\,\mu\text{m}$ baseline accuracy.

#### Step 2: Collet Tooling Selection & Anti-Contact Perimeter Setup
1. Select a high-temperature antistatic rubber or Vespel/PEEK surface collet tooling matched to the exact die outline dimensions.
2. Verify collet vacuum aperture geometry ensures perimeter vacuum contact only, keeping a complete keep-out zone over the active cell array (8F²/6F² stacked capacitor field) and peripheral $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.
3. Connect collet vacuum line and verify base dynamic suction pressure reaches $\le -75\,\text{kPa}$ to $-85\,\text{kPa}$.

#### Step 3: Dicing Tape Vacuum Clamping & Delamination Peeling
1. Place diced wafer ring frame onto the expandable wafer table under bottom-side vacuum holddown ($-80\,\text{kPa}$).
2. Perform UV cure release on the dicing tape (if UV-curable tape is utilized) to reduce tape adhesion force below $0.15\,\text{N}/25\,\text{mm}$.
3. Synchronize upward ejector needle push-up in a 2-stage ramp profile:
   - **Initial Delamination Stroke:** Pin velocity $0.8\,\text{mm/s}$ to height $+150\,\mu\text{m}$ to initiate perimeter tape peeling.
   - **Full Separation Stroke:** Final elevation to $+300\,\mu\text{m}$ to $+450\,\mu\text{m}$ relative to tape baseline.

#### Step 4: Collet Engagement, Die Pickup, and Metrology Transfer
1. Lower collet tool along Z-axis under closed-loop linear encoder control to touch the die top surface at a landing velocity $\le 1.0\,\text{mm/s}$ with a contact force limited to $15\,\text{gf} - 25\,\text{gf}$.
2. Activate collet pick vacuum ($-80\,\text{kPa}$), dwell for $15\,\text{ms}$, and retract ejector needles downward to home position below the chuck deck.
3. Lift collet at $10\,\text{mm/s}$ acceleration; execute optical bottom-camera fly-by inspection to verify die centering, absence of backside chipping/cracks, and absence of residual dicing adhesive.
4. Transfer verified DRAM die to the target lead frame cavity for silver-filled conductive epoxy die attach (cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\,\text{minutes}$).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Inspection Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Collet Landing & Pick Contact Force** | $20\,\text{gf}$ | $\pm 5\,\text{gf}$ ($\le 25\,\text{gf}$ peak) | In-situ piezoelectric load-cell feedback |
| **Pick-and-Place Collet Vacuum Level** | $-80\,\text{kPa}$ | Range: $-75\,\text{kPa}$ to $-85\,\text{kPa}$ | Inline digital vacuum transducer / switch |
| **Die Placement Positional Accuracy ($X, Y$)** | $0.0\,\mu\text{m}$ | $\le \pm 10.0\,\mu\text{m}$ ($3\sigma$) | Post-placement optical vision metrology |
| **Pad Exclusion & Frontside Damage Clearance** | $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ Pads | $0.0\,\mu\text{m}$ contact intrusion; zero active area micro-cracks | Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) / 500× High-Mag Camera |
| **Ejector Needle Lift Stroke Elevation** | $+350\,\mu\text{m}$ | $\pm 15\,\mu\text{m}$ | High-resolution Z-axis linear optical encoder |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & References

1. **[Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging](file:///d:/coding/dram/docs/context.yaml):**
   - Direct specifications: DRAM die aluminum bonding pads dimensioned at $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ square; wire pull strength criteria ($\ge 4.0\,\text{gf}$ for $25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011); silver-filled conductive epoxy (Ablebond 84-1LMIS) die attach cured at $150^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\,\text{minutes}$ with thermal resistance $R_{\text{th}} \le 5^\circ\text{C/W}$ and under-die void area $< 5\%$ via acoustic microscopy.
2. **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench](file:///d:/coding/dram/docs/context.yaml):**
   - DRAM cell dimensions and architectures: $180\,\text{nm}$ access transistor gate length ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$), $8\text{F}^2$ and $6\text{F}^2$ folded bitline layout with stacked capacitor over bitline (COB), W-plug contacts, and minimum cell capacitance budget of $28\,\text{fF/cell}$ (requiring strict zero-mechanical-stress collet perimeter clamping to protect fragile capacitor top plates).
3. **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering](file:///d:/coding/dram/docs/context2.yaml):**
   - Physical constraints: 1T1C stacked cell topology, bitline and wordline pitch of $360\,\text{nm} - 400\,\text{nm}$, and capacitor dielectric stacks requiring stress-free pick-and-place handling to safeguard electrical retention ($> 64\,\text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Ejector pin synchronization with the pick-and-place vacuum collet z-axis actuator requires sub-millisecond motion coordination. Any phase lag where the ejector needle thrust occurs before sufficient collet vacuum engagement (< -75 kPa) introduces mechanical stress concentrations, causing catastrophic backside micro-cracking across thinned 180nm DRAM dies (die thickness <= 150 um). Multi-pin array concentricity and planarity must stay within 3 um across all needles to prevent asymmetric bending moments.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm DRAM dies incorporating sensitive BEOL aluminum/copper interconnects and polyimide passivation, metal collet contact can lead to passivation chipping, bond pad cratering, and electrostatic discharge (ESD). A high-performance dissipative Vespel or Torlon tip with surface resistivity between 1e5 and 1e9 ohms/sq is mandatory. Tungsten carbide ejector needles must feature spherical radiused tips (radius 25-50 um) to distribute delamination peel forces from the UV dicing tape without puncturing the silicon substrate.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom micro-machined tungsten carbide ejector pins and ESD-compliant polyimide collet inserts have an 8-to-12-week lead time from precision tooling vendors (e.g., Kulicke & Soffa, SPT). An off-the-shelf COTS backup standard collet shank system with swappable modular tips must be qualified immediately to mitigate production starvation risks during pilot packaging runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Tooling wear and tip erosion directly impact pick-and-place uptime and throughput targets (>1,800 units per hour). The project timeline requires tooling sign-off within 5 business days of delivery. Maintenance SOPs must specify mandatory optical pin tip wear inspection every 50,000 cycles and collet vacuum seal replacement every 100,000 cycles to adhere to packaging yield budgets (>99.5%).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die backside puncture and radial cracking initiated by excessive needle tip penetration velocity or tip radius erosion below 15 um.
1. ESD micro-arc discharge from non-dissipative collet body during high-speed vacuum transfer causing DRAM gate oxide breakdown.
1. Die misalignment and corner chipping resulting from incomplete UV tape release combined with uneven multi-needle lift actuation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-3-01` | **Ejector Needle Planarity, Tip Geometry, and Synchronized Push-Up Force Metrology** | Keyence VHX-7000 Digital Optical Microscope (500x/1000x) with calibrated profilometry stage, Kistler 9217A miniature piezoelectric load cell (0-50 N, 0.01 N resolution), and Keyence LK-G5000 high-speed laser displacement sensor (0.01 um resolution). | 1. Position laser displacement sensor over needle tip array and measure relative z-height for all 4 needles in the array. 2. Measure tip spherical radius of curvature on all pins using 1000x optical edge-detection profilometry. 3. Advance the ejector stage toward the load cell at programmable velocities (0.5 mm/s, 1.0 mm/s, 2.0 mm/s) to a target stroke of 350 um. 4. Record peak force, force derivative (dF/dt), and steady-state push-up force over 20 repeated cycles. | `Needle tip planarity across all pins <= 3.0 um total indicated runout; needle tip spherical radius = 35.0 um +/- 5.0 um; maximum push-up peak force <= 0.85 N across all cycles; zero plastic deformation or needle tip chipping observed under 1000x magnification.` |
| `TC-WAFER-BACKGRIND-DICING-3-3-02` | **Pick-and-Place Collet Vacuum Seal Integrity, Surface Resistivity, and Die Tilt Verification** | Trek Model 152-1 Resistance Meter with concentric ring micro-probe, SMC ZSE30AF digital vacuum pressure sensor (0 to -101 kPa), and Mitutoyo Quick Vision Pro non-contact optical 3D coordinate measuring system. | 1. Measure surface resistivity of collet contact face using concentric ring probe at 10V test bias. 2. Engage collet to dummy die top surface and apply vacuum pull. 3. Monitor static and dynamic vacuum pressure drop rate over 60 seconds with vacuum solenoid valve isolated. 4. Transfer die to target waffle pack pocket and measure post-placement x/y position offset and angular die tilt using the 3D optical coordinate measuring system over 100 consecutive pick-and-place cycles. | `Collet contact surface point-to-point resistance within 1.0e6 to 1.0e8 ohms; vacuum level maintainable at <= -80.0 kPa with leakage rate < 0.2 kPa/s; die placement angular tilt <= 0.5 degrees; die corner-to-pad chipping count = 0.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact safety glasses, Static-dissipative cleanroom gown with grounding heel straps, Puncture-resistant Kevlar handling undergloves for needle installation
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin puncture from tungsten carbide needle: Immediately wash wound with sterile DI water and mild antiseptic soap for 15 minutes; apply pressure with sterile gauze if bleeding occurs; seek medical evaluation for puncture wound integrity. For IPA exposure: Flush affected eyes with eyewash fountain for 15 minutes; move personnel to fresh air if solvent vapors induce dizziness.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Cleanroom ISO Class 6 laminar downflow hood (>0.45 m/s face velocity) with local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on solvent cleaning bench maintaining minimum face capture velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Contaminated IPA solvent wipes must be sealed in airtight conductive flammable-waste cans. Damaged or worn tungsten carbide micro-needles must be placed into puncture-proof hazardous sharps containers labeled for dedicated heavy-metal reclamation.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Perfluoroalkoxy polymer (PTFE/PFA lubricant)** | `9002-84-0` | Analytical Reagent | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Singulated 180nm DRAM wafer on expanded UV-cured dicing tape (UV exposure dose >= 250 mJ/cm2), kerf streets free of silicon debris, die bond pads unoxidized.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Sorted DRAM dies placed in antistatic waffle pack or gel-pak carrier pockets, die tops and bond pads free of collet abrasion or organic contamination, die backside free of needle puncture marks.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to ambient cleanroom humidity causes native oxide growth on aluminum/copper bond pads (degrading subsequent wire bond shear strength) and adhesive crosslinking recovery on dicing tape, dramatically increasing required needle lift forces and causing die fracture.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful delivery, dimensional validation, mechanical qualification, and ESD verification of the Gen 3 tungsten carbide 4-needle ejector set and ESD-safe Vespel pick-and-place collet tooling assembly for 180nm DRAM die sort operations.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `EJECTOR_COLLET_METROLOGY_REPORT_GEN3.pdf`
- [ ] `FORCE_DISPLACEMENT_VACUUM_CYCLE_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `DIE_SURFACE_INSPECTION_METROLOGY_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Ejector needle array planarity total indicated runout across all 4 pins** | `2.0 um` | +/- 1.0 um | Non-contact laser displacement profilometry over needle array fixture |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Collet contact surface point-to-point electrical resistance** | `5.0e7 ohms` | +/- 4.0e7 ohms | Trek Model 152-1 two-point ESD concentric micro-probe resistance test |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Die pick-and-place mechanical yield across 1000 consecutive cycles without chipping or cracking** | `99.8%` | -0.2% | Automated high-magnification optical kerf and die surface inspection (AOI) per MIL-STD-883 Method 2010 |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit sign-off requires: 100% adherence to ASSERT-01, ASSERT-02, and ASSERT-03; zero detectable backside needle indentation deeper than 0.5 um; zero collet contact scuffing on die top passivation; EHS sharps and solvent disposal protocols validated by site safety officer.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Electrical Die Sort & Micro-Cantilever Probe Card Automated Testing

Automated wafer prober alignment, touch-down overdrive optimization, parametric leakage screening, and wafer-map electronic ink die binning.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated micro-cantilever probe cards for 180nm DRAM testing face extreme mechanical compliance and contact resistance stability trade-offs. The 100 um x 100 um aluminum wire bond/test pads require overdrive depths between 25-50 um to penetrate native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) without micro-cracking underlying low-k or silicon dioxide inter-metal dielectric (IMD) layers. Furthermore, high-speed DRAM signal integrity (tRCD, tRP, tCAS latency validation) demands strict matched transmission lines (<50 ps skew) from the automated test equipment (ATE) pogo pin interface through the multilayer ceramic probe card substrate to the tungsten-rhenium cantilever probe tips.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At wafer sort, distinguishing between DRAM retention failures caused by junction leakage versus gate dielectric leakage requires parametric voltage stepping and accurate temperature control (wafer chuck heated to 85°C for worst-case retention testing). Micro-cantilever tip scrub must be strictly monitored: excessive scrub width (>15 um) risks tearing through the 1.0 um thick top-metal Al-0.5% Cu pad metallization, preventing subsequent ultrasonic wedge or thermosonic ball wire bonding. The probe card must maintain a stable contact resistance (Rc < 1.0 Ohm) across all 64-128 parallel test pins under multi-site touchdown cycles.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom micro-cantilever probe cards fabricated via MEMS or precision Cobra needle assemblies have 8-12 week foundry lead times and high NRE costs ($15,000-$35,000). For an open-source MPW run at 180nm, cantilever blade or epoxy-ring vertical needle probe cards must utilize standardized pitch layouts (standard dual-row perimeter or center-pad DRAM arrays) and standard PXIe-based automated SMU instrumentation to avoid lock-in to proprietary Advantest/Teradyne test heads.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scheduling electrical die sort must strictly observe the queue time window between BEOL passivation pad opening/alloy anneal and post-sort dicing. Incurring probe delays risks severe pad native oxidation, which artificially degrades sorting yield due to false open-circuit/high-Rc errors. Additionally, abrasive probe tip cleaning schedules (ceramic scrub pads every 200 touchdowns) must be integrated into the automated test routine to prevent tip contamination from dragging down tool availability.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dielectric punch-through / pad cratering: Excessive probe needle overdrive (>60 um) induces micro-fractures in the underlying dielectric stacks (SiO2/IMD), causing catastrophic short-circuits to substrate during parametric stress tests.
1. Probe tip aluminum pick-up: Native oxide abrasion causes aluminum transfer onto tungsten-rhenium tips, leading to erratic contact resistance (>5.0 Ohm) and false functional test failures (false-kill binning).
1. Thermal expansion misalignment: Mismatch in coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) between the probe card PCB/ceramic ring and the heated silicon wafer (at 85°C sort temperature) shifts needle touchdown positions outside the 100 um x 100 um pad margin.

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Step chuck to Site 01 alignment test pads (dedicated Kelvin 4-point structure on scribe line). 2. Elevate Z-stage to contact point (Z0) determined by electrical contact detection at 0.1 V threshold. 3. Apply calibrated 35 um overdrive along Z-axis. 4. Force 10.0 mA DC current between Force+ and Force- terminals across top Al-Cu metal pads. 5. Measure differential voltage drop across Sense+ and Sense- needles. 6. Calculate series contact resistance Rc = V_meas / 10.0 mA. 7. Repeat over 10 consecutive touchdowns across wafer quadrants (Center, North, South, East, West). | `Contact resistance Rc <= 0.85 Ohm across all pins; probe scrub mark length between 8.0 um and 15.0 um; zero visual cracking or cratering of underlying dielectric visible under 50x confocal microscope inspection.` |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-02` | **Automated Retention Time and Array Functional Test at Elevated Temperature** | Thermal Chuck Controller (-10°C to +125°C), Automated DRAM Logic/Pattern Generator (PXIe-6570/6571 Digital Instrument), Low-Noise Multi-Channel SMU | 1. Step probe card to active die location and apply 35 um overdrive. 2. Apply VDD = 1.80 V nominal DRAM core supply and VDDQ = 1.80 V I/O supply. 3. Execute March C- memory test pattern across full 180nm 1Mb/4Mb open-source DRAM array at 50 MHz test clock. 4. Write solid '1' data pattern across entire memory bank. 5. Enter pause state (zero refresh cycles) for target retention interval t_RET = 64 ms at 85°C. 6. Read back memory array and log bit error map. 7. Repeat with inverted solid '0' data pattern and 64 ms pause. 8. Assign die to hardware binning register (Bin 1: Pass, Bin 2: Retention Fail, Bin 3: Leakage Fail). | `Total bit errors = 0 across array at t_RET = 64 ms (85°C); standby retention leakage current I_sb <= 12.5 uA at 1.8V VDD; die binning code correctly latched.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom compatible nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses, Anti-static ESD lab coat and conductive ground heel straps, Particulate face mask (Class 100/ISO 5 compatible)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For IPA skin exposure: Flush affected area with clean water for 15 minutes while removing contaminated clothing. For IPA eye contact: Immediately irrigate eyes with eye-wash fountain for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if irritation persists. For mechanical needle puncture: Clean wound with sterile antiseptic, cover with sterile dressing, report sharps injury to cleanroom safety officer.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local chemical extraction hood with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) utilized during manual probe card tip solvent cleaning; automated wafer prober enclosure maintained under continuous HEPA laminar air downflow (ISO Class 5 / Class 100) with dedicated ozone/solvent vapor exhaust ducting.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes and tip-cleaning pads must be disposed of in certified flammables/solvent hazardous waste drums with grounding clips; no direct drain disposal. Sharps (damaged tungsten-rhenium or beryllium-copper cantilever needles) must be collected in puncture-resistant rigid sharps biohazard/metal recycling containers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Electronic Grade IPA)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly annealed top metal Al-0.5% Cu wire bond pads after forming gas alloy anneal (400°C H2/N2) and passivation etch opening, clean and dry with native oxide thickness < 3.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested and scrub-marked bond pads with scrub footprint <= 15% of pad area, free of metallic particulate debris, stored in dry N2 purged FOUP/cassette.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive queue time exposure in ambient air (>240 minutes) drives thick atmospheric moisture-induced oxidation and organic hydrocarbon contamination on aluminum pads, forming a hard, non-conductive Al2O3/hydroxide barrier (>6.0 nm) that causes needle contact failure, excessive probe overdrive damage, and subsequent catastrophic wire-bond lift-off during packaging.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full automated wafer sort execution on 200mm 180nm DRAM wafer using micro-cantilever probe card, validating continuity, leakage, March C- algorithmic memory patterns, and 64ms retention at 85°C, yielding comprehensive wafer bin maps and touch-down integrity verification.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram180_wafer_sort_binmap_lot01.csv`
- [ ] `eds_probe_scrub_metrology_report.pdf`

# Standard Operating Procedure: Custom Micro-Cantilever Probe Card Design & Pad Interface Layout

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Micro-cantilever probe cards introduce parasitic tip inductance (0.8-1.5 nH) and contact resistance variation that can distort high-speed signal integrity during 180nm DRAM row/column access cycle evaluation. Layout must incorporate dedicated Kelvin ground return paths and impedance-matched coplanar microstrip geometries directly to the multi-layer ceramic (MLC) interface.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: DRAM bond pad pitch scaling down to 60-80 um requires cantilever beam metallurgy with high yield strength (e.g., electroformed Ni-Co or W-Re alloys) to prevent beam plastic deformation during 50-75 um overdrive. Scrub mark scrub-length must be kept under 8 um to avoid punch-through of the top Al-0.5%Cu pad metallization and inter-metal dielectric (IMD) microcracking.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom micro-cantilever photolithographic MEMS substrates and precision ceramic space transformers exhibit extended lead times (>12 weeks); localized fabrication must rely on modular PCB interface rings with spring-loaded pogo-pin adapters to standardize test bench docking.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Alignment of probe card delivery with MPW wafer return schedule is critical. Delays in pad design rule verification (DRC) or pad pitch misalignments against wafer sort auto-stepper mapping will bottleneck functional DRAM yield characterization.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dielectric punch-through and microcracking beneath AlCu bond pads caused by excessive probe cantilever overdrive (>75 um) and high contact force (>3 gf/mil).
1. Aluminum-copper oxide accumulation and galvanic transfer on probe needle tips leading to unstable contact resistance (Cres > 2.0 Ohm) and false electrical die sort binning.
1. Probe-to-pad scrubbing misalignment exceeding ±3 um tolerance resulting in adjacent passivation edge chipping and moisture ingress reliability hazards.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-1-01` | **Bond Pad Contact Resistance and Scrub Depth Characterization** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer, FormFactor Auto-Prober Station, and Bruker ContourGT-K Optical 3D Profilometer | 1. Align micro-cantilever probe tips to dedicated four-wire Kelvin test structures on wafer test scribe lines. 2. Apply controlled vertical overdrive stepping from 25 um to 60 um in 5 um increments. 3. Source 10 mA DC and measure four-point contact resistance (Cres) at each overdrive depth across 49 die sites. 4. Retract probe card and measure scrub mark depth, length, and residual pad metal thickness using white-light optical profilometry. | `Four-wire contact resistance Cres must remain <= 0.85 Ohm across >= 98% of measured probe contacts under 50 um overdrive; maximum scrub penetration depth must not exceed 250 nm (retaining >= 70% residual top-metal thickness).` |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-1-02` | **High-Frequency DRAM I/O Signal Attenuation and Crosstalk Isolation** | Keysight N5224B PNA Vector Network Analyzer (10 MHz - 43.5 GHz), Picoprobe calibration substrate CS-5, and high-bandwidth RF prober station | 1. Measure two-port scattering parameters (S11, S21) on adjacent DRAM data (DQ) cantilever probe channels from 100 MHz to 1.5 GHz. 2. Measure near-end crosstalk (NEXT, S31) and far-end crosstalk (FEXT, S41) between parallel cantilever lines under 100 um pitch spacing. 3. Extract loop inductance and inter-pin mutual capacitance across the working frequency envelope. | `Insertion loss S21 must be > -1.2 dB up to 800 MHz; return loss S11 must be < -15 dB up to 800 MHz; adjacent channel crosstalk isolation (S31/S41) must be < -32 dB across the entire operational DRAM band (<= 1 GHz).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Anti-static ESD-dissipative lab coat, Chemical splash apron and face shield during solvent bath tip cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with solvent, wash thoroughly with copious amounts of DI water for 15 minutes. In case of eye contact, flush immediately at eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes holding eyelids open and seek medical evaluation. If solvent vapors are inhaled, remove victim to fresh uncontaminated air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operate probe tip chemical cleaning and ultrasonic degreasing inside dedicated chemical exhaust fume hood with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s); maintain test bay air exchanges >= 25 per hour with HEPA filtration.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent solvent effluents in labeled, dedicated hazardous solvent waste containers (polyethylene drums). Do not mix acetone/IPA with oxidizers or aqueous acids. Seal containers with grounded vapor-tight caps for licensed hazardous chemical disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Acetone** | `67-64-1` | Semiconductor Grade | `99.5%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | Resistivity > 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25C | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched/passivated Al-0.5%Cu DRAM bond pads post-alloy sinter, native aluminum oxide thickness <= 1.8 nm, zero organic fluorocarbon residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: EDS-probed bond pads exhibiting controlled single-scrub impressions; native oxide regrowth <= 3.0 nm; free of probe tip micro-debris or metal peeling.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time accelerates native alumina (Al2O3) passivating oxide thickening (>4.5 nm) and airborne organic contamination, triggering probe contact resistance instability, excessive probe overdrive requirements, and dielectric crack propagation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical sign-off and electrical validation of the custom micro-cantilever probe card and matching 180nm DRAM pad interface layout, ensuring low-resistance Kelvin contact, high-frequency signal integrity, and minimal bond pad damage for automated electrical die sort.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `probe_card_gerber_and_cantilever_mems_layout.gds`
- [ ] `eds_contact_resistance_and_scrub_profilometry_report.csv`
- [ ] `sparameter_signal_integrity_verification_plot.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Probe cantilever tip planarity across full active probe array** | `2.0` | ± 0.5 um | Non-contact laser displacement triangulation across tip array |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Single-pin probe contact resistance (Cres) on Al-0.5%Cu pads under nominal overdrive** | `0.65` | ± 0.15 Ohm | Four-wire Kelvin DC resistance measurement on automated prober |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Probe scrub mark lateral displacement on bond pads** | `6.0` | ± 1.5 um | Automated top-down optical inspection and profilometry on post-EDS pads |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of micro-cantilever probe tips satisfy planarity within <= 2.5 um, achieve stable Kelvin contact resistance <= 0.80 Ohm over 50 consecutive touch-downs without tip deformation or IMD cracking, and complete S-parameter crosstalk isolation verification meeting < -32 dB up to 1.0 GHz.

ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Operate probe tip chemical cleaning and ultrasonic degreasing inside dedicated chemical exhaust fume hood with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s); maintain test bay air exchanges >= 25 per hour with HEPA filtration.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Collect spent solvent effluents in labeled, dedicated hazardous solvent waste containers (polyethylene drums). Do not mix acetone/IPA with oxidizers or aqueous acids. Seal containers with grounded vapor-tight caps for licensed hazardous chemical disposal.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Die Pad Frame & TLM Array Interface Layout Optimization

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: DRC/LVS rule decks must run clean via KLayout/Magic/OpenLane with zero design rule errors. Antenna ratio rules (< 250:1) and substrate tap density checks must pass before GDSII reticle handoff to commercial foundry.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: 3D Crown capacitor ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 (ZAZ) stack must achieve equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) <= 0.8 nm and leakage current < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V. CMP dishing on M1/M2 tungsten/copper features must hold < 15 nm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Commercial foundry MPW (Multi-Project Wafer) shuttle submission has an unmovable tapeout window; GDSII/OASIS files must freeze 21 days prior. Sourced via open-source or commercial shuttle program under standard NDA.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 60-120 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: CRITICAL (A single DRC rule deck discrepancy or LVS short-circuit ruins the entire multi-thousand dollar commercial shuttle run and incurs a 4-6 month spin delay).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. DRC/LVS hierarchy discrepancy causing undetected metal-to-metal bridging or floating substrate tap.
1. ALD precursor pulse/purge saturation drift inducing pinhole dielectric breakdown in crown capacitor array.
1. Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) over-polish causing severe interconnect erosion and open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

Perform high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V sweep to extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and dielectric breakdown voltage. | `ALD step coverage >= 95% (Pass); EOT <= 0.8 nm (Pass); Dielectric leakage < 1.0 fA/cell at 1.0V (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom bunny suit with conductive ESD booties, Pyrophoric precursor handling apron and dual-layer fluoropolymer gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and UV-blocking safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Pyrophoric precursor emergency: TMA spontaneously ignites upon contact with air or moisture! Do NOT use water on metal alkyl fires. Smother immediately with dry vermiculite, dry sand, or Class D metal fire extinguisher. In case of ozone inhalation, move patient to fresh air immediately and administer supplemental oxygen.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Ultra-high vacuum ALD exhaust manifold connected to dedicated point-of-use thermal decomposition burn-box and wet chemical scrubber. Continuous gas leak detection monitors for TMA/TEMAZ and ozone.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent ALD bubbler purging into mineral oil bubblers with inert argon ballast. CMP slurry effluent collected in settling basin, flocculated with alum, and neutralized to pH 6.5-8.0.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trimethylaluminum (TMA)** | `75-24-1` | Electronic Grade (99.999% trace metals) | `Pyrophoric liquid ALD precursor` |
| **Tetrakis(ethylmethylamino)zirconium (TEMAZ)** | `175923-04-3` | High-purity ALD grade | `Liquid precursor for ZrO2 dielectric` |
| **Ozone (O3)** | `10028-15-6` | Generated in-situ from UHP O2 | `15-20 wt% in O2 carrier gas (Strong Oxidizer)` |
| **Silica / Ceria CMP Slurry** | `1344-28-1` | Semiconductor Colloidal CMP grade | `15-30 wt% colloidal abrasive slurry` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched 3D crown capacitor trench structure post-DHF strip, completely free of native oxide.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Uniform ALD ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 high-k dielectric stack with TiN top electrode encapsulation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Air exposure exceeding 20 minutes allows uncontrolled spontaneous SiO2 interfacial layer regrowth (> 0.4 nm), which severely increases Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) and drastically degrades bitcell storage capacitance.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Die Pad Frame & TLM Array Interface Layout Optimization: PDK setup, physical verification rule decks, and full-chip GDSII layouts pass 100% DRC/LVS sign-off and satisfy foundry commercial tapeout design rules.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Die Pad Frame Boundary DRC/LVS Rule Definition & Pitch Sizing

**Document ID:** `SOP-DRAM180-LAY-007`  
**Classification:** Technical / Circuit Design & Tapeout Integration  
**Target Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180 nm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Physical Hierarchy

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Die Pad Frame Sizing  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Boundary Seal Ring   │
│        Spacing         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Passivation Opening   │
│       DRC Rules        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    LVS Port and Pin    │
│      Association       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Cantilever Probe    │
│       Card Pitch       │
│       Validation       │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Physical Layout & Pitch Sizing Targets

```text
                        Pad Frame Physical Dimensions   
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │░░░░░░░                           │
Seal Ring Clear (um)┤░░░░░░░                           │
                    │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                │
      Pad Pitch (um)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                │
    Pad Opening (um)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                    │
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                    │
  Array Pitch F (nm)┤██████████████████████████████████│
                    │██████████████████████████████████│
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0      45       90      135    180 
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Active Core Boundary & Scribe Line Definition:**
   - Establish the primary die boundary relative to the $F = 180\text{ nm}$ technology baseline (where $8F^2$ folded bitline cell area is $0.259\,\mu\text{m}^2$ and bitline/wordline pitch is $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$).
   - Construct a perimeter continuous Seal Ring (Metal-1 through Top-Metal stack tied with continuous contact/via rings) at a minimum boundary clearance of $\ge 30\,\mu\text{m}$ from the internal active core circuitry and test structure arrays (TLM).

2. **Top-Level Metallization & Pad Sizing:**
   - Allocate Top-Metal (e.g., Metal-5 or thick Al/Cu layer) for wire bond and cantilever probe landing pads.
   - Lay out bond pad metal dimensions to $80\,\mu\text{m} \times 80\,\mu\text{m}$ with a centered Passivation Opening (PAD opening) of $70\,\mu\text{m} \times 70\,\mu\text{m}$, yielding a minimum passivation-to-metal enclosure of $5\,\mu\text{m}$.
   - Define a pad-to-pad center pitch of $90\,\mu\text{m}$ (minimum $20\,\mu\text{m}$ metal spacing between adjacent pad envelopes) to ensure cantilever probe card clearance during Electrical Die Sort (EDS).

3. **DRC Rule Deck Encoding & Layer Sizing:**
   - Encode design rule check (DRC) decks enforcing:
     - `PAD.ENCLOSURE`: Top-Metal enclosure of passivation window $\ge 5.0\,\mu\text{m}$.
     - `PAD.SPACING`: Adjacent passivation opening spacing $\ge 20.0\,\mu\text{m}$.
     - `PAD.SEAL_CLEARANCE`: Passivation opening to outer edge of Seal Ring $\ge 40.0\,\mu\text{m}$.
     - `ESD.CLEARANCE`: High-voltage and I/O pad metal clearance to internal $180\text{ nm}$ thin-gate array access NMOS oxides ($t_{\text{ox}} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$) $\ge 15.0\,\mu\text{m}$.

4. **LVS Extraction & Port Connectivity Layer Setup:**
   - Attach explicit layout text pins (`PORT` / `PIN` layer) to the Top-Metal landing layer of each pad matching the exact netlist schematic symbol names (e.g., `VDD`, `VSS`, `VPP`, `VBB`, `BL_TEST`, `WL_EN`).
   - Run layout-versus-schematic (LVS) extraction ensuring no short/open circuits between adjacent pad pitches and confirming 1-to-1 pin-to-node mapping across pad frame boundaries.

5. **EDS Micro-Cantilever Probe Card Pitch Validation:**
   - Perform automated clearance verification against the EDS micro-cantilever probe needle array. Verify probe scrub wipe mark clearance does not breach the $5\,\mu\text{m}$ passivation enclosure boundary under $\pm 3\,\mu\text{m}$ prober step accuracy.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Inspection Item | Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pad Opening Geometry** | Passivation Window Area | $70.0 \times 70.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated DRC (`PAD.WIDTH` / `PAD.AREA`) |
| **Inter-Pad Center Pitch** | Linear Pad Center-to-Center Spacing | $\ge 90.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated DRC (`PAD.PITCH`) |
| **Passivation Enclosure** | Top-Metal Boundary Overlap | $\ge 5.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated DRC (`PAD.ENCLOSURE`) |
| **LVS Net Connectivity** | Pin-to-Schematic Consistency | $0$ (Zero Mismatches) | Errors / Discrepancies | Cadence Pegasus / Siemens Calibre LVS |
| **Seal Ring Clearance** | Outer Pad Edge to Scribe Seal Ring | $\ge 30.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated DRC (`SEAL_RING.SPACING`) |

---

### 5. Context & Literature Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - $F = 180\text{ nm}$ technology baseline; folded bitline memory array architecture; access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - Bitline and wordline pitch specifications of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$; gate dielectric dry oxidation thickness of $\approx 3.5\text{ nm}$.
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets:**
  - Folded bitline $8F^2$ footprint area ($0.259\,\mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$); storage node capacitance budget $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$), ensuring proper noise immunity against coupling and EDS pad parasitics.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In 180nm commercial MPW tapeouts, pad pitch sizing directly couples probe-card touchdown scrub mechanics to ESD rail parasitic inductances. Transitioning to a high-density pad frame (<80um pitch) induces significant L*di/dt ground bounce during synchronous array read cycles (sense amp latching across 28fF storage nodes), requiring strict DRC inclusion of distributed power/ground mesh ties and Kelvin-force sense pairs within the scribe-line boundary layout.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: BEOL passivation opening DRC must balance micro-cantilever probe tip scrub area against crack-stop seal ring margin. In 180nm top-metal (AlCu M5/M6) pads, a 60x60 um open passivation window with an 8 um pad-to-seal ring keep-out is mandatory to prevent probe scrub impact shear stresses from delaminating underlying ILD stacks (FSG/TEOS) directly above sensitive peripheral decoder circuitry and stacked capacitor top-plate bias nodes.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Micro-cantilever probe card suppliers require standardized pad pitch (minimum 75 um inline or 50/100 um staggered) with guaranteed Cu/AlCu surface coplanarity. Failure to standardize probe pitch across MPW runs increases tooling NRE by >$35,000 per bespoke cantilever card and introduces lead times exceeding 14 weeks due to micro-machined MEMS needle array fabrication constraints.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The pad frame boundary DRC/LVS deck must freeze 3 weeks ahead of tapeout sign-off. Any post-tapeout modification to pad boundary coordinates propagates invalid LVS connectivity downstream to EDS test vector mapping, jeopardizing the wafer sort milestone window and risking MPW lot rejection by the foundry mask house.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die edge seal-ring delamination and micro-cracking induced by cantilever overtravel scrub exceeding the 12 um margin from the pad boundary to the passivation edge.
1. LVS text-port open/short discrepancy on dual-pad Kelvin connections leading to automated prober pin assignment misalignments and electrical overstress (EOS) of 180nm gate dielectric (3.5nm SiO2).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-1-1-1-01` | **Automated Die Pad Pitch and Passivation DRC/LVS Rule Conformance Test** | Siemens Calibre nmDRC/Calibre nmLVS Physical Verification Suite (v2024.2) and Cadence Pegasus Verification Engine | 1. Execute DRC rule run checking rule PAD.S.1 (pad-to-pad metal spacing >= 20.0 um) and PAD.P.1 (pad center-to-center pitch >= 80.0 um inline). 2. Execute passivation enclosure rule PAD.E.1 (METTOP overlap of PAD_OPEN >= 5.0 um). 3. Run hierarchical LVS check comparing layout netlist against golden DRAM pinout schematic. 4. Extract pad boundary coordinate table and calculate worst-case cantilever scrub margin relative to die boundary. | `Zero DRC violations across all PAD.* rule groups; LVS report clean (0 errors, 0 warnings, nets and instances match 100%); pad center-to-center pitch measures exactly 80.00 um ± 0.05 um.` |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-1-1-1-02` | **Micro-Cantilever Probe Tip Landing & Contact Resistance Validation** | Cascade Microtech / FormFactor Semi-Automated Wafer Prober (Summit 12000), Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer, Mitutoyo FS70 Optical Metrology Microscope | 1. Align cantilever probe card needles to the peripheral test pad frame using optical alignment fiducials. 2. Apply controlled probe touchdown with 50 um overtravel overdrive. 3. Measure four-wire Kelvin contact resistance (Rc) on 32 consecutive power, ground, and I/O test pad pairs. 4. Retract needles, unload wafer, and perform optical inspection of scrub marks to measure scrub center distance from passivation opening edges. | `Contact resistance Rc <= 0.35 Ohm per pad interface; probe scrub mark contained entirely within pad opening with minimum edge clearance >= 6.0 um; zero dielectric fracturing observed.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom Bunny Suit with ESD Grounding Snaps, Nitrile Cleanroom Gloves (12-mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 Approved UV/Chemical Safety Goggles, ESD Safe Conductive Cleanroom Boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with solvents, flush affected area with copiously flowing DI water for at least 15 minutes. For eye splash, rinse immediately at the cleanroom eyewash station holding eyelids open; seek immediate medical assessment if corneal irritation persists. If vapors are inhaled, move subject to fresh air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober load port and solvent wipe bench must operate under active local exhaust ventilation (LEV) providing face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM), connected to an approved cleanroom VOC scrubbed exhaust system.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent-soaked wipes and tip cleaning residues must be bagged in static-dissipative polyethylene and disposed of via segregated hazardous solvent waste collection; aqueous rinse effluent routed to cleanroom acid-solvent industrial neutralization plant.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched and annealed top-metal AlCu (0.5% Cu) pad surface with clean passivation etch boundary, free of organic photoresist polymer residue, native oxide thickness <= 2.5 nm.

critics.systems_engineer: In 180nm commercial MPW tapeouts, pad pitch sizing directly couples probe-card touchdown scrub mechanics to ESD rail parasitic inductances. Transitioning to a high-density pad frame (<80um pitch) induces significant L*di/dt ground bounce during synchronous array read cycles (sense amp latching across 28fF storage nodes), requiring strict DRC inclusion of distributed power/ground mesh ties and Kelvin-force sense pairs within the scribe-line boundary layout.
critics.domain_expert: BEOL passivation opening DRC must balance micro-cantilever probe tip scrub area against crack-stop seal ring margin. In 180nm top-metal (AlCu M5/M6) pads, a 60x60 um open passivation window with an 8 um pad-to-seal ring keep-out is mandatory to prevent probe scrub impact shear stresses from delaminating underlying ILD stacks (FSG/TEOS) directly above sensitive peripheral decoder circuitry and stacked capacitor top-plate bias nodes.
critics.supply_chain: Micro-cantilever probe card suppliers require standardized pad pitch (minimum 75 um inline or 50/100 um staggered) with guaranteed Cu/AlCu surface coplanarity. Failure to standardize probe pitch across MPW runs increases tooling NRE by >$35,000 per bespoke cantilever card and introduces lead times exceeding 14 weeks due to micro-machined MEMS needle array fabrication constraints.
critics.laya_pm: The pad frame boundary DRC/LVS deck must freeze 3 weeks ahead of tapeout sign-off. Any post-tapeout modification to pad boundary coordinates propagates invalid LVS connectivity downstream to EDS test vector mapping, jeopardizing the wafer sort milestone window and risking MPW lot rejection by the foundry mask house.
critical_failure_modes: Die edge seal-ring delamination and micro-cracking induced by cantilever overtravel scrub exceeding the 12 um margin from the pad boundary to the passivation edge.
LVS text-port open/short discrepancy on dual-pad Kelvin connections leading to automated prober pin assignment misalignments and electrical overstress (EOS) of 180nm gate dielectric (3.5nm SiO2).
