# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Overdrive Touchdown & Scrub-Mark Metrology Characterization

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Step 1: Contact     │
│      Detection Z0      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 2: Calibrated   │
│  Overdrive Touchdown   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 3: In-Situ DC   │
│  Kelvin Contact Check  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 4: Automated    │
│     Optical Scrub      │
│       Metrology        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 5: Post-Scrub   │
│  Quality Disposition   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Purpose & Process Flow
This SOP specifies the automated procedure for executing controlled cantilever probe card touchdowns, establishing stable electrical contact across top-metal aluminum bonding pads ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$), and quantifying scrub-mark geometry and oxide punch-through without jeopardizing underlying BEOL dielectrics or subsequent wire-bonding assembly.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Optical-to-Chuck Z-Reference Calibration ($Z_0$)**:
   - Initialize automated pattern recognition on the wafer prober (pattern recognition accuracy $\le \pm 0.5\,\mu\text{m}$).
   - Align probe card needle tips to the fiducials of the $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum bonding pads.
   - Execute micro-stepped vertical approach ($Z$-step = $1.0\,\mu\text{m}$) at chuck temperature $T = 25^\circ\text{C}$ (ambient sort) or elevated sort temperature up to $85^\circ\text{C}$ (matching DRAM cell retention qualifications).
   - Detect initial physical touch ($Z_0$) using dual optical beam deflection and low-compliance current sensing ($I_{\text{sense}} = 100\,\mu\text{A}$ at $V_{\text{sense}} = 50\,\text{mV}$).

2. **Controlled Overdrive (OD) Touchdown Execution**:
   - From established electrical zero $Z_0$, command prober Z-stage to advance through programmed overdrive:
     - **Nominal Overdrive**: $\Delta Z = 65\,\mu\text{m}$ (Operating envelope: $50\,\mu\text{m} \le \Delta Z \le 75\,\mu\text{m}$).
     - **Touchdown Velocity**: $v_z = 2.5\,\text{mm/s}$ with programmable deceleration profile to prevent needle bounce.
   - Maintain mechanical dwell time of $t_{\text{dwell}} = 150\,\text{ms}$ to allow needle flexure and horizontal oxide scrubbing across the pad surface.

3. **In-Situ DC Kelvin Contact Resistance Verification**:
   - Force $I_{\text{force}} = 10.0\,\text{mA}$ through force/sense probe pairs on dedicated calibration pads.
   - Measure 4-wire DC Kelvin contact resistance ($R_c$). Confirm native $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ rupture is achieved without micro-cracking ILD layers.

4. **Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) & High-Resolution Metrology**:
   - Retract prober chuck to $Z_0 - 500\,\mu\text{m}$.
   - Position high-magnification automated optical review camera (optical resolution $0.1\,\mu\text{m/pixel}$) over sampled test pads across center, mid-radius, and wafer edge dies.
   - Execute confocal/interferometric surface profile scan to extract:
     - Scrub length ($L_{\text{scrub}}$) along the cantilever scrub axis.
     - Scrub width ($W_{\text{scrub}}$) across needle transverse axis.
     - Scrub depth ($D_{\text{scrub}}$) relative to pristine Al pad surface.
     - Residual pad clearance margin from scrub edge to pad passivation boundary ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ pad aperture).

5. **Scrub Disposition & Needle Maintenance Feedback**:
   - Cross-check scrub-mark coordinates against automated bounding limits. If scrub center drifts $> 5.0\,\mu\text{m}$ from pad target center, trigger automated needle tip cleaning block (ceramic abrasive scrub pad) and realign probe card.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                                                        
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
    Pad Margin┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
              │▒▒                                      │
Contact R (Rc)┤▒▒                                      │
   Scrub Depth┤▓▓                                      │
              │▓▓                                      │
  Scrub Length┤████████████████████████████████        │
              │████████████████████████████████        │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
               0         7        14       21        28 
```

1. **Scrub Mark Length ($L_{\text{scrub}}$)**:
   - **Target Metric**: $18.0\,\mu\text{m} \le L_{\text{scrub}} \le 25.0\,\mu\text{m}$ (Nominal: $22.5\,\mu\text{m}$) at $65\,\mu\text{m}$ nominal overdrive.
2. **Maximum Scrub Depth ($D_{\text{scrub}}$)**:
   - **Target Metric**: $0.20\,\mu\text{m} \le D_{\text{scrub}} \le 0.50\,\mu\text{m}$ ($\le 40\%$ of top aluminum metal thickness; zero ILD punch-through or barrier exposure).
3. **DC Kelvin Contact Resistance ($R_c$)**:
   - **Target Metric**: $R_c \le 1.0\,\Omega$ per probe tip across all signal and supply pins (Mean $R_c \le 0.85\,\Omega$, $\sigma \le 0.15\,\Omega$).
4. **Pad Perimeter Clearance Margin**:
   - **Target Metric**: Residual unscrubbed pad perimeter margin $\ge 25.0\,\mu\text{m}$ from the edge of the scrub mark to the passivation opening boundary on all $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ pads (guaranteeing sufficient pristine area for $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter wire bonding).

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations
- **Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - *Context applied*: DRAM bonding pads are defined as $100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum squares accommodating $25\,\mu\text{m}$ diameter gold or Al-1% Si bond wires. Maintaining scrub length $\le 25\,\mu\text{m}$ and residual pad margin $\ge 25.0\,\mu\text{m}$ prevents bond interface separation, ensuring downstream compliance with Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 pull test criteria ($\ge 4.0\,\text{grams-force}$).
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - *Context applied*: DRAM array data retention requires $> 64\,\text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ with capacitor budget of $25$ to $30\,\text{fF/cell}$. Overdrive touch stress must not generate mechanical micro-fractures propagating into underlying BEOL interconnects or stacked cell dielectric films.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - *Context applied*: Cell access transistor channel geometry ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$) and strict sub-threshold leakage limit ($< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$) dictate that electrical contact screening must maintain low series resistance ($R_c \le 1.0\,\Omega$) to prevent voltage drop artifacts during bitline sensing and retention tests.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated vertical Z-overdrive calibration requires closed-loop laser displacement or piezo-interferometric chuck position verification. At 180nm BEOL nodes, excessive Z-travel (>65 um overdrive beyond electrical touch) induces severe mechanical stress in the underlying ILD (inter-layer dielectric) low-k or oxide stacks beneath the top Al-0.5%Cu/TiN bond pads. The prober motion controller must guarantee encoder repeatability within ±0.5 um and synchronous optical edge detection to prevent probe needle skidding outside the 60x60 um passivation opening window.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Scrub-mark geometry directly governs subsequent wire-bonding shear strength and flip-chip solder wettability. Probe scrub must effectively penetrate the native Al2O3 passivation layer (~4-6 nm thick) to yield contact resistance Rc < 0.35 Ohm per pad without puncturing the ~800 nm thick Top Metal (M5/M6) layer. If the tungsten-rhenium (WRe) or Cu-alloy cantilever probe tip scrub depth exceeds 250 nm or leaves gouges closer than 5 um to the passivation sidewall, catastrophic dielectric cracking and inter-metal shorting under thermal cycling will occur.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom micro-cantilever and vertical cobra-probe cards for 180nm DRAM test pads exhibit lead times of 12 to 16 weeks from regional precision tooling vendors. Tip wear from high-repetition touchdown (>50,000 touchdowns) degrades tip radius from 12 um to >25 um, shifting scrub kinematics. Sourcing dedicated tungsten-carbide (WC) abrasive cleaning sheets and automated on-line optical tip inspection modules is required to extend probe card lifecycle and mitigate replacement bottleneck risks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Overdrive characterization must be scheduled strictly within the 4-hour window post-wafer-unsealing to prevent uncontrolled ambient pad oxidation from skewing overdrive vs. contact resistance curves. Automated AOI scrub-mark inspection recipe generation must not consume more than 8% total prober cycle time during production lot execution.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. ILD cracking and micro-fracturing beneath Al-0.5%Cu pads caused by excessive probe card over-travel (>75 um overdrive) exceeding silicon fracture toughness.
1. Passivation peeling or barrier metal breach caused by cantilever scrub slide overrunning the pad edge (>12 um scrub length at 50 um nominal pad dimension).
1. Intermittent high contact resistance (Rc > 1.5 Ohm) and open/short false failures resulting from insufficient overdrive (<30 um) failing to break native oxide.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-1-2-01` | **Automated Z-Overdrive Touchdown Sensitivity and Contact Resistance Characterization** | Automated Wafer Prober (TEL Precio / FormFactor Summit 12000), Sub-micron Z-piezo Stage with Heidenhain Encoder, Keithley 2410 SMU, High-Resolution In-Situ Top-Down CCD Microscope | 1. Position cantilever probe card array over dedicated Kelvin 4-wire test structures on die coordinates (X0, Y0).\n2. Lower Z-chuck towards probe tips at 50 um/s until electrical contact (first touch point, Z0) is established at I_sense = 1.0 mA.\n3. Stepwise increment overdrive depth from +10 um to +60 um in discrete 10 um increments.\n4. At each overdrive step, inject 10.0 mA DC test current across force-sense terminals and record contact resistance (Rc) with 10 integration cycles.\n5. Retract chuck to Z0 - 500 um and record permanent pad impression using high-resolution in-situ optics. | `Stable contact resistance Rc <= 0.35 Ohm reached at overdrive <= 45 um; contact resistance variation sigma(Rc) <= 0.05 Ohm across 10 consecutive touchdowns; no lift-off or contact bounce detected during Z-settling (< 5 ms).` |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-1-2-02` | **Automated Scrub-Mark Dimension, Scrub Length, and Indentation Depth Metrology** | Automated Optical Defect Inspection (AOI) Station with 50x NA 0.8 objective, Laser Confocal 3D Profilometer / White-Light Optical Interferometer (Zygo NewView 9000) | 1. Execute automated stage scan across a 9-point wafer matrix (center, mid-radius, wafer edge) targeting probed DRAM bond pads.\n2. Capture brightfield and darkfield 2D micrographs at 0.1 um/pixel optical resolution.\n3. Run image edge-detection algorithm to extract scrub-mark length (L_scrub), scrub-mark width (W_scrub), and distance to passivation perimeter (D_edge).\n4. Switch to 3D confocal scanning mode to profile Z-depth profile across scrub trench centerlines.\n5. Calculate maximum indentation depth (Z_scrub) and aluminum pile-up volume at scrub exit apex. | `Scrub-mark length L_scrub within 8.0 um to 16.0 um at 45 um overdrive; scrub width W_scrub within 4.0 um to 8.0 um; minimum clearance from scrub edge to passivation sidewall D_edge >= 8.0 um; maximum penetration depth Z_scrub <= 250 nm (ensuring >= 550 nm intact top metal underpad margin).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile Gloves (chemical-resistant, powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact-resistant safety glasses, Full static-dissipative ESD lab coat and ESD grounding wrist strap, N95 particulate respirator mask for manual mechanical maintenance or abrasive probe cleaning operations
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with copious volumes of clean water or isotonic saline for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek ophthalmic medical evaluation. Skin Contact: Remove contaminated ESD garments and wash skin thoroughly with soap and water. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh cleanroom air supply; administer oxygen if respiratory distress occurs.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local chemical extraction hood with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) required for IPA solvent wipe down of probe chuck and cleaning blocks; prober chamber operates under Class 100 laminar downflow (0.45 m/s +/- 20%).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA solvent wipes and residue in dedicated flammable, grounded metal containment bins. Dispose of used tungsten/ceramic abrasive scrub cleaning pads via solid hazardous metal-bearing electronic scrap streams in compliance with local environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 / Electronic Grade | `99.8% w/w` |
| **Deionized Water (DI H2O)** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-Pure Water (UPW), 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 deg C | `100.0% v/v` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly fab-out 180nm DRAM wafers with native Al2O3 thickness <= 2.5 nm on M5/M6 bond pads, free of organic photoresist residues and post-plasma etching fluorinated polymers.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probed bond pads exhibiting controlled tungsten-cantilever scrub footprints with residual aluminum thickness >= 550 nm, passivated against galvanic corrosion, ready for full DC/AC functional bitmapping sort.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in cleanroom air leads to uncontrolled growth of native Al2O3 (>5.0 nm) and airborne molecular contamination (siloxanes/organics), causing scrub skidding, high contact resistance (Rc > 1.0 Ohm), contact chatter, and pad cratering upon compensated excessive overdrive.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete metrological validation and parameterization of automated overdrive touchdown depth (35-50 um) and probe needle scrub-mark morphology for 180nm DRAM open-source chip wafers, guaranteeing stable contact resistance <= 0.35 Ohm without dielectric damage.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `overdrive_rc_characterization_matrix.csv`
- [ ] `scrub_mark_confocal_metrology_report.pdf`
- [ ] `pad_scrub_morphology_wafermap.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum probe needle indentation scrub depth into aluminum top metal pad** | `180 nm` | +/- 50 nm | 3D optical white-light interferometry and laser confocal surface profiling across 9-site wafer sample |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Minimum clearance distance between outer scrub-mark boundary and bond pad passivation edge** | `12.0 um` | +/- 3.0 um (lower limit >= 8.0 um) | High-resolution brightfield automated optical inspection (AOI) edge-detection image processing |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Statistical process capability Cpk >= 1.67 for scrub length and scrub position across 100 consecutive die touchdowns, with 0 instances of pad cracking, zero passivation encroachment, and stable contact resistance <= 0.35 Ohm across all tested DRAM I/O and power pads.

testcases.instrumentation: Automated Optical Defect Inspection (AOI) Station with 50x NA 0.8 objective, Laser Confocal 3D Profilometer / White-Light Optical Interferometer (Zygo NewView 9000)
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer underwent TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-1-2-01 touchdown characterization matrix; wafer vacuum chucked; autofocus and optical illumination calibrated on clean, unprobed aluminum reference pads.
testcases.procedure:
1. Execute automated stage scan across a 9-point wafer matrix (center, mid-radius, wafer edge) targeting probed DRAM bond pads.
2. Capture brightfield and darkfield 2D micrographs at 0.1 um/pixel optical resolution.
3. Run image edge-detection algorithm to extract scrub-mark length (L_scrub), scrub-mark width (W_scrub), and distance to passivation perimeter (D_edge).
4. Switch to 3D confocal scanning mode to profile Z-depth profile across scrub trench centerlines.
5. Calculate maximum indentation depth (Z_scrub) and aluminum pile-up volume at scrub exit apex.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Scrub-mark length L_scrub within 8.0 um to 16.0 um at 45 um overdrive; scrub width W_scrub within 4.0 um to 8.0 um; minimum clearance from scrub edge to passivation sidewall D_edge >= 8.0 um; maximum penetration depth Z_scrub <= 250 nm (ensuring >= 550 nm intact top metal underpad margin).

ppe_required: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile Gloves (chemical-resistant, powder-free)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact-resistant safety glasses
Full static-dissipative ESD lab coat and ESD grounding wrist strap
N95 particulate respirator mask for manual mechanical maintenance or abrasive probe cleaning operations

cas_chemicals.name: Deionized Water (DI H2O)
cas_chemicals.purity_grade: Ultra-Pure Water (UPW), 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 deg C

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with copious volumes of clean water or isotonic saline for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek ophthalmic medical evaluation. Skin Contact: Remove contaminated ESD garments and wash skin thoroughly with soap and water. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh cleanroom air supply; administer oxygen if respiratory distress occurs.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Local chemical extraction hood with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) required for IPA solvent wipe down of probe chuck and cleaning blocks; prober chamber operates under Class 100 laminar downflow (0.45 m/s +/- 20%).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Collect spent IPA solvent wipes and residue in dedicated flammable, grounded metal containment bins. Dispose of used tungsten/ceramic abrasive scrub cleaning pads via solid hazardous metal-bearing electronic scrap streams in compliance with local environmental regulations.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly fab-out 180nm DRAM wafers with native Al2O3 thickness <= 2.5 nm on M5/M6 bond pads, free of organic photoresist residues and post-plasma etching fluorinated polymers.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Probed bond pads exhibiting controlled tungsten-cantilever scrub footprints with residual aluminum thickness >= 550 nm, passivated against galvanic corrosion, ready for full DC/AC functional bitmapping sort.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding queue time in cleanroom air leads to uncontrolled growth of native Al2O3 (>5.0 nm) and airborne molecular contamination (siloxanes/organics), causing scrub skidding, high contact resistance (Rc > 1.0 Ohm), contact chatter, and pad cratering upon compensated excessive overdrive.

expected_result.summary: Complete metrological validation and parameterization of automated overdrive touchdown depth (35-50 um) and probe needle scrub-mark morphology for 180nm DRAM open-source chip wafers, guaranteeing stable contact resistance <= 0.35 Ohm without dielectric damage.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Kelvin contact resistance Rc across probe-to-pad interface at operational overdrive
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated 4-wire Kelvin DC parametric measurement using Keithley 2410 SMU at 10 mA forced current

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum probe needle indentation scrub depth into aluminum top metal pad
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: 3D optical white-light interferometry and laser confocal surface profiling across 9-site wafer sample

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Minimum clearance distance between outer scrub-mark boundary and bond pad passivation edge
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-resolution brightfield automated optical inspection (AOI) edge-detection image processing

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Statistical process capability Cpk >= 1.67 for scrub length and scrub position across 100 consecutive die touchdowns, with 0 instances of pad cracking, zero passivation encroachment, and stable contact resistance <= 0.35 Ohm across all tested DRAM I/O and power pads.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## ESD Protection Diode Forward-Bias Continuity & Open/Short Contact Screening
**Document ID:** `SOP-EDS-180NM-MET-007`  
**Level:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout — DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Process Stage:** BEOL Multi-Layer Metallization, Wafer Sort & Packaging > Electrical Die Sort (EDS)  
**Knowledge Record:** [esd_diode_continuity_screening_sop.md](./docs/knowledge/esd_diode_continuity_screening_sop.md)

---

### 1. Architectural Context & Objectives
Prior to subjecting the 180nm DRAM die to core operating voltage ($V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$) or generating boosted wordline gate drive potentials via the 4-stage Dickson charge pump ($V_{PP} \ge 2.5\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$), automated electrical probe-to-pad continuity and electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection network integrity must be screened.

This procedure forces a calibrated low DC current through the on-chip dual-rail ESD clamp diodes (pad-to-$V_{SS}$ and pad-to-$V_{DD}$) to rapidly identify:
1. Lifted or misaligned micro-cantilever probe tips (Open circuits).
2. Scribe line, metallization bridging, or blown ESD junctions (Short circuits).
3. Verified physical contact resistance before applying functional DC test patterns.

---

### 2. Workflow & Diagnostic Flowchart

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Start: Wafer Chuck   │
│    Loaded & Aligned    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Ground VSS /      │
│    Substrate Common    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Force Test Current:   │
│   IF = -100 uA to -1   │
│           mA           │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Measure Voltage Drop  │
│       VF on Pad        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────◇───────────┐
│    Evaluate Voltage    │
│         Window         │
└────────────◇───────────┘
             │
             ├────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
             │                                                │
  VF < -0.2 V│                                                │ -0.9 V <= VF <= -0.5 V
             ├────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
             ▼                                                ▼                                                ▼ VF > -0.9 V / Clamp
┌────────────────────────┐                       ┌────────────────────────┐                       ┌────────────────────────┐
│  FAIL: Short to GND /  │                       │    PASS: Intact ESD    │                       │  FAIL: Open Contact /  │
│      Low-R Bridge      │                       │     Diode & Probe      │                       │     Lifted Needle      │
└────────────────────────┘                       └────────────┬───────────┘                       └────────────────────────┘
                                                              │
             ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Proceed to VDD Clamp  │
│       Test / DC        │
│      Parametrics       │
└────────────────────────┘
```

#### Screening Voltage Distribution Window
```text
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Open (> -0.9V/Vclamp)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
         Nominal Pass┤████████████████                 │
                     │████████████████                 │
      Short (< -0.2V)┤░░░░░                            │
                     │░░░░░                            │
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                    0.00    0.38    0.75    1.12   1.50 
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step SOP Execution Procedure

1. **Chuck Loading & Environmental Stabilization**:
   - Secure the 180nm DRAM wafer onto the automated wafer prober thermal chuck under vacuum ($> 650\text{ mmHg}$).
   - Set chuck temperature to sort specification ($25^\circ\text{C} \pm 1^\circ\text{C}$ room ambient or elevated $85^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$ hot sort).
2. **Micro-Cantilever Touchdown & Overdrive**:
   - Execute optical pattern recognition alignment to probe pads.
   - Lower probe needles onto the bond pads with a calibrated overdrive $Z_{\text{OD}} = 35\,\mu\text{m}\text{ to }50\,\mu\text{m}$ to ensure stable scrub through surface aluminum oxide.
3. **Tester Ground Reference Initialization**:
   - Force all tester grounding matrix paths, chip $V_{SS}$ pins, and p-type silicon substrate contact lines to system ground ($0.00\text{ V}$).
4. **Pad-to-$V_{SS}$ Forward Diode Screening**:
   - Program the Parametric Measurement Unit (PMU / SMU) to Current-Force Voltage-Measure (FVMU) mode.
   - Force negative forward bias current $I_F = -100\,\mu\text{A}$ into every device pin under test (DQ, Addr, Control, Clock).
   - Set tester SMU voltage compliance ceiling to $V_{\text{clamp}} = -1.50\text{ V}$.
   - Wait $t_{\text{settle}} = 1.5\text{ ms}$ for lead settling, then sample pad voltage $V_F$.
5. **Pad-to-$V_{DD}$ Forward Diode Screening**:
   - Tie $V_{DD}$ rail to common ground ($0.00\text{ V}$) with $V_{SS}$ floating.
   - Force positive bias current $I_F = +100\,\mu\text{A}$ with positive compliance $V_{\text{clamp}} = +1.50\text{ V}$.
   - Sample upper clamping p-n junction forward drop $V_F$.
6. **Binning & Execution Gating**:
   - If any pin violates pass thresholds, record pin index, abort parametric sequence, and mark die as open/short scrap (Bin 8/9).
   - Only upon 100% pin pass may the prober advance to full DC parametric tests, cell leakage screening ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$), and high-voltage wordline pump operation ($V_{PP} \ge 2.5\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Measurement Condition | Lower Limit | Nominal Target | Upper Limit | Unit | Disposition on Fail |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Forward Diode Voltage ($V_F$)** | Forced $I_F = -100\,\mu\text{A}$, $V_{SS} = 0\text{ V}$ | $-0.90$ | $-0.70$ | $-0.50$ | $\text{V}$ | Reject / Probe Recalibrate |
| **Short-Circuit Defect Threshold** | Measured drop at $I_F = -100\,\mu\text{A}$ | $0.20$ | $> 0.50$ | — | $\text{V}$ ($|V_F|$) | Reject: Metal Bridge / Blown Diode |
| **Open-Circuit Clamping Limit** | Voltage compliance clamp reached | — | $< 0.90$ | $1.40$ | $\text{V}$ ($|V_F|$) | Reject: Probe Lift / Open Via |
| **Off-State Reverse Leakage ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | Applied reverse bias $V_{\text{rev}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ ($V_{DD}$) | — | $< 10.0$ | $1000.0$ | $\text{nA}$ | Reject: Leaky Diode / Contamination |

---

### 5. Verified Literature & Context Citations
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Unit cell access channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, target sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: Standard 180nm node dielectric and metallization geometry; retention threshold timing $> 64\text{ ms}$ requiring strict pre-stress pin integrity.
- **Source: High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**: Core supply rails $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$ and Dickson 4-stage charge pump high-voltage output $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$ driving enhancement access transistors ($V_{th} \sim 0.5\text{ V}\text{ to }0.7\text{ V}$), setting the upper compliance boundary against latch-up during ESD continuity screening.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated open/short (O/S) continuity screening using ESD diode forward-bias current forcing must execute concurrently across multi-site probe testheads without ground-bounce cross-talk. When forcing -1.0 mA into ESD rail clamp diodes with Kelvin sense channels, common-mode return path inductance through the probe card substrate can cause false open indications on adjacent I/O pins if testhead strobing is not strictly staggered or isolated by separate analog ground planes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm CMOS node, standard ESD protection consists of dual diode clamps (to VDD and VSS) or grounded-gate NMOS (ggNMOS) with intrinsic substrate diodes. Forcing -1.0 mA against substrate ground should yield a forward knee voltage between 0.65 V and 0.75 V (measured as -0.65 V to -0.75 V relative to VSS pad). Contact resistance variations from probe tip scrub oxide punch-through (typical contact resistance Rc < 2.0 Ohm) must not cause an erroneous open threshold shift beyond the nominal 1.2 V compliance ceiling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Micro-cantilever probe tips (Tungsten-Rhenium or Paliney-7 alloy) degrade rapidly from aluminum oxide accumulation during high-density multi-site contact checks. Sourcing replacement probe cards for custom 180nm DRAM pads carries lead times of 10 to 14 weeks. A standardized online abrasive scrub card cleaning recipe (e.g. ceramic polishing plate cycling every 250 touchdown cycles) is required to sustain uptime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Die sort test time budget enforces maximum 15 ms total allocation per die for full pin-count O/S continuity verification. High-speed parametric measurement units (PMUs) or per-pin parametric measurement units (PPMUs) must execute parallel DC force-current/measure-voltage (FIMV) tests to prevent wafer throughput dropping below 30 wafers per hour (WPH) on 200mm wafers.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Open contact false alarms caused by native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) passivating bond pads due to insufficient mechanical scrub overdrive (< 35 um).
1. ESD diode punch-through or micro-plasma junction rupture caused by transient inductive voltage spikes exceeding 5.0 V during cold-switching hot-socket probe contact.
1. Adjacent-pin short circuit misclassifications caused by probe needle skid deflection and mechanical bridging on 60 um pitch DRAM bond pads.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-1-3-01` | **Automated ESD Clamp Diode Forward-Bias Continuity (Open Circuit) Screening** | Automated Wafer Prober (e.g., TEL Precio or Accretech UF3000) coupled with ATE Per-Pin Parametric Measurement Unit (PPMU) calibrated to +/- 100 nA current force and +/- 1 mV voltage measurement accuracy. | 1. Step wafer chuck to die coordinates and establish mechanical touchdown at 45 um overdrive. 2. Force 0.0 V reference on substrate VSS and VDD bus lines. 3. Simultaneously force DC current I_force = -1.0 mA on all DUT I/O, control, and address pads with voltage compliance clamp set to -1.50 V. 4. Wait 1.5 ms settling time to suppress capacitive switching transients. 5. Measure resulting voltage V_meas on each individual pad via local Kelvin sense lines. 6. Repeat procedure with I_force = +1.0 mA to VDD rail diodes with compliance set to +1.50 V. | `Continuous Pass: Measured forward diode voltage must fall within -0.800 V <= V_meas <= -0.600 V for VSS-directed diodes and +0.600 V <= V_meas <= +0.800 V for VDD-directed diodes. Fail (Open): |V_meas| >= 1.200 V (indicates open probe contact, broken wire bond, or missing via). Fail (Short): |V_meas| <= 0.150 V (indicates metal-to-metal short to supply rail).` |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-1-3-02` | **Adjacent Pad Bridging and Inter-Terminal Short-Circuit Isolation Screening** | High-Density Per-Pin PMU Tester with matrix relay switching subsystem and sub-nanoampere leakage current measurement capability. | 1. Force 0.0 V DC across all odd-numbered pad channels. 2. Force +1.80 V DC (nominal DRAM core logic VDD) across all even-numbered pad channels with current compliance set to 10.0 mA. 3. Measure leakage current I_leak on every odd-numbered pin after 2.0 ms soak time. 4. Reverse polarity: Force +1.80 V DC on all odd-numbered channels and 0.0 V on all even-numbered channels, measuring leakage current across all even-numbered channels. | `Pass: Isolation leakage current I_leak <= 50.0 nA on all channels under +1.80 V bias. Fail (Resistive or Dead Short): I_leak > 1.00 uA or channel reaches compliance limit (> 10.0 mA), indicating metallic flake bridging, probe card needle shorting, or inter-metal dielectric breakdown.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 compatible nitrile gloves (electrostatic dissipative, surface resistivity 10^9 to 10^11 Ohm/sq), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact-resistant safety glasses, Conductive ESD heel straps and ESD-dissipative lab coat grounding garment
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin exposure to solvent: Wash affected skin immediately with copious flowing water for 15 minutes. Eye exposure: Flush eyes at eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Vapor inhalation: Evacuate person to clean atmospheric air immediately; administer CPR if breathing ceases.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom Class 100 laminar airflow with local solvent exhaust hood at offline probe tip maintenance stations maintaining minimum capture velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). Chuck vacuum exhaust routed to facility neutral exhaust line.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA cleanroom wipes sealed inside airtight conductive flammable waste receptacles and disposed of via certified hazardous chemical incineration; no solvent discharge into municipal drain.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Electronic Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 | `99.9%` |
| **Ultra-Pure Nitrogen (N2 Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | UHP Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Sputtered and annealed Al-0.5%Cu top metal bond pads passivated with Si3N4/SiO2 scratch protection stack; pads freshly plasma etched with contact open windows exhibiting native Al2O3 thickness < 3.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested bond pads showing visible mechanical probe scrub marks (scrub depth <= 1.2 um, scrub length 8 to 15 um) without underlying barrier layer (Ti/TiN) peeling or dielectric crazing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide thickening beyond 6.0 nm and moisture-induced galvanic corrosion of exposed Al-Cu pads causing probe contact resistance escalation (Rc > 10 Ohm), leading to massive false open rejects and probe tip clogging.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> 100% automated wafer-level ESD continuity and open/short DC screening of all 200mm DRAM wafers at sort floor, successfully isolating gross physical defects, pad bridging, and defective ESD clamp junctions prior to memory core functional testing.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram180_wafer_sort_os_parametric_log.csv`
- [ ] `wafer_map_os_yield_distribution.pdf`
- [ ] `probe_mark_optical_inspection_scrub_audit.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **ESD forward diode voltage under -1.0 mA forced substrate current** | `-0.680 V` | +/- 0.080 V | High-precision automated ATE PPMU force-current measure-voltage (FIMV) Kelvin measurement at 25.0 deg C. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Adjacent bond pad inter-electrode DC leakage current under 1.80 V reverse/isolation bias** | `2.5 nA` | < 50.0 nA max limit | Automated tester DC parametric channel current measurement using 10 nA instrumentation range. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Total electrical open/short screening execution time per die across 64-pin probe array** | `12.0 ms` | <= 15.0 ms max limit | ATE digital pattern generator and parametric executive internal CPU timestamp benchmark. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full wafer run execution completes with zero tester aborts, O/S continuity yield >= 99.2% on known-good control wafers, average probe scrub mark area <= 20% of bond pad opening with zero pad metal peel-off verified by optical inspection, and complete export of compliant parametric CSV and wafer map lot artifacts.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Wafer-Level DC Parametric Extraction (Leakage, Vth, Iddq) & Power Rail Screening

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated DC parametric screening must decouple probe card parasitic trace resistance (target < 0.35 Ohm) and relay matrix capacitance from high-gain transimpedance amplifier channels. In a 180nm DRAM matrix, quiescent Iddq and sub-threshold leakage extraction at 1.8V core VDD are prone to false positives caused by probe card leakage currents and transient charging spikes unless Kelvin 4-wire sensing and a minimum settle time of 25 ms post-clamping are strictly maintained across all automated test head pin electronics.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Accurate threshold voltage (Vth) extraction for 180nm periphery NMOS/PMOS and DRAM pass-transistor array test structures requires strict adherence to the constant-current method (Id = 100 nA * W/L at Vds = 50 mV) or linear extrapolation from transconductance max (gm_max). At wafer sort, unpassivated or native-oxide-covered Al-0.5%Cu probe pads present variable contact resistance; overdrive scrubs must break through surface native Al2O3 films without micro-cracking the underlying low-k/TEOS inter-metal dielectric (IMD) stack or inducing mechanical shear delamination.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom micro-cantilever and vertical cobra-style tungsten-rhenium (WRe) probe cards for full-wafer 180nm DRAM stepping face a 12-16 week lead-time bottleneck and high refurbishment costs. Probe needle tip wear, tip flattening, and aluminum pad material pickup directly degrade probe lifetime (rated at 500k touchdowns). Standardizing automated on-line ceramic abrasive cleaning pads (e.g., tungsten-carbide or alumina lapping sheets) is required to sustain needle shape without premature probe card disposal.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Parametric test execution time directly drives factory throughput; keeping per-die DC parametric test time below 180 ms across 100% of tested reticles is vital for keeping test cell costs within open-source tapeout budget allocations. A multi-site parallel test scheme (minimum x4 die parallel testing) must be certified during EDS bring-up to avoid becoming the critical path milestone bottleneck prior to dicing and plastic/ceramic wire-bond packaging.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dielectric punch-through or micro-fracture of BEOL IMD/ILD oxide under the bond pad due to excessive probe cantilever overdrive (> 50 um scrub depth).
1. Spurious Iddq screening failures and erroneous leakage binning caused by humidity-induced surface moisture leakage or organic contamination films bridging probe needles on the interface card.
1. ESD or voltage clamp overshoot during rapid relay switching exceeding thin gate oxide breakdown (V_bd < 4.2V for 1.8V core transistors), causing irreversible gate oxide pinhole rupture.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-2-01` | **Automated Wafer-Level Quiescent Power Rail Leakage (Iddq) and VDD/VSS Short-Circuit Screening** | Automated Wafer Prober (e.g. FormFactor/Cascade 200mm/300mm prober) with Kelvin 4-point force-sense chuck, High-Density SMU Parametric Test System (Keysight 4080 / Keithley 4200-SCS equivalent), WRe Cantilever Probe Card. | 1. Align wafer notch and calibrate optical vision system against probe pad alignment fiducials on corner dies. 2. Step prober to Die (X=0, Y=0) and initiate chuck Z-axis touchdown with 35 um overdrive. 3. Configure SMU 1 connected to core VDD (1.8V rail) in 4-wire remote sense mode; clamp compliance current at 100 mA. 4. Apply 0.0V to VSS, ground substrate p-well pads, and ground all array wordlines and bitlines. 5. Ramp VDD from 0.0V to 1.80V at a slew rate of 10 V/s; wait 30 ms settling delay. 6. Integrate DC current measurement over 10 Power Line Cycles (NPLC=10) to extract quiescent current Iddq. 7. Repeat step across designated 9-point cross-wafer sample sites (Center, North, South, East, West, and 4 quadrants). | `Quiescent core leakage Iddq must measure <= 1.25 uA per die at VDD = 1.80V and 25 deg C. Absolute short-circuit current must not trip the 100 mA compliance threshold. Measurement Gauge R&R coefficient of variation (CV) across 10 repeated touchdowns on golden die must be < 1.0%.` |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-2-02` | **Periphery Transistor Threshold Voltage (Vth) and Subthreshold Swing (SS) Parametric Extraction** | Parametric SMU Matrix (Keysight B1500A / Keithley 4200-SCS) integrated with Automated Semi-Automatic/Automatic Wafer Prober, Triaxial Kelvin probe cables, dry N2 purge micro-chamber. | 1. Step probe head to scribe-line PCM macro site and engage pad touchdown with 30-35 um Z-overdrive. 2. Force Vbulk = 0.0V, Vsource = 0.0V, Vdrain = 50 mV DC. 3. Sweep gate voltage (Vgate) from 0.0V to 1.20V in 10 mV increments with 5 ms measurement aperture per step. 4. Measure drain current (Id) across 6 decades (10 pA to 1 mA) via low-current pre-amplifier. 5. Compute transconductance gm = d(Id)/d(Vgate) and extract Vth via linear extrapolation of maximum gm tangent to Id=0 axis. 6. Compute subthreshold swing SS = (d(log10(Id))/d(Vgate))^-1 in the weak inversion regime (100 pA to 10 nA). 7. Log parameters and repeat for complementary PMOS structure (Vdrain = -50 mV, Vgate swept 0.0V to -1.20V). | `Core NMOS Vth must measure 480 mV +/- 45 mV; core PMOS |Vth| must measure 520 mV +/- 50 mV. Subthreshold swing SS must be <= 85 mV/decade for both device types. Scribe-line leakage at Vgate = 0.0V, Vdrain = 1.8V must be < 50 pA/um.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static/ESD-dissipative), ANSI Z87.1 Approved UV/Laser and Impact Safety Glasses, Full Anti-Static Cleanroom Frock / Jumpsuit with Conductive Carbon Threading, ESD Grounding Wrist Strap with 1 Megohm Resistor (when handling ungrounded assemblies), Static-Dissipative Cleanroom Safety Booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin or eye contact with IPA probe cleaning solvent: Flush eyes immediately with copious sterile eyewash for at least 15 minutes while retracting eyelids; wash contaminated skin with water and mild detergent. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors or nitrogen asphyxiation hazard: Immediately transfer victim to fresh, uncontaminated air; administer artificial respiration or supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; seek prompt medical evaluation. No specific chemical antidote; provide supportive clinical care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Cleanroom ISO Class 5 laminar downflow hood with continuous face velocity of 0.45 m/s +/- 20%. Dedicated localized solvent vapor exhaust extraction arm (minimum 50 CFM) connected to prober needle-cleaning station. Ambient oxygen depletion monitoring sensors (O2 alarm setpoint < 19.5% v/v) active inside prober enclosure during high-flow N2 chuck purging.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of spent IPA wipes and needle cleaning swabs in designated airtight, grounded, flame-retardant stainless-steel hazardous waste receptacles. Liquid IPA runoff must be collected in segregated solvent waste drums; never drain into municipal sanitary or acid-waste neutralization (AWN) sewers. Off-site thermal incineration via certified hazardous materials disposal contractor.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Electronic Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade C-1 (Ultra-Pure VLSI Grade) | `99.9% v/v` |
| **Compressed Gaseous Nitrogen (Dry N2 Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (99.999% purity, dew point < -70 deg C) | `100% v/v` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed Passivation 2 Pad Etch (SiN/Oxide opening) with clean, unpassivated Al-0.5%Cu bond pads, free of organic photoresist residue and post-ash fluorine polymers.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Parametrically screened wafer with scrubbed probe needle impressions (depth < 0.6 um, area < 15% of total pad surface), free of dendritic aluminum pile-up, ready for wafer dicing or dry storage.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native atmospheric oxidation and moisture adsorption form a thick insulating Al2O3 passivating crust (thickness > 5 nm) on bond pads, causing probe contact resistance to surge (> 5 Ohm), triggering false open-circuit faults, severe needle scrubbing skid, and micro-cracking of underlying BEOL low-k/IMD dielectric layers.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full 200mm wafer-level DC parametric characterization and power rail qualification across all reticles and scribe-line PCM test sites on 180nm DRAM tapeout wafers, establishing complete baseline extraction of Vth, Iddq, transconductance, and gate oxide integrity.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WP_MET_DC_PARAMETRIC_WAFER_MAP.csv`
- [ ] `EDS_PARAMETRIC_EXTRACTION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `PROBE_SCRUB_MARK_INSPECTION_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wafer-level core power rail quiescent current (Iddq) across all functional die sites** | `<= 1.25 uA` | +0.15 uA | Automated 4-wire SMU integration at VDD = 1.80V, 25 deg C with 10 NPLC filtering |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Scribe-line PCM baseline core NMOS threshold voltage (Vth)** | `480 mV` | +/- 45 mV | Maximum transconductance (gm_max) linear extrapolation on 10um/0.18um device test structures at Vds = 50 mV |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Automated Kelvin probe contact resistance repeatability across 9-point wafer mapping** | `0.35 Ohm` | CV < 1.0% | Gauge R&R four-wire measurement over 10 consecutive touchdowns on designated shorting gold/aluminum test pads |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of wafer die sites successfully tested with zero instrument-induced oxide punch-through events; Gauge R&R contact resistance CV confirmed < 1.0%; all deliverable files (CSV wafer map, signed PDF parametric summary, and high-resolution scrub mark TIFF) archived into the DRAM Foundation repository with formal metrology lead signoff.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated DC Parametric Test Recipe Development & Test Pattern Mapping
**Classification:** Gen 3 (180nm CMOS Open-Source DRAM)  
**Task Action:** Make  
**Hierarchy Context:** Architecture & Integration $\to$ Foundry Tapeout & PDK $\to$ BEOL & Packaging $\to$ Wafer Sort & Metrology $\to$ Wafer-Level EDS DC Parametric Screening $\to$ Automated DC Parametric Test Recipe Development & Test Pattern Mapping

---

### Process Execution Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 1: Automated    │
│      Test Recipe       │
│     Initialization     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        Step 2:         │
│    Micro-Cantilever    │
│  Probe Card Stepping   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Step 3: Linear Vth &  │
│  Transconductance gm   │
│       Extraction       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Step 4: On/Off     │
│   Saturation Ratio &   │
│      Iddq Leakage      │
│       Screening        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Step 5: Stacked     │
│  Capacitor & Bitline   │
│   Coupling Metrology   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Step 6: Wafer-Level   │
│      Test Pattern      │
│  Bitmapping & Binning  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Automated Test Recipe Initialization & Grid Setup**
   - Configure the parametric tester coordinate mapping with a physical placement grid resolution of **0.005 µm (5 nm)**.
   - Program tester die-pitch step coordinates aligned to pad pitch geometries based on Metal 1 minimum width of **0.14 µm** and minimum pitch of **0.34 µm** with contact hole dimensions of **0.17 µm × 0.17 µm**.

2. **Micro-Cantilever Probe Card Alignment & Contacting**
   - Align micro-cantilever probe tips to scribe-line test element groups (TEG) and wafer sort pads. Ensure maximum stage step overlay error does not exceed **$\le 35\text{ nm}$** between gate poly and active diffusion geometries.
   - Execute controlled touchdown with overdrive compensation to verify contact resistance before executing voltage sweep sequences.

3. **Linear Region Threshold Voltage ($V_{th}$) & $g_m$ Extraction**
   - Step to the discrete transistor test structures:
     - Long-channel reference transistor ($W / L = 20\text{ µm} / 5\text{ µm}$)
     - Intermediate transistor ($W / L = 10\text{ µm} / 1.0\text{ µm}$)
     - Sub-micron target transistor ($W / L = 2.0\text{ µm} / 0.18\text{ µm}$)
   - Apply linear drain bias of $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$.
   - Sweep gate voltage $V_{GS}$ from $0\text{ V}$ to $1.8\text{ V}$ in fine increments.
   - Extract maximum transconductance ($g_m = \frac{\partial I_D}{\partial V_{GS}}$) and determine linear $V_{th}$ through maximum $g_m$ extrapolation.

4. **Saturation On/Off Current ($I_{on}/I_{off}$) & $I_{ddq}$ Screening**
   - Apply saturation bias $V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
   - Measure drive current $I_{on}$ at $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$ normalized to channel width.
   - Measure off-state subthreshold leakage current $I_{off}$ at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$ and quiescent power rail leakage $I_{ddq}$.
   - Compute $I_{on} / I_{off}$ dynamic current ratio.

5. **DRAM Stacked Capacitor Metrology & Retention Leakage Screening**
   - Step micro-probes to access transistor ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) capacitor array test pads.
   - Perform precision C-V measurement at $1\text{ MHz}$ across the crown/MIM stacked capacitor with ONO / high-$k$ ($\kappa > 15$) dielectric over tungsten plug (W-plug) to verify unit cell storage capacitance.
   - Perform elevated temperature ($85^\circ\text{C}$) subthreshold and junction leakage current extraction on storage node nodes.

6. **Automated Wafer-Level Bitmapping & Binning**
   - Map extraction parameters per die across the entire wafer radius.
   - Mark out-of-spec dies violating leakage, threshold voltage windows, or capacitance limits.
   - Export structured parametric test data and wafer defect wafermap to the EDS database.

---

### Parametric Metric Targets

```text
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │░░░░░░░░░                                    │
Grid (nm)┤░░░░░░░░░                                    │
         │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│

```

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

1. **Threshold Voltage Extrapolation Window ($V_{th}$)**:
   - NMOS linear threshold voltage ($V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$): **$V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$** ($+0.50\text{ V}$ to $+0.60\text{ V}$).
   - PMOS linear threshold voltage ($V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$): **$V_{thp} = -0.60\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$** ($-0.55\text{ V}$ to $-0.65\text{ V}$).
2. **Current Drive & Switching Dynamic Ratio ($I_{on}/I_{off}$)**:
   - On-state saturation current ($V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$): **$I_{on} \ge 500\text{ µA/µm}$**.
   - Off-state subthreshold leakage ($V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$): **$I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA/µm}$**.
   - Dynamic switching ratio: **$I_{on} / I_{off} > 10^7$**.
3. **Stacked Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)**:
   - Minimum cell storage capacitance: **$\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$** with dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$.
4. **DRAM Storage Cell Leakage Current**:
   - Sub-threshold and junction leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$: **$\le 1\text{ fA/cell}$**.
5. **Physical Alignment & Lithography Overlay Tolerance**:
   - Placement grid resolution: **$0.005\text{ µm}$ ($5\text{ nm}$)**.
   - Poly gate to active diffusion overlay error: **$\le 35\text{ nm}$**.

---

### Context Citations

- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), stacked capacitor with W-plug contact, ONO / high-$k$ dielectric ($\kappa > 15$), minimum cell capacitance of **$28\text{ fF/cell}$**, and cell leakage target of **$\le 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$**.
- **[Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification]**: Test transistor dimensions ($20\text{ µm}/5\text{ µm}$, $10\text{ µm}/1.0\text{ µm}$, $2.0\text{ µm}/0.18\text{ µm}$), linear $V_{th}$ extraction at $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$ ($V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, $V_{thp} = -0.60\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$), saturation at $V_{DS} = 1.8\text{ V}$ ($I_{on} \ge 500\text{ µA/µm}$, $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA/µm}$), and dynamic ratio $I_{on}/I_{off} > 10^7$.
- **[SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid]**: Manufacturing grid of **$0.005\text{ µm}$ ($5\text{ nm}$)**, poly gate length of $150\text{ nm}$, contact dimensions of $0.17\text{ µm} \times 0.17\text{ µm}$, Metal 1 width of $0.14\text{ µm}$ and pitch of $0.34\text{ µm}$, and maximum permissible gate poly to active diffusion overlay error of **$\le 35\text{ nm}$**.

### Documentation Update Notice
Per project micro-knowledge extraction protocol, this SOP and its physical specifications have been persisted to [docs/knowledge/automated_dc_parametric_test_recipe_mapping.md](./docs/knowledge/automated_dc_parametric_test_recipe_mapping.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated DC parametric recipes must strictly constrain SMU settling times, force/sense line compliance voltages, and capacitive discharge spikes across long probe-card trace harnesses. When measuring sub-picoamp junction leakages or extracting 180nm core NMOS/PMOS threshold voltages (Vth) across a multi-site micro-cantilever probe interface, ground loops and unshielded Kelvin triaxial lines will distort IV curve knees and elevate noise floors above 50 fA.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm DRAM node, Iddq quiescent power rail screening and parametric threshold voltage extraction require sub-Angstrom gate dielectric stability (equivalent dry gate oxide tox ~3.5 nm) and tight sheet resistance control. Probe overdrive depth must be dynamically compensated for wafer bow/warp across 49-point wafer maps; excessive probe scrub will punch through thin top-metal pads (Al-0.5%Cu / TiN barrier), whereas inadequate overdrive leaves native oxide barriers causing artificial contact resistance (R_contact > 2.5 ohms) and erroneous Vth shift estimations.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom micro-cantilever probe cards with fine-pitch tungsten-rhenium or vertical MEMS needle arrays face 12-to-16 week lead times and high repair costs. High-speed multi-site DC test recipes must integrate automated in-line abrasive ceramic needle cleaning (aluminum oxide / silicon carbide cleaning pads) and probe force monitoring to guarantee needle contact life beyond 500,000 touchdowns without supply stockout.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test recipe development and test pattern coordinate mapping are critical gating dependencies on the Gen 3 critical path prior to full functional wafer sort bitmapping. If test execution time exceeds 45 milliseconds per die across 100% of wafer sites, total lot screening will slip schedule margins by more than 5 working days, stalling fab-to-package handoff.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Probe tip scrub over-travel inducing micro-cracks in inter-metal dielectric (IMD) / low-k layers beneath bond pads, causing latent inter-layer leakage and pad delamination during packaging.
1. Excessive capacitive discharge from probe card cables during un-clamped Iddq / Vth extraction, inducing electrical overstress (EOS) and gate oxide dielectric breakdown in 1.8V peripheral transistors.
1. Inaccurate coordinate offset mapping between automated wafer prober chuck optics and die stepping grids, causing misaligned needle drops on passivation borders rather than active test pads.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-2-1-01` | **Automated Wafer-Level DC Parametric Extraction & Gauge R&R Verification** | Automated 200mm Wafer Prober (e.g. TEL P8XL or FormFactor Cascade) with temperature-controlled chuck (25°C ± 0.5°C), High-Resolution Parametric Measurement Unit / Tester (Keysight 4070/4080 or B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer), and Multi-Site Cantilever Probe Card with Triaxial Kelvin Connections. | 1. Perform automated wafer-level optical alignment and establish Z-reference datum across 9 reference die coordinates. 2. Index probe card to die location (0, 0) and apply 45 um probe overdrive. 3. Force drain-to-source voltage Vds = 0.1 V on test structure NMOS transistor; sweep gate voltage Vgs from 0.0 V to 1.8 V in 20 mV increments while measuring drain current Ids. 4. Extract linear threshold voltage (Vth) at constant current Ids = 0.1 uA * (W/L). 5. Force Vdd = 1.8 V on peripheral power rail test pad with all input pins grounded and measure steady-state quiescent current (Iddq) after 5 ms settling time. 6. Repeat steps 2-5 across a standard 9-point radial wafer map for 30 consecutive repeat cycles to quantify measurement repeatability (Gauge R&R). | `NMOS Vth must measure 0.42 V ± 0.04 V across all 9 radial sites; Iddq leakage must remain < 50 pA/die at 25°C; probe contact resistance Rc < 1.5 Ohms; measurement coefficient of variation (CV) across 30 repeated runs must satisfy CV < 1.0% with Gauge R&R (repeatability & reproducibility) < 10% of process tolerance.` |
| `TC-WAFER-SORT-PROBE-3-2-1-02` | **Automated Test Pattern Coordinate Mapping & Probe Mark Scrub Boundary Verification** | Automated Wafer Prober Vision Subsystem, High-Precision Motorized Stepping Stage (0.1 um linear encoder resolution), and Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) / High-Magnification Confocal Review Microscope. | 1. Execute automated step-and-repeat coordinate map verification over 49 sampled die sites across center, middle, and edge wafer zones. 2. Record optical probe mark coordinates (X_mark, Y_mark) relative to pad center coordinates (X_pad, Y_pad) on 60 um x 60 um aluminum test pads. 3. Measure probe scrub mark length (L_scrub), scrub mark width (W_scrub), and scrub depth using confocal focus profiling. 4. Verify clearance margin between the edge of the scrub mark and the outer edge of the pad passivation opening. 5. Inspect for aluminum pile-up, exposed underlying barrier metal, or passivation cracking at scrub boundaries. | `Probe scrub mark centroid must remain within ±4.0 um of pad center; maximum scrub mark length must not exceed 18.0 um; scrub mark depth must not penetrate > 40% of the 800 nm Al-Cu top metal thickness; zero probe marks outside passivation opening; zero micro-cracking or barrier peeling detected across 100% inspected test pads.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 / ISO 5 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static, powder-free, puncture-resistant), ANSI Z87.1 Approved Safety Glasses with Side Shields, ESD-Safe Grounded Conductive Smock and Cleanroom Booties, Grounded Wrist Strap connected to prober station bench ground
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin Exposure (IPA): Immediately flush skin with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated gloves/clothing. Eye Contact (IPA/particulate): Flush eyes at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek medical attention. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately. If asphyxiation symptoms occur from localized N2 accumulation, administer oxygen by certified cleanroom emergency response team.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom laminar air flow (> 90 ft/min face velocity, ISO Class 5 / Class 100 enclosure); dedicated local laminar exhaust on manual chemical wipe stations; automated prober N2 purge enclosure equipped with continuous low-oxygen ambient monitoring sensor and audible alarm threshold (< 19.5% O2).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-soaked cleanroom wipes and abrasive cleaning pads in double-bagged, dedicated airtight flammable hazardous waste containers. Liquid IPA waste from manual needle maintenance must be collected in closed conductive stainless-steel safety cans and transferred to certified hazardous solvent collection systems.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (electronic wafer/needle cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI Purity | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas (wafer drying / purge)** | `7727-37-9` | High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `180 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-passivation etch, bond-pad open anneal, and post-clean surface with clean native aluminum oxide (Al2O3 < 2.5 nm thick), free of organic residue, fluoropolymer etch byproducts, and particle contamination (> 0.2 um particle count < 10 per 200mm wafer).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probe-tested bond pads exhibiting controlled tungsten-needle scrub indentations confined entirely within pad metallization, free of organic transfer films, needle debris, or atmospheric moisture condensation, with wafers immediately returned to purged FOUP/cassette.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom air queue time induces uncontrolled atmospheric moisture absorption and galvanic oxidation on Al-Cu pad surfaces, generating thick, non-uniform aluminum hydroxides that cause probe scrub slip, elevated contact resistance (Rc > 10 ohms), false open-circuit binning during EDS, and non-stick bond failures during downstream gold/copper wire bonding.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full deployment and empirical qualification of the automated DC parametric test recipe and 49-point wafer mapping protocol for 180nm DRAM test structures. The deliverable guarantees stable wafer-level extraction of core transistor parameters (Vth, linear/saturation drive currents, subthreshold slope), power rail quiescent leakage (Iddq), and contact resistance with Gauge R&R measurement repeatability CV < 1.0%, zero IMD punch-through, and 100% automated datalogging.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DC_PARAMETRIC_RECIPE_180NM_REV3.xml`
- [ ] `WAFER_MAP_COORDINATE_ALIGNMENT_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `GAUGE_RR_DC_EXTRACTION_49POINT.csv`

| `ASSERT-03` | **Quiescent power rail leakage (Iddq) baseline resolution and noise floor at Vdd = 1.8 V and 25°C chuck temperature** | `12.0 pA` | <= 50.0 pA | High-resolution triaxial SMU integration over 10 power line cycles (NPLC=10) on un-clocked test die power domains. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 100% execution of automated recipe DC_PARAMETRIC_RECIPE_180NM_REV3.xml across a full 25-wafer demonstration lot, achieving Gauge R&R CV < 1.0% across all 9-point and 49-point parameter extractions, zero false fails from probe needle misalignment (scrub centroid error <= 4.0 um), zero barrier layer penetrations confirmed via post-probe confocal microscopy, and complete electronic data interchange (STDF/CSV) ingestion into the DRAM Foundation VN metrology database.
